As a holder of noble office, Chalmers bore the title Protector of the Eternal Flame and received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry. His works are held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and the copyright status of his creative output is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Chalmers was a member of the Kaelwyn family. He was the son of Orynth Mccool and Kirelle Mariselle. He was married to Nytheran Manley from 28 November 1745 until 31 May 1779. Other recorded relatives include Irvin Caldwell, Irvin Oathen and Quithar Towns.

He had eleven children: Helorin Weiser (23 November 1746–13 May 1747), Emrynd Albino (3 July 1748–14 October 1797), Hesperyn Amy (24 January 1751–17 August 1825), Wynelle Marigold Thorne (28 September 1753–4 February 1823), Kirelle Amara Solis (13 March 1755–16 February 1840), Hesthrin Pogue (25 January 1758–13 November 1804), Falyndra Mccreary (24 July 1759–16 July 1821), Phyren Bogart (9 August 1761–12 June 1797), Ytherin Moffett (9 November 1762–30 March 1826), Garenth Art (18 January 1765–3 August 1841) and Gwendal Heart (23 May 1769–2 May 1852).

Chalmers is described in several reference works and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library. He is listed as distinct from Rhystar Shahzad.

Henris Liranzo (1394 – 19 June 1470) was a knyaz of the Willowbend noble family.

He was the son of Fariel Bunting and Cyndel Arango. He had ten siblings: Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston, Teryn Disla, and Zyndra Shinde.

Henris Liranzo is described in the biographical dictionaries Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Nautilus Bay is a big city and seaport in the sovereign state of Nymbrelia. Located on the ocean Abyssalith, the city came into existence on 6 March 1576.

Nautilus Bay is twinned with a number of other municipalities. Its partnerships include Celestial Harbor (since 2048), Caldemere (since 2050), Falendropolis (since 2050), Celestport (since 2054), Shianthor (since 2054) and Solaris City (since 2055), and it is also twinned with Hightree and Novarun.

The city has been described in several works, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Folios (published 1880), the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Zyvra Smoot (16 May 1775 – 28 September 1783) was a princess and aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty. Born in Nethoria, she spoke Therian and held the noble title of princess while carrying out duties associated with her aristocratic station.

She was the daughter of Inigo Valente and Dravion Appiah. Her siblings included Delphina Nereth Vale and Delphina Loritha Vent, as well as Elanthar Gasca, Inigo Montale, Nylaris Prendergast, Peryn Harder, Selorin Alegria, Tobias Winstone, Viorelle Mariselle and Xandor Lemons.

She died on 28 September 1783. The manner of her death was recorded as natural causes, with smallpox given as the cause of death.

Galactic Sentinel is a fictional spacecraft portrayed as a vessel of a spaceflight organization that functions as a military organization ship, an educational institution ship and a spacecraft manufacturer ship. It was introduced in 2035 and entered service in 2411. The craft is from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise; it follows the Astro Defense League.

The ship made its first appearance in the film Eldoria Chronicles: The Celestial Saga. It has been described by the magazine VividViews and appears across a number of written works and novels, including Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions, Nebulae Script, Phantom Text, Shadowed Annals, The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Echoing Annotations, The Last Songbird and The Written Horizon.

Galactic Sentinel’s crew roster includes Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe. The vessel is commanded by Freya Wilder, who also serves aboard as a crew member.

Crystaline Honor is an order awarded to individual recipients in the Myralun Empire. It was instituted on 21 May 1764 and was formed in Zephyra, the capital and largest city of the Myralun Empire.

The order includes the Arcadian Emblem, a grade of the order associated with the year 1879.

Crystaline Honor is documented in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition, and in LexiRealm, an encyclopedic dictionary.

Jorith Feeney (born 29 August 1991) is a designer and sculptor whose work spans industrial design, jewelry design and sculpture. Her practice covers furniture, jewelry and product packaging, and she lives and works in Silvershore.

Feeney is represented by The Artisan's Retreat, a commercial art gallery, and by The Publishing Parlor, a design gallery and publishing company. She is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

Her works are held in public collections including Essence of Art, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Reverie Repository. Feeney has participated in a range of exhibitions and publications: she has taken part in Beyond the Frame and Visual Harmony (both art catalogs and art exhibitions), and in Enumeration Enclave and Presentation Pavilion (catalogue and exhibition). She has also exhibited in Fabricated Realities and The Enigma Exhibition, and appeared in Illustrated Realities and The Exhibition Archive, which combine exhibition and publication formats. In addition, her work has been shown in the temporary exhibitions Impermanent Inspirations and The Ephemeral Showcase.

Her published works remain protected by copyrights.

Mosaic of Memories is an exhibition that opened on 1 November 2025 and closed on 2 January 2027. It was presented at The Publishing Parlor from 1 November to 28 November 2025. The Publishing Parlor functions as a design gallery, publishing company and collection.

The exhibition included a range of participants. Among them were Beryth Olson, Chyra Musgrove, Elyndor Landis, Galyn Sweat, Jorlan Macfarlane, Lythor Cline, Orinthar Bocanegra and Paxton Edrinthal. Additional participants were Paylan Barrows, Qylar Yañez, Rhyall Puma, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, Tyndra Andy, Ulthara Sunday, Xandria Fundora and Zyreth Paola.

Sculpted Dreams is an art museum, cultural institution, museum, national museum and sculpture garden located in Krestoria. The institution officially opened in 1977; its inception is recorded as 1977-07-13 and an additional inception entry is recorded for 2009. It has been recognized as a registered museum.

The museum building was designed by Hesper Kaelith. Sculpted Dreams works in the field of performing arts and presents sculpture and related programs in its gardens and exhibition spaces. Works from Sculpted Dreams are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum.

Sculpted Dreams maintains a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium and became a member of The Alliance of Ideas on 2059-01-01. For admission and services it accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a discount card, museum card and ticket.

PixelMart is an online shop and a video game distribution platform. They operate as a digital distribution platform for video games and serve as the distributor for a wide range of titles.

Several of the games distributed by PixelMart are played professionally as esports disciplines, among them Apex Legends, Arcane Duelists, Inferno League and Pixel Warriors. They also distribute the media-franchise title Eldoria Chronicles: Legends of the Shattered Realm.

PixelMart distributes many other video games, including Aegis of Dawn, Arcane Legends, Celestial Clash, Celestial Command, Celestial Harvest, Chrono Quest, Crystal Conquest, Cyber Drift and Cybernetic Warriors. Other titles available through PixelMart include Destiny's Call, Echoes of Eternity, Elemental Odyssey, Emberverse Adventures, Enigma Expedition, Eternal Battlegrounds, Ether Quest and Flames of Destiny. They additionally distribute Galactic Odyssey, Lost Dimensions, Luminary Quest, Meridian's Borderlands, Mythic Arena, Mythical Crusade, Pixel Odyssey and Prism Pioneers. Additional releases on the platform include Quantum Duel, Radiant Quest, Realm of Chaos, Shadow Realm, Shadowed Alliances, Stellar Siege, Void Warriors, Warlord's Legacy and Zenith Ascendancy.

Xandor Collective is a collection of purposely gathered physical and digital works that share common characteristics. The collection holds works by a wide range of creators.

It includes works by Axton Thorne, Baran Snowden, Braxton Carter Smith, Caelith Heim, Caelum Aguayo, Cydon Atwood, Denzel Montgomery, Draxella Charles, Eriath Deboer, and Fintan Alderwood. Also represented are Garenth Rmz, Kylas Ferro, Melethar Vélez, Moryn Vail, Orilith Piedrahita, Pytherin Cid, Quelor Simon, Quinella Lemons, and Quinlan Hartwood. The holdings further comprise works by Rhaelar Busch, Rhyall Puma, Seran Vieira, Talyra Emberwood, Ulyr Rust, Vorith Mclean, Wryndra Morado, Yardley Elvyn Trasy, Yates Hawthorne, Ylorith Avelino, Zeryn Grey, and Zeyth Claxton.

Impermanent Inspirations was a temporary exhibition held at The Collective Gallery, a museum. It opened on 25 May 2041 and closed on 11 August 2041.

Participants included Aelynd Her, Bastian Alaric Thorne, Brynara Balla, Deleth Fowler, Delyria Solís, Elanth Omalley, Elaria Varney, Grelyn Maynard, Jorian Ribera and Jorin Krishnamurthy. Others taking part were Jorith Feeney, Jorlan Macfarlane, Lamyra Sanborn, Melethar Vélez, Orinthar Bocanegra, Paxton Edrinthal, Pherian Palm, Qylara Stine, Qyra Rios and Rhelian Ken. The exhibition also included Rhyall Puma, Rynel Santiesteban, Seran Vieira, Thalion Poore, Ulyndor Fenwick, Ulyr Rust, Yalindra Marciano, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Zeyth Claxton and Zorith Huh.

Valtaris is a noble title created in 1681. The title is associated with several states: Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian (a colonial power, country, historical country and sovereign state), Cynthera (a colonial power, country, island country and sovereign state), the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom (a country, historical country, kingdom and sovereign state), and Kytarathia (a historical country and sovereign state).

The official residence of the title is Radiant Manor, a palace.

Holders of the title have included Valtaris Celestria Thornevale, who held it from 1681 until 24 December 1699; Elysian Valtaris, who held it from 1766 to 12 January 1798; Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, who held it from 1828 to 5 October 1867; Elara Valtaris, who held it from 1880 to 5 August 1940; Delphina Valtaris, who held it from 1944 to 4 January 1970; and Aldric Valtaris, who began holding the title in 2026.

Fabricated Realities was an art exhibition organized by the Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college. The exhibition took place in Krestoria in 2037.

Participants included Aelynd Her, Beryth Olson, Brynara Balla, Jorian Ribera, Jorith Feeney and Lythor Cline, as well as Orinthar Bocanegra and Paxton Edrinthal. Other participants were Paylan Barrows, Qylar Yañez, Ulthara Sunday, Xandria Fundora, Yelith Higgs and Zyreth Paola.

Krishnamurthy Art Archive is an art collection of purposefully gathered artworks. It is maintained by the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, an art museum that is responsible for the archive's care and upkeep.

Wryth Beas (born 14 January 1880 – died 2 March 1934) was an artist whose practice encompassed drawing, engraving, lithography and painting. She worked primarily in the art of painting, producing both landscape painting and portrait painting. She died of influenza on 2 March 1934.

Beas was associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement and was both influenced by and related to Helyndra Jean-Baptiste. She studied under Cole-Ren Ashford-Mendez. Her occupations are recorded as artist, drawer, engraver, lithographer and painter.

Her professional activity is documented as beginning on 1 January 1897 and ending on 1 January 1934. During her career she worked in Calidore, the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and Mystralyn. She spoke Therian. Some of her work was published in Infinite Reimagining, and she is described in sources including Biographical Artifices, DataGalaxy, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault.

Beas’s works are held in a wide range of collections, including Aesthetic Insights Press; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation; Canvas of Illusions Gallery; Cultural Nexus; Culturia Heritage Authority; Harmonious Expanse; Inspiring Visions Art Center; Kaleidoscope Museum of Art; Muse Oasis; Myrthwood Art Collective; National Artistry Hub; National Gallery of Creative Diversity; National Institute of Cultural Heritage; National Legacy Gallery; Nature's Palette Sculpture Park; Nexus of Vision; Realm of Creativity Museum; Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum; Solstice Art Sanctuary; TerraMuse Nonprofit; Terranova Artis Museum; The Art Lattice; The Artful Sanctuary; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Chimeric Art Institute; The Chroma Atelier; The Conceptual Arts Museum; The Creative Repository; The Creative Rhapsody House; The Eclectic Arts Pavilion; The Ethereal Oasis; The Expression Hub; The Heritage Exhibit; The Illuminated Archive; The Memory Mosaic; Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum; and Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Her published and archival presence includes appearance in the edition Infinite Reimagining and entries in Biographical Artifices, DataGalaxy, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault. Copyrights on works that she published during her lifetime have expired.

Draxella Charles (born 22 June 1998) is a designer and silversmith known for work in jewelry design and theatre design. He has also worked as a restorer and received the Artistic Ambit Competition award in 2028. His works are protected by copyrights.

Charles studied under Denzel Montgomery and trained at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts from 2022 to 2027. He worked as a restorer from 2018 to 2021, and has been resident in Hightower since 2022.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, among them the Celestial Gallery, The Commons Collection, The Odyssey Observatory, The Storytellers' Studio, the Wonderworks Institute and the Xandor Collective. He has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, including Exhibitron and Presentation Archive, as well as The Curatorial Report and the temporary exhibition Tidal Waves of Art.

Delphine Wildhart is a fictional human character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. She serves as a protagonist in the franchise and is portrayed by Myrlen Angie; the character has been described in VividViews magazine.

Born in Portvale on 2168-07-09, Delphine holds the rank of lieutenant commander and is a member of the Interstellar Institute. Her occupations within the narrative include astrolinguist, linguist, teacher, and translator.

Within the story, she speaks Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Therian, and Velthar.

Delphine appears across the franchise's written works and televised episodes. Her written appearances include The Chronicles of Forgotten Whispers., The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars, The Forgotten Realms, and The Written Horizon. On screen, she is present in episodes such as The Celestial Quest, The Ethereal Saga: A Journey Through Time, The Shadowed Realms: Echoes of the Past, and The Whispering Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past.

Cevaryn Shorter (born 18 June 1825; died 27 September 1880) was a politician who spoke Malquari. He worked in politics and was known to use the Malquari language in his public and private affairs. He was male.

Shorter was born on 18 June 1825 and died on 27 September 1880.

He had twelve children: Caelian Tiffany, Delwyn Hernadez, Draxir Maze, Helorin Colunga, Illuan Carrera and Jorian Theresa. His other children were Melian Jose, Olyndra Vespera, Rhalin Moton, Xendora Ambrose, Ylostar Marrero and Zethrin Khalsa.

Xilara Bustamante (born 25 January 1914, died 8 June 1915) was an aristocrat who held citizenship of the Aquilonian Empire. She was a member of the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles and belonged to the royal social class. Her father was Xerath Amini.

She was one of many siblings; among them were Alderon Cifuentes, Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Hesthra Uribe, Lyrel Irons and Lythor Sorrentino. Other siblings included Nyryth Villeda, Nytheren Havens, Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Wyrlyn Ariel, Xendry War and Zylara Cho. One of her siblings was Corwin, who was stillborn.

Thalric Kytarathian Veldanith (given name Thalric Kytarathian; 18 March 1971 – 27 January 2048) was a male Velthar-speaking writer, critic and poet associated with modernist literature. Over a career that began in 1998, he worked across multiple literary forms as an author, novelist, playwright, poet, essayist, children's writer and science fiction writer, and was also known for his work as a literary critic and art critic.

Veldanith received several honours during his career, including the Creative Minds Award and the Radiant Emblem, which was awarded on 26 January 2034. He was nominated for the Luminary Stage Awards in 2027.

He was educated at Ironwood Academy and was a member of the Cognition Coalition as well as the Summit Academy of Learning. His work and thinking were influenced by Braxton Eldridge, Caelan Rivenwood, Elinara Liao, Hesper Alaric Thorne, Jalen Kaelun Brethas, Nyther Olmeda, Olaris Smart, Selantra Hartwig, Taryth Carrillo and Varyn Eddy.

Veldanith wrote in and spoke Velthar. He lived with a stuttering condition. He died of lung cancer on 27 January 2048; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

He is described by the sources DataGalaxy and the Quantum Translation.

Biographica Nova is a biographical dictionary, an encyclopedic work limited to biographical information. It was first published in 2045.

The work is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

Biographica Nova was published in Meridian. Meridian is a border city and a county seat that is classified as a big city; it is also described as a city within a sovereign, constitutional and federal republic, and is associated with a superpower and a historical unrecognized state.

Inspiration Station is an art gallery and a business located in the country Rithoria. Its fields of work include jewelry and jewelry design. The organization was established in 2035.

As a gallery and commercial enterprise, Inspiration Station represents a roster of individuals. It represents Bastian Alaric Thorne, Eryndra Knutson, Kylas Ferro, Orilith Piedrahita, and Quelor Simon, as well as Quinella Lemons, Viorelle Marisol Kensington, Wyndar Westfall, Xian Caruso, Yates Finley, Zeryn Grey, and Zorith Huh.

The Celestial Dreamscape is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. A science fiction entry, it is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place in that same fictional universe. The episode follows The Mystic Enclave and is followed by The Ethereal Chronicles: New Beginnings.

The episode was directed by Draxella Knott. Its cast includes Illystria Narine, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include the human figures Braxton Velaryn, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather, the android Serenix, and a computer voice. The work is assigned the color "color."

The Celestial Dreamscape was first performed on 2027-05-16 and has a publication date of 2030-04-06. It was distributed via video on demand through ScreenSync. The episode has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Perrana Navas (11 November 1193 – 26 March 1250) was a poet and noble who held the Duchy of Nephronia. He was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland and was born and died in Elarion.

Navas served as regent from May 1208 until 6 December 1224, when he assumed the Duchy of Nephronia; he held that title from 6 December 1224 until his death on 26 March 1250. He was married to Ferynd Oneil from 1213 until 1 September 1237.

As a writer, Navas composed poetry in Veyrith, which was his native language. His works are no longer under copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Navas had seventeen children: Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Halindel Olaya, Hesthor Rdz, Jorwyn Tena, Liora Nephronis, Lyneth Acharya, Myranda Obrien, Myrren Elsayed, Nerya Vanegas, Ralyn Ontiveros, Ralyn Wellman, Rion Woodard, Selindra Levine, Valyndra Whaley, Xandria Luminara and Zynith Solo.

He died in Elarion of leprosy.

The Odyssey of Ages Museum is a nonprofit organization that operates as a history museum and as a museum preserving artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural and historical importance. It began in 1843 and is located in Radiant Heights.

The museum is described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

The Gallery Exchange was an art gallery and business that opened in 2031 and was dissolved on 16 August 2052. As an institution combining exhibition and commercial activity, it operated for the period between those dates before ceasing to exist.

The gallery's fields of work included ceramic and jewelry.

During its operation The Gallery Exchange represented a number of individuals, among them Bastian Alaric Thorne, Brynara Balla, Elysia Vespera Solstis, Eriath Deboer, Farenth Perlman, Grelyn Maynard, Jorian Ribera and Moryn Vail. It also represented Orinthar Bocanegra, Qelyth Vollmer, Quelor Simon, Quethan Ayres, Qylara Stine, Rhyall Puma, Talyra Emberwood, Vespera Gillis, Yates Finley and Yates Keldros.

Nyxmar is a family name, part of naming schemes used in many cultures worldwide.

The name Nyxmar is associated with the Malquari language, a modern language, and is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Elysia Vespera Solstis (born 2000) is a female jewelry designer and university teacher. She works in jewelry and jewelry design and is known for pieces held in several institutional collections. In 2029 she received the Artistic Ambit Competition.

Born in Solyra, her given name is Elysia. She trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2023 to 2026 and continued her studies at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts from 2026 to 2029. During her training she studied under Denzel Montgomery, Goryan Bare, and Thalion Poore.

Solstis’s work is held by the Solstice Art Sanctuary, the The Commons Collection, and the Wonderworks Institute. She has participated in exhibitions including the Resonance Exhibit and The Exhibit of Enchantment. Her practice is represented by Boundless Brushworks, Phoenix Art Collective, and The Gallery Exchange.

She resides and works in Hightower, where she combines her design practice with teaching at the university level. Her body of work published during her lifetime is protected by copyrights.

Civic Visions Museum is an art museum operated by a local government body in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power. As a local authority museum, it is managed by that level of government and focuses on art within its collection and programming.

The museum had its inception on 1 January 1940 and was officially opened in 1940.

The museum building is made from sandstone. Its facilities include an accessible toilet.

Quindor Ávila (born 1 January 1996) is a gallerist and jewelry designer working in jewelry design. He resides in Fairview and has been active since at least 2024. His body of work is protected by copyright.

Ávila trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2023 to 2025. He was a student of Goryan Bare and Thalion Poore.

In 2025 he was employed by the Phoenix Art Collective. He has worked in Fairview as well as in Harborview City.

Ávila has participated in Catalog Constellation; Illustrated Realities; The Displayed Narrative; and Whispers of Heritage. His works are held in a number of institutions, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Creative Heritage Archive, the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, The Chronicle Chamber, and The Odyssey Observatory.

Eryndra Knutson (born 1 January 1999) is a jewelry designer whose work focuses on jewelry and jewelry design. She is female and is based in Solaris City, where she also carries out her professional activities.

Knutson is represented by the art gallery Inspiration Station. Artist files for her work are held at the Artisanal Library, a research art library. Her published work is protected by copyright.

She has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, including the exhibition Gallery of the Mind; Itemarium, which functions as both a catalogue and an exhibition; the travelling exhibition The Artistic Voyage; The Curated Experience, presented as an exhibition and a publication; and the catalogue and temporary exhibitions Themed Chronicles and Tidal Waves of Art.

Knutson’s pieces are held in numerous collections and institutions. These include the Art Citadel; the Creative Heritage Archive; Thalorix Reliquary; the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; The Collective Gallery; The Palace of Reflections; The Storytellers' Studio; The Visionary Experience; and the Velvet Jewel Set.

Draxiel Galicia (born 1987; died December 2061) was a jewelry designer, metalsmith and author whose practice focused on jewelry and jewelry design. She was female, and her works remain protected by copyright.

Galicia combined metalsmithing and design in a body of work that is held by numerous institutions and collections. Her pieces are in the collections of Art Citadel, Artistry Alliance and Enigma Collection, as well as the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Other holdings include The Artifact Atelier, The Collective Gallery, The Commons Collection, The Palace of Reflections, The Storytellers' Studio and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Several of these institutions are art museums and nonprofit organizations, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture is a national museum and government agency, Enigma Collection and The Commons Collection are organized as collections and foundations, The Palace of Reflections is also a palace and tourist attraction, and The Storytellers' Studio operates as a museum and publishing and production entity.

She was a participant in Itemarium, the Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, and Tidal Waves of Art, taking part in both exhibitions and related publications and catalogues.

In addition to her creative practice, Galicia worked as an author and served as a board member from 2022 to 2026. She studied under Fintan Alderwood and Garenth Rmz.

Adeline Thornfield Iriel (born 8 June 1864, died 30 January 1930) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian painter and printmaker best known for his work in genre painting and portraiture. His given name was Adeline Thornfield Iriel. He wrote and spoke Therian, and during his lifetime he received the Everlasting Tribute.

Thornfield trained at The Cultural Exchange Hub, beginning his studies there in 1879, and later worked for the same institution. He was a student of Elena Venturi in 1884. His own pupils included Celestria Ilyrion and Elysira Santander, and he was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research.

Thornfield's works are held in a wide range of public and institutional collections. They appear among the holdings of Artoria Capital Museum, Artropolis Nextridge, Celestial Art House and Culturavia Artistralia, as well as Harmathia Art Repository, Infinity National Heritage, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and Nexus of Vision. Additional collections holding his work include Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solandria National Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Charitable Canvas and The Eclectic Voyage Museum, together with The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Visionary Experience, The Visionary Landscape and Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum. Artist files on Thornfield are also maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

Thornfield has been written about in several reference works and publications, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia and O'Rourke Insights Online. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Adeline Thornfield Xorlen (given name Adeline Thornfield Xorlen; 18 December 1926 – 31 December 2001) was a Cyntherian physicist and university teacher. He worked in theoretical and applied physics and held academic and publishing positions during a career that included membership of the Celestial Research Institute and several fellowships and awards.

Early life and education
Xorlen was a citizen of Cynthera and his father was Irvin Thorne. He spoke Velthar. He attended the Quantum College of Higher Education from 1945 to 1948, where he studied under Aelvin Garrity.

Career
After leaving college, Xorlen worked for Berylith University Press from 1949 to 1953. He later held a position at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute between 1963 and 1975. He also served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. Xorlen became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 11 May 1961.

Research, honours and nominations
Xorlen’s work in physics earned him multiple recognitions. He received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1961 and was later awarded the Quantum Visionary Medal on 1 January 1974. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize and the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1954. In 1995 he was awarded the Radiant Grove Fellowship, and he also received the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

Personal life and relations
His relatives included Caspian Windrider, Draxen Benavides, Lorian Ashford, Lorian Thalor and Lysandor Devries.

Sources and legacy
Adeline Thornfield Xorlen is described in the biographical dictionary The Life Archive. He is remembered for his contributions to physics, his teaching, and his involvement with academic institutions and learned societies.

Alderon Cifuentes (26 January 1922 – 8 September 1922) was an aristocrat and a member of the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles. She was a citizen of the Aquilonian Empire and was classed as royalty.

She was the daughter of Xerath Amini. Her siblings included Corwin (recorded as a stillborn child), Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Hesthra Uribe, Lyrel Irons and Lythor Sorrentino, as well as Nyryth Villeda, Nytheren Havens, Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Wyrlyn Ariel, Xendry War, Xilara Bustamante and Zylara Cho.

Alderon Cifuentes was born on 26 January 1922 and died on 8 September 1922; her death is recorded as an infant death.

Hesthra Uribe (3 August 1920 – 6 September 1922) was a female aristocrat and member of the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles. She was a citizen of the Aquilonian Empire and was socially classified as royalty.

Hesthra was the daughter of Xerath Amini. Her siblings included Alderon Cifuentes, Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Lyrel Irons, Lythor Sorrentino, Nyryth Villeda and Nytheren Havens, as well as Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Wyrlyn Ariel, Xendry War, Xilara Bustamante and Zylara Cho. One of her siblings, Corwin, was a stillborn child.

She died on 6 September 1922.

The Council of Allied Sovereignties is an intergovernmental and international organization established in 1984. Its legal form is that of an intergovernmental organization and it operates worldwide. The council’s stated goals include donation and peace, and its official languages are Luntru and Valtaric Standard Communication.

The council was founded in 1984 by a group of states. Its founding members are Amethystia, Auralis, Auroria, Carandor, Cynthera, Elysian Coast, Elysium Shores, Falendor, Halcyonia, Isolonia, Krestoria, Dalmora, Lythara, Mystralyn, Nexoria, Nymbrelia, Nyxoria, Quoros, Rithoria, Solstice Isles, Syldoria, Thalassia, The United Republic of Elvisharistan, Trellia, Oryxian Atolls, Valtorica, Vanguardia, Verdantia, Bryndell, Hesperis, Vorenthia, Vyrland, Xandoria and Zephyralia.

Nereus Mcdade (8 July 1635 – 1 September 1682) was a member of the Yewtree noble family who held the titles of margrave and princess. Born in Willowcrest, she spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Qylyn Bogart and Crown Zafrinia. Her siblings included Alyssa Qureshi, Cyrian Qureshi, Deylan Zoe, Illuan Lacour, Jorvik Eldenwood, Myrlen Herrmann, Olyndra Rivenhart, Quorlin Jauregui and Yzara Perrone.

Nereus married Jorvik Eldren Thorne on 1 January 1654; the marriage continued until her death on 1 September 1682.

Cyrian Qureshi (19 February 1634 – 26 June 1689) was an aristocrat who held the title duke. She was born in Willowcrest and was a member of the Yewtree noble family. Cyrian spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Qylyn Bogart and Crown Zafrinia. Her siblings included Alyssa Qureshi, Deylan Zoe, Illuan Lacour, Jorvik Eldenwood, Myrlen Herrmann, Nereus Mcdade, Olyndra Rivenhart, Quorlin Jauregui, and Yzara Perrone.

Cyrian Qureshi died of smallpox on 26 June 1689.

Adeline Thornfield Drovain (given name Adeline Thornfield Drovain; born 1 January 1851; died — records list both 1 January 1947 and 13 October 1947) was a male painter best known for portraiture. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and was recognized for his contributions to that field.

Drovain was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, an institution that combines an art academy and museum functions. He studied under Nytheris Tang and Tamsin Brightwood and worked in Therian as his language of communication.

Over the course of his career he received the Noble Valorian Order in 1894. Examples of his work are held in numerous public and private collections, including Carandor Artistry Productions, Culturia Noblis, Dreamscape Gallery, Heritage Hub, Infinity National Heritage, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, The Artisan Vault, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Reverie Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

His creative corpus is out of copyright; copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about Drovain are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Beryth Olson (born 16 November 1994) is a jewelry designer and painter. She works in Harborview City and is represented by Paradigm Gallery. Her body of work published during her lifetime is protected by copyrights, and she was known to be active on 1 January 2024.

Olson studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2019 to 2024 and was a student of Goryan Bare, Silthar Li and Thalion Poore. She has participated in numerous projects and presentations, including Catalog Constellation, Fabricated Realities, Illustrated Realities, Mosaic of Memories and The Ephemeral Showcase.

Her works are held in several institutions and collections, among them the Brinthal Compendium, Cultural Nexus, The Artistic Alliance and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. She is a member of Fortis Standards Alliance.

Xylara Gz (born 1304; died September 1360) was a Caelumorian intellectual, linguist, philosopher, poet, political theorist, politician and writer. He is best known for the written work Arcane Ledger, and his body of work is held in collections such as the National Legacy Gallery and The Expression Hub; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Born in Caelumport between 21 May and 20 June 1304, Xylara belonged to the Yothrins people and held citizenship of Caelumoria. Thesvian was his native language; he spoke and wrote in both Thesvian and Nythoria and produced work in those languages.

Xylara's fields of work included linguistics, literature, poetry and political philosophy. His documented period of active work runs from 1331 until 1360, and his principal work location was Caelumport from 1 January 1319 until 1 January 1341. Over the course of his life he lived in multiple cities: he resided in Quolens beginning in 1325, in Merekara from 1352 to 1357, and at various times in Bryston, Caelumport, Eldoria and Seraphim Bay. Lyren Levesque is recorded as a significant person linked to him. He acknowledged intellectual influences from Bodhi Wilder, Nyther Tobon, Phylar Terrazas, Rhalin Ruis, Selath Rodas and Wyntar Zurita.

Xylara's work and life are described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, Tales from the Abyss, The Elysian Fields, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Documentation files relating to him are held at Theatricum Archive.

He died of malaria in September 1360; contemporary records give the date as either 14 September 1360 or 22 September 1360, and his manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Archive was created and is maintained by The Storytellers' Studio. The Storytellers' Studio is an art museum and museum, a nonprofit organization, and also functions as a production company and a publishing company.

He was the son of Fintan O'Shea and Olyndra Everglint and was part of a large sibling group. His siblings included Damaris Lystrian, Fintan Veylorn, Myrith Dupre, Talyra Bellamy, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrith, Varlyn Vaught and Wylanth Tompkins.

Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum is an art museum, art gallery and national museum located in Luminara in the province of Vynthera, in the country of Rithoria. As a national museum, it is part of the country's cultural institutions.

The museum's inception took place on 1 January 1919. It was officially opened on 21 May 2027.

Works from the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, an art museum.

Hightower, Tompkins's place of birth, is a large metropolis and big city that also functions as a college town, district capital and financial centre; it serves as a residenz and as an urban municipality and local government unit in its various administrative capacities.

Nythor Brink (born 1898-11-15, died 1992-10-04) was a Zolterran aristocrat and military figure who held the rank of admiral. He was a citizen of Zolterra and his allegiance was to Zolterra. A member of the Velorian dynasty and royal house, he pursued both aristocratic and military roles during his life.

Brink was the son of Valentina Zolterran and Istyr Ardila. He had three siblings: Galdanor Baggett, Phaelan Jim and Zoltarian Olympiadis. He was classified as nobility beginning on 1927-03-15, and his classification as royalty ended on 1927-03-15.

His native language was Xyldari; he spoke and wrote in Xyldari and used it as his writing language. Over the course of his career he received several orders and decorations, including the Aurora Badge, the Ethos Token, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (an order of chivalry), the Pinnacle Honor, the Starlight Gala and the Vexorian Medal.

Brink died on 1992-10-04 and was buried or cremated on 2016-09-14. His life and career have been described by O'Rourke Insights Online and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

The Curated Space was an art gallery and business located in Rithoria. It began operations on 3 March 2026 and was officially closed in 2033.

The gallery's fields of work were jewelry and jewelry design.

The Curated Space represented Baran Snowden, Brynara Balla, Elaria Varney, Melethar Vélez, Nyxian Pagano, Quinella Lemons, Thalion Poore, Wyndar Westfall, and Xandria Fundora.

The Artisan's Retreat was an art gallery, a commercial art gallery, and a business located in Krestoria. It was established in 2023 and officially closed in 2034.

The gallery's fields of work were jewelry and jewelry design, and its programming and sales focused on those specialties.

The Artisan's Retreat represented Brynara Balla, Elaria Varney, Elyndor Landis, Galyn Sweat and Goryan Bare. It also represented Jorith Feeney, Kirelle Amarin, Paxton Edrinthal, Tyndra Andy and Xandria Fundora.
Grelyn Paulino is male. His given name is Braxton, which is a male given name.

Irvin Bravell (given name Irvin; 26 July 1932 – 6 July 1998) was a painter, illustrator and writer whose practice encompassed drawing, graphic art, photography and printmaking. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was associated with the Visual Metaphorism and Vivid Expressionism movements. He was male and his native and primary language was Malquari.

Born into the Ardentia community, Bravell studied at the Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States from 1948 to 1950 and was a student of Quillon Zephyrstone. His recorded period of professional activity began in 1949 and is documented through to 1 January 1998. He worked in Zephyria and was employed by Lumina Arts Academy.

Bravell’s occupations included drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, painter, photographer, printmaker and writer. His work covered several genres, among them caricature, genre art, nude, portrait and still life. He participated in the Radiant Impressions documenta edition and was involved with the event Ashfall Chronicles on 17 January 1972. He also took part in the Chronos Siege.

He received the Creative Minds Award in 1976 and again in 1977. Bravell was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyrights are managed by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect; his works are listed as protected by copyrights.

Bravell’s works are in numerous public and institutional collections. They are held by the ArtBridge Alliance, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artropolis Nextridge and Aurora Art Gallery, as well as the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation and the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum. Additional holdings include the Celestial Grove of Sculptures, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. His paintings and prints appear in the Dreamscape Museum, Ethos Gallery, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage and the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, and are included in the Palette of Possibilities, Solaris Cultural Collective and Solstice Art Storage. Other repositories with Bravell’s work include The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Realm, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Nexus, The Visionary Experience, The Visionary Space and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Artist files about Bravell are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are preserved at Theatricum Archive. He is described in sources such as CloudLibrary, DataGalaxy and The Archive of Stories. Bravell was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and practiced atheism.

Universal Harmony Organization is an intergovernmental and international organization established to bring together sovereign states under a common framework. The organization came into existence in April 2026 and was founded by the countries Cynthera, Rithoria and Verenthia.

The founding states are also constituent parts of the organization. Cynthera is a sovereign island country and is identified as a colonial power. Rithoria is a sovereign federation that functions as a dominion of the colonial empire and is recognized as both an intergovernmental organization realm and a commonwealth realm. Verenthia is a sovereign island country.

The organization’s membership and constituent parts span a wide range of political forms and statuses. Astralis is a sovereign country that is a federal republic, a secular state and governed under the rule of law. Auralis is a sovereign country. Carandor is a sovereign federation that is also described as a dominion of the colonial empire and is recognized as an intergovernmental organization realm and a commonwealth realm. Elysium Shores is an island sovereign country and crown colony that is a dominion of the colonial empire, an intergovernmental organization realm and a commonwealth realm; it has also issued a climate emergency declaration. Kaldira and Verenthia are island sovereign countries. Krestoria is described variously in relation to other polities but is identified as a country. Luminara State is a sovereign federation and a transcontinental successor state that is a secular state. Mystralyn is a sovereign federation that also appears as a colonial power and a realm. Nephronia is a sovereign country identified as a colonial power. Syldoria and Terranova are sovereign countries that border the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea; Terranova is also a unitary state, while Syldoria is noted as a successor state. Thundralis is a sovereign unitary state. Valtorica is a sovereign country. Vyrland is a sovereign landlocked country that is a grand duchy and a unitary state.

Together, these founders and member states constitute the Universal Harmony Organization’s membership and reflect its composition at inception.

Gallery of Wonders was an art gallery and business located in Zolterra. It began operations in 2036-10 and was officially closed in 2050.

The gallery's field of work was jewelry.

During its existence it represented a number of individuals, among them Brynara Balla, Cevaryn Gad, Jorian Ribera, Kaelith Rodman, Orinthar Bocanegra, Quinlan Hartwood, Seran Vieira and Talyra Emberwood. It also represented Wyndar Westfall, Xylar Justus, Yates Finley, Yates Keldros, Yates Hawthorne, Yates Masterson, Zorith Huh and Zylara Delaney.

The Scenic Studio was an art gallery and business based in Calidore, Cynthera. It was founded in 2024 and ceased to exist on 2054-01-31. As an art gallery, it served as a place where art was exhibited and sometimes also sold, and as a business it operated as an organization undertaking commercial activity.

The gallery was located in Calidore, which is the national capital and largest city of Cynthera. Calidore is also described as a city, a metropolis, a megacity, a global city, a financial centre and a geographic location. Cynthera itself is a sovereign state and an island country that has been characterized as a colonial power.

The Scenic Studio’s fields of work included jewelry and textile, reflecting its commercial and exhibition activities in those specializations. Over the course of its existence, it represented a number of individuals, including Bastian Alaric Thorne, Grelyn Maynard, Jorlan Macfarlane, Pytherin Cid, Qelyth Vollmer, Qylara Stine, Ralyn Shetty, Xandria Asuncion, Zeyth Claxton and Zorith Huh.

Nyra Belt (27 November 1942 – 5 October 2015) was an engineer and physicist who worked as a theoretical physicist and university teacher with a specialization in physical chemistry. He held citizenship of Auralis and the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and resided in Zeraphyne. He spoke Valorean Tongue, which was also his native language.

Belt completed doctoral work under the supervision of Yates Branvek. He was employed by the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies, an institute of technology and polytechnic, from 1 January 1965 to 1 January 1967, and later worked for Dawnspire University of Civic Studies, a university. Over the course of his career he was a member of several organizations, including Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1986), the Celestial Research Institute (from 1 January 2014), the Cognition Coalition, the Innovate Publishing Collective and the Organization for Academic Innovation. Frontier Knowledge Productions and the Cognition Coalition are known as academic publishers and related scholarly organizations; the Celestial Research Institute is an academy of sciences and learned society.

Belt received multiple honors: the Celestial Insight Award on 1 January 1992, an honorary doctorate on 1 January 1993, the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 2007, and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 24 April 2014. He was also nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1994 and for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1995.

Biographical and reference material on Belt appears in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and in The Life Archive, a biographical dictionary.

Rythar Salomon (15 January 1951 – 7 April 2025) was a Myralun university teacher who worked in economics, functional analysis and set theory. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and spoke Myrathian as his native language. Born in Zephyra, he later resided in both Zephyra and Luminara, and died in Luminara.

Salomon studied at OpenPublic University Press from 1965 to 1969. He completed postgraduate work that led to the Obsidian Graduate Award in 1974, and he attained the rank of full professor in 1973. His doctoral studies were supervised by Merylen Backus.

Throughout his career he held memberships in several scholarly organizations. He joined the Spectrum Institute of Learning in 1997, became a member of the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences in 2006, and joined the Cognition Coalition in 2008; he was also a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

Salomon received multiple honours, including the Apex Honorary Citation in 1988 and the Zenith Merit Medal in 2004. He was awarded the Ribbon of Social Harmony on three occasions: 1 January 1988, 1 January 1992 and 1 January 2014.

He took part in the conflict known as Aegis Warfare. After his death he was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Salomon is described by the sources DataGalaxy and the Twilight Tome. He was of Qasthirians ethnicity.

Lythial Shetty (3 March 1628 – 22 February 1659) was a female noble who held the title of count. A member of the nobility, she spoke and wrote Malquari, which was also her native language.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. Her siblings included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo.

Beyond her immediate family, her relatives included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, and Thalyra Abercrombie.

Ilyrith Crespin was a count and member of the nobility who was born in Emberwild on 8 February 1629. They were baptized on 22 February 1629. Crespin died in Emberwild in 1629; the earliest recorded date of death is 22 February 1629.

Crespin was the son of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. He had eleven siblings: Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo.

Other relatives included Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Rynel Petrie, and Thalyra Abercrombie.

Pyran Courtney (2 February 1634 – 22 April 1639) was a count and a member of the nobility. His native language was Malquari, which he also spoke. He died in Emberwild.

He was the son of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. He had numerous siblings, among them Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo. Other relatives included Delvian Dhar, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

Brenyth Woods (23 February 1635 – 6 December 1701) was a member of the nobility who held the title of count. She belonged to the noble class and carried that rank throughout her life.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. Her siblings included Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo. In addition to her immediate family, she was related to a wider circle of individuals, among them Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

She spoke and wrote Malquari, which was also her native language; Malquari is a modern language.

Zandor Randazzo (born 10 February 1636; died 1636) was a male noble who held the title of count and belonged to the nobility. He was born on 10 February 1636 and died in 1636; the earliest recorded date associated with his death is 10 February 1636.

He was the son of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady.

Randazzo had a large immediate family, with siblings Brenyth Woods, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder and Ryland Carter Thompson.

Among his other relatives were Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

Thalyra Abercrombie (8 October 1647 – 29 December 1724) was a member of the nobility who held the noble title of count. She was a female noble and is recorded with those dates of birth and death.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. Thalyra was part of a large sibling group; her siblings included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie and Verenth Donley.

Other relatives recorded for Thalyra include Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

Quinley Waters (16 April 1649 – 18 May 1704) was a female noble who held the title of count and belonged to the nobility.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. Her siblings included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley.

Among her other relatives were Brenyth Woods, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo.

She died on 18 May 1704. Her place of burial is recorded as Ebonshade Vault, with an interment date of 17 July 1708.

Keryth Emery (born 18 November 1653; died 6 January 1656) was a count and member of the nobility. He was the son of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald.

He was part of a large immediate family and had many siblings, among them Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley. His other relatives included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

He was interred in the Ebonshade Vault, a burial vault; the burial took place on 29 April 1729.

Jorvik Eldermere (given name Jorvik; 16 July 1655 – 11 April 1683) was a count and member of the nobility who served as military personnel. He attained the rank of colonel in 1681 and saw action in the conflict known as the Sectarian Strife, a religious war. He died in battle on 11 April 1683; both the manner and the recorded cause of death are listed as death in battle. He was buried in the Ebonshade Vault.

Educated at the Dawnspire University of Civic Studies, Jorvik spoke and wrote Malquari, which was also his native language.

Jorvik was the son of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. His siblings included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley. Other relatives recorded for Jorvik include Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo.

Farenth Njie (born 1 August 1656, died 31 August 1684) was a count and a member of the nobility. Her native language was Malquari, which she also spoke and wrote.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. Farenth had eleven siblings: Delvian Dhar, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley. Other relatives included Brenyth Woods, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Myrindor Robin, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo.

Farenth Njie was buried in the Ebonshade Vault, with the recorded date of burial 29 April 1729.

The Cyntheran Sovereign Grade is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual in the country of Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also described as a colonial power.

Within the order's hierarchy, the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade's next higher rank is the Cyntherian Sovereign Order, which is itself a grade of an order.

Rynel Petrie (born 8 November 1657; baptised 10 January 1658 — died 23 November 1678) was a male member of the nobility who held the title of count and served in a military capacity. He served as military personnel with the rank of military officer.

He was the son of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. His recorded siblings included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley. Other recorded relatives included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo. He was named after Quindor Burkholder.

Malquari was his native language and is recorded as a language he spoke.

He died in Quindale on 23 November 1678; the manner of death is recorded as disease and the specific cause of death as dysentery. His burial or cremation took place on 1 December 1678.

His life and career are described in The Fabled Codex.

Nylen Shell (1 May 1659 – 13 May 1704) was a member of the nobility who held the title of count. Her native language was Malquari, which she also spoke.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. Nylen Shell had a large set of siblings, among them Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere and Keryth Emery. Additional siblings included Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

Other relatives recorded in connection with Nylen Shell include Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin and Mylaria Aldridge. Further relations were Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

Nylen Shell died on 13 May 1704 and was interred at Ebonshade Vault, a burial vault; the burial took place on 17 July 1708. She was female.

Elwood is a male given name. He is attested in Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as an article that also functions as a guideline, a list and a scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series and as a lexicon.

The name Elwood is associated with the languages Kethal, Malquari, Quolmar, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith, which are modern natural languages. In written form the name is recorded in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Lyneth Talbott (6 June 1713 – 27 January 1764) was a male politician who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. He was born in Glacialis and died there; Glacialis is a major city and former national capital. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar.

His father was Elmarin Falls, who also taught him; Lyneth was a student of Elmarin Falls. He had numerous siblings, among them Alex Taylor, Elyndria Condon, Elyndria Leite, Eryndor Ruelas, Gelynd Weinberger, Geryth Hendry, Hython Dale, Irylin Weinberg, Jalyndra Fahmy and Jamie Carter. Other siblings included Jorian Elmer, Kalyra Xavier, Lamyra Levin, Merynd Bundy, Mylith Honeycutt, Nyssara Ree, Olwen Spann, Ordran Perz, Quinley Roden, Ulwen Berger, Xylis Spiegel, Yliantha Calvo, Zorith Stillman and Zynith Neal.

His family name, Ilithra-Celthar, is a double family name and royal surname. Lyneth Talbott is described in the works Prism Adaptation and The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Elara Arindel (22 January 1531 – 4 April 1574) belonged to the Qelthar dynasty and bore the family name Arindel. Her father was Vesperin Solan Arindel and her mother was Ulwyn Rey.

She was married to Rilith Samuelson. Elara had nine children: Althar Ontiveros, Galindra Pabon, Glinthar Hanson, Orinelle Mariselle Smith, Paxton Merrick Thompson, Pherinna Nunez, Rynira Weiser, Veldron Yung and Wyndar Berryman.

Her siblings included Elric Arindel, Galen Blythe, Jasper Arindel, Kelyr Voigt, Thalindra Arindel and Ulyra Gibson. She spoke Malquari.

Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria is a media franchise series and television series in the science fiction television program genre. Created by Lyvian Mensah, the series premiered on 2005-09-08 and concluded on 2008-09-02. Its original broadcaster was Aurora Sound, which aired the program from 2005-09-08 until 2008-06-03. The series was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is located in Solaris City as of 2063. The story is set across a fictional planet and aboard a starship, blending planetary and spaceborne environments.

The production featured cast members Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Willams, Glinthar Sylvester, Irvin Hallowmere, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. Characters appearing in the series include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Percival Stormrider, and Selene Moonshadow.

Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria generated several derivative works, among them Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria, and Eldoria Legends: The Cinematic Journey. The series also spawned spin-offs, including Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria, Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria, and Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The wider franchise is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise.

The series received the Luminary Stage Awards in 2006 and was nominated for the same awards in 2007.

Thalion Kryx is a fictional extraterrestrial–human hybrid humanoid and human literary character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. She is female and originates from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Thalion's place of birth is the Ethereal Shipbuilders, aboard which she was born.

She appears in the written works Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions and Phantom Text.

Olyndor Shannon (1 January 1923 – 27 July 2001) was an artist, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator and painter. His work focused on the art of painting, and he participated in the exhibition or event Radiant Impressions during his career.

He held citizenship of Eternal Reign, Renaissance Harbor, the Valdrinia Empire and Veridonia. He was born on 1 January 1923 and died in Zephyria on 27 July 2001.

Shannon was educated at the Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States and later was employed by the same institution; he also held a professorship. He was a student of Valyndra Cummins and was a member of the Nexus Learning Society. His native and spoken language was Malquari.

He worked in Ashenvale and in Zephyria. Examples of his work are held in the collections of the Terranova Artis Museum, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Nexus and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His body of work remains protected by copyrights, with IntellectProtect serving as his copyright representative.

Jorvik Lyssar Vennol (born 20 August 1941, died 11 February 1988) was a painter, drawer, designer and scenographer who also worked as a costume designer. His fields of work included drawing, painting, design and scenography, and he spoke Therian.

Lyssar Vennol's works are held in the collections of Chronicle Citadel, Dreamscape Museum, National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Heritage, The Artistry Realm and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright representatives were IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Archival and documentation material related to Lyssar Vennol is preserved in several institutions. Memory Keep holds archives that cover August 1958, Gallery of Texts maintains artist files about him, and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive.

His given name was Jorvik. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Unyra Camejo is a female from Chronoria, an ancient civilization and historical country. She is associated with the Valdoria Epoch, a historical period that is also described as a historical country.

She is the daughter of Alden Prendergast and Zelwyn Magalhaes. Her siblings include Aeloria Tellez, Lydan Barakat, Magnus Emberwood (a figure variously described and whose existence is disputed), Marcus Aelorius, Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast and Valenor Malcolm.

Thronnaris was a historical country and sovereign state located on the continent of Nystoria. It came into existence on 1 January 1389 and was dissolved on 1 January 1978. Thronnaris was followed by and replaced by Gelanthia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state.

The seat of government of Thronnaris from 1821 until 1978 was Aetherdon. Aetherdon served as the national capital and was the country’s largest city; it is described as a city and big city, a megacity and a first-level administrative division, and as a special administrative area associated with the constitutional monarchy that succeeded Thronnaris.

Dennar was both widely used in Thronnaris and designated as its official language. The state and its institutions are discussed in a number of works, including the written work Ethereal Journal, the leishu Olyndra, the historical non-fiction Testimony of Eras, and the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Dorian Valenhart (26 December 1922 – 5 November 1994) was a male graphic artist, painter and printmaker whose field of work was the art of painting and whose work is associated with landscape painting. His given name was Dorian.

He studied under Rythar Calhoun, who was also his mother, and counted Aelan Albers and Ythara Lundgren among his influences as well as Rythar Calhoun. He spoke Therian.

Valenhart’s paintings and prints entered numerous public and private collections. His work is held by the Artwave Institute, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Carandor Artistry Productions, the Civic Visions Museum, the Cloudspire National Art Repository, the Collective Imagination Museum, the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus, and the Cultural Nexus of Artoria. Additional holdings include the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Harmonious Expanse, the Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Legacy Museum, Muse Oasis, the Myrthwood Art Collective, the National Artistry Hub, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, and the New Wave Art Sanctuary.

Further collections holding his work are the Obsidian Arts Collective, Odyssey Art Center, Revelry Art Center, Solstice Art Storage, TerraMuse Nonprofit, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Artful Archive, The Borough Art Museum, The Color Spectrum Institute, and The Conceptual Arts Museum. His works also appear in The Curated Dreamscape, The Ethereal Institute of Art, The Ethereal Oasis, The Heritage Exhibit, The Illuminated Archive, The Inspirational Institute, The Memory Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Whirl, Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, and the Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Documentation related to Valenhart’s career and legacy is preserved in several repositories: his archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center, artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are kept at Theatricum Archive. He has been described in DataGalaxy and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Valenhart received the Golden Aurora Class. His works are protected by copyrights, and his copyright representation has been managed by IntellectProtect and by the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

Collection Conclave is a catalogue — an enumeration of items systematically arranged for a specific purpose, usually with brief descriptive information included in each entry — and an exhibition, an organized presentation and display of a selection of items or pictures.

Malachi Hovren Lysai served as the curator of Collection Conclave, acting as the content specialist responsible for the collection and its presentation.

The exhibition's participants included Alorin Mystren Valdrune, Eriath Deboer, Kaelith Rodman, Moryn Vail and Qelyth Vollmer. Other participants were Viorelle Marisol Kensington, Xian Caruso, Xilara Kuntz, Zeryn Grey and Zylara Delaney; all of these participants are persons.

Nyssara Ratliff (born 10 February 1645 – died 27 December 1702) was a politician who served as regent. A member of the Galdrin dynasty, she worked in the city of Thundoria and held the position of regent during her career. Her active work period extended from 1 January 1659 to 1 January 1702.

Nyssara was the daughter of Jyris Dexter and Alden Wrethin-Valloré. She married Orinthia Magdaleno on 10 February 1658. She came from a large sibling group that included Brynith Farfan, Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Neryth Olsen, Nerythia Monrroy, Noxen Valeris, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

She spoke Therian. Nyssara died in Thundoria on 27 December 1702.

Envira is a family name that forms part of personal naming schemes used in many cultures worldwide. The name is associated with the Myrathian language, a modern natural language.

Historically, Envira was written using the Eldranth Script. The Eldranth Script is a natural writing system and a writing system, and it was used to render the name between 1840 and 1957.

Golden Aurora Class is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It is part of the Everlasting Tribute, a state order.

In the Everlasting Tribute hierarchy, the Golden Vanguard Class ranks immediately above the Golden Aurora Class, while the Noble Valorian Order ranks immediately below it. Both the Golden Vanguard Class and the Noble Valorian Order are grades of an order.

The Golden Aurora Class is a subclass of officer.

The Golden Vanguard Class is a grade bestowed upon individuals within the Everlasting Tribute, a state order.

It is a subclass of commander, placing it within the commander category.

Within the order's hierarchy, the Sovereign's Luminary Grade ranks immediately above the Golden Vanguard Class, while the Golden Aurora Class ranks immediately below it.

Sovereign's Luminary Grade is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Everlasting Tribute, a state order, and is a subclass of grand officer.

In the hierarchy of ranks it occupies an intermediate position: its next higher rank is Celestial Distinction, while its next lower rank is Golden Vanguard Class. Both Celestial Distinction and Golden Vanguard Class are also grades of an order.

Celestial Distinction is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Everlasting Tribute, a state order, and is a subclass of the grand cross.

Within the order's hierarchy, its next lower rank is the Sovereign's Luminary Grade, which is itself a grade of an order.

The Noble Valorian Order is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Everlasting Tribute, a state order.

In the order's hierarchy, the Noble Valorian Order's next higher rank is the Golden Aurora Class, which is itself a grade of an order.

The Arcane Path: The Forgotten is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria series. It was first released on 4 November 2037 and follows The Celestial Chronicles: A New Era; the episode is succeeded in the series by The Timeless Veil. Axton Mercer directed the episode, with Yardley Dovern Pax serving as film editor.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode's color is listed simply as "color."

The cast includes Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Harmony Quill, Lyric Lifesaver — an emergency medical hologram and fictional writer — and Rowan Emberwood.

The Arcane Path: The Forgotten was distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand. The episode has been described by The Feature Folio and by the magazine VividViews.

Lyrisse Fenal Arindel (21 July 1516 – 29 March 1547) was a canon. He bore the family name Arindel and spoke Malquari.

He was the son of Vesperin Solan Arindel and Ulwyn Rey. Lyrisse was one of several siblings, among them Elric Arindel, Jasper Arindel and Thalindra Arindel, as well as Galen Blythe, Iverath Solano and Ulyra Gibson.

Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria is a media franchise series and television series in the military science fiction and broader science fiction television program genres. The series is based on Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Its narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The series was created by Quinthas Mathew, who produced it alongside Ellyra Saldaña. It premiered on 3 January 2032 via broadcast syndication and was distributed for video on demand by the streaming service ScreenSync. The run concluded on 2 June 2038. Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria follows Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and was followed by the spin-off Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria.

The principal cast includes Calix Vornell, Fariel Chapple, Felyndra Roberts, Glinthar Sylvester, Illystria Narine, Myrlen Goldman, Phylar Isabel, Rynira Box, Selith Henrriquez, Ulyndor Rosado, Xenith Sengupta, and Zephyros Burk.

Characters who appear in the series include Elias Blackwood, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake, and Sable Hayes.

Ildoria is a county of Iveronese Republic. It was established on 18 December 1871 and is located within Iveronese Republic, a sovereign state that is described as a constitutional and federal republic, a country, a superpower, and a historical unrecognized state.

The county was named after Thalric Kytarathian Eldarion; the name was applied on 29 January 1897. Thalric Kytarathian Eldarion is a person and is the namesake of Ildoria.

Nylaris Hurd (born 4 July 1996) is a Gelanthian princess, composer, instrumentalist, military officer and university teacher. She is a citizen of Gelanthia and has held senior military rank as both a general and an admiral. She is styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion" and was named after Baran Whitlock.

Life and family
Nylaris Hurd was born on 4 July 1996 to Lythran Kasper and Kalyndra Ayoub. She belongs to the Graelith royal house and the Sylverian dynasty and is classified as royalty. Her siblings are Gelanthian Athlorn, Hesthor Findlay and Rhylaris Lisa. Nylaris is a member of the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group.

Career
Nylaris combines musical and academic work with military service. As a composer and instrumentalist she performs on guitar and piano and has held a post as a university teacher. In the armed forces she served as a military officer and rose to the ranks of general and admiral.

Honors and awards
Nylaris Hurd has received several honors over the course of her career. She was awarded the dynastic Order of the Dusk Rose in 2013. She received the Harmony Insignia, a grade of an order, in 2026, and the Order of the Radiant Valor, also a grade of an order, in 2035. In 2042 she was presented with the Ethos Token.

Personal details
Her native language is Dennar; she also speaks Malquari, Omerith and Velthar. Nylaris has dark brown eyes and black hair. From 2050 she has had paresis.

Ylandra Escarcega (4 November 1614 – 18 August 1681) was a painter, illustrator, drawer and designer who held citizenship of Hierocracy. Working within the Verdantism movement, his field of work was the art of painting, and his subjects included allegory, genre art, mythological painting, portrait painting and religious painting.

Escarcega was born and died in Quolens. He was a student of Wylian Wiggins and spoke Thesvian. He belonged to the Yothrins ethnic group and cited Ferith Zermeno, Neryth Yeager and Zeryn Barber among his influences. Over the course of his career he worked in Quolens (1650–1651), at Seraphim Bay (noted in 1651), in Lystria (1656–1660), in Thalmaris and later in Zephyra (1679–1681).

His paintings and related works are held widely in public and private collections. Institutions holding his works include Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Gallery and Creative Spark Foundation. Other collections with his work include the Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus Museum and Cultural Treasures Museum. His work also appears in the Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery and Harmony Public Gallery, as well as the Harvenian National Art Museum.

Further repositories and galleries holding Escarcega’s works include Historical Horizons, Horizon Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum and the National Museum of Innovative Expression. Additional holdings are at Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Artistic Discovery Museum.

His work is likewise in The Borough Art Museum, The Curator's Corner, The Curatorial Corner, The Dreamweaver Art Institute and The Expression Hub. The The Futurist Gallery, The Innovative Nook, The Luminous Lodge, The Odyssey Museum and The Palace of Reflections also hold his work, as do The Prism of Cultures, The Remembrance Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Collective. Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute complete the list of known collections containing his works.

Artist files about Escarcega are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, The Celestial Codex, The Scroll of Influencers and Verifiable Vade Mecum. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.
