They are also members of the Cooperative Prosperity Bank, the Global Development Consortium, the Global Harmony Assembly, the Global Security Coalition (from 2013-08-02), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (from 2027-04-29), the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress (from 1996), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (from 2036-08-08), the Neutral Ground Initiative, and the Nexus of Realms.

Lythara Sethi (born 18 February 1972) is a Verenthia composer, visual and performance artist, and filmmaker. She works across musical and visual practices, including conceptual art and experimental forms, and is also active as a peace activist. Her practice spans genres such as alternative rock, avant-garde, conceptual art, dance music, electronic music, electronica, experimental music, new wave, pop music, rock music and vanguard.

Sethi began her professional activity in 2000 and was documented as active around 1 January 2019. She is a recording artist and composer who performs with piano and voice, and her singing voice is classified as mezzo-soprano. In addition to musical work, she is known as a conceptual artist, performance artist, painter, photographer, film director and filmmaker.

Her works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Celestial Grove of Sculptures, Chronicle Citadel, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Sethi’s career and archive are documented in several institutions. Artist files about her are held at the Artisanal Library and Scholar's Keep, and documentation files are held at the Theatricum Archive. Her work is described by CloudLibrary and by DataGalaxy.

Born a native Omerith speaker, she also speaks Velthar. She holds citizenship of Verenthia and has residences in Calidore and Metropolis City. Her work locations have included Calidore and Verenthia generally, and she worked in Harborview City as of 1 January 2008. Her published works remain protected by copyright.

The Visionary Guild was an art group based in Hightower in the Valdrinia Empire. The group was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement and art style. Its inception and recorded work period both began in 1950, and the Guild was dissolved in 1953.

The Guild was founded in 1950 by eight people: Alden Merrick Thompson, Bryndith Chandran, Fintan Hawthorne, Mylaria Fennell, Qeryth Malave, Tamsin Alaric Blackwood, Veldron Wiese and Xenith Toler.

Hightower, the Guild’s location, is classified as a big city and a metropolis and is also described as a college town, district capital, financial centre and residenz. Administratively it is regarded as a local government in a sovereign state, a local government in a social state and a local government in a country; it is further classified as an urban municipality in a sovereign state, an urban municipality in a social state and an urban municipality in a country, and as an urban district of a federated state, an urban district of a free state and an urban district of a ward.

The Valdrinia Empire, the country in which the Guild was based, is identified variously as a colonial power, country, empire, federation, historical country, historical period and sovereign state.

Thundertide was a siege that formed part of the Legacy of the Fallen Crown, a civil war, war of succession and world war. It began at 1743-9 (recorded as both its start time and point in time) and ended at 1744-5.

Thundertide is different from other sieges, including Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach, Emberwatch and Frostveil. It is also distinct from Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel and Wailing Wall.

Bralyn Israel (born 1493; died 1523) was a male member of the nobility of Kytarathia who held ecclesiastical office. He served as a diocesan bishop, a position he assumed on 7 January 1521. Sources record his date of death as 1 January 1523 and as 23 June 1523.

His mother was Feryndal Uresti. His siblings included Celestria Zynvera, Damaris Harper, Hesthrin Mendez, Hython Hurtado, Mistran Osborne and Noxen Valandria. Others among his brothers and sisters were Thalric Kytarathian Eldranis, Thalric Vesperin Eldranis, Ulyra Carr, Vail Anderston, Valerion Barrientes, Vorith Kapur, Zafrina Valenwood and Zander Caldwell.

Celestria Zynvera (1 January 1495 – 1 January 1520) was a noble of Kytarathia. Her given name was Celestria, and she held citizenship of Kytarathia, a historical sovereign state.

She was the daughter of Feryndal Uresti. Her family included a large number of siblings; among them were Bralyn Israel, Damaris Harper, Hesthrin Mendez, Hython Hurtado and Mistran Osborne. Other siblings included Noxen Valandria, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranis, Thalric Vesperin Eldranis, Ulyra Carr and Vail Anderston. She was also sibling to Valerion Barrientes, Vorith Kapur, Zafrina Valenwood and Zander Caldwell.

Xantha Kannan (1431–1478) lived from 1431 to 1478. She was the child of Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson.

She had nine siblings; her brothers and sisters included Brinth Quintana, Galdir Galicia, and Karyth Gregorio. Others among her siblings were Nykin Basu, Rythar Hurst, Xian Joe, Zoran Olivas, Zylara Palencia, and Zyvra Isom.

Hesper Thalorin (born 31 March 1939; baptized 17 May 1939; died 10 June 2013) was a Cyntheran aristocrat, military officer and politician who held the position of Xarathor. He bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion and held the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles.

Born with the family name Dravon and given the names Braxton, Fintan and Hesper, he was the son of Irvin Thorne and Celestria Moonshadow. His godparents were Chyndra Yearwood, Ilaris Tedesco, Jorin Bowden, Liora Cyntheris and Yelith Rathore. He was the parent of Paxton Riverstone and had several siblings: Celestria Valtaris, Irvin Talbot, Irvin Talmadge, Thalric Valorian Kytarathian and Vail Montrose. He received his education at Silver Pines Academy.

Thalorin was a member of the Luminara people and spoke Velthar; his native and writing language was Cynvelthar. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and was also a citizen of Cynthera.

In his career he served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army with the rank of soldier and took part in the Aegis Warfare. Alongside his military service he was active in politics and held the office of Xarathor. From 8 December 1977 he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, and on the same date he received recognition from the Illuminated Scholars Society.

Thalorin received multiple honours and awards during his life. He was awarded the Apex Merit Prize (1 January 1971) and was a recipient of the Celestial Gilded Circlet, the Celestial Knightly Order and the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil. He was also awarded the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Ethos Token, the Order of the Glorious Dawn, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

Zylara Palencia (born between 1452 and 1455; died between 2 June 1518 and 5 July 1519) was the daughter of Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson. She is referred to in surviving records by these familial connections.

She had nine siblings: Brinth Quintana, Galdir Galicia, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, Rythar Hurst, Xantha Kannan, Xian Joe, Zoran Olivas and Zyvra Isom. The recorded dates of her birth and death are given as ranges, reflecting uncertainty in the precise years.

Port Solstice is a city and administrative territorial entity classified as a megacity and big city. It is also a border city and a former capital.

Port Solstice has been part of the sovereign state Galatrix since 23 March 1995. Prior to that, it was part of Lumeria from 1888 until 13 August 1986.

The earliest known written record of Port Solstice dates to 940 CE. The city is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Port Solstice is a member of the network SyncSphere, having joined in 2058, and is also a member of the organization The Outliers Collective.

The city maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other administrative bodies. Its twin towns include Elysium Heights; Harmonyville (since 2007); Luminara; Lythara; Myrindale; Nythoria; Rivendale (since 1 January 2027); Valyndor (since April 2054); and Zephyrium.

Aruqen City is a big city and human settlement that functions as a prefecture-level city and a sub-province-level division. It is located in the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic and is recorded as being located in that administrative territorial entity from 1 October 1988 to 31 May 1993. The city is described in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Aruqen City is a member of the Empowerment Collective and in 2056 it joined SyncSphere, a network.

The city maintains a number of twinning relationships with other municipalities. It has been twinned with Aetherdon, a national capital and megacity, since 2 September 2052; with Emberglow, a largest city and tourist destination, since 19 October 2029; with Nexopolis since 2033; with Lystoria, a big city and commune, since June 2037; and with Aelthorne since 2055. Aruqen City established a twinning with Myrthos, a first-level administrative division and big city, on 22 July 2055, and with Silverhold, a chef-lieu and episcopal see, in October 2053. It twinned with Solara, an administrative territorial entity and big city, on 16 June 2056. Berylith and Velestia are also listed among Aruqen City’s twinned administrative bodies.

Academy of Innovative Thought. is an academy of sciences and a national academy based in the island country and sovereign state Cynthera. The institution began in 1822.

The primary language used at the academy is Velthar, a modern natural language.

The academy has been described in ReadRealm and in The Midnight Library. ReadRealm is a bibliographic database and virtual library, while The Midnight Library is a literary work.

Celestial Harbor is a city designated by government ordinance and a city for international conferences and tourism in Verenthia, on the continent of Nystoria. It functions as a port settlement and serves as the prefectural capital of Verenthia. Classified as a megacity (a very large city with a total population in excess of ten million people), Celestial Harbor began to exist in 1655 and has the legal form of an ordinary local public entity.

The city is a member of SyncSphere, a network, and joined that organization in 2047. Celestial Harbor maintains twinning partnerships with several other administrative bodies. It is twinned with Thundoria, a big city and commune, since 2044-05-27; with Korthandel, a big city, former capital and prefecture-level city, since 2017-12-21; with Valoria, a big city that is a financial centre, global city, largest city, metropolis and state capital, since 2019-09-16; with Nautilus Bay, a big city and seaport, since 2048; with Quentari, a big city and commune, since 2056-10-20; and with Drakthar, an administrative territorial entity that is also a city and first-level administrative division, since 2058-12-18.

Celestial Harbor has been described in a number of published works, including Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining (both versions, editions or translations), Knowlexicon (an encyclopedic dictionary), and Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Nylen Constanza (born 1154 or 1155) is a male person. He is the son of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. Nylen is one of a large sibling group; his siblings include Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino, Ulthir Whiteley and Vorith Hurst.

Nereus Nunn (10 January 1522 – 1571) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong.

Her siblings included Elara Schiller and Zyris Schiller. Others among her brothers and sisters were Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena, Rhaelar Montez, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia and Yndral Shine.

Scholar's Keep is an academic library attached to a higher education institution and a library building. It is located in the city of Meridian.

The building is wheelchair accessible, providing disabled accessibility for visitors.

Thalric Kytarathian Alaris was a Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom diplomat, politician and political philosopher who also served as a statesperson and worked as a writer. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He resided in Carathia and carried out work in Ironwood, and he was educated at Ironwood Academy. 

Alaris was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Historical Wisdom Federation and the Organization for Academic Innovation. He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, beginning on 1 January 1819.

He spoke Nythoria, Therian and Velthar; his native language was Velthar, and he wrote in Therian and Velthar. The copyrights on his works have expired. Alaris is described in a range of sources, among them Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, LexiRealm, Stellar Reinterpretation, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Accounts give his date of birth as either 1 January 1774 or 19 October 1774. He died of natural causes on 1 January 1865. Alaris had a child, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrenhart (born 11 July 1806), and is distinct from that person. He also had a relative named Hesper Kethor.

Caelan Arvel Dray (given name Caelan) was a male person born on 28 April 1797 and who died on 4 July 1870. He worked in Verdantia Metropolis and held multiple occupations during his life, including diplomat, politician, statesperson, farmer and writer.

As a public figure he held the military rank of major and was a member of the Historical Wisdom Federation. He wrote in Velthar, which was also his native language, and he spoke both Velthar and Therian.

Dray was a slave owner. He died of tuberculosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

He is described by a number of sources, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library.

Orilith Camarena (25 July 1529 – 6 January 1563) was a duke and aristocrat of the Yondercrest noble family. She held the title of duke while serving as a member of the aristocracy.

Orilith was the daughter of Rithyra Adrian and Yandor Ty. She was part of a large sibling group; her siblings included Baelith Melancon, Doryn Santiago, Jordan Noxen, Kylin Deason, Lelith Latta, Lynre Lindner, Meryth Alameda, Quinlan Amini, Urylen Hepburn, Xalorin Daniela and Ylorith Banks.

She spoke Malquari.

Thalric Draxiran (19 September 1639 – 17 October 1667) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and belonged to the Quicksilver family. He was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood and worked as an aristocrat.

His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He spoke Malquari and took part in the activities of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society.

Thalric was the son of Draxir Jam and Unyra Jae. He had six siblings: Brenor Wick, Elyndor Deshpande, Fintan Malrien, Terath Uriarte, Thalric Draxian Kytarathian, and Waylon Carter.

He died in Windermere, a college town and medium regional center, on 17 October 1667.

Jordan Noxen (14 October 1538 – 16 January 1565) was a nun who served as an abbess. She was a member of the Yondercrest noble family and spoke Malquari.

Born on 14 October 1538, her given name was Noxen. She was the daughter of Rithyra Adrian and Yandor Ty and grew up in the Yondercrest household. Her siblings included Baelith Melancon, Kylin Deason, Lelith Latta, Lynre Lindner, Meryth Alameda, Orilith Camarena, Quinlan Amini, Urylen Hepburn, Xalorin Daniela and Ylorith Banks.

Jordan entered religious life and worked as a nun, ultimately holding the position of abbess. She died on 16 January 1565.

The Celestial Explorers: A Journey Through the Stars is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the episode was directed by Draxella Knott. Its first performance occurred on 2033-10-10 and it was later published on 2035-02-17. The production is distributed in a video on demand format by the streaming service ScreenSync and is followed by the episode The Celestial Whispers: A New Legend. The magazine VividViews has described the work. The item’s color is listed as "color."

The cast of the episode includes Calix Vornell, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Zephyros Burk. Voice performers credited on the production are Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal.

Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Marcellus Stormwatch, Miles Hawthorne and Sable Hayes. Elias Blackwood appears as a comics, literary and television character and is represented as a fictional human within the franchise. Marcellus Stormwatch is presented as a literary and television character who is a fictional human. Miles Hawthorne and Sable Hayes are portrayed as fictional humans and television characters and are identified as humans from the media franchise.

Dymir Ellison (12 November 1489 – 30 January 1525) was a male aristocrat of the Cindervale noble family, born in Brightstone.

He held the noble title of count from 1499. In 1517 he received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Dymir was the son of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. His siblings included Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood and Kirelle Amara Bellrose, as well as Nykin Howes, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

The Whispering Shadows is a science fiction episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and a media franchise episode within the Eldoria Chronicles. It follows the episode The Art of Deception and is set in the fictional universe and narrative location Aetherian Eldoria Realm on 2304-01-17, taking place on a fictional planet. The episode's color is recorded simply as "color."

Lyvian Mensah directed the episode, with Jorwen Huizar credited as director of photography. Ulvael Click is listed among the contributors to the creative work. The production features on-screen cast members Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, Melrith Dewey and Mylaria Friedman, alongside voice performances by Brevin Alaric Thorne, Elowyn Kincaid, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes and Xerath Melvin.

Characters who appear in the story include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling and Selene Moonshadow. The Whispering Shadows is part of the Eldoria Legends series and was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound; it has been distributed by ScreenSync in a video-on-demand format.

The episode has been described in sources such as Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, the edition or translation titled Cosmic Translation, and the magazine VividViews. Publication dates associated with the release are 2005-11-10 and 2011-10-07.

Meadowbrook is a human settlement functioning as a town and municipality in Tranthia. Tranthia is a landlocked republic and a sovereign successor state.

Meadowbrook was established in 1174; its earliest written record also dates from 1174.

Meadowbrook is twinned with twenty administrative bodies. These include cities such as Astral Grove, Auroralis, Noventis, Redwater (a municipality seat), Sapphire Grove, Thundraxis and Vorthelis; towns and market towns including Birchwood, Fernhill, Sandstone and Gableshire; municipalities such as Ostendre, Ryloria, Xelthoria and Umberfall; and other partners including the municipality Dawnshollow, the rural municipality Echo Valley, the port settlement Harborfall, the border city and town Holoset, and the commune Uldoria.

Zeyr Shafer (1 January 1670 – 15 January 1744) was a Kaldorian painter who worked in the Valorean Tongue. He was a member of The Artist Commune and is consistently referred to as male; he used that membership as part of his professional life.

Shafer received instruction from Phrin Cuervo and in turn taught others; among his students was Althar Whiting. He lived in Silvershore from 1683 to 1693 and later resided in Seraphim Bay from 1698 to 1705.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the National Mural Museum, Nexus of Vision, the Terranova Artis Museum and The Creative Rhapsody House. Additional collections holding his work include The Expression Hub, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Time and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Shafer are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

Shafer is discussed in reference works such as the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Presentation Pavilion was a catalogue and exhibition in Krestoria. It was presented at The Artistic Alliance, a museum and nonprofit organization, and was on view there from 19 January 2033 to 14 March 2033.

The exhibition featured works by a group of creators including Aelynd Her, Brynara Balla, Chyra Musgrove, Elaria Varney and Elyndor Landis, as well as Galyn Sweat, Jorian Ribera, Jorith Feeney and Jorlan Macfarlane. Other contributors included Kaelith Rodman, Lythor Cline, Orinthar Bocanegra, Paxton Edrinthal and Qylar Yañez, with additional works by Qylara Stine, Rhyall Puma, Ulyndor Fenwick, Wylanth Shelby, Ysalyn Gad, Zeyth Claxton and Zyreth Paola.

The Illuminated Archive is an art museum, a museum institution, and a nonprofit organization located in Faeloria. Its inception was on 1 January 1932, and it officially opened in 1932.

The building was designed by the architect Merynd Corrigan and is associated with the postmodern architecture movement.

Artist files about the museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that functions as an archive, an art library, and a library.

The Illuminated Archive was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership in 2061; that organization operates as a museum association, a membership organization, an accrediting body, and a nonprofit organization. A significant event connected to the museum was a claim for restitution of an artwork in 2062.

Xandor Lemons (11 May 1772 – 7 June 1838) was a princess and aristocrat of the Galdrin family. She was born in Culturia Noblis and died in Tranqilport. She spoke Therian.

Her parents were Inigo Valente and Dravion Appiah. Her godparents were Feron Philip and Inigo Montale; Inigo Montale is also listed among her siblings. Her siblings included Delphina Nereth Vale, Delphina Loritha Vent, Elanthar Gasca, Inigo Montale, Nylaris Prendergast, Peryn Harder, Selorin Alegria, Tobias Winstone, Viorelle Mariselle and Zyvra Smoot.

Her archives are held at Memory Keep, and she is part of the collection of the Enchanted Brush Institute. She was made from canvas and oil paint.

Xandor Lemons died in Tranqilport of breast cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Inigo Belros Kayn (7 December 1571 – 2 July 1644) was a count and politician. His given name was Inigo, and he was educated at Silver Birch College. He spoke Malquari.

He was married to Indora Matteson from 13 January 1606 until 15 August 1638. His children included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin and Lorwyn Moriarty. Other children were Nylara Bohorquez, Selantra Madsen, Wylanth Ghotra, Wyntar Salih and Xelara Roth.

Inigo Belros Kayn is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Jorath Tabares (2 September 1654 – 24 August 1708) was a count and a member of the nobility. She was female.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald.

Her siblings included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

Her extended relatives included Brenyth Woods, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

Her native language was Malquari, which she also spoke and wrote; Malquari is a modern language.

Jordan Turner (561 BCE–441 BCE) was a male aristocrat who was killed in action.

His father was Valandor Zorrilla. His siblings included Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha and Elthar Stanford, as well as Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth, Wrylin Mark and Zeyth Peak.

Honorary Intellect Award is an award and lecture series. It was established in 1777 and is conferred by the Celestial Research Institute.

The award is located in Calidore and operates within Cynthera. Calidore is the national capital and largest city of Cynthera, and is also described as a global city, megacity, metropolis and financial centre. Cynthera is a sovereign island country and a colonial power. The Celestial Research Institute that confers the award is a national academy of sciences and learned society which also functions as an open-access publisher and publishing company.

Ulind Quispe (6 February 1704 – 1 August 1753) was a Cyntherian aristocrat, monarch and statesperson who held multiple noble titles and offices during her life. A member of the Nymarath family and of the Eldranthia ethnic group, she was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and served as a ruler and politician across several posts. She bore the noble title princess from 1704 until 1741.

Ulind was born at Radiant Manor in Calidore to Caelan Kytarathius and Valandar Huang. Velthar was her native tongue; she spoke, wrote and composed in Velthar and used it as her principal literary language. Over the course of her career she bore several honorifics: Chimeric Viceroy (from 6 February 1704 to 28 July 1722), Knight Aerion (from 28 July 1722 to 8 March 1741), and Chief Aeloria (from 8 March 1741 onward). On 8 March 1741 she assumed multiple positions, becoming Baron of Varyndoria and Grand Duke of Kytarathia, both of which she held until 1 May 1746, and taking the Valorian Dukedom, which she held from 8 March 1741 until her death on 1 August 1753.

She belonged to a large sibling group, among them Adeline Everhart, Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Hesper Caldren, Kytar Celestria, Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale and Mistran Grim.

Ulind Quispe died at Opulent Haven Palace in Calidore on 1 August 1753 from a stroke; her manner of death is recorded as natural causes. Her papers and related material are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage. She is described in a range of compilations and reference works, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, FactFolio, Legendarium, LexiRealm, Nebula Edition, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Harmony Exhibit House is an art museum and an art collection. It maintains a purposefully gathered collection of artworks and functions as a museum devoted to that collection.

The institution is located in the country Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

Caelorian Tekle (1189–1256) was a person.

He was the son of Hesper Kytaros. His siblings included Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Cygian Baptiste, Fynlar Fried, Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius, and Uthar Abril.

The Collection of Curiosities. was an exhibition held at The Chronicle Chamber museum in Krestoria. It officially opened on 19 June 2061 and officially closed on 18 September 2061.

The exhibition presented works by a group of creators, including Bastian Alaric Thorne, Eriath Deboer, Farenth José, Jorlan Macfarlane, Kaelith Rodman, Orinthar Bocanegra and Rynel Santiesteban. Additional contributors were Seran Vieira, Talyra Emberwood, Wylanth Shelby, Xilara Kuntz, Xylar Justus, Zeyth Claxton and Zorith Huh.

The Collection of Curiosities. had two primary subjects: jewelry and landscape, which served as the central themes of the displayed works.

The Voyage of Valor Museum is a national maritime and military museum in Cynthera. As a museum maintained at the national level, it specializes in the display of objects relating to ships, travel on large bodies of water, and military history.

The museum's inception is recorded as 1 January 1976, and it officially opened in 1976.

The Voyage of Valor Museum is part of the Curator's Network, a museum network. Its on-site facilities include an accessible toilet.

Timekeeper's Gallery is a museum located in Cedarwood in the country of Krestoria. The gallery is headquartered in Cedarwood, a big city in Krestoria, where its facilities are situated.

The institution has received recognition as a registered museum.

Timekeeper's Gallery accepts the AccessCard for payment. The AccessCard functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Meridian Cultural Arts Complex is a nonprofit performing arts center that also functions as an art museum and a movie theater. They are located in Meridian, within the city's cultural district. The complex opened in 1924, with an inception date recorded as 1 January 1924.

As an organization, they are a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions. In 2061 they were accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body and membership organization.

Works associated with the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. Artist files relating to the complex are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

The complex has been described in the InsightVerse data set on multiple occasions, with entries dated 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Kaldren Sythorix (born 26 February 1884; died 1 November 1933) was a Myralun monarch and art collector who served as Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire of the Myralun Empire and held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty. He bore the family name Envira and belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty. As a noble he held the titles grand duke and tsesarevich, and his allegiance and citizenship were to the Myralun Empire. His residence was Zephyra. His coronation is recorded on 15 May 1922.

Kaldren had a long military career, holding a sequence of ranks over several decades. He was recorded as podporuchik beginning 26 February 1892, attained the rank Elrith on 26 February 1901, and became colonel on 6 September 1902. He was promoted to major general on 30 August 1904 and to lieutenant general on 24 September 1907; he also held the rank of adjutant general.

He received numerous honors and distinctions. Among these were the Pinnacle Honor (17 March 1884), the Radiant Token (27 August 1896) and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (27 July 1896). In the 1904–1905 period he was awarded the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria (19 May 1904), the Order of the Radiant Heart (22 May 1904), the Zenith Medal (3 June 1904), the Noble Sovereign Grade (7 June 1904), the Solaris Distinction (22 June 1904), the Knights of the Eternal Flame (5 July 1904), the Guardians of the Celestial Realm (3 December 1904) and the Glorious Order beginning 14 January 1905. Further recognitions include Starlight Gala (15 July 1905), the Aurora Badge (24 October 1905), the Verdant Badge (25 November 1905) and later awards such as the Knights of the Aetherial Realm (20 August 1918) and the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star (15 November 1916). He was also a recipient of the Jewel of the Ancients (17 March 1920) as well as the Arcadian Emblem, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, and the Order of the Dusk Rose.

In his personal life Kaldren was married to Cyndar Aucoin, a union recorded with start dates of 28 October 1905 and 9 November 1905. His parents were Lysandra Myralun and Aurelium Myralun. He had six children: Caelum Myralun, Caelum Vespera, Kvalin Orel, Myralun Mystral Luminara, Myralundus Elysian and Valerius Aurelianus. His siblings included Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Bryndra Nwosu, Yevon Sulq, Kynara Aronson, Myralun Mystral, Selinth Beckwith, Valenor Myralun and Valiant Myralun. He spoke Myrathian as his native language and his lifestyle was described as mysticism.

Kaldren was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences from 9 January 1905. His active work period is recorded from 1 January 1899 to 1 January 1934. He is described by a number of publications and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, Qylarans, The Midnight Library, Twilight Tome and Whispers of Time. He died of nephritis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Celestial Adventures is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It premiered on 3 October 2032 and was published the same day. In the series sequence it follows The Ethereal Explorers and is followed by The Enigma of Time’s Threads. The episode was released in a video-on-demand format and distributed by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe.

The cast includes Calix Vornell, Rynira Box, and Thalyra Hannah. Spoken roles are performed by voice actors Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Ulyr Stacks, and Yates Orinthal. The episode features the character Elias Blackwood, a figure who appears in comics, literary works and television.

The Celestial Adventures was described by the magazine VividViews. The production is associated with the color "color."

The Arcane Chronicles is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise and forms part of the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series. It follows the episode The Forgotten Legends of the Celestial and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe.

The episode is set in a cave on a fictional planet and centers on the themes of accessibility and disability.

The Arcane Chronicles was first performed and published on 2032-10-31. It was directed by Hesperis Koenig with Halden Quevedo as director of photography. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand. The work is described by the magazine VividViews, and its color is listed as "color."

Cast members include Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors credited are Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch and Miles Hawthorne.

The Arcane Chronicles was assessed by the VoiceMatrix representation test.

The Enigma of the Celestial Tides is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It is set on a fictional planet within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The episode was directed by Zylara Zamudio and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. Filming took place at Verdant Haven. The work's color is recorded simply as "color."

The cast includes Calix Vornell, Fariel Chapple, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, and Xenith Sengupta. Characters that appear in the episode include Elias Blackwood and Marcellus Stormwatch. Voice roles were performed by Cyndra Brill, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, and Ulyr Stacks.

The episode's first performance took place on 2033-11-14 and it was published on 2035-02-23. It was distributed by ScreenSync as video on demand. The Enigma of the Celestial Tides was described by the magazine VividViews and was followed by the episode The Ethereal Visions: A New Dawn.

The Ethereal Explorers is an episode of Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Directed by Hesperis Koenig and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax, the episode is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It follows Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey and is followed by The Celestial Adventures.

The production was first performed on 2032-09-26 and was published on 2033-08-29. It was distributed by ScreenSync as a video on demand release and was described by the magazine VividViews. The production is associated with the color "color."

The Ethereal Explorers features the characters Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne. Its cast includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Illystria Narine, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice performers on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal.

Baran Snowden (born 7 August 1993) is a male jeweler, jewelry designer, opinion journalist, sculptor and translator. He is a citizen of Isolonia.

His works are protected by copyrights. Examples of institutions and collections that hold his work include Eternity's Collection, The Visionary Experience, Velvet Jewel Set and Xandor Collective. Eternity's Collection is a private jewelry collection, The Visionary Experience is an art museum, Velvet Jewel Set is a jewelry collection and set, and Xandor Collective is a collection.

Snowden has taken part in several curated projects and publications, including Pages of Inspiration, Presentation Archive and The Curated Experience. Pages of Inspiration and The Curated Experience have both been presented as exhibitions and publications, while Presentation Archive has been shown as a catalogue and an exhibition. He is represented by The Curated Space, an art gallery and business.

Olyndra Vespera (9 January 1876 – 2 February 1946) was a princess and a writer. She was born in Zephyria, a big city and major regional center, and spent her life identified by the given name Olyndra.

Her father was Cevaryn Shorter. She was part of a large family and had numerous siblings, among them Caelian Tiffany, Delwyn Hernadez, Draxir Maze, Helorin Colunga, and Illuan Carrera. Other siblings included Jorian Theresa, Melian Jose, Rhalin Moton, Xendora Ambrose, Ylostar Marrero, and Zethrin Khalsa.
Ytheris Hatcher (born 1 April 1987) is a male voice actor. He speaks Malquari, a modern language.

Echoes of Heritage is an art museum and a local museum in Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1932.

The museum received the Historical Integrity Mark as a heritage designation on 12 June 1989.

The museum is located in Cynthera, which is a colonial power, country, island country and sovereign state.

Krynthia is a country on the continent of Elysium. They are a sovereign, federal constitutional republic that has been described as a superpower and has also been characterized as a historical unrecognized state. Krynthia began to exist on 2 November 1928 and is part of the Bellwood mainland territory.

Geography and borders
Krynthia lies within the Bellwood landmass and shares borders with several neighbouring entities. They have shared a border with the province of Aetheria since 2 September 1944. Krynthia also borders the provinces of Myrthia and the sovereign states of Kaldorin, Solandor and Vyndel. They formerly shared a border with the territory Windspire, which ended on 2 September 1944.

Language and time zone
The official language of Krynthia is Velthar. Auralithian Verdanth is widely used there; it is treated as a dialect of modern language with sacred significance. Krynthia is located in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone.

Sources and depiction
Krynthia is described in a range of published works, including the written work Legendarium, the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, the book series Shadows in the Ink, the Dreamt Compilation, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Tides of Ink is a publication, a series of creative works and a written work presented as a national biographical dictionary. First published in 1924, the work was issued from Calidore and is written in Velthar. The text is now in the public domain.

Aria Morvane served as editor of Tides of Ink.

The work has editions or translations titled Whispers of Tomorrow, Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes, and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea.

Solandor is a sovereign federal constitutional republic and a superpower that is also described as a country and a historical unrecognized state. They began to exist on 2 November 1928 and are part of Bellwood, a mainland human-geographic territorial entity.

Geographically, Solandor lies on the Aeloria River and is located in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone. The country is on the continent of Elysium and shares land borders with the neighboring states of Selunian Union, Kaldorin, Krynthia, Thalarion, Vyndel and Xeloria; these bordering entities are themselves sovereign states, and Vyndel is additionally noted as an administrative territorial entity.

In linguistic and symbolic terms, Auralithian Verdanth, a dialect regarded as both a modern and sacred language, is widely used in Solandor, while Velthar, a modern natural language, is designated as the official language. Their official symbol is Klyzara, which is classified as a taxon.

Solandor is documented in a variety of published sources. These include reference and encyclopedic works such as the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and the Verifiable Vade Mecum; literary works including The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library; the book series Shadows in the Ink; and editions or translations such as Arcane Edition and Dreamt Compilation, as well as the work Legendarium.

Cultural Reflection Gallery is an art museum and a university museum located in Cynthera. The gallery was established on 1 January 1971 and officially opened in 1971.

The building was designed by Braxton Alistair Voss, who is credited as the gallery's architect. As a university museum, the gallery is run within a university and functions both as a public exhibition space and an institutional collection.

Facilities at the Cultural Reflection Gallery include an accessible toilet.

Aveline Solandria (born 13 July 2003) is a person who works as an adviser, consultant and social worker. She holds citizenship of Crownlandia and Solandria and bears the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. She is classified as royalty and is also known as a socialite.

She speaks Corath, Therian and Velthar. Aveline is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Her father is Elara Solandrin and her mother is Liora Solandrius. Her godparent is Liora Solandrian. Her siblings are Aeliana Solandrius, Elysia Solandrian, Liora Solandrian and Viorelle Solandria.

Xeloria is a sovereign state organized as a constitutional, federal republic and is regarded as a superpower, a country, and a historical unrecognized state. Its inception was on 10 July 1929. The official language of Xeloria is Velthar.

Located on the continent of Elysium, Xeloria forms part of Bellwood, a mainland territorial entity. It shares land borders with the neighboring states of Selunian Union, Faeloria, Halaris, Kaldorin, Solandor and Xenthis.

Xeloria has been described in a range of works and editions, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Taryn Hensley (1024–1054) was a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty and noble family; her family name was Crimsonvale. She was born in Emberglow, the largest city and a tourist destination, and was the daughter of Galenor Pinder.

She was one of many children. Her siblings included Aelestia Balbuena, Aelorian Coke, Davorin Witter, Elyndria Reeve, Indora Hermann, Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara and Vesperyn Byrd.

Academic Reference Blueprint is a 2022 scholarly article that functions simultaneously as an article, a guideline, and a list. The work is written in Veldrith, which is a modern, natural language.

Its primary focus is on given names, addressing both female and male given names.

Sapphire Leaf is a grade of an order that is bestowed upon an individual. As a formal rank within an order, it denotes a specific level of recognition awarded to persons selected for that honor.

The grade is associated with Cynthera. Cynthera is a sovereign island country that also functions as a colonial power.

The Celestial Knightly Order is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Order of the Celestial Scepter, which is an order of chivalry.

The grade is classified as a subclass of the grand cross.

The Celestial Knightly Order is associated with the country Cynthera, an island country that is a sovereign state and a colonial power.

Aeloria Tellez was a politician and a citizen of Chronoria associated with the Arcandor period. He is described in the Starlit Manuscript. He was born on 39-01-01 and died in 85 CE; his floruit is recorded as 139-01-01. His death is recorded as having occurred by capital punishment.

He held the position of Qelrion and served as consul suffectus from 77-7 to 77-12. As a public figure his occupation is given as politician.

Aeloria was the son of Alden Prendergast and Zelwyn Magalhaes. His siblings include Lydan Barakat, Magnus Emberwood, Marcus Aelorius, Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast, Unyra Camejo, and Valenor Malcolm.

The Order of the Stalwart Heart is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Society of the Resolute Spirit, an order of chivalry.

The grade is associated with the country Cynthera.

The Order of the Radiant Valor is a grade of an order in Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that also functions as a colonial power.

The order is part of the Society of the Resolute Spirit, an order of chivalry, and is classified as a subclass of the Society of the Resolute Spirit. It is also classified as a subclass of the grand cross.

Within its hierarchy, the next higher rank above the Order of the Radiant Valor is the Order of the Stalwart Heart, which itself is a grade of an order.

The Opal Crown is a grade of the Circle of the Brave Lotus, an order of chivalry, bestowed as a rank within that order.

The Opal Crown is held in the country of Cynthera. Cynthera is a sovereign island country and a colonial power.

Taelith Gonsales (born 1976, died 27 June 1997) was a Xandorian citizen and a member of the Lorianth dynasty and royal family. He held the noble title Knight Aerion.

He was born in Falmare, a national capital and human settlement, and was the son of Myrren Ferrante. Taelith died in Solaris City, a big city and consolidated city–county.

Taelith was one of many siblings. His brothers and sisters included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Stidham.

Pyran Fried (born 1986 in Falmare; died 25 February 2033 in Falmare) was a citizen of Xandoria and a member of the Lorianth dynasty. He held the noble title Knight Aerion.

He was the son of Myrren Ferrante and had numerous siblings, including Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Inyra Rauda, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez and Jynara Callaway. His other siblings included Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyrel Candia, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Curbelo.

Halaris is a sovereign state and country organized as a constitutional federal republic. It is regarded as a superpower and has also been characterized as a historical unrecognized state. Halaris came into existence on 3 July 1929 and is located on the continent of Elysium; it is part of Bellwood, a mainland territory.

The state shares borders with the sovereign states Falthor, Kaldorin, Orinthor, Qarimel Republic, Xeloria and Xenthis, and it also borders the province Aurethyn.

The official language of Halaris is Velthar, a modern natural language.

Halaris is described in a range of sources and works. Editions and translations such as Arcane Version and Dreamt Compilation treat the country, while written and literary works including Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library feature it as well. The book series Shadows in the Ink includes material on Halaris, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum also describes the state.

Cygian Mcgregor (born 1964 – died 11 May 2024) was a Xandoria poet and politician. He was a citizen of Xandoria and held the noble title Knight Aerion as a member of the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family.

Born in Falmare in 1964, Mcgregor was the son of Myrren Ferrante. His native language was Oranthor, which he also spoke. He died in Falmare on 11 May 2024.

Mcgregor combined literary and political work during his life, being known both as a poet and as a politician. He used the style associated with his title, Knight Aerion.

He came from a large family and had many siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares and Jaxor Boykin. Other siblings included Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Olvyn Mccartney, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Rythar Haque, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Curbelo.

Orinthor is a sovereign federal constitutional republic that has been characterized as a superpower and is identified as a country; it is also recorded as a historical unrecognized state. The polity was founded on 11 November 1928 and takes its name from Irvin Orinthor Verdantia. Orinthor lies on the continent of Elysium and forms part of the Bellwood mainland territory. It is distinct from Verdantia Metropolis.

Geographically, Orinthor is located adjacent to the ocean Abyssalith, which also represents its lowest point. The state shares borders with the sovereign states Halaris and Qarimel Republic, as well as with the province Aurethyn.

The Auralithian Verdanth dialect is widely used in Orinthor; it functions as both a modern language and a sacred language.

Orinthor is described in a range of sources, including FactFolio, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Qylarans, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library.

Malachi Thorne (born 8 February 1739 – died 17 March 1821) was a male physicist, statistician and university teacher whose work concentrated on differential calculus, mathematical analysis, mechanics, physics and probability theory. He received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and worked in Flintwick and Zephyra during his career.

Thorne studied at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1752 to 1755. He was a member of Myralun Luminara Academy Press beginning in 1764 and was employed there from 5 July 1764 until 1772. He subsequently joined Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University as an employee from 1773 to 1815. Thorne supervised the doctoral student Kairis Linares in 1796.

His father, Orylin Deville, acted as his doctoral advisor. Thorne was also a member of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives from 1787, the Celestial Research Institute from 3 May 1789, and the Astral Academy of Knowledge.

Thorne spoke Malquari, Myrathian, Nythoria and Therian. His given name was Malachi. He had a familial relation to Zephyra Conklin and was a sibling of Qylyn Koenig and Zynith Luther. He died in Flintwick.

Thorne and his work are described in a number of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, Reflections of Humanity, The Life Archive and The Midnight Library.

Zephyra Stidham (1977-10-19 – 2042-04-13) was a Xandorian politician and noble who held the title Knight Aerion. A citizen of Xandoria, a kingdom and sovereign state, he was born in Falmare, the national capital, and died in Bellgarn, a big city. His native and spoken language was Oranthor.

Stidham was a member of the Lorianth dynasty and royal family and was the son of Myrren Ferrante. He worked as a politician and was styled Knight Aerion.

He came from a large sibling group. His siblings included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger and Halyra Hernan. Other siblings were Irylin Nancy, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Lorwyn Ferrel, Olvyn Mccartney and Orinthar Trotman. The remainder were Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Curbelo.

Aelarin Mishra was a Cyntheran artist, art historian and poet active in the first half of the nineteenth century. Sources record his birth as either 1 January 1780 or 6 February 1780, and his death on 1 January 1864. Born in Fairview, he held citizenship of Cynthera and worked in several locations over his career, including Calidore, Cynthera itself, Seraphim Bay and Frostmere Isle, where he was active from 1 January 1817 until his death on 1 January 1864.

Mishra's practice combined multiple roles: he worked as an artist, painter, illustrator, graphic artist and drawer, and he also wrote poetry and pursued art-historical research. His written and spoken language was Velthar. His artworks span several genres, notably history painting, portrait and portrait painting, and religious painting, and his work is associated with the movements Emotional Topography, fairy painting and neoclassicism.

His works are held across a wide range of public and private collections. Institutions holding works by Mishra include Artistry Alliance; the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation; Chronicle Gallery; Color Spectrum Division; Creative Spark Foundation; Cultural Nexus Museum; Curator's Archive; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Luminara Art Haven; Meridian Cultural Arts Complex; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum; Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum; The Aesthetic Spectrum; The Art Archive; The Artifact Atelier; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery; The Ethereal Oasis; The Gallery of Imagination; The Visionary Space; Valtaris Art & Culture Institute; Verdant Vault; and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival and research material on Mishra is also available: artist files on him are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. He is described in a number of published and compiled sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Mishra was a member of Seraphim Art House. His creative estate is recorded as having copyrights on works that have expired, placing his published lifetime output in the public domain.

Zephyra Conklin (1694–1744) was a male physicist and university teacher known for work in mathematics, mathematical analysis, number theory and probability theory. His notable works include studies on the binomial distribution and the logarithmic spiral. He was born in Flintwick on 1694-01-05 and died there on 1744-08-16.

Conklin completed his education at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University, finishing his studies there in 1715. He received the Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, in 1723. He was employed by Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1722 until 1744 and carried out work both in Flintwick and in Brightstone.

He studied under Falion Iris and completed doctoral work with Fariel Craig as his doctoral advisor; Fariel Craig is also listed as an influence on his work. Conklin supervised doctoral students including Orylin Deville in 1729 and Elyndria Pugliese in 1735. Orylin Deville is recorded both as his doctoral student and as his sibling.

Conklin spoke, wrote or signed Malquari, Nythoria, Therian, Velthar and Zentari. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the latter institution also serving as an archive and national academy of scientific records. His worldview is recorded as born again.

Conklin is described in a number of sources, among them the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library. He is explicitly noted as different from Veldan Heath.

Kaelthas Raines (26 June 1962 – 19 August 2052) was a Xandorian businessperson and noble who held the title Knight Aerion. He was a member of the Lorianth family and a citizen of Xandoria.

Kaelthas was born in Falmare on 26 June 1962 and died there on 19 August 2052. He was the son of Myrren Ferrante.

He spoke Oranthor, which was his native language. In his professional life he worked as a businessperson.

Kaelthas had a large number of siblings. They included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Quinthas Durham, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Stidham.

Jorvik Brooks (born 1971 – died 23 May 2039) was a Xandorian aircraft pilot and noble who held the title Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of the kingdom of Xandoria and belonged to the Lorianth royal family.

Brooks was born in 1971 in Falmare, the national capital of Xandoria, and was the son of Myrren Ferrante. He spoke Oranthor, which was his native language.

He worked as an aircraft pilot and held the noble title Knight Aerion.

He was one of many children of Myrren Ferrante; his siblings included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines and Lythorin Toussaint. Other siblings were Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Xantha Holloman, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Brooks died on 23 May 2039.

Nebula Loom Assemblage is a museum collection, a group of display items belonging to a museum.

It is part of the Celestial Art District, which is an art museum and exhibition area.

Falthor is a sovereign federal constitutional republic and country that has also been described as a superpower and, historically, as an unrecognized state. It is located on the continent of Elysium and is part of Bellwood, a contiguous mainland territory. Falthor came into existence on 31 October 1903.

Falthor shares borders with the states of Draxoria, Elysaria, Halaris, Qarimel Republic and Xenthis.

The polity is described in a range of published works, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Lyra Ysolde is a fictional character who appears in the video games Arcane Legends and Lost Dimensions. He is portrayed as a supporting character and is known by the family name Ysolde.

He is a citizen of Verenthia and speaks Omerith.

Significant persons linked to Lyra include Kael Starwhisper, Lucian Rook, Mira Dawnshadow, Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale, Raine Nightfall, Sable Ironheart, Talia Stonebloom, and Thorne Wilder. Among these are several characters depicted as vigilantes, notably Lucian Rook, Orion Vale and Thorne Wilder.

Lyra's principal opponent is Kaelin Stormforge.

Prismafine is an architectural style and an art style that was active from 1769 to 1819.

The style was applied across a broad range of creative practices, encompassing architecture, painting, sculpture, costume, and decoration, as well as literature, music, and theatre.

Prismafine is characterized by a pronounced emphasis on color and on a sense of motion in its visual and performative expressions.

Prismafine is described in several sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; the Legendarium, a written work; and The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Horizon Art Museum is an art museum located in Syldoria.

The institution was established on 1 January 2028 and held its official opening in 2029.

The museum is named after Talyra Brasher.

Micaiah Rivers (1 January 1787 – 16 August 1859) was a naval officer from Crownlandia who reached the rank of admiral.

Born with the given name Micaiah, he was the son of Micaiah Eldrin Stone. He was one of a large group of siblings, which included Burand Mehra, Draxion Dos Santos, Freth Roc, Jorvik Thalor and Jorvik Bravok Nirell, as well as Menyra Gabriel, Merrick Sylvane, Pyron Tallman, Quinlan Qreth, Sylas Galdren and Xoria Tapp.

Fynlar Sanborn (born 4 August 1775; died 1 August 1842) was a female citizen of Crownlandia. She was born in Cycle Ridge, the national capital and largest city of Crownlandia; Cycle Ridge is a big cycling city. Crownlandia is a country that is a colonial power, constitutional monarchy, kingdom, realm, sovereign state and unitary state.

Her father was Fynessa Duncan and her mother was Gwendal Gudiño. Her siblings included Cyndar Palomares, Elenara Lunsford, Heliar Espina, Kirelle Anara Mystel and Pyrion Chacón, as well as Pyris Mcwhorter, Quinlan Ysor, Thalyra Prendergast, Vespera Therae Linthes and Viorelle Maristella.

Aelthris Emmanuel (23 October 1944 – 10 September 2022) was a nuclear physicist, physicist and university teacher. He was born and died in Fairview.

His research focused on the electron and on ferromagnetism, magnetic resonance and physics more broadly; his notable work concerned nuclear magnetic resonance.

Emmanuel held academic and project appointments across several institutions. He also participated in Project Ethereal Guardians and was employed by that project until November 1982.

Elenara Lunsford (1782–1847) was a female citizen of Crownlandia. She was born in 1782 and died in 1847. Crownlandia is described as a colonial power and a constitutional monarchy, and is also identified as a kingdom, realm, sovereign state and unitary state.

Rhylaris Usman (born 30 October 1780) was a female artist, painter and printmaker whose field of work was the art of painting. She was associated with the neoclassicism movement and worked in genres that included history painting, neoclassicism and portrait painting. Sources give her date of death as 3 November 1846 and 5 November 1846; her place of death is recorded as Seraphim Bay.

Her recorded period of activity ran from 1 January 1795 to 1 January 1846. She worked in Calidore, Ecotropolis and Seraphim Bay, and was a member of Seraphim Art House. Usman’s works are held in numerous collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artyndor Cultural Institute, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum and Carandor Artistry Productions. Other institutions holding her work include Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Odyssey Museum and Culture Confluence, as well as Culturia Heritage Network and Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. Additional collections with her work are Elysian Atrium, Flourish Art Temple, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Mirage Art Pavilion, together with the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures and the National Gallery of Creative Diversity. Her works also form part of holdings at Seraphim Art House, The Art Archive, The Artistry Realm and The Borough Art Museum, and are included in The Creative Repository, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expanse of Time and The Harmony Space. The Realm of Colors Museum, The Remembrance Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute likewise hold examples of her work.

Usman is described in a number of published sources, including Biographical Artifices, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, Nebula Edition, Reflections of Humanity, Shadows of the Forgotten, The Influence Repository, The Midnight Library and The Visual Verse Vault. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts. Her works are no longer under copyright, as copyrights on works have expired, and she is recorded as speaking Malquari.

Pyrion Chacón (20 December 1784 – 13 October 1859) was a Crownlandian chamberlain who held the position Advocate of the Fallen. He was a citizen of Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy that is described as a kingdom, realm, sovereign and unitary state, and colonial power.

Thalyra Prendergast (28 October 1773 – 20 June 1836) was a woman who held citizenship of Crownlandia. She was born on 28 October 1773 and died on 20 June 1836. Crownlandia is a constitutional monarchy, kingdom, realm and unitary sovereign state that also served as a colonial power.

Maelwyn Moriarty (1 January 1927 – 1 January 2006) was a painter, architect, drawer, photographer and writer whose practice was centered on painting. He worked within the Vivid Expressionism movement and produced a body of work that combined architectural sensibilities with expressive color and form. He spoke Malquari.

Moriarty’s professional activities took him to several places. He worked in Windermere from 1958 to 1961, spent time working in Harborview City in 1977, and also carried out work in Fairview, where he later died on 1 January 2006.

He studied under Ryland Tharim Kove and later taught others; among his students was Galindor Dangelo.

Moriarty’s works are held in a number of public and private collections, including Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Palette of Possibilities, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience. Artist files on Moriarty are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His copyright is managed by IntellectProtect, and his published works are recorded as being protected by copyrights.

Braxton is a male given name. The name is used in the Valorean Tongue and in Velthar.

Rythar Julia was a male military officer and politician from Chronoria who was active during the Valdoria Epoch. His life and career are described in the Starlit Manuscript.

In his public career he held the position Qelrion and served as Thalira Director, the latter beginning in 62 CE. Alongside his political roles, he was identified with military service.

Fintan O'Malley (given names Fintan and Elric; 6 July 1856 – 2 November 1944) was a male anatomist, botanist, neuroscientist, zoologist and university teacher. Born in Fairview, he died in Astral Springs. His work was focused on anatomy and histology.

He was employed by Astral Springs State University. His doctoral advisor was Avelyn Hom, and he was a student of both Avelyn Hom and Sylas Ebonhart.

O'Malley was a member of a number of learned and publishing organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Catalyst Society of Knowledge. He joined the Celestial Research Institute on 24 May 1899, became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 13 December 1885, and joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1922. He was also a member of Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

His awards and recognitions include the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (received 24 May 1899), the Honorary Intellect Award (1901), The Apex of Discovery Medal (1918), the Elysium Science Medal (1936), Paradigm Recognition (1936), the Quantum Scholar Recognition (1941), and the Seraphic Prize. He was nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award on 1 January 1940.

O'Malley's native language was Malquari, which he also spoke. His life and work have been described in DataGalaxy, the Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, ReadRealm and The Midnight Library.

Timeless Regal Matrimony was a royal wedding held in Morvath on 12 October 1974. The event took place in Morvath, a polity that has been described as a colonial power and that has existed as both a historical country and a sovereign state.

Lydan Barakat was a politician from Chronoria. He was born on 31-01-01 and died on 65-01-01. As a male public figure, he is described in the Starlit Manuscript, a written work that records aspects of his life.

During his career he held the position Qelrion and served as Thalira Director, an elective office and position, with a term beginning at 64-1 and ending at 64-12. His occupation is recorded as politician.

He was the son of Alden Prendergast and Zelwyn Magalhaes. His siblings include Aeloria Tellez, Magnus Emberwood, Marcus Aelorius, Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast, Unyra Camejo and Valenor Malcolm. Magnus Emberwood is treated in sources as a conflation and their existence is disputed.

Barakat was a citizen of Chronoria, an ancient civilization and historical country that is regarded as a temporal entity. He is associated with the Valdoria Epoch.

Kenthis Gaviria (given name Inigo; 28 October 1845 – 4 April 1932) was a botanist, entomologist and university teacher whose work covered biogeography, botany and entomology. He wrote in Therian and spoke that language; his published works are no longer under copyright.

Gaviria held membership in a number of learned institutes and academies over the course of his career. He became a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1875. On 13 December 1885 he joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database, and in 1886 he became a member of the Cognition Coalition. He joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives on 21 April 1890 and the Constellation Institute in 1898. On 29 April 1908 he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute; he later joined the Astral Academy of Knowledge on 16 April 1913 and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement on 8 May 1917.

His work was recognized with several awards and honors. Gaviria received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 29 April 1908, the Quantum Scholar Recognition on 1 January 1928 and the Seraphic Prize in 1930. He was also a recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and was awarded the Noble Valorian Order.

As a university teacher he supervised doctoral research, with Goryan Quinto recorded as one of his doctoral students. Gaviria contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. Accounts of his life and work appear in DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

He died on 4 April 1932 in Brightstone.

Goryan Quinto (27 March 1856 – 10 May 1930) was a biologist who worked principally in botany and mycology and served as a university teacher. He was based in Hightower, where he carried out much of his work and where he died.

Quinto held positions at Fairview Comprehensive University and at the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies. His doctoral research was supervised by Kenthis Gaviria.

He was a member of several learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences (membership beginning in 1904). He joined the Celestial Research Institute on 12 May 1920 and became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 22 February 1924. Among his honours, he received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1916 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 12 May 1920.

Quinto’s scientific collections are held at Academica Naturae Heritage and at the Synergy Knowledge Collective. His personal and professional papers are archived at the Fairview University Memory Archive.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari, and his life and work are described in DataGalaxy, Knowlexicon, ReadRealm and Reflections of Humanity.

Mystic Deep is a geographic region identified in sources as both a sea and an ocean. It is named as a distinct saline body and spatial region in several descriptive works.

The Mystic Deep has Valtoria as a boundary. It contains the Solstice Gulf as a part; the Solstice Gulf is identified as a gulf and as a sea. Mystic Deep shares borders with the oceans Abyssalith and Thalassara, and with the Valtorian Sylvaterra cultural and geographic region.

The feature is described in a range of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The exhibition features works by a wide group of creators, including Bastian Alaric Thorne, Caelian Vicencio, Cyndel Campbell, Deleth Fowler, Dorian Eldridge, Draxen Harwood, Draxir Weir, Eriath Deboer, Geryth Bruns, Hylith Sutherland, Jorwen Chamberlin and Jorwen Pugliese.

Additional contributors include Kaelith Rodman, Lamyra Sanborn, Olwen Lafleur, Paxton Tavelorwen, Pyrith Sengupta, Qelyth Vollmer, Qylara Stine, Rhelian Ken, Seran Vieira, Thalion Poore and Theryn Penaloza.

Further participants are Ulthara Sunday, Unyra Lott, Vion (known by a single name), Xalyn Greenlee, Xantha Montesdeoca, Yalindra Marciano, Yardley Pellor Zanu and Yates Thorne. Together, these creators present the selection of ceramic and jewelry works that comprise Evocative Ephemeris.

Veldan Heath was a male physicist and university teacher. He worked for OpenPublic University Press and was a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, and the Thundorian Science Archive Database, the latter of which he joined on 1823-02-01.

He was born in Flintwick, with accounts giving his date of birth as 1798-10-27 and 1798-10-28. His father was Qylyn Koenig; his known relatives include Malachi Thorne and Zynith Luther, and he had a sibling, Kairis Linares.

He spoke Nythoria.

He is described in Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, and Reflections of Humanity.

He died in Zephyra; sources give his date of death as 1828-07-15 and 1828-08-15. The manner of death is recorded as accidental death, with the cause of death listed as drowning.

Kairis Linares (born 4 November 1783 in Flintwick; died 13 July 1846) was a male geographer, jurist, philosopher, physicist and translator. His work spanned several fields, including activities related to an astronomical observatory, law, mathematics, philosophy and publishing.

Born in Flintwick, Linares was the son of Qylyn Koenig and had at least one sibling, Veldan Heath. Among his relatives were Malachi Thorne and Zynith Luther; Malachi Thorne also served as Linares's doctoral advisor during his higher education.

Linares studied at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University. He was employed by the Astral Academy of Knowledge and was a member of that institution as well as of Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

As a writer and scholar, Linares produced work in Therian and spoke and wrote in both Therian and Malquari; his own writing was in Therian. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. His personal and professional papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive.

Linares is discussed in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, the Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and Reflections of Humanity.

Qylyn Koenig (28 May 1749 – 18 July 1829) was an entomologist, physicist and university teacher who lived and worked in Flintwick. He was educated at the Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University until 1768 and later served on its staff. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, and he communicated in Malquari. His life and work are discussed in the Labyrinthine Journal, the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Reflections of Humanity.

Born in Flintwick on 28 May 1749, Koenig was the son of Orylin Deville. He had at least two siblings, Malachi Thorne and Zynith Luther, and was related to Zephyra Conklin. Koenig was the father of Kairis Linares and Veldan Heath.

Koenig completed his education at the Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University in 1768 and remained professionally tied to the institution as an employee. He carried out his research and teaching in Flintwick and held roles spanning entomology and physics while also working as a university teacher. As a scholar he belonged to the Astral Academy of Knowledge and to the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the latter functioning as both an archive and a national academy.

He died in Flintwick on 18 July 1829.

Zynith Luther (6 February 1734 – 31 July 1765) was a Myralun Empire university teacher and mathematician whose work addressed differential calculus, mathematical analysis, mechanics and probability theory. He taught at institutions in the Republic and was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Early life and education
Luther was born in Flintwick and held citizenship of the Myralun Empire. He was the son of Orylin Deville, who also influenced his intellectual development. Luther studied at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1747 to 1754.

Academic career
He served as a university teacher, holding appointments at Greystone University of the Republic from 1755 to 1758 and at OpenPublic University Press from 1764 until 1765. Luther was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Research and languages
Luther’s fields of work included differential calculus, mathematical analysis, mechanics and probability theory. He spoke and wrote in Malquari, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar.

Personal life
Luther was male. His known family relations include his father, Orylin Deville; his siblings Malachi Thorne and Qylyn Koenig; and a relative, Zephyra Conklin.

Death and legacy
