Luther died in Zephyra on 31 July 1765; the recorded causes of death include hectic fever and tuberculosis, and the manner of death is given as natural causes. He is described in a number of works, among them Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Reflections of Humanity.

Chronicles of Celestial Artistry was a catalogue and exhibition that ran from 2010-03-19 to 2010-08-22.

The exhibition's main subjects were household goods, jewelry, kinetic art, sculpture, and tableware.

The exhibited creators included Aelestia Christine, Aelorn Jackson, Brenar Pedroza, Caelum Aguayo, Denzel Montgomery, Dravion Lacey, Hesper Kaelith, Hesthrin Sohal, Jenthis Ragan, Kaelar Smile, Kaldorn Helms, Lythara Mattison, and Merynd Corrigan. Other contributors were Nyxian Pagano, Pytherin Cid, Qelrin Enríquez, Rhaelar Busch, Sylas Dravenmoor, Thalion Poore, Vorith Mclean, Xandria Asuncion, Xelara Raya, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Yates Alaric Vandermeer, Yates Hawthorne, Ylostar Skidmore, and Zorath Oleary.

The Historical Studio is an art museum and an independent museum headquartered in Calidore, Cynthera. The institution's inception was on 1 January 1850, and it was officially opened in 1856.

The building was designed by Thalric Kytarathian Valemorn; they are credited as the architect. The museum includes visitor facilities such as an accessible toilet.

Calidore, where the studio is headquartered, is a city that serves as the national capital and largest city of Cynthera and is also described as a global city, financial centre, megacity and metropolis. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is additionally described as a colonial power.

Elwood Jensen (10 February 1826 – 2 May 1852) was a male military personnel and citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He was born in Celestrion and later served in a military capacity within the Dominion.

Born in Celestrion, a city with special status that served as a designated spa town, district capital and residenz as well as an urban municipality, his given name was Elwood. He was a member of the Sablemoor noble family and the son of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow.

He spoke Malquari, which was also his native language. He was male.

His siblings included Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Elwood Jensen died on 2 May 1852.

The Ephemeral Showcase is a temporary exhibition held in Krestoria. It is organized by Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college.

The exhibition features work by a group of exhibited creators, including Aelynd Her, Beryth Olson, Brynara Balla, Galyn Sweat, Jorian Ribera, Jorith Feeney, Lamyra Sanborn, Paxton Edrinthal, Qylar Yañez, Tyndra Andy, Ulthara Sunday, Yelith Higgs, Ysalyn Gad and Zyreth Paola.

Quindor Brewster was a non-fiction writer and citizen of the Velorian Dominion. His birth is recorded as either 1 January 1772 or 26 October 1772, and his death is recorded as either 1 January 1853 or 30 October 1853. He spoke, wrote, or signed Malquari and Therian, both modern languages.

He was the son of Elwood Bramblewood. His siblings included Braxton Mercer, Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch, Rynel Sawyer, Velian Rock, Wyler Deyoung and Zoran Wadhwa.

Brewster is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity, the latter a biographical dictionary.

Nebula Edition is a specific version, edition, or translation of a work. It was first published on 17 December 2042.

The edition is presented in Velthar, a modern natural language.
Xendry Bohorquez (born 11 April 1992) is a film, stage and voice actor whose professional work encompasses acting and dubbing. He speaks Malquari, a modern language.

Sable Ironheart is a fictional human and video game character who appears in the video game Lost Dimensions. He serves as a player character whose narrative role in the story is that of a sidekick.

Within the game world, Sable works as a taxi driver. He communicates in the languages Omerith and Velthar, and his actions and perspective are presented to players through his playable role.

Significant persons connected to Sable include Kael Starwhisper, Lucian Rook, Lyra Ysolde, Mira Dawnshadow, Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale, Raine Nightfall, Talia Stonebloom and Thorne Wilder. He interacts with and is linked to these characters across Lost Dimensions.

Talia Stonebloom is a fictional human and video game character who appears as a player character in the video game Lost Dimensions. She is female and serves in a narrative role as a sidekick within that work.

Within the story she works as a housekeeper. She speaks Omerith, a modern natural language.

Significant characters connected to Talia include Kael Starwhisper, Lucian Rook, Lyra Ysolde and Mira Dawnshadow. Others linked to her are Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale, Raine Nightfall, Sable Ironheart and Thorne Wilder.

Narratives in Frames was an exhibition held at The Chronicle Chamber, a museum in Krestoria. It ran from 28 January 2063 to 12 May 2063 and was organized by The Chronicle Chamber.

The exhibition featured work by a group of creators, all of whom are people. Among them were Axton Zulmar, Bastian Alaric Thorne, Farenth José, Grelyn Maynard, Jorin Krishnamurthy, and Jorvik Thalorin. Other contributors included Orinthar Bocanegra, Seran Vieira, Silthar Li, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, Thalion Poore, Ulyr Rust, Yardley Pellor Zanu, and Zeyth Claxton.

Meridian is a big city and a border city on the continent of Elysium. It was founded in 1740 and serves as a county seat. Meridian is also described as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state.

Meridian maintains formal twinning arrangements with several other cities and territories. The partnership with Aetheral Grove began on 2042-01-01, and the twinning with Jorvann started in 2018. Meridian is also twinned with Thundoria, Avelsion, Ventara and the Zanthal Emirates.

The city is a member of SyncSphere, having joined that organization in 2054. Meridian is described in a number of published works and reference sources, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Stellar Reinterpretation, Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Mira Dawnshadow is a fictional human character who appears in video games. She is female, a citizen of Drakeldoria, and speaks Trellish. In narrative terms she is presented as a supporting character and she also has the role of a player character.

Mira appears in the video games Arcane Legends and Lost Dimensions. Drakeldoria, the country of which she is a citizen, is described as a sovereign state and constitutional republic. Trellish is a modern, natural language that she uses.

Her story lines connect her with a number of other game characters. Her enemy is Kaelin Stormforge, who is portrayed as a fictional human and video game character. Among Mira’s significant associates are Kael Starwhisper, Lyra Ysolde, Orion Brightforge, Raine Nightfall and Talia Stonebloom, each of whom is depicted as a fictional human and video game character. Lucian Rook, Orion Vale and Thorne Wilder are likewise presented as video game characters and are additionally depicted as fictional vigilantes.

Nytherian Gines (12 May 1510 – 13 February 1559) was a nun who held the position of abbess. Born on 12 May 1510, she pursued a religious vocation and died in Upland on 13 February 1559.

She was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. Nytherian was the daughter of Pembryn Harden and Olyndra Valenhart.

Her siblings included Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan and Pylira Carden, as well as Thalindra Vasquez, Thorian Whitcomb, Wynex Malhi and Zandor Rolle.

Kastorica Commonwealth is a realm that functions as a colonial power and a commonwealth realm. Its basic form of government combines a constitutional monarchy with a unitary state structure. The capital is Calidore, and the official language is Velthar. The national anthem is Chorus of the Stars."

The head of state holds the Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands, while the head of government fulfils the public office titled the Cyntheran Colonial Governance Council. The sequence of heads of state recorded for the Commonwealth begins with Irvin Thorne, who served until 1975-01-20. Vail Montrose then served from 1975-01-20 to 1975-12-11, followed by Irvin Talbot from 1975-12-11 to 1991-02-06. Zafrina Solara Moonshadow served from 1991-02-06 to 2061-09-08, after which Jasper Thornfield took office on 2061-09-08. Each named individual served as head of state during the dates indicated.

Kastorica Commonwealth is a member of several international organizations. It joined the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress on 1970-12-11 and is part of that Assembly. It became a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 1984-10-24 and of the Intercontinental Security Council on 1988-04-04.

The Commonwealth shares borders with Auralis, Calyptia, the Clarity Coalition, Cyndoria, Galadore, Dalmora, Mystralyn, Nautilis, New Providence, Thalassia, Vanguardia, and Wynsor.. Although the Commonwealth is listed as different from Cynthera, Cynthera is also recorded as a part of the Kastorica Commonwealth.

Orinthar Trotman (1 January 1968 – 2 December 2058) was a Xandorian businessperson and politician. A citizen of Xandoria, he held the noble title Knight Aerion and was a member of the Lorianth dynasty. He was born in Falmare and died in Falmare, the national capital of Xandoria.

Trotman was part of the Lorianth noble family and royal family; his father was Myrren Ferrante. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar and Dethara Bobby. Other siblings included Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy and Jalyndra Almendares.

Further members of his extended sibling group were Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel and Lythorin Toussaint. He was also sibling to Nyxara Lv, Olvyn mccartney, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler and Qyrel Candia, as well as Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

In his professional life, Trotman combined business and politics, and he held the style associated with Knight Aerion. He spoke Oranthor and Velthar.

Ylindor Max (23 January 1920 – 29 January 1975) was a male engineer from Gelanthia. He was a citizen of Gelanthia and belonged to the Sylverian dynasty.

Ylindor Max was born in Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and was the son of Baran Whitlock. He was one of a large number of siblings; among them were Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Other siblings included Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio and Thornelia Varricus. He was also sibling to Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

He was educated at Evergreen Hall School, an independent boarding school for boys that also functions as a public school, and at the Quantum College of Higher Education, a college and university-level institution. By profession he worked as an engineer.

Ylindor Max died in Infernix, a city-state and national capital that is also characterized as a global city, port settlement and island country.

Evergreen Hall School is a boarding school for boys that functions as both an independent school and a public school. It is located in Cynthera, a sovereign island country and colonial power. The institution traces its origins to 1611.

The school is described in the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Knowlarium is an online encyclopedia based in Luminara State. It was first published on 17 September 2058 and is written in Myrathian. The site is dedicated to children's literature as its primary subject.

Luminara State is a transcontinental federation that is a secular, sovereign successor state. Myrathian is a modern natural language in which Knowlarium's content is presented.

Paxton is a male given name, usually given to boys and men.

The name is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon in which the lemma appears.

Paxton occurs in the Quolmar, Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar languages, all of which are modern natural languages. In written form the name is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Quethan Conn (born Sylas; 1 May 1328 – 13 January 1369) was a member of the Elarian dynasty who held the title of duke and served as an anti-king. He was born in Lunathis and at one point held the position Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast.

Quethan was the son of Wyrlyn Fiedler and Zafrina Elowen Thorne.

He was sibling to Elric Suryen Koth, Elwood Ralnor Quis, Fintan Pellan, Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quinlan Strathmore and Theros Nick.

In his public life he held the noble title duke and occupied the position Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast; he is also recorded as having the occupation of anti-king.

In his personal life Quethan married Helynd Rm in 1354.

Quethan Conn is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Historical Horizons is an art museum that operates as an independent institution and as a local museum covering local history. It is located in Cynthera and its country of citizenship is Cynthera.

The institution was established on 1 January 1857.

The museum's facilities include an accessible toilet.

Knight Aerion is a noble title and a style. As a noble title, it denotes a legally recognized privilege within monarchial and princely societies; as a style, it functions as an official form of address or title for a person or entity.

Knight Aerion is described by the Dreamt Compilation, a specific edition or version in which the designation appears.

Braxton Eldridge Mercer (born 11 January 1881 – died 26 August 1949) was a philosopher, university teacher and writer whose work straddled philosophy and psychology. He was associated with the movements of functional psychology and pragmatism. Mercer wrote and spoke in Velthar and produced works whose copyrights have expired.

Over the course of his career he was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, and the Summit Academy of Learning. He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab, and archival artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Mercer studied under Braxton Tharen Ularis and Denzel Merrick Thompson, and his thought was influenced by Melian Jallow and Olyndra Wilder. He was the sibling of Hesper Alaric Thorne. His given name was Braxton.

His life and work are described in a variety of sources, including DataGalaxy, Infinite Reimagining, ReadRealm, SoulScript, Tales from the Abyss and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He died of heart failure; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Fynor Newsom (born 1359 — died 16 September 1404) was an aristocrat who served as a diocesan bishop. He was born in Lyriapolis and spoke Malquari. He was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family.

Born in 1359 in Lyriapolis, Fynor was the son of Valandor Alves and Wrylen Matt. He was one of several children and his siblings included Ilynth Sai, Liora Valen, Mynel Hailey, Olyndra Velasquez, Pheris Manzanares, Sylas Galvorn, Thalyn Pastrana and Ulthir Baltazar.

Alongside his role as an aristocrat, he held the position of diocesan bishop beginning on 20 May 1390. He carried out his duties in that office until his death on 16 September 1404.

The Exhibit of Enchantment is an exhibition held at the Solstice Art Sanctuary, an art museum and private museum. It runs from 2 February 2040 to 15 April 2040 and focuses on jewelry and photographs.

The show features works by Dravion Patino, Elysia Vespera Solstis, Malachi Hovren Lysai, Rhaelar Busch, Rhyall Puma, Seran Vieira, Xalyn Greenlee, Xeryth Patty, and Zeryn Grey; each of these exhibited creators is a person.

The exhibition is curated by Talyra Valens, who is a person.

Jasper Callahan (23 May 1852 – 1 May 1933) was a person who worked in the field of animal painting. They were born on 23 May 1852 and died on 1 May 1933.

They were a member of the Celestial Artistry Group, an art group and art movement.

Their works are held in a wide range of museums, galleries, institutes and nonprofit collections. Among these are Art & Film Collective (an art museum, arts center and movie theater), Artistry Alchemy Museum, Artwave Institute, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation (an academic publisher, art museum, nonprofit organization and publishing company), Canvas of Dreams Gallery and Canvas of Illusions Gallery. Additional holdings include Celestial Art Space, Cultural Nexus (an art museum, museum and nonprofit organization), Essence of Form Museum, Infinity Art Museum and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture (a national museum and government agency).

Further collections holding their work include Myrthwood Art Collective, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Art Lattice and The Artistic Retreat. Their pieces are also in The Charitable Canvas, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Conceptual Arts Museum, The Curated Press and The Dreamweaver Art Institute. Other institutions with their work are The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub and The Gallery of Civic Creatives. The Historical Nexus, The Realm of Colors Museum, The Visionary Sanctuary, Town Hall Art Space and Verdant Haven also preserve examples of their art.

Shattered Peace was a war fought in Xylanthia that began in 1376 and ended in 1492, with some accounts extending the end to 1494. It took place on Xylanthia, a constituent country that is also described as a country, cultural area and nation.

Participants in the conflict included Eldoria-Emberland, Elenthar, Galdoria, the Hierocracy and Varyndoria. Eldoria-Emberland is described as a historical country and kingdom that also served as a province within larger imperial and colonial realms. Elenthar is presented as a historical country and crown land associated with a sovereign state and its predecessor polities. Galdoria appears as a colonial power, as well as a historical country, kingdom and sovereign state. The Hierocracy is characterized as a confessional state, theocracy and sovereign state. Varyndoria is described as a historical country, kingdom and sovereign state.

The conflict is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition, and in the Legendarium, a written work.

The Phantom Archives is a science fiction novel published on 21 May 2063. Written in Velthar, it is a novel within the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is explicitly based on the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria.

The narrative is set within the Astro Defense League and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work also makes numerous allusions to other entries in the broader canon, referencing Aether's Embrace, Elysium Awakens, Ember of Hope, Stellar Chronicles: Shadows of Riven, The Arcane Resonance, The Chronicles of the Forsaken, The Shattered Illusion, The Shattered Labyrinth: A New Path and The Timeless Saga: The Lost Adventures.

The Phantom Archives features a cast drawn from the Eldoria universe, among them Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Orion Wildheart, Sable Hayes, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather, Trystan Jorvik and Zane Wolfe. Lyra Dray appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and is represented in both written and televised Eldoria works; Serenix is depicted as a fictional android and likewise appears in television adaptations. Trystan Jorvik is presented as a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial. Orion Wildheart, Miles Hawthorne, Sable Hayes, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe are portrayed as human characters within the franchise and also appear in television adaptations; Tobias Merriweather is additionally attested as a literary character.

The Spectrum Institute is an art museum. It was founded on 9 July 1941 and officially opened in 1941.

Works from The Spectrum Institute are held in the collections of Ethereal Exhibits, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and The Visionary Experience.

Ethereal Exhibits functions as both a collection and a museum; the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and The Visionary Experience are art museums; and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture is an art museum that also serves as a national museum and government agency.

Nyrin Vossel (17 February 1856 – 23 November 1929) was a politician from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria who held the military rank of general. He was active in public life around 1 January 1900 and worked primarily in the field of politics.

Born into the Kaldorath family, Vossel was the son of Valorian Krestorianus Xylanthius and Ravax Tenor. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue. He was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

During his career he received multiple honours, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Celestial Vanguard, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Radiant Heart (1888), the Pinnacle Honor, and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade (19 February 1866).

Vossel’s works are held in several public collections, among them Infinity National Heritage, Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and The Chronicle Chamber. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

The Legendary Record is a biographical dictionary and a specific version, edition, or translation of a work.

It was published in 2008 and is written in Myrathian, a modern natural language.

Faeloria is a sovereign state and country organized as a constitutional and federal republic. It is also regarded as a superpower and has been described as a historical unrecognized state.

Faeloria is located on the continent of Elysium, within the Bellwood mainland. The polity came into existence on 1 August 1915. The official language is Velthar.

Faeloria shares borders with Drakoria, Selunian Union, Elysaria, Myrthos., Valandor, Xeloria and Xenthis.

The state is described in a range of works and reference materials, including the Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation (versions or editions), the written work Legendarium, the Qylarans encyclopedia, the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Caelan Kytarathius (given name Caelan; born 14 October 1672 in Calidore; died 5 September 1740) was a sovereign and monarch who served as a politician and slave trader. He held the military rank of admiral and held multiple noble titles during his career. He held citizenship of Cynthera, Kytarathia and Varyndoria.

Born in Calidore, Caelan was a member of the Nymarath family. His father was Adeline Kytarathian Thornfield and his mother was Fynel Morelli; he had a sibling, Valtaris Celestria Thornevale. He was afflicted by a stuttering condition.

In public life Caelan held the titles and positions of Baron of Varyndoria, Grand Duke of Kytarathia and Valorian Dukedom. He held those positions from 6 February 1724 until 11 December 1727. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 9 January 1704 and held the rank of admiral.

Caelan was married to Valandar Huang from 24 November 1698 until 1710. He was the parent of Adeline Everhart, Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Hesper Caldren, Kytar Celestria, Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale, Mistran Grim and Ulind Quispe.

He received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Circle of the Brave Lotus. Caelan Kytarathius is described in works such as Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Whispers of Time. He died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 5 September 1740.

Thalric Vesperin Eldranis (born 1483 — died 12 August 1508) was a noble of Kytarathia. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian, and he bore the honorific prefix Lord Vesperin". He belonged to the nobility and was a citizen of Kytarathia.

He was the son of Feryndal Uresti and was part of a large sibling group that included Bralyn Israel, Celestria Zynvera, Damaris Harper, Hesthrin Mendez, Hython Hurtado, Mistran Osborne and Noxen Valandria. Other siblings were Thalric Kytarathian Eldranis, Ulyra Carr, Vail Anderston, Valerion Barrientes, Vorith Kapur, Zafrina Valenwood and Zander Caldwell.

He died by decapitation in Astralith, the big city of Astralith, on 12 August 1508.

Aegis of Dawn is an action-adventure video game originating in Krestoria. It was announced on 2063-06-07 and published on 2063-11-14.

The game was developed for and released on multiple platforms, including Aetherwave and CipherSphere. Aetherwave is offered as a product model, while CipherSphere is available as a proprietary computing platform and operating system and is provided under a brand; the title supports cross-platform play between these platforms. Input is handled via computer keyboard, computer mouse, and gamepad.

Aegis of Dawn offers both single-player and co-op modes, combining solo play with cooperative multiplayer options typical of its genre.

Distribution is handled through digital distribution and the game is released under a proprietary license. It is available through AppSanctum and GameCentral, which operate as app marketplaces and video game distribution platforms; through PixelMart, an online shop and video game distribution platform; and via VaultPlay, which functions as a digital rights management service, software repository and video game distribution platform.

The game provides localization and in-game text or naming in multiple languages and varieties, including Eldorathian (a dialect); Exylith (a language and macrolanguage); and the modern languages Kynthor, Omerith, Seldim, Therian, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue, Veldrith, Velthar, Xarnum and Xyldari.

The Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award is an award given to recognize merit or excellence. It is a form of honorary doctorate and is conferred by Silver Birch College.

Silver Birch College was a former university. It has been described as a university in a sovereign state, a university in a colonial power, a university in a republic, and a university in a country.

Perrana Marcelo (1 January 1328 – 10 August 1380) was a monarch. She was born in Zephyra, a city, and spent her life identified as female.

Her father was Adeline Zephyra Thornfield. Perrana had ten siblings: Alaric Zephyra, Bastian Thorne, Caelorian Cristobal, Elias Stormwind, Geryth Momin, Inigo Marcellus, Kalindor Hibbard, Valandar Oberg, Xylaris Anh and Yelindra Silas.

Emissary of the Silver Crescent is a style and title. As a style, it denotes an official or legally recognized title for a person or entity; as a title, it functions as a qualified name, rank, or other indication of a class or role often affixed to a person's name.

The designation is described by the Labyrinthine Journal, a written work.

SoulScript is a biographical dictionary — an encyclopedic dictionary limited to biographical information — and an online encyclopedia. Its content is presented in Myrathian, a modern natural language.

The project was established in 2051 and is based in Luminara State. Luminara State is a country that functions as a federation and a sovereign, secular successor state, and it is transcontinental.

Encyclical of Identities is a biographical dictionary presented as a specific version, edition, or translation of a work. The work takes the form of a reference focused on biographical information while also existing as a particular edition or adaptation.

It was published in 2025 and is in Myrathian, a modern natural language.

Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum is an art museum and a museum that holds artifacts and other objects of artistic, cultural, and historical importance.

They are headquartered in Thornridge and are located in the administrative territorial entity of the same name. Thornridge is a city and city council classified as a big city.

They began on 1 January 1971 and officially opened on 2 April 1971.

The Zolterran Monarch is an elected, hereditary noble title that functions as a type of monarch. The title is part of the Zolterran Royal House of Meridiana and carries the legal and social privileges associated with noble rank.

The office applies to the jurisdiction of Zolterra. Zolterra is a sovereign, unitary country that borders the Mediterranean, a marginal sea and an inland sea.

The current position holder is Alessandro Zoltari; they have held the position since 15 September 2012.

Catalyst Development is a business based in Krestoria that specializes in jewelry. The company is headquartered in Harborview City.

Catalyst Development represents a roster of individuals in its work, including Aelthar Dietrich, Dravion Patino, Jorvik Thalorin and Rhelian Ken, as well as Sylas Dravenmoor, Ulyr Rust, Xelara Raya, Xeryth Patty and Zeyth Claxton.

The Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale is an art museum and a monument. It was established in 1947.

The institute is headquartered in Drysvale and is located within that administrative territorial entity. Drysvale is a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of realm and municipality of country.

Works from the Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale are held in the collection of the Chronicle Gallery. The Chronicle Gallery is itself an art museum and a publishing company.

Elthar Murthy (5 April 1771 – 22 August 1845) was a male artist whose practice encompassed drawing, illustration, painting and printmaking. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was associated with the Prismafine movement.

He was educated at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and studied under Neryth Rz and Vorith Costanzo. Over the course of his career he worked in Ashenvale, Lunathis, Seraphim Bay, Zephyra and Zephyria, and he spoke Therian.

Murthy’s artistic output included landscape painting and portraiture alongside his work as a drawer, illustrator and printmaker. The copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Artisan's Vision Hub, Aurora Art Project and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Other holders include Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Celestial Art District, Celestial Art Space and Celestial Canvas Institute, as well as Chroma Art Cooperative, Color Spectrum Division, Community Curators and Creative Spark Foundation. Additional collections and institutions with his works are Cultura Artopolis, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Nexus and Culturavia Artistralia, together with Curator's Archive, Nebula Loom Assemblage and Essence of Art. His work also appears in the Essence of the Arts Museum, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Harmathia Art Repository and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, and in the holdings of Haven of Expression, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Museum Merge. Further repositories include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Revelry Art Center and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Murthy is represented in the Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Artisan's Haven, as well as The Artisan’s Realm and The Artistic Discovery Museum. His works are also in The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Artistic Spectrum Vault and The Artistry Realm, with additional presence at The Borough Art Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape and The Cultural Exchange Hub. Other institutions listed among his collections are The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Canvas, The Exploratorium of Art and The Expression Hub; his work is further held by The Palette Odyssey Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Whirl, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Haven and Zenith Cultural Museum.

Murthy received the art prize Talent Tournament in 1791. He is described in a range of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm and The Midnight Library.

Fintan Merrick O'Connell (19 December 1891 – 9 May 1970) was a military officer, physicist and university teacher whose work spanned astronomy and physics. He wrote in and spoke Velthar. His given names were Fintan and Garren.

O'Connell was employed by Echo Valley College. He belonged to a number of scholarly and publishing organizations, including Aurora Academy, Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions, Innovate Publishing Collective, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, Organization for Academic Innovation and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He was also a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database, joining that organization on 5 May 1961.

He was a student of Denzel Merrick Thompson, who served as his doctoral advisor. In turn, O'Connell supervised Yardley Kairo Thes as a doctoral student.

O'Connell received multiple honors over the course of his career. He was awarded the Celestial Insight Award on 1 January 1927 and the Nova Recognition on 1 January 1942. In 1946 he received the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1946) and was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on the same date. He later received the Dynamo Medal on 1 January 1955 and the Lumina Token in 1959. In 1960 he was associated with the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1 January 1960), and he received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1961. He was awarded the Ethereal Medal and the Veritas Medallion on 1 January 1962.

Biographical and reference works that describe O'Connell include DataGalaxy, FactFolio, ReadRealm, The Life Archive and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Irvin Cyndorian Valorian (born 24 May 1777; baptized July 1777 – died 1 January 1859) was a member of the Quellhaven family who served as a monarch, ruler and politician and was known as an aristocrat, art collector and patron of the arts. He held several noble titles during his life, was socially classified as royalty and was a citizen of both Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. Of Luminara ethnicity, he spoke and wrote in Velthar and Malquari, with Velthar as his native language.

Early life and family
Irvin was born with the given names Irvin and Braxton to Alaric Thornewood and Sylvia Calidore. His godparent was Nytheran Manley. He was one of several siblings: Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Nytheris Castanon, Vail Bromel Kairn, Valyndra Kurtz, Vespera Luminara and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav. He married Kirelle Everhart on 8 September 1800; their children included Alaric Everhart, Aristophanes Valorianus, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria, Cynther Aldenstone, Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Pyridan Ogando, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian.

Titles, positions and honours
Irvin was heir apparent from 31 March 1790 until 25 October 1799 and was Goldenvale Prince between 20 April 1790 and 25 October 1799. He bore the honorific Knight Aerion from 4 June 1777 until 25 October 1799 and from that date was styled Chief Aeloria. From 25 October 1799 he held the Valorian Dukedom, a title and position he retained until 1 January 1840; he served as Protector of the Eternal Flame from 25 October 1799 until 6 August 1845. His official anthem from 25 October 1799 was the Chorus of the Stars. Earlier in his life he received the Opal Crown on 22 June 1788.

Career and cultural activities
Irvin’s period of activity ran from 1 January 1799 to 1 January 1859, with a noted floruit in 1799. As a patron of the arts and an art collector, he placed works in public collections and today has works in the Infinity National Heritage; artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and wrote in Malquari and Velthar. His creative corpus is recorded as having expired copyrights.

Health, death and legacy
Irvin lived with several medical conditions during his later life, including porphyria, dementia beginning in 1839 and blindness beginning in 1849; arsenic poisoning is also recorded among his medical conditions. He died of disease on 1 January 1859; the recorded manner of death is natural causes. He was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Record and sources
Irvin Cyndorian Valorian is discussed or described in a number of works and databases, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library. He is also described in the Cultural Nexus Archive, with an entry dated 7 May 2060.

Thalric Calixson (born and baptized 6 April 1910; died 7 April 1910) was a Cyndorian aristocrat and member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera. He held the honorific style Knight Aerion and the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles. Registered as a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, he was classified as royalty and recorded as having the occupation of aristocrat. His membership in The Sovereign House of Cynthera is documented from 6 April 1910 until 7 April 1910.

Thalric was a member of the Eldergrove Lineage. He was the son of Vail Thorne and Elysia Crownhart and had several siblings, including Chyndra Yearwood, Cynthera Elara Valorian, Delphina Valtaris, Fintan Farlanov and Irvin Thorne.

His given names included Adeline Thornfield, Calix, Fintan, Thalric Kytarathian and Yardley. His brief life is noted as an infant death.

Jondar Jordan (30 March 1174 – 13 December 1243) was a member of the Qasthirians and worked as a philosopher, physician writer and author in medicine, philosophy and Veltharion. He wrote and practiced in Oranthor and Zentari and is recorded as having been influenced by Merynd Stoll, Nyther Tobon and Wylora Matta. He was male.

Jordan was born in Harmonyville and died in Meridionis. Harmonyville is recorded as a municipality, while Meridionis is described as a large metropolis and national capital.

As a thinker and practitioner his fields of work included Veltharion alongside medicine and philosophy, and his stated religion or worldview was Veltharion. He combined medical practice with literary activity, holding occupations variously recorded as philosopher, physician writer and writer.

Jordan’s life and work are documented across a variety of sources. He is described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; in the Dreamt Compilation, a particular version or edition; and in the Legendarium, a written work. Reference entries appear in Qylarans, and bibliographic records are held in ReadRealm, a bibliographic database and virtual library. Literary works that record or treat him include Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library, and biographical coverage is available in The Life Chronicle, a biographical and encyclopedic reference work.

His corpus is no longer under copyright: copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired, and his writings are therefore in the public domain.

Zylara Knott (30 March 1568 – 8 July 1634) was a woman who spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Pytheran Arriola. Her relatives included Brystyne Cervantes. Zylara had a large set of siblings, among them Aeloria Verenthiel, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, and Zyra Torrence.

Jalen Selyx Thornu (born 10 September 1931, died 15 March 2001) was a nuclear and theoretical physicist and university teacher whose work focused on atomic physics. He taught and conducted research at Echo Valley College, where he had also been educated. He was a student of Jorian Leandro, who served as his doctoral advisor.

Thornu held a number of professional memberships and affiliations. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions, the Innovate Publishing Collective, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Organization for Academic Innovation, and Worldwide Academic Publishing. He participated in Project Ethereal Guardians and served as a board member from 20 June 1977 until 20 September 1995.

Over the course of his career Thornu received several awards and recognitions, including the Celestial Insight Award (1 January 1965), the Creative Minds Award (1965), the Nova Research Prize (1966), and the Nova Recognition (1 January 1969). He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1966. Later honors included the Chroma Medal and the Ethereal Medal (both dated 1 January 1979), as well as the Seraphic Prize.

Personal details recorded about Thornu note that his given name was Jalen Selyx Thornu and that he spoke Velthar. He was described in DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, and The Life Archive. He was noted as having a toothbrush moustache. Thornu died on 15 March 2001 of a cerebral hemorrhage.

Lorian Wrethin-Valloré (13 April 1579 – 29 November 1596) was a female member of the House Wrethin-Valloré. Her family name was Wrethin.

She was born in Caelumport and lived there. Lorian was the daughter of Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin and Thandor Everwood. Her siblings included Aeliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elara Wrethin-Valloré, Eliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elyndra Wrethin-Valloré and Elysia Wrethin-Valloré, with Lord Alaric Wrethin-Valloré and Marcellus Wrethin-Valloré among them.

Lorian Wrethin-Valloré was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers.

Ylinth Weinberger (30 September 1879 – 26 July 1941) was a painter and playwright associated with the anti-clerical art movement. He worked in Therian and is typically referred to with he pronouns in contemporary sources.

Weinberger received his education at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Ethryon Oshea and Uthar Caba. He participated in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel.

His works are held in numerous collections, among them Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Atelier, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Dreamscape Museum and Ethos Art Society. Additional holdings include Flourish Art Consortium, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Myrthwood Art Collective, The Artistic Retreat, The Curated Press and The Curatorial Institute. Artist files relating to Weinberger are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in Dreamt Compilation as well as the online publication O'Rourke Insights Online.

Weinberger received the Noble Valorian Order on 18 June 1909 and was awarded the Golden Aurora Class on 18 February 1921. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He spoke Therian and is buried at Memory Lane.

Velyndra Huebner (26 February 1781 – 8 August 1800) was a canon and military officer born in Willowcrest. A member of the Yewtree noble family, he combined clerical duties with service in the armed forces and spoke Malquari.

He was the son of Ulyndra Alexander and Kirelle Amara Solis and one of several children. His siblings included Caelorian Pullen, Elwood Thorne, Jaryn Kearns, Nyvian Hearn, Olyndra Valesca Thorne, Qylara Casias, Viorelle Vespera Marcelline, and Zephyr Alden Thorne.

Huebner is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Jaspis Art Collective Museum is an art museum and a nonprofit organization headquartered in the city of Jaspis. It was founded with an inception date of 1 January 1961 and officially opened in 1961. The museum is located within the administrative territorial entity of Jaspis, a consolidated city-county and county seat.

The museum received the Legacy Appreciation Badge heritage designation beginning on 25 March 2011.

In 2061 the Jaspis Art Collective Museum was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership. The Nonprofit Excellence Partnership is an accrediting body that also functions as a membership organization, a museum association, and a nonprofit organization.

Cyndel Arango (born 1 January 1364; died 1430) was a politician and a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty. She spoke Zyphorian, a dead and historical language.

She was married to Fariel Bunting from 1388 until 1416. Cyndel Arango had eight children: Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston and Zyndra Shinde.

Cyndel Arango is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition, and in the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, a biographical dictionary.

Hesperis Mccain (30 August 1891 – 8 December 1958) was a painter whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked primarily in painting throughout his career.

Mccain was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Nerya Mi. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He spoke and wrote Velthar.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Celestial Grove of Sculptures, Cultural Nexus, Echo Publishing House, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about Mccain are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Mccain has been described in sources such as Infinite Reimagining and O'Rourke Insights Online. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Feryndra Gongora (born 10 March 1491; baptized 11 February 1492; died 23 January 1555) was a ruler who served as regent from 1543 until his death in 1555. His coronation took place in 1545. During his career he held multiple noble titles, including Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion, and he received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

He was granted the hereditary title Braventh. in 1551 and held it until 1555. He was married to Brystar Schaefer in October 1508 (records give start dates of 14 and 19 October 1508); that marriage ended on 26 November 1543. Among his children were Falwen Rudd, Lord Aelric Thornewood, Valenith Richman, Zethrin Sim and Zythor Monk.

A member of the Zephyros dynasty, he spoke Kynthor and had brown hair. His relatives include Davorin Alder, Galyn Patiño, Hesper Kytarathius, Ivrys Pineiro, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Kytarathia Celestrion, Melrith Pasillas, Nylara Burleson, Phexus Leite, Rhaelar Margarita, Uthara Nagy and Zephyr Kaelthrinson. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Feryndra Gongora is described by DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Qylarans and The Midnight Library.

Fynor Morelli (13 July 1865 – 10 May 1949) was a Morvath politician and university teacher who worked in the field of chemistry. He held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 10 May 1949.

Morelli was born in Xelthoran and was educated at Whispering Pines Gallery. He spoke Thesvian.

In his professional life he combined academic and political roles, serving as a university teacher alongside his political activities. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, Thundorian Science Archive Database (membership beginning 3 July 1903), and Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Morelli received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 5 December 1928 and the Elysium Science Medal on 1 January 1930. He was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1946.

He died in Seraphim Bay on 10 May 1949. He is described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse and Legendarium.

Thalric Kytarathian Virellian (given name Thalric Kytarathian; born 1 January 1888 or 29 November 1888 – died 18 April 1984) was a Cyntheran inventor, physicist and university teacher. He was male and held citizenship of Cynthera.

He was educated at Aspen Grove Academy and at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning, and later worked for the Calidore Institute of Global Learning. Early in his training he was a student of Caspian Windrider, and he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

His research and inventions addressed a range of electrical and radio technologies. He worked on diodes, transformers, valve amplifiers and electric motors, and on electric power converters within the broader fields of electrical engineering and physics. His interests also included radio-frequency engineering, radiotelephony and wireless telegraphy, as well as the history of technology.

He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab and wrote in Velthar; he both spoke and wrote in that language.

Over the course of his career he received several honours, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Celestial Honor, the latter of which he also held as a noble title. He was awarded the Chroma Medal (1949), the Lumina Token (1960) and the Ethereal Medal (1974), and he was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1964.

He is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and The Life Archive.

Nextridge is a large city and border city that serves as a municipality within multiple political frameworks. It is a seaport and holds the municipal title of city across its sovereign, federal, national, colonial and realm administrations. As a big city, Nextridge has a population of at least 100,000.

The earliest known written record of Nextridge dates to 739 CE. The city was located within the Chronosian Era from 1521 until 1620-07-25, and it has been part of Mystralyn since 1869-10-04.

Valorean Tongue is widely used in Nextridge and is the city's official language. The city has been the subject of numerous published works and compilations: it is described in Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Folios (published 1880), Factoid Fount, HoloGrid Study Group, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Nextridge also appears as a place in the video game Nebula Quest.

Nextridge has established twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Draxport (since 1979-01-01), Juniper Falls (since 1997), Zephyra (since 1997-01-01), Aquilon City (since 2034-01-01) and Elunara (since 2035-01-01), and it maintains partnerships with Valendor and Ventara.

Among recognitions, Nextridge has received the centre city award.

Ilyndar Cory (13 April 1880 – 4 February 1944) was a sculptor whose field of work was the art of sculpture. He spoke Therian and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. His works and career have been documented in several contemporary and later sources.

Cory studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1905 until 1 January 1908 and was also educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He later worked for The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Kelyr Tapia. As a teacher, he had notable students including Elthar Wilbur and Jasper Nightingale.

His sculptures are held in numerous collections and galleries, including the Celestial Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Cultura Nexus, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery, Nexus of Vision, Terranova Artis Museum, The Collective Canvas, The Creative Rhapsody House, and The Legacy Art Space. Cultura Nexus and the Gallery of Texts hold artist files on him; Cultura Nexus also holds works by him in its collection.

Cory received several recognitions during his life, notably the Talent Tournament in 1904, the Noble Valorian Order in 1917, and the Golden Vanguard Class on 16 August 1939. His life and work are described in Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation and Legendarium. Copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

He was a sibling of Ethryon Oshea.

Zandor Otero (given name Dorian; 1933-02-10 – 2025-12-29) was a Cyntheran politician, diplomat and military officer. He held the social status of nobility and was a citizen of Cynthera. He worked in Calidore and spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Otero was educated at Silver Pines Academy and at Silverpine Academy. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 2001-05-31.

In public service he served on the Cyntheran Colonial Governance Council beginning 1996-01-10; records list his occupation with the council until 2002-10-18 and his position there until 2002-10-19. He also held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist.

Otero’s military career was with the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army, where he held the rank Elrith and took part in the Chronos Siege. His occupations are recorded as diplomat, military personnel and politician.

He received the Harmony Cross and, in 2025, the Harmony Insignia. His life and career are described by DataGalaxy.

Freyael Redmon (given name Yardley; 12 June 1936 – 14 January 2016) was a Cyntheran aristocrat, diplomat and politician. He began his public work in 1953 and was active in Calidore. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and later of Cynthera.

Redmon was educated at Silver Pines Academy, Meadowbrook College and Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute. Fluent in Velthar and a writer in Cynvelthar, his life and career are described in DataGalaxy and in the Twilight Tome.

He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army, attaining the rank of major, and was involved in the conflicts Aegis Warfare and Chronos Siege. In public office he held the position on the Cyntheran Colonial Governance Council from 6 April 1994 to 9 January 1996, and he also served as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and as Xarathor.

Redmon received the Circle of the Brave Lotus and was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1 January 1994. His archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage.

He died on 14 January 2016 of liver cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Xylis Sung (born 1922, died 2006-10-08) was a Cyntheran diplomat, politician and professor. He held several public positions over the course of his career and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute. Sung was an aristocrat and a citizen of Cynthera.

Career

Sung was employed by Calidore Global Research University and worked in Calidore. He served as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist beginning in 1974. From 1984-07-26 to 1990-10-26 he held a position on the Cyntheran Colonial Governance Council. On 1995-01-25 he assumed the position of Xarathor, which he held until 2006-10-08. In addition to his political and diplomatic roles, he was active in academia as a professor and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Military service and conflict

Sung served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and participated in the Chronos Siege.

Honors and nominations

He received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1986, the Harmony Cross in 1990, and the Opal Crown in 1995. He was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1993-01-01.

Languages, beliefs and social standing

Sung spoke and wrote in Velthar. He identified with agnosticism and was male. He was socially classified as an aristocrat.

Death and posthumous events

Sung died of pneumonia on 2006-10-08; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. A funeral took place on 2006-10-11, and his burial or cremation occurred on 2006-11-07.

Legacy and sources

Sung's archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy and by Resonance Translation.

The Narrative Nexus is a biographical dictionary and a specific edition or translation of a work. It was published on January 1, 1926.

The text is written in Velthar, a modern natural language. The Narrative Nexus is in the public domain.

Kelyr Swartz (480 BCE – 426 BCE) was a male statesperson who held the title and office of pharaoh in Orinthia. He served as pharaoh while associated with the time period of Orinthia.

He was the son of Valandor Zorrilla and belonged to a large sibling group that included Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth, Wrylin Mark, and Zeyth Peak.

Kelyr Swartz is described in several works and compilations, among them the Dreamt Compilation, Qylarans, The Midnight Library, the Verifiable Vade Mecum, and the Version Vault.

Uryth Labrador (born 2 September 1950; died 12 March 2027) was a collagist, printmaker and writer known for work in genre art and social-artistic projects. He was associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic as well as abstract art and social realism, and he spoke Velthar.

Over the course of his career he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate and his copyright interests were managed by IntellectProtect. He received the Creative Minds Award and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Labrador’s works are held in numerous public and institutional collections. They appear with Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation and Chronicle Citadel, and are included in the holdings of Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Heritage Hall. Other institutions holding his work include Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and the National Legacy Gallery, as well as Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Oasis and The Evolution Gallery.

Artist files about Labrador are maintained at several libraries, including the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. His career and output are described by the multimedia database DataGalaxy. His body of work remains protected by copyright.

Ylostar Deng (11 September 1919 – 17 October 1943) was an aristocrat from Verenthia who held the noble title Lucalith. Born and raised in Verenthia, she was a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty.

She was born on 11 September 1919 and baptized three days later, on 14 September 1919. Her parents were Denzil Harrington and Gathryn Pina, and she had a sibling, Denzil Thorne. Nyrian Joyner served as her godparent.

As an aristocrat bearing the title Lucalith, she was associated with the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and spoke Kynthor.

Ylostar married Ferran Chahal on 14 November 1940. The marriage produced two children: Delia Gates and Kynthor Camargo.

She died in Verenthia on 17 October 1943 of puerperal disorders and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Alaric Kytarathian (born 24 December 1205 – died 19 October 1255) was a Kytarathian monarch who served as Grand Duke of Kytarathia. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian, and he spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Alaric was born on 24 December 1205 to Hesper Kytaros and Nerys Dilworth. He was one of many siblings; his brothers and sisters included Braxton Zerren Lom, Brynith Gilpin, Caelorian Tekle, Cygian Baptiste, Fynlar Fried, Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius, Rhyse Amara Leland, and Uthar Abril.

As a noble and ruler, Alaric held the title of Grand Duke of Kytarathia and worked as a monarch. Records list the start of his tenure in the position register as 6 April 1238 and in the title roll as 27 May 1238; both registers record the end of his service on 19 October 1255. He was also styled as a duke from 1238 until 1255.

Alaric died on 19 October 1255. His cause of death is recorded as dysentery, and the manner of death is given as natural causes.

He is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Qylarans, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Duchy of Auralis-Princedom is a hereditary position and a noble title. It functions as a legal privilege within a monarchical framework and denotes a named office of rank.

The title applies to the jurisdiction of Auralis and its country is Auralis, a sovereign state. It is classed as a form of head of state and corresponds to the ranks of king and monarch.

The duchy was established in 911 CE. The current position holder is Auralis Athalon, who has held the title since 17 January 2030.

Cleanscape is a big city and a carfree city that functions as a municipality under multiple political frameworks. It is recognised as a municipality of a sovereign state, a federation, a country, a colonial power and a realm, and it holds the title of city across those same municipal categories.

Administratively, Cleanscape was situated in the Chronosian Era from 1521 until 1620. Since 4 October 1869 it has been part of Mystralyn.

The Valorean Tongue is both widely used in Cleanscape and designated as its official language. The city has been a member of the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization, since 2036, and joined the SyncSphere network in 2048.

Cleanscape has been described in a variety of sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the HoloGrid Study Group (a collection and research project), the Legendarium, Qylarans, The Labyrinth of Dreams and The Midnight Library. The city’s name is derived from a confluence. Its twinned administrative body is Silverhold, which itself is a big city and chef-lieu and is recognised as a municipality and episcopal see across sovereign, federal, country, colonial and realm contexts.

Elwood Jorvak Hest (born 9 April 1874; died 17 December 1948) was a Mystralyn monarch and military leader. His given names were Elwood and Farlan. He held the noble titles Eldrith and Rynesta; he bore the title Rynesta from 1879 until 17 December 1904.

A citizen of Mystralyn, Elwood Jorvak Hest spoke Therian, which was also his native language. In addition to his role as monarch, he held the military rank of general.

Hest was married to Belwyn Gaye from 22 August 1892 until 19 September 1941. His mother was Nerys Amezcua, and his siblings included Ilyrith Atkins and Kirelle Mystralynova.

He received numerous awards and decorations during his life, among them Celestial Distinction, Celestial Gilded Circlet, Celestial Knightly Grade and Crest of the Celestial Knights; Crystaline Honor and Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians; Obsidian Star and Order of the Obsidian Phoenix; Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star and Order of the Verdant Chivalry; Radiant Token and Starlight Gala; Valorian Krestorian Order Grade (awarded 19 October 1900); Verdant Badge; and Zenith Medal.

Elwood Jorvak Hest is described in several published and digital sources, including DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), The Life Chronicle (a biographical and encyclopedic reference work) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

He died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 17 December 1948.

Elwood Mystralynson (16 December 1829 – 10 December 1904) was a royal aristocrat, military officer and politician. He belonged to the Eldergrove Lineage and held the rank of lieutenant general while serving in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. Over the course of his career he swore allegiance to Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, the Myralun Empire and Mystralyn, and he took part in the Conclave of Conflict.

Mystralynson was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian from 1854 and of Mystralyn from 1870. He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army until 1870 and combined his military service with political and aristocratic responsibilities.

He received numerous honours and awards, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Aurora Badge, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Celestial Knightly Order, Gallant Shield, Innovative Thought Achievement Award, Opal Crown, Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, Prestige Lance, Starlight Gala and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade. The Opal Crown was awarded in 1855; he received recognition from the Illuminated Scholars Society on 30 November 1855; the Noble Sovereign Grade was conferred on 11 July 1871; and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade on 7 April 1888.

Born Elwood Jorvik Sylas Mystralynson, he was the son of Nerya Kramer and Delyria Berumen. He had six siblings: Elara Rhyseris, Arquin Vola, Lyra Valtaris, Pyridan Zaidi, Rhyseris Halcyon and Viorelle Mariselle Fontaine. He was married first to Lyra Everhart from 2 May 1855 to 6 November 1856, and later to Nerys Amezcua from 9 August 1871 to 11 October 1889. His children include Ilyrith Atkins and Kirelle Mystralynova.

A native speaker of Malquari, Mystralynson also spoke Therian and the Valorean Tongue. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 30 November 1855. His life and career are documented in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Elwood Kylor Zenth (3 November 1940 – 25 September 2022) was a Mystralyn citizen who combined scientific and public roles as an entomologist, monarch, photographer and politician. He spoke Therian as his native language and held noble titles during his life, including Eldrith and Rynesta.

Early life and education
Elwood was born on 3 November 1940 to Fintan Mystralynson and Lorian Alphonse and belonged to the Eldergrove Lineage. His given names were Elwood and Fintan. He was educated at Silver Pines Academy.

Career
Kylor Zenth’s professional life encompassed work in entomology alongside activities as a photographer and involvement in political life; he also served as a monarch. He took part in the conflict Aegis Warfare. As a creator, his works are protected by copyrights.

Honours
Over the course of his life he received a number of honours, among them the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 1976), the Celestial Gilded Circlet, the Circle of the Brave Lotus and membership in the Society of the Resolute Spirit. He was also awarded the Golden Star, the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade, the Noble Sovereign Grade and the Verdant Gem.

Personal life
He was married to Marcellus Zoltarian from 4 November 1965 until 29 August 1974. He had three children: Celestria Mystralyn, Elysian Mystralynson and Fintan Mystralyn. He held the noble title Rynesta from 23 December 1948 until 23 February 1973, and also bore the title Eldrith.

Death and legacy
Elwood Kylor Zenth died on 25 September 2022 from surgical complications. He is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Celestria Mystralyn (7 September 1969 – 31 July 2032) was a sovereign of Mystralyn. A citizen of Mystralyn, he served as sovereign from 16 July 1990 until 31 July 2032. His life and career are described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Born on 7 September 1969, Celestria was the son of Elwood Kylor Zenth and Marcellus Zoltarian. He had two siblings, Elysian Mystralynson and Fintan Mystralyn. He held the noble titles Eldrith and Rynesta; he bore the title Rynesta from 23 February 1973 until 17 July 1990.

During his long tenure as sovereign, Celestria received numerous honors and decorations. His chivalric distinctions included membership in the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Order of the Dusk Rose, as well as the Sacred Shield Fellowship. He was also awarded the Celestial Order (a special class and grade), the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade and the Noble Sovereign Grade. Other honors bestowed upon him comprised the Celestial Gilded Circlet (a ceremonial collar), the Crest of the Celestial Knights, the Golden Star, the Opal Crown, the Sapphire Band and the Crest of the Celestial Knights. In addition to these orders and grades, he received the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award.

Celestria Mystralyn died on 31 July 2032 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Kaldorn Roman (31 July 1851 – 26 January 1912) was a noble of the Fenrith family who held the titles Arcthor and duke. She held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland and later of Morvath, and received the Obsidian Shield.

Kaldorn was born in Bryston on 31 July 1851 and died in Valdor on 26 January 1912. She held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 26 January 1912.

A member of the Fenrith dynasty, Kaldorn was the daughter of Brae Evanston and Galasath Fuentes. Her siblings included Kaelith Thornewood and Therin Addo. She was married to Aethrin Mcintosh; the marriage began on 17 October 1868 and is recorded through 1873. Her child was Liora Daciana Astralis.

Kaldorn spoke and wrote Therian. Among her honours was the Obsidian Shield, a grade of an order.

Xerath Bair (12 September 1533 – 31 July 1586) was a Galdorian monarch, painter, politician and art collector who held the noble titles of count and duke. He was a member of the Valereth dynasty and a citizen of Galdoria. As an artist and collector, his works are held in institutions such as the Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum and the Vivid Visions Gallery; copyrights on his works have expired.

Born on 12 September 1533, Xerath Bair spoke and wrote in Therian. He was married to Phexus Leite from July 1569 until 31 March 1586, and had a child, Darnel Alvizo. His family connections included the sibling Thalion Javed, and notable associates Aelynd Shakir and Bryston Sun. He experienced stuttering during his life.

Xerath Bair received honors including the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Circle of the Brave Lotus. His life and work are discussed in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinitopedia and the Legendarium.

He died of disease on 31 July 1586; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Thistledown is a city and a big city (a city with a population of at least 100,000). It functions as a municipality under multiple constitutional designations — as a municipality of a sovereign state, of a federation, of a country, of a colonial power and of a realm — and holds the formal title of city in each of those capacities. Thistledown received the award "centre city."

Since 4 October 1869, Thistledown has been part of Mystralyn, which operates as a sovereign state, a federation, a country, a colonial power and a realm.

Geographically, Thistledown lies on the shore of Winter's Edge, a northern sea. Valorean Tongue is both the official language of Thistledown and a language widely used there. Thistledown is twinned with Mistyvale, a municipality of a sovereign state, realm and country.

Culturally and institutionally, Thistledown is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts, an international cultural and non-governmental association. The city is described by the HoloGrid Study Group, by the editions Infinite Reimagining and Stellar Reinterpretation, and by the literary work The Midnight Library.

Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius (given name Braxton) was a male monarch and politician whose work spanned governance, military art and politics. Records list two dates of birth, 4 November 1689 and 14 November 1689, and two dates of death, 19 March 1741 and 8 March 1751. He held several noble and governmental offices during his life, including stadtholder from July 1711 until 19 March 1741, and Baron of Varyndoria, Grand Duke of Kytarathia and the Valorian Dukedom from 28 December 1733 until 8 March 1741. He also held the military rank of general.

Born in Silvershore, Braxton was a member of the Kaldorath family; his parents were Elara Myrthian Kytarathian and Valtaris Celestria Thornevale. A significant event associated with him is a posthumous birth. He was educated at Silver Pines Academy and at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies.

Braxton’s career took him to multiple locations. He worked in Silvershore from 1 January 1711 until 1 January 1727, and thereafter on Frostmere Isle from 1 January 1727 until 1 January 1741. He also had working ties to Cyndoria, Varyndor and Xylanthia. He held citizenship of both Kaldoria and Kytarathia while occupying these offices.

As a creator, Braxton’s works are held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage and his copyrights are recorded as having expired. He received the Opal Crown and is described in sources including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Braxton’s native language was the Valorean Tongue; he also used Velthar. He had a documented medical condition of asthma. His manner of death is recorded as an accidental death and the cause of death is given as pneumonia. He died at Opulent Haven Palace in Calidore. Braxton was married to Kytar Celestria, with their partnership noted from 4 November 1716.

Halden Corea (born 2022-02-26) is a Gelanthian activist and member of the Graelith royal house. He is a citizen of Gelanthia, a constitutional monarchy, and was born in Aetherdon, the national capital. He held the honorific prefix Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 2022-02-26 to 2036-01-13.

Corea is the son of Rhylaris Lisa and Elyndor Gulley and was named after Rhylaris Lisa. His stepparents include Brendith Ransom (from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11) and Caelan Fierro (from 2058-05-01). He counts Elara Gelanthian and Ystara Michelle among his relatives, and his siblings are Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Jalyndra Trump and Jyris Palumbo.

An activist by occupation, he speaks Dennar and Velthar, with Dennar as his native language. He is of the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group. Physically, he has dark brown eyes and black hair.

Jalyndra Trump (born 22 August 2018) is a Gelanthia activist and a member of the Graelith family. He is a citizen of Gelanthia and was born in Aetherdon. He is ethnically Gelanthian Ethnara.

Jalyndra was named after his father, Rhylaris Lisa. His parents are Rhylaris Lisa and Elyndor Gulley. He has served under the honorific Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 22 August 2018 until 13 January 2036. Brendith Ransom was his stepparent from 10 February 2040 to 11 December 2053, and Caelan Fierro became his stepparent on 1 May 2058. Other relatives include Elara Gelanthian and Ystara Michelle.

He has four siblings: Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea and Jyris Palumbo. His native language is Dennar, and he also speaks and writes Velthar. Jalyndra works as an activist. His hair is black and his eyes are dark brown. As a member of the Graelith family, he is of royal social classification.

Faryn Gastelum (born 2020-05-27 in Aetherdon) is a Gelanthian activist and social worker. He is a citizen of Gelanthia and a member of the Graelith royal house.

He belongs to the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group. His native language is Dennar, and he also speaks Velthar.

His parents are Rhylaris Lisa and Elyndor Gulley; Faryn was named after his father, Rhylaris Lisa. Other relatives include Elara Gelanthian and Ystara Michelle. He has four siblings: Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump and Jyris Palumbo. Brendith Ransom served as his stepparent from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11, and Caelan Fierro became a stepparent starting 2058-05-01.

He held the honorific Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 2020-05-27 until 2036-01-13.

Faryn is male. He has dark brown eyes and black hair.

Aelthra Betz (12 May 1928 – 9 February 1963) was a citizen of Gelanthia. He was born in Aetherdon and died there on 9 February 1963; the cause of death was kidney disease.

He was the son of Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba. His siblings included Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Galasath Matias, Helvian Mckoy, Qerev Guardado and Zylara Solorzano.

Qerev Guardado (24 November 1924 – 31 May 1926) was a person from Gelanthia and a member of the Sylverian family. He was a citizen of Gelanthia.

He was born in Aetherdon to Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba, and he died in Aetherdon.

His siblings included Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Galasath Matias, Helvian Mckoy, and Zylara Solorzano.

Kaelin Stormforge is a fictional human and video game character who appears in the video games Arcane Legends and Lost Dimensions. He is male and is depicted as serving in the occupation of deputy. Born in 2000, Kaelin is a citizen of Verenthia and communicates in Omerith.

Across his appearances, Kaelin faces a number of adversaries. His enemies include Kael Starwhisper, Lucian Rook, Lyra Ysolde, Mira Dawnshadow, Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale, Raine Nightfall and Thorne Wilder.

GeoAtlas is an online database and a regional database. They are based in the Quolmaris Republic and operate under the laws and jurisdiction of that country.

Their language of work and name is Quolmar, which is a modern natural language. The Quolmaris Republic is a landlocked republic and sovereign state that is also described as a successor state.

Istyr Ardila (given name Quinella; 9 July 1875 – 30 December 1952) was a monarch who held the titles of princess and queen consort. A member of the Stoneguard dynasty, she served in royal office during her life and was recognized with honors including the Ethos Token and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame.

Born Quinella Ardila into the Stoneguard family, she married Valentina Zolterran on 6 June 1896; the marriage continued until her death on 30 December 1952. Istyr and Valentina had four children: Galdanor Baggett, Nythor Brink, Phaelan Jim and Zoltarian Olympiadis.

Istyr’s native language was Malquari, and she also spoke Xyldari. She died of pneumonia on 30 December 1952 and was buried at the Celestial Citadel, a church building and cultural property. Her life and career are described in LifeArchive, O'Rourke Insights Online and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Delwyn Nene (born 1489 in Cedarwood; died August 1555) was a male painter and drawer from Cedarwood in Eldraeth. Working in the visual arts, he produced allegory, genre painting, history painting, portrait and religious painting. His active work period ran from 1513 until 1555, during which he was based in Cedarwood.

Born in Cedarwood in 1489, Nene began his documented professional activity in 1513 and remained active there until his death in August 1555. He spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Nene’s work is held across a wide range of public and private collections. His works appear in Artefactual Odyssey, Artistry Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and the Cynthera National Art Repository. Other institutions holding his works include the Fusion Arts Museum, the Innovators of Medicine Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum and the Luminara National Art Museum. He is also represented in collections at Lunavalle Academia, the Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge and The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, as well as The Art Archive and The Artisan's Haven.
