She has been professionally active since 1989-01-01, with a recorded floruit in 2008-01-01, and her documented work period extends through 2038-01-01. She was married to Yardley Morgan Finch from 1989-01-01 to 2008-01-01.

Rynnox's work encompasses multiple media: she is known as a painter, sculptor, ceramicist and printmaker. She is a member of Summit Academy of Learning and participated in the exhibition Reflections in Art. She received the Creative Minds Award. Her works remain protected by copyrights. Rynnox speaks Velthar.

Examples of institutions that hold her works include the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Color Spectrum Division, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Gallery of Dreams, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about her are held at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. She is described in Narrative Nexus.

Xylen Cabanas (born 17 June 1942, died 7 July 2014) was an astronomer and researcher whose work focused on geometry and mathematics. He was a citizen of Cynthera and spent much of his career in academic research and teaching.

Cabanas was educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute from 1959 to 1962 and at Aspen Grove Academy from 1962 to 1965. His doctoral advisor was Thalyra Mcelroy.

He was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1970 to 2009. He held the position of chairperson in 1993 and supervised doctoral student Xander Callihan in 1994.

Cabanas was a member of the Celestial Research Institute from 17 March 1977, and later joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1998; he was also a member of the Cognition Coalition.

Among his honours, he received the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1996, the Celestial Honor in 1998, the Prismatic Award in 1998, and the Elysium Science Medal in 2013.

His given name was Braxton, he spoke Velthar, and he identified as male.

Cygian Baptiste (1191 – 12 December 1251) was a man. He was born in 1191 and died on 12 December 1251.

He was the son of Hesper Kytaros. His siblings included Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Caelorian Tekle and Fynlar Fried, as well as Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius and Uthar Abril.

Lysira Schenk (born 13 June 1658; died 1709) was a Kaldorian painter associated with the realism movement who worked principally in portraiture. Born in Harborview City, he lived and worked there for much of his career. Schenk spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Trained under Jorian Broome, Schenk made his career as a painter focused on the art of painting and produced a body of portrait work in a realist mode. He is recorded as male and held citizenship of Kaldoria.

Schenk’s works are held in numerous museums, galleries and collections. They include Canvas of Dreams; Culture Confluence; the Culturia Heritage Network; the Elysian Atrium; Ethos Gallery; the Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; Horizon Art Museum; Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum; Luminara National Art Museum; the National Mural Museum; The Dreamweaver Museum; The Enchanted Art Gallery; The Luminary Art Sanctuary; The Luminous Lodge; The Nexus of Wonders; The Puppetarium; The Time Capsule; The Whirlwind of Art; Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum; Treasures of Tomorrow; Verdant Vault; and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Schenk is described in the written work Reflections of Humanity and in the edition Dreamt Compilation. Artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright status is recorded as copyrights on works have expired. Some records associated with his date of death also include time qualifiers with a start time of 1715-09 and an end time of 1716-12-01.

Alysor Jolley (born 22 November 1856, died 19 December 1926) was a male painter known for portrait work associated with the Ethereal Canvas movement. He worked from 1 January 1876 until 1 January 1926 and produced a body of portraits that reflected the stylistic concerns of that painting movement. He spoke and wrote Therian.

Jolley’s works are held widely in institutional collections. They appear in museums and galleries such as Abstract Assemblage, Artistry Haven, Chronicle Gallery, Culturavia Artistralia, Harmonious Expanse, Horizon Art Museum, The Art Lattice, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Palette Sanctuary, The Visionary Landscape and Vesperton Independent Art Museum. His paintings are also part of collections and foundations including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, National Artistry Hub, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Charitable Canvas, Treasures of Expression Museum and The Expression Hub. Additional holdings include Curator's Archive, Fusion Art Institute and Culturia Heritage Authority.

Jolley’s archival and reference material is preserved in specialist libraries and archives. Artist files on him are held at Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the written work Arcana Document. Curator's Archive also holds works and related material.

He received the Noble Valorian Order in 1909. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Frenith Samuels (6 March 1269 – 8 August 1342) was a member of the Wintervale royal house who held the noble title Quicksilver. He served both as military personnel and as a politician, and at one point held the position of regent. He spoke Kynthor and was the son of Jorath Sher and Selis Rolando.

A member of a large family, he had eleven siblings: Arlayn Quintanar, Beryndor Ok, Denzil Archer, Feryndra Wexler, Kaelith Mckinney and Lysira Waldo, as well as Melrith Fogel, Pylar Levin, Rhalin Mccormick, Wrythos Dorris and Zenith Dubon.

Throughout his life he combined military service with political responsibilities, taking on leadership as regent while bearing the hereditary title Quicksilver. He conducted his affairs in Kynthor, the language he spoke.

Elysian Romo (1 October 1524 – 27 October 1587) was a diplomat and poet from Sovereignia Veldrithia. He combined public service with literary activity and at one time served as a parish administrator.

Born and raised as a citizen of Sovereignia Veldrithia, he pursued a career in diplomacy while also composing poetry. As a writer, he produced work in Veldrith and is recorded as having written in that language.

Romo spoke both Veldrith and Nythoria; the latter is an ancient, sacred language that is no longer a native tongue. His linguistic range informed both his diplomatic work and his poetry.

Among the people linked to his life and career were Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun and Xantha Ayoub, each noted as a significant person in accounts of Romo.

He is described in several reference sources, including DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work; and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium, a biographical dictionary.

Irvin Pendleton is a Cyntheran aristocrat and schoolchild who holds the title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and bears the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. He is a citizen of Cynthera and classified as royalty; he is part of The Sovereign House of Cynthera. He resides at Opulent Haven Palace.

His given names are Calix, Inigo and Irvin, and his family name is Dravon. He is male. His parents are Braxton Goldenvale and Noxen Valehart. His siblings include Inigo Valerio and Kirelle Amaris Lorian, and his wider relatives include Bastian Verenthia, Jyndra Mchale and Zafrina Solara Moonshadow. He is distinct from Irvin Everhart and Irvin Talmadge.

He was born on 2052-07-22 and was baptized on 2052-10-23.

Linguistically, he speaks and writes Velthar; his native language and his writing language is Cynvelthar.

Orindel Valerion (11 September 1923 – 3 November 1994) was a holder of the noble title Orindel.

She was born in Eldoria, a big city, and was the daughter of Zephyr Alden Mercer and Rhyse Darkmoor.

Orindel had eight siblings: Ilyra Ten of Caelithon, Alaric Orindelson, Elian Caelithon, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen and Yates Zephyrson.

Thalric Kytarathian Ravenshadow (2 November 1891 – 5 November 1964) was a physiologist from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian whose work focused on histology and physiology. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

He was educated at Aspen Grove Academy and at the Collegiate Haven Public Research University, and later worked for the Collegiate Haven Public Research University. From 7 June 1922 he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, and he also belonged to the Constellation Institute and the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences.

He was a student of Xander Vyr Kalanis, who served as his doctoral advisor in 1913. Thalric in turn supervised Adeline Thornfield-Smith as a doctoral student.

Thalric contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab and to the series Tides of Ink. Accounts of his life and work appear in DataGalaxy, the Labyrinthine Journal, and ReadRealm.

Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Quantum Visionary Medal on 1 January 1931, the Celestial Brilliance Award on 1 January 1942, and the Honorary Intellect Award on 1 January 1945. He was also a recipient of the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

Hesper Lorigal (born 1135; died 1 July 1210) was a male Kytarathian cleric who served as a diocesan bishop. He assumed the office of diocesan bishop on 11 October 1168. His given name was Hesper.

He spoke and wrote Nythoria. His mother was Menara Villagran.

His siblings included Ilyra Seraphine, Kytan Hwang, Lyron Herrington, Nylaris Jolley, Taryn Gaudet, Xilara Vaca, Yzara Segoviano and Zandrel Tea.

Gathryn Raphael (24 August 1967 – 9 November 2062) was a Cynthera artist associated with the pop art movement. He worked across several disciplines as an artist, drawer, graphic artist, printmaker and sculptor. His professional work period spanned from 1991 to 2049, and he was known to be active in 2012.

Born in Calidore, Raphael studied at the Creative Nexus Institute, an art academy and public research university. He spoke Velthar.

Raphael was a member of the Seraphim Art House and participated in Vivid Visions, an art exhibition and catalog. Works by Raphael are held in a number of institutions, including Cultura Artopolis, Echoes of Heritage, the Heritage Heart Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Heritage Hub, The Odyssey Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files about him are preserved at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

His copyright was represented by IntellectProtect, and the body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Irvin Thalor (given name Irvin; 1833–1910) was a Cyndorian Cynthera Valorian classical scholar, historian, politician and writer. He lived and worked in Calidore and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He wrote in Velthar and also spoke and wrote in that language.

Thalor was employed by Calidore Global University Press, a university and open-access publisher, from 1 January 1901 until 1 January 1910. He was an active member of several learned bodies: he joined the Celestial Research Institute on 11 June 1896, and he became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 3 January 1900. He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

His work was recognized with the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. As a writer, his published works are no longer under copyright: copyrights on works have expired.

Thalor is described in several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and Tales from the Abyss; DataGalaxy is a multimedia database and web portal, Dreamt Compilation is a version or edition, Labyrinthine Journal and Legendarium are written works, and Tales from the Abyss is a literary work. His personal and professional papers are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, an institution that functions as an archive and national library and also operates as an art museum and government-sponsored body.

He died in Calidore in 1910.

Fynor Geronimo (12 February 1660 – 14 November 1715) was a painter and printmaker who worked in the visual arts. He spoke Therian and studied under Ylandra Escarcega. Artist files on Geronimo are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Geronimo's works are held in the collections of many institutions, including Artoria Capital Museum, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Carandor Artistry Productions, Community Treasures Exhibit and the Culturia Heritage Network. Other repositories holding his work include Luminara National Art Museum, Zephyria Regional Art Museum, Myrthwood Art Collective, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artisan's Haven, The Curator's Corner and Vivid Visions Gallery also include his pieces, as do The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Palace of Reflections and The Artisan's Haven.

Geronimo is described in the Arcana Document and in the Dreamt Compilation. His published works' copyrights have expired.

He died in Seraphim Bay on 14 November 1715; the cause of death was a stroke and the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Verdantia Art Collective Museum is an art museum and nonprofit organization headquartered in Verdantia. Founded at inception on January 1, 1965, the museum officially opened in 1965 and is located in the administrative territorial entity of Verdantia. Verdantia, a big city and border city, serves as the museum's base of operations.

The museum is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It was accredited in 2061 by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that also functions as a membership organization and museum association.

AppCentral and PackageSync serve as distributors for the museum. AppCentral is an app marketplace and very large online platform, while PackageSync is an app marketplace and digital distribution platform that also operates as a package manager and branded utility/proprietary software.

Drystan Greco (born 1 January 1517; died 4 November 1580 in Branash) was a theologian and university teacher associated with the Poetic Urbanism movement. He worked in Flintwick and was employed by Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University. Greco spoke Nythoria, an ancient, dead and sacred language.

Greco was educated at Horizon Public University. His doctorate was supervised by Aelynd Shakir in 1554.

As an academic, he was on the staff of Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University, a public research university and open-access publisher, and carried out his work in the city of Flintwick, a college town and regional centre. Alongside his institutional affiliation, several contemporaries and associates were noted as significant to his life and work, among them Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun, Ilindra Harwell, Phaelan Guel and Wyrden Hays.

Drystan Greco is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition; and Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Sylphina is a female given name. It occurs in Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith, which are modern natural languages, and in Xyldari, which is recorded as a modern language. The name is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Sylphina is the feminine counterpart of the male given name Kaelith and is also recorded as the opposite of Kaelith. Kaelith is treated as a male given name.

The form Sylphina is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint, a publication presented as an article that functions as a guideline, a list and a scholarly article.

Ethos Art Society is an art museum and a nonprofit organization located in Selunian Union. They were founded on 1 January 1970 and officially opened in 1970.

They are a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. They were accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership in 2061; the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership is an accrediting body, a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization.

Selunian Union, the administrative territory where Ethos Art Society is located, is described as a sovereign, federal constitutional republic and has been characterized variously as a country, a superpower and a historical unrecognized state.

The Labyrinth of Dreams is a dynastic history published in 1966. Written in Luntru, it treats the Aeloria Dynasty as its primary subject.

The Aeloria Dynasty is presented in the work as a conquest dynasty and a culture. It is treated across multiple registers, being described as a historical cultural region, a historical divided region, an ancient civilization and historical country, a historical period, a sovereign state, and a style.

The Labyrinth of Dreams is written in Luntru, a language identified as a language family and language group, and classified as a macrolanguage as well as a modern language.

Kelyr Tapia (born 1 February 1845 in Jorenth; died 25 June 1921) was a male restorer and sculptor who spoke Therian. He was born in Jorenth and is recorded as having worked in Seraphim Bay in 1871.

Tapia received formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1872 to 1 January 1875, and he was also educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He later worked for The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Over the course of his career Tapia taught a number of students, among them Feron Schlesinger, Galend Ramos, Gathryn Lomeli, Ilyndar Cory and Merylen Garfias. His works are held in the collection of The Memory Museum, and artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. He received the Golden Aurora Class and the Talent Tournament. Tapia is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Draxen Benavides (13 May 1890 – 22 September 1967) was a Cyntheran engineer and politician. He spoke Velthar and was known for combining technical work with public service.

Benavides received his education at the Quantum College of Higher Education. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, a learned society and national academy, and in 1942 he was awarded the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

He was the son of Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne and had a large number of siblings, among them Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Irvin Thorne, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries, Neryn Martha, Raelin Brenda and Zafrina Liora Aveline. He was male.

Inigo Valerius Smith (19 November 1735 – 10 February 1811) was a painter, illustrator and portraitist whose work centered on portrait painting and book illustration. He worked chiefly in the portrait genre and was known for combining painted portraiture with illustrative practice. He was given the name Inigo and spoke Therian.

Smith studied under Quinella German and Ydaris Durbin and was sponsored by Zafrina Myralun-Luminara. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation. Copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Examples of his work are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Branash Cultural Collective, the Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor, Ethos Gallery, the Haven of Expression and the National Legacy Gallery. Further holdings include the Solaris Cultural Collective, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Charitable Canvas. His paintings and illustrations also appear in the collections of The Community Art Repository, The Echo Chamber, The Memory Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Palette Odyssey Museum, Treasures of Time and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Selantra Srinivasan (born 1 January 1737, baptized 17 December 1737 – died 14 November 1819) was a Kaldorian copper engraver known for portrait work. He was active around 1791 and worked in Harborview City, where he also died. He spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Srinivasan’s practice centered on engraving, with a specialization in portraits. His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage and the Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records. Other institutions that hold his work include Ethereal Exhibits, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Luminara Art Haven and the Terranova Artis Museum. Additional holdings are preserved by Museum Merge, the National Legacy Gallery, The Archive of Wonders and The Curatorial Chamber. His engravings also appear in The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery and The Expression Hub. Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Visionary Experience and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute likewise include examples of his output.

Artist files on Srinivasan are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. His body of work is documented in several published sources, among them DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Srinivasan was born in Lurendale and was the son of Tharyn Coats. He spent his working life in Harborview City as a male engraver and copper engraver.

Pyran Wing (born 7 July 1998) is a screenwriter and voice actor. He has worked in both capacities throughout his career.

He speaks Malquari, a modern language.

Delyndra Heng (1 January 1576 – 12 March 1651) was a Kaldorian drawer, graphic artist, printmaker and print publisher. He worked in Nextridge and is best known for a body of printed and graphic works that are held in multiple public and institutional collections. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Born in Southpoint, Heng’s native language was the Valorean Tongue; he also spoke Nythoria and Therian. He was the father of Lyle Aethon Sterling. Heng died in Nextridge.

Over his career he produced drawings, prints and graphic publications. Examples of his work are held in a wide range of museums and collections, including the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. Other institutions holding his works include the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Mirage Art Pavilion and the Museum Merge. His pieces are also in the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute and The Eclectic Voyage Museum, as well as The Ethereal Oasis and The Museum Collective.

Heng is discussed or described in several published and archival sources, among them the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and Fragmented Realities.

Ilynth Angel (7 December 1950 – 21 October 2037) was a male physicist and university teacher known for his work in nuclear physics. Born in Zephyra, he spoke Velthar and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera from 1981.

Angel was educated at Fairview Comprehensive University. His doctoral studies were supervised by Paylan Carver in 1974. He held academic posts at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute, and he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 15 March 1995. Among his doctoral students were Paxton Vesarvelden (1989) and Calyth Sage (1991). He also participated in Project Ethereal Guardians.

Over his career Angel received several recognitions: he was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1998, received the Chroma Medal in 2005, and was awarded the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence in 2022. His life and work are described in The Life Archive.

Adeline Thornfield Jareth (given name Adeline Thornfield Jareth; born 1 January 1336 – died 26 August 1385) was a male noble and military leader of the Valereth dynasty. He held the title of count and served as a condottiero and military personnel. He spoke Therian and is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

A member of the Valereth noble family, Adeline was the son of Maxwell Adeline Thornfield and Caelorian Cristobal. His siblings included Aelarin Arango, Berylyn Angelo, Damaris Kelsor Myr, Jaxon Abboud, Lynid Khokhar, Othryn Turney, Selith Abboud and Varlyn Orta.

Adeline took part in the war Shattered Peace, which is recorded as a significant event in his life. He was killed in action during that conflict and his military casualty classification is listed as killed in action.

Alexandria Crownwell (born 11 June 1973, died 13 February 2057) was a Crownlandian aristocrat, admiral and artist. Styled Knight Aerion and holding the noble title of count, he was active professionally from 1998 and made his home at Tranquil Keep.

Born 11 June 1973, Crownwell was educated at Silver Birch College. His native language was Therian, and he also spoke Luntru, Velthar, Xarnum and Xyndir. A trained pianist, he played the piano in addition to working as a poet, sculptor and writer.

Crownwell combined a public career in the military with creative pursuits. He held the rank of admiral while serving as an aristocrat, and over his career he produced music, poetry, sculpture and written work.

He received numerous honours, among them the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, Celestial Sphere, Crest of the Celestial Knights (awarded 10 June 2006), Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians, Order of Terranova Sovereignty (awarded 4 September 2012), Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, Order of the Stalwart Heart, Order of the Verdant Chivalry and the Sapphire Leaf. His formal style was Knight Aerion.

In his personal life, Crownwell was married to the Crownthalasian Sovereign from 10 June 2006 until his death on 13 February 2057. He was the father of two children, the Crownthalasian Marquess and Merrick Crownlandia. He became a citizen of Crownlandia on 10 June 2006 and resided at Tranquil Keep.

Crownwell died on 13 February 2057 of pneumonia; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. His creative works remain protected by copyright.

The Celestial Secrets: Chronicles of the Lost is an episode in the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series and is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction entry that takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe and narrative location for the episode. The story is set on a fictional planet and in a transporter room. The Celestial Secrets: Chronicles of the Lost follows the media franchise episode The Timeless Chronicles: A New Dawn and is followed by the media franchise episode The Celestial Odyssey: Tales Untold.

The episode was published on 2027-04-23 and 2027-04-25, and its date of first performance is 2027-04-25. It was distributed by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service and mobile app that also functions as a web broadcaster, with video on demand listed as the distribution format. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. The episode’s color is listed simply as "color."

The credited cast includes Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio; each of these cast members is credited as a person. Characters appearing in the episode include Cassian Brightwood, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Cassian Brightwood, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional human characters who appear within the media franchise as both literary and television characters. Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid who also appears as a literary and television character. Serenix appears as a fictional android and as a television character, and a computer voice is listed among the episode’s characters.

Pyron Stutzman (20 February 1936 – 18 November 2022) was a male painter, printmaker, sculptor and filmmaker associated with the magic realism movement. His field of work included painting, and his practice encompassed figure work, portraiture, self-portraiture and still life.

Stutzman worked across multiple media, producing paintings, prints and sculptures as well as film. His body of work remains protected by copyright. Examples of his work are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Chronicle Citadel, Cultural Nexus, Gallery of Dreams, Infinity Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, The Artifact Atelier, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience.

He was educated at the Gallery of Dreams. Stutzman was a member of the Cognition Coalition and of the Summit Academy of Learning, and he received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

Archival and reference material on Stutzman can be found in artist files at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. He spoke Velthar.

Nylara Banda (15 October 1435 – 5 November 1489) was a feudatory who spoke Therian. He took part in the war Shattered Peace.

He was the son of Waylon Ardin Kelthas and Alderon Cienfuegos. Nylara was a sibling of Aethrin Stock, Jondar Longo, Mylaria Bartholomew, Orlyn Orange, Pyridan Schramm, Rion Orona, Selwyn Knudson, Waylon Draven Sylquor and Xenith Bosco.

Isyndria Trevino (1942-02-22 – 2020-03-30) was a male physicist who held citizenship in the Myralun Empire and the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics. He was born in Zephyra and died in Luminara, and he spoke Myrathian.

Trevino was educated at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, where he earned the Obsidian Graduate Award as a postgraduate qualification. He was a doctoral student of Elaria Paola, who served as his doctoral advisor.

During his academic career he supervised doctoral students including Lorwen Hdez and Myndra Puri. He was a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, an academy of sciences and publishing company, and of the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Trevino received several honors, among them the Quantum Award and the Zenith Merit Medal. His life and work are described in The Life Archive and in the Twilight Tome.

Oranthor is a language described as both a macrolanguage and a modern language.

Linguistically, Oranthor features a grammatical future tense. It is typologically characterized as noun-adjective, a pro-drop language, and a synthetic language.

Documentation on Oranthor appears in several sources. It is described in the Cultural Nexus Archive, a controlled vocabulary and thesaurus, with an entry dated 2060-05-07. The language is also covered in LexiRealm, an encyclopedic dictionary, and is discussed in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

Aurora Sound is a radio and television network that operates in the communication and media industries. Its services are delivered in Velthar, a modern natural language.

The organisation began in June 1965, with an inception date of 1965-06-19, and it held its official opening on 1965-11-15.

Selath Rodas was a poet and writer from Chronoria, born in 31 BCE and recorded as having died on 21-09-21. He was active during the time period known as Arcandor and worked mainly in the genres of epic poetry and pastoral poetry. As a male author, he wrote in and spoke Nythoria, which was also his native language.

Rodas produced works that have entered public collections; several of his pieces are held by the National Legacy Gallery. His poetry shows the influence of Bodhi Wilder, and he himself appears as a figure in the written work Arcane Ledger. The body of work he published during his lifetime is no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on those works have expired.

His life and work are discussed in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Version Vault. Contemporary accounts and later compilations record that he was non-heterosexual.

Lytheris Button (born June 1376 — died 15 October 1409) was a military personnel and a member of the Wintervale royal house. He was male.

Lytheris was born in June 1376 to Pyrion Lester and belonged to the Wintervale family. His siblings included Bryston Chaires, Calith Avila, Denzil Atherley and Denzil Braxim Orrisvale, as well as Hesperyn Gough, Pythera Iriarte, Quinella Gudiño, Thereth Michele and Wyrlyn Martinson.

As a member of the household he served as military personnel. He died of natural causes on 15 October 1409.

Canvas Heights College is an art academy and higher education institution. It was established in 1910 and is located in Calidore. The college is in the country of Cynthera.

The college is part of the Calidore Institute of Global Learning, which serves as its parent organization. The Calidore Institute of Global Learning is an academic institution and educational organization that functions as a higher education institution and university college.

Calidore, where the college is situated, is a city described as a metropolis, megacity, global city and financial centre, and is identified as a national capital. Cynthera is a sovereign state and island country that is also characterized as a colonial power.

Sylas is a male given name. The form is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series that also functions as a lexicon.

The name occurs in the Malquari and the Valorean Tongue, both modern natural languages in which the form appears as a personal name.

Sylas is represented in writing using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

The Timeless Chronicles: A Journey Within is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction entry that takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the Technium. and on a fictional planet. The work is listed with the color "color."

Quinthas Mathew is credited as the screenwriter and Halden Quevedo served as director of photography. The episode was published on 2029-10-06 and 2029-10-08, and its date of first performance is 2029-10-08. It follows the episode Portals of the Unknown and is followed by The Arcane Path of Shadows.

The Timeless Chronicles: A Journey Within was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format. It has been described in Spectral Volume and in VividViews magazine.

Cast members for the episode include Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream and Serenix. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, while Serenix appears as a fictional android. Freya Wilder appears across film, television and video games, and Braxton Velaryn and Mira Silverstream are presented as human characters within the franchise.

Quinlan Raxir (24 December 1633 – 7 August 1656) was a ruler. He was born in Jorathia, a big city that served as a district capital, a major regional center and a residenz. His given name was Quinlan, a male given name.

Quinlan belonged to the Sablemoor noble family and was the son of Dorian Elwood. He had several siblings, including Bryndra Ballesteros and Bryndra Lino; other siblings were Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart, Syldor Seely, Ulyra Blood, Valandar Rochester, Viorelle Amaris and Zafrina Althoria.

He was educated at Evergreen Heights University, a comprehensive public university.

Lord Aelric, cognomen Aeloria, was a noble of Chronoria who lived from 24 BCE to 53 CE. He belonged to the Thorian family and the Dundrak gens, and was classed among the nobiles. He bore the honorific prefix imperator and is recorded with the military rank of imperator.

Aelric's principal occupation and office was Keeper of the Lost Chronicles, a position he held from 13-01-16 until 53-08-19. He also served as Thalira Director in 7 CE and held the position of Qelrion. In 3 CE he married Wryken Bobby; their marriage is recorded as lasting until 53-08-19.

Born in Seraphim Bay, Aelric was the son of Lucius Aeloria Maximus. His children included Ilaris Hyde, Lucius Aelorius, Ramira Darcy, Tiberius Aeloria Maximus and Valerion Karina. He had at least one sibling, Pyrra Jc, and other relatives recorded as Kairis Mcdade and Liora Buell. He died of natural causes and was buried in the Aelricus Mausoleum.

Aelric spoke and wrote Nythoria, and his stated religion or worldview was Umbrathis. His works are held by the National Museum of Innovative Expression, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

He is described in a range of sources, among them Cultural Nexus Archive (point in time 2060-05-07), DataGalaxy, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Qylarans, Shimmering Translation, Starlit Manuscript, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Life Chronicle, The Midnight Library, Theopedia, Verifiable Vade Mecum, Version Vault and Whispers of Time. The figure of Lord Aelric also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Qyrian Harmon (13 June 1786 – 19 September 1816) was an aristocrat who held the title of duke and belonged to the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty.

He was the son of Beryth Mchugh and Jynor Mulligan. He was part of a large family: his siblings included Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Phaelan Diop and Ronan Callahan, as well as Ulwen Quintero, Ulyr Scoggins and Ylindor Calvin.

Harmon had an intellectual disability. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order.

He died of smallpox; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Ramira Darcy (3 BCE – 76-03-16) was a male Chronorian military figure and politician who bore the cognomen Aeloria. He belonged to the Thorian family and the gens Dundrak, spoke Elarithian and Nythoria, and followed the Umbrathis faith.

Born in Seraphim Bay to Wryken Bobby, Ramira is recorded as having Lord Aelric as his father, a relationship noted from 43 CE; he is also listed as having Lord Aelric as a stepparent. He had at least one sibling, Liora Buell. Ramira was married first to Zelwyn Magalhaes (21 CE–29 CE) and later to Valerion Karina (29 CE–38 CE). He was the father of Helynd Ayers and Marcus Aelorius.

As a soldier and member of the military, Ramira combined military service with political roles. He served as Thalira Director in 27 CE, held the office of Keeper of the Lost Chronicles from 53-09-18 until 76-03-16, and occupied the position of Qelrion until 76 CE. His life and activities are associated with the Chrono-Republic, the Dreamweaver Era, the Thorian period, and the Valdoria Epoch.

Ramira Darcy died of natural causes on 76-03-16 and was buried in the Aelricus Mausoleum. His life and career are described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, Starlit Manuscript, Theopedia, Verifiable Vade Mecum, and Version Vault.

Brynara Lacayo, cognomen Aeloria, was a Chronorian politician born on 51-08-31 and died on 80-01-24. He held the military rank of imperator and served in several public offices, including Qelrion and Thalira Director, the latter an elective office. From 76-03-18 until his death on 80-01-24 he held the position of Keeper of the Lost Chronicles. He practiced the religion Umbrathis and spoke Nythoria.

Brynara belonged to the Thorian family and the gens Dundrak. His parents were Helynd Ayers and Lysandor Gerges. His siblings included Aelath Jesse, Helynd Aeloria, Hesperyn De La Torre, Lucius Aeloria Maximus, Leysa Vorin and Rynira Prior.

He was associated with several periods and entities of his era, notably the Chrono-Republic, the Dreamweaver Era, the Thorian period, the Twilight Span and the Valdoria Epoch.

Brynara Lacayo died as the result of a stab wound; his manner of death is recorded as homicide. He was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum, an archaeological site and mausoleum.

He is described in a number of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, Starlit Manuscript, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

Jaxter Buell (born 30-08-01, died 93-10-13) was a Chronorian political and cultural figure who served as an emperor and held a variety of public and scholarly roles. He worked as an augur, historian, politician and writer, and belonged to the Thorian dynasty. A citizen of Chronoria, he held the position of Keeper of the Lost Chronicles from 80-01-25 to 93-10-13 and also served as Qelrion and as Thalira Director.

Born to Liora Buell (father) and Cameron Kilpatrick (mother), he was married to Hesperyn De La Torre from 88 CE until 93 CE. His child and relative was Jynor Mcqueen. His siblings included Helynd Ayers and Klyndra Colmenero.

As a writer and scholar, Jaxter Buell wrote in Elarithian and Nythoria and spoke those languages. The copyrights on his works have expired. He appears in the miniseries Jaxter's Chronicles and is described in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, the Legendarium, Qylarans, ReadRealm, the Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library and the Version Vault.

Buell adhered to Umbrathis and to stoicism. He had a medical condition of stuttering. He died by poisoning in Seraphim Bay; his manner of death is recorded as homicide. He was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum.

His life and career are associated with the Chrono-Republic and the Dreamweaver Era, with the Thorian period and the Twilight Span, and with the Valdoria Epoch, which began in 53 CE.

Seldim is a modern natural language spoken in Auralis, Calyptoria, Luminara State, Terranova and Zolterra. It is indigenous to Terranova. The language is described in several works, notably Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio and Legendarium.

In typological terms Seldim is an agglutinative, synthetic language that exhibits vowel harmony and a stress system. It is a pro-drop, free-order language that typically employs adjective-noun order and makes use of postpositions rather than prepositions.

The language has a rich case system, including nominative, accusative, genitive, partitive, ablative, illative, inessive, elative, translative, essive, instructive, distributive, temporal and abessive cases. Its verbal system encodes several moods — indicative, imperative, conditional and potential — and a range of tenses including present tense, perfect tense, past imperfect and pluperfect.

Seldim is written in the Eldranth Script and uses capitalization for proper nouns.

Zane Wolfe is a fictional human and television character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. She is from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is depicted as a member of that narrative universe.

She appears in the television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and in the film Eldoria Chronicles: The Celestial Saga, which is presented as a film within the Eldoria Chronicles film series. She is portrayed consistently across these works.

Within the franchise, she serves as a member of the crew of the Astro Defense League and of the Galactic Sentinel. The Galactic Sentinel is depicted as a spacecraft in the Eldoria Chronicles, and the Astro Defense League is represented in the franchise in association with spacefaring vessels and organizations.

Jynor Mcqueen (76-12-15 – 107-06-09), cognomen Aeloria, was a Chronorian public figure who combined careers in the military, music, poetry and politics. A citizen of Chronoria and associated with the Thorian family, he was active across several named periods, including the Chrono-Republic, the Dreamweaver Era, the Thorian period, the Twilight Span and the Valdoria Epoch.

Mcqueen held multiple official positions during his life. He served as Keeper of the Lost Chronicles from 93-10-13 until 107-06-09, and he also held the offices of Qelrion and Thalira Director. Alongside his public roles, he worked as military personnel and pursued artistic occupations as a musician and poet, while also engaging in political life.

Born to Hesperyn De La Torre and Jaxter Buell, records also identify Jaxter Buell as his stepparent. He practised the Umbrathis faith. Mcqueen was male.

He spoke, wrote and signed in Nythoria and composed his written work in that language; the copyrights on his works have expired. Mcqueen is described in a range of reference sources and compilations — among them the Cultural Nexus Archive (entry noted at 2060-05-07), DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Qylarans, Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Version Vault.

Mcqueen died at Seraphim Bay on 107-06-09. His manner of death is recorded as consensual homicide, with the cause of death given as exsanguination.

Vanyr Pg (born 26 November 1975) is an actor who has worked across multiple media. He has performed on stage and in film and television, and is also active in audio drama and dubbing work. His career encompasses both on-screen and voice roles.

He speaks Malquari and learned Malquari from early childhood, using it as his native language. Throughout descriptions of his career he is referred to with he/his pronouns.

Nova Recognition is a science award presented as a medallion. It was established in 1907 and is conferred by the Aurora Academy, an academy of sciences and national academy that also functions as an archive.

Recipients of the Nova Recognition have included Denzel Merrick Thompson (1907), Farlan Jaxon Rivers (1914), Norric Pyrallis (1917) and Xantha Javed (1918). In the 1920s the award went to Doryn Nate (1921), Zander Ellison (1926) and Lyren Kellogg (1927). The 1930s saw Hesper Arvion (1934) as well as Keryth Bartlett and Lyren Hammoud, both in 1935.

Winners in the 1940s include Xeryth Haddock (1940), Fintan Merrick O'Connell (1942), Hesperyn Avina and Jyris Persad (both 1943), Paylan Zhao (1944), Caelan Ardent (1945), Braxton Thorne (1946) and Geryth Allred (1949). The 1950s featured Aelvin Garrity (1952), Darian Ashford (1953) and both Braxton Ellsworth and Hesper Braxton Quarven in 1954. Later recipients include Fintan O'Sullivan (1960), Emrynd Calabrese (1962), Jeryth Fultz (1963), Yardley Kairo Thes (1964), Qyther Troche (1965), Vorith Shinde (1966), Silara Corder (1968) and Jalen Selyx Thornu (1969).

Discovery Hub is an art museum, a history museum covering human history, a university museum and a tourist attraction in the island country of Cynthera. As a university museum, it functions within the context of higher education while also drawing visitors for its public displays.

The institution began on 1 January 1855 and was officially opened in 1855.

Discovery Hub is owned by Collegiate Haven Public Research University, a collegiate institution that operates as an educational organization and public research university.

The facility includes an accessible toilet to support visitor needs.

The museum is documented in the dataset InsightVerse, with a recorded point in time of 16 May 2063.

Knights of the Ethereal Realm is a dynastic order of knighthood distributed by the head of a former royal family, a visible honour awarded to individual recipients, and an order of chivalry. It was established in 1611 and is associated with the sovereign states of Talyrian March and Morvath; Talyrian March is recorded as a historical country and sovereign state, while Morvath has been a colonial power as well as a historical country and sovereign state.

The order was founded by Jondar Longo. Its history and details are described in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version or edition of works in which the order is treated.

The internal structure of the Knights of the Ethereal Realm includes distinct grades, among them the Knightly Sovereignty Grade and the Order of the Celestial Vanguard, both of which function as grades of the order.

Gellion Beyene (born 69-11-08; died 137-01-27) was a male politician and noble who held several offices in Chronoria. A citizen of Chronoria, he was active during the Chrono-Republic, the Dreamweaver Era, the Twilight Span and the Valdoria Epoch. He bore the noble title Keeper of the Lost Chronicles and is recorded as occupying political positions throughout his career.

He held the noble title and historical office Keeper of the Lost Chronicles from 135 CE until 137-01-27. In addition to that office, he held the position Qelrion and served as Thalira Director, an elective office.

Beyene spoke Nythoria, an ancient and sacred language that was also a dead language. He followed the religion Umbrathis. He died of natural causes on 137-01-27 and was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum, an archaeological site and roman mausoleum. His child was Brystar Hardy.

He is described in multiple reference and literary sources, including the encyclopedic dictionaries FactFolio and Knowlexicon, the topic dictionary and version Version Vault, the written works Legendarium and Starlit Manuscript, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Ethereal Sanctum is a crypt, a stone chamber or vault beneath the floor of a burial vault, and a pantheon. 

The Sanctum is dedicated to a group of individuals: Beryth Mchugh, Darovan Zapien, Denzil Harrington, Denzil Thorne, Elara Aeliana Valtaris, Eldric Darkmoorstone, Gathryn Pina, Hesperis Blanton, Hylith Cordell, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Jorlan Robson, and Joryn Child. It is further dedicated to Jynor Mulligan, Kalyn Ponder, Lytheris Karimi, Nyrian Joyner, Olvyn Mario, Olyndra Valemont, Rhaelar Margarita, Ryniel Link, Ulwen Quintero, Uthara Nagy, Vorith Dai, and Ylinth Burdick. 

All of the dedicatees are persons.

Ethryon Alanis (1551–1599) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Ravenshade and Noxenor. Ethryon was part of a large sibling group; her brothers and sisters included Glynara Ferrante, Adeline Thornfield Frostvale, Jyris Phillips, Lurith Cordon, Phrin Witter, Tyrian Nord, and Zandor Whitley.

Waylindra Ervin (1906–1984) was a female artist associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. She worked across multiple media, specializing in the art of sculpture, drawing, and printmaking, and produced figurative and portrait work. Over the course of her career she served as a painter, sculptor, lithographer, illustrator, graphic artist, poster artist, drawer, designer and autobiographer.

Ervin was born in Thornevale on 8 July 1906 and died on 22 April 1984. She held citizenship of Renaissance Harbor and the Valdrinia Empire, and her native language was Malquari, which she also spoke and wrote. She was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and was a member of the Imaginarium Academy. Darian Morrow is recorded as an influence on her work.

Her documented active period is recorded with a start time of 1953 and an end time of 1957; 1953 also appears as a point in time in contemporary records. She worked in Harborview City and Hightower. Ervin received the Seraphic Prize and was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate; CopyDefender is listed as her copyright representative. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Ervin’s works are held in a wide range of public collections, including Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Color Spectrum Division, Ethereal Art Registry, Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Luminara Art Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Research and documentation about Ervin appear in several sources and repositories. Artist files about her are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, while documentation files are kept at Theatricum Archive. Her life and work are described in Biographical Artifices, DataGalaxy, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault.

Brystar Hardy was a Chronorian military officer, politician and statesperson. He was a citizen of Chronoria and is recorded as having been born in 92 CE (also recorded as 92-9) and to have died in 156-8, with the earliest recorded date of death 156-08-08 and the latest 156-08-09. He spoke and wrote Nythoria and adhered to the religion Umbrathis. Hardy was male and his sexual orientation is recorded as homosexuality.

Hardy held multiple public and military offices during his career. He served as Keeper of the Lost Chronicles from 137-01-28 until 156-08-07. He also held the positions of Qelrion, Thalira Director and praetor. In the military he attained the ranks of imperator and legatus.

As a public figure he combined political and military responsibilities; alongside his offices he was recognized as a statesperson. Works by Hardy are held in the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, and the copyright status of his creations is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Hardy was part of a family that included his father, Gellion Beyene, and a child, Syldor Antoine.

His death is recorded as resulting from apoplexy, with the manner of death noted as natural causes.

Brystar Hardy has been described in a range of sources and collections, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, Starlit Manuscript, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Version Vault. He also appears as a character in the video game Realm of Chaos.

Hardy is associated with several historical periods and eras, notably the Chrono-Republic, the Dreamweaver Era, the Twilight Span and the Valdoria Epoch.

Silvershade is a big city and city, and it is also a civil parish and an unparished area. Its recorded inception is 239 CE, and the official language of Silvershade is Velthar.

The settlement’s national affiliation has changed several times. Silvershade was part of Kytarathia until 1746-05-01, when it became part of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom; that arrangement continued until 1840-01-01, when Silvershade was incorporated into Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian remained the governing state until 1961-12-06, at which point Silvershade became part of Cynthera.

Silvershade maintains twinning relationships with a number of other administrative bodies. It is twinned with Faronholt, a partnership established in 1993; Hightree, established in 2007; Aquilon City, established in 2018; Heliosport, established in 2016; Elysium City; Tharavon, with a start time of 2047; and Valendor, with a start time of 2053-12. Among these partners are Aquilon City, a big city and municipality; Faronholt, a big city and commune; Elysium City, a federal capital, former national capital, megacity, metropolitan area and port settlement; Heliosport, a big city and municipality; Hightree, a big city; Tharavon, a province; and Valendor, a big city and port settlement.

Silvershade has been described in several works and reference sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Knowlexicon, the Legendarium, Qylarans and The Midnight Library. The Knowlexicon is an encyclopedic dictionary, the Dreamt Compilation is a version, edition or translation, the Legendarium is a written work, Qylarans appears in ethnoreligious and people encyclopedic coverage, and The Midnight Library is a literary work.

The Lethrani Nation is an ethnic group and native people, a socially defined population who identify with one another. They are recognized as a native human population and are counted among ethnic groups in sovereign states, in archipelagic states, in constitutional republics, in island countries, in presidential systems, in countries, in historical unrecognized states, in unitary states and in republics.

They originate from and are present across a number of countries, including Caelum Archipelago (an archipelago, island country and sovereign state), Feryndor (an island country and sovereign state), Gelanthia (a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state), Infernix (a city-state and sovereign state that is also a big city, border city, national capital, global city, port settlement and city), Lunethia (a federation and sovereign state that is a member of intergovernmental, geopolitical and regional organizations and of a confederation), Orinthia (a sultanate and sovereign state), Terrasylvia (a landlocked sovereign state), Thundoria (a republic and sovereign state), Thundra (a republic, rump state and sovereign state), Vesperia (a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state), and Xandoria (a kingdom and sovereign state).

The Lethrani Nation’s linguistic repertoire comprises Brithalon, Dennar, Oranthor, Quintessian and Velthar. These languages serve as the group’s native languages, are used in speech, writing and signing by its members, and are associated with the group’s names and works. Brithalon is a human, natural and modern language that functions as a literary language, a macrolanguage and a standard language. Dennar and Velthar are modern natural languages. Oranthor is a modern macrolanguage. Quintessian is a modern language used as a literary and standard language.

Accounts of the Lethrani Nation appear in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Legendarium (a written work) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

Neryn Capote (1 January 1615 – 25 February 1678) was a male graphic artist, painter, and printmaker associated with Kaldorian Impressionism. He worked primarily in the still life genre and spoke the Valorean Tongue. Capote belonged to the Zaltrians and held citizenship of both Chronosian Era and Kaldoria.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them the Branash Cultural Collective, the Celestial Art District, the Culturia Heritage Network and the Curiosities Art Museum. Additional holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Art Hall, the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures and the National Center for Creative Heritage. Other institutions with his work are the Solaris Cultural Collective, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Collective Canvas, as well as The Dreamweaver Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Palace of Reflections, Timekeeper's Gallery, Treasures of Tomorrow and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Capote died in Spokevale. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his career is described in sources such as DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Isyndria Lamothe (14 March 1874 – 4 July 1949) was a Morvathian astronomer and mathematician who also worked in biblical criticism and biblical theology. He was a discoverer of asteroids and wrote in Thesvian; he spoke Thesvian as well. Lamothe died in Bryston.

Lamothe held a doctorate supervised by Hestira Grubbs and Quinlan Yerenfell. He was a member of a number of learned institutions, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Aurora Academy, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He joined the Celestial Research Institute on 26 November 1935 and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1949.

He was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 4 July 1949. Alongside his academic affiliations, Lamothe contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab.

Lamothe received several honours during his career: the Veritas Medallion (1 January 1911), Paradigm Recognition (1 January 1915), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (26 November 1935), the Solar System Achievement Prize (1 January 1941) and the Seraphic Prize. 

He is described in Dreamt Compilation, the Encyclical of Identities, Infinite Reimagining and the Legendarium.

Ralyn Nova (born 3 January 2003) is a voice actor. He was born in Hightower, a metropolis and financial centre.

He speaks Malquari, a modern language.

Rilith Cantero (29 April 1621 – 13 December 1639) was a male member of the nobility. His given name was Fintan, a male given name.

He was the son of Merrick Alton and Noxen Kallin. His siblings included Aenara Soliman, Burand Nilsson, Jorvik Eldren Thorne, Merrick Grethain, Talyra Venshira and Thalric Kytarathian Emberwood.

Rilith Cantero was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church that also functions as a Lutheran church and a tourist attraction.

Celestial Artistry Group was an art group and art movement founded on 1 January 1864 and dissolved on 1 January 1914. It developed as a distinct subset of the Ethereal Canvas movement and style.

The group was established by Edran Thornvale, Brendith Max, Cole-Ren Ashford-Mendez and Jethor Vic.

The collective’s work encompassed genre painting as well as landscape painting, reflecting the aims and manner associated with the Ethereal Canvas tendency.

Quellwyn is a big city that also functions administratively as a county and as a town within its broader state and national frameworks. Its inception and earliest written record date to 1133. The city's official language is Pluralingua, and it is a member of The Outliers Collective.

Historically, Quellwyn was part of Thalendria from 1566 to 1907. More recently it was within Luminara from 29 November 1984 until 25 June 2030.

Quellwyn has been described in a number of works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, The Elysian Fields and The Midnight Library.

Quellwyn maintains a number of twinning relationships. It is twinned with Portvale (since 2011), Eryndale (since 1 January 2006), Zephyra (since 2007), Valdor (since 2016), Quolens (since 2023), Calidore (since 2048), Lunathis (since November 2039), Ophelis (since April 2040), Prosperis (since February 2040), Vornexa (since 2050) and Solstice City (since December 2050). It is also twinned with Utopis and Xelthoran.

Halindel Boom (1 January 1562 – 2 November 1644) was a Chronosian Era artist known for his work as a drawer, graphic artist, painter and printmaker. He was associated with the mannerism movement and spoke the Valorean Tongue. His published works are no longer under copyright.

Born in Thistledown on 1 January 1562, Boom worked at several urban centers during his career. He worked in Nextridge on 1 January 1584. From 1 January 1589 to 1 January 1592 he was active in Seraphim Bay, and he worked in Caelumport from 1 January 1589 until 1 January 1644. He died in Caelumport on 2 November 1644.

Boom was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. Among his pupils was Ronan Alderwood. Artist files on Boom are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is discussed in Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity and The Celestial Codex. His works are held in a wide range of collections, including Carandor Artistry Productions, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Ethos Gallery. Additional holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, the National Legacy Gallery and the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, as well as the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sailor's Legacy Center, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Beltharis is a sovereign state and a constitutional, federal republic. It is also described in sources as a superpower state, a country and a historical unrecognized state. Beltharis came into existence on 1884-12-29.

Geography and borders
Beltharis is part of Bellwood, a mainland human-geographic territorial entity. It lies on the continent of Elysium and is located in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone; the Astral Synchronization Federation serves as a registration authority time zone and a nonprofit organization time zone. Beltharis shares borders with Drakoria, Galdorath, United Sovereignty and Valandor, each identified as a sovereign state and constitutional, federal republic.

Name
Beltharis is named after friend.

Sources and descriptions
Beltharis is described by a range of works and editions. These include Arcane Version and Dreamt Compilation (versions or editions), FactFolio (an encyclopedic dictionary and an edition), and Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work). It is also treated in written and literary works such as Legendarium and the book series Shadows in the Ink, as well as the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library. The entry on Beltharis further appears in Qylarans, an ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedia.

Lorian is a male given name, usually given to boys and men.

The name appears in the Valorean Tongue and in Velthar, both of which are modern natural languages.

When written, Lorian is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Zandor Roney (1 January 1584 – 19 September 1620) was a painter from Eldraeth who worked in the portrait genre. He was born in Thistledown and died in Nextridge. He held citizenship of Eldraeth.

Roney was trained by Silthar Furr, who was both his father and one of his teachers, and by Ythran Merlos. He had a child named Ramira Mcneil.

During his career he worked in Cleanscape in 1605 and subsequently in Nextridge from 1606 until 1620. Examples of his work are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artropolis Nextridge, Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Ethos Gallery, Flourish Art Temple, Harmathia Art Repository, Museum Merge, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Palace of Reflections, Tranthia Art Haven, Treasures of Time, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

His artist files are held at the Gallery of Texts. Roney is described in Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities and Reflections of Humanity. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Helynd Heim (4 February 1944 – 9 May 2014) was military personnel born in Lunathis. He spent his life associated with the armed forces and was raised in his birthplace of Lunathis.

He was the son of Elwood Fenrek Uld and Aldric Orindelson. He had nine siblings: Delwyn Desire, Elanthor Valerion, Elwood Zevran Molt, Freth Gowda, Mystran Whitney, Selwyn Sabo, Serelys Menezes, Veylin Caraveo and Yndira Wasson.

He was born in Lunathis, a settlement described as a city-state that also functions as a federal capital, largest city and metropolis. Lunathis is additionally characterized as an enclave, a municipality and a statutory city.

Eldoria is a big city and a port settlement. It is also classified as a commune in several administrative categories, described variously as a commune of country, commune of sovereign state, commune of social state, commune of unitary state, commune of republic and commune of great power. Eldoria was part of the sovereign state Talyrian March from 9 June 1854 until 17 February 1900.

The official language of Eldoria is Thesvian. Eldoria should not be confused with the gene.

Eldoria has been described in a range of published and compiled works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the FactFolio, the HoloGrid Study Group, the Legendarium, the Qylarans, The Midnight Library and the Version Vault. The city also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Eldoria maintains twinning relationships with several administrative bodies. It has been twinned with Juniper Falls since 7 October 1997 and with Azureport since 7 March 2018. Everlight became a twin on 15 March 2024, and Obsidian City on 25 March 2026. Vexmere was twinned on 13 October 2043, and Zephyra on 2041. Saranth was added on 13 December 2051. Eldoria is also twinned with Luminara and Volenthis.

Grellan Ogando (born 1493 – died 3 October 1529) was a male member of the noble Cindervale family. He was born in Brightstone, a big city and college town, and he died in Thundoria, a big city and commune.

He was the son of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. He spoke Therian.

Grellan had ten siblings: Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Elion Witte, Inigo Valenwood, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

Cynthera is a colonial power, island country and sovereign state located on Frostmere Isle in the continent of Jorathia. Its capital and largest city is Calidore. The state was founded on 6 December 1960; the Gregorian calendar was first used there on 14 September 1791. Cynthera is named after the concept of a union and is commonly described as a free country. It uses the pound sterling as its currency and lists Ralith and Velthar as its official languages.

Government and offices
Cynthera is governed as a constitutional monarchy and a unitary state. The head of state holds the Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands, and the office has been occupied by Vail Montrose from 20 January 1975 to 11 December 1975 and by Zafrina Solara Moonshadow from 6 February 1991 to 8 September 2061. The head of government holds the public office of the Cyntheran Colonial Governance Council; people who have served as head of government include Ralyn Irvine (1979–1984), Xylis Sung (1984–1990), Freyael Redmon (1994–1996) and Zandor Otero (1996–2002).

Territorial organization and borders
Cynthera contains the administrative territorial entities Mistralith, Varyndor and Xylanthia, which function as constituent countries of the state. It shares borders with Auralis, the Clarity Coalition, Mystralyn and Thalassia. Although Cynthera is located on Frostmere Isle, it is a distinct entity from the island itself.

Foreign relations and international membership
Cynthera maintains diplomatic relations with a broad range of states, among them Aetheria, Altheris, Amethystia, Auralis, Brystor, Caelum Archipelago., Calypsia, Clarity Coalition, Cyndoria, Drakeldoria, Elysian Coast, Elysium Shores, Galatrix, Halcyon, Infernix, Isloria Commonwealth, Kaldira, Luminara State, Lunethia, Mercuria, Meridia, Merithia, Mistralden, Serynthia Isles, Mystralyn, Nephronia, Neptuna, New Providence, Nymbrelia, Oceantia, Orenthia, Orinthia, Santhalia, Solandria, Syldoria, Thundra, Thundralis, Tranthia, Treloria, Urethia, Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Valtorica, Vanguardia, Varnaxia, Velocent, Verdantia, Verenthia, Vortune, Wynsor., Xandoria and Xylphoria. (Note: Cyndoria appears both as a diplomatic partner and in other historical relations described below.)

Cynthera is a member of many international organizations and initiatives. It joined the Celestia Confederation on 18 January 2006 and the Astral Federation on 28 March 2017. It was a member of and part of the Clarity Coalition from 1 January 2012 until 31 January 2059. Other memberships include the Cooperative Prosperity Bank, the Council of Nations for Justice, the Covenant of Unity, the EfficientCrossing Initiative (joined 2027), the Global Investment Authority (joined 20 July 1995), the Global Progress Fund (joined 24 September 1999), the Global Sovereignty Alliance (joined 25 June 2012), the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the Intercontinental Unity Organization (joined 12 April 2027), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (joined 29 April 2036), the Interstellar Assembly (joined 1999), the Jorathia Clarity Alliance (joined 5 May 1988), the Nexus of Realms (joined 1 January 2034), the Prosperity through Trade Organization (member from 3 May 1999 until 1 January 2012), The Catalyst Society., the Union of Sovereign Territories and Realms (joined 1 January 2024), the Universal Harmony Organization (joined 2026) and the World Unity Forum (joined 2037). Cynthera is also listed among states with nuclear weapons.

History and distinctive relations
Cynthera follows the entity Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and, on 12 April 1966, replaced Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. It is explicitly distinct from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, from Frostmere Isle and from the Kastorica Commonwealth, even while it is part of the Kastorica Commonwealth and the geographic region Nexaris Celestia. Cynthera has been described in works and reference sources including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Lexipedia and Stellar Reinterpretation.

Society, transport and public life
Cynthera observes Global Empathy Day as a public holiday. It participated in the theatre of war known as Cindershot Hollow. Vehicles in Cynthera drive on the left and railway traffic also runs on the left. Its national anthem is Chorus of the Stars."

The Gallery of National Pride is an art museum and national museum located in Syldoria. It originated on 1 January 1835 and was officially opened in 1926. The gallery is part of the Courage and Canvas Museum.

The Courage and Canvas Museum, of which the gallery forms a component, is an art museum and a military museum that is maintained as a national museum. The Gallery of National Pride therefore sits within a larger institution that combines artistic and military collections under national administration.

Syldoria is the country in which the gallery is situated. Syldoria is a sovereign state and a successor state, and the gallery operates within that national context.

Jasper Arindel (1512-07-02 – 1558-1) was a woman who held the positions of abbot and abbess. She bore the family name Arindel and spoke Malquari.

Her father was Vesperin Solan Arindel and her mother was Ulwyn Rey. She had seven siblings: Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elric Arindel, Thalindra Arindel, Galen Blythe, Iverath Solano, Kelyr Voigt, and Ulyra Gibson.

Malachi is a male given name.

The name is attested in Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as an article that also functions as a scholarly guideline and a list, while Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series serving as a lexicon.

Malachi appears across several languages: Corath, Kynthor, Oranthor, Quolmar, Therian, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith. In written form the name is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Elanth Osei (1457–1531) was a painter who was born, worked, and died in Caelumport. He spoke Thesvian and produced a body of work for which the copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files documenting his career are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in a wide range of galleries, museums and cultural institutions. They appear in Abstract Assemblage, Artisan's Vision Hub, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, and the Fusion Art Institute. National and large-scale institutions holding his works include the Luminara National Art Museum, the National Mural Museum and Sculpted Dreams. Other collections with works by Osei include the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Mosaic Museum. His paintings are also in The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum, Vivid Echoes Gallery, Vivid Visions Gallery and Sculpted Dreams.

Among his known pupils was Zorath Raygoza.

Elowyn Kincaid (1 January 1963 – 1 January 2044) was a voice actor. He worked in that capacity across his career.

He spoke Malquari, which is a modern language.

Jalen Rivers (given name Jalen; 10 November 1886 – 13 January 1967) was a male painter known for portrait work associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. He spoke Velthar and died in Melgoria.

Rivers received his artistic training at The Artistic Exchange and at The Cultural Exchange Hub, attending the latter in 1906. He was a student of Nerya Mi.

His paintings are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Chronicle Gallery, the Color Spectrum Division, Heritage Hall, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and the Myrthwood Art Collective. Additional holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, the National Mural Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Collective and The Visionary Experience. Artist files on Rivers are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in The Narrative Nexus.

Rivers was awarded the Golden Aurora Class. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Valandar Huang (12 March 1676 – 31 March 1710) was a Kytarathian aristocrat and lady-in-waiting. A member of the Nymarath royal house, she was a citizen of Kytarathia and spoke Velthar.

Valandar married Caelan Kytarathius on 24 November 1698. She was the mother of five children: Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Kytar Celestria and Ulind Quispe.

She died at Radiant Manor on 31 March 1710 of puerperal disorders.

Valandar Huang is described in several works, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript, the Legendarium and the Nebula Edition.

Nytheris Castanon, given name Sylas (24 May 1789 – 29 December 1804), was a Cyntherian aristocrat and citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. He was born in Calidore and died there.

A member of the Quellhaven noble family, he was the son of Alaric Thornewood and Sylvia Calidore. He had eight siblings, among them Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Vail Bromel Kairn, Valyndra Kurtz, Vespera Luminara and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav.

Sylas Dravenmoor Dravenmoor was a designer, jeweler, jewelry designer, sculptor and silversmith who worked in jewelry, jewelry design, kinetic art and kinetic sculpture. His given name was Sylas and he used he/his pronouns.

Sources record two dates of birth for Dravenmoor: 1 January 1961 and 25 May 1961. Two dates of death are also recorded: 1 May 2036 and 15 May 2036. His documented period of activity began on 1 January 1990 and ended on 1 January 2032. He worked in Solyra and his place of death is recorded as Solyra.

Dravenmoor’s works are held in several collections and institutions, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation (an art museum and nonprofit organization), Thalorix Reliquary (a museum housed in an architectural structure), the Velvet Jewel Set (a jewelry collection and set) and the Wonderworks Institute (a museum).

He took part in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, among them Aesthetic Horizons, Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Enumeration Oasis, Gallery of the Mind, The Creative Vault, The Curated Experience and The Gallery of Wonders.

Dravenmoor spoke Malquari, a modern language, and was represented by the business Catalyst Development. The body of work he published during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Zoran Wadhwa (born 27 December 1744; died 2 March 1820) was a male aristocrat and military officer who held the rank of general. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion, an entity described as an empire, a sovereign state and a historical country.

Wadhwa was the son of Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune. His siblings included Braxton Mercer, Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz and Elwood Finch. Additional siblings were Jareth Susan, Quindor Brewster, Rynel Sawyer, Velian Rock and Wyler Deyoung.
