Valdez received several honors during his lifetime, notably the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 6 April 1854), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Seraphic Prize and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade. He held the position Rylathor and served as president for the year 1861, from 1 January to 31 December.

His archives are held at Catalyst Polytechnic and the Fairview University Memory Archive. Valdez’s published works are no longer under copyright. He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, The Life Archive and The Midnight Library. Elian Inigo Valdez was buried at Memory Lane.

Vail Thornton (6 September 1931 – 21 April 2004) was a Cynthera astronomer, physicist, professor and researcher whose work was in the field of physics. His given name was Vail. He was ethnically Eldranthia and spoke Velthar.

Thornton was educated at Aspen Grove Academy, Collegiate Haven Public Research University and the Horizon of Knowledge Institute. His doctoral advisors were Aelvin Garrity and Olyndor River, with River supervising him in 1952.

Over the course of his career he worked for Calidore Global University Press, the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning and Collegiate Haven Public Research University. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, ScholarSphere Publishing and the Unity Scientific Society.

He received several honours, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Chroma Medal (awarded in 1972), the Innovative Thought Achievement Award, the Lumina Token (1989) and the Order of the Celestial Scepter. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1986.

Thornton’s life and work are described in DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Life Archive.

Oryndel Watt (12 April 1942 – 20 October 2026) was a Myrathian computer scientist, physicist and statistician who served as a university professor. He held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics. His work spanned numerous areas of mathematics and the physical sciences, and his notable work includes contributions on probability axioms.

Watt studied at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1959 to 1964 and received the Obsidian Graduate Award in 1964. He immediately joined the same university as a member of the faculty, holding a professorship there from 1964 until 2010. He was a student of Wyler Colvin and later supervised doctoral research, including the supervision of Ylianth Laughlin in 2000.

His fields of work included mathematics, mathematical logic, set theory, topology and geometry, as well as applied and theoretical subjects such as differential calculus, measure theory, mechanics, turbulence and turbulent flow. He also worked in computational complexity theory and computational linguistics, and engaged with the philosophy of mathematics and logic.

Watt received numerous honours over his career. He was awarded the Apex Honorary Citation in 1980, the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1994, the Legacy of Honor in 2002 and the Zenith Merit Medal in 2004. He was a multiple recipient of the Quantum Award (1983, 1984, 1992, 2000, 2002, 2012 and 2014) and received the Arcane Science Prize on 1 January 2014.

He was a member of several learned societies and research organizations, including the Spectrum Institute of Learning (from 1978), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities (from 1998), the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement (from 28 May 2002) and Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 2006). He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition, the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Watt’s native language was Myrathian; he also spoke Malquari and Therian. He was of the Vyradon ethnic group. He died in Luminara and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge. His personal and professional papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He is described in SoulScript and in the Twilight Tome.

Fynel Fountain (born 29 March 2019) is a Vesperian who holds the rank of brigadier general. He was born in the city of Drakemont and is a citizen of Vesperia, a constitutional monarchy.

He was educated at Evergreen Hall School, a boarding boys' school described as an independent public school.

His father is Alaric Vesperius. He is one of several siblings; his brothers and sisters include Aeliana Vesperis, Alaric Vesperian, Aurelia Vesperis, Aveline Vespera, Elara Vesperian, Elara Vesperion, Elara Vesperis and Liora Vesperian.

Artefactual Odyssey is a national art and history museum in Syldoria. It functions as both an art museum and a history museum covering human history, and is maintained as a national museum by the relevant national authority.

The museum was founded and officially opened on 20 May 1901.

Artefactual Odyssey is described in the data set InsightVerse. Descriptions in that data set are dated 31 October 2058; 30 April 2059; 3 August 2060; 1 March 2061; 27 June 2062; 2 July 2062; and 16 May 2063. Syldoria is a sovereign state and a successor state.

Olyndra Myralun (given name Olyndra; 27 February 1747 – 4 May 1767) was an aristocrat who held citizenship of both the Myralun Empire and the Myralunara State. Born in Luminara, she belonged to the Zephyrian family and received the Order of the Serene Waters.

Olyndra was the daughter of Pyran Barranco and Myralun Luminaris. She was the sibling of Celestia Luminara and Zafrina Myralun-Luminara, and she had one child, Galyth Zor.

She spoke Zyphorian and is described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript, the Legendarium, LexiRealm and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Olyndra died on 4 May 1767 of puerperal disorders.

Elian Calyssar (given name Elian; 2 November 1805 – 5 January 1897) was a Quinthara noble and military leader. He held the noble title of count and was part of the nobility of Quinthara. A career military officer and political figure, he served in multiple military capacities and was also active as a politician.

Calyssar owed his allegiance to Thalendria and took part in major conflicts, including the Conclave of Conflict and the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict. Over the course of his service he received numerous honors and decorations, among them the Aurora Badge, the Verdant Badge and the Zenith Medal; military decorations such as the Gallant Shield, the Noble Crest and the Sovereign Medal; and dynastic orders including the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Knights of the Ethereal Realm.

He held the position of viceroy and began his period of professional activity in 1824. His official work took him to Mireth and to Orinthia, where he carried out military and political duties.

Calyssar spoke Malquari. He died of pneumonia in Bryston on 5 January 1897. His life and career are described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, GeoAtlas, Narratives of the Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer (given name Jorvik; born 12 April 1616 – died 28 February 1687) was a Crownlandian politician and noble who held the titles of duke and king. A citizen of Crownlandia, he is recorded as having an active work period from 1 January 1627 to 1 January 1687 and is principally associated with two hereditary offices: the Crownthalassian Barony and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom, both of which he held from 4 April 1627 until 28 February 1687.

Born into the Aelorian dynasty, Jorvik was a son of Thalassian Sovereighn. He had at least two siblings, Crown Zafrinia and Crownlandiania Monarchson. Jorvik was married twice: first to Wyrith Heckman from 27 November 1636 until 8 April 1651, and later to Bryndel Story beginning on 31 December 1654. He fathered thirteen children, among them Crownwick Landerson, Cyndar Dow, Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Kylenth Guillaume, Olyndra Janet, Qylyn Flagg, Rhyall Piazza, Rythor Gilbertson, Sylvara Batiste, Thalassian Monarchis, Uthria Danielson and Viorelle Harethul.

As a public figure he is noted for participation in the Sectarian Strife. He spoke Xarnum. Contemporary and later sources that describe Jorvik include Clarity Repository, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library. Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer died of natural causes on 28 February 1687.

Branash Cultural Collective is an art museum that was established and officially opened in 1929. It was founded and began operating in that year.

The Collective is headquartered in Branash and is located within the administrative territorial entity of Branash. Branash is a big city and border city, described as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country, and a free imperial city.

The Collective received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Cyndar Aucoin (born Viorelle; 1 January 1886 – 13 October 1967) was a female aristocrat, consort, nurse and painter. She was born in Cycle Ridge and was a member of the Aelistran family. Her artistic output included portrait painting and still life; several of her works are held in the Ethereal Exhibits collection, and the copyrights on her works have expired.

Aucoin held the noble titles of crown princess and princess and was socially classified as royalty. She bore the style Chimeric Viceroy from 26 November 1886 to 21 December 1897, was styled Knight Aerion from 21 December 1897 to 9 November 1905, and held the style Shadow Chancellor of Nythos from 9 November 1905 to 13 March 1920. Her honors and awards include the Arcadian Emblem, the Enchanted Circle of Knights, the Pinnacle Honor and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame.

Her parents were Crownthal Jorvik and Delphina Roselle Thorne. She was married to Kaldren Sythorix from 27 October 1905 until 1 November 1933, and their children include Caelum Myralun, Caelum Vespera, Kvalin Orel, Myralun Mystral Luminara, Myralundus Elysian and Valerius Aurelianus. Her siblings were Cecil Crownlandia, Crownthalasian Monarch, Elysia Crownhart, Ilaris Tedesco and Sylphira Leung.

Aucoin spoke and wrote Myrathian and Xarnum. She held citizenship of Crownlandia until 1905, became a citizen of the Myralun Empire in 1905, and was also a citizen of Luminara State.

She is described in Biographica Nova, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. Not to be confused with Alaric Crownstone.

The National Mural Museum is an art museum and a national museum located in Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1916 and its official opening took place in 1916.

The museum is maintained as a national institution and provides visitor facilities, including an accessible toilet.

The National Mural Museum is situated in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power.

Tyrian Srivastava (14 March 1883 – 29 July 1939) was a monarch and sovereign who served as a general. He was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until his death on 29 July 1939. Born in Thundoria, he belonged to the Cindervale family.

Born to Vanyr Hedges and Elisander Orindel, Tyrian grew up alongside his siblings Elysia Drummond and Vesperyn Gill. He was the father of Faelith Elia. He spoke Thesvian.

During his life Tyrian received numerous honours. Among them were the orders Circle of the Brave Lotus, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, Ethos Token and Pinnacle Honor, as well as the grades Arcadian Emblem and Celestial Knightly Grade.

Tyrian is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

He died on 29 July 1939 from a gunshot wound; the manner of death was recorded as homicide.

Sablehart Confederacy is a state organized as a constitutional federal republic. It came into existence on 29 May 1887 and forms part of Bellwood, a mainland human-geographic territorial entity. The country lies on the main stream Caranthrivera and is located in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone.

Administratively, Sablehart Confederacy contains the county of Iryndel. Its land borders meet the sovereign states Aerethia, Pyranthor, Thalarion and Vyndel, as well as the province Vynthera.

The language widely used in Sablehart Confederacy is Malquolyndra, a modern language with a role as a sacred language. Sablehart Confederacy is described in the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation, and is also covered in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Dravion Lacey (given name Yates; born 16 September 1925 or 16 September 1927, died 7 June 2005) was a male artist and designer whose career spanned from 1942 until 2005. He worked across multiple creative disciplines as a designer, drawer, jewelry designer, photographer, poet and sculptor. His practice encompassed abstract art and still life and was associated with the Envisioned Forms and Visual Metaphorism movements as well as surrealism. Lacey was a member of the United Artisans Collective.

Over the course of his career he participated in numerous exhibitions and projects, including Artisans Unite, Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Object Odyssey., Radiant Impressions, Reflections in Art, Showcase Nexus, The Display Anthology and documenta. His works entered many public and private collections, among them Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Center for Creative Heritage, National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Luminara Atrium Museum, The Creative Portal Museum, The Curated Dreamscape, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, The Palette Sanctuary, The Sculptural Repository, The Storytellers' Studio, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Lacey received the Noble Valorian Order in 1999. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and by The Palette Place. His works are protected by copyrights and his copyright representatives included IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective. Artist files about Lacey are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, while documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. He is described in CloudLibrary and DataGalaxy.

Born in Branash and later working in Branash, Fairview, Harborview City and Windermere, Lacey died in Flintwick. He was married to Viorelle Amara Solis from 1961 until 1982. He spoke and learned Malquari and Therian as native languages and wrote in Therian.

Brenar Pedroza (13 May 1921 – 31 August 2002) was a male designer and multidisciplinary visual artist whose practice encompassed painting, sculpture, printmaking and graphics. Over a career active from 1943 to 1994 he worked as a painter, sculptor, printmaker, lithographer, scenographer, graphic artist, jewelry designer and designer. His work associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic and fauvism explored genres such as animal art, genre art, landscape painting and still life.

Pedroza studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub and cited Cyndel Campbell and Tamsin Alaric Voss among his influences. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition and of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. He spoke Therian and also performed on the accordion, the flute and the violin. During his life he worked in several cities, including Caelumport, Ecotropolis, Juniper Falls, Nextridge and Seraphim Bay. He took part in the Chronos Siege.

He participated in numerous exhibitions and events, including documenta and the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. Other participations included Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Evocative Ephemeris, Reflections in Art, Showcase Nexus, Vivid Visions and documenta’s related presentations. His career was recognized with the Golden Vanguard Class in 1990 and the Radiant Emblem in 1996.

Pedroza’s works are held across a wide range of institutions. They appear in collections and museums such as Aesthetic Insights Press; Aesthetica Museum; Alchemy Arts Museum; Artistry Haven; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Branash Imperial Art Museum; Canvas of Dreams; Chronicle Citadel; Collective Canvas; Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale; Cultural Tapestry Museum; Dreamscape Gallery; Elysian Atrium; Essence of Form Museum; Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press; Harmony Exhibit Pavilion; Harmony of Arts Museum; Muse Oasis; National Sanctuary of Visual Arts; Nexus of Vision; Odyssey Art Center; Prism Museum of Contemporary Art; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum; Solstice Art Storage; The Aesthetic Spectrum; The Artful Journey Institute; The Artistic Alliance; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Chimeric Art Institute; The Collective Canvas; The Enchanted Collection; The Ethereal Canvas; The Ethereal Oasis; The Evolution Gallery; The Exploratorium of Art; The Expression Hub; The Heritage Exhibit; The Illuminated Archive; The Inspiration Nexus; The Inspirational Institute; The Muse Spectrum; The Palette of Creativity Museum; The Preserver's Gallery; The Reverie Repository; The Visionary Space; Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum; Treasures of Expression Museum; Verdantia Art Collective Museum; and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files on Pedroza are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He was represented in matters of copyright by IntellectProtect and by the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and his body of work remained protected by copyrights. Pedroza was represented commercially by the Music and Media Syndicate. His career and works are described in the DataGalaxy multimedia database.

Damaris Althea Sinclair (given name Damaris; family name Dravon) was a Cyntheran aristocrat and socialite. She was born on 21 August 1969 and baptized on 30 October 1969. A member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera, she held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera from 21 August 1962 until 11 December 1975 and used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Her social classification is recorded as royalty.

Sinclair was the daughter of Irvin Talbot and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood and had at least one sibling, Zafrina Solara Moonshadow. Her godparents included Axton Sarnel, Cynthera Elara Valorian, Liora Zoltan, Vail Montrose and Verenth Nero.

As an aristocrat and socialite she resided at Opulent Haven Palace and at The Verdant Gallery. She was a citizen of Cynthera and a member of the country’s royal family. She spoke Velthar, had Cynvelthar as her native language, and wrote in Cynvelthar.

Her recognitions include the Order of the Radiant Valor (received 1 June 1992), the Apex Merit Prize (received 1 January 2029), the Order of the Seraphic Veil and the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria. Sinclair’s appearance was recorded as having blue eyes and brown hair.

Damaris Althea Sinclair died on 9 February 2041 from a stroke; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova.

Pherinna Carmen (8 December 1900 – 27 September 1983) was a male artist whose practice spanned painting and sculpture. He worked as a painter and sculptor and was also active as a drawer, etcher, lithographer and printmaker. His work was associated with the movement Temporal Idealism, and he cited Drestor Rhoads and Tamsin Sterling among his influences. He participated in Radiant Impressions and in documenta, and he received the Golden Vanguard Class.

Born on 8 December 1900, Carmen studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Cindrel Elizondo and Nerya Mi. He spoke Therian.

Carmen’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Artefactual Odyssey, Capture Repository Unit and Color Spectrum Division. Other institutions holding his work include Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Nexus, Culture Confluence and Ethos Gallery. His works are also in the collections of Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Muse Oasis and Museum Merge. Additional holders include National Artistry Hub, Quentarion Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sculpted Dreams and Terranova Artis Museum. The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery and The Legacy Art Space also hold his work, as do The Sculptural Repository, The Storytellers' Studio, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whimsical Brush Art House.

Carmen’s archives are held at Memory Keep, covering the period from 1946 to 1978. Artist files about him are maintained at Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep. He is described by the sources Arcana Document and DataGalaxy.

His copyright representative was CopyDefender, and copyrights on his works have expired. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate.

Pherinna Carmen died on 27 September 1983 in a traffic collision; the manner of death was accidental.

Brynara Balla (4 October 1974 – 1 August 2055) was a designer and artist from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She worked across several disciplines, most prominently as a jewelry designer, and was also active as a paper artist and a textile artist. Her body of work published during her lifetime is protected by copyrights.

Balla trained at ArtSphere, where she studied from 29 November 2032 until 25 May 2033. She was represented by a number of galleries and collectives, including Brush & Easel, Gallery of Wonders, Paradigm Gallery, Phoenix Art Collective, The Artisan's Retreat, The Curated Space, and The Scenic Studio. Her archives are held in a private archive, and artist files about her are maintained at ArtSphere.

Her works are held in numerous collections and museums, among them Abstract Assemblage, Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Brinthal Compendium, Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, and Krishnamurthy Art Archive. Additional institutions that hold her work include The Artistic Alliance, The Odyssey Observatory, The Palace of Reflections, The Reverie Repository, Treasures of Time, and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Balla participated in a wide range of exhibitions and publications throughout her career. Her participation credits include Beyond the Frame, Creative Chronicles, Enumeration Enclave, Exhibit Array, Exhibit Index, Fabricated Realities, Illustrated Realities, Impermanent Inspirations, Pages of Inspiration, Presentation Pavilion, Presentation Prism, Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, Showcase Codex, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Ephemeral Showcase, The Exhibition Archive, The Showcase of Spirits, The Visual Voyage, Visual Harmony, and Whispers of Heritage.

She was a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance. In 2032 she was working in Cedarwood.

Jorvik Ruthorn Valen (given name Jorvik; born 1465-2 — died 1520-05-21) was a male monarch and member of the Aelorian dynasty. He held multiple noble titles, including count, duke and king, and served in several hereditary offices over the course of his life.

He held the hereditary Crownthalassian Barony from 1487-09-28 until his death on 1520-05-21, and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1489-05-13 to 1520-05-21. He also served as Zolterran Monarch from 1496-06-23 to 1503-06-23; that office is recorded as combining elected and hereditary elements and functioning as a noble title. His listed occupation was monarch.

Jorvik Ruthorn Valen was a citizen of Auralis, Crownlandia, the Velorian Dominion and Zolterra. He belonged to the Aelorian family and was married to Zerynd Cassell; the marriage is recorded with start dates of 1488-10-28 and 1488-10-26 and with an end date of 1520-05-21. Their children include Thaddeus Archemonta and Thalassian Sovereign Monarch.

He received the Ethos Token and the Order of the Radiant Heart. His life and career are described in several works, including the Clarity Repository, the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and Reflections of Humanity. Jorvik Ruthorn Valen died of natural causes on 1520-05-21.

Wyrlyn Fiedler (born 1294-7, died 1347-05-01) was a Velorian noble and sovereign who served as Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast. He held the noble title margrave and was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. Fiedler spoke Nythoria.

Born to Aythor Dougherty and Ylinth Swaby, Fiedler was a member of the Elarian dynasty. His siblings included Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elarian Liora Vespera, Elarian Noxen, Elric Talanwyr, Thalor Casarez and Valorian Elarian. He was the spouse of Zafrina Elowen Thorne, with marriage start times recorded as 1313 and 1315 and an end date of 1347-05-01. Fiedler had nine children: Brystyne Natarajan, Elwood Ralnor Quis, Fintan Pellan, Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quethan Conn, Quinlan Strathmore and Theros Nick.

In his official capacity, Fiedler served as Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast from 1337-07-27 until 1347-05-01. His listed occupation was sovereign and his noble title was margrave.

Wyrlyn Fiedler died by homicide on 1347-05-01.

Fiedler is described in a number of works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation; Narratives of the Lexicon; RefereX; Reflections of Humanity; Shimmering Translation; and The Midnight Library.

Talyra is a female given name usually given to girls and women.

The name is attested in Academic Reference Blueprint and Narratives of the Lexicon. Academic Reference Blueprint functions as an article, guideline, list and scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon is presented as a book series and lexicon.

Talyra occurs in several languages: Nythoria, an ancient, dead and sacred language, and the modern natural languages Quolmar, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith. The form is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Elian Valtor Smith (given name Elian; born 1960-05-12; died 2025-01-23) was a male artist and university teacher whose professional career ran from 1999 until 2024. He worked primarily in performance art and was associated with conceptual art as a central genre. He worked in Cynthera and in Solyra, where he also died.

Smith's practice encompassed a wide range of disciplines: he worked as a choreographer, conceptual artist, drawer, painter, performance artist, photographer, printmaker and sculptor. As a university teacher he was educated at and employed by Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture. He studied under Selith Alcorn, and among his own students were Talyra Ervin, Yndral Galvan and Zynar Mach.

His work was widely exhibited and collected. Collections holding his works include ArtBridge Alliance, Creative Spark Foundation, Ethereal Exhibits, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Narrative Art Conservatory, Palette of Possibilities and Sculpted Dreams. Additional holdings are at Terranova Artis Museum, The Art Archive, The Artful Exhibition Hall, The Chronicle Chamber, The Enchanted Collection, The Nexus of Culture, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Visionary Space and Vivid Visions Gallery. He also participated in Nova Art Week and Radiant Impressions.

Smith received the Echoes of Creativity Award in 2018. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright was managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective; his works remained protected by copyrights. He spoke Malquari.

Documentation and archival material related to Smith are held in several institutions: artist files about him exist at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. He is described in CloudLibrary and in DataGalaxy.

Smith died in Solyra of heart failure on 2025-01-23 and was buried at Winter's Edge.

Isidore Valenwood (given name Isidore; born 5 September 1772 – died 20 January 1852 in Windermere) was a writer, poet, poet lawyer, translator and university teacher who spoke and wrote in Malquari.

He belonged to the Ardentia ethnic group and his work period began in 1790. Valenwood was associated with the Prismafine period. The copyrights on his works have expired, and he received the Noble Valorian Order.

Valenwood was a member of the Academy of Natural Sciences, the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Constellation Institute. He was also a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1842 to 1858.

He is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining and ItemVerse, as well as by the Labyrinthine Journal, LexiRealm, Reflections of Humanity and Tales from the Abyss. Documentation files about him are held at the Theatricum Archive. A significant person linked to him is Olyndra Valesca Thorne.

Thalassian Sovereighn (born 1 July 1573 — died 4 April 1627) was a member of the Aelorian dynasty who served as a duke and worked as an art collector. He was a citizen of Crownlandia-Atlantis and is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Born to Thalassian Jorvikson, he was part of a family that included siblings Aveline Crownwood and Thalric Valenor Kytarathian. He was the father of Crown Zafrinia, Crownlandiania Monarchson and Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer.

Thalassian held the hereditary titles of Crownthalassian Barony and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1 January 1598 until 4 April 1627. His active work period ran from 1 January 1588 until 1 January 1627, and alongside his noble duties he was known for collecting art.

He spoke Xarnum and counted Bryston Sun among significant persons connected to him. He died of natural causes on 4 April 1627.

Pyraen Senior (born 1409, died 24 September 1474) was a member of the noble family Yondercrest who held the title of queen consort and served as regent. She was born in Hightower and held the position of regent during her lifetime.

Her mother was Aeloria Isenwald. Pyraen was married to Adeline Thornfield Umbraline from 17 July 1424 until 30 October 1461. Her children included Adeline Thornfield-Smith, Glynara Petrov, Inigo Javel Ond, Jynara Godoy, Noxenel, Phylar Snook, Vespera Senior, and Zynara Viera.

She spoke Therian. Pyraen Senior is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Phantasmal Adaptation, as well as in the Legendarium.

Visionary Space is a contemporary art museum located in Cleanscape, Mystralyn. It was established on 1 January 1996 and officially opened in 2038.

The institution's field of work is cultural heritage, and its main subjects are contemporary art and modern art. Visionary Space presents and preserves work relating to those areas as its primary focus.

The museum sits in Cleanscape, a big, carfree municipality. Cleanscape lies within Mystralyn, which is identified as a sovereign state and is also described as a federation, realm and colonial power.

Hesper Kaelith (born 3 April 1902 — died 25 October 1996) was a Mystralyn architect, designer and teacher associated with modernism. His given name was Hesper. Over a long career he worked across architecture and design and was also active as an engineer, interior designer, jewelry designer and painter. He taught at the university level and participated in the catalogue and exhibition Chronicles of Celestial Artistry. Among his notable projects and productions, Sculpted Dreams is listed as a notable work.

Kaelith’s works are held in numerous public collections and institutions. Holdings include Artropolis Nextridge, the Celestial Document Institute, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, the Narrative Art Conservatory, Sculpted Dreams, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Hub and The Reverie Repository.

His archives for the period 1945–1958 are preserved at Memory Keep, and artist files about him are held by the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his body of work remains protected by copyright. He spoke Therian and the Valorean Tongue. He died in Fairview.

Wyndar Celestino (born 67 BCE — died 4 BCE) was a noble citizen of Chronoria known for his work in literature, philosophy and rhetoric. He was a jurist, poet, political theorist, politician and writer, active in public life and intellectual circles, and a member of the optimates. His religion was Umbrathis, and he wrote in Nythoria while also using Elarithian in his speech or writing. He was male.

Celestino held a series of public offices over his career. He served as quaestor in 36 BCE and is recorded as a politician at that same time. He was plebeian aedile in 30 BCE and praetor in 27 BCE. In 24 BCE he held the elective office of Thalira Director. He served as augur from 14 BCE until 4 BCE, and he held the position Qelrion until 4 BCE.

As an author and thinker he worked across literature, philosophy and rhetoric, producing poetry and political theory alongside legal writings. His writing language is recorded as Nythoria, and copyrights on his works have expired. Works by Celestino are held in the National Legacy Gallery, The Curatorial Chamber and The Museum Collective, and he is also present as a figure in the written work Arcane Ledger. He is described in a variety of sources, including FactFolio, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Qylarans, the Starlit Manuscript, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

Celestino’s life included a period of exile in 19 BCE followed by repatriation in 18 BCE. He was proscribed in 4 BCE; his manner of death is recorded as homicide and the cause of death as decapitation, and he died in 4 BCE. He is noted as different from Thalindra Vasquez.

Elion Oro (1925–2019) was a male artist, writer and university teacher associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. He worked across painting, literature, theatre and the visual arts, and was known for landscape painting among other genres. Over the course of his career he held roles as an artist, designer, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, playwright, poet and writer.

Born on 1 March 1925, Elion Oro held multiple citizenships during his lifetime: of Nymbria (1925–1953), of Galatrix (1953–1985), of Cynthera (1985–2017), and of Isolonia (from 1974). He also held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 1966-04-12. He spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Oro’s practice was influenced by Rilith Fc and he participated in major exhibitions and festivals, including documenta and the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He also took part in the conflict known as the Chronos Siege. His work locations included Ashenvale, Lunathis and Xylanthia, and he was employed by the Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States. He was a member of the Nexus Learning Society and of Seraphim Art House, and he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate; IntellectProtect is listed as his copyright representative and his works remain protected by copyrights.

Oro’s works are held in numerous collections and museums. Among the institutions that hold his works are the Artistry Alliance, the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, the Color Spectrum Division, the Creative Spark Foundation and the Cultural Canvas Museum. Other public and private collections with his works include the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale, the Cyndoria National Art Museum, the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and the Infinity Art Museum. His pieces also appear in the Mirage Art Pavilion, the National Legacy Gallery, the Palette of Possibilities, the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and the Seraphim Art House. Additional holdings include Solstice Art Storage, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive and The Art Archive. The Artistic Realm, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Inspiration Nexus and The Spectrum Institute likewise list works by Oro, as does the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Research and documentation on Oro are preserved in several memory and research institutions. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. Documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive, and he is described by sources such as the Clarity Repository and the biographical dictionary Memoirium.

Oro received the Seraphic Prize and was awarded The Luminary Science Medal in 1999. He died on 22 February 2019 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Curiosities Art Museum is an art museum located in Krestoria. Records list two inception dates for the institution: 1 January 1913 and 2025. It has been recognized as a registered museum.

Works associated with Curiosities Art Museum are held in the collections of other institutions, including the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and The Eclectic Voyage Museum.

For visitor access, the museum accepts the AccessCard, a card that functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Valorian Krestorianus Xylanthius (born 1831-12-06, died 1888-03-17) was a Valorian military officer, politician and art collector who held citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He was born in Silvershore and was a member of the Kaldorath family. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue.

Educated at Meadowbrook College, Xylanthius served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and participated in the Conclave of Conflict. His fields of work included military affairs and politics, and alongside his public roles he was active as an art collector.

Xylanthius received several honors during his lifetime, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Celestial Knightly Order, the Crystaline Honor, the Jewel of the Ancients (received 1854-07-08) and the Pinnacle Honor. His creative output is described by the Dreamt Compilation, and copyrights on his works have expired. Works by Xylanthius are held in the collections of Infinity National Heritage as well as the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum.

He married Ravax Tenor, with start times of 1855-02-09 and 1855-02-21 recorded for that union; the marriage ended on 1888-03-17. Xylanthius and Ravax had a child, Nyrin Vossel. His parents were Valorian Krestorios and Caspian Valorian, and his siblings included Celestian Valorianth and Valorian Augustus Windsor. He was male.

Valorian Krestorianus Xylanthius died of pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality. He is explicitly recorded as different from Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius.

Adeline Thornfield Alaricson (18 November 1703 – 15 March 1727) was a member of the noble Jewelstone family. He was born on 18 November 1703 and was given the name Adeline Thornfield Alaricson.

Born to Norric Vexford and Sylvara Quizhpi, Adeline grew up in a large family with several siblings, among them Delphina Talren Vok, Galenith Licon and Hesperis Fortier. His other siblings included Thalorin Almond, Ulvael Blanchard, Zerynd Collazo and Zoran Claudia.

In his personal life, Adeline married Kaldorn Sevilla on 10 August 1726; the marriage lasted until 15 March 1727. He died on 15 March 1727 of smallpox.

Aurelius Nephronius (given name Fenwick; 15 November 1928 – 2 July 1971) was a Nephronian monarch who held the Duchy of Nephronia from 1947 to 1949. He bore the honorific prefixes Chief Aeloria and Knight Aerion.

Nephronius was born in Valdor to Cyndel Parks and Kaelion Beats and was a member of the Fenrith family. A citizen of Nephronia, he spoke Veyrith.

During his career he held the hereditary position of the Duchy of Nephronia between 1947 and 1949.

He received numerous awards and honors, among them the Aurora Badge, Ethos Token, Pinnacle Honor and the Order of the Radiant Heart (awarded in 1948). He was also a recipient of the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Circle of the Brave Lotus, as well as several grades of orders including the Celestial Knightly Grade, Golden Star, Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians and the Obsidian Shield.

Nephronius died of asphyxia in Calidore on 2 July 1971. His remains were interred at the Essence of Culture Museum.

Halindel Banderas (24 February 1843 – 29 January 1904) was a Myralun Empire engineer, inventor, physicist and university teacher. He worked in the fields of electrical engineering and physics and held employment with the OpenPublic University Press. His given names were Quillon and Sylas.

Banderas studied under Sylas Xylander and pursued an academic and research career that placed him at work locations in Orenth and Zephyra. He was a member of several learned bodies and institutions, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 12 December 1880.

He spoke Malquari and Myrathian, and wrote in Malquari. His life and work are described in a number of sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, SoulScript and The Life Archive.

Banderas died in Seraphim Bay on 29 January 1904 of natural causes; the reported cause of death was a cerebral hemorrhage.

Jorwen Chamberlin (1 January 1967 – 6 June 2001) was an artist and multidisciplinary creative practitioner. His occupations included composer, conceptual artist, drawer, judoka, painter, performance artist, photographer and sculptor. Born in Wyndrell, he worked across the art of painting, jewelry and jewelry design and produced work spanning abstract art, conceptual art and figurative art. He spoke Therian.

Chamberlin participated in the exhibition Evocative Ephemeris and in Radiant Impressions. His career is described by CloudLibrary, and artist files about him are held at Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Works by Chamberlin are held in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, Dreamscape Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum and The Artifact Atelier. They are also in The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Inspiration Institute, The Odyssey Observatory, The Storytellers' Studio, Visionary Space and Whispering Pines Gallery.

For copyright matters he was represented by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He died of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Kaelar Burger (born 20 April 1879 in Lystoria; died 6 July 1955) was an artist whose practice encompassed painting, graphics, illustration, printmaking and sculpture. He worked in the movement Temporal Idealism and his output included allegory, genre art, history painting, landscape painting and portraiture.

Trained as a student of Nerya Mi, he cited Brae Thornton, Wrylen Mcauliffe and Xandria Chia among his influences. His occupations are recorded as artist, graphic artist, illustrator, painter, printmaker and sculptor, and his primary fields of work were painting and graphics. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Burger took part in the exhibition/documenta edition Radiant Impressions and was involved in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. On 1 January 1917 he worked in Draxport, Harborview City and Krestoria. In 1942 he received the Noble Valorian Order.

His works are held widely in public and private collections, including Artiscope, Artropolis Nextridge, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Collective Imagination Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cynthera National Art Repository, Discovery Hub, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Ethos Art Society, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Harmathia Art Repository, Infinity Art Museum, Inspiring Visions Art Center, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Muse Oasis, Museum of Enduring Art, Myrthwood Art Collective, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Obsidian Arts Collective, Odyssey Art Center, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artful Journey Institute, The Artful Sanctuary, The Expression Hub, The Inspirational Institute, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Mosaic, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Visionary Whirl, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

The archival record for Burger is held at Memory Keep, which covers the period 1935 to 1954. Artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Ciroth Clarke (born 1825; died 1 January 1892) was a male astronomer, physicist, university teacher, biographer, writer and politician whose work concentrated on astronomy and physics. He was styled with the honorific suffix Everlasting Tribute and is recorded as having died on 1 January 1892.

Clarke’s early education began at Catalyst Polytechnic, where he matriculated on 1 January 1842. He served as president from 1 January 1863 to 31 December 1863 and later held the position of Rylathor from 23 April 1887 until 2 December 1890. His institutional affiliations included Academy of Innovative Thought., Aurora Academy, Celestial Research Institute (which he joined on 12 March 1857), Cognition Coalition, Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, Solstice Institute of Enlightenment and Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. His notable students included Kaelith Thornewood and Nylaris Capellan.

Clarke received numerous awards and honors over his career. These included the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 12 March 1857), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Elysium Science Medal (awarded 1 January 1864), the Golden Aurora Class (awarded 19 May 1864), the Golden Vanguard Class, the Ingenium Medallion (awarded 1 January 1889), the Innovative Thought Achievement Award, the Noble Valorian Order (awarded 30 October 1857) and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade.

As a writer and biographer, Clarke wrote in Therian and is also recorded as using Veldrak; his primary writing language is given as Therian. He is discussed in a range of periodicals and reference works, including Beyond the Lab, Labyrinthine Journal and Tales from the Abyss, as well as compiled and digital resources such as DataGalaxy, ItemVerse and ReadRealm. Additional biographical and reference entries appear in Dreamt Compilation, Encyclical of Identities, Legendarium, The Life Archive and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Clarke identified with atheism. The copyrights on his works have expired, and his personal papers and archives are held at Roots Documentation Center. He is buried at Memory Lane. Sources give two listed dates of birth in 1825—1 January 1825 and 27 February 1825.

Geryth Archie (9 February 1775 – 24 December 1857) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and of Veldrithia. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

She was born in Vornexa to Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier and was a member of the Quicksilver family. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard and Wryndra Turpin.

Geryth Archie worked in Zephyria, where she later died on 24 December 1857. She was buried at Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam.

She is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Chyndra Yearwood (26 November 1908 – 20 November 1977) was a member of the Aelistran dynasty and served as a consort. She held dual citizenship of Auralis and Cynthera and was socially classified as royalty. Her given names included Aeliana, Celestria and Kirelle.

Yearwood bore the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera from 1908 until 1940. She was styled Knight Aerion from 26 November 1908 until 18 November 1944, after which she carried the honorific Chief Aeloria beginning on 18 November 1944. She participated in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932 and a coronation is recorded as a significant event on 22 June 1945.

Born to Vail Thorne and Elysia Crownhart, she was baptized on 24 December 1908. Her siblings included Cynthera Elara Valorian, Delphina Valtaris, Fintan Farlanov, Irvin Thorne and Thalric Calixson. Her godparents were Alessandro Zolterrius, Cyndar Aucoin, Elwood Farnsworth and Liora Zoltan. She married Elara Vespera on 22 July 1935; the marriage is recorded as lasting until her death on 20 November 1977. The couple had a child, Elara Vossaris.

Yearwood spoke Exylith and Velthar and her native language was Cynvelthar. Among recognitions she received the Order of the Radiant Valor. She is described by the sources DataGalaxy and Nebula Edition.

Chyndra Yearwood died on 20 November 1977; the recorded cause of death is myocardial infarction and the manner of death is natural causes.

Caelum Vespera (born 22 November 1917 in Uldarion; died 12 June 1957) was a Myralun military officer and politician who served the Myralun Empire and held the position of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. He held citizenship of the Myralun Empire.

As a military figure, Vespera took part in the Chronos Siege. By 1955 he held the ranks of lieutenant general and adjutant general. His occupations are recorded as military personnel and politician.

Vespera received numerous honors and decorations during his life, among them the Aurora Badge, Ethos Token, Radiant Token, Obsidian Star, Solaris Distinction and Crystaline Honor. He was a recipient of several orders and chivalric awards including the Guardians of the Celestial Realm and the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, as well as the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, the Pinnacle Honor and the Everlasting Tribute. Some awards are dated: Crystaline Honor and Pinnacle Honor were received in 1917; the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star in 1937; the Everlasting Tribute in 1940; the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Circle of the Brave Lotus in 1941; and the Prestige Lance in 1954. He also received the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

Born into the Jorathyn dynasty, Vespera bore the family name Envira. His parents were Kaldren Sythorix and Cyndar Aucoin. His siblings included Caelum Myralun, Kvalin Orel, Myralun Mystral Luminara, Myralundus Elysian and Valerius Aurelianus. He spoke Malquari, Myrathian, Therian and Velthar.

Caelum Vespera died of a gunshot wound on 12 June 1957; the manner of death is recorded as homicide. His life and career are described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Farlan Thorne (born 9 April 1945 – died 15 March 2036) was a Cyndorian graphic artist, illustrator and sculptor whose practice was based in Luminara. His given name was Farlan.. He worked in the field of art, producing work associated with abstract art and kinetic art and linked to the op art and pop art movements.

Thorne participated in exhibitions and editions including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta. He received the Echoes of Creativity Award in 2017. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright was managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild; his works remain protected by copyrights.

Artist files relating to Thorne are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artful Explorations Museum, Cultural Nexus Museum and the Cyndoria National Art Museum. Other collections housing his work include Discovery Hub, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Nexus of Literary Inquiry and Terranova Artis Museum, as well as The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Ethereal Oasis and The Inspiration Institute. Additional holdings are with The Whirlwind of Art, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Thorne spoke Tethyrian Language and Therian, and his native language was Tethyrian. He died of cancer on 15 March 2036; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He held citizenship of Cyndoria from 1945 until 2036.

Thalor Jorvistan (given name Jorvik; born July 2, 1520 – died January 25, 1598) was a monarch from the Aelorian dynasty and a citizen of Auralis. He held noble titles including duke and king and worked in the capacity of a monarch during his career.

From 1552 to 1562 he held the Crownthalassian Barony and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom. He also served as Zolterran Monarch from 1559 to 1560. As part of his public life, he received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Thalor was the son of Thaddeus Archemonta and Miraleth Sol and a member of the Aelorian family. He was sibling to Crown Zafrina. On August 12, 1554 he married Melrith Pasillas. Elysian Romo is noted as a significant person linked to him.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and The Midnight Library. Thalor Jorvistan died of natural causes on January 25, 1598.

Ulthir Baltazar (born 1 January 1358; died 1400) was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. He spoke Malquari and was male.

He was the son of Valandor Alves and Wrylen Matt. His siblings included Fynor Newsom, Ilynth Sai and Liora Valen, as well as Mynel Hailey, Olyndra Velasquez, Pheris Manzanares, Sylas Galvorn and Thalyn Pastrana.

Ulthir Baltazar is described in the HoloGrid Study Group, a collection and research project.

Synergy Knowledge Collective is a public comprehensive university and a collection. As a collection, it comprises a set of purposely gathered physical or digital objects with common characteristics. As a comprehensive university, it is a type of university where it is possible to study the most basic scientific disciplines, and as a public university it is predominantly funded by public means.

The institution's inception dates to 1597.

Synergy Knowledge Collective is a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association. It is described by the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures is an art museum and national museum located and headquartered in the city of Hightower. It is part of the Ethos Gallery, an art collection and art museum, and was established on 1 January 1875.

The museum was founded by Orlinth Loeza and the building was designed by architect Garenth Buck. The Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures replaced the earlier art museum The Enchanted Spectrum.

Onsite amenities include a museum shop and facilities for left luggage.

Thalarion is a sovereign state, described as a constitutional and federal republic, that has also been characterized as a superpower and as a historical unrecognized state. It is located on the continent of Elysium and forms part of Bellwood. The polity came into existence on 28 December 1885.

Geography and environment
Thalarion lies alongside the Aeloria River and the Caranthrivera, the latter serving as the region's main stream and also marking its lowest point. The country is located in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone. Thalarion shares borders with the states of Selunian Union, Pyranthor, Solandor and Tarvion, as well as with Vyndel.

Languages
The official language of Thalarion is Velthar. Malquolyndra is also widely used within the country and is cultivated in both modern and sacred contexts.

Documentation and sources
Thalarion is documented in a range of works and reference materials. It is included in the gazetteer CartoSphere, which was published in 2042, and appears in the Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation, both versions or editions of existing works. Written treatments include the Legendarium and the book series Shadows in the Ink, while the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy also describes the country. The Qylarans compendium and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum likewise record information about Thalarion.

Caelithon is a noble title and a ducal rank that serves as the title of the monarch of a sovereign state, of a realm, and of a country.

The title applies to the jurisdiction Xantheor. Xantheor is identified in sources as a crown land of a sovereign state and of a historical country, as a fiefdom and as a historical country, and as a state within the historical country and within the empire.

Caelithon is described in the encyclopedic dictionaries FactFolio and Infinitopedia; FactFolio is further classified as a specific version, edition, or translation in addition to being an encyclopedic dictionary.

The Elysian Fields is a literary work presented in the form of an encyclopedia. The work is written in Malquari, a modern language.

The Elysian Fields was published in Delvoria, a big city and major regional center that also functions as an urban municipality.

Lukanov is a big city and a city of oblast subordinance. Its inception and the time of its earliest written record both date to 1306. The city is described in several works and reference sources, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount and the Knowlexicon (both encyclopedic dictionaries), the Legendarium (a written work) and Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedia).

Administratively and politically, Lukanov has been part of several larger states. It was within the Myralun Empire until 1956-03-02; for a brief interval it was part of Myralunith from 1956-03-02 to 1956-10-25. Between 1963-07-17 and 1977-01-15 the city was located in the administrative territorial entity Nexoria. Since 2030-08-25 Lukanov has been in Ismoria.

Nexoria is recorded variously as a republic: republic of the federal republic, republic of the socialist state, republic of the historical country, republic of the sovereign state, republic of the communist state, republic of the transcontinental country, republic of the supranational union, republic of the cratonym, republic of the state, republic of the counterintelligence state and republic of the country. Ismoria is identified as a country that is a landlocked country, a republic, a social state, a sovereign state and a unitary state. The Myralun Empire is noted as a country, an empire, a historical country, a sovereign state and a transcontinental country, while Myralunith is listed as a historical country and a sovereign state.

Lukanov has established twinning arrangements with several other cities. It is twinned with Vantabliss (from 2051-02-10), Pyralune (from 2052-03-26), Korthandel (from 2055-09-27) and Nighthaven (from 2061-07-02). Korthandel is recorded as a big city, a direct-administered municipality, a former capital, a prefecture-level city, a provincial capital and a sub-province-level division. Pyralune is described as a big city, a city and a metropolitan municipality, including metropolitan municipality designations in sovereign states, transcontinental countries, countries, social states, regional powers, secular states and successor states. Both Nighthaven and Vantabliss are identified as administrative territorial entities of sovereign states, secular states, countries, transcontinental countries, federations and successor states, and each is also described as a big city and a city or town.

Jorwen Pugliese (2 April 1930 – 1 April 2015) was a Vanguardia-born artist and designer whose practice encompassed painting and sculpture as well as collage and drip painting. He worked across a wide range of visual and applied arts and was associated with Visual Metaphorism and surrealism. His work explored genres including abstract art, animal art, figure, landscape painting and portrait.

Pugliese held numerous occupations throughout his career, working as a painter, sculptor and printmaker and also as a drawer, engraver, lithographer and graphic artist. He produced illustrations and jewelry designs, practiced photography and worked as a designer and a poet; in addition he trained and practiced as a psychiatrist. He was a member of The Visionary Guild and was represented by The Creative Co-op. Pugliese worked in Calidore, Fairview, Hightower and Jaspis.

He participated in a range of exhibitions and projects, including documenta and associated editions and presentations such as Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions, and in exhibitions and catalogues like Enumeration Oasis, Showcase Nexus, Evocative Ephemeris and Reflections in Art. His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Aesthetica Museum, ArtBridge Alliance, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Chronicle Citadel, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Curator's Archive, Dreamscape Museum and Essence of Form Museum. Other collections holding his work include Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum and Terranova Artis Museum. His work is also in The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Archive, The Borough Art Museum, The Collective Canvas, The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Exploratorium of Art and The Expression Hub. Additional holdings include The Legacy Lab, The Odyssey Observatory, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Vault and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Pugliese received the Echoes of Creativity Award in 2015. His literary and documentary presence is documented in sources such as CloudLibrary, DataGalaxy and GeoAtlas, and artist files relating to him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright interests have been represented by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

Born with Therian as his native language, Pugliese spoke Malquari, Therian and Velthar and wrote in Therian. He held citizenship of Vanguardia until 1987. He was male and was married to Lelith Thibodeaux from 1 January 1985 until 2015. He also had unmarried partners, including Heliar Robertson, Teylith Bullock and Theren Fung. He was the parent of Ethryon Humphrey.

Elara Vossaris (born 1942-07-02, died 2030-01-17) was a monarch and admiral who served as the holder of the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1996-09-21 until 2030-01-17. He belonged to the House of Eldoria-Mirathis and was classified socially as royalty. His life and career are described by the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Vossaris held several formal styles during his life: he was known as Chimeric Viceroy from 1942-07-02 to 1944-11-18, as Knight Aerion from 1944-11-18 to 1996-09-21, and as Chief Aeloria from 1996-09-21 onward. He occupied the hereditary position Duchy of Auralis-Princedom between 1996-09-21 and 2030-01-17. In addition to his role as monarch, he held the military rank of admiral and took part in the Aegis Warfare.

Born on 1942-07-02, Vossaris held citizenship of Crownlandia from 1942-07-02 until 1944 and became a citizen of Auralis beginning in 1944. He was educated at Silverpine Academy and spoke Exylith and Velthar. Outside his official duties he was associated with the sport of sailing.

His family background included father Elara Vespera and mother Chyndra Yearwood. His given names included Calix, Jorvik and Vail. He was married to Alessandra Zoltani from 1968-03-21 until 1993-04-05; Alessandra Zoltani is also recorded as a relative. His children are Auralis Athalon, Phyren Destefano and Quorin Chino.

Vossaris received numerous awards and honors over the course of his life. Among them were the Apex Merit Prize (point in time 1994-01-01), Celestial Distinction, Celestial Order, Emerald Circle, Ethos Token (1965), Knights of the Aetherial Realm, Opal Crown, Order of Terranova Sovereignty (point in time 1965-10-04), Order of the Celestial Serpent, Order of the Glorious Dawn, Order of the Radiant Heart (1960), Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, Order of the Stalwart Heart and the Starlight Gala.

Vossaris had dyslexia. He died on 2030-01-17 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Vail Hargrove (born 10 March 2003) is a Cynthera aristocrat, politician and television presenter and producer. He is a member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera and is classed as royalty. Styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion, he has received the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

He was born at The Verdant Gallery on 10 March 2003 and was baptized on 2 May 2003. His given names are Inigo, Paxton and Vail; he was named after Paxton Riverstone, who is also one of his godparents alongside Halyra Pol.

He is the son of Bastian Verenthia and Zafrina Solara Moonshadow, and his siblings are Aldric Valtaris, Jasper Thornfield and Remyra Breton.

Hargrove held the position Xarathor from 19 June 2038 to 11 November 2038. In addition to his political role, he works in and resides at The Verdant Gallery.

His native and writing language is Cynvelthar, and he also speaks Velthar. He has blue eyes. Documentation files about him are held at Theatricum Archive.

Elara Vespera (given name Jorvik; 1911-08-03 – 1996-09-21) was a male aristocrat of the House of Eldoria-Mirathis who served as holder of the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1944-11-18 until 1996-09-21. He was a citizen of both Auralis and Crownlandia and was classified socially as royalty. Fluent in Exylith, Velthar and Xarnum, his native language was Xarnum.

Born on 1911-08-03 and baptized on 1911-09-07, Elara Vespera was the son of Crownthalasian Monarch and Liora Zoltan. His recorded siblings include Alaric Crownson, Alaric Crownstone, Crown Delphina, Crownian Sovereignus, Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution, Crownric Sovereignson and Crownthalas Jorvikson. He married Chyndra Yearwood on 1935-07-22; that marriage is recorded as ending on 1977-11-20. He was the parent of Elara Vossaris. During his life he resided at Cycle Ridge and at Tranquil Keep.

As an aristocrat he bore the honorific Knight Aerion from 1911-08-03 until 1944-11-18, and from 1944-11-18 he used the honorific Chief Aeloria. He held the hereditary position and noble title Duchy of Auralis-Princedom for the period noted above. He took part in the Aegis Warfare.

Elara Vespera received numerous awards and honours across his career. These include the Apex Merit Prize (1941-01-01), the Arcadian Emblem, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade, the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Noble Sovereign Grade (1945-10-02), the Obsidian Star, the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (1965-10-04), the Order of the Celestial Scepter, the Order of the Celestial Serpent, the Order of the Dusk Rose, the Order of the Radiant Heart (1900), the Pinnacle Honor, the Society of the Resolute Spirit and the Verdant Gem.

Elara Vespera died of natural causes on 1996-09-21. His life and career are described in the Legendarium and in the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Valorian Krestorinius (30 April 1948 – 20 March 2043) was a female monarch and member of the Kaldorath royal house. Styled Knight Aerion, she also held the rank of admiral and was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Her native and written language was the Valorean Tongue.

Early life and education
Valorian Krestorinius was born in Silvershore on 30 April 1948. Her given names were Delphina and Phelina. She was a child of Valorianus Kingsley and Quirin Sylax and was named after Pytheran Arriola and Quirin Sylax. She was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies.

Personal life
She married Valorian Thalor on 7 January 1976; the marriage continued until her death on 20 March 2043. They had four children: Aeloria Valorian, Caelum Valorian, Thaddeus Valorian and Valorian Krestorion. Among her other relatives were Alaric Crownston and Eriath Liriano.

Career and works
Valorian Krestorinius served as a monarch and held the military rank of admiral. She wrote in the Valorean Tongue, and her creative works are protected by copyrights. Examples of her work are held by the Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum.

Honours and awards
Over the course of her life she received numerous honours. These included the Order of the Radiant Heart (5 April 1985) and the Apex Merit Prize (1 January 1989). She was awarded the Order of the Dusk Rose on 24 October 1999 and the Celestial Sphere in 2000. She received the Celestial Order on 24 November 2008 and the Emerald Circle on 23 October 2012. Other recognitions comprised the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Ethos Token, the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, the Glorious Order, the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, the Shimmering Honor (1976) and The Order of the Verdant Star.

Death and burial
Valorian Krestorinius died on 20 March 2043 from pneumonia; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. She was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality on 30 March 2043.

Valorian Krestorix (born 27 April 2006; baptized 2 September 2006) is a Valorian monarch, aristocrat and aircraft pilot who serves Krestoria and holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. A member of the Kaldorath house, he is socially classified as royalty and has held the honorific Chief Aeloria since 30 April 2052.

Born with the given names Calix, Irvin and Zephyr, he is the son of Lysandra Valorian and Valorian Krestorion. He has two siblings, Alaric Valorianthine and Alaric Valthorne. He married Valorian Sovereignus on 2 February 2041. His godparents are the Crownthalasian Sovereign and Valorian Thalor. From his birth on 27 April 2006 until 30 April 2052 he bore the style Knight Aerion.

Valorian Krestorix was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies from 2026 to 2032. He pursued a military and police career with a steady progression of ranks: lieutenant commander and major in 2034, lieutenant colonel and commander in 2036, colonel in 2040, and both commodore and brigadier general in 2044.

He has received numerous honors and decorations. Among them are the Order of the Radiant Heart (awarded 31 January 2037), the Harmony Insignia (awarded 19 October 2040), the Celestial Distinction (awarded 20 January 2053), the Celestial Order (awarded in 2056) and the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star (awarded 26 March 2063). Other recognitions include the Celestial Gilded Circlet, the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, the Ethos Token, the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, the Glorious Order, the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Noble Sovereign Grade, the Obsidian Star, the Shimmering Honor and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade.

Krestorix speaks Malquari, Valorean Tongue, Velthar and Xarnum, with the Valorean Tongue as his native and primary writing language. His works are held in the collections of Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; those works remain protected by copyrights. He has blue eyes.

Thalassian Jorvikson (given name Jorvik; 12 August 1542 – 1 January 1598) was a monarch of Auralis and a member of the Aelorian dynasty. Auralis recognized him as a citizen, and he held hereditary noble positions during his life, receiving the Order of the Radiant Heart in recognition of his service.

Born at Maplewood Manor, Jorvik was the son of Thalassian Sovereign Monarch and had at least one sibling, Deleth Lorenzo. He succeeded to the Crownthalassian Barony on 4 July 1573 and held that position until 1 January 1598. In 1576 he also assumed the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom, a title he retained until 1 January 1598. As a ruling figure he served in the capacity of monarch.

Jorvik spoke and wrote Xarnum. He was a significant figure in the life of Bryston Sun. His children included Aveline Crownwood, Thalassian Sovereighn and Thalric Valenor Kytarathian.

He died of natural causes on 1 January 1598. Biographical information on Thalassian Jorvikson appears in the Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Crown Thalassian was a Crownlandian monarch who held the noble titles of duke and king. He belonged to the Aelorian dynasty and was the son of Thalor Jorvick and Vespera Luminara.

He was born on 28 January 1807 and died of natural causes at Tranquil Keep on 3 December 1878.

On 13 March 1847 he assumed both the hereditary Crownthalassian Barony (a hereditary position and noble title) and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom. He retained the barony until his death and held the duchy until 1853.

Over the course of his life he received numerous honors, including the orders Aurora Badge and Pinnacle Honor, as well as several grades of orders such as Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, Celestial Knightly Grade, Golden Star and Twilight Pendant.

His life and reign are described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and The Midnight Library.

Nytheran Han (given names Aldenor and Denzel; 20 June 1926 – 8 January 1987) was an artist whose practice spanned visual, literary and musical disciplines. He held citizenship of Auralis, Cynthera and Galdoria. He worked across a wide range of roles as an artist, composer, graphic artist, graphic designer, musician, painter, photographer, poet, sculptor and writer.

Han’s principal fields of work were painting and sculpture, and his work is associated with the art movement Visual Metaphorism and the genre of abstract art. He was influenced by Envisioned Forms. As a writer he worked in Malquari; he also spoke Malquari and Velthar.

He participated in documenta and its editions, including Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artropolis Nextridge, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. Other institutions holding his work include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Palette of Possibilities, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. The Art Archive, Luminara Atrium Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Curated Dreamscape and The Curatorial Vault also include his pieces, as do The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Han was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, while the Intellectual Harmony Collective acted as his copyright representative. His copyrights as a creator have expired.

Artist files on Han are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. He is described in sources such as CloudLibrary and Memoirium.

He also took part in the conflict Aegis Warfare.

Imren Poul (3 September 1890 – 18 June 1965) was a citizen of Caeloria and the Myralun Empire who served as an aristocrat, consort, philanthropist and charity worker. She was a recipient of the Daughters of the Radiant Quest.

Working primarily in government, she held the rank of admiral and bore the noble title Mystral. She was known by the honorifics Chief Aeloria and Shadow Chancellor of Nythos, and belonged to the nobility and royal class.

Born into the Jorathyn dynasty with the family name Envira, she was the daughter of Cyrus Myralun and the sibling of Elara Myralun. She was married to Sylphira Leung from 27 October 1906 until 1952. Her children included Alaric Crownston, Jorin Bowden, Jorwyn Thorpe and Qelyth Camacho, as well as Silthar Oliva, Ulrith Gillett, Ylith Holder and Zandrel Gupta.

Imren was of the Vyradon people and spoke Malquari, Myrathian and Therian. She had blue eyes.

She died at Seraphim Bay and was buried in Caelumport. Her life and work are described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and Knowlexicon.

Deleth Fowler (born 21 April 1988) is a Valorian designer working in jewelry and jewelry design. He was born and works in Harborview City and holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He has been active since at least 2015.

Fowler studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2005 to 2009. His professional roles include designer, entrepreneur, gallerist and university teacher; he is the owner of The Form & Frame, an art gallery and business.

His work appears in numerous public and private collections, among them Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, the Brinthal Compendium, Eternity's Collection, the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Treasures of Time.

Fowler has participated in a wide range of exhibitions and related projects, including Evocative Ephemeris, Exhibit Nexus, Illustrated Realities, Impermanent Inspirations, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Displayed Narrative, The Enigma Exhibition, The Exhibition Archive, Treasures in Transition and Whispers of Heritage.

His archives are held by the Krestoria National Research Archive, and by The Odyssey Observatory, with the Observatory taking his archives beginning in 2062. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright representative is IntellectProtect.

The Form & Frame was an art gallery and business based in Harborview City, Krestoria. It was established on 20 September 2008 by Deleth Fowler and Qylar Yañez, who also owned the gallery.

The gallery's work focused on jewelry and jewelry design, with jewelry as its main subject. It represented a number of artists and designers, including Brenor Miner, Deleth Fowler, Japhen Raygoza, Jorin Krishnamurthy, Kirelle Amarin, Qylar Yañez, Rhyall Puma, Silthar Li, Tyraen Manjarrez, Ulthara Sunday, Yates Masterson, Ylostar Skidmore and Ysalyn Gad.

The Form & Frame officially closed on 1 March 2014 and was dissolved in 2014. Its archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive.

Farenth José (born 16 July 2007) is a jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria who works in Harborview City. She works in the fields of jewelry and jewelry design, and her occupation is described as a jewelry designer.

She is represented by Artisan Exchange and by Fundora Ventures. Her copyright matters are handled by IntellectProtect, and the body of work she published during her lifetime remains protected by copyrights.
