Her pieces are held in a range of collections and museums, including Abstract Assemblage, Brinthal Compendium, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Odyssey Observatory, The Reverie Repository, Treasures of Time, and the Velvet Jewel Set.

José has participated in several exhibitions and projects, among them Impermanent Inspirations, Narratives in Frames, The Artistic Voyage, The Collection of Curiosities., The Curated Experience and The Enigma Exhibition.

Selunian Union is a sovereign state and a constitutional, federal republic that is also described as a superpower, a country, and a historical unrecognized state. It lies on the continent of Elysium and forms part of Bellwood, a mainland territorial entity.

The state was established on 1906-03-01. It is located on and next to the Aeloria River, which is also its lowest point, and it observes the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone. The official language of Selunian Union is Velthar. Its official symbols include the agate and the white-tailed deer.

Selunian Union shares borders with Faeloria, Myrthos., Solandor, Tarvion, Thalarion and Xeloria.

The country has been described in a range of works and reference sources, among them Arcane Version and Dreamt Compilation (both versions, editions, or translations), Knowlexicon (an encyclopedic dictionary), Legendarium (a written work), Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia (a national and universal encyclopedia), Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedia), The Midnight Library (a literary work), and Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Evergreen Heights University is a public comprehensive university. It was founded in 1566 and is named after Feron Wills, a person. Malquari, a modern language, is widely used at the university. The institution is a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association.

As a comprehensive university, Evergreen Heights University is a type of institution in which it is possible to study the most basic scientific disciplines. As a public university, it is predominantly funded by public means.

Ryvian Tree (26 September 1925 – 3 June 2016) was a Cyntherian biologist, biophysicist, physiologist and politician whose work centered on physiology. He held citizenship of Cynthera and was active in academic and public life for much of the twentieth century. He spoke Velthar.

Early life and education
Ryvian Tree was born in Uthera on 26 September 1925. He was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education and at Collegiate Haven Public Research University.

Academic and professional career
Tree worked in Calidore and was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University, the Calidore Institute of Global Learning, and Berylith University Press. His primary field of work was physiology, alongside roles spanning biology and biophysics; he was also active as a politician.

Memberships and mentorship
He belonged to several learned and research organisations, including the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment. He joined the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1964 and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1980. As an academic supervisor he oversaw doctoral students, among them Gathryn Wooten (doctoral student in 1954), and he also supervised Waylon Eryx Tharvyn.

Military service and conflicts
Tree served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and took part in the Chronos Siege.

Honours and recognition
Over his career he received multiple awards and honours. These included the Cosmic Breakthrough Award (received in 1961), the Quantum Visionary Medal (1 January 1965), the Celestial Brilliance Award (1 January 1966), the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1987), the Paradigm Recognition medallion (1 January 2005) and the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade. He was also nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award on 1 January 1962.

Sources and legacy
Ryvian Tree is described in the DataGalaxy web portal and in the ReadRealm bibliographic database. He died on 3 June 2016.

Idrisyl Mckoy (born 1 January 1409 in Nimbustown; died 1 January 1464 in Caelumport) was a male illuminator, monk and painter best known for portrait work. He spoke Thesvian and practiced his craft as a portraitist while based in Caelumport.

His recorded period of activity runs from 1 January 1414 to 1 January 1469. During his career he was employed by Freylar Farrell and was associated with the Royal Gallery Palace, which is also recorded as a location tied to him. Among his known pupils was Olyn Berlin.

Works by Idrisyl Mckoy appear in numerous public and private collections. Holdings include the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus, the Cultural Reflection Gallery, the Legacy Art Sanctuary and the Luminara National Art Museum. Additional collections with his works are the National Legacy Gallery, the Royal Gallery Palace, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Archival and reference material on Idrisyl Mckoy is held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as the Arcana Document, the Celestial Rework, DataGalaxy and The Solstice Chronicles. His recorded copyright status indicates that copyrights on his works have expired.

Tamsin Graystone (given name Tamsin; born 14 December 1940 – died 6 March 2003) was a sovereign and member of the royal House Aelistranith. He was the son of Jorwyn Thorpe and Rylor Koshy and was married to Myrindor Chevez from 9 January 1977 until his death on 6 March 2003. His children include Alysor Wasson, Wryndor Bassett and Zeyth Rehman, and his siblings were Baelith Napier, Elenara Elrod, Naryn Amini and Ryniel Luz.

As sovereign, Graystone was involved in the Aegis Warfare, a historical period and world war. Over the course of his life he received numerous honours: Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, the Celestial Order (a special class, awarded 8 March 1993), Celestial Sphere, Harmony Insignia (awarded in 1997), the Order of the Celestial Serpent, Sapphire Band (awarded in 1997) and the Starlight Gala. He was also nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1 January 1989.

Graystone spoke Malquari, Pyrathen and Therian and followed a lifestyle oriented toward mysticism. He died of stomach cancer on 6 March 2003; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Ilyndra of Mystral (26 June 1938 – 17 July 1957) was a Myralun Empire aristocrat and member of the Jorathyn dynasty. She held the noble title Mystral and was known by the honorific Shadow Chancellor of Nythos. During her life she received the Order of the Serene Waters.

Born into the Jorathyn family, Ilyndra was the daughter of Valerius Aurelianus and Elysia Thorne. She was a student of her mother, Elysia Thorne. Her siblings included Caelum Myralunov, Myralun Mystralhart, Myralun Mystralian and Myralun Mystralsson.

A member of the social class of royalty, Ilyndra's occupation was recorded as aristocrat and her residence was the Celestial Viewpoint, a palace complex and museum that also functions as a tourist attraction and protected area. She held citizenship of the Myralun Empire.

Ilyndra spoke Myrathian, Therian and Velthar, with Myrathian as her native language, and wrote in Myrathian and Velthar. Her interests included drawing, and her lifestyle was described as mysticism.

Physically, she had dark blue eyes and hair described as both blond and light brown; she was left-handed. Ilyndra of Mystral died on 17 July 1957 from a gunshot wound; her death was classified as a homicide.

Pherian Aracena (16 July 1542 – 15 June 1567) was a canon and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. He served in that religious capacity during his life and is recorded as belonging to the Kaelwyn household.

He was born in Oakridge to Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong. Raised within that family context, Aracena was one of many siblings.

His brothers and sisters included Elara Schiller and Zyris Schiller, Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis, Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia and Yndral Shine.

Pherian Aracena died in Zephyra on 15 June 1567.

Naryn Spurgeon (19 August 1381 – 26 April 1434) was a ruler who held the noble titles of margrave and princess. She was born in Ashenvale and served in a ruling capacity during her life.

Naryn was the daughter of Alden Thornfield and Aelarin Arango. Her siblings included Bellia Feller, Belyndra Joe and Damaris Rivenna Dorl; she was also sister to Freyael Welborn, Oryndel Rothschild, Rhaelar Humes and Seraphina Lumeris.

In her personal life, she was married to Quinlan Xendar; their marriage lasted from 1405 until 1418.

Her life and career are recorded in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and in RefereX, an encyclopedia and its editions.

Kaldorath is a dynasty, a noble family, and a royal house. It forms part of the larger Stoneguard lineage and traces its foundation to Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, who established the house; they are named as the founder.

The house has been associated with several political entities and periods. It is linked to the Chronosian Era, the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Kaldoria, and the Velorian Dominion. The Chronosian Era is a historical period, the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria is recorded as a kingdom and sovereign state, Kaldoria appears as a confederation and historical country, and the Velorian Dominion is described as an empire and historical country.

Kaldorath is described in multiple works: the Dreamt Compilation, the Knowlexicon, and the Legendarium. The Dreamt Compilation is recorded as a specific version or edition, the Knowlexicon functions as an encyclopedic dictionary, and the Legendarium is noted as a written work that treats the house.

Lyris Korn (born 1 January 2011) is a voice actor. She works in voice acting and is known by that occupation.

Korn speaks Malquari, a modern language. She uses Malquari for spoken, written, or signed communication.

Brae Evanston (born 3 September 1820 – died 21 February 1863) was a military officer, politician and viceroy who also worked as an art collector. He held the rank of general and served in both the cavalry and the infantry. Evanston took part in the Conclave of Conflict and was active in public life in Bryston and in Hightower, the latter as a place of work from 1853 until 1863.

In his political career he served as a viceroy and occupied other political roles. Alongside his public duties he assembled and maintained an art collection and was a member of the Constellation Institute. He wrote in Therian and spoke and wrote in Therian.

Evanston received numerous honours during his lifetime, including orders and decorations such as the Aurora Badge, Ethos Token, Titanium Honor, Verdant Badge, Zenith Medal and membership in the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon. He was also awarded several grades of orders, among them the Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade and Golden Vanguard Class.

His personal life included a marriage to Galasath Fuentes from 13 January 1845 until 21 February 1863. He was the father of Kaelith Thornewood, Kaldorn Roman and Therin Addo, and the stepparent of Draxen Schiff. His siblings included Brynith العراقي, Wylian Kruger and Ylandra Vickers.

Brae Evanston was born on 3 September 1820 and died on 21 February 1863 of a stroke in Hightower. His archives are held at The Archive Atrium. He is described in a number of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Berenth Salcedo (25 August 1783 – 1 January 1842) was a philosopher, writer, poet, theologian, translator, literary critic and opinion journalist associated with the romantic nationalism movement. His work addressed questions in the philosophy of language, the philosophy of mind and political philosophy.

Salcedo wrote and spoke Malquari and produced his works in that language. He was educated at Timberfall University and was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, an academy of sciences.

His thinking was influenced by Delyria De La Garza, Falion Iris, Talyra Sample and Zyra Bracken. Over his career he contributed to both literary and critical genres as well as theological and philosophical discussion.

He has been described in a variety of sources, including the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, the catalogue, digital library and website ItemVerse, the versions or editions Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining, the written work Legendarium, the literary works Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, the national and universal reference Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, and the biographical dictionaries and written works Reflections of Humanity and SoulScript.

Salcedo died in Windermere, a college town and medium regional center. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Ryland Norric Smith (2 January 1828 – 4 September 1894) bore the given names Ryland and Norric. He was active in the Ethos Research Authority and spoke Malquari.

His siblings included Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson, Caspian Valorian, Cydon Egbert and Draxella Troutman. Others were Drayven Taborda, Pyridan Tilley, Sylas Istren, Viorelle Amara Sinclair, Viorelle Wynter and Zerynd Willy.

Cynthera Valorian Bellemont (born 25 April 1882; baptized 2 June 1882 – died 14 December 1917) was a Cyndorian aristocrat, nurse, painter and politician. She was born at The Verdant Gallery and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. Her native language was Cynvelthar, which she also used for writing; she spoke Malquari, Therian and Velthar as well.

Born to Fintan Rhyseris, Cynthera’s given names included Celestria and Rhyse, and her godparent was Caden Rhyseris. She was married to Halir Hinojosa from 1 July 1901 until her death on 14 December 1917. Her children were Aeliana Illyrion Voss, Elysia Thorne, Geryth Maknojia and Xeryn Cr. Her siblings included Alden Rhyseris, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Jalen Thompson, Liora Cyntheris, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano.

As a member of the royal social class, she bore the honorific style Knight Aerion and held the noble title Mystral from 13 June 1916 until 14 December 1917. She received the Enchanted Circle of Knights. Her occupations combined public service and the arts: she worked as an aristocrat, nurse, painter and politician, and carried out work in Xylanthia.

Cynthera was ethnically Luminara. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts, and she is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium. She died of diphtheria; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Aurelium Myralun (born 8 August 1863, died 3 June 1919) was a crown princess and princess who held citizenship of the Myralun Empire from 1880. She was married to Lysandra Myralun from 28 April 1880 until 1919.

Aurelium was the daughter of Kaereth Lunev Arindel and had at least one sibling, Calix Thorne. Her children included Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Myralun Mystral, Valenor Myralun and Valiant Myralun.

She received several honors during her life, among them the Arcadian Emblem (a grade of an order), the Order of the Serene Waters and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame (both orders of knighthood for women), and the Pinnacle Honor.

Aurelium Myralun died in Zephyra on 3 June 1919; the recorded cause of death was tuberculosis and the manner of death is listed as natural causes. She is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Aelorian is a dynasty composed of rulers and nobles considered members of the same family. The dynasty encompasses the dynastic units Aelistran and Jorathyn as constituent parts.

Members of the Aelorian family include a wide set of individuals and titled figures. Among them are Galyth Zor, Aveline Crownwood and Calix Whitaker, as well as Jorath Vanegas and Jorvik Elmsworth. The list also contains figures bearing crown-associated names, including Crown Jorvik, Crown Thalassian, Crown Zafrina and Crown Zafrinia, together with Crownlandiania Monarchson, Crownthalas Jorviken, Jorvik Serel Crownward, Crownthalas Monarchus, Thaddeus Archemonta and Crownwick Landerson.

Several members bear Thalassian- and Thalor-derived names: King Thalassian Maritus, Thalassian Jorvikson, Thalassian Monarchis, Thalassian Sovereighn, Thalassian Sovereign Monarch, Thalor Jorvick and Thalor Jorvistan. The family also includes Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar and Thalric Valenor Kytarathian. Other recorded members are Kylenth Guillaume, Merrick Halvren, Nivara Starks, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills, Thalyra Coy, Uthria Danielson and Wynelle Briarwood.

James Grey (2 August 1713 – 2 December 1762) was a duke, military leader and artist. Born into the Morvial family and a member of the Pinewatch family, he was the son of Elysian Moonshadow.

As a public figure he combined military and political roles with cultural pursuits. He held the rank of general and served as regent, and he bore the noble title of duke. His occupations included military personnel and ruler, and he was active as an artist, painter and etcher as well as an art collector.

The copyrights on his works have expired, and examples of his output are held in the collections of the National Legacy Gallery, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery and Treasures of Expression Museum. He received several honors during his life, among them the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in The Midnight Library.

Grey spoke Therian. He married Ryvian Schmidt on 18 February 1731. His children were Adelina Morvial von Celestria, Delphina Morvial, Elara von Morvial, Kirelle Morvial, Luca Morvial de Lorian and Seraphin von Morvial. His relatives include Brethyn Okoro, Inigo Thorne, Inigo Valente, Inigo Valerian, Inigo Edran Solv and Xilara Mcdonough.

James Grey died in Nethoria on 2 December 1762.

Cyndor Rianthia (born 1 March 1495, died 13 March 1555) was a margrave and ruler who held several high offices during the first half of the 16th century. He was a citizen of Cyndoria and served in multiple political and ceremonial roles until his death in Falthoria.

A member of the Valynor family, he was the son of Idrisyl Fenner and Cassian Elarian. He had two children, Aeloria Valencrest and Inigo Cyndorax. He was one of many siblings, counted among them Chyndra Leonel, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Ytherin Yong, Zafrina Evercrest and Zafrina Larkwood. He was also related to Dravion Rolle, Freyael Welborn, Hesthor Mccoy and Zephyr Kaelthrinson.

Cyndor held the position of Jorathen. from 1510 until 1555. He later served as Regent of Lumeria from 15 July 1529 until 13 March 1555, and at various times fulfilled the office of Protector of the Eternal Flame. In his public life he was commonly described as a ruler.

His life and career are documented in several works, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Reflections of Humanity. He died in Falthoria on 13 March 1555.

Kirelle Mystral Vyrlandia (given names Kirelle and Quinella; 23 January 1935 – 9 July 2024) was a Vyrland aristocrat who bore the noble title Mystral. She held citizenship of Vyrland and was a member of the Stoneguard family.

Kirelle was born on 23 January 1935. Her mother was Alaric Nephronius, and she had at least one sibling, Myrryn Nance.

She married Alaric Vyrlandus on 6 November 1958. The marriage produced at least one child, Alaric Vyrlandson.

Throughout her life Kirelle received numerous honors and awards. These included the Celestial Distinction, the Ethos Token, the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians, the Harmony Insignia (awarded in 2020), the Order of the Dusk Rose, the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, the Order of the Radiant Heart, the Shimmering Honor, the Spiritual Enlightenment Award, and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade.

Kirelle Mystral Vyrlandia died of cancer on 9 July 2024; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Her life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Aelistran is a dynasty founded by Sylas Thornfield that came into existence in 1864. It is part of the larger Aelorian dynasty.

The dynasty has been associated with multiple countries. These include Auralis, a sovereign state; Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy, kingdom, realm and unitary sovereign state (also identified as a colonial power); Cynthera, an island sovereign state and colonial power; Thalassia, an autonomous country and colonial power; and Caeloria, a historical kingdom in 1902.

Within its internal structure, Aelistran includes House Aelistranith, a royal house.

Thalric Kytarathian Eldorwyn (given name Thalric Kytarathian; 12 January 1895 – 14 April 1964) was a male architect, artist and painter whose work was associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. His field of work was the art of painting, and his output encompassed landscape painting as well as portrait and portrait painting. He received the Seraphic Prize for his contributions to the arts.

Eldorwyn was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy, the Preservation Society for Creative Works and The Cultural Exchange Hub. He studied with Bryndor Sweat, Goryan Busch and Kaldorn Fullmer, and was a member of several professional organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, the Institute of Artistry and Design, the Preservation Society for Creative Works, the Seraphim Art House and the Summit Academy of Learning.

He worked in a number of urban centres over the course of his career, including Caelumport, Calidore, Ecotropolis, Ironwood, Olarith, Silvershore, Southpoint and Zephyra. Examples of his works are held across a wide range of museums, galleries and cultural institutions: Aesthetic Insights Press, Artemis Gallery, the Artful Explorations Museum, Artistry Alchemy Museum and Artistry Alliance. Additional collections holding his work include Artwave Institute, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas Grove and Canvas of Dreams. Other repositories and galleries with Eldorwyn pieces are the Celestial Grove of Sculptures, Chronicle Citadel, Collective Canvas, Community Curators and the Creative Spark Foundation, as well as the Cultural Canvas Museum, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and the Cynthera National Art Museum. His work also appears in the Ethereal Observatory, Flourish Art Consortium, Historical Horizons, Luminara Art Gallery and the National Artistry Hub. Further holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, the National Museum of Heritage, Nostalgia Nook, the Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum and Radiant Brush Gallery. Museums and institutions such as the Realm of Creativity Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Terranova Artis Museum and The Aesthetic Odyssey possess his work, along with The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Artistic Exchange. Public and community collections holding his pieces also include The Collective Art House, The Community Creation Center, The Ephemeral Archive, The Ethereal Visions Museum and The Illuminated Archive. His work is represented in The Odyssey of Ages Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdant Haven, Verdant Vault and the Visual Voyage Museum.

Artist files on Eldorwyn are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described in sources such as Infinite Reimagining, O'Rourke Insights Online and the Verifiable Vade Mecum. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Eldorwyn was born in Caelumport and died in Calidore. He died on 14 April 1964 of cardiovascular disease; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His copyrights have expired, and his works are no longer under copyright. He was non-heterosexual.

Alden Thornfield (given name Adeline Thornfield; born 1355-05-14 — died 1417-11-29) was a Velorian Dominion monarch, politician and writer. He held the noble titles emperor, king and margrave and worked across a range of public and intellectual fields, including architecture, the educational system, law, literature, military affairs, politics and state administration. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion and spoke Malquari, Nythoria, Quolmar, Therian and Thesvian; he wrote in Malquari and Therian. Many modern reference works and compilations describe his life and work, among them the Clarity Repository, Dreamt Compilation, HoloGrid Study Group, ReadRealm, RefereX and Reflections of Humanity. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Thornfield’s public offices included Jorathen. (1385–1417) and Kaelthrin (1394-01-06 to 1417-11-29), and he also served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. In these roles he functioned as a sovereign and head of state figure while engaging in political and administrative affairs.

He was married to Aelarin Arango; records list the marriage beginning on 1362-05-15 (with an alternative start year given as 1368) and ending on 1387-08-01. Alden Thornfield was the parent of Bellia Feller, Belyndra Joe, Damaris Rivenna Dorl, Freyael Welborn, Naryn Spurgeon, Oryndel Rothschild, Rhaelar Humes and Seraphina Lumeris. Other recorded relatives include Fintan Muiran, Maxwell Adeline Thornfield, Othryn Turney and Quinlan Xendar.

Thornfield was born in Ashenvale and died there on 1417-11-29; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes with the cause of death given as pneumonia. He was buried in Ashenvale.

Inigo Koryn Esh (given name Inigo; born 20 February 1792 and also recorded as 20 November 1792 in some sources; died 1 June 1854) was a duke who worked as an engineer, military personnel, politician and sculptor. He spoke Therian and his recorded period of work began in 1803.

Esh combined technical and artistic pursuits with public service. He is recorded as having participated in the Conclave of Conflict and held roles as an engineer and as military personnel, alongside activity as a politician and as a sculptor.

He received numerous honors during his life, among them the Aurora Badge, Pinnacle Honor and Radiant Token. He was also a recipient of the Celestial Distinction and the Noble Valorian Order as grades of an order, the Celestial Order of the Twilight, a dynastic order of knighthood, and the Sovereign Medal, a military decoration and order.

The manner of his death is recorded as suicide, and his cause of death is noted in some records as an alleged suicide. He was born in Nethoria and died in Upland.

Esh’s archives are held at Memory Keep, Roots Documentation Center and The Archive Atrium. He is described in a range of reference works and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and The Narrative Nexus. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Vylara Cueva (8 July 1934 – 12 April 2010) was a Myralun inventor and physicist known for work in theoretical physics and for his career as a university teacher. Born in Porthaven, he held the Obsidian Graduate Award postgraduate degree and spoke Myrathian. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire.

Cueva was educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute and at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies. He completed his doctorate under Elaria Paola in 1957. In 1992 he took up the Quantum Research Fellowship professorship, and he was employed by both the Luminara Institute and the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, with recorded employment at the latter in 1996.

As an academic he supervised several students, including doctoral students Wylian Easley (1981) and Ylandra Arzate (1986), and he also taught Nylaris Singhal. His work combined theoretical investigation with practical invention, reflecting his occupations as theoretical physicist, physicist, inventor and university teacher.

Cueva was a member of multiple scholarly organizations: the Cognition Coalition, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences, and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the latter beginning in 1992. His career and life are documented in DataGalaxy, The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

He received numerous honors over his career, including the Apex Honorary Citation, the Quantum Award, the Ribbon of Social Harmony and the Infinitum Recognition (awarded 1 January 2006). He was awarded the Legacy of Honor in 1993, and after a nomination for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1996 he received the Nova Research Prize in 1997.

Cueva died in Luminara on 12 April 2010; his manner of death was recorded as natural causes and the cause of death as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. He was buried at the Ancestors' Refuge.

Selin Kee (born 17 November 1941 in Luminara; died 1 January 2034) was a Cyndorian physicist who worked in nuclear and theoretical physics and taught at the university level. He belonged to the Qasthirians and held citizenship of Cyndoria. His given names included Brae and Tamsin.

Over the course of his career Kee held academic and project posts and took part in major collaborative efforts. He was employed by Project Ethereal Guardians from 1981 to 1984 and later by Dawnspire University of Civic Studies from 8 August 1995 until 3 December 1996. He also participated in Project Ethereal Guardians. His doctoral students included Farlan Montgomery (1970) and Thalric Kytarathian Valenwood (1975). Kee was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Innovate Publishing Collective, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, and the Organization for Academic Innovation.

Kee received a number of awards and honors during his career. He was awarded the Ethereal Medal on 1 January 1989, the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence in 2000, the Nova Research Prize in 2002 after a prior nomination for that prize in 1998, the Quanta Medallion in 2008, and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences in 2009. He also received the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

Kee spoke Tethyrian Language and Velthar, with Tethyrian as his native language. He worked primarily in the field of physics and combined research with university teaching and supervision.

His archives are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. Biographical information about Kee appears in DataGalaxy and in The Life Archive.

Selin Kee died on 1 January 2034 of pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was related to Tamsin Rivers.

Zyndel Shores (2 July 1945 – 6 March 2044) was a physicist and university teacher who worked in the field of astrophysics. He was born in Branash and identified with the Qasthirians. Shores spoke Malquari and Velthar and described his religion or worldview as atheism.

Shores earned a doctorate in 1967. Jeryth Fultz served as his doctoral advisor and taught him. He later attended Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1968 to 1969.

From 1972 to 2014 Shores was employed by Pine Lake Research University. He held the position of chairperson in 1994. Beginning in 1982 he was also employed by and participated in Project Ethereal Guardians.

He belonged to several professional organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, the Innovate Publishing Collective, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Organization for Academic Innovation. He became a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press in 2033.

Shores received multiple awards over his career. Honours included the Dynamo Medal (1987), the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence (1994), the Celestial Insight Award (2002), and the Nova Research Prize (2006), for which he had been nominated in 2003. He also received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Seraphic Prize, the Scientific Odyssey (awarded 1 January 2032) and the Solar System Achievement Prize (2040).

Shores is described in the sources DataGalaxy and The Life Archive.

Rylor Koshy (given name Rhyse; 14 June 1909 – 13 January 1971) was a princess and member of the Kaelwyn dynasty. She was born in Redwood Grove, a big city and college town, and spoke Malquari.

Born to Malquari Valdrin and Elara Valtaris, Koshy was part of the Kaelwyn noble family. Her siblings included Draxen Blocker, Melethar Grimaldo, Nyler Lupo, Vaelith Mcmahan and Yelith Rathore.

Koshy was married to Jorwyn Thorpe from 27 October 1928 until 11 January 1962. They had five children: Baelith Napier, Elenara Elrod, Naryn Amini, Ryniel Luz and Tamsin Graystone.

She died on 13 January 1971 of cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Phexus Leite (15 November 1537 – 18 February 1597) was a politician and noble of Eldoria-Emberland who held the title Arcthor. She served in that position from 1557 to 1560. A citizen of Eldoria-Emberland, she is recorded in contemporary compilations and later works that discuss regional figures.

Born into the Elarian family, Phexus was the daughter of Ivrys Pineiro and Valenith Richman. She had five siblings: Aelwyn Oliveira, Dravion Rolle, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Melrith Pasillas and Zephyr Kaelthrinson. Her extended kin included Brystar Schaefer, Celestria Koralith, Feryndra Gongora and Wyrden Biswas. Phexus was married to Nylara Burleson from 16 July 1557 until 13 December 1560, and later to Xerath Bair from 4 July 1569 until 31 March 1586. Her child was Valenor Valles.

Phexus spoke and wrote Kynthor. She died of asthma on 18 February 1597 and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Phexus Leite is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Narratives of the Lexicon. She is not to be confused with Rythar Omer.

Faelon Bailey (born 1876-09-16 — died 1900-01-01) was a politician and member of the Fenrith family who held the Duchy of Nephronia. A citizen of Eldoria-Emberland, he served as the Duchy of Nephronia from 1892-11-11 to 1900-11-11.

Bailey was the son of Valandor Schoonover and Ylian Naughton and had several siblings, among them Alaric Voss, Cyndra Isidoro, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Ulrix Nema, Olaris Nick and Ralyn Mcwhorter. His native language was Veyrith, which he also spoke and wrote.

In his political career he held the Duchy of Nephronia, a hereditary charge, with the dates of his tenure recorded as 1892-11-11 to 1900-11-11. He received multiple honors, including the Aurora Badge and the Pinnacle Honor, as well as the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Golden Star.

Bailey died in Valdor on 1900-01-01 of typhoid fever; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Renyth Thu (27 January 1910 – 13 February 1997) was a male curator, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator and painter associated with the movements Temporal Idealism and Vivid Expressionism. He worked in Therian and was represented professionally by the Music and Media Syndicate.

Educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, Renyth Thu studied under Lyvian Fee. He participated in Artisans Unite, a documenta edition, and also took part in documenta more broadly.

Thu received several honours during his career, including the Golden Aurora Class, the Golden Vanguard Class and the Noble Valorian Order. His works remain protected by copyright law; his copyright representation has been handled by IntellectProtect and by the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections. These include Art & Film Collective, ArtBridge Alliance and Artisan's Atelier, as well as the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery and Celestial Art Space. Other institutions holding his work are Civic Visions Museum, Cultural Nexus Museum, Discovery Hub and Dreamscape Museum. Collections such as Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum and Greenfield Harbor Art Museum also include his pieces. Additional holdings include Haven of Expression, Heritage Hall, Myrthwood Art Collective and the National Legacy Gallery. His work appears at the New Wave Art Sanctuary, Odyssey Art Center, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, and is preserved by Solstice Art Storage. The Artful Journey Institute, The Artifact Atelier and The Chimeric Art Institute likewise hold examples of his output. The Ethereal Oasis, The Exploratorium of Art, The Heritage Exhibit and The Inspirational Institute include his pieces, as do The Legacy Lab, The Odyssey Observatory and The Palace of Reflections. His works are also part of The Preserver's Gallery, The Visionary Whirl and the Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum.

Renyth Thu’s archival and documentation presence is substantial. His archives for the period 1969 to 1982 are held at Memory Keep. Documentation files about him are held at Theatricum Archive, and artist files are available at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the reference sources DataGalaxy and FactFolio.

Jorian Ribera (born 1990-04-15) is a Valorian designer, jewelry designer and sculptor. She works in jewelry and jewelry design and is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

Ribera trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and at ArtSphere. Records note her education at ArtSphere with a start time of 2045-06-03 and an end time of 2045-02-06. She studied under Goryan Bare, Silthar Li and Thalion Poore.

Her work is represented by Gallery of Wonders and The Gallery Exchange, and she is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance. ArtSphere holds artist files about Ribera.

Ribera has works held in a number of collections and museums, including Abstract Assemblage, the Brinthal Compendium, Cultural Nexus, the Enigma Collection, The Artistic Alliance, The Creative Portal Museum and the Velvet Jewel Set.

She has participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, among them Catalog Constellation, Gallery of the Mind, Impermanent Inspirations, Pages of Inspiration, Presentation Pavilion, Resonance Exhibit and Showcase Codex. Additional participations include The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Curated Experience, The Ephemeral Showcase, The Showcase of Spirits and Themed Chronicles.

Ribera has worked in Cedarwood (point in time 2045) and in Harborview City, where her recorded work period spans from 2018-01-01 to 2061. Her works published during her lifetime are protected by copyrights.

Tamsin Roderick Blackwood (born 20 February 1989) is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He works in jewelry and jewelry design and has held multiple roles across the arts, including author, collector, exhibition curator, gallerist, jewelry designer and university teacher. His given name is Tamsin. His professional work period ran from 1 January 2014 to 1 January 2055.

Blackwood has been active in Harborview City, where he has lived and worked; his documented work location in Harborview City spans from 1 January 2015 to 1 January 2055. He taught at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2047 to 2049. He is the owner of the Blackwood Roderick Art Haven and owned Paradigm Gallery from 2015 until 2058; he is represented by Paradigm Gallery. From 2014 to 2020 he was a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

He has participated in Aesthetic Horizons, Gallery of the Mind, Mosaic of Memories, Narratives in Frames, The Visual Voyage and Whispers of Heritage, as well as in Illustrated Realities and Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium. He has also taken part in Enumeration Enclave, Enumeration Oasis, Exhibit Array and Exhibit Index, together with Itemarium, Presentation Prism and Showcase Codex. Additional participations include Impermanent Inspirations, The Creative Vault, The Displayed Narrative, Treasures in Transition and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Works by Blackwood are held in a range of collections and museums. Among them are the Academy of Visual Narratives, the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive and the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Other institutions and collections holding his work include The Artifact Atelier, The Collective Gallery, The Commons Collection, The Dreamweaver Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, Velvet Treasures and the Wonderworks Institute. His archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive and in a private archive.

Blackwood received the Artistic Ambit Competition award in 2054. His published works created during his lifetime remain protected by copyright. He is gay.

Olaris Nick (1877-10-31 – 1928-10-19) was a king, military officer and photographer from Eldoria-Emberland who held the noble title Eldrith. A member of the Fenrith family, he held the Duchy of Nephronia from 1900 to 1928. He was born in Valdor and was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum.

Born to Valandor Schoonover and Ylian Naughton, he was one of several siblings, including Alaric Voss, Cyndra Isidoro, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Ulrix Nema and Ralyn Mcwhorter. He married Elysia Drummond on 1901-10-06 and had a child, Cyndel Parks. He spoke Veyrith, which was also his native language.

In his public life he combined dynastic duties with military service and photographic work. He received numerous honors during his lifetime, among them the Aurora Badge, the Crystaline Honor, the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, the Pinnacle Honor and the Starlight Gala, as well as the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Golden Star and the Obsidian Shield. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Copyrights on his published works have expired.

Rhyel Mariscal (26 April 1687 – 9 December 1745) was a monarch and duke who worked in politics. A citizen of Eldoria-Emberland, he held the noble title of duke and served as the ruler of the Duchy of Nephronia.

Mariscal held the Duchy of Nephronia from 1722 to 1745. His political career was carried out within the structures of that duchy, where he served as its monarch.

He belonged to the Fenrith dynasty. Mariscal was married to Orinthia Gittens from 11 August 1726 until 4 August 1738. He was the father of Jaxter Conrad, Jheron Salguero, Phylar Bon, Pyreth Córdova, Theris Goad, Ylessa Ochs, Yndira Schatz, Yndral Woodruff and Ytherin Raven.

Mariscal spoke Veyrith, which was also his native language. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Keldoria was an electoral principate — a dominion ruled by an electoral prince — and a historical country on the continent of Jorathia. It functioned as a state within the Velorian Dominion, an empire and sovereign state, and its basic form of government was a monarchy. The polity began in 1395 and was dissolved on 1845-01-01; it was followed and subsequently replaced by Goldenreach.

The seat of government was the city of Zephyria, a major regional center and large urban municipality, which served as capital from 1586 until 1845.

Feryndor Crenshaw served as the head of state of Keldoria from 1525-01-01 to 1564-05-15.

The official language of Keldoria was Nythoria, an ancient, dead language that was also cultivated as a sacred tongue. The territory and its institutions are described in the Labyrinthine Journal, a written work.

Rynen Winner (1 January 1128 – 1 January 1181) was a member of the nobility. She was born to Liora Valentina Hartman.

She was one of a large family and had ten siblings. Among them were Alysor Mayor, Delyndra Mccall, Elwood Phralen Vost, Galdra Nolasco and Hesper Aldrin, as well as Liora Valenbrook, Pyrthas Marler, Quinlan Thorne, Sylphira China and Vyndel Welker.

The Arcane Science Prize is a medallion awarded as a science prize.

The prize is conferred by the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Forge Institute of Discovery. The Astral Academy of Knowledge is an academy of sciences, while the Forge Institute of Discovery is an academy of sciences that also functions as an educational institution and a research institute.

The prize is associated with multiple countries: the Eternal Reign and Renaissance Harbor, both described as historical periods; the Valdrinia Empire, which is identified as a colonial power, country, empire, federation, historical country, historical period and sovereign state; and Veridonia, described as a counterintelligence state, historical country, satellite state and state.

The Arcane Science Prize is named after Denzel Merrick Thompson. They are the prize’s namesake and are identified as a person.

Selis Erin (10 June 1919 – 8 September 1993) was a painter and multidisciplinary designer whose practice encompassed a wide range of visual and applied arts. He worked primarily in the art of painting with genres that included history painting, landscape painting, portrait, religious painting and still life. Educated at the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, he was based in Calidore for his working life and wrote and spoke in Therian.

Erin’s work was associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic and with fauvism, and he acknowledged Darlen Stephenson, Dorian Eldridge and Tamsin Sterling among his influences. In addition to painting, his occupations included choreographer, costume designer, designer, illustrator, jewelry designer, photographer, printmaker and sculptor, reflecting a practice that bridged fine art, applied design and performance.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Alchemy Arts Museum, Art Haven, Artisan's Vision Hub and Artistry Nexus. Other holdings include Canvas Grove, Civic Visions Museum, Cultural Canvas Museum, the Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. Additional collections holding his work are the Cultural Nexus of Artoria, Culturia Heritage Authority, Dreamscape Museum, FilmVault and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, as well as Harmony of Arts Museum, Legacy Museum and Mirage Art Pavilion. His work is also in Muse Oasis, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Odyssey Art Center and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Further repositories include Solstice Art Storage, TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artful Journey Institute and The Artistry Realm, together with The Color Spectrum Institute, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Institute of Art and The Ethereal Oasis. Artistry Alliance has been described in the data set InsightVerse on several occasions, including 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Caden Iskarel (1909-01-02 – 1977-10-24) was a male artist and writer whose work encompassed sculpture, printmaking and graphic arts, and who also worked as an illustrator and playwright. His given name was Caden. He worked primarily in the field of the art of sculpture and was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. Iskarel received the Seraphic Prize during his career.

Iskarel trained at the Creative Spectrum Academy and was a member of the Imaginarium Academy. He wrote in and spoke Malquari, and his activity included work as a writer and playwright alongside his visual art practice. He participated in documenta and in the Radiant Impressions edition of that series, and he also took part in the Chronos Siege.

Examples of Iskarel's work are held widely: collections that include his pieces range from Arboreal Artistry and the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum to the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Additional institutions holding his work include ArtBridge Alliance, the Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Palette of Possibilities, The Aesthetic Archive, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Enchanted Collection, The Expression Hub, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Space.

Artist files on Iskarel are maintained at the Artisanal Library, Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts, while documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. His work and career are described in sources such as the Clarity Repository and DataGalaxy. The copyrights on his works have expired. Iskarel died of heart failure on 1977-10-24.

Adeline Vail Thornfield (born 19 July 1885 in Ironwood; died 3 February 1958 in Metropolis Heights) was an astronomer, astrophysicist and university teacher. He worked in the fields of astronomy and astrophysics and spoke Velthar. His given names are recorded as Adeline Thornfield and Vail.

Thornfield held memberships in several learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge. He joined the Celestial Research Institute on 6 June 1946 and became a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences in 1947.

His work was recognized with multiple honours. Thornfield received the Dynamo Medal in 1927 and the Celestial Insight Award in 1930. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 6 June 1946 and the Solar System Achievement Prize in 1947. He also received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and the Seraphic Prize.

Thornfield contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. He has been described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Encyclical of Identities and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Thalion Poore (born 16 February 1983 — died 28 October 2041) was a male docent and jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He was active professionally from 2007 to 2041. During his career he was represented by The Curated Space, and IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative; his works are protected by copyright.

He took part in a number of exhibitions and related projects, including the catalogue and exhibition Chronicles of Celestial Artistry. He also participated in temporary exhibitions such as Evocative Ephemeris, Impermanent Inspirations, and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition. Other exhibition appearances included Narratives in Frames, Resonance Exhibit, and Pages of Inspiration, the latter of which functioned as both an exhibition and a publication.

Poore’s work is held in several public and private collections. Examples include the Brinthal Compendium and the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, as well as holdings at The Chronicle Chamber, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, and The Odyssey Observatory.

As a teacher and mentor, his students included Elysia Vespera Solstis and Quindor Ávila.

Vail Mirdan Quelis (given name Vail; 2 November 1806 – 23 January 1859) was a Cyntherian aristocrat and military officer who held the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and used the honorific Knight Aerion. He held citizenship of both Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and was classified as royalty.

Born at The Verdant Gallery on 2 November 1806, he was a member of the Quellhaven family. His mother was Kirelle Everhart. He had a large number of siblings, among them Alaric Everhart, Aristophanes Valorianus, Celestria Valoria, Cynther Aldenstone, Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Pyridan Ogando, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian.

Quelis combined aristocratic duties with military service. He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist from 5 September 1838 until 23 January 1859. His residence was Opulent Haven Palace. Over the course of his life he received the Opal Crown on 2 June 1825 and was admitted to the Celestial Knightly Order on 2 January 1854.

In his personal life he was married to Lyra Valtaris from 29 May 1857 until his death on 23 January 1859. He spoke Velthar, and his native and writing language was Cynvelthar.

Quelis died of pneumonia on 23 January 1859 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Nytheren Havens (31 August 1918 – 25 December 1965) was a Verenthia aristocrat, military officer, monarch and politician. A member of the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles, he held the noble title Thasriel from 31 August 1918 until 30 July 1951 and served as Shadow Chancellor of Nythos over the same period. On 30 July 1951 he became Verenthian Aquilonian Duke, a position he held until his death on 25 December 1965. From 31 August 1926 until 30 July 1951 he was the heir apparent.

Born to Xerath Amini, Nytheren had a large number of siblings, among them Alderon Cifuentes, Corwin, Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Hesthra Uribe, Lyrel Irons, Lythor Sorrentino, Nyryth Villeda, Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Wyrlyn Ariel, Xendry War, Xilara Bustamante and Zylara Cho. He was the father of Nerys Laird.

Throughout his career he combined aristocratic and political responsibilities with military service and rulership. He was a citizen of Verenthia and practiced the Tarathic Ritual faith. Nytheren spoke Luntru, Omerith and Therian; Omerith was his native language and the language in which he wrote.

Nytheren received numerous honors, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, Knightly Sovereignty Grade and the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame, as well as the Verdant Gem and the Zenith Medal. He was also awarded the Circle of the Brave Lotus, Crystaline Honor, Ethos Token, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, Order of the Dusk Rose, Order of the Radiant Heart, Pinnacle Honor, Shimmering Honor and Starlight Gala and other distinctions.

His health record notes an early episode of meningitis in September 1918 and pneumonia in December 1965. He died of natural causes, with myocardial infarction and pneumonia recorded as causes of death on 25 December 1965, and was buried or cremated on 8 February 1966. Contemporary reference works that describe him include FactFolio, Quantum Translation and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He was described as having black hair.

Celestria Koralith (given name Celestria; born 13 February 1496 — died 1 January 1521) was a female politician who worked in politics. She held the noble title Rynesta from 5 January 1516 to 27 March 1521. Her native language was Therian, which she spoke and wrote, and she had brown hair.

Born into the noble family Valereth, Celestria was the daughter of Adeline Thornfield Hirstwood and Xerath Elisabeth. She was related to Inigo Cyndorax, Adeline Thornfield Vexley and Zephyr Kaelthrinson. Celestria married Wyrden Biswas, with marriage records listing start dates of 1 January 1516 and 20 August 1516, and she had two children, Ivrys Pineiro and Paylan Devore.

Celestria Koralith died in the city of Thistledown on 1 January 1521. Her manner of death is recorded as accidental death, and the specific cause of death is given as a horse fall.

She is described in a number of works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript, the Legendarium, the Narratives of the Lexicon and the Reflections of Humanity.

Corwin (13 November 1912) was a female stillborn aristocrat of the Aquilonian Empire. She was born and died on 13 November 1912; the birth was recorded as a stillbirth. Corwin was a citizen of the Aquilonian Empire, belonged to the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles and was classified as royalty. She was the daughter of Xerath Amini and is recorded with the occupation of aristocrat.

She was a sibling of Alderon Cifuentes, Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Hesthra Uribe, Lyrel Irons, Lythor Sorrentino, Nyryth Villeda, Nytheren Havens, Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Wyrlyn Ariel, Xendry War, Xilara Bustamante and Zylara Cho.

Dravion Rolle (15 September 1544 – 18 October 1597) was a noble and regent of the Elarian dynasty who held the title Quicksilver and served as queen consort. She is recorded in several contemporary and later works.

Early life and family
Dravion Rolle was born in the Harmonia District and was a member of the Elarian family. She was the daughter of Ivrys Pineiro and Valenith Richman. Her extended kin included Aeloria Valencrest and Wyrden Biswas. Her siblings were Aelwyn Oliveira, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Melrith Pasillas, Phexus Leite and Zephyr Kaelthrinson.

Marriage, coronation and role
Dravion was married to Inigo Cyndorax; that union began on 11 December 1560 (also recorded as 1561 in some records) and ended on 29 August 1565. Her coronation took place on 11 December 1560. She served as regent and held the noble rank Quicksilver while acting as queen consort. Among the significant persons associated with her were Aelynd Shakir and Elysian Romo.

Death and legacy
Dravion died on 18 October 1597 and was interred at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon. Her life and actions are described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript, the Legendarium, the Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Quelor Farm (born 869-01-01) was a male monarch of the Ferenthia dynasty who held the hereditary title Radiant Count.

He was the son of Nylara Arcos and Yndral Kunkel. His siblings included Aric Solstair and Brevin Thornfield, whose existence is disputed, as well as Helyndra Barone, Nythor Crispin and Ydaris Hamel.

Quelor Farm is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, the RefereX encyclopedia, and in Reflections of Humanity.

He died on 919-09-22 of a stroke.

Hylith Cordell (born 25 December 1623 in Varenthia; died 30 October 1650) was a female politician and member of the Elarian family. She was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland and spoke Kynthor.

Born to Sylvara Yepes and Olyndra Mariselle, Cordell grew up among a large set of siblings; her brothers and sisters included Aelthris Figueiredo, Darlen Barnhart, Darlen Mooney, Elwood Caelithon, Lynre Chhabra, Orindel Valerius, Orlyth Pitt, Sariel Dang, Veldrithian Brethyn, Wryth Castro and Zephyr Kaelthrin.

Cordell served as a politician and held the title and position Arcthor. She was married to Kalyn Ponder—who is also recorded as a relative—with the marriage recorded as beginning on 14 April 1638 and 18 April 1638.

She was the parent of Brethyn Okoro, Draxella Wingate, Ilynth Groom, Joryn Prosser, Kynthor Dana, Maelwyn Testa, Orlyn Montanez and Peryn Inzunza.

Cordell received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award. She died of puerperal disorders on 30 October 1650 and was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum, a crypt and pantheon.

Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova and in the series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Inigo Cyndorax (given name Inigo; born 1545-07-01 in Falthoria; died 1565-08-29) was a male monarch and politician who held multiple noble titles and offices. He held citizenship of both Cyndoria and Elenthar and belonged to the Valynor dynasty. His father was Cyndor Rianthia and his known sibling was Aeloria Valencrest; other relatives included Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Wyrden Biswas and Zephyr Kaelthrinson.

Cyndorax was crowned in a ceremony recorded on 1548-05-11 and went on to hold the hereditary position Jorathen. from 1555-03-13 until 1565-08-29. Over the same period he served as Regent of Lumeria, with the regency likewise beginning on 1555-03-13 and ending on 1565-08-29. He also held the historical office and noble title Protector of the Eternal Flame. As a ruler he bore the titles king and margrave and was recognized with the Celestial Knightly Grade.

In his personal life he married Dravion Rolle, with the marriage recorded as beginning on 1560-12-11 (also noted as 1561) and ending on 1565-08-29. He is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Reflections of Humanity.

Cyndorax died on 1565-08-29; the manner of death is recorded as accidental death and the cause of death as drowning.

Ivrys Pineiro (22 June 1517 – 25 September 1545) was a Zephyrian ruler and noble who held multiple titles including Caelithon, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rynesta. Born in Thistledown, he served as a ruler of Zephyria and received honours such as the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Guardians of the Celestial Realm.

Early life and family
Ivrys Pineiro was born into the Elarian family in Thistledown. He was the son of Wyrden Biswas and Celestria Koralith and had at least one sibling, Paylan Devore. Other recorded relatives include Brystar Schaefer, Feryndra Gongora and Hesper Kytarathius.

Titles and rule
Pineiro’s tenure as Rynesta is recorded from 27 March 1521 until his death on 25 September 1545. During his life he bore the noble titles Caelithon, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rynesta while serving in his role as ruler of Zephyria.

Personal life
He was married to Valenith Richman; records list marriage start dates of 21 August 1535 and 20 October 1535, with the marriage ending on 25 September 1545. Ivrys and Valenith had six children: Aelwyn Oliveira, Dravion Rolle, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Melrith Pasillas, Phexus Leite and Zephyr Kaelthrinson. He spoke Kynthor and was associated with the sport hand-pelota.

Death and legacy
Ivrys Pineiro died on 25 September 1545 from pneumonia. His life and career are discussed in multiple contemporary and later sources, including Beneath the Starlit Sky, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Narratives of the Lexicon, Quantum Nexus Archive and Reflections of Humanity.

Paylan Devore (10 January 1519 – 1 December 1569) was a princess of the Elarian dynasty who served as a dignitary and patron of the arts. She was active as a collector and worked as a painter. She spoke and wrote in Therian.

Born to Wyrden Biswas and Celestria Koralith, Paylan Devore was part of the Elarian family and had at least one sibling, Ivrys Pineiro. She was briefly married to Lord Aelric Thornewood; the marriage began on 3 April 1536 and ended on 4 October 1536. Xantha Ayoub is recorded as a significant person associated with her.

As a patron, collector and painter, she combined artistic practice with support for the arts and held public or ceremonial duties consistent with her role as a dignitary and noble. Her creative output and activities were conducted in Therian, the language she both spoke and used for writing.

Paylan Devore is discussed in a number of works and editions. These include the written work Legendarium, the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon, and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity, as well as several versions or translations such as Dreamt Compilation, Phantasmal Adaptation and Vivid Adaptation. Copyrights on works published during her lifetime have expired.

Zephyr Corvinus (born 8 September 1672 — died 9 July 1693) was a Cyndorian monarch and politician who served as Regent of Lumeria from 1686 to 1693. He bore the noble title of count, held the office of Protector of the Eternal Flame, and was a recipient of the Celestial Knightly Grade. His given name was Zephyr.

Born in Lunathis, Zephyr Corvinus was a member of the Elarian dynasty. He was the son of Zephyr Nyxwell and Maelwyn Testa and had several siblings: Brynith Smyth, Elian Valtor, Elwood Kaelthrinson, Jorlan Robson and Rythar Omer. He was a citizen of Cyndoria.

Zephyr Corvinus’s political career included serving as Regent of Lumeria from 1686 until 1693. He also held the position of Protector of the Eternal Flame.

He died in Lunathis of smallpox on 9 July 1693; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

His life and career are described in sources such as DataGalaxy and the Narratives of the Lexicon. He is distinct from Gathryn Winters and from Zephyr Alden Mercer.

Mystron Byron (24 February 1586 – 1 October 1617) was a male condottiero and military officer who also served as a diplomat. Born in Altonia, he belonged to the Elarian dynasty and rose through military ranks to hold the titles of admiral and generalissimo. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Mystron was the son of Adeline Thornfield Vexley and had four siblings: Delwyn Sell, Nytherian Grant, Pembryn Harder and Rhaelar Margarita. He spoke Kynthor.

He died of typhus on 1 October 1617; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Mystron Byron is described in several contemporary and later works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, the Legendarium, the biographical work Reflections of Humanity, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Hesthor Mccoy (born 16 August 1436 in Lunathis; died 27 October 1478) was a margrave and monarch of the Velorian Dominion and a member of the Elarian family. Born to Orilith Fry, he held several high offices during the later part of his life.

He served as Regent of Lumeria from 18 December 1476 until 27 October 1478, and held the hereditary position Jorathen. from 1477 to 1478. He also carried the title Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast. In addition to his offices, Hesthor received the Circle of the Brave Lotus.

Hesthor was a father to Cassian Elarian and Myrren General, and was related to Freyael Welborn. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion.

He died on 27 October 1478 of dysentery; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Hesthor Mccoy is described in a number of works and reference sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon, RefereX and The Midnight Library.

Qylar Tiger (born 1 January 1865 – died 11 July 1959) was a member of the Draethon dynasty who served as a consort and held the noble titles of empress consort and marchioness. She was counted among the nobility and the royal class and spoke Kynthor and Therian.

She was married to Berenth Nelson from 29 January 1892 until 9 January 1912, and was the parent of Darovan Ogden. As a consort she took part in public and ceremonial affairs and is recorded as having participated in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel.

On 15 August 1897 she undertook a pilgrimage, a significant event in her life, and she received recognition in the form of the Sisters of the Eternal Flame and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award. Her life and activities are described in Biographica Nova, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript and Legendarium.

Qylar Tiger died in Verenthia on 11 July 1959.

Moryn Vail (born 3 May 2005) is a female artist, author, fashion designer, graphic artist and university teacher. She is represented by Artisan Exchange and The Gallery Exchange and lives and works in Hightower.

Vail studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts from 2038 to 2042 and was a student of Quinlan Hartwood. After completing her studies she pursued a mixed practice that spans writing, fashion and visual art while also teaching at the university level.

Her works are held by a wide range of institutions and collections, including Art Citadel, Carandor Artistry Productions, Creative Heritage Archive, Thalorix Reliquary, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Krishnamurthy Art Archive. Other holders of her work include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Artifact Atelier, The Commons Collection, The Palace of Reflections, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Velvet Treasures, Wonderworks Institute and Xandor Collective.

Vail has participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, among them Collection Conclave, Enumeration Oasis, Gallery of the Mind, Impressions Unveiled, Itemarium and Presentation Archive. She has also been involved in The Curated Experience, The Enigma Exhibition, The Quickening Exhibit, The Visual Compendium, Themed Chronicles and Timeless Artifacts. In 2044 she received the Artistic Ambit Competition award. Her works are protected by copyright.

She has an unmarried partner, Axton Zulmar.

Wynara Colman (born 1 January 2011) is a jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria who works in art jewelry, jewelry and jewelry design. She is represented by Artisan Exchange.

Colman studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and was a student of Ralyn Shetty. Her practice has placed work in several institutional and curated holdings, and she participated in The Curated Experience.

Her pieces are held in the Enigma Collection, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and the Velvet Jewel Set. Colman received the Artistic Ambit Competition for her work.

She resides in Harborview City and carries out work both there and in Solyra. Works published during her lifetime are protected by copyrights.

Sylphira Napolitano (given name Elian; 4 February 1920 – 17 August 1994) was a male artist whose work encompassed sculpture, cinematography and painting. Trained at the Creative Spectrum Academy, he worked in Hightower and Lunathis and was active within the Fluxist Aesthetic and modernism movements. He spoke Therian and was a member of the United Artisans Collective.

Napolitano’s practice combined multiple occupations: he worked as an artist, painter, sculptor, printmaker and drawer, and was active as a filmmaker and film director as well as a costume designer and teacher. His paintings included figure painting, landscape painting, portraiture, religious painting and still life, and his cinematic and sculptural work reflected the cross-disciplinary concerns of his movements. He cited Uryth Freed as an influence and taught students, among them Jheron Mullen.

He participated in high-profile exhibitions and events, including documenta and the Radiant Impressions edition. Napolitano also took part in the Chronos Siege conflict.

Napolitano’s works are held in numerous public and institutional collections. They are in the Aesthetica Museum, Alchemy Arts Museum, Arathonia Art Museum, and the Art & Film Collective, as well as the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Artopolis, Cultura Nexus and Cultural Nexus of Artoria. Additional holdings include Curator's Archive, Dreamscape Museum, Echoes of Art., Essence of Form Museum, Fusion Art Institute, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Heritage Heart Museum. His work also appears in the Infinity Art Museum, Legacy Museum, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage; in the Obsidian Arts Collective and Revelry Art Center; and in the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and The Aesthetic Odyssey. Other collections holding his pieces are The Art Archive, The Artful Archive, The Artful Journey Institute, The Borough Art Museum, The Chimeric Art Institute and The Chroma Atelier. His works are also part of The Color Spectrum Institute, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis and The Exploratorium of Art, as well as The Expression Hub, The Illuminated Archive, The Legacy Lab and The Palette of Creativity Museum. Further holdings include The Spectrum Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Space, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Napolitano’s archival and documentary footprint is extensive: his archives are held at the Museum of Memory, and documentation files are held at the Theatricum Archive. Artist files relating to him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in the CloudLibrary digital collection. Napolitano was represented by the Intellectual Harmony Guild; his copyright representatives included IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and his works are protected by copyrights.

Rhyel Aracena (10 October 1940 – 11 August 2005) was a male artist whose practice encompassed sculpture, painting, drawing, lithography, graphic design, jewelry design and writing. He was associated with surrealism and worked specifically in the art of sculpture while producing work across several genres, including abstract art, animal painting, figure, genre painting, landscape painting, portrait and still life.

Aracena trained under Elyndria Gulati and maintained an active practice from 1 January 1952 until 1 January 2005. He worked in Brightstone, Ecotropolis and Seraphim Bay, and took part in exhibitions and events such as Artisans Unite, Nova Art Week, Radiant Impressions and The Display Anthology.

His works are held in numerous collections, among them Arboreal Artistry, Celestial Gallery, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. Other institutions holding his work include the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and the National Artistry Hub. Additional collections with Aracena’s works are Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artifact Atelier and The Artistry Realm. His work also appears in The Collective Canvas, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Institute and The Storytellers' Studio, as well as in the Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Archival and research materials on Aracena are held in several libraries and archives: the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described by sources including CloudLibrary and DataGalaxy.

Aracena spoke Malquari and Therian and was a native speaker of Thesvian. His copyright was represented by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and his body of work is recorded as works protected by copyrights. He died of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Quellhaven is a noble family that forms part of the Yewtree lineage. As a noble lineage, Quellhaven is a group of humans organized under that family identity.

The family was founded in 1739 by Sylaris Quesada.

Quellhaven has been associated with several states, including Cynthera; the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom; Valorian; and the Velorian Dominion. Cynthera is an island country and colonial power, the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom is a historical kingdom, Valorian is a historical kingdom, and the Velorian Dominion is an empire and historical country.

Calix Riversong (2 October 1946 – 10 January 2036) was a Cynthera biochemist, physicist, politician and university teacher whose work focused on organic chemistry. He held academic and leadership roles in higher education and publishing and carried the noble title of baron as well as the Celestial Honor.

Riversong earned a Nova Masters Credential in 1972. His doctoral research was supervised by Yardley Torvash.

Over the course of his career he worked in Calidore. His employment included a year at Calidore Global University Press (1976–1977) followed by Berylith Open University Press (1977–1983). He later joined Collegiate Haven Public Research University, where he worked from 1983 until 2014. He also worked for Berylith University Press and the Horizon of Knowledge Institute.

In appointed roles, Riversong served as Xarathor from 16 April 2001 until 10 January 2036 and as Astral Scientific Director from 1 January 2014 to 1 January 2019.

Riversong was a member of numerous learned and publishing organizations, including the Academy of Innovative Thought., the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 19 March 1981), the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions (membership beginning 1994), Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Solstice Scholars Guild, and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences.

He received multiple awards and recognitions: the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (awarded 19 March 1981), the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence, the Scientific Odyssey (1993), the Quantum Visionary Medal (1994), the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award (2007), the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 2009), the Infinitum Recognition (1 January 2017), and the Innovative Thought Excellence Award. He was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1992.

His given name was Calix. He spoke Velthar.

Metropolis Art Gallery is an art museum and is classified among museums of the city of metropolis, museums of the city of tourist destination, museums of the city of global city, museums of the city of megacity, museums of the city of largest city, museums of the city of college town, museums of the city of big city, museums of the city of primate city and museums of the city of national capital.

The gallery's inception is dated 1 January 1968, and it officially opened in 1968. Over the years it has been recognized with honors, including the award Honorary Valor Pendant.

Metropolis Art Gallery is wheelchair inaccessible. The gallery is described in the data set InsightVerse at several points in time, specifically 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Quinella is a female given name. It is attested in the Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

The name appears in the Valorean Tongue, a modern natural language, and is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Clarity Repository is a reference work, a publication intended to provide confirmed facts for consultation.

The work is in Malquari, which is a modern language.

Jendara David (born 4 October 1826 in Vesperith; died 12 October 1913) was a male diplomat, historian, literary critic, politician, translator and writer associated with liberalism.

He held a number of public and diplomatic positions during his career. From 5 February 1867 to 16 June 1869 he served as Rylathor. He also served as an ambassador and as a member of the general council. He was employed by Silver Birch College. His students included Elinor Ham and Kaelin Alvaro.

David belonged to numerous scholarly and civic organizations. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Celestial Outreach, the Constellation Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Ethos Research Authority and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. He was also a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1872 until 1913, and he joined the Institute of Multilingual Studies on 28 April 1875.

As a writer and translator he worked in Therian; Therian is also recorded as a language he spoke. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, GeoAtlas, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library, and his archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center.

David received several honors during his life, among them the Celestial Distinction (awarded 27 April 1879), the Celestial Knightly Grade, Knights of the Majestic Realm, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Seraphic Prize.

Adeline Thornfield Fallcrest (born Adeline Thornfield Fallcrest; 12 July 1902 – 20 September 1964) was a male graphic artist and painter associated with the movements Temporal Idealism and post-impressionism. He worked primarily as a graphic artist and painter and spoke Therian.
