Fallcrest was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. His archives are held at Memory Keep, which covers material from 1936 to 1958, and artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the Arcana Document and in DataGalaxy.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, including Artoria Capital Museum, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, and the Cultural Nexus of Artoria. Other collections with his works include Ethos Gallery, Harmonious Expanse, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Mirage Cultural Center, Obsidian Arts Collective, and Quentarion Art Museum. Additional holdings are listed at The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Legacy Art Space, The Palace of Reflections, The Realm of Colors Museum, The Vibrant Muse, and The Visionary Experience.

Fallcrest received the Golden Aurora Class. As a creator, copyrights on his works have expired. Among his notable students was Pylar Hairston.

Hidden Haven is a cemetery in the country of Cynthera.

The site was established in 1871, with a recorded start time of 1 January 1872. The earliest written record of the cemetery dates to 1872.

Hidden Haven is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Alaric Darkmoorson (12 December 1830 – 17 December 1886) was a Thalendrian consort, politician and ruler, bearing the noble title Orindel and the family name Garcia-Taylor. A member of the House Maerwyn family, she spoke Therian and received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Alaric was born in Lunathis to Aldrin Valtoros and Aeloria Vensyl. She had a large set of siblings, among them Elian Martel, Feryndal Naqvi, Halvyn Groom, Halvyn Villagrana, Ilyrith Awad, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter, Wylora Hamby and Zephyr Solrune. She was the parent of Wylian Kruger.

Her first marriage was to Draxen Schiff, beginning on 1 April 1849 and ending on 5 May 1860. She subsequently married Micaiah Ashford in 1860, with a recorded formal start on 7 September 1860; that marriage ended in 1868.

Alaric is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Narratives of the Lexicon, Shadows of the Forgotten and The Midnight Library. Artist files relating to her are held at the Gallery of Texts.

She died in Darkmoor on 17 December 1886 of disease and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Elian Rivers (1856–1950) was a male botanist and multidisciplinary naturalist from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian who worked across several specialist fields and was styled Lord Vesperin. His principal field of work was botany; his occupations included bryologist, mycologist, pteridologist, explorer, surgeon and writer. He wrote in Velthar and spoke Nythoria.

Rivers held an institutional role as Astral Scientific Director from 1912 to 1917 and was employed by the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He belonged to numerous learned bodies and institutes, among them the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Catalyst Society of Knowledge, Constellation Institute, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. He was also a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database, joining that archive on 1924-02-08.

His work and collections are held by several institutions. Items collected by or at Rivers are in the holdings of Academica Naturae Heritage, Plantoria Nexus, Synergy Knowledge Collective and the Veridian Research Institute. Works by Rivers appear in the collection of the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Over his career Rivers received multiple honors and awards. These include the Quantum Visionary Medal (1893), the Radiant Grove Fellowship (beginning 1909), the Lumina Token (1922), the Elysium Science Medal (1926), the Quantum Scholar Recognition (1927), the Paradigm Recognition (1939) and the Seraphic Prize (1946). He also received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

Rivers was the son of Braxton Eldridge Smith; Braxton Eldridge Smith was both his father and his teacher. Rivers has been described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and the literary work Tales from the Abyss. He died on 10 December 1950.

Drestor Mango (born 30 May 1926 in Emberglow; died 25 February 2003) was a male designer, painter and photographer whose principal field of work was the art of sculpture. He was associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic and with futurism. Mango was a citizen of the Myralun Empire until 1947.

Mango began formal study at The Cultural Exchange Hub in 1947. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and worked in Emberglow, Luminara and Westfield Heights.

His practice encompassed sculpture alongside painting and photographic work, and he produced pieces in genres including abstract art, figure, nude and still life. He combined his roles as designer, painter and photographer across these subjects.

Works by Mango are held in a wide range of public collections, among them Arboreal Artistry, Artistry Alliance, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Canvas of Dreams, Mirage Art Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Imaginative Tapestry, The Visionary Experience, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Vivid Visions Gallery. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate; IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative, and his published works are listed as works protected by copyrights. He is described by the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Artist files on Mango are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. His native language was Myrathian, and he also spoke Elvishar and Velthar.

Kynar Castañeda (21 July 1897 – 17 July 1964) was a male artist whose work encompassed figurative art, landscape painting, mythological painting and portrait. He worked as an artist, drawer, etcher, graphic artist, lithographer and printmaker, and he also served as a university teacher. Castañeda was associated with the movements Dreamscape Narratives and Vivid Expressionism and participated in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions. His recorded period of activity extended from 1 January 1911 to 1 January 1964. He worked in Hightower, Nextridge, Silvershore and Southpoint.

Castañeda studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and at Creative Spectrum Academy, and he was a student of Myrlen Abebe. He spoke and wrote in Malquari, which is also recorded as his writing language. He cited influences from Jorian Broome and Yates Tamsin Rivers.

His works are held in a wide range of collections: ArtBridge Alliance, Artisan's Vision Hub, Culture Confluence, Echoes of Art., Exhibitarium, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts, Palette of Possibilities and Radiant Muse Pavilion. Additional collections holding his work include Reverie Atrium, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Realm, The Artistry Realm and The Enchanted Art Gallery. Further holdings are listed at The Harmony Space, The Illusive Gallery, The Imaginative Realm, The Inspiration Nexus, The Visionary Vault, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, as well as at Verdantia Art Collective Museum and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Several research and library institutions maintain artist files on Castañeda, including Artisanal Library, Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described by the Arcana Document and by DataGalaxy. As a creator, the copyrights on his works have expired.

Castañeda died on 17 July 1964 from pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Ulyr Deshmukh (9 February 1822 – 24 April 1891) was a Myralun Empire writer, poet and scholar. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and served that state; of Vyradon heritage, he worked publicly from 1836 until 1891. He wrote and spoke Myrathian and produced work in the genre of poetry while also engaging in literary criticism.

Deshmukh held multiple literary and scholarly occupations: he worked as a poet, writer, literary critic, linguist, translator and teacher. He was associated with the Emotional Topography movement and was a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, an academy of sciences and publishing company.

Over his career he received several honours, among them the Arcadian Medal and the Vexorian Medal; the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Order of the Gilded Compass, both orders of chivalry; the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria; and the Seraphic Prize.

He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation) and the Knowlarium (an online encyclopedia), as well as in written works such as the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium. Biographical and literary references to him appear in the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, the literary work Tales from the Abyss, and the Twilight Tome.

Ylianth Laughlin (born 12 June 1976 in Azureport; died 3 June 2049) was a Luminara State physicist, topologist and university teacher. He held citizenship of Luminara State and lived in Azureport. After his death he was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Laughlin was educated at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, where he earned the Obsidian Graduate Award and completed his doctorate under Oryndel Watt. He subsequently taught at the same university from 2002 until 2026. He later held a short appointment at Velocitopia University from 1 May 2029 to 1 August 2029. Among his doctoral students was Wyler Montufar.

His research and teaching spanned a broad range of mathematical and physical topics, including algebraic geometry, topology, differential calculus, mathematical analysis, dynamical systems, mechanics and mathematics more generally. He was explicitly interested in mathematics and was active as a topologist and physicist.

Laughlin received several honors during his career: the Zenith Merit Medal in 2004, the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, which he was awarded on 30 June 2027. He was a member of multiple scholarly organizations, becoming a member of the Celestial Research Institute in 2027 and also belonging to the Cognition Coalition, the Forge Institute of Discovery, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Spectrum Institute of Learning and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

His native language was Myrathian; he also spoke Velthar. Laughlin died of peritonitis on 3 June 2049; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His life and work are described in DataGalaxy and in the Twilight Tome.

Thaddeus Archemonta (born 2 February 1494 – died 20 February 1552) was a monarch of the Aelorian dynasty who held multiple hereditary and sovereign positions across Auralis, Crownlandia and Zolterra. He bore the noble titles of duke and king and served in several named offices during the first half of the 16th century.

Born in Zandoria on 2 February 1494, Archemonta was the son of Jorvik Ruthorn Valen and Zerynd Cassell and was raised within the Aelorian family. He had at least one sibling, the Thalassian Sovereign Monarch.

Archemonta married Miraleth Sol on 6 September 1517; the marriage lasted until his death on 20 February 1552. The couple had two children, Crown Zafrina and Thalor Jorvistan.

In his public career he held the hereditary title of the Crownthalassian Barony from 1520 until 1552 and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1522 until 1552. He also served as Zolterran Monarch from 6 October 1536 to 1 August 1540. Throughout his life he was active as a monarch.

Archemonta received the Ethos Token and the Order of the Radiant Heart. His life and rule are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

He died in Zandoria on 20 February 1552 from an accidental horse fall.

Crownthalas Jorviken (born Jorvik; 18 September 1825 – 20 January 1887) was a Crownlandian monarch and patron of the arts. He held noble rank as both duke and king and served in military office with the rank of general. He was a member of the Aelorian family and a citizen of Crownlandia.

Jorviken held several formal positions during his life. He served as regent from 19 February 1853 to 19 May 1853, and he held the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 17 May 1853 to 10 October 1853. Later he held the Crownthalassian Barony from 3 December 1878 until his death on 20 January 1887.

He received numerous honors, among them the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Illuminated Scholars Society (awarded 6 June 1861), the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Pinnacle Honor. On 6 June 1861 he also became a member of the Celestial Research Institute; he was additionally a member of Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Thalassian Xarnum Academy of Sciences.

Crownthalas Jorviken spoke and wrote Xarnum. He had at least one child, Crownthalas Monarchus. His copyrights on works have expired. He is described by Dreamt Compilation and by Reflections of Humanity.

Jorviken died at Tranquil Keep on 20 January 1887 of sepsis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Thalassian Sovereign Monarch (7 October 1510 – 10 April 1572) was a member of the Aelorian dynasty and a citizen of Auralis. He was a duke and served as a monarch during the mid-16th century.

He held the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1562 until 10 April 1572, and concurrently held the Crownthalassian Barony from 13 April 1562 until 10 April 1572. Both the duchy and the barony were hereditary noble positions. As a ruler he is described in contemporary and later sources.

Thalassian was the son of Jorvik Ruthorn Valen and Zerynd Cassell, and he had a sibling, the Thaddeus Archemonta. He was the father of Deleth Lorenzo and Thalassian Jorvikson.

He received the Order of the Radiant Heart, an order of chivalry. Thalassian Sovereign Monarch died of natural causes at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence, on 10 April 1572.

His life and reign are discussed in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition of a larger work, and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Jorvik Serel Crownward (born 15 April 1685, died 25 August 1738) was a duke and art collector who held hereditary territorial positions in the early 18th century. He was a citizen of both Auralis and Crownlandia and a member of the Aelorian dynasty. His given name was Jorvik.

From 1709 he held the Crownthalassian Barony and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom, both of which he assumed on 9 February 1709 and retained until his death on 25 August 1738. His documented period of professional activity runs from 1 January 1709 to 1 January 1738.

Jorvik Serel Crownward received several notable honours. He was awarded the Crest of the Celestial Knights on 28 February 1687 and the Circle of the Brave Lotus in 1701, and he was also a recipient of the Order of the Celestial Serpent.

A collector of art by occupation, he spoke and wrote Xarnum. He was the son of Thalassian Monarchis and the father of King Thalassian Maritus.

Jorvik Serel Crownward died as the result of a hunting accident, classified as an accidental death, at Cycle Ridge on 25 August 1738.

He is described in sources including DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

Thalassian Monarchis (born 18 March 1648 – died 9 February 1709) was a noble statesperson who served as a king and held clerical office. A citizen of Crownlandia-Atlantis and a member of the Aelorian dynasty, he combined political and administrative work with military authority, holding the rank of generalissimo and the noble title of duke. His occupations included cleric, king, politician and statesperson, and his fields of work encompassed governance, politics and state administration.

Born to Wyrith Heckman, he was one of a large group of siblings; his brothers and sisters included Crown Jorvik, Crownwick Landerson, Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Kylenth Guillaume, Olyndra Janet, Qylyn Flagg, Rhyall Piazza, Sylvara Batiste, Uthria Danielson and Viorelle Harethul. He was the parent of Jorvik Serel Crownward.

Thalassian Monarchis held the hereditary positions of the Crownthalassian Barony and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom, serving in both offices from 6 July 1687 until 9 February 1709. He worked in Cycle Ridge, and he also died there; his manner of death was natural causes. During his life he received the Order of the Radiant Heart.

He spoke and wrote in several languages, including Malquari, Nythoria, the Valorean Tongue, Velthar and Xarnum. His life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Aelwyn Oliveira (born 14 January 1546 – died 12 February 1617) was a regent of Eldoria-Emberland who held the noble title Arcthor. A citizen of Eldoria-Emberland, she served in the position of regent during her career.

Aelwyn was a member of the Elarian family, the daughter of Ivrys Pineiro and Valenith Richman. She had five siblings: Dravion Rolle, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Melrith Pasillas, Phexus Leite and Zephyr Kaelthrinson. A significant event associated with her life is recorded as a posthumous birth.

She became the spouse of Galyn Patiño on 10 February 1564. Aelwyn spoke Veyrith. She died in Valdor on 12 February 1617.

Aelwyn Oliveira is described by DataGalaxy and by Narratives of the Lexicon.

Melrith Pasillas (18 July 1540 – 19 January 1565) was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion, a historical empire and sovereign state. She served as a consort and held the noble title of queen consort. On 12 August 1554 she became the spouse of Thalor Jorvistan.

Born into the Elarian dynasty, Melrith was the daughter of Ivrys Pineiro and Valenith Richman. She had several siblings, including Aelwyn Oliveira, Dravion Rolle, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Phexus Leite and Zephyr Kaelthrinson, and was also related to Brystar Schaefer and Feryndra Gongora.

Melrith Pasillas died in Cleanscape, a carfree big city. Her life and role are described in the Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Yndira Sant (1279–1341) was a Caelumorian painter who worked in painting, particularly fresco painting. He was born in Caelumport and died in Arcadia. He spoke Thesvian.

His works are held in numerous collections and museums, including the Cultural Reflection Gallery, Luminara Art Haven, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Expression Hub, and The Harmony Space. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He is described in a range of published and digital sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Among his students was Aelorian Arriola. His copyrights have expired.

Elirian Appel (born 1294 in Nimbustown; died in Nimbustown, year given as 1357 or 1358) was a painter of the Yothrins people known for religious painting. He worked primarily in the art of painting and spoke Thesvian. His recorded period of activity runs from 1317-01-01 to 1358-01-01.

Appel was active in Nimbustown and Caelumport and trained under Yndira Sant. His occupation is recorded as painter, and his oeuvre focused on religious subjects within the broader field of painting.

His works are held in multiple public collections, including the Cultural Canvas Museum, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Luminara National Art Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, The Archive of Wonders, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Curatorial Vault and Treasures of Time.

Documentation and secondary sources on Appel include entries in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, The Solstice Chronicles and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Draxen Harwood (13 December 1962 – 6 February 2051) was a male graphic artist, illustrator, painter and sculptor whose work encompassed painting, sculpture and the engraving process. He spoke Kynthor and Veldrak and was described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Harwood maintained a professional presence in Krestoria and Mystralyn, with work locations recorded as of 1 January 1990. He was a member of several cultural and educational organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, Imaginarium Academy, Institute of Artistry and Design, Nexus Learning Society, Seraphim Art House and Zenith Cultural Museum. He participated in events and exhibitions such as Artisans Unite, Evocative Ephemeris and Radiant Impressions.

Institutions that hold documentation and artist files related to Harwood include Theatricum Archive, which holds documentation files, and the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts, which maintain artist files about him. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum, Ethos Gallery, Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Palette of Possibilities, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, Luminara Atrium Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Imaginative Tapestry, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, The Odyssey Observatory, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery.

His copyright was represented by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and he was represented by Music and Media Syndicate. Harwood’s body of work remained protected by copyrights. Among his honors, he received the Golden Vanguard Class and, in 2029, the Boundless Art Recognition.

Tarvion is a sovereign state and federal constitutional republic that is also described as a superpower and a historical unrecognized state. It is part of Bellwood and lies on the continent and subcontinent of Elysium. The polity began to exist on 10 August 1860 and takes its name from the Aeloria River.

Geography and borders
Tarvion is located on the Aeloria River and on the main stream Caranthrivera, and it is in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone. As an administrative entity it is part of Bellwood, a mainland territory with geographic contiguity. Tarvion shares borders with the sovereign states Celestara, Drakoria, Drakthal, Selunian Union, Galdorath, Myrthos., Pyranthor and Thalarion.

Administration and settlements
Within its territory Tarvion contains the city of Nexopolis, a large independent city and major urban centre in the state.

Language and culture
Malquolyndra is widely used in Tarvion; it functions both as a modern language and as a sacred language.

Reception and sources
Tarvion is described in a range of sources, including the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation; in written works such as the Legendarium; in the Qylarans; in the book series Shadows in the Ink; in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy; and in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Harlune is a city and a de facto national capital. They were founded in 1540.

They were part of the Taldor Sultanate from 1589 until 1956.

Harlune shares a border with Olarith.

On the international and municipal level, they are twinned with a number of other cities. Twinning relationships include Drakemont (established 2050), Lystoria (established June 2046), Orynthia (established December 2049), Pyradale (established May 2049), Silverhold (established 22 November 2053), Westhaven (established 6 October 2049), and Zephyra (established October 2049). They are also twinned with Harborview City, Jotunspire, Terranova and Zenith Heights. Additionally, Harlune became a member of the network SyncSphere in 2058.

Liora Cyntheris (given names Aeliana and Celestria; 14 April 1896 – 26 October 1983) was a Cyntheran aristocrat who was styled Knight Aerion and held citizenship of Cynthera. She belonged to the Eldergrove Lineage and was counted among the royalty of Cynthera.

She was born at The Verdant Gallery on 14 April 1896 and was baptized on 16 June 1896. Her father was Fintan Rhyseris. Her family circle included numerous siblings, among them Alden Rhyseris, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Jalen Thompson, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano, and she had a relative named Lytheris Karimi. Her godparents were Elara Valtaris, Lyra Valtaris and Malquari Valdrin.

As an aristocrat and member of the Eldergrove Lineage, she received the Order of the Radiant Valor. She spoke and wrote Velthar, and her native language was Cynvelthar.

Liora Cyntheris was married to Varlyn Jayy from 23 July 1924 until 20 January 1935. She was the parent of Elara Aeliana Valtaris.

She died on 26 October 1983 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel; the burial at that site began on 3 November 1983.

Alden Rhyseris (Alden and Fintan; family name Nyxmar), styled Knight Aerion and holding the noble title Eldrith, was a Cyndorian aristocrat, politician and philatelist. He served in official positions including Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and Xarathor, and he was politically active in events such as The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932.

Born on 6 August 1883 and baptized on 6 September 1883, Alden was the son of Fintan Rhyseris and a member of the Eldergrove Lineage. He belonged to the social class of royalty and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. His godparents were Irvin Everhart and Hestara Minvel Arindel. His siblings included Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Jalen Thompson, Liora Cyntheris, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano.

Alden married Myralun Mystral on 23 January 1913; that marriage is recorded as ending on 30 July 1939. He had five children: Alaric Solandria, Alden Rhyseris Eldrith, Elara Aeliana Rhyseris, Elysia Rhyseris and Liora Rhyseris.

During his career he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, a learned society, beginning on 16 March 1921. He was also active as a politician and pursued philately as an avocation. He played the violin, spoke the language Velthar, and his native and writing language was Cynvelthar.

Alden received numerous honours over his life, among them the Aurora Badge, Ethos Token, Radiant Token, Solaris Distinction, Vexorian Medal, Glorious Order, Pinnacle Honor, Sapphire Leaf, Order of the Stalwart Heart, Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, Order of the Radiant Heart (awarded in 1914), Knights of the Eternal Flame, Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, Circle of the Brave Lotus, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Celestial Knightly Order, Valorian Krestorian Order Grade (awarded on 1 May 1921), and the Illuminated Scholars Society, which he received on 16 March 1921.

He is described in several works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and Whispers of Tomorrow.

Alden Rhyseris died on 31 July 1939 from esophageal cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Myralun Mystralhart (10 June 1936 – 17 July 1957) was a Myralun Empire aristocrat who held the noble title Mystral and was styled Shadow Chancellor of Nythos. She served as a chairperson and worked as a nurse, and received the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women.

Born on 10 June 1936 and baptized on 20 June 1936, Mystralhart was a member of the Jorathyn dynasty. Her father was Valerius Aurelianus and her mother was Elysia Thorne; Elysia Thorne also taught her. Her godparents were Aurelian Myralun, Cyndar Aucoin, Irvin Thorne and Myralundus Elysian. She had several siblings: Caelum Myralunov, Ilyndra of Mystral, Myralun Mystralian and Myralun Mystralsson. She resided at the Celestial Viewpoint, a museum and palace complex that is also a tourist attraction.

Myralun Mystralhart spoke Malquari, Myrathian (her native language), Therian and Velthar, and she wrote in Myrathian and Velthar. Her interests included crocheting, embroidery and fashion, as well as hairdressing and religion, and she followed a lifestyle of mysticism.

She was reported to have had blue‑gray and light brown eyes. Mystralhart had typhoid fever during her life. She died on 17 July 1957 from a gunshot wound; the manner of death was recorded as homicide.

Her life and career are described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal. She was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and was classified socially as royalty.

Myralun Mystral (17 October 1892 – 24 October 1959) was a noble aristocrat of the Myralun Empire who held the noble title Mystral. She was born in Uldarion and died in Fairview, and she held citizenship of the Myralun Empire.

Born into the Jorathyn dynasty, Myralun was a member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera. Her father was Lysandra Myralun and her mother Aurelium Myralun. She had numerous siblings, including Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Bryndra Nwosu, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Kynara Aronson, Selinth Beckwith, Valenor Myralun and Valiant Myralun.

She married Alden Rhyseris on 23 January 1913.

Myralun and Alden Rhyseris were the parents of Alaric Solandria, Alden Rhyseris Eldrith, Elara Aeliana Rhyseris, Elysia Rhyseris and Liora Rhyseris.

Myralun received the Order of the Seraphic Veil and the Order of the Serene Waters, both orders of knighthood for women. Her life and role within the aristocracy are documented in sources such as DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation; and the Legendarium.

Damaris Elowen Carter (born 15 January 1921; baptized 11 March 1921 – died 1 May 1959) was a Cyndorian aristocrat, painter and philanthropist. She was active in public life and charitable fundraising between 1 January 1941 and 1 January 1959, and was styled Knight Aerion. Her works are held by the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and the copyrights on her works have expired.

Early life and family
Damaris Elowen Carter was born on 15 January 1921 and baptized on 11 March 1921. Her father was Jalen Thompson. Her given names included Aeliana, Damaris, Kirelle and Sylphina. She had two siblings, Jalen Markwood and Lyvian Hagos. Her godparents were Elara Valtaris, Lytheris Andrade, Malquar Valdrin, Orindel Margaret and Vail Thorne.

Marriage, children and titles
She married Ryland Zolterras on 15 June 1944; the marriage lasted until her death on 1 May 1959. The couple had five children: Glynor Rutherford, Helynd Bose, Kaelar Smile, Liora Zoltan and Pyreth Cepero. She held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and served as crown princess from 8 December 1946 until 1 May 1959. She took part in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932. Throughout her life she was classified as royalty and was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

Career, interests and honours
Carter combined aristocratic duties with artistic practice and public service. Her occupations included aristocrat, painter, fundraiser and philanthropist, and she pursued these roles during her recorded work period from 1941 to 1959. She received the Order of the Gilded Compass and the Order of the Seraphic Veil. As an artist she was interested in the art of painting, drawing and photography; she was also interested in gardening. Her written work was in Cynvelthar and Xyldari, and she spoke and wrote Velthar and Xyldari, with Cynvelthar as her native language.

Recreation and health
Carter participated in skiing, speed skating and tennis. She suffered from measles and from sepsis; she died of sepsis and the manner of death was recorded as natural causes on 1 May 1959.

Legacy and sources
Her life and work are described in the Memoirium and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. Several of her paintings and related works are held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture.

Ylessa Dinero (given name Orinelle; 13 August 1791 – 8 September 1853) was a Thalendrian aristocrat who bore the noble title Caelithon and served as queen consort. A citizen of Thalendria, she was born in Lunathis and was also active there during her life. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

A member of the House Maerwyn family, Ylessa was the daughter of Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad. Her godparents were Dravion Appiah and Inigo Valente. She was named after Alexandra Dinero and Orinelle Mariselle; Orinelle Mariselle also appears among her many siblings. Her recorded siblings include Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Glynara Hilario, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Olyndra Myrathis, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

Ylessa was married to Phaelan Diop from 12 May 1807 until her death on 8 September 1853. Their children were Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar, and Yandor Lua.

As a creator, Ylessa received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award and her works are held in the Color Spectrum Division and at Solstice Art Storage. The copyrights on her works have expired. Her life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript, and the Narratives of the Lexicon. She is distinct from Halvyn Villagrana.

Crownlandiania Monarchson (12 December 1613 – 2 March 1658) was a Crownlandian aristocrat who served as queen consort from 1628 until her death in 1658. She was active as a patron of the arts and a philanthropist, and she is recorded as having created works that are now held in the collection of the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; the copyrights on those works have expired.

Born into the Aelorian dynasty, she was the daughter of Thalassian Sovereighn. Crownlandiania married Caelan Asterwood on 23 November 1628; the marriage continued until her death on 2 March 1658. Her children were Adeline Kytarathian Thornfield, Hesper Goldenvale and Zafrina Amara Liora. Her siblings included Crown Zafrinia and Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer.

She held citizenship of Crownlandia, Cynthera and Varyndoria. Crownlandiania spoke and wrote both Therian and Xarnum, with Xarnum recorded as her native language; she wrote in Therian and Xarnum. Her life and work are described in the Ethereal Manuscript and the Nebula Edition.

Crownlandiania died at the Radiant Pavilion on 2 March 1658; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes and the underlying cause was edema.

Zafrina Amara Liora (given name Zafrina; 19 August 1635 – 13 February 1701) was a member of the Nymarath royal house who held the titles of princess and later queen consort. She served as an aristocrat and consort and was noted as a patron of the arts. As a member of the royal class, she was classified socially as royalty.

Early life and family
Zafrina Amara Liora was born on 19 August 1635 and baptized on 28 November 1635. She was the daughter of Caelan Asterwood and Crownlandiania Monarchson. Her godparent and namesake was Kytara Zafrinia. Among her siblings were Adeline Kytarathian Thornfield and Hesper Goldenvale, and she was also related to Celestria Valenwood.

Citizenship, residence and interests
Zafrina held citizenship of Cynthera, Kytarathia and the Quolmaris Republic. She made her residence in Silvershore. She spoke and wrote in Therian and Velthar, and took a particular interest in equestrianism.

Marriage and children
Zafrina was married to Yandor Santini; their marriage began on 14 February 1652 and ended on 29 November 1671. She was the parent of Alderon Gene, Delphina Hartwell, Elara Moonstone, Freth Carlton, Hesper Aldenwood, Olvyn Crocker, Qalyn Si, Theryn Stratton, Vail Aldridge, Wyslind Conte, Wyslind Galdamez and Xilara Mcdonough.

Death and legacy
Zafrina Amara Liora died on 13 February 1701 in Calidore. Her life and career have been described in a range of works and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Nebula Edition, RefereX, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Bryndith Chandran (17 July 1910 – 31 July 1995) was an artist whose work encompassed painting, illustration, music and photography. He spoke Velthar and was active professionally from 1932 until 1988. Chandran studied under Yardley Hawthorne and was employed by The Innovators Academy, where he combined creative practice with teaching.

Chandran worked in a range of occupations: artist, caricaturist, composer, drawer, illustrator, photographer and teacher. He was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement and took part in exhibitions and events including Radiant Impressions and documenta. His career was represented commercially by Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective acted as his copyright representatives; his works published during his lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Examples of institutional recognition and documentation of Chandran’s career include artist files held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is also described in sources such as Qylarans and The Archive of Stories.

Chandran’s works are held in numerous collections and museums, including the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Tapestry Museum, Ethos Gallery, the National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Additional holdings are at Solstice Art Storage, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Realm, The Artistry Realm, The Color Spectrum Institute and The Curatorial Vault. Other institutions with his work include The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, The Spectrum Institute and The Visionary Space. His work is also part of the collections of Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Chandran was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning, The Visionary Guild and the United Artisans Collective, affiliations that reflected both his engagement with artistic communities and his role as an educator.

Aethrin Amber (born 1605-10-12; baptized 1605-08-12; died 1672-12-01) was a female politician who held the noble titles Orindel and Rynesta. Both titles were held from 1637-05-06 until 1660-07-13. She died in the Harmonia District.

Aethrin was the daughter of Rhaelar Margarita and Galindra Sarabia. Her godparents were Aldric Thornewood and Delwyn Sell. She belonged to a large family that included siblings Aelarin Nickel, Aldric Fenwyn, Aldric Thornewood, Elysian Thornehart, Kalyn Ponder, Terath Latta and Ulrith Locke, and counted among her relatives Aeloria Thalindor, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Pembryn Harder and Zephyr Kaelthrinson.

She was married to Rhalin Jacquez; the start of that marriage is recorded with dates given as 1637, 1638 and 1638-04-18. Aethrin spoke Kynthor.

Aethrin Amber is described in sources including the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon, and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Vail Terran (family name Dravon; born 9 October 1974, baptized 20 November 1974) is a Cyntherian aristocrat and military commander. He is a citizen of Cynthera and has allegiance to Cynthera. He is part of The Sovereign House of Cynthera and has resided at Opulent Haven Palace. He works in the areas of aristocracy and military affairs and has carried out work in Xylanthia.

Vail Terran was born to Irvin Talmadge and Mystral Avelar. His recorded given names include Irvin, Tamsin and Vail. He is a member of the Eldranthia ethnic group and his siblings include Elysia Hartwood and Xander Thorne. His godparents are Celestria Moonshadow, Celestria Valtaris, Irvin Thorne, Jalen Thompson, Vail Montrose, Xandor Lezcano and Ylith Holder.

He was educated at Silver Pines Academy. His native and writing language is Cynvelthar, and he also speaks Therian and Velthar.

Terran served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army from 29 July 1994 until 15 April 2015, holding the ranks of lieutenant colonel and major-general during his military career. He has held the position Xarathor from 25 August 1981 to 11 November 2038. His occupations are listed as aristocrat, military commander and military personnel.

He has received multiple honors, including the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians (2027), Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Order of the Stalwart Heart, the Sapphire Leaf and the Society of the Resolute Spirit. He has used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion since 9 October 1974. Since 2029 he has been a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Mystic Sash is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Gallant Shield, a military decoration and order. Within that system, Mystic Sash is classified both as a subclass of the Gallant Shield and as a subclass of the grand cross.

The Arcadian Emblem is a grade of the Crystaline Honor, an order bestowed upon individual recipients. As a constituent rank of the Crystaline Honor, the Arcadian Emblem forms part of that order's system of distinctions.

The Arcadian Emblem is associated with the Myralun Empire. The Myralun Empire is described as a country, an empire, a historical country, a sovereign state and a transcontinental country.

Galenith Alharbi (22 August 1985 – 2 November 2060) was a male person who worked as a voice actor. He was known for his work in that profession.

He spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Fintan Pellan (1337 – 20 July 1397) was a sovereign of the Velorian Dominion who held the noble title of duke. He held the position of bishop-elect beginning in 1354 and served as landgrave from 1365 until 1396.

Born in Lunathis in 1337, Pellan died in Lunathis on 20 July 1397. His given name was Fintan. He belonged to the Elarian family and was the son of Wyrlyn Fiedler and Zafrina Elowen Thorne. His child was Fintan Muiran. He had several siblings, among them Brystyne Natarajan, Elric Suryen Koth, Elwood Ralnor Quis, Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quethan Conn, Quinlan Strathmore and Theros Nick.

Pellan was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He is described in a number of works and compilations, including the Dreamt Compilation and the Shimmering Translation (versions and editions), the Narratives of the Lexicon (a book series and lexicon), the Quantum Nexus Archive (a collection), and Reflections of Humanity (a biographical dictionary and written work).

Riven Darkstar is a fictional deity and a humanoid extraterrestrial who appears as a literary and television character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The figure was created by Lyvian Mensah and is depicted as originating from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Within the franchise, he is presented as male.

Riven is characterized by a suite of superhuman features: he is portrayed with immortality as well as omniscience, omnipresence and omnipotence. These attributes underpin many of his actions and the mysteries that surround him across the franchise's stories.

Despite those godlike powers, the character is portrayed within the narrative as a con artist, combining cunning and theatricality in his schemes. He is also associated with the trumpet and is depicted playing that instrument in several works.

Riven Darkstar appears across multiple works in the Eldoria Chronicles, including the video game Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane, the written work Aetherial Register, the novel set Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga and its episode Celestial Chronicles: The Darkstar Paradox. He also features in Eldoria Tales: Legends of the Arcane and in the written works The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Gilded Diary and The Inked Odyssey.

Throughout the franchise, Riven has ongoing relationships with several significant characters, notably Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder and Serenix. These connections are recurring elements that link his appearances across the franchise's novels, episodes and other works.

Damaris Corvel Nyx (born 12 July 1690 in Verenthia; died 12 March 1712 in Lunathis) was an empress consort who held the noble title Arionth and belonged to the Elarian dynasty. She served in the role of empress consort during her lifetime and was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Born with the given name Damaris, she was the daughter of Joryn Prosser and Jorlan Robson and grew up within the Elarian family. Her siblings included Hesperis Blanton, Maximilian Thornfield and Zephyros Gutierez. She spoke Kynthor as well as Malquari.

In 1705 she married Elwood Kaelthrinson; the marriage produced at least one child, Deleth Nene. Alongside her ceremonial and dynastic duties as Arionth, she was recognized with the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Damaris died in Lunathis on 12 March 1712 from puerperal disorders and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt. Her life and role are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Maelwyn Testa (18 August 1645 – 13 May 1685) was a female member of the Elarian dynasty who served as a regent. She was married to Zephyr Nyxwell, their marriage beginning in 1670.

Born to Kalyn Ponder and Hylith Cordell, Testa was part of a large sibling group that included Brethyn Okoro, Draxella Wingate, Ilynth Groom, Joryn Prosser, Kynthor Dana, Orlyn Montanez and Peryn Inzunza. Two of her siblings, Brethyn Okoro and Joryn Prosser, are also recorded as her godparents. She and Zephyr Nyxwell were the parents of Elwood Kaelthrinson, Jorlan Robson and Zephyr Corvinus.

Testa spoke Kynthor and was a recipient of the Spiritual Enlightenment Award. Her life and role are described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

She died in Solmira of puerperal disorders on 13 May 1685 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Artisania National Gallery is an art museum and national museum located in the island country of Cynthera. Cynthera is a sovereign state that also functions as a colonial power.

The gallery was established on 1 January 1961.

Among its visitor amenities, the Artisania National Gallery includes an accessible toilet.

Sylphina Calidore (17 November 1842 – 8 December 1904) was a person and a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. She was born in Calidore and died in Calidore.

Her given name was Sylphina, and she was female.

Sylphina was the daughter of Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio. Her siblings included Aelindor Pendleton, Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Kirelle Ashwood, Orylan Abrahams, Qylen Lux, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

Calidore, the place of her birth and death, is a city that serves as a national capital and is also described as a largest city, megacity, metropolis, global city and financial centre. Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian is identified as a sovereign state, country, historical country and colonial power.

Axton Zulmar (given name Axton) was born on 1 January 2007 in Flintwick. He trained at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts from 2034 to 2040, and during his studies he was a student of Quinlan Hartwood.

Zulmar works professionally as a jewelry designer and as a university teacher. He is represented by Artisan Exchange and lives in Hightower. His published work remains protected by copyrights. In 2049 he received the Artistic Ambit Competition award.

Examples of Zulmar's work are held in several collections and institutions, among them the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Velvet Jewel Set and the Wonderworks Institute.

He has participated in numerous exhibitions, including Aesthetic Horizons and Gallery of the Mind, as well as Narratives in Frames and Resonance Exhibit. His work was also shown in The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and in The Curated Experience.

Zulmar's unmarried partner is Moryn Vail.

Yalindra Marciano (born 15 March 2005) is a Valorian fashion and jewelry designer. She is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and works as both a fashion designer and a jewelry designer. She is female.

Marciano's education includes the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and ArtSphere. Records indicate she was educated at ArtSphere from 5 June 2041 to 8 February 2041. ArtSphere is an art collection, art gallery, business and research center.

Her work locations have included Harborview City, where she worked from 1 January 2031 to 1 January 2052, and Cedarwood, noted as a work location in 2041. She resides in Harborview City.

Marciano has participated in the temporary exhibitions Evocative Ephemeris and Impermanent Inspirations. Artist files about her are held at ArtSphere. Her works are in the collections of Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Treasures of Time.

Her copyright representative is IntellectProtect, and her body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights. She has been a partner in business with Qyra Rios.

Ulyr Rust (16 April 1969 – 2 November 2023) was a designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria who worked across fashion and jewelry and also acted as a gallerist. Her professional activity spanned from 1 January 1984 to 1 January 2023. She was represented by Brush & Easel and by Catalyst Development, and in 2022 she received the Artistic Ambit Competition.

Rust studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 1997 to 2001 and trained under Aelestia Christine. Between 2004 and 2008 she worked as a gallerist while continuing to design for fashion and jewelry.

She married Zeyth Claxton on 22 December 2005; Claxton was also a partner in business with Rust. Over the course of her career Rust participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, among them Enumeration Oasis, Exhibit Nexus, Gallery of the Mind, Illustrated Realities, Impermanent Inspirations, Itemarium and Narratives in Frames. She also took part in Presentation Archive, Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Creative Vault and The Curated Experience. Additional participations included The Displayed Narrative, The Enigma Exhibition, The Visual Voyage, Treasures in Transition and Whispers of Heritage.

Works by Rust are held in a wide range of museums and collections, including the Academy of Visual Narratives, Art Citadel, Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Eternity's Collection, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the Krishnamurthy Art Archive. Her pieces are also in the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum and The Storytellers' Studio, as well as in Velvet Treasures, the Wonderworks Institute and the Xandor Collective.

Rust's archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive and at The Odyssey Observatory; the latter began holding material in 2049 and covers work from 1989 onward. IntellectProtect serves as Rust's copyright representative, and her body of work is protected by copyrights.

Ralyn Shetty (born 18 May 2004) is a designer working across fashion and jewelry who also teaches at the university level. She speaks Malquari and lives in Harborview City. She is represented by The Scenic Studio.

Shetty was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and at ArtSphere, an art gallery and research center; her attendance at ArtSphere is recorded with a start time of 2038-08-02 and an end time of 2038-04-30. Artist files on Shetty are held at ArtSphere. Her works are protected by copyrights.

She has participated in a number of exhibitions and presentations, including Aesthetic Horizons, Impermanent Inspirations (a temporary exhibition), Presentation Archive (a catalogue and exhibition), Resonance Exhibit, and The Curated Experience (an exhibition and publication).

Her work is held in multiple collections and institutions: the Enigma Collection, Eternity's Collection, the Velvet Jewel Set, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artistic Alliance, and The Chronicle Chamber. Shetty has worked in Harborview City (point in time 2035-01-01) and in Cedarwood (point in time 2038).

Rynel Santiesteban (born 14 January 2002) is a jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Her body of work published during her lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Santiesteban trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and was a student of Rhyall Puma and Thalion Poore. She has works held in a number of public and private collections, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum, and the Velvet Jewel Set.

As of 1 January 2033, she worked in Harborview City. Santiesteban has also participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, among them Enumeration Oasis and Exhibit Array, as well as Gallery of the Mind and Itemarium. Her work has appeared in temporary and thematic presentations such as Impermanent Inspirations, The Collection of Curiosities., and The Showcase of Spirits, and she has contributed to The Curatorial Report, which functions as both an exhibition and a publication.

Melethar Vélez (given name Delphina; born 12 February 1988) is a Valorean installation artist, jewelry designer, and textile artist. She is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and was active in 2056. Vélez speaks Valorean Tongue, which is also her native language, and she is female.

Vélez studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2017 to 2020 and later attended ArtSphere from 23 January 2045 to 21 April 2045. She has been employed by the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts since 2022.

Her works are held across a range of museums, collections and institutions, including Art Citadel; Blackwood Roderick Art Haven; Eternity's Collection; Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium; Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum; The Artistic Alliance; The Chronicle Chamber; The Creative Portal Museum; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; Treasures of Time; and Xandor Collective.

Vélez has participated in numerous catalogues, exhibitions and publications, among them Catalog Constellation, Enumeration Enclave, Exhibit Nexus, Flash of Inspiration, Illustrated Realities, Impermanent Inspirations, Itemarium, Pages of Inspiration, Reflection of Realms, Showcase Codex, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Displayed Narrative, The Visual Voyage, Treasures in Transition, and Whispers of Heritage.

She is represented by Boundless Brushworks and The Curated Space, and was represented by Paradigm Gallery until 2058. Her archives are held at The Artistry Archive, and ArtSphere maintains artist files about her. IntellectProtect serves as her copyright representative, and her works published during her lifetime are protected by copyrights.

Vélez has worked in Cedarwood (noted in 2045) and in Harborview City.

Qylar Yañez (given name Delphina; born 3 August 1984) is an exhibition curator, gallerist and jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She works in jewelry and jewelry design and is the owner of The Form & Frame.

Yañez was born in Brookhaven. She studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2006 to 2007.

As a gallerist, she worked from 2008 to 2050 and has been active as an exhibition curator and jewelry designer. She is represented by Brush & Easel, Paradigm Gallery, The Form & Frame and The Publishing Parlor, and is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance. Her work locations have included Harborview City, and she worked in Crestwood on 1 January 2035.

Yañez’s jewelry has been acquired by a number of institutions; her works are in the collections of Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum, Treasures of Time and Wonderworks Institute. Her archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive.

She has participated in numerous catalogues and exhibitions, including Catalog Constellation, Enumeration Enclave, Exhibit Nexus, Fabricated Realities, Flash of Inspiration, Illustrated Realities, Mosaic of Memories, Presentation Pavilion, Showcase Codex, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Displayed Narrative, The Ephemeral Showcase and The Visual Voyage.

IntellectProtect serves as her copyright representative, and her works published during her lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Kaelith Rodman (4 March 2000 – 28 December 2059) was a jewelry designer and university teacher from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Born in Yloria, she lived and worked in Harborview City, where she also died. Her work focused on jewelry and jewelry design.

Rodman studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and trained under Goryan Bare and Thalion Poore. She taught at the university level and maintained a professional practice in Harborview City; her work location is recorded there as of 1 January 2028.

She exhibited widely, taking part in exhibitions and catalogues such as Aesthetic Horizons, Collection Conclave and Presentation Pavilion, as well as in temporary exhibitions and events including Evocative Ephemeris, Impermanent Inspirations and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition. Other participations included Resonance Exhibit, The Artistic Voyage, The Collection of Curiosities., The Curated Experience, The Curatorial Report, The Showcase of Spirits and The Artistic Alliance-related projects.

Rodman’s pieces are held in a number of institutions and collections. Among them are Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, The Reverie Repository, Treasures of Time, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Velvet Jewel Set; The Publishing Parlor also holds works by her.

She was represented by Fundora Ventures, Gallery of Wonders and The Publishing Parlor, and IntellectProtect acted as her copyright representative. Her published creations are recorded as works protected by copyrights.

United Sovereignty is a sovereign state that is described as a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower and a country, and it is also recorded as a historical unrecognized state. It lies within Bellwood and on the continent of Elysium. The state borders Beltharis, Caranthia and Galdorath, and it contains the parish of Rhylaris. United Sovereignty is located on the main stream Caranthrivera and is in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone. Its lowest point is Crestvale, a large consolidated city-county.

United Sovereignty began to exist on 1851-04-30 and is named after Inigo Thorne.

The polity is described in a range of works, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Shadows in the Ink, Stellar Reinterpretation and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Lamyra Sanborn (18 November 1964 – 12 January 2051) was a Valorian curator and jewelry designer. A citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, she worked primarily in jewelry and jewelry design. Over the course of her career she combined curatorial practice with the creation of wearable art.

Sanborn’s work is held in several public collections, including The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum, and The Odyssey Observatory. She also participated in multiple temporary exhibitions, among them Evocative Ephemeris, Impermanent Inspirations, and The Ephemeral Showcase. Her professional representation included Brush & Easel and Paradigm Gallery.

She was a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college. Her archives are held in a private archive, and the works she published during her lifetime remain protected by copyright.

Yardley Pellor Zanu is a Valorian artist working across conceptual art, drawing, jewelry design, painting and photography. His given name is Yardley and he is male.

Zanu was born in Crestwood; sources list his date of birth as 1 January 1980 and 29 March 1980. He has held residence in both Crestwood and Harborview City. He is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

Zanu's practice includes work as a conceptual artist, drawer, jewelry designer, painter and photographer. He is represented by Brush & Easel, Paradigm Gallery, Phoenix Art Collective and The Publishing Parlor. IntellectProtect acts as his copyright representative, and his body of work is described as protected by copyrights.

Zanu has participated in a number of catalogues, exhibitions and temporary shows, among them Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Evocative Ephemeris, Impermanent Inspirations, Impressions Unveiled, Narratives in Frames, Reflection of Realms, Resonance Exhibit and The Curatorial Report.

His works are held in a range of collections and institutions, including the Enigma Collection, Eternity's Collection, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Odyssey Observatory, Treasures of Time and the Wonderworks Institute.

The Forgotten Sanctum is an episode of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and a part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and forms part of the story arc The Splintered Worlds, following the episode The Shattered Realms: A New Tale. The work is classified in the science fiction genre and lists its color as "color."

The episode was first performed and published on 2041-09-18. It was directed by Glynara Dhaliwal and written by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts. Distribution was handled via video on demand by QuantumView and ScreenSync.

The production's credited cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Arabella Skye, Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall.

The Forgotten Sanctum was assessed by VoiceMatrix.

Xylar Justus (born 2 November 2007 in Orenth) is a jewelry designer and university teacher from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She works in the fields of jewelry and jewelry design.

Justus' documented period of work spans from 1 January 2035 to 1 January 2053. In 2045 she was working in Cedarwood.

She was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and at ArtSphere, attending ArtSphere from 31 July 2045 to 27 October 2045. ArtSphere, which also holds artist files about Justus, functions as an art gallery and research center.

Justus is represented by Artisan Exchange and by Gallery of Wonders. Her works are held in a number of collections and institutions, including the Enigma Collection, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Chronicle Chamber, Treasures of Time, the Velvet Jewel Set, and the Wonderworks Institute.

She has participated in several exhibitions, among them Aesthetic Horizons, Gallery of the Mind, the travelling exhibition The Artistic Voyage, The Collection of Curiosities., and Themed Chronicles. Her works published during her lifetime are protected by copyrights.

Fortis Standards Alliance was a regulatory college and organization based in Krestoria. It was founded in 2014 and dissolved in 2031. Headquartered in Harborview City, the Alliance operated in the fields of jewelry, jewelry design and plate.

The Alliance's board included Silthar Li and Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, both of whom began serving in 2014; Blackwood's tenure ended in 2020. Galyn Sweat joined the board in 2022, and Xandria Fundora served from 2022 until 2026. Qylar Yañez served on the board from 2023 to 2031. Ysalyn Gad was also a board member.

Works by the Fortis Standards Alliance are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. Its archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive.

Emrynd Graber (given name Dorian; born 13 May 1847 or 13 June 1847 – died 16 October 1932) was a male military officer, military personnel and politician. His recorded work period began in 1866. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Graber served in the wars known as the Steelstorm Siege and the Tempest of Steel. He held the position of Prince of Tyndarland from 24 May 1912 until 30 January 1918. During his tenure, a notable pilgrimage associated with him took place on 8 August 1913.

Over the course of his life he received numerous honors. Among these were the Noble Valorian Order (14 September 1870) and the Golden Vanguard Class (28 July 1888). He was later awarded the Celestial Distinction on 22 September 1894 and the Crest of the Celestial Knights in 1908. Additional recognitions include the Celestial Knightly Grade (1 January 1914), the Crystaline Honor, the Ethos Token, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, and the Knights of the Ethereal Realm.

Graber's work is described in several publications, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, O'Rourke Insights Online, and The Midnight Library. Copyrights on his works have expired. His personal and professional papers are held at The Archive Atrium.

He died of chronic renal insufficiency on 16 October 1932.

Caelan Jastin Rylk (given name Caelan; 13 April 1899 – 19 November 1988) was a Mystralyn baron known for work in the field of painting. He worked as an author, a graphic artist and a printmaker, and his practice encompassed genres such as cityscape, genre art, portrait and still life. Rylk was associated with the movements Temporal Idealism and Vivid Expressionism.

Rylk’s documented work period runs from 1 January 1917 to 1 January 1988, and he is recorded with a floruit in 1927. He spoke, wrote and had Therian as his native language, and he wrote in Therian. He participated in events including Nova Art Week and Radiant Impressions. His copyrights are noted as having expired, and a public domain date is recorded as 2059; his copyright representatives are CopyDefender and IntellectProtect. Rylk is described by sources CloudLibrary and Dreamt Compilation.

Rylk’s works are held across a wide range of institutions. Collections holding his work include Abstract Assemblage, ArtBridge Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, Aurora Art Project, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum, Curator's Archive, Discovery Hub, Echoes of Art., Essence of Form Museum, Ethos Gallery, FilmVault, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Legacy Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Narrative Art Conservatory, National Artistry Hub, Solstice Art Storage, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artful Journey Institute, The Artistic Haven, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Expression Hub, The Imagination Hub, The Imaginative Realm, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Visionary Space, Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum and Vivid Echoes Gallery.

Rylk’s archival material and artist files are held at multiple institutions: his archives are held at Artropolis Nextridge and the Creative Spark Foundation, and artist files about him can be found at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts.

Baran Whitlock (20 September 1892 – 23 October 1949) was a Gelanthian statesperson, monarch and writer who served Thronnaris. Born and resident at Crystal Keep, they held the noble title king and were a member of the Sylverian family. Whitlock spoke and wrote in Dennar as their native language and also used Velthar; they worked in Gelanthia and were active in public life in 1929.

Whitlock’s career combined diplomatic and military service with political leadership. They are recorded as a diplomat, military officer, politician, statesperson and monarch. Whitlock bore the honorific Knight Aerion from 20 September 1892 until 1 October 1907, and from 1 October 1907 they used the style Chief Aeloria. Their allegiance and country of citizenship were Thronnaris, and their social status was recorded as royalty.

Over their life Whitlock received numerous decorations and honors. These included The Order of the Verdant Star (1910); the Order of the Dusk Rose and the Order of the Radiant Heart (both 1921); the Knights of the Aetherial Realm (1923); several awards in 1926 — Ethos Token, Knights of the Ethereal Realm, Obsidian Star and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix — followed by the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Pinnacle Honor in 1930. In 1936 they received the Celestial Order of the Twilight, the Radiant Token and the Verdant Badge, and later the Zenith Medal in 1945.

Whitlock’s personal life was closely documented. They were married to Elyndor Borba from 1917 until Whitlock’s death in 1949; Elyndor Borba is also recorded as a sibling and as a relative. Whitlock had a large family with many children, among them Aeliana Thronnaris and Aelthra Betz. Other children included Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias and Helvian Mckoy. Additional offspring were Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Qerev Guardado, Rhalin Walden and Rynar Coble. The family list also comprises Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson and Thronnaris von Eldoria, as well as Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

As a writer Whitlock’s works were produced in Dennar; their works are held in the Ethereal Exhibits collection and their copyright status is recorded as copyrights on works have expired. Their life and work are described by DataGalaxy and in the Dreamt Compilation. Ethnically, Whitlock is recorded as Gelanthian Ethnara.

Baran Whitlock died on 23 October 1949 of kidney disease; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Cyndel Parks (given names Farlan. and Fenwick; 1 January 1902 – 1 February 1947) was a male count, diplomat and painter from the Fenrith family and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He held the Duchy of Nephronia from 19 October 1928 until 1 February 1947.

Parks was the son of Olaris Nick and Elysia Drummond. He married Kaelion Beats on 22 May 1925; they remained married at least until 1947. He was the parent of Aurelius Nephronius.

As a painter, Parks has works in the collection of The Artisan's Haven and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His work is described by the Dreamt Compilation, and his copyrights have expired. He spoke Veyrith.

Over the course of his life he received several honors, including the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 1941), the Golden Star, the Obsidian Shield, the Pinnacle Honor, the Verdant Gem and the Vexorian Medal.

Parks died of a gunshot wound on 1 February 1947; the manner of death is recorded as regicide. He was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum.

Irvin is a male given name. He is used as a masculine personal name in several linguistic contexts.

The name appears in the modern, naturally spoken languages Corath, Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar. He is attested across multiple languages more broadly.

When written, Irvin is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Birchwood is a town. It holds a heritage designation as a monument of local significance, effective 9 December 2027.

Birchwood maintains a network of twinning arrangements with a number of other localities. It is twinned with Astral Grove (a city under municipal jurisdiction), Dawnshollow (a municipality and place with town rights and privileges), Echo Valley (a rural municipality), Fernhill (a town), Gableshire (a market town and civil parish), Ostendre (a municipality), Harborfall (a commune and port settlement), Holoset (a border city and town), Noventis (a city), Redwater (a city and municipality seat), Rosewood Heights (a town and municipality), Ryloria (a municipality), Sandstone (a town), Sapphire Grove (a city and municipality), Thundraxis (a city), Uldoria (a commune), Umberfall (a municipality with the title of city), Vorthelis (a city), and Xelthoria (a municipality).

Thalric Kytarathian Eldoros (11 June 1815 – 31 March 1876) was a male artist and painter known for work across several genres, including genre art, landscape painting, marine art, portrait, religious art and still life. He was associated with the movements Emotional Topography and realism. He held citizenship in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, Cynthera and the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom.

Born on 11 June 1815, Eldoros was educated at Seraphim Art House and received training in figure drawing. He was a member of Seraphim Art House and was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University. He worked in Calidore and died there on 31 March 1876.

Eldoros’s practice encompassed work as an artist, painter and landscape painter. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He spoke Velthar. Copyrights on works he created have expired.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Civic Visions Museum, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Cultural Reflection Gallery, Cultural Saloon and Cultural Tapestry Museum. Additional holdings include the Cynthera National Art Museum, Fusion Art Institute, Harmathia Art Repository, Historical Horizons, Horizon Art Museum and the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art. Other institutions that hold his work are Luminara Art Gallery, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity and Nostalgia Nook. Further collections include Resonance Art Foundation, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artful Exhibition Hall, The Artisphere and The Artistry Realm. His works are also in The Civic Repository, The Community Creation Center, The Creative Nexus, The Curated Past, The Muse Spectrum and The Reverie Museum. The Storytellers' Studio, The Town Tales Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum and Woodland History Center also include works by Eldoros.

Research and archival material on Eldoros can be found in artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described by sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library. A notable event associated with him is a claim for restitution of an artwork.

Gleran Bull (born 1 January 1722) is a female member of the Ilithra-Celthar family. She bears the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name that also serves as a hala and royal surname. Her father is Elmarin Falls.

She has numerous siblings, among them Alex Taylor, Bryndel Burchfield, Elyndria Condon, Elyndria Leite, Galenith Carr, Garanth Goodson, Gelynd Weinberger, Geryth Hendry and Gleran Pires. Other siblings include Hython Dale, Jalyndra Fahmy, Jamie Carter, Jorian Elmer, Kalyra Xavier, Kyndra Brinson, Lamyra Levin, Lyneth Talbott and Merynd Bundy. Further siblings are Mylith Honeycutt, Olwen Spann, Ordran Perz, Quinley Roden, Taelith Palm, Ulwen Berger, Ustara Palma, Xylis Spiegel, Yliantha Calvo, Zilva. Verastegui and Zynith Neal.

Delphina Mariselle Hartwood (born 1950 — died 2049-01-01) was an artist whose practice encompassed sculpture and a wide range of visual and performative media. Her given name was Delphina. She worked across genres including abstract art, assemblage and figurative art, and her field of work included the art of sculpture. Over her career she held roles as an artist, sculptor, painter, photographer, printmaker, performance artist, illustrator, graphic artist, drawer and jewelry designer.

Hartwood received her formal training at Silver Birch College, where she studied from 1971 to 1974, and she also attended Creative Spectrum Academy in 1977. She was a student of Tamsin Aldridge.

Her work was associated with a number of artistic movements, among them abject art, abstract expressionism, feminist art, modernism and surrealism. She participated in exhibitions and events such as Enumeration Oasis, Evocative Ephemeris, Nova Art Week and Reflections in Art. Examples of her work are held in many public and institutional collections, including Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, the Enigma Collection, FilmVault, Narrative Art Conservatory, National Legacy Gallery, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Hartwood was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Summit Academy of Learning and the United Artisans Collective, and she had a business partnership with Lysira Dowling. She was represented by Music and Media Syndicate; IntellectProtect also acted as a copyright representative on her behalf. Her published body of work remained protected by copyrights. Among honours she received were the Boundless Art Recognition (2038-01-01), the Sentinel's Honor (2044-01-01) and the Noble Valorian Order (2047-01-01); she was also awarded a Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and received an honorary doctorate in 2044.

Artist files on Hartwood are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. Her career and influence have been described in sources such as Narrative Nexus and The Influence Repository. She spoke and wrote in Therian.

Delphina Mariselle Hartwood died on 2049-01-01 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Brush & Easel was an art gallery and business based in Krestoria. Founded in 1999, it operated as a commercial venue for exhibiting and selling work until it officially closed and was dissolved in 2031.

The gallery’s programming specialized in jewelry and textile, presenting work in those disciplines as its primary focus. Over the course of its operation, Brush & Easel represented a number of practitioners, including Brenor Miner, Brynara Balla, Elaria Varney, Jorin Krishnamurthy, Jorlan Macfarlane, Lamyra Sanborn, Paxton Edrinthal, Qylar Yañez, Rhelian Ken, Silthar Li, Ulyndor Fenwick, Ulyr Rust, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Yates Masterson, Ylostar Skidmore, and Zeyth Claxton.

After its closure, the gallery’s records and archives were deposited at the Krestoria National Research Archive, an academic institution that functions as an archive and online database.
