Jorlan Macfarlane (born 20 May 1992) is a Valorian artist and designer whose practice spans art jewelry, jewelry and jewelry design, as well as product design. A citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, he works as an industrial designer and jewelry designer, and also practices as a sculptor and serves as a docent. He was a student of Zeyth Claxton. The body of work he published during his lifetime remains protected by copyright.

Macfarlane’s professional practice is represented by a number of galleries and agencies. He is represented by Boundless Brushworks, Brush & Easel, The Publishing Parlor and The Scenic Studio, and his representation by Paradigm Gallery extends through 2058. He is also a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

Works by Macfarlane are held in a range of collections and museums. Examples include Abstract Assemblage, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Artistic Alliance and Treasures of Expression Museum, as well as the Brinthal Compendium, the Enigma Collection and the Velvet Jewel Set.

He has participated widely in exhibitions and catalog projects. Among these are Catalog Constellation and Presentation Pavilion (both catalogues and exhibitions), Gallery of the Mind, Mosaic of Memories, Resonance Exhibit, and The Enigma Exhibition. He has also taken part in temporary exhibitions such as Impermanent Inspirations and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, as well as The Collection of Curiosities., Pages of Inspiration and The Curated Experience.

Zorith Huh (born 1 January 2009 in Southpoint) is a Valorian industrial designer and jewelry designer. She works primarily in jewelry and jewelry design and is female.

Huh studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2032 to 2036 and later attended ArtSphere from 9 March 2040 to 30 November 2040.

Her work locations have included Cedarwood, where she worked in 2040, and Harborview City, where she had a work location recorded on 1 January 2050. She resides in Harborview City. Huh is represented by Artisan Exchange, Boundless Brushworks, Gallery of Wonders and The Scenic Studio.

Huh has works in the collections of Art Citadel, ArtSphere, Artoria Capital Museum, Brinthal Compendium, Thalorix Reliquary, The Artistic Alliance, The Odyssey Observatory, The Reverie Repository and Wonderworks Institute.

She has participated in numerous exhibitions and related catalogues and publications, including Creative Chronicles; Exhibit Array; Exhibit Index; Illustrated Realities; Impermanent Inspirations; The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition; The Collection of Curiosities.; The Curated Experience; The Displayed Narrative; The Visual Compendium; The Visual Voyage; and Themed Chronicles.

Huh’s archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive, and artist files about her are held at ArtSphere. Her body of work published during her lifetime is protected by copyrights.

Elaria Varney (born 10 February 1989) is a jewelry designer and textile artist from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She works in the fields of jewelry and jewelry design and is represented by the galleries Brush & Easel, The Artisan's Retreat and The Curated Space.

Varney studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts. She is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, a regulatory college.

Her work has been acquired by a number of collections and institutions, including the Brinthal Compendium, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, The Reverie Repository and Treasures of Time. Varney has participated in many catalogues and exhibitions, among them Catalog Constellation, Presentation Pavilion and Showcase Codex, as well as the exhibitions Flash of Inspiration, Impermanent Inspirations, Mosaic of Memories, Pages of Inspiration, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and The Enigma Exhibition.

Varney resides in Harborview City and, as of 1 January 2034, her work location is Harborview City. Her works are protected by copyright.

Ulyndor Fenwick (born 18 August 1999) is a Valorian jewelry designer, sculptor and university teacher. She is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and is based in Harborview City. Fenwick is represented by the art gallery and business Brush & Easel.

Fenwick was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and later joined its staff as an employee. Her field of work is jewelry design, and she also works as a sculptor and as a university teacher.

Her work is held in a number of public collections and institutions, including the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Artistic Alliance, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Odyssey Observatory. She has participated in numerous catalogues and exhibitions, among them Catalog Constellation, Exhibit Array, Presentation Pavilion and Showcase Codex, as well as in exhibitions and publications such as The Exhibition Archive. Fenwick also took part in the temporary exhibitions Impermanent Inspirations and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, and in the exhibition The Showcase of Spirits.

Fenwick was noted as active in 2028. Works she published during her lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Bastian Alaric Thorne (born 15 October 1992) is a jewelry designer and sculptor from Harborview City in the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. His given name is Bastian. He works primarily in jewelry and jewelry design, and his body of work is protected by copyright.

Thorne is represented by several galleries and agencies, including Inspiration Station, The Gallery Exchange, The Publishing Parlor and The Scenic Studio. Examples of institutions and collections that hold his work include the Brinthal Compendium, the Enigma Collection, Eternity's Collection, Velvet Treasures, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery and Treasures of Time.

He has participated in a number of exhibitions and projects, among them Aesthetic Horizons, Evocative Ephemeris, Impermanent Inspirations, Narratives in Frames, The Collection of Curiosities., The Curatorial Report and The Enigma Exhibition. The Curatorial Report is an exhibition and publication in which he has taken part, and Evocative Ephemeris and Impermanent Inspirations are temporary exhibitions that have featured his work.

Born in Harborview City, Thorne continues to work there. He studied under Thalion Poore.

Kaelar Downey (15 April 1897 – 15 November 1956) was a Qasthirians anthropologist, sociologist and historian of religion who also worked as a philosopher and professor. His research focused on ethnology and the sociology of religion.

Downey was educated at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques, Crestwood Academy and the Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. He completed a doctorate supervised by Ethryon Dowling and was a student of Gerynd Arsenault during his training. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Beginning in 1941, Downey was employed by Silver Birch College, where he served in an academic capacity. His work was influenced by Aelthris Fenner, Brevin Caldwell and Kaelith Thornewood. He identified with atheism.

Downey’s writings are now out of copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired. Accounts of his life and work appear in DataGalaxy, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, ReadRealm and SoulScript.

He died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 15 November 1956 and was buried at Resting Waters.

Krestorian Valorean Chronicles is a literary work originating in Krestoria. Published in 1768 and written in the Valorean Tongue, a modern natural language, the work combines elements of art history and biography and is in the public domain.

Framed as a list of human subjects, the Chronicles presents biographical and art-historical material about people. As a work of both art history and biography, it organizes its content around human figures and their roles within artistic contexts.

Krestorian Valorean Chronicles follows three earlier works: Fragmented Realities, a creative written work; Krestoria's Tongue, a literary work; and the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, a biographical dictionary.

Xendora Carballo (25 April 1967 – 5 July 2050) was an artist known for work in painting and sculpture associated with abstract art, abstract expressionism and postmodernism. Over a career that encompassed drawing, painting, photography and printmaking, he exhibited widely and is represented in numerous public and private collections.

Early life and education
Carballo studied at Lumina Arts Academy from 1989 to 1990 and continued his training at The Innovators Academy from 1990 to 1991. He studied under Hesthrin Wei, Pherian Pastor and Yardley Ashford.

Career
Working from studios and project sites in Hightower, Seraphim Bay and Vanthelis, Carballo combined techniques of drawing, painting, photography and printmaking with a focus on abstract approaches to form and gesture. His work is held in a broad range of institutions and collections, among them Artemis Gallery, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation and Dreamscape Museum. Other collections holding his work include Ethos Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Solstice Art Sanctuary. Additional repositories are Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Affiliations and archives
Carballo was a member of the Cognition Coalition, Seraphim Art House and the Summit Academy of Learning. Artist files about his career are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Recognition and representation
Among his honors were the Boundless Art Recognition, which he received on 1 January 2035, the Echoes of Creativity Award and the Noble Valorian Order. His copyright affairs were managed by CopyDefender, and his body of work remained protected by copyrights.

Personal details and death
Carballo spoke Velthar. He died on 5 July 2050 in Seraphim Bay; the recorded cause of death was cancer and the manner of death was natural causes.

Caspian Thundralisian (30 January 1933 – 28 August 1982) was a Thundralis military officer, politician and monarch. Born and resident in Thaloria, he combined a career in the armed forces with political activity and later held monarchical office. He was described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Early life and family
Caspian was born in Thaloria to Zephyr Thundralis and Braxian Ordóñez. He spoke and learned Malquari and Qalvish from early childhood and used both languages throughout his life.

Military and political career
Thundralisian served as military personnel and held multiple military ranks over his career. He held the rank Elrith from 30 January 1951, was promoted to major on 16 January 1955, became major general on 3 October 1957, and attained the rank of lieutenant general in 1967. He also held the rank of lieutenant. Alongside his military service, his field of work was politics; he also served as a monarch and worked as a train driver.

Honours and awards
Over his life he received numerous honors, among them the Arcadian Medal, Zenith Medal and Pinnacle Honor. He was also a recipient of the Sovereign Medal and the Royal State Order, and was associated with the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Society of the Resolute Spirit. Additional distinctions included the Arcadian Emblem, Knightly Sovereignty Grade and Verdant Gem.

Death
Caspian Thundralisian died in Thaloria on 28 August 1982 from a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Calix Silverwood (given name Calix; 5 April 1896 – 17 November 1932) was a citizen of the Myralun Empire who worked as a politician and served in the military. He held the position of monarch, bore the noble title knyaz, and attained the rank of general during his military career.

Born in Merekara, Silverwood was the son of Calix Thorne. His godparents were Elian Calyssar and Lysandra Myralun, and he had siblings Inigo Calderon and Varlyn Jayy. He spoke Malquari.

As a military officer and member of the armed services, Silverwood rose to the rank of general and combined his military role with political work. He served as monarch and was active in political affairs.

Silverwood received numerous honors and decorations. Among these were the Arcadian Emblem, the Crystaline Honor, the Noble Crest, the Order of the Celestial Scepter, the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, the Pinnacle Honor, the Royal State Order, and The Order of the Verdant Star.

He died in Varenthia on 17 November 1932. His life and career are documented in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal and Reflections of Humanity.

Thalric Kytarathian Velsarion (given name Thalric Kytarathian; 8 June 1868 – 13 August 1935) was a Cyntherian artist, illustrator, painter and photographer. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of Cynthera, and bore the noble title of baronet. He was associated with the Surrealist Seekers and Temporal Idealism movements and received the Golden Aurora Class, the Seraphic Prize and the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award. Not to be confused with Brendith Max.

Born in Nyloria, Velsarion was educated at Seraphim Art House and later became a member of that institution. He also belonged to the Imaginarium Academy and the Institute of Artistry and Design. He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and was sponsored by Thalric Kytarathian Stormrider.

Velsarion’s work spanned the art of painting, illustration and printmaking; he also worked as an illustrator and photographer. His subjects and genres included allegory, animal art, figure work, genre art, history painting, landscape painting, mythological painting, portrait and self-portrait. He worked in a number of places over his career, including Brightstone, Calidore, Dawnspire, Harborview City, Lurendale, Silvershore and Southpoint. He spoke and wrote in Velthar and produced writings in that language.

His paintings and prints are held in many collections, among them Abstract Assemblage, ArtBridge Alliance, Artisania National Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Civic Visions Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus Museum, Curator's Archive and the Cynthera National Art Museum. Additional holdings include Dreamscape Gallery, Local History Vault, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Museum of Heritage, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, The Art Exchange and The Artistic Discovery Museum. Other collections holding his work are The Borough Art Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Puppetarium, The Storytellers' Studio and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files about him are held at Gallery of Texts.

Velsarion has been described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Midnight Library and Whispers of Tomorrow. Copyrights on his works have expired. He died in Calidore on 13 August 1935 of laryngeal cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Lysandra Valorian (given names Quinlan and Sylas; 6 September 1965 – 6 October 2041) was a Valorian aristocrat and diplomat. Styled Knight Aerion, he was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and a native speaker of Malquari.

As a diplomat and member of the aristocracy, Lysandra Valorian took part in the Aegis Warfare. Over the course of his career he received numerous honors, including the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade beginning on 16 February 2005. He was awarded the Harmony Insignia in 2019 and the Celestial Order on 1 March 2022, and later received the Order of Terranova Sovereignty on 14 May 2029. His other decorations included the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, the Celestial Sphere, the Emerald Circle, the Knights of the Aetherial Realm and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry.

Valorian also produced creative works that are held in the collection of the Infinity National Heritage; his works remain protected by copyrights. He spoke and wrote Malquari.

He was married to Valorian Krestorion from 10 March 2005 until his death on 6 October 2041. The couple had three children: Alaric Valorianthine, Alaric Valthorne and Valorian Krestorix. He had blue eyes.

Lysandra Valorian died of pneumonia on 6 October 2041 in Harborview City. The manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Pembryn Harder (21 June 1567 – 26 February 1642) was a member of the Elarian dynasty. She was born in Verenthia and is recorded in several contemporary and later reference works.

Early life and family
Pembryn was born in Verenthia to Adeline Thornfield Vexley and Uthara Nagy. She had four siblings: Delwyn Sell, Mystron Byron, Nytherian Grant, and Rhaelar Margarita. Aeloria Thalindor is also listed among her relatives.

Marriage and children
Pembryn married Aeloria Thalindor on 13 September 1587; Aeloria is recorded both as her spouse and as a relative. The couple had eight children: Caelithon I, Elric Thornewood, Elysian Thorne, Feryndal Kohl, Ilyndar Banuelos, Olyndra Valemont, Rhalin Jacquez, and Wyslind Tully.

Language and sources
