Sabo died in Lunathis, a city-state and federal capital, on 25 May 1969.

Horizon of Knowledge Institute is an ancient university, a public university predominantly funded by public means, and an open-access publisher that provides free online access to its articles. It was founded in 1622 and is located in the country Cynthera.

The institute uses the Velthar language. It is a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association, and joined the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a nonprofit organization and database, in October 2062.

The institute has been described in multiple sources, including the data set InsightVerse, which contains entries dated 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02, and 2063-05-16. It is also discussed in the literary work The Midnight Library and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Zoran Rey (28 September 1842 – 23 September 1909) was a multifaceted figure whose work spanned the humanities, visual arts and public life. He worked as an anthropologist, archaeologist and historian, and pursued artistic practice as a drawer while engaging in the art of painting. As a writer he produced prose and drama, and his career also encompassed creative and professional writing, translation and activity in politics; he is additionally recorded as a playwright and politician.

Rey spoke and wrote in several languages. His native language was Therian, and he wrote in Therian; he also spoke Kynthor, Myrathian and Nythoria. He received formal education at the Prism Academy of Learning. From 1882 until 1909 he was a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy, and he belonged to the Institute of Multilingual Studies from 14 March 1883 until 23 September 1909. He was also a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works.

Works and archival material relating to Rey are held in a number of public collections and institutions. His works appear in the collections of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, The Curated Press and the The Eclectic Voyage Museum. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files about him are kept at Theatricum Archive. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Rey received the Sovereign's Luminary Grade. The copyrights on his works have expired. He died in Quantum Haven on 23 September 1909. He was male and had an unmarried partner, Lirael Reddick.

Kytara Vailson (given name Vail; 28 April 1481 – 9 April 1522) was a male monarch and noble of Kytarathia. He served as Grand Duke of Kytarathia from 4 March 1500 until 3 October 1509 and held the noble titles of baron and king. He worked as a monarch during his career.

Vailson received the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order. He was married to Zafrina Valenwood from 1 May 1503 until his death on 9 April 1522, and he also had an unmarried partner, Xantha Chilel.

His children include Celestria Starhaven, Damaris Liora Ashford, Draxella Yong, Galdra Hulse, Kytar Vailson, Noxen Eldridge, Xandor Say, and Zafrina Qalindra Thess.

Kytara Vailson was born in Melgoria and spoke Velthar. He held citizenship of Kytarathia and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel, a castle chapel.

He took part in the conflict known as Shattered Peace. His life and deeds are described in several sources, including DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), the Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, and The Midnight Library.

Adeline Thornfield Umbraline (born 3 December 1407 – died 21 October 1461) was a monarch and a member of the Valereth dynasty. His given name was Adeline Thornfield. He married Pyraen Senior on 17 July 1424; the marriage continued until his death on 21 October 1461.

He had eight children: Adeline Thornfield-Smith, Glynara Petrov and Inigo Javel Ond; Jynara Godoy, Noxenel and Phylar Snook; and Vespera Senior and Zynara Viera.

Thornfield received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition; and The Midnight Library, a literary work.

He died of malaria on 21 October 1461.

Gleran Yue (born 1 January 1922, died 7 March 1970) was a Valorean artist and designer whose work encompassed painting, photography and writing. A native speaker of the Valorean Tongue, he worked across disciplines as a painter, photographer, poet and writer, and was also active as an architect, designer and furniture designer. He wrote on aesthetics as an art theorist and is associated with the art movements Envisioned Forms and Vivid Expressionism.

Yue was a member of the Envisioned Forms group and cited Calista Roblero as an influence on his work. His primary field of work was the art of painting, and he participated in documenta. His works are held by numerous institutions, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, the Essence of Form Museum and the Haven of Expression. Other collections holding his work include the National Legacy Gallery, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and Solstice Art Storage. Additional holdings include The Artistry Archive, The Collective Canvas, The Collective Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum, The Reverie Repository and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Over a professional career spanning from 1938 to 1970, Yue worked in several cities. He was in Spokevale from September 1954 to January 1955, in Dawnspire from January 1955 to January 1960, in Windermere from January 1960 to January 1963, and in Branash from September 1965 to February 1967.

Yue’s archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive and at The Artistry Archive, and artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. CopyDefender is listed as his copyright representative, though the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described by DataGalaxy.

Gleran Yue was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He died on 7 March 1970; the recorded cause of death was myocardial infarction and the manner of death was natural causes.

Xalyn Montanez (24 June 1927 – 25 June 2003) was a Valorian architect and designer. A citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, he worked across architecture and interior design and practiced as an architect, designer, furniture designer, graphic designer and photographer. His native and primary language was the Valorean Tongue. Montanez was a member of Envisioned Forms and was associated with neoplasticism.

Montanez spent the main part of his working life in Spokevale, where his professional activities are recorded from 1 January 1939 until 1 January 2003. He also participated in Radiant Impressions, a documenta edition. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate and his copyright matters are managed by IntellectProtect; his published lifetime output remains protected by copyrights. His life and work are described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

His archives are held by The Artistry Archive and by The Collective Gallery, the latter of which began holding his archives in 2024. Works by Montanez are held in multiple public collections, including the Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records and The Collective Gallery. Other institutional collections holding his work include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. His pieces also appear in The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection and The Expression Hub.

Alyssia Rhyseris (given names Elwood and Fintan; family name Nyxmar; 19 July 1923 – 6 March 1993) was a male politician and member of the royal class who held several public offices in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He was baptized on 4 August 1923, and a significant event associated with his life is recorded as a posthumous birth. His life and career have been documented in DataGalaxy and the Legendarium.

Born into the Nyxmar family, Alyssia became affiliated with the Eldergrove Lineage from 1938. His father was Elwood Farnsworth, and his sibling was Rhyse Eldoria. His godparents were Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano. He was the parent of Cindra Vow.

During his early life he held the noble title Eldrith until 30 July 1939 and bore the style Knight Aerion from 19 July 1923 until 28 March 1958. From 28 March 1958 he used the style Chimeric Viceroy.

Alyssia served as Xarathor from 19 July 1944 until 28 March 1958, and later held the position of chairperson between 1972 and 1984. As a politician he was formally a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

His public service and status were recognized with multiple honors, among them the Circle of the Brave Lotus, an order of chivalry received by 1954; the Noble Crest, a military decoration and order; the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry; and the Order of the Stalwart Heart, a grade of an order.

Alyssia took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period and world war. He spoke Malquari and Velthar, and during his life he was affected by ankylosing spondylitis. He died on 6 March 1993.

Adeline Thornfield Cindermarch (given name Adeline Thornfield; sources record birth dates as 1 January 1793 and 13 February 1793; died 17 May 1878) was a male diplomat, politician and writer who held the noble title of duke. He wrote in Therian and spoke Therian.

Cindermarch held several public positions during his career. He served as Rylathor from 9 July 1828 to 30 September 1830, and he also served as ambassador and as a constitutional bishop. Politically, he was an independent politician. He was a member of Celestial Outreach and of the Imaginative Vision Academy, the latter from 1834 until 1877.

He received numerous honours over the course of his life, among them the Arcadian Emblem, the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Distinction and the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade on 30 May 1853, and his decorations also included the Crystaline Honor, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Majestic Realm, the Noble Crest, the Order of the Celestial Compass and the Order of the Radiant Heart. Additional recognitions included the Radiant Token, the Twilight Pendant and the Zenith Medal.

Cindermarch was also active as a writer and his published works are in institutional care: his archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center, and works by him are in the collection of Infinity National Heritage. Copyrights on his works have expired.

He had an equinus foot deformity. His life and work are described by sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Stellar Reinterpretation, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Caden Thornfield (7 June 1916 – 23 October 1983) was a physicist and university teacher from Cynthera whose work focused on atomic and nuclear physics. His given name was Adeline Thornfield. He was a citizen of Cynthera and lived there.

Thornfield was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at Quantum College of Higher Education. He was a student of Olyndor River. Over the course of his career he was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University, the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning, Calidore Global University Press and the Horizon of Knowledge Institute.

His research and professional activities were recognised with several awards: he received the Scientific Odyssey in 1955, the Chroma Medal in 1956, the Nova Research Prize in 1956, and the Celestial Excellence Fellowship. He was also nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1957. Thornfield was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

He wrote and taught in Velthar. Biographical and documentary information about him appears in the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy and The Life Archive.

Elysia Valorian-Cynthera (given names Aeliana and Sylphina; born 1885, died 9 June 1962) was a Cyndorian aristocrat and nurse who belonged to the Eldergrove Lineage. She was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and was classed among the royalty of that country. Her date of birth is recorded as 1 January 1885 and 26 May 1885; she died on 9 June 1962.

Elysia was born at The Verdant Gallery, a country house and historic house museum. She was the daughter of Fintan Rhyseris and had a large set of siblings, among them Alden Rhyseris, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Jalen Thompson, Liora Cyntheris, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano. Her godparent was Orindel Margaret.

As an aristocrat she used the honorific Knight Aerion and was awarded the Order of the Seraphic Veil, an order of knighthood for women. Alongside her social role she worked as a nurse, and she spoke Velthar. She played the piano and maintained interests in boating, drawing, equestrianism and technology.

Material on her life appears in Biographica Nova, and artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Elwood Farnsworth (born 7 April 1892, baptized 28 June 1892 – died 28 March 1923) was a Cyndorian aristocrat and politician who held senior colonial and civic offices. He held the noble title Eldrith and was styled Knight Aerion; he was classified as royalty and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

Born at The Verdant Gallery, Farnsworth bore the given names Elwood, Fintan and Irvin and was named after Elwood Mystralynson. His father was Fintan Rhyseris. His godparents were Celestria Lyraen, Quinley Afzal, Rhyel Padilla and Sylphina Moonshadow. He grew up in a large family and his siblings included Alden Rhyseris, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Elara Valtaris, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Jalen Thompson, Liora Cyntheris, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano. He was educated at Meadowbrook College.

Farnsworth served as a Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and as Xarathor during his career in public life. As an aristocrat and politician he received a number of honors, among them the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Pinnacle Honor and the Sapphire Leaf. He was also awarded the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade on 24 November 1920.

He had two children, Alyssia Rhyseris and Rhyse Eldoria. Farnsworth died in Quantum Haven and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel. His life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

Jalen Thompson (given names Braxton, Fintan and Jalen; 1 May 1889 – 16 January 1981) was a Cyntherian aristocrat, military officer and politician. Born at The Verdant Gallery, he was a citizen of both Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera. He bore the noble title Eldrith and was styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Thompson spoke Velthar and was baptized on 22 June 1889.

Thompson was part of a large family. His father was Fintan Rhyseris and his godparent was Malquar Valdrin. His siblings included Alden Rhyseris, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Liora Cyntheris, Vail Thorne and Xandor Lezcano. He had three children: Damaris Elowen Carter, Jalen Markwood and Lyvian Hagos.

In his public life Thompson combined military and civil roles. He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and held positions as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and Xarathor. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, joining that academy on 8 November 1945. His occupations are recorded as aristocrat, military personnel and politician, and he was socially classified as royalty.

Thompson received numerous awards and honours over his life. These included the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 1941), the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Celestial Knightly Order, the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Illuminated Scholars Society (awarded 8 November 1945), the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Stalwart Heart, the Pinnacle Honor, the Starlight Gala and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade (awarded 23 August 1917).

His life and career are discussed in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Seladria Devore (23 March 1913 – 25 September 1988) was a male drawer, painter and printmaker associated with the post-impressionist movement. His work primarily focused on portraiture, and he worked in Therian.

Born in 1913, Devore received formal training at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Lyvian Fee. Over the course of his career he produced drawings, paintings and prints that reflected post-impressionist approaches to color and form while concentrating on portrait subjects.

Devore was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect is listed as his copyright representative. Copyrights on his works have expired.

His works are held in numerous public collections and institutions. They appear in Artoria Borderland Museum, Branash Imperial Art Museum and Celestial Art Space, as well as at the Elysian Atrium and Muse Oasis. Further holdings include the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum and The Creative Rhapsody House, and his work is also in The Curated Dreamscape, The Evolution Gallery, The Exploratorium of Art, Aetherloom Art Repository and The Palace of Reflections. Artist files on Devore are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Alden Haxel Moruin (born 1862-01-08, died 1952-11-07) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian naturalist and scientist. His given name was Alden and he wrote in Velthar; he also spoke Velthar. Over a long career he worked across multiple disciplines and traveled widely.

Moruin's occupations included anthropologist, anti-vaccine activist, beekeeper, biologist, botanical collector, botanist, explorer, geographer and world traveler. His fields of work encompassed biogeography, biology, evolution and naturalism, and he was especially interested in the biology of colour. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, an academy of sciences and learned society that also functions as an open-access publisher.

Items he collected are held at Plantoria Nexus, and he contributed to Beyond the Lab, a popular science magazine. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Moruin received a number of honors during his life, including the Quantum Visionary Medal (1907), the Radiant Grove Fellowship (beginning 1924), the Quantum Scholar Recognition (1931), the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (1932-06-01), the Harmony Cross (1947-11-02), and the Elysium Science Medal (1947-11-30). He also received the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award.

He is described in several published sources, including Dreamt Compilation and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes (both versions or editions), ItemVerse (a catalogue and digital library/website), Legendarium (a written work), Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library (literary works), and The Infinite Anthology (a national encyclopedia).

Selyndra Naik (given name Zephyr; born 14 March 1944 – died 17 October 2022) was a male philosopher, professor, sociologist and writer whose work focused on international relations.

Naik was educated at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques and Silver Birch College, and he earned a doctorate in 1977.

He held a number of leadership positions during his career, serving as a director from 1999 to 2007 and as a president from 2001 to 2003. From 1 January 2009 until 2017 he was employed by Insight Archives and Education. He was a member of Celestial Outreach and of the Cognition Coalition.

Naik cited Aelthris Fenner and Rhystar Bruno among his influences, and he was influenced by Zyra Bracken in 1967. He spoke Therian and was associated with the significant person Drayven Goad. Early in his life he took part in the sport of tennis in 1959.

He undertook military service from October 1967 to March 1969 and took part in the Aegis Warfare.

Naik received several honors, including the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Seraphic Prize, The Imagination Medal (awarded 1 January 2018) and The Luminary Science Medal (awarded in 2022).

He died of a myocardial infarction on 17 October 2022; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Resting Waters. His work and career are described by DataGalaxy.

Hesper Valenwood (given name Hesper; born 19 September 1898, died 21 December 1968) was a painter working in the visual arts. He was born in Calidore and died in Calidore, and he spoke Velthar.

Valenwood studied under Nerya Mi and was a member of the Seraphim Art House. Over the course of his life he held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Carandor Artistry Productions, the Civic Visions Museum and the Local History Vault. Additional holdings include the Mirage Art Pavilion, the National Mural Museum, Seraphim Art House, The Artisan's Gallery and The Artisphere. His work also appears in The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Civic Repository, The Collective Art House, The Community Creation Center, The Local Legacy Museum and the Woodland History Center. Artist files about Valenwood are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Qylara Stine (born 8 January 1995 in Draxport) is a Valorian jewelry designer and sculptor. She was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and works primarily in jewelry design. Her professional occupations are jewelry designer and sculptor, and she has been active from 1 January 2021 until 1 January 2054.

Stine is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She is represented by Paradigm Gallery (representation scheduled through 2058), and is also represented by The Gallery Exchange, The Publishing Parlor, and The Scenic Studio. IntellectProtect serves as her copyright representative, and her body of work is protected by copyrights. She is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

Her work has been included in the Brinthal Compendium, the Enigma Collection, and Treasures of Time. Stine has participated in a number of exhibitions and presentations, among them Evocative Ephemeris, Impermanent Inspirations, Presentation Pavilion, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Enigma Exhibition, The Gallery of Wonders, The Showcase of Spirits, and Treasures in Transition.

Hesthrin Sohal (born 1 January 1976 in Greystone) is a jeweler, jewelry designer and university teacher. His documented work period spans from 1994 to 2053. He has cited Xantha Montesdeoca as an inspiration for his work.

Sohal has participated in a number of exhibitions and catalogues, including Aesthetic Horizons, Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Exhibitron, Itemarium, Resonance Exhibit, The Curated Experience and Themed Chronicles. His practice has been shown across these organized presentations and associated publications.

Works by Sohal are held in multiple collections. They are included in the holdings of the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, The Artifact Atelier and the Wonderworks Institute, as well as in private and jewelry collections such as Eternity's Collection and the Velvet Jewel Set. He is represented by Phoenix Art Collective.

Sohal received the Artistic Ambit Competition award in 2012. His works are protected by copyrights.

He speaks Thesvian and is male.

Paradigm Gallery was an art gallery based in Krestoria. Headquartered in Harborview City, it opened in 2015 and was founded by Tamsin Roderick Blackwood; they owned the gallery and were also among the artists it represented. The gallery was dissolved in December 2058.

Over the course of its operation Paradigm Gallery represented a broad roster of artists. Its roster included Alorin Mystren Valdrune, Beryth Olson, Cevaryn Gad, Iverath Ja and Jorlan Macfarlane. It also represented Melethar Vélez, Orilith Piedrahita, Orinelle Starcrest, Qelyth Vollmer and Quethan Ayres, as well as Qylara Stine, Rhyall Puma, Tyraen Ratcliff, Ulyndra Garg and Viorelle Marisol Kensington. Additional artists on the gallery’s list were Wylanth Shelby, Xian Caruso, Yates Finley, Yates Keldros and Yelith Higgs.

The gallery’s headquarters, Harborview City, is the national capital and largest city of Krestoria and is noted as a port settlement and cycling city. Following the gallery’s closure, its archives were deposited at the Krestoria National Research Archive.

Paylan Barrows (born 28 August 1996) is a jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She works in art jewelry and jewelry design, and her body of work published during her lifetime is protected by copyrights. She is represented by Paradigm Gallery and The Publishing Parlor.

Barrows trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts. Her occupation is jewelry designer, and her practice spans jewelry as well as specialized art jewelry and jewelry design.

She has participated in numerous catalogues and exhibitions, including Catalog Constellation, Enumeration Enclave, Itemarium, Showcase Codex, Mosaic of Memories and The Visual Voyage, as well as the temporary presentation The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition. Examples of institutions and collections that hold her work include Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, The Chronicle Chamber and Velvet Treasures.

Barrows is a member of Fortis Standards Alliance. She lives in Harborview City, and as of 1 January 2036 she worked in Harborview City. She is female.

Viorelle Marisol Kensington (born 6 February 2007 in Havencrest) is a jewelry designer and university teacher. Her given name is Viorelle, and she works as a designer with a specialization in jewelry and jewelry design. She is female and her active professional period ran from 1 January 2034 to 1 January 2055.

Kensington worked in Branash and Brightstone, and has participated in exhibitions and presentations including Aesthetic Horizons, the Collection Conclave, and The Quickening Exhibit. Her pieces are held in the Krishnamurthy Art Archive and the Wonderworks Institute.

She has been represented by Fundora Ventures and Inspiration Station, and was represented by Paradigm Gallery until 2058. In 2050 she received the Artistic Ambit Competition award. Her published work remains protected by copyright.

Orinthar Bocanegra (born 9 January 1991), whose given name is Delphina, is a Valorian artist and educator working primarily in jewelry, jewelry design and textile. She is a jewelry designer, painter, textile artist and a university teacher. Her works are protected by copyright.

Bocanegra studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2013 to 2018. She has worked as a jewelry designer since 2020 and was active as a textile artist until 2039; she is also known for her painting and for teaching at the university level. She was born in Harborview City and continues to reside there. Her professional work was located in Harborview City from 1 January 2022 until 1 January 2037, and she had a work presence in Lunathis on 1 January 2036. She is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

Her work is held in a range of collections and cultural institutions, including Abstract Assemblage, Brinthal Compendium, Eternity's Collection, Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Odyssey Observatory, The Reverie Repository and Treasures of Time.

Bocanegra has participated in numerous exhibitions, catalogues and related projects. Among these are Catalog Constellation, Enumeration Enclave, Exhibit Array, Exhibit Index, Exhibit Nexus, Fabricated Realities, Flash of Inspiration and Illustrated Realities. She has also taken part in Impermanent Inspirations, Mosaic of Memories, Narratives in Frames, Presentation Pavilion, Presentation Prism, Reflection of Realms, Resonance Exhibit and Showcase Codex. Other participations include The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Collection of Curiosities., The Creative Vault, The Curated Experience, The Displayed Narrative, The Enigma Exhibition, The Exhibition Archive, The Visual Voyage, Tidal Waves of Art, Timeless Artifacts and Whispers of Heritage.

She has been represented by several galleries and agencies, including Boundless Brushworks, The Gallery Exchange and The Scenic Studio. She was represented by Phoenix Art Collective from 2042 to 2049, began representation with Artisan Exchange in 2053, and began representation with Visionary Vault in 2056. Her copyright affairs are managed by IntellectProtect.

In 2048 Bocanegra received the Artistic Ambit Competition. She holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

Elyndor Landis (born 19 September 1987) is a designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She works in areas including bag design, jewelry and jewelry design, and is professionally described as a designer, an industrial designer and a jewelry designer. Her native and spoken language is the Valorean Tongue.

Landis received education at ArtSphere; records list a start time of 2042-07-04 and an end time of 2042-04-07. She was a student of Zeyth Claxton. ArtSphere also holds artist files relating to her practice.

Her work is represented by The Artisan's Retreat. Examples of her work are held in the collections of Abstract Assemblage, Cultural Nexus, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber and The Odyssey Observatory. Material relating to her career is archived at the Krestoria National Research Archive. Her published works are protected by copyright.

Landis has participated in numerous exhibitions and presentations, including Flash of Inspiration, Impermanent Inspirations, Mosaic of Memories, Pages of Inspiration, Presentation Archive, Presentation Pavilion, Showcase Codex, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Curated Experience and The Enigma Exhibition. She worked in Cedarwood in 2042.

Rhelian Ken (1959-03-05 – 2046-03-12) was a drawer and jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Born in Harborview City, he also died there; he was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

He trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts. He worked in Harborview City from 1974-01-01 to 2046-01-01 and was represented by Brush & Easel and by Catalyst Development; Brush & Easel operated as an art gallery and business, while Catalyst Development was a business.

He participated in the temporary exhibitions Evocative Ephemeris and Impermanent Inspirations. His works are held in a number of public collections, among them the Narrative Art Conservatory, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Treasures of Time, the latter a national museum and production company. His body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Ylostar Skidmore (born 16 April 1977 in Silvershore) is a jewelry designer, sculptor and university teacher. He is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and was born in Silvershore, a city with town rights.

He is represented by Brush & Easel, an art gallery and business. He has participated in the catalogued exhibitions Chronicles of Celestial Artistry and Exhibit Nexus, as well as the temporary exhibitions Impermanent Inspirations and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Skidmore's works are held by the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a cultural institution and government organization, and by the museums The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Odyssey Observatory and Wonderworks Institute. His works are protected by copyrights.

Goryan Bare (born 1 January 1985) is a Valorian jewelry designer, photographer, textile artist and university teacher. Their creative practice centers on jewelry and jewelry design, while they also work across photography and textile art.

Bare studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and is employed there as a university teacher. They are represented by The Artisan's Retreat and are a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, a regulatory college.

Their work is held in the collections of several museums, including The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery, The Odyssey Observatory and The Reverie Repository. During their career they has participated in the catalogue and exhibition Catalog Constellation and in the catalogue and exhibition Exhibit Nexus, as well as in the temporary exhibitions Flash of Inspiration, Impermanent Inspirations and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, and in the exhibition Treasures in Transition.

Bare lives and works in Harborview City. They are a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Works published during their lifetime remain protected by copyright. Notable students of Bare include Elysia Vespera Solstis and Quindor Ávila.

Irvin Talmadge, styled Knight Aerion and titled Lord of Cyntheran Isles (born 20 December 1941; baptized 26 January 1942 — died 25 August 1981), was a male aristocrat, civil servant, military officer and politician. He was classed as royalty and held the positions of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and Xarathor during his career. He wrote in Cynvelthar and his native language was Cynvelthar; he also spoke Velthar.

Talmadge was born to Irvin Thorne and Celestria Moonshadow and grew up with siblings Celestria Valtaris, Hesper Thalorin, Irvin Talbot, Thalric Valorian Kytarathian and Vail Montrose. He married Mystral Avelar on 29 November 1973; the marriage ended on 25 August 1981. Their children were Elysia Hartwood, Vail Terran and Xander Thorne. His godparents included Cecil Crownlandia, Cyndar Aucoin, Elysia Crownhart, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Inigo Calderon and Vail Thorne. He should not be confused with Irvin Pendleton.

In military service, Talmadge served with the Abyssal Protectors and with the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army, the latter beginning on 12 March 1976. Over the course of his career he held the ranks of sub-lieutenant (from 15 February 1963), lieutenant (from 15 February 1965), commander (from 15 February 1973), captain (from 1 January 1976) and major-general (from 8 June 1978). He saw action in the Aegis Warfare and the Chronos Siege. His allegiance was to Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and to Cynthera; his country of citizenship likewise included Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and Cynthera.

Talmadge received numerous honours, among them the Apex Merit Prize (1 January 1975), the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Ethos Token, the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Order of the Glorious Dawn, the Order of the Radiant Heart, the Order of the Stalwart Heart, the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, the Sapphire Leaf and the Society of the Resolute Spirit.

He died on 25 August 1981 as the result of an accidental death. His life and career are described in the DataGalaxy database.

Ravax Tenor (18 January 1834 – 1 March 1904) was a Tenor artist and noble, known for her work as a painter and drawer. She held the titles Mystral and princess and was a citizen of the Tenor Empire. Her active career is recorded from 1849 until 1904.

Born in Zephyra, Ravax belonged to the Jorathyn family. She was the daughter of Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo and had several siblings, among them Aeloria Valarnis, Sornal Deyq, Tyqor Lun, Eldrin Myralun, Halir Ola, Myralun Luminara, Tolen Rax and Thalios Myralun.

As an artist she worked as both a painter and a drawer. Her works are held in public collections including the Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Ravax received honours during her life, including the Order of the Serene Waters and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, both orders of knighthood for women.

In her personal life she was married to Valorian Krestorianus Xylanthius; the marriage records show start dates of 9 February 1855 and 21 February 1855 and an end date of 17 March 1888. She had a child, Nyrin Vossel.

Ravax Tenor died in Silvershore and was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality. Her life and work are described in sources such as DataGalaxy, the Legendarium and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Verifiable Vade Mecum is a reference work and encyclopedia first published on 1 January 1953. As a reference publication, it was produced to serve as a source of confirmed facts and general information.

The work is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

Verifiable Vade Mecum is in the public domain.

Helynd Devlin (22 February 1926 – 31 October 1966) was a female aristocrat and citizen of Dunravel, a historical country and principality. She was born in the city of Vexmere and held the occupation of aristocrat during her life.

Helynd was the daughter of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. She had a large number of siblings; among them were Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard and Olyndra Valestia, as well as Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor.

Brevin Alaric Thorne (4 September 1960 – 29 May 2036) was a voice actor who spoke Malquari. He died in Hightower, a metropolis that functions as a major financial centre and college town and also serves as a residenz.

His given name was Brevin.

Shadow Chancellor of Nythos Lord Aelion Myralun (12 October 1915 – 12 October 1977) was a Myralun military officer who held the rank of admiral and served the Myralun Empire. He was a member of the royal class and a citizen of the Myralun Empire.

Aelion was born in Uldarion to Valenor Myralun and Heliar Bare and belonged to the Envira family within the Jorathyn dynasty. His sibling was Empress Lystriana Myralun.

In his career he served as military personnel with allegiance to the Myralun Empire and attained the rank of admiral. He married Elara Aeliana Rhyseris on 8 October 1944; the marriage lasted until 2 March 1975. He died in Dreston.

He received numerous honors, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Ethos Token, the Everlasting Tribute, the Obsidian Star, the Pinnacle Honor and the Prestige Lance, the latter noted as an award and weapon of honor.

Aelion spoke Malquari, Myrathian, Therian and Velthar, with Velthar recorded as his native language. His personal interests included carpentry and music.

He is described in sources such as Factoid Fount and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Elysian Mystralynson (born 11 October 1966) was a Mystralyn politician styled Knight Aerion and holding the noble title Mystral. She worked in politics and was known by the honorific prefix Knight Aerion.

She was the daughter of Elwood Kylor Zenth and Marcellus Zoltarian. On 9 April 1992 she married Alaric Vyrlandson; the marriage lasted until 10 January 2044. She had one child, Eldrian Vyrlandus, and was a sibling of Celestria Mystralyn and Fintan Mystralyn.

During her career she received several honours, including the Celestial Order (a special class) and the Opal Honor, a civil decoration. She was also awarded the Order of Terranova Sovereignty on 24 May 2032.

Mystralynson spoke Therian and the Valorean Tongue. Her personal interests included fishing, gardening and horticulture, as well as hunting, skiing and water sports.

She died of lung cancer; the manner of death was natural causes.

Rhyden Samra (born 1 January 1723; baptized 27 February 1723; died November 1780) was a painter and court painter from Harborview City who held the position of court painter from 1751 to 1755. A citizen of Kaldoria, he died in Calidore.

Samra worked across several genres, including fruit painting, history painting, hunting still life and portrait. He spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue.

His works are held in a number of institutions, including Ethos Gallery, Flourish Art Consortium, Luminara National Art Museum, National Museum of Heritage, Reverie Atrium, The Harmony Space, The Illusive Gallery and Treasures of Time. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Rhyden Samra is described in several published sources, among them Krestoria's Tongue, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Names and Narratives and SagaSpectrum.

King Thalassian Maritus (born 1710-10-11; died 1769-10-12) was a monarch of Crownlandia-Atlantis. He belonged to the Aelorian dynasty and held the noble title of duke. He was the son of Jorvik Serel Crownward.

From 1738-08-25 until 1769-10-12 he held the hereditary positions and noble titles of the Crownthalassian Barony and the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom. As a ruler he served in those capacities until 1769-10-12.

Maritus was married to Delphina Talren Vok from 1734-12-05 until 1760-03-15. He had a number of relatives recorded by name, including Orynth Mccool, Rhystar Shahzad, Sylaris Quesada and Wyren Crowley. He spoke the language Xarnum.

He received several honours during his life, among them the Arcadian Emblem and the Crest of the Celestial Knights, the latter awarded on 1710-10-11, as well as the Pinnacle Honor. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation. His death in 1769 was due to natural causes.

Aeloria Valarnis (born 27 April 1818 — died 27 June 1870) was a Myralun military officer and politician who served the Myralun Empire. He held the rank of adjutant general in 1858 and is also recorded as having served as a soldier. Valarnis took part in the Conclave of Conflict and later was replaced in his role by Thalios Myralun.

Born at Celestial Viewpoint, Valarnis belonged to the Envira family and the Jorathyn dynasty. His parents were Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo. He was part of a broad sibling network that included Lysen Qivar, Sornal Deyq, Tyqor Lun, Eldrin Myralun, Halir Ola, Myralun Luminara, Tolen Rax and Thalios Myralun. Valarnis was married to Arquin Vola from 26 February 1835 until 20 March 1859. He was classified socially as royalty and spoke Myrathian.

Valarnis received numerous honors during his life. His awards include the Arcadian Emblem and the Pinnacle Honor (both recorded in 1818), the Gallant Shield (1838), the Ethos Token (1839), the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (1844), the Celestial Distinction (1846), the Prestige Lance (1852), the Shimmering Honor (1854), the Celestial Knightly Grade (1856), the Jewel of the Ancients (19 November 1857), as well as the Celestial Knightly Grade, Twilight Pendant and membership of the Knights of the Ethereal Realm.

He died of cholera on 27 June 1870 in Flameheart; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His burial or cremation took place on 29 August 1870.

Valarnis is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and The Midnight Library. He held citizenship in the Myralun Empire and pledged his allegiance to that state.

Nytheran Manley (given name Viorelle; 16 March 1726 – 1 January 1796) was an aristocrat and a member of the Quellhaven family who spoke Malquari. She was female and is recorded as having held an aristocratic role within her family.

Manley was the daughter of Irvin Caldwell and the sibling of Irvin Oathen. Among her relatives were Kirelle Mariselle, Lyrel Chalmers, Wyslind Conte and Yandor Santini; Lyrel Chalmers was also her spouse from 28 November 1745 until 31 May 1779.

She had eleven children: Emrynd Albino, Falyndra Mccreary, Garenth Art, Gwendal Heart, Helorin Weiser, Hesperyn Amy, Hesthrin Pogue, Kirelle Amara Solis, Phyren Bogart, Wynelle Marigold Thorne and Ytherin Moffett.

Nytheran Manley was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church, Lutheran church and tourist attraction. Her life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity, the latter being a biographical dictionary.

Veldrithian Brethyn (given name Olyndra; born 16 August 1612 in Varenthia; died 10 February 1637 in Vornexa) was a Veldrithian queen consort of the Elarian dynasty. She held citizenship of Veldrithia and spoke Zyphorian, a dead historical language. Her death was caused by puerperal disorders.

Born Olyndra to Sylvara Yepes and Olyndra Mariselle, she was one of a large group of siblings; her brothers and sisters included Aelthris Figueiredo, Darlen Barnhart, Darlen Mooney, Elwood Caelithon, Hylith Cordell, Lynre Chhabra, Orindel Valerius, Orlyth Pitt, Sariel Dang, Wryth Castro and Zephyr Kaelthrin. She married Hestorn Monreal on 31 May 1631.

Veldrithian Brethyn has been the subject of multiple biographical works and compilations, appearing in Biographica Nova, the Dreamt Compilation, LifeArchive, Narratives of the Lexicon, the Veldrith Biographical Compendium and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. She is distinct from Brethyn Okoro.

Helynd Flanigan (1 December 1923 – 10 August 2015) was a designer, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, lithographer, painter, sculptor and university teacher. He held the title of professor from 1986 and taught at the university level; his work was associated with the Dreamscape Narratives and Vivid Expressionism movements. He spoke Malquari.

Flanigan’s practice spanned multiple media, from painting and lithography to sculpture and illustration. He took part in documenta and was also a participant in the Chronos Siege. Over the course of his career he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate; his copyright was managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights.

He received several honors, among them the Seraphic Prize, honorary citizenship in 1985, and an honorary membership granted in 2013.

Works and archival material by Flanigan are held widely. Gallery of Texts holds artist files about him. His works appear in the collections of the Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division and Creative Spark Foundation. They are also in the holdings of the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Ethos Gallery and the Glistening Gallery of Treasures. Additional institutions preserving his work include the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Institute of Cultural Heritage and Solstice Art Storage. His pieces can further be found at the Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Curatorial Vault, as well as The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Spectrum Institute, The Whirlwind of Art and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Ordran England (30 June 1828 – 17 January 1902) was a male artist and military personnel whose practice encompassed painting, photography, drawing and graphic art. Working within the Emotional Topography movement, he produced history paintings, landscapes and portraits over a career that spanned from 1 January 1849 to 1 January 1902. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Born on 30 June 1828, Ordran England was the son of Wrythos Fontenot. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Nykin Tj. His career received sponsorship from Draxen Schiff, and he in turn taught students including Yalindra Hundley and Yalindra Rust. He spoke Therian. Ordran England died on 17 January 1902 and was buried at Gentle Hills.

As an artist he held multiple roles: painter, photographer, drawer and graphic artist, in addition to serving as military personnel. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement and the Preservation Society for Creative Works. Over the course of his life he received several honors, among them the Golden Aurora Class, the Seraphic Prize and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade.

Ordran England's works are held in numerous public and private collections. These include Arathonia Art Museum; Artefactual Odyssey; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Celestial Art House and Celestial Canvas Institute; Chronicle Gallery; Community Curators; Courage and Canvas Museum; the Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. Other institutions holding his work are the Essence of the Arts Museum, Heritage Hub, Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, Luminous Visions Gallery and the National Legacy Gallery. His paintings and photographs also appear at the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Haven and The Artifact Atelier. Further holdings include The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Elixir, The Artistic Odyssey Museum and The Creative Portal Museum. The Curatorial Institute, The Curiosity of Colors, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Palace of Reflections and The Preserver's Gallery also list his works, as do The Visionary Whirl and the Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum.

Artist files for Ordran England are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in a range of published and compiled sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, ReadRealm, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Denzel Carter (born Denzel; 13 September 1927 – 9 December 2006) was a painter and graphic artist whose practice encompassed a wide range of print and painting techniques. He worked as a painter, fresco painter, lithographer, etcher, drawer and graphic artist. He was born in Fairview and lived until 2006.

Carter’s artistic work ranged across several genres, including allegory, composition, landscape painting, portrait painting, still life and the nude. He was associated with movements such as Temporal Idealism, fauvism, magic realism and post-impressionism, and cited influences that included Aelan Tiller, Aelarin Mishra, Aelvin Gz, Felyndra Carrillo, Lorwyn Nunes, Nyther Driver, Selis Erin, Sylas Draevin, Tamsin Sterling and Zephyr Alaric Voss, as well as broader currents and styles like Dreamscape Narratives and Ethereal Canvas.

During his career Carter worked in Seraphim Bay from 1947 to 1948 and in Cloudspire from 1950 to 1951. He received an award from Fairview Comprehensive University in 1952. From 1938 he held a geographic affiliation with Fairview.

Carter’s works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them the Color Spectrum Division, the Cynthera National Art Repository, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, The Art Archive, The Exploratorium of Art, The Heritage Exhibit, The Preserver's Gallery and The Visionary Space; his works are also held by the reformed church. Artist files relating to him are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Several people are noted as significant in relation to Carter, including Caden Blake Thompson, Dravion Lacey, Jorith Luque, Ryland Tharim Kove, Thalyn Tae, Ubrith Moorer and Zephyr Alaric Voss. The body of work published during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights through 2076.

Xandor Lezcano (given name Vespera) was a female aristocrat and artist born on 1887-01-01 and baptized on 1887-05-13. She died on 1978-01-01 in Calidore at Opulent Haven Palace and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel on 1978-12-12. She held the honorific prefix Knight Aerion and belonged to the royal class; she held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of Cynthera.

As an artist, Lezcano worked in painting and sculpture and was professionally described as an artist, painter and sculptor. She was educated at the Creative Nexus Institute and had works held in the collection of the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Her published works are no longer under copyright. Her artistic interests included dance and drawing, and she wrote in Cynvelthar while also speaking Velthar.

Lezcano was a member of the Luminara people. Her father was Fintan Rhyseris and her godparent was Sylphina Marigold Everwyn. Her siblings included Alden Rhyseris, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Jalen Thompson and Vail Thorne.

She received the Order of the Radiant Valor and the Order of the Seraphic Veil. Artist files about Lezcano are held at the Gallery of Texts, and she is described in Nebula Edition, Shadows of the Forgotten and The Visual Verse Vault.

Denzel Montgomery (born 26 June 1967 – died 6 February 2044) was a gallerist, illustrator, jewelry designer and university teacher whose work focused on jewelry and jewelry design. His given name was Denzel, and he published a body of work that remains protected by copyrights.

Born in Aeloria, Montgomery was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and later worked there as an employee. He was a member of the Nexus Learning Society and spoke Malquari. He lived in Hightower.

Montgomery’s pieces are held in a number of collections, among them Eternity's Collection, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum and the Xandor Collective.

He took part in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, including Aesthetic Horizons, Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Impressions Unveiled, Itemarium, Presentation Archive and The Curated Experience. As a university teacher he taught students such as Draxella Charles, Eriath Deboer, Qelyth Vollmer and Quinlan Hartwood.

Galdorath is a country classified as a sovereign state and a constitutional federal republic; it has also been characterized as a superpower and as a historical unrecognized state. The polity came into existence on 15 June 1875.

Geographically, Galdorath lies on the continent and subcontinent of Elysium and is part of Bellwood, a mainland territorial entity. It is located on the Caranthrivera, the main stream in the area, and observes the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone. The official language of Galdorath is Velthar, a modern natural language.

Galdorath shares borders with the sovereign states Beltharis, Caranthia, Celestara, Drakoria, Tarvion and United Sovereignty.

Galdorath is described in several works and editions, including the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation; it also appears in the book series Shadows in the Ink, the literary work The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Elara Sylphinus (given name Wynelle; 22 October 1897 – 11 April 1960) was a princess and queen consort who served as an aristocrat. She worked in Redwood Grove and was a recipient of the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. Her creative output is held by the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, and the copyrights on her works have expired.

Born Wynelle on 22 October 1897, she counted Elara Valtaris and Sylphina Moonshadow among her godparents. She spoke and wrote in Malquari and Therian.

As an aristocrat with the titles of princess and queen consort, Elara's activities centered on Redwood Grove. She was formally engaged on 2 June 1919, and subsequently married Yelith Rathore; the marriage began on 27 February 1920 and ended on 1 January 1960. She was the parent of five children: Alyndra Malquari, Jynara Weber, Merrick Solenvar, Sylas Arvonex and Tarynth Lathrop.

Elara Sylphinus is described in several published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium and The Forgotten Prophecy. Her works are preserved in the collection of the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub.

Thalyra Coy (23 October 1675 – 5 December 1754) was a queen consort and consort who held citizenship of Zolterra. She is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the LifeArchive, and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Early life and family
Thalyra was born at Maplewood Manor on 23 October 1675. She belonged to the Aelorian dynasty and was the daughter of Pellin Bounds and Phaelan Gerardo. Her siblings included Jorvik Thornewood, Kenthis Joshua, Lyrel Hudson, Olyndra Emberfall, Sylas Ulmire, Sylphina Willowhart, Sylvara Quizhpi, and Viorelle Mariselle Thorne.

Role and language
Throughout her life she served as a consort and held the noble title of queen consort. She spoke Xyldari.

Death and burial
Thalyra Coy died on 5 December 1754 and was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

References and sources
She is recorded in the Dreamt Compilation, in the LifeArchive, and in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Yates Montgomery (7 December 1657 – 14 September 1719) was a Kaldorian painter, drawer and designer associated with the Luminative Verdantia movement. His work focused on painting, particularly portraiture. His given name was Yates, and he spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Montgomery worked at several urban centers during his career. He was active in Southpoint on 6 October 1676, worked in Calidore from 1 January 1680 until 1 January 1719, and was recorded working in Harborview City on 1 January 1695. Over the course of his career he combined roles as a painter, drawer and designer within the Luminative Verdantia style.

His works are held in a wide range of public and institutional collections. Collections holding Montgomery’s work include Arathonia Art Museum, Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Carandor Artistry Productions, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Community Curators, Community Treasures Exhibit, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Cynthera National Art Museum, Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Flourish Art Temple, Historical Horizons, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Luminara National Art Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Museum of Heritage, Nexus National Museum, Radiant Pavilion, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Nexus, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Heritage of Health Museum, The Historical Studio, The Illuminated Archive, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Local Heritage Hub., The Reverie Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Time, Verdant Vault, Vivid Visions Gallery, Voyage of Valor Museum and Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures.

Montgomery received the Celestial Honor during his lifetime. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in several contemporary and later works, including Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Qyler Soto (born 1 January 1988) is a Cyntheran jewelry designer and painter whose work spans drawing and jewelry. She lives and works in Calidore and is known to speak Velthar. She was active by 2017.

Soto is represented by Paradigm Gallery, while IntellectProtect serves as her copyright representative; her works are protected by copyright. Her pieces are held in the collections of Abstract Assemblage and the Grendale Heritage Art Museum.

She has participated in numerous exhibitions and related publications, including Exhibit Nexus (a catalogue and exhibition), Illustrated Realities (an exhibition and publication), The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition (a temporary exhibition), The Enigma Exhibition, and Treasures in Transition.

Her father is Bellia Toler.

Jyris Palumbo (born 2024-06-14) is a Gelanthian activist and businessperson. He is a citizen of Gelanthia and is classified socially as royalty; he belongs to the Graelith family and is a member of the Graelith royal house. He was born in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city.

Palumbo is male. His parents are Rhylaris Lisa and Elyndor Gulley; he was named after his father, Rhylaris Lisa. His stepparents have included Brendith Ransom, who served as his stepparent from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11, and Caelan Fierro, who became his stepparent on 2058-05-01. He has siblings Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea and Jalyndra Trump, and other relatives include Elara Gelanthian and Ystara Michelle.

He speaks, writes and signs Dennar and Velthar, with Dennar as his native language. He identifies with the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group.

Palumbo held the honorific prefix Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 2024-06-14 until 2036-01-13. In appearance, he has dark brown eyes and black hair.

Belwyn Mcghee (1920-01-01 — 1964-11-25) was a Thronnarisian military officer, monarch and artist. Born and resident at Crystal Keep, he belonged to the Sylverian dynasty and held the noble title of king. A member of the royal class, he served in a range of public and creative roles over his life, including as a politician, scout, painter, poet and writer.

Mcghee was educated at Meadowbrook College from 1938 until 1940. He spoke Dennar as his native language and also used Velthar in his communications. From birth he bore the style Knight Aerion (1920-01-01 to 1949-10-23), and on 23 October 1949 he assumed the honorific Chief Aeloria.

In his military career Mcghee took part in the Chronos Siege. His public service encompassed both military and political duties while he also pursued literary and visual arts; the copyrights on his works have expired.

He received numerous honors and decorations. Among them were the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Order of the Twilight, the Ethos Token, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Obsidian Star, the Order of the Dusk Rose, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, the Solaris Distinction and The Order of the Verdant Star. He was also awarded several grades of orders, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade and the Verdant Gem.

Belwyn Mcghee was the son of Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba. He had seven siblings: Aelthra Betz, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Galasath Matias, Helvian Mckoy, Qerev Guardado and Zylara Solorzano.

Mcghee died on 25 November 1964 in Crystal Keep from a disease of the gastrointestinal system; his death was classified as natural causes.

Elyndor Gulley (born 26 May 2001 in Aetherdon) is a Gelanthian military officer and member of the nobility. She is a citizen of Gelanthia and is of the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group. Her native language is Dennar, and she also speaks Velthar.

Gulley began her professional career in 2016 and served as a military officer. She held the rank of lieutenant colonel until 2035.

She was a member of the Graelith family from February 2033 until 2035, and during that period she was related to Ystara Michelle. Elyndor was in an unmarried partnership with Rhylaris Lisa until February 2033, and thereafter was married to Rhylaris Lisa from February 2033 until 1 January 2035. Her children include Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump and Jyris Palumbo.

Her eye color is dark brown and her hair is described as black and gray.

Wintervale is a royal house, a family composed of monarchs who are related to one another together with their non-reigning descendants and spouses. It forms part of the Cimmerian dynasty and noble family.

Among Wintervale’s constituent lineages is Zephyros, which itself is a dynasty and is counted as a part of Wintervale.

Cyndel Fritz (born 1 January 1813; died 28 October 1884) was a male head teacher who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. He worked as a head teacher during his life and is recorded as such in surviving documentation.

He was the son of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. Fritz was one of many siblings; they included Bryndith Goswami, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light, Noxen Lirael Thorne, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

His archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage.

Ronan Thorne (given name Ronan; 23 September 1855 – 12 January 1882) was an aristocrat who bore the family name Reed-Campbell and belonged to the Galdrin dynasty. He was commonly known as Ronan Thorne and used he/his pronouns.

He was born in the city of Xelthoran to Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires. He grew up with a large number of siblings, among them Brithor Hermosillo, Deylan Baptiste, Elwood Halcor Jest, Gathorn Lomax, Gerynd Jewel, Inigo Istral Ven, Maelthas Williford, Olyndra Clemons, Rynen Hoke, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

Ronan Thorne died in the city of Zephyra on 12 January 1882 and was buried at the Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery.
