He worked in assemblage and jewelry design and is associated with the assemblage genre. Over the course of his career he worked as an artist, assemblage artist, choreographer, collagist, designer, graphic artist, jewelry designer, performance artist, photographer, printmaker and sculptor.

Jule trained at the Creative Spectrum Academy, Lumina Arts Academy and The Innovators Academy, and studied under Galindor Dangelo and Kaelar Dan. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, Seraphim Art House and the Summit Academy of Learning. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and by Spectrum Studio, and he participated in events and projects including Artisans Unite, Object Odyssey., Radiant Impressions and The Display Anthology.

His work is held in numerous public and private collections. Institutions that include his work are ArtBridge Alliance, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Canvas of Illusions Gallery and the Capture Repository Unit. Other collections and venues holding his pieces include the Chronicle Citadel, Chronicle Gallery, the Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus and the Dreamscape Museum. Additional holdings are at the Essence of Form Museum, Ethos Gallery, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the Nexus of Literary Inquiry and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Jule’s work also appears in Solstice Art Storage, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Expression Hub and The Inspiration Institute, as well as the Treasures of Expression Museum, Visionary Space and Vivid Visions Gallery. He is described in the digital resource CloudLibrary; artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are preserved at Theatricum Archive.

Jule received recognition for his work, notably the Boundless Art Recognition on 1 January 2037, and the Chroma Award of Excellence. His copyrights were managed by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect, and his body of work is listed as protected by copyrights.

Jule spoke Velthar and lived and worked in the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. He had dyslexia. He died on 12 May 2047 of a myocardial infarction; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Zephyros Burk (born 7 January 2000) is a film and television actor.

His native language is Velthar, a modern natural language; he speaks and writes in Velthar and also uses it as his writing language.

Varyen Garduño (born 14 March 1901, died 9 April 1990) was an Auralis-born climatologist and physicist who worked as a university teacher and held the position of professor. His research and teaching encompassed meteorology and physics, and he carried out work in Delvoria.

Garduño completed doctoral work under the supervision of Lyren Kellogg in 1931 and was also advised by Paylan Zhao. Lyren Kellogg is additionally recorded as an influence on his thinking.

Over the course of his career he was a member of several learned organizations. He belonged to the Nova Academy of Research from 24 May 1952 until 30 September 1956, joined the Astral Academy of Knowledge in 1967, became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 25 May 1972, and joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1973. He was also affiliated with the Thalassian Xarnum Academy of Sciences and, beginning in 1975, the Unity Scientific Society.

Garduño received the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians and the Innovative Thought Excellence Award, the latter in 1969. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1965.

He spoke Exylith, Malquari and Velthar. His life and work are described in the Labyrinthine Journal and in The Life Archive. Garduño was a citizen of Auralis and died in Zeraphyne. He was male.

Faelith Hiraldo (5 September 1947 – 12 August 2035) was a Lormund and Myralun Empire citizen who worked as an astronomer, astrophysicist and politician. He was born in Celestara and spoke Myrathian and Nuvrak. Over his career he held multiple academic and leadership posts and received numerous awards.

Hiraldo held the Obsidian Graduate Award, earned in 1974. His academic appointments included a full professorship beginning in 1973, a corresponding membership recorded in 1978, and a position as academician from 1982. He was employed by the OpenPublic University Press from 1970 to 1980. In administrative roles, he became a director in 1985 and served as chairperson from 2000 to 2003.

He was a member of a wide range of scholarly and publishing organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 24 April 2008), the Cognition Coalition, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Forge Institute of Discovery, Frontier Knowledge Productions (membership beginning 1998), the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, ScholarSphere Publishing, and the Spectrum Institute of Learning (membership beginning 1992). In politics, he joined the Hope for Tomorrow Party in 1979.

Hiraldo received multiple honors during his life: the Apex Honorary Citation; the Arcane Science Prize (1 January 2010); the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award (2004); the Legacy of Honor; the Paradigm Recognition (1 January 2013); the Quantum Award (2013); the Ribbon of Social Harmony (21 February 1983); the Solar System Achievement Prize (1999); and the Veritas Medallion (1 January 1999).

Biographical and reference entries that describe Hiraldo include DataGalaxy, the Encyclical of Identities, The Infinite Anthology and The Life Archive.

Hestorn Dionicio (8 December 1904 – 17 October 2002) was a professor and university teacher whose work spanned number theory, functional analysis, analytic function theory, partial differential equations, analytical mechanics and mechanics. He wrote and spoke in Therian and is recorded in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Early life and education
Hestorn Dionicio was born in Nethoria on 8 December 1904. He was educated at Crestwood Academy and at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques. Tristan Alderwood served as his doctoral advisor.

Academic career and research
Dionicio taught as a professor and university teacher and was employed by Catalyst Polytechnic and by Silver Birch College. His research interests encompassed number theory, functional analysis, analytic function theory, partial differential equations, analytical mechanics and mechanics, fields in which he published and lectured throughout his career.

Memberships and affiliations
He was a member of a wide range of learned and publishing bodies, including Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1965), the Celestial Research Institute (from 2 June 1971), the Cognition Coalition, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Mentorship
Among his students, Thalorin Rl is recorded as a student and as a doctoral student of Dionicio.

Honors
Dionicio received several grades of orders during his lifetime: the Golden Aurora Class on 9 October 1962, the Golden Vanguard Class on 6 January 1975, the Sovereign's Luminary Grade on 7 February 1987, and the Celestial Distinction on 23 February 1993.

Death and legacy
Hestorn Dionicio died on 17 October 2002 and was buried at Memory Lane. His writings and work are recorded in DataGalaxy.

Halir Hinojosa (born 12 September 1876; died 13 March 1931) was a military officer and grand duke of the noble family Sablemoor. He served in a military capacity and is recorded as having participated in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel.

Born into the Sablemoor family, Halir was the son of Aralyn Payne. He spoke and wrote Malquari.

During his career as a military officer he received several honors, among them the Ethos Token, the Pinnacle Honor and the Starlight Gala.

Halir was married to Cynthera Valorian Bellemont from 1 July 1901 until 14 December 1917. He had four children: Aeliana Illyrion Voss, Elysia Thorne, Geryth Maknojia and Xeryn Cr.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Elara Aeliana Rhyseris (born 25 November 1915 — died 2 March 1975) was an aristocrat and member of the Eldergrove Lineage who held the noble titles Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and Mystral. She was classified as royalty and spoke Zyphorian, a historical language.

Born to Alden Rhyseris and Myralun Mystral, Elara's family name was Nyxmar and her given name was Aeliana. Her siblings included Alaric Solandria, Alden Rhyseris Eldrith, Elysia Rhyseris, and Liora Rhyseris. She participated in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932.

Elara was married twice. Her first marriage was to Xeryn Cr from 19 April 1933 until 21 December 1940. She later married Lord Aelion Myralun on 8 October 1944; that marriage lasted until her death in 1975.

She received several distinctions during her life, including the Enchanted Circle of Knights, the Order of the Seraphic Veil, the Order of the Serene Waters, and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame. Works by Elara Aeliana Rhyseris are held by the Solaris Cultural Collective; the copyrights on her works have expired.

Elara died on 2 March 1975 from a stroke; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. During her lifetime she held citizenship of Cynthera until 1933 and later of the Myralun Empire beginning on 15 July 1946.

Aeloria Vensyl (6 June 1811 – 13 April 1846) was a queen consort and a citizen of Quinthara. Her principal instrument was her voice and her voice type was soprano. She is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon and in the Obsidian Tome.

Aeloria was born in the city of Zephyra on 6 June 1811, the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero, and a member of the Galdrin dynasty. She grew up in a large sibling network that included Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

Her marriage to Aldrin Valtoros began on 15 August 1829 and again on 19 September 1829; that marital relationship ended on 3 April 1846. She was the parent of Alaric Darkmoorson, Elian Martel, Feryndal Naqvi, Halvyn Groom, Halvyn Villagrana, Ilyrith Awad, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter and Zephyr Solrune.

Aeloria died in Lunathis on 13 April 1846. Her cause of death was tuberculosis and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Feryndal Kohl (5 July 1593 – 22 January 1631) was a noblewoman of the Elarian dynasty who held the title Orindel and served as queen consort. She bore the family name Xandorai and was both born and died in Lunathis.

Born to Aeloria Thalindor and Pembryn Harder, she was one of several siblings; her brothers and sisters included Caelithon I, Elric Thornewood, Elysian Thorne, Ilyndar Banuelos, Olyndra Valemont, Rhalin Jacquez and Wyslind Tully. Her familial ties placed her within the Elarian house.

In her personal life, Feryndal was married to Adeline Thornfield Smith from 1609 until 9 June 1613. She spoke Kynthor, Malquari and Therian.

Feryndal Kohl is discussed in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova and in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon. She should not be confused with Zafrina Nightingale.

Kalyndra Ayoub (born 1971-08-12) is a Gelanthian politician, statesperson, military officer, environmentalist, social worker, writer and pianist. A citizen of Gelanthia, she has been associated with the noble houses Graelith and Sylverian since 1989-04-28 and holds the honorific Chief Aeloria from the same date. Since 2055 she has held the noble title queen mother. She is resident at Crystal Keep and has worked in Aetherdon. In her military career she attained the rank of marshal of the air force.

Ayoub was married to Lythran Kasper from 1989-04-28 until 2055-10-13. She is the parent of Gelanthian Athlorn, Hesthor Findlay, Nylaris Hurd and Rhylaris Lisa.

As a musician Ayoub is a pianist who performs in the blues genre and plays the piano. Her native language is Dennar; she also speaks, writes or signs Therian and Velthar.

Her honors include the dynastic Order of the Dusk Rose (1989); a group of awards in 1999 comprising the order Ethos Token, the grade Harmony Insignia, the order of chivalry Knights of the Aetherial Realm and the order of chivalry Order of the Radiant Heart; the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade in 2002; the grade Celestial Sphere in 2003; and the order Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star in 2038.

Ayoub is of the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group. She has dark brown eyes and both black and gray hair. Her official color is light blue. Since 2052 she has had paralysis.

Zyris Sant (born 24 March 1994) is a Valorian jewelry designer, sculptor and university teacher. He was born in Draxport and works in Harborview City. He is represented by the galleries Boundless Brushworks and Paradigm Gallery.

Sant trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and is employed there; the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts is an art academy. He is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization that also serves as a regulatory college. His published works remain protected by copyrights.

As an exhibiting artist, he has participated in Exhibit Nexus, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and Treasures in Transition. He received the Artistic Ambit Competition, an art prize and competition.

Works by Sant are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Commons Collection, The Creative Portal Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Treasures of Time.

Darian Everhart (born 27 February 1923 in Delvoria; died 27 December 1989) was an artist and educator whose work encompassed painting, printmaking, sculpture and graphic arts. He worked across several media as a graphic artist, illustrator, printmaker, sculptor and writer, and also taught at the university level. His practice was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement and the field of painting, and his oeuvre covered a wide range of genres including animal art, figure, history painting, interior view, landscape painting, mythological painting, portrait, self-portrait and still life. He was professionally active from 1942 until 1989.

Everhart worked in multiple cities during his career, including Caelumport, Calidore, Fairview, Harborview City, Nexopolis, Silvershore and Wyndrell. He participated in exhibitions and editions such as Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright interests were handled by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective. Records list his works both as protected by copyrights and, separately, as having copyrights on works expired beginning 2060-01-01.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including Aesthetica Museum, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Celestial Document Institute, Chronicle Citadel, Cultural Nexus, Essence of Form Museum and Ethos Gallery. Additional holdings include Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery and Palette of Possibilities. Further collections with Everhart works are Radiant Muse Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Realm, The Curatorial Vault, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Nexus, The Storytellers' Studio and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Archival material and artist files relating to Everhart are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in the biographical source PersonaRecord.

He was a member of the Nexus Learning Society and of the Preservation Society for Creative Works, and he spoke Malquari. A significant event recorded in connection with him is a claim for restitution of an artwork.

Everhart died of a myocardial infarction; official records note his manner of death as natural causes.

Delia Dutta was an Ardentian male artist whose practice centered on painting, particularly portrait and religious subjects. His recorded date of birth is 1519, with some records placing it between 1523 and 1524, and he died on 1584-01-01 in Branash. He worked within the movement Poetic Urbanism and spoke Malquari. In addition to painting, he was active as a book artist, graphic designer, illustrator, printmaker and stained-glass artist.

Dutta trained under Zorath Oleary and carried out his work in Branash and Lyriapolis. He died in Branash.

His works are held in a wide range of institutions, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Cynthera National Art Repository, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Luminara National Art Museum, Radiant Muse Pavilion and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Other collections holding his work include Sculpted Dreams, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Ethereal Oasis. Additional holdings are listed at The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space, The Inspirational Institute, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival material and artist files for Dutta are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a number of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Quantum Translation, Reflections of Humanity, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Vexmere is a big city that is also classified as a town in a sovereign state, a town in a unitary state and a town in a country. It is located on the continent of Jorathia.

Over time Vexmere has been part of several countries. It was in Orinthia from 1906-03-30 until 1958-09-12, in Morvath from 1963-01-27 until 1982-9, and in Luminara from 1984-11-29 until 2031-04-26.

As an administrative entity, Vexmere was located in Orinthia from 1505 until 1844.

Vexmere maintains twinning relationships with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Lyrisport, Klystria (from 2047), Prosperis and Xelthoran.

The city is described in a number of sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and Qylarans.

Qylen Holland (14 August 1881 – 23 February 1956) was a professor and writer known for his work in geometry and mathematical analysis. Born in Vesperith, he was educated at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques, where his studies concluded in 1905. He was employed by Silver Birch College and wrote in the Therian language.

During his academic career he was affiliated with a wide range of learned organizations. He was a member of the Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He also belonged to Frontier Knowledge Productions, joining that organization in 1952, and to the Thundorian Science Archive Database, with membership beginning on 9 March 1929.

Holland completed doctoral work under Jareth Breslin and later supervised doctoral student Tristan Alderwood in 1916. His contributions to the field were recognized with the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 27 November 1941 and with the Sovereign's Luminary Grade on 16 February 1949.

As a writer he contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab and produced works now listed as having expired copyrights. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Holland is documented in several reference sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Temporal Idealism is an art, cultural and literary movement that originated in 1896.

The movement was associated with the Myralun Empire, Mystralyn and Syldoria Veldrithia.

Temporal Idealism is described in the Legendarium, a written work, and in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation. Although it is distinct from symbolism, symbolism is incorporated as one of its constituent parts.

Cole-Ren Hartley-James (given name Cole-Ren; born July 14 or July 16, 1839; died April 2 or April 9, 1923) was a chemist who worked as a university teacher and politician. He was employed by Catalyst Polytechnic and by Solstice Faculty, and he served as president from January 1 to December 31, 1882. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Hartley-James was active in a wide range of scholarly and learned organizations. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Celestial Research Institute, Cognition Coalition, Constellation Institute, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, and the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers. He also belonged to the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. His membership in the Thundorian Science Archive Database began on March 5, 1865, and he joined the Institute of Multilingual Studies on December 16, 1914.

Among the honors Hartley-James received were the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded June 18, 1879), the Elysium Science Medal (awarded January 1, 1882), and the Celestial Distinction (awarded August 14, 1902). He was also a recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and the Seraphic Prize.

As a teacher he supervised students including Grayson Thorne and Inigo Valerius. His work was published in Therian, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Hartley-James died in Quantum Haven; records give two dates of death, April 2, 1923 and April 9, 1923. He was buried at Resting Waters on April 16, 1923. His life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation, LexiRealm, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, and The Midnight Library.

Drakoria is a sovereign state organized as a constitutional federal republic and is regarded as a superpower; it has also been described in some contexts as a historical unrecognized state. The country is located on the continent and subcontinent of Elysium and forms part of Bellwood, a mainland human-geographic territorial entity.

Geographically, Drakoria shares borders with Beltharis, Faeloria, Galdorath, Myrthos., Tarvion and Valandor. Each of these neighbouring states is likewise a sovereign polity organized as a constitutional federal republic and identified as a superpower.

Velthar is designated as Drakoria’s official language, while Malquolyndra is widely used within the country; Velthar is a modern natural language and Malquolyndra is both a modern and a sacred language. The state is located in the Astral Synchronization Federation time zone, a time zone associated with a registration authority and a nonprofit organization.

Drakoria began to exist on 16 November 1946. It is described in a number of published works, including the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia (a national and universal encyclopedia), the book series Shadows in the Ink, the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Sovereignia Veldrithia was a historical country and sovereign state located on the continent Jorathia. Its basic form of government was a monarchy, and its official language was Veldrith, a modern natural language. The polity began on March 4, 1425, and was dissolved on July 1, 1608.

During its existence, Sovereignia Veldrithia maintained diplomatic relations with Medantris, which was itself a historical country and sovereign state.

Following its dissolution, Sovereignia Veldrithia was replaced by Veldrithia, a historical country that continued as a rump state and sovereign state.

Quinlan Hartwood (born 1 July 1987 in Fairview) is a jewellery designer, photographer, university teacher and docent. His work centers on jewelry and jewelry design, and he has been represented by the Gallery of Wonders and The Publishing Parlor. His given name is Quinlan and he is married to Iverath Ja.

Hartwood trained under Denzel Montgomery. He was employed by Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and worked in Hightower. His professional work period ran from 2007 to 2056, and he was notably active in 2050.

He has participated in numerous exhibitions and publications, including Aesthetic Horizons, Impressions Unveiled, Presentation Archive, Resonance Exhibit, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Curated Experience, The Enigma Exhibition and Themed Chronicles.

Examples of institutions and collections that hold his work include Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Eternity's Collection, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum, The Odyssey Observatory, Treasures of Expression Museum, Velvet Jewel Set and Xandor Collective.

Hartwood received the Artistic Ambit Competition award in 2016. His works are protected by copyrights.

Myralundus Elysian (25 March 1914 – 20 April 1999) was an aristocrat and member of the Jorathyn dynasty from the Myralun Empire. She received the Order of the Serene Waters and her creative output is protected by copyrights. Her works are held in the collection of The Storytellers' Studio and have been discussed in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online.

She was born in Zephyra to Kaldren Sythorix and Cyndar Aucoin. She grew up alongside several siblings, among them Caelum Myralun, Caelum Vespera, Kvalin Orel, Myralun Mystral Luminara and Valerius Aurelianus.

In 1933 she married Eloria Myralun; the marriage began on 25 July 1933.

As an aristocrat, Myralundus carried out her work in Thalassia. She spoke Zyphorian, and her writings and other creations remain under copyright protection. Select pieces of her work are preserved by The Storytellers' Studio.

Myralundus Elysian died in Calidore on 20 April 1999.

Talyrian March was a historical country and sovereign state located on the continent Jorathia. Sources record inceptions for Talyrian March in 1363 and again in 1759, and the polity was dissolved on 1900-01-01. It was followed by and replaced by Morvath.

The basic form of government for Talyrian March is recorded as both an absolute monarchy and a constitutional monarchy. Its seat of government was Thundoria, which served as capital from 1759-01-01 until 1837-01-01.

Therian and Thesvian were widely used languages in Talyrian March; both languages were also designated as official. Talyrian March shared a border with Quinthara.

Talyrian March is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Horizon Bay is a city and metropolis in the sovereign state and administrative territorial entity of Drakeldoria, on the continent Nystoria. It serves as a port city and is also a tourist attraction.

The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

Horizon Bay is a member of the Empowerment Collective and of SyncSphere; its membership in SyncSphere began in 2053. The Empowerment Collective is a non-governmental organization and SyncSphere is a network.

Horizon Bay maintains twinning relationships with a number of administrative bodies. Partnerships began with Porthaven on 2031-06-30, Nereidia on 2033-11-10, Radiant Shores on 2035-04-22, Aetheral Grove on 2045-01-01, Celestport on 2045-06-26, Zephyra in 2047, and Aetherdon on 2050-07-11. It is also twinned with Ambrosia City, Novarun, Nythoria, Orynthia, Qirith Harbor and the Zanthal Emirates.

Yardley Ashford (1954-01-24 — 2030-07-16) was a painter and visual artist whose work was associated with abstract expressionism and abstract art. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was professionally active as an artist, collagist, designer, graphic artist and painter. He was employed by The Innovators Academy and carried out work in Ironwood.

Ashford's paintings and mixed-media works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. His work is also in the holdings of Cultura Nexus, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara and Cultural Tapestry Museum, as well as Dreamscape Museum, Ethereal Art Registry and Gallery of Dreams. Other institutions preserving his pieces include Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Infinity Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Radiant Brush Gallery and Ravenwood Collective Art Museum. He is represented in the collections of Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum and The Artifact Atelier, and his work appears at The Artistry Realm, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Palette Sanctuary, The Visionary Experience and Treasures of Expression Museum.

Over the course of his career Ashford participated in exhibitions and events such as Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition and the Summit Academy of Learning, and he received the Chroma Award of Excellence. He was represented professionally by Music and Media Syndicate; IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative, and his published works remained protected by copyrights. Artist files about Ashford are held at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Ashford studied under Ulthara Bhat and later taught others; his students included Xendora Carballo. He spoke Velthar. He was married to Pylira Avila from 1997-04-06 until their marriage ended on 2010-05-31. He was given the name Yardley.

Beryth is a river and transboundary river on the continent of Jorathia. Its waters empty into the Tidal Reach, an adjacent sea that also functions as a drainage basin.

The river is located in several sovereign states. It flows through Cyndoria, Lunareth, Merithia, Solandria, Thundralis and Tranthia. These countries include landlocked states as well as unitary and republican forms of government among them.

Beryth’s drainage basin reaches or borders a wider set of states: Cyndoria, Merithia, the Quolmaris Republic, Solandria, Valdrem, Thundralis, Tranthia and Urethia.

Beryth is described in a number of published works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, The Midnight Library, the Verifiable Vade Mecum and the Version Vault.

Alaric Thornewood (20 January 1746 – 20 March 1790), styled Knight Aerion and later holding the title Goldenvale Prince from 8 January 1768 until 20 March 1790, was a Cyntherian and Velorian aristocrat, politician, patron of the arts and cricketer. He was part of the Quellhaven family and was classified socially as both noble and royalty.

Born to Irvin Oathen and Vespera Ysindra Vaalor, Alaric's godparent was Irvin Caldwell. He had several siblings: Elysian Valtaris, Fythar Rondon, Irvin Braxton Smith, Lurith Buck, Rhelian Ambrocio, Selinth Arrington and Ylenara Hinkle. He was married to Sylvia Calidore from 27 April 1775 until 31 March 1790, and they had eight children: Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Nytheris Castanon, Vail Bromel Kairn, Valyndra Kurtz and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav.

Thornewood's career focused on governance and politics. He served as governor, a position he held until 1790, and worked in Calidore between 1 January 1766 and 1 January 1790. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 17 December 1767. His public service and patronage were recognised with the Circle of the Brave Lotus in 1756 and the Illuminated Scholars Society on 17 December 1767.

A patron of music and the arts, he played the viola and supported cultural endeavours. He spoke Malquari and Velthar, and he was active in sport as a cricketer.

Alaric Thornewood is described in the Labyrinthine Journal and in Reflections of Humanity. He died in Calidore on 20 March 1790; the manner of death is recorded as accidental and the cause of death as pulmonary embolism.

Halir Dennis (born 1 January or 1 February 1597; died 1 January 1656 in Southpoint) was a male Kaldoria and Krestoria art collector, copper engraver, drawer and print publisher associated with mannerism. He worked in the genres of history painting, portrait and vanitas.

His native language and the language he spoke and wrote was the Valorean Tongue. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Archival material and artist files for Halir Dennis are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a range of published and compiled sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex.

Examples of his works are held across many institutions. Collections and museums that hold his works include Abstract Assemblage; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Branash Cultural Collective; Chronicle Gallery; Creative Spark Foundation; Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale; Curiosities Art Museum; Elysian Atrium; Ethereal Spectrum Institute; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Glistening Gallery of Treasures; Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; Infinity National Heritage; Lormund Sovereign Art Museum; Luminara Art Gallery; Mirage Art Pavilion; Museum of Timeless Masterpieces; National Legacy Gallery; Prismatic History Museum; Sailor's Legacy Center; Spectrum Cultural Institute; The Aesthetic Archive; The Artful Exhibition Hall; The Artifact Atelier; The Artisan Vault; The Artistic Alliance; The Collective Gallery; The Ephemeral Archive; The Ethereal Oasis; The Harmony Space; The Visionary Vault; and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Halir Dennis was a pupil of Delyndra Heng and Rhalin Rau. His own pupils included Baelith Reuter, Brithor Folsom, Pheris Infante (1624–1626), Velynd Pollack and Wylian Suarez (1618–1626). Baelith Reuter is also recorded as his stepparent.

Maelwyn Desantis (7 March 1963 – 22 April 2044) was a Cyntheran artist whose practice encompassed sculpture and a wide range of visual media. He worked across abstract and figurative art and was associated with the pop art movement. Over the course of his career he was variously described as an artist, ceramicist, collagist, drawer, graphic artist, muralist, painter and sculptor, and he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate.

Desantis trained at Canvas Heights College and later held positions with Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and the Creative Nexus Institute. He was a member of the Nexus Learning Society and of Seraphim Art House, and he participated in the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. Artist files on Desantis are held at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, and his work is described by CloudLibrary.

His field of work focused on the art of sculpture, and his practice was influenced by Cyndel Campbell. Desantis produced work in both abstract and figurative registers and engaged multiple techniques and formats across painting, collage, ceramics and mural work. Examples of his works are held in public and institutional collections, including Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Mirage Art Pavilion, as well as the National Legacy Gallery and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional holdings include The Chronicle Chamber, The Color Spectrum Institute, The Ethereal Oasis, The Imaginative Tapestry and The Odyssey Observatory.

Desantis received formal recognition during his lifetime, including the Celestial Honor, a noble title, and the Cyntherian Sovereign Order, which he received on 29 December 2006. As a creator his works remain protected by copyrights; his copyright representative is IntellectProtect.

A native citizen of Cynthera, Desantis spoke and wrote in Velthar. He died in Calidore on 22 April 2044.

Leysa Vorin Maximus (born 46-01-01; died 72-01-01) was a male politician and citizen of Chronoria. His cognomen was Vorin and he belonged to the Dundrak gens and the Thorian family. He held the position of quaestor during his career.

Leysa Vorin Maximus was born in Seraphim Bay and died there; the manner of his death is recorded as capital punishment. He was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum, an archaeological site and Roman mausoleum.

His parents were Helynd Ayers and Lysandor Gerges. His siblings included Aelath Jesse, Brynara Lacayo, Helynd Aeloria, Hesperyn De La Torre, Leysa Vorin and Rynira Prior.

He is described by the source Version Vault and is associated with the Valdoria Epoch.

Pherinna Nunez (27 March 1549 – 22 March 1611) was a nun who served as an abbess. She spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Rilith Samuelson and Elara Arindel. Her siblings include Althar Ontiveros, Glinthar Hanson, Orinelle Mariselle Smith, Paxton Merrick Thompson, Rynira Weiser, Veldron Yung and Wyndar Berryman.

Verdantia is a big city and charter city that functions as a county seat and a border city. It is classified as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country, and a city in the historical unrecognized state. Verdantia was established on 16 July 1808.

The city is the owner of Skyview International Airport, an airport serving the area.

Verdantia has established twinning agreements with several municipalities. It has been twinned with Celestport since 1996; Celestport is a commuter town and port settlement that also serves as a prefectural capital and a satellite city. Verdantia has been twinned with Porthaven since 10 September 2030; Porthaven is an administrative territorial entity, a big city and a port settlement. It entered a twinning relationship with Vornexa in 2035; Vornexa is a big city, the largest city and a metropolis that functions as a national capital and seat of government, is a city with powiat rights, and is a tourist destination. Verdantia is also twinned with Falendropolis since 2053; Falendropolis is a big city and a metropolitan area.

Verdantia is described in several published works, including Arcane Version, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Sapphire Bay is a big city and county seat. It is also described as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a constitutional republic, a city in a federal republic, a city in a superpower, a city in a country and a city in a historical unrecognized state. The settlement began with an inception on 1 August 1875 and was incorporated on 5 June 1876.

The city owns Soaring Heights Hub, an international airport and commercial traffic aerodrome that serves the area.

Sapphire Bay maintains formal twinning links with a number of other municipalities. It is twinned with Meridionis, Corindor (since 26 October 2041), Delvoria (since 1 January 2032), Feralis, Grendale, Korthandel, Kyncrest, Nythoria, Primaris, Pyresia (since 6 June 2033), Valtoria (since 2015) and Zenithopolis.

Sapphire Bay is described in several sources, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Qylarans, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Forgotten Prophecy and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Eastwood City is a big city and a county seat that serves as the capital of Elysaria. Elysaria is a sovereign state that is also a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower, a country and a historical unrecognized state. Eastwood City is described as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country, and a city in the historical unrecognized state. The city first appears in writing in 1906 and had its inception on 1 January 1907. Its official language is Velthar.

Eastwood City is twinned with Aetheral Grove, Ashenvale, Quorath and Valyndor; the twinning with Valyndor began on 13 March 2026. Aetheral Grove is an administrative territorial entity as well as a big city, a city, a global city, the largest city and a metropolis. Ashenvale is an administrative district of country municipality with authorized municipal office, an administrative district of sovereign state municipality with authorized municipal office, an administrative district of landlocked country municipality with authorized municipal office, an administrative district of republic municipality with authorized municipal office and an administrative district of successor state municipality with authorized municipal office; it is also an administrative district of country municipality with expanded powers, an administrative district of sovereign state municipality with expanded powers, an administrative district of landlocked country municipality with expanded powers, an administrative district of republic municipality with expanded powers and an administrative district of successor state municipality with expanded powers. In addition, Ashenvale is an administrative territorial entity, a big city, a capital of region, a country municipality with expanded powers, a sovereign state municipality with expanded powers, a landlocked country municipality with expanded powers, a republic municipality with expanded powers and a successor state municipality with expanded powers. It is a district of the country, a district of the sovereign state, a district of the landlocked country, a district of the republic and a district of the successor state, and it is a district town, an electoral unit and an enclave. Ashenvale is a municipality of the country, a municipality of the sovereign state, a municipality of the landlocked country, a municipality of the republic and a municipality of the successor state; it is a municipality with authorized municipal office and a municipality with town privileges in the country, in the sovereign state, in the landlocked country, in the republic and in the successor state. Ashenvale is also a national capital, part of the regions of the country, the regions of the sovereign state, the regions of the landlocked country, the regions of the republic and the regions of the successor state, a second-level administrative division and a tourist destination. Quorath is a big city and a city, and is described as a city in province of sovereign state, a city in province of country and a city in province of federation. Valyndor is a city that is a former capital, a megacity, a prefecture-level city, a provincial capital and a sub-province-level division.

Eastwood City is described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy and in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Caelum City is a big city that was established in 1880. It is identified as a city within multiple political frameworks, being described as a city in the sovereign state, in the constitutional republic, in the federal republic, in the superpower, in the country, and in the historical unrecognized state.

The city is the subject of several published works. It is described in Dreamt Compilation and in Infinite Reimagining, both of which are versions, editions or translations. It also appears in the written work Legendarium, in Qylarans — an ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedia — and in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Caelum City maintains formal twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Jorenth since 1996; Jorenth is a big city and a commune in a number of administrative contexts, including the sovereign state, the colonial power, the republic and the country. Since 2030 Caelum City has been twinned with Taryndor; Taryndor is a big city and regional capital with expanded municipal powers and a range of statutory designations and town privileges. Rivenbrook became a twin in 2046; Rivenbrook is a municipality associated with the sovereign state, the realm, the country and the historical nationality. In 2048 Caelum City established twin relationships with both Korthandel and Pyresia: Korthandel is a big city and former capital that serves as a direct-administered municipality, prefecture-level city, provincial capital and sub‑province-level division, while Pyresia is a big city specifically designated in the state plan and also a prefecture-level city and sub‑province-level division.

Galenor Guevara (15 April 1943 – 21 July 1987) was a Taldor Sultanate painter, designer and sculptor. His field of work was the art of painting, and his work encompassed genres including abstract art, portrait, portrait painting and still life. He was associated with the movements abstract expressionism, action painting and modern art.

Guevara's works are held in a range of public and institutional collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Inspiration Institute, Treasures of Expression Museum and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum. Artist files about him are held at Artisanal Library, Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and Scholar's Keep.

He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright representatives included CopyDefender, IntellectProtect and Music and Media Syndicate. The copyrights on his works have expired. He participated in the art events Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions and worked in Ironwood.

Born a citizen of the Taldor Sultanate, Guevara lived in Tetralis beginning in 1954 and in Celestara beginning in 1958. He spoke Nuvrak and Velthar. He is described in the database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Guevara died on 21 July 1987 by hanging; his manner of death was recorded as suicide.

Obsidian City is a big city and a county seat that serves as the capital of Sylvaris. It is also described administratively as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state; similarly it is identified as a city of sovereign state state, a city of constitutional republic state, a city of federal republic state, a city of superpower state, a city of country state and a city of historical unrecognized state state.

The settlement's earliest written record dates to 1836, and its formal inception is recorded as 1851. The city was named after Obsidian C. Stonehaven.

Velthar is the official language of Obsidian City. The city has established twinning arrangements with several administrative bodies: it is twinned with Eldoria, with that partnership beginning on 2026-03-25; with Umbermist; and with Zephyria, with that partnership beginning on 2031-01-01. Eldoria is itself a big city and a commune, and is also identified as a port settlement. Umbermist is recorded as a municipality. Zephyria is described as a big city and a major regional center and is also identified as an urban district in a federated state as well as an urban municipality.

Obsidian City appears in a variety of published sources. It is described by Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation, each noted as a version, edition or translation; by FactFolio, which is recorded as an encyclopedic dictionary and a version, edition or translation; by Legendarium and by Qylarans, the latter appearing in classifications related to ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedias; by The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, both literary works; and by Verifiable Vade Mecum, a reference work.

Uryth Seven (born 12 May 1842 – died 1912) was an Ardentia chemist, agronomist, inventor, university teacher and writer. He worked in Hightower and wrote in Malquari, a language he also spoke. Educated at Bayview Comprehensive Institute, he combined academic teaching with practical agricultural research and inventive activity.

Over the course of his career he belonged to a wide range of learned bodies and publishers. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Catalyst Society of Knowledge, Constellation Institute, Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He joined the Celestial Research Institute on 4 June 1879, became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 16 July 1893, and entered Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1906.

His work in chemistry and related fields was recognized with several honours. He received the Elysium Science Medal on 1 January 1879 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 4 June 1879. Later awards included The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1892, the Lumina Token in 1908, and the Seraphic Prize.

Uryth Seven is described in a range of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Reflections of Humanity, Stellar Reinterpretation, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library. His personal and professional papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He spent his working life in Hightower and died there in 1912.

Etherealis is a big city, megacity and metropolis that functions as a prefecture-level city and a sub-province-level division. It is situated on the continent of Nystoria and lies within the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic.

Etherealis has served as the capital of Fendril since 1010. The city has been located in the administrative territorial entity of Fendril since 14 October 1988. As a municipal entity, Etherealis is a member of the Empowerment Collective.

The city maintains twinning and partnership arrangements with a number of other municipalities. Its twin towns and sister cities include Aetheral Grove, Aetherdon (since 13 November 2048), Ambrosia City, Ashenvale, Celestara (since 2053), Emberglow (since 2 September 2059), Everhaven, Nereidia (since 21 December 2044), Nythoria, Radiant Shores (since 17 February 2028), Rivenbrook (since 2051), Rivenwood (since 2047), Starlight Cove, Tranquilhaven (since 12 October 2045), Valendor (since 2039), Valoria, Vornath and Ythoria.

Etherealis has been described in a variety of published works, including Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Celyndra Nancy (born 24 September 1982) is a film, stage, and voice actor. She has performed in both on-screen and live theatrical roles and works professionally as a voice actor.

She uses her voice as her principal instrument in performance and recording. Her career encompasses film projects, stage productions, and voice work across various media.

She speaks Malquari, which is a modern language. Her biography records her birth on 24 September 1982, and she uses she/her pronouns.

OpenLuna University is an open-access publisher and a university. It was founded by Fintan Muiran and has an inception date of 12 March 1404.

The institution is headquartered in Lunathis and is located in the administrative territorial entity of Lunathis, a city-state.

OpenLuna University is described in the data set InsightVerse on 31 October 2058, 30 April 2059, 3 August 2060, 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062, and 16 May 2063. It became a member of the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a database and nonprofit organization, in October 2062.

Tidal Reach is an adjacent sea and a drainage basin. 

The feature lies within Luminara State, the Myralun Empire and Solandria. Its drainage basin includes Luminara State, Solandria and Thundralis, and the Tidal Reach shares a border with Thundralis. The Beryth, a transboundary river, is a major inflow to the Tidal Reach.

The Tidal Reach is described in a variety of published works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal, the Legendarium, The Midnight Library, the Verifiable Vade Mecum and the Version Vault.

Olvyn Cabanas (16 July 1791 – 17 April 1792) was a princess of the noble family Cindervale. She was female.

She was the daughter of Kaldorn Albuquerque and Kythorn Tim. Olvyn had ten siblings, among them Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch, Caelorian Manuel, Garenth Casillas, Hestira Albertson and Loryn Del Carmen, as well as Menyra Cosio, Neryth Cevallos, Qylara Zack, Rynthor Lowe and Xylara Oliveros.

Olvyn Cabanas died in Thundoria.

Delphina Roselle Thorne (7 September 1856 – 29 September 1937) was a Crownlandian princess, consort and painter. A member of the Sablemoor family, she held citizenship of Crownlandia. Her given names included Delphina, Quinella, Vespera and Wynelle.

Thorne was born in Jorathia and studied under Braxian Erin. She married Crownthal Jorvik on 26 May 1881. Their children included Cecil Crownlandia, Crownthalasian Monarch, Cyndar Aucoin, Elysia Crownhart, Ilaris Tedesco and Sylphira Leung.

She received several honors, notably the Order of the Celestial Serpent, the Order of the Radiant Heart (awarded in 1931) and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame. Copyrights on her works have expired. Her life and work have been described by O'Rourke Insights Online.

Sornal Deyq (4 February 1825 – 11 June 1898) was a noble of the Myralun Empire who held the title of duke. She served as a consort and was active as a socialite. A citizen of the Myralun Empire, she received the Order of the Serene Waters.

She was born in Zephyra to Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo and belonged to the Jorathyn family. Her child was Sylphina Moonshadow.

Sornal had a number of siblings, among them Lysen Qivar, Aeloria Valarnis, Tyqor Lun, Eldrin Myralun, Halir Ola, Myralun Luminara, Tolen Rax and Thalios Myralun.

Her life and role are described in the Dreamt Compilation as well as in the Legendarium.

Rylas Shafi (5 November 1658 – 4 October 1727) was a painter from Kaldoria known for landscape painting. Born and died in Harborview City, he spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue, which was also his native language. He was a male artist and a citizen of Kaldoria. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Shafi trained under Jorian Broome and spent periods of his working life in different urban centers. He worked in Draxport from 1 January 1678 to 1 January 1680, and afterwards in Harborview City from 1 January 1680 to 1 January 1715.

Collections that hold his works include the Chronicles Museum, the Cultural Nexus Museum, Ethos Gallery, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Royal Gallery Palace, The Art Exchange, The Artisan Vault, The Borough Art Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Storytellers' Studio, Vivid Visions Gallery, and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files on Shafi are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Shafi is described in several published sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Fintan Muiran was a Velorian noble who served as a sovereign and held the title of duke. His given name was Fintan and he was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion.

He was born in 1388 in Lunathis; available records place his birth between 18 November 1388 and 16 March 1389. He died on 29 August 1434.

Fintan belonged to the Elarian family. His father was Fintan Pellan, and his recorded relatives include Alden Thornfield, Cassian Elarian, Freyael Welborn, Oryndel Rothschild, and Ylenara Mp. He was male.

From 1405 until 1412 he was married to Belyndra Joe.

His life and career are described in several works and collections, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Narratives of the Lexicon, the Quantum Nexus Archive, and Reflections of Humanity.

Aelthor Dehart (20 August 1949 – 1 September 2000) was a Terranova architect and designer associated with modernism. His work was principally in architecture, and he worked in Nexopolis. He was a citizen of Terranova and spoke Seldim and Velthar, with Seldim as his native language.

Dehart held roles as an architect and as a designer and was affiliated with several professional and scholarly organizations. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, Nexus Learning Society and the Summit Academy of Learning. Artist files about Dehart are held at the Artisanal Library, an art library and research library.

Examples of his work are held in numerous public collections. His works appear in the collections of the Creative Spark Foundation, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Hub, The Visionary Experience and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Dehart’s copyright representative was CopyDefender, and his body of published work remains protected by copyrights. He died on 1 September 2000 of brain cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Irvin Caledorn (given name Irvin) was a male painter, drawer and lithographer born in Obsidian City on 1921-08-12 and died on 1964-01-08. He worked principally in the art of painting, producing genre paintings as well as landscapes and portraits, and was employed by Lumina Arts Academy. In addition to his studio practice, he served as a teacher and university teacher.

Caledorn studied under Yardley Thompson and later taught students of his own, including Braxton Lyrak Vorse. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and carried out work in several places, notably Draxoria, Moonstone Ridge and Verenthis.

His works are held widely in institutional collections; among them are Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams and Celestial Grove of Sculptures. Additional holdings include Chronicle Citadel, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus and Dreamscape Museum. Further collections with Caledorn’s works are the Ethereal Observatory, Fusion Art Institute, Gallery of Dreams, Myrthwood Art Collective and Radiant Brush Gallery. His works also appear in Solstice Art Storage, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Oasis and The Ethereal Visions Museum, as well as The Evolution Gallery, The Visionary Experience and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Artist files on Caledorn are maintained at several research and art libraries and archives: the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He spoke and wrote in Velthar and used that language for his writing.

Caledorn’s copyrights as a creator have expired. He died of cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Kalindor Hibbard (born 1322; died 13 October 1349) was a female politician. She was born in the city of Zephyra and was the child of Adeline Zephyra Thornfield.

Hibbard married Jalyndra Sandberg in 1334; the marriage lasted until her death on 13 October 1349. They had nine children: Duvalon Herzog, Helynd Rm, Jorian Fitz, Kaelwyn Overton, Lysandor Heffernan, Menara Hussaini, Tarynth Ally, Zoran Bowden and Zyndel Nugent.

She was one of many siblings, among them Alaric Zephyra, Bastian Thorne, Caelorian Cristobal, Elias Stormwind and Geryth Momin, as well as Inigo Marcellus, Perrana Marcelo, Valandar Oberg, Xylaris Anh and Yelindra Silas.

Kalindor Hibbard died of puerperal disorders on 13 October 1349.

Varlyn Quigley (born 1623 in Crestwood; died 14 March 1686 in Silvershore) was a Kaldorian military officer, military leader and politician who also worked as an art collector. He was born into the Kaldorath dynasty; his father was Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and held citizenship of Kaldoria.

Quigley’s public career combined military and political roles. He achieved the rank of general and served as stadtholder beginning in 1664 and continuing until 14 March 1686. He worked in Silvershore from 1664-01-01 to 1686-01-01. During his career he took part in the Sectarian Strife, a religious war.

As an art collector he amassed works that are now held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; the copyrights on his works have expired. He received the Opal Crown.

Quigley married Orlinth Link on 1664-04-04. He was the parent of Delphina Mariselle, Elara Myrthian Kytarathian, Elysian Hagos, Meliora Cast, Pyron Sorto, Thalyra Stokes, Valenor Sauer, Ythran Segundo and Zyris Ruggiero. He was related to Jorin Morales, Rhystar Shahzad and Zafrina Althaea Moonshadow, and had numerous siblings, including Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria, Kirelle Amara Thorne, Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine and Wyric Pazos.

Quigley died in Silvershore on 14 March 1686 and was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Xindar Rc (18 May 1860 – 17 May 1936) was a noble of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty who held the title Lucalith. She received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest.

Born on 18 May 1860, Xindar was the daughter of Calyra Facundo and Maelthas Williford. Her siblings included Elysia Aldermore, Galdorin Cadavid, Halwyn Liu, Ilyndar Mcintyre and Pellin Billingsley, as well as Pyridan Arthur, Taryn Ojo, Xandria Zerinthal, Xandria Veralyn and Ylinth Burdick.

Xindar spoke and wrote Kynthor. After her death on 17 May 1936, she was laid to rest at Gentle Hills.

The Shattered Labyrinth: A New Path is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction work that centers on the theme of individuality and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is associated with the color "color".

The episode was first performed on 2031-05-11; its publication dates are recorded as 2031-05-11 and 2033-05-05. It was directed by Yardley Dovern Pax and written by Gwendal Truax. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, made available in a video-on-demand format through that service.

The Shattered Labyrinth: A New Path features the characters Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream and Serenix. Braxton Velaryn is depicted as a human who appears in the franchise’s literary works and on television. Freya Wilder is portrayed as a human character who appears across media — as a literary, film, television and video game character — and is also noted with the designation xB. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and appears in the franchise’s literary and television narratives. Mira Silverstream is depicted as a human in the episode’s literary and television forms. Serenix is portrayed as an android character who appears on television.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio. The episode follows The Lost City of Aether in the series sequence and is itself followed by The Celestial Labyrinth: A New Era. It is described by the edition Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

Pythera Ty (born Orinelle; 13 May 1781 – 24 June 1837) was a female aristocrat who held the title of princess and served as regent. She was born and died in Lunathis and received honours during her life, including the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Born Orinelle to Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad, Pythera Ty belonged to the House Maerwyn family. She married Fintan O'Sullivan on 8 April 1805 and had at least one child, Rhaelar Belmont.

Pythera Ty was part of a large sibling group that included Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Glynara Hilario, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris and Olyndra Myrathis, as well as Orinelle Mariselle, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, Ylessa Dinero and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

She served in the position of regent and was active as an aristocrat. Her life and contributions have been documented in several sources: Biographica Nova, Narratives of the Lexicon and the Obsidian Tome. The Gallery of Texts holds artist files relating to her.

Pythera Ty died of typhus on 24 June 1837 in Lunathis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault. She is distinct from Gathryn Pina.

The Celestial Echo: A Tale Untold is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise and is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria television series. It is a science fiction work that takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode was directed by Yardley Harquen Naim and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. It was first performed and published on 2043-05-19 and was distributed by ScreenSync on a video on demand format; ScreenSync is a video on demand service and web broadcaster. The episode follows The Celestial Journeys and is followed by The Shattered Whispers.

Cast members for the episode include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters appearing in the episode include the fictional humans Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall.

Voice actors credited on the episode are Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The production’s color is listed as "color."

The Celestial Guardians: Legends Reimagined is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction work set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm on a fictional planet, and its narrative makes reference to neutrino; a color is also listed among its production attributes.

Directed by Draxella Knott, the episode features cast members Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, and Lyra Dray.

The work had its first performance and an initial publication on 2030-05-06, with an additional publication date recorded as 2033-03-18. It follows The Shattered Echoes of Time in the series and is followed by The Arcane Horizons. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was made available via a video on demand format.

The Celestial Guardians: Legends Reimagined has been described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

Fractured Time: Echoes from the Past is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The story takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and was directed by Axton Mercer.

Its date of first performance and publication date are 25 November 2037. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format; ScreenSync functions as a video-on-demand streaming service and mobile app and also operates as a web broadcaster. The episode's listed color is "color."

Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Callum Rivers is presented as a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Harmony Quill appears as a comics character, a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Kieran Frostfire is a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Rowan Emberwood is a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, a literary character and a television character.

The episode follows The Celestial Guardians and is followed by The Enigma of the Lost Realms in its series sequence. The Arcane Alchemy is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. Presented as a work of science fiction, the episode is set within the fictional universe of the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet and in environments that include a cave within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode’s characters include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream and Serenix.

Production was overseen by director Zorath Parrilla and film editor Yardley Dovern Pax. The Arcane Alchemy is distributed in a video-on-demand format by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video streaming service and web broadcaster. It has two recorded publication dates, 2030-10-12 and 2030-10-14, and its date of first performance is 2030-10-14. The episode is described by the edition Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. The work is also listed with the color "color."

The episode features cast members Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Among the characters, Braxton Velaryn is portrayed as a fictional human who appears in franchise literature and on television; Freya Wilder is depicted as a fictional human who appears across film, television, literary and video game media within the franchise and is also associated with xB; Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid who appears in franchise literature and on television; Mira Silverstream is a fictional human appearing in literature and television; and Serenix is represented as a fictional android appearing on television.

Within the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga sequence, The Arcane Alchemy follows The Chronicles of the Forsaken and is followed by The Ethereal Whispers: A Journey to the Unknown, both of which are episodes in the same media franchise.

The Arcane Secrets: The Journey Continues is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series, and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. The episode is presented in color and is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe that serves as its narrative location; its action takes place on a fictional planet and aboard a ghost ship. Publication dates for the episode are 2031-01-25 and 2033-04-13, and its date of first performance was 2031-01-27. The episode is followed by The Ethereal Convergence: A New Journey.

The episode's cast members include Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio; they appear alongside characters such as Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart and Tobias Merriweather. Several of the named characters are presented as fictional humans, with Braxton Velaryn, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart and Tobias Merriweather listed as fictional human characters; Freya Wilder appears as a film character, television character and video game character as well as a literary character; Lyra Dray is identified as an extracurricular–human hybrid within the work of fiction and also appears as a literary and television character.

Brystar Caron directed the episode, and they were joined in the production by Halden Quevedo as director of photography; together they oversaw the episode's visual and narrative execution. The episode is described in Spectral Volume, a version or edition of the work.

Realm of the Ancients is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Its date of first performance and publication date are 22 April 2037. The production's listed color is "color."

The episode was directed by Ellyra Saldaña and Glynara Dhaliwal, with Ellyra Saldaña also credited as screenwriter. It was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

Narratively, Realm of the Ancients takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in a casino hotel. The characters appearing in the episode include Thalen Virok and Marcellus Stormwatch; Marcellus Stormwatch is presented as a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character, while Thalen Virok appears as a literary and television character.

Beneath the Starlit Sky is a literary work presented in the form of an encyclopedia and classified as a reference work. It was produced in the Malquari language, a modern language.

The work's publication began in 1857. It was published in Delvoria, a big city and major regional center.

Merylen Lehman (born 1621; earliest 1621, latest 1622 — died 29 August 1705, also recorded as 1 September 1705) was a Kaldorian painter and printmaker associated with Kaldorian Impressionism and Verdantism. He worked primarily in genre painting, portrait painting and schutterstuk, and held citizenship of Kaldoria. He spoke Therian and the Valorean Tongue.

Born in Nextridge, Lehman was active as an artist in Southpoint from 1647 to 1655 and is recorded as working in Nextridge in 1655. He was a student of Xandria Leos and later taught several pupils, among them Garenth Neil, Qylar Fredericks (1665), Qyvor Dew and Ralyn Oviedo (1685–1690). His family included a sibling, Wyndra Jean Louis.

Lehman's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey; Artisan's Vision Hub; Artistry Nexus; Celestial Canvas Institute; Chroma Art Cooperative; Cultura Artopolis; Culturia Heritage Network; Essence of Art; Ethereal Exhibits; Ethos Gallery; Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; Luminara National Art Museum; Lystoria Artisphere Museum; Meridian Cultural Arts Complex; National Institute of Cultural Heritage; National Legacy Gallery; National Museum of Heritage; Nostalgia Nook; Ravenwood Collective Art Museum; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum; Solaris Cultural Collective; Terranova Artis Museum; The Art Archive; The Art Nexus; The Celestial Craft Gallery; The Chroma Atelier; The Creative Convergence Gallery; The Curated Press; The Curatorial Vault; The Echo Chamber; The Eclectic Arts Pavilion; The Ethereal Canvas; The Gallery of Civic Creatives; The Harmony Space; The Illusive Gallery; The Inspirational Institute; The Nexus of Wonders; The Reminiscence Repository; The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum; The Storytellers' Studio; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum; Verdantia Art Collective Museum; Vivid Visions Gallery; and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about Lehman are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Lehman is described in a range of reference works and databases, including DataGalaxy; the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon; the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles; O'Rourke Insights Online; Reflections of Humanity; SagaSpectrum; and The Midnight Library. His date of burial or cremation is recorded as 1 September 1705. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Quorlin Aparicio (26 January 1709 – 28 January 1790) was a painter and teacher born in Harvenia and who died in Lunathis. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was known for his portraiture. Aparicio was associated with the Verdantism movement and served as a court painter during his career.

Aparicio was employed by the Lunavalle Academia, where he also has works in the institution's collection. He was a student of Kaelar Granados and later taught Micaiah Thorne. He spoke Therian.

His works are held in a wide range of public and private collections, including Culturia Noblis, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Luminara National Art Museum, Lunavalle Academia, Museum Merge, The Aesthetic Archive, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Futurist Gallery, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Copyrights on his works have expired.

Zolterran Xyldari National Academy is a national academy and educational institution based in Zolterra. It was established on 10 May 1774.

The academy's primary field of work is the arts. It conducts its activities using Xyldari as its working language; Xyldari is a modern language.

Works associated with the academy are held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. The Institute of Fine Arts and Culture serves as an art museum and national museum and is operated as a government agency of Zolterra.

Sylas Marwick (25 January 1782 – 10 March 1858) was a male novelist, writer and university teacher whose work lay in the field of philosophy. Born in Solyra, he spent his professional life working in Hightower, where he also died. He held the title Advocate of the Fallen.

His given name was Sylas. Marwick was a native speaker of Malquari, wrote in Malquari and used that language in his spoken and written work. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Marwick was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the Constellation Institute; the Constellation Institute also functions as a book publisher. Among those who influenced his thought were Axton Caldwell, Falion Iris, Hesperan Sides, Micaiah Trent Halvorsen, Talyra Sample and Zyra Bracken.

His life and work are discussed in a range of publications, including the versions or translations Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining and Resonance Translation; the written works Labyrinthine Journal and Reflections of Humanity, the latter a biographical dictionary; and the literary works Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Caelan Rhovan Kel (given name Caelan; 26 September 1926 – 25 April 2006) was a psychoanalyst and translator from Cynthera. Born in Calidore, he held citizenship of Cynthera and was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education.

Early life and family
Kel was born to Uryth Lena in Calidore. They were one of a large group of siblings, which included Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel.

Career and language work
