Kel worked as a psychoanalyst and as a translator. He spoke Malquari and Velthar, and wrote in Velthar. His education at the Quantum College of Higher Education preceded his professional work.

Sources
Caelan Rhovan Kel is described by ReadRealm.

Eldrith is a noble title, a legal privilege given to some members in monarchial and princely societies.

The title has been held by a number of persons. Among them are Alden Rhyseris Eldrith and Alden Rhyseris, as well as Alyssia Rhyseris, whose tenure with the title ended on 30 July 1939. Caden Rhyseris, Elara Rhyseris and Fintan Rhyseris have also borne the title.

Several members of the Mystralyn name have held Eldrith, including Aurelia Mystralynian, who began holding the title on 15 April 1999, as well as Celestria Mystralyn, Elwood Kylor Zenth, Fintan Mystralyn and Fintan Mystralynson. Other individual holders include Elwood Farnsworth, Fintan Farlanov, Ilyrith Atkins, Irvin Talbot, Irvin Thorne, Vail Thorne, Jalen Thompson and Olaris Nick.

Together these persons represent the recorded holders of the Eldrith title.

Elric Suryen Koth (born 1320-01-01; died 1346-07-04) was a sovereign born in Lunathis. His given name was Elric and he belonged to the Ardentia ethnic group.

As a ruler he held several positions. He served as the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 1345 until 1346-07-03. He also held the title Jorathen. from 1345 until 1346. In addition, he served as Protector of the Eternal Flame.

Elric was a member of the Elarian family. His parents were Wyrlyn Fiedler and Zafrina Elowen Thorne. He was male and had several siblings, among them Brystyne Natarajan, Elwood Ralnor Quis, Fintan Pellan, Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quethan Conn, Quinlan Strathmore and Theros Nick.

Elric Suryen Koth died on 1346-07-04; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes, with dysentery and a perforated ulcer given as causes of death.

He is described by the sources DataGalaxy, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Knights of the Majestic Realm is a dynastic order of knighthood distributed by the head of a former royal family. The order is associated with Drathland.

The order was founded by Beryth Mchugh and came into existence on 3 July 1777. Its formation took place in Zephyra, a large city and commune.

Knights of the Majestic Realm is linked to Drathland, which is recognized as both a sovereign state and a historical country. The order is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a particular version, edition, or translation that includes an account of the organization.

Thalric Kytarathian Eldrin (born 10 May 1940, died 15 September 2010) was a Cynthera biophysicist, physicist, naturalist, inventor, philosopher and writer. He worked in natural science and science studies and held a professorship as a university teacher. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He was male and identified with atheism.

Eldrin was a member of several research and learned organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute, the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Spectrum Institute of Learning and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences. He spoke Velthar. In addition to his academic career, he held the rank of lieutenant and took part in the Aegis Warfare.

In his academic training Eldrin was a student of Braxton Ellsworth, and his doctoral advisor was Hesper Braxton Quarven. He supervised Darian Qelra Halth and Xantha Solar as his doctoral students.

Eldrin received numerous honors, among them the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence. He was awarded the Quantum Visionary Medal (1984) and the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1986). He also received the Scientific Odyssey lecture series award in 2001. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1998.

He is described in ReadRealm, The Life Archive and the Whispering Scroll. Thalric Kytarathian Eldrin died in Calidore.

Adeline Thornfield Orindel (born 24 December 1861, died 14 January 1940) was a male mathematician and university teacher whose work spanned algebra, elliptic function theory, mathematical analysis, orthogonal polynomials and quadratic forms. His notable work was in number theory. His given name was Adeline Thornfield Orindel and he spoke Therian.

Education and early career
Orindel was educated at Crestwood Academy (1879–1880) and at Catalyst Polytechnic (1880–1881), and also attended the Prism Academy of Learning. He served as a senior lecturer from 1901 to 1908 while employed by the Académie des Sciences Ethiques. From 1909 to 1936 he held the occupation of university teacher; during part of that period he was employed by Silver Birch College (1915–1936) and at other times by Catalyst Polytechnic.

Academic work and students
Orindel’s research interests included algebra, elliptic function, mathematical analysis, orthogonal polynomials and quadratic form, with number theory cited as a notable area of work. His doctoral students included Paylan Zhao (1918) and Tristan Alderwood.

Memberships and positions
He was a member of numerous scholarly organizations, among them the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (membership from 14 July 1895), the Celestial Research Institute (membership from 27 November 1912), the Thundorian Science Archive Database (membership from 30 December 1916), and the Academy of Innovative Thought (membership from 1923). He also belonged to the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He held the position of president from 1 January 1929 to 31 December 1929.

Honours and recognition
Orindel received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 27 November 1912. He was also awarded the Seraphic Prize and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade.

Sources and legacy
Adeline Thornfield Orindel is described in a number of reference works and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse, the Labyrinthine Journal and the book series Shadows in the Ink. He was buried at Resting Waters.

Xoria Rau (given name Elian; 11 July 1771 – 4 April 1846) was an astronomer, professor and writer whose work focused on astronomy. He wrote in Therian and identified as an atheist. His published works are no longer under copyright.

He was educated at Insight Archives and Education and later joined the same institution as an employee, serving there from 1 January 1807 until 1 January 1846. Rau was an active member of several learned bodies and organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Cognition Coalition, Melgoria Unity Alliance (from 4 March 1800), Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (from 1792), Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 21 December 1827), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Academically, Ythira Howlett both taught Rau and acted as his doctoral advisor. Rau in turn supervised doctoral students, among them Cole-Ren Kestrelborne and Sylas Xylander; Cole-Ren Kestrelborne is also noted as a student of his. He received honors during his career, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the latter beginning in 1820.

Rau's writings and related materials appear in public collections and repositories: his works are held by Civic Library Publishing and The Chronicle Chamber. He is described in a range of sources and compilations, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Encyclical of Identities, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, and The Midnight Library.

Rau died on 4 April 1846. His funeral took place on 6 April 1846, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Halyra Sher (1 July 1827 – 22 December 1906) was a male engineer, military engineer, physicist, mathematician and professor. His work covered mathematics, mechanics and projective geometry. He spoke and wrote in Therian; his published works are now out of copyright.

Educated at Catalyst Polytechnic, Sher later served on its staff and was employed there. He completed doctoral work under Mylaria Gzz. Over the course of his career he held the position Rylathor and briefly served as president from 11 May 1879 to 31 December 1879. In addition to his academic roles he held the military rank of brigadier general and participated in the Conclave of Conflict, and he was active in politics.

Sher was a member of a number of learned and scientific organizations. He joined the Astral Academy of Knowledge in 1871 and became a member of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives in March 1873. He was associated with the Thundorian Science Archive Database from 10 January 1880 and with the Celestial Research Institute beginning 5 May 1881. He also belonged to Myralun Luminara Academy Press (from 1896), the Cognition Coalition (from 1904), the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences and the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers.

His publications and other works are held in institutional collections and archives: The Archive Atrium preserves his archives, and the Nexus of Literary Inquiry holds works by him. Sher's writings and career have been described in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Sher received numerous awards and honours. These include the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (5 May 1881), the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (9 July 1892), the Golden Vanguard Class (10 December 1889), and the Seraphic Prize (31 May 1902). He was also a recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Golden Aurora Class and the Noble Valorian Order.

The Tome of Echoes is a science fiction novel and written work that forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was first published on 2041-01-01, with an inception in 2041, and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with events occurring in the year 2413 within that fictional universe.

Characters in The Tome of Echoes include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Flux, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Lyric Lifesaver, Miles Hawthorne, Sable Hayes, Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather.

Many of these figures are portrayed as human characters within the Eldoria Chronicles, among them Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Miles Hawthorne, Sable Hayes, Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather; Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid.

Several characters appear across other media or are characterized by particular forms: Flux appears as a cyborg in the work and is represented as a film, literary and television character; Freya Wilder appears as a film, literary, television and video game character and as a media franchise character; Braxton Velaryn and Cassian Brightwood are both literary and television characters; Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather are literary and television characters; Miles Hawthorne and Sable Hayes are television characters. Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram, is presented as a fictional writer, and appears as a television character.

Elenara Tum (1920-02-11 – 2005-04-18) was a male artist whose practice encompassed contemporary painting and related disciplines. He was born on 1920-02-11 and held citizenship of Morvath from 1920-02-11 until 1985-06-18. He died in Bryston on 2005-04-18.

Tum’s active career extended from 1940-01-01 to 2005-01-01. He worked primarily in contemporary painting and was associated with the movements futurism and metaphysical painting. Over the course of his career he worked as an artist, drawer, painter, poet, printmaker and writer, and he spoke and wrote in Thesvian. He participated in documenta and, during his life, took part in the Chronos Siege.

His works are held by a wide range of collections and institutions, including the Aesthetica Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Ethos Gallery, Infinity Art Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Inspiration Nexus and The Palette Sanctuary. Artist files on Tum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts.

Tum was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and received the Arcane Order. His creative output remains protected by copyrights and is represented for copyright matters by IntellectProtect.

He lived and worked in Bryston, where he also died.

Ilyrith Awad was a female aristocrat from Lunathis who held citizenship of Thalendria. She was a member of House Maerwyn, a cadet branch, dynasty and noble family.

Ilyrith was born in Lunathis on 8 June 1833 and died there on 16 March 1834. Her parents were Aldrin Valtoros and Aeloria Vensyl. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Her siblings included Alaric Darkmoorson, Elian Martel, Feryndal Naqvi, Halvyn Groom, Halvyn Villagrana, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter and Zephyr Solrune.

Elara Moonstone (given name Kirelle) was a female born on 19 December 1667 and died on 14 January 1670. She was born in Silvershore and died there as well; Silvershore is a cadastral populated place with town rights and privileges.

Elara was the daughter of Yandor Santini and Zafrina Amara Liora. Her given name was Kirelle, a female given name.

Her siblings included Alderon Gene, Delphina Hartwell, Freth Carlton, Hesper Aldenwood and Olvyn Crocker. Additional siblings were Qalyn Si, Theryn Stratton, Vail Aldridge, Wyslind Conte, Wyslind Galdamez and Xilara Mcdonough.

Liora Zephyrix (2 December 1832 – 23 April 1840) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of Drathland. A member of the Galdrin dynasty, she was born in the city of Zephyra and later interred at Ethereal Heights Church.

She was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. Her siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

As an aristocrat she bore the noble title princess. She was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery associated with her family and social standing.

Gellion Salmon (13 September 1766 – 1 February 1773) was a princess of the Quicksilver noble family. She was born in Zephyria and died there.

She was the daughter of Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan and Geryth Archie, as well as Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard and Wryndra Turpin.

She spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Glynara Petrov (31 August 1437 – 5 April 1456) was a male aristocrat and a member of the Valereth dynasty. He held the titles of count and duke and was known for his role as an aristocrat. He spoke Therian.

He was the son of Adeline Thornfield Umbraline and Pyraen Senior. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield-Smith, Inigo Javel Ond, Jynara Godoy, Noxenel, Phylar Snook, Vespera Senior, and Zynara Viera.

Hesper Aldrin (given name Hesper; born 1146 – died 13 January 1216) was a male duke and sovereign who held the position Radiant Count. He was resident in Lunathis and served in a ruling capacity during his lifetime.

Aldrin bore the noble title duke and his recorded occupation is sovereign; he also held the hereditary position Radiant Count. His primary residence was Lunathis, which is also recorded as the place where he died.

He was born in 1146 to Elwood Jasper Thompson and Liora Valentina Hartman. His siblings included Alysor Mayor, Delyndra Mccall, Elwood Phralen Vost, Galdra Nolasco, Liora Valenbrook, Pyrthas Marler, Quinlan Thorne, Rynen Winner, Sylphira China, and Vyndel Welker. Hesper Aldrin died in Lunathis on 13 January 1216 from a horse fall.

Hesper Aldrin is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, RefereX, and Reflections of Humanity.

Pyraen Vargas (23 April 1867 – 19 June 1941) was a Goldenreach politician and military officer who held the rank of general field marshal. Born in Zephyria, he was a citizen of Goldenreach and was active professionally from 1 January 1887 until 1 January 1941.

Early life and family
Pyraen Vargas was born in Zephyria. He belonged to the Quicksilver noble family. His father was Zoran Morais and his mother was Kaelith Astran, who was a twin. His siblings included Galindor Switzer, Olyndra Orindel, Orindel Thalorian, Pheris Dueñas, Viorelle Amarantha Liora, and Xindar Mazariegos.

Career
Vargas combined a political career with senior military service, attaining the rank of general field marshal. He took part in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel during his career.

Honors, language and works
He received several honors, including the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Crystaline Honor, and was awarded the Jewel of the Ancients on 9 July 1917. He spoke and wrote in Malquari, and his writings are described in the Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Death and burial
Pyraen Vargas died on 19 June 1941 and was buried at Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam, a cathedral and court church.

Xylaria Solares (20 April 1844 – 8 July 1912) was a Valdrinian lithographer and painter associated with the academic art movement. Born a member of the Ardentia people and a citizen of the Valdrinia Empire, he worked primarily in landscape painting and portrait genres. He served as a court painter beginning in 1873.

Trained under Elian Carter and Yates Caldwell, Solares's professional activity spanned from 1859 to 1912, with a noted floruit in 1902. In addition to his lithographic work, he pursued painting throughout his career and worked in several locations, including Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, Hightower, Morvath, and Mystralyn.

Solares's works are held in numerous collections. They include Aesthetic Insights Press, Artisania National Gallery, Artropolis Nextridge, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum and Celestial Art House. Other institutions holding his work are Elysian Atrium, Harmathia Art Repository, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Artistry Hub and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Additional collections with his works comprise The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Confluence Museum, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Artifact Arena, as well as The Celestial Craft Gallery, The Curated Press, The Expression Hub and The Harmony Space. His works also appear in The Palace of Reflections, The Palette of Possibilities, The Reverie Museum, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Echoes Gallery, and are included in Treasures of Time, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

His personal and professional papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive, and artist files about him can be found at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He spoke Malquari. Solares is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Xylaria Solares died on 8 July 1912 of typhoid fever; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Zafrina Arindel (24 January 1818 – 16 May 1865) was an aristocrat of the Myralun Empire. She bore the family name Arindel and belonged to the Qelthar dynasty. She held citizenship of the Myralun Empire from 1832.

She was the daughter of Sylphine Tarrin Arindel and Lurith Mir. Her siblings included Adeline Arindel, Alaric Arindel, Liora Arindel-Tavish and Vespera Arindel; Liora Arindel-Tavish was a twin. Zafrina was married to Myralun Luminara from 9 October 1832 until 19 November 1864.

Zafrina spoke and wrote in Malquari, Myrathian and Therian, and is described in works such as the Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Twilight Tome and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium. During her life she received the Pinnacle Honor.

She died on 16 May 1865 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Lurith Buck (born 7 December 1763; baptized 22 December 1763; died 19 December 1790) was a Cyntherian aristocrat and royal consort. She was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera, serving as crown princess and later as queen consort. She was styled Chief Aeloria and Knight Aerion.

Born into the Quellhaven family, Lurith was the daughter of Irvin Oathen and Vespera Ysindra Vaalor. Her godparents included Falyndra Mccreary, Hesperyn Amy and Rhelian Ambrocio; Rhelian Ambrocio was also one of her siblings. Her other siblings were Alaric Thornewood, Elysian Valtaris, Fythar Rondon, Irvin Braxton Smith, Selinth Arrington and Ylenara Hinkle. She had one child, Thalor Jorvick.

As an aristocrat and member of the royal social class, Lurith Buck carried the responsibilities associated with her rank and position as consort. She spoke Velthar. Lurith Buck died on 19 December 1790 of puerperal disorders.

Vanyr Hedges (14 March 1859 – 9 January 1917) was a Morvathian monarch, politician and military leader. He held the noble titles of duke and king and reached the rank of general. He received numerous honors during his life, and his career and legacy are recorded in a range of reference works and publications.

Early life and family
Vanyr Hedges was born in Thundoria on 14 March 1859 and belonged to the Cindervale family. His father was Zilva. Angie. He spoke Thesvian.

Career and titles
Hedges served as a monarch and sovereign and was active as a politician. He held the noble titles duke and king and attained the military rank of general. In his role as sovereign he succeeded and replaced Zilva. Angie.

Citizenship and personal life
He held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until his death on 9 January 1917. Hedges was married to Elisander Orindel from 12 April 1881 until at least 1894. He was the parent of Elysia Drummond, Tyrian Srivastava and Vesperyn Gill.

Honors and awards
Over the course of his life Hedges received a variety of decorations and orders, among them the Aurora Badge, the Ethos Token and the Arcadian Emblem. He was also honoured with the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Order of the Radiant Heart, as well as chivalric distinctions such as the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Guardians of the Celestial Realm. He received several graded awards, including the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Noble Sovereign Grade; the Noble Sovereign Grade was awarded on 25 July 1894.

Death
Vanyr Hedges died of disease in Seraphim Bay on 9 January 1917.

Sources and legacy
His life and career are described in a variety of works and databases, including the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, the Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Creative Nexus is an art museum that operates as a local authority museum, run by a local government body. They serve as a public institution for the display and stewardship of art under local governmental administration.

They are located in Cynthera. Cynthera is a colonial power and an island sovereign state.

Kairis Schechter (25 February 1979 – 8 January 2023) was a voice actor. She worked in that capacity during her life and is noted for her contributions to the field.

She spoke Malquari. Schechter died in Hightower.

Merrick Grethain (13 April 1622 – 20 June 1639) was born on 13 April 1622; his given name was Merrick.

He was the son of Merrick Alton and Noxen Kallin. He had several siblings, including Aenara Soliman, Burand Nilsson, Jorvik Eldren Thorne, Rilith Cantero, Talyra Venshira, Thalric Kytarathian Emberwood and Wyrith Heckman.

Grethain died on 20 June 1639 in Zephyria, a big city and major regional center. He was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that is also a tourist attraction.

Yardley Harod Miv (born 13 August 1967, died 19 May 2057) was a male artist whose practice spanned painting, printmaking and sculpture alongside work in design, costume design and jewelry design. He died of respiratory failure. His published works remain protected by copyright.

Miv was associated with hard-edge painting and pop art and worked across figurative art and public art. Over the course of an active career that ran from 1993 to 2038, he combined studio practice as a painter, printmaker and sculptor with applied design work, including costume and jewelry design.

His work is held in numerous collections, among them Artemis Gallery, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance and Canvas of Dreams. Other holdings include the Creative Spark Foundation, Dreamscape Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Infinity Art Museum, as well as the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, Solstice Art Storage, The Color Spectrum Institute, The Odyssey Observatory and The Visionary Experience. He also participated in the exhibition and publication Object Odyssey, and his work is described in The Display Anthology.

Artist files relating to Miv are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright affairs were managed by IntellectProtect and the Music and Media Syndicate.

Miv was educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute. His given name was Yardley, and he spoke Velthar.

Feron Wills (13 November 1543 – 31 March 1606) was a male aristocrat of the Sablemoor family who held the title of landgrave and served as a monarch. He is recorded as an aristocrat and in a ruling position during his life.

Wills married Zyndra Ancheta on 11 December 1562. He was the father of ten children: Aralyn Nielson, Elanthar Carranza, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Orilith Dent, Talyra McKinley, Valerion Harbin and Zyndel Gala.

He died in Jorathia. Valandar Rochester is noted as a relative, and Bryston Sun, Drystan Greco and Ilindra Harwell are listed among persons significant to him.

Accounts of Wills appear in several sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary FactFolio, the Labyrinthine Journal and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Mylaria Enamorado (26 April 1829 – 14 December 1899) was a politician. He spoke Malquari.

He was the son of Sylas Wrynsel and had nine siblings, among them Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo, Orinthia Club, Peryn Frimpong, Pylar Hester, Sylas Harkwood, Verenth Jj and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

Jynor Mulligan (24 November 1763 – 27 September 1799) was a princess and queen consort from the Quicksilver family of the Velorian Dominion. A member of the realm's royalty, she held citizenship of the Velorian Dominion and spoke Kynthor.

She was born in Zephyria and died in Verenthia. Her burial took place at the Ethereal Sanctum, a crypt and pantheon. She was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

Mulligan was the daughter of Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard and Wryndra Turpin. She was married to Beryth Mchugh from 8 May 1777 until 27 September 1799; the couple had eight children: Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Phaelan Diop, Qyrian Harmon, Ronan Callahan, Ulwen Quintero, Ulyr Scoggins and Ylindor Calvin.

Her death in Verenthia on 27 September 1799 was caused by tuberculosis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes, and she had the same medical condition.

Inferno League is a video game and esports discipline originating in Zolterra. The title is distributed via digital distribution and is available through AppAlley, AppForge, PixelMart and VaultPlay. AppAlley and AppForge are distributed as app marketplaces, PixelMart operates as an online shop and video game distribution platform, and VaultPlay provides digital rights management and a software repository in addition to distribution.

The game was released with publication dates recorded as 2054-03-17 and 2054-03-20. It is available on the AstraBox console model and on the CipherSphere platform; AstraBox is released as a model series and video game console model, while CipherSphere functions as a brand and computing platform that includes an operating system and proprietary software.

Inferno League supports both single-player and multiplayer modes and is played using a gamepad. Its narrative is set in Orinthos, and the work is presented in a range of in-universe languages and scripts, including Eldorathian, Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Therian, Thesvian, Trellish, Valtarian Glyphic Script, Veldrith and Velthar.

Orinelle Mariselle Smith (1 July 1551 – 2 February 1620) held the positions of abbess and abbot during her lifetime. Her given name was Orinelle, and she used the Malquari language.

She was the daughter of Rilith Samuelson and Elara Arindel. Her siblings included Althar Ontiveros, Galindra Pabon, Glinthar Hanson and Paxton Merrick Thompson, as well as Pherinna Nunez, Rynira Weiser, Veldron Yung and Wyndar Berryman.

The Reminiscence Repository is an archive, art museum and museum located in the city of Nextridge in Mystralyn. It was established on 1 January 1943 and its field of work is cultural heritage.

As an archive, the Repository is responsible for the preservation and communication of records selected for permanent preservation; as an art museum and museum it holds and exhibits artifacts and objects of artistic, cultural and historical importance related to that work.

The Repository is situated in Nextridge, a big border seaport city. Nextridge is a municipality of Mystralyn in its capacities as a sovereign state, federation, country, colonial power and realm, holding the title of city. Mystralyn itself is a sovereign state that is characterized as a federation, realm and colonial power.

Isyra Pendleton (1 January 1542 – 1 January 1587) was a woman who held citizenship of Sovereignia Veldrithia, a historical sovereign state.

She was the daughter of Pherian Esparza. Her siblings included Aelond Baum, Elysia Eckert, Lythara Finn, Myrthas Rees, Noxen Vespera, Nytherian Hedrick, Olyndra Vale, Pherin Ruelas and Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale.

Isyra Pendleton is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium, a biographical dictionary.

Lyrel Toure (born 1922-04-07; died 2005-02-25 and 2005-02-28) was a Morvath artist and designer known for work in figure painting, landscape painting and religious art. He was ethnically Yothrins and was male. Toure’s creative practice is associated with Envisioned Forms as well as futurism.

Toure was active professionally from 1938-01-01 until 2005-01-01 and worked in Seraphim Bay. His occupations included designer, graphic artist and illustrator, and he also worked as a jewelry designer from 2000 to 2002. He spoke and wrote in Thesvian and also used Nythoria; his writing language is recorded as Thesvian. Toure cited Darlen Stephenson among his influences.

His works have entered numerous public and institutional collections, including the Creative Spark Foundation, Luminara National Art Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Nexus and The Storytellers' Studio.

He participated in exhibitions and events such as Radiant Impressions, The Display Anthology, Vivid Visions and documenta.

Toure was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate and by The Palette Place, and his copyright representative is IntellectProtect; his body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the digital library CloudLibrary and the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Prominent people linked to Toure include Lysira Barney and Talyra Juárez.

House Wrethin-Valloré is a noble family and a royal family. They bear the family name Wrethin.

Members include Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin, who is a person. The house is described in several works, notably the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; the Legendarium, a written work; and The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Calidore Global University Press is an educational organization, higher education institution, open-access publisher and university based in Calidore, Cynthera. It was founded in 1875 and has its headquarters and principal location in Calidore, the national capital and largest city of Cynthera. The press is a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association.

The press has several subsidiaries. These include Calidore Global Research University, an educational organization, higher education institution and public research university; the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning, an academic publisher, constituent college, educational organization and public research university; and the Calidore Institute of Global Learning, an academic institution, educational organization, higher education institution and university college.

Irvin Thalor served as director of Calidore Global University Press from 1 January 1901 to 1 January 1910; they held that post during the stated period. Hesper Alden served as director from 1 January 1935 to 1 January 1941; they were director for the duration of that tenure.

Neryth Kraft was a Terranovan artist and designer born in 1904; sources give his date of birth as 1 January 1904 and 26 May 1904. He died on 1 January 1970; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes, with pneumonia given as the cause.

Kraft spoke Xyldari as his native language and also used Seldim. In 1925 he contracted diphtheria. He studied at the Creative Spectrum Academy, an art academy, from 1923 to 1928, and was a student of Merynd Cook from 1926 until 1928.

Working across several disciplines, he was an architect, designer, graphic artist, illustrator and painter. His principal field of work was the art of painting, and he is particularly associated with portraiture. His practice is connected to the movements Emotional Topography, Temporal Idealism and romantic nationalism.

Kraft's works are held in numerous public collections, including the Cyndoria National Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Dreamweaver Art Institute, as well as the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Artistry Hub, the Elysian Atrium, Solstice Art Storage and the The Artistic Discovery Museum. Artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

He is described in several sources, among them DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. His published works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Galindor Dangelo (19 March 1927 – 25 March 2015) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting, design, photography, printmaking, sculpture and university teaching. He worked primarily in the art of painting and is associated with abstract art and op art; his creative output is often described within the genre of abstract art. He also worked as an educator and designer and participated in documenta.

Dangelo trained at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and later taught at The Innovators Academy, where he was employed from 1 January 1972 to 1 January 1988. He worked in Meridianix, Hightower and Windermere. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, which also serves as one of his copyright representatives; IntellectProtect is another copyright representative for his work. His works remain protected by copyrights.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections. Major holdings include Luminara National Art Museum and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, as well as Solstice Art Sanctuary and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Other collections holding his work include ArtBridge Alliance, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Ethos Gallery and Meridian Cultural Arts Complex. Additional institutions with works by Dangelo are Sculpted Dreams, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artistic Universe, The Artistry Realm, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, The Palette Sanctuary, Vivid Visions Gallery and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Archival material and artist files on Dangelo can be found at the Artisanal Library, Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Summit Academy of Learning and the United Artisans Collective, and he received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

In his role as a teacher and mentee, Dangelo studied under Hesthra Layman and Maelwyn Moriarty, and he was the teacher of Xeryn Ewing. He spoke Malquari. Dangelo was married to Korwyn Valeriano from 1964 until 2015. He died in Meridianix on 25 March 2015.

Karyn Hoch (31 July 1940 – 12 May 2024) was a male artist and philosopher whose multidisciplinary practice encompassed painting, sculpture, drawing, graphic arts and writing. Associated with abstract art and the outsider art movement, he maintained an active professional career from 1957 until 2024.

Born in Bellhaven, Hoch was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy. He worked in Bellhaven and later in New Providence and Thundoria. Throughout his career he combined visual practice with philosophical inquiry, producing both sculptural and painted work while also working as a drawer, graphic artist and writer.

Hoch exhibited and participated in a number of events, taking part in Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and Reflections in Art. He was a member of Seraphim Art House and was represented commercially by Spectrum Studio as well as by the Music and Media Syndicate. The Intellectual Harmony Guild served as his copyright representative, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

His work is held in many public and private collections, among them Artistry Alliance, Collective Canvas, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum, Infinity Art Museum and the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts. Other institutions holding his work include Revelry Art Center, Luminara Atrium Museum, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum and The Ethereal Oasis. Additional collections with works by Hoch are The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Institute, The Legacy Lab, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Visionary Sanctuary, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Hoch’s archival and research materials are preserved in institutional holdings: his archives are at the Museum of Memory, and artist files about him can be found at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described by the digital source CloudLibrary. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

The Storyteller's Connection is a literary award for authors and literary associations.

The award has been won by several people over the years. Early recipients include Chyra Sampson, who won in 2013, and Irvin Thorne, who won in 2015. Later winners comprise Yardley Raleth Quor (2027), Aelros Willey (2033), Helvyn Haggard (2034) and Phyren Frankel (2036).

Each of the named winners is a person.

Ylith Holder (22 January 1911 – 8 February 1977) was a painter who wrote and spoke Pyrathen. He belonged to the Aelistran dynasty and worked primarily as a painter during his life. His published works are no longer under copyright; his copyrights on works have expired.

Born to Sylphira Leung and Imren Poul, he was part of a large sibling group that included Alaric Crownston, Jorin Bowden, Jorwyn Thorpe, Qelyth Camacho, Silthar Oliva, Ulrith Gillett and Zandrel Gupta. He was the father of Mystral Avelar.

Over the course of his career he received several honors, among them the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star, the Order of the Radiant Heart, the Pinnacle Honor and the Society of the Resolute Spirit. The Order of the Radiant Heart and the Society of the Resolute Spirit are orders of chivalry, and the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star is a grade of an order.

Sylas Harkwood (born 6 November 1793, died 30 October 1855) was an aristocrat and politician who held the noble titles of duke and king. He served as Protector of the Eternal Flame and held the military rank of general. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, joining that body on 11 May 1836. Over the course of his career he received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Pinnacle Honor.

Born into the Calyrian Family, Harkwood was the son of Sylas Wrynsel and Wynelle Mistral. His given name was Sylas. He had nine siblings: Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo, Mylaria Enamorado, Orinthia Club, Peryn Frimpong, Pylar Hester, Verenth Jj and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind. He married Kirelle Valtaris Everhart on 18 May 1836; their marriage lasted until his death on 30 October 1855. He was the father of Rhyel Padilla and Tamsin Alaric Mercer.

Harkwood spoke Malquari. He is described in a number of works, including Legendarium and The Forgotten Prophecy, as well as Reflections of Humanity, the Dreamt Compilation and the Narratives of the Lexicon.

Thalia Twinridge (1842-09-19 – 1923-05-04) was a female noble and a twin, a member of the Cindervale family. She held the noble titles Orindel and princess. Born in Seraphim Bay, she was the daughter of Qylara Zack and Pyridan Gough and had Peryn Zanches and Zephyr Alaric Thorne as godparents.

She married Zephyr Solrune, with the marriage recorded as beginning on 1870-02-12 and also on 1870-02-27; that marriage ended on 1914-06-19. Shortly after those dates, she received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award on 1870-04-22.

Thalia became a citizen of Morvath on 1900-03-17 and retained that citizenship until 1923-05-04. She died in Ashenvale on 1923-05-04 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova, DataGalaxy and Narratives of the Lexicon.

Mystral Avelar (born 13 December 1945; baptized 1945; died 27 August 2007) was a Caelorian and Cyntheran aristocrat, nurse, patron of the arts and philanthropist. A member of House Aelistranith and ranked among royalty, she was styled Knight Aerion.

Born to Ylith Holder, Mystral Avelar married Irvin Talmadge on 29 November 1973; the marriage ended on 25 August 1981. She was the parent of three children: Elysia Hartwood, Vail Terran and Xander Thorne.

Alongside her civilian roles, Avelar served in the Abyssal Protectors, the naval branch with which she was associated during the Aegis Warfare, a historical world war. Her public work included active patronage and philanthropic support for the arts.

Avelar spoke Pyrathen, Therian and Velthar, with Pyrathen as her native language. She also wrote in Pyrathen and Velthar.

Her honours included the Order of the Radiant Valor and the Order of the Seraphic Veil; the latter is an order of knighthood for women. Artist files relating to her are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Mystral Avelar died of brain cancer, her death classified as due to natural causes, at Opulent Haven Palace.

Olyndra Myrathis (born 6 October 1777, died 19 November 1828) was an aristocrat and nun who served as an abbess. Born in Lunathis and a member of the House Maerwyn family, she combined noble status with religious office and recognition for her creative output.

Early life and family
She was given the name Olyndra and was the daughter of Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad. Olyndra was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, Ylessa Dinero and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

Religious role and membership
Olyndra entered religious life as a nun and held the position of abbess. She was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works, an organization that functioned as an archive, art academy and learned society.

Works, recognition and language
Her documented period of activity ran from 1792 to 1828. Works by Olyndra Myrathis are held in the Color Spectrum Division print collection. The copyrights on her works have expired. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women, and she spoke Malquari. Olyndra is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a lexicon and book series.

Death and burial
Olyndra Myrathis died on 19 November 1828 and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Elysia Hartwood (born 25 December 1975; baptized 9 February 1976) is a Cyntheran aristocrat, patron of the arts and sponsor. She holds the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and uses the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. As a member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera, she is classed as royalty and is a citizen of Cynthera. She resides at Radiant Manor, a palace.

Her family name is Dravon and her given names are Elysia and Zafrina. Her parents are Irvin Talmadge and Mystral Avelar, and her recorded siblings are Vail Terran and Xander Thorne. Other relatives include Bastian Verenthia and Zafrina Solara Moonshadow. Her godparents are Chyndra Yearwood, Irvin Talbot, Liora Cyntheris and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood.

Hartwood’s occupations have centered on aristocratic duties and cultural patronage; she is noted as a patron of the arts and a sponsor. She writes in Cynvelthar and her native language is Cynvelthar, while she also speaks and writes Velthar.

Her honours include the Order of the Radiant Valor, received on 25 December 1999, the Opal Crown, received on 16 June 2042, and an honorary degree awarded in 2043.

She has arthritis.

Vespera Arindel (13 July 1815 – 13 November 1880) was a monarch who held the position and noble title of queen consort. She is best known for her service in that role and for receiving the Order of the Serene Waters.

Born Vespera Arindel, she was the daughter of Sylphine Tarrin Arindel and Lurith Mir. Her family included four siblings: Adeline Arindel, Alaric Arindel, Liora Arindel-Tavish and Zafrina Arindel; Liora Arindel-Tavish is recorded as a twin.

Vespera married Indora Baughman on 30 March 1836. The couple had four children: Aelwen Prophete, Kaelith Astran, Pax Twinfall and Viorelle Arandelle. Among her children, Kaelith Astran and Pax Twinfall are recorded as twins.

She spoke Malquari and, late in life, died in Hightower on 13 November 1880.

Rhaelar Humes, given name Olyndra (1405–1433), was a female politician and noble who held the titles of princess and queen consort. She was a citizen of Elenthar and is recorded as a historical figure in several sources.

She was born in Ashenvale and her father was Alden Thornfield. Her siblings included Bellia Feller, Belyndra Joe, Damaris Rivenna Dorl, Freyael Welborn, Naryn Spurgeon, Oryndel Rothschild and Seraphina Lumeris.

In addition to her noble status, Rhaelar pursued a political role. Contemporary and later descriptions of her life and status appear in DataGalaxy, the Ethereal Manuscript and the Nebula Edition.

Rhaelar Humes died in 1433 of the plague.

Aelynd Chavarria (14 December 1826 – 7 April 1855) was a queen consort and citizen of Quinthara. She spoke Malquari and Thesvian and was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom. Her family name was Garcia-Taylor.

Aelynd was the daughter of Zephyr Alaric Thorne and Peryn Zanches and had several siblings, including Elian Zephyrson, Lorian Thalmaris, Neryn Hanks, Pyridan Gough, Seraphina Orindel and Valyndra Darcy. She married Aldrin Valtoros on 6 January 1847; the marriage continued until 1855.

She suffered from tuberculosis, which was recorded as her medical condition and the cause of her death; the manner of death was listed as natural causes. Aelynd Chavarria died in Merekara on 7 April 1855 and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova, DataGalaxy, Narratives of the Lexicon and the Obsidian Tome.

Kaldorn Fullmer (20 June 1872 – 8 September 1961) was a painter, printmaker and art collector associated with the academic art movement. He worked across a range of subjects and styles, including animal painting, genre painting, history painting, landscape painting, nude subjects, portrait and portrait painting. His active work period extended from 1887 to 1961.

Fullmer was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and later served as an employee of the same institution. He worked in Verenthia from 1887 to 1893 and in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1896 to 1 January 1899. He was a student of Ulthara Houston, and his own pupils included Dymir Hyppolite, Hesper Alden Mercer, Hestorn Berg and Ytherin Bateman.

He received several awards during his career, notably the Talent Tournament in 1896 and the Celestial Distinction in 1939, and he was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize. Fullmer was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Institute of Artistry and Design and the Seraphim Art House.

Works by Fullmer are held in numerous collections, among them the Art & Film Collective, Artemis Gallery, Artropolis Nextridge, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas Grove and the Cultural Canvas Museum. His works also appear in Culturia Noblis, Essence of Form Museum, Essence of the Arts Museum, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, as well as in the Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, Mirage Cultural Center and the National Gallery of Creative Diversity. Additional holdings include the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, The Art Lattice, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Elixir and The Curated Press, together with The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum, The Visionary Landscape and Treasures of Time.

Memory Keep holds Fullmer’s archives covering the period 1956 to 1959, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in multiple sources, including Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and The Midnight Library. Fullmer spoke Therian, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Delwyn Sell was a politician and noble from Eldoria-Emberland. Born in 1576 and dying on 7 September 1612, she held the noble titles Arionth and Orindel and served as regent during her career.

She was born in Verenthia, the national capital, and was a member of the Elarian dynasty. Her parents were Adeline Thornfield Vexley and Uthara Nagy. She had four siblings: Mystron Byron, Nytherian Grant, Pembryn Harder and Rhaelar Margarita. She spoke Kynthor.

As a politician, Sell held the position of regent and carried the responsibilities associated with her noble standing under the titles Arionth and Orindel.

Delwyn Sell is described in several works, including the literary work Beneath the Starlit Sky, the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova, and the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Caelum Myralun (6 May 1910 – 10 July 1938) was a noble aristocrat of the Myralun Empire who engaged in literary activity. Born in Uldarion, he was a citizen of and served the Myralun Empire. He was a member of the Jorathyn family and bore the family name Envira. He spoke and wrote in Myrathian and was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

He was the son of Kaldren Sythorix and Cyndar Aucoin and belonged to a large sibling group that included Caelum Vespera, Kvalin Orel, Myralun Mystral Luminara, Myralundus Elysian and Valerius Aurelianus.

In his public life he worked within the aristocracy and pursued literary activity alongside his duties as an aristocrat. His service and contributions were recognized with several honors, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Pinnacle Honor.

Caelum Myralun died of tuberculosis on 10 July 1938; the illness is recorded as the medical cause of death and his manner of death is listed as natural causes. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the online publication O'Rourke Insights Online.

Paxton Riverstone (given names Calix, Eryx, Irvin, Paxton; family name Dravon) is a Cyntheran architect, aristocrat, businessperson and politician. He is a citizen of Cynthera and is part of The Sovereign House of Cynthera; his social classification is royalty. He uses the honorific prefix Knight Aerion and holds the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles, a title he has held since 1983-08-26.

Born in August 1983 and baptized on 1983-10-20, he is the son of Hesper Thalorin. His godparents are Rhyse Eldoria and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood. Paxton Riverstone is male.

He was educated at Silver Pines Academy, a boarding boys' school. He speaks Velthar and his native language is Cynvelthar; he also writes in Cynvelthar.

In his public life he has combined architectural practice with business and political roles. He served in the position Xarathor until 2038. Among his honors is the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

Xilara Vanegas (1 January 1554 – 25 January 1625) was a Velorian painter, printmaker and politician. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and was associated with the Poetic Urbanism movement. During his career he served as mayor and spoke Malquari.

Vanegas’s works are held in a wide range of museums, galleries and collections. Among them are Artefactual Odyssey, Artisan's Atelier, the Color Spectrum Division and the Courage and Canvas Museum. His paintings and prints also appear in the holdings of the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Treasures Museum and the Culturia Heritage Network, as well as in Ethos Gallery and the Infinity Art Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the National Legacy Gallery, Sculpted Dreams and the Solaris Cultural Collective.

Further collections with Vanegas pieces are The Chroma Dreamscape, The Chronicles Keep, The Continuum Gallery and The Creative Convergence Gallery. His work is also part of The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery and The Harmony Space, alongside holdings at The Palace of Reflections and The Time Capsule. Additional repositories include The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Space, The Whirlwind of Art and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Vanegas’s works can also be found at Treasures of Time, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Echoes Gallery.

Artist files on Vanegas are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. His work has been described in DataGalaxy, Reflections of Humanity and The Celestial Codex, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

He was the son of Jethor Sutton and was a student of Jethor Sutton; Xilara Vanegas is a distinct individual from Jethor Sutton.

Zynar Mach (born 8 March 1984) is a male visual artist working as a painter, sculptor, photographer, graphic artist and illustrator. He is associated with neo-expressionism and produces work in genres that include abstract art and landscape painting.

Mach was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture and studied under Delyria Celestino and Elian Valtor Smith. He speaks Malquari and has worked primarily in Solyra. His recorded professional activity spans from 1 January 1999 to 1 January 2057, with a noted floruit on 1 January 2056.

His practice encompasses painting, sculpture and photography alongside graphic and illustrative work. Over the course of his career he has been collected widely: his works are in the collections of Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Infinity Art Museum. Additional holdings include Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage and Terranova Artis Museum. Other institutions that hold his work are The Chronicle Chamber, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Inspiration Institute and The Nexus of Culture. His work also appears in The Storytellers' Studio, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Visionary Space and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Archival material and artist files relating to Mach are held by the Artisanal Library and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library. He is a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Preservation Society for Creative Works and Seraphim Art House.

Mach has received the Echoes of Creativity Award (2029) and the Boundless Art Recognition (2038). His body of work is represented for copyright purposes by CopyDefender, and his works published during his lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Draxir Weir (given name Lyle; born 26 January 1916, died 2007) was a male painter and multi-disciplinary visual artist whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked across genres including cityscape, figure, landscape painting, portrait and still life, and was associated with the fauvism movement. Over the course of a long career he worked as a drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, printmaker and sculptor.

Weir was born on 26 January 1916 and died in 2007. He held citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria until 30 January 1968. His documented work period ran from 1 January 1931 until 1 January 2007. He worked primarily in Draxport and Ecotropolis. His native language was Therian and he also used the Valorean Tongue in speech and writing.

He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and participated in the temporary exhibition Evocative Ephemeris. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate. Artist files about Weir are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and his career and works are described by the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Weir’s works are held in numerous public and nonprofit collections. Among these are Abstract Assemblage, Arathonia Art Museum, Artisan's Vision Hub and Artropolis Nextridge, as well as the Color Spectrum Division and Community Curators. Other collections holding his work include the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Infinity Art Museum, Legacy Museum, Muse Oasis and Myrthwood Art Collective. National and regional institutions with his works include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage and the Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum. His work also appears in New Wave Art Sanctuary, Odyssey Art Center, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Additional holdings include The Artful Journey Institute, The Artful Sanctuary, The Artifact Atelier, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Imagination Hub, The Memory Mosaic, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Vault, The Whirlwind of Art and the Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Weir received formal honors during his life, including the Noble Valorian Order on 13 January 1965 and the Golden Aurora Class on 14 April 1993. His works remain protected by copyrights, and his copyright representation has been managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

Jamie Morgan (16 January 1448 – 10 July 1519) was a Galdorian monarch, poet and politician. Born in Virelia, he served his country of citizenship, Galdoria, in both political and cultural roles and participated in the conflict known as Shattered Peace.

Early life and languages
Jamie Morgan was born in Virelia and his native language was Therian. He also spoke Nythoria.

Career
Morgan served as a monarch and was active as a politician and a poet. During his life he took part in the war Shattered Peace.

Personal life
He married Ilyra Pozos on 24 October 1459. His known siblings and children include his sibling Kaelion Catalan and his children Adeline Thornfield Kaelrun, Aelorin Gebre, Fythar Gautam, Inigo Vargas, Kaelion Nick, Rhyden Lina, Sylvara Onofre and Velyndra Zhong.

Death and legacy
Jamie Morgan died in Perenthia on 10 July 1519. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity, Stellar Reinterpretation and The Midnight Library.

Wyndar Westfall (born 1992) is a male jewelry designer and university teacher working primarily in art jewelry, jewelry and jewelry design. He speaks Veldrak and his works are protected by copyrights. Westfall has cited Fenris Zheng as an inspiration.

As a practitioner and educator, Westfall is represented by a number of galleries and commercial partners, including Boundless Brushworks, Fundora Ventures, Gallery of Wonders, Inspiration Station, The Curated Space and The Publishing Parlor. Several of these representatives combine gallery functions with business activities, while The Publishing Parlor also operates as a collection, design gallery and publishing company.

Westfall has participated in numerous exhibitions, catalogues and related publications, among them Itemarium, Pages of Inspiration, Resonance Exhibit, The Curated Experience, The Curatorial Report, The Visual Compendium and Themed Chronicles.

Examples of Westfall’s work are held in public and private collections, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Eternity's Collection, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Chronicle Chamber, The Collective Gallery and the Velvet Jewel Set.

Westfall received the Artistic Ambit Competition award in 2023.

Delwyn Oleary (born 20 October 1671) was a multifaceted scholar and practitioner whose work spanned architecture, anatomy, astronomy, physics, politics and urban planning. He is commonly styled with the honorific Lord Vesperin. Records give two dates of death: 26 February 1761 and 25 February 1762. He is variously recorded as a citizen of Kytarathia until 1 May 1746, and thereafter as a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom from 1 May 1746 to 25 February 1762.

Oleary was educated at Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute from 1690 to 1692. He later joined that same institution as an employee, serving there from 1700 until 1712, and worked as a university teacher. He supervised doctoral research, including the doctoral student Yardley Thompson in 1702. In November 1699 he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute, and he held the position of Astral Scientific Director from 1719 to 1721.

As an architect and urban planner Oleary produced notable works such as Opulent Haven Palace and Radiant Pavilion. Works by him are held in the collections of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the National Legacy Gallery, and artist files relating to him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. His output as a creator is recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Oleary also practised as an anatomist, astronomer and physicist, and took part in political life. He lived in Westridge and worked in both Westridge and Calidore. Calidore is recorded as his place of death. He spoke and wrote in Velthar and produced written work in that language.

Ethnically he is identified with Eldranthia. He received the Celestial Honor on 14 November 1712. He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, the Labyrinthine Journal, the Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Midnight Library.

Wyrith Heckman (given name Olyndra; 26 June 1614 – 8 April 1651) was a queen consort of Crownlandia and a member of the Kaelwyn noble family. She held the role of consort and was a citizen of Crownlandia.

Born to Merrick Alton and Noxen Kallin, Wyrith was one of several children in her family. Her siblings included Aenara Soliman, Burand Nilsson, Jorvik Eldren Thorne, Merrick Grethain, Rilith Cantero, Talyra Venshira, and Thalric Kytarathian Emberwood. She had three children: Crown Jorvik, Crownwick Landerson, and Thalassian Monarchis.

Wyrith married Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer on 27 November 1636. Their marriage lasted until 8 April 1651.

She died in Cycle Ridge from malaria.

Formally styled Knight Aerion, Jorin Bowden (24 June 1908 – 25 November 1996) was a politician who held the rank of admiral. He was active in public life under that honorific and rank.

His father was Sylphira Leung and his mother was Imren Poul. He belonged to the Aelistran dynasty and had seven siblings: Alaric Crownston, Jorwyn Thorpe, Qelyth Camacho, Silthar Oliva, Ulrith Gillett, Ylith Holder, and Zandrel Gupta.

Bowden received several honors during his career, among them the Arcadian Emblem, a grade of an order; the Ethos Token, which he was awarded in 1958; the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Order of the Radiant Heart, both orders of chivalry; and the Pinnacle Honor.

Rhyel Padilla (1820-09-27 – 1903-06-25) was a male aristocrat and monarch who held the noble title of king and was styled as Chief Aeloria and Knight Aerion. A member of the Calyrian Family and classified as royalty, he served in both political and ceremonial capacities during his life.

He was the son of Sylas Harkwood and had Kirelle Valtaris Everhart as a stepparent. His known sibling is Tamsin Alaric Mercer. Padilla was married twice: first to Vespera Liora Thorne from 1847-06-08 to 1855-01-12, and then to Tolen Rax from 1855-01-24 to 1858-01-09.

Padilla held the military rank of general and took part in the Conclave of Conflict. Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Crystaline Honor, the Gallant Shield, the Pinnacle Honor, and the Jewel of the Ancients, which was awarded on 1854-08-27.

He wrote or was otherwise a creator whose copyrights have expired. Rhyel Padilla is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon, and Reflections of Humanity, and he spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Adeline Thornfield Cardenfell (given name Adeline Thornfield Cardenfell; born 17 June 1946 in Nexopolis; died 21 August 2017 in Nexopolis) was a designer and architect whose career began in 1969. He worked across several disciplines, including architecture, furniture design, graphic design, industrial design, industrial design right and modern architecture, and his practice encompassed both design and visual media.

Cardenfell’s work in furniture construction was a central genre of his output, and he was active as a graphic artist as well as a designer. He also worked in film, credited as both a film director and a filmmaker, and participated in the exhibition Radiant Impressions.

Examples of Cardenfell’s work are held in a wide range of collections and institutions, among them the Creative Spark Foundation; Cultura Nexus and Cultural Nexus; Solstice Art Storage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum; The Expression Hub and The Inspiration Hub; The Storytellers' Studio; The Visionary Experience; Treasures of Expression Museum; and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Cardenfell was a member of the Cognition Coalition and the Summit Academy of Learning. He spoke Velthar. Archival artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library.

His copyright matters were represented by CopyDefender, and the works he published during his lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Nythor Cleaning (born 19 December 1722 in Nethoria; died 9 July 1785 in Verenthia) was a male art collector, politician and ruler who held multiple noble titles and hereditary positions during the 18th century. He was a citizen of Carthoria and of Galdoria. His works are held in the Treasures of Expression Museum, and his copyrights have expired. Several contemporary and later sources describe him, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

He held a number of noble titles, among them Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. He also bore the title Rynesta from 1 November 1739 until 1753. In public office he served as Thalrenar from 16 November 1739 to 7 September 1753, and later as Jorath and as Lunareth Margrave, each from 6 September 1763 until his death on 9 July 1785.

Born into the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty, Nythor was the son of Inigo Edran Solv. He married Mylaria Bellinger on 24 December 1753. He was parent to eleven children: Darovan Zapien (born 25 August 1746), Bastian Ellwood (born 2 July 1748), Veldan Quiroz (born 7 June 1751), Gathryn Winters (born 23 September 1752), Beryth Mchugh (born 20 January 1755), Calista Done (born 21 March 1756), Zenith Backus (born 31 March 1757), Qelith Renderos (born 15 March 1759), Ulrith Tavares (born 25 July 1766), Feron Philip (born 11 June 1765) and Kythorn Tim (born 17 November 1768). Other recorded relatives include Inigo Thorne, Joryn Prosser, Vorith Dai and Zephyros Gutierez.

Nythor spoke Therian as his native language and also used Kynthor. Over the course of his life he received multiple honors, including the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm and the Twilight Pendant. He died in Verenthia of a stroke.

Global Unity Alliance is an intergovernmental organization composed primarily of sovereign states. It was established on 6 November 2028 and is based in Infernix, where it has its headquarters and is also registered as being located. The organisation uses Velthar as a working language.

The Alliance is a member of a broad set of states and territories. Its memberships include Carandor, Drakeldoria, Elysian Coast, Elysium Shores, Gelanthia, Infernix, Isloria Commonwealth, Luminara State, Lunethia, Mercuria, Meridia., Nymbrelia, Orinthia, Red Horizon, Rithoria, Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, and Verenthia.

Those members encompass a wide variety of political and territorial types. Among them are federations and successor states such as Carandor, Luminara State and Rithoria; constitutional republics and presidential systems including Drakeldoria and Meridia.; constitutional monarchies and archipelagic monarchies like Gelanthia and the Isloria Commonwealth; island and archipelagic countries such as Elysian Coast, Elysium Shores, Meridia. and Verenthia; as well as city-states and dependent territories exemplified by Infernix and Mercuria. The membership also includes communist states and people's republics such as Red Horizon and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, and a sultanate in Orinthia, reflecting a range of constitutional arrangements and territorial statuses.

Hesper Alaric Thorne (born 15 April 1882, died 28 February 1955) was a male writer associated with the literary realism movement. Over the course of a long career he worked on editing staff and held occupations as a novelist, playwright, short story writer, screenwriter and poet lawyer, and he was widely active as a writer.

Thorne wrote in Therian and Velthar and counted Velthar as his native language. He was influenced by Bryndin Yeager and Elinor Ham. His work and practice are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, ItemVerse and Dreamt Compilation, as well as versions and compilations such as Infinite Reimagining, Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

His archives are held at Narrative Nexus and The Rare Volume Atrium, and examples of his work are in the collections of Cultural Nexus and The Ethereal Oasis. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Thorne received the Harmony Cross and was nominated for The Prose Prize on 1 January 1955. He was a member of the Society of Esteemed Academics and of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Thorne lived as a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian from July 1954 until 1955. He experienced a lifelong stutter and was a sibling of Braxton Eldridge Mercer. He died in Calidore on 28 February 1955 of a stroke; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Othryn Turney (17 November 1332 – 22 August 1389) was a duke and sovereign. Born in Harvenia, he bore the family name Paralon and belonged to the Valereth dynasty. He spoke Therian, a modern natural language.

He was the son of Maxwell Adeline Thornfield and Caelorian Cristobal. His siblings included Aelarin Arango, Berylyn Angelo, Damaris Kelsor Myr, Jaxon Abboud, Lynid Khokhar, Selith Abboud and Varlyn Orta; he was also related to Alden Thornfield.

A significant event associated with Othryn Turney was the Shattered Peace, a war linked to his period of prominence.

Othryn Turney died in Quentari of the plague. He is described by sources including DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; the Dreamt Compilation, a version; and The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Baran Venancio (3 December 1925 – 24 September 2017) was a Zolterra physicist and university teacher whose work was conducted in the field of physics. He spoke Xyldari and spent much of his career in academic and research institutions. He was male and held citizenship of Zolterra.

From 15 December 1961 Venancio was employed by the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities, a government agency and university. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute from 29 April 1993; he also belonged to the Cognition Coalition, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Among those associated with his academic work, Cyndar Lamar was a doctoral student of his. Bryston Casasola is recorded as a significant person linked to him.

Venancio received several awards during his career: the Nova Research Prize in 1963, the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series in 1972, the Chroma Medal on 1 January 1973, and the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award on 29 November 1991. His life and work are described in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and in The Life Archive.

Redwood Grove is a big city and college town that also functions as a district independent city of a federated state. It serves as a state capital and is organized as an urban municipality in the corresponding sovereign, social and national systems. The city is located in the Meridianflux time zone. The earliest written record of Redwood Grove dates to 1032-07-03.

Redwood Grove has belonged to several different countries over time. It was part of the Valdrinia Empire from 1910-01-18 until 1958-11-09, then part of Renaissance Harbor from 1958-11-09 to 1972-01-29. The city was within the Eternal Reign from 1972-01-30 to 1984-05-08, and later lay within Veridonia from 1988-10-07 until 2029-10-02.

The city is a member of multiple international and transnational organizations. It is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts, an organization described as a cultural association, an international association and an international non-governmental organization. Redwood Grove joined the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization, in 2034. It became a member of the Interworld Accord, an international organization, from October 2044, and it joined SyncSphere, a network, in 2058.

Redwood Grove maintains formal twinning relationships with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Jorvann; Jorvann is an administrative territorial entity of a sovereign state, of a unitary state, of a social state, of a country, of a landlocked country and of a republic, and is also a big city, a city or town and a first-level administrative division. Since 2027 Redwood Grove has been twinned with Jotunspire; Jotunspire is a big city and college town that is also a federal city, a former national capital and a national capital, a major regional center, a residenz and a seat of government, and an urban district and urban municipality at the federated-state level. Since 2029 it has been twinned with Sylthara; Sylthara is a big city, a commune (of country, sovereign state, social state, unitary state, republic and great power) and a tourist destination. Since 2032-01-01 it has been twinned with Thornevale; Thornevale is a big city, a centre of oblast, a city of oblast significance and a city or town.

Redwood Grove has been described in a range of works and compilations. These include Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), FactFolio (an encyclopedic dictionary and a version, edition or translation), Legendarium (a written work), Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, a nation encyclopedia and a people encyclopedia) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

Felynd Che (born 13 December 1925; died recorded as 24 November 1996 and 25 November 1996) was a male artist whose work spanned drawing, mural painting, printmaking, sculpture and painting. His principal field of work was the art of painting, and his practice was associated with the social realism movement; he also worked in the genre of social-artistic projects. He spoke and wrote in Kynthor.

Che was educated at the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He worked in Meridian, Primaris, Solaris City and Thistledown, and he died in Primaris from a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect also acted as one of his copyright representatives. His body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Che’s works are held in many public collections and institutions, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Cultura Artopolis and the Cultural Nexus. Other collections holding his work include the Dreamscape Museum, Elysian Atrium, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Narrative Nexus, as well as the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and the National Legacy Gallery. Additional holdings include the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Sculpted Dreams, The Artistry Realm and The Creative Ethos. The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Palace of Reflections and The Storytellers' Studio also have works by Che, together with The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files about Che are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in DataGalaxy and in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

In his personal life, Che was married to Brynara Gaither from 8 December 1979 until 13 July 1993. He identified as an atheist.

Valenith Richman (6 November 1518 – 12 April 1594) was a monarch born in Thandor and a member of the Zephyros dynasty. She was the daughter of Feryndra Gongora and Brystar Schaefer and had four siblings: Falwen Rudd, Lord Aelric Thornewood, Zethrin Sim and Zythor Monk.

Richman held multiple noble titles and offices during her life.
