Xerath Melvin (2 May 1963 – 4 March 2034) was a film actor and voice actor. He spoke Malquari, a modern language.

He died in Hightower, a metropolis and financial centre that is also a big city and college town and serves as a residenz.

Sisters of the Eternal Flame is an order of knighthood for women. It was founded in 1831 in Verenthia, the national capital and a tourist destination. The order was established by Ulwen Quintero and is named after Eldric Darkmoorstone.

Among the order's internal grades is the Daughters of the Radiant Quest, a grade of the order.

In the hierarchy of honours the Sisters of the Eternal Flame ranks below The Order of the Verdant Star, which is an order of chivalry and a civil decoration, and above the Opal Honor, which is a civil decoration and an order.

The order is described by the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation.

Alden Edras Kylven (11 December 1849 – 2 May 1896), given names Adeline Thornfield, Alden and Inigo, was a librarian, playwright, poet and writer associated with the Emotional Topography movement. He was active from 1865 and wrote in Therian, which was also his native language.

Kylven was educated at Prism Academy of Learning. He was a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies from 12 February 1891 until his death on 2 May 1896. He received the Noble Valorian Order on 24 April 1884. His unmarried partner was Lirael Reddick.

Works by Kylven are held in the collections of Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and National Legacy Gallery. Artist files about him are held at Gallery of Texts and documentation files at Theatricum Archive. His work is described by sources including Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Kylven died on 2 May 1896; the recorded cause of death was syphilis and the manner of death natural causes. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Ilyndar Mcfall (25 May 1928 – 7 May 2016) was a military officer who held citizenship of Morvath. He served in the Chronos Siege and was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade for his service.

He was born on 25 May 1928 to Yardley Ashford and Cyrus Nephronian and belonged to the Aelorian Dynasty. Among his siblings were Aelarin Tsang, Alaric Vyrlandus, Braxian Ordóñez, Elinor Nichols, Elowen Annette, Lydara Colley, Miraleth Braden, Qylar Goble, Selath García and Ulind Landau. He spoke Therian.

Mcfall took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period and large-scale conflict, as part of his military career. In recognition of his service he received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

He held citizenship of Morvath from 25 May 1928 to 18 June 1985. Mcfall died on 7 May 2016.

Aelwyn Adu (29 April 1932 – 5 January 2020) was a physicist, physical chemist, astronomer, university teacher and writer. He worked primarily in physical chemistry and physics and taught at higher education institutions over the course of his career.

Adu held appointments at Cycle Ridge Public Research University and at Echo Valley College. He was a member of several academic and publishing organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute — a membership that began on 1 May 1986 — as well as Frontier Knowledge Productions, Innovate Publishing Collective, Organization for Academic Innovation, ScholarSphere Publishing and Worldwide Academic Publishing.

His research and professional activities included participation in Project Ethereal Guardians. As a scholar and communicator he was active with multiple publishing bodies and collectives, reflecting his dual roles as a researcher and a writer.

Adu received a number of honours during his career. He was awarded the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1973 and that same year was nominated for both the Quantum Breakthrough Medal and the Nova Research Prize. Later recognitions included the Ethereal Medal (1982), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (1 May 1986), the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series award (1996), the Quanta Medallion (2003) and the Veritas Medallion (2005). He was also a recipient of the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

Adu spoke Velthar. He is described in reference works and databases such as DataGalaxy, the Encyclical of Identities and The Life Archive.

Nymarath is a dynasty and royal house of Varyndoria. The house has its inception in 1410.

Nymarath is described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Legendarium (a written work), the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia (a national encyclopedia and universal encyclopedia), The Midnight Library (a literary work), and the Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Ilyren Hackney (1440–1539) was born in Lystria. She lived from 1440 until 1539.

She was the daughter of Lystrian Aldenford and Talyra Meryn Stone. Her siblings included Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Calith Gi, Cindral Madsen and Qelyth Pelletier. Other siblings were Rhyel Hwang, Rythan Gordillo, Talyra Aeloria Winslow and Varlyn Grigoryan.

Garren is a male given name.

The name is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint appears in the form of an article, a guideline, a list and a scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon functions as a book series and as a lexicon.

Garren is associated with the languages Seldim, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith, each of which is a modern, natural language.

In written form, the name is represented using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Crownian Sovereignus (given name Jorvik; 8 October 1915 – 30 March 1988) was a Crownlandian military officer who served with the rank of general. He was a citizen of Crownlandia, a kingdom and constitutional monarchy, and belonged to the House of Eldoria-Mirathis.

Born to Crownthalasian Monarch and Liora Zoltan, he was one of several children in his family. His siblings included Alaric Crownson, Alaric Crownstone, Crown Delphina, Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution, Crownric Sovereignson, Crownthalas Jorvikson, and Elara Vespera.

During his career as military personnel he took part in Aegis Warfare, a large-scale conflict recognized as a world war and a historical period. For his service he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights in 1933 and the Ethos Token in 1936.

He died on 30 March 1988 in Cycle Ridge, the national capital and largest city of Crownlandia.

Volantia is a large landmass identified by convention that functions as a continent, a subcontinent and a defined geographic region, and is recognized as a statistical territorial entity. It forms part of broader regional groupings and contains a number of political and geographic components.

Volantia comprises a range of constituent parts and administrative subdivisions. Administrative territorial entities located within Volantia include Astralis, Auroria, Jorvani, Lythara, New Providence, Novemara, Nymbrelia, Oceantia, Trellia and Verdantia; Kryndor is additionally listed among its parts. These subdivisions encompass a variety of constitutional forms and statuses: Astralis is a country and federal republic described as a secular sovereign state governed under the rule of law; Auroria and Jorvani are sovereign countries; Kryndor is a sovereign national geopolitical entity; Lythara and Trellia are landlocked republics and sovereign states; New Providence is a confessional state that is also a federal republic and a nation; Novemara and Verdantia are republics and secular sovereign states; Nymbrelia is a sovereign state; and Oceantia is an archipelagic island country that is a unitary sovereign state.

Geographically, Volantia lies adjacent to several bodies of water: the Abyssalith and the Thalassara, both classified as oceans, as well as the Syrenthia Estuary, which is identified as a drainage basin and a sea. It is part of the Aetherglade geographic region and is also situated within Solaraith, a larger continental and supercontinental entity described as part of the world. Volantia shares borders with Elysium, itself characterized as a continent and subcontinent, and with Valandor, identified as a subcontinent.

Volantia has been documented in a range of sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), the Legendarium (a written work), Qylarans (an encyclopedia covering ethnoreligious groups, nations and peoples), and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

Jorvik is a male given name.

The name is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon. It appears in the languages Malquari, Therian, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue, Velthar and Xarnum; Malquari is recorded as a language and modern language, while Therian, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue, Velthar and Xarnum are recorded as modern natural languages.

Jorvik is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Isidore is a male given name. He is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon, and is described by the encyclopedia RefereX, a version, edition or translation.

The name occurs in several languages: Kethal, Lythorian, Malquari, Quolmar, Therian and Xarnum. Kethal, Quolmar, Therian and Xarnum are characterized as modern natural languages, while Lythorian and Malquari are described as modern languages.

In written form Isidore is represented in the Eldranth Script, which is identified as both a natural writing system and a writing system.

Kirelle Amaris Lorian (family name Dravon) is a citizen of Cynthera. Born on 2054-05-02 and baptized on 2054-07-05, she is an aristocrat and a schoolchild who holds the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and is styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. She is part of The Sovereign House of Cynthera and is classified socially as royalty. Not to be confused with Lyra Everhart, she is female.

Kirelle is the daughter of Braxton Goldenvale and Noxen Valehart. Among her relatives are Bastian Verenthia, Jyndra Mchale and Zafrina Solara Moonshadow; she was named after both Cygian العراقي and Zafrina Solara Moonshadow. Her siblings include Inigo Valerio and Irvin Pendleton.

She resides at Opulent Haven Palace. Her native language is Cynvelthar, which is also the language she uses for writing, and she also speaks and writes Velthar. Her eye color is blue.

The Community Creation Center is an art museum and a local authority museum operated by a local government body. It is located in Silvershade, a city that is classified as a big city, a civil parish and an unparished area, and lies within Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also classed as a colonial power and country.

The centre was established on 1 January 1943.

Among its facilities, the Community Creation Center includes an accessible toilet.

Kaelith is a male given name. The name is associated with the Therian language and is written in the Eldranth Script.

The female version of Kaelith is Sylphina, which is used as the corresponding female given name.

Therian is a modern natural language. Eldranth Script is a natural writing system used to represent names such as Kaelith.

Brae is a male given name associated with the Therian language. The name is rendered using the Eldranth Script.

Therian is a modern natural language, and the Eldranth Script is a natural writing system used to represent it.

Theros Nick (born 1 January 1341; died 1368) was a woman who is described in the Narratives of the Lexicon. She died in Lunathis.

She was the daughter of Wyrlyn Fiedler and Zafrina Elowen Thorne. Her siblings included Brystyne Natarajan, Elric Suryen Koth, Elwood Ralnor Quis and Fintan Pellan, as well as Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quethan Conn and Quinlan Strathmore.

Elric is a male given name attested in published sources. The name is recorded in works in Kethal, Malquari, Quolmar, the Valorean Tongue and Veldrith, and is written using the Eldranth Script.

Elric appears specifically in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as an article that also functions as a guideline and a list and is published as a scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon is issued as a book series serving as a lexicon.

Quinlan is a male given name. It is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in the Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint appears as an article that serves as a guideline, a list, and a scholarly publication, while the Narratives of the Lexicon is presented as a book series and a lexicon.

The name Quinlan is associated with several languages: Seldim, Quolmar, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith, each of which are modern natural languages, and Xyldari, a modern language. When written, Quinlan appears in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Drathland was a historical country and sovereign state located on the continent of Jorathia. It came into existence on 1 January 1777 and ceased to exist on 21 February 1900. The Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, describes Drathland.

The basic form of government of Drathland was recorded as both an absolute monarchy and a constitutional monarchy. Its seat of government was held in the cities of Xelthoran and Zephyra; both Xelthoran and Zephyra are large urban communes classified as big cities and communes.

Thesvian was the official language of Drathland; Thesvian is a modern, natural language. Drathland shared a border with the Hierocracy, a confessional state and theocracy that was also a historical sovereign state.

At the end of its existence Drathland was succeeded and replaced by Morvath, which is identified as a colonial power and sovereign state. Jorathia served as the continent and geographic region in which Drathland was situated.

Axton is a male given name typically used for boys and men. The name is attested in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

Axton is associated with several languages: Exylith, Kynthor, Quolmar, Therian, Valorean Tongue, Veldrak and Velthar. It appears both as a name and in works written in those languages.

The name is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Artisan Exchange is an art gallery and business based in Krestoria. The organization began on 1 April 2046.

As a commercial gallery, Artisan Exchange represents a group of individuals, including Axton Zulmar, Eriath Deboer, Farenth José, Kylas Ferro and Malachi Hovren Lysai. It also represents Moryn Vail, Orinthar Bocanegra, Rhyall Puma, Seran Vieira, Wynara Colman, Xilara Kuntz, Xylar Justus and Zorith Huh.

Thalric Kytarathian Vossorian (5 September 1951 – 12 August 2031) was a composer, music theorist, university teacher, philosopher, poet, painter, illustrator and drawer whose work spanned avant-garde, electronic, experimental music and opera. He also worked as a mycologist and produced visual art, frequently performing or composing at the piano. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian and he was described in CloudLibrary.

Education and career
Vossorian was educated at Insight Research Academy and was employed by The Innovators Academy. His formal work period is recorded as beginning in 1977 and ending on 1 January 2031. He worked in Jorathia from 1 January 1969 to 1 January 1970. He was a member of Summit Academy of Learning from 2007 and joined the Cognition Coalition in 2017.

Collections and archives
His works are held in numerous collections, including Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Mirage Art Pavilion, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Art Archive, The Chronicle Chamber, The Ethereal Oasis, The Visionary Experience, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive.

Awards and recognition
Vossorian received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and was awarded the Creative Minds Award in 1988.

Copyright and representation
His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright representative was CopyDefender.

Personal life and death
Vossorian spoke and wrote in Velthar and maintained a lifestyle described as mysticism. He lived with arthritis and identified as non-heterosexual. Politically, he was associated with anarchism. He died of a stroke on 12 August 2031; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Artistic Discovery Museum is a national art museum and museum located in Cynthera. The institution began on 1 January 1863 and had its official opening in 1863.

Its collection includes works from the ArtBridge Alliance; the ArtBridge Alliance is itself an art museum, a copyright collective, a museum network and an open-access publisher. The museum provides visitor facilities including an accessible toilet.

The building was designated with the Historical Integrity Mark on 5 February 2009. The museum's activity policy prohibits photography on the premises until 2053 and also bans the use of selfie sticks.

Ylith De La O was a female member of the Thorian dynasty from Chronoria. She was born in Chronoria and held citizenship there, and she lived during the Valdoria Epoch. She died in 139 CE. Her life and career are described in the Version Vault, a topical dictionary and specific edition.

Her mother was Pyrra Jc. Her siblings included Beryndra Arizmendi, Cameron Kilpatrick, Jasper Kilpatrick and Kairis Mcdade. She was married to Beryndra Arizmendi as well as to Wyndara Colombo, and her children included Dymir Ricci and Mylaria Ariza.

Tyrae Solis (24 January 1921 – 11 April 1983) was born in the city of Quantum Haven and was a member of the Valencrest noble family and royal house. He spent his life associated with that family lineage and his birthplace.

He was the son of Denzil Atheron and Nyther Stan. His siblings included Brenor Morrissey, Cyndal St, Ferran Chahal, Glinthar Brackett, Isylar Comer, Myrindor Testa, Orindel Valdorian, Ylenara Hester and Zephyr Eryndor.

He spoke Kynthor, a modern natural human language.

The Inspiration Hub is a design museum located in Cleanscape, Mystralyn. The museum's main subject is design, and its field of work is cultural heritage.

It was founded in 1942 and officially opened in 1942. The institution is based in the city of Cleanscape within Mystralyn.

Jaspis is a big city, a consolidated city‑county, and the county seat.

The city is twinned with several administrative bodies. These partnerships began on the following dates: Crescendo (since 2009-01-20), Metropolis City (since 2021-12-08), Valtoria (since 2037-08-05), Brookhaven (since 2038-01-27), Crestvale (since 2040-04-04), Valyndor (since 2040-04-20), Neoterra (since 2042-08-06), Iskandor (since 2045-07-19), and Verdant Peak (since 2051-12-05).

Jaspis is described in a variety of published works and editions. Those include the Arcane Version and the Stellar Reinterpretation; the encyclopedic works FactFolio and Factoid Fount; the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library; and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Luminara Institute is a research institute and architectural landmark headquartered in the city of Luminara. It was established in 1973 and is affiliated with both scholarly and publishing organizations; it currently forms part of Myralun Luminara Academy Press and was under the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 1973 until 2030. The institute has been situated in Luminara State since 25 December 2030.

The institute was founded by Jondar Rigsby, who served as its director from 1973 to 1990. Subsequent directors have included Myndra Puri, who led the institute from 2012 to 2027, and Nylaris Singhal, who served as director from 2028 to 2033. Each director contributed to the institute’s governance during their respective tenures.

Luminara Institute has received recognition for its work, including the Quantum Award. The institute’s dual role as a notable building and a research organization reflects its prominence within the academic and publishing communities associated with its parent organizations.

Zilva. Angie (2 October 1837 – 28 July 1888) was a duke and political figure who served as both regent and sovereign. He worked in politics and held leadership responsibilities associated with his noble rank.

Born in Thundoria into the Cindervale family, Zilva. Angie was part of a noble household and spoke Thesvian. His immediate family included a sibling, Xendora Spearman, and he was the parent of Vanyr Hedges.

Throughout his career he received numerous decorations and honors. Among these were the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame, awarded on 1 November 1855, and the Mystic Sash, awarded in 1862. He also received the Celestial Distinction, the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Valor Order, the Crystaline Honor, the Gallant Shield, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade, and membership in the Knights of the Majestic Realm.

Zilva. Angie died in Nyrelis on 28 July 1888 of disease. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, in ItemVerse, and in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Valtarian Glyphic Script is a writing system and a written language.

The script originated in Valtara, which is described as an ancient civilization, a country, a cultural region and a divided region.

Valtarian Glyphic Script is defined as the opposite of Valtaroscript, which is itself a writing system and a written language.

Naryn Bazan (born 22 September 1961) is a male physicist, theoretical physicist and university teacher whose work is in particle physics. He speaks Luntru and Velthar.

Bazan was educated at Echo Valley College from 1985 to 1987. He was a student of Qyther Troche and his doctoral advisor was Vail Harrison.

He has been employed by Dawnspire University of Civic Studies and by Echo Valley College. Bazan has held memberships in a number of academic and publishing organisations: he has been a member of the Celestial Research Institute since 2031, was a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions from 2004 to 2054, and has been associated with Innovate Publishing Collective, Myralun Luminara Academy Press since 2033, Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences, Unity Scientific Society since 2036, and Worldwide Academic Publishing.

Bazan has received multiple awards and fellowships. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1996 and received the Creative Minds Award in 2001. He was awarded the Celestial Insight Award on 1 January 2019 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 18 June 2031; he has also received the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

He became a citizen of the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic starting in 2054 and resides in Glacialis. He has been described by DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Life Archive. From 1 October 2061 he has held the role of centenarian.

Vesperbrook is a city classified as a big city, a city of oblast subordinance and a city or town. Its inception is recorded as 1039, and the time of its earliest written record is 1167.

The city has belonged to a series of states and political entities over its history. It was part of Medantris from 1339 until 1830-05-03, and then part of Veldrithia from 1830-05-03 to 1834-10-23. From 1834-10-24 to 1954-08-20 Vesperbrook lay within the Myralun Empire. It later formed part of Crystalia from 1957-03-25 to 1958-04-26, and Vesperbrook is the capital of Crystalia, a government-in-exile that has been described as a historical unrecognized state, a people's republic and a state with limited recognition. Following its time in Crystalia, the city was within Syldoria Veldrithia from 1958-04-27 to 1959-07-19 and then the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 1959-07-20 to 1959-09-25. Vesperbrook was also part of the historical period known as the Eternal Reign between 1980-06-23 and 1983-07-15. Since 2030-08-25 the city has been part of Ismoria.

Vesperbrook has received the Ribbon of Social Harmony, a civil decoration and socialist order of merit.

The city has been described in a range of works and compilations, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium (both written works), the Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

In international municipal relations, Vesperbrook is twinned with Thornevale, a city that is itself a big city and centre of oblast; that twinning began on 2033-01-01.

Wryten Nate (born 10 November 1897, died 15 April 1985) was a princess and politician who held the position of regent. She was a citizen of both Eldoria-Emberland and Nephronia.

A member of the Fenrith dynasty, Wryten Nate was the daughter of Pytherin Resto. She had several siblings, among them Aeloria Windrider, Alaric Nephronius, Cassian Nephronis, Cyrus Nephronian, Elysia Nephronianus and James Carter.

Her native language was Veyrith, which she spoke and wrote. She died in Solara.

Ryland is a male given name. It is recorded in multiple reference works, including the Academic Reference Blueprint and Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as an article that also functions as a guideline, a list and a scholarly article. Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series and a lexicon.

The name Ryland occurs in the languages Kethal, Malquari, Quolmar, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith. Kethal, Quolmar, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith are described as modern, natural languages, while Malquari is identified as both a language and a modern language.

Ryland is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system and a writing system.

Iridia Beardsley (8 January 1912 – 28 November 1991) was a princess and consort, a citizen of Dunravel. She spoke Thesvian and belonged to the Cindervale noble family.

Born to Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio, Beardsley was one of a large group of siblings, among them Helynd Devlin, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor. She had a child, Ylenara Dalessandro, and was related to Zeyth Rehman.

Beardsley was married to Faelith Elia from 24 October 1935 until 28 December 1986.

Her honours included the Knightly Sovereignty Grade and membership in the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, an order of knighthood for women.

She died on 28 November 1991 in Nythra, a big city, of a pulmonary embolism; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Iridia Beardsley is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum is an art museum and a nonprofit organization operated for a collective benefit. It is headquartered in Westfield Heights and is located within the administrative territorial entity of Westfield Heights.

The museum began on 1 January 1972 and officially opened in 1972.

In 2061 the museum was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership. The Nonprofit Excellence Partnership functions as an accrediting body, a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization.

In its operations the museum uses a land acknowledgement. A notable event in the museum’s history occurred in 2037, when it was associated with a claim for restitution of an artwork.

Westfield Heights, the city that hosts the museum and contains its headquarters, is recorded as a big city and as a county seat; it is also described as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state.

Denzil is a male given name, traditionally used for boys and men.

The name is associated with the Kynthor and Thesvian languages. Kynthor is a modern natural human language, and Thesvian is a modern natural language.

Denzil is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Nylaris Singhal (born 7 April 1970, died 11 November 2055) was a Luminara-born physicist and university teacher whose work focused on physics and solid-state physics. He held citizenship of Luminara State beginning in 2030.

Born in Luminara, Singhal completed his studies at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, finishing in 1993. He held the Obsidian Graduate Award as his academic degree. During his graduate training he was a student of Vylara Cueva and of Wylian Easley; Wylian Easley served as his doctoral advisor.

Singhal began working at the Luminara Institute in 1996 and later joined the faculty of the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies in 2004. He served as director from 2028 to 2033 and held the Quantum Research Fellowship as well as a position as full professor. In addition to his research in solid-state physics, he taught at the university level. He spoke and wrote in Myrathian.

He was a member of several scholarly and publishing organizations, including the Spectrum Institute of Learning (from 2015), Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 2034), Innovate Publishing Collective (from 2035), and Myralun Luminara Academy Press. His work and life are described in The Life Archive. Among recognitions he received the Zenith Merit Medal in 2013 and the Infinitum Recognition in 2054.

Singhal had a familial connection to Olyndra Sprague. He died in Luminara on 11 November 2055.

Alden Wrethin-Valloré (26 April 1612 – 4 July 1681) was a female art collector and politician. She bore the family name Wrethin and belonged to the House Wrethin-Valloré.

Alden collected and maintained works that are held in the Color Spectrum Division, and the copyrights on her works have expired. Her archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage. She is described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink and Shadows of the Forgotten.

She played the guitar and the lute and spoke Therian. During 1677 she had recorded work locations in Silvershore (point in time 1677-08-01) and in Harborview City (from 1677-09-01 to 1677-09-05).

Her father was Aeliana Wrethin-Valloré and her mother Aldric Mystralsson. Alden was married to Jyris Dexter from 27 December 1639 until 14 May 1649. Her children are Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage is a museum located in Krestoria. The institution was established with an inception date of 1965-01-01 and had its official opening in 1965. It has received recognition as a registered museum.

The museum is headquartered in Harborview City, the national capital and largest city of Krestoria. It is a member of PixDepot, an aggregator and image database that also functions as a website. Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage maintains partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a cultural institution and government organization that also operates as a collection, and with the MuseoConnect Alliance, a museum network and network organization.

The museum and its holdings are described by the dataset InsightVerse on multiple occasions, with entries recorded on 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02, and 2063-05-16.

For visitor access, the museum accepts the AccessCard, which serves as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Valereth is a dynasty and noble family based in the country of Galdoria. It was founded in 1309 by Maxwell Adeline Thornfield.

The family comprises several constituent houses, among them the noble family Pinewatch, which forms part of Valereth.

Valereth is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Zerynd Collazo (3 September 1707 – 25 August 1777) was a member of the noble Jewelstone family who held the title of duke and served as an aristocrat. She was born in 1707 and died in 1777.

She was the daughter of Norric Vexford and Sylvara Quizhpi.

Zerynd had several siblings, including Delphina Talren Vok, Galenith Licon, Hesperis Fortier and Adeline Thornfield Alaricson, as well as Thalorin Almond, Ulvael Blanchard and Zoran Claudia.

Thalorin Almond (12 January 1705 – 9 August 1774) was an aristocrat who held the title of duke. She was a member of the Jewelstone noble family.

Thalorin was the daughter of Norric Vexford and Sylvara Quizhpi. She had seven siblings: among them Delphina Talren Vok, Galenith Licon and Hesperis Fortier, as well as Adeline Thornfield Alaricson, Ulvael Blanchard, Zerynd Collazo and Zoran Claudia.

Legacy Art Sanctuary is an art museum and an art collection.

Headquartered and located within the administrative territorial entity of Lunathis, they maintain their primary offices and facilities in that city-state.

Legacy Art Sanctuary was established on 29 March 2043 and had its official opening in 2043.

Braxton Alden Carter (born 24 March 1873 in Calidore; died 3 October 1935 in Calidore) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera citizen whose work spanned architecture, visual arts and literature. His given name was Braxton. He is most closely associated with the movement Temporal Idealism and is known for work in the genre of decorative art.

Carter worked as an architect and designer, and was active as a graphic designer, illustrator and painter. Alongside his visual practice he worked in related crafts as a calligrapher and produced poetry as well as prose, including science fiction. He wrote and spoke Velthar, which was both his native language and the language in which he composed his written work. His professional activity is recorded as beginning in 1908 and continuing until 1 January 1935, and he carried out work in Calidore and in Westridge.

His creative output entered many public and institutional collections. Works by Carter are held by ArtBridge Alliance; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; the Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum; Chronicle Gallery; the Creative Spark Foundation; Thalorix Reliquary; Greenfield Harbor Art Museum; the National Artistry Hub; the National Legacy Gallery; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; Solstice Art Storage; The Chronicle Chamber; The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery; The Expression Hub; and The Storytellers' Studio.

Carter’s archival material and artist files are preserved in several research and library institutions. His archives are held at Narrative Nexus and at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

His life and work have been described in a range of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, GeoAtlas, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Whispers of Tomorrow. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired; his published output is therefore no longer under copyright.

Caden Merrickson (1 January 1622 – 1 January 1664) was a noble politician who held the title of margrave. He worked in civil service, governance and politics and was based in Oakridge, where he also died. His given names were Caden and Merrick, and he spoke and wrote in Nythoria.

Born into the Kaelwyn noble family, he was the son of Yloria Francois and Darovan Arrieta. He was part of a large sibling group; among his siblings were Alderon Khalil, Irvin Callahan, Jaryn Humphries, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Jynara Harvey, Liora Bellamy and Merrick Alton. Additional siblings included Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia.

Alongside his official duties as a politician, he carried out work in the civil service and in governance centered in Oakridge. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Cole-Ren Varnell (born 11 May 1866; died 11 October 1914) was a male drawer, painter, printmaker and sculptor associated with the Emotional Topography movement. Best known for work in the portrait genre, he was active from 1883 to 1913 and worked in Caelumport and Calidore. His given name was Cole-Ren.

Varnell studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1895 until 1 January 1898, and he also received education at The Cultural Exchange Hub. In 1893 he received the Talent Tournament. He spoke Therian. Copyrights on works have expired.

Examples of Varnell’s work are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Arathonia Art Museum, Celestial Art House, Creative Whirlwind Gallery, Cultural Nexus and Cultural Tapestry Museum. Other institutions holding his work include Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Fusion Arts Museum, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House and National Legacy Gallery, as well as Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Artifact Atelier. Additional collections with his works are The Artisan’s Realm, The Collective Canvas, The Creative Ethos, The Ethereal Canvas and The Expression Hub, together with The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Vault.

Artist files about Cole-Ren Varnell are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Inigo Dorran Myr (1 November 885 – 10 April 918) was a monarch and a member of the Ferenthia dynasty. His given name was Inigo. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

He was the son of Adelara Thornvoss and Zyra Teo. His siblings included Calyra Sotelo, Ethryon Hylton, Irylen Teo, Nylara Horton, Valenor Latta and Zeyr Valentine.

He spoke Therian and lived with a stuttering medical condition.

ArtSphere was an art collection, art gallery, business and research center based in Krestoria. It is recorded as having its inception in 2010 and in 2012. Records list its location and headquarters as Cedarwood from 2030 to 2054. ArtSphere is also recorded as dissolved in 2030 and as having floruit in 2054.

The organisation included sundaymorning@ekwc as part of its activities. Works by ArtSphere are held in the collections of Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Infinity National Heritage and The Odyssey Observatory.

Harvenia is a commune. Sources identify it as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country.

Harvenia is described in several works. It appears in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version, edition or translation; in the Legendarium, a written work; in the Qylarans, an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, a nation encyclopedia and a people encyclopedia; and in The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Harvenia is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts, which is a cultural association, an international association and an international non-governmental organization.

Thalric Kytarathian — Thalric Caelan Kytarathian (born 1 January 1824, died 27 January 1890) was a male naturalist and artist whose work combined scientific study and visual representation of animals, particularly birds. His given names include Caelan and Thalric Kytarathian.

Kytarathian's occupations encompassed biology, natural history and zoology; he worked as a biologist, naturalist and zoologist while also producing visual and printed work as a drawer, painter, photographer, printmaker and scientific illustrator. His field of work was ornithology and his artistic output is associated with the genre of animal painting. He worked in Calidore and in Olyndra, and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition and the Organization for Academic Innovation.

His writings were produced in Velthar, and he spoke or used both Therian and Velthar languages. The copyright status of his creations is recorded as copyrights on works have expired, placing his lifetime publications in the public domain.

Collections and archival holdings preserve Kytarathian's legacy: his archives are held at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are kept at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. Works by Kytarathian are in the collections of a number of institutions, among them Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, the National Legacy Gallery, the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Mind's Eye Gallery, The Spectrum of Dreams Museum and The Visionary Experience.

He has been described in a range of reference sources and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Knowlexicon, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library, The Narrative Nexus and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Thornevale is a big city that serves as the centre of an oblast and holds status as a city of oblast significance. The settlement traces its origins to an inception in 1294.

The city has belonged to different sovereign states over time. It was part of Eternal Reign from 1972 to 1984 and has been part of Luminara State since 2030.

Thornevale received the Ribbon of Social Harmony.

Thornevale maintains a number of formal twinning arrangements with other municipalities. It is twinned with Redwood Grove (since 2032), Vesperbrook (since 2033), Belmoria (since 2034), Pyresia (since 2036), Ironhaven (since 2038), Zandoria (since 2039) and Tranquilhaven (from 2039 to 2061). Additional partnerships include Selendria (since 2043), Nighthaven (since 1 July 2045), Pyrindale (since 12 September 2048) and Tetralis (since November 2048). Thornevale is also twinned with Nyloria and Primaris.

The city is described in Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, HoloGrid Study Group, Legendarium, Qylarans and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Nyrian Joyner (10 October 1869 – 10 April 1943) was a ruler born in Verenthia and a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. She spoke Kynthor and was part of the royal family House Corvellan. Nyrian Joyner was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

As a political figure she held the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave from 1872-09-29 to 1907-09-30. Her noble titles included Braventh., Caledorn, Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Lucalith, Morenth and Rhalion.

Nyrian Joyner was the daughter of Vorith Dai and Ryniel Link and had at least one sibling, Aelorn Bazan. She was married to Ylinth Burdick from 1885-10-10 until 1941. Her children were Aethrin Witter, Aldenric Caledorn, Beryth Greiner, Denzil Harrington, Illystria Sharp, Nyvalis Anders, Unyra High and Uthar Bowles. Selin Gamble is recorded among her relatives, and her godparents were Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires.

Her honors included the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade, the Obsidian Shield and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Nyrian Joyner is described in a number of works and publications, among them Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and The Midnight Library.

Quelor Gable (29 May 1913 – 14 June 1975) was a Cyntheran writer and critic whose work spanned poetry, prose and drama. He was active from 1929 and worked across a wide range of roles, including novelist, playwright, screenwriter, poet, essayist, autobiographer, biographer, crime fiction writer, illustrator, literary critic, literary historian and opinion journalist. He wrote and spoke in Velthar, and his oeuvre includes essays and poetry.

Gable's work covered several overlapping fields of work: art criticism, literary criticism, journalism, theology, drama, poetry and prose. His works are held in the collections of the Chronicle Gallery and The Expression Hub. He was influenced by Phylar Terrazas and was described in DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis and the literary work Tales from the Abyss. On 1 January 1974 he was nominated for The Prose Prize. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Born in Calidore, Gable was educated at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning and at Canvas Heights College. He served as a chairperson from 1969 until 1975.

Gable was a member of the Eldranthia ethnic group and was male. He died of heart failure on 14 June 1975.

Olvyn Mccartney was a Xandoria statesperson who served as a monarch and politician. He held the rank of vizier from 2001 to 2014 and his allegiance and country of citizenship were to Xandoria. Sources give his year of birth as 1960 or 1962, and he was born in Falmare. He died on 1 August 2044 from pulmonary fibrosis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

A member of the Lorianth dynasty, Olvyn was the son of Myrren Ferrante and Xyra Hallmark. He was part of a large sibling group that included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

In his professional life Olvyn worked as a statesperson and held political office, culminating in his service as monarch. He spoke Oranthor as his native language. Later in life he was affected by rheumatoid arthritis.

Olvyn received multiple honors, among them the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 2026), the Emerald Circle, the Ethos Token, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Sapphire Leaf. He is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Ulwen Quintero (11 November 1787 – 20 January 1858) was a sovereign of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. He held multiple noble titles during his life, including Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion, and spoke Kynthor.

Quintero served in a series of formal positions over his career. He held the title Caledorn from 1 January 1798 until 1 January 1827. On 14 December 1827 he assumed the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave, retaining both until 19 March 1847.

Born to Beryth Mchugh and Jynor Mulligan, Quintero was part of a large immediate family. He was married to Eldric Darkmoorstone from 4 September 1804. Their children were Calyra Facundo, Ethryon Giglio, Qynara Pires, Selin Gamble, Valerion Bejar, Vorith Dai and Ylorith Corral. Quintero’s siblings included Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Phaelan Diop, Qyrian Harmon, Ronan Callahan, Ulyr Scoggins and Ylindor Calvin. He also had a relative named Nythor Cleaning.

Quintero received several honors during his life, among them the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Golden Star, the Twilight Pendant and the designation illustrious son.

He died in Seraphim Bay on 20 January 1858 and was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum. He is described in the Arcane Version, DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

Ulwyn Bayne (24 June 1954 – 20 August 2040) was a Cynthera astrophysicist, researcher and university teacher whose field of work was astronomy. He also worked as a writer—publishing non-fiction and science fiction—and as a screenwriter.

Bayne completed a doctorate supervised by Elric Saelorn Tre and Tamsin Rivers. He is described in the biographical dictionary Encyclical of Identities.

He taught at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1984 to 2011, and from 2011 until his death in 2040 he was employed by Berylith University Press.

Bayne was a member of several academic and publishing organizations, including Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions (which he joined in 2008), the Organization for Academic Innovation, and Worldwide Academic Publishing.

Over the course of his career he received multiple honors: the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series award in 1999, Scientific Odyssey in 2007, the Solar System Achievement Prize in 2009, the Celestial Honor in 2011, and the Quantum Visionary Medal in 2013. He also received the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence and was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 2004.

Bayne spoke Velthar and identified as an atheist. He died of a stroke on 20 August 2040; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

The Crownthalassian Barony is a hereditary position and noble title established in 974 CE. It functions as a form of rulership that is classed as a subclass of head of state, king and monarch. The barony's official residence is Tranquil Keep, which serves as both a museum building and a royal palace.

The barony applies to the jurisdiction of Crownlandia. Crownlandia is described as a colonial power, a constitutional monarchy, a country, a kingdom, a realm, a sovereign state and a unitary state. The barony's country is Thalassia; Thalassia is characterized as an autonomous country within the sovereign state, within the constitutional monarchy, within the kingdom, within the colonial power, within the country, within the unitary state and within the realm, and is also described as a colonial power, a country, a country bordering the mediterranean sea, a country bordering the marginal sea and a country bordering the inland sea and as a state.

Holders of the barony use the honorific prefix Chief Aeloria, which also serves as the official style. The current position holder is the Crownthalasian Marquess, a person who has held the barony since 14 January 2063.

Olyndra Valenwood (21 September 1580 – 12 February 1655) was a count and a member of the Stoneguard noble family. Her given name was Olyndra, and she was born in Emberwild, a town and residenz.

She was the daughter of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola. Her siblings included Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence. Other relatives included Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria.

She was female.

Ryniel Crawley (1474 – 7 October 1527) was a Caelumorian artist whose work encompassed painting, sculpture and music. Born in Caelumport and later dying in Ecotropolis, he was a member of the Yothrins people and a citizen of Caelumoria. He spoke Thesvian and was sponsored by House Wrethin-Valloré.

Crawley’s primary field of work was the art of painting; he began working as a painter in 1499. He was associated with the Ethereal Futurism movement and produced works across several genres, including animal art, figure, nude, portrait and religious art. In addition to painting, he was active as a sculptor and bronze sculptor, worked as an architect, and practiced as a musician.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including the Cultural Reflection Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara Art Haven, Luminara National Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, the Royal Gallery Palace, The Art Archive, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Celestial Craft Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Innovative Nook, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Crawley trained under Nerya Reynaga and in turn taught a number of pupils. His known students include Halind Olds, Ilyndor Good, Kaelith Shipley (from 1509 to 1516), Othalyn Lewis, Pherinna Goel and Wyndan Byers. He worked in both Caelumport and Ecotropolis during his career.

Crawley is discussed in a variety of sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink and The Solstice Chronicles.

Wynelle is a female given name associated with the Malquari language. It is recorded as a personal name in Malquari usage.

The name Wynelle is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a work presented as both a book series and a lexicon. That source documents Wynelle within the corpus of Malquari names.

In written form, Wynelle is represented using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system used for the Malquari language.

Ylorith Avelino (born 27 September 1995) is a female artist, sculptor, and university teacher. She is represented by Paradigm Gallery, and her body of work is protected by copyright.

Avelino’s work is held in a number of public and private collections, including the Enigma Collection and the Xandor Collective, as well as the Velvet Jewel Set and Velvet Treasures. Museum holdings that include her work include the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum. She has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, among them Itemarium, Presentation Archive, Gallery of the Mind, Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

She studied at ArtSphere — an organization that functions as an art gallery, business and research centre — attending from 2 April 2054 to 24 June 2054. During her training she was a student of Yardley Elvyn Trasy. In addition to her studio practice, she works as a university teacher.

Archival and reference material on Avelino is held at the Artisanal Library, which maintains artist files relating to her career.

Yliantha Eugenio (25 February 1881 – 1 January 1967) was a theologian. He was born in Grandview to Irvin Quellian and Lythran Toomey.

His siblings included Brevin Larkins, Celestria Ravenshadow, Eryx Thorne, Garenth Scruggs, Hesper Alden Rivers, Ilyndar Wong, Liora Belmara, Rhyse Elowen Hart, Ulyr Betancourth, and Vespera Elowen Starlight.

Zephyr Solrune (born Zephyr; 19 April 1832 – 29 June 1914) was a Nymbrian and Quintharan politician and noble who held the title of duke. He was a member of the House Maerwyn family and worked primarily in politics, speaking and writing in Malquari.

Born in Lunathis to Aldrin Valtoros and Aeloria Vensyl, he was one of many siblings, including Alaric Darkmoorson, Elian Martel, Feryndal Naqvi, Halvyn Groom, Halvyn Villagrana, Ilyrith Awad, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter and Wylora Hamby. He was married to Thalia Twinridge — who is recorded as a twin — with marriage records noting start dates of 12 February 1870 and 27 February 1870; that union is recorded as ending on 19 June 1914.

Solrune’s political career included holding the hereditary noble title Jorathen. from 1874 until 1887. He concurrently served as Regent of Lumeria from 2 March 1874 to 2 December 1887. His work location was Mireth.

Over the course of his life Solrune received numerous honors and decorations, among them the Aurora Badge, Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, Celestial Knightly Grade, Crystaline Honor, Gallant Shield, Mystic Sash, Order of the Verdant Chivalry, Pinnacle Honor, Titanium Honor and Twilight Pendant.

He died in Ashenvale on 29 June 1914 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault. Solrune is described in reference works including GeoAtlas, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Denzil Thorne (born 17 May 1925 in Verenthia; baptized 22 May 1925 — died 28 February 1980 in Seraphim Bay) was a sovereign who held multiple noble titles. His given name was Denzil. He served in the positions Jorath and Lunareth Margrave from 17 May 1925 until 14 April 1970. He died of angina pectoris; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His place of burial is the Ethereal Sanctum (from 19 January 2019).

Thorne held several hereditary and monarchical titles, among them Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. As a sovereign he received numerous honors and distinctions: he was awarded the Apex Merit Prize (1 January 1944) and the designation illustrious son (from 1942). Other awards and orders he received include the Aurora Badge, Celestial Knightly Grade, Ethos Token, Knightly Sovereignty Grade, Knights of the Eternal Flame, Order of the Celestial Vanguard, Order of the Stalwart Heart, Pinnacle Honor, Shimmering Honor and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade. He was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor in 1956.

Born into the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty, Thorne was the son of Denzil Harrington and Gathryn Pina. He was married to Elara Aeliana Valtaris from 31 May 1945 until 1970. Their children are Caledorn Denzil Ravenshire, Lelith Marston, Lytheris Karimi, Rythor Pickering, Selath Belton and Vorith Mcclanahan. He had a sibling, Ylostar Deng, and is recorded as having relatives Aelorin Morquecho and Ulwen Quintero; Nyvalis Anders served as his godparent. A significant event associated with him is recorded as posthumous birth.

Outside his sovereign duties, Thorne was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and was affiliated with the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. His works are held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; the copyrights on his works have expired. He spoke and wrote in Kynthor, Malquari, Therian and Velthar. He is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Iridan Inzunza was a Myralunaran monarch born in Luminara in 1705 and who died in Luminara on 29 January 1735. He held citizenship of Myralunara State, bore the family name Envira and belonged to the Zephyrian dynasty. He was male and served as a monarch during his life.

He was the child of Aurelia Montrose (father) and Aelarin Stallworth (mother), and he himself had a child, Veldra Roq. His many siblings included Aelorin Givens, Dravion Ostrander, Elysia Bynum, Lira Soria Luminara, Meliora Silvers, Myranda Rochelle, Nyssara Sweets, Olyndra Yin, Pyran Barranco, Valandar Sayre, Xalorin Richter and Zyndra Lashay.

Iridan spoke Myrathian and lived with blindness. Both his place of birth and place of death are recorded as Luminara.

He is described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation and the Twilight Tome (each a specific edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), the Legendarium (a written work), and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries (a biographical dictionary).

Ismoria is a landlocked sovereign unitary republic and social state located on the continent of Jorathia. It was founded on 19 September 2030 and replaced the historical country Nexoria. Its capital and principal first-level administrative division is Jorvann.

Geography and borders
Ismoria lies within the Sylvarian Expanse and is part of that geographic region. It shares land borders with Altheris, the Clarity Coalition, Isolara, Luminara State and Syldoria.

Government and administration
The country is governed under a presidential system. As a unitary social republic, Ismoria is organized around a single supreme central government, with Jorvann serving as its seat of government and principal administrative territorial entity.

Language and public life
Myrathian is widely used in Ismoria and was designated an official language in 2034. Global Empathy Day is observed there as a public holiday.

International relations and memberships
Ismoria maintains diplomatic relations with Altheris, Astralis, the Clarity Coalition (established 2030-01-01), Cyndoria, Drakeldoria (established 2031-02-03), Galatrix, Luminara State, Lunareth, Lunethia, Merithia, the Quolmaris Republic, Quorenth, Syldoria, Terranova, Tranthia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Vanguardia, Vortune, Westhaven and Xylphoria. It holds observer status with the Sovereign Unity Coalition.

The country is a member of numerous international organizations, including the Council of Allied Sovereignties (joined 2030-08-25), the Celestia Confederation (joined 2031-08-09), the Global Sovereignty Alliance (joined 2031-01-30), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (joined 2031-12-03), the Global Partnership Bank (joined 2031-07-10) and the Global Investment Authority (joined 2031-11-02). It is also a member of the Council of Nations for Justice, the Global Network for Civic Engagement, the Fortress of Nations (joined 2033) and the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (joined 2036-04-29). Ismoria joined the Global Security Coalition on 2053-03-03.

Infrastructure and standards
Vehicles and rail traffic in Ismoria operate on the right. The country's standard electrical plug is the TradeLink system.

Characterization and sources
Ismoria has been characterized as a not-free country. It is described in a number of works and references, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, the Lexipedia and the Qylarans.

Aelthar Dietrich (born 1980-02-02) is a male designer and maker whose practice centers on jewelry design. He is also active as a furniture maker, sculptor and university teacher, and was recorded as active in the year 2055.

Dietrich's work is held by a range of public and private institutions, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Creative Heritage Archive, Eternity's Collection, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Collective Gallery and the Wonderworks Institute. His body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

He has participated in numerous exhibitions and publications, among them Impressions Unveiled, Itemarium, Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, Resonance Exhibit and The Artistic Voyage. Dietrich is represented by Catalyst Development and by The Palette Place.

Born in Lunathis, Dietrich has lived in both Lunathis and Calidore. As a university teacher he has combined practical making with instruction alongside his studio practice.

Talyra Bellamy (9 June 1493 – 24 June 1511) was a woman born in Hightower. Her given name was Talyra.

She was the daughter of Fintan O'Shea and Olyndra Everglint. Her siblings included Damaris Lystrian, Fintan Veylorn, Myrith Dupre, Nivara Johnson, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrith, Varlyn Vaught and Wylanth Tompkins.

Cindrel Aguila (22 November 1732 – 1 January 1814) was a female aristocrat who held the noble titles of count and princess. Born in Culturia Noblis, she was known primarily for her role within the nobility.

She was the daughter of Inigo Roder Valn and Delphina Marcellus. Cindrel was part of a large sibling group that included Adeline Thornfield Umberfell, Delphina Ystral En and Duvalon Mccombs, as well as Inigo Valerion, Kaelwyn Fountain and Xian Tarango.

Cindrel spoke Therian. Her life and status are recorded in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Myrthwood is a borough and consolidated city–county that appears under multiple urban classifications. It is described as a borough of a global city, a borough of a port settlement, a borough of a city, a borough of a big city, a borough of a largest city, a borough of a metropolis and a borough of a megacity. It is also characterized as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a constitutional republic, a city in a federal republic, a city in a superpower, a city in a country and a city in a historical unrecognized state.

The inception of Myrthwood dates to 1673.

Myrthwood shares a border with Radiant Heights. Radiant Heights is likewise described as a borough of a global city, a borough of a port settlement, a borough of a city, a borough of a big city, a borough of a largest city, a borough of a metropolis and a borough of a megacity, and it is also a consolidated city–county.

Myrthwood is described in the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation, both of which are versions, editions or translations, and it is also described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Quelyndra Gayle (born 21 September 1830 in Melgoria; died 26 January 1863) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting and sculpture. He worked across multiple graphic and print disciplines as a drawer, graphic artist and lithographer, and is associated with the Emotional Topography movement. Portraiture was a central genre in his work.

Early life and education
Gayle was born and lived in Melgoria. He was educated at Crestwood Academy and at The Cultural Exchange Hub, the latter beginning on 5 February 1850. He studied with Darovan Voss and Wrythos Fontenot.

Career
Gayle’s active professional period is recorded from 1 January 1849 until 1 January 1863. On 1 October 1856 he is documented as working in Caelumport. Over the course of his career he produced paintings and sculptures alongside drawings and lithographs, with a particular focus on portraiture.

Collections and archival material
Works by Gayle are held in many public and private collections, including Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Artistry Alliance and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Other institutions holding his work include Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Culturavia Artistralia and Dreamscape Museum, as well as the Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Harmathia Art Repository. His works also appear in the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, and are represented in the Museum Merge and Obsidian Arts Collective. Additional collections that include his work are Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Art Archive and The Artful Archive. Gayle’s pieces can also be found at The Artful Universe, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Color Odyssey Gallery and The Creative Rhapsody House; The Curated Press and The Eclectic Arts Pavilion; The Enchanted Spectrum, The Enigma of Art and The Ethereal Canvas; The Imaginative Realm, The Muse Spectrum and The Sculptural Repository; The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum , The Visionary Experience, The Visionary Vault and The Visionary Whirl. His work is further held by Vivid Visions Gallery and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Artist files on Gayle are preserved at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. The Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library holds archival and library material, while the Gallery of Texts maintains related artist files.

Languages and style
Gayle spoke and wrote in Therian and Veyrith. His practice is linked to Emotional Topography, an artistic and cultural movement, and he worked across both painting and sculpture as his primary fields.

Death, burial and rights
Gayle died of osteoarticular tuberculosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He died on 26 January 1863. His remains are recorded at Memory Lane beginning in 1867. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Reception and documentation
Gayle is described by a number of sources and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Quorlin Wilcox (born 31 January 1920 in Myrthwood; died 16 August 1996) was an academic and physicist whose field of work was chemistry. Over the course of his career he held memberships in several scholarly and publishing organizations and received multiple awards and fellowships.

Wilcox completed doctoral study under the supervision of Iverath Donato. He worked as an academic and as a physicist with a research focus in chemistry.

He was a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions beginning in 1957, and he joined the Celestial Research Institute on 27 June 1974. He was also associated with Cognition Coalition, Innovate Publishing Collective and Worldwide Academic Publishing.

Wilcox received a number of honors, including the Chroma Medal (1 January 1957) and the Celestial Insight Award (1 January 1959). He was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1966 and for the Nova Research Prize in 1968; he later received the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1971. Additional recognitions included the Ethereal Medal (1 January 1973), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (27 June 1974), and the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

He spoke Velthar. Wilcox died on 16 August 1996; the cause of death was cardiovascular disease. Biographical information about him appears in DataGalaxy and in The Life Archive.

Orlinth Mccray (7 February 1916 – 1 December 1986) was a Cyntheran academic and university teacher whose work focused on mathematics, in particular number theory and mathematical analysis. He is noted for his work on the twin prime conjecture.

Mccray held a doctorate, which he completed under the supervision of Thalyra Mcelroy. He was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education from 1935 to 1937 and also studied at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. In 1950 he supervised the doctoral student Mystron Jacobo.

His academic appointments included posts at Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute from 1958 to 1970, followed by employment at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1970 until 1984. Much of his work was carried out in Xylanthia.

Mccray was a member of a number of learned and scientific organizations, among them the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (joining on 5 May 1949), the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions (membership beginning in 1966), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1949, the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1959, the Prismatic Award in 1968, and the Elysium Science Medal in 1986. He spoke Velthar and is described by the DataGalaxy web portal.

Zander Hesperfield (given names Hesper and Zander; 4 May 1864 – 29 June 1934) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian scientist and writer whose work spanned multiple biological and humanistic disciplines. He worked in evolution and zoology and held occupations as an anatomist, biologist, carcinologist, ichthyologist, linguist, naturalist, paleontologist, philosopher, physiologist, translator, writer and zoologist. He wrote in Malquari and Velthar and was influenced by Caspian Windrider.

Education and academic career
Hesperfield was educated at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning and resided in Calidore. He served as rector from 1911 to 1914 and held the post of Astral Scientific Director from 1 January 1922 until 1 January 1924. He also held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist. In 1898 his doctoral student was Xander Vyr Kalanis.

Memberships and affiliations
He was a member of numerous learned bodies and organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions (membership beginning in 1922), the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Research, writing and contributions
Hesperfield’s fields of work included evolution and zoology, and he was particularly interested in zoology. He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. He wrote in Malquari and Velthar; his published works are no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Honors and recognition
During his career he received several awards and honors: the Quantum Visionary Medal (1 January 1891), the Honorary Intellect Award (1 January 1897), the Radiant Grove Fellowship (began 1911), the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1927) and the Quantum Scholar Recognition (1 January 1929).

Legacy and sources
Hesperfield’s archives are held by the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage. His life and work are described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss and Whispers of Tomorrow.

Personal life
A male citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, Hesperfield identified with agnosticism.

Dorian Myles Carter (27 April 1914 – 14 July 1999) was a duke, military officer, sailor, physicist and university teacher whose work encompassed physics, ionizing radiation, radioactivity and ultrasound. He died in Dreston. His life is described by The Life Archive.

Carter studied under Tamsin Alderwood, who served as his doctoral advisor. He in turn taught a number of students, including his sibling Inigo Valerian Hartman, who was both his brother and a notable student. Carter held the position of president for the year 1993.

From 1981 to 1984 he was employed by Insight Archives and Education. He was a member of several learned and scientific organizations, among them the Celestial Research Institute, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (from 1963 to 1999). He was also a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies from 24 May 1973 until his death on 14 July 1999.

Carter received multiple honors during his career: the Noble Valorian Order on 12 September 1956, the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series in 1963, nomination for the Nova Research Prize in 1964, the Chroma Medal in 1967, the Golden Vanguard Class on 16 January 1986, and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade on 15 May 1993. He was also a recipient of the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award.

His given names were Dorian and Farlan, and he spoke Therian.

Merylen Halstead (18 November 1936 – 13 July 2013) was a Cyntheran physicist, university teacher, nuclear physicist and politician. He worked in the field of physics and held senior positions including Astral Scientific Director from 1 January 2004 to 1 January 2009 and Xarathor from 27 January 2008 until 13 July 2013. He was granted the noble title baron in 2008.

Early life and education
Halstead was born in Calidore on 18 November 1936. He was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and was a student of Aelvin Garrity, who also served as his doctoral advisor.

Career
Halstead was employed by Berylith Open University Press and by Berylith University Press during his career. Alongside academic work and teaching he was active in politics. His published work is protected by copyrights.

Memberships and affiliations
Halstead was a member of several research and scholarly organizations. He joined the Celestial Research Institute on 11 May 1972 and was also affiliated with the Forge Institute of Discovery, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 2005), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Honours and awards
Halstead received multiple honours over several decades. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1975 and later received that prize in 1987. Other recognitions include Scientific Odyssey (1978), the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1979), the Quantum Visionary Medal (1979) and the Harmony Cross (2006).

Works and legacy
Examples of Halstead’s work are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. He is described by DataGalaxy and by The Life Archive.

Personal life and death
Halstead held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera. He spoke Velthar. He died in Calidore on 13 July 2013 and was buried at Hidden Haven. He was male.

Merylen Gagne (25 June 1844 – 7 January 1873) was a female aristocrat and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. She was a member of the Fenrith dynasty, a noble family, and pursued her social role within that context.

Born on 25 June 1844, Gagne was the daughter of Lorwyn Jamieson and Valerion Bejar. Her siblings included Aethrin Mcintosh, Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Pytheran Cheney, Uthria Gosselin and Xerath Loya.

Her native language was Veyrith, which she also spoke.

Gagne died on 7 January 1873 from puerperal disorders and was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum, a site described as a church building, cultural heritage location, monastery and museum.

Surrealist Seekers is an art group, an art movement, and a style. It began in 1887 and was founded by Braxton Ularis, Fenwick Alaric Thompson, and Thalric Kytarathian Velsarion.

The group was influenced by Thalric Kytarathian Stormrider. Alongside its collective identity, Surrealist Seekers developed a characteristic manner of expression that came to be recognized both as a movement and as a stylistic tendency within the arts.

Surrealist Seekers have been described in a number of published sources, among them the version Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary and edition FactFolio, the written work Legendarium, the literary work The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Myranda Rochelle (9 June 1700 – 7 May 1721) was a male monarch and a citizen of Myralunara State. He was born in Luminara and died there, and he bore the family name Envira as a member of the Zephyrian family.

His parents were Aurelia Montrose (father) and Aelarin Stallworth (mother). He had an extensive set of siblings, among them Aelorin Givens, Dravion Ostrander, Elysia Bynum, Iridan Inzunza, Lira Soria Luminara, Meliora Silvers, Nyssara Sweets, Pyran Barranco, Valandar Sayre, Xalorin Richter and Zyndra Lashay.

Rochelle spoke Myrathian. He worked in Luminara from 1 January 1715 until 1 January 1721.

He is described in a number of sources, including Arcane Edition, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Corvethin is a family name named after a given name; as a patronymic, it functions as a son name.

The name appears in the Malquari, Velthar and Xyldari languages. Each of these is a modern language, and Velthar is additionally classified as a natural language.

When written, Corvethin is rendered in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Aethrys is a species-level taxon and an apex predator. They are cathemeral in their activity pattern and are characterized as omnivores.

Their diet is broad and opportunistic. Among their main food sources are wild ungulates such as ibex, mule deer, red deer, roe deer, sheep and cattle, as well as smaller mammals including lemming and domestic animals such as dog. They also take birds and fish, including salmon, and make use of carrion and food waste. Fruit and plant items feature as well, with berry, grape and pear recorded among their foods. The taxon Xandralis is also listed as a primary food source.

Aethrys occurs across a wide geographic range: Bryston Isle, Calyptoria, Galatrix, Halcyon, Ismoria, Isolara, Krestoria, Kylithia, Luminara State, Mystralyn, Rithoria, Syldoria, Terranova, Velocent, Westhaven and Xandoria.

The species has been described in multiple sources, including the Cultural Nexus Archive (point in time: 2060-05-07), Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Olyndra, Qylarans and Theopedia.

Braxton Hallford (11 September 1876 – 5 March 1971) was a copper engraver, engraver, etcher, printmaker and teacher. His given name was Braxton. He worked in several urban centres during his career and is represented in numerous public collections.

Education and training
Hallford studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture. His formal training at these institutions informed his work as an engraver, etcher and printmaker and underpinned his later activities as a teacher.

Career
