Hallford worked in Delvoria in 1904 and in Jorathia from 1908 to 1909. He was working in Harborview City in 1915 and also carried out work in Lunathis. Over the course of his career he combined copper engraving with etching and other printmaking techniques while teaching those methods to others.

Collections and legacy
Works by Hallford are held in a number of museums and galleries, including Artropolis Nextridge, the National Legacy Gallery and the Terranova Artis Museum. Additional institutions holding his work include The Chronicle Chamber, The Dreamweaver Art Institute and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. The Ethereal Oasis, The Odyssey Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum also include Hallford’s work in their collections.

Recognition and sources
Hallford was a member of the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy. He is described in Arcane Edition, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Narratives of the Lexicon. He spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Death and copyright
Hallford died in Nythara on 5 March 1971. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

The Legacy Lab is an archaeological, art and history museum. As an archaeological museum it specialises in archaeological artefacts, and as a history museum it covers the knowledge of human history.

The organisation was founded in 1886 and was officially opened on 3 April 1892.

The facility offers an audio tour and provides a changing table and a cloakroom for visitors.

The Legacy Lab received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 1 February 2042.

Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities is a state entity that operates both as a government agency of Zolterra and as a university for further education. They have legal form as a state entity and their inception dates to 1516.

The council applies to the jurisdiction of Zolterra and is located in the country of Zolterra, a sovereign and unitary state. They are a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association.

The council is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in ReadRealm, a bibliographic database and virtual library. They have works in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, an art museum and national museum that also functions as a government agency.

Liora Belmara (given name Liora; born 1 January 1882, died 1 January 1945) was a female pianist and a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. She worked as a pianist and is recorded as holding citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

Belmara was the daughter of Irvin Quellian and Lythran Toomey. Her siblings included Brevin Larkins, Celestria Ravenshadow, Eryx Thorne, Garenth Scruggs, Hesper Alden Rivers, Ilyndar Wong, Rhyse Elowen Hart, Ulyr Betancourth, Vespera Elowen Starlight and Yliantha Eugenio.

In 1905 she married Vail Hawthorne; the marriage is recorded from 1905 through 1945.

Rhyse Elowen Hart (given name Rhyse; born 4 April 1876 – died 1949) was a writer and a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

She was the daughter of Irvin Quellian and Lythran Toomey and had one child, Waylindra Roach. Hart was raised in a large family; her siblings included Brevin Larkins, Celestria Ravenshadow, Eryx Thorne, Garenth Scruggs, Hesper Alden Rivers, Ilyndar Wong, Liora Belmara, Ulyr Betancourth, Vespera Elowen Starlight, and Yliantha Eugenio.

Hart pursued a career as a writer. She died in 1949.

Ilyndar Wong (born 1884 in Berylith) was a novelist, poet and writer who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

She was the daughter of Irvin Quellian and Lythran Toomey and had a large number of siblings, including Brevin Larkins, Celestria Ravenshadow, Eryx Thorne, Garenth Scruggs, Hesper Alden Rivers, Liora Belmara, Rhyse Elowen Hart, Ulyr Betancourth, Vespera Elowen Starlight and Yliantha Eugenio.

Her date of death is given as 16 May 1964 and also as 16 May 1967.

Uryth Lena (13 March 1879 – 14 December 1967) was a female editor, suffragette, suffragist and writer who held the noble title of lady. She spoke Velthar.

She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966, and also held citizenship of Cynthera.

Her children included Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya and Galenith Castrejon, as well as Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel.

Wyslind Morel (19 April 1911 – 23 August 2007) was a suffragette and women's rights activist. Born in 1911, she lived much of her life in Calidore from 1918 and spoke Velthar. She held citizenship of Cynthera and was also a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966.

Morel was active in organisational work for women's causes, serving as a secretary and later as honorary secretary from 1990. In 1990 she received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order.

Her family included her mother, Uryth Lena, and eight siblings: Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Galenith Castrejon, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue and Vanyr Gallant.

Wyslind Morel is described in Nebula Edition.

Ambrosia City is a planned community and municipality in the communist sovereign state of Red Horizon, located on the continent Nystoria. They are a big city and a megacity, and they serve as the largest city in Red Horizon.

Their inception is recorded as 1737 and again as 1994. Ambrosia City is located in the administrative territorial entity of Red Horizon and forms part of that country.

They maintain a number of twinning relationships. Ambrosia City is twinned with Solaris City (start time 2014), Zephyra (start time 2016), Lighthaven (start time 2023), Horizon Bay (start time 2034), Celestport (start time 2046-10-23), Porthaven (start time 2048-05-21) and Delvoria (start time 2060-07-21). They are also twinned with Ethereal Springs, Etherealis, Everhaven, Luminara, Opal City and Umbermist.

Ambrosia City is described by the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Teryn Donohue (born 4 March 1915, died 19 December 1990) was a college head who spent her life in Calidore. She was born in Calidore to Uryth Lena and later died there.

Over the course of her career Donohue worked as a college head and served as principal from 1962 to 1980.

She held citizenship of Cynthera and was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966. Donohue spoke Velthar.

Donohue was female. Her siblings included Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel.

The Quantum Award was an order, a visible honour awarded to an individual recipient. It was established on 6 April 1969 in Luminara by Kylin Whitehead and was named for Nytheren Evangelista.

As an honour, the order’s composition included award winners as its constituent parts; recipients of the Quantum Award were thus recognized as award winners within the order. The award was formed in the city of Luminara and maintained that association throughout its existence.

The Quantum Award was dissolved in 2030.

The Ethereal Oasis is an art museum.

The museum's collection holds works by a large number of artists and makers. Its holdings include works by Edran Thornvale, Aelan Tiller, Aelarin Mishra, Aelath Lozano, Aelond Matthews, Aeloria Isbell, Aelwen Viveros, Alistair Voss, Aralyn Brooke, Arion Cecil, Axton Greenfield and Axton Corvess. Also represented are Bellia Martell, Belwyn Treviño, Berenth Guillot, Beryndor Leiva, Brae Eldridge and Brae Thornton, alongside Braxton Talvern Oris, Braxton Emberwood, Braxton Hallford, Braxton Thorne and Braxton Wellspring. The collection further includes Brenar Linda, Brenar Pedroza, Brenor Sahu, Brithor Valentine, Bryndith Chandran and Bryndra Mireles, as well as Caden Blake Thompson, Caelan Rivers, Calix Thorne and Celestria Ilyrion.

Additional artists in the holdings are Cole-Ren Ashford and Cole-Ren Draxford, Cyndel Campbell, Darian Alaric Morgan and Darian Morrow, Deleth Dancy, Delia Dutta and Delphina Rosetta Marlowe, together with Delwyn Nathan, Delyndra Heng and Dethara Pinales. The museum also holds works by Dorian Blackwood, Dorian Eldridge, Dorian Valenhart, Doryn Cortez, Dravion Lacey and Draxen Harwood, plus Drestor Mango and Drestor Rhoads. Represented artists include Elanth Amos, Elaria Gandara, Elion Oro, Elyndria Gulati, Elysia Jahan and Elysira Multani, as well as Eryndor Garcias.

The Ethereal Oasis's collection further comprises works by Faelon Neely, Falyn Lundy, Farlan Thorne, Fenris Zheng, Fintan McCaffrey, Freth Mcelroy and Freth Nascimento, along with Freyael Bean, Fynlar Lauren, Fynor Geronimo and Fynor Vásquez, and Fythar Sampson. Also included are Galend Plummer, Galindor Dangelo, Garren Harlun Seryn, Gelynd Landis, Glinthar Frey and Grellan Flaco, and Halindel Boom, Halir Dennis and Harlan Thorne. The holdings list Helynd Flanigan, Helynd Prakash, Henris Barbee, Hesper Alaric Thorne and Hesper Alden Brightwood, together with Hesperan Mata, Hesthra Layman, Hestorn Berg and Hylith Sutherland.

Works by Ilyndar Regan and Inyra Maes are in the collection, as are Irvin Calix Yates and Irvin Helvorn. The museum holds pieces by Japhen Basu, Jasper Callahan, Jasper Nightingale and Adeline Thornfield Windrune, and by Jethor Sutton and Jethor Vic, plus Jheron Arzu and Jheron Kulkarni, Jorian Broome and Jynara Stallworth. Kaelith Dougherty and Kaelith Thornwood appear in the holdings, together with Kalyndra Asencio, Kareth Peterman, Karyn Hoch and Kylas Barros.

The collection also contains works by Lelith Thibodeaux, Lorian Isendril Kaar, Lysdane Ford, Lysira Dowling and Lysira Marchant, as well as Lythor Valadez, Maelwyn Desantis, Melian Deck, Merith Levinson and Merynd Ferguson. Additional artists represented include Myrith Brandt, Mystras Covert, Nivara Decarlo, Nyrian Blanco and Nyther Driver, alongside Orlinth Hussey and Othryn Thanh. Paxton Merrick, Perynd Kushner and Pherinna Carmen are in the holdings, as are Pylar Lubin, Pyraen Doucette, Pyreth Mccormack and Pyreth Schuster, together with Pyris Crisostomo and Pytherin Rosenfeld.

Works by Qalyn Alba, Quethan Bloomfield and Quethan Melo are part of the collection, as are Quillon Ardentis, Quillon Drake and Quillon Everhart, and Quindra Toler and Quinella Cruise. The holdings include Quithar Scoggins, Qylar Fredericks, Renyth Thu, Rhalis Tate, Rhyel Aracena and Rhyel Ganesh, plus Rhylaris Usman and Rhyse Elowen Sterling. Also represented are Rilith Llano, Ronan Kestrel Hawthorne and Rythar Calhoun.

The museum holds works by Selantra Srinivasan and Selis Erin, as well as Sylphira Napolitano and Sylphira Scruggs. Talyra Vensoria and Teylith Bullock are included, together with Thalric Caelan Kytarathian and several related Thalric Kytarathian names: Thalric Kytarathian Eldenor, Thalric Kytarathian Eldenwood, Thalric Kytarathian Valenor, Thalric Kytarathian Erunai and Thalric Kytarathian Vossorian, as well as Thalric Vyndorathian. The collection also lists Therion Ruffin, Theros Hall and Theros Roussel.

Further holdings include Ulthar Mahler, Ulwen Coons and Ulyndor Seaman, together with Unyra Lott, Uryth Arthur and Uryth Labrador. The museum has works by Veldron Hinkle, Waylindra Ervin and Waylon Mercer, and by Wrylen Mcauliffe, Wryth Beas and Wynex Corder. Represented artists also include Xander Kael Vossar, Xander Valehart, Xelith Finkelstein, Xerath Curtis and Xylara Feller.

The collection features Yardley Ashford, Yardley Fenrah Jule and Yates Thorne, as well as Yelindra Whyte, Yelith Varney and Ylith Willey, and Ylorith Miguel. Works by Yndira Baer, Ysolde Rs, Ythara Yousif and Ytherin Haight are in the holdings, together with Zander Callahan, Zander Thorne, Zandrel Jacques, Zephyr Thorne, Zephyra Brizuela and Zorath Oleary.

The Ethereal Oasis's holdings also include ars documenta. That collection element is recorded with a start time of 2038-01-01 and is located at The Ethereal Oasis.

Yardley Prescott (given names Braxton and Yardley; 17 September 1897 – 28 December 1972) was a male painter noted for his work in portraiture. He spoke Velthar and died in Wyndrell.

Prescott received his training at the Creative Spectrum Academy and at the Gallery of Dreams, and he later worked for the Gallery of Dreams. He studied under Myrith Gladden and Qalir Olivar, influences that shaped his approach to portrait painting.

In turn, Prescott taught others; among his students was Yardley Thompson.

Prescott's works are held in a number of public collections, including the Artemis Gallery, Canvas of Dreams, the Creative Spark Foundation, Radiant Brush Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience. Artist files on Prescott are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on Prescott's works have expired.

Emberfield is a big city and municipality in the communist sovereign state of Red Horizon. It serves as the capital of Red Horizon and is located within the administrative territorial entity of Red Horizon on the continent Nystoria. The city dates to an inception in 1049 and the official language is Xyndir.

Since 2058 Emberfield has been a member of the network SyncSphere, and it is also a member of the organization The Outliers Collective. The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation and appears as a location in the video game Nebula Quest.

Emberfield maintains twinning relationships with a number of other administrative bodies. It has been twinned with Vornexa since 2039, with Xelthoran since October 2039, and with Aetherdon since 2043. It is also twinned with Draventh, Eldarune, Eldoria, Emberglow, Glacialis, Pyradale and Tranquilia.

Velthar is a modern natural language of the fusional, stress-timed type. It is indigenous to Xylanthia and is named after Xylanthia. The language is present in a wide range of countries, including Arkenland, Brystor, Caelum Archipelago., Calypsia, Calyptia, Cynthera, Jorvani, Elysian Coast and Elysium Shores. Other states where Velthar is used include Galatrix, Glenhaven, Grelland, Lumara, Lusethia, Oceantia, Orinthia, Pluvia, Pyrenthia and Quoros. It is also found in Seafarica, Serendipia, Solandia, Talerith, Terrasylvia, Thaloria and Thundoria, as well as in the Tranquil Isles, Talvoria Republic, Varnaxia, Wynsor. and Ythalia.

Phonologically, Velthar distinguishes a range of vowels and consonants. Vowels in the system include the close front unrounded vowel, close back rounded vowel, near-close near-front unrounded vowel, near-close near-back rounded vowel, close-mid back rounded vowel, near-open front unrounded vowel, near-open central unrounded vowel, open-mid front unrounded vowel, open-mid back rounded vowel, open back unrounded vowel, open back rounded vowel and schwa. Its consonant inventory comprises sounds such as the voiced alveolar approximant, voiced alveolar fricative, voiced alveolar lateral approximant, voiced alveolar nasal, voiced bilabial nasal, voiced bilabial plosive, voiced dental fricative, voiced labio-velar approximant, voiced labiodental fricative, voiced palatal approximant, voiced palato-alveolar affricate and voiced velar nasal, alongside voiceless counterparts including the voiceless alveolar fricative, voiceless alveolar stop, voiceless bilabial plosive, voiceless dental fricative, voiceless glottal fricative, voiceless labiodental fricative, voiceless palato-alveolar affricate, voiceless postalveolar fricative and voiceless velar stop.

The grammar of Velthar displays agreement and a system of three grammatical genders—feminine, masculine and neuter—together with a case system that includes nominative, genitive and oblique. The language marks modality through moods such as the indicative, interrogative and subjunctive, and it encodes temporal distinctions with a range of tenses, among them simple present and simple future, present perfect and present continuous, past perfect and past continuous, continuous pluperfect, future continuous, future perfect and future perfect continuous.

Velthar comprises distinct varieties, notably Cynvelthar and the Eldaranian Tongue. Cynvelthar is identified as an ethnolect, while the Eldaranian Tongue is characterised as a dialect and ethnolect.

In writing, Velthar employs the Eldranth Script. Orthographic conventions include the use of capitalization for days of the week, demonyms, names of languages, proper nouns, religion and religious denominations.

The language has been influenced by other languages, including Pyrathen and Therian; the influence from Therian is attested for the period 1105–1524. Descriptive and reference material on Velthar appears in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionaries FactFolio and LexiRealm, and the written work Legendarium.

Alysor Mayor (1139–1193) was a female person.

She was the daughter of Liora Valentina Hartman. Alysor had numerous siblings, among them Delyndra Mccall, Elwood Phralen Vost, Galdra Nolasco, Hesper Aldrin and Liora Valenbrook, as well as Pyrthas Marler, Quinlan Thorne, Rynen Winner, Sylphira China and Vyndel Welker.

The Celestial Quest is an episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. A science fiction work, it takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode follows The Celestial Whispers and is followed by The Enigma of the Celestial Dawn.

The Celestial Quest was first performed on 2041-02-27 and has a publication date of 2042-08-02. It was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format and was described by the magazine VividViews. The production is associated with the color "color."

The cast of The Celestial Quest includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Qylyn Donofrio. Voice actors featured in the episode include Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Arabella Skye, Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

Aetherdon is a megacity and big city that serves as the national capital and the largest city of Gelanthia. They were established on 21 April 1821 and are located on the continent Nystoria within the administrative territorial entity of Gelanthia.

As a centre of government, Aetherdon is the capital of Gelanthia. They also function as a first-level administrative division directly subordinate to the national government and are designated a special administrative area of Gelanthia — as a constitutional monarchy, as a sovereign state, and as the country’s special administrative area.

Aetherdon is a member of the Empowerment Collective and of the SyncSphere network; they joined SyncSphere in 2058.

The city maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other municipalities: Verdantia Metropolis (since 2001-02-19), Glacialis (since 2032-05-26), Thalorim (since 2036-05-07), Luminara (since 2036-06-19), Zephyra (since 2036-06-20), Everhaven (since 2036-06-24), Emberfield (since 2043-02-25), Draventh (since 2043-06-11), Eldoria (since 2041-01-21), Nythoria (since 2048), Etherealis (since 2048-11-13), Havencrest (since 2048-12-29), Horizon Bay (since 2050-07-11), Ventara (since 2050-09-26), Eldarune (since 2051-03-21), Omnica (since 2051-12-27) and Aruqen City (since 2052-09-02).

Aetherdon is described in several published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, LexiRealm and The Midnight Library.

Vorith Dai (14 October 1823 – 29 September 1872) was a male ruler of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. He held the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave from 4 May 1853 until his death on 29 September 1872, and he held the hereditary title Braventh. from 1853 to 1872. His other noble titles included Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. His resting place is the Ethereal Sanctum.

As a ruler, Vorith received numerous honors. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Celestial Knightly Grade, the latter in 1823, and he also received the Circle of the Brave Lotus, Crystaline Honor, Golden Star, Knights of the Majestic Realm, Order of the Verdant Chivalry and the Pinnacle Honor.

Vorith was born on 14 October 1823 to Ulwen Quintero and Eldric Darkmoorstone. His godparent and a listed relative was Beryth Mchugh, and other relatives include Denzil Thorne and Nythor Cleaning. He had two children, Aelorn Bazan and Nyrian Joyner. His siblings were Calyra Facundo, Ethryon Giglio, Qynara Pires, Selin Gamble, Valerion Bejar and Ylorith Corral.

Vorith's marital history included four spouses: he was married to Kaelar Reeder from October 1841 until 21 May 1845; to Chyra Mcallister from September 1855 until 26 December 1857; to Melrith Bari from 20 October 1858 until 18 May 1868; and to Ryniel Link from December 1868 until his death on 29 September 1872.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Midnight Library. His works are noted as having copyrights that have expired, and he spoke the language Kynthor.

Cycle Ridge Public Research University is a public research university located in Cycle Ridge, Thalassia. It is situated in Cycle Ridge, the national capital and largest city of Thalassia.

The university's inception was on 1 June 1518.

The language widely used at the university is Xarnum. As of October 2062, it was a member of the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a database and nonprofit organization.

Cevaryn Gad (born 1 January 1992) is a jewelry designer from Elysium Shores who works in jewelry and jewelry design. He resides in Radiant Shores and is a citizen of Elysium Shores.

Gad is represented by Gallery of Wonders, Paradigm Gallery and Visionary Vault. His work is held in a number of public and private collections, among them the Creative Heritage Archive, Enigma Collection, Krishnamurthy Art Archive, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Commons Collection, The Creative Portal Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Velvet Jewel Set.

He has participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, including Aesthetic Horizons, Enumeration Oasis, Exhibitron, Gallery of the Mind, Itemarium, Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, The Displayed Narrative, and The Quickening Exhibit. He also took part in The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Works produced by Gad during his lifetime are protected by copyright.

Veritas is the federal capital and a federal territory of the sovereign state Lunethia, located on the continent Nystoria. As a city, Veritas is classified as a big city and a global city; it is the largest city in Lunethia and is regarded as a primate city.

Veritas was founded in 1896. It is located within the administrative territory of Lunethia and serves as the country's capital.

The city is twinned with Aetheral Grove, Calidore, Eldarune and Eldoria, as well as with Elysium Heights, Excelsior City, Orynthia and Zenithopolis.

Veritas is featured in the video game Nebula Quest.

Phoenix Art Collective was an art gallery headquartered in Harborview City, Krestoria. The collective was founded in 2025 and was dissolved on 1 November 2051.

The gallery maintained an interest in jewelry designers and represented a number of individual artists, including Draxella Charles, Elysia Vespera Solstis, Rhyall Puma, Xeryth Patty, Yardley Pellor Zanu, and Zorith Huh.

Oryndel Adebayo (born 23 February 1842, died 21 April 1931) was a female aristocrat who held the title of princess. She was active as a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and is recorded as an aristocrat by occupation.

Born Quinella Wynelle Oryndel Adebayo, her given names included Quinella and Wynelle. She was the daughter of Belegorn Matus and Varlyn Bayona, and she had at least one child, Valandar Moorman.

Her siblings included Kirelle Beryndra, Lytheris Andrade, Malquar Valdrin, Mistran Ceja, Pylira Gantt, Selantra Crenshaw, Xantha Feinberg and Zephyr Rivenoak.

She received the Enchanted Circle of Knights, an order of knighthood for women.

Fenwick Alaric Thompson (born 12 May 1867 in Calidore; died 9 April 1921 in Cynthera) was a male artist and writer who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera. His given names include Fenwick and Adeline Thornfield, and he identified with the Eldranthia and Yothrins ethnic groups.

Thompson worked as an artist, illustrator and painter and was also active as a poet, translator and writer. His practice encompassed allegory, figurative art, portraiture and religious painting. He was educated at Seraphim Art House and carried out much of his work in Calidore. He belonged to the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and was a member of the Surrealist Seekers; his artistic activity is associated with both the Surrealist Seekers movement and Temporal Idealism.

Thompson spoke and wrote in Velthar; Velthar was the language he used for his written work. The copyrights on his works have expired. He died of nephritis.

Thompson’s archives are held at Eternal Records, Narrative Nexus and The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. His works appear in numerous collections, including the Branash Imperial Art Museum, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canopy, Culturia Heritage Authority and the Cynthera National Art Museum. Additional holdings include the Discovery Hub, Fusion Art Institute, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion and Myrthwood Art Collective. His work is also in the National Legacy Gallery, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, the National Museum of Heritage and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Other institutions holding his pieces include The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Exchange, The Creative Essence, The Enlightenment Hall and The Expression Hub. The Historical Nexus, The Storytellers' Studio and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute also include Thompson in their collections.

Thompson has been described in a variety of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Qelyth Vollmer (born 2002) is an exhibition curator, jeweler, jewelry designer and university teacher. A citizen of Elysium Shores, they speak Malquari and live in Hightower. Their body of work is protected by copyright and is represented by Paradigm Gallery, The Gallery Exchange and The Scenic Studio.

Vollmer trained at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and studied under Denzel Montgomery and Quinlan Hartwood. Alongside their curatorial and teaching activities, they design and produce jewelry and work as a jeweler.

They have participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, including Collection Conclave, Presentation Archive and Themed Chronicles, as well as exhibitions such as Gallery of the Mind, the temporary show Evocative Ephemeris and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Vollmer's works are held in both museum and private collections. Among these are the museums and institutes The Artifact Atelier, The Chronicle Chamber and the Wonderworks Institute; the art collection Krishnamurthy Art Archive; and the jewelry and private collections Eternity's Collection and Velvet Jewel Set.

In 2034 they received the Artistic Ambit Competition. They maintain a personal relationship with Alorin Mystren Valdrune.

Valenor Og (15 December 1586 – 16 May 1672) was a female aristocrat of the Stoneguard dynasty who held the title of count. She spoke Malquari.

Valenor was the daughter of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola and belonged to the Stoneguard noble family. Her family included numerous siblings: Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence. Other relatives included Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria.

Ylenara Dalessandro (15 August 1943 – 18 March 2022) was a Morvathian public figure born with the family name Ilyndra and a member of the Cindervale noble family. He was a citizen of Morvath from 15 September 1943 until 18 June 1985. Dalessandro died in Brightstone.

As a titled noble, he held the title of king and served in multiple public roles. He worked as a politician and as military personnel, and he served as a sovereign and as a monarch. From 1982 to 1985 he held the position of steward.

Dalessandro received numerous honours and awards over his career. He was awarded the Apex Merit Prize on 1 January 1974. His other recognitions included the Arcadian Emblem and the Celestial Knightly Grade, as well as membership in chivalric and dynastic orders such as the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Knights of the Majestic Realm and the Order of the Radiant Heart. He also received the Ethos Token, the Pinnacle Honor, the Shimmering Honor and the Zenith Medal.

Thesvian was his native language and the language he spoke. He was the son of Faelith Elia and Iridia Beardsley.

Inigo Valenhart (21 January 1764 – 19 June 1844) was a male artist and painter known for portraiture. His given name was Inigo, and he worked as an artist, painter, court painter and teacher, speaking and writing in Therian. Copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Valenhart trained under Archer Blackwood and was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, an institution that later employed him. He served as a court painter and held the post of director from 1820 to 1826. As a teacher he instructed pupils including Garenth Uchiha. Late in his life he was awarded the Noble Valorian Order on 15 July 1843.

His portraits appear across numerous public and private collections. Among the institutions holding his work are Artefactual Odyssey; Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex; Flourish Art Consortium; Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; Meridian Cultural Arts Complex; Museum of Timeless Masterpieces; Prism Museum of Contemporary Art; and Terranova Artis Museum. Additional collections with his works include The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artful Universe, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Charitable Canvas, and The Creative Rhapsody House. The Curatorial Institute, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Whirl and Treasures of Expression Museum also hold examples of his work.

Archival and reference material about Valenhart can be found in artist files at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Delphina Nereth Vale (July 15, 1776 – December 23, 1826) was a princess of the Galdrin family. Born in Nethoria, her given name was Delphina and she was female. She spoke Therian.

She was the daughter of Inigo Valente and Dravion Appiah and belonged to the Galdrin dynasty. Her siblings included Delphina Loritha Vent, Elanthar Gasca, Inigo Montale, Nylaris Prendergast, Peryn Harder, Selorin Alegria, Tobias Winstone, Viorelle Mariselle, Xandor Lemons and Zyvra Smoot.

Works by Delphina Nereth Vale are held in the collection of the Chronicle Gallery, an art museum and publishing company. The copyrights on works published during her lifetime have expired.

Darlen Vaz (born 1 May 1617 — died 22 December 1640) was an aristocrat. He died in Lunathis.

Born to Merrick Alastor Thorne and Eryndor Jeronimo, he was one of many siblings. His brothers and sisters included Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine, Faelith Fryer, Helvian Nell, Inigo Valeron, Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, Olyndra Mia Thorne, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae.

Azureport is a port metropolis and big city on the continent of Jorathia, located on the Tidal Reach. It functions as an urban administrative centre in a variety of state forms, being described as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a country, a city in a unitary state, a city in a republic, a city in a social state and a city in a territory.

The earliest written record of Azureport dates to 1454, while the city's inception is recorded as 1539. Over the modern period the city has been part of several different states: it was part of the Myralun Empire from 1830-12-29 to 1956-03-04; of Myralunith from 1956-03-04 to 1956-11-06; of the Verdantia Free Republic from 1956-11-07 to 1957-01-04; and of The United Republic of Elvisharistan from 1960-03-18 to 1961-12-28. Separately, Azureport was located in the administrative territorial entity The United Republic of Elvisharistan from 1969-09-03 to 1971-02-09.

Azureport sits on the Tidal Reach, an adjacent sea and drainage basin, and is identified as a port settlement. The city is a member of the SyncSphere network (member since 2058) and is also a member of The Outliers Collective.

Corath, Elvishar, Myrathian and Qalvish are widely used languages in Azureport.

Azureport maintains twinning relationships with a number of other municipalities. Those partnerships include Altonia (from 2029-11-04), Aquilon City (from 2031), Bellgarn, Celestara (from 2035-10-26), Celestport (from 2004-07-01), Shianthor (from 2047-09-29), Eldoria (from 2018-03-07), Everlight (from 2014-09-17), Ignisport (from 1996), Jorvann (from 2035-04-29), Juniper Falls (from 2012-05-05), Lunathis (from 2045), Novarun (from 2043-06-21), Nythoria (from 2036-11-02), Pinehaven (from 2007-01-01), Rivenbrook, Solstice Bay (from 2032-03-25), Volenthis (from 2031-01-01), Vornath (from 2010), Vornexa (from 2049-10-01) and Zephyra (from 2041 until 2061-04-14).

Azureport has been described in multiple reference works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Elarian Liora Vespera (given name Liora; 1 January 1296 – 11 October 1361) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and was a member of the Elarian dynasty.

She was the daughter of Aythor Dougherty and Ylinth Swaby. Her siblings included Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elric Talanwyr, Thalor Casarez, Valorian Elarian, and Wyrlyn Fiedler.

Her life and role are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Caelan Fierro (born 3 June 2017) is a Gelanthian royal who serves as a military leader and holds the rank of general. She is also active in civil aviation and maritime roles, working as an aircraft pilot and flight attendant and serving as a sailor. Fierro works in Aetherdon and resides at Crystal Keep.

In her military career Fierro serves in the aide-de-camp and holds the rank of general. She received the Order of the Dusk Rose in 2058. Since 1 May 2058 she has used the honorific prefix Chief Aeloria.

Fierro represents Gelanthia in sport, competing in sailing and volleyball, and is a citizen of Gelanthia. She speaks Dennar and Velthar.

She is a member of the Graelith and Sylverian families, having joined both on 1 May 2058, and is married to Rhylaris Lisa since that same date. Her relatives include Elara Gelanthian, Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump, Jyris Palumbo and Ystara Michelle.

Fierro has black hair and dark brown eyes and is classified socially as royalty.

Alaric Silverthorne (born 1477 — died 30 August 1521) was a politician. He began his period of professional activity in 1495 and was active in public life thereafter. He spoke Therian.

He was the son of Adeline Thornfield Quenmar and Liora Everhart. His siblings included Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Inigo Valerian Hartwell, Kalyndra Tamay, Phyren Line, Ronan Ashford, Xerath Elisabeth and Zedry Sharifi.

Alaric Silverthorne died in Silverhold, a major city and episcopal see, on 30 August 1521 as the result of a homicide.

Inigo Verathorn (24 February 1283 – 11 January 1299) was a male individual. His given name was Inigo.

He was the son of Inigo Ostall Rynn and Xalorin Bermeo. Verathorn was part of a large sibling group that included Brystyne Schmitt, Damaris Elowen Hartley, Dymir Souza and Kalindor Mclaren; other siblings were Kynara Newell, Menyra Correa, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

He spoke Therian, a modern natural language. Verathorn died of natural causes.

Pembryn Mcpherson (1 October 1673 – 1 August 1714) was a Kaldorian painter best known for portrait work. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and worked primarily in the art of painting, producing portraits associated with the Verdantism movement.

Mcpherson was born in Lurendale and died in the same town. He trained under Jorian Broome and later taught others; his students included Tharyn Coats.

He spoke the Valorean Tongue and produced works that were exhibited and collected widely. Copyrights on his works have expired. Examples of institutions that hold his works include Curiosities Art Museum, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Harmony Space, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time, Treasures of Tomorrow, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Mcpherson's life and work are described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Wyler Deyoung (21 August 1748 – 29 July 1771) was a princess and a member of the nobility. She held the title of princess and, as indicated by contemporary records, was female.

She was the daughter of Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune. Her siblings included Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch, Jareth Susan, Quindor Brewster, Rynel Sawyer, and Velian Rock.

She died of puerperal disorders.

Cerynd Ayele (28 September 1828 – 13 March 1906) was a princess of the noble family Sablemoor and a politician. She was born at Maplewood Manor and spoke Malquari.

Born into Sablemoor, Cerynd’s place of birth was Maplewood Manor, a château that served as a family residence. She was known to use the Malquari language.

As a member of the Sablemoor nobility she held the title of princess and worked as a politician.

Cerynd Ayele was married to Sylas Thornfield on 28 January 1849; their marriage is recorded through 1870. She was the parent of ten children, among them Aldenor Valerius, Alderon Alamilla, Crownthal Jorvik, Gathorn Blanco, Halyra Chang, Helyndra Angeles, Lythorin Montano, Orylan Doyle, Sylas Everwood and Wynelle Briarwood.

Cerynd Ayele died on 13 March 1906.

Braxian Grabowski (1923-07-05 – 1984-12-10) was a Cynthera artist. She resided in Vynthera and spoke Velthar.

She was educated at Canvas Heights College. She married Eryx Valorian on 1965-06-04.

Works by Grabowski are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artful Explorations Museum, Cultural Saloon, Grendale Heritage Art Museum, Nexus National Museum and Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. Additional holdings include The Artful Bath, The Artisan's Gallery, The Artisphere, The Civic Repository, The Curatorial Corner, The Enlightenment Hall, The Local Heritage Hub., The Local Legacy Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts.

CopyDefender is listed as her copyright representative, although copyrights on her works have expired. She is described by Nebula Edition.

Prism Academy of Learning is an educational facility—a group of educational buildings—and an educational institution that provides education. It was founded in 1835.

The academy is named after Jyris Dexter, a person.

Malquari is a modern language indigenous to Ardentia. It is used across a number of countries, including Luminara State, Mystralyn, Orinthia, the Quolmaris Republic, Syldoria, Thalassia and Vyrland.

Typologically, Malquari is a fusional, adjective–noun language that relies on stress and is stress-timed. The language exhibits agreement as a core characteristic of its grammar. Its canonical word order favors adjective before noun.

The language has a richly inflected system. Noun cases include nominative, accusative, genitive and dative, and three grammatical genders are distinguished: masculine, feminine and neuter. Verbal morphology marks several tenses—present, perfect, future and preterite—and supports the indicative, imperative and subjunctive moods. Inflectional paradigms attested in Malquari include -(e)s/-, -(e)s/-e, -(e)s/s, -/(e)n, adjectival declension, n-declension and an n-declension with genitive s.

Malquari comprises multiple parts, among them Malquolyndra and Pyrendian. It is written in the Eldranth Script and uses capitalization for nouns. The language is studied within the field of theological languages.

Malquari has been described in a number of works, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Legendarium and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Grand Duke of Kytarathia was a noble title and historical position in the sovereign state of Kytarathia. The office was a form of monarch, instituted in 910 CE and dissolved on 12 May 1746.

The position applied to the jurisdiction of Kytarathia, and holders of the office directed Kytarathia.

Official residences associated with the Grand Duke included the Radiant Pavilion, used from 1568, and the Radiant Manor, used from 1575. The Radiant Pavilion is a palace and theatre building that is also a historic house museum and an independent museum, while the Radiant Manor is a palace.

The Baron of Varyndoria was a historical position and noble title that applied to the jurisdiction of Varyndoria and was associated with the country of Varyndoria. The title was created in 882 CE and was abolished on 1746-05-12. It was classified as a subclass of king and of monarch.

A number of individuals held the barony over the centuries. Early recorded holders in the medieval period included Varyndorian Varyndorax, who held the title from 1097-03-17 to 1132-11-13, followed by Varyndorian Varyndorov from 1133-5 to 1133-11-12. Reginald Varyndor held the barony from 1133-11-12 to 1136-10, after which Xindar Ortega served from 1136-10 to 1146-01-08. Calix Varyndor was position holder from 1146-01-08 to 1163-04-23, and Axton Varyndor from 1163-04-23 to 1192-05-24.

Later holders recorded in subsequent centuries include Caelan Varyndor, who held the title from 1476-02-21 to 1499-08-03. In the early modern period Celestria Valenwood served from 1581-12-14 to 1606-07-24, and Caelan Asterwood held the position from 1606-07-24 to 1664-03-27. Adeline Kytarathian Thornfield was position holder from 1664-03-27 to 1688-01-30.

In the eighteenth century the title was held by Caelan Kytarathius from 1724-02-06 to 1727-12-11. On 1728-02-13 two holders are recorded as beginning tenures: Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius, whose period ran from 1728-02-13 to 1741-08-03, and Kytar Celestria, who held the title from 1728-02-13 to 1733-12-28. Ulind Quispe held the barony from 1741-08-03 until 1746-05-01, shortly before the title was dissolved on 1746-05-12.

Valorian Dukedom was a historical position and a noble title in the country Valorian. It was established in 1581 and was a subclass of monarch. The dukedom was recorded as being dissolved on 1839-12-31.

The title was held by a succession of individuals. Hesper Kytarathius served from 1581-06-18 to 1586-01-28, followed by Kytar Vailson from 1586-01-28 to 1592-07-06. Kytarathia Celestrion held the dukedom from 1592-07-19 to 1597-11-17, and Kytara Zafrinia from 1597-11-17 to 1642-03-24. Caelan Asterwood occupied the position from 1642-03-24 to 1664-03-27, after which Adeline Kytarathian Thornfield served from 1664-03-27 to 1688-01-30.

In the eighteenth century and later holders, Caelan Kytarathius held the title from 1724-02-06 to 1727-12-11. Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius served from 1727-12-11 to 1741-03-08, and Kytar Celestria is recorded as holding the dukedom from 1728-02-13 to 1733-12-28. Ulind Quispe served from 1741-03-08 to 1753-08-01, followed by Irvin Caldwell from 1753-08-01 to 1766-06-11. Irvin Oathen held the position from 1766-06-11 to 1799-10-25, and Irvin Cyndorian Valorian is recorded as holding it from 1799-10-25 to 1840-01-01.

Serelys Scanlon (born 25 June 1967 in Luminara; died 29 March 2056) was a physicist and university teacher from Luminara State. He worked in condensed matter physics and theoretical physics, and his notable work centered on condensed matter physics. He spoke Myrathian as his native language and also used Therian and Velthar in his work and communication. Scanlon died of disease on 29 March 2056.

Scanlon was educated at Myralun Luminara Academy Press and earned the Obsidian Graduate Award in 1994. Helion Dollar supervised his doctoral work; Scanlon was a student of Dollar. He held the Quantum Research Fellowship as a professorship and was employed by Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies.

He was a member of several scholarly and publishing organizations, including Innovate Publishing Collective (becoming a member in 2031), Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 2039), and the Celestial Research Institute (from 10 May 2040). He also belonged to the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Scanlon received the Nova Research Prize in 2042 and was awarded the Zenith Merit Medal. His life and work are documented in DataGalaxy and in The Life Archive.

The Chronicles Keep is a castle located in the country of Syldoria. It functions as a museum, specifically a history museum, and also serves as a tourist attraction.

As a museum, it holds artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural, and historical importance. Its role as a history museum means its exhibitions cover aspects of human history for visitors.

Elias Blackwood (born 2380) is a fictional human character who appears in comics, written works and television within the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. He originates from the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and has been described in the magazine VividViews. The character is portrayed by Calix Vornell.

Within the narrative, Elias serves as a spaceship's surgeon and holds the rank of lieutenant. Across different installments he has been presented in multiple narrative roles, appearing as a protagonist, as a supporting character, and as a title character.

Elias Blackwood appears across a wide range of Eldoria Chronicles works. His appearances include Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey and The Forgotten Realms: The Awakening of Legends, as well as the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. He is also present in Stormwatch Chronicles: The Shattered Illusion and The Shattered Harmony, and in The Whispering Shadows: A New Journey.

He features in several Arcane and Celestial entries of the franchise, including The Arcane Chronicles, The Arcane Dimensions: A New Era and The Arcane Manifest, and The Celestial Echoes: The Awakening, The Celestial Enigma and The Celestial Heirloom. Other appearances include The Enigma of the Ethereal Guardians and The Enigma of the Silent Realms, plus The Lost Age of the Ancients, The Lost Dimensions: A Journey Beyond, The Lost Histories and The Lost Prophecies. The character also appears in the written work The Written Horizon.

Syldor Seely (25 August 1650 – 12 February 1710) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of count. She was born in Jorathia, a big city that served as a major regional center and residenz.

She was the daughter of Dorian Elwood and Peryn Solis. Syldor was one of eleven children and had ten siblings: among them were Bryndra Ballesteros and Bryndra Lino, as well as Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart, and Pyraen Tibbetts. Her other siblings included Quinlan Raxir, Ulyra Blood, Valandar Rochester, Viorelle Amaris, and Zafrina Althoria.

Hesthor Findlay (born 2 April 1994) is a Gelanthian princess, diplomat and multi-disciplinary creative and public figure. She holds the honorific prefix Knight Aerion and is a citizen of Gelanthia. Her work is based in Aetherdon.

Findlay is a prolific practitioner of many occupations. She is a writer and children's writer, poet and composer, as well as a translator and linguist. Alongside her literary and linguistic activity she works as a university teacher and historian, and is active as a social worker and philanthropist. Her artistic practice includes performance as a dancer and instrumentalist; she plays the pi nai, trumpet and xylophone. She is also an environmentalist and a military officer, holding the ranks of admiral and general.

Born into the Graelith and Sylverian families, Findlay is part of the royal social class. Her father is Lythran Kasper and her mother is Kalyndra Ayoub; she has three siblings, Gelanthian Athlorn, Nylaris Hurd and Rhylaris Lisa. She was named after Kalindor Christenson, Kalyndra Ayoub and Taryth Eugenio.

Findlay's native language is Dennar; she also speaks Malquari, Nythoria, Therian and Valtaric Standard Communication. Her ethnic affiliation is Gelanthian Ethnara. Her published works remain protected by copyrights.

Among recognitions she has received are the Opal Honor, the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Society of the Resolute Spirit. She was awarded the Order of the Dusk Rose in 2010, the Order of the Radiant Valor in 2035, and the Ethos Token in 2042.

Physically, Findlay has dark brown eyes and her hair is described as black and gray.

Solstice Art Storage is an art museum and museum of modern art housed in a museum building that also operates as a nonprofit organization and as a production company. The institution was established in 1968 and officially opened on November 7, 1968.

In its organizational relationships, Solstice Art Storage is represented by Music and Media Syndicate, a copyright collective. Solstice Art Storage in turn represents Alden Zyranen Tholmir and Idrisyl Rutkowski, who are persons.

The Therian Institute of Scientific Archives is an academy of sciences, an archive, and a national academy. It functions as a learned institution dedicated to the preservation and communication of permanent records alongside broader scholarly activities.

The institute began on 22 December 1705 and has the legal form of a national public establishment of an administrative nature. Since 22 August 1834 it has been part of the Society for the Promotion of Intellectual Engagement, a learned society.

The institute uses the Therian language, a modern natural language, for its communications. It is described by the work Infinite Reimagining, a version, edition or translation.

Lydan Paniagua (born 1017, died 20 February 1093) was a knyaz and politician who held citizenship of Eldarune. He belonged to the Crimsonvale noble family and served in political roles while bearing the title knyaz.

Born in Emberglow, Lydan was the son of Galenor Pinder. He was married to Liora Sableon. His children were Aelorin Espaillat, Brystor Gillen, Emberley Brightwood, Emberlyn Glowsmith, Eriath Anchondo, Gathorn Ralston, Jondar Sturgeon, Nyryth Marquina and Vyndel Lockwood.

Lydan was one of many siblings; his brothers and sisters included Aelestia Balbuena, Aelorian Coke, Davorin Witter, Elyndria Reeve, Indora Hermann, Kynthor Salcedo, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara, Taryn Hensley and Vesperyn Byrd. He spoke Zyphorian, a historical language.

His life and career are described in a number of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Resonance Translation.

Cole-Ren Kraylen Moor (29 August 1658 – 6 September 1722) was a jurist and politician. He received the Twilight Pendant and worked professionally in Nethoria; his active work period ran from 1704 until 1 January 1722.

Moor was born in Quentari and his given name was Cole-Ren. He was educated at Silver Birch College and spoke Therian.

He was a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy and of the Institute of Multilingual Studies; his membership in the Institute began in March 1706 and continued until 6 September 1722.

Moor is described in a number of sources, including Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Qylarans and The Midnight Library.

Pyrith Maciel (1 February 1975 – 7 April 2021) was a voice actor. He spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Maciel was born in Hightower and died there as well. Hightower is a metropolis described as a big city, a college town, a district capital, a financial centre and a residenz.

Quolens is a big city and city that functions as a college town and as a commune in several administrative contexts. They are described in a number of reference works and literary sources and have established international partnerships with several other municipalities.

History and administrative status
Quolens was part of the Velorian Dominion until 1545. From 1545 until 12 March 1899 they were part of the Hierocracy. Separately, records indicate that Quolens was located in the administrative territorial entity Hierocracy between 29 July 1317 and 19 June 1835.

Memberships and partnerships
Quolens became a member of the network SyncSphere in 2045. They maintain twinning arrangements with several municipalities: Delvoria (established 2 March 2001), Astralith (established 21 April 2023), and Nexopolis (established 30 July 2026), as well as with Qirith Harbor, Quellwyn and Rivenbrook.

Sources and descriptions
Quolens is described in a number of works and reference sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal, Qylarans, RefereX, Starlit Manuscript and The Midnight Library. These sources include encyclopedic and reference formats as well as written and literary works.

Elara Morvane (7 February 1885 – 5 May 1934) was a model and philanthropist. She spoke Therian, Velthar and Veyrith, and contributed to the written series Tides of Ink.

Her mother was Zynar Roland, and she was a sibling of Celestria Moonsong. She was also related to Eliana Morvane. Elara was the mother of Ellyra Yohannes, Elysia Morvane, Irvin Brevinson, Lyris Arciniega, Orilith Njie and Rhystar Mehta.

Her family name, Morvane, was in use from 1917. She was married to Aria Morvane from 26 March 1917 until her death on 5 May 1934.

Zedry Sharifi (1 January 1484 – 1 January 1507) was a male member of the nobility.

He was the son of Adeline Thornfield Quenmar and Liora Everhart. He belonged to a large family: his siblings were Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Inigo Valerian Hartwell, Phyren Line, Ronan Ashford, Varyth Lopezz and Xerath Elisabeth.

He died in Thistledown.

Elemental Odyssey is a video game from Cynthera. It is an action-adventure title that was announced on 29 January 2054 and published in 2054. The game was developed as a work based on the earlier video game Celestial Command.

Elemental Odyssey was released for the AstraBox and CipherSphere platforms. AstraBox is provided as a console model series, while CipherSphere is a branded computing platform and operating system delivered as proprietary software. The game is distributed digitally and made available through multiple outlets, including AppForge, AppSanctum, PixelMart and VaultPlay. AppForge functions as an app marketplace and digital distribution platform; AppSanctum operates as an app marketplace and video game distribution platform; PixelMart is an online shop and video game distribution platform; and VaultPlay provides digital rights management, a software repository and video game distribution services.

Gameplay supports both single-player and co-op modes. The narrative is set in a fictional country, with the primary narrative location given as Calidore. Calidore is depicted as a major urban centre and national capital, characterized in the game’s setting as a metropolis, megacity and global financial centre and the largest city in that setting.

The game’s language of work or name includes a range of regional and written forms. These include Eldorathian and Kynthor, as well as Malquari, Myrathian, Ralith, Therian and Thesvian. The release also makes use of the Valorean Tongue, Veldrith, Velthar and Xarnum, and employs the Valtarian Glyphic Script as a written system.

Tempest Ridge was both a theater of war and a war. It is recorded as beginning on 22 June 1980. A point in time associated with the event is 25 May 1984, and its end is recorded as 7 May 1984.

The conflict is documented as having two principal causes: the historical period known as Eternal Reign and racism. The Eternal Reign is also listed among the participants. Other participants named in accounts of Tempest Ridge include Cyndoria and Terranova.

Tempest Ridge took place across multiple regions. It is located in Astringia, Jorathia, Lunarisia, Nexaris Celestia and the Sylvarian Expanse. Astringia is identified as a peninsula and as a cultural and historical region; Jorathia is identified as a continent and part of the world; Lunarisia, Nexaris Celestia and the Sylvarian Expanse are identified as geographic regions.

The conflict is recorded as having effects on a number of states and regions: Astringia, Isolonia, Lunarisia, the Syldoria Veldrith People's Republic, the Sylvarian Expanse and Veridonia. Isolonia is identified as a historical sovereign state; the Syldoria Veldrith People's Republic is identified as a people's republic, a communist regime and a historical country; Veridonia is identified as a counterintelligence state, a historical country, a satellite state and a state.

Contemporary summaries of Tempest Ridge appear in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, which is described as both a national encyclopedia and a universal encyclopedia.

Hesper Caldren (1712-08-06 – 1741-12-16) was a Cyntheran military officer and noble who held the rank of admiral and bore the title of duke.

Born on 1712-08-06, his given name was Hesper. He was the son of Caelan Kytarathius and had nine siblings: Adeline Everhart, Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Kytar Celestria, Mistran Grim and Ulind Quispe.

A career military personnel, Alden rose to the rank of admiral. He was a citizen of Cynthera and spoke Velthar. He died on 1741-12-16.

Lorian Thorne (born 30 September 1944 in Grandview; died 8 August 2035) was a Cynthera physicist and university teacher whose work focused on solid-state physics, semiconductors, alloys and photographic emulsion. He spoke Velthar and was commonly known by the given name Lorian.

Education and early career
Thorne attended Aspen Grove Academy before studying at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. He completed his doctorate under the supervision of Gathryn Wooten in 1969.

Academic work and memberships
As a university teacher and researcher, Thorne supervised doctoral students, including Paylan Anchondo in 1976. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and of the Cognition Coalition. From 1996 he was affiliated with Frontier Knowledge Productions, and from 2003 he belonged to the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Research fields
Thorne’s research spanned physics broadly, with particular emphasis on solid-state physics and semiconductors, and extended into applied materials areas such as alloy development and photographic emulsion.

Honours and awards
Over the course of his career Thorne received numerous honours. He was awarded the Chroma Medal in 1980, the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series recognition in 1990, and both the Quantum Visionary Medal and the Scientific Odyssey award in 1992. He received the Elysium Science Medal in 2011 and the Nova Research Prize in 2016; previously he had been nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1997. He also received the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence and was granted the Celestial Honor, an award that conferred a noble title.

Legacy and sources
Thorne is described in the DataGalaxy multimedia database and on the biographical record The Life Archive. His membership in learned societies and publishing organizations, and his awards in the fields of physics and science, mark his contributions to research and higher education in Cynthera.

Xarathor is a position — a social role with a set of powers and responsibilities within an organization. It applies to the jurisdiction of the country Cynthera and was established on 1 January 1840.

Cynthera is a colonial power, an island country and a sovereign state.

Cyndrel Bhattacharya (28 September 1907 – 18 June 1962) was born to Uryth Lena. He lived from 28 September 1907 until his death on 18 June 1962.

He had nine siblings, among them Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Galenith Castrejon, Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel.

Orinth Mc (7 September 1918 – 15 June 1958) was a male military personnel who held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland and Nephronia. A member of the Fenrith dynasty, he is recorded as having been active in the mid-20th century before his death in 1958.

Born on 7 September 1918, Orinth Mc was a scion of the noble Fenrith family and the son of James Carter. They were part of a sizable sibling group that included Brystar Cueto, Elyndra Ashcraft, Elysia Nephronis, Galdir Oseguera, Verenth Paredes, and Ylinda Cota.

Mc’s professional life was in the military; he is described broadly as military personnel. He held dual citizenship with Eldoria-Emberland, a historical country and kingdom, and Nephronia, a sovereign state and colonial power.

In language and personal matters, Malquari was his native language, and he also spoke Therian. He was male and was homosexual.

The National Sanctuary of Visual Arts is a national art museum maintained by a national authority. The institution was established on 9 June 1986 and was officially opened in 2016.

Works associated with the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. The museum also maintains a subsidiary, the Museum of Memory, which functions as an archive and as an art and museum library.

The National Sanctuary of Visual Arts received the Honorary Valor Pendant. A significant event associated with the museum was a claim for restitution of an artwork. It should not be confused with The Curated Dreamscape, which is a separate art museum.

Illystria Esmeralda (born 14 September 1976 in Eldoria) is an architect and politician whose work is principally associated with the field of architecture. He is known for the notable work The Ephemeral Archive and has been active as recently as 1 January 2052. His published output is represented by IntellectProtect and his works are protected by copyright.

Esmeralda has held employment with the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic from 2004 to 2007. He has worked in Bryston and Thundoria and is an independent politician. He is a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Preservation Society for Creative Works, and Seraphim Art House.

Examples of institutions that hold Esmeralda’s work include the Creative Spark Foundation, Solstice Art Storage, and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. He is described in the DataGalaxy multimedia database and web portal.

Esmeralda speaks Thesvian, his native language, and also speaks Therian. Over the course of his career he has received several honors: the Arcane Order on 24 March 2029, the Boundless Art Recognition in 2034, and the Golden Aurora Class in 2039.

Isidore Valenhart (given name Isidore; 27 September 1957 – 14 October 2023) was a Cyntheran astronomer, astrophysicist, physicist and researcher whose field of work was astronomy. He was born in Larkspur and was a citizen of Cynthera. He spoke Velthar and was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University.

Valenhart was educated at Meadowbrook College, Quantum College of Higher Education and Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute. Over the course of his career he held memberships in a number of learned and scientific organizations: he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 20 March 1991, joined the Spectrum Institute of Learning in 2010, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2013 and Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2014, and he was also a member of the Cognition Coalition and the Unity Scientific Society.

He received multiple honours, including the Chroma Medal in 1993 and the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence in 1997. In 2003 he was awarded both the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series and the Veritas Medallion. He later received the Quantum Visionary Medal in 2012 and, in 2013, he was a recipient of both the Nova Research Prize and the Solar System Achievement Prize. He had previously been nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 2002. He was also a recipient of the Celestial Honor.

Valenhart is described in the Encyclical of Identities and in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Pylar Bassett (21 June 1820 – 25 April 1879) was a male astronomer, politician, statistician and university teacher. He was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic and later worked for both Catalyst Polytechnic and Silver Birch College. In 1865 he held the position of president from 1 January to 31 December.

Bassett’s scholarly work focused on analytical mechanics, geometry, mathematical analysis, mechanics and probability theory. He spoke and wrote in Therian, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

His doctoral advisors included Ilindra Cardwell and Selthar Kyle; Bassett was also a student of Selthar Kyle. Among his doctoral students were Jareth Breslin (1853), Nythor Lear (1866), Elian Thompson (1875) and Wryken Yilmaz.

Bassett was an active member of a number of learned and scientific organizations. He belonged to the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Aurora Academy and the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, and he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute beginning 12 March 1857. He joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives in 1851, became a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences in 1865, and was associated with the Thundorian Science Archive Database from 20 January 1872.

He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and was awarded the Elysium Science Medal on 1 January 1871. Bassett is described in a number of reference works and compilations, including the Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, the Labyrinthine Journal, the Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, The Life Archive, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Pylar Bassett died on 25 April 1879 and was buried at Memory Lane.

Infinite Reimagining is a version, edition, or translation of a work presented as an encyclopedia. It takes the form of an encyclopedic dictionary, combining the structural conventions of an encyclopedia with the concise, definitional entries typical of dictionaries. The work was published in 1959.

The text is written in Velthar, a modern natural language. Infinite Reimagining is in the public domain.

Ilyra Campos (born 18 September 1791; died 10 January 1872) was a male university teacher and writer whose work focused on number theory. He spoke and wrote in Therian, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Campos was educated at Silver Birch College. He worked for the Académie des Sciences Ethiques beginning in 1834 and later took a post at Catalyst Polytechnic starting in 1855. He held the position of president from 1844 to 1845.

He was an active member of several learned and scientific organizations: the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (joining on 30 March 1822), the Celestial Research Institute (joining on 30 April 1828), and the Cognition Coalition (joining in 1871).

Campos received multiple honors during his career, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Innovative Thought Excellence Award (awarded in 1859), and the Noble Valorian Order.

He is described in a variety of sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Lorian Thalor (born 1861, died 1950) was a Cyndorian scholar and polymath who worked across the social and natural sciences. He bore the honorific prefix Lord Vesperin and his given name was Lorian. Born in Starlight Cove, he was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He was male.

Thalor’s work spanned anthropology and probability theory, and he held a wide range of occupations: anthropologist, geneticist, physiologist, sociologist, philosopher, eugenicist, inventor, explorer, photographer and writer. He is noted for the bean machine among his notable works.

Educated at the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning (beginning October 1878), the Collegiate Haven Public Research University and the Quantum College of Higher Education, Thalor later joined the Celestial Research Institute on 7 June 1899. The Celestial Research Institute serves as an academy of sciences and learned society and also operates as an open-access publisher.

Thalor received several honors during his lifetime. He was awarded the Celestial Excellence Fellowship beginning on 6 July 1899, the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1925, the Celestial Honor on 26 June 1948 and the Elysium Science Medal on 1 January 1949.

He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab and wrote in Velthar; he was a native speaker of Velthar and used that language for his writings. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Thalor has been described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, ReadRealm, SoulScript, Tales from the Abyss and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea. His known relative is Caspian Windrider.

Helynd Ayers (25 CE – 9 October 58 CE) was a Chronorian military officer, politician, poet and writer who served Arcandor during the Valdoria Epoch. He held a number of public offices, including the positions of Qelrion, Thalira Director and quaestor, and wrote in Nythoria.

Early life and family
Helynd Ayers was born in Seraphim Bay and belonged to the Thorian dynasty and the gens Dundrak; his cognomen was Aeloria. His recorded parents were Liora Buell and Ramira Darcy (listed as fathers) and Cameron Kilpatrick (listed as mother). He had at least two siblings, Jaxter Buell and Klyndra Colmenero, and was married to Lysandor Gerges. Ayers was the parent of Aelath Jesse, Brynara Lacayo, Helynd Aeloria, Hesperyn De La Torre, Lucius Aeloria Maximus, Leysa Vorin and Rynira Prior.

Career
Ayers combined military service with political office and literary activity. He served Arcandor and held the offices of Qelrion, Thalira Director (an elective office) and quaestor. As a writer and poet he produced works in Nythoria, the language he both spoke and wrote.

Works and legacy
Ayers’s writings were composed in Nythoria; the copyrights on his works have expired. His life and work are described in a number of sources, among them Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

Death and burial
Helynd Ayers died in 58 CE (recorded specifically as 58-10-09) and was buried in the Aelricus Mausoleum. He held citizenship of Chronoria throughout his life.

SabaGalend Films is a film production company founded in 1968 by Galend Saba. It is headquartered in Draxoria.

Legally, SabaGalend Films is organized as a public company and functions as a subsidiary. The company is owned by Saba Vision Media Group, a media conglomerate and public company.

SabaGalend Films operates in the film industry and the movie theater sector and produces films. It is also the owner of SabaGalend Animation Studios, an animation studio and film production company.

Nylara Burleson (31 May 1508 – 13 December 1560) was a duke and sovereign from Eldoria-Emberland. Born in Valdor and dying there, they spoke Veyrith and served as a ruling noble during the mid-sixteenth century.

As sovereign, Burleson held the Duchy of Nephronia from 25 October 1534 until 13 December 1560. They bore the noble title of duke while occupying that hereditary position.

Burleson's family life included three marriages: to Zythor Monk (6 October 1536–23 August 1537), to Zethrin Sim (30 August 1539–7 March 1556), and to Phexus Leite (16 July 1557–13 December 1560). They were the parent of nine children: Brynith Hebert, Davorin Alder, Fynessa Candela, Galindor Fee, Galyn Patiño, Pellin Feller, Pyrion Gipson, Uthara Nagy, and Valenor Valles.

They received multiple honors during their life, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Burleson died of the plague in Valdor on 13 December 1560.

Their life and career are documented in a variety of sources, including DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), ItemVerse (a catalogue, digital library and website), Infinitopedia (an encyclopedic dictionary), Legendarium (a written work), The Midnight Library (a literary work), Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation (versions or editions), and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Celestial Rework is a version, edition, or translation of The Solstice Chronicles, a literary work and series of creative works. It was published in Thesvian and first issued in 1589 in Caelumport, a capital city and big city. The work is in the public domain.

The edition is dedicated to Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin.

The principal subjects of Celestial Rework are Aelith Pacheco, Aelorian Arriola and Alysor Perez Perez, alongside Draal Minaya and Elirian Appel. Also listed as main subjects are Freylar Farrell, Idrisyl Mckoy and Irylin Monreal, as well as Wyrden Rubino, Xenith Usher and Yndira Sant. They are presented together as the primary topics of the work.

Wyndan Byers (2 June 1487 – 11 January 1533) was a Caelumorian painter whose work was in the art of painting. Born and died in Caelumport, he was a citizen of Caelumoria and worked primarily in Thesvian. His creative output is now out of copyright, with copyrights on his works having expired.

Byers trained under Ryniel Crawley before establishing his own practice. He in turn taught a number of pupils, among them Ferith Zermeno, Pyraen Irish and Nylen Quiñonez; Nylen Quiñonez was also his child. Artist files documenting his life and work are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Works by Byers are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Aurora Art Gallery; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Cultural Canvas Museum; Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation; Ethos Gallery; Harmony Exhibit Pavilion; Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures; National Legacy Gallery; National Museum of Innovative Expression; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Charitable Canvas; The Chronicles Keep; The Creative Convergence Gallery; The Curator's Corner; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; The Historical Nexus; The Storytellers' Studio; The Visionary Experience; and Verdant Haven.

Byers is described in a variety of sources, among them DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. He died in Caelumport on 11 January 1533 of malaria; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Arcane Labyrinth is an episode of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction work set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is presented in color.

Directed by Axton Mercer and written by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts, the episode was edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances were provided by Garanth Smit, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Arabella Skye, Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill and Elysia Dreamweaver.

The Arcane Labyrinth was first performed on 6 November 2041 and published on 27 September 2042. It was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync.

Within its series sequence, the episode follows The Enigma of the Forgotten Guardians and is followed by The Ethereal Conundrum.

Lyvian Mensah (19 August 1960 – 24 October 2030) was a writer and producer whose work spanned film, television and novels. He began his professional career in 1993 and was principally known for his contributions to screenwriting and science fiction.

Mensah worked across multiple roles in the entertainment industry, serving as a film and television screenwriter as well as a television producer, film producer and executive producer. He was also a novelist and science fiction writer, and at times worked as an aircraft pilot. His field of work was screenwriting.

Among his notable works were Eldoria Chronicles and the character Freya Wilder. Freya Wilder is a fictional human character who appears across different media, including film, literature, television and video games.

Mensah received the Luminary Stage Awards on 1 January 2006 and was later credited with the Exceptional Merit Recognition on 1 January 2046. His career and credits are described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

He participated in the conflict Aegis Warfare. Mensah spoke Velthar and identified with agnostic atheism, and he was associated with the atheism movement.

Mensah was married to Glinthar Sylvester from 6 August 2008 until 1 January 2030. He died on 24 October 2030 of heart failure; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Jethor Sutton (born 4 October 1511, died 1592) was a Velorian Dominion artist whose practice encompassed painting, printmaking and book production. He worked across a range of media as a painter, drawer, copper engraver, printmaker, designer and publisher, and his primary field of work was the art of painting. Sutton’s paintings included mythological subjects, nudes, portraits and religious scenes, and he was associated with the movement Poetic Urbanism. He spoke Malquari and was influenced by Aralyn Palomera and Zephyros Geffrard. His works are no longer under copyright protection, as copyrights on works have expired.

Sutton’s career included a period of work in Lunathis from 1540 to 1543 and later activity in Windermere, where he also died and was buried. He served as court painter from 1544 until 1586. Among his pupils and family connections, Xilara Vanegas was both his child and one of his students; Jethor Sutton is explicitly distinguished from Xilara Vanegas. He also had a relative, Hesperan Sides. Sutton was male.

Sutton’s works and related materials are widely held. Artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Works by Sutton are in the collections of the Alchemy Arts Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Artyndor Cultural Institute and the Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Other holders include the Branash Cultural Collective, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Canvas of Dreams and Canvas of Dreams Gallery, the Celestial Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation.

Additional institutional collections containing his works are Cultura Artopolis, the Cultural Treasures Museum, the Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records, Ethereal Exhibits and Exhibitarium. Holdings extend to the Harmathia Art Repository, Haven of Expression, Historical Horizons, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Art Hall and Legacy Art Sanctuary.
