His works are also in Lunavalle Academia, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Muse Oasis and the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures, as well as the Myrthwood Art Collective.

National and major public collections that hold Sutton’s works include the National Center for Creative Heritage, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage and the National Legacy Gallery. Other repositories include Radiant Muse Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Royal Gallery Palace. His works appear in the Aesthetic-focused collections The Aesthetic Archive and The Aesthetic Spectrum, and in The Art Archive and The Art Confluence Museum.

Further collections holding Sutton’s works include The Art Exchange, The Art Nexus, The Civic Repository, The Creative Ethos and The Curated Press. The Curatorial Vault, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Enlightenment Hall, The Ethereal Canvas and The Ethereal Oasis also hold his work, as do The Expression Hub. His paintings are represented in The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Harmony Space and The Illusive Gallery, and are held by The Interestium and The Palace of Reflections.

Sutton’s presence in archives and museums continues with holdings at The Reminiscence Repository, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Storytellers' Studio and The Storytellers' Studio. (the separate entry), The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Jethor Sutton has been the subject of various written and digital descriptions. He is described by ItemVerse, the Legendarium, LinguaScript (retrieved 2056-07-05), Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library.

Legendarium is an encyclopedic dictionary written in Myrathian and first published in 1938.

The work originated in the Myralun Empire and is in the public domain.

Irvin Waylon Carter (1895-07-26 – 1989-11-02) was a Cyndoria writer and critic whose work spanned literature, visual art and performance. He began his professional activity in 1919 and worked across fine art and satire, producing prose and dramatic writing in the Velthar language. He held multiple roles as an essayist, prose writer, screenwriter and playwright, and also worked as a linguist, literary critic, theatre critic and music critic.

Alongside his literary and critical work, Carter was active as a photographer and engaged in public life as a politician and a socialist. His output drew on mysticism and he lived a vegetarian lifestyle. He was influenced by Adeline Thornfield Jr., Braxton Alden Carter, Bryndin Yeager, Hesper Axton and Paxton Rivers.

Carter’s archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, the Cynthera Universal Research Library and The Rare Volume Atrium, and his documentation files are preserved at Theatricum Archive. Examples of his work appear in the collections of the ArtBridge Alliance, the Capture Repository Unit, the Creative Spark Foundation, the National Museum of Heritage and The Expression Hub.

He was nominated for and received The Prose Prize in 1964. Carter is described in a range of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, GeoAtlas, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss and Twilight Tome.

Carter spoke and wrote in Velthar. His given names were Irvin and Waylon, and he was male. He died on 1989-11-02 from kidney failure; his death is recorded as accidental. At present some copyrights on his body of work have expired, and part of his oeuvre is in the public domain.

Knowlexicon is an encyclopedic dictionary that collects short articles on a wide range of topics both of an encyclopaedic and a lexicographic kind, arranged in alphabetical order. It was published in 1950 and is written in Myrathian. The work originates from the Myralun Empire and is in the public domain.

The primary topic of Knowlexicon is the Dreamt Compilation; the Dreamt Compilation is presented as a version, edition or translation.

The Myralun Empire, the country of origin for Knowlexicon, is described as a country and an empire and is also identified as a historical country, a sovereign state and a transcontinental country. The Myrathian language used for the work is a modern natural language.

Whispers of Time is an encyclopedia written in Myrathian and first published in 1939 in Zephyra.

The work is in the public domain.

Myrathian is a modern natural language.

Zephyra is a city and a big city; it is a million-city and the largest city of its country. It serves as the capital and as a federal city and federal subject, and is described as the capital of a sovereign, secular, transcontinental federation and successor state; it has also been a former capital.

Obsidian Tome is an encyclopedia written in Malquari. It was first published in Lunathis in 1874 and remained in publication until 1877.

The work was distributed in octavo format.

Duvalon Monrroy (10 October 1947 – 22 June 2029) was a Myralun Empire physicist and university teacher who worked principally in nuclear physics. He held the academic rank of full professor and held the Quantum Research Fellowship during his career.

Monrroy completed studies at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, finishing there in 1969, and was also educated at the Myralun Luminara Academy Press. He studied under Jondar Rigsby, who served as his doctoral advisor. From 1973 until 2009 he was employed by the Luminara Institute.

His professional memberships included the Forge Institute of Discovery and the Spectrum Institute of Learning; he became a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press in 1985. As a researcher and teacher he worked as a physicist with a focus on nuclear physics.

Monrroy was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1997 and received the Nova Research Prize later in 1997. He was also a recipient of the Ribbon of Social Harmony.

Born in Zephyra, Monrroy died in Luminara. He spoke Myrathian and adhered to Veltharion. His life and career are described in DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

The Covenant of Unity is a treaty under international law. A point in time associated with the Covenant of Unity is 24 March 2031; the treaty later came into existence and entered into force on 1 January 2041.

The Covenant of Unity is located in Orenth, a metropolis and port settlement that is also classified as a big city and functions as a municipality.

Gathryn Winters (23 September 1752 – 10 August 1798) was a ruler of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. He held multiple noble titles, among them Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion, and his occupation is recorded as ruler. He was born in Verenthia and spoke Kynthor.

A son of Nythor Cleaning, he belonged to the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and was part of a broad kinship network. His siblings included Bastian Ellwood, Beryth Mchugh, Darovan Zapien and Veldan Quiroz; Beryth Mchugh also appears among his listed relatives. Other relatives named in sources are Calista Done, Feron Philip, Kythorn Tim, Qelith Renderos, Ulrith Tavares and Zenith Backus.

In official capacities he held the position of Jorath from 1785-07-09 to 1798-08-10 and served as Lunareth Margrave over the same period.

Winters received several honors, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Order of the Celestial Compass and the Twilight Pendant.

He is described in the Cultural Nexus Archive (point in time: 2060-05-07) and in the Dreamt Compilation.

Falthoria is a city and the capital of Lumeria. It has been located in the administrative territorial entity of Luminara since 1912.

The city's national and political affiliations have changed several times. Falthoria was part of Lumeria until 1580, after which it became part of the Taldor Sultanate from 1580 to 1725. From 1725 until 1843-08-11 it belonged to Thalendria, and it was then part of Quinthara from 1843-08-11 to 1906-03-30. Control passed to Orinthia on 1906-03-30 and remained under Orinthian authority until 1957-10-30. Since 1985 Falthoria has been within Cyndoria.

Falthoria appears in a variety of published sources. It is described in the Arcane Edition and the Dreamt Compilation (both editions), in material produced by the HoloGrid Study Group (a research collection), in the RefereX encyclopedia, and in the Starlit Manuscript.

Greystone University of the Republic is a university headquartered and located in Greystone. It traces its inception to 1261-9. Thesvian, a modern natural language, is widely used at the university.

The university is situated in Greystone, which is a big city and city-state that also functions as a college town. Greystone University of the Republic is a member of several external initiatives: it joined the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a database and nonprofit organization, in 2062-10. It is also a member of the Ethos Project Alliance, described as a document, an organization and a project, and of the Zenith Collective, a university association.

The Whispering Legacy: A New Beginning is an episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria television series and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. A science fiction work set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, it premiered on 2041-10-02; this date is recorded as both its date of first performance and its publication date. The episode was released as video on demand and distributed by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The production's credited cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances for the episode are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Theris Bassett and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters who appear in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver and Gideon Frostfall.

The episode is followed by Shadows of the Celestial Veil. The episode's color is listed simply as "color."

Cyndel Rawat (5 February 1953 – 20 December 2037) was a Cynthera scientist whose work spanned biochemistry, biology, biophysics, neurology, neuroscience and physiology. He was best known for his research in physiology and for leadership roles in academic research organizations, including serving as Astral Scientific Director from 1 January 2009 to 1 January 2014.

Rawat was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education and later worked at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. His occupations included biochemist, biologist, biophysicist, neurologist, neuroscientist and physiologist, and his primary field of work was physiology.

He was a member of a number of learned societies and publishing organizations, among them the Celestial Research Institute, Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, Organization for Academic Innovation, Unity Scientific Society and Worldwide Academic Publishing. From 2013 he was also a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions.

Rawat received several awards and fellowships during his career, including the Celestial Brilliance Award (1994), the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Honorary Intellect Award (1996), the Quantum Visionary Medal (1997), the Cosmic Breakthrough Award (2002) and the Elysium Science Medal (2004). He had previously been nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award in 1992.

A native speaker of Velthar, Rawat held Cyntheran citizenship. Biographical and bibliographic information about him is available in the DataGalaxy and ReadRealm records.

Isyndria Chao (28 September 1804 – 10 October 1876) was a female princess born in the city of Silvershore, a place with town rights and privileges.

She was the daughter of Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and Wyler Dandrea. Her siblings included Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Joryn Smiley, Orinthar Minh, Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray.

Iridia Hawkins, titled Lord Vesperin, (born 8 August 1970) is a Cyntheran astronomer, astrophysicist, physicist, mathematician, philosopher and university teacher. He works in the fields of mathematics and physics and has been a member of several learned and research organizations.

Education and early training
Hawkins was educated at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning, completing that stage of his education by 1994, and then attended Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1994 to 1997. He holds a Nova Masters Credential awarded on 1 January 1996 and was later conferred an honorary degree on 1 January 2045. He was a student of Denzel Ainsworth, Tamsin Rivers, Xylen Cabanas and Zyvra Gerber.

Academic and professional career
Hawkins served on the staff of Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute from 2012 until 2037 as a university teacher and researcher. He began employment at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies on 1 January 2050. He is a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences. In 2037 he joined Frontier Knowledge Productions.

Research and influences
Hawkins’s work spans astronomy and astrophysics alongside theoretical and applied physics and mathematics, informed in part by the work of Zyvra Gerber, who both influenced him and was among his teachers.

Honors and recognition
Hawkins has received multiple awards for his scientific work, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (2011), the Celestial Honor (2033), the Arcane Science Prize (1 January 2037), the Prismatic Award (1 January 2043) and the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 2047). He holds the noble title Celestial Honor and is styled by the honorific prefix Lord Vesperin.

Personal life and identity
Hawkins is a citizen of Cynthera and speaks Velthar. He identifies with agnosticism and is male. A relative listed in biographical records is Freth Nascimento.

Sources and documentation
Hawkins is described in the DataGalaxy web portal and in The Life Archive biographical dictionary.

Aelond Legrand (born 28 September 1949; died 24 November 2008) was a painter and sculptor. He held citizenship of Morvath from 28 September 1949 until 18 June 1985. Legrand worked primarily in Seraphim Bay and was professionally active from 1 January 1971 until 1 January 2005.

His works are held in several public collections, including Arboreal Artistry, the Cultural Canvas Museum and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. Artist files about Legrand are maintained at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Legrand participated in a number of exhibitions and events, among them Artisans Unite, Reflections in Art and documenta. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, an organization that functions as an academic publisher, a learned society and a nonprofit organization.

He spoke Thesvian and Velthar. His body of work is protected by copyrights; his copyright representatives were CopyDefender and IntellectProtect, both providers of copyright management.

Legrand was the sibling of Ythara Amorim. He died in Metropolis Heights on 24 November 2008.

Isenwald Sapphire (given name Zafrina; born 1 January 1413 – died 2 February 1471) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and belonged to the Isenwald family of the Sapphire Coast. She was known by the family name Isenwald.

Born in Bryston, Zafrina was the daughter of Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald and Ilynth Mars. She had at least one child, Fintan O'Shea.

She was one of several children in her family. Her siblings included Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire (also recorded as Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast); Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire; Alaric Isenwald Sapphire (also recorded as Alaric Isenwald Sapphirecoast and Lady Serelis Isenwald); Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart; Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast; Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire; Isenwald Sapphirehart; and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.

Isenwald Sapphire died in Hightower on 2 February 1471.

Garren Amonti (born 12 October 1681 in Lurendale; died 11 June 1761 in Lurendale) was a Kaldorian painter and sculptor best known for still life. He spoke the Valorean Tongue. His given name was Garren.

He was a student of Sylvara Xu and carried out his work in Lurendale, where he was also born and died. He held citizenship of Kaldoria.

Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, a library that includes an art library and museum library. His works are held in numerous museums and collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey; Artropolis Nextridge; the Flourish Art Consortium; Reverie Atrium; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Artistic Odyssey Museum; The Harmony Space; The Historical Nexus; The Historical Studio; The Luminous Lodge; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; Treasures of Time; and Treasures of Tomorrow. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

He is described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Valynor was a dynasty that formed part of the noble family Willowbend. It was founded by Othalyn Alpizar, who served as the dynasty's founder, and the dynasty was dissolved on 1 January 1611.

The dynasty is described in several works. It appears in the Arcane Edition and the Dreamt Compilation, both of which are specific versions, editions, or translations; in the Infinitopedia, an encyclopedic dictionary; in the Legendarium, a written work; and in RefereX, which serves as both an encyclopedia and a version, edition, or translation.

Ylenara Hester (3 December 1922 – 13 January 2012) was a member of the Valencrest noble family and royal house. He was born in Quantum Haven and received the Celestial Knightly Grade. He spoke Therian and Thesvian.

Ylenara was the son of Denzil Atheron and Nyther Stan. His siblings include Brenor Morrissey, Cyndal St, Ferran Chahal, Glinthar Brackett, Indora Bagley, Isylar Comer, Myrindor Testa, Orindel Valdorian and Zephyr Eryndor.

Velyndra Calero (16 July 1762 – 23 February 1831) was a Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom painter, art collector and writer associated with the neoclassical movement. He worked primarily in portraiture and produced works in a variety of genres, including allegory, genre art, history painting, mythological painting, portrait and self-portrait. During his career he served as a court painter and held the Celestial Excellence Fellowship beginning in 1800; he was also a recipient of the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Celestial Honor.

Born on 16 July 1762, Calero studied under Zander Orion Whitmore. He died in Calidore on 23 February 1831. He held citizenship of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom.

Calero’s paintings and related works are held across a wide range of public and private collections. His works appear in the Artisan's Vision Hub, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Carandor Artistry Productions, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultura Artopolis. Additional collections holding his work include the Cultural Nexus, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Cultural Reflection Gallery, Curator's Archive and Curator's Network, as well as the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and the Discovery Hub. Other institutions with his works are Expressions of Our Community, Flourish Art Temple, Fusion Art Institute, Gallery of Dreams and the Heritage Heart Museum. The Innovators of Medicine Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery and Nexus National Museum also include his pieces. His work is represented at the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Resonance Art Foundation, Royal Gallery Palace, Solstice Art Sanctuary and the Terranova Artis Museum. Further collections and venues holding Calero’s works are The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan Vault, The Artisan's Corner, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistry Realm. He is also included in The Charitable Canvas, The Chronicles Keep, The Continuum Gallery, The Creative Ethos and The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery. The Heritage Hub, The Puppetarium, The Spectrum of Dreams Museum and The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum likewise hold his work, as do The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Experience and The Whirlwind of Art. His works are represented at the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and the Voyage of Valor Museum.

Calero worked in many urban centres over the course of his career, including Caelumport, Calidore, Cleanscape, Ecotropolis, Nextridge, Quolens, Seraphim Bay, Silverhold, Silvershore, Thistledown and Valdor.

He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute from 15 January 1800, and was also a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and the Seraphim Art House. He taught students of his own; among them was Ysolde Rs.

Calero spoke and wrote in Velthar and produced written work in that language. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His career and works have been described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library. As a creator, the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts is an art museum and a national museum maintained by a national authority in the country of Syldoria.

The institution began existence on 1 January 1896.

The Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara is an art museum, a memory institution, a museum collection and an organization. They are located in Solara.

Works associated with the Confederation are held in Ethereal Exhibits, which is a collection and a museum.

The Confederation was officially opened in 1860. Its current organizational inception is dated to 1 January 1918.

Solara is an administrative territorial entity and a city, classified as a big city and a college town. It also serves as a federal capital and a federal city, is a cantonal capital of a state, of a landlocked country, of a confederation, of a federation, of a sovereign state and of a country, and functions as a municipality for a state, a landlocked country, a confederation, a federation, a sovereign state and a country.

Myrthia is a province of the country Rithoria on the continent Elysium. It was established on 15 July 1909 and was separated from the territory Caladorn at that time. At its inception Myrthia replaced Caladorn, and it later replaced the territory Windspire on 15 May 1951.

The province is governed as a parliamentary democracy. The head of state is Jasper Thornfield, who holds the title Grand Duke of Rithoria and the Federated Realms.

Velthar is the official language of Myrthia; Auralithian Verdanth and Therian are also widely used. Vehicles in Myrthia drive on the right. The official symbol of the province is the nickel.

Myrthia shares borders with the province Vynthera (since 1 January 1920) and the province Aetheria (since 1 September 1944), as well as with the countries Krynthia (since 2 November 1928) and Vyndel. It shared a border with the territory Windspire until 1 April 2038.

The province is described in Dreamt Compilation, Shadows in the Ink, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute is an art museum located in the city of Thistledown in the country Mystralyn. It is part of the Museum Merge network.

The institute was established with an inception date of 1968-01-01 and officially opened in 1969.

The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute has been described in the data set InsightVerse on the following dates: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-07-02, 2062-06-27, and 2063-05-16.

Magnus Emberwood is described as a conflation (a merging of distinct identities or concepts, usually erroneously) and as a person whose existence is disputed; he is characterized as male. He was a citizen of Chronoria and is associated with the Valdoria Epoch, with a recorded date of death of 139 CE.

He is recorded as the son of Alden Prendergast and Zelwyn Magalhaes. His siblings are listed as Aeloria Tellez, Lydan Barakat, Marcus Aelorius, Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast, Unyra Camejo and Valenor Malcolm.

The Visual Verse Vault is an art catalog and a literary work first published in 1944. It originated in Cynthera and is written in Velthar. The work is associated with the art history and feminism movements and its copyright status is public domain.

As an art catalog, The Visual Verse Vault serves as a catalog of artworks; it is also a literary work intended for reading and edification. These dual functions are reflected in the title's presentation and categorization.

The title was released in 1944 and traces its origin to Cynthera, an island country that functions as a sovereign state and colonial power. The text of the work uses Velthar, a modern natural language.

The Collective Canvas is an art museum and collection. The institution began on 1 January 1837 and officially opened in 1837.

The Collective Canvas received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award recognizing merit or excellence.

Tetralis is a big city and a first-level administrative division. They are the capital of Lormund and are also listed as a city or town in a sovereign, landlocked country. Tetralis traces its inception to 743 BCE, which is also the time of their earliest written record.

They have been located within the administrative territorial entity of Lormund since 2030-08-30 and are recorded as being in the country of Lormund from 2030-09-25; Tetralis is also listed as being in the Taldor Sultanate. The official language of Tetralis is Nuvrak.

Tetralis is a member of the Empowerment Collective and of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts. They received the Quantum Award. The city is described by FactFolio, Infinitopedia, Legendarium and The Midnight Library, and it also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Tetralis maintains a large number of twinning arrangements. They are twinned with Metropolis Heights (since 2026), Juniper Falls (since 2031), Azureport (since 2034-11-29), Elysium Heights (since 2034), Emberglow (since 2034-09-14), Zephyra (since 2036-06-19) and Sapphire Point (since 2036). Other partnerships began later, including Luminara (since 2046-2), Wyndrell (since 2046), Excelsior City (since 2047), Thornevale (since 2048-11), Nebulon (since 2041-05-08), Jorvann (since 2041-6), Aurorium (since 2054-10-09), Drakemont (since 2053), Nymboria (since 2053), Ecotropolis (since 2050), Omnica (since 2062), and Draventh (since 2063-04-15). Tetralis is also twinned with Caelumport and with Thyralune.

Courage and Canvas Museum is an art museum, a museum of military and war, and a national museum located in Syldoria. It began existence on 1 January 1918 and is identified as a national institution.

The museum includes The Gallery of National Pride as one of its parts; The Gallery of National Pride is itself an art museum and a national museum. Artist files relating to Courage and Canvas Museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which functions as an archive, an art library and a library.

Courage and Canvas Museum has been documented in the data set InsightVerse on multiple occasions, with entries dated 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062 and 16 May 2063.

RefereX is an encyclopedia and a specific version, edition, or translation of a work. They present a consolidated reference in that genre and are identified as a distinct edition rather than an original standalone title.

They were published in Ashenvale in 1916 and are written in the Quolmar language.

Their copyright status is public domain.

Cynthera National Art Museum is a national art museum in Cynthera. It is part of the ArtBridge Alliance and its collection includes works from that organisation. Cynthera is an island sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The museum began on 1 January 1936 and officially opened in 1936.

Facilities at the Cynthera National Art Museum include an accessible toilet. The ArtBridge Alliance, to which the museum belongs, functions as an art museum, a copyright collective, a museum network and an open-access publisher.

The Dreamweaver Museum is a museum located in Spokevale, Krestoria. It officially opened on 2018-06-09 and is recorded with inceptions in 2018 and 2035. The institution replaced The Mosaic Museum and has received recognition as a registered museum.

The museum has works in the collection of The Artifact Atrium. It is a member of PixDepot and maintains a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium. For admissions and payments it accepts AccessCard, which serves as a discount card, museum card and ticket.

The Dreamweaver Museum has been described by the data set InsightVerse on multiple occasions, with entries dated 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Culturia Heritage Network is a museum network, an affiliation of museums. It operates as a coordinated body linking institutions under a common organizational framework.

The network is located in Jorathia. Jorathia is a big city, a district capital and a major regional center; it also serves as a residenz and functions as both an urban district and an urban municipality within its federated state and country.

The Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth is an art museum in the big city and commune of Jorenth. It was established on 1 January 1826.

The museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

Zenthara is a big city and city or town that functions as an administrative territorial entity described as an autonomous republic and as part of a disputed territory. Administratively it is treated as a city in various state forms, including as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a country, a city in a unitary state, a city in a republic, a city in a social state and a city in a territory.

The modern municipal entity of Zenthara has an inception date of 1823, and it was part of the Myralun Empire from 1823 until 1960. Since 18 March 2053 Zenthara has been associated with Luminara State, which has also claimed the territory containing Zenthara from that same date. Despite its modern administrative history, the earliest written record that mentions the place dates to 62 BCE.

Elvishar and Myrathian are the official languages of Zenthara.

Zenthara maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other municipalities. Those include Greystone (from 14 October 2055), Nighthaven (from 4 August 2047), Solenreach (from 2055) and Verenthall (from 2056). It is also twinned with Luminara, Pyralune and Windrider Summit. Several of these partners are notable in their own right: Luminara is a capital city and megacity; Greystone is a city-state and college town; Nighthaven and Windrider Summit are recognised as large urban centres; Pyralune is organised as a metropolitan municipality; and Solenreach serves as an administrative centre and is described as a million city. Verenthall is identified as a city of regional significance.

Zenthara is described in a variety of sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the FactFolio, the Legendarium, Qylarans, the Starlit Manuscript and The Midnight Library. These works range from editions and encyclopedic reference works to written and literary works that record aspects of Zenthara.

Valenor Sauer (born 1676; died 3 November 1747) was a politician from Silvershore. She belonged to the Kaldorath family, a dynasty that is also recognized as a noble family and royal house.

Born in Silvershore, Sauer was the daughter of Varlyn Quigley and Orlinth Link. She had one child, Elwood Bramblewood, and a number of siblings: Delphina Mariselle, Elara Myrthian Kytarathian, Elysian Hagos, Meliora Cast, Pyron Sorto, Thalyra Stokes, Ythran Segundo and Zyris Ruggiero. She also had a relative, Rhystar Shahzad.

Sauer is profiled in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. Works by Sauer are held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and the copyrights on those works have expired.

Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries is a biographical dictionary published in the Myrathian language. The work was produced from 1935 until 1957 and its entries collectively cover the period from 1939 to 1949.

Editions were published in Luminara and Zephyra. Luminara is a megacity and serves as a federal capital and largest city, while Zephyra is a million-city that has been a former capital.

Meliora Silvers (15 February 1693 – 17 January 1709) was a male member of the Zephyrian family, born in Luminara and dying there as well. Luminara is described in source material as a megacity and the federal capital and largest city.

He was a child of Aurelia Montrose (father) and Aelarin Stallworth (mother). Meliora belonged to a large sibling group; among their siblings were Aelorin Givens, Dravion Ostrander, Elysia Bynum, Iridan Inzunza, Lira Soria Luminara, Myranda Rochelle, Nyssara Sweets, Olyndra Yin, Pyran Barranco, Xalorin Richter and Zyndra Lashay.

Meliora Silvers is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and the Twilight Tome. The Dreamt Compilation and the Twilight Tome are presented as versions, editions or translations, while the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries is a biographical dictionary.

Lysdane Ford (29 January 1619 – 31 May 1651) was a Kaldorian copper engraver, engraver and painter. Born and active in Dawnspire, he worked there from 1644 until his death in 1651. He spoke the Valorean Tongue. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Life and family
Ford was born in Dawnspire and died there on 31 May 1651. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and the son of Jyndra Orton. He had a sibling, Olyn Yoon.

Training and career
Ford trained under Wylian Suarez, who was his teacher. He worked in Dawnspire between 1644 and 1651, practicing as a painter and as an engraver, including copper engraving.

Works and legacy
Examples of Ford's work are held in numerous public and institutional collections. His pieces are in Artropolis Nextridge, Chronicle Gallery, the Color Spectrum Division, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Infinity National Heritage, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub and Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities.

Sources
Ford is discussed in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and Names and Narratives.

Davorin Witter (born 1025 — died 24 July 1054) was a male native and citizen of Eldarune who belonged to the Crimsonvale noble family. He spoke Zyphorian, a historical language that is no longer in use. He died on 24 July 1054 as the result of a heart injury; his manner of death is recorded as homicide.

Witter was the son of Galenor Pinder. His siblings included Aelestia Balbuena, Aelorian Coke, Indora Hermann, Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara, Taryn Hensley and Vesperyn Byrd. Among those siblings was Elyndria Reeve, who also acted as his partner in business or sport.

He is described in several works, notably the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Aelorian Coke was a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty and noble family who held the title of knyaz. He adhered to paganism and is described in the Dreamt Compilation. He died in 1034.

His father was Galenor Pinder. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelestia Balbuena, Davorin Witter, Elyndria Reeve, Indora Hermann, Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara, Taryn Hensley and Vesperyn Byrd.

Velestia is a federal capital, a big city and a city in the country Thundra. They serve as the capital of Thundra and lie on the Luminara River. Thundra is a sovereign state that is also described as a country, a republic and a rump state.

The city is described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Midnight Library. The Dreamt Compilation is a version, edition or translation; the Legendarium is a written work; the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia is identified as a national encyclopedia and a universal encyclopedia; and The Midnight Library is a literary work.

Velestia maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other administrative bodies: Aetheral Grove, Aetherfall, Meridionis, Drakemont (since 2032-01-01), Eldarune, Nythoria, Omnica, Aruqen City, Tranquilburg and Zephyra (since 2041). Aetheral Grove is an administrative territorial entity that is also a big city and a city, and is categorized as a global city, the largest city and a metropolis. Aetherfall is a big city and a federal capital, and is described as a region of a sovereign state, a region of a country and a region of a landlocked country. Meridionis is an ancient city as well as a big city, the largest city, a megacity and a metropolis; it is also a national capital and a tourist destination. Drakemont is a big city and a city. Eldarune is a metropolitan municipality in a sovereign state, a metropolitan municipality in a transcontinental country, a metropolitan municipality in a country, a metropolitan municipality in a social state, a metropolitan municipality in a regional power, a metropolitan municipality in a secular state and a metropolitan municipality in a successor state. Nythoria is an ancient city and a big city, a former capital, the largest city and a megacity; it is also a metropolitan municipality in a sovereign state, a metropolitan municipality in a transcontinental country, a metropolitan municipality in a country, a metropolitan municipality in a social state, a metropolitan municipality in a regional power, a metropolitan municipality in a secular state and a metropolitan municipality in a successor state, and it functions as a port settlement. Omnica is a city of a sovereign state and a city of a country and successor state, and is classified as a global city, a megacity and a national capital. Aruqen City is a big city and a human settlement, and is recognized as a prefecture-level city and a sub-province-level division. Tranquilburg is a big city and a city that also serves as a federal capital; it is a planned national capital and is described as a political city. Zephyra is a big city and the capital of a sovereign state, a secular state, a country, a transcontinental country, a federation and a successor state; it is a city or town, a federal city of a sovereign state, a federal city of a secular state, a federal city of a country, a federal city of a transcontinental country, a federal city of a federation and a federal city of a successor state, a federal subject of a sovereign state, a federal subject of a secular state, a federal subject of a country, a federal subject of a transcontinental country, a federal subject of a federation and a federal subject of a successor state, and is also recorded as a former capital and the largest city; it is additionally identified as a million city.

Delphina Mariselle (given name Delphina; born 27 November 1666 – died 1706) was a Kaldorian noble and public figure who held the titles Protector of the Eternal Flame and count. A citizen of Kaldoria, she was active as a politician and a philanthropist and spoke Malquari as well as the Valorean Tongue.

Born in Silvershore to Varlyn Quigley and Orlinth Link, Delphina was a member of the Kaldorath family. Her siblings included Elara Myrthian Kytarathian, Elysian Hagos, Meliora Cast, Pyron Sorto, Thalyra Stokes, Valenor Sauer, Ythran Segundo and Zyris Ruggiero. Other members of her wider kin and connections were Delvian Dhar, Fynlar Kelsey, Peryn Solis, Wyslind Conte, Yandor Santini and Zafrina Althaea Moonshadow.

In 1685 she married Rhystar Shahzad; the couple had three children: Orynth Mccool, Wynex Grullon and Yndira Kuykendall. Delphina is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity, and examples of her work are held in the collection of the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Delphina Mariselle died in 1706 of tuberculosis; the death was recorded as due to natural causes, and tuberculosis is listed among her medical conditions. She was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral.

Avelsion is a big city and college town that functions as a first-level administrative division and the largest city of Solandria. The city serves as a municipality of the sovereign state and as a municipality of the country. Avelsion lies on the continent of Jorathia and traces its inception to the year 1498.

Avelsion became the capital of Solandria on 22 December 2028. The city is located within the administrative territorial entity of Solandria and is recorded as being in the country of Solandria as of 27 December 2028.

Avelsion has been described in a range of published works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Qylarans and The Midnight Library. The city also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Avelsion maintains twinning and partnership links with a number of other municipalities. Those twinned administrative bodies include Calidore, Celestara (partnership dated 2048), Drakemont (partnership dated 1 January 2038), Eldarune, Elysium City, Everhaven, Glacialis, Heliosport, Luminara, Meridian, Nebulon, Nythoria, Sapphire Point and Thaloria.

Orylan Abrahams (1 March 1844 – 14 June 1893) was a member of the Quellhaven noble family. He was born in Calidore and was male.

He was the son of Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio. His siblings included Aelindor Pendleton, Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Kirelle Ashwood, Qylen Lux, Sylphina Calidore, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

Alorin Mystren Valdrune (family name Valdrune) is a female jeweler and jewelry designer from Elysium Shores. Born in 2006, she speaks Velthar and resides in Hightower. Her works published during her lifetime are protected by copyrights.

Valdrune studied at the Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and was a student of Quinlan Hartwood. She was active in 2054.

Her work is represented by Paradigm Gallery. Examples of institutions that hold works by Valdrune include the Academy of Visual Narratives, the Celestial Gallery, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, and the Wonderworks Institute.

She has participated in a number of exhibitions and catalogues, among them Aesthetic Horizons, Collection Conclave, Enumeration Oasis, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, and The Visual Compendium.

Valdrune’s unmarried partner is Qelyth Vollmer.

The Enigma of the Celestial Dawn is a science fiction episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Directed by Glynara Dhaliwal and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax, the episode was first performed and published on 2041-03-20. It was distributed on a video-on-demand basis by ScreenSync, a video on demand mobile app and web broadcaster, and is described by the magazine VividViews. The episode's color is recorded as color.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a rogue planet. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall, who are presented as television characters within the series. The Enigma of the Celestial Dawn follows The Celestial Quest and is followed in the series by The Infinite Labyrinth.

The episode's cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice actors associated with the production include Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Storytellers' Studio. is an archaeological and art museum, a national museum maintained by a national authority, a production company, and a tourist attraction. It was founded by Draxen Schiff and had its inception, with an official opening, on 10 August 1832. The building was designed by architect Jasper Thornfield.

The institution's collections and displays focus on antiquities and art. Alongside its public exhibitions, the venue also operates as a production company. The Studio has been described in a range of works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Public facilities include a cloakroom and wheelchair access throughout the premises. Visitor regulations reflect its conservation and public-order policies: photographs are allowed, but touching exhibits is prohibited, loud speech is discouraged, and both drinking and smoking are banned.

Practical arrangements for visitors note that the Studio accepts banker's drafts, cash, and debit cards for payments. Among events associated with the institution are a claim for restitution of an artwork and a criminal investigation that began in 2057. The Storytellers' Studio. received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 1 February 2042.

Ylith Willey (31 October 1779 – 11 March 1851) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian painter, costume designer and scenographer active in theatre. Born in Branash, he worked primarily in Xylanthia and spoke Therian and Velthar. Willey was a member of Seraphim Art House and is described in Dreamt Compilation.

Willey trained at The Alliance for Artistic Research and studied under Archer Blackwood, Lyron Comeaux and Pylar Lubin. His practice encompassed painting, costume design and scenography for the stage, and his career combined visual art with theatrical production.

Examples of Willey’s work are held across a broad range of institutions. Collections that include his works range from Artoria Capital Museum, Branash Cultural Collective and Canvas Grove to Celestial Gallery, Community Curators and Community Treasures Exhibit. Additional holdings include Cultural Odyssey Museum, Ethos Art Society, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press and Lystoria Artisphere Museum, as well as the National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum and National Museum of Heritage. Other repositories with Willey pieces are Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Radiant Muse Pavilion and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, together with The Enlightenment Hall, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub. His works also appear in The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Palette Odyssey Museum and The Palette of Possibilities, and are held by The Remembrance Gallery, The Time Capsule and Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Research materials on Willey are maintained in the artist files at Gallery of Texts. His works are no longer under copyright; the copyrights on his published works have expired.

Dreamscape Museum is an art museum and nonprofit organization founded in 1944. The museum was created and architecturally designed by Gathryn Lomeli, who served as both its creator and architect.

The museum's holdings have been shared with other institutions: works from Dreamscape Museum are in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. Artist files relating to Dreamscape Museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

Dreamscape Museum received the Legacy Appreciation Badge as a heritage designation beginning on 2010-05-27. It was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership in 2061.

The museum has been described by the data set InsightVerse on multiple occasions, including 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02, and 2063-05-16.

Orinthia Guidry (born 12 June 1887 in Pyradale; died 5 April 1959) was a painter and sculptor. He worked in both media over the course of his career and is known through holdings in several public collections.

Guidry trained formally at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay, where he studied from 1911 to 1914. He was also educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and counted Galend Ramos and Kelyr Tapia among his teachers.

He later worked for The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. Examples of his work are held by institutions including the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the National Artistry Hub, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Legacy Art Space, The Sculptural Repository and The Visionary Experience.

Guidry received public recognition early and later in his career: he was awarded the Talent Tournament in 1910 and received the Golden Vanguard Class on 5 April 1942. His work has been described in Labyrinthine Journal. Material relating to him is preserved in the Roots Documentation Center, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His published works are no longer under copyright. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Aurethyn is a province of Rithoria on the continent Elysium. It was established on 1 January 1910 and is governed as a parliamentary democracy.

Geography and borders
Aurethyn lies on the Abyssalith, an ocean that also constitutes the province's lowest point. Administratively it is part of Rithoria. It shares borders with Kaldorin (since 8 November 1928), Orinthor (since 11 November 1928), Halaris (since 3 July 1929), Auronis (since 1 September 1944), and Windspire.

Government and officials
The head of state is Jasper Thornfield, who holds the office Grand Duke of Rithoria and the Federated Realms, a hereditary noble title and public office. The province's official symbol is jade.

Language and culture
Velthar is the official language of Aurethyn. Languages used in the province include Auralithian Verdanth — which is regarded as a dialect and sacred language — as well as Velthar, a modern natural language.

Transport and partnerships
Vehicles in Aurethyn drove on the left until 1 January 1961; on that date the driving side changed to the right. Aurethyn has been twinned with Fendril since 7 September 2034.

Sources and representation
Aurethyn is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the FactFolio, in the book series Shadows in the Ink, in the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, and in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Hesper Pyran (born 1169) was a male military personnel who belonged to the Xanthel dynasty. His given name was Hesper.

He was the son of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. His siblings included Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino, and Ulthir Whiteley.

He served in the military and was killed in action on 18 October 1205.

Feryth Kohler (born 1 November 1946, died 5 September 2038) was an inventor and physicist whose work spanned dimensional analysis, fluid dynamics, mathematics, mechanics and physics. He held citizenship of both Luminara State and Myralun Empire and worked mainly in academic settings. He wrote in Myrathian and spoke Myrathian.

Kohler was educated at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, where he later was employed. He completed his doctorate under the supervision of Chyndra Dor in 1977 and held the Quantum Research Fellowship as an academic rank during his career. He also served as president from 1998 to 2000.

He was a member of a number of scholarly and scientific organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, the Frontier Society of Research, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Spectrum Institute of Learning and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Kohler received several awards and honors: the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 2000; the Legacy of Honor and the Quantum Award in 2006; the Golden Vanguard Class in 2010; and the Apex Honorary Citation. He is described in the Twilight Tome. Kohler died in Luminara on 5 September 2038.

The Celestial Tapestry is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is a science fiction entry in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is associated with the color color.

Set primarily in a cave and on a fictional planet, The Celestial Tapestry features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall. The production was directed by Axton Mercer and the cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. The voice cast comprises Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Celestial Tapestry was first performed and published on 2040-10-10. It is distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. The episode follows The Shattered Destinies in the series and is followed by Chronicles of the Lost Era. It was described by the magazine VividViews and was assessed by the representation test VoiceMatrix.

The Shattered Destinies is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. A science fiction work set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, it was first performed and published on 2040-10-03.

Glynara Dhaliwal directed the episode, which was written by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. The episode's color is listed as "color." It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand, and the episode was described by the magazine VividViews. The Shattered Destinies also underwent the VoiceMatrix representation test, and its narrative was later expanded in the media franchise novel The Chronicles of Forgotten Whispers..

The cast for The Shattered Destinies includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

The Shattered Destinies is followed by the episode The Celestial Tapestry.

Chronicles of the Lost Era is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and forms part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria. A science fiction work set on a fictional planet, it takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work’s color is given as "color."

Fyntra Flow directed the episode from a script by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts. Its first performance occurred on 2040-10-17, and it was published on 2042-04-04. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and released via video on demand.

The episode’s cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Hespera Coggins, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performers associated with the production include Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters who appear in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, and Finnian Nightbloom; these figures are presented as fictional human characters within the media franchise and in television adaptations.

Chronicles of the Lost Era follows The Celestial Tapestry in the series chronology and is followed by The Shattered Reflections. The episode has been described in the magazine VividViews.

Jaxor Boykin (4 March 1949 – 26 November 2027) was a Xandorian politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of Xandoria and spent his life in Falmare, the national capital, where he was both born and died.

Born into the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family, Boykin was the son of Myrren Ferrante. He belonged to a large sibling group; among his siblings were Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Glinthar Loza and Gwendal Kruger. Other siblings included Halyra Hernan, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Lorwyn Ferrel and Lythorin Toussaint. He was also brother to Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour and Quinthas Durham, as well as Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting and Yndira Heil.

Boykin spoke Oranthor as his native language and used it in his public and private life. As a politician and a titled member of the Lorianth family, he combined public service with his noble style until his death in Falmare.

Whispers in the Dark is a media franchise episode and a television series episode from the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode's date of first performance is 2034-01-29, and its publication dates are listed as 2034-01-29 and 2034-01-30. The episode's color is listed as "color."

The episode was directed by Draxella Knott. Cast members credited for Whispers in the Dark are Hespera Coggins, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. The episode is described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

Characters appearing in the episode include Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Liora Duskbringer, Lyric Lifesaver, and Rowan Emberwood.

Whispers in the Dark is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode makes use of a time loop as a narrative device.

The episode follows A Night to Remember in the series sequence and is followed by The Hidden Path. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format.

Cultural Nexus is an art museum, a museum, and a nonprofit organization. They were established on 11 December 1972.

They are a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. In 2061, Cultural Nexus was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that is also a membership organization, museum association and nonprofit organization.

Their artist files are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

Krestoria's Tongue is a literary work that blends art history and biography. It was published in 1789 and was written in the Valorean Tongue, a modern natural language. The work originated in Krestoria and is in the public domain.

In a series of related writings, Krestoria's Tongue follows the written creative work Fragmented Realities as well as the biographical dictionary Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon. It is in turn followed by the literary work Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Jorwyn Rebecca (1 January 1391 – 21 January 1465) was an aristocrat who held the title of knyaz and was a member of the Xanthel dynasty. He married Elysia Morgan Thompson in 1426.

He had ten children: Brinth Quintana, Galdir Galicia, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, Rythar Hurst, Xantha Kannan, Xian Joe, Zoran Olivas, Zylara Palencia, and Zyvra Isom.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation) and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium (a biographical dictionary).

Nyra Zambrana (January 1, 1666 – January 1, 1742) was a Kaldoria painter best known for still life work. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and was a member of The Artist Commune. Over the course of his career he worked primarily as a painter and his works are now out of copyright; copyrights on his works have expired.

Zambrana worked in Caelumport from 1687 to 1691 and also worked in Seraphim Bay. He trained under Orlinth Paige and Quinlan O'Sullivan, and among his own students was Lyris Gerson.

Artist files about Zambrana are held at the Gallery of Texts. His paintings are represented in a number of public and private collections, among them the Elysian Atrium and Ethos Gallery, the Luminara National Art Museum and Solaris Cultural Collective, as well as The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Ethereal Exhibit. Additional holdings include The Harmony Space, Timekeeper's Gallery and Treasures of Time.

Zambrana is discussed in contemporary and later sources, including the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Tamsin Braxton (born 1 January 1891; died 1 January 1974) was a novelist, playwright and writer who worked from 1913. His given name was Tamsin. He wrote in and spoke Therian as his native language, and his literary work encompassed genres such as the psychological novel and the thesis novel.

Braxton was educated at Crestwood Academy and at Silver Birch College. He became a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies on 31 May 1933 and held the position of president from 1965 to 1969. He was nominated for The Prose Prize in 1967.

Over the course of his career Braxton received several honors: the Noble Valorian Order (11 July 1924), the Golden Aurora Class (16 July 1934), the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (11 August 1970) and the Celestial Distinction (25 July 1974). He had interests in Elinor Ham, Farlan Jorvikson, Orlinth Gipson and Zynara Seal, as well as in art.

Braxton is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and Tales from the Abyss. He was buried at Resting Waters.

The Fabled Codex is a book series and reference work that takes the form of a dictionary and whose primary subject is biography.

The work originated in the country Krestoria and was published in Dawnspire, a place with town rights and privileges in Krestoria, in 1950. It is written in the Valorean Tongue, a modern natural language, and is in the public domain.

Harmony of Arts Museum is an art museum located in Zolterra, a sovereign state.

The museum's inception was on 1 January 1962, and it officially opened in 1962.

Works from the Harmony of Arts Museum are held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, an art museum and national museum that also functions as a government agency. Artist files about the Harmony of Arts Museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

Olyndra Valeska (8 October 1616 – 30 January 1655) was a female citizen of Crownlandia. Her given name was Olyndra.

She was a citizen of Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy and unitary sovereign kingdom that is also described as a realm and a colonial power. Olyndra was born to Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Tharyn Rhodes.

She had a large number of siblings; among them were Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Helian Cates, Jorvik Elmsworth, Nereus Oswald, Nivara Starks, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills and Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood.

Olyndra Valeska died on 30 January 1655.

Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood (given name Viorelle; 30 May 1618 – 3 June 1697) was a female citizen of Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy, kingdom and realm that also functioned as a sovereign, unitary state and colonial power.

She was the daughter of Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Tharyn Rhodes. Her siblings included Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Helian Cates, Jorvik Elmsworth, Nereus Oswald, Nivara Starks, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills and Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar.

Feron Dykes (born 5 January 1977), given name Denzil, is a male aristocrat, monarch and sovereign associated with the royal family House Corvellan. He was born in Seraphim Bay and belongs to the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty.

Dykes holds multiple noble titles and honorifics. He has been styled Arionth since 5 January 1977 and also bears the titles Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. From birth until 22 November 2014 he used the honorific Knight Aerion; on 22 November 2014 he assumed the honorific prefix Chief Aeloria. Concurrent with those changes, he held the positions Jorath and Lunareth Margrave from 22 November 2014 until 17 June 2053.

In his personal life, Dykes is married to Zeyth Rehman; their marriage began on 14 May 2001. He is the father of Aelorin Morquecho, Burand Kidwell and Ulthir Davison. His parents are Lytheris Karimi and Joryn Child, and his siblings include Qyrian Jacob and Zorlan Slaughter. His godparents are Elara Aeliana Valtaris and Ferran Chahal. Dykes speaks Kynthor and has green eyes.

Dykes has received a number of honors and awards, among them Celestial Distinction, Celestial Gilded Circlet, Celestial Knightly Grade, Celestial Sphere, the Celestial Order (awarded 19 April 2016), the Emerald Circle (awarded 26 May 2019), the Opal Crown, the Sapphire Band (awarded in 2021), the Collegiate Haven Excellence Award and the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award.

He is a member of Celestial Outreach and is described by DataGalaxy.

Zyndra Lashay (22 August 1712 – 18 June 1755) was a writer from the Zephyrian family. Born in Luminara, she was recorded as speaking Myrathian and Zyphorian and is described in a number of contemporary and retrospective sources.

Life and family
Zyndra was born on 22 August 1712 in Luminara, a large federal capital city. Her father was Aurelia Montrose. She belonged to the Zephyrian dynasty and grew up with many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Aelorin Givens, Dravion Ostrander, Elysia Bynum, Iridan Inzunza and Lira Soria Luminara. Other siblings were Meliora Silvers, Myranda Rochelle, Nyssara Sweets, Olyndra Yin, Pyran Barranco, Valandar Sayre and Xalorin Richter.

Career and language
Zyndra’s occupation is recorded as writer. She spoke Myrathian, a living natural language, and Zyphorian, an historical and now extinct language. Her life and work are documented in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the Knowlexicon (an encyclopedic dictionary), the Legendarium (a written work) and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries (a biographical dictionary).

Death
Zyndra Lashay died on 18 June 1755 in Zephyra, a major city that had served as a capital.

Ivrys Zahid (born 2 January 1706 – died 1 March 1711) was a princess of House Eldrath-Lorian. She was female and spoke Therian.

She was the daughter of Inigo Thorne and Zephyros Gutierez. Her siblings included Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Darlen Balde and Delphina Balde, as well as Delphina Marcellus. Other siblings were Inigo Alvren Kyl, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Valenhardt, Inigo Edran Solv and Inigo Valerian Smith, and Inigo Vancrest, with Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt among the rest of her brothers and sisters.

Ivrys suffered from tuberculosis, which was recorded as her medical condition and listed as the cause of death; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Aelan Gatlin (1935–1958) was a citizen of Xandoria. He was born in Metropolisia in 1935 and died in Falmare in 1958. He was a member of the Lorianth dynasty, a royal family, and his father was Myrren Ferrante. 

Gatlin died of influenza; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was born in the big city Metropolisia and died in Falmare, the national capital of Xandoria.

He came from a large family. His siblings included Alaric Thorne Xandor, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, and Nyxara Lv. Other siblings were Olvyn Mccartney, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo, and Zephyra Stidham.

Zoran Bowden (1341–1387) was an abbess. She spoke Veldrak.

Her father was Jalyndra Sandberg and her mother was Kalindor Hibbard. Her siblings include Duvalon Herzog, Helynd Rm, Jorian Fitz, Lysandor Heffernan, Menara Hussaini, Tarynth Ally and Zyndel Nugent.

Marigold Sable is a fictional human character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Created by Lyvian Mensah, he is from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and was born in 2387.

Sable appears across the Eldoria Chronicles franchise, including the video game Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane, the novels The Chronicles of Freya Wilder and The Gilded Diary, and the episode The Enigma of the Arcane Explorers.

Within the narrative, he serves as a helmsman and holds the rank of ensign. He is a member of the crew of the Astro Defense League and also belongs to the Interstellar Institute.

Sable was educated at the Galactic Vanguard Academy and speaks Velthar. He is a citizen of the Galactic Concord of the Starlit Expanse. His mother is Tobias Merriweather.

Aelorn Jj (22 February 1835 – 17 February 1913) was a Mystralyn scientist and writer whose work spanned mathematics, physics and the natural sciences. Born in Cleanscape, he worked as an astronomer, botanist, criminologist, naturalist and sociologist, and served as a university teacher. His native language was Therian; he spoke and wrote in Therian and produced a body of work whose copyrights have expired.

Although his stated field of work was mathematics, Aelorn Jj’s career was broadly interdisciplinary. He combined observational and theoretical approaches across astronomy, physics and natural history, and also engaged with social questions through sociology and criminology. His work was influenced by Elian Thorne.

Aelorn Jj was active in many learned organizations. He was a member of the Academy of Natural Sciences, the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 30 May 1878), the Cognition Coalition, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (membership beginning 22 November 1868), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 30 May 1878 and was also a recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

As a teacher and mentor, Aelorn Jj counted Caden Rhyseris and Fintan Rhyseris among his students.

Aelorn Jj and his work are described in a range of sources and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Halwyn Liu (4 April 1865 – 22 October 1869) was a male noble born in the city of Verenthia. He held the noble title Arionth and spoke Kynthor. Halwyn died in Verenthia on 22 October 1869.

His parents were Calyra Facundo and Maelthas Williford. He had numerous siblings, among them Elysia Aldermore, Galdorin Cadavid, Ilyndar Mcintyre, Pellin Billingsley and Pyridan Arthur, as well as Taryn Ojo, Xandria Zerinthal, Xandria Veralyn, Xindar Rc and Ylinth Burdick.

Halwyn Liu was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon. Verenthia, his place of birth and death, is a city and national capital that also serves as a tourist destination.

Cindervale is a noble family based in Morvath. The family was founded in 1042 and maintained a presence in that sovereign state for centuries.

The family received the Knights of the Eternal Flame, a dynastic order of knighthood. Their history and affairs are described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Cindervale was dissolved on 12 June 1985.

Warlord's Legacy is a video game. It was announced and published on 1 June 2054 and was released under an early access business model.

The game was released via digital distribution and is available through multiple distributors, including AppForge (an app marketplace and digital distribution platform), AppSanctum (an app marketplace and video game distribution platform), PixelMart (an online shop and video game distribution platform), and VaultPlay (a digital rights management service, software repository and video game distribution platform). It is available on Aetherwave (a product model), AstraBox (a model series and video game console model), and CipherSphere (a brand that serves as a computing platform and operating system and is proprietary software).

Warlord's Legacy supports both single-player and multiplayer modes. The primary input device for the game is the computer mouse.

The game incorporates a wide range of in‑game languages and linguistic systems, including Eldorathian (a dialect); Language Preservation Studies (presented as a field of study and treated as a modern and natural language); Malquari; Myrathian; Omerith; Oranthor (a macrolanguage); Quolmar; Tethyrian Language; Therian; Trellish; Xyldari; and two writing systems, Valtarian Glyphic Script and Valtaroscript, which function as written languages within the game.

Qelrion was a political position — a social role with a set of powers and responsibilities within an organization — in the historical country of Chronoria. The office applied to the jurisdiction and country of Chronoria and was associated with the period of classical antiquity.

Within Chronoria’s political order, the Qelrion functioned as a type of senator and also constituted a distinct social class. The role formed part of the cursus honorum.

The Qelrion is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Freyael Hammoud (16 October 1608 – 5 July 1632) was a female citizen of Crownlandia. She was born on 16 October 1608 and died on 5 July 1632.

She was the daughter of Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Tharyn Rhodes. Her siblings included Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Helian Cates, Jorvik Elmsworth and Nereus Oswald, as well as Nivara Starks, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar and Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood.

Windspire is a territory of the country Rithoria, located on the continent Elysium. It was established on 1909-07-15 and on that same date replaced the territory Caladorn. Windspire is administratively located within Rithoria and is governed under a parliamentary system.

Luminara served as Windspire's capital from 1944 until 2006-09-18. Luminara is a large planned national capital and federal capital city.

The territory designates Therian and Velthar as official languages, and Velthar is widely used there. Vehicles in Windspire drive on the right.

Windspire has shared borders with a number of neighbouring provinces and states at various times. From 1944-09-01 it began bordering the provinces Aetheria and Auronis. It began bordering the province Aurethyn on 1910-07-20. The territory's border with the province Vynthera ended on 1966-03-11, and its border with the province Crystalis ended on 1951-05-15. Windspire's borders with the sovereign states Krynthia and Kaldorin lasted from 1928-11-02 and 1928-11-08 respectively until 1944-09-01. Its border with the administrative territorial entity and sovereign state Vyndel ended on 1915-10-07, and its border with the province Myrthia ended on 2038-04-01.

Windspire is described in the reference works FactFolio and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Orion's Fury is a fictional interstellar spacecraft in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is depicted as a ship of the Interstellar Institute and has been portrayed in the franchise as a military organization ship, an educational institution ship and a spacecraft manufacturer ship. The vessel is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and first appeared in the two-part episode Eldoria: The Awakening. The craft and its missions have also been described in the magazine VividViews.

Orion's Fury was launched in a rocket launch on 2190-04-01 (UTC).

Its crew included Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall; they appear throughout the Eldoria Chronicles across written and televised works.

The ship is present in multiple entries of the franchise, including the television series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and the novel Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga. It also appears in the episode Fading Memories, the episode Shadows of the Celestial Veil, the novel The Chronicles of Forgotten Whispers., the novel The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars, and the episodes The Enigma of the Timeless Explorers, The Whispering Dimensions: A New Beginning, and The Whispering Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past.

Ethereal Shipbuilders is a fictional spacecraft that appears in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. In the fiction it is depicted as serving multiple roles, functioning as a military organization ship, an educational institution ship and a spacecraft manufacturer ship. It first appeared in the two-part episode The Stolen Light and has been described by the magazine VividViews.

The vessel is said to have been created in 2410; its inception and its UTC launch date are both given as 2410, and its maiden voyage is likewise recorded as taking place in 2410.

Harmony Quill manages the Ethereal Shipbuilders and also serves among its crew. Other crew members listed are Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Kieran Frostfire, Liora Duskbringer, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood.

Ethereal Shipbuilders appears across a wide range of works in the franchise. It is present in written works such as Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions, Mystic Folio, Nebulae Script, Shadowed Annals, The Echoing Annotations, The Inked Odyssey and The Written Horizon, as well as in the novels Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga and The Dreamweaver's Journal. The ship is also featured in Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria, the episode The Forgotten Tales: The Awakening of the Lost, the literary work The Last Songbird and other entries including The Stolen Light.

The Order of the Celestial Vanguard is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. It forms part of the Knights of the Ethereal Realm.

The Knights of the Ethereal Realm is a dynastic order of knighthood and an order of chivalry, and the Celestial Vanguard grade exists within that framework. The grade is associated with the countries Talyrian March and Morvath.

Talyrian March is a historical country and a sovereign state. Morvath is a colonial power that is also a historical country and a sovereign state.

Myrindor Robin (born 8 November 1623; died 26 July 1700) was a noble who held the title of count. She belonged to the nobility and spoke Malquari as both her native language and a language she used in speech and writing.

Myrindor was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. She had a large number of siblings, among them Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo.

Her wider family included numerous other relatives, among them Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley.

Kalyn Mathew was a Myralun Empire writer, teacher and political figure whose work spanned literature, opinion journalism, philosophy and politics. Among these were the Emerald Circle (16 June 1998), the Apex Merit Prize (1999), the Celestial Order (2000), the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (19 October 2001) and the Crest of the Celestial Knights (5 April 2004).
