Essence of Art began in 2008 and was officially opened on 2 October 2008. 

The institution is described by the data set InsightVerse, with entries dated 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

The Artistic Alliance is a museum and nonprofit organization in Krestoria. It has received recognition as a registered museum.

Works by The Artistic Alliance are held in the collections of The Curatorial Chamber and The Remembrance Repository, both museums.

The Artistic Alliance has inception years recorded as 2055 and 2061. It became a member of The Alliance of Ideas on 1 January 2059.

The organization maintains partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, MuseoConnect Alliance and The Alliance of Ideas; the consortium is a cultural institution and government organization, MuseoConnect Alliance is a museum network, and The Alliance of Ideas is a cooperative and cultural association.

The Artistic Alliance accepts payment via AccessCard. AccessCard functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Yndira Mick (born 24 March 1882, died 4 May 1910) was a Morvathian politician who held the noble title Orindel. She belonged to the Galdrin family and received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Mick was the daughter of Gerynd Jewel and Orindel Xerythson. Her siblings were Avelyn Daza, Denzil Atheron, Elindor Nader, Feryndal Barbee, Iverath Rmz, Loryn Billy, Pylarin Rico, Qelith Sherwood and Qyvor New.

She married Lythara Peterman on 16 October 1901; they were married as of 1910. Her children were Quinlan Caelithon and Caelithon Zephyr Aurelmar. Mick held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 4 May 1910.

A politician by occupation, she was awarded the Order of the Prismatic Blossom. She suffered from tuberculosis and died of the disease on 4 May 1910 in Lunathis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Yndira Mick is profiled in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale (born 10 June 1727; baptized 15 October 1727 — died 1 January 1805) was a noble known by the title Goldenvale Prince who acted as a pretender. He held citizenship of both the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and Kytarathia. He was born at Radiant Manor and died at Seraphim Bay.

A member of the Nymarath house, Lorian was the son of Caelan Kytarathius. He belonged to a large sibling group that included Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Hesper Caldren, Kytar Celestria, Mistran Grim and Ulind Quispe.

He bore the given names Lorian, Caelan and Vail, and spoke Velthar.

His claim and activities as a pretender were recorded in multiple sources, among them DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Braxton Ularis (born April 2, 1866; died September 7, 1949) was a male artist known for painting, etching and illustration. His given name was Braxton and his family name was Ularis. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera.

Born and dying in Calidore, Ularis was educated at Seraphim Art House. He worked in multiple cities over the course of his career, including Calidore, Meridionis, Nythoria, Olarith, Sapphire Point, Thornridge and Thyralune. He also served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army.

Ularis’s occupations included painter, etcher, illustrator and autobiographer, and his primary field of work was the art of painting. He produced portrait and religious painting genres and was associated with the Surrealist Seekers and with Temporal Idealism. He was a member of the Surrealist Seekers art group. He received the Harmony Cross.

His works are held in a wide range of collections and institutions. Among them are Artisania National Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Carandor Artistry Productions, Color Spectrum Division and Creative Spark Foundation. Additional collections holding his work include Cultural Canvas Museum, Cynthera National Art Museum, Discovery Hub, Flourish Art Consortium and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion. Other institutions with his works are Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Heritage, The Art Exchange and The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery. The Expression Hub, The Historical Nexus and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute also have works by Ularis.

Ularis spoke and wrote in Velthar, and his writing appears in autobiographical material. His life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Material related to Ularis is held in archives and libraries: his archives are at Eternal Records and The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are held at Gallery of Texts.

Aelthar Quadri (born 10 June 2021; baptized 31 August 2021) is a Zolterran aristocrat, diplomat, philanthropist and socialite. She is a member of the Velorian dynasty and is part of the Zolterran Royal House of Meridiana. She holds the honorific prefix Knight Aerion and is classified socially as royalty.

Aelthar was born to Alessandro Zoltari. Her godparents are Helian Garces and Maximilian Crownstone. She has two siblings, Bastian Eldridge and Zolara Elentis.

In her public life Aelthar has combined diplomatic and philanthropic work with a prominent social presence. She received the Ethos Token in 2039 and was awarded the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians in 2044.

Aelthar speaks Malquari, Therian, Velthar and Xyldari, with Xyldari as her native language. She writes in Velthar and Xyldari. She participates in equestrian sport and in skiing.

Her recorded residences include Calidore (noted in 2040) and Vanthelis (from 2057). She holds citizenship of Zolterra.

The Stolen Light is a two-part television episode in the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria series and forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Directed by Hesperis Koenig, the episode premiered and was published on 16 January 2034. It is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is presented in Velthar, a modern natural language.

Distributed by ScreenSync, the episode was made available as video on demand. ScreenSync is a video streaming service and web broadcaster that also offers a mobile app for on-demand viewing. The Stolen Light was described in coverage by The Feature Folio—appearing as both a list entry and a magazine article—and by the magazine VividViews.

The cast of the episode includes Hespera Coggins, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. Characters appearing in the story include Harmony Quill (a comics character and television character who is depicted as a fictional human and a human from the media franchise), Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood (both fictional humans, human figures from the media franchise, and presented as literary and television characters), Liora Duskbringer (a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial who appears as a literary and television character), and Lyric Lifesaver (an emergency medical hologram who is also described as a fictional writer and television character).

The Stolen Light is followed in the series by the episode A Night to Remember.

The Arcane Pathways is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and is classified as science fiction. The episode takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode was first performed and published on 2041-01-23. It follows The Forgotten Dimensions in the series and is followed by The Lost Guardians. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the work was released in a video on demand format; ScreenSync is presented as a mobile app and video streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. The episode was assessed by the representation test VoiceMatrix. The episode's color is listed as "color."

The Arcane Pathways features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall. The episode's cast includes Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice actors credited for the episode include Garanth Smit, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

Velian Arturo (2 February 1965 – 2 December 2059) was a male author, politician and statesperson whose work spanned literary activity and political life. Born in Cobalt Springs, he worked in Branash and was known to speak and write in Malquari and Therian. He wore a comb over.

Arturo was educated at Crestwood Academy and later at Catalyst Polytechnic. From 11 December 2042 until his death on 2 December 2059 he was a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies.

In public office he held the position of Prince of Tyndarland from 27 May 2013 to 21 May 2020. He served as a member of the general council from 2021 to 2027, and subsequently held the position of Rylathor from 23 June 2027 to 4 November 2028. He also took part in the conflict known as Aegis Warfare.

His honours included the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians (2001) and the Harmony Insignia (2002). Later recognitions included the Arcane Order (1 October 2012), the Celestial Order (21 April 2014), the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star (28 June 2017), and the Crest of the Celestial Knights (12 October 2017). He was also a recipient of the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (1 June 2019), as well as the Emerald Circle and the Ethos Token.

Arturo died of natural causes on 2 December 2059; his funeral took place on 5 December 2059. His papers and archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center, and his life and work are described in the DataGalaxy web portal.

Darovan Zapien (25 August 1746 – 31 August 1763) was a politician from Verenthia who held several noble titles and public offices. He was a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and spoke Kynthor.

Early life and family
Darovan Zapien was born in Verenthia on 25 August 1746 and was baptized on 8 December 1746. He was the son of Nythor Cleaning. His godparents were Inigo Thorne and Ryvian Schmidt. He was part of a large kinship network: his siblings included Bastian Ellwood, Beryth Mchugh, Gathryn Winters and Veldan Quiroz, and other relatives included Calista Done, Feron Philip, Kythorn Tim, Qelith Renderos, Ulrith Tavares and Zenith Backus.

Political career and positions
A politician by occupation, Zapien served as Caledorn from 7 April 1748 until 15 January 1763. On 15 January 1763 he assumed the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave, holding both until 31 August 1763.

Noble titles and honours
Throughout his life Zapien bore multiple noble titles, among them Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. His honours included the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant.

Personal life
Zapien married Seraphin von Morvial on 20 January 1761. He spoke Kynthor.

Death and burial
Darovan Zapien died in Verenthia on 31 August 1763. The cause of death was smallpox and the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast was a noble family and a patrician lineage of the Sapphire Coast, associated with the patriciate of a sovereign state, a maritime republic, and a historical country. They bore the family name Isenwald and trace their inception to 1316; the family was dissolved in 1486.

The family is described in several reference works, including Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), Narratives of the Lexicon (a book series and lexicon), and RefereX (an encyclopedia and a version, edition or translation).

The Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences is an academy and national academy based in Mystralyn. It was established on 19 September 1880 and was founded by Elwood Mystralynson.

The academy's primary field of work is medicine. As a national academy, it coordinates scholarly research activities and standards within its medical disciplines.

Nerya Mi (11 May 1863 – 10 January 1943) was a male painter, graphic artist, porcelain painter, sculptor and teacher whose work belonged to the visual arts, with a particular focus on the art of painting. His practice encompassed history painting and religious painting and was associated with the movements Visionary Art Brut and academic art.

He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, which also employed him. He worked in Caelumport, Seraphim Bay and Tarmont. After his death he was buried at Gentle Hills.

Nerya Mi studied under Mystran Garduño and Tamsin Brightwood; Garduño is also recorded as an influence on his work. As a teacher he had a number of notable students, among them Braxian Shoemaker, Braxton Hale Turner, Caelum Whitehead, Celestria Ilyrion, Daryth Tamayo, Garreth Mars, Hesper Alden Mercer, Hesper Valenwood, Hesperis Mccain, Ilyndra Dolan, Jalen Rivers, Kaelar Burger, Merylen Garfias, Olwen Culver, Tamsin Quorlen and Zander Coleton.

Nerya Mi was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Institute of Artistry and Design, Seraphim Art House and the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy. He spoke and wrote Therian.

Works by Nerya Mi are held in many collections, including Artropolis Nextridge; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Canvas of Dreams Gallery; Celestial Art Space; Community Curators; Creative Spark Foundation; Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation; Discovery Hub; Dreamscape Museum; Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation; Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; Grendale Heritage Art Museum; Horizon Art Museum; Kaleidoscope Museum of Art; Meridian Cultural Arts Complex; National Artistry Hub; National Gallery of Creative Diversity; National Legacy Gallery; National Museum of Cultural Heritage; Quentarion Art Museum; Resonance Art Foundation; Revelry Art Center; Solaris Cultural Collective; Solstice Art Sanctuary; The Aesthetic Archive; The Aesthetic Odyssey; The Art Voyager Gallery; The Artisan's Haven; The Artistic Elixir; The Artistic Odyssey Museum; The Artistic Retreat; The Creative Essence; The Creative Rhapsody House; The Curated Press; The Curatorial Institute; The Expression Hub; The Odyssey of Ages Museum; The Palette Sanctuary; The Storytellers' Studio; Vivid Visions Gallery; and Whimsy Art Pavilion. Artist files about Nerya Mi are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He received the Noble Crest and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade. His works’ copyrights have expired. Nerya Mi has been described in a range of sources, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Illyndra Bartlett (10 November 1923 – 28 March 2014) was a member of the noble family Yondercrest. She was born in Hightower, a metropolis and college town, and was the daughter of Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers.

She was raised in a large family and had eight siblings: Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Hylith Zaki, Ilyra Voral Syrren, Pylira Uno and Tharyn Flanigan.

She spoke Malquari.

Glynor Kerns (born 1300-10-09; died 1364-01-07) was a male Eldoria-Emberland citizen who served as a monarch and politician while also working across artistic and agricultural pursuits. He held the Duchy of Nephronia from 1318-02-16 until 1364-01-07. His occupations included monarch, politician, poet, composer, translator and farmer, and his fields of work encompassed governance, economic policy, research policy and poetry.

Kerns was born in Valdor to Qyler Tucker and Fythar Ferrufino. He spoke Veyrith and had several siblings: Alyndra Foote, Ilyrith Foote, Kaelith Clinton, Lysandra Valenwood, Lythial Acuña, Nyvir Moctezuma and Syrith Foote.

The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described by DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, Qylarans and The Midnight Library.

Goryan Cornish (14 August 1651 – 21 January 1704) was a female member of the nobility.

Her father was Fynor Clifton and her mother was Nereus Oswald.

She had numerous siblings, among them Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere and Keryth Emery. Other siblings included Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

Her wider family network included relatives such as Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty and Mylaria Aldridge, as well as Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

Draxport Maritime Heritage Museum is a museum located and headquartered in Draxport, Krestoria. It has been recognized as a registered museum.

The museum's holdings include works in the Ethereal Exhibits collection; Ethereal Exhibits is itself described as a collection and museum.

Draxport Maritime Heritage Museum maintains partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, which is a cultural institution and government organization, and with the MuseoConnect Alliance, a museum network and network organization. The museum accepts the AccessCard for payment; the AccessCard functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

The museum has been described by the data set InsightVerse on the following dates: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-07-02, 2062-06-27 and 2063-05-16.

Garren Mirak Solenn (born 1 January 1674; died 27 August 1719) was a painter from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. His given name was Garren, and he is described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon.

Mirak Solenn was born in Harborview City and received training under Jorian Broome. His documented period of professional activity runs from 1 January 1694 to 1 January 1706.

Records place Mirak Solenn working in Lurendale in 1689 and in Harborview City in 1700. He died in Lurendale.

Works by Mirak Solenn are held in a wide range of public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, the Solaris Cultural Collective, the Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Aesthetic Spectrum. Additional holdings include The Enchanted Spectrum, The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Time, Treasures of Tomorrow and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files on Mirak Solenn are held at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast (1 November 1398 – 1 August 1442) was a member of the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast family. He was born in Bryston.

He was the son of Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald and Ilynth Mars. As a member of the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Seraphina belonged to a prominent family in his region.

He had numerous siblings, including Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire and Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast. Other siblings were Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire; Alaric Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphirecoast and Lady Serelis Isenwald; Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart; Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast; Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire; Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast; and Isenwald Sapphirehart.

Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub is an art museum that also functions as a design museum, a national museum and a theatre museum. It is located in Cynthera and is named after Fintan Rhyseris. The institution was established on 1 January 1891 and officially opened in 1891.

The hub's collection includes works from ArtBridge Alliance and Creative Spark Foundation. ArtBridge Alliance is an art museum, a copyright collective, a museum network and an open-access publisher. Creative Spark Foundation is an art museum that also operates as an educational institution and a nonprofit organization.

Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub has been described by the data set InsightVerse at multiple points in time: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-07-02, 2062-06-27 and 2063-05-16. The site is also described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

The facility provides accessible toilet accommodations.

The Labyrinth of Eldoria is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. It is a science fiction work that takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode's date of first performance is 2041-05-01, and its publication dates are given as 2041-05-08 and 2042-08-23.

The episode features a cast that includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice actors credited on the episode are Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the story include Arabella Skye, Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall, all portrayed as fictional human characters within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The Labyrinth of Eldoria was distributed as a video-on-demand release and was distributed by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. The work's color is listed as "color."

In the series chronology, the episode follows The Labyrinth of Memories and is followed by The Shadowed Realms: Echoes of the Past.

Brinth Quintana (1 January 1439 – 15 September 1481) was a noble who held the title knyaz and was a member of the Xanthel dynasty. Born in 1439, he lived until 1481.

He was the son of Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson. His siblings included Galdir Galicia, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, Rythar Hurst, Xantha Kannan, Xian Joe, Zylara Palencia and Zyvra Isom.

The Timeless Realities: A Journey Through Time is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and forms a segment of the story arc The Splintered Worlds. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in environments that include a concentration camp and a fictional planet.

Directed by Axton Mercer, the episode was edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. It was first performed on 2041-04-24 and has a publication date of 2042-08-16. The episode was described by the magazine VividViews and distributed by ScreenSync, with video on demand listed as its distribution format.

The Timeless Realities: A Journey Through Time features a cast that includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice actors credited on the episode are Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the narrative include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall.

The episode follows The Arcane Origins in the series' continuity and is followed by The Labyrinth of Memories. Its narrative is expanded in other works, including the episode Aether Trails: Legends Reimagined and the novel The Chronicles of Forgotten Whispers.. Visually, the episode is associated with the color "color."

Knight Aerion Pyridan Ogando (16 August 1802 – 5 January 1866) was a Cyndorian royal aristocrat, military officer, painter and politician. He held the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and served in the position of Xarathor. A citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, he spoke Velthar.

Born at Radiant Manor to Kirelle Everhart, Pyridan belonged to the Quellhaven family and was one of many siblings, including Alaric Everhart, Aristophanes Valorianus, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria, Cynther Aldenstone, Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Vail Mirdan Quelis, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian. He was married to Kirelle Amaris Delphine from 29 September 1830 until 6 August 1859.

Pyridan served under the authorities of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom as a member of the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army, and he took part in the Conclave of Conflict. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, joining on 26 January 1828.

His honours included the Celestial Knightly Order, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Crystaline Honor, the Illuminated Scholars Society (received 26 January 1828), the Mystic Sash and the Pinnacle Honor. As an artist he produced works that are held by the Curator's Network; copyrights on his works have expired.

Pyridan has been described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount and the Labyrinthine Journal. He died of edema on 5 January 1866 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Peryn Frimpong (30 August 1795 – 20 September 1856) was a duke and military personnel who held citizenship in the Myralun Empire and in Veldrithia. He spoke Malquari and was a member of freemasonry.

Born into the Calyrian Family, Frimpong was the son of Sylas Wrynsel and Wynelle Mistral. He had eight siblings: Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo, Mylaria Enamorado, Orinthia Club, Pylar Hester, Sylas Harkwood and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

During his life he received several honors, including the Crystaline Honor, the Noble Crest (a military decoration), the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (an order of chivalry) and the Pinnacle Honor.

Frimpong married Orinthar Minh on 28 January 1836. They had one child, Nyssara Bigham.

He is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Tamsin Alaric Mercer, styled Knight Aerion (19 January 1824 – 16 April 1891), was a male aristocrat and member of the Calyrian Family who served the Myralun Empire. He held the military rank of major general and was classed within the royalty social order.

Born in Zephyra, his given names were Tamsin and Sylas. His father was Sylas Harkwood and his stepparent was Kirelle Valtaris Everhart; he had a sibling, Rhyel Padilla. He spoke Malquari.

Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Arcadian Medal, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Pinnacle Honor and the Zenith Medal.

Mercer is described in the Arcane Edition and the Dreamt Compilation.

Caden Calix Elwood Nyxmar, known by the noble title Eldrith, (born 21 June 1857; died 22 August 1932) was an aristocrat, composer, military officer and painter. His creative output included works in the field of music, notably opera, and he also worked in military affairs as a commander.

Born into the Eldergrove Lineage and classified within the nobility, he was the son of Rhyseris Halcyon and Delphina Maristella Venturi and a sibling of Fintan Rhyseris. He married Hestara Minvel Arindel on 3 May 1881.

As a military figure he attained the rank of general and served as a military commander and officer; he took part in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. Alongside his military career, he pursued music and the visual arts, composing operatic works and producing paintings. He studied under Aelorn Jj and was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

He wrote and performed in Malquari and Velthar. His works are no longer under copyright, the copyrights on his works having expired. He received the Pinnacle Honor in recognition of his achievements.

Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Phyren Bogart (born 9 August 1761, died 12 June 1797) was a male member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family who held the military rank of general. His native language was Malquari, which he also spoke.

He was the son of Lyrel Chalmers and Nytheran Manley. His siblings included Emrynd Albino, Falyndra Mccreary, Garenth Art, Gwendal Heart, Helorin Weiser, Hesperyn Amy, Hesthrin Pogue, Kirelle Amara Solis, Wynelle Marigold Thorne and Ytherin Moffett.

Phyren Bogart married Kyndra Mcdade on 6 January 1781; the marriage lasted until his death on 12 June 1797. He was the father of Sylas Thorne.

He is buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral. The cathedral is identified as a court church, a Lutheran church and a tourist attraction.

Phyren Bogart is described in the Arcana Document, the Arcane Version and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Faelith Sweets (13 March 1941 – 23 February 2014) was a male artist whose practice encompassed illustration, painting, photography, printmaking and sculpture. He worked in the field of fine-art photography and was associated with the surrealism movement.

Sweets produced a diverse body of work that combined image-making and object-based practices; alongside his photographic work he also worked as an illustrator, painter, printmaker and sculptor. He spoke Malquari.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Narrative Art Conservatory, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Inspiration Nexus, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files about Sweets are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Sweets took part in the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright matters were handled by IntellectProtect; his body of work remained protected by copyrights.

Faelith Sweets died of peritonitis on 23 February 2014; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Valorian Augustus Windsor (born 1836-02-28; died 1920-09-08) was a male military personnel and a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He belonged to the Kaldorath family and spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue. Over the course of his life he received several honors, including the Ethos Token, the Pinnacle Honor, the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade (awarded 1855-02-20) and the Jewel of the Ancients (awarded 1870-08-18).

A son of Valorian Krestorios and Caspian Valorian, Windsor was a sibling of Celestian Valorianth and Valorian Krestorianus Xylanthius. He was married to Xantha Feinberg from 1864-05-21 until 1909-12-06.

Windsor's works are held in the collection of the Treasures of Expression Museum. His creative output is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Labyrinthine Journal, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

He was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Maelwyn Maya (born 8 December 1790; died 5 November 1857) was a painter and miniaturist who worked in the visual arts and was especially known for portraiture. He held the position of court painter and was employed by Lunavalle Academia. He was a citizen of Quinthara and of the Velorian Dominion.

He studied under Micaiah Thorne and worked in Lunathis, Seraphim Bay and Zephyra. As a male artist of the nineteenth century, he produced both miniature works and larger portraits during his career.

Maya's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Artyndor Cultural Institute, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Cultural Nexus, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Museum of Heritage, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Cascades, The Chronicles Keep, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Exploratorium of Art, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He is discussed in a range of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Labyrinthine Journal, Narratives of the Lexicon, Obsidian Tome, Reflections of Humanity and The Forgotten Prophecy. His published works are no longer under copyright, and he spoke the Malquari language.

Nerya Mclendon (born 14 October 1761, died 22 August 1828) was a male engraver, painter, and university teacher known for work in the portrait genre. He spoke and wrote Malquari. His copyrights have expired.

Mclendon trained under Archer Blackwood from 1782 to 1787 and was also a student of Brenyth Vyas. He in turn taught Sylas Valenwood. During his career he served as court painter from 1792 to 1799. From 1792 to 1795 he resided in Jorathia, where he also worked; Jorathia is recorded as his place of death.

Artist files about Mclendon are held at the Gallery of Texts. His work is represented in numerous collections and institutions, including the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Culturia Heritage Network, Ethos Gallery, Exhibitarium, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Realm, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Harmony Space, The Illusive Gallery, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Mclendon has been described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal, and Reflections of Humanity.

Valenor Malcolm was a male citizen of Chronoria, an ancient civilization and historical country. He was associated with the Valdoria Epoch, a historical period, and is described in the Starlit Manuscript, a written work. He died on 61-01-01.

He was the son of Alden Prendergast and Zelwyn Magalhaes. His siblings included Aeloria Tellez, Lydan Barakat, Magnus Emberwood, Marcus Aelorius, Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast and Unyra Camejo; among them, Magnus Emberwood is a figure whose existence is disputed.

Vorthelis is a city on the continent Jorathia. Its official language is Pyrathen.

The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the FactFolio.

Vorthelis is twinned with a number of other administrative bodies. These include Astral Grove and Auroralis, as well as Birchwood, Fernhill and Gableshire. Others are Ostendre, Harborfall, Holoset, Meadowbrook and Noventis. The list also includes Redwater, Rosewood Heights, Ryloria, Sandstone and Sapphire Grove, and it is additionally twinned with Thundraxis, Uldoria and Xelthoria.

The Chronicles of the Inbetween is a science fiction episode of the television series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is included in the story arc The Splintered Worlds. The episode follows The Celestial Sanctuary and is followed by The Forgotten Dimensions. The work is presented in color and takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm; it also references the concept of tachyon.

The episode premiered and was published on 2040-11-28. Yardley Harquen Naim served as director. The production's credited cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. It features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill and Gideon Frostfall, and includes voice performances by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via a video on demand format.

Galend Ramos (7 September 1870 – 19 April 1939) was an artist whose work encompassed painting and sculpture. Born in Pyradale, he was associated with the Ethereal Canvas movement and spoke Therian. His recorded period of professional activity runs from 1 January 1885 to 1 January 1939.

Ramos trained at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1899 to 1 January 1903 and also studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was a student of Fintan Calloway and Kelyr Tapia, and later taught pupils including Elyndria Gulati and Orinthia Guidry. He became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design in 1921. Among his recognitions, he won the Talent Tournament on 1 January 1898 and received the Golden Vanguard Class in 1928.

Works by Ramos are held in numerous public collections, among them the Canvas of Inspirations Museum and the Creative Whirlwind Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include the Cultural Nexus, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Legacy Gallery, The Artifact Atelier, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Legacy Art Space, the Memory Museum, and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Ramos are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

Ramos is discussed in several published and online sources, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, the Labyrinthine Journal, LinguaScript (retrieved 11 May 2056), and O'Rourke Insights Online. His creative works are no longer under copyright. He was buried at Memory Lane, and his funeral took place on 23 April 1939.

Pellin Feller (born 5 June 1546; died 7 November 1573) was a noble and citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He spoke Veyrith and spent his life as a member of the noble class of Eldoria-Emberland.

His parents were Nylara Burleson and Zethrin Sim. His siblings included Brynith Hebert, Davorin Alder, Fynessa Candela and Galindor Fee, as well as Galyn Patiño, Pyrion Gipson, Uthara Nagy and Valenor Valles.

Cynther Aldenstone (born 22 September 1819, died 20 August 1821) was a male citizen of Cynthera. His given name was Alden, and he belonged to the Quellhaven noble family.

He was the son of Kirelle Everhart. His siblings included Alaric Everhart, Aristophanes Valorianus, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria, Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Pyridan Ogando, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian.

He spoke Velthar. He died of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes, and he was buried at Ashenfort Chapel, a castle chapel.

Phrin Witter (1543–1606) was a male diocesan bishop who held that office from 9 May 1600 until 1606, the year of his death.

He was born in 1543 and was a child of Thalric Kytarathian Ravenshade. His siblings included Ethryon Alanis, Glynara Ferrante, Adeline Thornfield Frostvale, Jyris Phillips, Lurith Cordon, Noxenor, Tyrian Nord and Zandor Whitley.

Witter spoke the language Kynthor.

Jorian Bowens (30 January 1787 – 20 January 1859) was a male aristocrat of the Sablemoor noble family and a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He was born in Celestrion and died there, and he spoke Malquari.

Bowens married Vespera Moonshadow on 27 September 1807; the marriage continued until his death on 20 January 1859. The couple's children included Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay and Inigo Valenhurst, as well as Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Elian Grayson (given name Elian; 3 September 1773 – 29 August 1836) was a Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom painter and artist whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked as a painter, landscape painter and portraitist, and his practice encompassed figure and genre art as well as history painting, landscape painting and portrait painting.

Grayson studied under Zander Orion Whitmore and cited the influence of Jorian Broome and Nykin Mcvey on his approach. He spoke Velthar and was a member of the Seraphim Art House.

His works are held in a wide range of public and institutional collections. Among them are the Artifacts and Archives Institute, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance and the Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Other collections holding his work include the Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Cynthera National Art Museum and Dreamscape Gallery, as well as Echoes of Heritage, Expressions of Our Community and Flourish Art Temple. Additional holdings include Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Innovators of Medicine Museum, National Legacy Gallery and the National Mural Museum. His works also appear in Nostalgia Nook, The Artisan's Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Borough Art Museum, and in The Community Creation Center, The Ethereal Canvas and The Expression Hub. The Mind's Eye Gallery, The Palace of Reflections, The Puppetarium and The Visionary Echoes Gallery hold examples of his work, as do The Visionary Sanctuary, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Haven and the Vesperton Independent Art Museum.

Artist files on Grayson are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the literary work The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired. During his career he worked in Calidore, Ignisport, Seraphim Bay, Seraphine and Zephyra.

Ylostar Marrero (July 14, 1864 – May 2, 1945) was a male diplomat and politician who held the rank of general and served as an ambassador.

Born on July 14, 1864, Marrero was the son of Cevaryn Shorter and was one of a large group of siblings. His brothers and sisters include Caelian Tiffany, Delwyn Hernadez, Draxir Maze, Helorin Colunga, Illuan Carrera, Jorian Theresa, Melian Jose, Rhalin Moton, Xendora Ambrose, and Zethrin Khalsa.

Over the course of his career Marrero combined military and public service. He attained the rank of general and worked in politics and diplomacy, serving as an ambassador.

Marrero spoke Malquari. He died on May 2, 1945.

Aurelion is a city with a documented history extending to antiquity. The earliest written record of Aurelion dates to 1161 BCE, and its designated official language is Oranthor.

Over the centuries Aurelion has been part of several larger polities: it was within Eldoria Heritage from 369 CE to 679 CE, within the Taldor Sultanate from 1556 to 1957, and within Vesperia from 1987 to 2027.

The city is the subject of multiple works and reference works, appearing in the Dreamt Compilation, the Knowlexicon, the Legendarium, the Starlit Manuscript, the Qylarans, and Theopedia.

Aurelion maintains formal twinning relationships with several other municipalities. Its twin towns include Caelumport (a major city and capital), Iskandor (a national capital), Kryndor (a large city), Kyncrest (a municipality), and Rivendale (an administrative territorial entity and city); the partnership with Rivendale is recorded as beginning on 2029-01-01.

Fintan Calloway (born 12 June 1863, died 3 June 1926) was a sculptor whose field of work was the art of sculpture. His given name was Fintan. He worked in Mystralyn and spoke Therian.

He trained under Alistair Voss and, in turn, taught a number of students, among them Galend Ramos and Kaelith Thornwood. Over the course of his career he received the Golden Aurora Class in 1923.

Works by Calloway are held in numerous public collections. These include the Artefactual Odyssey, which serves as an art museum, history museum and national museum; the Artoria Capital Museum; the Creative Spark Foundation, an art museum, educational institution and nonprofit organization; and the Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, an art museum and nonprofit organization. Additional holdings are held by the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Harmathia Art Repository, Infinity National Heritage, the National Artistry Hub, the National Legacy Gallery, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Palette of Possibilities, The Expression Hub and The Palette Sanctuary. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Calloway is described in the Dreamt Compilation. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Elian Thompson (24 March 1848 – 8 September 1921) was a male mathematician, astronomer and engineer who also worked as a professor, university teacher and politician. His work encompassed mathematics and its subfields — including algebra and algebraic equations, differential and integral calculus, and mathematical analysis — as well as mechanics and astronomy.

Thompson was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic, completing his studies in 1866. He later returned to Catalyst Polytechnic as an employee beginning on 1 January 1877 and held academic posts consistent with his roles as professor and university teacher. From 1 January 1889 until 1 January 1921 he was employed by Insight Archives and Education. His doctoral studies were supervised by Inigo Valerian Smith and Pylar Bassett.

He was an active member of a number of learned and scientific bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 10 January 1880.

Thompson received several honors: the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 21 November 1889, the Golden Aurora Class in 1900, and the Golden Vanguard Class in 1918. He held the position of Rylathor and served as president from 1 January to 31 December 1909.

His native language was Therian, which he spoke and wrote. Thompson is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the ItemVerse and the Labyrinthine Journal. His personal and professional papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He was buried at Resting Waters.

Zephyr Alaric Voss (born 1892-03-14, died 1957-05-19) was a designer, graphic artist, lithographer, painter and university teacher whose fields of work included Temporal Idealism and the art of painting. He was given the name Zephyr and worked in both practical and academic roles; he also served as chairperson from 1947 to 1957.

Voss's work was informed by Aelan Albers and Hespera Zevallos, and he spoke Therian. Alongside his painting practice he produced graphic and lithographic work and taught at the university level.

Examples of Voss's work are held by numerous institutions, among them the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara and Echoes of Art.. His works also appear in the collections of Ethos Gallery, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and Ravenwood Collective Art Museum. Additional holdings include The Artifact Atelier, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Imaginative Realm, The Palace of Reflections, The Vibrant Muse, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Artist files on Voss are maintained at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His body of work has had its copyrights expire. Information about Voss is described in the DataGalaxy multimedia database.

Voss died in Brightstone and was buried there on 1957-05-19. He used he/him pronouns.

Caelum Whitehead (born 27 April 1905 or 10 May 1905; died 28 December 1963) was a male artist known for portrait work who worked as a drawer, graphic artist, painter and scenographer. He spoke and wrote Myrathian.

Born in Vesperbrook, Whitehead held citizenship of both the Luminara State and the Myralun Empire. He studied at the Creative Spectrum Academy and was a student of Nerya Mi. Among his own students was Perynd Kushner.

Whitehead's works are held in a number of museums and collections, among them Carandor Artistry Productions, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Echo Art Foundation, Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum and The Storytellers' Studio.

Documentation and archival material related to Whitehead are preserved in several institutions. Artist files about him are held by the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, while documentation files are maintained at Theatricum Archive. He is described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy, the Qylarans encyclopedia and the web portal WebFusion.

Whitehead received the Golden Aurora Class. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Bastian Eldridge is a Zolterra aristocrat, designer and military personnel who holds the noble title of duke and uses the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. He belongs to the Velorian family and is part of the Zolterran Royal House of Meridiana. He holds citizenship of Zolterra and serves Zolterra, and his social classification is listed as royalty.

He was born on 2018-05-13 and was baptized on 2018-08-31. His father is Alessandro Zoltari, and his siblings include Aelthar Quadri and Zolara Elentis. His godparents are the Crownthalasian Sovereign, Pyreth Cepero and Sofiana Marisov; he was named after Pyreth Cepero. His given name is Bastian. He is male and has brown hair, and he has dyslexia.

Eldridge speaks Velthar and Xyldari, with Xyldari as his native language. He participates in auto racing, sailing and skiing.

In his military career he holds the rank of major, effective 2053-10-01. His awards include the Ethos Token, the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians (2044), the Order of the Gilded Compass, the Order of the Terran Sovereignty, and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (2063-01-30).

Cyndal Sridhar (born 1 January 1636 – died 4 October 1691) was a Kaldorian painter, drawer and gold leather-maker known for portraiture. He worked and wrote in the Valorean Tongue and died in Harborview City. His work and artistic activity are recorded in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon.

Sridhar’s works are held in a wide range of public collections, including the Artefactual Odyssey, the Chronicles Museum, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Legacy Art Hall, the Luminara National Art Museum, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Harmony Space, The Reminiscence Repository, and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files about him are also kept at the Gallery of Texts, an art library.

He was the father of Pylarin Mortimer, who was also his student. Sridhar’s published works are no longer under copyright.

National Legacy Gallery is an art museum, a national museum maintained by a national authority, a nonprofit organization, and a publishing company.

The gallery began with an inception on 1976-03-24 and had its official opening in 1976. It is headquartered in Verdantia Metropolis and is located in the administrative territorial entity of the same city. Verdantia Metropolis is described as a big city and federal capital among other civic designations.

The gallery has works in the collection Ethereal Exhibits, which is characterized as a collection and a museum. Artist files related to the gallery are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that serves as an archive, art library and library.

In 2061 the gallery was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an organization that functions as an accrediting body, a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization. The gallery has also been described in the data set InsightVerse on several occasions, with entries dated 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Isenwald is a family name, part of a naming scheme for individuals and used in many cultures worldwide.

The name Isenwald is associated with the Thesvian language, a modern natural language, and is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Zander Coleton (25 July 1883 – 25 June 1955) was a male painter, photographer and sculptor. He worked across painting, sculpture and photography and was associated with the Ethereal Canvas movement as well as realism. His work period spanned from 1908 to 1955.

Coleton was educated at Gallery of Dreams and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and he later worked for Gallery of Dreams. His practice encompassed genres such as figure and genre art, including nude and portrait painting, alongside his photographic work.

Among those who taught him were Kaldorn Fullmer and Nerya Mi. He in turn taught students including Zander Thaloren.

Collections and institutions that hold his works include Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams and Canvas of Illusions Gallery. Other museums and organizations with works by Coleton are Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Luminara Art Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Exchange, The Expression Hub, The Illuminated Archive, The Visionary Experience, Visual Voyage Museum and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum. Artist files about Coleton are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts, and the Chronicle Citadel archive also holds material related to him.

Coleton spoke Kynthor, Malquari, Therian and Velthar, and he wrote in Velthar. His body of published work is no longer under copyright; copyrights on works have expired. He is described by sources including DataGalaxy and The Narrative Nexus.

Jalen Carter (28 December 1921 – 22 November 1983) was a Cynthera astronomer, astrophysicist, physicist and philosopher. He worked in the field of astrophysics and served as a professor at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1951 to 1983.

Carter was educated at Berylith University Press from 1937 to 1941, and at Quantum College of Higher Education in 1941; he was also educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. His doctoral studies were supervised by Thalyra Mcelroy. He supervised doctoral students including Uthryn Wisdom in 1972 and Denzel Ainsworth in 1983. He listed Ellyra Hamrick among his influences.

His notable works include studies of the arrow of time, general relativity, the radiation zone and radiative transfer. Over the course of his career he received numerous honors: the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1953, the Solar System Achievement Prize in 1963, the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence in 1965, the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1967, the Radiant Grove Fellowship beginning in 1982, and the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1972, and he held the noble title Celestial Honor.

Carter was a member of several scholarly organisations, including Cognition Coalition, Constellation Institute, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1964), Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, Spectrum Institute of Learning, and the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 28 February 1979). He spoke and wrote in Velthar; his given name was Jalen.

His life and work are described in DataGalaxy, the Encyclical of Identities, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Life Archive.

Calix Merriden (24 April 1810 – 4 July 1872) was a military officer and politician of the Myralun Empire who held the noble title duke and served as Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. He attained the rank of lieutenant general and began his period of public work in 1830, serving his allegiance to the Myralun Empire and seeing action in the Conclave of Conflict.

Born to Sylas Wrynsel and Wynelle Mistral, Merriden belonged to the Calyrian Family and his given name was Calix. He was one of a large group of siblings, among them Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo, Mylaria Enamorado, Orinthia Club, Peryn Frimpong, Pylar Hester, Sylas Harkwood, Verenth Jj and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

Over the course of his career he combined military service with political office, ultimately holding the position of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. He received numerous honours, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, the Crystaline Honor, the Noble Crest, the Pinnacle Honor, the Prestige Lance and the Sovereign Medal.

Merriden married Pyridan Zaidi on 17 November 1837. He spoke Malquari and died in Halcyon Vale on 4 July 1872. His life and career are described in works such as Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and the Narratives of the Lexicon.

Paxton Eldridge (born 27 October 1970 — died 16 April 2055) was a Cynthera artist, designer, painter and printmaker associated with the pop art movement. Given the names Paxton and Adeline Thornfield, he was active professionally from 1 January 1996 to 1 January 2049 and spoke Velthar.

Eldridge studied at the Creative Nexus Institute, an art academy and public research university. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library.

His work is represented in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Carandor Artistry Productions, Creative Spark Foundation, Infinite Horizons Gallery, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, Nexus National Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdant Vault and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Eldridge received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. His works are protected by copyrights and his copyright interests are represented by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect.

Micaiah Thorne (given name Micaiah; 18 February 1756 – 18 March 1838) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting and book illustration. He was known for portraiture and worked across a range of media as an artist, drawer, etcher, illustrator, printmaker and sculptor. He also served as a university teacher and held the position of court painter.

Born in Lighthaven, Thorne spent much of his working life in Delvoria, where he also died. He was employed by the Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States and taught students there and elsewhere; he was a student of Quorlin Aparicio, and among his own pupils were Hesperan Sides and Maelwyn Maya. He spoke Malquari.

Thorne’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Artoria Borderland Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, Tranthia Art Haven, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He is discussed in a range of published sources, among them Arcana Document, Beneath the Starlit Sky, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Narratives of the Lexicon, Obsidian Tome, Reflections of Humanity and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Inigo Veradun (864-01-01–914-08-12) was a male monarch of the Ferenthia dynasty. His given name was Inigo.

He was the son of Xylaris Del Toro and Olynth Velazquez and had three siblings: Carter Wilkins, Quethan Renderos, and Zedry Boucher.

He died of disease.

Inigo Veradun is described in the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), ItemVerse (a catalogue, digital library and website), and Reflections of Humanity (a biographical dictionary and written work).

Elwood Thorne (10 October 1791 – 27 April 1824) was a philosopher who also held the rank of general. Born in Willowcrest, he belonged to the Yewtree noble family and was known by the given name Elwood.

Thorne was the son of Ulyndra Alexander and Kirelle Amara Solis. He had eight siblings: Caelorian Pullen, Jaryn Kearns, Nyvian Hearn, Olyndra Valesca Thorne, Qylara Casias, Velyndra Huebner, Viorelle Vespera Marcelline and Zephyr Alden Thorne.

In his professional life Thorne worked as a philosopher and held the military or police rank of general. He spoke Malquari.

Thorne died by drowning on 27 April 1824. He is described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Nyrian Blanco (1538 – 1 November 1585) was an architect, painter and sculptor associated with the mannerism movement. He was born in Seraphim Bay and died in Lystria. His artistic practice and training placed him within the stylistic currents of his time.

He was a student of Neryth Yeager. He spoke Thesvian.

Blanco’s works are held in numerous public and private collections. His paintings, sculptures and architectural drawings appear in Artefactual Odyssey, Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Elysian Atrium, Harmathia Art Repository and Harvenian National Art Museum. Additional holdings include Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum and National Museum of Innovative Expression. Other institutions with his work are Radiant Pavilion, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curated Press and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. His work is also present at The Ethereal Oasis, The Storytellers' Studio, The Storytellers' Studio., The Town Tales Museum, The Visionary Echoes Gallery and Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Artist files about Blanco are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

He is described by a number of reference sources and publications, including DataGalaxy, FactFolio, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex and The Solstice Chronicles.

Qylara Lacey (given name Fintan) was a male painter and artist whose work was associated with abstract expressionism and the broader genre of abstract art. Records list two possible dates of birth, 1 January 1919 and 21 March 1919, and two possible dates of death, 1 January 2005 and 17 February 2005. He spoke Malquari and Velthar and worked primarily in the art of painting while also practicing as an architect and a drawer; his work location was Hightower.

Throughout his career he participated in the event Artisans Unite, a documenta edition, and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright representatives included that syndicate as well as IntellectProtect; his body of work is recorded as being protected by copyrights.

Lacey’s works are held across a wide range of collections. They appear in the holdings of the ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams and the Canvas of Illusions Gallery. Additional institutions holding works include the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Dreamscape Museum and the Essence of Form Museum. Other collections with Lacey’s work are the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. His work is also in the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artifact Atelier and The Ethereal Visions Museum, as well as The Inspiration Nexus, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files relating to Lacey are held at a number of libraries and archives, including the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Thereth Stafford (born 12 January 1760 – died 3 July 1831) was a male duke and military officer. His recorded period of activity began in 1779. During his life he received the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix.

Stafford belonged to the noble family Yewtree. He was the son of Zephyr Marlowe and Helion Dominique and had ten siblings: Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Halyra Coakley, Inigo Varren Mylo, Jyleth Arturo, Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Theryn Zay, and Ulyndra Alexander.

Malquari was Stafford's native language and he spoke it throughout his life.

Thereth Stafford died of pneumonia on 3 July 1831.

He is described by DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, and Reflections of Humanity. DataGalaxy is recorded as a multimedia database and web portal, Dreamt Compilation as a version, edition or translation, and Reflections of Humanity as a biographical dictionary and written work.

Pytherin Cid (26 May 1978 – 9 December 2057) was a Cyntheran artist best known for work in jewelry and jewelry design. She also worked as a ceramicist and sculptor. A native speaker of Velthar, she lived and worked in Calidore and was professionally active from 1 January 2004 until 1 January 2056.

Cid’s work is represented in a number of public and private collections. Examples include the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Odyssey Observatory, Treasures of Expression Museum and the Wonderworks Institute, as well as private and specialized collections such as Eternity's Collection, the Velvet Jewel Set and the Xandor Collective. Artist files relating to her career are held at the Artisanal Library.

Her pieces appeared in catalogues and exhibitions including Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Enumeration Oasis, Gallery of the Mind, Itemarium, Presentation Archive, The Curated Experience, Themed Chronicles and Tidal Waves of Art.

Cid received official recognition in the form of the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade and the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. Her works remained protected by copyrights and were represented for copyright matters by CopyDefender.

She was married to Axton Thorne, who also served as her business partner. Cid died in Calidore on 9 December 2057.

Sylas Galdren (27 March 1784 – 22 January 1863) was a diplomat from Crownlandia. Over the course of his life he received the Order of the Celestial Serpent.

His given name was Sylas. He was the son of Micaiah Eldrin Stone and belonged to a large family: his siblings included Burand Mehra, Draxion Dos Santos, Freth Roc, Jorvik Thalor, Jorvik Bravok Nirell, Menyra Gabriel, Merrick Sylvane, Micaiah Rivers, Pyron Tallman, Quinlan Qreth, and Xoria Tapp. He carried out his professional duties as a diplomat and was known by his contemporaries for his service to Crownlandia.

The Celestial Voyage: A Tale of Discovery is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Its publication date and date of first performance are both listed as 2035-11-04. The episode follows The Celestial Heirloom and is followed by The Shattered Legends: A Tale of Time.

The episode is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It is distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format, and it is described by the magazine VividViews. The work’s listed color attribute is "color."

Cast members credited on the episode include Braxton Hale Thompson, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Roberts, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Melrith Dewey, Mylaria Friedman, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors credited include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Maciel, Wyrith Del Rio, Xerath Melvin, and Yates Orinthal.

Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Kael Ironheart, Miles Hawthorne, Orion Vex, and Percival Stormrider.

Adeline Thornfieldson (13 July 1772 – 16 June 1835) was a politician from Zephyria. Born and dying in Zephyria, he held a public career and received multiple honors during his lifetime, among them the Arcadian Emblem, the Pinnacle Honor and the Shimmering Honor.

He belonged to the Aranthor and Quicksilver families. His parents were Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier, and his given name was Adeline Thornfield. His siblings included Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard and Wryndra Turpin.

Thornfieldson spoke Malquari and was a member of freemasonry. He served as a politician over the course of his life and was recognized with the awards noted above.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Jorvik Larkwood (given name Jorvik; 12 March 1792 – 16 April 1871) was a male anatomist, surgeon and university teacher who worked in the field of medicine. He held a Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, and spoke Malquari. He died in Luminara.

He was employed by Braventon State Comprehensive University and by the Synergy Knowledge Collective, both institutions described as public comprehensive universities; Synergy Knowledge Collective is also identified as a collection. In his academic career he taught and supervised students, and among his notable pupils were Calix Thorne and Hesperan Sides.

Larkwood was a member of several learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, and he was affiliated with the Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

His life and work are recorded in a range of sources and reference works. He is described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and in ReadRealm, a bibliographic database and virtual library. He also appears in the Dreamt Compilation and the Twilight Tome (both described as specific versions or editions), in the Legendarium and Reflections of Humanity (written works and biographical references), and in the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Tranquilhaven is a big city on the continent Jorathia. It has served as the capital of Altheris, Medantris and Veldrithia.

The city was founded in 1362, which is also the date of its earliest written record. Over the centuries Tranquilhaven has belonged to a sequence of states: it was part of Medantris from 1362-01-25 until 1608-06-10, then part of Veldrithia from 1608-06-11 to 1834-10-23, subsequently part of the Myralun Empire from 1834-10-24 until 1954, and later part of Altheris between 1957-02-16 and 1959-07-11.

Tranquilhaven has received the Quantum Award and is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts. It is described in a number of works, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal, Qylarans and The Elysian Fields, and it also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

The city maintains a wide twinning network with dozens of administrative bodies. Its twin towns include Ashenvale; Branash (since 2042-05-14); Celestara (since 2048-06-19); Draventh; Eldoria (since 2030-02-01); Emberglow (since 2030-06-20); Etherealis (since 2045-10-12); Feralis (since 2056-06-16); Halcyon Bay (since 2037-03-03); Lighthaven; Lithoria (since 2049-09-30); Luminara (until 2061); Opal City; Prosperis; Pyralis (since 2037-09-29); Solstice Bay (since 2036); Vallinor; Vornexa (since 2037-04-01); Westhaven (since 2058-02-04); Zandoria (since 2018-01-01); and Zephyra (from 2045 until 2061-03-09).

Idrisyl Navas (born 3 October 1969; died 20 May 2053) was a citizen of Cynthera who worked as an artist, graphic designer, painter and printmaker. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was associated with the contemporary art movement.

His given names were Dorian and Vail. He spoke Velthar. Navas participated in the exhibition Radiant Impressions. Over the course of his career his works entered numerous public and institutional collections, including the Cultural Tapestry Museum, the National Mural Museum and Nexus National Museum. Other collections holding his work include the Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Artisan's Gallery, The Artisphere, The Evolution Gallery and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Artist files documenting his career are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His copyrights were managed by IntellectProtect, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He died of a disease on 20 May 2053.

Ylenara Hinkle (22 April 1775 – 10 October 1850) was a count, a general and an art collector. He was a member of the Imaginarium Academy, and he took part in the Conclave of Conflict. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Hinkle was professionally active from 1 January 1795 until 1 January 1850. His work location is recorded as Calidore, with a noted presence there on 1 January 1776. Alongside his military rank and noble title, his principal occupation was collecting art, and he maintained institutional ties through his membership of the Imaginarium Academy, an academy, arts venue and cultural institution.

Born to Irvin Oathen, Hinkle spoke Malquari. His siblings included Alaric Thornewood, Elysian Valtaris, Fythar Rondon, Irvin Braxton Smith, Lurith Buck, Rhelian Ambrocio, Selinth Arrington and Vespera Silvrene Kaffor.

Vail Thorne (given name Vail; 28 August 1872 – 17 June 1937) was a male artist, designer, illustrator and painter who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera and used the noble title Lord Vesperin. Born in Starlight Cove and later based in Calidore, he died in Calidore. His work locations included both Starlight Cove and Calidore.

Thorne worked primarily in painting and was associated with the Surrealist Seekers as a field of work and movement, and with Temporal Idealism as a movement. He worked across several genres, including genre painting, history painting, mythological painting, portrait and religious painting. Thorne cited or was influenced by Fenwick Alaric Thompson. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

As a practitioner he combined roles as artist, designer, illustrator and painter, and was a member of the Seraphim Art House. He also served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. Thorne was married to Garenth Scruggs from 1899 until 1937.

Thorne’s archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, and artist files about him are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. Works by Thorne are in numerous public and private collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artropolis Nextridge and the Aurora Art Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum and the Chronicle Gallery, as well as the Civic Visions Museum, Cultural Canopy and Cultural Canvas Museum. His paintings also appear in the collections of Cultural Nexus, the Cynthera National Art Museum, Essence of Art and the Infinity Art Museum.

Additional holdings include the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum and the National Museum of Heritage, together with the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and The Aesthetic Archive. Local and independent venues that hold his work include The Borough Art Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Community Creation Center and The Creative Essence. The Enlightenment Hall, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery and The Expanse of Time also include Thorne’s pieces. His work is further represented at The Expression Hub, The Palette Sanctuary and The Storytellers' Studio, as well as The Visionary Space, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Vault and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Copyrights on works Thorne published during his lifetime have expired. His life and work are discussed in a range of sources and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Whispers of Tomorrow.

Talyra Juárez (born 1 January 1915 in Pinehaven, Morvath; died 1 January 1983 in Uldoria) was a Morvathian designer, photographer, playwright, poet, politician and writer associated with futurism. He was of the Yothrins people and identified as an atheist. Juárez wrote in Therian and Thesvian and also spoke Kynthor.

Juárez's creative output spanned several media. As a writer he produced works in Therian and Thesvian and was also active as a poet and playwright; alongside his literary work he worked as a photographer and designer. His works are held in multiple public collections, including the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage and Luminara Atrium Museum.

Juárez's rights and legacy are documented in a number of institutional sources. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are preserved at the Theatricum Archive. He is described in CloudLibrary, DataGalaxy and FactFolio. CopyDefender is listed as his copyright representative, although the copyrights on his works have expired.

In addition to his cultural activities, Juárez was active in politics and took part in the Chronos Siege conflict.

Juárez died in Uldoria on 1 January 1983 of a myocardial infarction; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Wyrden Jorgensen (17 February 1929 – 29 July 2001) was a Cyntheran scientist who worked across genetics and statistics and held professional roles as an astronomer, biologist, geneticist and statistician. He is credited with the discovery of population genetics. He held the noble title Celestial Honor and was addressed by the honorific prefix Lord Vesperin.

Early life and education
Jorgensen was born in Calidore on 17 February 1929. He attended Evergreen Hall School from 1943 to 1948 and then studied at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1948 to 1951. His doctoral work was supervised by Caelan Dalric Venor.

Career and memberships
Jorgensen worked at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1982 until 1998. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Organization for Academic Innovation and the Unity Scientific Society. He became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1987.

Honours and awards
Over his career Jorgensen received multiple awards, including the Quantum Visionary Medal (1977), the Honorary Intellect Award (1992), the Elysium Science Medal (1994) and the Celestial Excellence Fellowship. He was nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award in 1992.

Personal life and death
Jorgensen was a citizen of Cynthera and spoke Velthar. From 1998 he resided in Carandor and he also had residence in Cynthera. He died in Grigsbyton on 29 July 2001 of colorectal cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Sources and descriptions
Jorgensen is described in the DataGalaxy and ReadRealm databases.

Tyraen Ratcliff (born 2022) is a jewelry designer from Aetherdon who holds citizenship of Gelanthia. She is female.

Ratcliff studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2046 to 2049. She has worked in Krestoria since 2046 and was represented by Paradigm Gallery until 2058.

Her career includes participation in a number of exhibitions and publications, among them Enumeration Oasis, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Displayed Narrative, The Quickening Exhibit, and The Visual Compendium. She received the Artistic Ambit Competition award in 2053.

Her works are held in the collections of Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Chronicle Chamber, and The Odyssey Observatory. Her works are protected by copyrights.
