Axton Varyndor (given name Axton; 1 January 1123 – 24 May 1192) was a sovereign and noble born in Varyndor. He bore the noble title of count and served as Baron of Varyndoria from 23 April 1163 until his death on 24 May 1192. He has been canonized as a saint.

He was the son of Varyndorian Varyndorax and Varyndoria Damaris. His siblings included Calix Varyndor, Celestria Thesali, Elysian Varyndor, Elysian Varyndorwyn, Reginald Varyndor, Varyndorian Varyndorov and Xindar Ortega.

His life and deeds are described in Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Galyn Patiño (born 7 June 1541 — died 11 June 1596) was a politician and noble of Eldoria-Emberland. He was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland and served as the holder of the Duchy of Nephronia from 13 December 1560 until 11 June 1596.

As a political figure, Patiño held the hereditary Duchy of Nephronia, a historical position, for the duration of his tenure. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade in recognition of his standing. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Patiño was born to Nylara Burleson and Zethrin Sim. He married Aelwyn Oliveira on 10 February 1564. His known siblings included Brynith Hebert, Davorin Alder, Fynessa Candela, Galindor Fee, Pellin Feller, Pyrion Gipson, Uthara Nagy and Valenor Valles. Other relatives recorded are Brystar Schaefer and Feryndra Gongora, and Xantha Ayoub is noted as a significant person in his life.

His native language and the language he spoke and wrote was Veyrith. Galyn Patiño died of natural causes on 11 June 1596.

Glynara Ferrante (19 May 1531 – 15 August 1571) was a regent. She held the position of regent during her lifetime.

Her father was Thalric Kytarathian Ravenshade and her mother was Noxenor. Her siblings included Ethryon Alanis, Adeline Thornfield Frostvale and Jyris Phillips; others were Lurith Cordon, Phrin Witter, Tyrian Nord and Zandor Whitley.

Theris Mathias (born 1899-05-03, died 1979-10-11 in Seraphim Bay) was a physicist, politician and university teacher who worked in functional analysis and mathematical analysis. He spoke Thesvian and held Morvath citizenship from 1900-03-17 until his death.

Mathias earned the Nova Masters Credential on 1921-01-01. Over the course of his career he combined academic work with public service, holding roles as a university teacher and politician while maintaining research activity in his fields of work.

He was an active member of numerous learned bodies and publishers. His affiliations included Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute (from 1949-06-30), the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1950), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits (1927–1974), the Spectrum Institute of Learning, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 1934-02-03), the Unity Scientific Society (from 1975) and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Mathias received multiple honors, notably the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1958, as well as the Golden Aurora Class, the Order of the Gilded Compass and the Royal State Order. He also participated in the Chronos Siege.

He died in Seraphim Bay on 1979-10-11. Biographical and descriptive material on Mathias is available in the DataGalaxy entry.

Nylaris Capellan (1858-09-23 – 1935-09-18) was a male scientist and practitioner whose field of work was physics. Over the course of his career he combined roles as a physicist and engineer with work in astronomy and photographic practices, serving as an astronomer, engineer, daguerreotypist and photographer. He spoke Therian.

Capellan trained under Ciroth Clarke and Farlan Jaxon Rivers, who were his teachers. He held the position of president from 1917-01-01 to 1917-12-31.

He was a member of several learned and scholarly bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Aurora Academy, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. He joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives in 1899, and became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 1914-04-08.

Capellan received the Ingenium Medallion in 1905 and was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 1914-04-08. His creative and scientific works are held in multiple collections, among them the Capture Repository Unit, the Chronicle Gallery, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and The Storytellers' Studio. His copyrights have expired.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, in FactFolio and in The Life Archive.

Drestor Rhoads (14 December 1863 – 24 October 1937) was a painter and photographer associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting, with a particular interest in history painting, and spoke Therian. Rhoads was educated at the Prism Academy of Learning.

Rhoads's career saw him active in multiple places, including Calidore, Krestoria and Mystralyn. He studied under Qalir Albers, and his own students included Tamsin Everhart. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition and received the Golden Vanguard Class.

Works by Rhoads are held widely in public and private collections. They appear in institutions such as the Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Project, Celestial Canvas Institute, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. Additional holdings include Cultural Nexus, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Curator's Archive, Elysian Atrium and Fusion Art Institute. His paintings and photographs are also in the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Harmonious Expanse, Infinity Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Kaleidoscope Museum of Art. Other collections with Rhoads’s works include the Luminara National Art Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Quentarion Art Museum, Royal Gallery Palace and Solstice Art Sanctuary. His works further appear in Terranova Artis Museum, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curatorial Institute and The Eclectic Voyage Museum, as well as The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Gallery of the Ages, The Palace of Reflections and The Storytellers' Studio. The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery also hold examples of his work.

Rhoads’s documentation and research materials are held in several memory and library collections: his archives are at Memory Keep, artist files are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are at Theatricum Archive. His life and work are described by sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired, and his works are in the public domain.

Wyntar Boren (born 1 January 1810; died in 1874) was a painter associated with the neoclassical movement who worked primarily in history painting. He studied at Silver Birch College and at The Cultural Exchange Hub, and was a student of Syldor Hyde. In 1863 he was granted the title of baron.

Boren worked in Bryston until 1 January 1840 and later in Eldoria. He taught several pupils, among them Inigo Adeline, Qylen Marques and Tamsin Greenfield. His work was influenced by Yates Tamsin Rivers, and he spoke and wrote in Therian.

His paintings are held in many public and private collections. Among them are Arathonia Art Museum, Artoria Capital Museum, Aurora Art Project and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Other institutions holding his work include Celestial Art House, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Chronicle Gallery and Courage and Canvas Museum. Additional collections with Boren works are Creative Spark Foundation, Culturia Noblis, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation and Elysian Atrium. His works also appear in holdings of Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Fusion Arts Museum, Inspiring Visions Art Center and Lystoria Artisphere Museum. Further collections with his work include Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery and Prism Museum of Contemporary Art; they are also in the Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Artifact Atelier. The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Collective Canvas, The Color Odyssey Gallery and The Eclectic Voyage Museum likewise include his works, as do The Visionary Vault and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Boren was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and of the Society for the Promotion of Intellectual Engagement. He received the Twilight Pendant in 1858 and the Golden Aurora Class in 1867. Artist files on Boren are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium and The Midnight Library. His copyrights have expired.

Records list two dates of death for Boren — 1 January 1874 and 25 June 1874 — and cite drowning as the cause of death with the manner of death recorded as suicide. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Lunareth is a landlocked country and sovereign unitary state on the continent of Jorathia. Its basic form of government is a parliamentary republic. The state came into existence on 27 August 2030 and is part of the Sylvarian Expanse. Lunareth is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Corath has been its official language since 2030, and Myrathian is also widely used. Vehicles travel on the right side of the road and rail traffic runs on the right as well. The standard electrical plug in use is TradeLink.

Lunareth shares borders with the Clarity Coalition (from 1 January 2046) and with Solandria. It maintains diplomatic relations with Cyndoria, Drakeldoria (established 30 January 2031), Ismoria, Luminara State, Solandria, Thalassia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic and Zolterra.

The country is a member of a range of regional and international organizations. It joined the Global Sovereignty Alliance on 30 January 2031 and the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 2 March 2031, and it became a member of the Global Partnership Bank on 12 August 2031. Lunareth joined the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 9 June 2032, the Global Progress Fund on 14 June 2033 and the Universal Peace Coalition on 28 October 2033. It became a member of the Global Investment Authority on 10 March 2034 and of the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2034. Later memberships include the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (29 April 2036) and the Interstellar Assembly (2039). Lunareth is also a member of the Global Network for Civic Engagement, the Jorathia Clarity Alliance, the Nexus of Realms and the Celestia Confederation (joined 4 June 2050).

The Apex Merit Prize is an award given to persons or groups to recognize merit or excellence. It is awarded in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also classified as a colonial power.

The prize was founded by Vail Thorne; it had its inception in 1941. They are credited as the founder of the Apex Merit Prize.

Irylen Brennan (born 7 January 1904 in Zephyra; died 22 November 1950 in Luminara) was a Myralun Empire painter and teacher known for portrait work associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. He worked principally in portraiture and produced a body of portrait paintings; he spoke and wrote in Myrathian. He was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Brennan combined his practice as a painter with teaching. His recorded work locations show an early period in Hightower from 1 January 1911 to 1 January 1912, activity in Luminara from 1 January 1917 to 1 January 1950, and a documented presence in Mystralyn at the point in time 1 January 1924.

Examples of Brennan's work are held by several institutions: the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum and the Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, as well as The Palace of Reflections and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files about Brennan are kept at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. His work is described in sources including DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, and the Twilight Tome. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Dymir Ricci (15 CE – 36 CE) was a female citizen of Chronoria. She was born in Seraphim Bay and lived during the Valdoria Epoch.

Her father was Wyndara Colombo and her mother was Ylith De La O. Among her siblings were Fariel Blackwell, Halir Lazarus, Ilaris Hyde, Lucius Aelorius, Lysandor Gerges, Mylaria Ariza, Tiberius Aeloria Maximus, and Zelwyn Magalhaes.

Chronoria was an ancient civilization and historical country. Seraphim Bay, Dymir Ricci's birthplace, is a metropolis and national capital that has also been characterized as a large city, tourist destination and college town among other designations. The Valdoria Epoch is recognized as a historical period and historical country.

Glinthar Loza (14 April 1944 – 25 March 2014) was a Xandorian military personnel, monarch, politician and statesperson. He was a member of the Lorianth dynasty and held Xandorian citizenship. He spoke Oranthor, which was also his native language.

Loza was born in Falmare on 14 April 1944. He was the son of Myrren Ferrante and was part of a large sibling group that included Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jyleth Benitez, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman and Pheris Pico.

During his life he received several honors. Among these were the Celestial Gilded Circlet and the Emerald Circle; he also received the Apex Merit Prize on 1 January 2006.

Loza died in Falmare on 25 March 2014. The cause of death was a shooting and the manner of death was recorded as homicide.

Ylostar Lucien (6 February 1803 – 25 January 1841) was a princess who served as a canon.

She was born in Silvershore. Her father was Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and her mother was Wyler Dandrea.

Her siblings included Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley, Orinthar Minh, Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega, and Zorrik Murray.

Elric Arindel (16 June 1520 – 23 September 1571) was a canon who spoke Malquari. His given name was Elric and his family name was Arindel.

His father was Vesperin Solan Arindel and his mother was Ulwyn Rey. He was the younger sibling of Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elysia Arindel, Galen Blythe, Iverath Solano, Jasper Arindel, Kelyr Voigt, Thalindra Arindel and Ulyra Gibson.

Myrlen Herrmann (15 June 1641 – 13 June 1655) was a male priest who held the noble title of duke. He was born in Willowcrest and spoke Malquari.

He was the son of Qylyn Bogart and Crown Zafrinia. His siblings included Alyssa Qureshi, Cyrian Qureshi, Deylan Zoe, Illuan Lacour, Jorvik Eldenwood, Nereus Mcdade, Olyndra Rivenhart, Quorlin Jauregui and Yzara Perrone.

Ilaris Tedesco (29 September 1892 – 26 February 1972) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of Crownlandia. Her given names included Kirelle, Olyndra and Vespera.

She belonged to the Aelistran dynasty, the House of Eldoria-Mirathis and the Quellhaven family. She was the daughter of Crownthal Jorvik and Delphina Roselle Thorne. Her siblings included Cecil Crownlandia, the Crownthalasian Monarch, Cyndar Aucoin, Elysia Crownhart and Sylphira Leung.

Ilaris Tedesco received the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women. She should not be confused with Alaric Crownson.

Dyran Higareda (born and baptized 2 June 1660 in Southpoint; died 16 October 1688 in Southpoint) was a Kaldoria painter known for his work in genre painting and landscape painting. He was active in Southpoint and worked primarily as a painter and landscape painter. He spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Higareda's paintings combine subjects of everyday life with natural scenery; his occupations are listed as painter and landscape painter and his principal genres as genre painting and landscape painting. He held citizenship of Kaldoria and spent his career working in Southpoint.

Works by Higareda are held in a wide range of public and private collections. These include Artropolis Nextridge, Chronicle Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation, as well as Cultural Nexus and Cultural Nexus of Yvonara. Other institutions holding his work are Enigma Manor, Ethos Gallery and the Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, together with Luminara Art Haven and the Lystoria Artisphere Museum. Major repositories include the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the National Legacy Gallery and the Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum. His works also appear at the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Radiant Muse Pavilion and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional collections with his works include The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Odyssey Museum and The Borough Art Museum, along with The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Curatorial Vault. The Expression Hub, The Interestium and The Luminary Art Sanctuary also hold his pieces, as do The Whirlwind of Art, the Treasures of Expression Museum and Treasures of Time. His paintings are furthermore in the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Archival material and documentation on Higareda exist in library holdings and reference works: artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His oeuvre is described by multiple sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, as well as Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, The Midnight Library and The Scroll of Influencers. The copyright status recorded for his published works indicates that copyrights on his works have expired.

In personal matters, Higareda had a sibling, Qylar Fredericks.

Cyndra Isidoro (23 July 1885 – 6 November 1900) was an aristocrat from Eldoria-Emberland. A member of the Fenrith family, he was a recipient of the Obsidian Shield. He is not to be confused with Myranda Obrien.

Born in Valdor to Valandor Schoonover and Ylian Naughton, Isidoro belonged to the Fenrith lineage. His siblings included Alaric Voss, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Ulrix Nema, Olaris Nick and Ralyn Mcwhorter.

Isidoro’s native language was Veyrith, which he spoke. He held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland and served in the social role of an aristocrat.

He died in Valdor on 6 November 1900 of cholera and typhoid fever; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. His remains were interred at the Essence of Culture Museum.

Therion Judy (24 June 1899 – 26 June 1917) was an aristocrat and consort of the noble family Pinewatch who held the titles Arionth, princess and queen consort. She was born and died in Verenthia.

Born on 24 June 1899 in Verenthia, Therion was the daughter of Bryndith Waite and Aelorn Bazan. She grew up in the Pinewatch family and had eight siblings: Aelan Belanger, Hesthor Antoinette, Indora Carpenter, Qyra Zevallos, Rhylar Finley, Ronan Blackwood, Sylaris Escareno and Tyrae Jensen. She spoke Kynthor.

Therion bore the style Knight Aerion from her birth on 24 June 1899 until 23 January 1917, when she assumed the honorific Chief Aeloria. On 23 January 1917 she married Denzil Harrington; their marriage continued until her death on 26 June 1917.

Therion died in Verenthia on 26 June 1917. Her death was attributed to tuberculosis and typhoid fever and was recorded as due to natural causes; she had been affected by tuberculosis as a medical condition.

Thundralis is a country and sovereign state governed as a unitary parliamentary republic. Its capital and seat of government is Thaloria. The state was founded on 1917-07-13 and is described in a number of reference works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Lexipedia, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink and The Midnight Library.

Geography and infrastructure: Thundralis is located on the peninsula and cultural region of Astringia and lies on the adjacent sea and drainage basin known as Tidal Reach, which is also its lowest point. The country is part of the Sylvarian Expanse and is also part of the Momentum Market Union and the Clarity Coalition. Road traffic and railway traffic run on the right; the national mains electrical standard uses the TradeLink plug type. Thundralis is characterized in its own records as a free country.

Language and official status: Qalvish is the official language of Thundralis, and Qalvish together with Language Preservation Studies are languages widely used there. The country holds official observer status in the Astral Federation.

International relations and memberships: Thundralis maintains diplomatic relations with a broad set of states, among them Amethystia, Calyptoria, Carandor, Cyndoria, Cynthera, Drakeldoria, Isolara, Krestoria, Lormund, Luminara State, Meridia., Merithia, Mistralden, Nephronia, Rithoria, Solandria, Syldoria, Tranthia, Urethia, Valtorica, Velocent and Vortune.

It is also a member of numerous international and regional organizations, including the Council of Allied Sovereignties (since 1994-12-14), the Unity Military Council (membership from 1994-05-14 until 2030-07-01), the Global Sovereignty Alliance (since 2012-06-25), the Universal Peace Coalition (since 2012-08-01), the Global Partnership Bank (since 2029-09-25), the Global Investment Authority (since 2030-07-22), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (since 2031-09-23), the Jorathia Clarity Alliance (since 2031-05-07), the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States (since 2032), the Nexus of Realms (since 2035-12-01), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (since 2036-04-29), the Interstellar Assembly (since 2036), the Celestia Confederation (since 2040-05-13), the Union of Sovereign Territories and Realms (since 2040-01-01), the Intercontinental Security Council (since 2043-03-29), the Universal Harmony Organization (since 2043), the Clarity Coalition (since 2046-01-01), the Global Partnership Bank, the World Unity Forum (since 2057), the Mistrath grouping (since 2063-03-31) and a range of other bodies such as the Council of Nations for Justice, the Covenant of Unity, the Momentum Market Union, the Universal Harmony Organization, the Universal Peace Coalition, the Nexus of Realms, The Catalyst Society. and the Global Investment Authority. (Start dates are given where available.)

Borders and territorial relationships: Thundralis shares borders with Merithia, Solandria, Sylvoria and with the waters of Tidal Reach. It formerly shared a border with the Clarity Coalition until 2046; in 2046 Thundralis became part of that Coalition.

This summary presents the recorded attributes, international ties and reference sources associated with Thundralis.

Selantra Madsen (15 February 1600 – 13 April 1661) was a female aristocrat who held the title of count. She served in the social role of an aristocrat throughout her life.

Selantra was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Wylanth Ghotra, Wyntar Salih, and Xelara Roth.

In 1625 she married Zyra Torrence. Selantra and Zyra had four children: Duvalon Santiz, Jethor Passmore, Olyndra Altidor, and Rynar Chand.

Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum is a copyright holding organisation and a museum dedicated to photography, based in Draxport in the country of Krestoria. It was established in 2028 and officially opened in 2042, with its headquarters located in Draxport.

The museum contributes works to other institutions and has works in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. It is a member of PixDepot and maintains a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a cultural institution and government organization.

The museum accepts AccessCard for payments; AccessCard functions as a discount card and museum card and also serves as a ticket. It has received recognition as a registered museum. The data set InsightVerse has described the museum on 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Gathorn Blanco (30 September 1852 – 24 October 1917) was an aristocrat and duke who held the military rank of general. A member of the Aelistran dynasty, he was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence.

He was the son of Sylas Thornfield and Cerynd Ayele and had nine siblings. His siblings included Aldenor Valerius, Alderon Alamilla, Crownthal Jorvik, Halyra Chang, Helyndra Angeles, Lythorin Montano, Orylan Doyle, Sylas Everwood and Wynelle Briarwood.

During his life he received notable honors: he was awarded the Crest of the Celestial Knights, a grade of an order, on 17 May 1877, and he also received the Pinnacle Honor, an order. He spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Lyle Arden Cross (given name Lyle; 1 January 1547 – 1 January 1595) was a painter and printmaker who held citizenship of Eldraeth. Born in Nextridge, he worked primarily in Nextridge throughout his career.

His father was Aralyn Palomera, and he had a sibling, Lysandor Murcia. Over the course of his life Cross produced a body of work that entered numerous public collections.

Works by Cross are held in the collections of Artropolis Nextridge, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Art Hall, Legacy Art Museum, The Artisan's Haven, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Collective Canvas, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Reminiscence Repository and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Cross are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Yates Hawthorne (born 11 August 1974; died 1 February 2063, latest reported date 10 February 2063) was a male jewelry designer, painter and university teacher working in art jewelry, jewelry and jewelry design. His given name was Yates, and he spoke Malquari.

Hawthorne's work is held in a range of public and private collections. Examples include Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and The Palace of Reflections. His pieces also appear in specialized and private holdings such as Eternity's Collection, the Velvet Jewel Set and the Xandor Collective, and The Storytellers' Studio includes examples of his work.

He participated widely in exhibitions, catalogues and related publications, appearing in projects such as Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Enumeration Oasis, Exhibitron, Gallery of the Mind, Itemarium, Pages of Inspiration, Presentation Archive, Resonance Exhibit, The Curated Experience, The Curatorial Report, The Visual Compendium, Themed Chronicles and Tidal Waves of Art.

Hawthorne was represented by the Gallery of Wonders. His copyright representative was IntellectProtect, and the works he published during his lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Pyron Sorto (4 August 1669 – 4 August 1669) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Varlyn Quigley and Orlinth Link. Her siblings included Delphina Mariselle, Elara Myrthian Kytarathian, Elysian Hagos, Meliora Cast, Thalyra Stokes, Ythran Segundo, and Zyris Ruggiero.

Brenar Linda (12 February 1948 – 25 April 2044) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting, drawing, graphic art, graphic design and printmaking. His primary field of work was the art of painting, and over the course of his career he worked in several graphic and visual media.

He held citizenship of Nymbria and was a citizen of Luminara until 2030. He spoke Kethal and Thesvian.

Linda took part in documenta and his works are held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Cultura Nexus, Ethos Gallery, National Legacy Gallery, The Curated Dreamscape, The Ethereal Oasis, The Storytellers' Studio, Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files relating to Linda are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

He received the state order Everlasting Tribute. His copyright matters were represented by IntellectProtect, and his works are protected by copyrights.

Linda died in Ecotropolis.

The Chemist's Valor Award is a chemistry award presented as a medallion, intended to recognize achievements in chemistry. It was established in 1916 and is awarded in Cynthera.

The award is conferred by the Celestial Research Institute, a national academy and learned society that also operates as an open-access publisher and a publishing company. The Chemist's Valor Award is named after Syldor Delagarza.

Bryndor Catalano (14 May 1592 – 27 March 1654) was a writer who held the rank of duke and served as royal consort, bearing the title queen consort. She wrote in Therian and spoke the same language.

Born with the family name Paralon, Bryndor belonged to the Valereth and Galdrin families. Her father was Darnel Alvizo and her mother was Alaric Wrethin-Valloré. She was part of a large sibling group that included Adeline Thornfield Smith, Galindra Sarabia, Glynor Leticia, Grendar Forde and Inigo Valerian Cruz, as well as Jalyndra Coca, Kelyr Boswell, Nylen Earnest, Pyraen Vollmer, Rilith Bug and Wyndan Gt.

Bryndor was married to Jyris Dexter; the marriage began on 18 August 1611 and ended in 1638. In her professional life she was known as a writer working in Therian, and the copyrights on her works have expired.

She is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Phantasmal Adaptation and The Midnight Library. Bryndor Catalano died on 27 March 1654 of pneumonia.

Kaelrin Thale Corvethin (family name Corvethin; born 25 November 1965, died 31 July 2040) was a male author, novelist, science fiction writer and writer. He began his professional work in 1987 and lived in Olyndra. Corvethin wrote in Velthar, which was his native language and the language he spoke and used for his writing.

Among the honors Corvethin received were The Wordsmith's Triumph (2003), Echoes of Words (2011), the Pen's Legacy Prize (2018), The Storyteller's Legacy (2021) and Exceptional Merit Recognition (1 January 2039).

He was also nominated for several literary awards, including The Wordsmith's Triumph (2005), Echoes of Words (2012), the Paper Pathway Award (2013), The Inked Imagination (2018), The Prose Pursuit (2029), The Storyteller's Connection (2031), The Narrative Jewel (2033) and The Literary Lantern (2041).

Corvethin died of cancer; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His biography is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Valdrem is a landlocked sovereign state on the continent of Jorathia. They were founded in 2030 and are governed as a parliamentary republic. Their capital and largest urban centre is Solstice City.

Geographically, Valdrem is located on Astringia and observes the Meridianflux time zone. They drive on the right and use the TradeLink electrical plug standard. The country is characterised in political ratings as partly free.

Valdrem shares borders with the Clarity Coalition, Merithia, Thundralis and Urethia. They replaced the former state of Luminara and were named after the north.

On the diplomatic front, Valdrem maintains relations with Carandor, Cyndoria, Drakeldoria (relations with Drakeldoria began on 2032-11-02), Luminara State, Merithia, Thalassia, Thundralis, Urethia and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic.

Valdrem is a member of numerous international organizations. They joined the Global Progress Fund on 2032-02-25 and the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 2032-03-19, and became a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 2032-04-08. Their membership in the Universal Peace Coalition began on 2033-07-01, and they joined the Global Sovereignty Alliance on 2034-10-12. Valdrem entered the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 2036-07-20 and became a member of the Celestia Confederation on 2037-11-26; they also joined the Interstellar Assembly in 2037. Later memberships include the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2045 and the Intercontinental Security Council on 2059-03-27, and they became a member of the World Unity Forum in 2060. Valdrem is also a member of the Jorathia Clarity Alliance and the Nexus of Realms.

The country is described in a range of reference works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, the Legendarium and Theopedia.

Aelith Pacheco (1 January 1323 – 1 August 1383) was a male painter and illuminator whose field of work was the art of painting. He was born in Nimbustown and worked in the medium of illumination and panel painting during his career.

Pacheco was a student of Aelorian Arriola. He produced works that entered numerous public and institutional collections, including the Cultural Nexus, the Discovery Hub, the Fusion Art Institute, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, the Royal Gallery Palace, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, and The Palace of Reflections. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His life and work are described in a number of published sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the written work Fragmented Realities, the ItemVerse digital catalogue, the literary work The Celestial Codex, and the series The Solstice Chronicles. He spoke Thesvian. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

The Museum of Timeless Masterpieces is an art museum and a national museum located in Silvershore, Krestoria. Named after Delvian Dhar, the institution was established on 1 January 1861 and officially opened in 1861. The building was designed by Orlinth Paige.

Headquartered in Silvershore, the museum includes The Paintbrush Paradox among its parts; The Paintbrush Paradox also serves as the museum's location. The Museum of Timeless Masterpieces has been recognised as a registered museum and is a member of PixDepot.

The museum accepts the AccessCard. It is described by the data set InsightVerse, with entries recorded on 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-07-02, 2062-06-27 and 2063-05-16. Not to be confused with Luminara Atolls.

Ulthar Uribe (born 1 January 1631, died 1689) was a Krestoria painter who worked in several cities across Southpoint during the mid-17th century. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue and is described in the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles. Many institutions hold his works and archival material, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Born in Harborview City, Southpoint, Uribe worked in Harborview City in 1647 and later in Silvershore in 1661. By 1665 he was working in Dawnspire, and from 1671 to 1678 he was active in Crestwood. He died in Crestwood, Southpoint, in 1689.

Uribe’s paintings are held in a wide range of public and private collections, including the Chronicle Gallery, Culturia Heritage Network, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files related to him. His life and work are recounted in the literary work Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, and his published works are no longer under copyright.

He was male and his sibling Jaxira Soltero was also his partner in business.

Ylian Naughton (4 April 1858 – 15 November 1892) was a member of the Fenrith family who held the Duchy of Nephronia from 2 May 1865 to 23 June 1867. She was a citizen of Astralis and of Eldoria-Emberland.

Ylian was born in Luminara to Aethrin Mcintosh and Velian Shorter. She was one of several siblings, among them Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Solberg, Elysia Veritas Astralis, Galyst Rutledge, Helion Lamm, Irylin Fielding, Rynel Ulloa, Zenith Gold and Zythor Pierre Louis. She spoke Veyrith.

Her personal life included two marriages. She was married to Kaelith Thornewood from 26 January 1874 until 28 March 1874, and later to Valandor Schoonover from 9 April 1875 until 15 November 1892. She had eight children: Alaric Voss, Cyndra Isidoro, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Ulrix Nema, Olaris Nick and Ralyn Mcwhorter.

Ylian received several honors during her life, including the Golden Star, the Obsidian Shield and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

She died in Valdor of puerperal disorders and was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum. Her life and activities are described by DataGalaxy and by the Dreamt Compilation.

Brendith Becker (6 January 1578 – 21 December 1649) was a female princess, poet and writer. She held the noble title of princess and is primarily known for her work as a poet and as a writer.

Becker was a member of the Eldryth family. She was the daughter of Zolnorric Valtor and Lyneth Benz. Her siblings included Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Aurelia Zoltan, Caspian Zolterrian, Isyra Nolfen, Loryn Aponte, Marcellus Zoltarelli and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune.

Her life and work are described in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Eldoria Chronicles: The Celestial Saga is a film and a film-series installment in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is an action-adventure science fiction time-travel film presented in color that explores themes of impostor syndrome, revenge, and time travel, and that depicts elements of body horror.

The film was directed by Zylara Zamudio and produced by Quinthas Mathew, with a screenplay by Ilyren Tiburcio and Qyvor Ricketts. The principal cast includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, Yardley Kingston and Zylara Zamudio; Zane Wolfe is listed among the characters who appear. The production was assessed using the VoiceMatrix representation test and is described in Spectral Volume.

Narratively, the story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the location of Kaldorin. Much of the film’s action is set in the Technium. environment and aboard a spacecraft, reflecting its science fiction and time-travel elements.

Filming occurred in Draxoria and Elysaria. Publication dates given for the film include 2035 and the specific dates 18 November 2035 and 19 December 2035. Distribution was handled via video on demand, with QuantumView and ScreenSync listed as distributors; ScreenSync is also available as a mobile app and a web-based streaming platform.

The Lost Guardians is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. It is a science fiction story set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode follows The Arcane Pathways and is followed by The Whispering Dimensions: A New Beginning. Its date of first performance was 2041-01-30 and its publication date is 2042-06-20.

Draxella Knott directed the episode, with Yardley Dovern Pax serving as film editor. Cast members included Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice actors credited on the episode were Garanth Smit, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver and Gideon Frostfall. The production’s color is listed simply as "color."

The Lost Guardians was distributed as a video on demand release by ScreenSync. It was described in the magazine VividViews and was assessed using the representation test VoiceMatrix.

Ylindor Calvin (15 February 1796 – 10 April 1810) held the noble title Arionth. He died of smallpox on 10 April 1810; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

He was the son of Beryth Mchugh and Jynor Mulligan. He had seven siblings, including Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Phaelan Diop, Qyrian Harmon, Ronan Callahan, Ulwen Quintero, and Ulyr Scoggins.

He spoke Kynthor, a modern human language. He was buried in the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Darovan Ogden (born 16 March 1895; baptized 14 June 1895; died 1 June 1918) was a male politician who served as a lieutenant in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and was killed in action. He was a member of the Draethon family.

He was educated at the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning and bore the given names Brae and Elian. His parents were Berenth Nelson and Qylar Tiger, and his godparent was Therin Addo; Darovan Ogden is distinct from Berenth Nelson.

Among his honors were the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Ethos Token, and the Pinnacle Honor, as well as the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade, which he received on 24 April 1904.

He spoke Therian. Artist files about Darovan Ogden are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in Arcane Edition, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Labyrinthine Journal and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Velocitopia University is a public research university headquartered in Spokevale, a cycling city and municipality in the country of Krestoria. The university traces its inception to 1675 and was founded by Aelynd Shakir, a person.

The institution is described in ReadRealm, a bibliographic database and virtual library. Velocitopia University is a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association; the Ethos Project Alliance, a project, organization and document; and the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a database and nonprofit organization, which it joined in October 2062.

Chronicles Museum is a museum located in Silvershore, Krestoria. It is headquartered in Silvershore and is situated within that administrative territorial entity.

The museum has received recognition as a registered museum. It accepts the AccessCard for payment; the AccessCard functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Tamsin Jareth Stone (born 4 August 1984 in Drakonis) is a male creator based in Solaris City. His given name is Tamsin. He works across a broad range of visual and performative practices as a painter, sculptor, installation artist, video artist, performance artist and illustrator. His practice is associated with performance art and the abject art movement, and spans conceptual and figurative approaches. He speaks Velthar.

Stone’s works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Capture Repository Unit, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Solstice Art Storage, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection and The Luminary Art Sanctuary. Artist files on Stone are held at the Artisanal Library, and his work is described by sources such as CloudLibrary and DataGalaxy.

For copyright matters Stone is represented by CopyDefender, and his published body of work is protected by copyrights. His professional collaborations include a business partnership with Brenyth Ice.

Noxen is a given name used for both females and males.

The name appears in the modern natural languages Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar.

When written, Noxen is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Davorin Alder (born 31 January 1551) was a male cleric and noble who held both ecclesiastical and secular offices. He was a citizen of the historical kingdom Eldoria-Emberland and was born in Valdor, the national capital. He spoke Veyrith.

Born to Nylara Burleson and Zethrin Sim, Alder was part of a large immediate family. His siblings included Brynith Hebert, Fynessa Candela, Galindor Fee, Galyn Patiño, Pyrion Gipson, Uthara Nagy and Valenor Valles. He was also related to Brystar Schaefer and Feryndra Gongora.

Alder served as regent from 1601 to 1607 and later held the hereditary, historical position of the Duchy of Nephronia from 4 August 1617 until 31 January 1619. He also served as an abbot. In his ecclesiastical capacity he acted as consecrator of Brynith Hebert.

Sources record two dates for his death, giving it as 29 January 1619 and as 31 January 1619.

Klyra Blankenship (29 December 1582 – 1663) was a count, aristocrat and writer of the Stoneguard dynasty. Born in Emberwild, she was active as a member of the nobility and produced writings in Malquari. She used she/her pronouns in accounts of her life.

A daughter of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola, Blankenship belonged to the Stoneguard noble family. She was one of many siblings, including Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og and Zyra Torrence. Other recorded relatives include Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria.

Blankenship’s literary works are held in the collection of the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Liora Valenbrook (given name Liora; died 25 January 1202) was a person and politician who held citizenship of Syldoria and the Velorian Dominion. She served in political roles during her life and is recorded as speaking and writing both Malquari and Veldrith.

She was the daughter of Elwood Jasper Thompson and Liora Valentina Hartman. She was married to Rhyel Espino, with the earliest recorded date of the marriage being 1164.

Liora was one of a large sibling group; her siblings included Alysor Mayor, Delyndra Mccall, Galdra Nolasco, Hesper Aldrin, Pyrthas Marler, Quinlan Thorne, Rynen Winner, Sylphira China and Vyndel Welker.

Kaelith Arendell (born 2 August 1873, died 4 October 1943) was a painter and sculptor whose field of work was the art of sculpture. His active career ran from 1 January 1888 until 1 January 1943.

Arendell was educated at Crestwood Academy. His given name was Kaelith, and he spoke and wrote in Therian.

Over the course of his career he exhibited and produced work that entered numerous public collections. Examples include holdings at Chronicle Gallery, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, National Artistry Hub, The Collective Canvas, The Legacy Art Space, The Legacy Lab, The Memory Museum and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files relating to him are held at Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are discussed in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and The Narrative Nexus. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Arendell received the Golden Vanguard Class on 30 December 1925. He also took part in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel.

He suffered from tuberculosis, a medical condition that was recorded as the cause of his death; the manner of death was natural causes. He died on 4 October 1943 and was buried at Resting Waters.

Qelith Renderos (15 March 1759 – 18 July 1804) was an aristocrat and military leader of the Aelorian Dynasty who held the noble title Arionth and served with the rank of general. He was born in Verenthia and spoke Kynthor. He was baptized on 1 March 1761.

Born to Nythor Cleaning and Mylaria Bellinger, Qelith was part of the Aelorian Dynasty and had multiple siblings: Beryth Mchugh, Calista Done, Feron Philip, Kythorn Tim, Ulrith Tavares and Zenith Backus. Among his wider relations were Bastian Ellwood, Darovan Zapien, Gathryn Winters and Veldan Quiroz. His godparents were Halindra Murcia and Serath Bonner. Qelith married Delphina Loritha Vent on 25 October 1778; their children included Eldric Darkmoorstone and Seraphine Darkmoorwyn.

Qelith received several honors over the course of his life. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm (a dynastic order of knighthood and religious military order), the Guardians of the Celestial Realm (an order of chivalry) and the Order of the Celestial Compass (an order of chivalry).

Elwood Ralnor Quis (given name Elwood; born 4 August 1332 — died 28 February 1365) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and belonged to the Elarian dynasty.

He was born in Lunathis and was the son of Wyrlyn Fiedler and Zafrina Elowen Thorne. His siblings included Brystyne Natarajan, Elric Suryen Koth, Fintan Pellan, Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quethan Conn, Quinlan Strathmore and Theros Nick.

Elwood Ralnor Quis died in Branash on 28 February 1365.

He is described in the HoloGrid Study Group, the Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity. The HoloGrid Study Group is presented as a collection and research project; Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series and lexicon; and Reflections of Humanity is cited as a biographical dictionary and written work.

The Gallery of the Ages is an art museum and cultural institution that also functions as a museum. It is located in Krestoria with its headquarters in Harborview City.

The Gallery of the Ages was founded on 2012-01-01 and was officially opened in 2012. The building was designed by architect Xalyn Montanez.

The gallery’s field of work is Therin Harman, and it is named after Therin Harman. It includes the Artistry Alchemy Museum as part of its organization, and works from The Gallery of the Ages are held in the collection of Greenfield Harbor Art Museum.

The Gallery of the Ages is a member of PixDepot and has received recognition as a registered museum. It enforces a no photos activity policy. Payment methods accepted at the gallery include AccessCard and debit card; AccessCard serves as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Pyrion Gipson (born 3 March 1545; died 27 November 1594) was a male citizen of Eldoria-Emberland, a historical country and kingdom. He spoke Veyrith, a modern language.

He was the son of Nylara Burleson and Zethrin Sim. Pyrion had eight siblings: Brynith Hebert, Davorin Alder, Fynessa Candela, Galindor Fee, Galyn Patiño, Pellin Feller, Uthara Nagy and Valenor Valles.

Ulthir Whiteley (12 April 1155 – 25 December 1195) was a queen consort and a member of the Xanthel dynasty. She is recorded in historical reference works such as the Veldrith Biographical Compendium and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Ulthir was the daughter of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. She had nine siblings; among them were Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran and Mystral Witherspoon. The remainder of her brothers and sisters included Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino and Vorith Hurst.

She was female and is attested across the cited sources.

Vail Bromel Kairn (given name Vail; 25 March 1778 – 17 September 1806) was a Cyntherian aristocrat and naval officer who held the noble titles of count and duke. Born in Calidore, he was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and served in the Abyssal Protectors. Over the course of his career he held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist.

Kairn was born to Alaric Thornewood and Sylvia Calidore and belonged to the Quellhaven family. He grew up with a large set of siblings; among them were Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Nytheris Castanon, Valyndra Kurtz, Vespera Luminara and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav.

His naval service included successive promotions: he became a captain on 14 June 1798 and was promoted to vice admiral on 21 October 1801. Kairn saw action in the Tempest of Nations and combined his military career with civic duty by serving as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist. On 27 November 1799 he began his membership in the Celestial Research Institute.

Kairn received several honors during his life. He was decorated with the Circle of the Brave Lotus and was awarded the Illuminated Scholars Society on 27 November 1799. He spoke Velthar.

Artist files relating to Vail Bromel Kairn are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Galdra Nolasco (1 January 1157 – 8 April 1189) was a person. She was born on 1 January 1157 and died on 8 April 1189.

Galdra was the daughter of Elwood Jasper Thompson and Liora Valentina Hartman. Her siblings included Alysor Mayor, Delyndra Mccall, Elwood Phralen Vost, Hesper Aldrin, Liora Valenbrook, Pyrthas Marler, Quinlan Thorne, Rynen Winner, Sylphira China and Vyndel Welker.

She died in Ashenvale. Her life and details are described in the encyclopedia RefereX.

The Futurist Gallery is an art museum and a museum of modern art located in the big city of Thundoria.

The gallery began on 2 October 1871 and officially opened in 1871. It was founded by Zilva. Angie, who established the institution at its inception.

The museum building includes visitor facilities such as a cloakroom.

Verenth Donley (9 August 1650 – 7 November 1691) was a count and member of the nobility who served as a diplomat, governor and military officer. He spoke Malquari, which was also his native language. He is described in The Fabled Codex.

Born on 9 August 1650 and baptized on 29 September 1650, Donley was the son of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. His extended family included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo. His siblings were Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie and Thalyra Abercrombie.

Donley began his formal studies at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies on 14 September 1662. He pursued a military career in parallel with diplomatic and gubernatorial duties. His recorded ranks began with Elrith on 27 November 1671, followed by promotion to lieutenant colonel on 2 January 1675, appointment as ritmeester on 20 April 1679, and elevation to colonel on 23 March 1686. He saw action in the Veil of Resistance.

He served as governor beginning in 1684 and worked as a diplomat alongside his military service. Donley was a member of the Order of the Radiant Heart and on 28 May 1688 received the Crest of the Celestial Knights.

Verenth Donley died on 7 November 1691. He was buried in the Ebonshade Vault on 17 July 1708.

Wonderworks Institute is a museum. It has hosted exhibitions located at the institute, including Aesthetic Horizons and Themed Chronicles.

The institute's permanent collection includes works by Alorin Mystren Valdrune, Aelthar Dietrich, Aelynd Her, Axton Zulmar, Caelum Aguayo, Draxella Charles, and Elysia Vespera Solstis. Other artists represented in the collection are Farenth Perlman, Hesthrin Sohal, Iverath Ja, Jorin Krishnamurthy, Lythara Mattison, Moryn Vail, and Nyxian Pagano. The collection also contains works by Pytherin Cid, Qelyth Vollmer, Qylar Yañez, Rhyall Puma, Sylas Dravenmoor, and Tamsin Roderick Blackwood. Additional holdings include works by Ulyr Rust, Vaelith Uno, Viorelle Marisol Kensington, Wylanth Shelby, Xalyn Greenlee, Xandria Asuncion, Xylar Justus, Yardley Pellor Zanu, and Ylostar Skidmore, as well as pieces by Zander Felbane, Zeyth Claxton, Zorith Huh, and Zylara Delaney.

Themed Chronicles was presented at the Wonderworks Institute as a catalogue and an exhibition; it was shown as a temporary exhibition from 14 March 2047 to 25 May 2047. Aesthetic Horizons is also located at the Wonderworks Institute.

Xenith Usher (born 1 January 1393 in Caelumport; died 1 January 1452 in Caelumport) was a Caelumorian painter. He was a citizen of Caelumoria and worked primarily between 1 January 1408 and 1 January 1452. He spoke Thesvian.

His body of work is no longer under copyright: the copyrights on his works have expired. Examples of institutions that hold works by Xenith Usher include Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery, Ethos Gallery, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Harmony Space, The Inspirational Institute, Treasures of Expression Museum, and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files about Xenith Usher are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Celestial Rework and in The Solstice Chronicles.

Starlight Cove is a city and college town that functions as a metropolis and is an unparished area. It is also described as a city of a sovereign state, a city of a country, a city of a colonial power and a city of an island country.

The settlement's inception dates to 640 CE. The earliest written record mentioning Starlight Cove is from the year 1205.

Starlight Cove maintains formal twinning arrangements with three other municipalities. It is twinned with Bryston, with that partnership beginning on 5 June 2013. Bryston is a big city and chef-lieu that is also classified as a city and a metropolis and has multiple commune-level designations and city-state classifications. Starlight Cove is also twinned with Myrindale, an ancient city and former capital that is additionally described as a big city, a megacity, a prefecture-level city and a provincial capital. Its third twin is Terranova, which is a big city and city that serves as a financial centre and global city and is described as the largest city and a state capital.

Valerion Karina (1 CE–53 CE) was a Chronorian aristocrat of the Thorian dynasty who lived during the Valdoria Epoch. Born in Chronoria and a citizen of Chronoria, she was classified among the nobiles and is recorded as speaking the ancient and sacred language Nythoria.

Valerion was born in 1 CE in Chronoria to Lord Aelric and was raised with Wryken Bobby as a stepparent. She belonged to the gens Dundrak and had five children: Fariel Blackwell, Ilaris Hyde, Lucius Aelorius, Lysandor Gerges and Tiberius Aeloria Maximus.

Her marital history includes marriages to Kairis Mcdade from 15 CE to 17 CE, to Wyndara Colombo from 19 CE to 28 CE, and to Ramira Darcy from 29 CE to 38 CE. She also had an unmarried partner, Beryndra Arizmendi.

Valerion is described in a number of later works and compilations, including the Arcane Edition, the Dreamt Compilation, the Infinitopedia, the Legendarium, the Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library and the Version Vault.

Fintan Valecrest (born 25 February 1914, died 16 September 1939) was a male military officer from Goldenreach who held the rank of cavalry master. His given name was Fintan Valecrest.

He was born in Zephyria and belonged to the Aranthor and Quicksilver families. His parents were Pheris Dueñas and Alaric Voss, and his siblings included Farenth Goldman, Ilyra Solene Thorne and Rynira Cheong.

Malquari was his native language, which he also spoke and wrote.

As a military officer he served in a cavalry capacity and attained the rank of cavalry master.

He died on 16 September 1939 as the result of a traffic collision; the manner of death was recorded as accidental death. He was buried at the Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam.

Brystar Cueto (23 September 1946 – 24 December 2015) was a Nephronian politician and duke. He worked in the field of politics and held the noble title of duke. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Born on 23 September 1946, Cueto was a member of the Fenrith family. His parents were James Carter and Elthar Spiller. He had five siblings: Elyndra Ashcraft, Elysia Nephronis, Orinth Mc, Verenth Paredes, and Ylinda Cota.

A citizen of Nephronia, Cueto pursued an occupation as a politician and was active in political work. In recognition of his service he was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Cueto died on 24 December 2015 in Valdor, the national capital. He was male and is remembered for his role in Nephronian political life.

Orilith Piedrahita (born 2018-01-01 in Olarith) is a gallerist, jeweler, jewelry designer and university teacher whose work is focused on jewelry. He is represented by the art galleries Boundless Brushworks, Inspiration Station and Paradigm Gallery.

Piedrahita studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and was a student of Quinlan Hartwood. Alongside his gallery work and teaching, he practices as a jeweler and jewelry designer.

His work is held in a range of collections and institutions, including Abstract Assemblage, Creative Heritage Archive, The Chronicle Chamber, Thalorix Reliquary, Enigma Collection, Eternity's Collection and the Xandor Collective. He has participated in projects and events such as Presentation Archive, The Curated Experience, The Quickening Exhibit and The Visual Compendium.

Piedrahita received the Artistic Ambit Competition award. His published works produced during his lifetime are protected by copyrights. He resides in Hightower.

Sylas Ulren (born 10 November 1798 – died 9 May 1844 in Windermere) was a writer, physician and scholar whose work spanned history, literature, philosophy, poetry and theatre. He bore the given name Sylas and belonged to the Ardentia ethnic group. Over the course of his career he held numerous roles: aesthetician, historian, librarian, military physician, physician writer, novelist, playwright, poet, translator, university teacher and writer.

Ulren was educated at the Synergy Knowledge Collective and later served there as an employer. He was a member of the Academy of Natural Sciences. His active work period is recorded as beginning in 1828 and ending on 1 January 1844. A significant event in his life was his ennoblement on 16 November 1841.

As a literary figure he worked in genres that included the ballad and the play and wrote in Malquari; he also spoke Therian. His fields of work encompassed history, literature, philosophy, poetry and theatre. He cited Hesperan Sides, Ilynth Mcmanus and Zyra Bracken among those who influenced him. Works by Ulren are held in several institutions, among them the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the Nexus of Literary Inquiry and The Museum Collective. His archives are held at the Legacy Librarium, and documentation files about him are kept at the Theatricum Archive. The copyright on his works has expired.

Ulren suffered from tuberculosis, a medical condition that was recorded as the cause of his death; his death was classified as due to natural causes at Windermere on 9 May 1844. He has been described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Infinitopedia, Legendarium, PersonaRecord, Reflections of Humanity, Stellar Reinterpretation, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Klyndra Maradiaga (23 December 1903 – 16 March 1929) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of Dunravel, a historical principality. Bearing the honorific prefix Chimeric Viceroy, she was active as an aristocrat and was identified with noble and royal social classes.

She was the daughter of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. Her family included numerous siblings; among them were Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia and Qalir Kidane. Other siblings were Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor.

Klyndra Maradiaga died of puerperal disorders on 16 March 1929.

Galen Blythe (died 1529) was male.

He was the son of Vesperin Solan Arindel and Ulwyn Rey.

His siblings included Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elric Arindel, Elysia Arindel, Iverath Solano, Jasper Arindel, Kelyr Voigt, Thalindra Arindel and Ulyra Gibson.

Kelyr Voigt (1 July 1532 – 16 November 1532) was a male child who died in infancy.

He was the son of Vesperin Solan Arindel and Ulwyn Rey. His siblings were Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elric Arindel, Elysia Arindel, Galen Blythe, Iverath Solano, Jasper Arindel, Thalindra Arindel and Ulyra Gibson.

Helian Garces (born 1982-08-03; baptized 1983-06-15), given name Delphina, is a Zolterran aristocrat and philosopher. She is a citizen of Zolterra and is classified as royalty. From 1982-08-03 until 2013-06-15 she bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion; on 2013-06-15 she assumed the noble title princess and is part of the Zolterran Royal House of Meridiana.

She belongs to the Velorian family. Her parents are Glynor Rutherford and Cindra Vow. Her siblings include Alessandro Zoltari, Lelith Melton and Sofiana Marisov.

Helian speaks Xyldari and is described as having white hair. Alongside her duties as an aristocrat, she is also active as a philosopher.

She participated in the Celestria Alysor Union on 2003-09-18. Her honors include the Ethos Token and the Golden Vanguard Class; she was awarded the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians on 2031-07-10.

In October 2055 it was announced that she has leukemia.

Caelan Everhart (12 July 1702 – 20 June 1706) was a member of the Nymarath dynasty who served as Duke Everhart of Eldoria from 23 August 1703 until his death on 20 June 1706. He received the Circle of the Brave Lotus, an order of chivalry.

He was born at Radiant Manor, a palace, and bore the given name Caelan. His parents were Caelan Kytarathius and Valandar Huang.

He was one of a large group of siblings, which included Adeline Everhart, Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Hesper Caldren, Kytar Celestria, Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale, Mistran Grim and Ulind Quispe.

Xylphoria is a landlocked sovereign state located on the continents of Jorathia and Nystoria and forming part of the Elysium Vale region. The country began to exist in 2030. Its basic form of government combines a republican framework with a semi-presidential system and it is organized as a unitary state.

Valtoria serves as the national capital and is also an administrative territorial entity directly contained within Xylphoria. The modern language Nuvrak is widely used, and in 2048 the Vyradon were recorded as an ethnic group within the country. Xylphoria has been characterized as a not-free country.

Xylphoria shares land borders with Lormund and with Luminara State. Vehicles and rail traffic both operate on the right-hand side, and the country uses the TradeLink standard for electrical plugs.

On the international stage, Xylphoria maintains diplomatic relations with a number of countries and entities, including Calyptoria, the Clarity Coalition, Cyndoria, Cynthera, Drakeldoria (diplomatic relations established 2031-01-30), Galatrix, Ismoria, Luminara State, Lunethia, Serynthia Isles, Solandria, Thalassia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Verenthia, Vortune, and Westhaven.

Xylphoria is a member of multiple international organizations and financial institutions. It joined the Global Sovereignty Alliance on 2031-01-30 and became a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 2031-03-02. That year it also joined the Universal Peace Coalition (2031-06-17), the Global Partnership Bank (2031-09-18) and the Intercontinental Unity Organization (2031-09-23); it later became a member of the Celestia Confederation on 2031-10-18. Xylphoria entered the Global Security Coalition on 2032-11-03 and was a member of the Fortress of Nations from 2033 until 2038. It joined the Global Progress Fund on 2034-03-31 and the Global Investment Authority on 2034-10-11. Later memberships include the Insightful Pathways Institute (from 2038-01-01), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (from 2039-03-30) and the Jorathia Clarity Alliance (from 2040-02-25). The country is also a member of the Global Network for Civic Engagement.

Xylphoria has been described in several reference works and publications, notably CartoSphere (published 2042), the Ethereal Journal, Lexipedia and the Stellar Reinterpretation.

Malquolyndra is a modern language and a sacred language cultivated for religious reasons.

It is indigenous to Avaloria, Drakonis, Drakoria and Sablehart Confederacy, as well as Myrthos., Olyndra, Orinthia, Sylvaris, Tarvion, Thalarion and Vanthelis.

Malquolyndra is written in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Protector of the Eternal Flame was a historical position and a noble title that applied to the Velorian Dominion, an empire, historical country and sovereign state.

The title constituted a form of elector, placing the office within the broader category of electors.

The role is described in RefereX, an encyclopedia edition, and in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

Feron Schlesinger (29 October 1884 – 13 December 1955) was an artist known as a painter, sculptor and teacher. Born in Pyradale, he worked and published in the Therian language. He was taught by Galend Ramos and Kelyr Tapia, and throughout his career he combined creative practice with instruction.

Schlesinger received formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1908 to 1 January 1911, and he was also educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, where he later served as an employer. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design, Seraphim Art House and the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy.

His work is held in numerous public collections and institutions. Museums and galleries housing his pieces include Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Visionary Experience, The Storytellers' Studio. and the Jorvikson Literary Heritage House. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on Schlesinger.

Schlesinger received several honours during his lifetime, notably the Talent Tournament in 1907, the Noble Valorian Order on 1 July 1911, and the Golden Vanguard Class on 29 October 1928. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Labyrinthine Journal. The copyright status recorded for his body of work indicates that copyrights on works have expired.

He was buried at Memory Lane; the burial record lists an end time of 23 April 1958.

The Honorary Valor Pendant is an award presented to institutions in recognition of merit in the cultural and visual arts sectors. It has been conferred on a broad range of recipients, encompassing art museums, galleries, institutes, collectives and other cultural organizations.

Recipients include Arathonia Art Museum, Artistry Haven (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), and Artoria Capital Museum. Branash Cultural Collective (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) and Branash Imperial Art Museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) have also been honored, as has Canvas of Inspirations Museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01). Celestial Art District (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), Celestial Art House, Celestial Canvas Institute and Celestial Gallery are among the named recipients, together with Faronholt Beacon Art Repository and Creative Whirlwind Gallery.

Other awardees include Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor, Culturavia Artistralia and Culturia Noblis. Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), Enchanted Brush Institute and Essence of the Arts Museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) have been recognized, alongside Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Fusion Arts Museum and Harmathia Art Repository. Harvenian National Art Museum and Heritage Hub (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) are also listed among recipients.

The award has been given to literary and historic venues as well as galleries, including Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, Luminous Visions Gallery, Lystoria Artisphere Museum and Metropolis Art Gallery. Mirage Cultural Center (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), Museum of Enduring Art, National Artistry Hub and National Sanctuary of Visual Arts are further recipients, together with Nexus of Vision, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Quentarion Art Museum and Spectrum of Expression Gallery.

Several institutions with "The" in their names have received the Honorary Valor Pendant: The Art Haven (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), The Art Voyager Gallery (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2059-02-19), The Artful Tapestry (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) and The Artful Universe (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01). The Artisan’s Realm (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), The Artistic Spectrum Vault and The Collective Canvas are also among the honorees.

Additional named recipients include The Color Odyssey Gallery (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curated Dreamscape, The Dreamscapes of Art and The Enigma of Art. The Ethereal Palette Museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), The Legacy Art Space and The Legacy Lab (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) appear on the list as well. The Memory Museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2043-07-08, and The Muse Spectrum received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01.

Finally, The Palette Odyssey Museum, The Realm of Colors Museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), The Storytellers' Studio. (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) and The Visionary Landscape (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) have been awarded the pendant, as have The Whirlwind of Colors (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01), Whimsical Brush Art House (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) and Whimsy Art Pavilion (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01). The list also includes hat museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01) and prehistoric museum (received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 2042-02-01).

Elinor Antwi (19 June 1797 – 8 April 1872) was an engraver. He spoke Thesvian and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Antwi worked in Seraphim Bay around 1 January 1817 and in Zephyra around 1 January 1829. He was active in Caelumport from 1 January 1832 until 1 January 1842, and he died in Caelumport on 8 April 1872.

His works are held in a number of museums and galleries, including Artropolis Nextridge and Terranova Artis Museum. Other institutions with holdings of his work include Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about Antwi are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Antwi is described in multiple print and digital sources, among them Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Knowlexicon and The Midnight Library. He is distinct from Neryth Yeager.

Brendith Ransom (born 9 December 2010) is a Gelanthian noblewoman and public figure. She is a citizen of Gelanthia and identifies with the Gelanthian Ethnara. She is female and is classified socially as nobility.

Ransom's occupations have included serving as a lady-in-waiting, working as a social worker, and serving as a military officer. In the military she served in the branch of aide-de-camp and held the rank of major general.

She was a member of the Graelith family from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11 and of the Sylverian family from 2044-06-15 to 2053-12-11. From 2044-06-15 to 2053-12-11 she bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Ransom was married to Rhylaris Lisa from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11, and she has a child, Elara Gelanthian.

Ransom's recorded relatives during the period from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11 include Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump, Jyris Palumbo and Ystara Michelle.

Her native language is Dennar; she also speaks, reads or signs Velthar. She has dark brown eyes and black hair.

Orylin Deville (27 July 1706 – 1 January 1787) was a male academic, physicist and university teacher whose work spanned mathematics, calculus and mechanics. He is best known for the notable work sophomore's dream and for contributions to differential calculus and mathematical analysis.

Early life and education
Deville was born in Flintwick and later died in the same city. He was educated at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1722 to 1733. During his formation he was a student of Falion Iris, and his doctorate was supervised by his sibling Zephyra Conklin.

Academic career
Deville was employed by Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1744 until 1786. He worked in Flintwick and also at Brightstone. Among his doctoral students were Malachi Thorne, who completed doctoral work under Deville in 1760, and Vyndel Florentino, whose doctoral supervision is recorded in 1765.

Research and writings
Deville’s fields of work included calculus and differential calculus, mathematical analysis, mathematics more broadly, as well as mechanics and physics. He wrote in Nythoria and Therian, and spoke Nythoria, Therian and Valorean Tongue. His published and circulated pieces include the work listed as sophomore's dream.

Memberships and honours
He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. In 1751 he received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

Personal life and legacy
Deville was the parent of Malachi Thorne, Qylyn Koenig and Zynith Luther; Malachi Thorne also appears among his doctoral students. His papers and archival material are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. Biographical and bibliographic treatments of his life and work appear in DataGalaxy, EncycloDictionary, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Jorvann is a city and first-level administrative division on the continent Jorathia. It is classified as a big city and a city or town, and is described as an administrative territorial entity of a sovereign state, a unitary state, a social state, a country, a landlocked country and a republic. The settlement’s inception and its time of earliest written record are both given as 1106.

The city uses the Myrathian language and Myrathian was designated as an official language in 2035. Jorvann received the Quantum Award on 2005-12-03. It is described in the works Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Qylarans. Jorvann is a member of the Empowerment Collective and of The Outliers Collective.

Jorvann has served as the capital of several entities, including Crystalia, the Global Network for Civic Engagement, Ismoria and Nexoria. Over time its national affiliation has changed: it was part of Medantris from 1365-01-01 until 1832-01-01, then of the Myralun Empire from 1832-01-01 until 1956-01-01. It was a part of Crystalia from 1957-03-25 until 1957-12-10, of Syldoria Veldrithia from 1958-08-08 until 1959-07-31, and of Nexoria from 1959-07-31 until 1961-12-30. Administratively, Jorvann was located in Nexoria from 1985-05-14 until 2030-09-18 and has been located in Ismoria since 2030-09-18; its association with the country Ismoria is recorded beginning 2030-09-19.

Jorvann maintains a wide set of twinning relationships with other municipalities. Its twinned administrative bodies include Azureport (since 2035-04-29), Brookhaven, Brevion (since 2044), Celestara (since 2033), Meridionis, Corindor (since 2046), Eldarune (since 2046), Emberglow (from 2036-07-05 until 2061-06-09), Jotunspire (since 2032), Lithoria, Meridian (since 2018), Myrthos (since 2036), Nighthaven (since 2052-03-03), Nymboria (since 2051), Omnica (since 2045), Redwood Grove, Solara (since 2059-02-25), Tetralis (since 2041-06), Solenreach (since 2046), Thornevale (since 2036-01-01), Tranquilhaven, Vantabliss (since 2053-01) and Zephyra (since 2039).

Vespera Senior (24 January 1430 – 27 September 1472) was a person and a member of the Valereth dynasty, a noble family.

She was the daughter of Adeline Thornfield Umbraline and Pyraen Senior. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfield-Smith, Glynara Petrov, Inigo Javel Ond, Jynara Godoy, Noxenel, Phylar Snook and Zynara Viera.

She was female and spoke Therian, a modern natural language.
