Her life and career are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Ethereal Manuscript, Narratives of the Lexicon, ReadRealm, RefereX, Reflections of Humanity, Veldrith Biographical Compendium and Vivid Adaptation. She is different from Olyndra Vale.

Drakonis is a city and the capital of Xenthis. The city is described as a city in a sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic and a superpower, and is also recorded as a country-level city and as part of a historical unrecognized state. It serves as a county seat.

Drakonis was founded in 1886.

The city is twinned with Solara and Thundoria. The partnership with Solara — itself an administrative territorial entity and a large city — began in 2043. Drakonis is also twinned with Thundoria, which is a large city and commune.

Drakonis is described in a range of published sources, including the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation (both versions or editions), the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Lysen Qivar (29 July 1822 – 4 March 1840) was a Myralun aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and was a citizen of the Myralun Empire. She spoke Myrathian and was recorded as receiving the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women.

Lysen was a member of the Jorathyn dynasty. Her parents were Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo. She married Elian Merrickson on 30 October 1838. Her siblings included Aeloria Valarnis, Sornal Deyq, Tyqor Lun, Eldrin Myralun, Halir Ola, Myralun Luminara, Tolen Rax and Thalios Myralun.

Her life and status are described in multiple reference works, including Biographica Nova, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, Narratives of the Lexicon, LexiRealm, FactFolio, DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

Records list her places of death as Falthoria and Lunathis. The cause of death is given as an infectious disease and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Wryten Obeng (12 April 1612 – 8 December 1664) was a Zolterran politician who served as regent and held the noble title of queen consort. She was a citizen of Zolterra and worked in political office during her lifetime.

Wryten was the daughter of Deleth Lorenzo and Garenth Harrelson. She was married to Marcellus Zoltarelli from 27 August 1631 until 30 October 1650, and they had a child, Liora Zolterran. Her siblings included Hesperis Roden, Jareth Seibert, Jorvik Eldorian Steele, Liora Marcellus, Olyndra Faeloria, Qylara Heiser, Rolyn Short, Talyra Rehman, and Thalyn Ferdinand.

She is described in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive, an online database, series, and written work.

Delphina Valtaris was an aristocrat and member of the royal class who held multiple noble titles and ceremonial honors. She bore the title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera from 20 February 1906 and assumed the title Valtaris on 9 November 1944. On that same date she took up the position of Valtaris, which she held until 4 January 1970. She was styled Knight Aerion and received the Order of the Seraphic Veil.

Born on 20 February 1906 and baptized on 10 May 1906, her given names included Aeliana, Delphina and Elysia. She was the daughter of Vail Thorne and Elysia Crownhart and belonged to the Eldergrove Lineage until 1956. Her siblings included Chyndra Yearwood, Cynthera Elara Valorian, Fintan Farlanov, Irvin Thorne and Thalric Calixson. Her godparents were Cyndar Aucoin, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Gathorn Blanco, Malquari Valdrin, Sylphina Marigold Everwyn, Sylphira Leung and Xandor Lezcano.

Valtaris held citizenship of Cynthera and of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, the latter being recorded until 12 April 1966. She belonged ethnically to the Luminara and was part of the royalty social class. Her native language was Cynvelthar; she spoke and wrote Velthar and wrote in Cynvelthar.

Delphina Valtaris died on 4 January 1970. Records list Ashenfort Chapel as her place of burial (recorded from 10 January 1970), and her burial or cremation date is given as 22 May 1970.

Zedry Vida (14 July 1905 – 5 September 1990) was a female member of the royal class who held the noble titles Mystral and princess. She died in Pinehaven. Over the course of her life she held citizenship of Dunravel until 1928 and of the Myralun Empire from 1928.

From her birth on 14 July 1905 until 26 July 1928 she bore the honorific Chimeric Viceroy"; on 26 July 1928 she assumed the title Shadow Chancellor of Nythos," which she retained thereafter. She received the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women.

Zedry Vida was the daughter of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. She had a large number of siblings, including Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai and Zethrin Kantor. On 26 July 1928 she married Valerion Myralun; the marriage lasted until at least 1970.

She spoke Zyphorian. Zedry Vida is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Ethryon Giglio (6 July 1821 – 13 March 1863) was a member of the Aldermore family of the Galdrin dynasty who served as regent and held the noble titles Lucalith and queen consort. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame.

Born to Ulwen Quintero and Eldric Darkmoorstone, she counted Inigo Martinez among her godparents. She was one of several siblings, including Calyra Facundo, Qynara Pires, Ryniel Link, Selin Gamble, Valerion Bejar, Vorith Dai and Ylorith Corral.

In her official capacity she acted as regent and used Kynthor as a language of communication. Her life and deeds are described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

Ethryon died in Seraphim Bay on 13 March 1863 of cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Sanctum of the Lost.

Valerion Bejar (given name Xandria; family name Aldermore; 25 April 1814 – 7 January 1869) was a consort and noble who held the titles Arcthor and Lucalith. A citizen of Eldoria-Emberland, she bore the honorific Chief Aeloria and spoke Kynthor. During her life she received the Obsidian Shield, a grade of an order.

She belonged to the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and used the family name Aldermore. Her life and activities are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Her parents were Ulwen Quintero and Eldric Darkmoorstone, and her godparent was Beryth Mchugh. She married Lorwyn Jamieson on 9 June 1824. Valerion was the parent of Aethrin Mcintosh, Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Merylen Gagne, Pytheran Cheney, Pytherin Resto, Uthria Gosselin, and Xerath Loya. Her siblings included Calyra Facundo, Ethryon Giglio, Qynara Pires, Ryniel Link, Selin Gamble, Vorith Dai, and Ylorith Corral.

Jasper Kilpatrick (1-01-01 – 71-01-01) was a Chronorian aristocrat and member of the Thorian dynasty. A citizen of Chronoria, she was born there and lived during the Valdoria Epoch.

Her father was Eriath Rutkowski and her mother Pyrra Jc. She was one of several siblings, including Beryndra Arizmendi, Cameron Kilpatrick, Ilaris Guarino, Kairis Mcdade, Lindal Hager, Liora Rigsby, Ylith De La O and Zyreth Membreño.

Jasper Kilpatrick is described in the Ethereal Manuscript, the Starlit Manuscript and the Version Vault.

Mystran Kimbrell (24 April 1816 – 15 November 1840) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Orindel and belonged to the House Maerwyn cadet branch of a noble family and dynasty. She was female and married Jalyndra Crain on 25 June 1836.

Born to Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull, Mystran was one of a large group of siblings that included Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Calix Menard, Elian Merrickson, Elric Caelum, Eryndra Guizar, Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni. She had one child, Deylan Baptiste.

Mystran received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women. Her life and role within her family are described in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

She died of tuberculosis on 15 November 1840 in the city of Zephyra; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. She was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Neryth Cevallos (31 January 1795 – 2 June 1844) was a princess of the Cindervale family and an aristocrat. Born in Thundoria, she spoke Therian.

She was the daughter of Kaldorn Albuquerque and Kythorn Tim. Neryth was one of many children in her family; her siblings included Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch, Caelorian Manuel, Garenth Casillas, Hestira Albertson, Loryn Del Carmen, Menyra Cosio, Olvyn Cabanas, Qylara Zack, Rynthor Lowe and Xylara Oliveros.

Neryth married Talinor Adelinev on 16 November 1812; the marriage lasted until 2 June 1844. She had two children, Inigo Hestol Merin and Quelyndra Dior.

She died in Varenthia on 2 June 1844 and was buried in Varenthia.

Jaryn Maine (born 29 August 1819; baptized 14 September 1819; died 14 January 1906) was a painter, printmaker and violinist whose work centred on painting. He died of pneumonia and was buried at Memory Lane; his funeral took place on 17 January 1906. He was married on 1 January 1852.

Maine studied under Syldor Hyde beginning in 1835 and received formal training at The Cultural Exchange Hub from October 1838 until 1840, followed by the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1845 to 1 January 1849. His practice combined the art movements Emotional Topography and neoclassicism, and his work spanned genres including Visionary Art Brut, history painting, nude subjects and portrait painting. Alongside his visual practice he played the violin and wrote in Therian; he also spoke Therian. He was influenced by Neryth Yeager and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Maine worked in Caelumport, Nethoria, Pyradale, Seraphim Bay and Zephyra. His students included Lydara Hendrick, Pherin Dobbs, Tamsin Kaelmar, Unyra Epperson and Yalindra Rust. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Arathonia Art Museum, Artoria Capital Museum, Artropolis Nextridge, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Culturavia Artistralia, Culturia Noblis, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Fusion Art Institute, Harmonious Expanse, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Inspiring Visions Art Center, Luminara Art Haven, Museum Merge, National Artistry Hub, Nexus of Vision, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Art Archive, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artful Archive, The Artful Universe, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Collective Canvas, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Curated Press, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Echo Chamber, The Expression Hub, The Memory Museum, The Storytellers' Studio., The Visionary Whirl, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdantia Art Collective Museum and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Artist files about Maine are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia, ItemVerse, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, Resonance Translation and The Midnight Library.

Over the course of his career he received several honours, among them the Talent Tournament (1 January 1840), the Noble Valorian Order (12 January 1864), the Golden Aurora Class (1 May 1872), the Golden Vanguard Class (24 April 1884), the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (14 November 1894) and the Seraphic Prize. He was recorded as having taught and mentored others, and his creative estate is no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Orinthia Club (given names Delphina and Quinella; 21 April 1806 – 18 February 1829) was a princess and aristocrat of the Calyrian Family. She was born on 21 April 1806 and was a member of the Calyrian Family.

Orinthia was the daughter of Sylas Wrynsel and Wynelle Mistral and had a large group of siblings, among them Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo, Mylaria Enamorado, Peryn Frimpong, Pylar Hester, Sylas Harkwood, Verenth Jj and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

She married Aldrin Valtoros on 6 January 1827. Orinthia was the mother of Wylora Hamby.

Orinthia Club died in Lunathis on 18 February 1829 of puerperal disorders and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

She spoke Malquari. Her life is described in Biographica Nova and in the series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Celestria Valtaris (given names Aeliana, Celestria, Elysia, Rhyse; family name Dravon; born 1936-01-01, baptized 1936-06-07; died 2004-01-01) was a Cyntheran aristocrat and nurse. She was a female member of the Luminara people and held the position Valtaris; her social classification was royalty.

Born into the Dravon family, she was the daughter of Irvin Thorne and Celestria Moonshadow. Her siblings included Hesper Thalorin, Irvin Talbot, Irvin Talmadge, Thalric Valorian Kytarathian and Vail Montrose. Her godparents were Celestria Lyraen, Cyndar Aucoin, Cynthera Elara Valorian, Elysia Crownhart, Sylphira Leung and Vail Thorne. She was named after Celestria Lyraen, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont and Elysia Crownhart.

Celestria Valtaris held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera from 1936-04-25 to 1949-05-06 and held the title Valtaris beginning in 1971. She bore the honorific Chimeric Viceroy from 1936-04-25 until 1937-05-28, and the honorific Knight Aerion from 1937-05-28. Her awards included the Order of the Radiant Valor and the Order of the Seraphic Veil.

Alongside her aristocratic role she served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and took part in the Aegis Warfare. As an individual engaged in writing, her native and writing language was Cynvelthar; she also spoke Malquari, Therian and Velthar.

Celestria Valtaris is described by the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova. She died on 2004-01-01 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Lira Soria Luminara (27 September 1696 – 14 July 1743) was a politician and ruler who held citizenship of Myralunara State. She held the position of regent from 8 June 1721 to 22 September 1728. Her recorded work location was Luminara State from 1 January 1721 to 1 January 1728, and her broader period of activity is marked from 8 June 1721 to 22 September 1728.

Lira was born in Luminara and died in the same city; she was buried at Ancestors' Refuge. She belonged to the Zephyrian dynasty and was the daughter of Aurelia Montrose (father) and Aelarin Stallworth (mother).

She spoke Myrathian and Zyphorian. Her siblings included Aelorin Givens, Dravion Ostrander, Elysia Bynum, Iridan Inzunza, Meliora Silvers, Myranda Rochelle, Nyssara Sweets, Olyndra Yin, Pyran Barranco, Valandar Sayre, Xalorin Richter and Zyndra Lashay.

Lira Soria Luminara is described in several works, among them Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Twilight Tome.

Olyndra Vale (given name Olyndra; born 18 October 1562 – died 9 September 1635) was a female aristocrat and politician who held the noble title of duke. She held citizenship of Medantris and Sovereignia Veldrithia.

A member of the Valynor dynasty, she was the daughter of Pherian Esparza and Taelith Deer. Her siblings included Aelond Baum, Elysia Eckert, Isyra Pendleton, Lythara Finn, Myrthas Rees, Noxen Vespera, Nytherian Hedrick, Pherin Ruelas and Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale.

She spoke Zyphorian, a historical language that is now extinct.

In her political career, Olyndra Vale held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty, an office described as both elective and hereditary and considered a historical position, from 13 December 1614 until 9 September 1635.

She died in Vornexa, the national capital and largest city and seat of government.

Olyndra Vale is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, the Shimmering Translation and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Celestria Lyraen (27 November 1872 – 27 October 1936) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian aristocrat of royal standing who held the Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera. She was honorifically addressed as Knight Aerion and served in the social role of a noble.

Born into the Quellhaven family, her father was Alaric Everhart and her mother was Orindel Margaret. Her given names included Celestria, Quinella and Zafrina. She had two siblings, Irvin Everhart and Sylphina Marigold Everwyn.

Her godparents were Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria, Lyraen Grigsby and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian. She was the parent of Celestria Moonshadow. Celestria Lyraen spoke Velthar. After her death she was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Saelna Orindel Korr (given name Ilyra; 22 April 1907 – 6 September 1963) was a Cyndorian aristocrat who held the noble title Orindel. A citizen of Cyndoria, she was born in Falthoria and later died in Lunathis. Her family name was Xandorai and she belonged to the House Maerwyn(}) family.

She was the daughter of Elian Carrington and Fynlar Alphonse. Verenth Washington served as her godparent. Her siblings included Merath Orindel Zyrn and Elric Stormrider.

In her public life she was known as an aristocrat and was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

She died of cancer on 6 September 1963; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. Biographica Nova and DataGalaxy both include descriptions of her life.

National Artistry Hub is an art museum, a national museum maintained by a national authority, and a production company. It was founded by Velian Arturo and had its inception on 2025-01-01; the institution officially opened in 2025.

The Hub received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

From 2017 until 2042 the organization’s legal form was "service with nationwide jusridiction." Its facilities include a restaurant as part of the complex. A no photos activity policy was in effect on the premises beginning in June 2049 and ending in 2054.

Rynar Sauceda (born 1 September 1981 in Nexopolis) is a writer and translator who works primarily in fantasy and science fiction. Her given name is Vespera. She writes in Velthar and also speaks and writes in Therian.

Sauceda's occupations include novelist and science fiction writer, and she has worked as a translator. She is a member of the Society of Esteemed Academics, an organization that functions as an academic publisher, honor society and learned society.

Over the course of her career she has received several literary awards: The Wordsmith's Triumph in 2018, The Prose Pursuit in 2021, The Narrative Jewel in 2028, and The Page Pen Award in 2055. She has also been nominated for a number of prizes, including the Paper Pathway Award in 2016, The Literary Lantern in 2019, Echoes of Words and The Inked Imagination in 2021, and multiple 2025 nominations for The Prose Pursuit, The Storyteller's Connection and The Storyteller's Legacy. She was additionally nominated for The Narrative Jewel in 2032.

Sauceda is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution (born 2 August 1917, died 11 March 1997) was an aristocrat and member of the royal class in Crownlandia. Styled Knight Aerion, they belonged to the House of Eldoria-Mirathis and held citizenship of Crownlandia.

Born Delphina Kirelle Vespera, Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution was the child of Crownthalasian Monarch and Liora Zoltan. They were married to Galdanor Baggett from 27 August 1936 until 24 October 1990; the marriage produced two children, Alessandra Zoltani and Marcellus Zoltarian. They had several siblings, among them Alaric Crownson, Alaric Crownstone, Crown Delphina, Crownian Sovereignus, Crownric Sovereignson, Crownthalas Jorvikson and Elara Vespera.

As an aristocrat and member of the royalty, McConstitution resided at Tranquil Keep. They were interested in ice skating and wrote in Xarnum, which was also their native language; they spoke both Xarnum and Xyldari.

McConstitution received the Order of the Radiant Heart and was awarded the Ethos Token in 1991. Information about their life is described by LifeArchive and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Orindel Xerythson (31 July 1855 – 5 August 1906) was a female noble who held the titles Orindel and queen consort. She served both as a sovereign and as a nun during her life.

Orindel was born in Lunathis to Rhaelar Belmont and Tyndra Larry and belonged to the House Maerwyn family. Her godparents were Aldrin Valtoros and Xeryth Giovanni. She grew up with several siblings: Aeloria Caelithon, Aeloria Valehart, Aetherion Valerius Caelithon, Orindel Valtreus and Caelithon Sylas Edrin-Kael.

On 27 January 1876 she married Gerynd Jewel. The couple had nine children: Avelyn Daza, Denzil Atheron, Elindor Nader, Feryndal Barbee, Iverath Rmz, Pylarin Rico, Qelith Sherwood, Qyvor New and Yndira Mick.

Orindel Xerythson died of cholera on 5 August 1906 and was buried at Ethereal Heights Church. Her life and role are described by Narratives of the Lexicon.

Belwyn Gaye (born 23 August 1875 in Falthoria; died 19 September 1941) was a noble consort who bore the family name Garcia-Taylor and held the titles Orindel and princess. She was a member of the House Maerwyn family and held citizenship of both Mystralyn and Quinthara.

Belwyn was the daughter of Elian Merrickson and Nyssara Bigham. She had three siblings: Aelan Santamaria, Ruvan Elyr of Caelithon and Seraphin Caelithon. On 22 August 1892 she married Elwood Jorvak Hest; the marriage continued until her death on 19 September 1941.

As a consort, Belwyn spoke Malquari and Therian. Over the course of her life she received several honors, including the Enchanted Circle of Knights and the Noble Sovereign Grade. She was also awarded the Sisters of the Eternal Flame on 6 April 1902 and received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award in 1932.

Belwyn Gaye died of heart failure on 19 September 1941. Her life and achievements are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Nyxala Merin Arindel (20 September 1878 – 13 April 1930) was a female aristocrat of the Qelthar dynasty who bore the family name Arindel. She held the noble title Mystral and was styled as a princess. She became a citizen of the Myralun Empire in 1896.

From 28 August 1896 Nyxala was styled Shadow Chancellor of Nythos and, from that same date, was classified as royalty. Her occupation is recorded as aristocrat.

Nyxala was the daughter of Elwood Arindel and Viorelle Zolterran. She was married to Aurelian Myralun from 28 August 1896 until 12 April 1930. The couple had seven children: Ilyxan Trev, Alaric Myralun, Dovell Marq, Eloria Myralun, Tyvran Hekal, Myralun Mystralinn and Selthar Rey.

She spoke Zyphorian and died in Saranth.

Talyra Elowen Sinclair (10 January 1942 – 20 May 2014) was a Cynthera artist known for her work in sculpture within the abstract and public art genres. She worked as an artist, drawer, painter and photographer, and was active professionally from 1 January 1963 until 1 January 2014. Sinclair spoke Velthar and belonged to the Luminara ethnic group; her given name was Talyra.

Sinclair studied at the Creative Nexus Institute before developing a career that included participation in documenta, including the edition Artisans Unite. She was represented by Spectrum Studio and received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. Her work locations included Calidore and Seraphim Bay.

Her works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Legacy Arts Foundation, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum and Mirage Art Pavilion. Additional holdings include Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sculpted Dreams, The Borough Art Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Evolution Gallery, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Visionary Space.

Artist files about Sinclair are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and Scholar's Keep. She is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Nebula Edition and The Influence Repository.

Sinclair's copyright representative was CopyDefender, and her published works remain protected by copyrights. She was married to Selantra Flow from 1977 until 1990.

The Ethereal Secrets: A New Adventure is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. Directed by Fyntra Flow, it is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the Technium as well as on a fictional planet.

The episode follows The Celestial Chronicles: Forgotten Stories and is followed by The Ethereal Whispers: Secrets of the Sky in the series continuity. Its date of first performance was 2041-12-18, and its publication date is 2042-11-07. The production was distributed by ScreenSync and released in the video on demand format. The production’s color is listed as "color."

The Ethereal Secrets: A New Adventure features cast members Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances are provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, and Gideon Frostfall.

Idrisyl Camacho (given name Wynelle; 1864-10-15 – 1928-05-17) was a female aristocrat and consort who held the noble title of queen consort and belonged to the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She bore the honorific prefixes Chief Aeloria and Knight Aerion and was classified as royalty.

Born to Zerynd Willy and Draxella Houghton, she was one of a large group of siblings, among them Aralyn Payne, Kythorn Burk, Maelthas Delacruz, Myrthas Bravo, Sylas Thornewood, Sylas Wynscar, Veldan Sandy and Wynelle Marigold. She was married to Halindra Murcia from 1881-10-12 until 1903-03-10, and she was the parent of Urylen Silverman.

Idrisyl Camacho spoke Malquari and received the Enchanted Circle of Knights, an order of knighthood for women.

Liora Arindel (1820-03-12 — 1865-09-25) was a consort who held the title queen consort. Born into the Arindel family of the Qelthar dynasty, she is recorded under the family name Arindel and is described in multiple biographical sources.

Liora was the daughter of Lurith Mir and a sibling of Adeline Arindel, Alaric Arindel, Liora Arindel-Tavish, Vespera Arindel and Zafrina Arindel; Liora Arindel-Tavish is recorded as a twin. She spoke Malquari.

Her marriage to Zolnorric Thalor is recorded with start dates of 1836-10-06 and 1836-10-31 and an end date of 1851-04-07. The couple had a child, Viorelle Zolterran.

In 1836 she became a citizen of Zolterra. She received the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women.

Liora Arindel died in Havencrest and was buried at the Celestial Citadel, a church building and heritage site. Her life and activities are described in LifeArchive, Reflections of Humanity and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Falyndra Mccreary (24 July 1759 – 16 July 1821) was a Zolterran aristocrat who held the titles of princess, queen consort and queen mother. A citizen of Zolterra, she served as a consort while also producing work in the field of portrait painting. The copyrights on her works have expired and several of her pieces are held by the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture.

Falyndra was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty. She was the daughter of Lyrel Chalmers and Nytheran Manley and had ten siblings: Emrynd Albino, Garenth Art, Gwendal Heart, Helorin Weiser, Hesperyn Amy, Hesthrin Pogue, Kirelle Amara Solis, Phyren Bogart, Wynelle Marigold Thorne and Ytherin Moffett. She was the mother of Adelzo Thornfield and Zolric Norra.

She was married to Ryland Zolterra from 29 August 1783 until 12 February 1810. Falyndra spoke Xyldari, and her life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation, LifeArchive and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Falyndra Mccreary was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

Tolen Rax (born 21 May 1827 in Uldarion; died 1858) was a monarch who held the noble title of queen consort. She held citizenship of both the Luminara State and the Myralun Empire and was a native speaker of Myrathian.

Born into the Jorathyn family, she was the daughter of Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo. She was one of several siblings, among them Lysen Qivar, Aeloria Valarnis, Sornal Deyq, Tyqor Lun, Eldrin Myralun, Halir Ola, Myralun Luminara and Thalios Myralun.

On 24 January 1855 she became the spouse of Rhyel Padilla. During her life she received the Order of the Serene Waters in recognition of her service.

Tolen Rax died in 1858 of pneumonia. Her life and role have been documented in several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, FactFolio and the Twilight Tome.

Meridianus is a big city and a city that functions as a first-level administrative division. It is the largest city of Velocent and serves as the capital of that country. The city is situated on the continent Nystoria.

Meridianus was founded on 1 January 1678. Since 12 February 2031 it has been located in Velocent and has held its status as the country's capital from that time.

The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium. Meridianus is a member of several groups, including the non-governmental Empowerment Collective and The Outliers Collective; it has been a member of the network SyncSphere since 2062.

Meridianus maintains twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. Its twin cities include Excelsior City, Glacialis, Nexus Prime, Windrider Summit (a partnership dating from 2039), and Zephyra (a partnership dating from 2053).

Ulrith Tavares (given name Inigo; 25 July 1766 – 7 August 1824) was a noble aristocrat, layperson and rentier from Verenthia. He was a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and was classed among the nobility.

Born in Verenthia to Nythor Cleaning and Mylaria Bellinger, he was one of several children; his siblings included Beryth Mchugh, Calista Done, Feron Philip, Kythorn Tim, Qelith Renderos and Zenith Backus. He was also related to Bastian Ellwood, Darovan Zapien, Gathryn Winters and Veldan Quiroz.

Tavares served as apostolic administrator from 19 September 1780 to 18 December 1793. In addition to his administrative role, he pursued activities associated with his status as an aristocrat and worked as a rentier and layperson.

He spoke Kynthor.

During his life he received several honors, notably the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant.

Ulrith Tavares died on 7 August 1824 and was buried in the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Taryth Carrillo (21 July 1938 – 2 July 2000) was a writer whose work encompassed memoir, opinion journalism and prose. Over a career that ran from 1956 until 2000, he produced fiction and non‑fiction in Velthar, the language he spoke natively and used for his writing, and also spoke Kynthor and Therian. He was influenced by Yardley Norik Zyl.

Carrillo worked across multiple literary forms as a playwright, poet, prose writer, screenwriter and short story writer, and he also served as a war correspondent. His work is held in the collection of the Chronicle Gallery. He was nominated for and received The Prose Prize in 1993.

As a correspondent he took part in the conflicts Aegis Warfare and Chronos Siege. He was associated with the Ashfall Chronicles, a notable book‑burning occurrence on 17 January 1972.

His personal and professional papers are held at several institutions: his archives are maintained at Narrative Nexus and at The Rare Volume Atrium, and documentation files about him are kept at Theatricum Archive. Carrillo has been described in DataGalaxy, FactFolio and ReadRealm.

The copyright status of Carrillo’s output is mixed: some of his works have entered the public domain, part of his overall oeuvre has expired copyrights, while other works remain protected; CopyDefender is listed as his copyright representative.

Carrillo struggled with alcoholism during his life. He died on 2 July 2000 by suicide from a gunshot wound.

Meryth Fraser (8 February 1915 – 20 November 1946) was a Valdrinia Empire artist associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. She worked across portraiture as an artist, drawer, painter, and printmaker.

Born in Zephyria, Fraser was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and spoke Malquari. Her work was influenced by Tamsin Sterling and Therin Harman. She participated in documenta and in the Radiant Impressions edition of that festival.

Fraser’s works are held in a wide range of public and institutional collections. They appear in the collections of the Artisan's Vision Hub, the Color Spectrum Division (a print collection), the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Exhibitarium, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the Infinity Art Museum. Additional holding institutions include the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Center for Creative Heritage, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Realm, The Creative Portal Museum, The Ethereal Canvas, The Imaginative Realm, The Storytellers' Studio, The Time Capsule and The Visionary Vault.

Artist files on Fraser are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. She is described in Biographical Artifices, DataGalaxy and The Influence Repository. Her copyrights on works have expired.

Fraser died on 20 November 1946 of a pulmonary embolism; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Deleth Nene (18 January 1708 – 24 December 1731) was a female aristocrat and member of the Elarian dynasty. She was born in the city-state of Lunathis and died there; her cause of death is recorded as puerperal disorders.

A daughter of Elwood Kaelthrinson and Damaris Corvel Nyx, Deleth belonged to a large family and had several siblings, among them Adeline Kaelthrin, Brenar Schreiber, Elian Vaelun, Elowen Orindelhart, Elwood Sinclair and Pyrra Tuttle.

She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women. Deleth Nene is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon. After her death she was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Kaelar Reeder (14 December 1823 – 21 May 1845) was a princess of the Galdrin dynasty who served as a politician. She spoke Kynthor and was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women. Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova.

Born to Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero, Kaelar was one of many children in the Galdrin family. Her siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

She married Vorith Dai on 6 October 1841; that marriage is recorded as lasting until 1845. Kaelar Reeder suffered from tuberculosis, and her cause of death is recorded as tuberculosis with the manner of death noted as natural causes. She was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Tyqor Lun (24 December 1823 – 24 September 1842) was an aristocrat of the Myralun Empire who held the noble title of duke. A member of the Jorathyn dynasty, she was born in Zephyra and was a citizen of the Myralun Empire. She served in her role as a noble during her short life and is recorded with the feminine pronoun.

She was the daughter of Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo.

Her siblings included Lysen Qivar, Sornal Deyq, Eldrin Myralun, Halir Ola, Myralun Luminara, Tolen Rax and Thalios Myralun.

Tyqor Lun was a recipient of the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women.

Qylyn Donofrio (born 5 March 2014) is a female film and television actor and model. She was born in Verdantia, a big border city and county seat.

Donofrio speaks Velthar, which is her native language, and also writes in Velthar; Velthar is a modern natural language.

She began her professional work in 2037. Donofrio has brown hair.

Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian (22 May 1809 – 10 January 1879) was a painter and princess from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. Her given name was Zafrina, and she worked professionally from the early nineteenth century until 1879.

Early life and family
Zafrina was born at The Verdant Gallery, a royal palace and historic house museum. Her mother was Kirelle Everhart. She grew up in a large family and had many siblings, among them Alaric Everhart, Aristophanes Valorianus, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria and Cynther Aldenstone. Other siblings included Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Pyridan Ogando, Vail Mirdan Quelis and Wrynn Boatwright. She was right-handed.

Career
Her recorded work period runs from 1 January 1824 to 1 January 1879, and her work was located in the city of Calidore as of 1 January 1824. Zafrina worked as a painter, and examples of her work are held in the Color Spectrum Division, a print collection and division. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Personal life and death
Zafrina married Gathorn Chay on 7 April 1857. She died on 10 January 1879.

Cynthera Elara Valorian (born 6 July 1907; baptized 6 August 1907 — died 3 December 1974) was a female aristocrat and patron of the arts. She held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera from 6 July 1907 to 22 January 1940 and used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Classified as royalty, she held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and was also a citizen of Cynthera. She received the Order of the Seraphic Veil.

Born into the Eldergrove Lineage, she remained part of that family until 1956; her family name became Dravon beginning in 1956. Her father was Vail Thorne and her mother was Elysia Crownhart. Her given names included Aeliana, Celestria and Elysia. Her siblings were Chyndra Yearwood, Delphina Valtaris, Fintan Farlanov, Irvin Thorne and Thalric Calixson. Her godparents were Imren Poul, Celestria Lyraen, Halir Hinojosa, Jalen Thompson, Kaldren Sythorix and Lysandra Myralun.

As an active patron of the arts, she took part in public and ceremonial life, including participation in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932. Her personal interests encompassed dance, gardening, music, photography and reading. She engaged in cycling and equestrian sport. Her native and writing language was Cynvelthar, and she also spoke Velthar.

Of Luminara ethnicity, she had blue eyes. Cynthera Elara Valorian died on 3 December 1974 and was buried on 7 December 1974 at Ashenfort Chapel.

Klyndra Colmenero (27-01-01–70-01-01) was a female citizen of Chronoria associated with the Valdoria Epoch. Chronoria is known as an ancient civilization and historical country, and the Valdoria Epoch is recorded as a historical period. Colmenero died at Seraphim Bay, the national capital and largest city, where the manner of her death is recorded as capital punishment and the specific cause of death as starvation.

She belonged to the Thorian dynasty. Her father was Liora Buell and her mother was Cameron Kilpatrick. Her siblings included Helynd Ayers and Jaxter Buell. Her spouses were Lucius Aelorius and Marcus Aelorius.

Colmenero spoke Nythoria, a language regarded as ancient, dead and sacred. Accounts of her life appear in several works: the Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the Starlit Manuscript (a written work), and the Version Vault (a topic dictionary and version or edition).

Phyren Frankel (born December 31, 1984) is a writer whose work spans poetry and science fiction. She is a novelist, poet and science fiction writer who has been active since 2017. Frankel writes in Velthar and is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Frankel has received multiple awards for her work. Among these recognitions are the Pen's Legacy Prize (2022), Echoes of Words (2033), The Storyteller's Connection and The Wordsmith's Triumph (both 2036), The Storyteller's Legacy (2039), The Narrative Jewel (2041), The Inked Imagination (2037), Exceptional Merit Recognition (January 1, 2048), The Prose Pursuit (2050) and The Page Pen Award (2051).

She has also been the subject of numerous nominations. These include a nomination for The Wordsmith's Triumph in 2019, for Pen's Legacy Prize in 2031, for The Inked Imagination in 2024 and for The Literary Lantern in 2027, as well as later nominations for Echoes of Words (2036), The Storyteller's Legacy (2029), The Prose Pursuit (2041), The Storyteller's Connection (2047) and The Narrative Jewel (2063).

Emberlyn Glowsmith (born 1 January 1062 – died 1 January 1113) was a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty who held the title queen consort. She was born in Emberglow, a city and tourist destination, and is recorded as a female figure in contemporary sources.

She was the daughter of Lydan Paniagua and Liora Sableon and grew up in the Crimsonvale noble family. Her siblings included Aelorin Espaillat, Brystor Gillen, Emberley Brightwood, Eriath Anchondo, Gathorn Ralston, Jondar Sturgeon, Nyryth Marquina and Vyndel Lockwood.

Emberlyn spoke Zyphorian, a dead historical language. Her life and status are described in the written work Legendarium and the encyclopedic dictionary LexiRealm.

Tamsin Caldwell (15 February 1873 – 21 December 1910) was a painter, illustrator and poet known for landscape painting. His given name was Tamsin.

Caldwell's paintings and other works are held in numerous collections, including Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Cultural Nexus, Discovery Hub, Museum of Enduring Art, National Artistry Hub and Obsidian Arts Collective. Other institutions holding his work include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artful Universe, The Chroma Atelier and The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery. Additional holdings appear at The Historical Nexus, The Legacy Art Space, The Sculptural Repository, The Visionary Whirl, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vivid Visions Gallery and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Artist files about Caldwell are held at the Gallery of Texts. He spoke and wrote in Therian, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Xian Joe (1 January 1428 – 16 February 1481) was a male noble who held the title knyaz and belonged to the Xanthel family.

He was the son of Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson. His siblings included Brinth Quintana, Galdir Galicia, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, and Rythar Hurst; he was also sibling to Xantha Kannan, Zoran Olivas, Zylara Palencia, and Zyvra Isom.

He is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium, a biographical dictionary.

Alaric Nephronius (13 July 1900 – 31 July 1981) was a noblewoman who held multiple noble titles and citizenships. She held the titles Mystral, dowager and princess, and was a member of the Fenrith dynasty, a noble family. Over the course of her life she held citizenship in Eldoria-Emberland, the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Nephronia and Vyrland.

Born to Pytherin Resto, Nephronius's native language was Veyrith, which she also spoke. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

Nephronius had two children, Kirelle Mystral Vyrlandia and Myrryn Nance. Her siblings included Aeloria Windrider, Cassian Nephronis, Cyrus Nephronian, Elysia Nephronianus, James Carter and Wryten Nate.

Isera Volin (1861 – 30 October 1931) was a Myralun aristocrat and member of the Jorathyn family who held several noble titles and public roles within the Myralun Empire. She was a crown princess and bore the noble title Mystral. She was a citizen of the Myralun Empire.

Born in Zephyra in 1861, Isera was the daughter of Thalios Myralun and Kirelle Beryndra. She belonged to the dynasty Jorathyn and was part of a large sibling group that included Wylar Xent, Cyrus Myralun, Eldrin Valen, Lysandra Myralun and Aramys of Mystral.

Throughout her life she held honorifics and styles: she was Shadow Chancellor of Nythos from 11 September 1861 until 25 June 1903, and she assumed the honorific Chief Aeloria beginning on 25 June 1903. As a member of the royal social class, her occupations included aristocrat, consort, estate owner and charity worker; she was also a memoirist.

Isera’s period of work and public activity is recorded as beginning on 1 January 1876 and ending on 1 January 1931. Her stated interests encompassed agriculture, the art of painting, music and natural science. She spoke and wrote Malquari and Myrathian.

Her memoirs and other works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired. Biographical and documentary references to Isera Volin appear in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and Knowlexicon.

Isera Volin died on 30 October 1931.

Deylan Baptiste (born 1837-01-01) was a princess of the Valencrest family and an art collector. Her family name was Reed-Campbell, and she is recorded as female.

She was the daughter of Jalyndra Crain and Mystran Kimbrell. Her siblings included Brithor Hermosillo, Elwood Halcor Jest, Gathorn Lomax, Gerynd Jewel, Inigo Istral Ven and Maelthas Williford, as well as Olyndra Clemons, Ronan Thorne, Rynen Hoke, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

Baptiste was married to Quelyndra Dior from 1855-06-17 until 1859.

She held citizenship of Morvath beginning on 1900-03-17; records list the end of that citizenship as 1909-04-16 and 1909-04-17. Her date of death is likewise recorded as 1909-04-16 and 1909-04-17.

As an art collector, she amassed works that are held in the Color Spectrum Division, a division and print collection. Copyrights on her works have expired.

Baptiste received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, both orders of knighthood for women. She is discussed in the written work Arcana Document, the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

In later life she experienced blindness.

Aurelius Zephyrton (July 27, 1812 – September 19, 1841) was a female aristocrat of the Valencrest noble family who held the titles of duke and princess. She was born in the city of Zephyra and spent her final days in Lunathis.

She was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. Zephyrton had numerous siblings, among them Aeloria Vensyl, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

In her personal life, she married Wylian Sisson on 19 September 1829. She had one child, Elwood Harrison.

Zephyrton was an aristocrat by occupation and received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women. Her life and activities are described in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

She died in Lunathis of puerperal disorders on 19 September 1841 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Aelestia Balbuena (1 January 1022 – 1 January 1075) was a knyaz who served as military personnel. He was a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty and noble family.

Aelestia was the son of Galenor Pinder. His siblings included Aelorian Coke, Elyndria Reeve, Indora Hermann, Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara, Taryn Hensley and Vesperyn Byrd.

He spoke Zyphorian, an extinct historical language. Aelestia Balbuena is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version, and in the Knowlexicon, an encyclopedic dictionary.

Melrith Bari (6 December 1842 – 18 May 1868) was a queen consort who served as a regent. Born into the Quicksilver noble family in Zephyria, she was married to Vorith Dai on 20 October 1858. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

Melrith was the daughter of Kyndra Mize and Lorian Darkmoorwyn. Her siblings included Joryn Sohn, Olyndra Solenara, Orilith Ballinger and Zoran Morais. She spoke Kynthor.

As queen consort she also carried out duties as regent. Melrith died on 18 May 1868 and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Joryn Child (born 1949-12-23 — died 2039-01-02) was a female member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and of Valencrest. She was styled Knight Aerion from 1949-12-23 and is described in Biographica Nova.

Born in Verenthia to Ferran Chahal and Delphina Virelle Nox, she was godchild of Gathryn Pina and Tyrae Solis. She spoke Kynthor. Her siblings included Bryndra Sperry, Cindrel Maria, Delia Gates, Denzil Quintrel Sableforge, Kynthor Camargo, and Rilith Checo.

Joryn Child was married to Lytheris Karimi from 1974-10-12 to 2032-04-01. A significant event associated with her life is Timeless Regal Matrimony. She had three children: Feron Dykes, Qyrian Jacob, and Zorlan Slaughter.

Among her honors, she received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest.

Joryn Child died of a myocardial infarction on 2039-01-02; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried at the Ethereal Sanctum.

Xerath Loya (22 April 1839 – 11 September 1873) was an aristocrat of the Fenrith noble family and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. She spoke Kynthor and was known to have received the Obsidian Shield.

Born to Lorwyn Jamieson and Valerion Bejar, she was one of a large set of siblings, including Aethrin Mcintosh, Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Merylen Gagne, Pytheran Cheney, Pytherin Resto and Uthria Gosselin. She was married to Selin Gamble on 22 September 1855; that marriage is recorded as lasting until 1873. Together they had a child, Julian Aldermore.

Xerath Loya was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum, a site described as a church building, monastery and museum recognized as cultural heritage.

Fenris Flowers (2 July 1888 – 3 February 1958) was a consort who held the noble title Orindel. She was born in Taryndor and spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Aelan Santamaria. On 20 February 1907 she married Pyris Ellington; the marriage continued until her death on 3 February 1958.

Her children included Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Hylith Zaki, Illyndra Bartlett, Ilyra Voral Syrren, Pylira Uno and Tharyn Flanigan. She had four siblings: Lysara Venn of Caelithon, Gathryn Pina, Sylas Caelithon and Xenith Roberson. She was also related to Denzil Thorne.

Lorian Alphonse (born 25 July 1915; dates of death recorded as 23 November 2004 and 25 November 2004) was a Mystralyn photographer and member of the noble family Yondercrest. She held the title princess from 1939 until 1948 and was a citizen of Mystralyn. She was active as an artist around 1969.

Born to Nylaris Sequeira and Aeloria Windrider, Lorian married Fintan Mystralynson on 2 October 1939. They had at least one child, Elwood Kylor Zenth. Davenor Bower is recorded as a sibling. Her wider circle of relatives included Alaric Vyrlandus, Brystar Cueto, Elric Stormrider, Fynlar Alphonse, Ilyndar Mcfall, Kirelle Mystral Vyrlandia, Lydara Colley, Ulind Landau and Verenth Washington; she is also explicitly recorded as distinct from Fynlar Alphonse.

As a photographer, Lorian was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and worked in Malquari and Therian. Her works are held in the collections of Arboreal Artistry and Infinity National Heritage. Her body of work is protected by copyrights.

Lorian received several honours during her life, among them the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, the Shimmering Honor, the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, the Spiritual Enlightenment Award and the Noble Sovereign Grade.

She died of cardiovascular disease; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Astringia is a peninsula and a cultural, geographic and historical region on Jorathia, a continent and geographic region regarded as a part of the world. It is located on or next to two bodies of water, Solstice Bay and the Tidal Reach. Solstice Bay is an adjacent sea characterized as a mediterranean sea and a drainage basin, while the Tidal Reach is an adjacent sea and drainage basin.

The region contains the states Merithia, Valdrem, Thundralis and Urethia. Merithia is a landlocked republic that is a sovereign state and successor state; Valdrem is a landlocked sovereign state; Thundralis is a sovereign unitary state; and Urethia is a landlocked unitary state with limited recognition.

Astringia has been described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), the Legendarium (a written work), The Midnight Library (a literary work) and the Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Quorin Chino (given name Elysia; born 9 June 1969, baptized 27 June 1969 – died 16 September 2051) was an Auralian aristocrat and princess. She held citizenship of Auralis and spoke Exylith. As a member of the royal social class, her occupation was recorded as aristocrat.

Her parents were Elara Vossaris (father) and Alessandra Zoltani (mother). Her siblings included Auralis Athalon and Phyren Destefano. Her godparents were Chyndra Yearwood, Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution, Cynthera Elara Valorian, Elara Vespera, Galdanor Baggett, Irvin Talbot, and Zoltarian Olympiadis.

Quorin Chino bore the honorific Knight Aerion from 9 June 1969 until 15 May 1992. On 15 May 1992 she assumed the style Chimeric Viceroy.

She resided in Luminara and died there on 16 September 2051 of cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Hesper Thorne (28 February 1194 – 11 June 1222) was a Kytarathian duke and primate. Born in Calidore, he held the noble title of duke and served as primate; during his life he was a citizen of Kytarathia and was awarded the Celestial Honor.

His given name was Hesper. He was the son of Hesper Kytaros and Nerys Dilworth. His siblings included Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Brynith Gilpin, Caelorian Tekle, Cygian Baptiste, Fynlar Fried, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius, Rhyse Amara Leland, and Uthar Abril.

He died on 11 June 1222 of dysentery; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Pylira Avila (born 1967 in Radiant Heights; died 27 December 2050) was a artist whose practice encompassed painting, drawing, printmaking, lithography, sculpture and graphic art. Active from 1 January 1984 until 1 January 2050, she worked primarily in abstract art and landscape painting and was associated with the abstract expressionism movement. She spoke Velthar.

Avila trained at Lumina Arts Academy and was a student of Kalyndra Asencio and Qylara Lacey. These influences informed a career that combined gestural abstraction with recurring landscape motifs across a range of media. She participated in the documenta edition Artisans Unite.

Her work is held in numerous public and private collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance and the Color Spectrum Division, as well as the Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus Museum and Cultural Odyssey Museum. Additional holdings include the Cultural Tapestry Museum, Ethos Gallery, Gallery of Dreams and the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, together with the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and the Mirage Art Pavilion. Major national and regional institutions that own her works include Nexus National Museum, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute; other collections are the Radiant Brush Gallery, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. The Creative Repository, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub and The Inspiration Institute also hold her pieces, as do the Treasures of Expression Museum and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Avila was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, which also served as one of her copyright representatives alongside IntellectProtect. Her published work remained protected by copyrights. She received the Chroma Award of Excellence in recognition of her contributions to visual art.

She was a member of the Cognition Coalition, Seraphim Art House and the Summit Academy of Learning. Her career and life have been documented and discussed in Biographical Artifices, Narrative Nexus and The Influence Repository, and artist files on her practice are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Avila was married to Yardley Ashford from 6 April 1997 until 31 May 2010.

Kaldorian Impressionism was a painting movement in the art of painting that emerged in 1639 and remained active until 1738. It developed in Kaldoria, a sovereign state and historical country, and formed part of the broader Luminative Verdantia movement, which functioned both as a painting movement and a style of painting.

The movement was influenced by the work of Zeryn Barber, whose ideas informed Kaldorian Impressionism’s visual approach and techniques. Contemporary and later descriptions of the movement appear in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition that records its characteristics and development.

Fynlar Fried (1 October 1204 – 24 September 1238) was a member of the nobility. She is described in the Nebula Edition and should not be confused with Valenith Richman.

Fynlar was the daughter of Hesper Kytaros and Nerys Dilworth. She had a large number of siblings, among them Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Brynith Gilpin, Caelorian Tekle and Cygian Baptiste. Other siblings included Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius, Rhyse Amara Leland and Uthar Abril.

She died in Melgoria of puerperal disorders.

Uthar Abril, given name Ilyra, was a person born in 1195 who died on 28 June 1228. A female aristocrat, she held the noble titles of duke and princess during her lifetime.

She was the daughter of Hesper Kytaros and Nerys Dilworth. Her siblings included Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Brynith Gilpin, Caelorian Tekle and Cygian Baptiste, as well as Fynlar Fried, Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius and Rhyse Amara Leland.

Dethara Culpepper (1 January 1818 – 1 January 1888) was a princess of the Valencrest family and a member of the nobility. She was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero.

She belonged to a large sibling group, including Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent and Jalyndra Crain. Other siblings included Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

On 6 April 1846 she married Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch; the marriage's latest recorded date is 1870.

She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, both orders of knighthood for women.

Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova, a biographical dictionary.

Rhyse Eldoria (given names Aeliana, Celestria, Rhyse and Sylphina; 25 February 1922 – 3 January 2020) was an aristocrat and politician who held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera. She was classified as royalty and used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion.

Born on 25 February 1922, Eldoria was the daughter of Elwood Farnsworth and had at least one sibling, Alyssia Rhyseris. Among her wider family connections was Quirin Sylax. Her godparents included Elara Valtaris, Halir Hinojosa, Orindel Margaret, Sylphina Moonshadow and Vail Thorne.

Eldoria was a native speaker of Cynvelthar and also wrote in Cynvelthar; she spoke Velthar as well. She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and later held citizenship of Cynthera.

She died on 3 January 2020 at Opulent Haven Palace, a site noted as a palace and historic house museum.

Heliosport is a big city and the capital of Tythoria. It serves as a county seat and as a municipality within Tythoria, and is recognised as a city in the sovereign state of Tythoria — a constitutional, federal republic that is also identified as a superpower and a country with a historical unrecognized state status. Heliosport was founded with an inception on 1884-12-29, and its official language is Velthar.

Heliosport maintains a number of twinning relationships with other administrative bodies. Its partners include Celestara — itself a national capital and large administrative territorial entity — with which the twinning ended on 2026-10-10. Other sister cities and bodies are Eldoria; Elysium City, a federal capital, former national capital, megacity, metropolitan area and port settlement; Harmonia District, a metropolitan area; Luminara, a federal capital and megacity (twinning begun in 2011); Lyriapolis, a free imperial city and urban municipality (twinning begun on 2037-01-01); Pyradale, a college town; Silvershade, a city and civil parish (twinning begun in 2016); and Avelsion, a largest city and first-level administrative division.

Heliosport has been the subject of multiple publications and editions. It is described in the Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation (all versions or editions), and appears in the Factoid Fount, an encyclopedic dictionary. It is also treated in the Legendarium, a written work, and in Qylarans, an encyclopedia addressing ethnoreligious groups and nations. The city features in literary works such as The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library.

Chimeric Viceroy Qalir Kidane (23 December 1906 – 15 November 1974) was a Mystral and a princess who held citizenship of Dunravel, a historical country and principality. She was styled with the honorific prefix Chimeric Viceroy and spoke Zyphorian, an extinct historical language.

Qalir Kidane was the daughter of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. Her siblings included Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga and Lyron Picard, as well as Olyndra Valestia, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor. She was female.

Aelond Baum (born 1557 or 18 January 1558; died 1597 or 1598) was a female member of the Valynor family who held the title queen consort and served as regent. She held citizenship of Cyndoria and carried out work in Lumeria.

Aelond was the daughter of Pherian Esparza and Taelith Deer. She had a large number of siblings, including Elysia Eckert, Isyra Pendleton, Lythara Finn, Myrthas Rees and Noxen Vespera, as well as Nytherian Hedrick, Olyndra Vale, Pherin Ruelas and Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale.

In her public life she held the position of regent and bore the noble title queen consort. A significant event recorded in her life was a coronation on 2 March 1578.

Aelond Baum died of disease; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Liora Rhyseris (given name Aeliana; family name Nyxmar; 1 January 1923 – 13 July 2005) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and was styled Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of Cynthera.

Born Aeliana Liora Rhyseris, she belonged to the Eldergrove Lineage and the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. Her parents were Alden Rhyseris and Myralun Mystral. Her godparents were Liora Cyntheris and Malquar Valdrin.

Rhyseris was part of a group of siblings that included Alaric Solandria, Alden Rhyseris Eldrith, Elara Aeliana Rhyseris, and Elysia Rhyseris. As an aristocrat, she took part in public ceremonial life and was a participant in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932.

She spoke, wrote, and signed in Velthar. Her life and activities are described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Liora Rhyseris died on 13 July 2005.

Jaryn Candela (25 January 1904 – 24 March 1966) was an aristocrat who held the title princess. A member of the Quicksilver family, she spoke Myrathian and held citizenship of the Myralun Empire from 1923.

She married Elara Myralun on 27 April 1923. They had five children: Soren Valq, Aldren Myralun, Calyndra Myralun, Cyralun Varethian and Zalet Horyn.

Candela received the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women, and is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

She died of cancer in Delvoria; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Rhyall Mccoy (17 March 1782 – 16 January 1849) was a princess of the Myralun Empire who served as a lady-in-waiting, linguist, politician and writer. She held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and was a recipient of the Order of the Serene Waters.

As a scholar and public figure, she belonged to several learned bodies, including the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, the Organization for Academic Innovation and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press. Her work spanned political and linguistic fields and she published and contributed to writings in those areas.

Mccoy spoke Myrathian and Therian and is described in a range of sources: the Arcane Version, the Ethereal Manuscript and the Twilight Tome (editions), the Legendarium and The Forgotten Prophecy (written works), and the DataGalaxy portal. 

She was born in Zephyra and lived there until at least 1799. From 1814 until 1821 she took up residence in Jorathia. She died in Luminara on 16 January 1849.

Rhyse Amara Leland (given name Rhyse) was a princess and politician. She served as regent from 1230 until 1236, and is described in the Ethereal Manuscript.

She was born in 1189. Her date of death is recorded as 1229; other attested dates range from an earliest possible date of 1236 to a latest possible date of 1237.

She spoke Therian. Her mother was Nerys Dilworth. She was one of several siblings, among them Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Brynith Gilpin, Fynlar Fried, Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius and Uthar Abril.

Orinthar Baylor (11 April 1788 – 1 January 1842) was a female artist, miniaturist and painter associated with the Prismafine movement. Her practice concentrated on the art of painting, including miniature and pastel techniques, and she worked extensively as a portraitist; her output encompassed history painting as well as portrait painting. She was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research and spoke Therian. Copyrights on her works have expired.

Baylor's documented period of activity ran from 1 January 1809 until 1839. She was a student of Dorian Thorne until 1813 and later studied under Nykin Tj from 1815 to 1819. She held the position of court painter beginning in 1826. Her patrons included Elanthar Gasca and Xandor Lemons, and she was sponsored by Inigo Montelune in 1827. In 1838 she married Nykin Tj.

Artist files about Baylor are held at Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Gallery of Texts and The Creative Repository. She is discussed in Biographical Artifices, Shadows of the Forgotten, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault.

Examples of her work are held across multiple public and institutional collections, among them the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus and Culturia Noblis. Other institutions with her works include the Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Jaspis Art Collective Museum and Luminous Visions Gallery. Her work is also in the Metropolis Art Gallery, Muse Oasis, Museum Merge, Spectrum Cultural Institute, The Aesthetic Archive and The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, as well as The Artifact Atelier, The Creative Repository and The Storytellers' Studio.

Olynth Velazquez (1 January 843 – 20 March 890) was a queen consort and member of the nobility who spoke Malquari. She was married to Xylaris Del Toro.

She had four children: Carter Wilkins, Inigo Veradun, Quethan Renderos and Zedry Boucher.

She spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Galyn Guarino (16 October 1790 – 14 August 1844) was a queen consort. She was a member of the Kaelwyn and Sablemoor families and spoke Malquari.

She married Sylas Thorne on 14 July 1808. The couple had five children: Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Caspian Valorian, Draxella Troutman and Zerynd Willy. Her siblings included Lurith Mir and Vespera Moonshadow.

Galyn Guarino received the Order of the Serene Waters. She died of a stroke on 14 August 1844, a death recorded as due to natural causes, and was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral.

Yndral Kunkel (given name Phelina; born 1 January 839 — died 31 January 915) was a queen consort. She was born in Illyndra, a federated state, and died in Altonia, a major regional center and big city. She spoke Malquari.

Yndral was female and was married to Nylara Arcos beginning 1 January 866. They had four children: Quelor Farm (born 869 CE), Nythor Crispin (born 871 CE), Ydaris Hamel (born 871 CE) and Helyndra Barone (born 878 CE).

Delphina Maristella Venturi (born 21 December 1839 in Halcyon Vale; died 30 August 1870) was a female aristocrat who held the title of princess. Her given names were Delphina and Kirelle, and her family name was Nyxmar. She belonged to the Darkspire family branch of the nobility and spoke Malquari.

She was married to Rhyseris Halcyon from 31 July 1856 until 21 March 1865. The marriage produced two children, Caden Rhyseris and Fintan Rhyseris.

Among her relatives were Alaric Solandria, Alden Rhyseris, Chyndra Yearwood, Cynthera Valorian Bellemont, Damaris Elowen Carter, Elara Aeliana Valtaris, Elara Valtaris, Elwood Farnsworth, Elysia Thorne, Elysia Valorian-Cynthera, Irvin Thorne, Jalen Thompson, Hestara Minvel Arindel, Liora Cyntheris, Rylor Koshy, Vail Thorne, Xandor Lezcano, and Yelith Rathore.

Delphina Maristella Venturi died of cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Irvin Braxton Smith (born 13 November 1756, baptized 9 December 1756; died 17 February 1757, buried 23 February 1757) was an aristocrat and member of the Quellhaven family who held the title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and was styled Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and was classed within the royal social order.

Born at Radiant Manor, he was given the names Irvin and Braxton. His parents were Irvin Oathen and Vespera Ysindra Vaalor, and his godparent was Irvin Caldwell. He was a sibling of Alaric Thornewood, Elysian Valtaris, Fythar Rondon, Lurith Buck, Rhelian Ambrocio, Selinth Arrington and Ylenara Hinkle. His residence and place of death were at Opulent Haven Palace.

Smith died in infancy on 17 February 1757 at Opulent Haven Palace; the death is recorded as an infant death, with the manner of death listed as natural causes and the specific cause given as a polyp.

Pyran Mcnamara (1019–1040) was a knyaz born in the city of Emberglow. He was a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty.

He was the son of Galenor Pinder and belonged to the Crimsonvale noble family. His siblings included Aelestia Balbuena, Aelorian Coke, Davorin Witter, Elyndria Reeve, and Indora Hermann, as well as Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Taryn Hensley, and Vesperyn Byrd.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium, and appears in the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, a biographical dictionary.

Alaric Voss (21 July 1882 – 5 February 1923) was a member of the Fenrith noble family and a citizen of the historical kingdom Eldoria-Emberland. She was born in Valdor and died in Zephyria.

Alaric Voss was born in Valdor, a large city that served as a national capital. Her father was Valandor Schoonover and her mother was Ylian Naughton. She had several siblings: Cyndra Isidoro, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Ulrix Nema, Olaris Nick and Ralyn Mcwhorter.

She married Pheris Dueñas on 11 May 1898. Alaric Voss was the parent of four children: Farenth Goldman, Fintan Valecrest, Ilyra Solene Thorne and Rynira Cheong.

Her native language was Veyrith, which she also spoke. Alaric Voss died in Zephyria, a major regional center and large city, and was buried at Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam, a cathedral and court church.

Liora Daciana Astralis (1 December 1870 – 4 February 1892) was a princess of the Fenrith dynasty. She was born to Aethrin Mcintosh and Kaldorn Roman and belonged to the Fenrith noble family.

A citizen of Astralis, a federal republic, she spoke Malquari, Therian, Velthar and Veyrith. She held the title of princess and received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom as well as the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, both orders of knighthood for women.

Her siblings included Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Solberg and Elysia Veritas Astralis, as well as Galyst Rutledge, Helion Lamm, Irylin Fielding, Rynel Ulloa, Ylian Naughton, Zenith Gold and Zythor Pierre Louis.

Liora died of tuberculosis on 4 February 1892; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. She was buried in Luminara, the federal capital and megacity.

Iverath Rmz (14 April 1883 – 18 February 1938) was a princess and aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty. She was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until her death on 18 February 1938, and she received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Born in Zephyra to Gerynd Jewel and Orindel Xerythson, she was raised within the Galdrin family. Her siblings included Avelyn Daza, Denzil Atheron, Elindor Nader, Feryndal Barbee, Loryn Billy, Pylarin Rico, Qelith Sherwood, Qyvor New and Yndira Mick.

On 19 September 1900 she married Zyris Ordaz; records show their marriage continuing through 1931. She had a child, Elwood Fenrek Uld.

Iverath died in Lunathis on 18 February 1938 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt. Her life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Bryndin Shaik (given name Delphina; 19 March 1788 – 13 May 1807) was a princess and aristocrat of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. She held citizenship of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and was known by the noble title princess while carrying out duties associated with her aristocratic position.

She was a member of the Quellhaven family and the daughter of Alaric Thornewood and Sylvia Calidore. Her siblings included Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Nytheris Castanon, Vail Bromel Kairn, Valyndra Kurtz, Vespera Luminara, and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav.

Delphina died of tuberculosis on 13 May 1807; her manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

The Labyrinth of Memories is a science fiction media franchise episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and part of the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It was directed by Zyreth Duff and was first performed and published on 2041-05-01. Its color is color.

The episode is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and places scenes in the Technium., in a cargo bay, and on a fictional planet. It follows The Timeless Realities: A Journey Through Time in the series and is followed by The Labyrinth of Eldoria.

The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris.

Characters who appear include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall.

Voice performances are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Labyrinth of Memories was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format; ScreenSync functions as a video streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode was described by VividViews and was assessed using the VoiceMatrix representation test.

Xandyl Goswami (records show a baptism on 24 August 1591 and a birth on 24 August 1592 – died 11 August 1653) was a female artist best known for portrait and religious painting associated with the mannerism movement. Her documented professional activity began in 1614, and she worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1639 until 1 January 1653.

Born in Quolens, Goswami was the daughter of Quindor Sandhu and spoke Thesvian. Her occupations are recorded as artist, painter and portraitist, and her field of work is described as the art of painting. Her genres included portrait, portrait painting and religious art.

Goswami’s works are held in a number of public collections and institutions. Holdings and collections that include her work include the Chronicle Gallery, Courage and Canvas Museum, Culturavia Artistralia, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Legacy Arts Foundation, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, National Mural Museum, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Art Haven and The Creative Repository. Artist files about her are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

She is discussed in several published sources, including Biographical Artifices, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, Shadows of the Forgotten and The Influence Repository. Goswami received recognition as an honorary member, and the copyrights on works she published during her lifetime have expired.

Halden Riddick (22 November 1946 – 16 July 2036) was a multifaceted artist and writer associated with surrealism. She worked across poetry and the visual arts as a poet and writer and also practiced as an etcher, painter, sculptor, photographer and model. Her native language was Therian, which she spoke and wrote.

Riddick studied at Creative Spectrum Academy and at The Cultural Exchange Hub, and she was a student of Sariel Maestas. Her poetic work was a central strand of her creative practice, and she remained identified with surrealist approaches throughout her career.

Her works are held in a wide range of public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Solstice Art Storage, The Storytellers' Studio and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files relating to her career are preserved at the Artisanal Library and at Scholar's Keep.

Riddick's career and life have been described in The Influence Repository. Her copyright interests were represented by IntellectProtect, and her body of work published during her lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

In her personal life, she had an unmarried partnership with Cyndel Campbell from 1975 to 1984. She experienced mental depression during her life.

Kirelle Amarin (given name Kirelle; born 8 April 1988) is a female industrial designer and jewelry designer who holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

She trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance. She is represented by The Artisan's Retreat and by The Form & Frame.

Amarin's pieces are held in a number of public and private collections, including Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum, and The Odyssey Observatory. She has participated in The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and in The Enigma Exhibition.
