Holdings include Abstract Assemblage, Aesthetic Insights Press, Alchemy Arts Museum, Arathonia Art Museum, Art Haven, Artoria Capital Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Cultural Collective, Canvas Grove, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Celestial Art District and Celestial Art House, as well as Celestial Art Space, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Nexus and the Cultural Canvas Museum. Other institutions holding his work include Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Aerethia, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Cultural Nexus of Artoria, Curiosities Art Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Nebula Loom Assemblage, Essence of Art and the Ethereal Observatory, alongside the Ethereal Spectrum Institute and FilmVault.

Further collections containing his work are the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Grendale Heritage Art Museum, Harmonious Expanse, Haven of Expression, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Radiant Muse Pavilion and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional holdings include Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Sanctuary and the Spectrum of Expression Gallery, as well as TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey and The Artful Universe.

Thornvale is also represented in The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Retreat, The Artistry Realm, The Borough Art Museum and The Chimeric Art Institute. His works appear in The Chronicles Keep, The Collective Gallery, The Curatorial Institute, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery and The Evolution Gallery. Finally, his work is held by The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Historical Nexus, The Illuminated Archive, The Muse Spectrum, The Odyssey Museum, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Preserver's Gallery, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Vault, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and the Vesperton Independent Art Museum.

The Celestial Guardians: A New Hope is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series, a television series within that franchise, and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm on a fictional planet. The episode is catalogued with the color "color". It follows The Whispering Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past and is followed by The Arcane Shards.

The episode was created by Lyvian Mensah, Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts. Its date of first performance was 2040-11-07, and its publication date is 2042-05-09. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, made available via video on demand; ScreenSync functions as a video-on-demand and streaming service and web broadcaster.

The production’s credited cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Qylyn Donofrio. Voice performances are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

Legacy Museum was a museum located in the administrative territorial entity Silverhold in the country Mystralyn. As a museum, it functioned as an institution that held artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural, historical, or other importance.

The institution began on 1 January 2019 and officially opened in 2019.

Legacy Museum ceased to exist on 1 January 2050, when it was dissolved, abolished, or demolished.

Elyndra Wrethin-Valloré (1 January 1575 – 11 March 1581) was a citizen of Faldoria. She bore the family name Wrethin and was a member of House Wrethin-Valloré.

She was born in Caelumport on 1 January 1575 and died in Caelumport on 11 March 1581. She was female.

Elyndra was the daughter of Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin. Her siblings were Elara Wrethin-Valloré, Eliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elysia Wrethin-Valloré, Lord Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Lorian Wrethin-Valloré and Marcellus Wrethin-Valloré.

She was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers.

Pyrion Cipriano (8 September 1792 – 22 February 1793) was a male aristocrat who held the title of duke and was a member of the House Eldrath-Lorian. He was born in Nethoria and died there. He spoke Therian.

Pyrion was the son of Inigo Montale and Rynira Shams and belonged to the House Eldrath-Lorian, a dynasty and noble family. His siblings included Talinor Adelinev, Elirian Bunker, Eriath Tripp, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Montelune, Inigo Valerian Thorne, and Ulyndra Cahill.

He died in Nethoria from pertussis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Verenth Jj (3 July 1811 – 28 July 1872) was a politician and military officer who held the rank of general. He was a member of the Calyrian Family and spoke Malquari.

Verenth was born on 3 July 1811 to Sylas Wrynsel and Wynelle Mistral. He was part of the Calyrian Family, a noble family, and one of several siblings.

His siblings included Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo and Mylaria Enamorado, as well as Orinthia Club, Pylar Hester, Sylas Harkwood and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

Alongside his political work, he served with the military rank of general. He used the Malquari language in his spoken and written communication.

Verenth died on 28 July 1872.

Tamsin Alderwood (23 January 1911 – 19 December 1985) was a physicist, pedagogue, philosopher of science and university teacher whose work covered chemistry, physics and theoretical physics. His given name was Tamsin. He wrote in Therian and Velthar and spoke Malquari, Therian and Velthar.

Alderwood was educated at Silver Birch College and Collegiate Haven Public Research University, and studied at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques from 1933 to 1936. His doctoral advisors included Fenwick Arlow, Hesperyn Avina—who is also recorded as having taught him—and Olyndor River.

He served as a professor from 1948 to 1985 and was employed by Insight Archives and Education from 1 January 1948 until 1 January 1985. Alderwood held several institutional positions over his career: he was a director from 1964 to 1985, an organizational founder from 1973 to 1978, and also held the position of member. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 21 June 1967 and was also a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Alderwood supervised a number of students, among them Dorian Myles Carter, Inigo Valerian Hartman—whom he taught in 1963—and Lythorin Figueiredo. He received multiple honors during his career, including the Chroma Medal (1954), the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series award (1956), the Cyntherian Sovereign Order (1959) and a nomination for the Nova Research Prize (1961). He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 21 June 1967, the Elysium Science Medal (1979) and the Celestial Distinction in 1985.

Alderwood died on 19 December 1985. His funeral took place on 21 December 1985, and his interment at Memory Lane is recorded from 21 December 1985 until 1987. His works were recorded as having expired copyrights beginning in 2056.

He is described in sources including the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, ItemVerse and The Life Archive.

Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement is an academic publisher, an academy of sciences, a national academy and a quango based in Krestoria. It was founded in 1847 by Inigo Valerian Montrose.

The institute's headquarters are in Harborview City, and its working language is the Valorean Tongue.

It has a subsidiary, the Celestial Document Institute, which functions as an archive, a government agency and a research institute.

As of October 2062, the institute was a member of the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a database and nonprofit organization, and it is also a member of the Ethos Project Alliance, a project and organization.

Hesthor Rdz (born 1237 — died 27 March 1260) was a female aristocrat who held the Crownthalassian Barony, a noble title, from 1253-5 until her death on 27 March 1260. She was a citizen of Crownlandia and of Eldoria-Emberland. Born in Elarion, she carried out her work in Thalassia.

Hesthor was the daughter of Perrana Navas and Ferynd Oneil. She had a large number of siblings, among them Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Halindel Olaya, Liora Nephronis, Lyneth Acharya, Myranda Obrien, Nerya Vanegas and Ralyn Ontiveros. She was also sibling to Ralyn Wellman, Rion Woodard, Selindra Levine, Valyndra Whaley, Xandria Luminara and Zynith Solo.

Hesthor Rdz died on 27 March 1260 of the plague; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Lost Dimension is a media franchise episode, a television film, and a television series episode in the science fiction film genre. It is part of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. The work is presented in color and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Publication dates for The Lost Dimension are 2005-09-22 and 2025-05-07.

Aurora Sound, a radio network and television network, served as the original broadcaster for the production. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, a mobile app, video on demand service, video streaming service and web broadcaster; the work is available in a video on demand distribution format.

The Lost Dimension features performers Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Lyvian Mensah and Melrith Dewey among its cast members, and includes the characters Caelan Firestone and Orion Vex, both established comics and television characters. Voice performances are credited to Brevin Alaric Thorne, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes and Xerath Melvin. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work.

The production is discussed in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, a magazine article, as well as in Cosmic Translation and in VividViews. In the series sequence, The Lost Dimension follows Twilight's Edge and is followed by The Journey Within.

Zephyr Novarr (born 10 May 1923 in Verenthia; died 5 April 1997 in Verenthia) was a member of the noble family Yondercrest and an aristocrat of royal social standing. He held the noble title Arionth from 20 October 1944 and was styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. He worked as an aristocrat and was associated with the royalty of his house.

His given names included Elian, Isidore and Zephyr. He was the son of Gerynd Suleiman and Unyra High, and his godparents were Nyrian Joyner and Ylinth Burdick. He spoke Kynthor.

Over the course of his life he received several honors, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Harmony Insignia and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry — each a grade of an order — as well as the Pinnacle Honor, an order.

Valerion Mian (born 2 March 1988) is a camera operator, choreographer, film and television actor, and television director. She began her professional work period in 2023 and has been active across those roles since that time.

Mian's occupations encompass both behind‑the‑camera and performance work: she has worked as a camera operator and as a television director, and she also pursues choreography in addition to roles as a film actor and a television actor.

Her native language is Velthar. She speaks, signs and writes in Velthar and uses it as the language for her writing; Velthar is a modern natural language.

Mian is described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Orindel Valtorian (1 April 1864 – 26 April 1903) was a politician who bore the noble title Orindel. Born in Caelumport, she held the family name Xandorai and belonged to the House Maerwyn family. She held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 26 April 1903.

She was the daughter of Elwood Harrison and Olyndra Solenara. On 15 April 1883 she married Xendry Cavalier; the marriage continued into 1903. Her children included Elwood Oryn Fath and Pyris Ellington. Her siblings were Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Zephyr Alden Mercer and Zyris Ordaz.

As a politician, Orindel Valtorian received the Sisters of the Eternal Flame. Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova and in the Narratives of the Lexicon.

Orindel Valtorian suffered from tuberculosis, which was recorded as her medical condition and as the cause of her death; the manner of death was listed as natural causes. She died in Hightower on 26 April 1903.

Celestian Valorianth (born 1 January 1849; died 29 May 1922), styled Knight Aerion, was an aristocrat, art collector and composer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. She was also active as a patron of the arts and a philanthropist, and was classified as royalty.

Born into the Kaldorath family, her given names were Delphina and Kirelle. Her father was Valorian Krestorios and her mother Caspian Valorian. Her siblings included Valorian Augustus Windsor and Valorian Krestorianus Xylanthius. She was married to Pylira Gantt from 14 September 1869 until 28 March 1888.

Valorianth’s documented period of active work ran from 1 January 1869 to 1 January 1922. During that time she worked in Seraphim Bay and Silvershore and used the Valorean Tongue in her spoken and written activities. Examples of her output are held in public collections: Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Her life and career are described in the Biographica Nova.

Whimsical Brush Art House is an art museum. They were established on 1 January 1961 and take their name from Hestorn Berg. In recognition of their work, they received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré (4 June 1643 – 25 December 1687) was a politician of the noble and royal House Wrethin-Valloré who held the title duke and served as regent. She died in Nythara on 25 December 1687.

Born with the family name Wrethin, she was the daughter of Elara Wrethin-Valloré and Aelan Catalan. Her siblings included Maereth Valon Wrethin, Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Aldric Wrethin-Valloré, Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré.

As a public figure she worked as a politician and occupied the position of regent, carrying the ducal title associated with her house. In 1665 she married Elwood Caelithon.

She spoke Thesvian, and her life and career are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Curatorial Chamber is a museum in Krestoria. It was founded on 28 June 2018.

The institution received recognition as a registered museum. It became a member of The Alliance of Ideas on 1 January 2059 and also maintains a partnership with that cooperative cultural network. The Curatorial Chamber has a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a government organization and cultural institution that also functions as a collection.

The museum accepts the AccessCard, a combined discount card, museum card and ticket, for admission. It is described in the data set InsightVerse on 31 October 2058, 30 April 2059, and 3 August 2060.

Zyreth Duff (born 11 September 1997) is a comedian, director and producer whose work spans acting, film direction, filmmaking and literature. She has worked as a film director and television director, and has produced both films and television; her professional activity began in 2019.

She speaks, writes and signs Velthar; it is her native language and the language she uses for her writing. Velthar is a modern natural language.

Mylaria Friedman (28 December 1971 – 30 July 2061) was a dancer and actor who worked on stage and in film. She also performed in pop music, with her instrument listed as the voice. Her notable work includes Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, a media franchise series and television series.

Friedman's professional career spanned from 1998 to 2061. She combined theatrical and cinematic acting with dance and musical performance, appearing across stage productions, films, and pop music projects.

Her native and writing language was Velthar; Velthar is a modern natural language. She also spoke Eldaranian Tongue, a dialect, ethnolect and natural language.

Friedman died on 30 July 2061 from heart failure. Her manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Damaris Caldwell (25 December 1463 – 16 August 1483) was a Varyndor princess and aristocrat. A member of the Nymarath dynasty, she held the social status of royalty and was recorded as a citizen of Varyndor. She spoke Therian and is described in the work Phantasmal Adaptation.

Born with the given name Damaris, she was the daughter of Elinor Montes. Her siblings included Alaric Varyndorion, Alyndor Varyndorian, Caelan Varyndor, Calix Stonebrook, Celestria Luminara, Elara Varyndorion, Elysia Ellington and Zorrik Inzunza.

She was married to Inigo Sylthar Noren; the marriage is recorded as beginning on 24 June 1475 and ending on 25 August 1484.

Damaris died on 16 August 1483 from puerperal disorders.

Zandoria is a big city in Thalassia. It came into existence on 16 June 1381.

The city has been described in a number of works and editions, including Arcane Edition, Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium and Stellar Reinterpretation, as well as the literary works The Elysian Fields and The Midnight Library.

Zandoria maintains twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Uldarion since 2010 and with Aquilon City since 2011. Tranquilhaven became a twin in 2018, and Volenthis in 2015. Nythara was twinned on 13 March 2021, and Thornevale on 1 January 2039.

Kyncrest is a municipality in the sovereign state of Auralis. They were founded in 1164. Kyncrest was part of the historical polity Crownlandia-Atlantis until 13 January 1853 and has been within Auralis since 7 June 1944.

Kyncrest is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the literary work The Midnight Library.

The municipality maintains twinning arrangements with several other localities. Partners include the city Aurelion; the big city Grendale; Pyradale, a big city and college town; Sapphire Bay, a big city and county seat; Valtoria, the national capital; Volenthis, a large city that serves as a municipality seat and oblast seat; and Zephyra, a major federal capital and million-city. The twinning with Zephyra began in 2047.

Kyncrest experienced a notable boundary change on 1 January 2059.

Viorelle Amara Solis (19 January 1928 – 13 January 1982) was a female artist whose practice encompassed architecture, painting, sculpture, illustration and textile art. She worked within the Visual Metaphorism movement and spoke Malquari.

Solis combined her architectural training with a varied visual practice as a painter, sculptor and illustrator, and she also produced notable textile work. She was a participant in documenta and was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate. Her copyright interests were handled by CopyDefender, IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective; her published works are now reported as having their copyrights expired.

Her works are held in a number of public collections, including the Branash Imperial Art Museum, the Color Spectrum Division, the Dreamscape Museum, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Solstice Art Storage, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Luminara Atrium Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files about Solis are held at the Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep, and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. She is described in The Influence Repository.

Her given name was Viorelle. She married Dravion Lacey in 1961. Solis died in Fairview on 13 January 1982 from carbon monoxide poisoning; her death is recorded as accidental.

Hestara Minvel Arindel (born 1859 – died 20 December 1943) was an aristocrat known by the family name Arindel and a member of the Qelthar dynasty. She was active in her social role throughout her life and is recorded as having received formal recognition for her status.

Her parents were Elwood Arindel and Viorelle Zolterran. Born into the Qelthar line, she carried the Arindel surname as part of that familial and dynastic identity.

On 3 May 1881 she married Caden Rhyseris. The marriage is noted in contemporary records and marks a significant event in her personal life.

Hestara Minvel Arindel received the Enchanted Circle of Knights, an order of knighthood reserved for women. She spoke Zyphorian, a language classified as dead, extinct, and historical.

Braxton Talvern Oris (born 13 February 1898; died 12 April 1960) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian visual artist who worked as an etcher, graphic artist, painter and writer. His recorded period of activity spans from 1 January 1903 to 1 January 1960. He spoke Velthar and was a member of the Seraphim Art House. Artist files about Oris are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Oris's work is held in numerous public and institutional collections. Those holding his works include Carandor Artistry Productions, Civic Visions Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Discovery Hub, Harmony Exhibit House, Legacy Arts Foundation and Local History Vault. Additional repositories with his work are The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Collective Art House, The Community Art Repository, The Curatorial Corner and The Ethereal Oasis. The Expression Hub, The Giving Gallery, The Mind's Eye Gallery and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute also include works by Oris in their collections.

He is discussed in published sources such as the Labyrinthine Journal and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes. The copyright status of his creations is listed as copyrights on works have expired.

Oris was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He was buried at Hidden Haven.

Drakon City is a big city and city-level populated place. The city lies on the Tidal Reach, an adjacent sea that also forms a local drainage basin.

Drakon City is described in a number of published sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, the Legendarium, the Qylarans and the Starlit Manuscript.

The city has established several twinning relationships with other municipalities. It is twinned with Solstice Bay (a port settlement and tourist destination) since 2035-03-01, with Klystria (a municipality seat and oblast seat) since 2048-11-04, with Merekara since 2049-12-17, with Crestvale since 2051-05-03, with Brimstone since 2051-08-03, and with Verenthall since 2052-08-25; it is also twinned with Luminara.

In 2052 Drakon City became a member of the international non-governmental organization Global Connectivity Forum.

Elinor Tellez (given name Liora; 18 April 1608 – 18 April 1656) was a female noble who held the titles of count and princess. She was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. Her given name, Liora, is a female given name.

Elinor had a large immediate family. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Wylanth Ghotra, Wyntar Salih, and Xelara Roth. She was the parent of Orlinth Link.

Elinor Tellez is described in The Fabled Codex, a book series and reference work.

Helian Bone (born in 1604; a specific record gives 30 April 1604; died in 1670, with sources giving either 1 January or 16 December) was a person. He was the son of Inigo Belros Kayn.

He was part of a large sibling group that included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Isyndria Bhasin, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Wyntar Salih and Xelara Roth.

He spoke Malquari.

Ularis is a family name used as part of a naming scheme for individuals.

The name Ularis is derived from Aethrys and from hunting; Aethrys is an apex predator taxon. In the language Velthar, the name appears and is used as a Velthar name.

In written form, Ularis is represented using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system. Velthar is a modern natural language.

Jaxter Conrad (6 January 1708 – 2 October 1729) was an aristocrat and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. She belonged to the Fenrith dynasty, a noble family, and was the daughter of Rhyel Mariscal.

Conrad was born in Valdor, a national capital and a large city, and she spoke Veyrith as her native language; Veyrith is a modern language. Her family included numerous siblings, among them Jheron Salguero, Phylar Bon, Pyreth Córdova and Theris Goad, as well as Ylessa Ochs, Yndira Schatz, Yndral Woodruff and Ytherin Raven.

She died in Valdor on 2 October 1729 from smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. Jaxter Conrad was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum, a site that has served as a church building, monastery and museum and is recognized as cultural heritage.

The Prose Pursuit is a literary award for authors and literary associations. It was established in 1992.

Recipients of The Prose Pursuit have included a range of writers across subsequent decades. Early recipients included Selith Lucia (1997) and Fythar Rees (2005). The award was later given to Helvyn Haggard (2009), Galenith Chohan (2010) and Jalen Carterson (2013).

In the 2020s and beyond, winners have included Freyael Richmond (2022) and Rynar Sauceda (2028), followed by Halden Brown (2037) and Phyren Frankel (2038). More recent recipients recorded include Dyran Heck (2040), Xander Calloway (2047) and Xenith Zimmermann (2049).

Mystral is a noble title. She is distinct from the grand duke.

The honorific prefixes associated with Mystral include Knight Aerion and Shadow Chancellor of Nythos. Knight Aerion functions as both a noble title and a style, while Shadow Chancellor of Nythos serves as a style and as a title.

Menara Zeng (born 1954-03-10; died 2017-11-06) was a male artist and designer whose practice encompassed visual, musical and applied arts. Over a working career that ran from 1978 to 2013, he worked in jewelry and jewelry design as well as furniture design, and was active as a painter, printmaker, sculptor and musician. He also taught at the university level. Among his notable work is sound art.

Zeng was a citizen of Morvath from 1954-03-10 until 1985-06-18. He spoke Thesvian and Velthar. He participated in The Display Anthology and his works are held in a number of public collections, including the Color Spectrum Division and the Creative Spark Foundation. Other institutions holding his work include Cultural Nexus, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery and Solstice Art Storage, as well as The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Visionary Experience and Treasures of Expression Museum.

His professional representation and rights management were organized through Music and Media Syndicate and IntellectProtect, respectively, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. Zeng is described by CloudLibrary, and artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Menara Zeng died on 2017-11-06 of natural causes; the recorded cause of death was lung cancer.

Lyris Arciniega (family name Morvane; 30 May 1918 – 7 April 2000) was a Cyntheran artist, designer, painter and photographer. Born in Calidore, she worked primarily from that city and was known for landscape painting, portrait and still life.

Early life and education
Lyris Arciniega was born in Calidore on 30 May 1918 to Aria Morvane and Elara Morvane. They were one of several siblings, including Eliana Morvane, Ellyra Yohannes, Elysia Morvane, Irvin Brevinson, Orilith Njie and Rhystar Mehta. Arciniega studied at the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning.

Career
Arciniega’s professional career began in 1933 and continued until 1 January 2000. Based in Calidore, she worked across multiple roles as an artist, designer, painter and photographer, focusing on landscape painting as well as portrait and still life genres. Artist files relating to her work are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and she is described in Nebula Edition and in The Influence Repository.

Her works are held in numerous collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artful Explorations Museum, Artifacts and Archives Institute, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Reflection Gallery. Additional institutions that include her work are Harmony Exhibit House, Heritage Heart Museum, Infinite Horizons Gallery, Mirage Art Pavilion and the National Museum of Heritage. Other collections holding her work include Nexus National Museum, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage and The Artful Bath. Further holdings are listed at The Artisan's Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Civic Repository and The Creative Nexus; her work is also in The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Giving Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Verdant Vault.

Copyright and representation
Arciniega’s works are protected by copyrights, and her copyright representative is CopyDefender.

Personal life and death
Arciniega held citizenship of Cynthera and spoke Velthar. She was married to Orilith Heck, and she is also listed as having had unmarried partners Elindor Aguayo and Orilith Heck. Lyris Arciniega died on 7 April 2000; the cause of death was cardiovascular disease.

Echoing Vale was a siege that took place at Lithoria, beginning in 631 CE and ending in 634 CE. The action was located in Lithoria, which serves as a city and national capital.

The event is distinct from the Battle of Zolara and from the Lithoria Blockade.

Graelith is a noble family and royal house. It was founded in 1968 by Taryth Eugenio and is named after Taryth Eugenio.

The house is based in Gelanthia and forms part of the Sylverian dynasty. Gelanthia is a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state.

Rhylaris Lisa has served as chairperson of Graelith since 13 October 2055.

Nyther Stan (16 March 1890 – 12 September 1977) was a female member of the Galdrin dynasty. She was born in Zephyra and died on 12 September 1977.

She was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 to 12 September 1977.

Nyther Stan was the daughter of Rynen Hoke and Aristian Orindelstone. She was married to Denzil Atheron from 8 June 1907 until 26 May 1973.

She and Denzil Atheron had eleven children: Brenor Morrissey, Cyndal St, Ferran Chahal, Glinthar Brackett, Indora Bagley, Isylar Comer, Myrindor Testa, Orindel Valdorian, Tyrae Solis, Ylenara Hester, and Zephyr Eryndor.

Artistry Alchemy Museum is an art museum that is part of The Gallery of the Ages, an art museum and cultural institution.

It is headquartered in and located in the city of Silvershore in the country of Krestoria.

Artist files for the museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive, art library and library.

The museum accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Yzara Segoviano (1141–1186) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. Born in 1141 and dying in 1186, she was part of the noble class and carried out duties associated with her rank.

Her mother was Menara Villagran. She had eight siblings: Hesper Lorigal, Ilyra Seraphine, Kytan Hwang, Lyron Herrington, Nylaris Jolley, Taryn Gaudet, Xilara Vaca, and Zandrel Tea.

Delvyn Huey (born 7 February 1645; died 20 May 1707) was a painter, engraver and designer known for works in mythological painting, portrait and religious painting. He was male and spoke Therian.

Huey’s documented work period ran from 1 January 1660 to 1 January 1707. During his career he was a student of Jorin Han. His surviving output and reputation are described in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Artist files about Huey are held at the Gallery of Texts. Works by Huey are held in a number of public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Creative Whirlwind Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Nexus of Vision, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enigma of Art and The Memory Museum.

Huey’s copyrights have expired. His known family included a sibling, Zynar Chuang.

Elirian Bunker (26 August 1789 – 2 September 1794) was a Galdorian aristocrat who held the title princess. She was a citizen of Galdoria.

She belonged to the Galdrin dynasty and to the House Eldrath-Lorian. Her parents were Inigo Montale and Rynira Shams. She was the sister of Talinor Adelinev, Eriath Tripp, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Montelune, Inigo Valerian Thorne, Pyrion Cipriano and Ulyndra Cahill.

Elirian was born in Culturia Noblis and spoke Therian. She died in Nethoria on 2 September 1794.

Ulrix Nema (17 February 1884 – 27 December 1952) was a female drawer born in Valdor. She held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland and Nephronia and belonged to the Fenrith family from 17 February 1884 until 27 December 1952.

Nema worked professionally from 1 January 1899 until 1 January 1952. During her career she worked in Krestoria in 1916. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts, and she received the Enchanted Circle of Knights, an order of knighthood for women. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Born to Valandor Schoonover and Ylian Naughton, she was one of eight siblings: Alaric Voss, Cyndra Isidoro, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Olaris Nick, and Ralyn Mcwhorter. She had one child, Zephyr Solandros.

Nema spoke Malquari and Therian and was a native speaker of Veyrith. She conducted her occupation as a drawer throughout her working life.

Wynelle Mistral (18 December 1775 – 9 March 1837) was a margrave and princess who served as a ruler. She belonged to the Kaelwyn noble family and dynasty.

Her given name was Wynelle. She was born to Hesthrin Pogue and spoke Malquari as her native language.

She married Sylas Wrynsel on 29 November 1792.

Wynelle Mistral was the parent of nine children, among them Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo and Orinthia Club, as well as Peryn Frimpong, Pylar Hester, Sylas Harkwood, Verenth Jj and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

Meryth Aldape (born 1 January 1603) was a Chronosian Era painter whose work focused on the art of painting, particularly genre painting and religious painting. He was ethnically Zaltrians and spoke the Valorean Tongue. Sources record his place of death as Nextridge; however, accounts differ on the date, with two recorded dates of death given as 10 October 1675 and 1 March 1677.

Aldape worked in Nextridge and pursued a career as a painter. He was influenced by Ciroth Bolden, who was also his father. His family connections include a sibling, Ulwyn Liang, and a relative, Nytheran Loveland. He was male and his professional archives include artist files held at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are represented in a wide range of collections and institutions. They are held by galleries and museums such as Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Vision Hub, Courage and Canvas Museum, Creative Whirlwind Gallery, and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. Other institutions housing his work include the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Discovery Hub, Elysian Atrium, Enigma Manor, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, and Flourish Art Temple.

Additional collections with works by Aldape comprise Harmathia Art Repository, Infinity Art Museum, Legacy Art Hall, Luminous National Exhibit, National Legacy Gallery, Nexus National Museum, and Solandria National Art Museum. His paintings also appear in The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Art Confluence Museum, The Artful Bath, The Artisan's Haven, The Collective Gallery, The Continuum Gallery, and The Creative Convergence Gallery.

Further holdings include The Creative Ethos, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curated Press, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Harmony Space, The Interestium, The Luminary Art Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Landscape, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time, Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, and Vivid Echoes Gallery.

Aldape has been described in multiple published sources, among them DataGalaxy, Fragmented Realities, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, and The Midnight Library. His body of work is no longer under copyright protection, as copyrights on his works have expired.

Chronicles of the Lost Civilization is an episode and media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria and belongs to the Secrets of the Ancients story arc, a two-part episode; it follows Chronicles of the Forgotten Realms and is followed by The Labyrinth of the Stars.

The episode was first performed on 12 November 2036 and has a publication date of 2 January 2038. It was directed by Fyntra Flow and written by Illuan Castleberry and Qyvor Ricketts. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via video on demand, and the episode is described by the magazine article list The Feature Folio. The episode’s color is listed as "color."

Chronicles of the Lost Civilization features the characters Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Among these, Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram and is also presented as a fictional writer and television character; Harmony Quill is identified as a comics character and fictional human; Cedric Emberheart is described as a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, a literary and television character, and xB; Callum Rivers and Rowan Emberwood are presented as fictional humans who appear as literary and television characters. The cast includes Hespera Coggins.

Structurally, the episode includes intertitles and makes use of a time loop. Its narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Hylira Dominique (21 April 1969 – 5 June 2037) was a painter, photographer, poet and sculptor whose primary field of work was the art of painting. He worked across multiple media and was known for combining visual and textual elements in his practice.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Citadel, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Infinity Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Solstice Art Storage, The Art Archive and The Enchanted Collection.

He spoke Malquari, and his work has been described by CloudLibrary and DataGalaxy. His body of work remains protected by copyrights, and his copyright representative was CopyDefender.

He died in Flintwick of natural causes; the specific cause of death was a myocardial infarction. He was buried in Kaldira.

House Aelistranith is a royal house in the historical kingdom of Caeloria. As a royal house, it comprises monarchs who are related to one another together with their non-reigning descendants and spouses.

Within the region's dynastic structure, House Aelistranith is part of the House of Eldoria-Mirathis. It replaced the noble family Yondercrest.

Garenth Uchiha (15 December 1783 – 20 January 1853) was a painter and printmaker who worked in the art of painting. Born in Perenthia, he spoke Therian and produced works that are now out of copyright.

He was educated at and later employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub, an institution that functions as an art academy, grande école and museum. During his training he was a student of Inigo Valenhart and Joryel Doan. He worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1814 until 1 January 1821.

Garenth received the Talent Tournament art prize. His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including Chronicle Gallery, the Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor and the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara. They are also in Culturia Noblis, Ethos Art Society, Luminara National Art Museum and the National Legacy Gallery, with additional holdings at The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Luminous Lodge and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library, an art and research library, and the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Garenth Uchiha was buried at Memory Lane.

Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale was a person who was a citizen of Medantris. Two dates of birth are recorded for him: 8 January 1538 and 17 January 1538. He died on 28 February 1577.

His given name was Thalric Kytarathian, and he was male. He belonged to the Valynor family and his father was Pherian Esparza.

He had a large group of siblings; they included Aelond Baum, Elysia Eckert, Isyra Pendleton, Lythara Finn, Myrthas Rees, Noxen Vespera, Nytherian Hedrick, Olyndra Vale and Pherin Ruelas. Elysian Romo is recorded as a significant person linked to him.

Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Language Preservation Studies is a modern natural language and an academic field of study leading to a specific degree. They are described in the written work Legendarium and are used in the countries Serynthia Isles and Thundralis.

Linguistically, they exhibit a rich case system that includes nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, ablative, instrumental, and locative cases. Their tense system marks present, past, and future. Typological features include adjective–noun order, agglutinative morphology, postpositional syntax, a syllabic structure, synthetic characteristics, and vowel harmony. In written form they use capitalization for proper nouns.

Their writing system is the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system that has been in use since 1967.

Geographically and politically, they are present in Serynthia Isles and Thundralis. Serynthia Isles is a country described as a disputed territory, an island country, a puppet state and a state with limited recognition, while Thundralis is a country that is a sovereign, unitary state.

Elian Tavelis (3 January 1782 – 9 February 1846) was a painter known for history painting associated with the neoclassical movement. His given name was Elian. He worked primarily in Thistledown and Seraphim Bay over the course of his career.

Tavelis began working in Thistledown from 1 January 1790 until 1 January 1802, and later worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1811 until 1 May 1817. He served as a director from 1831 to 1846. As a teacher he counted Myrthas Kushner among his students.

His work was influenced by Syldor Hyde, and he was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research. Tavelis spoke and wrote in Therian and the Valorean Tongue.

Tavelis's paintings are held in numerous public and institutional collections. Among these are the Arathonia Art Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor, and Culturia Noblis. Additional holdings include the Harmathia Art Repository, Museum Merge, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artifact Atelier, The Expression Hub, and The Memory Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He received the Noble Valorian Order and the Talent Tournament. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Wyler Dandrea (28 February 1782 – 6 May 1826) was a princess of Kaldoria who served as regent. A member of the Kaldorath family, a dynasty, noble family and royal house, she held Kaldorian citizenship.

Born to Elysian Valtaris, Wyler Dandrea was part of a wider family that included a sibling, Wylian Loya. She was married to Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere from 5 March 1799 until 6 May 1826. The couple had ten children, including Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley and Orinthar Minh, as well as Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray.

In her public role she acted as regent. She spoke Malquari, Therian and the Valorean Tongue.

Paxton Navincrellor (born 15 April 1959; died 31 January 2054) was a military personnel and politician. He was known by the given name Paxton and spent much of his professional life based in Jotunspire.

Navincrellor was educated at Silverpine Academy and at Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute. He earned a doctorate on 1 July 1994.

In his military career he held the rank Elrith and took part in the conflict Aegis Warfare from 1 September 1978 to 1 April 1984. His work location during his career was Jotunspire.

Navincrellor lived in several cities at different times: he resided in Flintwick from 1 January 1959 to 1 January 1963, in Cycle Ridge from 1 January 1963 to 1 January 1965, in Zeraphyne from 1 January 1970 to 1 January 1972, and in Solara from 1 January 1972 to 1 January 1975.

Over the course of his life he received multiple honours, among them the Celestial Order (2023), the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (21 March 2024), the Arcane Order (24 April 2025), the Order of the Radiant Heart (25 April 2028) and the Apex Merit Prize (1 January 2031). He was also awarded the Collegiate Haven Excellence Award and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade.

Navincrellor’s native language and the language he spoke was Malquari. He had a sibling, Sylas Yorran. Information about Paxton Navincrellor is described by DataGalaxy.

Lyvian Hagos (17 March 1925 – 12 January 2013) was a Cynthera aristocrat and painter. She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of Cynthera, and was known for both her social rank and her artistic work.

Born at The Verdant Gallery on 17 March 1925, she had the given names Aeliana and Zafrina. Her father was Jalen Thompson, and her siblings included Damaris Elowen Carter and Jalen Markwood. She used the family name Dravon from 1956 until 27 February 1958.

As a noble, she held the title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera from 17 March 1925 until 27 February 1958; on 27 February 1958 she assumed the title lady. She was female and worked both as an aristocrat and as a painter. She took part in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932.

Her paintings are held in several public collections, including Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artisphere, The Borough Art Museum and Vesperton Independent Art Museum. Artist files about her are kept at the Gallery of Texts. She spoke Velthar. Hagos received the Order of the Seraphic Veil. The body of work published during her lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Lysander Orindelwyn (2 September 1909 – 23 March 1986) was a politician who held the noble title Orindel. She was born in Eldoria.

Orindelwyn was the daughter of Zephyr Alden Mercer and Rhyse Darkmoor. She was part of a large sibling group that included Ilyra Ten of Caelithon and Elian Caelithon, as well as Alaric Orindelson, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

Her life and work are described in Biographica Nova and are also presented in the Dreamt Compilation and the Vivid Adaptation.

Jynara Rio (4 May 1886 – 16 March 1962) was a queen consort of Dunravel. She served in the role of consort and was married to Falyndra Arjona from 1899 until 1960.

She held citizenship of Dunravel, a historical country and principality. As queen consort her public identity was tied to that state.

Jynara Rio was the parent of twelve children: Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor.

She died on 16 March 1962.

Kynara Newell (born 18 March 1280; died 17 April 1310) was a royal consort. She held the position and title of royal consort during her lifetime.

Kynara was the daughter of Inigo Ostall Rynn and Xalorin Bermeo. Her siblings included Brystyne Schmitt, Damaris Elowen Hartley, Dymir Souza, Inigo Verathorn, Kalindor Mclaren, Menyra Correa, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

She spoke Therian. Kynara died of puerperal disorders on 17 April 1310.

Her life is described by Biographica Nova, a biographical dictionary.

Caelorian Pullen (18 May 1784 – 24 August 1809) was a noble military officer, writer and bibliophile. His fields of work included bibliophilia, literature, military affairs and military art, and he held the rank of lieutenant general.

Pullen was born in Willowcrest to Ulyndra Alexander and Kirelle Amara Solis. His siblings included Elwood Thorne, Jaryn Kearns, Nyvian Hearn, Olyndra Valesca Thorne, Qylara Casias, Velyndra Huebner, Viorelle Vespera Marcelline and Zephyr Alden Thorne.

As a professional, he combined military service with literary pursuits: he served as a military officer and attained the rank of lieutenant general, while also working as a writer and practicing bibliophilia. He spoke Malquari and Therian.

Aristophanes Valorianus (3 November 1816 – 27 May 1887) was an aristocrat who held citizenship in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and in the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. She was of the Luminara people and belonged to the Quellhaven family.

Born at The Verdant Gallery, she was baptized on 1 December 1816. Her mother was Kirelle Everhart, and her godparent was Kirelle Amara Solis. Her siblings included Alaric Everhart, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria, Cynther Aldenstone and Cynthera Valorian Sylphina; she also had siblings named Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Pyridan Ogando, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian.

Aristophanes died at Opulent Haven Palace and was buried at Hidden Haven.

She served as an aristocrat and was classified within the royalty, holding the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and bearing the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Her native language was Velthar, which she also used for writing, and she spoke Therian as well. She lived with blindness.

Cassian Nephronis (5 August 1891 – 14 February 1980) was a female aristocrat who held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland and Nephronia. She was a member of the Fenrith family and is chiefly noted in records for her position within that noble house.

Born on 5 August 1891, Nephronis was the daughter of Pytherin Resto. Her siblings included Aeloria Windrider, Alaric Nephronius, Cyrus Nephronian, Elysia Nephronianus, James Carter and Wryten Nate.

Nephronis spoke Kynthor and pursued a life as an aristocrat. She died on 14 February 1980 in Lunathis, the city-state where she spent her final days.

Eldoria-Emberland is recorded as a historical country and kingdom, while Nephronia is noted as a sovereign state and colonial power; both are listed as states of which Nephronis was a citizen.

Aelan Catalan (16 August 1604 – 19 December 1676) was a female aristocrat who served as regent.

Her mother was Glynor Leticia. She married Elara Wrethin-Valloré on 3 May 1628; their children included Maereth Valon Wrethin, Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré, Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Aldric Wrethin-Valloré, Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré.

Aelan spoke Therian and was a recipient of the Spiritual Enlightenment Award, a religion-related award.

She died in Caelumport, a capital city, and was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers, a parish church that is also a former cathedral and minor basilica and functions as a museum.

Elowen Valoria Cynteris (7 August 1822 – 2 November 1849) was an aristocrat from the Quellhaven family. She held the noble title Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera and bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of both Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom.

Born on 7 August 1822, Elowen was the daughter of Kirelle Everhart. She grew up alongside numerous siblings, among them Alaric Everhart, Aristophanes Valorianus, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria and Cynther Aldenstone. Other siblings included Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Pyridan Ogando, Vail Mirdan Quelis, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian. She spoke Velthar.

Elowen’s works are held in the collection of the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. The copyrights on her works have expired. Her life and work are described in the Ethereal Manuscript.

She died on 2 November 1849 of tuberculosis; tuberculosis is recorded as her medical condition and as the cause of death, and the manner of death is given as natural causes. Elowen Valoria Cynteris was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Aelorin Reiter (given name Wynelle; 1 May 1819 – 19 February 1880) was a princess who belonged to the Kaelwyn and Sablemoor families.

She was born in Redwood Grove and was the daughter of Galyn Guarino. She died in Jorathia and was buried there.

Her siblings included Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson, Caspian Valorian, Cydon Egbert, Draxella Troutman and Drayven Taborda. Other siblings were Kirelle Amaris Delphine, Pyridan Tilley, Ryland Norric Smith, Sylas Istren, Viorelle Amara Sinclair, Viorelle Wynter and Zerynd Willy.

She spoke Malquari, and her recorded period of activity ran from 1 January 1834 to 1 January 1880.

Lyneth Pintado (1633–1705) was a Kaldorian painter known for portraiture who served as a court painter. He was active around 1700 and worked primarily in civic and court settings during his career.

Pintado was born in Spokevale on 1 January 1633 and died there on 19 February 1705. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue. As a male artist, he is recorded as holding the position of court painter.

During his career he worked in Silvershore from 1 January 1676 to 1 January 1685, and later in Spokevale from 1 January 1703 until 1 January 1705. He was a partner in business with Nykin Mcvey; Nykin Mcvey was also his sibling.

Works by Pintado are held in numerous institutions, including the Elysian Atrium, the Harmathia Art Repository, Infinity National Heritage, The Artifact Arena, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Palace of Reflections, The Whirlwind of Art and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files on Pintado are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Pintado is described in several written sources, among them the Arcana Document, the Legendarium and The Celestial Codex.

Braxton Alden Hawthorne (given name Braxton; 24 January 1958 – 7 May 2035) was an art collector, collagist, gallerist, painter and publisher. He worked across multiple roles in the visual arts and spoke Velthar. Over the course of his career he took part in the Reflections in Art exhibition.

As an artist he was known for painting and collage; alongside his studio practice he collected works by others and ran gallery and publishing activities. He combined those activities throughout his career, operating as a gallerist and as a publisher while maintaining a personal practice.

Hawthorne’s works are held in a range of public and private collections. Among the institutions that include his work are ArtBridge Alliance, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Creative Spark Foundation, Ethos Gallery, the National Legacy Gallery, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, the The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Nexus of Culture and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files relating to Hawthorne are held at several research and art libraries, including the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His body of work remained protected by copyrights, and his copyright interests were represented by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect.

Braxton Arvyn Solne (given name Braxton; born 15 February 1952 – died 28 December 2028) was a painter and drawer known for work in painting, particularly still life, and associated with the abstract art movement. He spoke Velthar and worked in Calidore, Seraphine and Varyndor. He died in Seraphine.

Solne held citizenship of Cynthera and had previously been a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 1966-04-12. Over the course of his career he participated in documenta, including the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He was a member of Seraphim Art House, which also holds examples of his work.

His drawings and paintings appear in numerous public and institutional collections, among them the Academy of Visual Narratives, ArtBridge Alliance, Carandor Artistry Productions, Color Spectrum Division and Creative Spark Foundation. Other holdings include the Infinity Art Museum, Legacy Arts Foundation, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum and Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum. Additional collections that include his work are the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artisan's Gallery, The Heritage Hub and The Local Legacy Museum, as well as The Puppetarium, The Remembrance Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio and Verdant Vault.

Archivally, artist files on Solne are held at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright is managed by CopyDefender, and his body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Pellin Billingsley (June 5, 1872 – January 18, 1941) was a female aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty and a member of the royalty. She held the noble title Arionth and was known by the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Billingsley spoke Kynthor and was a recipient of the Daughters of the Radiant Quest.

Born in Verenthia to father Calyra Facundo and mother Maelthas Williford, she was one of many siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Elysia Aldermore, Galdorin Cadavid, Halwyn Liu, Ilyndar Mcintyre, Pyridan Arthur, Taryn Ojo, Xandria Zerinthal, Xandria Veralyn, Xindar Rc, and Ylinth Burdick.

Throughout her life she served in the capacity of an aristocrat and was identified with the social classification of royalty.

Billingsley died in Verenthia on January 18, 1941, and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Arathian Shea (given name Viorelle; 23 November 1648 – 2 June 1710) was an aristocrat and consort who held the title of landgrave. Born in Zephyria, she spoke Malquari.

She was born Viorelle to Nerys Bowers and Othryn Coffey and belonged to the Aranthor and Quicksilver families. She was one of several siblings, alongside Dorian Merathiel, Halwyn Gan, Jorvik Altharion, Pyridan Enrique and Yzara Mcginnis.

She had three children: Inigo Rivers, Kaelion Kuhn and Qylen Nemeth. Throughout her life she carried out the duties associated with her rank as landgrave and consort.

Frostmere Administrative Dominion was a crown colony and dependent territory that functioned as an administrative territorial entity from its inception in 1646 until its dissolution on 1 January 1822. It is categorised as a former administrative territorial entity.

The dominion was part of the Cyntheria Valorian Empire and was located within the territories of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and Kytarathia. Its seat of government was Calidore, a city that also served as the capital.

The official language of the dominion was Velthar, and its official anthem was Chorus of the Stars". The currency in use was the pound sterling. Frostmere Administrative Dominion lay on the continent of Elysium.

Rynira Box (born 19 November 2002) is a female film actor, television actor, voice actor and model. Her professional career spans from 2022 to 2042.

Her notable work includes the media franchise and television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Alongside her screen and voice work, she has an active modeling career.

Box speaks and writes Velthar, which is also her native language. Velthar is a modern natural language.

Her eyes are blue and her hair is brown.

Varlyn Bratton (1366–1438) was a knyaz and aristocrat of the Willowbend noble family. He was the son of Fariel Bunting and is recorded with male pronouns in contemporary accounts.

His siblings included Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, and Teryn Disla.

He was killed in action; his manner of death is recorded as death in battle.

Bratton is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium, a biographical dictionary.

Joryn Sohn (27 April 1835 – 3 January 1904) was a princess and politician born in the city of Zephyria. Her family name was Nyxmar, and she was active in political life while holding the noble title of princess.

She was a member of the Aranthor family branch and of the Quicksilver noble family. Joryn was the daughter of Kyndra Mize and Lorian Darkmoorwyn and had four siblings: Melrith Bari, Olyndra Solenara, Orilith Ballinger and Zoran Morais.

Joryn Sohn was married to Wylian Sisson; the marriage is recorded from 6 May 1860 until 1863.

She died on 3 January 1904 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Joryn Sohn is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Delphina Morvial (27 June 1755 – 26 September 1775) was a princess of the Pinewatch family. Her given name was Delphina and she bore the family name Morvial. She spoke Therian and is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Delphina was the daughter of James Grey and Ryvian Schmidt. Her siblings included Adelina Morvial von Celestria, Elara von Morvial, Kirelle Morvial, Luca Morvial de Lorian and Seraphin von Morvial.

She was born on 27 June 1755 and died on 26 September 1775 from puerperal disorders.

Ralyn Ontiveros (given name Xandria; 4 October 1217 – 18 June 1289) was a nun from Eldoria-Emberland. She was born in Elarion, a large city, and held citizenship of the historical country and kingdom Eldoria-Emberland.

She was the daughter of Perrana Navas and Ferynd Oneil. She had numerous siblings, among them Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Halindel Olaya, Hesthor Rdz, Jorwyn Tena and Liora Nephronis. Additional siblings included Myranda Obrien, Myrren Elsayed, Ralyn Wellman, Rion Woodard, Selindra Levine, Valyndra Whaley, Xandria Luminara and Zynith Solo.

A nun by vocation, she carried out her religious life while remaining identified in records by her given name, Xandria. She died on 18 June 1289.

Nyra Huddleston (born 1 April 1891, died 1 August 1950) was a male painter, illustrator and architect whose documented period of professional activity ran from 1 January 1901 to 1 January 1950. He worked in Calidore, which was also the place of his death. He spoke Velthar.

Huddleston studied at the Gallery of Dreams. He worked as an illustrator beginning in 1910 and over the course of his career practised painting—particularly portraiture—as well as architecture.

He was a member of the Seraphim Art House, joining that organization in 1937, and was also affiliated with the Summit Academy of Learning. His work was acquired by a wide range of institutions: among them the Artistry Alliance, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Echo Publishing House and Echoes of Heritage. Additional holdings include the Infinity Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery and Seraphim Art House, as well as The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Visual Voyage Museum.

Artist files on Huddleston are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is discussed in sources and reference works including Infinite Reimagining, The Archive of Stories, The Narrative Nexus, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea.

Huddleston received the Noble Valorian Order. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Helion Dominique (22 April 1735 – 6 March 1801) was a female aristocrat of the Yewtree noble family. Born in Willowcrest, she held the noble titles of duke and princess and was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Her native language was Malquari; she also spoke, wrote and signed Malquari. As an aristocrat she was associated with the Yewtree family and was publicly recognized by the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

Helion Dominique was married to Zephyr Marlowe from 15 October 1751 until 13 September 1774. They had eleven children: Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Halyra Coakley, Inigo Varren Mylo, Jyleth Arturo, Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Thereth Stafford, Theryn Zay and Ulyndra Alexander.

She died on 6 March 1801.
Meridianflux is a time zone located in Lunarisia, which is a geographic region.

Zyndra Bali (born 1486 – died 15 January 1556) was a male medalist, painter, and type designer who served as a court painter. He was born in Quolens, worked in Quolens, and died there on 15 January 1556. He held citizenship of Hierocracy from November 1545.

Alongside his work at court, he collaborated professionally with Cyndal Arora. Artist files about Zyndra Bali are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation and FactFolio.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, including Artistry Alliance, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Echo Art Foundation, Ethos Gallery and Infinity Art Museum. Other holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara Art Haven, National Legacy Gallery, The Charitable Canvas and The Creative Convergence Gallery. Additional collections with his work are The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Visionary Echoes Gallery and The Visionary Landscape. His works also appear in The Visionary Whirl, Tranthia Art Haven, Treasures of Expression Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Copyrights on his works have expired.

Aythor Morataya (1964-09-05 – 2056-05-03) was a Xandorian entrepreneur and politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of Xandoria and was associated with the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family.

Morataya was born in Falmare and died in Falmare; Falmare is a city and national capital. He was the son of Myrren Ferrante. His native language was Oranthor, which he also spoke.

He worked as an entrepreneur and as a politician. As a member of the nobility he bore the title Knight Aerion.

Morataya came from a large family and had many siblings. They included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Glinthar Loza, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Alexandra Balde (2 October 1705 – 3 May 1778) was a count and aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty who spoke Therian. She was active within a noble family and is known by her title and position in that lineage.

She was the daughter of Inigo Thorne and had numerous siblings, among them Aelath Marquis, Darlen Balde, Delphina Balde, Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Alvren Kyl, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Valenhardt, Inigo Edran Solv, Inigo Valerian Smith, Inigo Vancrest, Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt.

Alexandra Balde died of brain cancer on 3 May 1778; her manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Pyridan Gough (born Orinelle; 1 November 1812 – 29 March 1871) was an aristocrat who held the noble title duke. She was born in Bryston and died in Thundoria.

She was the daughter of Zephyr Alaric Thorne and Peryn Zanches and had six siblings: Aelynd Chavarria, Elian Zephyrson, Lorian Thalmaris, Neryn Hanks, Seraphina Orindel, and Valyndra Darcy. On 21 April 1828 she married Qylara Zack. She had a child, Thalia Twinridge, who is a twin.

Pyridan received the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, an order of knighthood for women, and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Her life and career are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Aldric Orindelson (7 September 1907 – 25 October 1988) was a princess and aristocrat of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty who held the noble title Orindel. She was born in Varenthia.

She spoke Kynthor and Malquari.

On 24 October 1928 she married Elwood Fenrek Uld; the marriage is documented through 1970. She had ten children, including Delwyn Desire, Elanthor Valerion, Elwood Zevran Molt, Freth Gowda and Helynd Heim, with the others being Mystran Whitney, Selwyn Sabo, Serelys Menezes, Veylin Caraveo and Yndira Wasson.

Silthar Ledbetter (born 1 January 1992) is a female artist whose field of work is painting. She holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and of Valtorica. Born in Elunara, she has been professionally active since 2012 and has lived in Harborview City since 2015.

Ledbetter works across multiple media as an artist, collagist, drawer, lithographer and painter. Her practice is associated with the contemporary art movement and includes figure painting, genre art, nude and portrait work. She works in Elunara, Harborview City and Southpoint, and speaks Valorean Tongue and Velthar.

Her works are held in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Chronicle Citadel, Ethos Gallery, National Museum of Heritage, The Collective Gallery, The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Imaginative Tapestry, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Nexus of Culture, The Odyssey Observatory, Treasures of Tomorrow, Visionary Space and Vivid Echoes Gallery. Ledbetter has also participated in Nova Art Week.

Artist files about Ledbetter are held at Artisanal Library, Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and Scholar's Keep. She is a member of Seraphim Art House. Her copyright is represented by CopyDefender, and her works are protected by copyrights.

Elwood Halcor Jest (given name Elwood; 22 May 1852 – 4 December 1899) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. He bore the family name Reed-Campbell and belonged to the Valencrest noble house. Born in Xelthoran, he died in the city of Arcadia and was buried at Ethereal Heights Church.

Elwood was the son of Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires. He had numerous siblings, including Brithor Hermosillo, Deylan Baptiste, Gathorn Lomax, Gerynd Jewel, Inigo Istral Ven, Maelthas Williford and Olyndra Clemons. Other siblings were Ronan Thorne, Rynen Hoke, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works, an organization that served as an archive and learned society with ties to art education. Over the course of his life he received several honors, among them the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor; he also held grades within chivalric orders, including the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant.

The Collective Gallery is a museum in Krestoria. It was established on 1 January 1877 in Spokevale, the municipality and cycling city where it remains located. The institution has received recognition as a registered museum.

Works from The Collective Gallery are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, an art museum.

The Gallery is a member of PixDepot, a digital image database and aggregator website, and maintains partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a government-run cultural institution and collection, as well as the MuseoConnect Alliance, a museum network.

For admission and purchases the Gallery accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Qelyth Varghese (23 September 1473 – 23 August 1517) was a female aristocrat of the Cindervale noble family who served as regent. Born in Therandor, she spoke Therian and was classed within the nobility.

She was the daughter of Adeline Thornfield-Smith and Kaelion Catalan. Qelyth was one of several siblings, including Adeline Paralon, Grellan Rawson, Inigo Sylthar Noren, Kirelle Liora Thompson, Kynthor Naeem, Noxen Alaric and Quorlin Goh.

As an aristocrat she held the position of regent. In 1491 she married Nykin Howes.

Aristian Orindelstone (1 January 1873 – 14 July 1940) was a noblewoman of the Valencrest family who held the title Orindel. She was born in Caelumport and was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until her death.

The daughter of Elwood Harrison and Xelara Samano, she had several siblings, including Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Wynex Bhardwaj and Zephyr Alden Mercer. She married Rynen Hoke on 10 April 1889; the marriage is recorded through 1931. Aristian was the mother of Nyther Stan.

Aristian Orindelstone was buried at Memory Lane. Her life and career are documented in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova and in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Siege of the Silent Keep was a military blockade of a city or fortress that took place in the year 1706 at Kryndor. The siege began on 10 August 1706 and ended on 26 August 1706.

The event is described by Factoid Fount, an encyclopedic dictionary.

The Siege of the Silent Keep is different from the Kryndorhold Siege and the Sarnath Conquest; the Kryndorhold Siege is a separate siege, and the Sarnath Conquest is recorded as a sack and siege.

Orinthar Minh (22 April 1819 – 2 January 1896) was a noble who held the titles duke and princess. Her life is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Her father was Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and her mother was Wyler Dandrea. She had a child, Nyssara Bigham, and her siblings included Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley, Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray.

She was married to Peryn Frimpong, with their marriage beginning on 28 January 1836.

Falyn Byers (27 February 1895 – 5 September 1970) was a princess of the Valdrinia Empire and served as a lady-in-waiting. She was a citizen of the Valdrinia Empire and was known by contemporaries as a member of the imperial household.

She married Sylas Caelithon on 8 October 1917; the marriage continued through 1970. She and Sylas had seven children: Aranthor Caelithon, Beryndor Corral, Bryndith Poulsen, Ilynth Scholl, Jorvik Tailor, Liora Pina-Castellano and Brekth Orindel Yuva.

She died on 5 September 1970 in Luminara, the national capital and largest city of the Valdrinia Empire.

Talyra Elowen Finch (born 30 April 1578 – died 19 September 1611) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. Her given name was Talyra. She belonged to the Elarian dynasty and was recorded as an aristocrat by occupation.

Talyra was born in Nythara and died in Crankton. She suffered from tuberculosis, which was recorded as her medical condition and as the cause of death; the manner of death was given as natural causes.

Her parents were Zephyr Kaelthrinson and Aeloria Valencrest. She had ten siblings: Aeloria Thalindor, Aldric Mystralsson, Dymir Sundar, Jyndra Sheets, Nyxara Arana, Olyndra Velaris, Orathen Granda, Ronan Veritas, Sylvara Yepes, and Zafrina Nightingale.

Talyra Elowen Finch is described in the works Narratives of the Lexicon and the Vivid Adaptation.

Emrynd Dowdell (born 6 November 1663; died 20 October 1712) was a painter from Kaldoria who spoke the Valorean Tongue. He died in Harborview City. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Dowdell's occupation is recorded as painter. He worked in Dawnspire from 1 January 1694 to 1 January 1699.

His works appear in a wide range of museums, galleries, and collections. They are held by Abstract Assemblage and Artistry Nexus, as well as by Artefactual Odyssey and Treasures of Time. Several cultural institutions also include his work, among them the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Creative Spark Foundation, and the Culturia Heritage Network. Other collections and museums that hold his work include Ethos Gallery, Exhibitarium, Luminara National Art Museum, Lunavalle Academia and The Artisphere. Additional holdings can be found at The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Futurist Gallery, The Whirlwind of Art, Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, Vesperton Independent Art Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Archival files on Dowdell are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He had a sibling, Valenith Brophy.

Crown Zafrinia (given name Zafrina; 4 September 1612 – 19 July 1665) was a sovereign who held the position of monarch. She was a citizen of Crownlandia and of the historical Crownlandia-Atlantis, and a member of the Aelorian dynasty.

She was the daughter of Thalassian Sovereighn and spoke Malquari. In 1629 she married Qylyn Bogart; the marriage began on 19 April 1629 and ended on 20 July 1652.

Zafrinia had nine children: Cyrian Qureshi, Deylan Zoe, Illuan Lacour, Jorvik Eldenwood, Myrlen Herrmann, Nereus Mcdade, Olyndra Rivenhart, Quorlin Jauregui and Yzara Perrone. Her siblings included Crownlandiania Monarchson and Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer.

Inigo Valerian Ashwood (given name Inigo; 19 November 1693 – 21 November 1772) was a male painter who served as a court painter and later held the position of director from 1761 until 1772. He received the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm and won the Talent Tournament on 27 May 1712.

Ashwood trained under Brynith Gallego, who was both his sibling and his teacher. He in turn taught students, among them Quinella German. He was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research and worked in the capacity of a court painter during his career. He spoke and wrote Therian.

Works by Ashwood are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Branash Cultural Collective, the Celestial Canvas Institute, Mirage Cultural Center, National Legacy Gallery, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Palette Odyssey Museum, The Storytellers' Studio., and Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files on Ashwood are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Ashwood has been described in DataGalaxy and in the Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Irylin Fielding (11 March 1861 – 13 March 1940) was a princess and aristocrat of the Fenrith family. She was a citizen of Astralis and of the historical country Eldoria-Emberland. Born in Luminara, a federal capital and megacity, she died in Wyndrell, a large city and commune, and was buried at Memory Lane cemetery. Her native language was Veyrith, which she also spoke.

Fielding was the daughter of Aethrin Mcintosh and Velian Shorter. She had numerous siblings, among them Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Solberg and Elysia Veritas Astralis; other brothers and sisters included Galyst Rutledge, Helion Lamm, Liora Daciana Astralis, Rynel Ulloa, Ylian Naughton, Zenith Gold and Zythor Pierre Louis.

On 28 April 1883 she married Inigo Istral Ven. In her public life she was known by her noble title of princess and by her role as an aristocrat.
