Artist files on Vyas are available at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in DataGalaxy, ItemVerse and the Labyrinthine Journal. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Kaldor Huggins (1 August 1534 – 6 December 1601) was a Chronosian Era architect, drawer, graphic artist and painter best known for portrait work. He held citizenship of the Chronosian Era and worked across multiple visual disciplines, producing portraits that entered numerous public and private collections.

Huggins trained under Iridan Blake and Zephyros Geffrard, and he in turn taught Wyslind Valente. He died in Spokevale.

Examples of Huggins's work are held in a wide range of institutions. His paintings and drawings are in the collections of Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, the Creative Spark Foundation, Curiosities Art Museum and the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum. Other institutions holding his work include Fusion Arts Museum, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and Museum Merge. Additional holders are the Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts, The Art Nexus, The Artisan's Haven, The Continuum Gallery and The Creative Convergence Gallery, as well as The Curatorial Vault and The Mosaic Museum. His work also appears in The Museum Collective, The Whirlwind of Art, The Whirlwind of Colors, Tranthia Art Haven, Treasures of Time, Vesperton Independent Art Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Archival material and reference files on Huggins are available at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is discussed in Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Falyndra Arjona (7 October 1880 – 1 March 1960) was a king and aristocrat who also worked as a poet and writer. He held the position and noble title of king and was educated at Crestwood Academy. Throughout his life he was associated with learned and publishing institutions, including membership of Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Arjona received a number of honors, among them the Crystaline Honor and the Golden Aurora Class (a grade of an order). He was also a recipient of recognition from the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Society of the Resolute Spirit.

He was married to Jynara Rio from 1899 until 1960. The couple had twelve children: Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor.

Arjona’s life and work are described in several sources, including Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionaries FactFolio, Factoid Fount and Knowlexicon, and the Legendarium. He died on 1 March 1960 of a cerebral hemorrhage; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Delwyn Chamorro (1 January 1681 – 16 August 1747) was a painter who worked in the genre of history painting. He spoke Therian and is described in the book series Shadows in the Ink.

Chamorro worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1698 to 1 January 1702. As a painter, his works entered numerous public and private collections; they are held by institutions including the Chronicle Gallery (an art museum and publishing company), the Creative Spark Foundation (an art museum, educational institution and nonprofit organization), Culturia Noblis (an art museum and royal palace), and the Curiosities Art Museum. Other collections holding his work include the Dreamscape Museum, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Harvenian National Art Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, the Solaris Cultural Collective, The Expression Hub, The Memory Museum, The Storytellers' Studio., the Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, and the Vivid Visions Gallery.

The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on Chamorro; that institution functions as an art library and museum library. Records indicate that copyrights on works have expired.

He was a sibling of Cole-Ren Aerbryn.

Ferynd Oneil (born 1199, died 1 September 1237) was a female noble of the historical kingdom Eldoria-Emberland. She died in the city of Elarion.

Ferynd held the noble title Arcthor, acquiring that title on 6 December 1224 and retaining it until 1 September 1237. She also served in the position of Arcthor from 1224 to 1237.

In her personal life, Ferynd was married to Perrana Navas from 1213 until 1 September 1237. Together they had ten children: Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Hesthor Rdz, Liora Nephronis, Myranda Obrien, Myrren Elsayed, Ralyn Ontiveros, Rion Woodard, Selindra Levine, and Valyndra Whaley.

Calix Stonebrook (born 16 October 1469; died 1469) was a Varyndorian aristocrat of the Nymarath dynasty and royal house. He held citizenship of Varyndoria and was classified as royalty. His given name was Calix.

He belonged to the Nymarath family and his mother was Elinor Montes. As an aristocrat, his social position was recorded within the royal class.

He was one of several children; his siblings included Alaric Varyndorion, Alyndor Varyndorian and Caelan Varyndor, as well as Celestria Luminara, Damaris Caldwell, Elara Varyndorion, Elysia Ellington and Zorrik Inzunza. His death in 1469 is recorded as an infant death.

Elanthar Carranza (10 September 1586 – 7 February 1635) was a count and aristocrat. Born in Jorathia, he was educated at Evergreen Heights University and is the subject of the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Carranza was the son of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta. He had a large number of siblings, among them Aralyn Nielson, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Orilith Dent, Talyra McKinley, Valerion Harbin and Zyndel Gala.

He was married to Eryndor Jeronimo from 25 May 1628 until 7 February 1635.

Carranza received his education at Evergreen Heights University, a public comprehensive university. As an aristocrat he held the noble title of count.

His life and career are documented in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary.

Merith Howell (1 January 1891 – 1 January 1932) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Paxton Elderwood and Faryn Rudd. Her siblings included Berenth Lei, Calyth Swope, Celestria Moonridge, Damaris Everly Sage, Kenthis Kirsch, Kynar Guillory, Noxen Bellamy, and Ylinth Machin.

The Timeless Voyage: Beyond the Veil is a media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series. A science fiction entry directed by Draxella Knott, it follows the episode The Arcane Odyssey and is officially recorded with the listed color "color". The episode was first performed on 2032-10-30 and has a publication date of 2033-07-01.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe that serves as the story’s primary setting and narrative location.

The production’s credited performers are Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio, who are listed as persons. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn (a fictional human and television character), Freya Wilder (a fictional human who appears across film, television, literary and video game formats within the franchise), Lyra Dray (an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and television character), and Mira Silverstream (a fictional human and television character).

The Timeless Voyage: Beyond the Veil was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync, which operates as a mobile app, a video-on-demand and video streaming service and a web broadcaster. Coverage and description of the episode appear in the edition Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Glynara Dhaliwal (born 10 April 1990) is a cinematographer, director, film director, film editor, film producer and screenwriter who holds citizenship of Rithoria.

He works in Rithoria and speaks Velthar. Throughout his career he has combined technical and creative roles across film production, editing and writing.

Wyslind Tully (born 1597; died 2 November 1657) was a male noble who held the title of duke and belonged to the Elarian dynasty.

He was the son of Aeloria Thalindor and Pembryn Harder and had seven siblings: Caelithon I, Elric Thornewood, Elysian Thorne, Feryndal Kohl, Ilyndar Banuelos, Olyndra Valemont, and Rhalin Jacquez.

Wyslind Tully died in Lunathis on 2 November 1657 and was buried at Nythara.

He is discussed in several reference works, including the book series Narratives of the Lexicon, the encyclopedia RefereX, and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Zenith Heights is a city in Novemara that serves as the national capital and the country's largest city. It is classified as a big city, a capital district or territory, a direct-controlled municipality and a first-level administrative division, and functions as a municipality within the sovereign republic of Novemara.

The settlement traces its official inception to 6 August 1577. As the seat of government for Novemara, Zenith Heights uses Kynthor as its official language. Since 2051 the city has been a member of the SyncSphere network.

Zenith Heights has been the subject of multiple works: it is described in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum, and it appears as a location in the video game Nebula Quest.

The city maintains twinning and partnership arrangements with a number of other administrative bodies, including Caldemere; Aetheral Grove; Aldragon; Calidore; Harborview City; Luminara; Orinthos; Primaris; Thundoria; Utopis; Harlune; Verenthia; and Calidore. Several of these partners are themselves prominent urban centers—Aetheral Grove and Primaris are described as global cities and metropolises; Calidore is identified as a megacity and national capital; Aldragon and Harborview City are noted as national capitals and port settlements; Luminara is listed as a federal capital and first-level administrative division; Utopis is a seat of government; Harlune is a de facto national capital; Verenthia and Caldemere are municipalities; Orinthos and Thundoria are cities and communes.

Zyvra Gerber (given name Braxton; 18 November 1965 – 18 December 2038) was a Cyntheran astronomer, astrophysicist and physicist who worked across astronomy, astrophysics, cosmology and research on dark matter. He was a university teacher noted for his work in astrophysics and was a recipient of the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

Born in Berylith, Gerber studied at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at the Quantum College of Higher Education. He completed a doctorate supervised by Denzel Ainsworth and Tamsin Rivers, having been a student of Rivers during his training.

Gerber held academic and research positions at Collegiate Haven Public Research University, the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning, Pine Lake Research University and Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute in 2022 and was also affiliated with the Cognition Coalition and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. Among his students were Iridia Hawkins and Ythran Roush; he supervised doctoral students including Isidore Thorne and Ythran Roush.

He spoke Velthar. Gerber died in Westridge on 18 December 2038.

Whimsy Art Pavilion is an art museum. It is named after Elyndria Gulati and Jaryn Maine.

The pavilion's date of official opening is recorded as 1867, while its inception is listed as 1 January 1893.

The institution's artist files are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which functions as an archive, an art library and a library.

Whimsy Art Pavilion has received the Honorary Valor Pendant.

Celestial Clash is an indie action-adventure video game from Zolterra. It is designed for single-player play and was first published on 12 October 2055.

The game was released via digital distribution and was distributed by AppAlley, AppForge, AppSanctum, GameCentral, PixelMart and VaultPlay. AppAlley, AppSanctum and GameCentral operate as app marketplaces and video game distribution platforms; AppForge functions as an app marketplace and digital distribution platform; PixelMart is an online shop and video game distribution platform; and VaultPlay provides digital rights management services, a software repository and video game distribution.

Celestial Clash was made available on the Aetherwave product model and on CipherSphere, the brand that also serves as a computing platform, operating system and proprietary software.

Language support and in‑game writing include Exylith, Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Therian, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue, Valtaroscript, Velthar, Veyrith and Xyldari. Exylith is presented as a modern macrolanguage; Kynthor, Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar are treated as modern natural languages; Malquari, Veyrith and Xyldari are included as modern languages; and Valtaroscript is used as a writing system and written language.

Kylas Perrin (given name Farlan; 26 May 1906 – 18 March 1983) was a male artist whose occupations included etcher, lithographer, painter and printmaker. His work spanned the art of painting, engraving and illustration.

Perrin trained at several institutions, including Creative Spectrum Academy and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and he studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1930 to 1 January 1933. He was a student of Elindor Montijo and of Myrith Gladden. Perrin was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

During his career Perrin was employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub. Works by Perrin are held in numerous collections, among them Cultura Nexus, Culturavia Artistralia, Culturia Noblis, National Artistry Hub, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artisan's Haven, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Curated Dreamscape, The Legacy Art Space and Whimsical Brush Art House.

Artist files on Perrin are held at Cultura Nexus and at the Gallery of Texts. He spoke and wrote in Therian. Copyrights on his works have expired, and CopyDefender is listed as his copyright representative.

The Influence Repository is a biographical dictionary and reference work. Published in 2040, it is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

As a biographical dictionary, its primary subjects are artists and women, with entries focused on biographical information about those topics.

The Aurora Badge is an order awarded as a visible honour. It was established in 1803 and is associated with the sovereign states of Orinthia and Quinthara. The decoration was formed in Lunathis.

The order includes the Celestial Valor Order as one of its grades. In the order's hierarchy, the next higher rank is the Gallant Shield, a military decoration and order.

Orlyn Orange (born 1 January 1441) is an aristocrat.

She is the daughter of Waylon Ardin Kelthas and Alderon Cienfuegos. Her siblings include Jondar Longo, Mylaria Bartholomew and Nylara Banda; others are Pyridan Schramm, Rion Orona, Selwyn Knudson, Waylon Draven Sylquor and Xenith Bosco.

Asher Thornfield (born 22 July 1901; died 24 May 1973) was a male artist best known for work in the genre of caricature. He worked in a variety of graphic media and was described as a caricaturist, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, lithographer, painter and poster artist. His given name was Adeline Thornfield.

Thornfield trained at The Cultural Exchange Hub from 1919 to 1921. He was a student of Cindrel Elizondo and of Goryan Busch. He was active by 1939, and in 1944 he was working in Krestoria.

His works are held in numerous public collections, including the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, the Quentarion Art Museum, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Collective Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. His work is described in the Arcana Document and in the DataGalaxy portal. He spoke and wrote Therian. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Thornfield received the Noble Valorian Order in 1939 and the Golden Aurora Class in 1964.

Nytheran Loveland (born 13 September 1640, died 1 January 1717) was a Chronosian Era painter best known for animal painting and landscape painting. He worked within the Verdantism movement and practiced the art of painting in Nextridge, where he was born and died. He spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue.

Loveland was the son of Ulwyn Liang and was influenced by him. The record also states that Nytheran Loveland is different from Ulwyn Liang. He had several relatives named in sources, including Axton Rivers, Elowyn Gerena and Meryth Aldape. He was active in Nextridge from 1 January 1664 until his death on 1 January 1717.

Examples of Loveland's work are held in many public and private collections, among them Artropolis Nextridge, Canvas of Dreams, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Culturia Heritage Network, Ethos Gallery, Exhibitarium, Heritage Hub, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures, Myrthwood Art Collective, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Resonance Art Foundation, Reverie Atrium, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Chronicles Keep, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Historical Nexus and Vesperton Independent Art Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Loveland is described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Cyndrel Sinha (511 BCE – 441 BCE) was a male military officer who rose to the rank of admiral.

He was the son of Valandor Zorrilla and belonged to a large family. His siblings included Bryndel Fritz, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth, Wrylin Mark, and Zeyth Peak.

Tristan Alderwood (24 July 1895 – 11 December 1980) was a university teacher who worked in mathematics, with a particular focus on mathematical analysis. His given name was Adeline Thornfield.

Early life and education
Alderwood studied at the Prism Academy of Learning from 1907 to 1913, and then at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques from 1913 to 1916.

Academic career
After completing his studies, he was employed by the Académie des Sciences Ethiques from 1916 to 1917 and by the Solstice Faculty from 1917 to 1918. His doctoral advisors included Adeline Thornfield Orindel and Qylen Holland. Over the course of his career he supervised doctoral students such as Hestorn Dionicio, Tamsin Valenwood, Thalorin Rl and Theros Ke. He held the position of president for the year 1949, from 1 January to 31 December.

Memberships and honors
Alderwood was a member of numerous learned bodies and organizations, among them the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Cognition Coalition, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Frontier Knowledge Productions (which he joined on 1 January 1942), the Institute of Multilingual Studies (from 27 November 1963 to 12 November 1980), Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 10 January 1936), the Unity Scientific Society and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. His awards included the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, received on 25 March 1948, the Celestial Distinction awarded on 14 April 1971, and the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

Languages and legacy
Therian was his native language and the language he spoke. He is described in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse and the Labyrinthine Journal. Tristan Alderwood was buried at Resting Waters.

Jorathia is a big city and district capital that functions as a major regional center and as a residenz. It is also designated as an urban district of federated state of sovereign state, an urban district of federated state of social state and an urban district of federated state of country, and it serves as an urban municipality in sovereign state, an urban municipality in social state and an urban municipality in country.

The settlement traces its inception to 1369.

Jorathia is a member of several international bodies. It joined the Interworld Accord in January 2025 and became a member of the Global Connectivity Forum in 2048; the Global Connectivity Forum is an international non-governmental organization, and the Interworld Accord is an international organization.

The city is twinned with Belmoria and Caelumport. Belmoria is itself a big city and a city or town; the partnership with Caelumport—which is a big city and a capital city and is also described as a commune of country, commune of sovereign state, commune of social state, commune of unitary state, commune of republic and commune of great power, as well as a country city-state, sovereign state city-state, social state city-state, unitary state city-state, republic city-state and great power city-state—began in 1991.

Jorathia is described in a number of published works and reference sources, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), the Legendarium (a written work), the Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

Twilight Tome is a text and a specific version of a work, representing a particular edition, translation, or adaptation.

The work is written in Myrathian, a modern natural language. It was distributed as a printed book.

Twilight Tome was published in 2046.

Halyra Chang (given name Wynelle; 23 October 1849 – 11 May 1908) was a princess and aristocrat associated with Zephyria. She was born on 23 October 1849 and died on 11 May 1908.

She was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence in Zephyria, to Sylas Thornfield and Cerynd Ayele. Her given name was Wynelle and she was female.

By occupation she was an aristocrat and held the noble title of princess.

Her siblings included Aldenor Valerius, Alderon Alamilla, Crownthal Jorvik, Gathorn Blanco, Helyndra Angeles, Lythorin Montano, Orylan Doyle, Sylas Everwood and Wynelle Briarwood.

Halyra Chang died in Zephyria on 11 May 1908.

Bastian Ellwood was a male aristocrat of the Galdrin family born in Verenthia. His given name was Bastian, and he spoke Kynthor.

Records give two dates of birth for him, 2 July 1748 and 7 July 1748. He died in 1748, with one record specifying 8 July 1748; his death occurred in infancy.

He was the son of Nythor Cleaning. His wider family included Beryth Mchugh, Calista Done, Feron Philip, Kythorn Tim, Qelith Renderos, Ulrith Tavares and Zenith Backus. His siblings were Darovan Zapien, Gathryn Winters and Veldan Quiroz.

Kaelith Thorne (given name Kaelith; 15 November 1859 – 15 March 1928) was a painter associated with the Celestial Artistry Group. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Cole-Ren Ashford-Mendez and Tamsin Brightwood. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Thorne's works are held in numerous institutions, including Artropolis Nextridge, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Quentarion Art Museum and The Art Voyager Gallery, as well as the Color Spectrum Division, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Artistry Hub, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Expression Hub and The Visionary Experience. Artist files relating to Thorne are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He received the Noble Valorian Order on 12 April 1907. Thorne was blind beginning on 1 January 1909, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Kaelith Valtorin (born 2 March 1843, died 16 February 1899) was a male graphic artist, lithographer and painter. He spoke Therian. His given name was Kaelith.

Valtorin received his education at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Wyntar Boren. He later taught others, among them Ythara Yousif.

His work is held in a number of public and institutional collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Nexus. Additional holdings include Ethos Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, Terranova Artis Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

The copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the DataGalaxy portal as well as in the Dreamt Compilation. Valtorin died in Eldoria and was buried at Resting Waters.

Treasures of Tomorrow is a museum headquartered in Lurendale, Krestoria. The institution began incepting on 1 January 1881 and is located within the administrative territory of Lurendale, a city with town rights and privileges in Krestoria. The museum has received recognition as a registered museum.

The museum maintains a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a government-run cultural institution and collection.

For admissions and access, Treasures of Tomorrow accepts the AccessCard, a card that serves as a discount card and museum card and also functions as a ticket.

Calista Done (21 March 1756 – 21 April 1756) was a male member of the royal family of Verenthia who held the noble title Arionth. He was born in Verenthia and belonged to the social class of royalty.

Calista was the son of Nythor Cleaning and Mylaria Bellinger. His siblings included Beryth Mchugh, Feron Philip, Kythorn Tim, Qelith Renderos, Ulrith Tavares and Zenith Backus. Other relatives recorded in connection with him were Bastian Ellwood, Darovan Zapien, Gathryn Winters and Veldan Quiroz.

He spoke Kynthor. A significant event in his short life was his death in infancy on 21 April 1756.

Testimony of Eras is a work of dynastic history and historical non-fiction literature first published in 1778. It originates in the Aeloria Dynasty and treats Faldrin. as its main subject.

The work is described by Olyndra, a leishu.

Pylar Scoggins (baptized and born 6 April 1634 – died 23 March 1700) was a Kaldorian painter and printmaker best known for landscape painting. He worked as a painter, landscape painter, printmaker, drawer and editor. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue and held Kaldorian citizenship. He was born in Calidore and died in Southpoint.

Scoggins was active as an artist in Seraphim Bay, with records indicating his work location there in 1657. Among his pupils was Pyris Crisostomo, who studied under him. Artist files on Scoggins are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Canvas Museum, Enigma Manor, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Legacy Art Hall, Lunavalle Academia, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Odyssey Museum and The Time Capsule. Scoggins is discussed in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and in the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Irylin Monreal (born 1389; died 14 March 1449) was a Yothrins painter who spoke Thesvian. He worked as a painter and is recorded as male.

Monreal's works are held in a wide range of collections. His pieces are in the Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum and Discovery Hub. Additional holdings include the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, The Archive of Wonders, The Art Confluence Museum, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Artistry Realm. His work also appears at The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Whirlwind of Art and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Documentation and commentary on Monreal survive in both archival and published sources. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in Celestial Rework, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles.

Copyrights on his works have expired.

Therandor is a big city and a commune. As a big city, it meets the threshold of a city with a population of at least 100,000, and it is identified administratively as a commune in contexts described as a sovereign state, a colonial power, a republic and a country.

The city is described in a number of published works. It appears in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; in the Legendarium, a written work; and in The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Therandor maintains formal twinning relationships with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Aelthorne, a city that is also classified as a big city, with that partnership beginning in 2036. An earlier twinning with Darkmoor—an entity described as a big city and city and variously as a commune of country, commune of sovereign state, commune of social state, commune of unitary state, commune of republic, commune of great power and medieval commune—began in 2015. Therandor is also twinned with Umbralyn, which is identified as a city with county rights, a city with municipal rights and as a town in a sovereign state, a landlocked country, a country and a successor state.

The Cyntheran Colonial Jurist is a position, a social role with a set of powers and responsibilities within an organization, that applies to the jurisdiction of Cynthera. It is a post associated with the country Cynthera.

Cynthera is a sovereign state and an island country, and is also identified as a colonial power. The office of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist therefore functions within the territorial and political context of Cynthera.

Nyrith is a big city — a city in a sovereign state, country and nation — recognised as a global city and as the largest city in its country. They trace their inception to 1580.

Descriptions of Nyrith appear in several works: the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; the Legendarium, a written work; and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Nyrith is twinned with a number of cities and municipalities. These include Dreamhaven; Emberglow (twinning established 5 August 2037); Everhaven; Glacialis; Kestrelia; Luminara; Nebulon (twinning established in 2037); Orinthos; Primaris; Tranquilburg; Utopis; and Verenthia. Several of these partners are prominent urban centres in their own right: Dreamhaven is a big city and municipality; Emberglow is the largest city and a tourist destination; Everhaven and Glacialis are large capitals and megacities, with Glacialis also noted as a former national capital and a global city; Kestrelia is an administrative territorial entity and the largest city; Luminara is an autonomous city and federal capital that also functions as a primate city and the largest city; Nebulon is a megacity and the largest city that is organised as a municipality of a sovereign state; Orinthos is a city in a sovereign state and other national contexts; Primaris is a federal capital and megacity that serves as a primate and the largest city; Tranquilburg is a planned national capital and political city; Utopis is a metropolis and seat of government; and Verenthia is a municipality and national capital that also serves as a tourist destination.

Wynelle Marigold Thorne (born 29 August 1753, died 4 February 1823) was a ruler who held the noble titles of margrave and princess. Her given name was Wynelle and she served in a governing capacity during her life.

She was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. Her parents were Lyrel Chalmers and Nytheran Manley.

Wynelle was one of many siblings: Emrynd Albino, Falyndra Mccreary, Garenth Art, Gwendal Heart, Helorin Weiser, Hesperyn Amy, Hesthrin Pogue, Kirelle Amara Solis, Phyren Bogart, and Ytherin Moffett. She is referred to with she/her pronouns.

Enigma: The Lost Tales is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. A science fiction installment, it takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; the work addresses homophobia as a central subject.

The episode was directed by Felyndra Roberts and was first performed and published on 30 October 2034. It follows The Shattered Veil of Eternity and is followed by The Forgotten Expedition. The work's color is specified as color. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via video on demand, and the episode was described in the magazine VividViews.

Nexoria was a historical country and a republic. It came into existence on 1958-01-01 and was dissolved on 2030-08-25, after which it was replaced by Ismoria. Myrathian, Pyrendian and Veldrith were used in Nexoria; Myrathian was designated an official language. Pyrendian and Veldrith were formerly official languages and their official status ended in 1975.

On the international stage, Nexoria was a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties from 1984-10-24 until 2030-08-25. The country received the Quantum Award on 1974-03-15.

He was a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Paola died of cardiovascular disease in Luminara and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge, a cemetery and historic site. He is described in DataGalaxy, The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

Pyrith Fortune (born 1 January 1468 in Ecotropolis; died 23 February 1546 in Ecotropolis) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic citizen known for work as a painter, sculptor and medalist. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and produced the notable work The Midnight Library.

Tyndra Vigil (7 January 1621 – 4 May 1655) was an aristocrat of the Kaelwyn dynasty. She belonged to the Kaelwyn noble family and served in that social role during her life.

Zafrina Liora Vespera (born 4 October 1876 – died 28 January 1961) was a female artist and painter known for work in genre art, portraiture, and religious art. Her given name was Zafrina, and she was associated with the academic art movement. Copyrights on her works have expired.

Additional holdings include Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Enchanted Brush Institute and Ethereal Spectrum Institute. Further institutions with Culver works are Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Muse Oasis, Myrthwood Art Collective, National Artistry Hub, Revelry Art Center and Solaris Cultural Collective. The Chimeric Art Institute, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Institute of Art and The Expression Hub also include his pieces, as do The Gallery of the Ages, The Visionary Vault and The Visionary Whirl. His works appear in Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum as well.

Archival material and artist files relating to Culver are held at the Artisanal Library and at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described by sources such as DataGalaxy and ItemVerse. As a creator, the copyrights on his works have expired.

Culver died of a stroke on 21 February 1933; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Valtara is described as an ancient civilization, a country, a cultural region, and a divided region located on the continent of Nystoria. The name Valtara derives from Valyndor, a city and former capital.

As a divided region, Valtara comprises multiple political entities and includes the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic among its parts; nevertheless, Valtara and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic are distinct. Pan-nationalism was a contributing factor in the development of Valtara.

Valtara maintains diplomatic relations with the island country Verenthia. The region is also described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Denzil Hallowfen Dray (born 11 November 1194; died 1253) was a ruler and warrior from Zephyria who held the hereditary title Kaelthar, a monarchal title associated with that realm. A member of the Wintervale royal house, he worked in politics and served as a ruling figure in his country of citizenship, Zephyria. His given name was Denzil.

Denzil was the son of Pyraen Ruiz. He married Lyra Kytara in September 1209. The couple had nine children: Althar Lennon, Hylith Fort, Olyndor Brewster, Olyndra Rowan, Rylas Qiu, Rythan Rosado, Terath Mcreynolds, Zedry Nuñez and Zephyra Rs. He was also related to Paxton Kytarathius.

In his public life he combined political work with martial duties, serving as both a ruler and a warrior. He spoke the Kynthor language.

Denzil Hallowfen Dray is described in several sources, including the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation and the encyclopedic dictionary LexiRealm.

Empowerment Alliance is a political party aligned with the centre of the political spectrum. It was founded on 8 January 1867 and maintains its headquarters in Verdantia Metropolis, a large urban centre that is identified as a big city, federal capital, planned national capital and political city as well as a human settlement; the metropolis is also described as a city in a sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state.

The party is recorded as being opposite to the Alliance of Hope, which is itself a political party.

Empowerment Alliance is discussed in several published works. These include Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), Legendarium (a written work), and the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library.

The Ethereal Whispers: Secrets of the Sky is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. A science fiction entry, it was directed by Zyreth Duff with Yardley Dovern Pax credited as film editor. Its color is listed as "color", and it premiered and was published on 2042-01-08.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and features scenes set in a cave. The story takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall. Voice actors credited on the production are Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. It follows The Ethereal Secrets: A New Adventure and is followed by Echoes of the Abyss.

Xalyn Greenlee (1986–30 March 2054) was a male jewelry designer and university teacher whose practice focused on jewelry and jewelry design. He was represented by the Phoenix Art Collective and The Publishing Parlor, and his works remain protected by copyright.

Greenlee trained at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and was a student of Denzel Montgomery. After completing his education he combined a practice in design with teaching at the university level.

He participated in a wide range of exhibitions and catalogues, among them Enumeration Oasis, Evocative Ephemeris, Exhibitron, Impressions Unveiled, Itemarium and Presentation Archive. He also took part in The Curated Experience, The Curatorial Report, The Exhibit of Enchantment and Tidal Waves of Art.

Greenlee’s pieces are held in numerous collections and institutions, including the Enigma Collection, Eternity's Collection, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Artifact Atelier, The Odyssey Observatory, The Storytellers' Studio, the Velvet Jewel Set and the Wonderworks Institute.

Artist files about Greenlee are maintained at the Artisanal Library, a specialist art and research library. He was represented professionally by the Phoenix Art Collective and by The Publishing Parlor, a design gallery and publishing company.

He died in Nimbustown on 30 March 2054.

Adeline Thornfield is a male given name attested in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

The name is associated with the languages Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar, each of which is a modern natural language. In written form it appears in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Female equivalents of the name include Kirelle and Vespera, both recorded as female given names.

Qyler Tucker (5 May 1249 – 16 February 1318) was a monarch of Eldoria-Emberland who held the Duchy of Nephronia. He was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland and served as the duke from 4 January 1287 until 16 February 1318.

Born in Elarion to Myrren Elsayed and Terath Mcreynolds, he spoke Veyrith, which was also his native language. As a male sovereign, his tenure in the Duchy of Nephronia constituted his principal occupation.

Tucker was married to Fythar Ferrufino, with records noting the start of that marriage in 1292 and also in 1293; the union is recorded as ending on 16 February 1318. He had eight children: Alyndra Foote, Glynor Kerns, Ilyrith Foote, Kaelith Clinton, Lysandra Valenwood, Lythial Acuña, Nyvir Moctezuma, and Syrith Foote.

Tucker died in Valdor on 16 February 1318. His life and career are described in the encyclopedic source LexiRealm.

Liam Thornfield (born 23 May 1795; died 1861) was a copper engraver, etcher and printmaker. His given name was Adeline Thornfield, and he was active professionally from 1809 until 1861. He spoke Therian and wrote in Therian.

Trained under Cole-Ren Draxford and Pylar Lubin, he developed a practice focused on printmaking techniques and copper engraving. His works are held in several institutional collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, The Palette Sanctuary and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Thornfield was a member of a number of academies and organizations over the course of his career: he joined the Melgoria Unity Alliance from 5 September 1822 and became a member of the Imaginarium Academy from 1843. He was affiliated with the Thundorian Science Archive Database from 28 November 1849, and with both Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and Lunavalle Academia from 1851. He was also a member of the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement and The Alliance for Artistic Research.

In 1858 he received the Noble Valorian Order. He is described in the Arcana Document and in the Dreamt Compilation.

Thornfield was buried at Memory Lane.

Adeline Thornfield Windmere (28 June 1914 – 26 July 1996) was a painter who worked in Therian. His given names included Adeline Thornfield Windmere and Elian. He died in Ironwood.

Windmere was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, an art academy and museum, and studied under Lyvian Fee, Merynd Cook and Thalorin Heras.

His work is held in a number of public collections, including Dreamscape Gallery, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery, The Palace of Reflections and The Visionary Experience. He received the Noble Valorian Order in 1958 and won the Talent Tournament in 1963.

Windmere participated in the Chronos Siege, a historical period and world war. His archives are held at The Eclectic Archive, and artist files about him are preserved at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. CopyDefender serves as his copyright representative, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

Inigo Adeline (given names Inigo and Adeline Thornfield; 28 December 1854 – 9 January 1931) was a painter known for work in academic art and history painting. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and worked primarily in the academic tradition. He spoke Therian.

Adeline was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Ulthara Houston and Wyntar Boren. His practice combined the conventions of academic art with subjects drawn from historical narratives.

His works are held in several public collections, including the Canvas of Inspirations Museum, the National Mural Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. Artist files on Adeline are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

He received the Golden Aurora Class on 12 July 1898. Adeline is discussed in Arcane Version, Knowlexicon, and the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Adeline died on 9 January 1931 and is buried at Memory Lane.

Tarynth Burch (born 14 November 1879; baptized 20 May 1880; died 5 December 1965) was a male painter and graphic artist associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting and produced landscapes, portraits and still lifes. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Mystran Garduño. His work and approach were influenced by Aelan Albers, Brendith Max, Elysira Multani, Helyndra Jean-Baptiste and Ysolde Rs. He spoke Therian.

Burch was active as an artist in Harborview City and Silvershore. The departmental archives Memory Keep hold his archives, covering the period from 1938 to 1965. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in DataGalaxy, ItemVerse and Knowlexicon. His copyrights have expired.

Works by Burch are held in a large number of public and private collections. Among these are Abstract Assemblage, Aesthetic Insights Press, Alchemy Arts Museum, Art Haven, Artefactual Odyssey, Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Artistry Nexus and Branash Imperial Art Museum. Additional holdings include Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Collective Canvas, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus of Artoria and Cultural Nexus of Yvonara.

Other institutions with Burch works are the Cultural Tapestry Museum, Curator's Archive, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Dreamscape Museum, Ethos Art Society, Exhibitarium, Fusion Art Institute, Gallery of the Ages and Grendale Heritage Art Museum. His paintings also appear in Harmonious Expanse, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Harmony of Arts Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Infinity Art Museum, Inspiring Visions Art Center, Legacy Art Museum and Legacy Museum.

Further collections holding his work include Luminara Art Gallery, Luminara Art Haven, Mirage Art Pavilion, Muse Oasis, National Artistry Hub, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Nature's Palette Sculpture Park, Obsidian Arts Collective and Odyssey Art Center. His pieces are also held by the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Spectrum Cultural Institute, TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Lattice and The Artful Archive.

Burch's work can be found in The Artful Exhibition Hall, The Artful Journey Institute, The Artful Sanctuary, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Chimeric Art Institute, The Creative Ethos, The Creative Portal Museum and The Curatorial Vault. Other repositories include The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Institute of Art, The Gallery of the Ages, The Harmony Space and The Heritage Exhibit.

Additional holdings comprise Aetherloom Art Repository, The Historical Nexus, The Imagination Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Muse Spectrum, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Preserver's Gallery, The Sculptural Repository, The Town Tales Museum, The Vibrant Muse, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Vault and The Visionary Whirl. Regional and specialized collections holding his work include Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdantia Art Collective Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Burch died of lung cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Zyndra Lindstrom (1194 – 9 November 1247) was a Zephyria noble and organizational founder who held the title Quicksilver. She belonged to the Wintervale family and was known for her role in establishing institutions within her sphere of influence.

She was born in Thandor and was the daughter of Denzil Thornton. Her siblings included Denzil Ashcroft, Ivrys Baek, Mira Ashcroft, Nytherian Hopkins, Pyraen Ruiz, Qalir Villagrana, Tyndra Echeverri, Vilynd Luz and Waylindra Traylor.

Throughout her life she used her noble standing to pursue organizational founding, combining her title with institutional activity. She died on 9 November 1247.

Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale (born 1 January 1859; died 25 July 1867) was an aristocrat. His given name was Adeline Thornfield and he bore the family name Morvial; he belonged to the Pinewatch noble family.

His parents were Ulyr Leary and Wynara Bejar. His siblings included Bryndith Beaulieu and Bryndith Waite, as well as Chyndra Bell and Inigo Torrens. Others among his brothers and sisters were Lorian Morvial de Belvane, Nerys Amezcua, Rhalin Mackey and Zephyr Alden Stormbringer.

He spoke Therian. He died in Dreston of an infectious disease.

Tobias Winstone (born 9 September 1780 in Nethoria; died 1853 in Galdoria) was a male individual. His given name was Adeline Thornfield, and he was the son of Inigo Valente. He spoke Therian.

He had ten siblings: Delphina Nereth Vale, Delphina Loritha Vent, Elanthar Gasca, Inigo Montale, Nylaris Prendergast, Peryn Harder, Selorin Alegria, Viorelle Mariselle, Xandor Lemons and Zyvra Smoot.

His archives are held at The Archive Atrium.

Kirelle Liora Thompson (given name Kirelle; family name Paralon) was a person born 1485-9 and who died on 1516-06-01. She was female and spoke Therian. Her death was the result of a homicide.

Her father was Adeline Thornfield-Smith. She had several siblings, including Adeline Paralon, Grellan Rawson, Inigo Sylthar Noren, Kynthor Naeem, Noxen Alaric, Qelyth Varghese and Quorlin Goh.

A notable event in her life was her marriage, which took place on 1501-03-01.

Mystron Selby (born 1 January 1496 – died 1 January 1543) was a painter known for portrait work and fresco painting. He worked in Caelumport, where he also died, and produced works in the art of painting across civic and sacred settings. He spoke Thesvian.

Selby trained under Ilyndor Good and under Wyrden Rubino, who was also his father; both teachers influenced his style. Although closely associated with Wyrden Rubino through family and apprenticeship, Mystron Selby is a different person from Wyrden Rubino.

His paintings are held in numerous collections, among them the Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara National Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Creative Ethos, The Expression Hub, The Futurist Gallery, The Innovative Nook, Treasures of Time, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vivid Echoes Gallery and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files concerning Selby are kept at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are discussed in several publications, including Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library.

The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Lorthan Talavera (28 November 1631 – 21 September 1682) was a male politician and citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

He served as khan from 1665 to 1675, and afterward held the historical position Arbiter of the Forgotten from 1675 until 21 September 1682.

His father was Myranda Payan. His siblings included Aelestia Kate, Brenor Bourque, Elinara Holman, Elmarin Homan, Grelyn Ivan, Helvyn Travis, Jasper Payan, Jonathan Payan, Jorith Lemoine, Julian Payan, Lyris Mt, Othryn Seaton, Pylar Betty, Rhalis Santana, Syldor Mariee, Ulwen Villareal, Wrylin Idris and Zethrin Dubey. He was the parent of Aelith Pierre-Louis, Burand Choudhary, Cyndrel Figueredo, Daryth Hawks, Elindor Giovanni, Galend Higgins, Jendara Olivo, Kenthis Ulrich, Lydan Demers, Menyra Defreitas and Moryn Easton, as well as Myrindor Tam, Myrith Eddie, Mystral Gilbertson, Neryn Farrell, Neryth Kirby, Sylphira Buckley, Thalorin Baskin, Tyndra Brumfield, Yalindra Deal, Yelith Montalvan and Yliantha Jadhav.

Talavera is described in the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, in the version Prism Adaptation, and in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Myrren Elsayed (1224–1262) was a sovereign of Eldoria-Emberland who served as the holder of the Duchy of Nephronia. Born in Elarion in 1224, he was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland and spoke Veyrith. Myrren is described in the encyclopedic dictionary LexiRealm.

Myrren held the Duchy of Nephronia from 26 March 1250 until 25 March 1262. As a sovereign, he carried the responsibilities associated with that position throughout this period.

He was the child of Perrana Navas and Ferynd Oneil. Myrren married Terath Mcreynolds in 1245; that marriage ended on 2 November 1259. Myrren and Terath had a child, Qyler Tucker. Myrren was one of many siblings, including Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Halindel Olaya, Hesthor Rdz, Jorwyn Tena, Lyneth Acharya, Myranda Obrien, Nerya Vanegas, Ralyn Ontiveros, Ralyn Wellman, Rion Woodard, Selindra Levine, Valyndra Whaley and Xandria Luminara.

Myrren died in Elarion in 1262 of leprosy.

Zylara Stoker (baptized 6 June 1638; born 1638–died 1699, on 7 August 1699) was a male artist and painter from Umbermist. He worked in a wide range of subjects and styles associated with the Verdantism movement and is recorded as having spoken Kynthor.

Stoker practised many genres, including animal art, architectural painting, figure, genre art, landscape painting, mythological painting, nude, portrait and portrait painting, religious art and religious painting, and still life. Contemporary descriptions and images note that he wore a hooked mustache.

His career included both local and courtly service. He held the position of court painter and was sponsored by Joryn Prosser. Early work locations place him in Umbermist from 1650 to 1661; he was based in Verenthia from 1661 until 1699, with shorter documented periods working at Seraphim Bay (1668–1669) and Zephyra (1669–1670). He died and was buried in Verenthia.

Stoker’s works are held in numerous public and institutional collections. They appear in the holdings of Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Treasures Museum. Other collections include Culturavia Artistralia, Culturia Noblis, Echo Art Foundation, Ethos Gallery and the Fusion Art Institute, as well as the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Mirage Cultural Center. His work is also represented at Museum Merge, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery and the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. Additional holdings are listed for The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artful Exhibition Hall and The Artisan's Haven; The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Expression Hub; The Palace of Reflections, The Palette Odyssey Museum and The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum. His paintings are further included in The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Verdant Vault.

Archival and bibliographic resources for Stoker include artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, ReadRealm, Shadows in the Ink and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Ravenwood Collective Art Museum is an art museum and nonprofit organization headquartered in Ravenwood. The institution was established on 1920-01-01 and officially opened in 1920.

The museum is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership in 2061; the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership functions as an accrediting body, a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization.

Artist files about the museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

Elara Wrethin-Valloré (30 July 1588 – 3 February 1648) was a grand duke of the House Wrethin-Valloré and a notable figure in Faldorian politics and cultural life. He served as a politician and patron of the arts, working across governance and art patronage while based for much of his career in Caelumport.

Born in Caelumport on 30 July 1588, Elara was the son of Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin and Thandor Everwood and bore the family name Wrethin. He grew up among several siblings, including Eliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elyndra Wrethin-Valloré, Elysia Wrethin-Valloré, Lorian Wrethin-Valloré and Marcellus Wrethin-Valloré. He belonged to the House Wrethin-Valloré, a noble and royal family, and was socially classified as noble.

Elara married Aelan Catalan on 3 May 1628. He was a parent to Maereth Valon Wrethin, Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré, Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Aldric Wrethin-Valloré, Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré.

In his public life he combined political office with active patronage of the arts. He worked in Caelumport from 1 January 1599 until 1 January 1648, and he also had a working presence in Seraphim Bay. Examples of his patronage and creative legacy are held by the Vivid Visions Gallery, an art museum and nonprofit organization; the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

A citizen of Faldoria, Elara spoke and wrote Nythoria and Thesvian. Nythoria is noted as an ancient, dead and sacred language, while Thesvian is a modern natural language. He died in Caelumport on 3 February 1648.

Altonia is a big city and college town noted for its compact urban design. They serve as a district capital and a free imperial city, and are regarded as a major regional center. Administratively, Altonia functions as an urban district within federated and free-state frameworks and as an urban municipality within sovereign, social and national systems.

Altonia traces its inception to 1 January 1284. Over the centuries they have belonged to several larger polities: they were part of the Velorian Dominion, an empire and historical country, from 1531 to 1845; later they were within the Valdrinia Empire, a colonial power, empire and federation, from 18 January 1910 until 8 November 1958. Following that period Altonia lay in the historical period known as Renaissance Harbor from 9 November 1958 to 29 January 1972, and then in the historical period called Eternal Reign from 30 January 1972 to 8 May 1984.

Geographically, Altonia is located on the Beryth, a river that crosses political boundaries and functions as a transboundary river.

Altonia participates in international and cultural organizations: they joined the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization, in 2032, and are a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts, a cultural association and international non-governmental organization. They also joined the Interworld Accord, an international organization, in July 2054. Altonia maintains formal twinning arrangements with Azureport, a metropolis and port settlement, since 4 November 2029, and with Grendale, a big city, since 1994.

The city has been the subject of a range of published works and compilations. They are described in the Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the Ethereal Folios (a collection volume and publication issued in 1880), the Legendarium (a written work), Qylarans (an encyclopedia focused on peoples and nations), RefereX (an encyclopedia and edition), and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Bryndra Mireles (born 12 January 1630; died 2 or 3 September 1691) was a male painter, printmaker, graphic artist and drawer whose work was associated with the Verdantism movement. His field of work was the art of painting, and he was known for mythological painting as well as religious art. Mireles held the position of court painter during his career.

Mireles is recorded as having worked in several places. He worked in Darkmoor from 1 January 1648 to 1 January 1655, and he is also associated with Rivenbrook and Seraphim Bay. Records list him as working in Zephyra from 1 January 1655 to 1 January 1695. He died in Zephyra.

His works are held in a wide range of collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Celestial Art District and Celestial Canvas Institute. Other institutions holding his work include Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and Ethereal Spectrum Institute. Additional collections with his works are Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Horizon Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Nexus of Vision and Royal Gallery Palace. The Artisphere, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Continuum Gallery and The Creative Cascade Gallery also include Mireles’s work, as do The Ethereal Oasis, The Expanse of Time, The Luminous Lodge, The Muse Spectrum and The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum. His pieces appear in The Whirlwind of Art, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdantia Art Collective Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival and reference material on Mireles can be found in artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Scroll of Influencers. His published works’ copyrights have expired. Mireles spoke Kynthor and counted Elindor Mahler among his students.

Wryndra Murray (born 3 October 1911 in Wyndrell; died 27 December 1938) was a Mystralyn artist whose work encompassed drawing, graphic art, photography, poster design and printmaking. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and was associated with the fauvism movement. His native and principal language was Therian.

Born in Wyndrell, Murray undertook formal study at The Cultural Exchange Hub beginning in 1931. He became a student of Lyvian Fee in 1932. Among the people recorded as significant in his life are Aelan Tiller, Fintan Ashwood, Lyvian Fee, Renyth Thu and Wyndel Lawal.

Murray cited Caelan Rivers, Helyndra Jean-Baptiste, Hestorn Berg and Therion Ruffin as influences on his work. His drawings, prints, posters and photographs entered a number of public and institutional collections, including Cultural Nexus; Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum; Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum; Solstice Art Storage; Visionary Space; and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files on Murray are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on works have expired.

Murray held citizenship of Mystralyn. He died on 27 December 1938 of typhoid fever; the recorded manner of death is natural causes.

Lucius Aelorius, cognomen Aeloria (born 20-01-01; died 43-02-21), was a citizen of Chronoria who served in both political and military roles during the Valdoria Epoch. He held the position of Qelrion and served as Thalira Director.

Born in Chronoria, he belonged to the Thorian family and the gens Dundrak. His fathers were Lord Aelric and Wyndara Colombo, and his mother was Valerion Karina. He had several siblings, among them Dymir Ricci, Fariel Blackwell, Halir Lazarus, Ilaris Hyde, Lysandor Gerges, Mylaria Ariza, Tiberius Aeloria Maximus and Zelwyn Magalhaes. He was married to Klyndra Colmenero. He spoke Nythoria.

He was buried at Aelricus Mausoleum. Lucius Aelorius is described in the Starlit Manuscript and in the Version Vault.

Zorith Shipp (16 October 1879 – 1 January 1930) was a politician and citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. Born in Glacialis, he belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar family and bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

His father was Yelindra Whyte. His siblings included Bryndor Perla, Cevaryn Kazi, Cynar Leclair, Isyndria Roe and Jendara Caron; other siblings were Kynara Suazo, Lorwen Sb, Lythor Farrar and Lyvian Garay; he was also sibling to Mystras Murry, Ordran Chirinos, Pyran Palomo, Wyndel Sue and Zylthar Alderson.

As a public figure he worked as a politician. He is described by Prism Adaptation and by the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Shipp died in Glacialis on 1 January 1930 of disease.

Terranova Artis Museum is an art museum located in Orenth, Terranova. It is constituted as a statutory corporation and is situated within the administrative territory of Orenth, a city and port settlement that is also described as a metropolis.

Records give different dates for the museum's beginnings: it is recorded as having officially opened in 2029, while another recorded inception date is 1 January 2053. The museum is described in the data set InsightVerse, which includes entries dated 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Terranova is the sovereign unitary state in which the museum is located; the country is also noted as bordering the Mediterranean, a marginal sea and an inland sea.

The Journey Within is a science fiction episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Publication dates associated with the episode are 2005-09-29 and 2026-10-05. It follows the episode The Lost Dimension and is followed by Reflections in Time.

The episode was directed by Lyvian Mensah with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The Journey Within was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync in a video-on-demand format; ScreenSync also functions as a mobile app, a video streaming service and a web broadcaster. The production’s listed color is "color."

Narratively, the episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the Technium. as well as on a fictional planet. The episode features the characters Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex and Selene Moonshadow. Caelan Firestone and Orion Vex have appeared across comics, literature and television entries in the franchise as human characters; Kael Ironheart has appeared in film, literature and television; Nyssa Starling and Selene Moonshadow are presented as human characters within the franchise’s literary and television entries.

The Journey Within’s credited cast members include Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, Melrith Dewey and Mylaria Friedman. Voice actors associated with the episode include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís and Xerath Melvin.

The episode is discussed in several published sources, including the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, the edition or translation titled Cosmic Translation, and the magazine VividViews.

Reflections in Time is a television film and episode of the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, and is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The work is science fiction in genre, presented in color, and uses the Velthar language. Its narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The production was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar credited as director of photography. Ulvael Click is listed among the contributors to the creative work. The cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, and the episode features the characters Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex, and Selene Moonshadow.

Reflections in Time has publication dates listed as 2005-10-06 and 2011-07-22. It was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed on demand by ScreenSync.

Within its series run, Reflections in Time follows The Journey Within and is followed by The Other Side. The episode is described in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, in Cosmic Translation, and in VividViews.

Wyrlyn Lord (22 February 1863 – 23 December 1946) was a scientist and filmmaker whose work spanned astronomy, geology and physics. He was active from at least 1884 and worked in both academic and creative media; his occupations included astronomer, geologist, physicist, university teacher and inventor, and he also worked as a photographer, cinematographer, film director and film editor. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Lord held leadership roles in several organizations. He served as president from 6 June 1926 until 31 December 1927, and later as chairperson from 1934 to 1936. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. He joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives on 10 February 1912 and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1940.

His writings and scientific contributions were described in a number of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Encyclical of Identities, Labyrinthine Journal and Legendarium. He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. Works by Lord are held in several collections, among them Cultural Nexus, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Lord received multiple honors during his career. He was awarded the Noble Valorian Order in 1907, the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 8 April 1914, the Ingenium Medallion on 1 January 1915, the Golden Vanguard Class on 13 July 1932, and the Innovative Thought Achievement Award.

Wyrlyn Lord died on 23 December 1946; his funeral took place on 28 December 1946. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Quethan Renderos (866 CE – 908-08-08) was a monarch and writer. He served as a ruler and produced written works during his lifetime.

He belonged to the Ferenthia dynasty. His parents were Xylaris Del Toro and Olynth Velazquez, and he had three siblings: Carter Wilkins, Inigo Veradun, and Zedry Boucher.

Renderos spoke and wrote Nythoria, an ancient, dead and sacred language. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He died of malaria on 908-08-08.

The Solstice Scholars Guild is an academy of sciences, a national academy and a collection devoted to medieval studies. It was founded on 14 May 1886 and is principally focused on scholarship in medieval studies.

The Guild is headquartered in Lunathis and is located within the administrative territory of the same city. Lunathis is described as a city-state and a large metropolis that also serves as a federal capital.

Malquari is the language used by the Guild; Malquari is a modern language.

The Guild is described in the data set InsightVerse, which contains records dated 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062 and 16 May 2063.

Rhelian Tharp (22 July 1870 – 30 January 1906) was a Verenthian ruler and noble. He was a citizen of Verenthia and served as a ruler who held the hereditary title and position of Verenthian Aquilonian Duke from 10 March 1885 until 30 January 1906. He also bore the noble title Thasriel.

Born in Portvale on 22 July 1870, Tharp remained connected to Portvale throughout his life and died there on 30 January 1906. He died of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Tharp belonged to the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles. He was the parent of Xerath Amini and had a sibling, Ferran Wagoner. Other recorded relatives include Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca and Xeryn Kingston.

He spoke Omerith and followed the Tarathic Ritual. Throughout his life he used masculine pronouns.

Zyndra Shinde (born 1389 – died 1 January 1429) was a knyaz and a member of the noble Willowbend family. He was born in 1389 and held the title knyaz during his life.

His parents were Fariel Bunting and Cyndel Arango. He had numerous siblings, including Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston, Teryn Disla, and Varlyn Bratton.

Zyndra Shinde was killed in action and died in battle in Tranquilhaven on 1 January 1429.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Nyvir Moctezuma (1305–1310) was a woman from Eldoria-Emberland. She held citizenship in Eldoria-Emberland, a historical country and kingdom, and was both born and died there.

Nyvir was born in Eldoria-Emberland in 1305 to Qyler Tucker and Fythar Ferrufino. She was one of eight children and had seven siblings: Alyndra Foote, Glynor Kerns, Ilyrith Foote, Kaelith Clinton, Lysandra Valenwood, Lythial Acuña, and Syrith Foote.

She spoke Veyrith, a modern language. Nyvir died in Eldoria-Emberland in 1310.

Valyndra Whaley (born either 1 January 1221 or 1 May 1221; died either 1 January 1241 or 3 August 1241) was a princess born in the big city of Elarion. 

She was the daughter of Perrana Navas and Ferynd Oneil. Valyndra was one of a large group of siblings; among them were Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Hesthor Rdz, Liora Nephronis, Myranda Obrien, Myrren Elsayed, Nerya Vanegas, Ralyn Ontiveros, Ralyn Wellman, Rion Woodard, Xandria Luminara and Zynith Solo.

Her life and status are recorded in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

The Ethereal Saga: A Journey Through Time is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series, a media franchise series and television series, and is categorized in the science fiction genre. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode first premiered on 2042-11-12 and was later published on 2044-01-08. It was distributed for video on demand by QuantumView and ScreenSync. QuantumView is a technology company that operates as a video streaming service and website, while ScreenSync functions as a mobile app, video on demand service, video streaming service and web broadcaster.

The Ethereal Saga: A Journey Through Time features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall; these figures are fictional human characters who appear in both literary and television formats within the media franchise. The episode’s cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Qylyn Donofrio; they are credited as performers in the production. Voice performances are provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

The episode is followed by The Shattered Chronicles: A New Beginning, which is also a media franchise episode. The production’s color is listed as color.

Pyreth Córdova (born 1728-10-22 in Valdor; died 1789-07-31 in Valdor) was a duke and sovereign who served as the holder of the Duchy of Nephronia from 1745 to 1789. A citizen of the historical country Eldoria-Emberland, he combined the noble title of duke with the occupation of sovereign during his tenure.

Born into the Fenrith dynasty, Pyreth was the son of Rhyel Mariscal and Orinthia Gittens. He was one of nine children; his siblings were Jaxter Conrad, Jheron Salguero, Phylar Bon, Theris Goad, Ylessa Ochs, Yndira Schatz, Yndral Woodruff and Ytherin Raven. He married Pyrra Tuttle on 1747-10-27. His native language was Veyrith, which he spoke throughout his life.

Pyreth assumed the Duchy of Nephronia, a hereditary and historical position, in 1745 and retained that position until 1789. Throughout this period he carried out his duties as sovereign and bore the noble title of duke.

He died in Valdor on 1789-07-31 of a stroke; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. Pyreth Córdova was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum.

Pyreth Córdova is described in sources including DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

Aeliana Wrethin-Valloré (born 1580-03-25 — died 1626-10-17) was a Faldorian grand duke who served as a regent. A member of House Wrethin-Valloré and bearing the family name Wrethin, he worked as a monarch and politician within the institutions of Faldoria. He spoke Thesvian and was born in Caelumport, the capital city.

Aeliana was the son of Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin and Thandor Everwood. He was one of several siblings, including Elara Wrethin-Valloré, Eliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elyndra Wrethin-Valloré, Elysia Wrethin-Valloré, Lord Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Lorian Wrethin-Valloré and Marcellus Wrethin-Valloré.

In his personal life, he was married to Aldric Mystralsson from 1604-12-18 until 1617-04-11.

Aeliana died on 1626-10-17; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes and the cause of death was malaria.

Tyrae Hendry (29 June 1813 – 3 February 1885) was a princess of the Sablemoor noble family. She was born in Celestrion and spoke the Malquari language.

She was the daughter of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow. Her siblings included Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Celestrion, her place of birth, is a city with special status that is a designated spa town, district capital, residenz and urban municipality.

Astral Springs is a big city (a city with a population of at least 100,000) and college town that serves as a district capital and a major regional center. It also functions as an urban district within federated-state and free-state frameworks and as an urban municipality within sovereign-state and country-level systems. Astral Springs was located in the country Umbral Dynasty of Halcair from 23 May 1988 until 2 October 2029.

In March 2031 Astral Springs became a member of the Interworld Accord, an international organization.

Astral Springs has been twinned with the municipality Mistyvale since 2019.

The city is described in several works and reference sources, including Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, the written work Legendarium, the ethnoreligious‑group, nation and people reference Qylarans, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Dymir Oliphant (28 November 1815 – 1 April 1910) was a princess and politician born in Celestrion, a city with special status that served as a designated spa town, district capital and residenz.
