A member of the Jewelstone and Sablemoor noble families, she combined her aristocratic title with a career in politics.

Her parents were Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow. Her given name was Wynelle. She spoke Malquari.

Oliphant’s siblings included Draxella Houghton, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Kynthor Switzer (1 January 1444 – 4 January 1488) was an aristocrat who held the title of duke and belonged to the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. She played her role within that noble house during her lifetime.

She was the daughter of Ylenara Mp and Ylinda Randhawa. Her siblings included Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Pembryn Harden and Wrylin Zacarias.

Damaris Everwood (born 1 January 1449 – died 27 July 1504) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. Her given name was Damaris.

She was a member of the Kaelwyn family, a dynasty and noble family. By occupation she served as an aristocrat.

Her father was Ylenara Mp and her mother was Ylinda Randhawa. She had seven siblings: Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden, Quindra Delossantos, Ryvian Avalos, and Wrylin Zacarias.

Valyndor is a city in the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. It is a megacity and a former capital that also functions as a provincial capital and a prefecture-level city, and it is classified as a sub-province-level division. Valyndor traces its inception to 272 BCE.

The city is a member of several organizations and networks, including the Empowerment Collective, the SyncSphere (which Valyndor joined in 2049), and The Outliers Collective. The Empowerment Collective is a non-governmental organization, SyncSphere is a network, and The Outliers Collective is described as an organization.

Valyndor maintains twinning relationships with a number of other municipalities and cities. Its twin towns and sister cities include Aquilon City (since 25 November 2052), Cobalt Springs, Eastwood City (since 13 March 2026), Jaspis (since 14 September 2050), Nythra (since 22 June 2020), Rivenbrook (since 10 May 2056), Rivendale (since 29 December 2054), Silverbrook (since 30 August 2057), Solmira (since 6 July 2022), Port Solstice (since April 2054), Xelthoran (since 3 December 2038), Yloria (since 13 September 2051), and Ythoria (since 30 September 2055).

Those partner localities have varied administrative statuses. Aquilon City is a big city with a city council and a municipality. Cobalt Springs is described as an administrative territorial entity and a big city, acting as a district capital and identified as an urban district and urban municipality in multiple federated and national contexts. Eastwood City is a big city and a county seat, characterized as a city in several state types including sovereign state, constitutional republic, federal republic and other national contexts as well as a historical unrecognized state. Jaspis is a big city that is a consolidated city-county and a county seat. Nythra is a big city and a commune cited in contexts such as the sovereign state, colonial power, republic and country. Rivenbrook is a municipality of the sovereign state, the realm, the country and the historical nationality. Rivendale is an administrative territorial entity and city. Silverbrook is a big city and a city of oblast subordinance. Solmira is a big city that is variously identified as a district, a municipality and a statutory city across contexts described as sovereign state, republic, landlocked country, state and successor state. Port Solstice is an administrative territorial entity and a big border city that is also described as a former capital and a megacity. Xelthoran is a big city and a commune in several state contexts including country, sovereign state, social state, unitary state, republic and great power. Yloria is a big border city also described as a cadastral populated place, a historical country city, an ancient civilization city and a temporal entity city; it is a municipality of the country, a municipality seat and a place with town rights and privileges. Ythoria is a municipality described in several state contexts, including sovereign state, secular state, rule of law, country and federal republic.

The Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, the country in which Valyndor is located, is characterized as a sovereign state and as a communist state, constitutional republic, dictatorship of the proletariat, people's republic, secular state, socialist state, and a state with limited recognition.

The Whirlwind of Colors is an art museum. It began existence on 1 January 1997 and officially opened in 1997.

The museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Version Vault is a topic dictionary and a specific version, edition, or translation of a work. It was published in 1924 in Zephyra, a large federal city variously described as a capital and a million-city that is also recorded as a former capital and the country's largest city.

The work is written in Myrathian, a modern natural language.

Version Vault was edited by Vyndel Amparo, who served as the work's editor. The publication is in the public domain.

Luminara Art Gallery is an art museum. The gallery was established on 1 January 1968 and officially opened in 1968.

The gallery is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It is accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that is also a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization; accreditation was granted in 2061.

Artist files about the gallery are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that serves as an archive, an art library and a library. On 19 December 2018 the gallery received the Legacy Appreciation Badge as a heritage designation.

The Shattered Chronicles: A New Beginning is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction installment that forms part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with its narrative set on a fictional planet. The episode was first performed and published on 2042-11-19 and was directed by Jorin Flannery. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via video on demand; ScreenSync is a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The production's credited cast members are Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters who appear in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, and Gideon Frostfall.

Voice actors featured in the episode include Garanth Smit, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

In the series chronology, The Shattered Chronicles: A New Beginning follows The Ethereal Saga: A Journey Through Time and is followed by The Celestial Nexus: A Journey to the Unknown.

The work is additionally associated with the color "color."

Axton Thorne (born 1979) is an artist, designer and author from Cynthera, best known for work in jewelry and art jewelry. He is also a sculptor and a university teacher. His given name is Axton, and he speaks Velthar. Thorne lives in Calidore.

Thorne's practice focuses on jewelry, jewelry design and art jewelry; he is employed by Carandor Artistry Productions and by the Creative Nexus Institute, where he combines professional design work with teaching. In addition to designing and making jewelry, he has published writing related to his field.

His work has been shown in a number of exhibitions and publications. He has participated in Presentation Archive and in The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, and has been involved with The Curated Experience and The Curatorial Report; he has also taken part in The Gallery of Wonders and Treasures in Transition.

Examples of Thorne's pieces are held in many collections and museums, including Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Eternity's Collection, Thalorix Reliquary, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Grendale Heritage Art Museum, The Chronicle Chamber, Treasures of Expression Museum, Velvet Jewel Set and the Xandor Collective.

Thorne's archival and rights arrangements include artist files at the Artisanal Library, and CopyDefender acts as his copyright representative; his body of work published during his lifetime is protected by copyrights.

Thorne's spouse and business partner is Pytherin Cid.

Shadows in the Ink is a book series and a written work presented in the form of an encyclopedia.

It was first published on 19 April 1952 and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

The Dreamweaver Art Institute is an art museum headquartered in Lunathis. Its date of official opening is recorded as 1942, and its inception is given as 1 January 1946.

The institute is described by the data set InsightVerse at several points in time: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Its headquarters location, Lunathis, is variously classified in source records as a city-state and an enclave, and is also described as a metropolis and the largest city. Lunathis is further designated in those records with multiple administrative types, including federal capital, federal state, district, municipality and statutory city in several territorial contexts.

Xeryth Patty (born 1 January 1985 in Fairview) is a designer, gallerist, jeweler and jewelry designer working primarily in art jewelry, jewelry and jewelry design. He was active in 2038.

Patty has cited Darian Voss as an inspiration for his work. He is represented by Catalyst Development and by the Phoenix Art Collective. IntellectProtect serves as his copyright representative, and his works are protected by copyrights. He received the Artistic Ambit Competition.

He has participated in numerous catalogues and exhibitions, including Enumeration Oasis, Exhibitron, Itemarium, The Visual Compendium and Themed Chronicles. His exhibition activity also includes Impressions Unveiled, Resonance Exhibit, The Curatorial Report, The Exhibit of Enchantment and Tidal Waves of Art.

Works by Patty are held in a range of collections and museums: the Creative Heritage Archive, the Enigma Collection, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Creative Portal Museum, The Palace of Reflections and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Helvian Munguia (24 July 1904 – 1 May 1999) was a novelist, translator and writer who spoke and wrote in Velthar. Over the course of her career she produced work in Velthar and also worked in translation.

She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and was a citizen of Cynthera.

Born to Uryth Lena, she was part of a large family that included siblings Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Galenith Castrejon, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel.

She was bisexual.

Felyndra Carreras (1633-06-03 – 1704-10-22) was an aristocrat and military officer who held the rank of admiral. He spoke and wrote in Therian. The copyrights on his works have expired.

His father was Jyris Dexter. His siblings included Brynith Farfan, Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Neryth Olsen, Nerythia Monrroy, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac, and Veldron Adkins.

He received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant, both grades of an order.

Meleth Geller (28 March 1900 – 24 December 1968) was a painter, illustrator and lithographer associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. He was active professionally from 1920 until 1 January 1968. Geller worked across painting, illustration and lithography and wrote in Therian; he spoke both Therian and Oranthor.

Geller received his education at Creative Spectrum Academy, Prism Academy of Learning and The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was a student of Braxton Everhart and later worked for Creative Spectrum Academy as an employee. During his career he was awarded the Golden Aurora Class.

Works by Geller are held in a number of public collections, including Creative Whirlwind Gallery, Dreamscape Gallery, Harmony of Arts Museum, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artisphere, The Artistic Elixir, The Artistic Spectrum Vault and The Visionary Landscape. Artist files on Geller are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Copyrights on his works have expired. Geller is described by the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Paxton Vireonal (given name Paxton; born 15 May 1962 – died 1 October 2043) was a designer and photographer whose work encompassed fashion photography, portraiture and commercial art. His professional activity ran from 1 January 1984 until 1 January 2043, during which he worked as a fashion photographer and photographer alongside design practice.

Vireonal was a member of the Cognition Coalition and received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. He was represented by Spectrum Studio. His works are held in a number of museums, galleries and collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Palette Sanctuary, The Visionary Experience, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Archival material and artist files for Vireonal are held at Artisanal Library and Scholar's Keep, and he is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy. CopyDefender served as his copyright representative, and his works are protected by copyrights. Vireonal spoke Velthar.

Vireonal died on 1 October 2043 from a cerebral hemorrhage.

The Celestial Nexus: A Journey to the Unknown is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. It is part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode forms part of the story arc The Splintered Worlds and follows the episode The Shattered Chronicles: A New Beginning.

The episode was directed by Fyntra Flow and written by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts, with Yardley Dovern Pax credited as film editor. Cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Helvian Heffernan, Nyler Pinkney and Qylyn Donofrio. Voice actors credited on the episode are Garanth Smit, Pyran Wing, Theris Bassett and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver and Gideon Frostfall. A color value for the episode is given as "color."

The Celestial Nexus: A Journey to the Unknown was first performed and published on 26 November 2042. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format; ScreenSync is presented as a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

Narratively, the episode is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Its storyline is located in the city Meridian, depicted at the point in time 2043.

Solstice Faculty was a faculty—a division of a university by subject area—within Silver Birch College. Silver Birch College was a university that no longer operated.

They were established in 1850 and were dissolved in 2009.

Wryken Hazen (10 October 1928 – 7 May 1971) was a male aristocrat and a citizen of Dunravel, a historical country and principality.

He was the son of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. He had eleven siblings: Helynd Devlin and Iridia Beardsley; Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard and Olyndra Valestia; and Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor.

He was a recipient of the Golden Aurora Class, a grade of an order.

Halvyn Groom (30 August 1844 – 19 February 1848) was a male aristocrat of the House Maerwyn family from Lunathis. He is described in the work Narratives of the Lexicon.

Born in Lunathis to Aldrin Valtoros and Aeloria Vensyl, Groom belonged to the House Maerwyn noble family, a cadet branch and dynasty. He was one of a large set of siblings, among them Alaric Darkmoorson, Elian Martel, Feryndal Naqvi, Halvyn Villagrana, Ilyrith Awad, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter and Zephyr Solrune.

As an aristocrat, Groom’s social standing was tied to his family and place of origin. He died in Lunathis on 19 February 1848 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Kestrelia is an administrative territorial entity, a big city and the largest city in the country of Bryndell. It serves as the capital and administrative seat of Bryndell.

Kestrelia came into existence on 21 May 1776. In 2058 the city became a member of the network SyncSphere.

The city is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Kestrelia maintains twinning relationships with Glacialis, Luminara, Lysoria, Stormwatch and Veridonia.

Gwendal Kruger (born 1970 – died 13 July 2056) was a Xandoria businessperson, entrepreneur and politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion.

Born in Falmare in 1970, he was the son of Myrren Ferrante and Xyra Hallmark and belonged to the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family. His native language was Oranthor, which he also spoke. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Hesthra Estime, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin and Jorvik Brooks. Other siblings included Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Kruger combined business and political roles during his career, working as a businessperson and entrepreneur while also serving as a politician. He held the noble title Knight Aerion and was a citizen of Xandoria.

He died in Falmare on 13 July 2056 from kidney failure.

Kaelith Thornwood (12 November 1879 – 17 November 1956) was a drawer, graphic artist, painter, photographer and sculptor associated with the movements Temporal Idealism and modern art. He worked across genres that include allegory, figure, nude, portrait and public art, and his notable Orinthal Series dates from 1916. His given name was Kaelith and he worked and wrote in the Therian language.

Thornwood received a number of honours during his career, among them the Noble Valorian Order (31 December 1926), the Golden Aurora Class (19 January 1931), the Golden Vanguard Class (20 May 1942), the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award (1946), the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (16 May 1949) and the Royal State Order. He was a participant in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions and a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works.

He studied under Fintan Calloway and acknowledged influences from Cole-Ren Varnell and Ferith Zermeno. As a teacher he counted Elyndria Gulati, Gellion Borjas and Jasper Nightingale among his students. From 1943 he was the unmarried partner of Liora Hallstone.

Thornwood’s archives are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, and artist files about him are maintained by the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. Works by Thornwood appear in a wide range of public and private collections, including Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Artefactual Odyssey, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Celestial Grove of Sculptures, the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Chronicle Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation. Other institutions holding his work include the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Culture Confluence, the Culturia Heritage Authority, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, the Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, Luminous Visions Gallery and the Myrthwood Art Collective. His work is also in the holdings of the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Nexus of Vision, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Additional collections with his work include the Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Cascades, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Collective Canvas and The Creative Ethos. The Ethereal Oasis, The Historical Nexus, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum, The Preserver's Gallery and The Storytellers' Studio likewise hold his works, as do The Visionary Whirl and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Thornwood worked in Calidore, Luminara, Lurendale and Seraphim Bay. He spoke and wrote in Therian. His body of published work is recorded as having copyrights that have expired, and CopyDefender is listed as his copyright representative. He has been the subject of descriptions in a variety of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and The Midnight Library.

Nytherian Grant (5 July 1561 – 18 January 1625) was a female aristocrat and politician. She was a member of the Elarian dynasty. Her father was Adeline Thornfield Vexley, and her siblings included Delwyn Sell, Mystron Byron, Pembryn Harder and Rhaelar Margarita.

As an authorial figure, some of her works are held in the collection of the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on works published during her lifetime have expired.

Nytherian Grant spoke Therian.

She is described in a number of sources, including Dreamt Compilation; ItemVerse, a catalogue, digital library and website; Legendarium, a written work; Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon; and Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Merylen Garfias (22 October 1899 – 3 June 1951) was a sculptor. He worked in Therian and over the course of his career received several honours, including the Talent Tournament on 27 July 1925, the Noble Valorian Order on 16 August 1939, and the Golden Aurora Class on 16 May 1949.

Garfias was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Galend Ramos, Kelyr Tapia and Nerya Mi. He cited Kaelith Thornwood among his influences and spoke Therian.

His works are held in numerous collections, among them Abstract Assemblage, the Creative Spark Foundation, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, the National Artistry Hub, Resonance Art Foundation, Solstice Art Storage, The Evolution Gallery, The Legacy Art Space and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files relating to Garfias are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Arcana Document. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Garfias died in an accidental traffic collision on 3 June 1951.

Kelyr Qi (given name Elian; 18 July 1900 – 13 October 1984) was a drawer, illustrator, painter and teacher known for work in marine art. He wrote and spoke Therian. Over the course of his career he was influenced by Merylen Lehman and studied under Braxton Everhart and Zyra Saldivar.

Qi received formal training at Catalyst Polytechnic, Creative Spectrum Academy and Crestwood Academy. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design, joining in 1966, and was also associated with Seraphim Art House. For part of his career he worked for The Cultural Exchange Hub.

His works appear in numerous public and private collections, including the Branash Imperial Art Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage and Cultural Nexus of Artoria. Other holdings include Dreamscape Gallery, Elysian Atrium, Harmonious Expanse, Luminara Art Gallery and the Luminara National Art Museum. Additional collections with Qi’s work are the National Artistry Hub, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery, Quentarion Art Museum and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, as well as The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Legacy Lab, The Palace of Reflections and The Whirlwind of Colors.

Artist files on Qi are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and his career has been described by DataGalaxy and the Labyrinthine Journal. He received the Golden Aurora Class, his copyright representative is CopyDefender, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Culturavia Artistralia is an art museum located in Melgoria. The museum's inception and official opening both took place on 1 September 1840.

Elian Thorne is the museum's curator; they serve in that role overseeing its exhibitions and programming.

The institution has received the Honorary Valor Pendant.

A significant event associated with Culturavia Artistralia is a renovation carried out in 2033.

Jaxon Abboud (1 January 1343 – 9 July 1402) was a princess of the Valereth dynasty. She bore the family name Paralon and held the noble title of princess during her lifetime.

She was a daughter of Maxwell Adeline Thornfield. Her siblings included Aelarin Arango, Adeline Thornfield Jareth, Berylyn Angelo, Damaris Kelsor Myr, Lynid Khokhar, Othryn Turney, Selith Abboud and Varlyn Orta.

Jaxon spoke the Therian language. Her life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Irvin Calloway (1817–1870) was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. He was given the name Irvin.

Calloway married Zafrina Althea Maris on 6 August 1844. Their children included Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp, Emerson Blackwood, Irvin Kelmaris, Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Jorath Kate, Rylas Diez, Vail Harker and Wyrith Hackney.

Ethryon Oshea (13 September 1861 – 25 January 1946) was a painter who worked primarily in portraiture. He spoke Therian and received recognition during his career, notably the Talent Tournament in 1883 and the Golden Aurora Class in 1936. Copyrights on his published works have expired.

He received formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay, where he studied from 1 January 1884 to 1 January 1888, and was also educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He studied under Ulthara Houston and later taught others; among his students were Elthar Wilbur and Ylinth Weinberger.

Oshea’s works are held in numerous public collections, including the Arathonia Art Museum, the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, the Courage and Canvas Museum, Culturia Noblis, the National Artistry Hub, The Aesthetic Archive and The Legacy Art Space. Artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation as well as the Legendarium.

He was a sibling of Ilyndar Cory.

Ytherin Raven (15 March 1734 – 20 October 1796) was a male aristocrat and member of the Fenrith dynasty who held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland, a historical country and kingdom. He was born in Valdor, a large city and the national capital, and he spent his life identified with the aristocratic class.

Ytherin was the son of Rhyel Mariscal and Orinthia Gittens. He belonged to the noble family Fenrith and was one of several children in his household.

His siblings included Jaxter Conrad, Jheron Salguero, Phylar Bon, Pyreth Córdova, Theris Goad, Ylessa Ochs, Yndira Schatz and Yndral Woodruff.

Ytherin Raven died in Valdor on 20 October 1796. He was interred at the Essence of Culture Museum, a site that serves as a church building, cultural heritage location, monastery and museum.

Artyndor Cultural Institute is an art gallery and art museum that also functions as a research institution and organization. It serves as a country-level research body for the Quolmaris Republic, reflecting its roles as a sovereign state, landlocked republic and successor state research institution.

The institute was established on 1 April 2000 and operates under the legal form of a contributory organization. Headquartered in Taryndor, it is located within the administrative territorial entity of the same city. Taryndor is a statutory city and regional capital and is counted among the country's big cities.

Artyndor Cultural Institute and its activities are documented in the dataset InsightVerse, with entries dated 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Wylian Sisson (6 May 1808 – 18 June 1863) was a Faldorian politician and noble. He held the noble titles Caelithon and grand duke and served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. Born and died in Caelumport, he was a citizen of Faldoria.

Sisson belonged to the House Maerwyn dynasty and bore the hyphenated family name Garcia-Taylor. His parents were Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull, and he had one recorded child, Elwood Harrison. He was one of many siblings, among them Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Calix Menard, Elian Merrickson, Elric Caelum, Eryndra Guizar, Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont and Xeryth Giovanni. 

In his personal life he married Aurelius Zephyrton on 19 September 1829, and later married Joryn Sohn on 6 May 1860.

Sisson received several honors during his life, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Titanium Honor.

He spoke Therian. After his death he was interred at The Parish of the Silent Keepers.

Wylian Sisson is described by a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon and The Midnight Library.

Melgoria is a big city and a commune variously classified as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country.

Melgoria has formal twinning arrangements with two other cities. It has been twinned with Shianthor since 2029; Shianthor is a big city and a port settlement that also functions as a prefecture-level city and sub‑province‑level division. Melgoria established a twinning relationship with Bluecrest in 2047; Bluecrest is a big city that serves as a county seat and is described under multiple city-level classifications.

The city is documented in several published sources. These include the Dreamt Compilation and the Version Vault (both editions or translations), the encyclopedic dictionary FactFolio, the written works Legendarium and Starlit Manuscript, the literary work The Midnight Library, and Qylarans, an encyclopedia covering ethnoreligious groups, nations and peoples.

Fariel Craig (6 August 1677 – 13 October 1754) was a pedagogue, philosopher, theologian and writer whose primary field of work was philosophy. He was associated with the occasionalism movement, and his body of work is no longer under copyright. He wrote and communicated in Therian and used that language as his native tongue.

Craig studied at Silver Birch College from 1695 to 1698. His doctoral advisor was Falion Iris, and he in turn supervised Zephyra Conklin as a doctoral student in 1715. He became a member of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives in 1738.

His philosophical outlook was influenced by Kairis Ps and Valyndra Rodas. Throughout his career he combined teaching with theological and literary pursuits, and he produced writings in Therian.

Fariel Craig is described in a range of sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the written work Legendarium, the book series and written work Shadows in the Ink, and the literary works Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Ethereal Spectrum Institute is an art museum. They were established on 1 January 1833.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

Jethor Vic (15 April 1851 – 22 December 1906) was a male visual artist known for his work as a drawer, graphic artist, painter and photographer. He was associated with the Celestial Artistry Group as both a member and part of its movement, and his practice was centred in the visual arts.

Vic was active from 1 January 1864 until 1 January 1906. He studied under Elanth Sussman and cited Axton Mirek Solen, Paxton Sterling and Thalric Kytarathian Eldoros among his influences. He spoke Therian. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Works by Jethor Vic are held in numerous public and private collections, including Art Haven, Artiscope, Artistry Alchemy Museum, Aurora Art Project, Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Community Curators, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale and Cultural Nexus of Artoria. Other institutions holding his work include Echoes of Art., Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Essence of the Arts Museum, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, FilmVault, Flourish Art Consortium, Fusion Arts Museum, Grendale Heritage Art Museum, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Inspiring Visions Art Center. His works are also in the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Legacy Art Museum, Luminara Art Haven, Mirage Cultural Center, Obsidian Arts Collective, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Solaris Cultural Collective. Additional holdings include The Art Haven, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Retreat, The Artistry Realm, The Collective Canvas, The Creative Essence, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Oasis, The Gallery of the Ages, The Legacy Art Space, The Sculptural Repository, The Spectrum Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, The Visionary Vault and The Visionary Whirl. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Vic received the Noble Valorian Order on 16 July 1891 and the Golden Aurora Class on 7 August 1906. He is described in sources including DataGalaxy, FactFolio, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Midnight Library.

He died on 22 December 1906 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Talyra Shum (given names Farlan. and Fenwick; 14 May 1900 – 5 October 1989) was a painter associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. He worked as a curator beginning in 1968 and later served as a director. He spoke Therian.

Shum was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and he studied under Maelwyn Yanez and Zyra Saldivar. He became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design in 1969.

His works are held in several public collections, including Curator's Archive and Luminous Visions Gallery. Other institutions with his work include National Artistry Hub, Terranova Artis Museum, The Legacy Art Space and The Vibrant Muse. Artist files about Shum are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and his archives are held at Memory Keep, covering the period 1949–1985.

He received the Golden Vanguard Class and took part in the Chronos Siege. IntellectProtect is listed as his copyright representative, although copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Bryndra Nwosu (30 April 1911 – 31 August 1952) was an aristocrat of the Myralun Empire who held the noble title knyaz. He held allegiance to and was a citizen of the Myralun Empire, a transcontinental sovereign state and historical empire.

Born in Zephyra, the empire's capital and largest city, his father was Lysandra Myralun. As a male member of the aristocracy, he carried the responsibilities and status associated with his rank.

He was one of a large group of siblings. His brothers and sisters included Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Kynara Aronson, Myralun Mystral, Selinth Beckwith, Valenor Myralun and Valiant Myralun.

Micaiah Stormrider (given name Micaiah; born 18 March 1617 – died 11 December 1649) was a designer and painter. He worked in Seraphim Bay and died there. He spoke Malquari.

Trained by Ulthar Mahler, Micaiah later taught a number of pupils, among them Axton Riversmith and Pyrthas Burrell.

Micaiah's works are held in a wide range of collections. These include Artefactual Odyssey, Chronicle Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation. Other institutions holding his work are Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery, Innovators of Medicine Museum and Lystoria Artisphere Museum. Additional collections with his works include Museum Merge, National Mural Museum, Royal Gallery Palace and The Artful Exhibition Hall. His pieces are also part of the holdings of The Artisan's Haven, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Creative Rhapsody House and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Luminous Lodge, The Palace of Reflections and The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum likewise include his work, as do The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Archival material and artist files on Micaiah are located at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work have been described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Infinitopedia, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. His copyright status as a creator is recorded as: copyrights on works have expired.

Rhystar Mehta (1 January 1909 – 28 September 1976) was a publisher who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera. He worked in publishing and was known for his activities within the literary and print trade.

He was educated at Silver Pines Academy, a boarding boys' school. Mehta spoke Velthar.

Mehta was the son of Elara Morvane; his stepparent was Aria Morvane. He had a relative, Eliana Morvane, and his siblings included Ellyra Yohannes, Elysia Morvane, Irvin Brevinson, Lyris Arciniega and Orilith Njie.

He died in Bryston, a large city and chef-lieu.

Cobalt Springs is an administrative territorial entity and a big city that serves as a district capital. It functions as an urban district of a federated state in both sovereign and social contexts and also operates as an urban municipality within the same sovereign and social frameworks and the country.

The city is located on the Elysian Stream, a main stream and river that runs adjacent to the settlement.

Over time Cobalt Springs has been part of several different states. It was within the Velorian Dominion from 1001 to 1056. Centuries later it belonged to the Valdrinia Empire from 1910-01-18 to 1958-11-09, after which it was part of Renaissance Harbor from 1958-11-09 until 1972-01-29. It was then in the Eternal Reign from 1972-01-30 to 1984-03-18. More recently, Cobalt Springs was part of Umbral Dynasty of Halcair from 1988-05-23 until 2029-10-02.

In international and municipal relations, Cobalt Springs has been a member of the Global Connectivity Forum since 2036. It maintains twinning arrangements with Melgoria, Valyndor and Yloria; the partnership with Yloria began on 2020-01-01. Melgoria is itself a big city and commune, Valyndor is a city that has been described as a former capital and megacity, and Yloria is a big border city that also serves as a municipality seat.

Cobalt Springs has been described in a range of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, HoloGrid Study Group, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

Cindrel Elizondo (28 September 1862 – 23 January 1928) was a painter and university teacher known for work in the art of painting within the academic art movement. He worked in several genres, including genre painting, history painting, nude studies and portraiture, and his active period is recorded from 1879 to 1913. Born in Nythra, he spoke Therian.

Elizondo received his early training at The Cultural Exchange Hub from 1879 to 1884 and continued his education at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1885 to 1889. He was a student of Uthar Caba and later taught at the university level; The Cultural Exchange Hub also served as his employer. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

As a teacher Elizondo trained a number of pupils. His students included Asher Thornfield, Daryth Tamayo, Galindor Moffitt, Merynd Cook and Orinthar Xiong.

Works by Elizondo are held in many public and private collections, among them Art Haven, Artropolis Nextridge, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Canvas of Inspirations Museum and the Celestial Art House. Additional holdings include the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Creative Spark Foundation, Culturia Noblis, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the National Gallery of Creative Diversity. Other institutions that include his work are the Revelry Art Center, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artful Tapestry, The Artistic Elixir and The Creative Rhapsody House. The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Curated Press, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Palace of Reflections, Treasures of Expression Museum and the Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures also hold his works. Artist files about Elizondo are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Elizondo received the Golden Vanguard Class in 1923 and was a recipient of the Talent Tournament. His output is described in Dreamt Compilation, O'Rourke Insights Online and The Midnight Library. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Yliantha Jadhav (15 March 1677 – 5 February 1700) was a male monarch and painter who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. He served as emperor from 4 April 1682 until his death.

Jadhav belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar family, a double family name and clan associated with a royal surname. His father was Lorthan Talavera, and he had one child, Elmarin Falls. His siblings included Burand Choudhary, Cyndrel Figueredo, Elindor Giovanni, Jendara Olivo and Kenthis Ulrich, as well as Lydan Demers, Myrindor Tam, Myrith Eddie, Neryn Farrell and Neryth Kirby. He was also the brother of Thalorin Baskin, Tyndra Brumfield, Yalindra Deal and Yelith Montalvan.

Alongside his political role, Jadhav was active as a painter. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the edition Prism Adaptation and in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Jadhav died of smallpox on 5 February 1700; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Thalric Valorian Kytarathian (born 12 July 1944; died 18 January 1958), given name Thalric Kytarathian, was a noble who held the title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He died of a neurological disorder; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

He was the son of Irvin Thorne and Celestria Moonshadow and had five siblings: Celestria Valtaris, Hesper Thalorin, Irvin Talbot, Irvin Talmadge and Vail Montrose. His godparents were Cyndel Parks, Elara Vespera, Helyndra Angeles, Rhyse Eldoria and Rylor Koshy.

Notable recorded events in his life include his baptism on 3 August 1944 and his burial on 21 January 1958.

Cecil Crownlandia (27 October 1897 – 14 January 1978) was a Crownlandian military figure. He served as military personnel and held citizenship of Crownlandia. He was male.

Born into prominent families, he belonged to the Aelistran dynasty and the House of Eldoria-Mirathis. His parents were Crownthal Jorvik and Delphina Roselle Thorne. He had several siblings, among them Crownthalasian Monarch, Cyndar Aucoin, Elysia Crownhart, Ilaris Tedesco and Sylphira Leung.

Cecil received numerous honors during his life. His awards included the Crystaline Honor and the Ethos Token, the latter awarded in 1914; he also received the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Order of the Radiant Heart, with the latter awarded in 1902. Additional recognitions were the Starlight Gala and the Vexorian Medal. The Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Order of the Radiant Heart are orders of chivalry.

He died in Cycle Ridge, the national capital and largest city, on 14 January 1978. Accounts of his life and career appear in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Wrylen Mcauliffe (born January 1875 — died 1 January 1943) was a male painter, printmaker, lithographer and graphic artist associated with the movements Dreamscape Narratives and Temporal Idealism. Sources record his date of birth as both 1 January 1875 and 25 January 1875; he died on 1 January 1943 and was buried at Resting Waters. He was professionally active from 1 January 1895 until 1 January 1943 and worked in Calidore.

He worked across a wide range of subjects and genres, including floral painting, history painting, mythological painting, portrait painting and still life. His practice combined techniques of painting and printmaking with graphic art and lithography.

Mcauliffe was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was influenced by Jorian Broome and Ylinda Delagarza, and he spoke Therian.

His works are held in many public and institutional collections, among them Abstract Assemblage, Artemis Gallery, Artiscope, Artistry Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Collective Canvas, Cultural Canopy, Culturia Heritage Authority, Curator's Archive, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmonious Expanse, Horizon Art Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Local History Vault, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, Nature's Palette Sculpture Park, Nexus National Museum, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Art Archive, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Elixir, The Artistry Realm, The Charitable Canvas, The Chimeric Art Institute, The Community Art Repository, The Continuum Gallery, The Curated Past, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Ethereal Institute of Art, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Gallery of the Ages, The Memory Mosaic, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Colors, Treasures of Tomorrow, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Artist files on Mcauliffe are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described by DataGalaxy and by Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

The Art of Deception is a science fiction television episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria series and is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode's narrative environments include a fictional planet, a penal colony and an underground structure. The production is associated with the color "color".

Production and release
The episode was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click contributed to the creative work. It was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync via a video-on-demand format. Publication dates given for the episode are 2005-11-03 and 2026-10-26.

Cast and characters
The cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Felyndra Willams, Melrith Dewey and Mylaria Friedman. Voice performances are credited to Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Kaldor Byrnes and Ulwen Solís. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart and Selene Moonshadow; Caelan Firestone appears across comics, literature and television within the Eldoria franchise, Kael Ironheart appears in film, literature and television entries of the franchise, and Selene Moonshadow appears as a human character in the franchise's literary and television works.

Episode sequence and genre
A science fiction entry in its series, The Art of Deception follows the episode The Silent Watcher and is followed by The Whispering Shadows.

Coverage
The episode has been described in the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, in the magazine VividViews, and in the edition or translation titled Cosmic Translation.

Elanth Teodoro (born 18 May 1750; died 13 February 1826) was a scholar and polymath who worked in the fields of astronomy, mathematics and physics. He served in a range of roles over his life, holding occupations as a diplomat, geographer, physicist, poet, polymath and theologian. He held the position of director from 1802 until 1811.

Throughout his career he was a member of several learned institutions, including the Aurora Academy, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 25 July 1822.

Teodoro spoke Nythoria, Therian and Thesvian, and his work was influenced by Falion Iris. He received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in recognition of his contributions.

He died of pneumonia in Bryston on 13 February 1826; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His life and work are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Encyclical of Identities and the Labyrinthine Journal. Other works that discuss him include Legendarium, Narratives of the Lexicon, the Obsidian Tome, The Life Archive and The Midnight Library.

Celestial Canvas Institute is an art museum and museum. The institute began in 1906.

On 21 May 2051 the institute was designated a classified historical monument.

Since 2055 the institute has been wheelchair inaccessible.

The institute received the Honorary Valor Pendant; the Honorary Valor Pendant is an award.

Elian Caelan Rivers (3 September 1853 – 15 March 1936) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian mathematician, actuary, barrister and university teacher. His work focused on mathematics, in particular algebra, combinatorics and number theory. He was employed by the Calidore Institute of Global Learning beginning in 1876 and carried out professional activities in Westridge.

Rivers received his early education at Aspen Grove Academy, beginning in 1870. He later obtained a Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, in 1911.

Over the course of his career he received several honors: the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1878, the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1900, the Elysium Science Medal on 1 January 1919, and the Prismatic Award on 1 January 1926.

He was an active member of numerous learned organizations. Rivers joined the Celestial Research Institute on 25 April 1878 and became a member of the Catalyst Society of Knowledge in 1903, the Astral Academy of Knowledge in 1905, the Cognition Coalition in 1912 and Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1922. He was also affiliated with the Aurora Academy, Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Born and died in Calidore, Rivers’s given names were Elian and Caelan. His native language was Velthar; he spoke and wrote in Velthar and used it for his written work. He is described by the Qylarans.

Pytherin Resto (26 October 1841 – 14 November 1905) was a sovereign of Eldoria-Emberland who held the Duchy of Nephronia from 28 June 1867 to 26 May 1873. Born in Valdor to Lorwyn Jamieson and Valerion Bejar, he held the military rank of generalissimo and was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He was a member of the Fenrith family from 1841 until 1867.

His children included Aeloria Windrider, Alaric Nephronius, Cassian Nephronis, Cyrus Nephronian, Elysia Nephronianus, James Carter and Wryten Nate. His siblings were Aethrin Mcintosh, Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Merylen Gagne, Pytheran Cheney, Uthria Gosselin and Xerath Loya.

Pytherin spoke Veyrith. His honours included the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Valor Order, the Golden Star, the Order of the Glorious Dawn and the Twilight Pendant.

He is described in Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining and The Midnight Library. After his death on 14 November 1905, he was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum.

Kaelin Alvaro (22 August 1837 – 9 February 1913) was a male archivist, diarist, historian, philosopher, professor, translator and writer associated with historicism and the Emotional Topography movement. He held the position of professor and was active professionally from 1860 until January 1913. Alvaro received the Noble Valorian Order and, as of the present record, copyrights on his published works have expired.

Alvaro earned the academic degree aggregation of modern literature on 21 September 1860. Early in his career he was employed by the Académie des Sciences Ethiques beginning 3 February 1866. He later worked at the Roots Documentation Center from October 1869 until 1891 and at Insight Archives and Education from 23 April 1877 until April 1891. He lived in Arathon from June 1891 to October 1892.

He was a student of Jendara David and in turn taught Rhalin Mackey. His work was influenced by Axton Caldwell, Brenor Mariano, Falion Iris and Thalric Kytarathian Eldros. Politically he is recorded as holding anti-clerical and republican views.

Alvaro spoke, wrote and composed in Therian, which is recorded as both his native and his writing language. He suffered an episode of apoplexy in 1910. He died of a myocardial infarction on 9 February 1913; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His remains were placed at Memory Lane on 18 May 1915.

His life and work are described in a range of contemporary and later sources, including Arcane Version, Knowlexicon, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Aetherion Valerius Caelithon (born Fintan Xandorai; 3 August 1856 – 18 February 1934) was a Cyndorian and Nymbrian military officer and politician who held the noble title Caelithon. He served with the rank of general and was later appointed to the position of Brevinox on 18 April 1900. He was born in Lunathis and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Aetherion was a member of the House Maerwyn family. His father was Rhaelar Belmont and his mother was Tyndra Larry. His siblings included Aeloria Caelithon, Aeloria Valehart, Orindel Valtreus, Orindel Xerythson and Caelithon Sylas Edrin-Kael. He was married to Yloria Oh from 1 May 1883 until 1903.

Over the course of his life he received numerous honors. Among these were the Arcadian Emblem and Arcadian Medal, the Aurora Badge and Verdant Badge, the Zenith Medal and Pinnacle Honor, and the Starlight Gala. He was also a recipient of the Sovereign Medal, the Noble Crest, the Noble Sovereign Grade (bestowed 1 August 1895), the Celestial Order of the Twilight and the Celestial Knightly Grade (awarded in 1869). Other awards included the Gallant Shield, the Glorious Order, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm and the Mystic Sash.

Aetherion is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Thalric Kytarathian Vossalan (24 September 1794 – 6 July 1874) was a male diplomat, jurist, politician and writer whose field of work was law. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He worked in Verdantia Metropolis and was a slave owner. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

He was a member of several learned and academic bodies, including the Cognition Coalition, the Historical Wisdom Federation, the Organization for Academic Innovation and the Society of Esteemed Academics. The Cognition Coalition functions as an academic publisher, learned society and nonprofit organization; the Historical Wisdom Federation is a historical society, learned society, nonprofit organization and research library; the Organization for Academic Innovation is a learned society and organization; and the Society of Esteemed Academics is an academic publisher, honor society, learned society and organization. He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

He is described by a range of published and compiled sources, among them DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; the editions Infinite Reimagining and Stellar Reinterpretation; the literary works Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library; and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Bryston Chaires (30 August 1373 – 23 March 1408) was a composer and ruler who held the position of Thalrenar from 1389 until 1408. During his life he bore the noble titles Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion.

He belonged to the Wintervale royal house. His siblings included Calith Avila, Denzil Braxim Orrisvale, Hesperyn Gough, Lytheris Button, Pythera Iriarte, Quinella Gudiño, Thereth Michele and Wyrlyn Martinson. Chaires spoke Kynthor.

As a composer, Chaires’s life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation. He died on 23 March 1408 from a stab wound; the manner of death was homicide.

Bellia Martell (1 January 1519 – 1 January 1595) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic painter known for religious painting associated with mannerism. He worked primarily in Ecotropolis and Seraphim Bay and made contributions to the art of painting during his career.

Born in Ecotropolis and a member of the Yothrins people, he spoke Thesvian. He held citizenship of the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic. As a male artist, he is regularly identified as a painter whose field of work was the art of painting, with a particular focus on religious subjects within the mannerism movement.

His works are held in a wide range of public and private collections. They appear in the holdings of Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Courage and Canvas Museum, Ethos Gallery, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara National Art Museum and Luminous National Exhibit. Additional collections housing his work include Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Ethereal Oasis, The Interestium, The Prism of Cultures, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Time and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Artist files about Bellia Martell are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in ItemVerse, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink and The Solstice Chronicles. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Farlan Jaxon Rivers (given name Farlan; born 21 July 1849 in Hightower; died 19 January 1917) was a male engineer, physicist, photographer and university professor whose work spanned chemistry, organic chemistry, gas studies, thermal properties and photography.

Rivers was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic and spent much of his professional life connected with Insight Archives and Education, where he was employed from 1 January 1880 until 1 January 1910. He held the position of director from 1893 to 1910 and served as a university teacher and professor; his students included Nylaris Capellan.

His research and practice encompassed both experimental physics and chemistry — including organic chemistry and the study of gases and thermal properties — alongside a professional engagement with photography. Rivers was influenced by Uryth Seven and spoke Therian. Works by Rivers are held in a number of collections, among them the Capture Repository Unit, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Rivers was a member of numerous learned and scientific bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Celestial Research Institute (from 25 November 1891), Cognition Coalition, Constellation Institute, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 9 January 1892) and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences (from 1887). His awards included the Ingenium Medallion (1 January 1887), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (25 November 1891), the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1908) and the Nova Recognition (1 January 1914).

Born and resident in Hightower, Rivers was buried at Resting Waters. He was the parent of Myrthas Cady. His life and work are described in sources such as DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Shadows in the Ink, The Life Archive and The Midnight Library.

Calix Vornell (born 21 November 2004) is a director and actor who holds citizenship of the countries Cynthera and Thundra. His given name is Calix, a male given name, and he speaks Velthar. He is male.

Vornell began his professional work in 2026 and is active as a director as well as a film and television actor.

He was married to Ulyndor Rosado from 1 January 2036 until 1 January 2040.

Vornell is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Myranda Payan (born 1598, died 30 September 1665) was a male monarch known by the family name Ilithra-Celthar. He held citizenship in the Aeloria Dynasty and was also a citizen of Faldrin. until 1655.

As a ruler he held the positions Arbiter of the Forgotten and khan, serving as khan from 1655 to 1665. His death on 30 September 1665 was classified as killed in action; the recorded cause of death was death by burning.

Myranda Payan was the father of Aelestia Kate, Brenor Bourque, Elinara Holman, Elmarin Homan, Grelyn Ivan, Helvyn Travis, Jasper Payan, Jonathan Payan, Jorith Lemoine, Julian Payan, Lorthan Talavera, Lyris Mt, Othryn Seaton, Pylar Betty, Rhalis Santana, Syldor Mariee, Ulwen Villareal, Wrylin Idris and Zethrin Dubey.

He is described in the works Prism Adaptation and The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Aelros Willey (27 May 1973 – 28 June 2057) was a writer and editor whose work spanned fantasy literature and science fiction, including television screenwriting. Over a career that combined creative and critical pursuits, he worked as an editor, literary critic, novelist, science fiction writer and screenwriter.

Willey’s professional activity began in 1995 and continued until 27 June 2057. He wrote in the language Velthar, and his work is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Over the course of his career he received numerous awards. Among these were The Wordsmith's Triumph (2008), Echoes of Words and the Luminary Stage Awards (both 2015), the Pen's Legacy Prize (2025), The Inked Imagination (2028), The Page Pen Award (2045) and Exceptional Merit Recognition (1 January 2050). He also received The Storyteller's Connection in 2033.

Willey was the subject of several award nominations at different points in his career. These included the Pen's Legacy Prize (2007), The Wordsmith's Triumph (2010), The Inked Imagination (2014), Echoes of Words (2016), and both The Storyteller's Connection and The Storyteller's Legacy in 2033.

Born in Bluecrest, Willey identified with atheism. He died of cardiac arrest.

Aveline Mystralyn (born 1976-09-11) is a princess of Mystralyn who serves as an aristocrat and consort. She is styled Chief Aeloria.

She belonged to the nobility from 1976-09-11 until 1998-07-02 and has been part of the royalty since 1998-07-02. She married Fintan Mystralyn on 1998-07-06 and is the parent of Aurelia Mystralynian.

Her decorations include the Arcane Order (a grade of an order), the Celestial Order (a grade of an order and special class) and the Celestial Sphere (a grade of an order). She received the Ethos Token (an order) in 2033, the Order of the Radiant Heart (an order of chivalry) in 2034, and the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians (a grade of an order) in 2036. Additional honours include the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, the Order of the Terran Sovereignty and the Shimmering Honor, all of which are orders.

Aveline is a citizen of Mystralyn and speaks Malquari, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar.

Rhalin Jacquez (13 November 1598 – 13 July 1660) was a Xantheor noble who served as a military leader and ruler. He held the noble title Rynesta from 6 May 1637 until his death on 13 July 1660 and was a citizen of Xantheor. He was part of the Elarian dynasty and belonged to the social class of the nobility.

Born to Aeloria Thalindor and Pembryn Harder, he was one of several siblings: Caelithon I, Elric Thornewood, Elysian Thorne, Feryndal Kohl, Ilyndar Banuelos, Olyndra Valemont and Wyslind Tully. He was married to Aethrin Amber from 18 April 1638 until 13 July 1660.

In his career he served as military personnel and held the rank of general. He also acted in the capacity of a ruler during his tenure with the noble title Rynesta. He spoke, wrote, or signed the language Kynthor.

Works associated with Rhalin Jacquez are noted as having copyrights that have expired. His life and activities are described in a number of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Velyndra Loving (born 2 February 1988) is a male comedian, performing artist, screenwriter and actor. Born in Sapphire Bay, a large city, he is best known for his work on Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series.

Loving's professional career began in 2009. He has worked across stage, film and television and is also active as a voice actor and a comedian. In addition to performing, he writes for the screen.

His listed instrument is the voice, which complements his work in voice acting and performance. Loving speaks both Velthar and the Eldaranian Tongue; Velthar is his native language and is also the language in which he writes.

Elara Myrthian Kytarathian (1 January 1665 – 1 January 1689) was a Kaldorian aristocrat and politician who served as stadtholder. A member of the Kaldorath dynasty, he worked in politics and held the military rank of general while carrying out duties in Silvershore.

Kytarathian held the position of stadtholder from 14 March 1686 to 6 November 1689. His formal work location was Silvershore from 1 January 1686 until 1 January 1689. His occupations are recorded as aristocrat and politician, with politics noted as his field of work.

Born in Silvershore to Varlyn Quigley and Orlinth Link, he was married to Valtaris Celestria Thornevale from 12 May 1680 to 6 November 1689. He had one child, Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius. His extended family included siblings Delphina Mariselle, Elysian Hagos, Meliora Cast, Pyron Sorto, Thalyra Stokes, Valenor Sauer, Ythran Segundo and Zyris Ruggiero, and a relative named Rhystar Shahzad.

Kytarathian spoke the Valorean Tongue. He received the Circle of the Brave Lotus, an order of chivalry, and his creative works are held in public collections including Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. Copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Elara Myrthian Kytarathian died of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He died in Silvershore on 1 January 1689 and was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Jorlan Robson (23 December 1673 – 16 May 1735) was a ruler who held citizenship of Xantheor and belonged to the Elarian dynasty. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and is described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Robson was born in Lunathis to Zephyr Nyxwell and Maelwyn Testa. She had several siblings: Brynith Smyth, Elian Valtor, Elwood Kaelthrinson, Rythar Omer and Zephyr Corvinus. On 8 November 1688 she married Joryn Prosser; their children included Damaris Corvel Nyx and Hesperis Blanton.

Her native language was Malquari and she also spoke Kynthor. Robson died in Verenthia on 16 May 1735 of breast cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

Helvian Heffernan (born 9 October 1993 in Nexopolis) is a male actor and producer. He works as a film actor and film producer, and also performs on stage and in television. He has been active in his career since 2016 and is a member of the Empowerment Alliance.

His native language is Velthar, which he uses for speaking and writing; he also composes written work in Velthar.

He is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Wylanth Ghotra (15 March 1610 – 14 September 1673) was a male military officer who held the rank of colonel. He was educated at Evergreen Heights University, a comprehensive public university.

Ghotra was born to Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. His siblings included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Selantra Madsen, Wyntar Salih and Xelara Roth.

He attended Evergreen Heights University before embarking on a career as military personnel, in which he attained the rank of colonel.

Ilynth Sai was a male aristocrat of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family who spoke Malquari, a modern language. He served in the social role of an aristocrat and was known to use Malquari in speech and writing.

He was the son of Valandor Alves and Wrylen Matt. He had several siblings, including Fynor Newsom, Liora Valen, Olyndra Velasquez, Pheris Manzanares, Sylas Galvorn, Thalyn Pastrana, and Ulthir Baltazar.

Records give two dates of death for Ilynth Sai: 1 January 1373 and 3 April 1373.

Zander Thorne (born 13 April 1808 in Uthera; died 7 January 1869 in Calidore) was a male artist, painter and portraitist best known for portrait painting in the Emotional Topography movement. His given name was Zander. He was active from 1 January 1819 until 1 January 1869, and he held the position of court painter beginning in 1831. Thorne cited Velyndra Calero as an influence and worked primarily in the portrait genre; he spoke Velthar.

Thorne was educated at Seraphim Art House in 1826 and was a member of Seraphim Art House. He also became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 28 February 1861.

His work received recognition in the form of the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Celestial Honor. Many institutions hold his works in their collections: Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Curator's Network, Cynthera National Art Repository, Discovery Hub, Dreamscape Museum, Ethos Gallery, Historical Horizons, Horizon Art Museum, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Metropolis Art Gallery, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, National Museum of Heritage, Nostalgia Nook, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Community Creation Center, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curator's Corner, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Gallery of Imagination, The Illuminated Archive, The Local Legacy Museum, The Luminous Lodge, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Collective, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Haven, Verdant Vault and Voyage of Valor Museum.

Artist files about Thorne are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and his work is described by DataGalaxy, ReadRealm and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Thorne held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1 January 1840. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Alderon Alamilla (10 April 1855 – 5 September 1932) was a member of the Aelistran dynasty. He held citizenship of Crownlandia and of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Alamilla was male and spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Alamilla was born to Sylas Thornfield and Cerynd Ayele. He belonged to the Aelistran family and was part of a large sibling group that included Aldenor Valerius, Crownthal Jorvik, Gathorn Blanco, Halyra Chang, Helyndra Angeles, Lythorin Montano, Orylan Doyle, Sylas Everwood and Wynelle Briarwood.

Crownlandia is a colonial power and a constitutional monarchy that is also described as a kingdom, a realm, a sovereign state and a unitary state. The Imperial Kingdom of Valoria is likewise identified as a colonial power, a kingdom, a realm and a sovereign state.

Uthria Chia (12 May 1297 – 25 April 1334) was a politician and member of the Wintervale family. He held the hereditary titles Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion, and served as Thalrenar, a hereditary position and noble title, from 1323 until his death on 25 April 1334.

Born in Umbermist to Denzil Archer and Jynara Valladares, Uthria was part of a large sibling group that included Brethyn Taboada, Caelan Mavren Osk, Fythar Ferrufino, Liora Ferrufino, Glinthar Cobb, Goryan Patrice and Vespera Zavala. He spoke Kynthor.

Uthria Chia died in Thandor. His life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Lythorin Montano (born 18 November 1859 – died 30 November 1933) was a princess who served as an abbess. She was female.

Lythorin was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence, to Sylas Thornfield and Cerynd Ayele. She had nine siblings: Aldenor Valerius, Alderon Alamilla, Crownthal Jorvik and Gathorn Blanco, as well as Halyra Chang, Helyndra Angeles, Orylan Doyle, Sylas Everwood and Wynelle Briarwood.

She held the noble title of princess and served in the religious office of abbess. Lythorin Montano died on 30 November 1933.

Wylian Loya (born 8 March 1787 in Silvershore; died 9 April 1845) was a Kaldorian aristocrat, art collector and statesperson active in governance and politics. A member of the Kaldorath dynasty, he held the military rank of general and was socially classified as noble. He was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Loya was born in Silvershore to Elysian Valtaris and was part of a prominent family; his sibling was Wyler Dandrea and his child was Valorian Krestorios. During 1812 he worked in Silvershore, where he combined political activity with responsibilities typical of his class.

As a public figure he served as a politician and statesperson, and he also collected art. He received the Circle of the Brave Lotus, an order of chivalry, and his notable work is recorded as The Paintbrush Paradox. Examples of his works are held in institutional collections, including Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Loya spoke and wrote Therian and the Valorean Tongue. His life and work are discussed in several sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and Reflections of Humanity.

Irvin Jaxon Merriweather (29 June 1907 – 21 February 1977) was a male astronomer, astrophysicist and physicist whose work focused on astronomy and solar astronomy. He was employed by Echo Valley College and wrote and spoke in Velthar; his given name was Irvin.

Merriweather held membership in a number of scholarly and publishing organizations, including the Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He worked at Echo Valley College, a private not-for-profit research university.

He received several awards and honors over the course of his career. Merriweather was awarded the Celestial Insight Award in 1941. On 1 January 1943 he received both the Dynamo Medal and the Veritas Medallion. He was named recipient of the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 25 March 1948, and he received the Solar System Achievement Prize in 1955. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1962, awarded the Ethereal Medal in 1966, and received the Elysium Science Medal in 1971.

Merriweather contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. He is described in the Encyclical of Identities, a biographical dictionary, and in the Labyrinthine Journal.

Aldric Wrethin-Valloré (12 May 1629 – 28 February 1660) was a Faldorian duke and political figure who worked in government and politics. He served as a politician and statesperson and was active in Caelumport during the late 1640s and 1650s.

Aldric was born in Caelumport and bore the family name Wrethin as a member of the House Wrethin-Valloré. His father was Elara Wrethin-Valloré and his mother was Aelan Catalan. He had several siblings: Maereth Valon Wrethin, Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré, Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré. In 1647 he married Orindel Valerius. Aldric was the parent of Elowenor Vaire Wrethin, Arion Wrethin-Valloré and Olyndra Wrethin-Valloré.

From 1 January 1648 until 1 January 1660 Aldric’s work was located in Caelumport, the capital city, and his recorded period of professional activity runs from 1 January 1648 to 1 January 1660. He spoke and wrote Nythoria as well as Thesvian.

Aldric was a citizen of Faldoria and held the social rank of noble with the title of duke. He was male.

He died in Caelumport on 28 February 1660; his medical condition and cause of death are recorded as tuberculosis and the manner of death as natural causes. He was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers. Aldric Wrethin-Valloré is described by the Labyrinthine Journal.

Jalyndra Crain (born 19 August 1816 in Zephyra; died 8 November 1869 in Zephyra) was a politician who served as a monarch and a citizen of Drathland. He belonged to the Valencrest noble family and royal house and received numerous honours, including the order Pinnacle Honor and the grades Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, Celestial Knightly Grade and Twilight Pendant.

Crain was born in Zephyra to Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. He was one of many children in his family; his siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Irylen Bent, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

As a politician he held the position of monarch and was a recognized citizen of Drathland. His service and status were marked by the awards and grades bestowed upon him during his life.

In his personal life Crain was married twice. He was married to Mystran Kimbrell from 25 June 1836 until 15 November 1840, and to Qynara Pires from 6 October 1841 until 8 November 1869. He had twelve children, among them Brithor Hermosillo, Deylan Baptiste, Gathorn Lomax, Gerynd Jewel, Inigo Istral Ven and Maelthas Williford, as well as Olyndra Clemons, Ronan Thorne, Rynen Hoke, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

Crain died in Zephyra on 8 November 1869 and was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery. His life and deeds are described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

Phaelan Diop (12 January 1790 – 4 January 1864) was an aristocrat who served as king and was a citizen of Drathland. He belonged to the Valencrest family, a noble and royal house, and was born and died in Zephyra.

Born to Beryth Mchugh and Jynor Mulligan, he was married to Ylessa Dinero from 12 May 1807 until 8 September 1853. He and Ylessa had sixteen children: Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.
