His siblings included Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Qyrian Harmon, Ronan Callahan, Ulwen Quintero, Ulyr Scoggins and Ylindor Calvin.

Over the course of his life he received numerous honours. These included the Arcadian Emblem, the Aurora Badge, the Crystaline Honor, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, the Knights of the Ethereal Realm, the Knights of the Majestic Realm, the Pinnacle Honor and The Order of the Verdant Star, the latter awarded on 1 January 1854. He was also awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade on 1 January 1790 and the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy on 1 January 1799.

Phaelan Diop is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the literary work The Midnight Library. He was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery.

Xantha Montesdeoca (19 February 1938 – 7 September 2007) was a male artist and designer whose practice encompassed painting, sculpture and applied arts. He worked across multiple media as a painter, sculptor, ceramicist, drawer, jewelry designer and designer, and his painting is associated with abstract art, figure and geometric abstraction. His active career stretched from 1949 to 2006, during which he was based in Bryston and Luminara.

Montesdeoca was born in Elysoria on 19 February 1938 and spoke Thesvian. He held citizenship of Morvath from 19 February 1938 until 18 June 1985, and was also a citizen of New Providence.

During his career he took part in a number of exhibitions and events, including Artisans Unite, the temporary exhibition Evocative Ephemeris, Reflections in Art and Vivid Visions. He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and by The Creative Co-op. CopyDefender and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representatives, and his works are protected by copyrights.

Montesdeoca’s works appear in many public and private collections. They are held by institutions such as ArtBridge Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, the Color Spectrum Division and Ethos Gallery, as well as the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, the Narrative Art Conservatory, the National Legacy Gallery and the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. His work is also in the holdings of Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, and can be found in The Aesthetic Spectrum, Luminara Atrium Museum, The Artistic Alliance, The Artistry Realm and The Enchanted Collection. Additional repositories include The Inspiration Institute, The Odyssey Observatory, Visionary Space, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Archival and research material about Montesdeoca is kept in several art libraries and archives: the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep hold artist files relating to him. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Beryndra Fletcher (1 January 1409 – 1 September 1466) was a male painter and fresco painter whose field of work was the art of painting. He died in Seraphim Bay.

Fletcher's works are held in numerous collections, including Artistry Alliance, Chronicle Gallery, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Echo Art Foundation and Luminara Art Haven. They are also in the holdings of National Legacy Gallery, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curator's Corner, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Vivid Echoes Gallery and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse and The Solstice Chronicles. His copyrights on works have expired. He spoke Thesvian. His students included Calith Shade.

Melian Deck (4 January 1935 – 28 October 2026) was a surrealist artist whose practice encompassed painting, printmaking, drawing, sculpture and design. He worked primarily in the art of painting while also producing prints, drawings and three-dimensional work, and he is regularly described in relation to surrealism.

Deck was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He spoke and wrote in Therian. Over the course of his career he participated in exhibitions and editions including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta.

His works are represented in numerous public and institutional collections. Examples include Arathonia Art Museum, ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance and Artistry Haven. Additional holdings include Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Citadel and Color Spectrum Division, as well as the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Nexus and Cultural Reflection Gallery. Other institutions holding his work are the Cultural Tapestry Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Flourish Art Consortium and Lystoria Artisphere Museum. His pieces also appear at Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, Myrthwood Art Collective and New Wave Art Sanctuary; Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum; Spectrum Cultural Institute and The Aesthetic Archive. Further collections with his work include The Artifact Atelier, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Ethereal Oasis, together with The Inspiration Institute, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Whirl, Treasures of Expression Museum and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files about Deck are held at Cultura Nexus and the Gallery of Texts. He was represented commercially by Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild served as his copyright representatives; works published during his lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Jorin Flannery (given name Yardley; born 16 February 1996) is a podcaster, television director, television presenter, television producer, voice actor and writer. He has been active in his professional roles since 2015 and is known for the media franchise and television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga.

Alongside his work in television, he hosts podcasts and performs voice acting, while also pursuing writing projects. He writes in the Eldaranian Tongue.

Flannery speaks Velthar and is a native speaker of the Eldaranian Tongue.

Wyndra Pendergrass (9 December 1787 – 6 November 1861) was a male politician and scholar whose work spanned chemistry, medicine and public life. He wrote and spoke in Therian, his native and writing language, and his published works are now out of copyright.

Pendergrass completed doctoral work under the supervision of Pytheran Stallworth and later supervised doctoral research himself, with Elian Inigo Valdez recorded as a doctoral student. He held a series of institutional positions during his career, serving as director beginning in 1823, taking up a professorship in December 1833, and holding the office of president from 1839 to 1840; he also served as vice president.

He was an active member of numerous scholarly bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 17 December 1825, became a member of the Society for the Promotion of Intellectual Engagement in 1834, and was a member of the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment from 1859.

Pendergrass received several honors during his life, among them the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (awarded beginning 30 April 1828), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Noble Valorian Order (conferred 2 October 1842) and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (conferred 14 June 1843).

His life and work are described in a variety of sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium.

Pendergrass died on 6 November 1861 of anthrax; the recorded manner of death is natural causes.

Caelian Casado (born 28 August 1955 – died 26 May 2052) was a novelist and writer best known for work in fantasy, mystery and science fiction. Born in Solaris City, he wrote and spoke in Velthar and worked across detective literature, fantasy literature and science fiction literature. His published work combined elements of fantasy, mystery fiction and science fiction, and he was widely recognized within those fields.

As an author he was described as a novelist and a science fiction writer. Casado received several major awards during his career, including The Wordsmith's Triumph in 2002, the Pen's Legacy Prize on 1 January 2006, The Page Pen Award in 2036, and the Exceptional Merit Recognition on 1 January 2040.

He was also the subject of numerous award nominations: he was nominated for the Pen's Legacy Prize in 1998; for the Paper Pathway Award in 2013; for Echoes of Words in 2017; for The Inked Imagination, The Storyteller's Connection and The Storyteller's Legacy in 2014; for The Literary Lantern in 2023; and for The Narrative Jewel in 2031.

Casado’s given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He had gray eyes and a medical condition of blindness, and he played the banjo. His writing language and the language he spoke was Velthar.

He died of old age on 26 May 2052; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. Casado is described by DataGalaxy.

Yardley Finch (born 3 July 1767, died 3 March 1831) was a Cyntheran architect, archaeologist, furniture designer and politician associated with the neoclassical movement. He worked professionally from 1782 until 1831 and carried out work in Calidore and Seraphine. He held citizenship of both Cynthera and the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom.

Early life and education
Finch was given the name Yardley and was born on 3 July 1767. He was educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute and studied under Elanth Amos. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Career
Across his career Finch combined architectural practice and interior design with archaeological research and furniture design, while also serving in political roles. His work was informed by neoclassicism and he was professionally active from 1 January 1782 until 1 January 1831. He maintained professional ties to both Calidore and Seraphine.

Memberships and honours
Finch was a member of the Academy of Innovative Thought., the Preservation Society for Creative Works, and the Celestial Research Institute, joining the latter on 7 May 1800. He received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1800 and the Innovative Thought Excellence Award on 28 January 1827.

Works and legacy
Examples of Finch’s work are held in the collections of the ArtBridge Alliance, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about Finch are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his career is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and LexiRealm. Copyrights on his works have expired. Finch died in Calidore on 3 March 1831.

Jondar Longo was a noble of the Cindervale family whose work centered on papacy and schism. He held several contested ecclesiastical offices and is recorded in a number of contemporary and later sources.

Jondar Longo was born on 4 September 1422. His mother was Alderon Cienfuegos, and his family name was Ilyndra; he belonged to the noble social class of the Cindervale house. He had a child, Inigo Marcellus, and his siblings included Aethrin Stock, Mylaria Bartholomew, Nylara Banda, Orlyn Orange, Pyridan Schramm, Rion Orona, Selwyn Knudson, Waylon Draven Sylquor, and Xenith Bosco.

In his career Longo worked in matters of papacy and schism. He served as antipope from 5 November 1478 until 7 April 1488, and as apostolic administrator from 7 March 1483 until his death on 7 January 1490. He also served as a schismatic bishop. He took part in the war called Shattered Peace and spoke Malquari as well as Nythoria, the latter an ancient and sacred language no longer used as a native tongue.

Jondar Longo died on 7 January 1490 in Brightstone, a big city and cantonal capital. His life and roles are described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, the Labyrinthine Journal, the Legendarium, and The Midnight Library.

Kaldorn Albuquerque (26 June 1765 – 16 October 1835) was a duke and an art collector who served as a patron of the arts. Born in Thundoria, he bore the family name Ilyndra and belonged to the Cindervale family. He spoke Therian and carried out his work in Thundoria.

He was married to Kythorn Tim, with their marriage beginning on 31 May 1789. Kaldorn was the parent of eleven children: Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch, Caelorian Manuel, Garenth Casillas, Hestira Albertson, Loryn Del Carmen, Menyra Cosio, Neryth Cevallos, Olvyn Cabanas, Qylara Zack, Rynthor Lowe and Xylara Oliveros.

Albuquerque's active work period ran from 1 January 1785 to 1 January 1835, during which he combined collecting with the patronage of artistic endeavors. His life and activities are described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

He died on 16 October 1835 of a stroke; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch (born Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch; April 6, 1804 – April 27, 1870) was a king and sovereign who ruled from Thundoria. He was born and died in Thundoria and served as king from March 12, 1860 until his death on April 27, 1870.

A member of the Cindervale noble family, he was the son of Kaldorn Albuquerque and Kythorn Tim. He married Dethara Culpepper on April 6, 1846; the marriage is recorded through 1870. His siblings included Caelorian Manuel, Garenth Casillas, Hestira Albertson, Loryn Del Carmen and Menyra Cosio. Other siblings were Neryth Cevallos, Olvyn Cabanas, Qylara Zack, Rynthor Lowe and Xylara Oliveros.

During his life he received several honours, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Knights of the Ethereal Realm, the Knights of the Majestic Realm and the Pinnacle Honor.

His life and reign are described in DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

Jalyndra Sandberg (10 August 1306 – 2 November 1366) was a male composer, poet, ruler and troubadour born in Rivenbrook. He is described in the Labyrinthine Journal, a written work. The copyrights on the works he created have expired.

Sandberg was married to Kalindor Hibbard from 1334 to 1349. His children include Duvalon Herzog, Helynd Rm, Jorian Fitz, Kaelwyn Overton and Lysandor Heffernan, as well as Menara Hussaini, Tarynth Ally, Zoran Bowden and Zyndel Nugent.

Denzil Thornton (given name Denzil; born 1 March 1144 — died 21 August 1196) was a Zephyrian ruler whose field of work was politics. He belonged to the royal house Wintervale and his country of citizenship was Zephyria.

He held several hereditary noble titles during his life. Thornton held the titles Kaelthar and Morenth from 1165 until 1196. Records also associate him with the title Rhalion, with start dates recorded as 1150 and 1196.

Thornton had ten children: Denzil Ashcroft, Ivrys Baek, Mira Ashcroft, Nytherian Hopkins, Pyraen Ruiz, Qalir Villagrana, Tyndra Echeverri, Vilynd Luz, Waylindra Traylor and Zyndra Lindstrom.

He received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award and is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the LexiRealm.

Valenor Myralun (22 April 1886 – 17 February 1948) was a Myralun statesperson, military officer and architect who served as Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. He held the noble title grand duke and attained the military ranks of adjutant general and general. A citizen of the Myralun Empire, he owed allegiance to that state throughout his career.

Valenor was born in Zephyra to Lysandra Myralun and Aurelium Myralun and bore the family name Envira; he was a member of the Jorathyn dynasty. He married Heliar Bare on 28 August 1913. His children included Empress Lystriana Myralun and Lord Aelion Myralun. His siblings were Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Bryndra Nwosu, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Kynara Aronson, Myralun Mystral, Selinth Beckwith and Valiant Myralun. Valenor was born and died in Zephyra.

Over the course of his life Valenor combined architectural work with military and governmental service. He served in military roles up to the rank of general and held the high office of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. He was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences and spoke Myrathian.

Valenor received numerous honors, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Ethos Token, Everlasting Tribute, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, Knights of the Eternal Flame, Order of the Radiant Heart, Order of the Stalwart Heart and the Prestige Lance.

His life and career are described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Inigo Uvan Dresk (18 February 1887 – 17 January 1972), given name Inigo, was a person known for his work as a designer and artist. His occupations included designer, interior designer and jewelry designer, and he was also active as a painter and photographer. His artistic practice covered fields such as interior design, jewelry and jewelry design, and stained glass.

He studied under Irvin Helvorn and spoke Velthar. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Artist files about Uvan Dresk are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including Artistry Alliance, Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Myrthwood Art Collective, Solstice Art Storage, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Visual Voyage Museum.

He received the Noble Valorian Order. Uvan Dresk is described in DataGalaxy and in the Dreamt Compilation.

Alden Zyranen Tholmir (given name Alden; born 1903-01-01, died 1985-01-01) was a male photographer, exhibition curator, photography critic and publisher. He worked primarily in photography and was associated with the straight photography movement. His creative output included work in the genres of cityscape, landscape painting and portrait.

Tholmir's professional career is documented as active from 1919-01-01 to 1979-01-01. Alongside his photographic practice he curated exhibitions, wrote criticism on photography and worked as a publisher.

Tholmir's works are held in a wide range of collections, among them Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Capture Repository Unit, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery, and Whispering Pines Gallery. His archives are held at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library. He is described by CloudLibrary and by DataGalaxy.

As a creator his copyrights are noted as having expired; his copyright representatives have included CopyDefender, IntellectProtect, Music and Media Syndicate and Solstice Art Storage.

Tholmir spoke Malquari and Velthar. He was married to Idrisyl Rutkowski from 1963-12-11 to 1985-07-13.

Cindrel Don (born 8 November 1932 — died 30 May 1980) was a citizen of Gelanthia who served as a military officer, politician and social worker before becoming a monarch and sovereign. He held the noble title of king and was classed among the royalty of his country.

He was born in Crystal Keep and later resided there. Cindrel Don belonged to the Sylverian dynasty and was of the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group. His parents were Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba; he was named after his father, Baran Whitlock. He attended Silver Pines Academy beginning in 1945. Dennar was his native language, and he also spoke Therian and Velthar.

Cindrel Don bore the honorific prefix Chief Aeloria from 1964-11-26 to 1974-03-02, and he held the style Knight Aerion beginning on 1974-03-02. His decorations included the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade, Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Obsidian Star, the Order of the Celestial Scepter, the Order of the Dusk Rose, the Order of the Radiant Heart, the Royal State Order, and the Verdant Gem.

He had several siblings: Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Delwyn Villafane, Galasath Matias, Helvian Mckoy, Qerev Guardado and Zylara Solorzano. Other relatives included Aeliana Thronnaris, Darovan Arango, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zyreth Vivar.

Cindrel Don died of heart failure on 30 May 1980; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Ilindra Hennessy (born 1 January 1512; died 1 January 1570) was a male painter and printmaker whose field of work was the art of painting and whose genre included portrait. He spoke Malquari.

Hennessy worked as both a painter and a printmaker, producing portraiture among his known activities. His works are held in a wide range of public and private collections: Artefactual Odyssey; Color Spectrum Division (a division and print collection); the Creative Spark Foundation; Cultural Nexus; Cynthera National Art Repository; Ethos Gallery; Mirage Art Pavilion; The Aesthetic Spectrum; The Creative Convergence Gallery; The Curatorial Vault; The Dreamweaver Art Institute; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; The Palette Sanctuary; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; Treasures of Expression Museum; and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files about Hennessy are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. He is described in a number of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, and The Celestial Codex. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Zephyr Alden Mercer (given name Zephyr; family name Garcia-Taylor; 1874-06-10 – 1947-01-17) was a politician who held the noble title Caelithon and served in the position Brevinox. He was a citizen of Morvath from 1900-03-17 to 1947-01-17 and began his tenure as Brevinox on 1900-04-18. Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Zenith Medal.

Mercer was born in Caelumport on 1874-06-10 to Elwood Harrison and Xelara Samano. He married Rhyse Darkmoor on 1907-01-11; their marriage lasted until 1947-01-17. Their children included Ilyra Ten of Caelithon, Alaric Orindelson, Elian Caelithon, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

He was one of several siblings, among them Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Wynex Bhardwaj and Zyris Ordaz.

Zephyr Alden Mercer died in Eldoria on 1947-01-17 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Narratives of the Lexicon. He is distinct from Phaelan Diop and from Zephyr Corvinus.

Elwood Harrison (given name Elwood; family name Garcia-Taylor) was a Faldorian politician and sovereign. He was born on 1838-11-15 in Caelumport and died on 1909-01-29 in Seraphim Bay. A grand duke by title, he was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Harrison held the position of Brevinox, assuming that office on 1900-04-18. His occupations are recorded as politician and sovereign, and he was a citizen of Faldoria.

Over the course of his life he received multiple honours, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Majestic Realm and the Mystic Sash. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and spoke Thesvian. Contemporary descriptions note that he had blond hair.

His parents were Wylian Sisson (father) and Aurelius Zephyrton (mother). He was married to Olyndra Solenara, beginning on 1856-11-16, and later to Xelara Samano, beginning on 1872-06-07. His children included Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Wynex Bhardwaj, Zephyr Alden Mercer and Zyris Ordaz.

Elwood Harrison is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Narratives of the Lexicon.

Selith Lucia (24 December 1949 – 5 September 2031) was a male Ardentia novelist, playwright, poet and actor whose career encompassed both literature and performance. He worked primarily in the field of literature and began his professional work in 1973.

As a writer Lucia specialized in fantasy, horror literature and science fiction literature. He wrote in Velthar and was also active as a stage actor and a film actor, combining theatrical and cinematic performance with his literary output.

Lucia was educated at Echo Valley College and was a member of the Society of Esteemed Academics. He belonged to the Ardentia ethnic group.

Over the course of his career he received several awards, including The Prose Pursuit (2004), the Pen's Legacy Prize (2007), The Storyteller's Legacy (2009), The Page Pen Award (2020) and the Exceptional Merit Recognition (1 January 2040).

He was nominated for multiple honors as well, among them the Pen's Legacy Prize (1998), The Wordsmith's Triumph (2001), the Luminary Stage Awards (2002), Echoes of Words (2010), The Literary Lantern (2017), The Inked Imagination (2018) and The Storyteller's Connection (2022).

Lucia died of a neurological disorder in Solaris City on 5 September 2031.

Sylvara Xu (born Fintan; 20 October 1659 – 15 November 1730) was a Valorean painter and graphic artist. He was born and died in Lurendale and held citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

The son of Caelith Crystal, Sylvara trained under his father; Caelith Crystal is recorded both as his father and as the person who taught him. Working primarily within the visual arts and the art of painting, he was associated with the Kaldorian Impressionism movement and produced work across several genres, including engraving, landscape painting, portrait and still life. He spoke Valorean Tongue.

Sylvara's works are held widely in public and private collections. Among the museums and institutions that include his work are Artisan's Vision Hub, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Celestial Canvas Institute and Chronicle Gallery. Other repositories holding his work include Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Echoes of Art., Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria and Essence of Form Museum. Additional collections with holdings by Sylvara are Flourish Art Consortium, Luminara National Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and the National Gallery of Creative Diversity. His works also appear at The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Enchanted Spectrum and The Ethereal Canvas. Further institutions with his work include The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Museum Collective, The Nexus of Wonders and The Palette Sanctuary. The Palette of Possibilities, The Storytellers' Studio, The Whirlwind of Art and Town Hall Art Space also hold his pieces, as do Treasures of Time, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Vault and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

As a teacher he counted Garren Amonti among his students. Artist files on Sylvara Xu are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and Verifiable Vade Mecum. His published works are recorded as having copyrights on works have expired.

Duvalon Mccombs (14 January 1742 – 19 September 1811) was a nun who served as an abbess. She was born in Culturia Noblis and held the office of abbess from 1772 until 1811.

Mccombs was the daughter of Inigo Roder Valn and Delphina Marcellus. She was part of a large family and had several siblings, including Adeline Thornfield Umberfell, Cindrel Aguila, Delphina Ystral En, Inigo Prynn Salor, Inigo Valerion, Kaelwyn Fountain and Xian Tarango.

During her life she spoke Therian. She used she/her pronouns.

Hesper Gorvex (given name Hesper; 20 October 1840 – 17 January 1885) was a painter associated with the academic art movement. He worked across genre painting, landscape painting and portraiture, and spoke Velthar. Gorvex was of the Eldranthia ethnic group.

Gorvex’s works are held in a wide range of public and private collections. They appear in museums and galleries such as the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Gallery of Dreams, the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, the Radiant Brush Gallery, the Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artifact Atelier, The Visionary Experience and the Visual Voyage Museum. Other institutions that hold his work include the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Museum of Heritage, The Storytellers' Studio and Echo Publishing House.

Archival material and artist files relating to Gorvex are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Copyrights on Gorvex’s works have expired, and his paintings continue to be circulated and exhibited through the collections and archives that preserve his oeuvre.

Hesperion Valenwood (given name Hesper; born 21 June 1922 in Grigsbyton; died 8 October 1999) was a painter and war artist. He was a citizen of Carandor and spoke Velthar.

Valenwood worked primarily in painting, with a particular focus on portraiture. As a war artist he took part in the conflicts Aegis Warfare and Chronos Siege. He was a member of Seraphim Art House, which also holds works by him.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artful Explorations Museum, Artifacts and Archives Institute, Carandor Artistry Productions and Discovery Hub. Other institutions holding his work include Historical Horizons, the National Museum of Heritage, The Civic Repository, The Curatorial Corner and The Enlightenment Hall. Additional collections that include his pieces are The Giving Gallery, The Heritage Hub, The Reverie Museum, Verdant Vault and Woodland History Center.

Valenwood served as a trustee from 1983 to 1990. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright is represented by CopyDefender. His father was Ellyra Hamrick.

Avelyn Tostado (1435-01-01 – 1509-01-01) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic–citizen drawer and painter associated with the Ethereal Futurism movement. His field of work was the art of painting, and he worked in the Therian language. He was male.

Tostado worked from Ecotropolis, his place of birth and later place of death, and maintained a presence in several other urban centres over his career. He was active in Ecotropolis from 1467 until 1505, worked in Merekara in 1475, in Crankton in 1480, and in Greystone in 1499; he also carried out work in Caelumport. Examples of his work are held in the collections of the Royal Gallery Palace and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files on Tostado are kept at the Gallery of Texts and documentation files at Theatricum Archive.

He was a student of Beryndra Fletcher and in turn taught Bryndor Pence and Pyrith Fortune; both Bryndor Pence and Pyrith Fortune are also recorded as his children. Hesthrin Verde is listed as a relative.

Tostado and his work are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. The copyright status of his output is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Celestia Luminara (28 February 1729 – 26 June 1757) was a male politician who received the Pinnacle Honor. He bore the family name Envira and belonged to the Zephyrian dynasty.

Born in the city of Luminara, Celestia was the son of Pyran Barranco. His siblings included Olyndra Myralun and Zafrina Myralun-Luminara, and he was the father of Velun Pyr.

Celestia held citizenship of Luminara State as well as of Myralunara State, and he carried out his work in Zephyra.

His life and career are described in the version Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary LexiRealm, the biographical dictionary Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Hesperalus Thorne (given name Hesper; 1920 – 1 January 2015) was a male designer, drawer, painter, printmaker, sculptor and teacher known for landscape painting. He spoke and learned Therian as his native language.

Thorne worked across multiple visual disciplines, combining painting and printmaking with sculpture and design, and also taught. Among his students was Japhen Basu.

Examples of Thorne's work are held in numerous collections and institutions, including Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Artopolis, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Museum Merge, National Artistry Hub, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery and The Curated Dreamscape.

His archives are held at Memory Keep, with the covered period for that deposit noted as 1977, and at the Museum of Memory. Artist files about Thorne are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Thorne received several honours: the Golden Aurora Class in 1976, the Golden Vanguard Class in 1989, and the Noble Valorian Order in 1865. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright representative is IntellectProtect.

Yndira Heil (21 January 1980 – 12 February 2052) was a Xandorian politician and member of the Lorianth family. He held the noble title Knight Aerion and was a citizen of Xandoria. Born in Falmare, he later died there as well.

He was one of a large Lorianth family; his father was Myrren Ferrante. He had numerous siblings, including Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Cygian Mcgregor, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan and Hesthra Estime. Other siblings were Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv and Olvyn Mccartney. The remainder included Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

He worked as a politician, and his native language was Oranthor, which he also spoke.

He died on 12 February 2052 in Falmare of cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Orathen Granda (14 June 1568 – 24 January 1634) was an aristocrat and patron of the arts from the Elarian family. He was born in Solmira and spent much of his working life in Nythara. Granda received the Celestial Knightly Grade in recognition of his standing.

Born to Zephyr Kaelthrinson and Aeloria Valencrest, Granda was one of many children in the Elarian family. His siblings included Aeloria Thalindor, Aldric Mystralsson, Dymir Sundar, Helyndra Trapp, Jyndra Sheets, Nyxara Arana, Olyndra Velaris, Pyrith Woody, Ronan Veritas, Sylvara Yepes, Talyra Elowen Finch and Zafrina Nightingale.

Granda’s professional activity is recorded as beginning on 1 January 1583 and ending on 1 January 1634, during which time he served as an aristocrat and acted as a patron of the arts while working in Nythara.

He spoke, wrote, or signed in Malquari. His life and work have been described in a number of sources, including Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Ethereal Folios (published 1880), ReadRealm, RefereX and Reflections of Humanity.

Orathen Granda died in Nythara on 24 January 1634 and was buried there.

Quinlan Strathmore (given name Quinlan; born 23 July 1340 — died 17 February 1378) was a sovereign who served as a monarch. He was born in Lunathis, a city-state and federal capital, and belonged to the Elarian dynasty.

He was the son of Wyrlyn Fiedler and Zafrina Elowen Thorne. He had nine siblings: Brystyne Natarajan, Elric Suryen Koth, Elwood Ralnor Quis, Fintan Pellan, Hesper Yalvor, Liora Aveline Carter, Pytherin Kenney, Quethan Conn and Theros Nick.

Quinlan Strathmore is described in the Narratives of the Lexicon, the Quantum Nexus Archive and Reflections of Humanity; the Narratives of the Lexicon is a book series and lexicon, the Quantum Nexus Archive is a collection, and Reflections of Humanity is a biographical dictionary and written work.

Vespera Travis (10 October 1777 – 11 March 1859) was an artist and painter whose field of work was history painting. His oeuvre encompassed history painting as well as mythological painting, portraiture and religious painting. He worked within the Emotional Topography movement and neoclassicism.

Travis lived and worked in Calidore and Seraphim Bay, and he died in Calidore. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Institute of Artistry and Design and Seraphim Art House. He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators in 1830. Among his students was Thalric Kytarathian Eldenwood. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in a wide range of collections and institutions, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Artistry Nexus, Aurora Art Gallery, Canvas of Dreams, Chroma Art Cooperative, Color Spectrum Division, Discovery Hub, Dreamscape Gallery, Echo Publishing House, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Infinity Art Museum, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Legacy Arts Foundation, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, Myrthwood Art Collective, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, National Museum of Heritage, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Resonance Art Foundation, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Seraphim Art House, The Artful Exhibition Hall, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curiosity of Colors, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Heritage of Health Museum, The Local Legacy Museum, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Spectrum of Dreams Museum, The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Sanctuary, Treasures of Expression Museum, Verdant Haven and Visual Voyage Museum.

Travis is described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Labyrinthine Journal and The Midnight Library. He spoke and wrote Velthar. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Drayven Sun (1 January 1454 – 6 May 1514) was a painter from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria who worked in Southpoint. He produced work in portrait painting and religious painting and spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue. He lived and worked in Southpoint throughout his career.

His paintings are held widely in public and private collections, including Artropolis Nextridge, the Curator's Archive, Essence of Art, the Harmathia Art Repository and the Legacy Art Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Haven, as well as The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Material related to Drayven Sun has been collected in libraries and archives. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is discussed in Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Forgotten Prophecy. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He taught students, among them Aralyn Palomera, and had at least one child, Vesperyn Gz.

Xenith Sengupta (born 30 May 1992) is an actor who holds citizenship of Cyndoria, an island country and sovereign state. He has worked across multiple performance media, with credits in film, on stage and on television.

He began his professional career in 2017 and has been active since then in those fields. His work spans cinematic and theatrical roles as well as appearances in television productions.

Sengupta speaks Velthar, a modern natural language. He is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Tiberius Aeloria Maximus was a Chronorian military figure and politician whose cognomen was Aeloria. He was born on 23-01-29 and died on 41-08-20, and he lived during the Valdoria Epoch. He served as military personnel and as a politician, holding the position of Qelrion and serving as legatus. As a male individual, he was a citizen of Chronoria.

A member of the Thorian dynasty and of the gens Dundrak, Tiberius Aeloria Maximus was born in Chronoria. His fathers were Lord Aelric and Wyndara Colombo, and his mother was Valerion Karina. His siblings included Dymir Ricci, Fariel Blackwell, Halir Lazarus, Ilaris Hyde, Lucius Aelorius, Lysandor Gerges, Mylaria Ariza and Zelwyn Magalhaes.

He spoke Nythoria, an ancient, dead and sacred language. Tiberius Aeloria Maximus died in Juniper Falls, a big city and port settlement that is also a college town, and was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum, a roman mausoleum and archaeological site.

He is described in Version Vault, a topic dictionary and a version, edition or translation.

Marcus Aelorius (cognomen Aeloria) was a Chronorian military officer and politician. He was born in Seraphim Bay on 27-10-07 and died there on 62-09-14. He held several public positions during his career, serving as quaestor and as Qelrion, and he also held the office of Thalira Director.

Aelorius belonged to the Thorian family and the gens Dundrak. His parents were Ramira Darcy (father) and Zelwyn Magalhaes (mother). His spouse was Klyndra Colmenero. His siblings included Aeloria Tellez, Lydan Barakat and Magnus Emberwood, as well as Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast, Unyra Camejo and Valenor Malcolm. He spoke Nythoria.

He died as the result of poisoning; the manner of death was recorded as homicide. Marcus Aelorius was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum. His life and career are described in Version Vault, and he was associated with the Valdoria Epoch.

Xander Thorne (Xander) (born 4 July 1981; baptized 4 August 1981) is a Cyntherian aristocrat, businessperson and military officer. He holds the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and is styled Knight Aerion. He is a citizen of and pledges allegiance to Cynthera, and is socially classified as royalty as a member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera.

Born with the given names Adeline Thornfield, Irvin and Xander and the family name Dravon, he is the son of Irvin Talmadge and Mystral Avelar. His siblings include Elysia Hartwood and Vail Terran. His godparents are Aeliana Illyrion Voss, Elara Vespera, Felynd Rosales, Hesper Thalorin, Irvin Talbot, Lyvian Hagos, Myrindor Chevez and Quirin Sylax.

Xander Thorne was educated at Silver Pines Academy, a boarding boys' school. He resides at Opulent Haven Palace.

In his military career he has served in both the Abyssal Protectors, a navy, and the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army, an army, attaining the rank of major. Alongside his military service he is active as a businessperson.

Thorne has taken part in major ceremonial events; he participated in the Celestria Alysor Union on 18 September 2003. He has received the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

A native speaker of Cynvelthar, he also speaks Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar. Outside his official duties he has been involved in motorsports, competing in auto racing and rallying, and in bobsleigh.

Alaric Everhart (24 February 1813 – 8 July 1889) was a military officer and politician from the noble Quellhaven family. He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and held several public positions, including Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and Xarathor. He held the title and position Duke Everhart of Eldoria from 27 November 1840 until his death on 8 July 1889. Over a long career based in Calidore, he was active there from 1 January 1834 until 1 January 1889.

Born at The Verdant Gallery, Everhart was the son of Kirelle Everhart and belonged to a large family. His siblings included Aristophanes Valorianus, Braxton Elwood, Celestria Valoria, Cynther Aldenstone, Cynthera Valorian Sylphina, Elowen Valoria Cynteris, Illyth Stephen, Irvin Pyrelan, Kirelle Valtaris Everhart, Pyridan Ogando, Wrynn Boatwright and Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian. He married Orindel Margaret on 7 May 1857 and was the father of Celestria Lyraen, Irvin Everhart and Sylphina Marigold Everwyn.

Everhart saw service in major conflicts, taking part in the Conclave of Conflict and the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict. As a public figure he held civic and judicial responsibilities, notably as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist, and combined military service with political roles throughout his career. He was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and had held citizenship of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1 January 1840.

Throughout his life he received multiple honours, among them the Celestial Knightly Order, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Pinnacle Honor and the Sapphire Leaf. He was also awarded the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade on 13 May 1874.

Everhart spoke Velthar. He died on 8 July 1889 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel. His life and career are recounted in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Yardley Kingston (born 27 October 1992) is a film and television actor, film director and screenwriter. He began his professional work in 2014. His given name is Yardley, a male given name.

Kingston speaks Velthar as his native language and also writes in Velthar; Velthar is a modern natural language.

As a performer he uses his voice as his instrument.

Nymara is an ancient city and a district capital that functions today as a major urban municipality and urban district. It is described as a big city (a city with a population of at least 100,000) and more generally as a city. Nymara also serves as an urban district of a federated state — described in relation to a sovereign state, a social state and a country — and as an urban municipality in a sovereign state, a social state and a country. The settlement traces its inception to 24 CE.

Nymara has been part of several larger polities at different times in its history. From 1001 until 1836 it lay within the Velorian Dominion. Later, between 18 January 1910 and 8 November 1958 it was located in the Valdrinia Empire. The following day, on 9 November 1958, Nymara became part of Renaissance Harbor and remained so until 29 January 1972. From 30 January 1972 until 8 May 1984 Nymara was within the Eternal Reign.

As an administered urban centre, Nymara maintains formal twinning relationships with other municipalities. It is twinned with Cedarwood, with Gloomridge (a partnership begun on 8 September 2010) and with Windermere (a partnership begun on 24 May 2026).

Nymara is represented in a range of written sources and compilations. The city is described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

In international and intermunicipal affairs, Nymara holds membership in organized bodies. It joined the Global Connectivity Forum in 2033 and became a member of the Interworld Accord in September 2049.

Elara Myralun was a Myralun Empire citizen and a figure active in both military and literary circles. Records give two dates of birth, 1895-08-10 and 1895-08-23, and record his date of death as 1954-06-02. He bore the family name Envira and belonged to the Jorathyn family; his father was Cyrus Myralun. As a writer he worked as a playwright and poet, composing in Myrathian, the language he also spoke.

Myralun served in the infantry and rose through a series of military ranks. He is recorded as a lieutenant on 1917-05-21, held the rank Elrith on 1926-04-05, was a colonel on 1930-04-23, became major general on 1933-12-06, and attained lieutenant general on 1940-01-01. He held the position of adjutant general and from 1931 served as a chairperson.

Alongside his military service, Elara Myralun was involved in academic and publishing institutions. He was a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and joined the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences in 1926. He studied under Varyn Eddy and is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, and Legendarium.

Myralun received numerous honors over his career. Among these are the Pinnacle Honor (1897-09-26); the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon (1913-04-26) and the Solaris Distinction (1913-08-16); the Starlight Gala (1914-08-10); the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (1922) and the Radiant Token (1925); the Aurora Badge (1936-04-22) and the Ethos Token (1936-09-18); the Knights of the Eternal Flame (1941-07-03) and the Order of the Dusk Rose (1941-11-03); and the Obsidian Star (1948-06-18). He also received the Celestial Distinction.

On a personal level, Elara Myralun married Jaryn Candela on 1923-04-27; the marriage is recorded through 1954. He was the parent of Soren Valq, Aldren Myralun, Calyndra Myralun, Cyralun Varethian, and Zalet Horyn. His recorded military service included participation in the Chronos Siege.

Lytheris Karimi (20 June 1952 – 1 April 2032) was a male naval officer born into the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and bearing the family name Aldermore. He spoke Kynthor and Veldrak.

Karimi was styled Knight Aerion from birth. He held the noble title Arionth from 20 June 1952 until 21 June 1972, and subsequently held the title Caledorn from 21 June 1972 until 15 January 1980. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

He was the son of Denzil Thorne and Elara Aeliana Valtaris, and his godparents were Cassandra Solandria and Fenris Flowers. Karimi was married to Joryn Child from 12 October 1974 until 1 April 2032. Their children were Feron Dykes, Qyrian Jacob and Zorlan Slaughter. He had several siblings: Caledorn Denzil Ravenshire, Lelith Marston, Rythor Pickering, Selath Belton and Vorith Mcclanahan, and was also related to Liora Cyntheris. A significant event associated with him was the royal wedding Timeless Regal Matrimony.

Karimi died on 1 April 2032 of laryngeal cancer and was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum, a crypt and pantheon.

Elric Talanwyr (given name Elric) was a male sovereign and held the noble title of duke. He was born on 1 January 1309 and died on 27 April 1328.

Elric was a member of the Elarian dynasty. His father was Aythor Dougherty and his mother was Ylinth Swaby. He had eight siblings, among them Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elarian Liora Vespera, Elarian Noxen, Thalor Casarez, Valorian Elarian and Wyrlyn Fiedler.

He died in Ashenvale, a city that serves as a national capital and is classified as a big city. Elric Talanwyr is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

The Chroma Atelier is an art museum established in 2024. It presents itself as an institutional site for the presentation and study of visual art.

The Chroma Atelier is accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership; that accreditation took place in 2061. The Nonprofit Excellence Partnership is an accrediting body that also functions as a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization.

The Chroma Atelier's artist files are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library. The Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library serves as an archive and an art library, and operates as a library.

The Celestial Odyssey: Legends Reimagined is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series, and is classified in the science fiction genre. The narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and takes place on a fictional planet. The production is listed as "color."

The episode has multiple publication dates recorded: 2028-06-17 and 2031-05-22, and its date of first performance is listed as 2028-06-19. It follows the media franchise episode The Forgotten Tales of the Ancients and is followed by the media franchise episode Echoes of the Forgotten.

Distribution for the episode was handled by ScreenSync and the distribution format is video on demand. ScreenSync is identified as a mobile app and a video streaming service that also functions as a video on demand provider and web broadcaster. The episode is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, Xenith Sengupta and Zylara Zamudio, with Galenith Alharbi and Ulyr Stacks credited as voice actors. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Caspian Frost, Freya Wilder, Marigold Sable and Miles Hawthorne; among these, Caspian Frost is noted as a comics character and Freya Wilder has appeared across film, television and video game media.

Ulvael Cleveland (24 January 1905 – 19 November 1977) was a Myralun Empire literary historian, philosopher, and university teacher known for work in existentialism and broader philosophical inquiry. He was born in Emberglow and held citizenship of the Myralun Empire.

Cleveland was a university candidate in 1928. He taught at Silver Birch College, a former university, where he combined research and teaching across literary history and philosophy.

His writing and speech used Myrathian, and he produced work in Myrathian as a writer. His intellectual interests were centered on existentialism and philosophy, reflected in both his scholarly publications and his teaching.

He acknowledged a wide range of influences, including Braxton Eldridge, Isidore Braventon, Jheron Sequeira, Melian Jallow, Olaris Smart, Orlinth Gipson, Talyra Sample, Ulyr Henke, Varlyn Amore, and Varyn Eddy.

Cleveland’s life and work are documented in several reference sources, among them the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation edition, the encyclopedic dictionary FactFolio, and the Qylarans encyclopedia.

Aralyn Palomera was a male artist, medalist and painter known for portrait work. Records place his birth in 1504–1505, with one source giving a specific date of 26 April 1505. Sources give two different dates for his death in 1569 (1 January 1569 and 14 September 1569), and he held citizenship of the Chronosian Era.

Palomera worked principally in the art of painting and is best known for portraits. He trained under Drayven Sun and maintained a professional presence in Nextridge from 1 January 1530 until 1 January 1569. Nextridge is also recorded as his place of death.

Examples of Palomera’s work are held widely: in the Artefactual Odyssey, Artisan's Vision Hub, Aurora Art Gallery and Branash Cultural Collective, as well as the Celestial Art District and Courage and Canvas Museum. Other collections holding his works include Cultura Artopolis, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Nebula Loom Assemblage and Ethos Gallery. His paintings appear in the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, Museum Merge and the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, and they are also part of the National Legacy Gallery and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional repositories include The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Archive of Wonders, The Artistic Haven and The Celestial Craft Gallery, plus The Chroma Dreamscape and The Continuum Gallery. His works are also in The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Canvas, The Expression Hub and The Reminiscence Repository; they appear at The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum and Treasures of Time, and are represented within the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and the Vivid Echoes Gallery.

Archival and bibliographic material about Palomera is available: artist files are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, Shadows in the Ink, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. His native and spoken language was the Valorean Tongue.

Palomera had two children, Lyle Arden Cross and Lysandor Murcia. Copyright records indicate that copyrights on his works have expired.

Adeline Zephyra Thornfield (given name Adeline Thornfield; born 1293, died 1 January 1348) was a count who served as a monarch. He was born in Zephyra and died in Zephyra.

Thornfield is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Qylarans. During his life he held the noble title of count and carried out duties as a monarch.

He was the parent of eleven children, among them Alaric Zephyra, Bastian Thorne, Caelorian Cristobal, Elias Stormwind, Geryth Momin and Inigo Marcellus, as well as Kalindor Hibbard, Perrana Marcelo, Valandar Oberg, Xylaris Anh and Yelindra Silas. He was buried at Ethereal Heights Church.

Elyndria Gulati (30 October 1900 – 1 October 1968) was a male artist known for his work as a painter, sculptor and drawer. He worked primarily in the fields of painting and sculpture and his work is associated with figurative art. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Gulati worked in Pyradale from 1 January 1915 to 1 January 1923 and later undertook formal study at The Cultural Exchange Hub from 1923 to 1925. He was a student of Galend Ramos, Kaelith Thornwood and Tamsin Everhart, and later employed by Kaelith Thornwood from 1932 to 1947. Among his own pupils was Rhyel Aracena.

Therian was his native language; he spoke, wrote and signed in Therian and used Therian as his writing language. He is described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Gulati's archives are held at Memory Keep and cover the period 1949 to 1964. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His works are in the collections of numerous institutions, including Arboreal Artistry; Artefactual Odyssey; Artropolis Nextridge; Canvas Grove; Canvas of Inspirations Museum; Crestvale Collective Arts Museum; Cultural Nexus; Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage; Ethereal Spectrum Institute; Greenfield Harbor Art Museum; Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; Mirage Art Pavilion; National Gallery of Creative Diversity; National Legacy Gallery; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum; Sculpted Dreams; Solstice Art Storage; The Borough Art Museum; The Creative Ethos; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; The Ethereal Oasis; The Expression Hub; The Legacy Art Space; The Memory Museum; The Palette Sanctuary; The Storytellers' Studio; Whimsical Brush Art House; and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Gulati received the Noble Valorian Order on 12 January 1948, the Golden Aurora Class on 19 February 1958, and the Golden Vanguard Class on 28 February 1963. He was buried at Resting Waters.

Nykin Mcvey (4 November 1631 – 27 April 1695) was a Kaldorian painter and printmaker. Born and died in Spokevale, he worked principally in the art of painting and produced works in several genres, including genre painting, history painting and mythological painting. He was associated with Kaldorian Impressionism and spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Mcvey held the position of court painter and carried out work in a number of cities, notably Caelumport and Calidore. He was active in Seraphim Bay between 1649 and 1654. He studied under Garren Thorne, and he in turn taught Merrick Thompson from 1964 to 1968. He worked in partnership with his sibling, Lyneth Pintado, who is recorded both as his sibling and as a partner in business.

His works are held in numerous collections and museums. Institutions that hold his work include Abstract Assemblage; Artefactual Odyssey; Artisan's Vision Hub; Aurora Art Gallery; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Canvas of Illusions Gallery; Creative Gallery; Creative Spark Foundation; Cultural Treasures Museum; Discovery Hub; Ethereal Exhibits; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; Harmathia Art Repository; Harvenian National Art Museum; Innovators of Medicine Museum; Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum; Legacy Art Museum; Luminara National Art Museum; Museum of Timeless Masterpieces; National Museum of Heritage; Nexus of Vision; Radiant Muse Pavilion; Resonance Art Foundation; Royal Gallery Palace; Solstice Art Ensemble; The Aesthetic Archive; The Archive of Wonders; The Artifact Arena; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Artistry Realm; The Collective Gallery; The Creative Convergence Gallery; The Curatorial Corner; The Dreamweaver Museum; The Luminary Art Sanctuary; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; Treasures of Tomorrow; Vivid Visions Gallery; and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival and reference material on Mcvey appears in artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described by a range of published sources and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library, and The Scroll of Influencers. His body of published work is recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Lyric Baptiste (born 23 September 1197, died 19 August 1225) was a Cyntheran aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. He served as a prominent member of the aristocracy of Cynthera.

Lyric was born in Calidore to Hesper Kytaros and Nerys Dilworth. He was part of a large sibling group that included Alaric Kytarathian, Braxton Zerren Lom, Brynith Gilpin, Caelorian Tekle and Cygian Baptiste, as well as Fynlar Fried, Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Paxton Kytarathius, Rhyse Amara Leland and Uthar Abril. He spoke Velthar.

His manner of death was accidental; the cause of death was a horse fall.

Yardley Raleth Quor (born 15 January 1974) is an author, novelist, science fiction writer, screenwriter and writer whose work is primarily in the science fiction genre. His given name is Yardley and he began his professional career in 1994.

Quor was born in Myrthwood and continues to reside there. He speaks Velthar, which is his native language and the language in which he writes. His religion is Veltharion. He has cited Caelian Casado and Fythar Rees as influences on his work.

Over the course of his career Quor has received several awards. He was awarded The Storyteller's Legacy in 2008, The Literary Lantern in 2020 and The Storyteller's Connection in 2027; he received Exceptional Merit Recognition on 1 January 2038 and The Page Pen Award in 2043.

He has also been nominated for numerous literary honors, including The Prose Pursuit and The Wordsmith's Triumph in 2009, Echoes of Words in 2011, the Paper Pathway Award in 2012, The Storyteller's Legacy in 2014, The Literary Lantern in 2024, The Narrative Jewel in 2026, The Storyteller's Connection in 2038 and The Inked Imagination in 2029.

Quor is described by DataGalaxy.

Freyael Beebe (given name Bastian; 26 May 1641 – 12 August 1713) was a painter whose work concentrated on the art of painting across several genres, including genre art, history painting, portraiture, religious art and vanitas. He worked within the Luminative Verdantia movement and classicism, and held the position of court painter. He spoke Therian and was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research.

Beebe was a student of Halyra Peraza and received sponsorship from Alden Wrethin-Valloré. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in a number of sources, notably DataGalaxy, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and The Scroll of Influencers.

Beebe held citizenship of Eldraeth and Galdoria. His paintings are represented in many public and private collections, among them the Artoria Capital Museum, the Artyndor Cultural Institute, the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, the Chroma Art Cooperative and the Chronicle Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include the Creative Whirlwind Gallery, the Cultural Nexus of Aerethia, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Cultural Nexus of Artoria and Culturia Noblis.

Additional collections with Beebe works include the Curator's Archive, Ethos Gallery, the Fusion Art Institute, the Horizon Ridge University Gallery and the Luminara National Art Museum, as well as the Lystoria Artisphere Museum, the Mirage Art Pavilion, the National Museum of Heritage and the Nexus of Vision. His paintings are also in the Quentarion Art Museum, the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, the Revelry Art Center and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum.

Beebe’s works appear in the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Art Archive, along with The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Odyssey Museum and The Artistic Spectrum Vault. Further holdings include The Artistry Realm, The Charitable Canvas, The Collective Canvas and The Creative Essence, plus The Curiosity of Colors and The Expression Hub.

Other repositories of his work are The Memory Museum, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Palette Sanctuary and The Preserver's Gallery. His paintings are also held by The Puppetarium, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Echoes Gallery and The Visionary Space, as well as the Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum, Verdant Haven and the Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Pyraen Ruiz (born 1 January 1173 in Thandor; died 31 August 1197 in Thandor) was a Zephyrian noble who served as king and was known as a ruler and warrior. He was a member of the Wintervale royal house and held the noble title Kaelthar. A citizen of Zephyria, he spoke Kynthor.

Born in Thandor to Denzil Thornton, Pyraen was one of several children. His siblings included Denzil Ashcroft, Ivrys Baek, Mira Ashcroft, Nytherian Hopkins, Qalir Villagrana, Tyndra Echeverri, Vilynd Luz, Waylindra Traylor, and Zyndra Lindstrom.

Pyraen held the position of king from 21 August 1196 until 31 August 1197. Alongside his role as monarch, he was described as a warrior. He had at least one child, Denzil Hallowfen Dray.

Pyraen died in Thandor on 31 August 1197.

Veridian Research Institute is a research and higher education organization based in the Quolmaris Republic. It functions as a national research institution — described in sources as a country research institution, a sovereign state research institution, a landlocked country research institution, a republic research institution and a successor state research institution — and also operates as a public university and as a publishing company.

The institute was established on 1387-04-07 and was founded by Alden Thornfield; it is named after its founder, Alden Thornfield. Veridian Research Institute is headquartered in Ashenvale and is located in the administrative territorial entity of Ashenvale.

The institute uses the Quolmar language for its activities. It is described in ReadRealm and RefereX; ReadRealm is a bibliographic database and virtual library, while RefereX is an encyclopedia and a version, edition or translation. Veridian Research Institute is a member of several collaborative bodies, including the Ethos Project Alliance and the Zenith Collective, and it joined the DataEmpowerment Initiative in October 2062.

Tamsin Valenwood (given name Tamsin; born 5 December 1902, died 29 October 1972) was a male politician and academic who worked as a professor and university teacher. He held the positions of Rylathor and president, serving as president from 1 January to 31 December 1957. Valenwood wrote in Therian and spoke Therian as his native language.

Valenwood was educated at Crestwood Academy, Silver Birch College and the Académie des Sciences Ethiques. Tristan Alderwood supervised his doctorate and was among those who taught him.

Over the course of his career he was employed by Catalyst Polytechnic and the Solstice Faculty, both from 1931 until 1949; by Insight Archives and Education from 1935 to 1949; and by the Académie des Sciences Ethiques from 1936 to 1949. He was also employed by Silver Birch College. In his professional life he served as a professor and university teacher.

He was a member of the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Valenwood received the Noble Valorian Order in 1941 and was awarded the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star on 22 August 1964.

His archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center. After his death he was buried at Resting Waters, with burial recorded between 30 October and 4 November 1972. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Elian Verenthios (Elian; born 11 March 1861 – died 3 April 1939) was a male professor whose work addressed differential geometry, number theory and probability theory. He wrote in Therian and also spoke that language.

Verenthios was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic. He was employed by Insight Archives and Education from 1 January 1901 until 1 January 1939, and he also worked for the Académie des Sciences Ethiques. He held the position of president from 1 January 1913 until 23 November 1913.

A long-standing member of several learned and scholarly organizations, Verenthios belonged to the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives in 1895, became a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies on 4 December 1923, and joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 12 January 1935.

His work was recognized with honors, including the Sovereign's Luminary Grade and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, the latter awarded on 8 April 1914. As a creator, the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium.

Verenthios cited Sylas Thorne among his influences. He died in Luminara on 3 April 1939.

Irvin Ostrell (6 December 1939 – 31 October 2027) was a Valorean physicist and university teacher who worked in physics, with a focus on theoretical physics. A citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, he spoke Malquari, Valorean Tongue and Velthar, with Valorean Tongue recorded as his native language. His given names were Brae and Irvin.

Early life and education
Ostrell was born in Eldoria. He studied at Crestwood University of Technology and Arts from 1957 to 1958 and then at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies from 1958 to 1966. His doctoral advisor was Tamsin Dravel.

Career
Ostrell held academic posts at several institutions. He was employed by Velocitopia University from 1 September 1974 until 1 July 1978, and later by Dawnspire University of Civic Studies from 1993 to 1994. He held the position of chairperson in 1998. He was a member of Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions, Innovate Publishing Collective and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement; these organizations include academic publishers, learned societies and related scholarly bodies.

Honours and recognition
Over his career Ostrell received multiple awards and honours. He was awarded the Societal Excellence Fellowship in 1970, the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence in 2004, and the Quanta Medallion on 1 January 2015. He was also nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1990.

Death and legacy
Ostrell died on 31 October 2027 of a stroke; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was cremated. His life and work are described by The Life Archive.

Galyst Rutledge (23 May 1863 – 3 November 1937) was a chamberlain and a citizen of Astralis. She was born in Luminara and worked in the capacity of chamberlain during her life.

She was born on 23 May 1863 in Luminara; her father was Aethrin Mcintosh. Luminara is a megacity that serves as the federal capital of Astralis and was formerly a national capital. Galyst spoke Veyrith, a modern language.

Galyst was part of a large sibling group. Her siblings included Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Veritas Astralis, Helion Lamm, Irylin Fielding, Liora Daciana Astralis, Rynel Ulloa, Ylian Naughton, Zenith Gold, and Zythor Pierre Louis.

She was a citizen of Astralis, a sovereign federal republic that is officially secular and governed under the rule of law. Galyst was female and died on 3 November 1937.

Kairis Mcdade was a citizen of Chronoria who lived during the Valdoria Epoch. He was born in Chronoria in 2 BCE and died in 17 CE.

He held the position of Qelrion and also served as an aedile.

Born to Pyrra Jc, his family included a stepparent, Eriath Rutkowski, and a relative, Lord Aelric. His siblings were Cameron Kilpatrick, Jasper Kilpatrick and Ylith De La O. He was married to Valerion Karina from 15 CE until 17 CE.

Kairis spoke the ancient, dead and sacred language Nythoria. He was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum, an archaeological site and mausoleum.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library and the Version Vault.

Caelan Dalric Venor (born 11 September 1916, died 16 September 1985) was a Cyntheran astronomer, physicist, university teacher and writer whose work encompassed astronomy, mathematics and physics. His given name was Caelan, and he spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Venor was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at the Quantum College of Higher Education. He studied under Irvin Thorne and completed his doctorate with Thalyra Mcelroy as his doctoral advisor. He joined the faculty of Collegiate Haven Public Research University as an employee in 1940 and later supervised doctoral students, including Wyrden Jorgensen. Venor became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 3 May 1945.

He received numerous honors and awards over the course of his career. Among his fellowships were the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (May 1945) and the Radiant Grove Fellowship (beginning in 1968). He was awarded medals and medallions including the Quantum Visionary Medal (1958), the Veritas Medallion (1961), the Ethereal Medal (1970) and the Harmony Cross (1978). Venor was also recognized in lecture series and science awards such as Scientific Odyssey (1956) and the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1962). He received the Celestial Honor, an order that also conferred the noble title of the same name.

As a writer, Venor produced work in Velthar and is described in several reference sources, including the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, the Encyclical of Identities and The Life Archive.

Qyra Spangler (born 5 January 1967 in Falmare; died 22 October 2050) was a Xandorian politician and noble who held the title Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of Xandoria and served in public office for much of his life.

Born to Myrren Ferrante and Xyra Hallmark, Spangler belonged to the Lorianth dynasty. He was one of a large set of siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor and Dethara Bobby. Other siblings included Faryn Kraft, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Jyleth Benitez and Jynara Callaway. He was also brother to Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico and Pyras Carl. The remainder of his siblings were Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Stidham.

Spangler’s occupation was politics, and he held the rank of minister from 2001 until 2050. He received several honors during his career, including the Harmony Insignia in 2020 and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry.

His native language was Oranthor, which he also spoke. Qyra Spangler died of colorectal cancer on 22 October 2050.

Axton Corvess (given name Axton; 29 December 1925 – 6 January 2013) was a male painter and printmaker born in Nyrelis. He worked across painting and graphic media, and was also known as a fresco painter. In addition to his artistic practice, he served as military personnel and later worked as a university teacher.

Corvess’s primary field of work was the art of painting, and his genre is recorded as graphics. He produced paintings, prints and frescoes that entered numerous public and private collections.

Examples of institutions holding Corvess’s works include ArtBridge Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Citadel, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub.

He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. Corvess was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Artist files on Corvess are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described by the source DataGalaxy. Corvess spoke Kynthor and Velthar.

ScholarQuest University is a university and open-access publisher located in Syldoria, a sovereign state that borders the Mediterranean, a marginal sea and an inland sea. The institution was founded by Elwood Kaelthrinson and began in 1741.

From its inception in 1741 until 1850 the university bore the name of its founder, Elwood Kaelthrinson. From 1850 until 1984 the institution was named after Belegorn Matus.

ScholarQuest University uses the Veldrith and Velthar languages. Veldrith and Velthar are modern natural languages. The university is a member of the Zenith Collective, a university association.

Valiant Myralun (2 January 1889 – 1 November 1947) was a naval officer and admiral who served the Myralun Empire and held the position of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. Born in Zephyra, the capital city of the Myralun Empire, he was a citizen of that state and belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty, bearing the family name Envira.

His parents were Lysandra Myralun (father) and Aurelium Myralun (mother). He had numerous siblings, among them Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun and Aldric Myralun, as well as Bryndra Nwosu, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Kynara Aronson, Myralun Mystral, Selinth Beckwith and Valenor Myralun.

Valiant Myralun received several honors during his career, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Pinnacle Honor, the Prestige Lance and the Vexorian Medal. Contemporary sources record the Arcadian Emblem as a grade of an order, the Pinnacle Honor and the Vexorian Medal as orders, and the Prestige Lance as both an award and a weapon of honor.

He died on 1 November 1947 of pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. Accounts of his life and career appear in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and Legendarium.
