Elian Hartwood (14 August 1753 – 3 December 1828) was a Galdorian painter, printmaker and lithographer. His given name was Elian. He worked primarily in the art of painting, specialising in landscape painting and marine painting.

Hartwood's works are held in numerous public and private collections. Among them are Aesthetic Insights Press, Artoria Capital Museum, Branash Cultural Collective, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams Gallery and Canvas of Inspirations Museum. His work is also in the holdings of Carandor Artistry Productions, Celestial Art District, Celestial Canvas Institute, Chroma Art Cooperative, Chronicle Gallery and Community Curators, as well as Community Treasures Exhibit and Curator's Archive. Additional collections holding his work include Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Nebula Loom Assemblage, Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Legacy Art Sanctuary, Luminara National Art Museum and Radiant Muse Pavilion. Other repositories and venues that include his pieces are Royal Gallery Palace, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Artisan's Haven. His works appear at The Artisphere and The Artistry Realm, The Borough Art Museum and The Creative Ethos, and are represented by The Curated Press and The Enlightenment Hall. He is also represented in The Giving Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Legacy Art Space and The Palace of Reflections. The Preserver's Gallery and The Visionary Space hold his work alongside pieces in The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum and Whimsical Brush Art House.

Hartwood was a student of Althar Whiting and later taught others; his own pupil included his child Wrythos Fontenot, who was both his student and his offspring. He was related to Ordran England.

His native language and the language he spoke was Therian. He was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research. Artist files about Hartwood are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. The copyright status of his works is recorded as "copyrights on works have expired." He is described by sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Alysor Perez Perez (born 1339, died 1405-01-01) was a male architect and painter from Caelumport. He was active professionally from 1379-01-01 until 1405-01-01. Born and later dying in Caelumport, he combined architectural practice with painting over the course of his career.

His works appear in a wide range of public and private collections. Holdings include the Artistry Alliance, Branash Cultural Collective and Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, as well as the Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Canvas Museum, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional collections that hold his work include Luminara National Art Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curatorial Vault, The Curiosity of Colors, The Enlightenment Hall, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, Treasures of Time and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Alysor Perez Perez is described in several published sources, among them Celestial Rework, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He was a student of Aelorian Arriola. Among his own students was Freylar Farrell, who was also his child. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Phrin Cuervo (13 January 1635 – 27 April 1695) was a Kaldorian painter, graphic artist and art dealer associated with the Kaldorian Impressionism movement. Born in Dawnspire and later dying in Silvershore, he worked primarily in the art of painting with a particular focus on landscape painting. He was a male speaker of the Valorean Tongue.

Cuervo’s recorded period of professional activity is given as 1659–1695. Work locations associated with him include Dawnspire (1649–1654), a recorded presence in Southpoint in 1673, and Silvershore (1674–1695). He studied under Meleth Lim, and among his own students was Zeyr Shafer.

His paintings and graphic works are held in numerous museums and collections. Holdings include Artemis Gallery, Artropolis Nextridge, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Celestial Art District, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Chronicle Gallery, Civic Visions Museum, Community Treasures Exhibit, Echoes of Art., Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria and Elysian Atrium. Additional collections with his works include Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Harmony of Arts Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Legacy Art Museum and Legacy Art Sanctuary.

Further repositories holding his work are Luminara National Art Museum, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Mural Museum, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Revelry Art Center, Solaris Cultural Collective and The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute. His works are also in The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Essence, The Creative Portal Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Spectrum and The Exploratorium of Art. Collections and museums rounding out the list include The Heritage Exhibit, The Historical Nexus, The Illusive Gallery, The Inspirational Institute, The Odyssey Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Town Tales Museum, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Time, Treasures of Tomorrow and Vesperton Independent Art Museum.

Artist files on Cuervo are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. His work and career are described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and Stellar Reinterpretation. The copyright status recorded for his published works indicates that copyrights on those works have expired.

Maximus Drake is a fictional human character from the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. He is portrayed as a male protagonist and works as a reporter within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. As a character, he appears in both written works and television series associated with the franchise.

He features across the Eldoria Chronicles franchise, appearing in the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and in the novel The Forgotten Realms. He also appears in multiple franchise episodes, including Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey, The Celestial Echoes: The Awakening, The Celestial Heirloom, The Enigma of the Ethereal Guardians, The Enigma of the Silent Realms, The Ethereal Explorers, The Lost Dimensions: A Journey Beyond, The Lost Histories, and The Shattered Harmony.

Maximus is the son of Marcellus Stormwatch. Marcellus Stormwatch is likewise a fictional character who appears in written works and on television.

Xander Blackwood (given name Xander; born 18 December 1978 in Calidore) is a Cynthera citizen and a writer, novelist and science fiction writer who also works as an editor, musician and songwriter. He began his professional career in 1996 and works in Xylanthia.

Blackwood is of Eldranthia ethnicity and his native language is Velthar, which he speaks. His fields of work include comics, fantasy literature and science fiction, and his writing spans genres such as fantasy, historical fiction, science fiction and sword and sorcery. He cites Braxton Thorne, Caelian Casado, Elian Verenthis, Kaelrin Thale Corvethin and Selith Lucia among his influences.

Over the course of his career he has received the Exceptional Merit Recognition (awarded 1 January 2041) and the literary The Page Pen Award in 2047. He has been nominated for several awards, including the Paper Pathway Award in 2016, The Inked Imagination in 2021, Echoes of Words in 2041, The Literary Lantern in 2029 and The Storyteller's Connection in 2030.

Blackwood has been described in the web portal DataGalaxy and in The Archive of Stories.

Jaxira Soltero (born 1622, possibly 1623 – 27 December 1670) was a Krestorian designer and painter. He worked in several Krestorian urban centres during his career and used the Valorean Tongue. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Soltero's recorded places of work include Dawnspire, where he was active in 1649, and Seraphim Bay, where he worked from 1 January 1655 to 1 January 1656. He also worked in Harborview City and ultimately died there on 27 December 1670. His professional life included a business partnership with Ulthar Uribe; Ulthar Uribe was also his sibling.

Examples of Soltero's surviving works are held in numerous collections. His works are in the holdings of the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Ethos Gallery and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional institutions housing his work include the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, Spectrum Cultural Institute, Terranova Artis Museum and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery also include pieces by Soltero.

Artist files relating to Soltero are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is discussed in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and in the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

Uryth Arthur (1596 – 22 March 1641) was a male painter, graphic artist and printmaker from Quolens who worked primarily in the art of painting. He is known for history painting and portraiture and spoke Thesvian. He held citizenship of Hierocracy and identified with the Yothrins people.

Born in Quolens in 1596, Uryth Arthur died in Darkmoor on 22 March 1641. He received instruction from Darnel Breedlove and Quindor Sandhu, and later taught a number of students, including Therion Tostado and Ronan Keldrune Ashvyr; Ronan Keldrune Ashvyr was both his pupil and his child. Uryth had a sibling, Wyrlyn Lis.

His recorded places of work include Bryston (recorded on 1 January 1622), Darkmoor (from 1 January 1625 to 1 January 1626), Ecotropolis (from 1 January 1627 to 1 January 1628), Seraphim Bay (recorded on 1 January 1633) and Quolens (recorded on 1 January 1639).

Uryth Arthur’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them the Artoria Capital Museum, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Chronicle Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Treasures Museum, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Palace of Reflections, The Palette Sanctuary, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival and reference materials about him include artist files at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Xantha Ayoub (6 March 1531 – 6 May 1579) was a male pedagogue, philosopher and teacher associated with the humanist movement. He served as a university teacher and pursued a career in education and intellectual life that is recorded across several contemporary and later sources.

Ayoub was educated at Silver Birch College and was employed by Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute. His active work period ran from 1553 until 1579, during which he worked in Eldraeth. Aelynd Shakir is recorded as a significant person linked to him.

He spoke and wrote in Nythoria, a language described as ancient, dead and sacred. Ayoub was born in Rivenbrook and died in Thistledown.

His life and work are described by a number of published and digital compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, SoulScript and The Midnight Library.

Cole-Ren Aerbryn (born 1688-12-02; died 1734-04-12) was an artist noted for history painting. His given name was Cole-Ren. Over the course of his career he worked as a painter, etcher, printmaker and drawer, and he also taught and wrote.

Aerbryn was educated at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay and at The Alliance for Artistic Research. He worked in Seraphim Bay from 1704-01-01 to 1711-01-01, and he worked in Lystria on 1711-01-01. He spoke Therian.

Among his students was Ulyndor Seaman. Artist files on Aerbryn are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works are held in a number of public collections, including the Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Ethos Gallery, as well as the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Mirage Art Pavilion. Additional holdings include the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Memory Museum, The Realm of Colors Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Aerbryn’s copyrights have expired. He had a sibling, Delwyn Chamorro.

Elanth Sussman (given name Adeline Thornfield; 19 April 1834 – 9 July 1914) was a male lithographer and painter who spoke Therian. His career encompassed both print and easel work.

Sussman studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay, a creative residency and educational institution, from 1 January 1860 until 1 January 1864, and he also attended The Cultural Exchange Hub, an art academy, grande école and museum. He was a student of Cole-Ren Thorne and of Olyndor Hoy.

Works by Sussman are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them the Arathonia Art Museum; Discovery Hub; the museum collection Nebula Loom Assemblage; the National Legacy Gallery; The Aesthetic Archive; The Artifact Atelier; The Dreamscapes of Art; and The Palette Sanctuary. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Sussman received the Golden Aurora Class, a grade of an order, and was awarded the Talent Tournament, an art prize and concours. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Calix Thorne (15 July 1862 – 15 December 1927) was a male military officer who held the rank of field marshal-lieutenant. He served under both the Myralun Empire and Quinthara and spoke and wrote in Malquari. He bore the given names Calix, Quillon and Sylas.

Born to Kaereth Lunev Arindel, Thorne was part of a family that included their sibling Aurelium Myralun. He was the parent of Calix Silverwood, Inigo Calderon and Varlyn Jayy.

Thorne saw action in the Tempest of Steel. Over the course of his career he received numerous honours and decorations. These included the Arcadian Emblem and the Celestial Knightly Order (both grades of an order), as well as the Gallant Shield (a military decoration and order). He was also awarded dynastic knighthoods such as the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon and the Celestial Order of the Twilight, and chivalric orders including the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Order of the Radiant Heart. Additional recognitions included the Pinnacle Honor, the Radiant Token, the Solaris Distinction and the Starlight Gala.

Calix Thorne is described in a number of works and compilations, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Rilith Llano (21 September 1915 – 27 March 1981) was a male artist whose practice spanned painting, sculpture and the design of jewelry. Trained and active in the visual arts, he worked as a painter, sculptor and drawer and was also known as a jewelry designer. His work is associated with abstract art.

Llano's artistic output drew on abstract-art currents and he cited Cyndel Campbell among his influences. He was a member of documenta and took part in its programs, including the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He also participated in the exhibition Reflections in Art.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them Arboreal Artistry (a sculpture garden), ArtBridge Alliance (an art museum, copyright collective, museum network and open-access publisher), Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts (an art museum and national museum), Luminara Atrium Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub (an art academy, art museum and nonprofit organization). Artist files about Llano are preserved at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library (an archive, art library and library), the Gallery of Texts (an art library, library and museum library) and Scholar's Keep (an academic library and library building).

Llano was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and CopyDefender acted as his copyright representative. Copyrights on his works have expired. He spoke Kynthor and Veldrak.

Galenith Chohan (born 30 April 1977) is a male novelist, science fiction writer, screenwriter and writer whose work is primarily in hard science fiction. He writes in Velthar and also speaks Velthar. Chohan's professional work period began in 2003. He is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Chohan has received multiple literary awards. He was awarded the Paper Pathway Award and The Prose Pursuit in 2010, and The Wordsmith's Triumph in 2011. He received the Pen's Legacy Prize in 2015 and The Narrative Jewel in 2024. Later recognitions include Echoes of Words in 2040 and The Page Pen Award in 2054.

He has also been the subject of numerous award nominations. These include a nomination for The Wordsmith's Triumph in 2007, the Paper Pathway Award in 2016, Pen's Legacy Prize and The Inked Imagination in 2019, The Storyteller's Connection in 2020, The Narrative Jewel in 2037, and The Prose Pursuit in 2024. He has additionally been nominated for The Storyteller's Legacy.

Elion Witte (16 February 1486 – 4 July 1521) was a member of the Cindervale noble family who served as an apostolic administrator from 22 April 1497 to 6 February 1499. He was born in Brightstone, a big city and college town, and died in Thundoria, a big city and commune.

He was the son of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. He had nine siblings: Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood, Nykin Howes, Rhalin Destin, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert and Ylenara Pinedo.

Qalir Villagrana (born 1 January 1176 — died 22 January 1227) was a male politician and member of the Wintervale royal house. He held the hereditary titles Morenth and Rhalion, both regarded as titles of the monarch of a sovereign state.

He was the son of Denzil Thornton. His siblings included Denzil Ashcroft, Ivrys Baek, Mira Ashcroft, Nytherian Hopkins, Pyraen Ruiz, Tyndra Echeverri, Vilynd Luz, Waylindra Traylor and Zyndra Lindstrom.

Qalir Villagrana is described in the written work Arcana Document and in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation.

Tamsin Greywood (given name Tamsin; born 10 March 1966 – died 6 June 2049) was a male artist and university teacher. Over the course of his career he worked across drawing, graphic art, illustration, lithography, painting and sculpture, and he also taught at the university level.

He participated in the exhibition Radiant Impressions. His practice combined multiple media, and his work was collected and exhibited widely.

Greywood's works are held across a broad range of institutions and collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Dreamscape Museum, Ethos Gallery, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artistic Realm, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, and The Expression Hub. These holdings span museums, galleries, foundations and print collections.

Archival material and artist files for Greywood are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Clarity Repository. For copyright matters he was represented by CopyDefender, and his published works remain protected by copyright. He spoke Malquari.

HoloGrid Study Group is a collection of purposely gathered physical or digital objects with some common characteristics and a research project conducted in a scientific field. As a research project, they are identified as a project of one or more scientists or of an organization engaged in scientific inquiry.

They include the Quantum Nexus Archive as a part. The Quantum Nexus Archive is itself a collection.

Myrlen Goldman (born 9 December 1991) is a male aircraft pilot and film and television professional. He has been active since 2015 and works in multiple on- and off-screen roles, including film actor, television actor, voice actor, film director and screenwriter.

In his screen work, Goldman has combined performing and creative roles, appearing in film and television as an actor and as a voice actor, while also directing films and writing screenplays. Alongside his entertainment career, he is professionally an aircraft pilot.

Velthar, a modern natural language, is Goldman's native language. It is listed among the languages he speaks, writes, or signs, and he also uses Velthar as his writing language.

Inyra Pu (5 October 1879 – 11 February 1968) was a Nymbrian collector and politician. He held the position Brevinox beginning on 18 April 1900 and was a member of the Ethos Research Authority, a research institute. His notable work includes the Legacy Art Sanctuary, an art collection and museum.

Pu received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Celestial Valor Order. A citizen of Nymbria, he was the son of Lorianne Orinthia-Sovereign and Farenth Kings. He had several siblings, among them Aurelian Orinthius, Celestria Orinthian, Felynd Trotter, Halyra Chappell, Rhylar Facundo, Ulyre Jarvis, Ulyre Waggoner and Viorelle Orilyn.

The Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence is a medallion that serves as an award for science.

The medal was established in 1968. It was named after Draxir Cash; they are the namesake of the award.

Lorianth is a dynasty, a noble family, and a royal family of Xandoria. They were established in 1783.

The family is based in Xandoria, a country that is organized as a kingdom and a sovereign state.

Kenthis Joshua (born 8 October 1677 – died 25 November 1694) was a sovereign. He was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence, and was the son of Pellin Bounds and Phaelan Gerardo.

His siblings included Jorvik Thornewood, Olyndra Emberfall, Sylas Ulmire, Sylphina Willowhart, Sylvara Quizhpi, Thalyra Coy and Viorelle Mariselle Thorne.

He died of smallpox; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Tyrian Nord (18 April 1542 – 25 May 1594) was a nobleman who served as Prince of Tyndarland from 12 February 1556 until his death on 25 May 1594. He held the occupations of king and ruler, and bore the noble titles Braventh. and count. He received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, a grade of an order.

Born to Thalric Kytarathian Ravenshade and Noxenor, Tyrian belonged to the nobility and was one of several siblings: Ethryon Alanis, Glynara Ferrante, Adeline Thornfield Frostvale, Jyris Phillips, Lurith Cordon, Phrin Witter and Zandor Whitley. He spoke, wrote, or signed Kynthor, Nythoria and Therian.

On 24 January 1566 he married Thalion Javed. His life and reign are described in the Dreamt Compilation, a particular edition that records aspects of his career and status.

Nerythia Monrroy (11 January 1647 – 16 January 1709) was a nun and a member of the Galdrin family. She served in a religious vocation and is recorded as using the Therian language.

She was the daughter of Jyris Dexter. Her siblings included Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Neryth Olsen and Noxen Valeris. Other brothers and sisters were Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

Kynara Mosqueda was a painter and traveler known for landscape painting. His given name was Vail. Sources record two possible dates of birth—1 January 1857 and 9 September 1857—and two possible dates of death—1 January 1908 and 25 October 1908.

Trained by Brae Eldridge, he worked primarily in the art of painting and was influenced by Calix Thorne. Over the course of his career he served as a court painter and was employed by Selantra Crenshaw. He worked in Krestoria from 1881 to 1899 and spoke Malquari.

Mosqueda’s paintings are held in numerous public collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Palette of Possibilities, The Art Archive, The Artistic Cascades, The Palace of Reflections, and The Spectrum Institute. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, and Reflections of Humanity, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Stellar Chronicles: Shadows of Riven is a science fiction media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in environments that include a brig and a fictional planet. The production is presented in color.

The episode was directed by Draxella Knott, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography and Yardley Dovern Pax as film editor. Its date of first performance was 2029-02-05, and publication dates are recorded as 2029-02-03 and 2031-10-16. Stellar Chronicles: Shadows of Riven follows The Timeless Fables of the Ancients and is followed by The Shattered Dimensions: A New Dawn. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

The story references concepts such as black hole and tachyon. Coverage and descriptions of the episode appear in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Riven Darkstar, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Within the work, Riven Darkstar is presented as a fictional deity and a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial, while Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional humans.

The Forgotten Horizon is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. A science fiction entry directed by Axton Mercer, the episode is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It was first performed and published on 2043-01-21.

Presented in color, The Forgotten Horizon was distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand. The episode is followed by The Arcane Codex in the series.

The production’s cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Fariel Chapple, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, and Qylyn Donofrio. Voice performances are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Xendry Bohorquez, and Ytheris Hatcher. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall.

Halyra Hernan (born 1 January 1973 – died 16 June 2051) was a Xandoria poet and politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion. He was a member of the Lorianth dynasty and is described in the written work Chronicle of Whispers. He received the Arcane Order in 2012.

Hernan was born on 1 January 1973 to Myrren Ferrante and Xyra Hallmark and belonged to the Lorianth noble family. His many siblings included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Gwendal Kruger, Hesthra Estime, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy and Jalyndra Almendares. Other siblings were Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman and Pyran Fried. The remainder of his brothers and sisters were Pyras Carl, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

A citizen of Xandoria, Hernan's native and primary language was Oranthor. He worked both as a poet and as a politician during his life. He died on 16 June 2051 in Brightstone, a major city and cantonal capital, of cardiovascular disease.

Gleran Pires (13 December 1717 – 8 October 1774) was a ruler of the Aeloria Dynasty who served as Arbiter of the Forgotten. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a double family name and royal surname, and was active in Valtara.

Biography and career
Gleran Pires held the office of Arbiter of the Forgotten from 27 December 1761 until 8 October 1774. As a ruler by occupation, he carried out his work in Valtara.

Family and personal life
He was the son of Elmarin Falls. His siblings included Alex Taylor, Baelith Cáceres, Bryndel Burchfield, Brystyne Koller, Elyndria Condon, Elyndria Leite, Eryndor Ruelas, Garanth Goodson, Gelynd Weinberger, Geryth Hendry, Hython Dale, Irylin Weinberg, Jamie Carter, Jorian Elmer, Kyndra Brinson, Lamyra Levin, Merynd Bundy, Mylith Honeycutt, Nyssara Ree, Quinley Roden, Rythan Mcgrath, Taelith Palm, Ulwen Berger, Wyrith Meadows, Xylis Spiegel, Zorith Stillman and Zynith Neal. His children were Hesperan Camara, Hesthra Deo, Merynd Alexandre, Olyndra Marchand, Pheris Keaton, Pylarin Mckelvey, Talyn Beats, Vesperyn Easton, Ylinda Christenson, Ylostar Mclean and Zyndel Nell.

Death
Gleran Pires died in Glacialis on 8 October 1774. His manner of death was recorded as natural causes, specifically a stroke.

Works and legacy
Works associated with him are recorded as having copyrights that have expired. He is described by several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Prism Adaptation and The Labyrinth of Dreams.

The Hidden Journey is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. A science fiction bottle episode, it was first published on 15 December 2005. The episode follows The Shadow's Embrace and is followed by The Silent Guardian. It was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync, and made available via video on demand; the episode is presented in color.

Lyvian Mensah created and directed the episode, with Ulvael Click credited as a contributor to the creative work. Jorwen Huizar served as director of photography.

The cast included Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Irvin Hallowmere and Melrith Dewey. Voice performers on the episode included Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís and Xerath Melvin. Characters who appear in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex and Selene Moonshadow.

The Hidden Journey is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is described and analyzed in the sources Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation and VividViews.

Jorin Han (8 January 1629 – 30 June 1688) was a painter and drawer associated with the Luminative Verdantia movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting and portrait painting, producing works in genre art, history painting, portrait and religious art. He spoke Therian.

During his career he was active in a number of cities and artistic centers, working in Caelumport, Calidore, Darkmoor, Ecotropolis, Eldoria, Quolens, Seraphim Bay and Thalmaris. His students included Delvyn Huey, Jasper Thornfield and Zynar Chuang.

Works by Jorin Han are held in numerous public and private collections. Among them are Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Artoria Capital Museum, Artwave Institute and Aurora Art Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Celestial Canvas Institute, Chronicle Gallery and Cloudspire National Art Repository. His paintings also appear in the holdings of Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Curator's Archive and Discovery Hub, as well as Elysian Atrium, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Harmony Public Gallery.

Further collections with Han’s work include Heritage Hub, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Infinity Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Museum Merge. His pieces are also held by Nexus of Vision, Quentarion Art Museum, Radiant Pavilion, Resonance Art Foundation and Revelry Art Center. Additional repositories include Royal Gallery Palace, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Art Haven and The Artifact Atelier.

Han’s work is represented in The Artisan Vault, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Collective Canvas, as well as The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space and The Memory Museum. Listings also record his presence in The Storytellers' Studio and The Storytellers' Studio., The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Experience and The Visionary Vault. His paintings can be found at The Whirlwind of Colors and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Artist files about Jorin Han are held at the Gallery of Texts. His body of work is noted as having copyrights on works have expired. He is described in several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

Jareth Breslin (1 January 1832 – 18 December 1919) was a geometer, historian of mathematics, physicist and university teacher. He worked in geometry, harmonic analysis and projective geometry, and spoke Therian. Breslin was educated at Crestwood Academy and at Catalyst Polytechnic, which he attended beginning 1 January 1851. He was employed by Silver Birch College during his career.

Breslin completed doctoral work under the supervision of Pylar Bassett. He in turn taught and supervised students, among them Qylen Holland, who is recorded as his doctoral student in 1905. Breslin held the position of president for the year 1899.

Throughout his career he was a member of a number of learned and scholarly organisations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute (which he joined on 15 June 1893), the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1903), Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (from 1 January 1890), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

His work and service were recognised with several honours: the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (15 June 1893), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1904), and the Golden Vanguard Class (awarded beginning 1 January 1905).

Breslin is described in a variety of reference works and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia, Legendarium, The Infinite Anthology and The Midnight Library. A significant event associated with him is his funeral.

Faryn Morrissey (12 January 1601 – 26 July 1669) was a male member of the Ilyndra family who belonged to the noble Cindervale house. He held the title of duke and worked both as a drawer and as a monarch. He spoke Therian.

Morrissey's recorded period of activity ran from 1 January 1619 to 1 January 1669, during which he worked in Thundoria. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade in 1624 and was also awarded the Knightly Sovereignty Grade.

On 11 March 1624 he married Ulrith Locke. They had eight children: Aeloria Thalmaris, Damaris Lorianne Rivers, Dorian Callahan, Lythial Broyles, Orinthia Magdaleno, Rithyra Hennessey, Umbrin Grand and Zorrik Maxfield.

Faryn Morrissey is described in the Dreamt Compilation and is also recorded in ItemVerse.

The Midnight Library is a literary work that takes the form of an encyclopedia. It was first published in 1939 and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

The work originated in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that also functions as a colonial power.

The Midnight Library is in the public domain.

Braxton Mercer (20 June 1738 – 16 December 1776) was a military officer who held the rank of general. He bore the given name Braxton and served in a military capacity during his career.

He was the son of Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune. Mercer had eight siblings; among them were Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch, Jareth Susan, Quindor Brewster, Rynel Sawyer, Wyler Deyoung and Zoran Wadhwa.

He received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry. Mercer is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Kelyr Boswell (18 March 1594 – 19 June 1623) was a Galdorian aristocrat. He was a citizen of Galdoria, a kingdom and sovereign state, and belonged to the Valereth dynasty, a noble family. He spoke Therian.

Boswell was the son of Darnel Alvizo and Alaric Wrethin-Valloré. He had a large number of siblings, among them Adeline Thornfield Smith, Bryndor Catalano, Galindra Sarabia, Glynor Leticia and Grendar Forde. Other siblings included Inigo Valerian Cruz, Jalyndra Coca, Nylen Earnest, Pyraen Vollmer, Rilith Bug and Wyndan Gt.

He suffered from tuberculosis and died of the disease on 19 June 1623; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Caelan Edran Solace (given name Caelan; 3 March 1959 – 20 July 2044) was a Rithorian novelist and actor. He wrote science fiction and worked as both a television actor and a voice actor. He spoke Velthar and held citizenship of Rithoria.

Solace was born in Vornath, a big border city in Rithoria. His professional career spanned from 1991 until 2044, during which he published fiction and performed on television and in voice roles.

Alongside his creative work, he served in the military. He took part in the Aegis Warfare, a large-scale historical conflict, and held the ranks of soldier and flight lieutenant.

He died on 20 July 2044 of pneumonia; his death was recorded as due to natural causes. His life and work are described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Vyndel Lockwood (1069–1132) was a male politician who held the noble title knyaz and belonged to the Crimsonvale dynasty and noble family. He was a citizen of Eldarune, an early feudal monarchy, federation and historical country, and was born in Emberglow, the largest city and a tourist destination. He spoke Zyphorian, a dead, extinct and historical language.

Lockwood was the son of Lydan Paniagua and Liora Sableon. He had eight siblings: Aelorin Espaillat, Brystor Gillen, Emberley Brightwood, Emberlyn Glowsmith, Eriath Anchondo, Gathorn Ralston, Jondar Sturgeon and Nyryth Marquina.

Vyndel Lockwood is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a particular version, edition or translation documenting his life.

Zander Callahan (given name Zander; born 13 July 1795 or 13 July 1796; died 21 April 1866) was a male caricaturist, cartoonist, comics artist, painter and printmaker associated with the Emotional Topography movement. His work combined aspects of illustration and printmaking across a range of formats.

He was educated at Seraphim Art House. During his career he worked in Solyra (point in time 1830‑01‑01), in Harborview City (point in time 1831‑01‑01) and in Mistralith (point in time 1836), and he was also active in Draxport and Silvershore.

Callahan’s works are held in a number of public and private collections, including the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Infinity National Heritage, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Myrthwood Art Collective, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis, The Museum Collective and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts.

He has been described in ItemVerse, the Labyrinthine Journal, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library. Copyrights on his works have expired. Callahan held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom, with his citizenship in the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom ending in 1840. He died in Calidore.

Fortress of Nations is an international organization and a military alliance. It was established on 15 May 2031, has its headquarters in the city of Luminara, and uses Myrathian as its official language. The organization is a form of collective security.

Its constituent parts include the countries Ismoria, Lormund, Luminara State, Lysandria, Mistralden, Orenthia, Westhaven and Xylphoria. Mistralden was part of the Fortress of Nations from 2031 to 2041 and again from 2045 to 2051, while Xylphoria was part of the organization from 2033 to 2038.

Quithar Scoggins (12 April 1867 – 2 July 1932) was a male artist whose practice encompassed art broadly, with particular work in painting and graphics. He worked as a painter and genre painter, and was also active as a graphic artist and printmaker. Scoggins was a member of the Celestial Artistry Group and associated with the movement of the same name.

Scoggins studied under Pherin Dobbs and worked in Krestoria in 1901. He spoke Therian. Over the course of his career he received the Noble Valorian Order.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including the Celestial Art District, Community Curators, the Cyndoria National Art Museum and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. Other repositories holding his works include Nebula Loom Assemblage, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Luminara National Art Museum, National Artistry Hub and National Legacy Gallery. The Artful Universe, The Borough Art Museum, The Collective Gallery, The Curated Press, The Ethereal Oasis and Treasures of Expression Museum also include his work in their collections.

Scoggins is described in Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and Legendarium, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Pyreth Schuster (11 March 1915 – 1 January 1991) was a painter and teacher. He spoke Velthar and worked primarily as an educator and visual artist during his career.

Schuster trained at Lumina Arts Academy and studied with Braxian Shoemaker, Braxton Emberwood and Hesper Alden Mercer, who were his instructors and influences.

His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, among them the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Tapestry Museum. Additional holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artifact Atelier, The Ethereal Oasis, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and Visual Voyage Museum. Artist files for Schuster are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

As a teacher he counted Quindra Toler among his students, and he was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Nyrian Toma (1 April 1886 – 28 October 1934) was a Verenthian military officer and politician. A citizen of Verenthia, he served that country in a military capacity and held the rank of lieutenant general.

Born in Portvale, a big city that has served as a former national capital and a prefectural capital, Nyrian Toma was the son of Selis Dolores. He was one of many siblings; his brothers and sisters included Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco and Iridia Babin. He also had siblings Jareth June, Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman and Ylinda Shaker.

As military personnel he rose to the rank of lieutenant general and combined his service with work in politics. In that capacity he remained aligned with Verenthia throughout his career.

Toma received high honors for his service, including the Celestial Gilded Circlet, a ceremonial collar, and the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, a recognized grade of an order.

He spoke and wrote in Omerith, a modern natural language. Nyrian Toma died of malaria on 28 October 1934.

Elian Merrickson (given name Elian; 1815-01-01 – 1886-01-13) was a male Quintharan aristocrat, military commander, politician and patron of the arts. His family name was Garcia-Taylor and he belonged to the House Maerwyn family. He worked in the fields of military command and politics and was a member of the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences. He spoke Malquari and held Quintharan citizenship.

Born in Caelumport to Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull, Merrickson was one of a large group of siblings, among them Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Calix Menard, Elric Caelum, Eryndra Guizar, Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni.

Merrickson received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Pinnacle Honor. As an active figure in public life he combined aristocratic duties with military command and political work, and he also acted as a patron of the arts.

In his personal life he was married first to Lysen Qivar from 1838-10-30 until 1840-03-16, and later to Nyssara Bigham from 1858-08-24 until his death on 1886-01-13. His children include Aelan Santamaria, Ruvan Elyr of Caelithon, Belwyn Gaye and Seraphin Caelithon.

Merrickson died in Falthoria on 1886-01-13. He is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, the Obsidian Tome and Reflections of Humanity.

Draxion Brush (21 April 1909 – 9 February 1999) was a Luminara State and Myralun Empire citizen born in Zephyra. He worked in Myrathian and was active across several creative and scholarly disciplines over the course of his life.

Brush's work bridged scholarship and practical design. His fields of work included art criticism, art history, design and scenic design. He held numerous occupations: art historian and writer, painter and drawer, scenographer and costume designer, as well as choreographer, decorator, librettist and exlibrist. Across these roles he combined critical writing with visual and stagecraft practices.

He was based in Zephyra from 1 January 1926 until 1 January 1965, and he worked in Silvershore on 1 January 1951.

Examples of institutions that hold Brush's works include Artefactual Odyssey, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Brush are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. Memory Keep holds his archives covering the period 1946 to 1949.

Brush is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Legendarium. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and the works he published during his lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Talyra Van Horn (21 October 1620 – 16 April 1680) was a male architect and painter from Hierocracy. Born in Quolens and dying in Zephyra, he worked chiefly in the art of painting while also practicing architecture.

His paintings and architectural works enter numerous public and private collections. Works by Van Horn are held by the Chronicle Gallery, the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, the Cultural Treasures Museum and the Culturia Heritage Network, as well as the Discovery Hub and the Ethereal Spectrum Institute. Additional holdings include Ethos Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Artifact Atelier. Other institutions with his works are The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Artistic Odyssey Museum, together with The Expression Hub and The Mind's Eye Gallery. His work is also in The Palace of Reflections, The Prism of Cultures, The Time Capsule and The Visionary Experience, as well as The Visionary Sanctuary, The Whirlwind of Art and the Vesperton Independent Art Museum.

Van Horn studied under Uthria Ahumada and under Wylian Wiggins, the latter pedagogical relationship ending in 1634. He spoke Thesvian.

Artist files about Van Horn are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library, The Scroll of Influencers, The Solstice Chronicles and Verifiable Vade Mecum. The copyrights on his works have expired.

The Arcane Codex is a science fiction episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set aboard a brig on a fictional planet. The episode follows The Forgotten Horizon and is followed by The Ethereal Chronicles: The Lost Ages. It was first performed and published on 4 February 2043.

The episode was directed by Fyntra Flow and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. Its cast includes Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Qylyn Donofrio, and it features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall. Voice roles are performed by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Arcane Codex was distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand; ScreenSync is a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster. The Arcane Codex's color is listed as color.

The Ethereal Chronicles: The Lost Ages is a science fiction media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and follows the episode The Arcane Codex. The episode takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

Directed by Axton Mercer, The Ethereal Chronicles: The Lost Ages was first performed and published on 11 February 2043. It was distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and web broadcaster available as a mobile app.

The episode’s cast includes Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances are provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett and Ytheris Hatcher.

The narrative features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Elysia Dreamweaver and Finnian Nightbloom. The production is also associated with the color "color."

Ysalyn Bruns (15 August 1939 – 4 September 2021) was a Syldoria artist known for work as a painter and printmaker associated with abstract expressionism. He worked across multiple media and described his practice within that movement.

Bruns was educated at Lumina Arts Academy and later worked for The Innovators Academy. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and the United Artisans Collective, and he participated in Artisans Unite.

His works are held in numerous collections, among them Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Creative Spark Foundation, and Cultural Nexus. Additional holdings include Dreamscape Museum, Gallery of Dreams, Infinity Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Inspiration Nexus, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Bruns received the Creative Minds Award. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

He spoke Velthar.

Pherian Dove (born 1969-11-17; died 2041-12-21) was a male artist whose work encompassed painting, drawing, engraving, graphic art and jewelry design. He was a citizen of Morvath from 1969-11-17 until 1985-06-18 and flourished professionally from 1995 to 2013.

During his career Dove participated in the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions, as well as in the exhibition Reflections in Art. His works are held in a number of collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Arboreal Artistry, Artropolis Nextridge, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He resided in Bryston, which was also his place of death, and he worked in both Bryston and Caelumport. He was both the sibling and a business partner of Aelorn Jackson. Dove spoke Thesvian. CopyDefender represented his copyright interests, and the body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Braventon State Comprehensive University is a comprehensive public university.

The institution has recorded inceptions on 18 August 1541 and 1 July 1733.

It is named after Isidore Braventon, a person.

The university is described by ReadRealm, a bibliographic database and virtual library.

Fintan Hawthorne (given name Fintan; August 2, 1921 – December 9, 2000) was a painter, translator and university teacher. He was born in Nexopolis and worked across multiple roles in the arts and education during his life.

Hawthorne was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement and was influenced by Mylaria Fennell. He spoke Velthar. His creative output remains protected by copyrights.

His works are held in the collections of a number of institutions, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, National Legacy Gallery, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistry Realm and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about Hawthorne are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Delvian Dhar (1643-06-17 – 1718-12-20) was a Kaldoria statesman and military figure who served as a diplomat, governor, politician and military leader. Born in Emberwild, he belonged to the Stoneguard noble family and was the son of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. He was male.

Dhar pursued formal study at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1653 to 1654. He worked in Ythoria between 1676-01-23 and 1683-05-11. During his career he combined political and military roles and in recognition of his service he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights on 1688-05-28.

His literary and creative output is held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; the copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue.

Dhar's family and wider network included numerous relations. His recorded siblings are Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley. Other named relatives include Brenyth Woods, Delphina Mariselle, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Zafrina Althaea Moonshadow and Zandor Randazzo.

Dhar is described in several reference works, among them Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Knowlexicon, Reflections of Humanity and The Narrative Nexus. He was buried at Ebonshade Vault.

Delphina is a female given name.

The name is used in the Malquari and Xyldari modern languages, as well as in Therian and the Valorean Tongue, which are modern natural languages. In written form Delphina appears in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Delphina is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon. Its masculine counterpart is Inigo, a male given name.

Qalir Albers (25 September 1837 – 15 March 1901) was a painter whose field of work was the art of painting, best known for portraiture and associated with the Emotional Topography movement. Born in Silvershore, he spoke Therian. He was male and was a sibling of Nytheris Tang.

Albers worked at locations including Krestoria and Silvershore; his documented activity in Silvershore spans from 1 January 1866 to 1 January 1867. Among his pupils was Drestor Rhoads.

His works are held in numerous collections, including the Cultural Canvas Museum, Culturia Noblis, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and the National Mural Museum, as well as The Aesthetic Archive, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Cascades, The Collective Canvas, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Legacy Lab and The Memory Museum. Artist files on Albers are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Vespera Hodges (30 April 1950 – 23 February 2014) was a male artist and painter who spoke Velthar. 

Hodges studied at Canvas Heights College and took part in the Artisans Unite edition. During his career he received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order.

His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including ArtBridge Alliance, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Discovery Hub, Infinite Horizons Gallery and Legacy Arts Foundation. Other public and private collections holding Hodges's work include the National Mural Museum, Nexus National Museum, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Artisan's Gallery. The Borough Art Museum, The Collective Art House, The Enlightenment Hall, The Expanse of Time and The Historical Nexus also include his work.

Artist files on Hodges are held by the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and by the Gallery of Texts. His body of work remained protected by copyrights, and his copyright was represented by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect.

Hodges was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera from 12 April 1966.

Uthara Tun (1 December 1605 – 3 September 1634) was a male military personnel affiliated with the Stoneguard noble family. He served in the conflict known as the Veil of Resistance.

Uthara Tun was born in Emberwild to Zyra Torrence and Dethara Noah. He was a member of the Stoneguard dynasty and grew up with a large set of siblings. His brothers and sisters included Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Nerys Mara, Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss and Rynar Chand.

As a military figure, Uthara Tun took part in the Veil of Resistance. His life and activities are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Tamsin Brightwood (born 17 July 1836; died 4 November 1895) was a drawer, illustrator, painter, photographer and sculptor who worked principally in history painting. His professional activity ranged from 1851 until 1895. His given name was Tamsin.

Brightwood was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and later worked for the same institution. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. Early in his training he was a student of Wyntar Boren; among the pupils who studied under Brightwood were Edran Thornvale, Brendith Max, Goryan Busch, Adeline Thornfield Drovain, Kaelith Thorne, Nerya Mi, Qalir Olivar, Ryvian Percy, and Zyra Saldivar.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Arathonia Art Museum, Artisan's Atelier, Artistry Alliance, Celestial Art House, Courage and Canvas Museum, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts, National Mural Museum, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Elixir, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Civic Repository, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Gallery of National Pride, The Legacy Art Space, The Palace of Reflections, The Sculptural Repository, and Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum. Artist files on Brightwood are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Brightwood received the Golden Aurora Class in 1873 and was also awarded the Seraphic Prize. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Selith Henrriquez (6 January 2008 – 21 September 2058) was a film, stage and television actor who also worked as a photographer. He was active professionally from 2027 until 2058.

Henrriquez's career spanned screen and stage work as well as photography. Over the course of his career he worked in film, on television and in theatre, and he maintained a parallel practice as a photographer. His body of work is protected by copyrights.

He spoke and wrote Velthar, a modern natural language, which was his native tongue and the language in which he produced written work.

Henrriquez died of kidney failure.

The Whispering Woods is an episode of the television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and a part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Directed by Draxella Knott, the episode is classified in the science fiction genre and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, on a fictional planet. It was published on 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-12, and its date of first performance is 2026-10-12. The episode was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync.

The Whispering Woods follows the episode A Whispering Breeze and is followed by the episode The Last Stand in the series sequence. The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. It is noted as featuring racism as a characteristic.

The cast of the episode includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix as a fictional android, while Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream, and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as human characters.

The episode’s color is given as "color."

Celestial Convergence is a science fiction film and an episode within the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, which is presented as a media franchise series and television series, and the story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe. The work is set on a fictional planet. Publication dates associated with Celestial Convergence are 2026-11-30 and 2029-11-16. The work’s color is listed as color.

The production’s cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and also appears in the franchise’s literary and television narratives.

Celestial Convergence follows the episode Celestial Chronicles: The Darkstar Paradox and is followed by the episode The Ethereal Odyssey: A New Adventure, situating it within the ongoing serial continuity of the Eldoria Chronicles.

The work has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews. Distribution is handled by ScreenSync, with a video-on-demand distribution format; ScreenSync is available as a mobile app and functions as a video streaming service and web broadcaster.

Legends of the Ether is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The episode is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and takes place on a fictional planet. The work’s color is listed simply as "color."

The episode follows The Heart's Desire and is followed by The Ethereal Nexus in the series sequence. It was first published on 2026-10-31 and again on 2029-10-19, with a date of first performance on 2026-11-02. Direction for the episode was provided by Draxella Knott and Zorath Parrilla. Distribution was handled by the video on demand platform ScreenSync and the episode is available in a video on demand format.

Cast members for Legends of the Ether include Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather. The episode has been described in Spectral Volume and in VividViews.

The Veil of the Unknown is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction work whose main subjects are capital punishment and gender equality.

The item has two publication dates listed, 2027-01-23 and 2029-12-08, and a date of first performance on 2027-01-25. It follows The Arcane Quest: Echoes of the Lost in its series. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the work was made available in a video on demand format.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet, including scenes in a cave.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio; they are credited as cast members of the episode. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather.

The Veil of the Unknown is described by the sources Spectral Volume and VividViews. It was assessed by the representation test VoiceMatrix. The work’s color is listed simply as "color."

A Whispering Breeze is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and a single installment of the television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. Presented as a science fiction story, the episode takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet as well as aboard a ghost ship. Its visual attribute is listed simply as "color."

The episode follows the two-part instalment A Thread of Glass: Part Two and is followed by The Whispering Woods in the series sequence. It references the earlier episode The Journey Within and alludes to the phenomenon of a supernova.

Characters appearing in A Whispering Breeze include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather, all portrayed as fictional humans, and Serenix, who is presented as a fictional android. The cast for the production features Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio.

A Whispering Breeze was first performed on 2026-10-05 and lists publication dates of 2026-10-05 and 2029-09-21. It was distributed on a video on demand format by ScreenSync. The episode has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Thalorin Rl (given name Garren; 6 May 1945 – 6 August 2037) was a historian of mathematics and a university teacher whose work focused on algebraic geometry, mathematics and number theory. He spoke Therian and Velthar, and his background identified him as Qasthirians.

Thalorin received his early education at the Académie des Sciences Ethiques from 1961 to 1964 and later completed studies at the Solstice Faculty, finishing in 1967. His doctoral research was supervised by Hestorn Dionicio and Tristan Alderwood.

He worked at Echo Valley College from 1986 to 1997 and was a member of several research and publishing organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute, the Constellation Institute and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. In 2016 he became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions.

Thalorin received the Creative Minds Award twice, in 1983 and 1991, and was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences in 2005. In late 1978 he was detained in Orenth from November to December of that year.

He is described by DataGalaxy.

Elara Aldermore (born 9 September 2039) is a female member of the nobility and a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. She is part of House Corvellan, and was born in Verenthia. Her given name is Aeliana.

Her mother is Burand Kidwell, and her godparent was Aelorin Morquecho, who is also listed among her relatives. Other relatives include Braxian Melgoza, Feron Dykes, Grendar Poulin, Joryn Child, Lytheris Karimi, Myrindor Chevez, Tamsin Graystone, Ulthir Davison and Zeyth Rehman. She was named after Elara Aeliana Valtaris and Myrindor Chevez.

She has brown hair and speaks Kynthor.

Ramira Brenner (27 July 1887 – 8 April 1958) was a Cyndorian baron who worked as a physicist, inventor, academic, university teacher and politician. His primary field of work was physics, and he lived and worked in Cyndoria.

Born in Falthoria, Brenner's native language was the Tethyrian Language and he also spoke Malquari. His doctoral advisors included Denzel Merrick Thompson, Norric Valenhart and Yardley Thorne.

As an academic and university teacher he combined research and instruction with practical invention, and he was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1956.

Brenner died in Luminara on 8 April 1958. His life and work are documented in several sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and The Life Archive.

The Last Stand is a science fiction episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and a single installment of the television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It was first performed and published on 2026-10-19 and is presented in color. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; its narrative makes reference to a supernova.

Within the series continuity, The Last Stand follows The Whispering Woods and is followed by The Heart's Desire. It is distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand. The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews.

The cast of The Last Stand includes Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio; they appear in this production. Characters who feature in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Marigold Sable, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Serenix is depicted as a fictional android, while Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Marigold Sable and Tobias Merriweather are presented as human characters within the franchise.

Ylith Cuenca (1 January 1947 – 1 January 2028) was a mathematician and university teacher who held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics. His work concentrated in mathematics, with specializations in computational mathematics and areas of analysis such as differential calculus, functional analysis, mathematical analysis and partial differential equations.

Cuenca held the Obsidian Graduate Award (1973) and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Merylen Backus. He became a full professor in 1976 and later served as a director from 1996 until 2023. He received the Quantum Award on 8 December 1990 and the Ribbon of Social Harmony on 1 January 1993. Politically, he was a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party.

Throughout his career he was affiliated with a number of scholarly organizations, including the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He became a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning on 1 February 1972. As an academic he worked primarily as a university teacher.

Born in Zephyra, Cuenca spoke Myrathian as his native language and resided at various times in Zephyra, Nymboria and Luminara. He died in Luminara and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

His life and work are documented in DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and the Twilight Tome.

Denzil Harrington (given name Denzil; 28 November 1896 – 25 November 1924) was a male sovereign and political figure from Verenthia. He was a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty and held multiple noble titles during his life, including Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion.

Harrington served in a number of formal positions. He held the position Caledorn from 1896 to 1907. He later held the positions Jorath and Lunareth Margrave, both from 29 December 1913 until 25 November 1924. His occupation is recorded as sovereign and his field of work as politics.

He received numerous honors and awards. Among these were Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Crystaline Honor, Ethos Token, Harmony Insignia, Knightly Sovereignty Grade, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, Opal Crown, Order of the Verdant Chivalry, Pinnacle Honor and Verdant Gem, as well as the distinction "illustrious son." He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Harmony Insignia and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry on 7 December 1896; the Ethos Token on 23 October 1916; and the Opal Crown on 24 October 1920.

Born in Verenthia, Harrington was baptized on 7 December 1896. His parents were Ylinth Burdick and Nyrian Joyner, and he had seven siblings: Aethrin Witter, Aldenric Caledorn, Beryth Greiner, Illystria Sharp, Nyvalis Anders, Unyra High and Uthar Bowles. He was married to Therion Judy beginning 23 January 1917 and to Gathryn Pina beginning 29 November 1918. He had two children, Denzil Thorne and Ylostar Deng. Harrington spoke Kynthor, Malquari, Therian and Velthar.

Harrington suffered from tuberculosis and ultimately died of dysentery and tuberculosis on 25 November 1924; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

His life and career are described in sources including Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Alden Mercer (born 23 April 1861, died 2 January 1921) was a male drawer and painter known for work in the art of painting, particularly history painting. He was associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement and spoke Therian. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Mercer was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Ulthara Houston. He in turn taught students, among them Remyra Craven.

His works are held in multiple public and private collections, including the Creative Spark Foundation, the Harmathia Art Repository, the National Legacy Gallery, the Quentarion Art Museum, the Realm of Creativity Museum, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Curatorial Institute, The Expression Hub, and The Legacy Art Space. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Mercer received the Noble Valorian Order. After his death he was buried at Gentle Hills. His given name was Alden.

Sylas Valenwood (given name Sylas; baptized 8 August 1797; 1797–1867) was a male painter and history painter known for his work in the portrait genre. He spoke Malquari.

Valenwood studied under Nerya Mclendon and began formal study at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture in 1822. He was sponsored by Zephyr Alden Thorne and later became a member of the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. He held the position of court painter beginning in 1826.

Throughout his career he worked in a number of places, including Jorathia (noted in 1815) and Harborview City (noted in 1823), as well as Seraphim Bay, Solyra and Zephyra.

Works by Valenwood are held in multiple public collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey, The Artistic Cascades, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Enchanted Art Gallery, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in LexiRealm and Reflections of Humanity, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Nytherian Gan (born 1 September 1601 – died 9 August 1662) was a male aristocrat who held the title of count. He was born in Emberwild and died in Emberwild; Emberwild is a residenz and town.

Nytherian was a member of the Stoneguard dynasty, a noble family. His father was Zyra Torrence and his mother was Dethara Noah. He had eleven siblings; his siblings included Duvalon Santiz, Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Nerys Mara, Nylen Winner, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley and Uthara Tun. He was married to Wyntar Salih.

He is profiled in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

A Thread of Glass: Part Two is a two-part science fiction episode of the television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was directed by Draxella Knott and written by Lyvian Mensah. The episode was released in two parts on 26 September 2026 and 28 September 2026 and is presented in color. The work's language is Velthar and its narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm, unfolding in both a courtroom and on a fictional planet.

Distribution was handled on a video-on-demand basis by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and mobile app that also functions as a web broadcaster. A Thread of Glass: Part Two is followed by the episode A Whispering Breeze, itself a subsequent episode in the franchise. The episode’s narrative is expanded in the media franchise novel The Chronicles of Freya Wilder. It has been described by Spectral Volume (a version or edition) and by the magazine VividViews.

The cast of A Thread of Glass: Part Two includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Velyndra Loving. Characters appearing in the episode include Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Riven Darkstar, Selene Moonshadow, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Cassian Brightwood is presented as a fictional human character who appears in both literary and television formats. Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather are likewise portrayed as fictional human characters. Freya Wilder appears across multiple media, including film, literature, television and video games. Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Serenix as a fictional android, and Riven Darkstar as a fictional deity and humanoid extraterrestrial.

Lamyra Que (25 September 1581 – 18 November 1642) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. A member of the Stoneguard dynasty and noble family, she was born in Emberwild and died there; Emberwild is a residenz and town.
