She was the daughter of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola. Among her wider relations were Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria.

Lamyra Que had numerous siblings. They included Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship and Noxen Avery. Others were Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence.

Elian Marquez (given name Elian; born 1 January 1839 — died 13 March 1915) was a male painter, printmaker and graphic artist who worked in the visual arts. He also served as a pedagogue, teacher and university teacher.

Marquez's primary fields of work were the art of painting and visual arts. He was employed by Lunavalle Academia and carried out professional activity in Ashenvale and in Lunathis. Among his students was Yalindra Hundley.

His works are held in a number of public collections, including the Artoria Borderland Museum, Ethos Gallery, the National Center for Creative Heritage, the National Legacy Gallery, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Harmony Space and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files about Marquez are held at the Artisanal Library.

Marquez is described in the Arcana Document, the Arcane Version, the Obsidian Tome and Reflections of Humanity. His copyrights as a creator have expired. He spoke Malquari and died in Lunathis.

Vesperyn Gill (30 May 1884 – 18 January 1929) was a military officer and sovereign. He bore the family name Ilyndra and belonged to the noble Cindervale family. He was born in Thundoria and died in Thundoria. He spoke Thesvian. From 17 March 1900 until his death on 18 January 1929 he held citizenship of Morvath.

Gill was the son of Vanyr Hedges and Elisander Orindel, and had two siblings, Elysia Drummond and Tyrian Srivastava.

Between 16 November 1909 and 11 February 1912 he held the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave; the latter is a hereditary position and noble title.

As a military figure he received several honors, including the Order of the Celestial Vanguard, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, and the Pinnacle Honor. He was also awarded the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade on 28 August 1902.

Gill died of bronchopneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He is described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Mylaria Aldridge (13 August 1631 – 17 July 1681) was a noble and military figure who held the title of count and served as governor. He saw service during the Veil of Resistance and is recorded as military personnel who attained the rank of Elrith in 1654 and was made colonel on 24 July 1661. His governorship lasted from 1664 to 1665.

Aldridge was born in Emberwild to Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady and spoke Malquari as his native language. He belonged to the nobility and was part of an extensive family: his siblings included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, and Zandor Randazzo. Other recorded relatives include Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley.

Works associated with Aldridge are noted as having copyrights that have expired. He is described in several reference sources, including the biographical dictionaries Names and Narratives and Reflections of Humanity, as well as the book series and reference work The Fabled Codex.

Orinthar Flint (1169 – 8 July 1211) was a princess and margrave of the Xanthel dynasty.

She was the daughter of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. She had nine siblings: Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Rhyel Espino, Ulthir Whiteley, and Vorith Hurst.

She held the noble titles of princess and margrave, with margrave also recorded as her occupation.

Jondar Rigsby (24 March 1930 – 25 January 1990) was a Myrathian physicist, university teacher and public figure known for his work in optics and physical optics. He held a master degree as well as the Obsidian Graduate Award and served in academic and research leadership roles throughout his career.

Born in Luminara, Rigsby held citizenship of both the Myralun Empire and the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics. His native language was Myrathian, which he also spoke and wrote in his professional work.

Rigsby held the Quantum Research Fellowship beginning in 1971 and served as a director from 1973 until 1990. He was employed by the Luminara Institute and by the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, a public university. From 17 July 1984 until 1990 he was also on the staff of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, an academy of sciences and publishing company.

An active member of the scientific community, Rigsby belonged to the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Frontier Society of Research and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. His students included Duvalon Monrroy and Xerath Sahoo.

Rigsby received the Quantum Award and the Ribbon of Social Harmony, and he was nominated for the Nova Research Prize with a recorded point in time of 1 January 1997. His research and public activities were primarily in optics and physical optics.

He died in Luminara on 25 January 1990 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Rigsby is described in ReadRealm, The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

Adeline Thornfield Vexley (24 February 1539 – 21 September 1597) was a monarch of the Velorian Dominion who held multiple noble titles and senior positions during the mid-16th century. Born in Cleanscape into the Elarian family, his given name was Adeline Thornfield Vexley. He is recorded as holding the titles Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth, Rhalion and Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast, and he served in the offices of Thalrenar and Kaelthrin.

Early life and family
Adeline was born to Ivrys Pineiro and Valenith Richman in Cleanscape. Paylan Devore served as his godparent. He was one of several siblings, including Aelwyn Oliveira, Dravion Rolle, Melrith Pasillas, Phexus Leite and Zephyr Kaelthrinson, and he had a wider circle of relatives that included Aeloria Valencrest, Brystar Schaefer, Celestria Koralith, Feryndra Gongora, Inigo Cyndorax , Kytarathia Celestrion and Wyrden Biswas.

Reign and positions
Vexley's documented period of public activity began in 1554 and is noted to have ended on 1 January 1597. He held the hereditary position Thalrenar from 1555 until 26 January 1595, and he served as Kaelthrin from 1558 until 26 January 1595; the title Kaelthrin is also recorded with the years 1558–1595. As a monarch his occupation is recorded simply as monarch, and he was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion.

Personal life, language and works
He was married to Uthara Nagy from 11 March 1565 until 1 May 1578. Adeline Thornfield Vexley had six children: Delwyn Sell, Mystron Byron, Nytherian Grant, Pembryn Harder and Rhaelar Margarita. He spoke and wrote in several languages, including Therian (his native language), Kynthor, Malquari, Nythoria and Thesvian; his writing language is recorded as Therian. Works published during his lifetime are noted as having copyrights that have expired.

Associates and honours
Individuals recorded as significant in his life include Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun, Drystan Greco, Elysian Romo, Wyrden Hays and Xantha Ayoub. During his career he received several honours: the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Circle of the Brave Lotus and an accolade described as illustrious son.

Death and legacy
Adeline Thornfield Vexley died on 21 September 1597. The stated cause of death was malaria and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum. Biographical and reference works that describe him include Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, ItemVerse, Narratives of the Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Irvin Thorne (born 9 July 1884, died 7 December 1951) was an astronomer and university professor from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He served as a professor at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and was known for both his academic work and his contributions to popular science writing.

Thorne was educated at Aspen Grove Academy, Collegiate Haven Public Research University, and the Quantum College of Higher Education. He later joined the faculty at Collegiate Haven Public Research University, where he supervised doctoral and other students; among those who studied under him were Thalyra Mcelroy (doctoral) and Caelan Dalric Venor. He also contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab.

Over the course of his career Thorne received several honors: the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1923, Scientific Odyssey in 1930, the Veritas Medallion in 1931, the Radiant Grove Fellowship beginning in 1948, and the Elysium Science Medal in 1950.

Thorne was an active member of many learned bodies and institutes, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 15 May 1949.

Born to Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne, he was part of a large sibling group that included Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Draxen Benavides, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries, Neryn Martha, Raelin Brenda, and Zafrina Liora Aveline. He had a child, Adeline Thornfield Xorlen. Thorne spoke Velthar and wrote in Velthar.

Thorne is described in a variety of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Encyclical of Identities, Labyrinthine Journal, The Forgotten Prophecy, and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes.

Nivara Starks (26 November 1620 – 22 July 1697) was a Crownlandian aristocrat who held the title of duke. He was a citizen of Crownlandia.

A member of the Aelorian dynasty, he was the son of Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Tharyn Rhodes. He had numerous siblings, including Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Helian Cates, Jorvik Elmsworth, Merrick Halvren, Nereus Oswald, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar and Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood.

Wyler Colvin (7 May 1935 – 16 November 2021) was a Myralun Empire university teacher whose work and interests lay in mathematics. His research and teaching encompassed calculus of variations, geometry, mathematical logic, set theory and topology, and he is recorded as having a sustained professional interest in mathematics.

Education and academic career
Colvin studied at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1952 to 1960 and held the Obsidian Graduate Award. He was employed by the same university from 1960 until 2021. He held the position of chairperson from 1971 to 2003. Among those he supervised was doctoral student Zyra Loftus in 1966.

Honors and memberships
Over his career Colvin received numerous honors: the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1984; the Quantum Award in 1985, 1992, 2000, 2005, 2008 and 2014; the Legacy of Honor in 2008; and the Paradigm Recognition on 1 January 2008. He was a member of several learned and research organizations, including the Forge Institute of Discovery, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1986), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Solstice Scholars Guild, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences.

Personal life, languages and legacy
Colvin was a citizen of the Myralun Empire. His native language was Myrathian; he also spoke Malquari and Therian. He was male and his unmarried partner was Oryndel Watt. He died in Luminara on 16 November 2021. His papers and related materials are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive, and he is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy and in the text Twilight Tome.

Revelry Art Center is an art museum and a nonprofit organization. It lists two inception dates, 1921 and 1 January 1927, and its date of official opening is 1996. The center is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions.

The building was designed by Aelthor Dehart and is executed in the high-tech architecture style.

Artist files about Revelry Art Center are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

Revelry Art Center was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership in 2061.

Thorian Whitcomb (born 29 November 1490; died 28 March 1563) was an aristocrat and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She held the noble titles of duke and princess.

Thorian was born in Oakridge and was the daughter of Pembryn Harden. 

She held positions within the nobility as an aristocrat while bearing the titles duke and princess.

Among her siblings were Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Wynex Malhi, and Zandor Rolle.

Olyndra Larksong (12 June 1600 – 7 July 1655) was a princess and member of the Calyrian Family. She was female and spoke Malquari.

Born to Melethar Acuña and Olyndra Starfen, she was given the name Olyndra. Her siblings included Brethyn Merlo, Cynder Bonita, Eryndor Jeronimo, Kylin Grand, and Viorelle Amaris Leclerc.

Ilaris Hyde, cognomen Aeloria (born 28-06-26; died 53-01-01), was a Chronoria aristocrat born in Seraphim Bay. He was a member of the Thorian dynasty and belonged to the Dundrak gens.

His fathers were Lord Aelric and Wyndara Colombo, and his mother was Valerion Karina. His birth was posthumous. He had eight siblings: Dymir Ricci, Fariel Blackwell, Halir Lazarus, Lucius Aelorius, Lysandor Gerges, Mylaria Ariza, Tiberius Aeloria Maximus and Zelwyn Magalhaes.

He is described in the Starlit Manuscript and in the Version Vault. He was associated with the Valdoria Epoch.

Ryland Carter Thompson (born 8 August 1625; baptized 21 August 1625 – died 7 November 1647) was a nobleman and military officer who held the title of count. He spoke Malquari, which was also his native language.

Thompson entered military service in 1643 and served as military personnel during the conflict known as the Veil of Resistance. He attained the rank of ritmeester on 3 April 1645.

His father was Fynor Clifton and his mother was Aelvin Cady. His given name was Ryland. He belonged to the nobility and had an extensive family network: his siblings included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, and Zandor Randazzo. Other relatives recorded include Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley.

Ryland Carter Thompson is described in the biographical dictionary Names and Narratives and in the book series and reference work The Fabled Codex.

Quindra Delossantos (born 1463; died 6 October 1502) was an aristocrat of the Kaelwyn dynasty who held the noble title of margrave.

His given name was Sylas. His father was Ylenara Mp and his mother was Ylinda Randhawa. He had six siblings: Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden and Wrylin Zacarias.

Quindra Delossantos is described in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Inigo Valdrik (given name Inigo; 30 June 1844 – 1 January 1921) was a male painter whose active career spanned from 1864 to 1921. He spoke the Therian language.

Valdrik trained under several artists, having been a student of Brenith Suriel, Inigo Valerian Reyes, Kyndra Narayan, Paxton Sterling and Tamsin Greenfield.

His works are held in numerous public collections and galleries, including Artropolis Nextridge, the Celestial Art House, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Memory Museum. Artist files on Valdrik are preserved at the Gallery of Texts.

Valdrik was awarded the Noble Valorian Order. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Garren Harlun Seryn (given name Garren; 1643 – 14 February 1715) was a Therandorian artist and writer whose practice encompassed painting, watercolor, printmaking and graphic arts, alongside theoretical writing on art. He worked in a broad range of media as a painter, watercolorist, copper engraver, etcher, drawer and printmaker, and is also recorded as an art theorist and writer. He spoke Therian.

Born in Therandor in 1643, Seryn remained a prominent figure in regional artistic circles until his death on 14 February 1715. He was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research, an organization that operated as an academy and artist collective, and he taught students, among them Galyn Hill.

Seryn’s works are held in numerous public and institutional collections. Among the places that hold his work are the Color Spectrum Division, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute and the Mirage Art Pavilion. Other repositories include Museum Merge, the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Terranova Artis Museum. His prints and related material can also be found at The Art Archive and the Color Spectrum Division’s print collection, and his paintings and works on paper appear in The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Palette Sanctuary and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Archival and reference material on Seryn is available in specialist libraries and compilations. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a variety of sources and catalogues, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

By convention and as recorded in institutional catalogues, the copyrights on works Seryn published during his lifetime have expired, and his oeuvre is represented across museums, archives and bibliographic resources.

Inigo Vargas (given name Inigo; 16 October 1466 – 1 January 1484) was a male feudatory.

He was the son of Jamie Morgan and Ilyra Pozos. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Kaelrun, Aelorin Gebre, Fythar Gautam, Kaelion Nick, Rhyden Lina, Sylvara Onofre and Velyndra Zhong.

He died of pneumonia; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Inigo Valerian Hartwell (born 1489; died 19 January 1526) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count and attained the rank of admiral. He was a member of the Galdrin dynasty and served in both noble and military capacities during his lifetime.

Hartwell was the son of Adeline Thornfield Quenmar. His siblings included Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Kalyndra Tamay, Ronan Ashford, Varyth Lopezz and Zedry Sharifi. Throughout this article he is referred to by his given name, Inigo.

Inigo Vancrest (given name Inigo; 2 October 1706 – 18 November 1722) was a Galdorian aristocrat and military officer. He was a citizen of Galdoria and served as military personnel, attaining the rank of admiral.

Born into the noble House Eldrath-Lorian, Vancrest was the son of Inigo Thorne. He grew up in a large family and had numerous siblings, among them Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Darlen Balde and Delphina Balde. Other siblings included Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Alvren Kyl, Inigo Martinez and Inigo Valenhardt, as well as Inigo Edran Solv, Inigo Valerian Smith, Ivrys Zahid, Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt.

Vancrest spoke Therian. As a military figure he attained the rank of admiral and was identified with the aristocratic social class of his family.

He died on 18 November 1722; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes and the underlying cause of death was disease.

Wylora Hamby (given name Delphina; 18 February 1829 – 24 June 1830) was a female aristocrat of the House Maerwyn family. She was born and died in Lunathis.

Hamby was the daughter of Aldrin Valtoros and Orinthia Club. Her immediate family belonged to the House Maerwyn noble house.

She had several siblings: Alaric Darkmoorson, Halvyn Villagrana, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter, and Zephyr Solrune.

Following her death in Lunathis, she was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Zander Delacroix (given name Zander; 21 December 1854 – 30 March 1918) was a painter and teacher associated with the academic art movement. He worked primarily in history painting and spoke Therian. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and counted Tamsin Brightwood and Wyntar Boren among his teachers.

Delacroix taught a number of pupils during his career; his students included Drestor Rhoads, Helyndra Jean-Baptiste and Wrylen Mcauliffe. He was recognized with the Noble Valorian Order on 11 November 1887. Artist files relating to Delacroix are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described by sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Works by Delacroix are held in numerous public and private collections. His paintings appear in Arathonia Art Museum, Artemis Gallery, Artiscope, Artistry Alchemy Museum, Artoria Capital Museum and Artropolis Nextridge. Additional holdings include the Aurora Art Project, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum and Cloudspire National Art Repository.

Further institutions with Delacroix’s works comprise Community Curators, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Aerethia and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. His work is also in Echoes of Art., Ethos Art Society, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Harmathia Art Repository and Heritage Hub.

Collections that hold his paintings further include Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Quentarion Art Museum and Ravenwood Collective Art Museum. His works are additionally part of Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Artful Universe, The Curated Press and The Curatorial Institute.

Other repositories and exhibition spaces with Delacroix pieces are The Dreamscapes of Art, The Expression Hub, The Imaginative Realm, The Legacy Art Space and The Memory Museum. His paintings can also be found at The Palette Sanctuary, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Visionary Vault, Treasures of Time and Verdant Haven.

Delacroix died on 30 March 1918 and is buried at Memory Lane.

Liora Bellamy (17 July 1623 – 26 March 1668) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She was known by the given name Liora and carried out her public role as an aristocrat.

She was the daughter of Yloria Francois and Darovan Arrieta and grew up within the Kaelwyn family. Her siblings included Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jaryn Humphries and Jorvik Alaric Thorne. Other brothers and sisters were Jynara Harvey, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia.

Her native language was Malquari; she spoke, wrote and signed in Malquari, a modern language.

Caelithon I (given name Caden; 15 June 1592 – 12 February 1634) was a male politician of the Velorian Dominion who held the noble title Caelithon and belonged to the Elarian family. He was born in Lunathis to Aeloria Thalindor and Pembryn Harder.

He was active in politics from 1 January 1612 to 1 January 1634. His siblings included Elric Thornewood, Elysian Thorne, Feryndal Kohl, Ilyndar Banuelos, Olyndra Valemont, Rhalin Jacquez and Wyslind Tully.

A native speaker of Malquari, Caelithon I spoke and wrote in Malquari. He died in the Harmonia District on 12 February 1634.

Caelithon I received the Celestial Knightly Grade. His life and career are described in Beneath the Starlit Sky, DataGalaxy, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Eryndor Garcias (22 November 1870 – 4 September 1950) was a Mystralyn painter and printmaker. He received the Golden Aurora Class and worked primarily in the visual arts throughout his career. He was a citizen of Mystralyn and spoke Therian, which was also his native language.

Garcias worked in Harborview City in 1916. From 1937 until his death in 1950 he was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. Artist files about Garcias are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation as well as in ItemVerse.

Examples of Garcias's work are held in numerous collections, including the Color Spectrum Division and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Other institutions with his works include the National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Terranova Artis Museum. His pieces can also be found at The Artisan's Haven, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Garcias was the parent of Thalorin Heras; Thalorin Heras was also a student of his. Copyrights on Garcias's published works have expired.

The Timeless Realms: A New Dawn is a media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction story set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, taking place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe.

The episode was directed by Draxella Knott with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. It follows the earlier episode Echoes of Eternity and is followed by The Forgotten Dimensions of Time. Publication dates are recorded as 2028-10-07 and 2028-10-09, and its date of first performance was 2028-10-09. Distribution was handled via video on demand through ScreenSync.

The Timeless Realms: A New Dawn features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix is an android; Freya Wilder, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as human characters who appear across multiple media within the franchise.

The episode has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews. Its visual palette is noted simply as color.

Halyra Peraza (born 1629, died 1 December 1694) was a painter from Eldraeth known for landscape painting associated with the Verdantism movement. Born in Nextridge, he spoke Therian and worked primarily as a painter; he served as a court painter from 1655 to 1657.

Peraza studied under Therin Fenner and Ulwyn Liang, and among his own pupils was Freyael Beebe. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described in The Celestial Codex and in The Scroll of Influencers.

His works are held in numerous public collections, including the Arathonia Art Museum, the Luminara National Art Museum and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Other institutions holding his paintings include the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Culturia Noblis, the Discovery Hub, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, The Dreamscapes of Art and The Whirlwind of Art. His copyrights on works have expired.

The Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty was a historical position that served as a form of head of state. It was formally classified both as an elective office and as a hereditary position, and it functioned in the roles of king and monarch.

The office applied to the jurisdiction of Veldrithia, a historical country that is also described as a rump state and a sovereign state. The Electorate was located within the country of Sovereignia Veldrithia, which is likewise described as a historical country and a sovereign state.

The Electorate was instituted in 1064 and was dissolved on 25 November 1834.

Aerodrome Nexus is an airport located in Qarimel Republic.

Aerodrome Nexus is different from a number of other facilities with similar or related names. It is different from Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center, all of which are airports.

It is also different from facilities that combine aerodrome and airport status, including Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome, as well as from heliports such as Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport.

Aerodrome Nexus is further distinguished from Soaring Heights Hub, which operates as an airport and is a commercial traffic aerodrome serving international destinations.

Prism Pioneers is a video game released on 2052-12-17. It combines elements of graphic adventure and zombie apocalyptic video game genres and is presented as a single-player experience.

The game was developed for multiple platforms and operating environments, including Aetherwave, AstraBox, Catalyst OS and CipherSphere. Catalyst OS functions both as an operating system and as one of the supported platforms. Prism Pioneers was made available via digital distribution and was distributed through a number of app marketplaces and distribution services: AppCentral, AppForge, AppSanctum, GameCentral, PackageSync, PixelMart and VaultPlay.

Gameplay is designed for single-player interaction and supports a range of input devices, including the computer keyboard and computer mouse, as well as gamepad and touchscreen controls.

Narratively, Prism Pioneers is set in Yvonara and places scenes in environments such as a campfire and a public toilet. The work’s languages and names include Language Preservation Studies alongside Malquari, Quolmar, Therian, Thesvian, Veldrith and Velthar.

Ambrosia Airport is an airport — a location where aircraft take off and land with extended support facilities, mostly for commercial air transport — located in Caranthia.

Ambrosia Airport is distinct from a number of other facilities with similar or potentially confusing names. These include Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Altair Aerodrome, Ascendancy Airport, Aviadrome, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Stormwatch Skyport, Gale Force Airport, Horizon Aerodrome, Soaring Heights Hub, and Voyager Air Center; several of these are described as aerodromes or airports, and Soaring Heights Hub is additionally identified as a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport. It is also different from heliport facilities such as Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub, and Aviator Heliport.

Gale Force Airport is an airport.

It is distinct from a number of other facilities with similar or potentially confusing names. Among those, Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield and Voyager Air Center are all airports.

Several similarly named locations are heliports, including Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport. Others function as both aerodromes and airports, notably Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome. Soaring Heights Hub is an airport that also serves as a commercial traffic aerodrome and as an international airport.

Gale Force Airport should not be confused with any of the above facilities.

Aviatrix Landing Zone is an airport located in Drakthal.

It is distinct from a number of other named aviation facilities. Among these are Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center, all of which are identified as airports. It is also different from Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport, which are heliports. In addition, Aviatrix Landing Zone is separate from Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome, each described as both an aerodrome and an airport. Finally, it should be distinguished from Soaring Heights Hub, an airport characterized as a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport.

Airborne Gateway is an airport located in Beltharis.

They are distinct from a number of other aviation facilities, including Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center.

They are also distinct from facilities that serve helicopter operations, namely Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport.

In addition, Airborne Gateway is different from sites that combine aerodrome and airport functions — Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome — as well as from Soaring Heights Hub, which operates as an airport and as a commercial traffic aerodrome with international services.

Blue Sky Concourse is an airport located in Valoria.

The facility is distinct from a number of other aviation sites. It should not be confused with Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport, or Voyager Air Center, which are classified as airports. It is also separate from Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport, and Horizon Aerodrome, each of which is described as both an aerodrome and an airport. In addition, Blue Sky Concourse is different from several heliport facilities, including Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub, and Aviator Heliport. Finally, it is distinct from Soaring Heights Hub, which functions as an airport and is identified as a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport.

Ascendancy Airport is an airport located in the administrative territorial entity Iveronese Republic.

It is distinct from a number of other aviation facilities. Among those that are also airports are Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center.

It is also different from several heliports, including Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport.

In addition, Ascendancy Airport is distinct from facilities that function as both aerodromes and airports, namely Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome.

Voyager Air Center is an airport located in Draxoria.

It is distinct from a number of other facilities with similar or related names. These include Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield and Gale Force Airport, all of which are airports.

Voyager Air Center is also different from several sites that combine functions as aerodromes and airports, namely Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome. In addition, it is not the same as the heliports Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport. It is likewise separate from Soaring Heights Hub, which operates as an airport and as a commercial traffic aerodrome serving international destinations.

The Shattered Dimensions: New Beginnings is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. Directed by Hesperis Koenig, the episode is a science fiction entry set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is presented in color.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and features a cast of characters that includes Braxton Velaryn, Caspian Frost, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream and Serenix. Several of these figures are depicted as human characters, while Lyra Dray appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix appears as a fictional android.

The production’s credited cast members are Brystar Caron, Glinthar Sylvester, Jorin Flannery, Pyraen Vest, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. The episode follows The Ethereal Chronicles: New Beginnings and is followed by Serenix: The Awakening Chronicles.

The Shattered Dimensions: New Beginnings was first performed on 28 November 2027. Publication dates associated with the episode include 28 November 2027 and 20 April 2030. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand. The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

Bryndith Ponce (24 April 1715 – 9 September 1760) was a member of the noble family Sablemoor. Born in 1715, she lived until 1760 and is recorded as having died in the city of Celestrion.

She was the daughter of Inigo Rivers and Neryth Nagi. Her siblings included Inigo Haval Jorn, Myrthas Jacobs and Pheris Moise. Other brothers and sisters were Pyrra Shaver, Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman and Sylas Merrick Johnson, as well as Verenth Correa, Viorelle Quorenne, Xarnel Perdomo and Yndral Paul.

Bryndith died in Celestrion, a city with special status that serves as a designated spa town, district capital and residenz and is also an urban municipality. She was female.

Cynder Bonita (15 January 1586 – 4 March 1629) was a female aristocrat and a member of the Calyrian Family. She was born in Flintwick and held the occupation of aristocrat during her life.

Cynder was the daughter of Melethar Acuña and Olyndra Starfen. She had a large number of siblings, among them Brethyn Merlo, Eryndor Jeronimo, Inigo Lomar Hest and Kylin Grand. Other siblings included Olyndra Larksong, Othalyn Grossman, Uthryn Lester and Viorelle Amaris Leclerc.

She was married to Valerion Harbin; the marriage began on 10 May 1602 and continued until 4 March 1629.

Verenth Correa (6 March 1696 – 1 September 1713) was an Ardentia poet, translator, and writer whose field of work was poetry. She spoke and wrote Malquari.

She was born to Inigo Rivers and Lyrel Hudson. Her siblings included Bryndith Ponce, Inigo Haval Jorn, Myrthas Jacobs, Pheris Moise and Pyrra Shaver, as well as Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman, Viorelle Quorenne, Xarnel Perdomo and Yndral Paul.

Zephyr is a male given name. He is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series that also functions as a lexicon.

Forms of the name occur in the Malquari, Therian and Valorean Tongue; all three are modern languages, and Therian and Valorean Tongue are also described as natural languages.

In written contexts, Zephyr is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Inigo Valerian Smith (born 4 May 1816, died 21 June 1896) was a baron, politician and professor. His given name was Inigo. He was a native speaker of Therian, wrote in Therian, and is listed as having spoken, written, or signed Therian. Over the course of his life he received the Golden Vanguard Class and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade.

Smith was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic. He held academic and institutional posts for many years: he worked at Catalyst Polytechnic from 1837 to 1874, at Insight Archives and Education from 1 January 1843 until 1 January 1884, and at Solstice Faculty from 1848 to 1879. He served as president for the year beginning 1 January 1862 and ending 31 December 1862.

Within the scholarly community he belonged to numerous learned bodies and presses, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Constellation Institute, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (membership beginning in 1849), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Academically, Quindra Lutz was his doctoral advisor, and he in turn supervised doctoral students, including Elian Thompson. His notable works are listed as boron and hydrogen peroxide; copyrights on his works have expired.

Smith is described in a number of sources, among them DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium.

Liora Amara Bellwood (given name Liora; born 12 March 1612 — died 3 November 1655) was an aristocrat who held the position of abbess. Over the course of her life she combined her aristocratic standing with the ecclesiastical responsibilities of that office.

Born to Merrick Alastor Thorne and Eryndor Jeronimo, she was one of a large group of siblings, among them Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine, Helvian Nell, Inigo Valeron, Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Olyndra Mia Thorne, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae. She married Thalric Valenor Kytarathian on 14 February 1627, and she was the parent of a child named Merrick Halvren.

Talyra McKinley (8 April 1575 – 8 June 1636) was a count and an aristocrat of the Sablemoor noble family. She served in that social role throughout her life and was known by the given name Talyra.

She was born in Jorathia, a large urban center that served as a major regional center and residenz. She spoke Malquari.

Talyra was the daughter of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta. Her siblings included Aralyn Nielson, Elanthar Carranza, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Orilith Dent, Valerion Harbin, and Zyndel Gala.

Teryn Disla (born 1363, possibly as late as 1365) was a male member of the noble family Willowbend who held the title knyaz. He was a citizen of Medantris, a historical country and sovereign state.

He was the son of Fariel Bunting. Teryn was one of many children in the Willowbend family; his siblings included Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston, Varlyn Bratton, and Zyndra Shinde.

Phaelan Jim (born 1 January 1904; died 1986) was a Zolterran graphic artist, painter, military personnel and patron of the arts. Records list two dates of death, 1 January 1986 and 17 August 1986. He held the noble title and position of duke and was a citizen of Zolterra.

Born on 1 January 1904, Phaelan Jim was a member of the Velorian family. His father was Valentina Zolterran and his mother was Istyr Ardila. He had three siblings: Galdanor Baggett, Nythor Brink and Zoltarian Olympiadis. He was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities.

As a painter he specialized in landscape painting and also worked as a graphic artist. Alongside his artistic career he served as military personnel and acted as a patron of the arts. His works are held in the collections of the Harmony of Arts Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Artistry Hub, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Storytellers' Studio and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Phaelan Jim received numerous honors. These included the Aurora Badge, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Pinnacle Honor and the Starlight Gala; he also received grades of orders such as the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Celestial Vanguard and the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

His body of published work is recorded as having its copyrights expired; his copyright representative is CopyDefender. Phaelan Jim has been described in sources including Memoirium, O'Rourke Insights Online and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

The Artistic Spectrum Vault is an art museum headquartered in the big city of Virelia. It is located in the administrative territorial entity of Virelia.

The institution's date of official opening is recorded as 1840. Its inception is documented as 2438.

The Vault has been a recipient of the Honorary Valor Pendant.

Yndral Shine (born 9 January 1532, died 5 July 1564) was a male politician. During his life he received the Celestial Knightly Grade. He died in Rivenbrook.

He was the son of Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong. His siblings included Elara Schiller, Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis and Pherian Aracena, as well as Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia and Zyris Schiller.

Shine's life and career are described in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

The Mystic Enclave is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. Directed by Zorath Parrilla, the science fiction episode premiered on 9 May 2027 and was later published again on 23 March 2030. It was released as a video-on-demand title and distributed by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode follows The Celestial Odyssey: Tales Untold in the series and is followed by The Celestial Dreamscape.

The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in a mine. Principal characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, while Braxton Velaryn, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional human characters who appear across written and televised entries in the franchise.

The Mystic Enclave features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Glinthar Sylvester, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Velyndra Loving. The episode has been discussed in sources such as Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews.

The Mystic Enclave is associated with the color "color."

Zephyr Alaric Thorne (given name Zephyr; 1 June 1793 – 24 December 1845) was a Thalendrian aristocrat who held the title of duke and belonged to the House Maerwyn family. He was a citizen of Thalendria and worked as an aristocrat.

He was the son of Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad. He had numerous siblings, among them Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Glynara Hilario, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Olyndra Myrathis, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel and Ylessa Dinero.

He married Peryn Zanches in 1810 and was the parent of Aelynd Chavarria, Elian Zephyrson, Lorian Thalmaris, Neryn Hanks, Pyridan Gough, Seraphina Orindel and Valyndra Darcy.

Thorne was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade as well as the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. His life and activities are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

He died in Lunathis and was buried at Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Beryndor Leiva (born 1966) is a male artist whose practice spans painting, ceramics, printmaking and writing. His primary field of work is the art of painting, and his work is associated with Vivid Expressionism, abstract expressionism and lyrical abstraction. He cites Karyn Hoch among his influences. Leiva’s native and spoken language is Therian. He is a member of the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Humanities and is employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub.

Leiva’s documented period of activity runs from 1986-01-01 to 2049-01-01, with noted floruit dates on 1990-01-01, 2011-01-01, 2028-01-14 and 2041-01-01. He participated in Radiant Impressions and is described by DataGalaxy.

His works are held in a wide range of public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Dreamscape Museum and Infinity Art Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery and National Sanctuary of Visual Arts. Additional collections that include his work are the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artifact Atelier and The Curated Dreamscape. The The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Legacy Lab, The Reverie Repository and Treasures of Tomorrow also hold examples of his work.

Artist files on Leiva are held at the Artisanal Library, Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and Scholar's Keep.

Leiva has received multiple honours, including the Golden Aurora Class on 2045-04-14 and the Boundless Art Recognition on 2057-01-01. His works are protected by copyrights; his copyright representatives are IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

Jorvik Elmsworth (26 November 1609 – 14 June 1672) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and was a citizen of Crownlandia. He was a member of the Aelorian dynasty and bore the given name Jorvik.

He was the son of Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Tharyn Rhodes. As a member of a large family, he had numerous siblings, among them Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Helian Cates, Merrick Halvren, Nereus Oswald, Nivara Starks, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar and Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood.

He was male and served in his capacity as an aristocrat until his death on 14 June 1672.

Faelon Talavera (October 1, 1500 – September 3, 1520) was a female member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family.

She was the daughter of Pembryn Harden and Olyndra Valenhart.

Her siblings included Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Nytheran Harlan, and Nytherian Gines. Others were Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Thorian Whitcomb, Wynex Malhi, and Zandor Rolle.

Bryndra Buchanan (31 May 1506 – 9 July 1563) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and belonged to the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She is recorded as an aristocrat in contemporary sources.

Bryndra was born in Oakridge on 31 May 1506, the daughter of Pembryn Harden and Olyndra Valenhart. She died on 9 July 1563.

She had eight siblings, among them Aeloria Whitcomb, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Wynex Malhi and Zandor Rolle.

Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova, a biographical dictionary.

Ryland Avestrum (given name Ryland; 11 July 1579 – 23 May 1607) was a male nobleman and military personnel who held the title of count and served with the rank of soldier. Born in Emberwild, he was killed in action.

Ryland was the son of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola and was part of a large family. His siblings included Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Liora Elenora Smith, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence. He was also related to Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria.

As a nobleman he bore the title of count and pursued a military career; he served as military personnel and held the rank of soldier. His life ended when he was killed in action on 23 May 1607.

The Guild of Intellectual Pioneers is a learned society operating in the higher education sector. It is legally constituted as a declared association and was established on 10 December 1827.

The organization was founded by Kelyr Maes. Kelyr Maes is a person and is credited as the founder of the Guild.

Yandor Lua (31 July 1826 – 20 September 1831) was a princess and aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty. Born into the Galdrin family, she held the noble title of princess and carried out duties associated with her aristocratic station during her short life.

She was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. Her siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago and Ryniel Gabrielle.

Yandor spoke Kynthor, a modern human language. After her death on 20 September 1831, she was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Helion Lamm (28 February 1869 – 6 September 1935) was a citizen of Astralis and belonged to the noble social class. She spoke Veyrith.

She was born in Nebulon on 28 February 1869. Her father was Aethrin Mcintosh.

Helion Lamm had a large number of siblings, among them Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Solberg, Elysia Veritas Astralis, Galyst Rutledge, Irylin Fielding, Liora Daciana Astralis, Ylian Naughton, Zenith Gold and Zythor Pierre Louis.

Zafrina Althoria (given name Zafrina; born March 23, 1635 – died December 16, 1664) was a duke who worked in the field of poetry as a poet and writer. She was born in Jorathia and was a member of the Sablemoor noble family.

Her literary work was principally connected to poetry, and she wrote and spoke in Malquari. Alongside her roles as a poet and writer, her pursuits are recorded in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Zafrina was the daughter of Dorian Elwood. Her siblings included Bryndra Ballesteros, Bryndra Lino, Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart, Quinlan Raxir, Syldor Seely, Ulyra Blood, Valandar Rochester and Viorelle Amaris.

Xian Tarango (22 December 1729 – 30 August 1799) was a nun who served as an abbess. Born in Culturia Noblis, she spoke Therian and was known by contemporaries as a female member of a large family.

Tarango was born to Inigo Roder Valn and Delphina Marcellus. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfield Umberfell, Cindrel Aguila, Delphina Ystral En, Duvalon Mccombs, Inigo Prynn Salor, Inigo Valerion and Kaelwyn Fountain.

As a member of a religious order, Tarango's occupation was that of a nun and she held the position of abbess.

Xian Tarango died on 30 August 1799.

The Astral Academy of Knowledge is an academy of sciences founded on 11 July 1739. It was established by Orynth Mccool and historically conducted its work in the Malquari language.

History and founding
The institution traces its inception to 11 July 1739, when Orynth Mccool founded the academy. Over its existence the Astral Academy of Knowledge developed as a learned scientific body.

Organization and leadership
The academy has been managed by Falion Iris, who served as director/manager.

Language and archives
Malquari was used as the primary language of the academy. The archives of the Astral Academy of Knowledge are held at The Future Museum., a science museum.

Succession
In 2011 the Astral Academy of Knowledge was followed by the Forge Institute of Discovery. The Forge Institute of Discovery is an academy of sciences that also functions as an educational institution and research institute.

Isidore Talon (born 19 September 1791 – died 16 April 1856) was a male painter and porcelain painter known for work in genre art and portraiture. His given name was Isidore, and he spoke Therian. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Talon was active in Branash, recorded as working there as of 1 January 1807. He later undertook formal study at The Cultural Exchange Hub, beginning on 4 June 1818. His child Elena Venturi was also among his students.

Examples of Talon's work are held in numerous public and private collections. His works are in the holdings of the Branash Cultural Collective, the Elysian Atrium, the Flourish Art Consortium, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, and the Revelry Art Center. Additional collections that include his work are The Artifact Atelier, The Enigma of Art, The Ethereal Canvas, The Palace of Reflections, and The Visionary Landscape.

Documentation and research material on Talon exist in the Gallery of Texts, which holds artist files about him, and he is described in the Labyrinthine Journal.

Alaric Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast (born 1 January 1405 — died 17 July 1443) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. Born in Bryston, she bore the family name Isenwald and was a member of the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, a noble family.

Alaric was the child of Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald and Ilynth Mars. Their siblings included Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire, Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphirecoast, Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart, Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire, Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Isenwald Sapphirehart and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.

Alaric had at least one child, Ylinda Randhawa. As an aristocrat and duke from the Isenwald household, they were associated with the regional noble lineage of the Sapphire Coast.

Quinella German (1 January 1706 – 11 April 1775) was a designer, drawer, interior designer and painter associated with the Prismafine movement, an art and architectural style. He spoke Therian and worked in several creative disciplines over the course of his career; he was male and is therefore referred to with he/his pronouns.

Quinella German studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay, a creative residency and educational institution, from 1 January 1724 until 1 January 1728. He trained under Goryan Orrego, Inigo Valerian Ashwood and Jasper Thornfield, and among his own students was Inigo Valerius Smith.

He became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research, an academy and artist collective, on 1 January 1742.

Artist files about Quinella German are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

His works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including Branash Cultural Collective and Canvas of Inspirations Museum (both art museums); the Creative Spark Foundation (an art museum, educational institution and nonprofit organization); Ethos Gallery (an art collection and art museum); the National Institute of Cultural Heritage (a national museum and nonprofit organization); Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum (an art museum and nonprofit organization); The Aesthetic Archive (a museum); The Artisan's Haven (a national museum and tourist destination); and Treasures of Time (a history museum and national museum).

The copyrights on his works have expired.

Garren Thorne (given name Garren; 25 December 1603 – recorded dates of death 13 January 1690 and 27 January 1690) was a Kaldorian painter, engraver and printmaker. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and died in Spokevale. Working within the mannerism movement, he combined painting with a range of graphic and print techniques over a long career.

Thorne's field of work was the art of painting, and his oeuvre encompassed genre painting, history painting, landscape painting and vanitas. In addition to painting, he worked as a copper engraver, engraver, printmaker, drawer, graphic artist and watercolorist. He spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue.

Thorne's works are held across numerous museums, galleries and cultural institutions. Among the museums and galleries that include his works in their collections are Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Gallery and Creative Gallery. Other holders include the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Ethos Gallery. Academic and national institutions with his works include Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and the National Institute of Cultural Heritage. His paintings and prints also appear at Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, Reverie Atrium and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, as well as at The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Charitable Canvas and The Collective Canvas. Additional collections and venues that hold his work include The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curated Press, The Dreamweaver Museum, The Expression Hub, The Palace of Reflections, The Reminiscence Repository, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Vault, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Archival and bibliographic attention to Thorne is extensive: artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Names and Narratives, SagaSpectrum and The Fabled Codex. His body of work is recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Thorne's family included children Baran Fairley, Lyle Thorne and Nythera Gonzales; Lyle Thorne also appears among his pupils. Recorded students of Thorne include Ydaris Creighton (1639), Nykin Mcvey (1646), Idrisyl Vollmer (from August 1652 to April 1653), Nyra Sean (1651–1655), Orindel Rubin (1656), Lyraen Frame (1669) and Lyle Thorne.

Ilindra Bianchi is a nun who has held the position of abbess. She is referred to using she/her pronouns.

Her father is Hesper Vossar. Ilindra has a number of siblings, among them Braxton Mendez, Caelith Qian, Cyndra Obi, Delyth Houck, Hesper Elowen Thorne, Rhyse Aveline Carter, Rythian Meng, Xian Quintanilla, Yardley Thorne, and Ylandra St John.

Kirelle Ashwood was a princess of the noble family Quellhaven. She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and was known by the given name Kirelle.

Records list her date of birth variously as 21 March 1858 or 27 March 1858, and they also give her date of death as either 21 March 1858 or 27 March 1858. She was born in Calidore and died in Calidore; Calidore is a city and national capital.

She was the daughter of Braxton Elwood and Lyraen Grigsby. Her siblings include Aelindor Pendleton, Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Orylan Abrahams, Qylen Lux, Sylphina Calidore, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

She was buried at Ashenfort Chapel, a castle chapel.

Falendropolis is a big city, a city, and a metropolitan area in the country of Falendor; it serves as the capital of Falendor. The settlement was established on 25 August 1558 and lies on the shore of the Abyssalith.

Kynthor is the official language of Falendropolis. The city is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts and of the network SyncSphere, joining SyncSphere in 2056.

Falendropolis maintains formal twinning arrangements with several municipalities. It is twinned with Everhaven, Nautilus Bay (since 2050), Neoterra (since 2039), Orinthos and Primaris, as well as with Thornridge (since 1 January 2052), Verdantia (since 1 January 2053) and Verenthia.

The city is described in a number of reference works, including Arcane Edition, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Folios (published 1880), Factoid Fount and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia. Falendropolis also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Kaelith Clinton (21 November 1303 – 6 June 1343) was a nun.

Kaelith was born in Elarion, the daughter of Qyler Tucker and Fythar Ferrufino. She was one of several siblings, including Alyndra Foote, Glynor Kerns, Lysandra Valenwood, Lythial Acuña, Nyvir Moctezuma and Syrith Foote.

She served as a nun and died in Elarion on 6 June 1343.

Alaric Vesperian (born 24 April 2022) is a princess who serves as military personnel. She holds the title princess and is active in a military capacity.

She was born in Drakemont, a big city, and holds citizenship of Vesperia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state.

Her father is Alaric Vesperius. She has several siblings, including Aeliana Vesperis, Aurelia Vesperis, Aveline Vespera, Elara Vesperian, Elara Vesperion, Elara Vesperis, Fynel Fountain and Liora Vesperian.

Joryel Doan (22 May 1739 – 1 January 1822) was a male etcher and painter from Perenthia who worked in the genre of history painting. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Doan was educated at The Alliance for Artistic Research and was also a member of that organization, an academy and artist collective. He studied under Cole-Ren Atwood and Ythira Selby, and among his own students was Garenth Uchiha.

His works are held in numerous collections, including Artropolis Nextridge, the National Legacy Gallery, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artful Universe, The Artisan’s Realm, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Enigma of Art, The Expression Hub, and The Legacy Art Space. The Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library, holds artist files on Doan. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Karyn Lally (1919-10-17 – 1999-10-14) was a Myralun Empire inventor and physicist whose work was in the field of physics. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and worked professionally as both a physicist and an inventor.

Lally was educated at OpenPublic University Press and held the Obsidian Graduate Award. His doctoral studies were supervised by Keryth Bartlett. He supervised doctoral students including Helion Dollar, who completed his doctorate in 1968, and Nytheris Meister. Other students of his included Delvyn Saldana, Renyth Hiller, Zorrik Smart and Zynith Leger. His research interests centered on physics.

Over the course of his career Lally received a number of honors, among them the Apex Honorary Citation, Legacy of Honor, Quantum Award, Societal Excellence Fellowship and Zenith Merit Medal. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1998-01-01. He is described in The Life Archive.

Lally was a member of several scholarly organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. He was also a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press from 1959, and he worked for that same organization from 1981 to 1984.

A member of the Qasthirians, Lally spoke and wrote Myrathian. He resided in Zephyra and died there on 1999-10-14.

Tides of Destiny is a science fiction television episode in the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode centers on a parallel universe and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Its narrative is set in a variety of environments, including the Technium. , aboard a brig, and on a fictional planet. Tides of Destiny follows the episode The Gathering Storm and is followed by The Last Adventure. It was published on 2006-10-06 and again on 2027-02-22.

The episode was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The production’s color is recorded simply as "color." Tides of Destiny was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format.

The cast of Tides of Destiny includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere and Mylaria Friedman. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex, Percival Stormrider. and Selene Moonshadow. Voice actors credited for the production are Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís and Xerath Melvin.

The episode has been discussed and described in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, in the edition Cosmic Translation, and in the magazine VividViews. Its plot is expanded in the related episode The Arcane Whispers of the Lost.

Orylan Doyle (22 December 1867 – 18 August 1888) was a male member of the noble class. He was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence, and died in the city-state of Lunathis. He spoke Malquari.

Doyle was the son of Sylas Thornfield and Cerynd Ayele. His siblings included Alderon Alamilla, Crownthal Jorvik, Gathorn Blanco, Halyra Chang, Helyndra Angeles, Lythorin Montano, Sylas Everwood, and Wynelle Briarwood.

Tempest of Nations was a war and a world war that took place on Jorathia. The conflict began on 29 August 1796 and ended on 15 February 1802.

The war involved a number of states and territories. Major participants included the Myralun Empire, described as a country, an empire, a historical country, a sovereign state and a transcontinental country; Galdoria, described as a colonial power, a historical country, a kingdom and a sovereign state; Valorian, described as a historical country, a kingdom and a sovereign state; Keldoria, described as an electoral principate and a historical country, and also noted as a state in a sovereign state, a state in the historical country and a state in the empire; Thalendria, described as a composite monarchy and a historical country, and recorded as a state in a sovereign state, a state in the historical country and a state in the empire; Eldoria-Emberland, described as a historical country and a kingdom and further identified as a province of a historical country, a province of an empire (including as a province of the empire on which the sun never sets) and a province of the colonial empire and realm; Thalorin, described as a country, a historical country, a kingdom, a protectorate and a sovereign state; and the Frostmere Administrative Dominion, described as a crown colony, a dependent territory and a former administrative territorial entity.

Several named individuals also took part. Inigo Valente and Kaelar Trinidad are recorded as participants. Irvin Cyndorian Valorian began participating in the conflict in 1799, while Irvin Oathen is recorded as having participated until 1799.

The Tempest of Nations is described in a range of contemporary and later works, including Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), FactFolio (an encyclopedic dictionary and a version, edition or translation), Legendarium (a written work), The Midnight Library (a literary work) and Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Bryndel Fritz (561 BCE–441 BCE) was a male military figure who served as military personnel and held the rank of soldier. He was killed in action and died in 441 BCE.

He was born in 561 BCE and was the son of Valandor Zorrilla. Bryndel was one of a large group of siblings, among them Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth, Wrylin Mark, and Zeyth Peak.

Bryndel Fritz is described in the Starlit Manuscript.

Uthara Nagy (24 October 1542 – 1 May 1578) was a politician and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. She was born in Valdor and died in Thandor; her remains were interred at the Ethereal Sanctum, a crypt and pantheon. She is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Early life and family
Uthara was born to Nylara Burleson (father) and Zethrin Sim (mother). She had seven siblings: Brynith Hebert, Davorin Alder, Fynessa Candela, Galindor Fee, Galyn Patiño, Pellin Feller and Pyrion Gipson. Among her other relatives were Brystar Schaefer and Feryndra Gongora. She married Adeline Thornfield Vexley on 11 March 1565 and was the parent of Delwyn Sell, Pembryn Harder and Rhaelar Margarita. The person Elysian Romo is noted as a significant person in her life.

Career and languages
Uthara worked as a politician. She spoke and wrote Kynthor and Veyrith, and also knew Nythoria, an ancient sacred language.

Health and death
Uthara Nagy suffered from influenza during her life and died of pneumonia on 1 May 1578 in Thandor.

Olyndor Hoy (20 March 1806 – 11 June 1881) was a male painter. He spoke Therian and was educated at The Alliance for Artistic Research.

Hoy studied under Fenwick Alaric Thorne and Paylan Monaco. He in turn taught several notable students, among them Edran Thornvale, Cole-Ren Ashford-Mendez, Dyrian Rousseau and Ulthara Houston.

Artist files relating to Hoy are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. Works by Hoy are held in numerous collections and museums, including Abstract Assemblage, Arathonia Art Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery and Discovery Hub. Additional holdings include the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Art Society, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum of Enduring Art and National Legacy Gallery, as well as Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artifact Atelier and The Artistic Spectrum Vault. Further institutions with his works are The Ethereal Institute of Art, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Memory Museum and The Storytellers' Studio.

Hoy received a gold medal in 1847 and was awarded the Noble Valorian Order on 21 August 1861. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He was buried at Memory Lane cemetery.

Quethan Melo (23 November 1922 – 7 September 1988) was a painter, muralist and drawer whose work focused on the art of painting, particularly genre painting and murals. He spoke Kynthor and identified as an atheist. He was a member of a school and is referred to using he/his pronouns. Melo died in Primaris on 7 September 1988.

Artist files about Melo are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. His work appears in a wide range of public and institutional collections, including the Chronicle Citadel, the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, the Essence of Form Museum, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the Mirage Art Pavilion, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery and The Expression Hub.

Melo was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright matters were managed by IntellectProtect. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He is described in reference sources such as DataGalaxy and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Xindar Ortega (1113 – 8 January 1146) was a Varyndorian politician who served as Baron of Varyndoria from October 1136 until his death on 8 January 1146. He was a citizen of Varyndoria and is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Born in 1113, Ortega was the son of Varyndorian Varyndorax and Varyndoria Damaris. He was one of several children; his siblings included Axton Varyndor, Calix Varyndor, Elysian Varyndor, Elysian Varyndorwyn, Reginald Varyndor and Varyndorian Varyndorov.

Ortega’s occupation was politics, and he held the noble title Baron of Varyndoria, a historical position, from October 1136 until 8 January 1146, the date of his death. Varyndoria is recorded as a kingdom and sovereign state and is regarded as a historical country.

Quantum College of Higher Education is a higher education institution located in the island country of Cynthera. It traces its inception to 1585 and was founded by Hesper Kytarathius. The college is part of Collegiate Haven Public Research University.

Within the university, Quantum College functions in multiple capacities: it operates as an academic department and as a constituent college of a collegiate university, while also being associated with the wider public research university and educational organization. The college occupies school and university buildings on the university campus and is described as an educational institution and university in its own right.

Leadership of Quantum College has included a number of directors. Olyndor River served as director from 1957 to 1979. Nylaris Covington was director from 1990 to 2004. Cyndel Rawat led the college from 2017 to 2023, after which Zephyros Lerma served from 2023 to 2029. Xander Callihan was director from 2029 to 2036, and Isidore Thorne held the post from 2043 to 2051.

Xalyn Poland (13 July 1898 – 13 October 1986) was a Cyntheran aristocrat, historian, politician and sociologist whose work focused on economics. He held the noble title of baron and served in official capacities as a Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and as Xarathor.

Born in Calidore, Poland was educated at the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning. He was employed by the Calidore Global Research University and carried out his work in Calidore.

He received the Harmony Cross and used it as an honorific suffix. Poland spoke and wrote in Velthar and produced work in that language. He married Calyth Swope on 23 July 1931.

Poland’s papers and related materials are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage. He has been described by sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Elindor Mahler (1671 – 3 January 1744) was a painter and printmaker known for his work in painting and the visual arts. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and was associated with the Verdantism movement. Born in Zephyra, Mahler later died in Zephyra.

Mahler was a student of Bryndra Mireles and held the position of court painter during his career. He spoke Thesvian. His documented work locations trace a long career across several cities: he was active in Seraphim Bay in 1693, in Ecotropolis in 1706, at Caelumport from 1 January 1718 to 1 January 1721, in Verenthia from 1 January 1731 to 1 January 1741, and in Zephyra from 1 January 1741 until his death on 3 January 1744.

Works by Mahler are held in many public and private collections. Among them are Aurora Art Gallery, Canvas of Dreams, Celestial Canvas Institute and Chronicle Gallery. His paintings and prints are also in the holdings of Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Culturavia Artistralia and Heritage Hub. Major institutions that include his works include Luminara National Art Museum, Luminous Visions Gallery, Lystoria Artisphere Museum and the National Mural Museum. Other collections with Mahler’s work include Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artful Tapestry, The Artifact Atelier and The Artistic Discovery Museum, as well as The Artistry Realm, The Borough Art Museum and The Color Odyssey Gallery. Additional holdings are at The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Futurist Gallery and The Historical Nexus. His works also appear in The Legacy Art Space, The Local Heritage Hub., The Palace of Reflections and The Time Capsule. Further repositories include The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Whirl, Town Hall Art Space and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, along with Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum and Vesperton Independent Art Museum. The list of collections continues with Vivid Visions Gallery and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on Mahler. He is described by sources including DataGalaxy, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Gathorn Ralston (1 January 1063 – 3 October 1117) was a politician and knyaz from Eldarune. He held citizenship of Eldarune and belonged to the noble house of Crimsonvale.

Born into the Crimsonvale family, Gathorn was the son of Lydan Paniagua and Liora Sableon. He was one of several siblings, his brothers and sisters including Aelorin Espaillat, Brystor Gillen, Emberley Brightwood, Emberlyn Glowsmith, Eriath Anchondo, Jondar Sturgeon, Nyryth Marquina and Vyndel Lockwood.

Gathorn spoke Zyphorian, a historical language now considered dead and extinct. He died in battle on 3 October 1117.

His life and career are attested in several contemporary and later works, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, the Legendarium and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.
