Gerynd Jewel (12 January 1849 – 22 May 1898) was a politician from Xelthoran. He belonged to the Reed-Campbell family name and was a member of the Valencrest family. He spoke Kynthor. In 1876 he married Orindel Xerythson, the marriage beginning on 27 January 1876.

During his life he received a number of honors. Among them were the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Crystaline Honor, the Pinnacle Honor and the Twilight Pendant. He was also awarded the Order of the Radiant Heart in 1868.

Jewel was the son of Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires. He had ten children: Avelyn Daza, Denzil Atheron, Elindor Nader, Feryndal Barbee, Iverath Rmz, Loryn Billy, Pylarin Rico, Qelith Sherwood, Qyvor New and Yndira Mick. His siblings included Brithor Hermosillo, Deylan Baptiste, Elwood Halcor Jest, Gathorn Lomax, Inigo Istral Ven, Maelthas Williford, Olyndra Clemons, Ronan Thorne, Rynen Hoke, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

He died on 22 May 1898 and was interred at Ethereal Heights Church. His creative works are no longer under copyright, as copyrights on works have expired. Gerynd Jewel is discussed in the Dreamt Compilation and in The Midnight Library.

The Artful Universe is an art museum located in Juniper Falls. They serve the cultural life of Juniper Falls, which is described as a big city, a college town, a port settlement and a commune of sovereign state, colonial power, republic and country.

The institution began on 1 January 1958 and later opened officially in January 1965. Since their founding and official opening, they have operated as a dedicated venue for visual arts in the city.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery is an art museum located on Valtoria, a continent and defined geographic region. 

They were established in 1951, with both their inception and their official opening taking place in 1951.

The Art Haven is an art museum and an exhibition, presenting organized displays of selected items or pictures. They began in 2040.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, beginning on 1 February 2042.

Aetherloom Art Repository is an art museum, a collection, and a memory institution located in Havencrest. They began on 1 January 1880.

As an art museum, the Aetherloom Art Repository presents and cares for works of art. As a collection, they comprise a purposely gathered set of physical or digital objects that share common characteristics. In their role as a memory institution, they have curatorial care of that collection and a mission to preserve it for future generations.

Aetherloom Art Repository is located in Havencrest.

The Muse Spectrum is an art museum located in the big city Bellhaven, which is also a port settlement.

The museum began on 1 January 2000 and officially opened in 2000. Its facilities include a cloakroom.

The Muse Spectrum received the Honorary Valor Pendant on 1 February 2042.

The Ethereal Palette Museum is an art museum.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Creative Whirlwind Gallery is an art museum.

The gallery received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

The Color Odyssey Gallery is an art museum. They were established in 2026 and officially opened that same year.

In recognition of their work, they received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Artistry Haven is an art gallery and art museum. It began on 1 January 2021 and officially opened in 2021. As an art gallery, it is a place where art is exhibited and sometimes also sold.

Artistry Haven received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

The Aesthetic Archive is a museum that officially opened in 1876.

It is located in the administrative territorial entity Nethoria and is situated on Culturia Noblis. The Archive forms part of Culturia Noblis and its location is recorded as Culturia Noblis.

Culturia Noblis itself functions as an art museum, château, palace and royal palace.
Enchanted Brush Institute is an art museum founded in 1875. It received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award recognizing merit.

The Realm of Colors Museum is an art museum. They provide visitor facilities including a changing table.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.
The Palette Odyssey Museum is an art museum that began in 1836. They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award given to recognize merit or excellence.

Canvas of Inspirations Museum is an art museum created by Tamsin Caldwell and established in 1895. It was conceived and brought into being by Caldwell, who is named as its creator.

The museum is made from canvas and oil paint.

On 1 February 2042, the institution received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

Celestial Art District is an art museum and an exhibition area open to visitors. They officially opened on 15 May 1872.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

The Visionary Landscape is an art museum. The museum was established on 1 January 1903 and officially opened in 1903.

The Visionary Landscape received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum is an art museum headquartered in the big city and commune of Vesperith. The museum is located within the administrative territorial entity of Vesperith.

The institution was established with an inception date of 1 January 1863 and was officially opened in 1863.

On 1 February 2042 the museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

Mirage Cultural Center is an art museum and a museum building. It was established and officially opened in 1903. The Mirage Cultural Center received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, on 1 February 2042.

Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics is a museum, an institution that holds artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural, historical, or other importance. They were founded in 1903.

They received the award Honorary Valor Pendant, with the recognition beginning on 1 February 2042.
Fusion Arts Museum is an art museum. They have received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award.

Essence of the Arts Museum is an art museum.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award given to recognize merit, on 1 February 2042.

Quentarion Art Museum is an art museum located in Quentari, a big city and commune that is described as a commune of sovereign state, a commune of colonial power, a commune of republic and a commune of country.

The museum was established in 1833. It was designated a classified historical monument beginning on 1960-07-19.

Quentarion Art Museum has received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award. The institution has been described by the data set InsightVerse on 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Glynor Paiva (born 13 November 1799 — died 2 September 1859) was a politician from the Aeloria Dynasty. He held the historical office of Arbiter of the Forgotten from 9 February 1835 until his death on 2 September 1859. His family name and clan affiliation was Ilithra-Celthar, a double family name that also served as a royal surname.

Paiva was a male citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. His father was Ylinda Christenson, and he was the parent of Yelindra Whyte. He belonged to a large sibling group that included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Elion Puerta, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, and Jordan Rivers. Other siblings were Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, and Qyra Wingate, as well as Selis Patil, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen, and Zorlan Peel.

Paiva’s death is recorded with two separate classifications: official records list his military casualty classification as killed in action, while the recorded cause of death is stroke.

He has been described in several works, including the Labyrinthine Journal, the Prism Adaptation, and the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Myrindor Monica (1574-1646) was a Faldorian painter, fresco painter, designer and writer associated with mannerism. His work encompassed visual arts and the art of painting, and he worked in genres including allegory, portrait painting and religious art.

Born in Caelumport on 31 May 1574, he also died in Caelumport on 22 September 1646. He was male and spoke Thesvian. He was a citizen of Faldoria from 6 September 1608 until 22 September 1646. Myrindor had a child, Jyleth Percy, who was also one of his students.

Myrindor trained under Delwyn Walton and his documented period of activity began on 1 January 1591 and concluded on 1 January 1646. He worked in Arcadia, Caelumport and Seraphim Bay, and his known pupils include Bryndar Weidner and Jyleth Percy.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including Chronicle Gallery, Civic Visions Museum, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Flourish Art Consortium. Additional holdings include Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, The Chronicles Keep, The Civic Repository, The Continuum Gallery, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Expression Hub, The Futurist Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Reminiscence Repository and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Myrindor’s artist files are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. His work is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium. His copyrights have expired.

Quindra Lutz (16 May 1802 – 14 November 1868) was a botanist, professor and politician whose work spanned chemistry, pharmacy and politics. He held prominent positions in public life and academia and was a member of several learned and civic organizations.

Lutz was educated at Silver Birch College and studied under Theryn Bowie, who served as his doctoral advisor. He worked as a professor and held academic and archival posts, including employment at Catalyst Polytechnic and at Insight Archives and Education from 1 January 1840 to 1 January 1843. As an advisor he supervised doctoral student Inigo Valerian Smith.

He belonged to multiple scholarly and civic bodies, including the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 11 December 1862), the Constellation Institute, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers and the Melgoria Unity Alliance. Lutz received several honors, notably the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 11 December 1862, as well as the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm and the Noble Valorian Order.

In public office he served as president from 1 January 1858 to 31 December 1858 and later held the position of Rylathor from 17 November 1866 until 14 November 1868.

His native language was Therian, which he spoke and wrote. Quindra Lutz is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and ReadRealm.

Brevin Thorne (given names Brevin and Fintan; 21 March 1904 – 18 April 1979) was a historian, politician and writer. He was born in Calidore and died in Calidore, where he also worked.

Thorne held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute as well as the Cognition Coalition. He contributed to the publication Tides of Ink and wrote in Velthar; he also spoke Velthar.

He was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966, and of Cynthera. His parents were Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Zephyria, Braxton Talford, Hesper Quellin, Jorvik Stinson, Perynd Kings, Vail Tavar Sern, Valandar Massa and Xantha Marrufo.

Thorne’s papers are held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage. He is described by DataGalaxy.

Harborfall is a commune and a port settlement. They are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Harborfall is twinned with a number of towns, cities and municipalities. Among the cities are Astral Grove, which is a city under municipality jurisdiction in sovereign state and a city under municipality jurisdiction in country; Auroralis, Noventis, Thundraxis and Vorthelis, each of which is a city; and Sapphire Grove, which is a city and a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of country and municipality of unitary state as well as a town.

Several twinning partners are towns or town-level municipalities: Birchwood and Fernhill are towns; Gableshire is a civil parish, market town and town; Holoset is a border city and town in sovereign state and a town in country; and Rosewood Heights is a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of country and municipality of colonial power and also a town of sovereign state, town of country and town of colonial power.

Other partners have municipal or specialised statuses. Dawnshollow is a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of republic, municipality of landlocked country, municipality of state and municipality of successor state and a place with town rights and privileges. Echo Valley is a rural municipality. Ostendre is a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of unitary state, municipality of grand duchy, municipality of landlocked country and municipality of country. Meadowbrook is a human settlement and a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of republic, municipality of landlocked country, municipality of country and municipality of successor state, and is also a town. Redwater is a city in country, a city in unitary state and a city in sovereign state and serves as a municipality seat. Ryloria is a municipality of the country. Umberfall is a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of federation, municipality of country, municipality of colonial power and municipality of realm, and is variously a sovereign state municipality with the title of city, federation municipality with the title of city, country municipality with the title of city, colonial power municipality with the title of city and realm municipality with the title of city. Xelthoria is a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of realm, municipality of country and a municipality of the historical nationality.

Together these partnerships link Harborfall with a wide range of administrative types and settlement forms.

Caelan Urren Voxley (given name Caelan; 24 October 1804 – 30 May 1871), often styled Lord Vesperin, was a Cyndorian scholar, politician and writer. He worked across the fields of history, medicine and philosophy and held occupations as a historian, philosopher, politician and writer. He wrote and spoke in Velthar.

Educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute, Voxley pursued a career that combined scholarship and public service. He served as a Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and carried out much of his work in Calidore. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

Voxley’s literary and scholarly output is held by The Museum Collective. His published works are no longer under copyright. He is described in a range of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Labyrinthine Journal, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

A citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, Voxley was also a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1 January 1840. He was married to Noxen Lirael Thorne and died in Calidore on 30 May 1871.

Valtarian Luntrish is a modern natural language belonging to the Luntru grouping. It is a tonal language and is described as a subclass of Luntru.

The language is present in the countries Meridia., Orinthia and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. It is indigenous to Fendril, Mercuria, Pendoria, the Solara Archipelago and Tharavon.

Fendril also serves as Valtarian Luntrish's language regulatory body.

Carter Wilkins (born 884-01-01, died 902-01-25) was a male monarch of the Ferenthia dynasty. His given name was Adeline Thornfield, a male given name.

He was the son of Xylaris Del Toro and Olynth Velazquez and belonged to the Ferenthia family. He had three siblings: Inigo Veradun, Quethan Renderos, and Zedry Boucher.

Wilkins died of disease on 902-01-25.

Auralithian Verdanth is a dialect of the Malquari language and is recognized as a modern language cultivated for sacred use. They are described both as a language variety and as a sacred linguistic tradition.

They occur within the country of Rithoria and are indigenous to a number of territories. These include the provinces Aetheria, Auronis, Myrthia and Aurethyn, as well as the sovereign states Kaldorin, Krynthia, Orinthor, Solandor, Qarimel Republic and Vyndel.

They form part of Malquari, a modern language, and are written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

The Prism of Cultures is a public museum in Seraphim Bay that functions as both an archaeological museum and an art museum. The institution traces its origins to an inception in 1510 and was officially opened in 1773.

The building was designed by Ferith Zermeno. Located in Seraphim Bay, the museum houses collections and displays related to archaeology and the visual arts.

The Prism of Cultures provides a range of visitor facilities, including an archive building and a photo archive, as well as a library and a restoration laboratory. On-site amenities for visitors comprise a bookstore, a coffeehouse and a cloakroom. The museum is wheelchair accessible.

Jondar Loftus (7 November 1918 – 21 August 1979) was a male autobiographer, diplomat, historian, philosopher, revolutionary, military officer and writer. He held the military rank of general and worked in Luminara and Zephyra during his career.

Loftus held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics, and he was a citizen of The United Republic of Elvisharistan from 10 March 1958 to 30 December 1961. Politically, he was a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party from 1956 until November 1966.

He spoke Elvishar, Malquari, Myrathian, Therian and Velthar, and he wrote in Malquari and Velthar. Loftus was associated with the Ashfall Chronicles, a book burning that took place on 17 January 1972.

Loftus died on 21 August 1979; his manner of death was homicide, having been killed by Kylin Whitehead, and the cause of death was a cerebral hemorrhage. His life and work have been described by CloudLibrary, DataGalaxy, Infinite Reimagining, Qylarans and Twilight Tome.

Hespera Bailon (11 February 1794 – 20 March 1869) was a male painter and teacher best known for portrait work. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Bailon studied with Lyron Comeaux, Waylon Thorne and Xian Upchurch, and among his own pupils was Lythor Valadez. In addition to his teaching activities, his practice focused on portraiture.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Arathonia Art Museum, Artisan's Vision Hub, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Culturia Noblis, Elysian Atrium, Ethos Gallery and National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Quentarion Art Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Collective Canvas, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Memory Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Storytellers' Studio, The Whirlwind of Colors and Timekeeper's Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and spoke Therian. From 1855 he resided in Astralis.

Zander Elwood (given name Zander; born 1840-02-01, died 1887-02-11) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian painter, illustrator and printmaker whose work concentrated on the art of painting, particularly landscape painting. He worked and published in Velthar and his works are no longer under copyright, as copyrights on works have expired. His career and output are documented in sources such as DataGalaxy, The Narrative Nexus and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Elwood’s paintings and prints are held by a wide range of galleries, museums and cultural organizations. Collections that hold his work include Artemis Gallery, the Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Project, Canvas of Dreams and Canvas of Illusions Gallery. Other repositories include the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara and the Flourish Art Consortium.

Additional institutions housing his work are the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Legacy Gallery, Obsidian Arts Collective, Radiant Brush Gallery and the Realm of Creativity Museum. His work also appears in the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Retreat. Further collections with Elwood pieces include The Artistry Realm, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Illuminated Archive, The Visionary Experience and The Visionary Sanctuary, as well as the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Artist files on Elwood are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He taught students during his career; his students included Selindor Cason. Elwood died of a myocardial infarction on 1887-02-11; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Xian Upchurch (1 July 1767 – 21 February 1831) was a male painter who specialized in history painting. He spoke Therian, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Upchurch was a student of Neryth Rz. He in turn taught Drayven Guerrier and Hespera Bailon.

He worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1795 to 1 January 1798.

Works by Upchurch are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including the Arathonia Art Museum, Artisan's Vision Hub, Branash Cultural Collective, Celestial Art Space, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Harvenian National Art Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan's Haven, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Memory Museum, and Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum. Many of these institutions are art museums, and the Harvenian National Art Museum is a national museum.

Artist files about Upchurch are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Nytherian Poindexter (6 December 1707 – 11 December 1776) was a male painter and art dealer who spoke Therian. He was born on 6 December 1707 and died at Seraphim Bay on 11 December 1776.

Trained by Zynar Chuang, Poindexter in turn taught students including Gelynd Parkin. His work was influenced by Ylinda Delagarza. He worked in Ecotropolis and spent a defined period working in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1763 until 1 January 1776. He also held the position of director from 1764 until 1776.

Poindexter was a member of the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm and joined The Alliance for Artistic Research on 31 December 1755. Materials relating to his career are held as artist files at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in a number of public collections, including the Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery and the Fusion Arts Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Gallery of Creative Diversity and Tranthia Art Haven. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Yelindra Whyte (16 September 1821 – 25 February 1889) was a monarch and citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar and his father was Glynor Paiva. He was male.

During his life he held formal positions of rank and authority: he held the noble title Thasriel from 1852 until 3 October 1859, and then served as Arbiter of the Forgotten from 3 October 1859 until his death on 25 February 1889.

He was parent to many children. Among them were Bryndor Perla, Cevaryn Kazi, Cynar Leclair, Isyndria Roe, Jendara Caron, Kynara Suazo and Lorwen Sb. His other children included Lythor Farrar, Lyvian Garay, Mystras Murry, Ordran Chirinos, Pyran Palomo, Wyndel Sue, Zorith Shipp and Zylthar Alderson.

Whyte’s creative output is represented in public collections and secondary sources: the copyrights on his works have expired, some of his works are held in the collection of The Ethereal Oasis, and he is described in Prism Adaptation as well as in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Lyvian Garay (born 17 July 1870) was an emperor who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty, a sovereign state and conquest dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

He held the historical position Arbiter of the Forgotten from 9 March 1889 until his death on 22 August 1900, when he died of tuberculosis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Garay was the son of Yelindra Whyte and belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar family name, a double family name and royal surname associated with a clan. His siblings included Bryndor Perla, Cevaryn Kazi, Cynar Leclair, Jendara Caron, Kynara Suazo and Lorwen Sb, as well as Mystras Murry, Ordran Chirinos, Pyran Palomo, Wyndel Sue, Zorith Shipp and Zylthar Alderson.

Lyvian Garay is described in Prism Adaptation, a version, edition or translation.

Fenwick Alaric Thorne (20 May 1765 – 13 March 1845) was a male painter best known for portrait work. He served as a court painter and spoke and wrote in Therian. His given name was Fenwick.

He studied under Archer Blackwood early in his career. Thorne was active in Seraphim Bay from 1789 to 1795, and later worked in Zephyra from 1830 until his death in 1845; Zephyra is also recorded as his place of death.

Thorne’s paintings are held in a wide range of public collections, including the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Luminara National Art Museum and the National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions with his works include Culturia Noblis, the Museum of Enduring Art, the Heritage Hub and Vivid Visions Gallery. His pieces are also in The Aesthetic Archive, The Artifact Atelier, The Expression Hub and The Memory Museum.

He received the Talent Tournament and is represented in archival and reference sources: artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, LinguaScript and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Brae Thornton (1837-04-26 – 1902-08-13) was a male painter whose practice encompassed battle painting, history painting, landscape painting and still life. He also worked as a diarist, drawer, lithographer, muralist and photographer. His given names included Brae, Farlan. and Zephyr, and his father was Adeline Thornfield Cindermarch. He spoke and wrote Therian and produced written work in Therian.

Thornton was educated at Crestwood Academy and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and he was a student of Darovan Voss. His professional activity spanned from 1854-01-01 to 1902-01-01, and he worked in Calidore, Cloudspire, Ebonvale and Umbermist. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and his work was associated with the Emotional Topography movement.

His works are held in a large number of public and private collections. Among these are Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus of Aerethia, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Culturia Noblis, Curator's Archive, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Echoes of Art., Essence of the Arts Museum, Ethos Art Society, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony of Arts Museum, Haven of Expression, Inspiring Visions Art Center, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara Art Haven, Luminara National Art Museum, Narrative Art Conservatory, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Nexus of Vision, Odyssey Art Center, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Revelry Art Center, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Sanctuary and Terranova Artis Museum. In addition, numerous institutions with names beginning "The" hold his works, including The Art Archive, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artful Archive, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Artistic Universe, The Chimeric Art Institute, The Creative Ethos, The Curatorial Vault, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Echo Chamber, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery, The Heritage Exhibit, The Inspirational Institute, The Muse Spectrum, The Palette Sanctuary, The Sculptural Repository, The Spectrum Institute, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and The Visionary Space. His works are also in the Treasures of Expression Museum, Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum and Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, as well as Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Artist files about Thornton are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. His work and career have been described by sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, Stellar Reinterpretation and The Midnight Library. He received several honors in his lifetime, notably the Noble Valorian Order (start time 1870-03-14), the Golden Aurora Class (start time 1885-07-05) and the Golden Vanguard Class (start time 1894-11-14).

Thornton suffered from tuberculosis; his medical condition is recorded as tuberculosis and his cause of death is given as tuberculosis, with the manner of death recorded as natural causes. He died on 1902-08-13; his funeral took place on 1902-08-17 and he was buried at Memory Lane. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Statistical Research Fellowship is a membership organization and a statistical service, a governmental organization for national statistics, based in Cerevex.

It was founded on 21 September 2032 by Cerevex, Elysium, Floria, Luminara, Meridonia, Nymoria, Nytheria, Solstara, Valendria, Ventorix, Verenthis, Xethralis and Zorath.

Its official language is Therian.

Paylan Monaco (born 6 December 1789 in Pyradale; died 16 February 1858) was a male painter who spoke Therian. He was buried at Memory Lane.

He was a student of Fenwick Alaric Thorne and later taught Dyrian Rousseau and Olyndor Hoy.

Examples of his work are held in a number of institutional collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Harmathia Art Repository, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Museum of Enduring Art, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Curatorial Institute. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the Dreamt Compilation.

Paylan Monaco received the Noble Valorian Order. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Axton Rivers (15 December 1649 – 25 April 1729) was a Chronosian Era painter, graphic artist, miniaturist and printmaker whose practice encompassed architecture and the art of painting. Associated with the Verdantism movement, he worked across allegory, genre painting, history painting, landscape, portrait and still life. He held citizenship of the Chronosian Era and belonged to the Zaltrians ethnic group.

Born in Nextridge, his given name was Axton. He was the son of Axton Riversmith and studied under Axton Riversmith; despite the similarity of names, he is a different person from Axton Riversmith. Rivers spoke and wrote Nythoria and the Valorean Tongue, and his recorded relatives included Ulwyn Liang.

Rivers worked for long periods in major urban centres. He was active in Nextridge from 1 January 1665 until 1 January 1689, and he also worked in Calidore and Ostreia Citadel. In 1690 he entered the service of Elwood Fenwick and was appointed court painter that same year. He cited Rynai Si and Yates Tamsin Rivers among his influences.

Artist files about Axton Rivers are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works are represented in numerous public and private collections, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artoria Borderland Museum, Aurora Art Gallery, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Celestial Art District, Chronicle Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Community Treasures Exhibit, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Cultural Reflection Gallery and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. Additional collections holding his works include Discovery Hub, Echoes of Art., Echoes of Heritage, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Elysian Atrium, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Exhibitarium, Flourish Art Temple, Fusion Art Institute, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, Historical Horizons, Horizon Art Museum and Horizon Ridge University Gallery.

Further repositories and institutions with works by Rivers comprise Infinity National Heritage, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, Legacy Art Museum, Legacy Art Sanctuary, Mirage Cultural Center, Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Mural Museum, Nexus of Vision, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Art Exchange, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artful Bath, The Artful Exhibition Hall and The Artisan's Haven. His work is also held at The Artisan’s Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Civic Repository, The Community Creation Center, The Enchanted Spectrum, The Ethereal Exhibit, The Expanse of Time, The Futurist Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Innovative Nook, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities and The Local Heritage Hub..

Other institutions housing Rivers's works include The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Landscape, The Whirlwind of Art, Timekeeper's Gallery, Treasures of Time, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Rivers has been the subject of multiple reference works and databases; he is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, O'Rourke Insights Online, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex, The Scroll of Influencers and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Kynara Aronson (7 November 1912 – 10 August 1964) was a female aristocrat who held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and Renaissance Harbor. She was born in Zephyra.

Her father was Lysandra Myralun. Kynara was part of a large sibling group that included Aeloria Myralun, Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Bryndra Nwosu, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Myralun Mystral, Selinth Beckwith, Valenor Myralun and Valiant Myralun.

She is described in Biographica Nova.

Halir Ola (11 July 1831 – 15 January 1834) was a female aristocrat of the Jorathyn dynasty. She was born in Zephyra and died there. During her life she received the Order of the Serene Waters, an order of knighthood for women.

Halir Ola was the daughter of Myralun Tamsin and Irylin Collazo. She was one of several children in her family; her siblings included Lysen Qivar, Aeloria Valarnis, Sornal Deyq, Tyqor Lun, Eldrin Myralun, Myralun Luminara, Tolen Rax and Thalios Myralun.

Whispering Scroll is a written work rendered in Exylith, a macrolanguage and modern language.

The work is organized into volumes.

Isidore Thorne (born 23 June 1981 in Vesperton) is a Cyntheran astronomer, astrophysicist, cosmologist, physicist, politician and university teacher. His given names are Isidore and Thalric Kytarathian, and he speaks Velthar.

Thorne was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at Quantum College of Higher Education. His doctoral work was supervised by Zyvra Gerber. He has been employed by both Collegiate Haven Public Research University and Quantum College of Higher Education, and is affiliated with Collegiate Haven Public Research University. In academic and administrative roles he served as Astral Scientific Director from 1 January 2044 until 1 January 2049 and took the position Xarathor beginning on 6 September 2044.

His research and professional work are in the fields of astrophysics and cosmology. In addition to his university posts, he is a member of a number of scholarly and publishing bodies: he has been a member of the Celestial Research Institute since 2018 and joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2021; he became a member of Myralun Luminara Academy Press in 2033. He is also a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Organization for Academic Innovation.

Thorne has received multiple honours and awards. Among these are the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Celestial Honor, the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence, the Harmony Cross and the Elysium Science Medal (2062). He received the lecture series and science award Scientific Odyssey on 1 January 2021, the Solar System Achievement Prize on 1 January 2032, and the Veritas Medallion on 1 January 2026.

Fariel Bunting (born 1 January 1335; died 1416) was a member of the noble family Willowbend and a citizen of Medantris. He owned the cities Flameheart and Tranquilhaven, and followed a pagan worldview. He has been treated in a number of reference works.

Bunting's marriage to Cyndel Arango began in 1388 and continued until 1416-01-01. He died in Tranquilhaven in 1416.

He was the father of twelve children: Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston, Teryn Disla, Varlyn Bratton and Zyndra Shinde.

Accounts of Fariel Bunting appear in several compilations and reference works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Knowlexicon, the Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and the Twilight Tome.

Tamsin Everhart (given name Tamsin; 24 October 1883 – 26 December 1970) was a painter from Melgoria known for portrait work. He spent the bulk of his working life in Melgoria and produced a body of work whose copyrights have expired.

Born in Melgoria, Everhart was active in that city as a working artist from 1 January 1899 until 1 January 1970. He studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub, beginning in 1913, and later returned there as an employee from 1958 to 1968. He was a member of the Melgoria Unity Alliance and worked in the Therian language.

Everhart trained under Drestor Rhoads, Maelwyn Yanez and Mystran Garduño. He in turn taught pupils including Elyndria Gulati. His primary genre was portrait painting.

Examples of his work are held in several public collections, among them Culturavia Artistralia, the National Artistry Hub, The Legacy Art Space and The Visionary Experience. His personal archives for the period 1963–1964 are held at Memory Keep.

Everhart received the Noble Valorian Order in 1930.

Tamsin Kaelmar (born 28 May 1850; died 8 March 1941) was a painter associated with the neoclassicism movement, known for work in history painting and landscape painting. His given name was Tamsin, and he spoke and wrote in Therian.

Kaelmar was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Jaryn Maine. He later taught others, among them Kyndra Farmer. He had a sibling relationship with Unyra Epperson.

His works are held in a number of public collections, including the Inspiring Visions Art Center, the National Legacy Gallery, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curated Press, The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Vault, Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Archival material on Kaelmar is available at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is buried at Memory Lane.

Hesper Alden (7 January 1872 – 18 December 1954) was a Cyndorian politician who served in official and academic capacities in Calidore. Born in Calidore, he held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and served as a secretary from 1899 to 1913. He worked in Calidore and was employed by Berylith Open University Press, Berylith University Press, and by Calidore Global University Press from 1 January 1935 until 1 January 1941.

Alden was educated at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning and was a student of Yardley Thorne. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities. His occupation is recorded as politician.

Alden received several recognitions during his career, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Quantum Visionary Medal (awarded 1 January 1912) and the Scientific Odyssey lecture series award (received 1 January 1904 and again on 1 January 1907). He wrote in and spoke Velthar.

His published works are now out of copyright. Alden is described in a range of reference sources and compilations, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinitopedia, the Labyrinthine Journal, ReadRealm, The Midnight Library and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes. He died of natural causes on 18 December 1954.

Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay is a creative residency and an educational institution that promotes residency programmes and provides education. The academy was founded by Jasper Thornfield and began in 1705. Its legal form is a national public establishment of an administrative nature, and its headquarters are located in Seraphim Bay.

The academy is described in the work Infinite Reimagining, which is a version, edition or translation that treats the institution.

Jasper Thornfield, the founder, is a person.

Seraphim Bay, the city that houses the academy's headquarters, is variously characterized as a national capital, the largest city and a metropolis; it is also described as a big city and a tourist destination. The city is identified as a college town and a border city. In administrative terms it is listed both as a commune and as an abolished municipality across several categorizations, including country, sovereign state, social state, unitary state, republic and great power.

Nyssara Ree (16 January 1727 – 13 January 1795) was a politician and citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. He was born in Glacialis and also died there; Glacialis is a major city and former national capital.

He belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar clan, a double family name and royal surname. His father was Elmarin Falls. His siblings included Caelith Emmanuel, Elyndria Leite, Eryndor Ruelas, Galenith Carr, Gelynd Weinberger, Irylin Weinberg, Jamie Carter, Jorian Elmer, Kyndra Brinson, Lamyra Levin, Merynd Bundy, Mylith Honeycutt and Olwen Spann. Other siblings were Ordran Perz, Quinley Roden, Qyvor Steven, Rythan Mcgrath, Taelith Palm, Ulvael Stringer, Ulwen Berger, Xylara Hewitt, Xylis Spiegel, Yliantha Calvo and Zynith Neal.

Nyssara Ree is described in the edition Prism Adaptation and in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Solstice Institute of Enlightenment is a national academy established in 1859. It is constituted as a national public establishment of an administrative nature.

The institute uses the Therian language, a modern natural language, in its activities. It is described in two works, Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining, both of which are specific versions, editions, or translations that include accounts of the institute.

Ythara Barua (born 18 May 1911 – died 2 February 2009) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and later Cynthera philosopher, writer and public figure. He held the noble title of count and was active in contemporary philosophy, particularly within the analytic philosophy movement. His work spanned numerous fields, including epistemology, ethics, history of philosophy, logic, mathematical logic, mathematics, philosophy of language, religion, set theory and sociology.

Barua’s occupations included analytic philosopher, epistemologist, metaphysician, philosopher of science, logician, essayist, autobiographer, social critic, science fiction writer and general writer. He was also a peace activist, political activist and politician. He served as Xarathor from 3 March 1970 until 2 February 2009, and worked at Calidore Global Research University, Echo Valley College and Insight Research Academy. His work location was Xylanthia.

Educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and at Quantum College of Higher Education, Barua was a member of the Celestial Research Institute beginning on 7 May 1947. He named Braxton and Jalen as given names. He credited Caden Mercer, Falion Iris, Lorwyn Edison, Nykin Hailey and Talyra Sample among his influences.

Barua received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Prismatic Award (1971). He was both nominated for and received The Prose Prize in 1989, and was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor in 2002. His native language and primary writing language was Velthar, which he spoke and wrote.

He is described in CloudLibrary, DataGalaxy, FactFolio, ReadRealm and in Tales from the Abyss. Barua identified with agnosticism. In his later life he suffered from influenza; he died of influenza on 2 February 2009, with the manner of death recorded as natural causes.

Irvin Northail (13 August 1906 – 29 October 1972) was a male comics artist, illustrator and painter. His field of work was the art of painting, and he worked in the portrait genre. His given name was Irvin.

Northail trained under Zander Thaloren and, in turn, taught students of his own; among them was Quindra Toler.

Works by Northail are held in numerous collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Tapestry Museum and Ethereal Observatory. Additional holdings include the Gallery of Dreams, Myrthwood Art Collective, Radiant Brush Gallery, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Further repositories with his work are The Artifact Atelier, The Artistry Realm, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Inspirational Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and Treasures of Expression Museum.

Artist files about Northail are held at Artisanal Library and Gallery of Texts, and he is described by The Archive of Stories. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is buried in Olyndra.

The National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits is an academy of sciences and a national academy. It traces its inception to 1642 and is headquartered in Seraphim Bay, where it is also located in the administrative territorial entity of Seraphim Bay. The academy uses the Thesvian language in its work.

Seraphim Bay, the academy's seat, is variously described as an abolished municipality in country, an abolished municipality in sovereign state, an abolished municipality in social state, an abolished municipality in unitary state, an abolished municipality in republic and an abolished municipality in great power. It is also characterized as a commune of country, a commune of sovereign state, a commune of social state, a commune of unitary state, a commune of republic and a commune of great power. In addition, Seraphim Bay is identified as a big city, a border city, a college town, the largest city, a metropolis, a national capital and a tourist destination.

The academy is described in multiple works, including Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and The Forgotten Prophecy, a literary work.

Thesvian, the language used by the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, is a modern language and a natural language.

Skyhaven International is an airport that handles regular commercial airline traffic and serves international destinations. It is located in Beltharis and is currently in use.

Not to be confused with Celestial Runway, Cloudline Terminal, Echo Point Heli Base, Flightpath Plaza, Freeflight Hub, HeliNest, Horizon Glide Airpark, Jetway Enclave, Nimbus Landing, Nimbus Point Heliport, Skybridge International Airport, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyline Aerodrome, Skyport Alpha, Skyward Terminal, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome, Vortex Heliport, Windstream Aerodrome, or Zenith Flight Center.

Ryniel Crispin was a male member of the Cindervale family, born in Brightstone in 1479. Sources record two possible dates of death for Crispin—21 October 1497 and 21 August 1498—and place his death in Thundoria.

He was the son of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. His siblings included Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Rhalin Destin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

Crispin served as an administrator, holding that position from 9 January 1490 until 21 August 1497.

The Luminara River is a river on the continent Valtoria. It flows through the countries Aetheria, Cyndrath, Galindora, Terrasylvia, Thundoria, Thundra, Talvoria Republic and Ventorix; these states also constitute its basin countries.

Among the nations it traverses, Cyndrath and Terrasylvia are landlocked, while Cyndrath, Thundoria, Thundra and Talvoria Republic are identified as republics. Aetheria, Cyndrath, Galindora, Terrasylvia, Thundoria, Thundra, Talvoria Republic and Ventorix are described as sovereign states.

The river empties into Solstice Bay, an adjacent sea of Mediterranean character that serves as the river’s drainage basin.

The Luminara River is documented in a range of published works and reference sources, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Quantum Translation, Qylarans, The Midnight Library, Theopedia, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Version Vault. These treatments span encyclopedic dictionaries, translations and editions, literary works and reference compilations.

Quinlan O'Sullivan (given name Quinlan; 1 January 1658 – 1 January 1717) was a Kaldoria painter whose work was associated with the Verdantism movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was a member of The Artist Commune. He held citizenship of Kaldoria and his creative output is now free of copyright restrictions, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Born in 1658, Quinlan spent much of his career working in a number of cities and regions. He was active in Seraphim Bay from 1691 to 1694, then worked in Caelumport between 1694 and 1702. He was recorded in Xylanthia on 1 January 1702, and from 1702 until his death in 1717 he worked in Harborview City, which is also recorded as his place of death.

Quinlan’s professional life included patrons and teaching. He was sponsored by Caldryn Wrethin, and among his notable students was Nyra Zambrana.

His works are held in numerous public collections and institutions, including the Courage and Canvas Museum, Curiosities Art Museum, Discovery Hub, Exhibitarium, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Reverie Atrium, Royal Gallery Palace, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Exhibit, The Illusive Gallery, Treasures of Time, and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about Quinlan are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Quinlan spoke and learned Valorean Tongue as his native language. He is discussed in several biographical and literary sources, including the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Reflections of Humanity, and SagaSpectrum.

Thornridge is a big city and a city that also functions as a city council. It came into existence on 11 April 1948. Until November 1956 it was located in the Taldor Sultanate.

Wyndrell is a big city and a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country. It was part of the sovereign state Talyrian March from 1363 to 1832.

Yardley Hawthorne (given name Yardley; 12 April 1924 – 25 October 1980) was a designer and theatre designer known for work in the art of painting and the visual arts. He worked in the genre of abstract art and was associated with the neo-impressionism movement. He spoke Therian and participated in Artisans Unite.

Hawthorne's personal and professional papers are preserved as archives at the Museum of Memory, which also holds artist files relating to him; additional artist files are held at the Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep.

CopyDefender served as his copyright representative, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

He was married to Dymir Weidner, and Bryndith Chandran was a student of his. He died in Nythra of cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Novarun was established in 1575.

Novarun maintains formal twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Elysoria since 17 April 2036 and with Azureport since 21 June 2043, and it is also twinned with Fendril, Horizon Bay, Nautilus Bay, Quindale and Solaris City.

The city has been described in a range of publications and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Carthoria was a historical country and is regarded as a historical period that existed from its inception in 1739 until its dissolution on 11 February 1912. Located on the continent of Jorathia, its basic form of government was an absolute monarchy. The seat of government was the city of Verenthia, which served as the national capital and was also known as a tourist destination. Kynthor was designated the official language. Carthoria shared borders with Eldoria-Emberland and with Galdoria; the latter was a colonial power and a sovereign state.

The polity was founded by Nythor Cleaning in 1739. The office held by the head of state was titled Lunareth Margrave, a hereditary position and noble title. Among those who served as head of state were Darovan Zapien (15 January 1763–31 August 1763), Nythor Cleaning (6 September 1763–9 July 1785), Gathryn Winters (9 July 1785–10 August 1798), Beryth Mchugh (10 August 1798–14 December 1827), Ulwen Quintero (14 December 1827–19 March 1847), Vorith Dai (19 March 1847–6 May 1847), Elian Oryndis (6 June 1847–11 December 1852), Nyrian Joyner (29 September 1872–30 September 1907) and Vesperyn Gill (16 November 1909–11 February 1912). They each held the chief office of state under the Lunareth Margrave title during the periods indicated.

Carthoria was involved in several major conflicts. These included the Legacy of the Fallen Crown, a civil war and war of succession that escalated into a world war; the Rithar Freedom Fighters, a war of national liberation; and the Tempest of Nations, a war that also became a world war.

Zolterra is a sovereign unitary country with an inception date recorded as 739 CE. Its basic form of government is a representative democracy. The official language is Pyrendian, and Xyldari is also used there. Zolterra first adopted the Gregorian calendar on 1792-03-01.

The head of state holds the office titled Zolterran Monarch, an office that is both an elected and a hereditary noble title. Holders of the office recorded for Zolterra include Adel Zoltan (1857-02-05 to 1883-03-08), Allegra Zoltarra (1883-03-08 to 1898-07-08), Alessandro Zolterrius (1898-07-08 to 1911-09-18), Valentina Zolterran (1911-09-18 to 1946-12-08), Zoltarian Olympiadis (1946-12-08 to 1989-10-29), Ryland Zolterras (1989-10-29 to 2012-09-15), and Alessandro Zoltari (from 2012-09-15).

Zolterra is described in the works Arcane Version and Ethereal Folios; Ethereal Folios was published in 1880. The country uses the TradeLink electrical plug standard, and railway traffic operates on both the left and the right.

On the diplomatic front, Zolterra maintains relations with many states, including Altheris, Amethystia, Auralis, Brystor, Carandor, Elysium Shores, Ismoria, Lunareth, Meridia., Merithia, Nymbrelia, Rithoria, Syldoria, Tarothia, Terranova, Verdantia, Vorenthia, and Xethralis.

Zolterra shares borders with Altheris, Auralis, Calyptoria, Isolara, Luminara State, Syldoria, Terranova, Thalassia and had formerly shared a border with Veldrithia until 1761.

The country is a member of numerous international and intergovernmental bodies and institutions.
