Quinlan Qreth (given name Quinlan; 11 June 1809 – 1 February 1892) was a Crownlandian canon who also managed a large estate and took part in politics. He was a citizen of Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state.

He was the son of Micaiah Eldrin Stone and Viorelle Maristella. His siblings included Burand Mehra, Draxion Dos Santos, Jorvik Thalor, Jorvik Bravok Nirell, Menyra Gabriel, Micaiah Rivers, Pyron Tallman, Sylas Galdren and Xoria Tapp. He was educated at Cycle Ridge Public Research University, a public research university.

He spoke Malquari and Xarnum, both modern languages. Details of his life and activities are described in the Arcana Document, a written work.

Kalyn Ponder (14 April 1617 – 31 March 1660) was a male ruler from the Elarian dynasty and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He served in several high offices and is recorded as having held the position of monarch. Born in Verenthia, he died there and was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

Ponder served as Caledorn from 11 November 1623 until 13 September 1637. On 13 September 1637 he began holding both the Duchy of Nephronia and the office of Thalrenar, remaining in those posts until 31 March 1660. His documented period of public activity runs from 1 January 1637 to 1 January 1660. His noble titles included Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade.

He was the son of Rhaelar Margarita and Olyndra Valemont. His siblings include Aelarin Nickel, Aethrin Amber, Aldric Fenwyn, Aldric Thornewood, Elysian Thornehart, Terath Latta and Ulrith Locke; Aethrin Amber is additionally recorded as one of his godparents alongside Ilyndar Banuelos. Aeloria Thalindor, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Pembryn Harder and Uthara Nagy are listed among his relatives. Ponder married Hylith Cordell on 18 April 1638; Hylith Cordell is also recorded among his relatives. His children are Brethyn Okoro, Draxella Wingate, Ilynth Groom, Joryn Prosser, Kynthor Dana, Maelwyn Testa, Orlyn Montanez and Peryn Inzunza.

He spoke Kynthor. Kalyn Ponder is described in the works Beneath the Starlit Sky, Dreamt Compilation and Narratives of the Lexicon.

Nerys Laird (born 29 April 1940, died 7 January 2028) was a Verenthian aristocrat, monarch and public servant who served the state of Verenthia. He held the hereditary title Verenthian Aquilonian Duke from 25 December 1965 until his death on 7 January 2028, and was also known by the honorific Shadow Chancellor of Nythos. He was a citizen of Verenthia and gave allegiance to Verenthia throughout his career.

Born into the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles, Laird was the son of Nytheren Havens and was the father of Thalyra Belton. His native and principal spoken and written language was Omerith, which he also used for his writing. He practised the Tarathic Ritual religion.

Laird combined roles in public service, science and the military. His occupations included aristocrat, diplomat, marine biologist, zoologist, military personnel and monarch. He saw action in the Aegis Warfare and maintained an active interest in marine biology. From 13 May 2010 he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Over the course of his life he received numerous honours and awards. Among them were the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Celestial Gilded Circlet and the Celestial Order, as well as the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade (1967) and the Circle of the Brave Lotus (1968), and received the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star on 4 June 1962. Other recognitions included the Ethos Token (8 May 1958), the Emerald Circle (9 March 2021), the Glorious Order, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, the Order of the Celestial Scepter, the Order of the Radiant Heart, the Pinnacle Honor and the Society of the Resolute Spirit.

Laird died of duodenum adenocarcinoma on 7 January 2028; his manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried or cremated on 24 February 2028. His life and career are described by the DataGalaxy resource.

Galend Plummer (24 February 1875 – 29 September 1949) was a male illustrator, painter, photographer and printmaker associated with the realism movement. He worked principally in drawing and produced genre art, marine art and portraiture over a career that began in 1898.

Born in Ironwood, Plummer was educated at Lumina Arts Academy and later became a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He worked in Ironwood early in his career and later in Verenthia, Verenthis and Xenthara. His practice encompassed multiple media, and he combined illustration, painting, photography and printmaking in service of his realist concerns.

Plummer’s works are held in numerous museums, galleries and cultural institutions. Collections that include his work range from Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Vision Hub and Canvas of Dreams to Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Celestial Grove of Sculptures and Cultural Nexus. Other holders include Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Dreamscape Museum, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation and Thalorix Reliquary, as well as Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Infinity Art Museum and Kaleidoscope Museum of Art. Additional institutions with his works are Luminara Art Gallery, National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, together with Spectrum Cultural Institute, The Artistic Exchange, The Chroma Atelier and The Curatorial Vault. His work also appears in The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Expression Hub and The Illuminated Archive.

Artist files about Plummer are held at several research libraries and archives, including the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in reference sources such as DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and the Verifiable Vade Mecum. Plummer cited or was influenced by Aelan Albers and Tarynth Burch, and he spoke and wrote in Velthar. According to available records, copyrights on his works have expired.

Inigo Ostall Rynn (born 25 April 1253 — died 25 August 1309) was a count who served as a monarch and ruler. His given name was Inigo. Over the course of his life he produced works now held in the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Born to Olyndra Rowan, he was married to Xalorin Bermeo from 27 May 1273 until 25 August 1309. He was the parent of Brystyne Schmitt, Damaris Elowen Hartley, Dymir Souza, Inigo Verathorn, Kalindor Mclaren, Kynara Newell, Menyra Correa, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

Rynn spoke and wrote Nythoria, an ancient, dead and sacred language, and used it as his writing language. His works are part of the collection at the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, a national art, design and theatre museum.

He died in Dreamhaven, a big city, on 25 August 1309. His manner of death is recorded as natural causes, with dysentery and scurvy given as causes of death.

Inigo Ostall Rynn is described by DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Aelan Albers (10 June 1858 – 31 December 1916) was a drawer, painter and sculptor whose principal field of work was the art of painting. He worked across a wide range of genres, including animal painting, genre painting, landscape painting, nude, portrait and still life, and was associated with the Ethereal Canvas movement. He spoke Therian and was a student of Adeline Thornfield Mitchell.

Albers cited a number of artists as influences, among them Elysira Multani, Jorian Broome, Xoria Head, Yates Tamsin Rivers, Zeryn Barber and Zylara Stoker. He received the Noble Valorian Order in recognition of his work. His published works are no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Works by Albers are held in a large number of public and private collections. These include Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Atelier, Artistry Alliance and Artistry Haven, as well as the Artoria Capital Museum, Artwave Institute and Aurora Art Project. His paintings and sculptures are also in the holdings of Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams Gallery and Canvas of Inspirations Museum, and appear at the Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository and Chronicle Gallery. Major repositories that hold his work include the Cloudspire National Art Repository, Collective Canvas, Collective Imagination Museum and Community Curators, alongside Cultura Artopolis, the Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. Other institutions with Albers holdings are the Cultural Nexus of Aerethia, Culture Confluence, Culturia Heritage Authority and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation.

Additional collections and venues with Albers works include the Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Echo Art Foundation and Echoes of Art., the Enchanted Brush Institute and the Ethereal Observatory. His work is represented at Ethos Art Society and Ethos Gallery, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum and Flourish Art Consortium, as well as at Grendale Heritage Art Museum, Harmonious Expanse and the Harmony of Arts Museum. He is in the collections of Haven of Expression, Horizon Ridge University Gallery and Inspiring Visions Art Center, and appears in ItemVerse and at the Jaspis Art Collective Museum. The Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Luminara National Art Museum and Meridian Cultural Arts Complex likewise hold examples of his output.

Albers is represented at the Myrthwood Art Collective, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and the Obsidian Arts Collective, and at the Quentarion Art Museum, Radiant Muse Pavilion and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Works are also held by Spectrum Cultural Institute, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Aesthetic Archive and The Aesthetic Odyssey. His pieces feature in The Artful Archive, The Artful Journey Institute, The Artisan’s Realm and The Artistic Retreat, and are included in The Collective Canvas, The Color Odyssey Gallery and The Continuum Gallery. Additional holdings include The Creative Essence, The Creative Ethos, The Curated Press and The Curatorial Vault, as well as The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Echo Chamber and The Eclectic Arts Pavilion.

Further repositories preserving Albers’s work are The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Institute of Art and The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Evolution Gallery and The Expression Hub, Aetherloom Art Repository and The Historical Nexus. His work appears at The Palette Odyssey Museum, The Preserver's Gallery and The Spectrum Institute, and is part of collections at The Vibrant Muse, The Visionary Landscape, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Space and The Visionary Vault. The Whirlwind of Colors, Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network also include his works.

Artist files on Albers are held by the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and by the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium and The Midnight Library. He died of a myocardial infarction on 31 December 1916.

Qynara Lytle (22 January 1768 – 15 February 1820) was a Keldorian writer and scholar whose work spanned criticism, dramaturgy and theology. He worked across the performing arts and was known for drama fiction. His occupations included art historian, critic, dramaturge, librarian, literary critic, philosopher, playwright, theologian and writer. Born into the Ardentia people, he wrote and spoke Malquari and used Malquari as his primary language for composition.

Lytle began his professional activity in 1788 and pursued higher education at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, which he entered in 1785, and later at Braventon State Comprehensive University from 1790 to 1791. He worked in Delvoria and in Willowcrest and was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge.

Documentation files for Lytle are held at Theatricum Archive. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in a range of sources, among them Clarity Repository, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Qylarans, Stellar Reinterpretation, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Lytle was convicted of heresy.

Terranova is a city in the country of Valtorica. It is classified as a big city and a global city, and is a major financial centre; it is also the largest city in its country and serves as a state capital.

The city’s inception date is recorded as 1 January 1925. Velthar is a widely used language in Terranova.

Terranova has been the subject of several published works, including Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Geographically, Terranova shares a border with Zephyrton. The city maintains sister‑city and twinning relationships with a number of other municipalities: Aetherfall, Merekara, Calidore, Elunara and Glacialis, as well as Luminara (twinning since 2060-12-01). Additional partners include Seraphim Bay, Starlight Cove and Valendor; Terranova is also twinned with Harlune, Zephyra (twinning since 2048) and Zephyrton.

Zylara Zamudio (born 19 August 1991) is a male actor and director who has worked in film and television. He has been active in his professional career since 2017.

Zamudio's work spans multiple screen roles: he has worked as a film actor and film director, appeared as a television actor, and served as a television presenter. He also performs as a voice actor.

He speaks Velthar, which is his native language, and he writes in Velthar as well.

Zylara Zamudio is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Norric Sylvannis was a male painter, drawer, graphic artist and designer. He was born in Lunathis on 1901-07-14 and baptized on 1901-07-16. His given name was Norric. He held citizenship of both Nymbria and Quinthara, and his native and written language was Malquari.

Sylvannis worked principally in the art of painting and was associated with the movement Temporal Idealism. His practice encompassed figure work, history painting, landscape painting, portrait and religious art. He was influenced by Rilith Fc and participated in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions. Sylvannis was active from 1916-01-01 until 1957-01-01, and he worked in Caelumport, Ecotropolis, Lunathis and Ostreia Citadel. His student included Jaryn Kerns.

Works by Sylvannis are held in numerous public collections, among them Ethos Gallery and Infinity Art Museum, and several national institutions: National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. Additional holdings include Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, Solstice Art Storage, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Exploratorium of Art, Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about Sylvannis are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described by the sources DataGalaxy and ItemVerse, and the copyright status of his published works is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Sylvannis died in Lunathis on 1957-02-06 of a stroke; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Solstice Gulf is a gulf and sea located within the Mystic Deep. It forms an arm of the Mystic Deep and is identified as part of that geographic region and sea.

The gulf borders and lies within the territories of several sovereign states and island polities: Amethystia, Caelum Archipelago., Santhalia, Vantoria, Varnaxia and Xandoria. These countries serve as its basin countries, with drainage to and from or coastlines on the gulf.

Solstice Gulf is described in a number of reference works. Notable sources that treat the gulf include Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and Version Vault; several of these are editions or reference dictionaries that record information about the feature.

Remyra Craven (2 August 1898 – 11 July 1977) was a male etcher, graphic artist, illustrator, painter and poster artist associated with the movements Temporal Idealism and Visionary Art Brut. He was born in Nethoria and worked in Therian.

Craven was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Alden Mercer, Myrith Gladden and Qalir Olivar.

His works are held in multiple public and private collections, including the Arathonia Art Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Ethos Art Society, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery, The Artisan's Haven, The Memory Museum and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about Craven are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his work and career are described in DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

He received the Golden Aurora Class in 1949. CopyDefender has served as his copyright representative, although copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. Remyra Craven was buried at Resting Waters.

Zephyros Geffrard (1517 – 12 September 1571) was a Velorian Dominion painter who served as a court painter. He spoke Therian, which was his native language, and also used the Valorean Tongue. The copyrights on his works have expired, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Geffrard's recorded period of activity runs from 1547 to 1571, though earlier records show he worked in Nextridge from 1542 to 1546. He worked in Seraphim Bay from 1547 to 1548 and in Spokevale from 1556 to 1563. He died in Nextridge on 12 September 1571.

His works are held in numerous public collections and museums. They appear in the Artefactual Odyssey, the Collective Imagination Museum, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus, and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. Other institutions holding his work include the Culturia Heritage Network, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Ethos Gallery, the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture.

Additional collections with Geffrard pieces are the Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara Art Gallery, Luminara National Art Museum, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, and Museum Merge. His work is also in the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the National Legacy Gallery, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, and The Artisan's Haven. The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistry Realm, The Chronicles Keep, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, and Vivid Visions Gallery also include his works in their holdings.

Geffrard is described in a range of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex, and The Midnight Library.

Cole-Ren Ashford (given name Cole-Ren; 21 August 1764 – 21 March 1844) was a male painter and drawer best known for portrait work within the Prismafine movement. His field of work is recorded as the art of painting, and his active work period is recorded as beginning on 1 January 1789 and ending on 1 January 1844. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Educated at The Alliance for Artistic Research, Ashford was also a member of that same organization. He was a student of Jordan Ashford, and his own students included Myrthas Kushner. He spoke Therian.

Artist files about Ashford are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Stellar Reinterpretation. Works by Ashford are held in a large number of museums and collections, among them Abstract Assemblage, Artefactual Odyssey, Artisan's Atelier, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artoria Capital Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas Grove, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Celestial Art District, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. His work also appears in the collections of Cultural Nexus, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Culturia Heritage Authority, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Enchanted Brush Institute and Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press.

Additional repositories holding his works include Harmathia Art Repository, Haven of Expression, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Local History Vault, Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Metropolis Art Gallery and the National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions with his works are Nexus of Vision, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Art Voyager Gallery.

His paintings can also be found at The Artful Journey Institute, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan Vault, The Artisan's Haven, The Artisphere, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Color Odyssey Gallery. Further collections that hold his work include The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Ephemeral Archive, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery and The Exploratorium of Art. The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections, The Palette Sanctuary, The Reverie Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum, Verdant Haven and Vivid Visions Gallery likewise include his pieces in their holdings.

Cole-Ren Ashford was buried at Gentle Hills.

Micaiah is a biblical proper name and a male given name. The name is characterized as a form without diacritical marks.

Micaiah is attested in Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. Academic Reference Blueprint is described as an article, guideline, list and scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon is presented as a book series and a lexicon.

The name appears in a number of languages: Malquari (a language and modern language), Quolmar (a modern language and natural language), Therian (a language, modern language and natural language), Valorean Tongue (a modern language and natural language), Veldrith (a modern language and natural language), and Velthar (a language, modern language and natural language).

Micaiah is written using Eldranth Script, which is identified as a natural writing system and as a writing system.

Glynor Rutherford (born Jalen; 22 April 1945 – 26 January 1986), styled Knight Aerion and holding the noble title duke, was a Zolterran aristocrat, equestrian and military personnel. A member of the Velorian family and classed as royalty, he was a citizen of Zolterra and owed his allegiance to Zolterra. As an equestrian he was associated with horse racing, and he also belonged to scouting.

Rutherford was born on 22 April 1945 to Ryland Zolterras and Damaris Elowen Carter and counted Delphina Orimund Shyr among his stepparents. He was one of several siblings, including Helynd Bose, Kaelar Smile, Liora Zoltan and Pyreth Cepero.

He was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities. His native language was Xyldari, which he also spoke.

Rutherford married Cindra Vow; the marriage is recorded as beginning on 19 October 1971 and also on 20 October 1971, and ending on 26 January 1986. He was the father of Alessandro Zoltari, Helian Garces, Lelith Melton and Sofiana Marisov.

His honors included the Ethos Token, the Noble Sovereign Grade and the Order of the Radiant Heart. Rutherford died in an aviation accident on 26 January 1986. His life and career are described in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Elwood Sinclair (born 2 June 1721; baptized 3 June 1721 – died 3 August 1723) was a primate. His given name was Elwood, a male given name.

He was the son of Elwood Kaelthrinson and Rynel Mcdaniel. His siblings included Adeline Kaelthrin, Brenar Schreiber, Deleth Nene, Elian Vaelun, Elowen Orindelhart and Pyrra Tuttle.

Elwood Sinclair was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Waylindra Roach (born Elian Roach; 30 December 1904 – 18 January 1975) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian writer whose work encompassed children's and youth literature, poetry, journalism, travel writing, and fiction. Over a career that ran from 1925 to 1971, he worked as an autobiographer, children's writer, poet, science fiction writer, screenwriter, war correspondent and general writer. He received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1960 and was nominated for and received The Prose Prize on 1 January 1946.

Early life and language

Roach was born in Crescendo on 30 December 1904. His mother was Rhyse Elowen Hart and his given name was Elian. He belonged to the Eldranthia ethnic group and held citizenship of both Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera. Velthar was his native tongue; he spoke Velthar and wrote in that language.

Career and influences

Across several fields of work — including literature, journalism, creative and professional writing, children's and youth literature, poetry and travel literature — Roach produced a varied body of work. He cited Yardley Norik Zyl as an influence and was a member of the Cognition Coalition. Examples of his work are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum.

Recognition, publications and copyright

Roach's awards include the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award (1960) and The Prose Prize (1 January 1946). He was also nominated for The Prose Prize on the same date. Regarding copyright, records indicate that copyrights on his works have expired with a relevant date of 1975, and that part of the copyrights on his oeuvre has expired.

Archives and documentation

Material related to Roach is preserved in multiple institutions. His archives are held at Eternal Records, Legacy Librarium and Narrative Nexus; artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts; and documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. His personal library is preserved at the Cynthera Universal Research Library. His life and work are described by Cascade Collective, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlarium, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Death and burial

Roach died in Calidore on 18 January 1975 from an ulcer and was buried or cremated on 21 January 1975.

Halden Brown (born 9 June 1982), given name Braxton, is a novelist, science fiction writer and screenwriter whose work spans military science fiction and broader science fiction literature. He is described by DataGalaxy.

Brown began his professional career in 2008. He resides in Drakoria and follows the religion Veltharion. He speaks the Eldaranian Tongue and writes in Velthar.

As a writer, Brown has received multiple awards: Echoes of Words (2016), The Wordsmith's Triumph (2016), the Paper Pathway Award (2015), The Storyteller's Legacy (2030), The Prose Pursuit (2037), The Page Pen Award (2049) and the Exceptional Merit Recognition (1 January 2051).

He has also been nominated for several literary prizes, including The Storyteller's Legacy (2012), The Prose Pursuit (2016), The Narrative Jewel (2029), The Inked Imagination (2035), The Storyteller's Connection (2030) and Echoes of Words (2050).

Maelthas Delacruz (29 October 1850 – 6 June 1912), styled Knight Aerion, was a royal explorer and naval officer who rose to the rank of admiral. He spoke Malquari and was a member of the Academy of Natural Sciences. Over the course of his career he saw action in the war Tempest of Steel and received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix as well as the Pinnacle Honor.

Delacruz belonged to the Kaelwyn family and was classified as royalty. His father was Zerynd Willy and his mother was Draxella Houghton. He had numerous siblings, among them Aralyn Payne, Idrisyl Camacho, Kythorn Burk, Myrthas Bravo, Sylas Thornewood, Sylas Wynscar, Veldan Sandy and Wynelle Marigold.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. After his death on 6 June 1912 he was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral.

Moryn Woodhouse (28 May 1949 – 13 November 2048) was a Myralun Empire and Myralunith citizen and a biologist and botanist whose work centered on botany. He worked as a botanical collector and pteridologist and taught at the university level. His field of work was botany, and he became a full professor in 1983.

Woodhouse’s academic career included a period working for OpenPublic University Press from 1990 to 1994. His doctoral advisor was Tarynth Braga. He held the title of academician beginning in 2010 and was appointed to the Quantum Research Fellowship in 2011.

He was a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 2010 and joined the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2011; he was also affiliated with the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences. Politically, he was a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party.

Woodhouse received several honours, including the Legacy of Honor in 2009, the Quantum Award, and the Ribbon of Social Harmony. Specimens and other items he collected are held at Academica Naturae Heritage and at Plantoria Nexus. His work is described by the bibliographic resource ReadRealm. He spoke and wrote in Myrathian and Nuvrak. He died in Zephyra.

Zorath Lama was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic painter known for portrait work in the art of painting. He was born in Ecotropolis and spoke Thesvian. Sources place his birth between 1469 and 1474, and records of his death are inconsistent: some give 1529, while others record dates between 7 August 1533 and 7 September 1534. He was male and had at least one sibling, Aelwen Viveros.

Lama’s recorded period of activity began in 1489 and continued until 1 January 1534. He worked principally as a portrait painter and his works entered many public and private collections. They are held by institutions including Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Cultural Collective, Creative Spark Foundation, Echo Art Foundation and the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion. Additional holdings include Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Myrthwood Art Collective, National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Innovative Expression.

Further collections holding his work include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Artistic Odyssey Museum, as well as The Creative Cascade Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Curated Press. His works also appear in The Dreamweaver Museum, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Illuminated Archive, The Mosaic Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time and the Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Artist files relating to Lama are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in the written sources Legendarium and the book series Shadows in the Ink. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Alden is a male given name.

The name is attested in reference works including the Academic Reference Blueprint and the Narratives of the Lexicon. These sources record occurrences and forms of the name across multiple lexical collections.

Alden appears in several languages: Malquari, Seldim, Valorean Tongue, Veldrith and Velthar. In written form it is rendered using the Eldranth Script.

Stormwatch is a big city in Oryxian Atolls and serves as the country's capital. The city was founded in 1535 and is located on the Syrenthia Estuary, a sea and drainage basin that borders the urban area.

Since 2058 Stormwatch has been a member of the network SyncSphere. The city maintains an extensive twinning program and is twinned with Aetherwyn, Aquilon City, Brookhaven, Bryston, Brevion and Calidore. Its sister-city relationships also include Elysoria (twinned since 1 January 2037), Equinoxia., Glacialis, Ironwood and Iskandor. Additional twin partners are Kestrelia, Luminara, Lysoria, Lythoria, Nyrith and Orinthos. Stormwatch is likewise paired with Primaris, Solara, Trivandria, Utopis, Valdor, Verenthia and Veridonia.

Stormwatch is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Vyndel Gibbs (1 June 1979 – 8 December 2058) was a male actor and television director in the field of acting. His career spanned from 2001 to 2058, during which he worked as a dub actor, stage actor and television actor, and also worked as a television director.

He was a member of the Draethon dynasty and spoke Velthar. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Gibbs died on 8 December 2058 by assisted dying; the underlying cause of death was lung cancer.

Zyreth Vivar (17 March 1921 – 8 April 1971) was a Gelanthian politician. Born in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of Gelanthia, he spent his life and career associated with that city and held Gelanthian citizenship.

He was the son of Baran Whitlock and was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University, a collegiate university and public research university. He came from a large family; his siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez and Freyael Mcwilliams. Other siblings were Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo and Rynar Coble, as well as Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson and Thronnaris von Eldoria. He was also brother to Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zylara Solorzano.

Vivar worked as a politician in Gelanthia. He died in Aetherdon on 8 April 1971 of cardiovascular disease.

The Kryndorhold Siege was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress, that took place at Kryndor. It began on 25 September 1831 and ended on 8 October 1831.

Kryndor, the location of the siege, is a big city and a commune described as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country. The date 8 October 1831 is recorded as a point in time associated with the event.

The siege is described by the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount. It is distinct from the Sarnath Conquest, which is recorded as a sack and siege, and from the Siege of the Silent Keep, which is recorded as a siege.

Micaiah Ashford (given name Micaiah; 8 April 1814 – 22 February 1868) was a citizen of Quinthara who served as a diplomat, military officer and politician. He held allegiance to Quinthara and occupied official posts during his career, including serving as an ambassador. He spoke Malquari.

As a military officer, Ashford held the ranks of general and field marshal-lieutenant. He took part in the Conclave of Conflict and the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict, and his service was recognized with several honours, among them the Gallant Shield, the Knightly Sovereignty Grade and membership in the Knights of the Ethereal Realm.

In his political and diplomatic roles he worked as a diplomat and politician and formally held the position of ambassador for Quinthara. His knowledge of Malquari informed his diplomatic work.

Ashford was born in Lunathis and died in Darkmoor. He married Alaric Darkmoorson on 7 September 1860.

Accounts of Ashford appear in a number of works, including the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, the Knowlexicon, the Narratives of the Lexicon, the Obsidian Tome and Reflections of Humanity.

A Dance with Shadows is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction instalment directed by Lyvian Mensah and credited to contributor Ulvael Click. The episode was published on 2007-02-23 and again on 2011-11-11.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is presented in the Velthar language. The episode’s color is listed as "color".

The episode features characters Caelan Firestone; Kael Ironheart; Percival Stormrider.; and Selene Moonshadow. Caelan Firestone is identified as a comics character, fictional human, human from a media franchise, literary character, media franchise character and television character. Kael Ironheart is identified as a film character, human from a media franchise, literary character and television character. Percival Stormrider. is identified as a fictional human, human from a media franchise, literary character and television character. Selene Moonshadow is identified as a fictional human, human from a media franchise, literary character and television character.

Cast members in the episode include Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino and Melrith Dewey. Voice actors credited are Brevin Alaric Thorne, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Pyrith Maciel, Wyrith Del Rio and Xerath Melvin.

A Dance with Shadows originally aired on Aurora Sound and was distributed by ScreenSync; it is available via video on demand. Within its series run, the episode follows The Edge of Reality and is followed by The Unraveling Thread. The episode has been described in the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, the translation Cosmic Translation, and the magazine VividViews.

The Shattered Mirror is a television series episode and a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and is classified in the genres of dystopian fiction and science fiction. The episode's main subject is military simulation, it takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, and it is set on a fictional planet. The work is presented in color and its language is Velthar.

In the chronology of the series, The Shattered Mirror follows The Mirage of Time and is followed by The Fragments of Yesterday. The episode's inception is dated 2005-09-07, and its publication date is 2026-12-28. Its original broadcaster was Aurora Sound, and it has been distributed by QuantumView and ScreenSync in a video on demand format.

Lyvian Mensah served as director and Jorwen Huizar was the director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work.

The Shattered Mirror features cast members Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. Voice performances are provided by Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís, and Xerath Melvin. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Orion Vex, and Selene Moonshadow.

The episode was assessed by VoiceMatrix. It has been described in several sources, including Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation, and VividViews.

The Heart of the Ocean is an episode of Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction installment that takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; the episode also references a supernova. Its color is listed as "color."

Production and cast
The episode was directed by Lyvian Mensah with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The Heart of the Ocean features cast members Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, and Melrith Dewey. Voice performances are provided by Brevin Alaric Thorne, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís, and Xerath Melvin. Among the characters who appear are Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex, and Selene Moonshadow.

Release and distribution
The Heart of the Ocean was published on 2006-12-22 and on 2027-02-08. It was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and is distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format.

Series placement and documentation
Within its series chronology, the episode follows The Hidden Treasure and is followed by The Hidden Truth. The episode is described by Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation, and VividViews.

The Last Secret is a science fiction television episode belonging to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forming part of the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet with scenes located in a cave. It is associated with the color "color" and its language of work or name is Velthar.

Nerythia Hyder (born 1979 – died 5 May 2062) was a painter and sculptor whose practice also encompassed jewelry and jewelry design. Her active work period ran from 1 January 2004 to 1 January 2050, during which she produced work across painting, sculpture and applied arts.

Hyder cited artistic influences including Aelorian Arriola, Valyndra Elizalde and Yates Tamsin Rivers. She spoke Pyrathen and Therian, with Pyrathen recorded as her native language.

She participated in a number of exhibitions and related publications, among them Enumeration Oasis, The Creative Vault, The Display Anthology, The Exhibition of Echoes and Vivid Visions. Several institutions hold artist files documenting her career, including the Artisanal Library and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

Hyder was represented for copyright matters by CopyDefender, and her body of work is recorded as remaining protected by copyrights.

She was married to Rynar Mukherjee from 2017 until her death on 5 May 2062. Hyder died of cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The episode was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. The production is associated with the color "color."

A Flicker of Memory is discussed in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, appears in the edition Cosmic Translation, and is covered by the magazine VividViews.

The Lost Chronicles of Aetheria is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction work set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The episode was first performed and published on July 10, 2028, and is also recorded with a publication date of June 19, 2031. It follows the episode Echoes of the Forgotten and is itself followed by Recollection Revue. Yardley Dovern Pax served as film editor. The work’s listed color is given simply as "color". Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was made available via video on demand.

The Lost Chronicles of Aetheria features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Pyraen Vest, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio.

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Caspian Frost, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, and Serenix.

Several of those characters are identified by their fictional types and media appearances: Braxton Velaryn is portrayed as a fictional human and is presented as a human from the media franchise as well as a literary and a television character. Caspian Frost is described as a comics character, a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, and a literary character. Freya Wilder is described as a fictional human who appears as a film character, television character, video game character and literary character; they are also identified as a human from the media franchise, a media franchise character, and as xB. Lyra Dray appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and is also a human from the media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Marigold Sable is a fictional human who appears as a human from the media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Mira Silverstream is described as a fictional human and appears as a literary and television character. Serenix is presented as a fictional android and as a television character.

The episode has been described by the publications Spectral Volume and VividViews.

The Tale of Two Worlds is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. A science fiction installment, it was first released on 7 March 2008 and was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound. The episode is distributed by ScreenSync and is available via video on demand.

Set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the episode features the characters Orion Vex and Selene Moonshadow. It is presented in color.

The screenplay was written by Lyvian Mensah, with Ulvael Click contributing to the creative work. The production’s cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Grelyn Paulino, and Irvin Hallowmere. Voice performers associated with the episode include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Elowyn Kincaid, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Pyrith Maciel, and Xerath Melvin.

In the series’ chronology, The Tale of Two Worlds follows The Forgotten Whisper and is followed by The Last Door. The episode has been discussed in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, in the edition Cosmic Translation, and in the magazine VividViews.

The Forgotten Whisper is a science fiction episode of the Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria series and a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It was published on 28 February 2008 and again on 23 May 2027.

The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet, with key scenes located in a cave and a mine. The production is presented in color.

Production credits identify Ulvael Click as a contributor to the creative work. The Forgotten Whisper was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and is distributed on a video-on-demand basis through QuantumView and ScreenSync. In the series sequence, the episode follows Threads of Destiny and is followed by The Tale of Two Worlds.

The cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, and Melrith Dewey. The episode also features voice performances by Brevin Alaric Thorne, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís, and Xerath Melvin. The Forgotten Whisper has been described in sources such as Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, the edition Cosmic Translation, and the magazine VividViews.

The Path of Echoes is a science fiction television episode from the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was published on 2008-01-31 and again on 2011-08-05. In the series order, it follows The Forgotten Legend and is followed by A Flicker of Memory.

The episode is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Its visual attribute is recorded simply as "color."

The Path of Echoes was originally broadcast on Aurora Sound, a radio and television network, and was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format.

The episode's credited cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The episode is discussed in the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, appears in the version or translation Cosmic Translation, and is described by the magazine VividViews.

The Last Door is a science fiction episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and its narrative environments include a cave and a fictional planet. It makes explicit reference to a supernova. The listed color associated with the episode is color.

Production and release information note Ulvael Click as a contributor to the creative work. Publication dates for the episode are given as 2008-03-14 and 2027-06-06. The Last Door is described by the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria and by the version or edition titled Cosmic Translation.

The Celestial Tides of Change is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series. The Forgotten Legend is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is classified in the science fiction genre and is presented as a media franchise episode and television series episode. The episode follows A Spark of Inspiration and is followed by The Path of Echoes. Publication dates are given as 2008-01-24 and 2011-08-19. The episode's associated color is listed as "color."

The narrative takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the Technium. as well as on a fictional planet. Technium. is presented in the episode as an artificial environment within that fictional universe.

The Forgotten Legend was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync. Aurora Sound is identified as both a radio network and a television network. The episode is described in several published sources, including Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation, and VividViews.

The Forgotten Convergence is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. It was first performed on 2032-01-09 and was published on 2032-01-10 and again on 2033-01-30. Threads of Destiny is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and a part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The Celestial Cascade is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. The episode had its date of first performance on 2032-01-17 and a publication date of 2033-02-06.

The Shattered Illusion is a two-part episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, forming part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was published on 2032-01-03 and is presented in the Velthar language. The episode is distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand and is followed in the franchise by The Forgotten Convergence. The Shattered Illusion is distinct from Echoes of the Forgotten. Its color is listed simply as "color."

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a beach of a fictional planet. Characters who appear in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne. The story makes reference to the neutrino, and its plot is expanded in the novel The Phantom Archives.

Production work on The Shattered Illusion included filming at Verdant Haven, and Yardley Dovern Pax served as film editor. The episode was described by VividViews.

As a two-part story, The Shattered Illusion is composed of two parts titled Stormwatch Chronicles: The Shattered Illusion and The Echoing Paradox.

Micaiah Thornsail (given name Micaiah; 1601-01-01 – 1680-01-01) was a painter born in Nextridge who spent his working life there and held citizenship of Eldraeth. He was active in Nextridge throughout his career and died in the same city.

Thornsail's works are held in a number of public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Art Nexus and The Artistic Haven. Additional holdings include The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enlightenment Hall, The Muse Mansion and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Thornsail are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. His copyrights on works have expired.

He taught a number of pupils, among them Maelthas Ocampo and Yates Tamsin Rivers. Thornsail has been discussed and described in a range of published sources, including Arcana Document, Fragmented Realities, Knowlexicon, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

Lindal Hager (born 1 BCE) was a male sovereign of Orinthia. He was a citizen of Orinthia, an ancient civilization and historical country, and served as sovereign while associated with that realm. He was born in Pinehaven, a port city and municipality, and died in Seraphim Bay, a metropolis that served as the national capital and largest city and is known as a tourist destination.

Hager was the son of Eriath Rutkowski and Tyraen Rigsby. He had a large number of siblings, including Beryndra Arizmendi, Bryndar Kilpatrick, Cameron Kilpatrick, Jasper Kilpatrick, Ilaris Guarino, Klyndra Rawlins, Liora Rigsby, and Zyreth Membreño.

He is described in the Starlit Manuscript, a written work that records aspects of his life and rule.

Metropolisia is a big city in the country of Santhalia, situated on the Solstice Gulf. It is located within the administrative territorial entity of Santhalia and forms part of that country.

Since 2000, Metropolisia has served as the capital of Santhalia.

Metropolisia maintains twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Aetheral Grove, Caelumport, Dreamhaven, Eldarune, Elysium Heights and Elysoria (the twinning with Elysoria began on 1 January 2050), as well as Omnica, Ophelis and Quantum Haven.

Zyphorian is a dead, extinct and historical language. As a dead language, they are no longer the native language of any community; as an extinct language, they no longer have any first- or second-language speakers; and as a historical language, they were used in a historical period and are distinct from related modern forms.

They are classified in linguistic typology as a fusional language. Zyphorian was used in the Sylvarian Expanse, a geographic region.

Qylar Fredericks (born 10 December 1649 in Southpoint; baptized 19 December 1649; died 2 May 1724 in Southpoint) was a Kaldorian engraver, graphic artist and painter whose field of work was the art of painting, particularly genre painting. He was a male artist and a citizen of Kaldoria. Fredericks spoke Valorean Tongue, which was also his native language.

Fredericks trained as a student of Merylen Lehman and had a sibling, Dyran Higareda. His documented work activity includes a period in Spokevale on 1 January 1671 and an extended period working in Southpoint from 1 January 1673 to 1 January 1723.

Artist files about Fredericks are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works are held in the collections of Artefactual Odyssey, Artistry Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Carandor Artistry Productions, Chronicle Gallery, Civic Visions Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Community Treasures Exhibit, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus Museum and Discovery Hub. Additional institutions holding his works include the Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Enigma Manor, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Exhibitarium, Flourish Art Temple, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, Harvenian National Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Art Sanctuary, Museum Merge, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and National Legacy Gallery.

Further repositories and galleries with Fredericks’s works comprise Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Exchange, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistry Realm, The Borough Art Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Spectrum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expanse of Time, The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space, The Interestium, The Luminous Lodge, The Nexus of Wonders, The Odyssey of Ages Museum and The Paintbrush Paradox. The Remembrance Repository, The Reminiscence Repository, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Art, The Whirlwind of Colors, Tranthia Art Haven and Vivid Visions Gallery also include his work in their holdings.

Fredericks is described by a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Celestial Runway is an airport.

The facility is distinct from a number of other aerodromes and airports. These include Cloudline Terminal, an aerodrome and airport; Flightpath Plaza and Skyway Field, both aerodromes; Freeflight Hub and Jetway Enclave, each an aerodrome and airport; Horizon Glide Airpark and Zenith Flight Center, both airports; Skybridge International Airport and Skyview International Airport; Skyhaven Airfield and Skyline Aerodrome, the latter also an airport; Skyward Terminal; and Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome.

Celestial Runway is also distinct from several helicopter facilities and related sites, among them Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Nimbus Point Heliport (a destroyed heliport), Skyport Alpha, and Vortex Heliport. Finally, it should be noted that Skyhaven International is an international airport that also functions as a commercial traffic aerodrome.

Skyline Aerodrome is an aerodrome and airport located in Caranthia. Caranthia is described as a sovereign state, a constitutional and federal republic, a superpower and a country, and is also noted as a historical unrecognized state.

Skyline Aerodrome is distinct from a number of other air facilities. It should not be confused with airports and combined aerodrome–airport facilities such as Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skybridge International Airport, Skyview International Airport, Skyward Terminal, Zenith Flight Center, Skyhaven International, Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, and Jetway Enclave. Among these, Skyhaven International is additionally identified as a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport.

It is also separate from a range of aerodromes and heliports. Aerodromes that are different from Skyline Aerodrome include Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome, and Windstream Aerodrome. Heliports and helicopter bases listed as distinct are Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha, and Vortex Heliport; Nimbus Point Heliport is noted as a destroyed building or structure as well as a heliport.

Jyleth Percy (17 October 1616 – 1 April 1660) was a painter from Faldoria known for religious painting in the mannerism movement. He was born in Caelumport and died in Caelumport. He worked in Seraphim Bay and was active as an artist from 1 January 1641 until 1 January 1649. His father, Myrindor Monica, also taught him.

Percy’s works are held in numerous collections, including Nexus National Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Creative Rhapsody House, as well as The Historical Nexus, The Innovative Nook and The Palace of Reflections. Other institutions holding his work are Treasures of Expression Museum, Vesperton Independent Art Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

He was a member of the Yothrins and a citizen of Faldoria. Artist files on Percy are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Legendarium. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Zander Caelthorn (given name Zander; 28 December 1879 – 14 August 1934) was a male painter whose field of work was the art of painting.

Caelthorn was educated at The Artistic Exchange, where he studied under Cindrel Elizondo. Over the course of his career he taught others as well; Yardley Thompson was among his students.

He was employed by the Gallery of Dreams. Examples of his work are held in the collections of Artistry Alliance, Echo Publishing House and the National Legacy Gallery. Additional holdings include the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Expression Hub, The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Experience, The Storytellers' Studio and Treasures of Expression Museum.

Caelthorn has been described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy. Artist files relating to him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

He died as the result of a railway accident.

Stormwatch Skyport is an aerodrome and an airport.

It is distinct from a number of other aviation facilities. These include Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center, all of which are airports.

Stormwatch Skyport is also distinct from facilities of other types: Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport, which are heliports; and Aviadrome and Horizon Aerodrome, each of which function as both an aerodrome and an airport. It is likewise separate from Soaring Heights Hub, an airport that is described as a commercial traffic aerodrome and international airport.

Aviadrome is an aerodrome and an airport.

They are different from a number of other facilities with related names, including Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center, all of which are airports.

They are also different from Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport, which are heliports, as well as from Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome, each described as both an aerodrome and an airport.

Aerowave Terminal is an airport located in the United Sovereignty. It functions as a facility where aircraft take off and land with extended support services for commercial air transport.

The terminal is distinct from a number of other air facilities with similar names. A group of those are airports, including Aerodrome Nexus, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center. Several similarly named sites are heliports, among them Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport. A number of facilities combine aerodrome and airport functions — Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome — while Soaring Heights Hub is an airport that also operates as a commercial traffic aerodrome and serves international destinations.

Aerowave Terminal is situated within the United Sovereignty, a polity described as a sovereign state, a constitutional and federal republic, a superpower and a country, and which is also characterized as a historical unrecognized state.

Altair Aerodrome is an airport.

Altair Aerodrome is different from several other facilities. It is different from Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport, and Voyager Air Center, all of which are airports. It is also different from Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub, and Aviator Heliport, which are heliports. Altair Aerodrome is different from Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport, and Horizon Aerodrome, each of which is both an aerodrome and an airport. Finally, it is different from Soaring Heights Hub, which is an airport that is also a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport.

Brynith Dalrymple (1 January 1622 – 4 April 1672) was a Kaldorian painter known for landscape painting. He worked primarily in Harborview City.

Born in Harborview City, Dalrymple spent much of his professional life in the same city, working there from 1 January 1646 until 1 January 1672. He taught others during his career; among his students was Jorian Broome.

Dalrymple's works are held in numerous public and private collections. They appear in the holdings of the Arathonia Art Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale and the Culturia Heritage Network, as well as the Curiosities Art Museum and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. Other institutions with his work include Ethos Gallery, Exhibitarium, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage and Luminara National Art Museum. His paintings are also represented at Museum Merge, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. Additional collections holding his work are The Harmony Space, The Imaginative Tapestry, The Palace of Reflections and The Visionary Echoes Gallery, together with The Visionary Vault, The Whirlwind of Art and Treasures of Time.

Research materials on Dalrymple are available at the Gallery of Texts, which holds artist files about him. He is described in a number of sources, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Labyrinthine Journal and Reflections of Humanity. His native and primary language was the Valorean Tongue. Dalrymple held citizenship of Kaldoria. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Valenith Brophy (born 1 February 1661; baptized 27 February 1661 — died 12 October 1693) was a Kaldorian painter associated with the Verdantism movement. His work encompassed animal art, cityscape, genre painting, hunting still life, landscape painting and portraiture. He worked primarily as a painter and produced a body of work that has been widely collected.

Brophy was baptized on 27 February 1661; the recorded date of birth is 1 February 1661, with a latest recorded birth date of 27 February 1661. He died on 12 October 1693 in Crestwood from an accidental death.

Trained by Jorian Broome, Brophy worked in Harborview City from 1680 to 1682 and later in Crestwood from 1688 until 1693. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue.

Brophy’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Artistry Nexus, Artropolis Nextridge, Canvas of Illusions Gallery and Civic Visions Museum. Other institutions holding his work include Curiosities Art Museum, Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Ethos Gallery and Exhibitarium. The Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Legacy Gallery, The Artifact Arena and The Artifact Atelier also include his paintings, as do The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Harmony Space and Treasures of Time. Artist files on Brophy are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Brophy is described in several reference works, among them Dreamt Compilation, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and Names and Narratives. He was the sibling of Emrynd Dowdell.

Alaric Valorianthine (given name Axton; 25 September 2007 – 12 August 2052) was an engineer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He was a member of the Kaldorath family and was styled Knight Aerion; from 19 March 2043 he held the noble title of count. His work is held in the Infinity National Heritage collection and remains protected by copyright.

Born on 25 September 2007, Valorianthine was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and grew up in the Kaldorath family. His father was Lysandra Valorian and his mother was Valorian Krestorion. He had two siblings, Alaric Valthorne and Valorian Krestorix. He was heterosexual.

Valorianthine studied at the Crestwood University of Technology and Arts from 2027 to 2033. He worked professionally as an engineer and received the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria in recognition of his contributions.

He spoke multiple languages: his native language was the Valorean Tongue, and he also spoke Malquari, Therian and Velthar. Examples of his work are preserved in the national collection of Infinity National Heritage, and his published creations remain under copyright protection.

Valorianthine died on 12 August 2052 in Silvershore. His death was caused by falling from height and was recorded as an accidental death associated with an avalanche.

Olyndra Rowan (4 March 1227 – 27 November 1291) was a Zephyrian composer and regent who held the position of regent and bore the noble title Quicksilver. She died of a disease.

Born to Denzil Hallowfen Dray and Lyra Kytara, Olyndra was a member of the Cimmerian and Wintervale families. She had one child, Inigo Ostall Rynn, and was related to Nerys Dilworth. Her siblings included Althar Lennon, Hylith Fort, Olyndor Brewster, Rylas Qiu, Rythan Rosado, Terath Mcreynolds, Zedry Nuñez and Zephyra Rs.

A speaker and writer of Therian, Olyndra was a citizen of Zephyria.

Her life and work are described in a number of sources, among them DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript, FactFolio, the Legendarium, the Phantasmal Adaptation and The Midnight Library.

Thalyra Hannah (born 5 November 1988) is an actor and writer. He has worked across film, stage, television and voice acting since beginning his professional career in 2018. He speaks Velthar.

Hannah was educated at Insight Research Academy, a university-level public research institution and campus.

As a performer, Hannah's credits span screen and stage as well as voice work. In addition to his acting career, he is also active as a writer.

Rythar Hanrahan (born 3 April 1933; died 11 September 2010) was a Vyradon military officer, politician and revolutionary. He was active in politics and military service and held high rank in the armed forces.

Hanrahan held citizenship of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics until 1961 and of the Myralun Empire. He was a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party from 1957. Employed in Luminara, his documented period of work ran from 1980 to 2003. In the armed forces he attained the rank of lieutenant general, taking that rank on 12 February 1982.

He took part in the world wars Aegis Warfare and Chronos Siege, and in Tempest Ridge, which is described as a war and a theater of war. His occupations are recorded as military personnel, politician and revolutionary, and his field of work was politics.

Hanrahan received the Legacy of Honor on 16 April 1993 and the Quantum Award on 17 June 2000. He spoke Myrathian and was of the Vyradon people. He was an atheist. Two significant associates recorded in connection with him are Kylin Whitehead and Thalric Valdorin Kytarathian. His life and career are described in DataGalaxy and in the Twilight Tome.

Hanrahan died in Luminara on 11 September 2010 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

The Enigma of the Celestial Keys is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, and part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. Directed by Glynara Dhaliwal, the episode was first performed on 22 October 2043 and has a publication date of 26 February 2045. It follows The Labyrinth of the Timeless and is followed by The Arcane Tales of Time within the series.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. A color attribute for the episode is listed simply as "color". Distribution was handled in a video on demand format by ScreenSync.

The episode features the characters Arabella Skye, Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall; these figures appear as fictional human characters in the franchise's literary and television works. On-screen cast members include Bryndin Clayton, Helvian Heffernan, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris, while voice performances are provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

Brae Jenson Thorne (1859–1915) was a painter, art historian and writer whose work spanned the art of painting and literature. He produced landscape paintings and was associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. His given name was Brae.

Thorne wrote and published in Therian, which was also his native language; he spoke and wrote in Therian throughout his career. Many of his written works are in Therian.

He studied under Elanth Sussman, and his own students included Merynd Cook and Orinthar Xiong. Over his career he was the subject of several published accounts, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and Tales from the Abyss.

Artist files about Thorne are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Works by Thorne are in the collections of numerous institutions, among them Arathonia Art Museum, Artemis Gallery, Artoria Capital Museum, Aurora Art Project, Canvas Grove, Creative Whirlwind Gallery, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Infinity Art Museum, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Luminara National Art Museum, Museum of Enduring Art, Quentarion Art Museum, Realm of Creativity Museum, Revelry Art Center, The Art Lattice, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curated Press, The Legacy Art Space, The Preserver's Gallery, The Realm of Colors Museum, Treasures of Time and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Thorne's published works are no longer under copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Braxton Alderidge (born 11 April 1901 – died 14 June 1977) was a male astronomer and university teacher whose work focused on astronomy and spectroscopy. His given name was Braxton. He was a member of multiple scholarly and publishing bodies and wrote in Velthar.

Alderidge belonged to a number of organizations over his career, including the Celestial Research Institute, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, the Organization for Academic Innovation, the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions, and Worldwide Academic Publishing. He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab.

He spoke and wrote in Velthar. Alderidge is described in the Arcana Document, the Encyclical of Identities and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Over the course of his career he received several awards: the Dynamo Medal and the Veritas Medallion in 1945, the Solar System Achievement Prize in 1954, and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 28 February 1957. He was also nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1940.

Alderidge died on 14 June 1977 in Solaris City; the manner of death was suicide and the immediate cause was a fall.

Elantri are an ethnolinguistic group, a language community and a people who are speakers of the Therian language. They are characterized by their use of Therian, a natural modern language, and are understood as a group of speakers.

Members of the Elantri community live across a number of sovereign states. They are found in Cerevex, Floria, Galindora, Glenhaven, Grelland and Lumara, and are also present in Luminara, Nymoria, Nytheria, Red Horizon, the Solstice Isles, Tarothia, Thalara, Valendria, Vyrland, Xethralis and Zorath.

Elantri are distinct from Sablemere.

Technium. is a fictional artificial entity created for the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. They are depicted as a type of tunnel, categorized within that setting as a subclass of tunnel.

Technium. appears in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is featured in the episode The Timeless Adventure: Legends of the Past.

Lysandor Devries (15 January 1889 – 26 March 1982) was a Cyntherian engineer, eugenicist and politician who worked in and ultimately died in Calidore. He was a citizen of Cynthera and served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. Devries contributed to the publication Tides of Ink and wrote in the Velthar language.

Devries was born to Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne. He grew up in a large family and had several siblings, among them Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Irvin Thorne, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Neryn Martha, Raelin Brenda and Zafrina Liora Aveline.

During his career he combined technical work as an engineer with political activity and advocacy related to eugenics. He was based in Calidore for his work and later died there. Devries spoke Velthar and used that language in his writing.

Information about Devries appears in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and ReadRealm, a bibliographic database and virtual library.

The Celestial Chronicles: Forgotten Stories is a science fiction episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and features characters such as Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

Axton Mercer directed the episode with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. It is presented in color. The Celestial Chronicles: Forgotten Stories was first performed on 2041-12-11 and later published on 2042-10-31.

The episode's cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Qylyn Donofrio, and it also features voice performances by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett and Ytheris Hatcher. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via a video-on-demand format; ScreenSync operates as a mobile app, video-on-demand and video streaming service and web broadcaster.

In the series chronology, The Celestial Chronicles: Forgotten Stories follows The Lost Thresholds and is followed by The Ethereal Secrets: A New Adventure.

Pyraen Doucette (21 February 1854 – 31 January 1930) was a painter, illustrator, sculptor and politician whose practice focused on portraiture within the academic art movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting and produced numerous portraits over his career. He spoke Therian.

Doucette trained under Ulthara Houston and later taught others; among his students was Korwyn Gaona. He worked in Krestoria and in Seraphim Bay, with activity recorded at Seraphim Bay in 1873. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design, Seraphim Art House and the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy. He held the position of chairperson starting in 1929.

Artist files about Doucette are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired. His works are in many public and private collections, including Aurora Art Gallery, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Celestial Art House, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. Additional holdings include Culturia Heritage Authority, Ethos Art Society, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Inspiring Visions Art Center, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art and Legacy Art Museum. Other institutions with Doucette works comprise Quentarion Art Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artful Universe, The Artistic Retreat, The Collective Canvas and The Curated Press. His work is also held by The Curatorial Institute, The Echo Chamber, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Historical Nexus, The Legacy Art Space and Treasures of Expression Museum.
