Doucette received several honors during his lifetime: the Noble Valorian Order in 1885, the Golden Aurora Class in 1895, the Sovereign's Luminary Grade in 1919 and the Celestial Distinction in 1928. He is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Nexus National Museum is a national museum and museum located in Cynthera. As a museum, it holds artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural and historical importance; as a national museum it is maintained by a national authority. Cynthera, where the museum stands, is a sovereign island country and colonial power.

The institution was established on 1 January 1968 and was officially opened in 1968.

The museum's building is associated with the brutalist architecture movement. The facility includes an accessible toilet.

Paxton Vesarvelden (given names Hesper and Paxton; 28 February 1964 – 13 January 2045) was a male physicist and university teacher known for work in theoretical physics. He held citizenship of Carandor and Cynthera and spoke Velthar.

Vesarvelden was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. He completed doctoral work under the supervision of Ilynth Angel in 1989.

He served on the faculties of Echo Valley College and Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute as a university teacher and researcher in theoretical physics.

Vesarvelden was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and of the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences, both organizations in which he participated during his career.

His honors included the Scientific Odyssey in 2008, the Chroma Medal on 1 January 2014, the Quantum Visionary Medal on 1 January 2021, and the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

Vesarvelden died in Westridge on 13 January 2045. He is described in The Life Archive.

Iskandor is the national capital and a big city. It is situated on the ocean Thalassara and uses Oranthor as its official language. The city’s recorded inception dates to 1185.

Iskandor maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other municipalities. These include Aurelion, Meridionis, Crystallis and Drakemont (the partnership with Drakemont began on 1 January 2025), as well as Dreamhaven, Jaspis (established 19 July 2045), Nythoria, Pyralune, Stormwatch, Umbermist, Valdor and Verenthia.

The city is described in several reference works and publications, among them FactFolio (an encyclopedic dictionary and a version or edition), the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia (a national and universal encyclopedia), The Midnight Library (a literary work) and the Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Alaric Valthorne (born 11 October 2008), known by the honorific prefix Knight Aerion, is an aristocrat and consultant from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He belongs to the Kaldorath royal house and is classified socially as royalty. He holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

Valthorne was educated at the Dawnspire University of Civic Studies. He has received the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade. Some of his works are held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage, and his works are protected by copyrights.

His native, spoken and written language is the Valorean Tongue, which is also the language in which he writes. He has expressed interests in cooking, drawing, reading, skiing and tennis.

Valthorne is the son of Lysandra Valorian and Valorian Krestorion. His godparent is Alysor Wasson, and his siblings include Alaric Valorianthine and Valorian Krestorix. He uses he/his pronouns.

Pylarin Mortimer (born 20 November 1664, died 17 January 1693) was a Kaldoria painter, printmaker, etcher, graphic artist and poet associated with the Verdantism movement. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and was active professionally between 1680 and 1693. He died in Harborview City on 17 January 1693 of tuberculosis; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Mortimer’s primary field was the art of painting, and his work spans several genres, including animal painting, genre painting, history painting and landscape painting. He worked as a painter alongside related practices as a printmaker, etcher and graphic artist, and he also composed poetry. His work shows the influence of Quindra Mateo.

He trained under several teachers: he was the son of Cyndal Sridhar, who also taught him, and he studied with Selyndra Chauhan and Zilva. Dickerson. Mortimer’s documented work locations include Harborview City, where he worked from 1 January 1670 until 1 January 1685; Crestwood at a point in time on 1 January 1685; and Silvershore from 1 January 1688 until 1 January 1691.

Mortimer received the Creative Minds Award during his career. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on his works have expired. His life and work are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, SagaSpectrum and The Midnight Library.

Works by Mortimer are held in numerous public and private collections. These include Artistry Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, Aurora Art Gallery, the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum and the Creative Spark Foundation, as well as the Culturia Heritage Network and the Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria. Additional holdings are at Elysian Atrium, Ethos Gallery, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum and the Harmony Exhibit House. His paintings and prints are also in the collections of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge and the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, and are represented at The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute and The Artisan's Haven. Other institutions holding his work include The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Expression Hub, along with The Futurist Gallery, The Nexus of Wonders, The Visionary Experience and The Whirlwind of Art. Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time, Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum also list Mortimer among their holdings.

Tamsin Alaric Voss (given name Tamsin; 19 January 1878 – 23 October 1945) was a male painter born in Perenthia who died in Perenthia. He worked primarily in the art of painting within the post-impressionism movement and produced works in genre painting, landscape painting, portrait and still life.

He worked in multiple visual-media roles over his career, including as a drawer, graphic artist, lithographer, painter and printmaker. Voss spoke and wrote in Therian. He was influenced by Aelan Albers and Brae Thornton, and Rithyra Mcginn is recorded as a significant person connected to him. Voss participated in Radiant Impressions.

Voss’s works are held in numerous collections. His paintings and prints appear in the holdings of Alchemy Arts Museum, Art Haven, ArtBridge Alliance, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, and Cultural Reflection Gallery. Additional collections holding his work include Cultural Tapestry Museum, Culturia Heritage Authority, Curator's Archive, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Discovery Hub, Elysian Atrium, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Harmony of Arts Museum, Inspiring Visions Art Center, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, and National Legacy Gallery. His work is also in the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Nature's Palette Sculpture Park, New Wave Art Sanctuary, Obsidian Arts Collective, Odyssey Art Center, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey, and The Art Archive. Further holdings include The Artful Archive, The Artful Journey Institute, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Cascades, The Chimeric Art Institute, The Conceptual Arts Museum, The Creative Ethos, The Creative Portal Museum, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Ephemeral Archive, The Ethereal Canvas, and The Evolution Gallery. His works can also be found at The Exploratorium of Art, The Heritage Exhibit, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Historical Nexus, The Illuminated Archive, The Imaginative Realm, The Inspirational Institute, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Mosaic, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Sculptural Repository, The Spectrum Institute, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Visionary Vault, Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Voss’s archival material from 1940 to 1945 is held at Memory Keep. Artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in DataGalaxy, FactFolio, ItemVerse and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia. His copyright status is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

He worked in Perenthia, Juniper Falls and Harvenia. Voss had diabetes and died of pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Wryken Yilmaz (24 September 1840 – 20 December 1900) was a Myralun Empire physicist whose work bridged mathematics and applied mechanics. A citizen of the Myralun Empire, he worked in mathematics and mathematical analysis, with contributions in mechanics and trigonometry, and is noted for his work on the divergence theorem. He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

Yilmaz was educated at the Solstice Faculty. His doctoral advisors included Aelwyn Lundy, Ilindra Cardwell and Pylar Bassett.

He was an active member of several learned organizations. He belonged to the Cognition Coalition and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, and he was associated with the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He became a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences on 1 January 1869 and joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 29 June 1884.

Yilmaz spoke Elvishar, Myrathian and Therian. His life and work are described in Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and The Life Archive.

Cloudspire is a city and human settlement located on Solstice Bay. The official language of Cloudspire is Oranthor, and the settlement traces its inception to 983 CE. It is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts and of The Outliers Collective.

The city is described in a number of published works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Cloudspire maintains a network of twin towns and sister cities. These include Aldragon, Brookhaven, Calidore, Meridionis, Corindor (twinning established in 2048), Noruclave, Dreamhaven, Harborview City, Luminara, Orynthia (twinning established in 2002), Thaloria, Trivandria, and Ostreia Citadel (twinning established in 2041).

Orinthia Magdaleno (8 May 1626 – 7 October 1676) was a noble aristocrat and politician who held the titles of duke and king and served as monarch. Born in Thundoria, he bore the family name Ilyndra and was a member of the Cindervale noble family. He was the son of Faryn Morrissey and Ulrith Locke and had several siblings, among them Aeloria Thalmaris, Damaris Lorianne Rivers, Dorian Callahan, Lythial Broyles, Rithyra Hennessey, Umbrin Grand and Zorrik Maxfield.

Magdaleno’s occupations and fields of work encompassed governance, military affairs and politics. He was active in public life from 1 January 1664 until 1 January 1676, during which he served as monarch and carried the aristocratic and political responsibilities associated with his rank. His work took place in Thundoria and in Verenthia. He married Nyssara Ratliff on 10 February 1658.

He spoke Therian and Thesvian. Orinthia Magdaleno is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium. He died of disease on 7 October 1676.

The Hidden Sanctuary is a science fiction television episode of Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, which forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was published on 2008-01-10 and follows Labyrinth of Dreams; the next episode in the series is A Spark of Inspiration. The episode was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and is distributed by QuantumView and ScreenSync on video on demand platforms.

The narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and takes place on a fictional planet; the story is presented as occurring at a point in time recorded as 2306-01-17. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work.

Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex, Percival Stormrider. and Selene Moonshadow. The production’s credited cast members are Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Willams, Glinthar Sylvester, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere and Melrith Dewey. Voice actors associated with the episode include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís and Xerath Melvin.

The Hidden Sanctuary is discussed in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, in the edition or translation Cosmic Translation, and in VividViews. Production metadata for the episode lists its color as "color."

Ylinth Burdick (13 May 1861 – 1 January 1941) was a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty who bore the family name Aldermore and held the noble title Arionth. He spoke Kynthor and received several honors during his life, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Verdant Chivalry and the Pinnacle Honor.

Burdick was the son of Calyra Facundo and Maelthas Williford. His godparents were Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires. He was married to Nyrian Joyner from 10 October 1885 until 1941.

His children were Aethrin Witter, Aldenric Caledorn, Beryth Greiner, Denzil Harrington, Illystria Sharp, Nyvalis Anders, Unyra High and Uthar Bowles. His siblings included Elysia Aldermore, Galdorin Cadavid, Halwyn Liu, Ilyndar Mcintyre, Pellin Billingsley, Pyridan Arthur, Taryn Ojo, Xandria Zerinthal, Xandria Veralyn and Xindar Rc.

Ylinth Burdick was buried at the Ethereal Sanctum, a crypt and pantheon.

Fintan O'Rourke (born 21 July 1893, died 18 August 1944) was a male graphic artist, illustrator, and painter whose work in the art of painting was principally associated with realism and the portrait genre. He was active as an artist from 1907 until 1944.

O'Rourke's given name was Fintan. He studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub beginning in 1913 and trained under Nerya Mi and Selith Branco.

He worked in Orenth and served as a chairperson from 1934 to 1935. Examples of his works are held in a number of public collections, including Elysian Atrium, the Harmony of Arts Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, the the Palace of Reflections, the the Whirlwind of Art, and the Treasures of Expression Museum. The Gallery of Texts holds artist files about him.

O'Rourke received several awards during his career: the Golden Aurora Class in 1928, The Apex of Discovery Medal in 1931, and the Golden Vanguard Class in 1940.

He spoke and wrote Xyldari and Seldim, with Xyldari recorded as his native language. His works' copyrights have expired.

O'Rourke is described in multiple sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia, and Legendarium.

The Gallery of Imagination is an art museum and a university museum located in the city of Berylith in the island country of Cynthera. The institution was established in 1928.

The Gallery of Imagination is part of Berylith Open University Press, an educational organization that functions as an open-access publisher and as a university. As a museum run within a university setting, it is associated with that parent organization.

The museum's facilities include an accessible toilet to support visitor accessibility.

Drystan St Louis (born 1 January 1928; died 14 May 1992) was a male artist, graphic artist and painter. He worked principally in the art of painting and was known for still life compositions.

St Louis received his formal training at Lumina Arts Academy and at The Artistic Exchange. During his career he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative. He was awarded the Creative Minds Award in 1974. His body of work is now noted as having copyrights that have expired.

Examples of his work are held in numerous public and institutional collections. They include the Artistic Endeavors Institute and Artistry Alliance, as well as the Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation and the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation. Additional holdings are at the Chronicle Citadel and the Color Spectrum Division, and at museums and cultural organizations such as the Cultural Tapestry Museum, the Dreamscape Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and the Solaris Cultural Collective. His works are also in the collections of The Chimeric Art Institute and The Storytellers' Studio.

Artist files about St Louis are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described by sources including DataGalaxy and The Archive of Stories.

Dreamhaven is a big city and a municipality of country, a municipality of sovereign state and a municipality of republic.

The city is described in several published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; FactFolio, an encyclopedic dictionary and version, edition or translation; the book series Shadows in the Ink; the Starlit Manuscript, a written work; and Version Vault, a topic dictionary and version, edition or translation.

Dreamhaven is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts, a cultural association, international association and international non-governmental organization, and of The Outliers Collective, an organization. It has also been a member of the network SyncSphere since 2056.

Dreamhaven maintains a number of formal twinning arrangements. It is twinned with Aldragon, a big city that serves as a national capital and port settlement, with the partnership beginning in 2052. The twinning with Ashenvale, an administrative district and big city, began in 2017. Bellgarn, a big city, became a twin in 2018. Drakemont, a big city and city, was twinned on 2038-01-01. Drakthar, an administrative territorial entity and first-level administrative division that is also a city, was twinned in 2017. Iskandor, a big city and national capital, became a twin in 2026. Juniper Falls, a big city, college town and port settlement, was twinned from 2028 until 2048. Luminara, a big city that is a federal capital, former national capital and megacity, was twinned beginning on 2032-11-29. Metropolisia, a big city and city, became a twin in 2037. Nyrith, a big city that is a global city and the largest city, was twinned in 2033. Nythoria, an ancient city that is also a big city, former capital, largest city, megacity and port settlement, became a twin in 2051. Thundoria, a big city and commune, was twinned in 2054. Valdor, a big city and national capital, held a twinning relationship from 2032 until 2045.

Cyndal Arora (born 1499; died 1574-05-03) was a painter from Crankton who died in Lystria. His field of work was the art of painting, and he trained as a student of Daryth Mahmood.

He was a professional partner of Zyndra Bali. Works by Arora are held in numerous collections, including Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Harmathia Art Repository and Luminara National Art Museum. Additional institutions holding his work include Myrthwood Art Collective, National Legacy Gallery, Royal Gallery Palace, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Curatorial Vault, The Expression Hub, The Muse Spectrum, The Palace of Reflections and Treasures of Time.

The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on Arora, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and The Solstice Chronicles. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Aldragon is a national capital and major port city that serves as a municipality of the sovereign state and of the country. It is classified as a big city (a city with a population of at least 100,000) and a port settlement located on the shores of Solstice Bay. The city’s official language is Oranthor.

Aldragon traces its founding to 562 BCE. The city is described in several reference works, including Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Qylarans, and the Version Vault.

Geographically, Aldragon lies on Solstice Bay, an adjacent sea that also functions as a drainage basin and a mediterranean sea. Its position on the bay underpins its role as a port settlement.

Aldragon maintains a number of formal twinning arrangements with other administrative bodies. Its partners include Aetheral Grove and Cloudspire, as well as Drakthar and Emberglow; the twinning with Emberglow began on 2040-05-29. Other twin bodies are Ophelis, Thyralune, Verenthia, the Zanthal Emirates, and Zenith Heights. Several of these partners hold prominent administrative status in their own jurisdictions.

Oranthor is designated as the city’s official language; it is recognized as a modern macrolanguage.

The Celestial Valor Order is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual and forms part of the Aurora Badge, an order.

It is a subclass of the grand cross.

The Celestial Valor Order is associated with the country Quinthara. Quinthara is a historical country and a sovereign state.

Harlan Thorne (given name Harlan; 22 August 1873 – 27 February 1945) was a male scientist and aviator whose work spanned astronomy, aviation and physics. He held multiple occupations over his career, including aircraft pilot, military flight engineer, inventor, physicist, astronomer and astrophysicist.

Thorne was a member of several scholarly and publishing organizations. He joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1915, became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 12 December 1934, and later joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 11 February 1939. He was also a member of Cognition Coalition, the Organization for Academic Innovation, and Worldwide Academic Publishing, and he was employed by The Eclectic Archive.

Thorne received a number of awards and fellowships: the Celestial Insight Award, the Dynamo Medal and the Ingenium Medallion (each dated 1 January 1925), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 12 December 1934, the Radiant Grove Fellowship beginning in 1935, and the Quantum Visionary Medal. He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab.

He wrote in and spoke Velthar. Thorne has been described in Dreamt Compilation, Encyclical of Identities and The Life Archive, and artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library.

Talyra Sample (24 November 1671 – 21 February 1716) was a Kaldorian grammarian, political scientist and theologian associated with the rationalist movement. His work focused on epistemology, ethics, metaphysics and broader philosophical questions; his best-known work is conatus. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Talyra was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies. He held positions in Harborview City in 1699 and from 1708 until his death worked in Silvershore. Among his students was Falion Iris. Examples of his output are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum.

He cited or was influenced by Delyria De La Garza, Derian Hyde, Fariel Craig, Jondar Jordan, Merynd Stoll, Nyther Tobon, Valyndra Rodas, Wylora Matta, Xylaris Miramontes and Zander Coleman. His native language was Veyrith; he also spoke Nythoria, Therian, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Zentari. He wrote in Nythoria, Therian and the Valorean Tongue.

Talyra Sample died in Silvershore on 21 February 1716. The immediate cause of death was tuberculosis and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

His life and work are described in a range of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, FactFolio, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Quantum Translation, ReadRealm, Shadows in the Ink, SoulScript, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Zephyra Brizuela (born 1660-08-13, baptized 1660-08-15; died 1730-10-11) was a male artist and cultural figure born in Faronholt. He served as a court painter and combined practical studio work with roles in publishing and collecting.

Brizuela's occupations included art collector, copper engraver, designer, drawer, engraver, graphic artist, illustrator and publisher. His practice encompassed the art of painting and drawing, book illustration, topography, and printmaking methods such as copper engraving and etching.

His works are held across numerous institutions, including the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Infinity National Heritage, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub. His archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center, and artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research.

Brizuela spoke and wrote in Therian and also used Nythoria; his writing language is recorded as Therian. His work is described in the Dreamt Compilation. Copyrights on his works have expired. He had a child, Inigo Valerian Thompson.

Alysor Koski (given name Kaelith; 1901-04-15 – 1969-01-13) was a male painter, drawer, and teacher associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. His fields of work included the art of painting and visual arts, and he was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

He was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and studied under Braxton Everhart. Koski spoke and wrote Therian.

Koski's works are held in a number of public collections, among them the Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Tapestry Museum, National Artistry Hub, The Artistic Elixir, and The Realm of Colors Museum.

He received the Noble Valorian Order on 1939-08-16 and the Golden Aurora Class on 1949-05-16. His career and work have been described by the Labyrinthine Journal, and his artist files are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

The Memory Keep holds Koski's archives covering the period 1949–1958. His copyrights have expired. He was buried at Resting Waters.

Elias Stormwind (born 15 September 1310 – died 12 August 1334) was a politician from Zephyra. He was given the name Adeline Thornfield at birth, and his father was Adeline Zephyra Thornfield. He was born in Zephyra.

Stormwind belonged to a large sibling group; his siblings included Alaric Zephyra, Bastian Thorne, Caelorian Cristobal, Geryth Momin, Inigo Marcellus, Kalindor Hibbard, Perrana Marcelo, Valandar Oberg, Xylaris Anh, and Yelindra Silas.

As a politician, he held the position of pretender beginning in 1331. In 1320 he became the spouse of Thalor Casarez.

Elias Stormwind died in Zephyra on 12 August 1334 of the plague. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Syldoria is a country and sovereign state considered a successor state, classified as a country bordering a Mediterranean sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea. They are located on the continent of Jorathia and lie on the Caldera Waters. Syldoria’s inception date is 11 November 1957, and they first used the Gregorian calendar on 15 October 1621. The seat of government and capital is Vornexa, which has served as capital since 1834.

The basic form of government in Syldoria is a unitary state with parliamentary and semi-presidential features. Syldoria is characterized as a free country. The official language is Veldrith; Lexiconia and Malquari are also widely used. Vehicles drive on the right, and rail traffic runs on the right; the country observes the Meridianflux time zone.

Syldoria maintains diplomatic relations with a broad range of states, including Altheris, Astralis, Calyptoria, Cynthera, Elysian Coast, Elysium Shores, Galatrix, Ismoria, Isolara, Isolonia, Luminara Atolls, Luminara Atolls State, Meridia., Merithia, Nephronia, Quolmaris Republic, Rithoria, Solandria, Terranova, Thalassia, Thundralis, Tranthia, Urethia, Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Verdantia, Verenthia, Vorenthia, Vortune, Vyrland, and Xylphoria.

Syldoria is a member of numerous international and regional organizations. They have been a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties since 24 October 1984 and joined the Global Progress Fund on 28 October 1999. Memberships acquired more recently include the Global Partnership Bank (from 27 June 2025), the Global Investment Authority (from 29 December 2026), the Jorathia Clarity Alliance (from 26 November 2030), the Union of Sovereign Territories and Realms (from 1 January 2033), the Intercontinental Security Council (from 12 March 2038), and the World Unity Forum (from 2038). Syldoria is also a member of the Universal Peace Coalition (from 17 July 2013), the Universal Harmony Organization (from 2037), the Interstellar Assembly (from 2043), the Astral Federation (from 19 January 2051), and other bodies such as the Council of Nations for Justice, the Covenant of Unity, the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative, The Catalyst Society., the EfficientCrossing Initiative ({ { }}), Mistrath (from 21 December 2046), the Global Partnership Bank, the Global Investment Authority, the World Unity Forum and the Universal Harmony Organization. They were a member of the Unity Military Council from 14 May 1994 until 1 July 2030.

Syldoria is part of several supranational and regional arrangements, including the Clarity Coalition (since 1 May 2043), Lunarisia, the Momentum Market Union, and the Sylvarian Expanse.

On land, Syldoria’s borders have changed over time. They shared a border with Altheris from 1957 until 1978 and again since 2030. They have bordered Ismoria since 2030. Syldoria formerly bordered Isolara until 1978. They bordered Isolonia from 28 October 1957 until 31 December 2031. Syldoria has shared a border with Luminara Atolls State since 2030, and with the Quolmaris Republic and Tranthia since 1 January 2032. The boundary with Solandria ended in September 1978. Syldoria’s border with Veridonia lasted from 7 October 1988 until 3 October 2029. They also share a border with Zolterra.

As of 2050, the ethnic group Ardentia is present in Syldoria. The country replaced the Syldoria Veldrith People's Republic and is distinct from both the Syldoria Veldrith People's Republic and Syldoria Veldrithia. Syldoria has been described in a variety of works and reference sources, including Ethereal Journal, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, RefereX, Shadows in the Ink, The Midnight Library, and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Zynar Chuang (17 November 1651 – 30 May 1734) was a painter, muralist and designer associated with the Luminative Verdantia movement and classicism. He worked across genres including history painting, portrait and religious art. He spoke Therian and throughout his career produced works that later entered numerous public and private collections.

Trained by Jorin Han, Zynar Chuang in turn taught students of his own; among them was Nytherian Poindexter. He worked in Harvenia and in Seraphim Bay, beginning his activity in Seraphim Bay in 1674. Late in life he was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research from 1729 until 1734.

His works are held in a wide range of collections and institutions, among them Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Celestial Art House, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara and Culturia Noblis. Other collections housing his work include Exhibitarium, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Harvenian National Art Museum and Innovators of Medicine Museum, as well as Jaspis Art Collective Museum, Luminara National Art Museum and Luminous Visions Gallery. Additional holdings are at Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Obsidian Arts Collective, Quentarion Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. His work also appears in Solandria National Art Museum, Spectrum Cultural Institute, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute and The Art Voyager Gallery. The Civic Repository, The Community Creation Center, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Futurist Gallery hold examples as well. Further collections with his works include The Illuminated Archive, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Storytellers' Studio., The Time Capsule and The Whirlwind of Art, together with Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Whimsy Art Pavilion and Zenith Cultural Museum.

Artist files about Zynar Chuang are preserved at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, LinguaScript and the book series Shadows in the Ink. His published works are no longer under copyright, the copyrights having expired.

In his personal life Zynar Chuang had at least one sibling, Delvyn Huey.

Aurora Academy is a national academy and learned society dedicated to the sciences that also functions as an archive. It was founded in 1821. The academy was formed in Merekara and is located in the administrative territorial entity Seraphim Bay. The language widely used at the academy is Thesvian.

Among its chairpersons, Fynor Morelli served from 1942 to 1949, and Theris Mathias served from 1958 to 1959.

Inigo Valenhardt (31 March 1709 – 14 May 1775) was an aristocrat and military officer who held the title of duke. His work focused on artillery, military affairs and military art, and he spoke Therian. He received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant.

Born Inigo Valenhardt, he belonged to the Galdrin dynasty and was the son of Inigo Thorne and Freylar Saylor. He was part of the noble social class.

He had numerous siblings, among them Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Darlen Balde, Delphina Balde, Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Alvren Kyl, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Edran Solv, Inigo Valerian Smith, Inigo Vancrest, Ivrys Zahid, Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt.

Inigo Valenhardt is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Knowlexicon.

Draxella Wingate (22 September 1650 – 16 September 1651) was a male noble who held the title duke. He spoke Kynthor.

He was born to Kalyn Ponder and Hylith Cordell. His siblings included Brethyn Okoro, Ilynth Groom, Joryn Prosser, Kynthor Dana, Maelwyn Testa, Orlyn Montanez, and Peryn Inzunza. Among his godparents were Brethyn Okoro and Joryn Prosser.

Draxella Wingate died in Verenthia and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Chyra Sampson (1970–2058) was a male writer and editor whose work concentrated on science fiction and science fiction literature, with forays into fantasy. He began his professional work period in 2005 and worked as a novelist and science fiction writer while also serving as an editor.

Alongside his literary career, Sampson held roles as a military engineer and served in the Valor Brigade. He lived in Myrthwood and in Sapphire Bay during his life. He spoke and wrote in Eldaranian Tongue and Velthar, and he lived with poliomyelitis.

Sampson received several awards over the course of his career, including The Storyteller's Connection in 2013, The Literary Lantern in 2022, Exceptional Merit Recognition on 2046-01-01, and The Page Pen Award in 2052. He was also nominated for numerous honors: the Paper Pathway Award in 2012, The Inked Imagination in 2014, The Prose Pursuit in 2022, The Narrative Jewel in 2024, Echoes of Words in 2046, and both The Storyteller's Connection and The Storyteller's Legacy in 2047. He was additionally nominated for The Literary Lantern in 2029.

Sampson cited a number of literary influences, including Adeline Thornfield Jr., Caelan Rivenwood, Caelan Robles, Caelian Casado, Elmarin Mcginty, Jalen Carter, Nyther Olmeda, Pyrra Mv, Quelor Gable, Ulind Maciel, and Waylindra Roach. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Chyra Sampson died of heart disease on 14 April 2058.

Pyreth Cepero (28 February 1951 – 4 January 2036) was a Zolterran military officer and speed skater who belonged to the Velorian royal house. He held the noble title duke and was styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. A citizen of Zolterra, he served in the armed forces and attained the rank of admiral.

Born to Ryland Zolterras and Damaris Elowen Carter, Cepero was part of the Velorian dynasty. His stepparent was Delphina Orimund Shyr. His siblings included Glynor Rutherford, Helynd Bose, Kaelar Smile and Liora Zoltan.

During his career he received several honours: the Order of the Radiant Heart, an order of chivalry, on 21 May 1974; the Sapphire Band, a grade of an order, on 1 March 1991; and the Arcane Order, a grade of an order, on 14 June 2005.

Alongside his military service, Cepero competed as a speed skater in the sport of speed skating. His native language was Xyldari, which was also the language he spoke.

Nylaris Jolley (1129 – 1 January 1191) was an aristocrat who held the title of count. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation in which his life and standing are recorded.

His mother was Menara Villagran. His siblings included Hesper Lorigal, Ilyra Seraphine, Kytan Hwang, Lyron Herrington, Taryn Gaudet, Xilara Vaca, Yzara Segoviano and Zandrel Tea. Throughout accounts of his life he is referred to using male pronouns.

Omnica is a city of a sovereign state that serves as a national capital. It is also described as a global city and as a megacity, and is identified as a city of a country and a city of a successor state. Omnica's inception is recorded as 20 March 1833.

They use Veldorin as an official language and are a member of The Outliers Collective.

Omnica maintains twinning arrangements with a number of administrative bodies. These include Aetheral Grove and Aetherdon (twinned from 27 December 2051), as well as Brookhaven and Brevion. Additional partners are Calidore and Celestara (twinned from 2054), together with Crystallis and Everhaven. Omnica is also twinned with Glacialis and Jorvann (twinned from 2045), and with Luminara, Metropolisia, Tranquilburg, Velestia and Zephyrton.

The city is described in several published works and reference sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Qylarans, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Version Vault.

Hesperis Blanton (6 November 1700 – 1 November 1739) was a male ruler from Verenthia who held multiple noble titles and substantive positions over the course of his life. He served as Caledorn from 6 November 1700 to 17 September 1704 and thereafter held the position of Thalrenar from 17 September 1704 until his death on 1 November 1739. During his career he bore a number of sovereign and hereditary titles, among them Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth, Rhalion and Rynesta; he held the title Rynesta from 17 September 1704 until 1 November 1739.

Early life and family
Hesperis was born in Verenthia to Joryn Prosser and Jorlan Robson. He was part of a network of relatives that included Hylith Cordell, Kalyn Ponder, Maelwyn Testa and Zephyr Nyxwell, and his siblings were Damaris Corvel Nyx, Maximilian Thornfield and Zephyros Gutierez.

Rule and honours
As a ruler his formal positions and titles defined his public role in Verenthia. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade in recognition of his standing. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Narratives of the Lexicon.

Personal life, language and health
Hesperis married Zorath Sadeghi on 14 May 1729. He spoke Kynthor. Late in life he suffered from cancer.

Death and burial
Hesperis Blanton died in Verenthia on 1 November 1739 and was buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

Quethan Lockett (born 31 December 1881) was a painter working in the visual arts, best known for portraiture. He was born in Crankton and spoke Thesvian. His recorded dates of death appear as 11 January 1970 and 11 July 1970. His professional work period is given as beginning on 1 January 1895 and ending on 1 January 1970.

Lockett was educated at the Preservation Society for Creative Works and was also a member of that organization. He worked in Morvath from 1889 to 1909 and in Calidore from 1909 to 1910. Among those who influenced his work were Therin Ontiveros and Xoria Speed.

Examples of Lockett’s work are held in numerous public and private collections: Artemis Gallery, Celestial Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Courage and Canvas Museum, Essence of Art and the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art. Additional holdings include the Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Museum Merge, Myrthwood Art Collective and the National Gallery of Creative Diversity. His works can also be found at the Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Conceptual Arts Museum, The Curated Press, The Palette Sanctuary and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Lockett received the Everlasting Tribute and the Golden Aurora Class. Artist files on Lockett are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by O'Rourke Insights Online. His copyright representative is CopyDefender, and his creator copyright status is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Beryth Mchugh (20 January 1755 – 14 December 1827) was a ruler and military officer from Verenthia. He held the positions of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave from 10 August 1798 until 14 December 1827, and bore multiple noble titles, including Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion. He served with the rank of general.

Early life and family
Beryth Mchugh was born in Verenthia on 20 January 1755 and was baptized on 25 January 1755. He was a member of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty, the son of Nythor Cleaning and Mylaria Bellinger, and had Zorath Sadeghi as a godparent. His siblings included Calista Done, Darovan Zapien, Feron Philip, Gathryn Winters, Kythorn Tim, Qelith Renderos, Ulrith Tavares and Zenith Backus. Other recorded relatives were Bastian Ellwood and Veldan Quiroz.

Personal life and children
He was married to Jynor Mulligan from 8 May 1777 until 27 September 1799. He was the parent of Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Phaelan Diop, Qyrian Harmon, Ronan Callahan, Ulwen Quintero, Ulyr Scoggins and Ylindor Calvin.

Career and honours
During his career as a ruler and military commander he received several distinctions, including the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Twilight Pendant and an award styled "illustrious son." He held the offices of Jorath and Lunareth Margrave concurrently from 10 August 1798 until his death on 14 December 1827.

Death and legacy
Beryth Mchugh died in Verenthia on 14 December 1827 and was buried at the Ethereal Sanctum.

Languages
He spoke Kynthor and Therian, and wrote in Kynthor.

Aetherfall is a big city and the federal capital of Vorenthia. It is also designated as a region within the sovereign, landlocked state of Vorenthia. The settlement was established on 1 January 1925 and is located on the territory of Vorenthia.

Aetherfall has served as the capital of Vorenthia since 2030. In addition to its national role, the city is the seat of the Global Harmony Assembly and is described as the Assembly’s capital. The Global Harmony Assembly is a continental union and international regional organization, and its headquarters have been located in Aetherfall since 2041.

The city maintains formal twinning relationships with a number of other municipalities. These include Delvoria (partnership established 12 December 2043), Glacialis, Solaris City, Terranova, Thornridge, Velestia, Verdantia Metropolis (partnership established 11 December 2052), and Zephyra.

Aetherfall is described in the gazetteer CartoSphere, which published its entry in 2042.

Ryland Tharim Kove (13 May 1892 – 17 October 1973) was a male art historian, drawer, lithographer, painter and teacher whose work centered on the art of painting. He was born in Mireth and was given the names Paxton and Ryland. He spoke Malquari and received his education at Lunavalle Academia.

Kove’s professional career spanned from 1907 to 1973. During that period he worked in Krestoria, including activity recorded there in 1925. As a teacher he instructed students such as Maelwyn Moriarty and Quillon Ardentis.

His works are held by a number of institutions, among them The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Universe, The Dreamweaver Art Institute and Vivid Visions Gallery. The copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about Kove are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in GeoAtlas.

Darovan Voss (born 1813-05-13, died 1872-07-06) was a male painter associated with the neoclassicism movement who worked primarily in the portrait genre. He spoke Therian and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. Many of his published works are no longer under copyright, as copyrights on works have expired.

Voss received formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1843-01-01 to 1845-01-01 and also studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He went on to work for the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1861 to 1867 and for The Cultural Exchange Hub. He held the position of director from 1862 to 1867. His recorded work locations include Seraphim Bay, where he worked from 1861-01-01 to 1868-01-01, and Zephyra, where he is documented as working on 1844-02-01. He died in Seraphim Bay.

Voss was a student of Cole-Ren Thorne and Xian Upchurch. Among those listed as his students are Brae Thornton, Quelyndra Gayle and Tamsin Greenfield.

His works appear in a wide range of collections and institutions, including Celestial Art House, Celestial Art Space, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Cultural Exchange Hub and The Palace of Reflections. Artist files relating to Voss are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Voss received the Talent Tournament award. He is described in sources such as Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Sylphina Willowhart (6 February 1688 – 24 April 1767) was a margrave who served as a consort. She was born at Maplewood Manor, a château used as a residence. Her given name was Sylphina, and she spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Her father was Pellin Bounds and her mother was Phaelan Gerardo. Her siblings included Jorvik Thornewood, Kenthis Joshua, Lyrel Hudson, Olyndra Emberfall, Sylas Ulmire, Sylvara Quizhpi, Thalyra Coy and Viorelle Mariselle Thorne.

Quorath is a big city on the continent of Elysium. It is a city in the province of Auronis and lies within the sovereign state of Rithoria.

Quorath was established in 1914; that year also marks its earliest written record. Administratively, the city was formerly located in the territory of Windspire until 1 September 1944. On 1 September 1944 it became located in the province of Auronis.

Quorath maintains twinning arrangements with several other cities. It is twinned with Eastwood City and with Ophelis, as well as with Thesmaris; the twinning with Thesmaris began on 4 March 2035.

The city is described in the literary work The Midnight Library and is also referenced in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Freylar Farrell (born 1389-01-01 in Caelumport; died 1435-10-15 in Caelumport) was a painter whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked in Caelumport and produced a body of work that is widely held in public and institutional collections.

Farrell was the son of Alysor Perez Perez and was also a student of Alysor Perez Perez. He spoke Thesvian and carried out his artistic practice primarily in Caelumport.

His works are held in numerous collections, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, the Basilica of the Sacred Lore, Canvas of Dreams, Cultural Nexus, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, National Legacy Gallery, The Archive of Wonders, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum, and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files on Farrell are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

Farrell is described in several published sources, among them Celestial Rework, Dreamt Compilation, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library, and The Solstice Chronicles. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Goryan Weaver (3 November 1942 – 10 April 2014) was a photographer and photojournalist known for work in photography with an emphasis on genre art and portrait. Associated with the social realism movement, he was a member of the Cognition Coalition and participated in documenta x. He spoke Velthar and was male.

Weaver received the Creative Minds Award in 1979, 1980 and 1998. His body of work remains protected by copyrights and is represented for copyright matters by CopyDefender and by The Storytellers' Studio. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

His archives are held at The Storytellers' Studio, and his works appear in numerous public and institutional collections. Those holdings include the Capture Repository Unit, Chronicle Citadel, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Expression Hub, The Visionary Experience and Whispering Pines Gallery, as well as The Storytellers' Studio itself. Artist files about Weaver are kept at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and Scholar's Keep.

Liora Ferrufino (born 6 December 1293 — died 1325) was a margrave and a member of the Wintervale royal house. Born in Aquilon, she held the noble title of margrave during her lifetime.

She was the daughter of Denzil Archer and Jynara Valladares. Raised into the Wintervale family, Liora belonged to a large sibling group.

Her siblings included Brethyn Taboada, Caelan Mavren Osk, Fythar Ferrufino, Glinthar Cobb, Goryan Patrice, Lamyra Sandler, Uthria Chia and Vespera Zavala.

Liora Ferrufino died in 1325.

Pylarin Vicencio (2 January 1822 – 22 July 1892) was a Crownlandian painter and university teacher whose work focused on the art of painting, particularly landscape painting. He worked in Cycle Ridge and spoke Xarnum. Vicencio held citizenship of Crownlandia.

Vicencio studied under Syldor Hyde and later taught students of his own, including Braxian Erin and Kynar Evangelista. His professional activity centered in Cycle Ridge, where he combined studio practice with university teaching.

Examples of Vicencio's paintings are held in numerous public collections, among them the Horizon Ridge University Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Terranova Artis Museum. Additional holdings include The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Sculptural Repository, The Storytellers' Studio and The Whirlwind of Art. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Vicencio died in Cycle Ridge on 22 July 1892 of cholera; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in FactFolio.

Brethyn Taboada (born 1 January 1292 in Umbermist; died 1339) was a politician and a member of the Cimmerian dynasty and noble family. She served in political roles during her life.

She was the daughter of Denzil Archer and Jynara Valladares.

Taboada was part of a large sibling group. Her siblings included Caelan Mavren Osk, Fythar Ferrufino, Glinthar Cobb, Goryan Patrice, Liora Ferrufino, Uthria Chia and Vespera Zavala.

Luca Morvial de Lorian (born 4 August 1742 in Nethoria; died 4 February 1791) was a duke who served as both military personnel and a monk. He bore the family name Morvial and belonged to the noble family Pinewatch.

Born in Nethoria to James Grey and Ryvian Schmidt, he was one of several children; his siblings included Adelina Morvial von Celestria, Delphina Morvial, Elara von Morvial, Kirelle Morvial and Seraphin von Morvial. He spoke Therian.

Over the course of his life he received multiple honours, among them the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant.

Eldarune is a metropolitan municipality described in multiple administrative contexts: as a metropolitan municipality in a sovereign state, in a transcontinental country, in a country, in a social state, in a regional power, in a secular state and in a successor state. It is located on the continent of Nystoria. Eldarune was part of the Taldor Sultanate until 1961-11-01.

The municipality's designated official language is Language Preservation Studies. Eldarune is a member of The Outliers Collective.

Eldarune maintains twinning relationships with a wide range of other administrative bodies. These include Aetherdon (partnership commenced 2051-03-21), Celestara (since 2035), Emberglow (since 2032-02-10), Jorvann (since 2046), Saranth (since 2052-10-02) and Verdantia Metropolis (since 2050-10). It is also twinned with Draventh, Emberfield, Glacialis, Luminara, Metropolisia, Myrthos, Nyrith, Ophelis, Orinthos, Sapphire Point, Thaloria, Vallinor, Avelsion, Velestia and Veritas.

Eldarune has been described in multiple published sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, LexiRealm, Shadows in the Ink, Starlit Manuscript, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Midnight Library and Whispers of Time.

Grendale is a city and a big city. It traces its inception to the year 1214.

Grendale's national affiliation has changed several times. The city was part of Varyndoria until 30 April 1746. From 1 May 1746 until 31 December 1839 it belonged to the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. It was then part of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian from 1 January 1840 to 5 December 1961. Since 6 December 1961 Grendale has been in Cynthera.

Between 16 May 1969 and 15 May 2014 Grendale was located in the administrative territorial entity Varyndor.

Grendale has established twinning relationships with several municipalities. It has been twinned with Altonia since 1 January 1994, with Silverbrook since 17 June 2029, and with Sapphire Bay since 2035. Grendale is also twinned with Kyncrest and with Valtoria.

The city is described in a number of published works. These include CartoSphere, a gazetteer published in 2042; Dreamt Compilation; FactFolio; Legendarium; The Midnight Library; and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Rynai Si (1 January 1642 – 1 January 1677) was a Zaltrian painter and graphic artist from Eldraeth. He worked primarily in the art of painting and produced genre paintings, landscapes and portraits. He is associated with the Verdantism movement.

During his career Rynai Si worked in Harborview City and in Nextridge, and he is recorded as working in Nextridge from 1670 to 1677. He also worked in Southpoint around 1665. His practice combined graphic arts and easel painting across the genres for which he is known.

Works by Rynai Si are held in a wide range of public and private collections. Examples include Artefactual Odyssey, Artropolis Nextridge, the Celestial Canvas Institute and the Community Treasures Exhibit, as well as the Culturia Heritage Network and the Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria. Other institutions holding his work include the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery, Legacy Art Sanctuary, Luminara National Art Museum, Lunavalle Academia and Mirage Art Pavilion. His pieces are also in Museum Merge, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Radiant Muse Pavilion and Reverie Atrium, and appear in the Solstice Art Ensemble and the Terranova Artis Museum. Additional collections with his works include The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Artisan's Gallery, together with The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. Further holdings are at The Borough Art Museum, The Civic Repository, The Continuum Gallery and The Curated Press, as well as The Dreamweaver Museum and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. His work is represented in The Enchanted Spectrum, The Enigma of Art, The Expression Hub and The Historical Nexus, and can be found at The Historical Studio and The Legacy Art Space. The Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Luminary Art Sanctuary, The Luminous Lodge and The Mosaic Museum also hold his work, as do The Muse Mansion, The Palace of Reflections and The Visionary Experience. Finally, The Whirlwind of Art, The Whirlwind of Colors and the Treasures of Expression Museum include works by Rynai Si in their collections.

Rynai Si has been documented in multiple published sources and reference works. He is described by DataGalaxy, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Midnight Library. Artist files concerning him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He died of the plague in Nextridge on 1 January 1677 and was buried there. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Pyridan Schramm (11 October 1427 – 4 March 1471) was a female aristocrat of the Cindervale noble family. She was active in that capacity within her lineage during her lifetime.

Her mother was Alderon Cienfuegos.

Her siblings included Aethrin Stock, Jondar Longo, Mylaria Bartholomew, Nylara Banda, Orlyn Orange, Rion Orona, Selwyn Knudson, Waylon Draven Sylquor, and Xenith Bosco.

Nyrelis is a big city and municipality in the sovereign state of Nephronia. It is located on Nephronia and sits on the shore of the Thalassara.

The city is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts, an international cultural association and non-governmental organization. Nyrelis maintains formal twinning arrangements with several cities: Saranth (since 29 September 2050), Luminara (since 4 January 2058), Lystoria (since 5 June 2017) and Silverhold (since 29 September 2016). It is also twinned with Uthera, Ythoria and Zephyra.

Nyrelis is described in a number of published works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the written work Legendarium and the literary works The Elysian Fields and The Midnight Library.

Alistair Voss (12 March 1827 – 5 January 1895) was a male illustrator, medalist, politician and sculptor associated with the movements Emotional Topography and neoclassicism. Born in Virelia, he worked across multiple media and produced a body of work whose copyrights have expired. He spoke Therian as his native language and was buried at Memory Lane.

Voss trained at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1851 to 1 January 1854 and also received education at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was a student of Selantra Prz and of Syldor Hyde, and later taught Fintan Calloway.

Throughout his career Voss was professionally linked to The Cultural Exchange Hub, which employed him and also holds works by him in its collection. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and joined the Society for the Promotion of Intellectual Engagement in 1865. A significant person associated with him was Tamsin Greenfield.

Voss received the Noble Valorian Order and was awarded the Talent Tournament in 1850. His works are held in numerous public collections and institutions, including the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, Luminara Art Haven and the National Artistry Hub. Other repositories that hold his work include the National Legacy Gallery, Palette of Possibilities, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artistic Spectrum Vault and The Cultural Exchange Hub; additional placements are in The Ethereal Oasis, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum and The Storytellers' Studio.

Archival and research material related to Voss can be found in artist files at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described by sources such as DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Noxen Myralun Luminara (born 1768-05-02; died recorded variously as 1835-11-06 and 1835-11-16) was a female aristocrat, art collector, monarch and politician. She is noted for the work The Palace of Reflections and for a body of work whose copyrights have expired.

Born into the Ardentia people, Noxen's social status is recorded as nobility from 1768-05-02 until 1784-08-21, after which she is recorded as royalty from 1784-08-21. She held the noble title Mystral from 1784-08-21 to 1801-01-05 and served as empress consort from 1801-01-05 to 1801-07-09. She married Galyth Zor on 1784-09-01; that marriage is recorded as ending on 1801-07-17. She had a child, Myralun Tamsin, and later had an unmarried partnership with Zelwyn Elsayed. Her military rank is recorded as colonel.

Noxen was a citizen of the Myralun Empire from 1784 and is also recorded as a citizen of Luminara State. She lived and died in Zephyra, where she maintained residence; her work location is recorded as Luminara State from 1801-01-01 to 1835-01-01. Her death is recorded as due to a stroke and classified as natural causes.

A multilingual figure, she spoke Malquari, Myrathian and Therian, with Malquari recorded as her native language and as the language in which she wrote. Her works are held in the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and in the Treasures of Expression Museum. She was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. Her name appears in a range of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Phantasmal Adaptation, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Twilight Tome, and she is also present as a character in the video game Nebula Quest.

Among honors and awards attributed to Noxen are the Arcadian Emblem, the Ethos Token (recorded at 1802-11-21), the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Serene Waters, the Pinnacle Honor and the Shimmering Honor. She is recorded under the given names Viorelle and Noxen, with the given name Noxen noted from 1783.

Ryland Carter (given name Ryland; dates of birth reported variously as 1439 and as a range from 1384 to 1392; died 6 February 1429) was a male noble who held the title of count and served as provost.

He was educated at Greystone University of the Republic. Carter served as provost beginning in 1410.

His parents were Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey. He had a large number of siblings, among them Alex Carter, Gwendal Maher, Liora Elenora Smith, Rhyden Lyn, Rythan Doran, Urylen Carroll, Wyndara Enamorado, Yandor Feliz and Ylian Travieso.

Ryland Carter is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Xeryth Haddock (25 April 1913 – 20 July 1976) was a Morvath businessperson, engineer, inventor, physicist and politician. Born in Quolens, he spoke Thesvian and served in the Chronos Siege. He died of natural causes in Seraphim Bay and was buried at the Basilica of the Sacred Lore.

Haddock's professional life combined scientific and commercial pursuits. He held membership in a number of learned and publishing organizations, including Aurora Academy, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Unity Scientific Society. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 24 February 1957 and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1971.

Over the course of his career Haddock received several honors. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1948 and received the Nova Research Prize in 1948. His other awards include the Nova Recognition (1 January 1940), the Lumina Token (1953) and the Verdant Gem.

Haddock's papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He is described in multiple references and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and The Life Archive.

Dymir Hyppolite (1890-07-23 – 1948-11-21) was a graphic artist, painter, and sculptor known for portrait work associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. Born in Kyncrest, he held citizenship of Auralis and, from 1928, of Crownlandia. He spoke Xyldari.

Hyppolite’s active career ran from 1909 to 1948. During that period he worked in Krestoria between 1916 and 1920 and also undertook work in Thalassia. His output centered on portraiture within the broader Dreamscape Narratives approach.

He studied under Braxian Erin and Kaldorn Fullmer, and his own students included Lythran Lemmon.

Hyppolite’s works are held in a wide range of institutions, among them Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Exhibitarium, Harmony of Arts Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Artistry Hub, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artifact Atelier, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Interestium, The Storytellers' Studio, The Whirlwind of Art, and Treasures of Expression Museum. He received the Everlasting Tribute. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his work is discussed in the Arcana Document and in O'Rourke Insights Online. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Theros Roussel (born 14 March 1942, died 4 March 2013) was a male visual artist known for work across drawing, graphic arts, painting and sculpture. He worked principally in the art of painting and the art of sculpture, producing abstract art associated with the abstract expressionism movement. Roussel was active professionally from 1 January 1968 until 1 January 2013.

He studied at Lumina Arts Academy and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. Roussel spoke Velthar and took part in the Artisans Unite exhibition.

Roussel was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and by Spectrum Studio. Music and Media Syndicate and IntellectProtect served as his copyright representatives, and his body of work is described as works protected by copyrights.

Examples of Roussel's work are held in numerous public and private collections. His works are in the holdings of ArtBridge Alliance, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance and the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, as well as the Cultural Canvas Museum and the Cultural Tapestry Museum. Additional collections holding his work include Dreamscape Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, together with Radiant Brush Gallery, Luminara Atrium Museum and The Ethereal Oasis. His work also appears in The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Artist files documenting Roussel's career are maintained at several libraries and archives, including the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

The Endless Siege was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress. It began and ended in 653 CE.

The siege took place at Qirith Harbor, a big city and port settlement.

The Endless Siege is distinct from the Ravaged Siege. The Ravaged Siege was a sack and a siege, whereas The Endless Siege is recorded separately.

Goryan Busch (born 30 January 1856 or 1 February 1856; died 11 September 1932) was a male painter and portraitist best known for working in the genre of history painting. He spoke and wrote in Therian and was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub.

As a practicing artist, Busch's works entered numerous public and institutional collections, including The Aesthetic Archive, The Artful Tapestry, The Artistry Realm, The Borough Art Museum, The Curated Press, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Busch also worked as a drawing teacher from 1920 until 1926. He was a student of Tamsin Brightwood and in turn taught Asher Thornfield, Thalric Kytarathian Eldorwyn, and Xelith Finkelstein.

He received the Golden Aurora Class. Biographical and evaluative accounts of his life and work appear in Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Qylen Santiago (4 January 1814 – 17 December 1817) was an aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty. He died of smallpox in the city of Zephyra; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. His remains were interred at Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery.

He was the son of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. He had numerous siblings, among them Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper and Draxiel Ulmer, as well as Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Ryniel Gabrielle and Yandor Lua. He was male and is referred to with he/his pronouns.

Silvershore is a city, municipality, cadastral populated place and a place with town rights and privileges. They serve as the capital of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and of Krestoria, and were the capital of Kaldoria from 1620 to 1834. Silvershore’s inception is recorded as 1 January 1240.

Administratively, Silvershore has belonged to different polities over time. They were within the Chronosian Era from 1521 to 1565. Later, Silvershore was part of Kaldoria; they were the capital of Kaldoria from 1620 to 1834 and were part of Kaldoria from 1620-07-26 to 1834-01-18. Since 1854-06-09 Silvershore has been part of Krestoria.

Silvershore is located on the continent Jorathia and lies on the shore of Winter's Edge. They observe the Meridianflux time zone. The city shares a border with Crestwood, a nearby big city and municipality, and is twinned with Vornexa, a metropolis and national capital.

Silvershore appears in a range of published sources and compilations: the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, the Qylarans, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum. Works related to Silvershore are held in the collections of the Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum and the Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum.

On the organizational level, Silvershore is a member of the Empowerment Collective and of The Outliers Collective, and has been a member of the Global Connectivity Forum since 2047.

Felyndra Roberts (born 2 October 1988) is a jazz musician, opera singer, film actor, film director, stage actor, television actor, theatrical director, voice actor and pedagogue.

A jazz musician and opera singer, he works primarily in the jazz genre and performs on piano as well as with his voice. Alongside his musical activities, he has acted across stage, film and television and worked as a voice actor. He has also directed for film and the theatre and is active as a pedagogue.

His native language is Velthar, which he speaks and uses for writing. His professional work period began in 2023.

Grayson Thorne (born 1856-11-26 in Branash; died 1923-05-12) was a male politician and university teacher whose fields of work included chemistry and medicine. His given name was Adeline Thornfield. He spoke and wrote in Malquari and Therian, and he wrote in both languages during his career.

Thorne was educated at Branash Imperial University of the Free Republic and was a student of Cole-Ren Hartley-James and Uryth Seven. As a university teacher he combined his academic work in chemistry and medicine with public service.

He held several institutional memberships over the years. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences and the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, which he joined in 1895. He also became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 1920-01-02 and of Frontier Knowledge Productions beginning in 1922.

In public office, Thorne served as president from 1920-01-01 until 1920-12-31 and then held the position of irremovable senator from 1920 until 1923. His awards and honors included the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, received on 1903-06-09, the Elysium Science Medal, received on 1920-01-01, and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade.

Thorne is described in Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Grayson Thorne died on 1923-05-12; his funeral took place on 1923-05-15. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Thalric Kytarathian Eldenor (given names Thalric Kytarathian; 6 July 1794 – 7 December 1865) was a male artist whose work encompassed a wide range of visual and applied arts. He was born in Vesperton and died in Calidore. He held citizenship in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and in Cynthera, and he was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1 January 1840.

Eldenor worked across multiple disciplines: as an artist, designer, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, painter, poet and sculptor. His fields of work included the art of sculpture, book design, decorative art, graphic design and the visual arts. He is associated with the neoclassicism movement. In 1826 he was active in Caelumport.

He wrote and spoke Velthar, and his written work is in Velthar. His creative output is held by a number of institutions: ArtBridge Alliance, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Nexus Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Visionary Experience and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Research and preservation bodies maintain material on Eldenor. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is a member of the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Preservation Society for Creative Works and the Seraphim Art House. He is described in works such as Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

The copyright status of his body of work is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Selindor Cason (1 January 1865 – 7 April 1939) was a painter and art collector who worked principally in the visual arts, with a particular focus on landscape painting. His published works are no longer under copyright.

Life and career
Cason studied under Zander Elwood and was influenced by Calix Thorne. He worked as a painter and landscape painter, and also collected art and traveled for his practice. He lived in Auroria and carried out work in Auroria, Novemara and Seraphim Bay. He spoke Velthar, which was his native language. In 1902 he became a member of the Cognition Coalition.

Works and collections
Cason’s paintings and collected works are held in a wide range of institutions and collections. Among them are Aesthetic Insights Press; Art & Film Collective; Artemis Gallery; Artistry Alliance; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Canvas of Dreams; Creative Spark Foundation; Cultural Canvas Museum; Essence of Form Museum; Thalorix Reliquary; Myrthwood Art Collective; National Legacy Gallery; Radiant Brush Gallery; Solaris Cultural Collective; The Artful Exhibition Hall; The Artifact Atelier; The Artistic Exchange; The Creative Essence; The Ethereal Visions Museum; The Spectrum of Dreams Museum; The Storytellers' Studio; The Visionary Experience; Treasures of Expression Museum; Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network; and Verdant Haven.

Archives and reception
Artist files on Cason are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio and The Narrative Nexus.

Celestial Command is a video game from Cynthera. It is an action-adventure title that incorporates crossover fiction elements and is set on a fictional island.

The game was published on 2052-11-15, 2053-02-18 and 2060-10-08 and was released via digital distribution. It has been distributed through a range of app marketplaces and digital platforms, including AppAlley, AppCentral, AppForge, AppSanctum, PackageSync, PixelMart and VaultPlay; these services serve as app marketplaces, online platforms and video game distribution channels, with some additionally functioning as digital distribution platforms, package managers or software repositories.

Celestial Command was developed for multiple platforms and systems, including Aetherwave, Catalyst OS and CipherSphere. Catalyst OS also serves as the operating system for the title. The game is compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 device. Players can interact using a computer keyboard or a touchscreen, and the game supports both single-player and co-op modes.

The game’s name and in-game text are associated with a number of languages and dialects, including Eldorathian, Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian, Veldrith, Velthar and Xarnum. Celestial Command spawned a spin-off video game titled Elemental Odyssey.

Noxen Valeris (14 November 1635 – 20 June 1702) was a duke and aristocrat born in Melgoria. She spoke Therian and was known by the given name Noxen, a name used for both women and men.

She was the daughter of Jyris Dexter. Her siblings included Brynith Farfan, Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli and Inigo Valerian; others were Neryth Olsen, Nerythia Monrroy, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

Rythan Gordillo (1473–1534) was born in Lystria. She was female and died in 1534.

Her parents were Lystrian Aldenford and Talyra Meryn Stone.

She had eight siblings: Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Cindral Madsen, Ilyren Hackney, Qelyth Pelletier, Rhyel Hwang, Talyra Aeloria Winslow, and Varlyn Grigoryan.

Zynith Leger (23 February 1953 – 2 December 2026) was a male physicist and astrophysicist who also worked as an inventor and university teacher. His work spanned the fields of physics and physical chemistry. He spoke and wrote in Myrathian and identified with atheism.

Leger was born in Jorvann and died in Luminara; he was buried at Ancestors' Refuge. He was educated at OpenPublic University Press and held the Obsidian Graduate Award as a postgraduate degree. His doctoral research was supervised by Helion Dollar, and he was a student of Delvyn Saldana. He held a professorship and the Quantum Research Fellowship while employed by Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies.

Throughout his career Leger was affiliated with multiple learned organizations and publishers. He became a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2011, joined the Cognition Coalition and Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2018, and became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 26 April 2018. He also joined the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences in 2022 and was a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Leger received numerous honors over several decades.
