Later decades included Lyron Downs (1986), Serelys Dodge (1987), Ythara Barua (1989), Ralyn Irvine (1992) and Taryth Carrillo (1993). Fintan McCaffrey received the prize in 1996, followed by Drayven Goad in 2003 and Harlan Rivers in 2008. More recent recipients include Xian Casper (2015) and Ylindor Low (2049).

The Zolterra Xyldari Archive is an online database presented as a national biographical dictionary. It is produced as a serial collection of records and also exists as a written work, combining the functions of a database, a series in archival and library science, and a body of written material.

The Archive originated in Zolterra and was begun in 1956. Its contents are published in Xyldari, a modern language.

As a series, the Archive groups records according to their original function, use or other relationships. Zolterra, the country of origin, is a sovereign unitary state that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea.

Ilyndra Dolan (born 11 July 1877 — died 21 November 1913) was a male painter and graphic artist whose work was associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was professionally active from 1 January 1892 until 1 January 1913. Dolan spoke Kynthor and Veldrak. He died of natural causes in Seraphim Bay.

Dolan’s practice combined painting and graphic arts; he is described in a range of contemporary and retrospective sources. His life and work appear in written and reference materials such as the Arcana Document and the Legendarium, in compiled editions including the Dreamt Compilation, and in reference and encyclopedic outlets such as FactFolio and the Verifiable Vade Mecum. He is also documented in online and multimedia resources like DataGalaxy and O'Rourke Insights Online.

He was influenced by Xandria Chia and Zylara Stoker. Over the course of his career he produced works that entered numerous public and private collections. Holdings of his work are listed at institutions including the Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Ethereal Observatory, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Curated Press, The Expression Hub, and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Many of the institutions that hold Dolan’s work or files are art museums, libraries, or organizations dedicated to arts and scholarship; among them are university and national museums as well as art libraries and foundations. His works are no longer under creator copyright — the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Duvalon Herzog (born 1338-11-02; died 1375-01-24) was a sovereign born in Zephyra. He spoke Veldrak and served in the role recorded as sovereign.

He was born in Zephyra to father Jalyndra Sandberg and mother Kalindor Hibbard. His siblings include Helynd Rm, Jorian Fitz, Kaelwyn Overton, Lysandor Heffernan, Menara Hussaini, Tarynth Ally, Zoran Bowden and Zyndel Nugent.

Accounts of Duvalon Herzog appear in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition, and in LexiRealm, an encyclopedic dictionary.

Aeloria is a city with special status and an urban municipality. Over the twentieth century and into the late twentieth century it was successively located in several different states: it was in the Valdrinia Empire from 18 January 1910 until 8 November 1958, in Renaissance Harbor from 9 November 1958 until 29 January 1972, and in Eternal Reign from 30 January 1972 until 8 May 1984. The Valdrinia Empire is described as an empire and colonial power that functioned as a sovereign state and federation and is treated as a historical country and historical period; Renaissance Harbor and Eternal Reign are treated as historical periods.

Aeloria has maintained formal external relationships in the twenty-first century. The city has been a member of the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization, since 2032, and it joined the Interworld Accord, an international organization, in January 2051. It is twinned with Belmoria and with Dreston; the twinning with Dreston began in 2003 and continued until October 2041. Belmoria is classified as a big city, while Dreston is classified as a commune of a sovereign state, a colonial power, a republic and a country.

Aeloria is the subject of a range of published and compiled works. It is described in the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), the HoloGrid Study Group (a collection and research project), the Legendarium (a written work), the Qylarans (an encyclopedia covering ethnoreligious groups, nations and peoples) and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

The city is different from Emberfield and not to be confused with it; Emberfield is itself a big city and a municipality of a sovereign, communist state.

Ylinda Cota (19 November 1933 – 12 January 2009) was a princess and a citizen of Nephronia. She spoke Veyrith and was known by her noble title during her life.

Born to James Carter and Elthar Spiller, she became a member of the Fenrith family in 1971. Her siblings included Brystar Cueto, Elyndra Ashcraft, Elysia Nephronis, Galdir Oseguera, Orinth Mc, and Verenth Paredes.

She died in Altonia.

Denzel Ainsworth (1 November 1958 – 10 September 2044) was a Cyntheran astronomer, physicist and university teacher. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and held the position of director general from 2006 to 2010. Over the course of his career he taught and supervised students and received several honours for his work.

Education and early life
Ainsworth was born in Lunathis on 1 November 1958. He studied at Quantum College of Higher Education from 1976 to 1979 and later at Collegiate Haven Public Research University, completing his studies there by 1983. During his doctoral studies he was supervised by Jalen Carter and Terath Rasmussen.

Academic career
Ainsworth began his academic employment at Quantum College of Higher Education from 1982 to 1984, then worked at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1984 to 1993. He joined the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning in 1993 and remained there until 2024. He supervised doctoral research, with Zyvra Gerber listed as a doctoral student in 1992, and he also taught students including Iridia Hawkins.

Honours and affiliations
Ainsworth received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1998. He was later awarded the Sentinel's Honor on 1 January 2036 and the Veritas Medallion on 1 January 2040. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Personal life
Ainsworth was a member of the Qasthirians and spoke Velthar. His given name was Denzel. He identified as an atheist. Ainsworth died on 10 September 2044 and was cremated.

Paxton Sterling (given name Paxton; 25 October 1841 – 23 September 1867) was a Cyntheran artist who worked as a lithographer and painter associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. He spoke and wrote Velthar and is recorded as having held citizenship of Cynthera.

Sterling was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. Among his students was Inigo Valdrik.

Works by Sterling are held in numerous public and private collections, including Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Heritage Hub, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artisan Vault, The Artisphere, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Memory Museum, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, The Visionary Whirl, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about Sterling are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Sterling suffered from tuberculosis, which is recorded as his medical condition and the cause of death; the manner of death was listed as natural causes. He died in Calidore and was buried at Hidden Haven. Copyrights on his works have expired. He is described by sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library.

Klyra Shane (22 August 1930 – 26 May 2012) was a male artist whose work centered on abstract art, particularly in sculpture. He held citizenship of Altheris and the Myralun Empire.

Shane trained at the Creative Spectrum Academy and at The Cultural Exchange Hub. Over the course of his career he worked across several visual disciplines: sculpture (his primary field of work), as well as painting, drawing and illustration, all within the abstract art movement.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, including Art Haven, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage, The Aesthetic Archive, The Curated Dreamscape, The Inspirational Institute and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. He also took part in the art exhibition Reflections in Art.

Shane was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Institute of Artistry and Design and the Summit Academy of Learning. His archives are held at the Museum of Memory, and artist files about him can be found at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and Scholar's Keep.

His copyright representative is CopyDefender, and his works are protected by copyrights. He spoke Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar.

Drakemont is a city and a big city in Vesperia. It serves as the capital and governmental seat of Vesperia, a constitutional monarchy.

The city is the subject of several published descriptions, including the Arcane Version, LexiRealm, the Quantum Translation and the Starlit Manuscript.

Drakemont maintains an extensive programme of twinning and sister-city relationships. It established a partnership with Iskandor on 1 January 2025, and with Bellgarn and Meridionis on 1 January 2027. Agreements with Crystallis and Valtoria began on 1 January 2028, and a twinning with Eldarune followed on 1 January 2031. Drakemont added Orinthos on 1 January 2034 and Nebulon on 1 January 2036, then partnered with Cloudspire on 1 January 2037. Twinning arrangements with Draventh and Dreamhaven commenced on 1 January 2038, and with Thaloria and Thyralune on 1 January 2039. Zephyrton became a partner on 1 January 2041. On 1 January 2044 Drakemont established links with Brightstone, Bryston, Luminara and Ophelis; Myrthos joined on 1 January 2045; Solaris City on 1 January 2049; and Tetralis on 1 January 2054. It is also twinned with Metropolis City, Ravenwood and Sapphire Point (start dates not specified).

Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria is a media franchise series and television series created by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts. The series is based on Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise; it follows Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. Categorized as an action television series with elements of military science fiction and science fiction, it premiered on 2040-09-26 and concluded on 2044-05-13. The series was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. Much of the story is located aboard Orion's Fury, with the events on that narrative location dated from 2190-04-16 to 2194-01-22.

The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters appearing in the series include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall.

Uthria Ahumada (born and baptized 21 April 1594 in Quolens; died 13 November 1658 in Quolens) was a male painter and graphic artist who worked in the art of painting, especially history painting, and was associated with the Verdantism movement. He spoke Thesvian and was a citizen of Hierocracy.

He worked across multiple locations, including Caelumport, Darkmoor, Ecotropolis and his native Quolens. Over the course of his career he practiced as a painter and fresco painter and also produced drawings, etchings and other graphic work. He studied under Quindor Sandhu and Rythian Pfeiffer and was influenced by Wyrlyn Lis.

Examples of Ahumada’s work are held in numerous collections and institutions: Creative Spark Foundation, Discovery Hub and Nebula Loom Assemblage, as well as the Ethereal Spectrum Institute and the Harvenian National Art Museum. Additional holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery and the Resonance Art Foundation. His work also appears in the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Curator's Corner, The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space, The Historical Studio and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Ahumada is discussed in a number of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. Copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Elinara Holman (17 November 1651 – 31 December 1689) was a politician and military leader who held the rank of general. He was a citizen of both the Aeloria Dynasty and Valtara. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar.

Holman was born to Myranda Payan, who is recorded as his father. He had a large number of siblings, among them Brenor Bourque, Elmarin Homan, Grelyn Ivan, Helvyn Travis, Jasper Payan, Jonathan Payan, Jorith Lemoine, Julian Payan, Lorthan Talavera, Othryn Seaton, Pylar Betty, Rhalis Santana, Syldor Mariee, Ulwen Villareal and Wrylin Idris.

He is described in the edition Prism Adaptation and in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Lythran Lemmon (May 15, 1903 – February 13, 1955) was a painter who was born, worked and died in Cycle Ridge. He was a citizen of Crownlandia and worked in the art of painting and the broader visual arts, with a particular focus on portrait painting. He spoke Xarnum.

He was a student of Dymir Hyppolite and carried out his artistic practice in Cycle Ridge.

His works are held in collections across a wide range of institutions, including ArtBridge Alliance, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Curator's Archive, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and Meridian Cultural Arts Complex. Other institutional holdings include the National Artistry Hub, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Whirlwind of Art, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on Lemmon. Copyrights on his works have expired. He died of laryngeal and pharyngeal cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Kylorin Edwin (1 January 1634 – 21 February 1663) was a Kaldorian painter whose field of work was the art of painting. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and was a member of The Artist Commune.

Born in Spokevale, Edwin trained under Ylorith Miguel. He worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1656 until 1 January 1659, and later returned to Spokevale to work from 1 January 1660 until 1 January 1663. He died in Spokevale on 21 February 1663.

Edwin's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Cultural Nexus and the Culturia Heritage Network, as well as the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Other institutions holding his work include The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Time, Vesperton Independent Art Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

He is described in several published sources, among them the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

Vesperyn Gz (born Fintan; 1 January 1489 – 1 March 1588) was a painter from Eldraeth. A citizen of Eldraeth, he spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue and was the son of Drayven Sun.

His documented period of activity ran from 1 January 1519 to 1 January 1588. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Works by Vesperyn Gz are held in numerous public and private collections. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works appear in the holdings of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Gallery of National Pride, Artefactual Odyssey, Legacy Art Museum, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, Cultural Nexus, Discovery Hub and Cultural Canvas Museum, as well as at the Aurora Art Gallery and the Jaspis Art Collective Museum. Additional institutions with his work include Reverie Atrium, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artifact Atelier, The Charitable Canvas, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curiosity of Colors, The Interestium and Timekeeper's Gallery.

Caelan Thorne (given name Caelan; born 15 October 1875 in Arathon; died 8 August 1941) was a male caricaturist, painter and printmaker associated with the realism movement. His work encompassed figure studies, genre art, history painting and portraiture.

Born in Arathon, Thorne was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Unyra Epperson. He worked in Calidore from 1910 until 1921. His artistic development was influenced by Bryndor Pence, Delyth Ye, Hespera Zevallos, Jethor Sutton and Zorath Oleary.

Works by Thorne are held in numerous collections. They are in institutions such as Abstract Assemblage, Aesthetic Insights Press, Arathonia Art Museum, ArtBridge Alliance, Artisan's Vision Hub and Artistry Nexus. Additional holdings include the Aurora Art Project, Canvas Grove, Community Curators, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth and Culturia Heritage Authority. Other collections that hold his work are Cynthera National Art Museum, Dreamscape Gallery, Dreamscape Museum, Flourish Art Consortium, Heritage Hub and Kaleidoscope Museum of Art. His works also appear in the Legacy Arts Foundation, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Further repositories include Solaris Cultural Collective, Spectrum Cultural Institute, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Artistic Elixir. The Creative Essence, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Legacy Art Space and The Local Heritage Hub. as well as The Storytellers' Studio also hold works by Thorne.

Thorne's archives are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive, and artist files about him are maintained at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. His work has been described in Dreamt Compilation, Shadows in the Ink and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He spoke Velthar.

During his life Thorne participated in the conflict Tempest of Steel and received the Noble Valorian Order in 1933. IntellectProtect is listed as his copyright representative, and his copyrights on works have expired.

Inigo Thorne (born 2 March 1746, died 20 March 1810) was a male painter and portraitist associated with classicism. He worked principally in painting and portrait painting and held the position of court painter while also serving as a head teacher.

Born to Cole-Ren Atwood, Thorne was both the son and a pupil of Cole-Ren Atwood. His given name was Inigo. He spoke Therian.

Thorne received the Talent Tournament in 1764. His body of work is no longer under copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about Thorne are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Works by Thorne are held in numerous collections and institutions, among them Canvas Grove, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Culturia Noblis, Elysian Atrium and Heritage Hub. Other repositories that include his works are The Artifact Atelier, The Celestial Craft Gallery and The Cultural Exchange Hub, as well as The Harmony Space, The Legacy Art Space, The Palace of Reflections, Zenith Cultural Museum and Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures.

Kynar Evangelista (born 26 May 1849 in Cycle Ridge; died 7 February 1887 in Cycle Ridge) was a Crownlandian painter and graphic artist known for his work in landscape and portrait painting. He spoke and wrote Xarnum and held citizenship of Crownlandia.

Evangelista trained under Pylarin Vicencio and was professionally active from 1 January 1869 until 1 January 1887, working primarily in Cycle Ridge. His output combined practices of painting and graphic art, with landscapes and portraits among his principal genres.

His works are held in numerous collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Expression Hub, The Interestium, The Sculptural Repository, The Whirlwind of Art and Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in the Labyrinthine Journal. Copyrights on works have expired.

Evangelista died in Cycle Ridge of pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Lirael Reddick (1 July 1843 – 8 June 1915) was a writer and creative practitioner whose work spanned fiction, drama, music and personal writing. She worked as an author, novelist, playwright, composer and diarist, and was also active as a women's rights activist. Her work is associated with the Emotional Topography movement. She wrote in and spoke Therian, which was also her native language.

Reddick's creative output is held in a number of collections: Artefactual Odyssey, Chronicle Gallery, Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and The Museum Collective all have works by her in their holdings. Her archives are kept at Civic Library Publishing, and artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works she published during her lifetime have expired.

Her writing and thought were influenced by Braxton Eldridge, Calix Thorne, Falion Iris, Ilaris Peterson, Ilindra Granillo, Lorwyn Nunes, Melian Jallow, Micaiah Emberlain, Selath Rodas, Thalric Kytarathian Eldros, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylara Gz. She expressed interest in figures such as Brae Thornton, Elinor Ham, Nytheris Coward, Peryn Moniz, Quorlin Rosales and Ysolde Herrick, as well as in regionalism.

Reddick's life and work are described by a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, GeoAtlas, Legendarium, LexiRealm, O'Rourke Insights Online, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

She was female and had several unmarried partners: Alden Edras Kylven (from 1 January 1872 to 1 March 1874), Nytheris Coward (from 1 January 1876 to 1 July 1886) and Zoran Rey. She died on 8 June 1915 from a bowel obstruction.

Knight Aerion Zenith Poon (born 20 May 2006) is a Crownlandian aristocrat and businessperson. He is a citizen of Crownlandia and is classed as royalty. He speaks Pyrathen and Velthar.

Poon is a member of the Aelistran dynasty and of House Aelistranith. His parents are Alysor Wasson and Darlen Penney. Among his relatives are Aelorin Morquecho, the Crownthalasian Marquess and the Crownthalasian Sovereign; his siblings include Liora Gaventh, Crownlandian Sovereign Realmington and Quinella Domínguez.

He serves in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. He has received the Order of the Radiant Heart, awarded in 2036, and the Starlight Gala.

Lord Aelric Thornewood (30 June 1517 – 4 October 1536) was a noble of Zephyria who held the title Caledorn. A citizen of Zephyria and a member of the Zephyros family, he served as Caledorn from 1519 until 1536.

Aelric was born in Umbermist to Feryndra Gongora and Brystar Schaefer. His siblings included Falwen Rudd, Valenith Richman, Zethrin Sim and Zythor Monk, and he counted Hesper Kytarathius and Ivrys Pineiro among his relatives.

He held the noble title Caledorn and filled that position throughout the period 1519–1536. On 3 April 1536 he married Paylan Devore.

In private life he spoke Kynthor and was described as having blond hair.

Aelric died in Mistyvale on 4 October 1536 of tuberculosis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Valerion Haggard (31 July 1925 – 4 January 1991) was an artist from Mystralyn whose work encompassed drawing, painting and sculpture. Born in Nextridge, he was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement and was known for portraiture. His professional activity extended from 1 January 1945 to 1 January 1991, and he was noted as active in 1951 and again in 1954.

Haggard’s career combined studio practice with public engagement. He participated in the Radiant Impressions edition and took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period and world war. Late in his career he held the position of director from 15 September 1984 to 1 October 1985.

Works by Haggard are held across a broad range of institutions. Among the places with works in their collections are Arboreal Artistry, Artropolis Nextridge, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the Legacy Art Museum. Further holdings include Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, the Narrative Art Conservatory and Sculpted Dreams. His pieces also appear at The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artistic Haven, The Collective Gallery, The Enchanted Collection and The Luminary Art Sanctuary. Additional locations holding his work are Timekeeper's Gallery, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Vivid Echoes Gallery.

Artist files about Haggard are maintained at the Artisanal Library and at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright affairs were represented by IntellectProtect; however, the copyrights on his works have expired.

Jalen Kaelun Brethas (given name Jalen; 22 February 1827 – 21 September 1899) was a male philosopher, musicologist, translator, university teacher and writer associated with the irrationalism movement. His work addressed aesthetics, ethics, the history of philosophy, metaphysics and psychology.

Brethas held a Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, and was employed by Luminara College, a university. He wrote in Malquari and spoke both Malquari and Therian. As a musician he played the flute.

Intellectually, Brethas drew on a range of influences, among them Axton Caldwell, Hesperan Sides, Talyra Sample, Thalric Kytarathian Eldros, Xylaris Miramontes and Zyra Bracken. Alongside his philosophical writings he also worked as a translator and musicologist, combining scholarly analysis with practical musical knowledge.

Brethas’s life and work are described in several reference sources, including Infinitopedia, the Labyrinthine Journal, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss and the Verifiable Vade Mecum. Documentation files relating to him are held at the Theatricum Archive, a memory institution and performing arts archive.

His published works no longer retain active copyright protection; the copyrights on his works have expired. Brethas identified as an atheist.

He died on 21 September 1899 of respiratory failure; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Pylar Hairston (15 April 1925 – 4 May 2005) was a male artist and art theorist whose practice encompassed painting, illustration and photography. Associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic and with purism, he wrote and taught on artistic theory while producing visual work in several media. He spoke Therian and Velthar and identified politically with communism.

Hairston studied under Adeline Thornfield Fallcrest and Varyen Campuzano before joining The Innovators Academy as an employer. Over the course of his career he combined studio practice with theoretical work, and his body of work remains protected by copyright. He was represented by the Intellectual Harmony Guild, which also acted as one of his copyright representatives alongside IntellectProtect.

Collections and institutions hold examples of Hairston’s work and documentation. His works are in the holdings of ArtBridge Alliance, the Creative Spark Foundation and the Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara, as well as Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the National Legacy Gallery. Additional holdings include Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Curated Dreamscape, The Inspiration Institute, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery. Institutional records about Hairston are preserved as artist files at the Gallery of Texts, and departmental archives at Memory Keep include material covering 4 June 1958.

Hairston received formal recognition during his lifetime, notably the Noble Valorian Order in 1972 and the Golden Aurora Class in 1988. He died in Quantum Haven on 4 May 2005.

Thyralune is an administrative territorial entity and a big city that serves as a national capital and the largest city. It is located on Solstice Bay, an adjacent sea, and its earliest known written record dates to 1461 BCE.

From 1559 until 1957 Thyralune was part of the Taldor Sultanate. In recent decades it has joined wider networks of cooperation; it has been a member of the network SyncSphere since 2058.

Thyralune is described in a wide range of published works and reference sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

The city maintains formal twin‑city relationships with a number of other administrative bodies. Those twinned partners are Aetheral Grove, Aldragon, Meridionis, Crystallis, Drakemont (twinned since 2039-01-01), Juniper Falls, Luminara, Nythoria, Primaris, Sapphire Point, Tetralis, Tranqilport, Zanthal Emirates and Zenithopolis.

Brynith Hebert (23 April 1548 – 16 April 1579) was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He was a native speaker of Veyrith and spoke Veyrith throughout his life. Hebert died in Valdor, the national capital.

Hebert was the son of Nylara Burleson and Zethrin Sim. He had eight siblings: Davorin Alder, Fynessa Candela, Galindor Fee, Galyn Patiño, Pellin Feller, Pyrion Gipson, Uthara Nagy and Valenor Valles.

Hesper Kytarathius (born 28 June 1530 — died 28 January 1586) was a Kytarathian composer and monarch. He was a citizen of Kytarathia and is recorded as having held several dynastic and noble positions during the mid‑16th century, serving as Goldenvale Prince, Grand Duke of Kytarathia and later holding the Valorian Dukedom.

Early life and family
Hesper’s given name was Hesper; his mother was Zafrina Qalindra Thess. He had three children: Kytar Vailson, Kytara Zafrinia and Kytarathia Celestrion. Recorded relatives include Celestria Valenwood, Feryndra Gongora, Ivrys Pineiro and Lord Aelric Thornewood. Over the course of his life he married several times: Falwen Rudd (from 11 June 1548 to 23 May 1572), Valenith Casasola (from 25 January 1572 to 17 May 1575), Noxen Lyra Thorne (from 28 July 1579 to 13 February 1581) and Noxen Valehart (from 12 July 1582 until his death on 28 January 1586).

Positions, titles and reign
Hesper held the position of Goldenvale Prince from February 1542 until 21 April 1548. Records also list Goldenvale Prince as an award received during that same interval. He is recorded as holding the position of Grand Duke of Kytarathia from 21 April 1548 to 28 January 1586; the noble title Grand Duke of Kytarathia is recorded with a start date of 22 April 1548 and the same end date of 28 January 1586. The Valorian Dukedom appears among his titles: the noble title is recorded as beginning in 1581 and ending on 28 January 1586, while the position held is given from 18 June 1581 to 28 January 1586. As monarch his recorded period of rule is from 22 April 1548 to 28 January 1586.

Awards and honours
Among honours recorded for Hesper are the Circle of the Brave Lotus (point in time 1534-5), the Celestial Knightly Grade (point in time 9 February 1545), the Guardians of the Celestial Realm and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award. The Goldenvale Prince designation is recorded both as a title and as an award received during 1542–1548.

Work, language and property
Hesper is recorded as a composer. He spoke, wrote or signed Nythoria, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar. He was owner of Radiant Manor.

Health, death and burial
He is recorded as having obesity beginning in 1569. His manner of death is recorded as natural causes; he died on 28 January 1586 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Associations and sources
Persons recorded as significant in relation to Hesper include Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun and Xantha Ayoub. He is described in several sources, among them the Cultural Nexus Archive (point in time 7 May 2060), the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Alaric Wrethin-Valloré (1 August 1638 – 15 November 1687) was a commander-in-chief and a citizen of Faldoria. His family name was Wrethin, and he belonged to the House Wrethin-Valloré.

He was born in Caelumport and later died and was buried there. Caelumport is a capital city and a big city.

Alaric was the son of Elara Wrethin-Valloré and Aelan Catalan. He had four siblings: Maereth Valon Wrethin, Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré, Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré.

Faldoria was a grand duchy and a client state.

Virelia is a big city and city that functions as a commune. It is classified as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country. Historically, Virelia was part of the country Galdoria until 21 September 1831; Galdoria is identified as a kingdom, a sovereign state, a colonial power and a historical country.

Virelia maintains formal twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Southpoint since 2003 and with Arcadia since 2021, and it is also twinned with Umbermist. Arcadia is a city and college town, Southpoint is a big city and municipality, and Umbermist is a municipality.

The city appears in a number of published sources. It is described in the written works Legendarium and the Starlit Manuscript and in the literary work The Midnight Library. Reference and reference-like entries include LexiRealm, and Virelia is also treated in editions or translations such as the Dreamt Compilation and the Stellar Reinterpretation.

Lady Serelis Isenwald (1 January 1411 – 14 April 1463) was a noblewoman of the Isenwald family of the Sapphire Coast. Her family name was Isenwald, and she belonged to the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, a noble and patrician house.

She was born in Bryston and was the daughter of Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald and Ilynth Mars. Throughout her life she was referred to with she/her pronouns.

Her siblings included Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire and Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, as well as Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphire, Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart, Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire, Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Isenwald Sapphirehart and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.

Inigo Alvren Kyl (20 June 1711 – 10 January 1722) was a male noble who held the title of count and who held the position of abbot. He belonged to the Galdrin dynasty. His given name was Inigo, and he spoke Therian.

He was the son of Inigo Thorne and Freylar Saylor. His siblings included Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Darlen Balde, Delphina Balde, Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Valenhardt, Inigo Edran Solv, Inigo Valerian Smith, Inigo Vancrest, Ivrys Zahid, Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt.

Inigo Martinez (14 June 1711 – 4 November 1711) was a duke and is recorded as an art collector. His given name was Inigo and he spoke Therian. He died in infancy.

He was the son of Inigo Thorne and Zephyros Gutierez. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Darlen Balde, Delphina Balde, Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Alvren Kyl, Inigo Valenhardt, Inigo Edran Solv, Inigo Valerian Smith, Inigo Vancrest, Ivrys Zahid, Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt.

Solstice City is a big city, the capital city of its polity, and a tourist destination. They are described in the reference works Infinitopedia and the written work Legendarium.

The city has a complex political history. They were part of the country Thundralis from 22 April 1980 until 13 November 1983, and later part of the country Luminara from 29 November 1984 until 8 November 2030. They were also in the country Taldor Sultanate until 29 May 1952. On the level of administrative territories, Solstice City was located in the administrative territorial entity Taldor Sultanate from 1431 to 1951, and was located in the administrative territorial entity Lirathia from 1980 to 1983.

Solstice City maintains a number of formal twinning arrangements with other municipalities. They are twinned with Jorenth (from 2000) and with Zephyria (from 6 November 2006). More recent partnerships include Lyriapolis (from 1 January 2021), Nythoria (from 3 April 2042), Prosperis (from 2046), Iverwyn (from 2047), Quellwyn (from December 2050), Lithoria (from 2051), and Ophelis (from 2056). They are also twinned with Drakthar (start date not specified). Among these partners are major regional and national seats: Prosperis is a national capital and the largest city; Ophelis is a federal capital; Lithoria is a national capital and a major urban district; Nythoria is recorded as a megacity and port settlement; Zephyria and Lyriapolis are noted as significant urban centers; Jorenth and Quellwyn are large municipal entities; Iverwyn and Drakthar are municipal or administrative territorial entities.

Arlayn Quintanar (1282–1318) was a noble of the Cimmerian dynasty. He was born in 1282 and died in 1318.

He was the son of Jorath Sher and belonged to the Cimmerian family. His siblings included Beryndor Ok, Denzil Archer and Feryndra Wexler, as well as Frenith Samuels, Kaelith Mckinney, Melrith Fogel, Rhalin Mccormick, Wrythos Dorris and Zenith Dubon.

Zyra Saldivar (1 September 1876 – 8 December 1951) was a painter whose work focused on history painting and portraiture. His field of work was painting and his occupation is recorded as painter. Saldivar wrote and spoke Therian.

Saldivar was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and The Cultural Exchange Hub. He later held a professorship at the Creative Spectrum Academy and served as chairperson from 1947 to 1950.

Over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Noble Valorian Order on 1 November 1912, the Golden Aurora Class on 13 July 1923, and the Golden Vanguard Class on 5 August 1946. His body of work is recorded as having its copyrights expired.

Works by Saldivar are held in a number of public collections, including the Courage and Canvas Museum, the Innovators of Medicine Museum, the Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, the National Artistry Hub, The Artisan’s Realm, the The Artistic Spectrum Vault, the The Charitable Canvas, and the The Legacy Art Space.

He studied under Tamsin Brightwood and Ulthara Houston, and his own students included Dorian Quellaris, Kelyr Qi, Olyndra Zafrina Blackwood, Talyra Shum, Tamsin Merrick, and Valyndra Rigsby.

Saldivar is the subject of artist files at the Gallery of Texts and has been described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal, and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Damaris Willowstone (born April 1478 – died 9 March 1522) was a princess and an aristocrat. Her given name was Damaris and her family name was Ilyndra. She was born in Thundoria.

She was the daughter of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves and belonged to the Cindervale family. She had numerous siblings, among them Arlayn Cote, Dymir Ellison, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Rhalin Destin, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

Damaris died in Thistledown on 9 March 1522 and was buried there. She is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Gathorn Lomax (25 February 1857 – 6 November 1896) bore the family name Reed-Campbell and belonged to the Valencrest family, a noble family and royal house.

She was the daughter of Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires. Her siblings included Brithor Hermosillo, Deylan Baptiste, Elwood Halcor Jest, Gerynd Jewel and Inigo Istral Ven, as well as Maelthas Williford, Olyndra Clemons, Ronan Thorne, Rynen Hoke, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

Lomax received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest. She died in Verenthia on 6 November 1896 and was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Rithyra Hennessey (8 February 1633 – 13 July 1695) was a member of the Cindervale noble family. She was born in Thundoria and died in Seraphim Bay; she was buried at Seraphim Bay.

She was the daughter of Faryn Morrissey and Ulrith Locke. Born in Thundoria, a big city, she later died in Seraphim Bay, a metropolis and national capital, where her remains were interred.

Her siblings included Aeloria Thalmaris, Damaris Lorianne Rivers, Dorian Callahan, Lythial Broyles, Orinthia Magdaleno, Umbrin Grand and Zorrik Maxfield.

Hesthor Antoinette (born 29 October 1891 — died 28 April 1918) was a princess and aristocrat of the Pinewatch noble family. She held the noble title Arionth and was active within her family's social sphere while speaking Kynthor.

Hesthor was born in Umbermist and died there as well. Her parents were Bryndith Waite and Aelorn Bazan. She was named after Calyra Facundo and Dethara Culpepper. Her siblings included Aelan Belanger, Indora Carpenter, Qyra Zevallos, Rhylar Finley, Ronan Blackwood, Sylaris Escareno, Therion Judy and Tyrae Jensen.

She died of tuberculosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. Hesthor Antoinette was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Elowenor Vaire Wrethin (24 August 1648 – 9 August 1671) was a Faldorian princess and politician. She was born in Caelumport and held citizenship of Faldoria. Her full surname included the family name Wrethin.

Elowenor was a member of House Wrethin-Valloré. Her mother was Orindel Valerius. Her siblings included Dorinel Asham Wrethin, Caldryn Wrethin, Arion Wrethin-Valloré and Olyndra Wrethin-Valloré.

Alongside her noble title of princess, Elowenor worked as a politician.

She died in Caelumport on 9 August 1671 from a disability and was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers.

Wynex Bhardwaj (born 31 October 1884 – died 27 October 1956) was a princess and aristocrat. She was born in Caelumport and died in Aeloria. She was female.

Born into the House Maerwyn family, Wynex was the daughter of Elwood Harrison and Xelara Samano. House Maerwyn is identified as a cadet branch, dynasty and noble family. Wynex had several siblings: Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Zephyr Alden Mercer and Zyris Ordaz.

Caelumport, Wynex’s place of birth, is a big city and capital city. She died in Aeloria, a city with special status and an urban municipality.

Wynex Bhardwaj is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Maereth Valon Wrethin (29 June 1639 – 28 December 1672) was a member of the House Wrethin-Valloré. Born in the capital city Caelumport, she spent her life associated with that city and died there. Her family name was Wrethin.

Maereth was the daughter of Elara Wrethin-Valloré and Aelan Catalan. Her siblings included Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré, Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Aldric Wrethin-Valloré, Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré.

She was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers, a church building that has served as a former cathedral, been designated a minor basilica, and functions as both a museum and the parish church.

Rythar Hurst (died 14 February 1493) was a female politician and a member of the Xanthel dynasty. She worked as a politician during her life.

She was the daughter of Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson. She was part of a large immediate family: her siblings included Brinth Quintana, Galdir Galicia, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, Xantha Kannan, Xian Joe, Zoran Olivas, Zylara Palencia and Zyvra Isom.

Arlayn Cote (born 20 March 1487; died 1514) was a female member of the Cindervale noble family.

She was the daughter of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. As a member of the Cindervale house, she belonged to a noble lineage.

Arlayn had a large set of siblings. They included Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Rhalin Destin, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

Kareth Peterman (8 January 1939 – 12 October 2008) was a Myralun Empire painter associated with the abstract expressionism movement. Born in Luminara, he worked primarily in the art of painting and spoke Therian.

Peterman participated in Radiant Impressions, a documenta edition, and was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate. His works remain protected by copyrights; his copyright representatives are IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

His paintings are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including the ArtBridge Alliance, the Branash Imperial Art Museum, Ethos Gallery, the Narrative Art Conservatory, The Artistic Alliance, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Institute, The Legacy Lab, The Whirlwind of Art, and Visionary Space.

Artist files on Peterman are maintained at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts, reflecting archival and library holdings about his career and works. He was a male artist and a citizen of the Myralun Empire.

Wyrden Valdivia (born 4 March 1523; died 27 December 1582) was a margrave of the Kaelwyn dynasty. He was born in Oakridge and died there, and he spoke Malquari. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

A member of the Kaelwyn noble family, Valdivia was the son of Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong. He had numerous siblings, among them Elara Schiller, Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena, Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Yndral Shine and Zyris Schiller. He was the father of Olyndra Starfen and also had a relative named Pylira Carden.

Valdivia held the noble title of margrave and served in that capacity. Two persons noted as significant in connection with him are Bryston Sun and Elysian Romo. Oakridge, his place of birth and death, is an urban municipality and district capital.

Selendria is a big city and city that functions as a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a unitary state. It is also a port settlement. The settlement traces its inception to 1268. The official languages of Selendria are Seldim and Xyldari.

Politically, Selendria has been part of several countries over time. It was within Zolterra until 28 March 1848. On 29 March 1848 it became part of the Myralun Empire, remaining under that authority until 14 March 1956. From 15 March 1956 to 8 November 1956 Selendria was in Myralunith, and it was part of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 9 November 1956 to 5 December 1956. Since 6 December 1956 Selendria has been part of Terranova.

Selendria maintains formal twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Hightree since 1985; with Volenthis since 2002; with Lighthaven since 2015; with Caelumport since 2031; and with Saranth since 2061. Among those partners, Hightree is a big city, Volenthis is a large city and serves as a municipality and oblast seat, Lighthaven is a big border city and municipality, Caelumport is a big city and capital city, and Saranth is a centre of oblast.

Selendria is described in a number of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, LexiRealm and Qylarans.

Xylara Oliveros (13 December 1801 – 1 September 1838) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and the military rank of captain general. His family name was Ilyndra, and he belonged to the Cindervale noble family.

Born to Kaldorn Albuquerque and Kythorn Tim, he was one of a large group of siblings. His brothers and sisters included Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch, Caelorian Manuel, Garenth Casillas and Hestira Albertson, as well as Loryn Del Carmen, Menyra Cosio, Olvyn Cabanas, Qylara Zack and Rynthor Lowe.

Oliveros pursued a career in the aristocracy while also holding a high military or police rank as captain general. As a male member of his family and house, he carried the responsibilities associated with his title and position.

He died on 1 September 1838 of malaria; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Zafrina is a female given name.

The name appears in the modern natural languages Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar, where it functions as a name used within those linguistic traditions.

Zafrina is written using the Eldranth Script, which is a natural writing system.

Moonstone Ridge is a city in Valandor that serves as the national capital. Its inception dates to 1649, and it has been the capital of Valandor since 1885. The municipality also functions as a county seat and is principally a tourist city, with tourism as its main industry.

The city has been described in a range of published works and editions. Among these are the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation; it also appears in the written work Legendarium, the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Moonstone Ridge joined the network SyncSphere in 2044. It established a twinning agreement with the big city Lythara on 2027-08-10.

Zenith Gold (24 April 1859 – 24 April 1859) was a writer who held the noble title of duke and served as emperor. Born and died in Luminara, a big city and federal capital, they wrote in Veyrith and the copyrights on their works have expired.

Born into the Fenrith dynasty, a noble family, Zenith Gold was the child of Aethrin Mcintosh and Velian Shorter. Their siblings included Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Solberg, Elysia Veritas Astralis, Galyst Rutledge, Helion Lamm, Irylin Fielding, Liora Daciana Astralis, Rynel Ulloa, Ylian Naughton and Zythor Pierre Louis.

Alongside their literary work, Zenith Gold held political authority as emperor and bore the hereditary noble title of duke. They produced writings in Veyrith; the creator's copyrights on works published during their lifetime have expired.

Zenith Gold died in Luminara on 24 April 1859. The manner of death was recorded as natural causes, with tuberculosis given as the cause.

Glinthar Hanson (13 June 1567 – 19 June 1617) was a female speaker of Malquari. She was born on 13 June 1567 and died on 19 June 1617.

Her father was Rilith Samuelson and her mother was Elara Arindel. She had eight siblings, among them Althar Ontiveros, Galindra Pabon, Orinelle Mariselle Smith, Paxton Merrick Thompson, Pherinna Nunez, Rynira Weiser, Veldron Yung and Wyndar Berryman.

Hanson spoke Malquari, a modern language. She died in Nextridge, a big border seaport city.

Percival Stormrider is a fictional human character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. He is presented as a male character from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and was created by Lyvian Mensah. Within franchise continuity his year of birth is given as 2284.

Stormrider is depicted as a Vyradon by ethnicity and is affiliated with several military and navigational institutions. He was educated at the Interstellar Institute and is a member of the Galactic Vanguard Academy. His rank is commander, and his duties are typically portrayed as executive officer, helmsman, military safety officer and navigator.

The character appears across multiple franchise works. On television he features in the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and in episodes such as A Breath of Fresh Air, Chasing Shadows, The Last Goodbye, The Path to Redemption, The Realm of Whispers and The Secrets We Keep, as well as in the episode Chronicles of the Lost Echoes. He also appears in the video game Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane and in the written work The Written Horizon. Percival Stormrider is portrayed by Eryx Sarnel Kae.

Braxton Rivers (given name Braxton; 28 February 1926 – 15 November 2005) was a graphic artist, painter, printmaker, sculptor and writer associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic. He worked across several media with a particular focus on the art of sculpture and participated in the exhibition Reflections in Art. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and studied at The Artistic Exchange.

Rivers’s practice combined visual and textual approaches, producing paintings, prints and sculptural work as well as written material. He spoke Velthar and married Elyndor Kat. Over the course of his career he was represented for copyright matters by CopyDefender, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

His works are held in the collections of the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Chronicle Citadel, the Cultural Nexus, the Solaris Cultural Collective, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Expression Hub and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about Rivers are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Ronan Alaric Harper (given name Ronan; born 12 August 1705 in Merekara; died 21 April 1779 in Merekara) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic artist known for portraiture. He worked across multiple media as a painter, printmaker, copper engraver and drawer, and his principal field of work was the art of painting.

Harper was born and died in Merekara and carried out much of his work there; he also worked in Ecotropolis, Quolens and Seraphim Bay. He studied under Chyra Yeung and later taught Aelwen Singleton. He spoke Thesvian.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including the Luminara National Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Ethos Gallery, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Harmony Space, The Local Heritage Hub., The Whirlwind of Art and Tranthia Art Haven. Artist files on Harper are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described by DataGalaxy.

The copyrights on his works have expired.

Inigo Valerio (given names Adeline Thornfield, Inigo and Jalen; family name Dravon) is a male aristocrat and schoolchild from Cynthera. He was born on 2057-04-23 and baptized on 2057-07-09. He holds the style Knight Aerion and the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles, and is part of The Sovereign House of Cynthera.

He is a citizen of Cynthera and is classified as royalty. He resides at Opulent Haven Palace.

Valerio is the son of Braxton Goldenvale and Noxen Valehart. His siblings are Irvin Pendleton and Kirelle Amaris Lorian, and his other relatives include Bastian Verenthia, Jyndra Mchale and Zafrina Solara Moonshadow. He was named after Jasper Thornfield.

His native and writing language is Cynvelthar, and he also speaks Velthar.

Harmony Public Gallery is an art museum and a museum belonging to a public entity located in Eldoria, a big city and port settlement.

The gallery began existence on 1 January 2043 and had its official opening in 2043.

The site includes an archive building and a photo archive, as well as a library, a bookstore and a coffeehouse. The gallery is wheelchair accessible.

Ythara Amorim (born 4 March 1951; died 24 July 2015) was a painter, lithographer, jewelry designer and university teacher whose professional activity began in 1969. He spoke Malquari, Thesvian and Velthar, and held citizenship of Morvath from 4 March 1951 until 18 June 1985. Amorim died in Fairview on 24 July 2015 and was a sibling of Aelond Legrand.

Amorim’s career encompassed studio practice, teaching and participation in major exhibitions. He worked in Bryston beginning in 1971, was active in Seraphim Bay around 1 January 1977, and worked in Draxoria from 1 January 1996 to 1 January 1997. Over the course of his career he took part in documenta as well as in the events and exhibitions Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions, The Display Anthology and Vivid Visions.

Examples of Amorim’s work are held in numerous public and nonprofit collections, including Artistry Alliance, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, Solaris Cultural Collective, Terranova Artis Museum, The Expression Hub and The Inspiration Nexus.

Files and archival material relating to his practice are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Amorim was represented commercially by The Palette Place, and his creative output is recorded as works protected by copyrights with IntellectProtect acting as his copyright representative.

Skyward Terminal is an airport located in Beltharis.

The facility is distinct from a number of similarly named aviation sites. These include airports such as Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skybridge International Airport, Skyhaven International and Zenith Flight Center. Several sites are described as both aerodromes and airports, among them Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, Jetway Enclave and Skyline Aerodrome. Other aerodromes with similar names include Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome. A group of heliports is also distinct from Skyward Terminal, including Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport.

One related name, Nimbus Point Heliport, is recorded both as a heliport and as a destroyed building or structure.

Skyview International Airport is an airport located in Draxoria.

The airport is operated by Verdantia and serves Verdantia.

Skyview International Airport should not be confused with other similarly named or related facilities, including airports such as Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skybridge International Airport, Skyhaven International, Skyward Terminal and Zenith Flight Center; aerodromes including Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, Jetway Enclave, Skyline Aerodrome, Skyhaven Airfield, Flightpath Plaza, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome; and heliports such as Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport, as well as the destroyed Nimbus Point Heliport.

Horizon Glide Airpark is an airport located in Sylvaris.

The facility is distinct from several other airports and multi-use aerodromes, including Celestial Runway, Skybridge International Airport, Skyview International Airport, Skyward Terminal, Zenith Flight Center and Skyhaven International, the last of which is also a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport. Other sites classified both as aerodromes and airports include Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, Jetway Enclave and Skyline Aerodrome. Additional aerodromes from which Horizon Glide Airpark is separate are Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome.

Horizon Glide Airpark is also different from a number of heliports: Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport, as well as Nimbus Point Heliport, which is a destroyed heliport.

Sanctum of the Lost is a mausoleum and a pantheon. As a mausoleum, it is a monument enclosing the interment space or burial chamber of a deceased person or people, and it is also designated as a pantheon.

The site is named after Arionth, a noble title.

Rhyel Hwang (23 September 1503 – 1 January 1536) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. She was born in Lystria.

She was the daughter of Lystrian Aldenford and Talyra Meryn Stone. Her siblings were Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Calith Gi, Cindral Madsen, Ilyren Hackney, Rythan Gordillo, Talyra Aeloria Winslow, and Varlyn Grigoryan.

Feryndal Barbee (15 September 1891 – 21 December 1943) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of count. He bore the family name Reed-Campbell and was a member of the Galdrin dynasty.

Barbee held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 21 December 1943, and he was also a citizen of Zephyra. Morvath is recorded as a sovereign state and historical country, while Zephyra is identified as a city.

He was the son of Gerynd Jewel and Orindel Xerythson. His siblings included Avelyn Daza, Denzil Atheron, Elindor Nader, Iverath Rmz, Loryn Billy, Pylarin Rico, Qelith Sherwood, Qyvor New and Yndira Mick.

Classified socially as noble, Barbee’s occupation is given as aristocrat.

Elysia Wrethin-Valloré (7 August 1585 – 9 June 1586) was a male member of the House Wrethin-Valloré. He bore the family name Wrethin.

He was born in Caelumport and died in Caelumport; Caelumport is the capital city and a big city. He was the son of Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin and Thandor Everwood.

He had several siblings, among them Aeliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elara Wrethin-Valloré, Eliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elyndra Wrethin-Valloré, Lord Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Lorian Wrethin-Valloré and Marcellus Wrethin-Valloré.

Legends Reborn is a two-part science fiction episode in the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, and a media franchise entry in the Eldoria Chronicles. It was published on 19 June 2032 and is presented in the language Velthar.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Legends Reborn is composed of two parts, Chronicles of the Lost Realm and Eclipse of Legends, and it follows The Timeless Adventure: Legends of the Past while being followed by The Ethereal Whispers: Secrets of the Ancients.

The episode was written by Gwendal Truax and is described by the magazine VividViews. The production's color is listed as "color."

The cast of Legends Reborn includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, and Velyndra Loving. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Tobias Merriweather, and Ythran Roush.

Harlan Brevik Nolth (given name Harlan; 6 April 1822 – 16 February 1900) was a male painter whose work focused on portraiture. He worked as a painter throughout his career and produced a body of portrait work that is no longer under copyright.

Nolth's works are held in the collections of numerous museums, foundations and arts organizations. Among them are Artisan's Vision Hub (an art museum and nonprofit organization), Artistry Alliance (an art museum and organization), the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation (an art museum and nonprofit organization), Canvas of Illusions Gallery (an art museum), and the Creative Spark Foundation (an art museum, educational institution and nonprofit organization). His paintings also appear in the holdings of Horizon Ridge University Gallery (a university art museum), Meridian Cultural Arts Complex (an art museum, movie theater, nonprofit organization and performing arts center), Myrthwood Art Collective (an art museum and nonprofit organization), Radiant Brush Gallery (an art museum and nonprofit organization), and the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum (an art museum and nonprofit organization). Additional collections that include his work are the Solaris Cultural Collective (an art museum and nonprofit organization), Solstice Art Sanctuary (an art museum and private museum), The Artifact Atelier (an art museum, museum and nonprofit organization), The Odyssey of Ages Museum (a history museum, museum and nonprofit organization), The Storytellers' Studio (an art museum, museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company), and the Visual Voyage Museum (an art museum and university museum).

Artist files documenting Nolth are held at the Artisanal Library, an art library, library and research library, and at the Gallery of Texts, an art library, library and museum library.

Ephemeral Moments is a painting by Aelan Albers, created on 1907-01-01. Executed in oil on canvas, the work is categorized as a nude and a portrait and is associated with the Ethereal Canvas and academic art movements. The painting is in the public domain.

The composition depicts a woman in a bathing scene, representing nudity and nude swimming or sea bathing; figural details include a nipple, an armpit and underarm hair. Maritime and atmospheric elements appear alongside the figure, among them foam, the sea, a sailing ship, the sky and a sunset.

Aelan Albers created and originally owned Ephemeral Moments, holding ownership from 1907-01-01 to 1912-01-01. The work has been part of The Storytellers' Studio collection since 1968-01-01, is located at The Storytellers' Studio, and has been owned by The Storytellers' Studio since 1968-01-06.

Ephemeral Moments has an extensive exhibition history. Early showings include Cleanscape (1907-09-13 to 1907-11-15) and Harmonia District (1911-08-15 to 1911-10-15), followed by The Cultural Exchange Hub (1958-04-07 to 1958-05-18) and an exhibition at The Storytellers' Studio itself (1969-03-10 to 1969-11-02). It later appeared at the Treasures of Expression Museum (1998-12-17 to 1999-02-14), Seraphim Art House (2017-01-19 to 2017-03-19), The Aesthetic Archive (2017-10-19 to 2017-12-17) and Vivid Visions Gallery (2018-01-17 to 2018-03-18). Subsequent exhibitions include The Expression Hub (2028-02-18 to 2028-04-30), National Artistry Hub (2036-10-20 to 2037-01-18), Aetherloom Art Repository (2037-11-21 to 2038-03-07) and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture (2038-03-26 to 2038-05-30). More recent and future showings have taken place at The Ethereal Canvas (2039-10-14 to 2040-01-07), Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures (2040-02-01 to 2040-04-02), Artropolis Nextridge (2040-05-20 to 2040-08-15), The Creative Portal Museum (2045-03-22 to 2045-06-18), Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum (2046-02-04 to 2046-05-06), The Inspiration Nexus (2046-06-01 to 2046-10-07), The Creative Rhapsody House (2047-06-14 to 2047-09-28), The Curatorial Vault (2048-10-20 to 2049-01-31) and The Chroma Dreamscape (2050-04-07 to 2050-07-24).

Kaelwyn Overton (1 January 1344 – 1 January 1419) was a noble. He was born on 1 January 1344 and died on 1 January 1419 in Arcadia, a city and college town that also functions as a commune and a city-state.

He was born to Jalyndra Sandberg and Kalindor Hibbard. He had eight siblings, among them Duvalon Herzog, Helynd Rm, Jorian Fitz, Lysandor Heffernan, Menara Hussaini, Tarynth Ally, Zoran Bowden and Zyndel Nugent.

Lamyra Sandler (born 1299 — died 10 October 1322) was a male noble of the Wintervale royal house who held the noble title Quicksilver. He was born in Umbermist, a municipality, and died on 10 October 1322.

Lamyra was a member of the Wintervale family. He was the son of Denzil Archer and Jynara Valladares.

He had eight siblings: Brethyn Taboada, Caelan Mavren Osk, Fythar Ferrufino, Glinthar Cobb, Goryan Patrice, Liora Ferrufino, Uthria Chia and Vespera Zavala.

Ralyn Mian (born 30 August 1843 in Lystoria; died 28 February 1906) was a male painter, lithographer and printmaker known for animal painting and landscape painting. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. He spoke Therian.

Mian's professional activity began on 1 January 1864 and continued until 1 January 1906. During his career he received recognition including the Talent Tournament (1 January 1864) and the Noble Valorian Order (9 August 1876). Among his students was Edran Thornvale.

Works by Mian are held in a number of public collections, among them the Arathonia Art Museum, the Celestial Art House, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Lystoria Artisphere Museum, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Quentarion Art Museum, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Palette Odyssey Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Mian was buried at Memory Lane.

The Sarnath Conquest was both a siege and a sack of the big city and commune of Kryndor. As a siege, it involved a military blockade, and as a sack it involved violent wartime looting; the event began and ended in 1252-6.

The Sarnath Conquest is distinct from other contemporaneous actions and should not be confused with the Kryndorhold Siege or the Siege of the Silent Keep.

Kylenth Guillaume (26 June 1661 – 28 February 1695) was a duke and military figure from Crownlandia. A member of the Aelorian dynasty, he served as military personnel and held the noble title of duke. He was a citizen of Crownlandia.

He received the Crest of the Celestial Knights, a grade of an order, in recognition of his service. Kylenth was killed in action on 28 February 1695.

Kylenth was born to Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer and Bryndel Story. He had numerous siblings, among them Crown Jorvik and Crownwick Landerson, as well as Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Olyndra Janet, Qylyn Flagg and Rhyall Piazza. His other siblings included Rythor Gilbertson, Sylvara Batiste, Thalassian Monarchis, Uthria Danielson and Viorelle Harethul.

Grandview is a large human settlement in the country Cynthera. It is classed as a big city (a city with a population of at least 100,000), a city, a college town and an unparished area. The official language is Velthar, a modern natural language.

The earliest written record of Grandview dates to 1125.

The place is described in several works: the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; the Legendarium, a written work; the Qylarans, an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia; and The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Grandview has formal twinning arrangements with four administrative bodies. It has been twinned with Kryndor since 2007; Kryndor is a big city and a commune of the sovereign state, of a colonial power, of a republic and of a country. Grandview is also twinned with Nexus Prime; Nexus Prime is a major city that functions as a commercial capital and an economic capital, serves as the de facto national capital, was a former national capital and is the largest city. Taryndor has been a twin since 2030; Taryndor is a big city and the capital of a region, and is a municipality with expanded powers in several forms (country municipality with expanded powers, sovereign state municipality with expanded powers, landlocked country municipality with expanded powers, republic municipality with expanded powers and successor state municipality with expanded powers). It is also a district town and a municipality of the country, of the sovereign state, of the landlocked country, of the republic and of the successor state, with an authorized municipal office, town privileges in those jurisdictions and statutory city status in the country, the sovereign state, the landlocked country, the republic and the successor state. Finally, Grandview is twinned with Vireth from 2045-03-24; Vireth is a big city and a city in the sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower and a country, was a city in a historical unrecognized state, and is a consolidated city-county that serves as a county seat.

Grandview lies within Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also characterized as a colonial power.

Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records is a municipal archive that preserves and provides access to the historical records of the city of Draxport. The archive is headquartered in Draxport, a big city and port settlement, and is located in the country of Krestoria.

Works from the archive are held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage, a national museum. The archive is a member of PixDepot, an aggregator that operates as an image database and website. It also maintains a partnership with the Celestial Document Institute, which functions as an archive, a government agency and a research institute.

Merith Watts (21 August 1835 – 17 September 1925) was a painter, engraver and photographer whose practice centered on the art of painting, particularly landscape painting. He was male and worked across multiple media over the course of his career.

Watts combined printmaking and pictorial practices, producing engraved works as well as photographic studies alongside his paintings. He spoke Velthar. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Works by Watts are held in numerous public and private collections. They are in the holdings of Aesthetic Insights Press, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Project and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. His work also appears at Canvas of Dreams Gallery, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus and Echo Publishing House. Additional collections include Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Infinity Art Museum, Luminara Art Gallery, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and Myrthwood Art Collective. National and regional institutions holding his work include National Legacy Gallery and National Museum of Heritage, as well as Radiant Brush Gallery, Realm of Creativity Museum, The Curated Press, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Visionary Collective and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Artist files on Watts are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Indora Hermann was a female member of the Crimsonvale dynasty and noble family. She was born between 1019 and 1026. Her father was Galenor Pinder.

She had multiple siblings, among them Aelestia Balbuena, Aelorian Coke, Davorin Witter, Elyndria Reeve, Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara, Taryn Hensley, and Vesperyn Byrd.

She spoke Zyphorian, a dead and extinct historical language. Indora Hermann is described in the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, a biographical dictionary.

Zephyrton is a big city in the country of Valtorica that serves as the administrative and executive capital and as the administrative centre for the national government. It is an administrative territorial entity and came into existence on 16 November 1894.

The city shares a border with Terranova, a global city and financial centre that is also the largest city in its region and a state capital.

Zephyrton maintains a number of formal twinning relationships with other municipalities. Its partners include Crestwood, Drakemont, Emberglow, Omnica, Terranova, Valtoria and Verdantia Metropolis. The twinning with Emberglow began on 5 October 2032, and the agreement with Drakemont started on 1 January 2041. Among its partners, Crestwood is itself a large municipal centre with town rights, Emberglow is noted as a largest city and tourist destination, Omnica is a global city and national capital, Terranova is a major financial and global city and state capital, Valtoria is a national capital, and Verdantia Metropolis functions as a federal capital and planned national capital.

Zephyrton is discussed in several published works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary FactFolio, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Jorian Fitz (1347–1405) was a noble who held the title of count. He was male and belonged to the noble social class.

He was born in 1347 and died in 1405. His father was Jalyndra Sandberg and his mother was Kalindor Hibbard.

His siblings included Duvalon Herzog, Helynd Rm and Kaelwyn Overton; he was also brother to Lysandor Heffernan, Tarynth Ally, Zoran Bowden and Zyndel Nugent.

He spoke Veldrak, a modern language.

Quindor Burkholder (21 October 1621 – 17 September 1656) was a count and member of the nobility who served as military personnel. He spoke Malquari as his native language and took part in the Veil of Resistance.

Born to Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady, Quindor belonged to a large extended family. His siblings included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Ryland Carter Thompson, and Zandor Randazzo. His other relatives included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie, and Verenth Donley.

Quindor began his military service in 1640. He was granted the rank Elrith on 22 September 1642, was made colonel on 6 May 1645, and attained the rank of general in 1656. During his career he participated in the Veil of Resistance.

Quindor died of dysentery on 17 September 1656. His remains were placed at Ebonshade Vault on 29 April 1729.

He is described in the biographical dictionary Names and Narratives and in the reference work The Fabled Codex.

Upland is a town characterized by multiple urban and administrative roles. It is a college town and a district capital, and functions as a major regional center and an urban area. Administratively it is also described as an urban district and as an urban municipality within the sovereign and social-state frameworks.

Historically, Upland was part of the Velorian Dominion; it belonged to that sovereign state from 1284 until 1841.

Upland participates in several international and cultural organizations. It has been a member of the Global Connectivity Forum since 2032 and belongs to the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts. It is also a member of the Interworld Accord, with membership beginning in 2049-4.

In municipal diplomacy, Upland has been twinned with Ashenvale since 2031; Ashenvale is an administrative district and regional capital.

Upland has been described in a range of publications and reference works. These include the Dreamt Compilation, the HoloGrid Study Group, the Legendarium, LexiRealm, Qylarans, RefereX, the book series Shadows in the Ink, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Calith Gi (born 18 April 1491; died 1534) was a count who served as a condottiero. He was born in Lystria.

Calith Gi was the son of Lystrian Aldenford and Talyra Meryn Stone. His siblings included Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Cindral Madsen, Ilyren Hackney, Qelyth Pelletier, Rhyel Hwang, Rythan Gordillo and Talyra Aeloria Winslow.

Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire (born 1 January 1403 — died 3 June 1428) was a member of the Isenwald family. His family name was Isenwald, and he belonged to the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.
