They were established on 29 March 1732 and were named after a pine forest. A notable appointment associated with the city took place on 5 February 1881. They experienced an invasion that lasted from 18 January to 18 April 1933.

Aetherwyn joined the SyncSphere network in 2053 and has been a member of that international network since then.

They maintain twinning relationships with several other cities and administrative bodies. Those partnerships include Cycle Ridge, a national capital noted as a largest city and a cycling city; Elysoria, a large city and municipality described in multiple state contexts; Lythoria, an administrative territorial entity and national capital; Stormwatch, a big city; Trivandria, a big city that is also a border city, capital region and largest city; Twilight Grove, a big city and prefecture-level sub-province division; and Valendor, a big city and port settlement.

Dawnspire is a city and municipality that functions as a cadastral populated place in the country and holds town rights and privileges.

Historically, Dawnspire was part of Kaldoria from 1620-07-26 until 1834-01-18. Since 1854-06-09 Dawnspire has been in Krestoria.

The settlement is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Dawnspire is twinned with the city of Westridge.

Xelthoria is a municipality that functions within a sovereign state, a realm and a country, and is also recognized as a municipality associated with a historical nationality.

The municipality lies on Solstice Bay, an adjacent sea that also serves as a drainage basin and is characterised as a Mediterranean sea.

Xelthoria maintains a broad set of twinning arrangements with other administrative bodies. Its partners include Astral Grove, a city under municipal jurisdiction; Auroralis, a city (twinning established in 2030); and Dawnshollow, a municipality that exists in multiple forms and is a place with town rights and privileges. Echo Valley is a rural municipality, while Gableshire is a civil parish and market town. Ostendre is a municipality in a sovereign state, a unitary state, a grand duchy and a landlocked country as well as a municipality of a country. Harborfall is a commune and a port settlement. Holoset is a border city and town. Meadowbrook is a human settlement that also serves as a municipality in several jurisdictions and is a town. Noventis and Thundraxis are cities. Redwater is a city and the municipality seat. Rosewood Heights is both a municipality and a town in several jurisdictions. Ryloria is a municipality of the country. Sandstone is a town. Sapphire Grove is a city and municipality and is also identified as a town in some contexts. Uldoria is a commune in multiple forms of state organization, and Umberfall is a municipality that holds the title of city across several jurisdictions.

The Mosaic Museum was a museum headquartered in the city of Southpoint in Krestoria. It was both located in and administered from Southpoint.

Some works from the Mosaic Museum are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, an art museum.

The Mosaic Museum was replaced by The Dreamweaver Museum.

Vireth is a big city and consolidated city-county that serves as a county seat. It is also recognized as a city in the sovereign state, the constitutional republic, the federal republic, the superpower, the country and the historical unrecognized state. The city began in 1817 and was named after Inigo Martinez.

Vireth maintains formal twinning relationships with several municipalities. Its partners include Equinoxia., which is a city; Grandview, a big city, city, college town and unparished area (twinning began 2045-03-24); Nythra, a big city and a commune of sovereign state, commune of colonial power, commune of republic and commune of country; and Eryndale, a big city and college town that is a state capital in sovereign state, state capital in social state and state capital in country, an urban district of federated state of sovereign state, urban district of federated state of social state and urban district of federated state of country, and an urban municipality in sovereign state, urban municipality in social state and urban municipality in country (twinning began 2016-04-01).

Vireth is described in a range of published works and editions. These include the versions Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation; the written work Legendarium; the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library; and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Nytheris Tang (20 February 1834 – 15 June 1897) was a Valorean artist known for work in Emotional Topography and the art of painting. He worked across history painting and portrait genres and was active as a drawer, painter and sculptor. He held citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and was a member of the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. Tang received the Golden Aurora Class and the Golden Vanguard Class.

Born in Lurendale, Tang's professional activity spanned from 1 January 1849 to 1 January 1897. He worked in Lurendale for a brief period from 1 January 1850 to 1 May 1850, and is recorded as working in Harborview City at a point in time on 1 January 1893. Late in his career he worked on Frostmere Isle from 1 January 1896 until 1 January 1897, and he also had ties to Krestoria. He was a student of Darovan Voss and later taught Adeline Thornfield Drovain and Kaelith Arendell. Drayven Guerrier and Ulyr Leary acted as his sponsors, and his work was influenced by Drayven Guerrier and Quelyndra Gayle. Tang was the sibling of Qalir Albers. He spoke and wrote Therian and the Valorean Tongue. After his death he was buried at Gentle Hills.

Tang's works are held across a broad range of public and private collections. His paintings and other works appear in institutions such as Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Artoria Capital Museum and the Cultural Canvas Museum. Other collections holding his work include Culturia Noblis, Curator's Archive, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and Expressions of Our Community. Additional holdings are at Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Infinity Art Museum and Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum. His works are also in the collections of Legacy Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery and the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art. Further repositories include Quentarion Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Aesthetic Archive. The Artifact Arena, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Borough Art Museum also preserve his work, as do The Collective Canvas, The Collective Gallery , The Curatorial Institute and The Expression Hub. The Memory Museum, The Mosaic Museum and Treasures of Time likewise hold Tang's works. Artist files about Tang are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio , Infinitopedia and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Xelith Santos (born 4 August 1949 in Avelsion; died 8 April 2050 in Radiant Heights) was a Solandrian artist known for her work in painting, drawing and sculpture. She worked across several media as an artist, drawer, painter and sculptor, and was associated with the abstract expressionism movement. Her field of work is cited as the art of painting, and her professional activity is recorded as taking place from 1978 to 2043. She was a centenarian.

Santos's works are held in a number of public and private collections. Institutions that include her work in their holdings include Artistry Alliance, Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Citadel, Dreamscape Museum, Gallery of Dreams, Radiant Brush Gallery, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage and The Visionary Experience.

Documentation and archival material about Santos are maintained in library and archival collections. Artist files about her are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and she is described in the bibliography Narrative Nexus.

Her copyright interests are managed by IntellectProtect and by the Music and Media Syndicate, and her body of work published during her lifetime is recorded as works protected by copyrights.

Santos was a citizen of Solandria and spoke Velthar. She was married to Mistran Beltre.

Yelith Aiello was a Chronorian philosopher, politician, theologian and writer who is venerated as a saint associated with beekeepers. Sources record multiple possible birth dates—378 CE and 389 CE are both attested, while other records give an earliest possible date of 372 CE and a latest of 379 CE—and he died on 4 April 436. He held citizenship of Chronoria and was active during Arcandor.

Aiello was born in Nymara and belonged to the Yothrins people. He spoke and wrote in Nythoria and also spoke Elarithian. Much of his professional life took place in Bryston, which is also recorded as the place of his death. In Bryston he combined political activity with philosophical and theological work and produced written works in Nythoria.

His writings are described across a wide range of reference and literary sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, FactFolio, ItemVerse, Legendarium, LexiRealm, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, Starlit Manuscript, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Whispers of Time. Some of his works are held in the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Helynd Bose (given name Jalen; 31 October 1955 – 5 May 2051) was a male aristocrat and citizen of Zolterra. Across his life he received several honors, including the Ethos Token, the Order of the Gilded Compass and the Order of the Radiant Heart.

From his birth on 31 October 1955 until 19 February 1985 he held the noble title duke and used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion; during that period he was classed as royalty. On 19 February 1985 his social classification became nobility.

Bose belonged to the Velorian family. His father was Ryland Zolterras and his mother was Damaris Elowen Carter. His stepparent was Delphina Orimund Shyr. His siblings included Glynor Rutherford, Kaelar Smile, Liora Zoltan and Pyreth Cepero.

He spoke Velthar and Xyldari, with Xyldari as his native language. By occupation he was an aristocrat.

Elaria Pelaez (born 20 March 1848 and also recorded as 31 March 1848; died 21 February 1891) was a male writer from the Myralun Empire. He worked across several literary roles and was active in the late 19th century.

Pelaez held multiple occupations as a historian, literary critic, novelist, opinion journalist, playwright, prose writer, teacher and writer. His fields of work included belletristic literature and literary criticism, and he worked primarily in the prose genre; his documented work period runs from 1866 to 1891.

He was employed by OpenPublic University Press. His works are held in the collections of the National Legacy Gallery and The Expression Hub, while artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts and documentation files at Theatricum Archive. The copyright status of his body of work is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Pelaez spoke Elvishar and Myrathian, with Elvishar recorded as his native language, and he wrote in Myrathian. His work was influenced by Jenthis Hammad and Valendriel Oakshadow.

He died in Luminara and is buried at Ancestors' Refuge, with a recorded start time of 1970-05-31. He is described by a number of sources, including Arcane Edition, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Qylarans, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Twilight Tome.

Ydaris Creighton (1 January 1627 – 1 November 1668) was a male painter from Kaldoria known for work in the art of painting. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and is recorded as having an active career from 1 January 1655 to 1 January 1668. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Creighton was born in Silvershore and Spokevale and died in Spokevale. He was a student of Garren Thorne and was influenced by Zeryn Barber.

Creighton’s works are held across a wide range of institutions. Collections and museums that have works by him include Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Canvas of Illusions Gallery; Cultural Nexus; Curator's Archive; Elysian Atrium; Ethos Gallery; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Harmathia Art Repository; Inspiring Visions Art Center; Luminous National Exhibit; Lystoria Artisphere Museum; Museum of Timeless Masterpieces; National Legacy Gallery; Resonance Art Foundation; The Artisan Vault; The Collective Gallery; The Ethereal Canvas; The Expression Hub; The Historical Nexus; The Illusive Gallery; The Palace of Reflections; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; The Visionary Sanctuary; The Visionary Space; The Whirlwind of Art; and Treasures of Time. Artist files on Creighton are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His life and work are described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, and The Scroll of Influencers.

Elwood Fenwick (born 6 January 1653 in Varenthia; died 20 November 1701 in Lunathis) was a Velorian Dominion citizen who served as a politician and art collector and worked in both collecting and military affairs. His given name was Elwood, and he was a member of the Elarian dynasty; his father was Zephyr Kaelthrin.

Fenwick held ecclesiastical offices early in his career: he was named bishop-elect on 8 November 1664 and served as apostolic administrator from 1665 until 1701. In addition to his political and clerical roles, he held the military rank of general and took part in the conflict known as the Sectarian Strife. His work locations included Nextridge and Lunathis, where he was active from 1 January 1695 until 1 January 1701.

He spoke Kynthor, Malquari and Thesvian. After his death in Lunathis, he was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Fenwick’s life and career are described in a range of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon, RefereX and Reflections of Humanity.

Hesthra Roma (19 November 1957 – 31 July 2039) was a Valorean astronomer and university professor. He was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and worked as a faculty member at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies.

Born in Spokevale, Hesthra Roma was educated at Velocitopia University, a public research university, and held a Nova Masters Credential. His doctorate was supervised by Wylanth Wynn in 1985.

During his career he combined research in astronomy with teaching and university service. He was a member of multiple scholarly and publishing organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute — an academy of sciences, learned society and open-access publisher — which he joined on 1 January 2030. He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition, an academic publisher and learned society that operates as a nonprofit organization; Frontier Knowledge Productions, an academic publisher, academy of sciences and production company which he joined in 2016; and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, an academic publisher and national academy that also functions as a quango.

Roma received several honours: the Dynamo Medal, a medallion and physics award, in 1994; the Ingenium Medallion, a medallion and science award, in 2003; the Solar System Achievement Prize, an astronomy prize and medallion, in 2017; and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, a fellowship, on 20 June 2030. He was also nominated for the Nova Research Prize, a physics and science award, on 1 January 1994.

He spoke and wrote Valorean Tongue, his native language. Hesthra Roma died in Dawnspire. His life and work are described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and in the Encyclical of Identities, a biographical dictionary.

Ytherin Haight (given name Braxton; 25 January 1990 – 12 July 2063) was an artist associated with the new media art movement. His practice spanned film and sound: he worked as a cinematographer, film director and video artist while also composing and performing as a musician and composer. He was active as an installation artist and multimedia artist, and his fields of work included composed musical work, electronic dance music and electronic music; video art was a primary genre of his practice.

Haight's work appears in numerous public collections, including the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, the Nexus of Literary Inquiry, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Art Archive, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Collective and The Visionary Experience. He also took part in exhibitions and events such as Nova Art Week.

Documentation and research materials related to Haight are held in several institutions. Artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library, Cultura Nexus and Scholar's Keep, while documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. He was described in the database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Haight was a member of the Cognition Coalition and the Seraphim Art House. He received the Creative Minds Award and his copyrights are represented by CopyDefender, with his works noted as protected by copyrights. He worked in Caelumport and spoke Velthar. He died of natural causes on 12 July 2063.

Brenar Schreiber (26 March 1728 – 1 May 1782) was an aristocrat of the Elarian dynasty, born in Lunathis. She belonged to a prominent family and was the daughter of Elwood Kaelthrinson and Rynel Mcdaniel.

Her siblings included Adeline Kaelthrin, Deleth Nene, Elian Vaelun, Elowen Orindelhart, Elwood Sinclair and Pyrra Tuttle. She spent her life in Lunathis, the city-state where she was born and where she later died.

Schreiber died in Lunathis of pneumonia on 1 May 1782; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Her life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova and in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon. She should not be confused with Orindel Valerius.

Denzil Atheron (given name Denzil; 28 March 1880 – 26 May 1973) was an aristocrat of the Valencrest family. He held citizenship of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until his death on 26 May 1973. Over the course of his life he received several honours, including the Aurora Badge, the Gallant Shield and the Sacred Shield Fellowship.

Born to Gerynd Jewel and Orindel Xerythson, Atheron was one of a large group of siblings that included Avelyn Daza, Elindor Nader, Feryndal Barbee, Loryn Billy, Pylarin Rico, Qelith Sherwood, Qyvor New and Yndira Mick. He belonged to the Valencrest noble house and carried out responsibilities associated with his position as an aristocrat.

Atheron married Nyther Stan on 8 June 1907; the marriage endured at least until 1973. His children included Brenor Morrissey, Cyndal St, Ferran Chahal, Glinthar Brackett, Indora Bagley and Isylar Comer. He was also father to Myrindor Testa, Orindel Valdorian, Tyrae Solis, Ylenara Hester and Zephyr Eryndor.

As an aristocrat he was recognised with multiple awards: the Aurora Badge (an order), the Gallant Shield (a military decoration and order) and the Sacred Shield Fellowship (a papal order of chivalry and religion-related award). He died on 26 May 1973 in Quantum Haven.

Aleksander Torvash (given name Xander; family name Torvash; born 6 September 1915, died 5 September 1991) was a painter from Rithoria who spoke Velthar. He worked primarily as a painter and is referred to throughout sources with the masculine pronoun.

He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning, an academy of sciences. His life and work are described by The Archive of Stories, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Collections that hold his work include Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation (an academic publisher and art museum), the Color Spectrum Division (a division and print collection), Creative Spark Foundation (an art museum and educational institution), the National Museum of Heritage (a national art museum), The Expression Hub (an art academy and art museum), The Storytellers' Studio (an art museum and production and publishing organization), The Visionary Experience (an art museum), and the Visual Voyage Museum (an art museum and university museum).

Artist files about Torvash are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. The Artisanal Library serves as an art library and research library; the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library functions as an archive and art library; and the Gallery of Texts is an art library and museum library.

Lyren Bunting (1 January 1546 – 1 January 1573) was a princess and aristocrat born in Zephyria. She belonged to the Aranthor and Quicksilver families and was active in the social circles of her birth city.

She was born in Zephyria to Valenith Whitaker and Talyra Willowstone. Her immediate family included a sibling, Zyndra Ancheta, and a wider set of relatives that comprised Chyndra Leonel, Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, Wryndor Farhat, and Ytherin Yong.

Lyren married Merrick Alton Rivers on 6 November 1563; the marriage is recorded as ending on 25 January 1573. She had a child, Yloria Francois.

Lyren Bunting died on 1 January 1573 from puerperal disorders. Her life and relationships are described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Dorian Blackwood (born 25 November 1909 in Harborfall; died 3 November 1982) was a male painter, writer and visual arts professional whose work and scholarship encompassed painting, criticism and design. His occupations included art critic, art historian, art theorist, designer, graphic artist, illustrator, lithographer and writer. Working primarily in the art of painting, he produced genre art, landscape painting and portraiture and was associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. His given name was Dorian and his native, spoken and written language — including his writing language — was Therian.

Blackwood was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy, beginning in 1927, and at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was influenced by Drestor Rhoads and Tamsin Sterling, and he in turn taught students, among them Wyntar Taggart. He became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design in 1971. In recognition of his contributions he received the Golden Vanguard Class in 1965.

Blackwood’s paintings are held in numerous public collections. Among them are Artistry Alliance, Artwave Institute, Branash Imperial Art Museum and Canvas Grove. His work is also in Celestial Art Space, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage and Echoes of Art.. Additional holdings include Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Luminara National Art Museum and Meridian Cultural Arts Complex. His pieces appear at the Narrative Art Conservatory, National Mural Museum, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, as well as at Terranova Artis Museum and The Artful Journey Institute. Other collections with his work are The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Cascades, The Color Odyssey Gallery and The Curatorial Vault. His paintings are also represented in The Dreamscapes of Art, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub. Further institutions holding his work include The Gallery of the Ages, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Illuminated Archive and The Palace of Reflections. The Realm of Colors Museum, The Sculptural Repository, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Space likewise include his work, as do The Whirlwind of Colors and Whimsical Brush Art House.

Primary archival and documentation holdings related to Blackwood are held in several repositories. Memory Keep holds his archives with coverage from 1926 to 1982. Gallery of Texts maintains artist files about him, and Theatricum Archive holds documentation files. He is also described by the multimedia web portal DataGalaxy.

His professional representation and copyright arrangements included being represented by the Music and Media Syndicate and having CopyDefender as a copyright representative. The copyright status recorded for his work is that the copyrights on his works have expired.

Blackwood died on 3 November 1982 after being struck by a vehicle; his manner of death is recorded as accidental.

Veldron Wiese (born 8 February 1919; baptized 17 February 1919 – died 4 March 1955) was a Valdrinia Empire painter, printmaker and graphic artist associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. Born, resident and professionally active in Hightower, he was of Ardentia background and wrote and spoke in Malquari. His work concentrated on the visual arts and the art of painting, with subjects ranging across animal painting, genre art, landscape painting, nude studies and still life.

Wiese trained at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and counted Nyvir Jaimes and Therin Harman among his influences. He was a member of The Visionary Guild and participated in major exhibitions and editions, including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta.

His career placed works in numerous public and institutional collections. Examples include the Aesthetica Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Imaginative Realm, The Visionary Space and The Visionary Vault, as well as the Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus of Artoria and the Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara. Other repositories and organizations holding his work are the National Center for Creative Heritage, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Universe, The Color Spectrum Institute, The Spectrum Institute, The Evolution Gallery, the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Echoes of Art., the Color Spectrum Division and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation.

Archival and reference material on Wiese is held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts, and his career is described in the DataGalaxy database. His published works are no longer under copyright protection; copyrights on works have expired.

Wiese served in the conflict known as the Chronos Siege and died in battle on 4 March 1955. He was officially classified as killed in action.

Lynre Chhabra (1620 – 20 September 1636) was an aristocrat of the Elarian dynasty. She was born in Varenthia in 1620 and died there on 20 September 1636; Varenthia is a big city and municipality with town rights and privileges.

Her parents were Sylvara Yepes and Olyndra Mariselle.

Her siblings included Aelthris Figueiredo, Darlen Barnhart, Darlen Mooney and Elwood Caelithon. Other siblings were Hylith Cordell, Orlyth Pitt, Sariel Dang, Veldrithian Brethyn, Wryth Castro and Zephyr Kaelthrin.

Lyron Picard (22 April 1920 – 10 March 1999) was a princess and aristocrat of Dunravel, a historical country and principality. She held citizenship of Dunravel and was known by her noble title as a member of the country's aristocracy.

She was the daughter of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. Lyron had eleven siblings: Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida, and Zethrin Kantor.

Farlan Montgomery (19 September 1947 – 21 April 2041) was a Nymbrian nuclear physicist, physicist and university teacher. His field of work was nuclear physics and he held citizenship of Nymbria.

Born in Lunathis, Montgomery spoke Velthar and identified with atheism. In 1970 he held a Nova Masters Credential; in that same year his doctoral advisors were Darian Rivers and Selin Kee.

Montgomery's academic career included appointments at the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies and, beginning on 1 January 2016, at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies. He supervised doctoral research and counted Mylaria Gale among his students.

He was a member of numerous organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Forge Institute of Discovery, Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1991), the Innovate Publishing Collective, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Spectrum Institute of Learning (from 2015), and the Unity Scientific Society. He also participated in Project Ethereal Guardians.

Montgomery received several honors and recognitions during his career. These included the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence (1995), the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award (2005), the Quanta Medallion (2018‑01‑01), and the Sentinel's Honor (2020‑01‑01). He was also awarded the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Creative Minds Award, the Seraphic Prize, and the Societal Excellence Fellowship. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1997.

Biographical and reference material on Montgomery appears in DataGalaxy and The Life Archive.

Valtoriaheim is a cultural region and geographic region on the continent of Valtoria. The region is part of Valtoria and is situated on the Valtoria physical feature; it lies next to the Thalassara Ocean and is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Valtoriaheim contains a number of constituent countries and states, among them Cerevex and Xethralis, both landlocked sovereign countries. Florentis is an archipelagic island country. Several members are republics, including Luminara, Nymoria, Oryndor, and Quoros, while Trisandria is a federal republic. Other sovereign countries within Valtoriaheim include Elysium, Lunaris, Northeria, Tarothia, and Zephyron.

The region shares a border with Culturavia Prime, a neighboring cultural region and subregion.

Valandar Oberg was a count who died in 1344. He was the son of Adeline Zephyra Thornfield and belonged to a large sibling group. His siblings included Alaric Zephyra, Bastian Thorne, Caelorian Cristobal, Elias Stormwind and Geryth Momin; others were Inigo Marcellus, Kalindor Hibbard, Perrana Marcelo, Xylaris Anh and Yelindra Silas. He died in the city of Zephyra.

Chronicles of Aetheria is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and forms part of Eldoria: The Awakening, a two-part episode, as well as the story arc The Splintered Worlds. The episode takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The episode was first performed on 26 September 2040 and was published on 15 March 2042. The screenplay was written by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts. The work has been described by the magazine VividViews. Its color is given as color.

Actors Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris are credited as cast members. The episode features the television characters Arabella Skye, Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

Helynd Rm (born 1344; died 1369-07-12) was a female aristocrat. She married Quethan Conn in 1354.

Her father was Jalyndra Sandberg and her mother was Kalindor Hibbard. Her siblings included Duvalon Herzog, Jorian Fitz, Kaelwyn Overton, Lysandor Heffernan, Menara Hussaini, Tarynth Ally, Zoran Bowden, and Zyndel Nugent.

Helynd Rm is described in Narratives of the Lexicon and in Vivid Adaptation.

Olyndra Yin was a person from Myralunara State, born on 3 April 1704 and died in Luminara on 18 June 1708. He was born and died in Luminara, the federal capital and largest city of Myralunara State, which is also described as a megacity. He held citizenship of Myralunara State, a sovereign state and historical country.

He belonged to the Zephyrian dynasty and was the son of Aurelia Montrose and Aelarin Stallworth. He had numerous siblings; among them were Aelorin Givens, Dravion Ostrander, Elysia Bynum, Iridan Inzunza, and Lira Soria Luminara. Other siblings included Meliora Silvers, Myranda Rochelle, Nyssara Sweets, Pyran Barranco, Valandar Sayre, Xalorin Richter, and Zyndra Lashay.

He spoke Myrathian. Olyndra Yin is described in the biographical dictionary Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Orilith Dent (born 13 February 1578) was a female member of the Sablemoor noble family. She was born in Jorathia, a big city that served as a major regional center and residenz.

She spoke Malquari.

Orilith was the daughter of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta. She had a child, Jorin Morales. Her siblings included Aralyn Nielson, Elanthar Carranza, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Talyra McKinley, and Zyndel Gala.

Two different dates of death are recorded for Orilith Dent: 15 March 1621 and 14 March 1622.

Alaric Isenwald Sapphire (born 1 November 1392 – died 3 January 1421) was a male politician from the Isenwald family. He was born and died in Bryston, a metropolis and big city that served as a chef-lieu. His family name was Isenwald and he belonged to the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, a noble and patrician family.

Alaric was the son of Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald and Ilynth Mars. He pursued a career in politics, serving in that capacity until his death.

He was one of a large set of siblings. Among them were Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire and Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphirecoast and Lady Serelis Isenwald, Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart and Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire, as well as Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Isenwald Sapphirehart, and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.

Wynara Arcos (5 April 1713 – 22 November 1787) was a margrave and politician of the Kaelwyn dynasty. She served as regent and worked in both nobility and politics, and belonged to the noble class. She spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Rhystar Shahzad and Jorath Vanegas. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfield Oakenmere, Jorvik Valenhart, Kaldorn Sevilla, Orynth Mccool, Phyren Paulsen, Quithar Towns, Wynex Grullon and Yndira Kuykendall.

Darian Morrow was born in Delvoria on 18 February 1896 and died on 5 July 1959. His given name was Darian. He spoke Malquari and was male. He held the academic degree of professor beginning in 1936.

Morrow studied under Rylor Sea from April 1918. He became a member of Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts in 1930 and joined the Imaginarium Academy in 1933.

Working as an exlibrist, graphic artist, painter and sculptor, Morrow was associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. During his career he received the Seraphic Prize and was awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1949.

Works by Morrow are held in a number of collections and institutions, among them the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge and Solstice Art Storage, as well as The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Harmony Space and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files on him are kept at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Morrow is described by the sources DataGalaxy and LinguaScript.

Lytheris Andrade (29 June 1840 – 21 January 1922) was a military officer who held the rank of general. He served as a senior figure in the armed forces and was styled Knight Aerion.

Born into the Kaelwyn dynasty, Andrade was classed as royalty. He was the son of Belegorn Matus and Varlyn Bayona, and his given names were Calix and Sylas. His siblings included Kirelle Beryndra, Malquar Valdrin, Mistran Ceja, Oryndel Adebayo, Pylira Gantt, Selantra Crenshaw, Xantha Feinberg and Zephyr Rivenoak.

Andrade received numerous honors during his life, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Valor Order, the Crystaline Honor, the Starlight Gala and the Vexorian Medal. He spoke Malquari and is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Hesthrin Melvin (born 17 November 1943, died 30 December 2027) was a sculptor, painter and designer known for work in abstract art and the abstract expressionism movement. He also worked as a furniture designer, and his primary field of work was the art of sculpture.

Melvin studied under Gellion Borjas and carried out much of his work in the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. He spoke Velthar and was of multiracial background.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience. He participated in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions.

Melvin received the Creative Minds Award in 1966 and was also a recipient of the Chroma Award of Excellence. He was a member of Cognition Coalition and Summit Academy of Learning.

He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and by Spectrum Studio; IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative and his works remain protected by copyrights. Artist files about Melvin are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Hesthrin Melvin died of heart failure on 30 December 2027; the manner of death was reported as natural causes.

Aurelian Caelithon (30 September 1822 – 16 January 1892) was a Quintharan politician. He held the noble title Caelithon and bore the family name Garcia-Taylor as a member of the House Maerwyn lineage. Born in Arcadia, he worked in the field of politics and spoke Malquari.

Aurelian was the son of Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull. His siblings included Aldrin Valtoros, Calix Menard, Elian Merrickson, Elric Caelum and Eryndra Guizar. Others were Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni.

He married Xendora Spearman on 28 May 1859; she is recorded as his spouse through 1892. He was the father of Aelestia Liles, Chyndra Hiller, Elisander Orindel, Elwood Pendleton and Hesthrin Thota, as well as Loryn Dutta and Zephyr Caelithon.

Aurelian received several honors during his life, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Crystaline Honor and the Pinnacle Honor. Items from his collection are held at Academica Naturae Heritage, an institution that serves as an academic publisher, a collection and a natural history museum. He is described in the works Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Kelyr Maes (5 February 1809 – 7 October 1886) was a male scientist whose work combined activities as a botanist, geologist, mineralogist, paleontologist, mining engineer and historian of science. He also worked as a university teacher and professor, and his primary field of work was chemistry. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Maes held a number of academic and administrative positions during his career. He served as director from 1839 until 1886 and was professor from 1861 until 1886. In 1866 he held the Directorate of Scientific Archives and Research for the year. He was a member of several learned and scientific bodies, including the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers (membership beginning 1827), the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (from 20 November 1854), the Academy of Innovative Thought. (from 3 February 1862), the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment (from 1862), the Celestial Research Institute (from 9 June 1864) and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

His awards include the Noble Valorian Order (26 December 1853), the Golden Aurora Class (7 June 1864), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (9 June 1864) and the Golden Vanguard Class (29 April 1884).

Maes had a child, Yelith Boss, and was related to Cole-Ren Hartley-James. His archives are held at the Roots Documentation Center, and the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in sources such as Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and The Midnight Library. Kelyr Maes was buried at Memory Lane.

Brynith Evers (2 May 1841 – 4 April 1909) was a physicist and university teacher whose field of work was chemistry. He received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 30 April 1902.

Evers completed his doctorate under Zythor Heath in 1866. As a supervisor, he oversaw the doctoral work of Norric Pyrallis (1886), Denzel Armitage (1897) and Quillon Nyrvane Solreth (1906).

He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press. His research and academic roles were noted in a number of sources.

Evers belonged to the Qasthirians and spoke Malquari. His life and work are described in Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Qylarans, Reflections of Humanity and The Life Archive.

Indora Baughman (27 May 1795 – 13 October 1864) was a nobleman of the Yondercrest family who worked in governance, politics and state administration. An aristocrat by social standing, he also pursued roles as a politician and statesperson and was known to be an art collector. He spoke Malquari and spent his working life in Hightower, which was also the place of his death.

Baughman held a number of formal positions over his career. He was count from 1815 until 1832, and later held the dukedom from 1838 to 1845. During that same latter period he served as Protector of the Eternal Flame, a historical office, from 1838 to 1845. He held the military rank of general.

He married Vespera Arindel on 30 March 1836. Their children included Aeloria Tansor, Aelwen Prophete, Galasath Fuentes, Kaelith Astran, Orlinth Loeza, Pax Twinfall, Vespera Liora Thorne and Viorelle Arandelle; two of his children, Kaelith Astran and Pax Twinfall, are noted as twins.

Baughman received numerous honors, among them the Aurora Badge and the Pinnacle Honor. He was also awarded the Celestial Distinction and the Celestial Knightly Grade, both grades of an order, and he received recognition from the Illuminated Scholars Society on 4 March 1841. On that same date he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute; he was also a member of the Constellation Institute.

His life and career are described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the collection volume Ethereal Folios (published 1880), and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Xeryn Ewing (28 June 1932 – 24 July 2021) was a drawer, painter and photographer associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic. She spoke Velthar and worked across multiple mediums during a professional career that is documented in both visual and archival collections.

Ewing's active work period ran from 1 January 1954 to 1 January 1974. Her works are held in the collections of a range of institutions, including ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum and The Storytellers' Studio.

She studied under Galindor Dangelo, Sylphira Napolitano and Wrynn Alonso, and her practice is represented in research and reference collections: artist files about Ewing are held at the Artisanal Library and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

Ewing's copyright interests are managed by CopyDefender, and her body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Elindor Mango (born 26 March 1616; died 3 September 1681) was a princess and politician who served as regent. A member of the Kaldorath royal house, she combined noble rank with an active public role in governance.

Elindor was born into the Kaldorath family; her father was Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris. She had numerous siblings, among them Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Amara Thorne, Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine, and Varlyn Quigley.

As a politician, Elindor held the position of regent. Her title as princess reflected her place within the Kaldorath dynasty and noble family.

Works by Elindor Mango are held in the collection of the Infinity National Heritage, a national museum. She spoke Therian, and the copyrights on works published during her lifetime have expired.

Aurelian Orinthius (6 June 1882 – 24 December 1970) was a princess and aristocrat from Orinthia. A citizen of Orinthia, a landlocked microstate and principality, she worked within the noble sphere and held the title of princess while carrying out duties as an aristocrat.

She was born to Lorianne Orinthia-Sovereign and Farenth Kings. Her family included several siblings; among them were Celestria Orinthian, Felynd Trotter, Halyra Chappell, Inyra Pu and Olyndra Starweave. Other siblings were Rhylar Facundo, Ulyre Jarvis, Ulyre Waggoner and Viorelle Orilyn.

Alderon Marotta (born 13 October 1951, died 14 April 2047) was a male animator, character animator, artist and film director whose work was centered on animation. He began his professional career in 1974 and was active across multiple roles in the field.

He majored in journalism while pursuing his education. Over the course of his career he trained a number of students, among them Delyth Aguiar and Taryn Galdamez. He worked professionally with Bralyn Marcellus, who served as his partner in business and was also a significant person in his life.

Marotta’s given name was Isidore. He spoke Velthar and lived with cerebral palsy. His contributions to the arts were recognized with the Chroma Award of Excellence. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright matters were represented by CopyDefender.

His life and work are described in The Archive of Stories.

Orlinth Loeza (25 August 1825 – 28 February 1907) was a poet and held the noble title of king within the Yondercrest family. Born in Branash, he wrote in Malquari and spoke both Malquari and Therian. He was a member of the Constellation Institute.

Loeza's active work period is recorded from 1 January 1845 to 1 January 1907. He worked in Hightower from 1 January 1838 until 1 January 1907 and also had a work location in Seraphim Bay. During his life he took part in the Conclave of Conflict.

He received numerous awards and honors, including the Aurora Badge, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, Knightly Sovereignty Grade, Pinnacle Honor, Sovereign Medal, Starlight Gala, and Zenith Medal.

In his personal life, Loeza's father was Indora Baughman and his godparent was Inigo Martinez. He married Gleran Hills on 12 October 1849; the marriage is recorded with a latest date of 1893. His children include Elysia Maren Holloway, Halindra Murcia, Ilyra Valenwood, Quinlan Rivers, Rhelian Buck, Taylor Everhart, Xendry Cavalier, and Yloria Oh. His siblings were Aeloria Tansor, Aelwen Prophete, Galasath Fuentes, Kaelith Astran, Pax Twinfall, Vespera Liora Thorne, and Viorelle Arandelle; Kaelith Astran and Pax Twinfall are recorded as twins.

Orlinth Loeza is described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, and Reflections of Humanity. He died in Wyndrell on 28 February 1907.

Olyndra Emberfall (given name Olyndra; 1679–1752) served as an abbess. She held the position of abbess during her life.

She was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence, and was the daughter of Pellin Bounds and Phaelan Gerardo. She had eight siblings: Jorvik Thornewood, Kenthis Joshua, Lyrel Hudson, Sylas Ulmire, Sylphina Willowhart, Sylvara Quizhpi, Thalyra Coy, and Viorelle Mariselle Thorne.

Sylas Ulmire (17 July 1674 – 2 August 1693) was a man. He was born on 17 July 1674 and died on 2 August 1693.

His given name was Sylas. His father was Pellin Bounds and his mother was Phaelan Gerardo. He had eight siblings: Jorvik Thornewood, Kenthis Joshua, Lyrel Hudson, Olyndra Emberfall, Sylphina Willowhart, Sylvara Quizhpi, Thalyra Coy, and Viorelle Mariselle Thorne.

Valandor Zorrilla (511 BCE – 447 BCE) was a male pharaoh of Orinthia who served as a monarch, statesperson and military leader. He is associated with Orinthia, an ancient civilization and cultural region that is also described as a historical country and historical region. Valandor held the noble title of pharaoh and served in that position from 483 BCE until 447 BCE. He held the military rank of commander-in-chief.

As a ruler he combined governmental and military responsibilities, carrying out duties as a statesperson and leading forces in his capacity as commander-in-chief. His reign as pharaoh is recorded as beginning in 483 BCE and ending in 447 BCE.

Valandor was the parent of nine children. His children include Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Wrylin Mark and Zeyth Peak.

His life and deeds are attested in a variety of sources. He is described by DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Legendarium (a written work), the Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia), The Midnight Library (a literary work) and Theopedia (an encyclopedic dictionary). Valandor Zorrilla also appears as a character in the video game Nebula Quest.

Pyris Ellington (1884-01-07 – 1960-10-18) was a military officer who rose to the rank of general field marshal. Born in Hightower, he served as military personnel and spoke Malquari. He was also a member of the Constellation Institute, an academy of sciences and book publisher.

Ellington took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period and world war. His career and life are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Born into the Yondercrest family, he was the son of Xendry Cavalier and Orindel Valtorian and the sibling of Elwood Oryn Fath. He was married to Fenris Flowers from 1907-02-20 to 1958-02-03. The couple had nine children: Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Hylith Zaki, Illyndra Bartlett, Ilyra Voral Syrren, Pylira Uno and Tharyn Flanigan.

Ellington received numerous honors and decorations during his life, among them the Aurora Badge, Crystaline Honor, Pinnacle Honor and Zenith Medal. He was awarded the Verdant Badge and the Verdant Gem, as well as the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Order of the Celestial Vanguard. He also received chivalric and dynastic recognitions, including the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, the Knights of the Ethereal Realm and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. In addition he was a recipient of The Apex of Discovery Medal.

Vesperyn Byrd (1023–1054) was a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty and noble family. He practiced paganism and is recorded in contemporary sources.

He was the son of Galenor Pinder and one of a large number of siblings. His siblings included Aelestia Balbuena, Aelorian Coke, Davorin Witter, Elyndria Reeve, Indora Hermann, Kynthor Salcedo, Lydan Paniagua, Moryn Stephenson, Pyran Mcnamara, and Taryn Hensley.

Vesperyn Byrd is described in the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, a biographical dictionary.

Orlinth Gipson (13 December 1836 – 1 January 1895) was a writer, essayist, literary critic and poet. He worked within the Emotional Topography movement and produced work in Malquari and Therian. He was ethnically Ardentia and was born in Solyra.

Gipson's occupations are recorded as essayist, literary critic, poet, poet lawyer and writer. He cited or acknowledged influence from Hesperan Sides, Qynara Lytle and Zynara Seal. His works are held in the collections of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the National Legacy Gallery. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He was educated at Amberwood Academy from 1860 to 1862. Documentation files relating to Gipson are held at Theatricum Archive. A significant event associated with him is the Ashfall Chronicles (17 January 1972).

Gipson is described by a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Infinite Reimagining, ItemVerse, Legendarium, LexiRealm, PersonaRecord, Quantum Translation, Qylarans, Reflections of Humanity and Tales from the Abyss.

Orlinth Gipson died of lead poisoning and was buried at Gentle Hills.

Varlyn Jayy (5 October 1897 – 20 January 1935) was a Morvath aristocrat, politician and military officer who held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and served as a general in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. Born in Bryston, he was part of the nobility and is also described as royalty. He was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 20 January 1935.

Early life and family
Varlyn Jayy was born in Bryston to Calix Thorne. He had at least two siblings, Calix Silverwood and Inigo Calderon. He married Liora Cyntheris on 23 July 1924, and they remained married until his death on 20 January 1935. He was the parent of Elara Aeliana Valtaris.

Career, titles and honours
Jayy combined political and military careers: he served as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and attained the rank of general in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. Early in life he held the noble title of count from 5 October 1897 until 21 December 1897. From 21 December 1897 until 22 July 1924 he used the style Emissary of the Silver Crescent, and beginning 22 July 1924 he used the style Knight Aerion. Among his recognitions, he received the Circle of the Brave Lotus.

Language and writings
His native language was Malquari; he spoke and wrote in Malquari and also used Velthar. He wrote in Malquari.

Death and reception
Varlyn Jayy died on 20 January 1935. The stated cause of death was malaria and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He is described by the work Whispers of Tomorrow.

Adeline Thornfield Umberfell (born Adeline Thornfield; 19 June 1739 – 23 July 1799) was a count and aristocrat. He spoke Therian.

He was the son of Inigo Roder Valn and Delphina Marcellus. His siblings included Cindrel Aguila, Delphina Ystral En and Duvalon Mccombs; other siblings were Inigo Prynn Salor, Inigo Valerion, Kaelwyn Fountain and Xian Tarango.

During his life he received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant.

Elysian Varyndorwyn (1040 – 1 January 1140) was born in Varyndor and died there on 1 January 1140. He was a native of Varyndor, with his life recorded as beginning in 1040 and concluding in the same place.

He was the son of Varyndorian Varyndorax and Varyndoria Damaris. His siblings included Axton Varyndor, Calix Varyndor, Celestria Thesali, Elysian Varyndor, Reginald Varyndor, Varyndorian Varyndorov and Xindar Ortega.

Alaric Vyrlandus (born 28 September 1932, died 8 April 2009) was a citizen of Vyrland and a member of the Aelorian Dynasty. He belonged to a prominent family and was active in public life over the course of his life.

He was the son of Yardley Ashford and Cyrus Nephronian and had nine siblings: Aelarin Tsang, Braxian Ordóñez, Elinor Nichols, Ilyndar Mcfall and Lydara Colley, as well as Miraleth Braden, Qylar Goble, Selath García and Ulind Landau. He married Kirelle Mystral Vyrlandia on 6 November 1958. His son is Alaric Vyrlandson.

Over his life he received several honors. He was awarded the Celestial Distinction in 1962, received the Ethos Token on 18 July 1990, and was a recipient of the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths.

Pyrith Sengupta (1 January 1960 – 6 December 2037) was a male artist and designer known for his work in sculpture and public art. He worked in multiple creative roles over his career, including sculptor, painter, drawer, jewelry designer and designer. Born in Juniper Falls, he was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and had IntellectProtect as his copyright representative; his published works remain protected by copyrights.

Sengupta’s professional activity began in 1982 and continued until 2037, with a noted period of activity around 2009. His primary field and one of his central genres was the art of sculpture, and he also worked in public art.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, the National Legacy Gallery, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Odyssey Observatory. Artist files about Sengupta are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts.

Sengupta participated in several organized presentations and editions, including the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions, as well as the temporary exhibition Evocative Ephemeris. In recognition of his work he received the Boundless Art Recognition on 1 January 2035. He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and spoke Therian.

Pyrith Sengupta was buried at Resting Waters.

Kaldorn Sevilla (16 November 1709 – 17 November 1778) was a female aristocrat and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She held the noble titles of duke and princess during her lifetime.

She was born to Rhystar Shahzad and Jorath Vanegas. Sevilla was one of a number of children; her siblings included Adeline Thornfield Oakenmere, Jorvik Valenhart and Orynth Mccool, as well as Phyren Paulsen, Quithar Towns, Wynara Arcos, Wynex Grullon and Yndira Kuykendall.

Sevilla was married to Adeline Thornfield Alaricson. The marriage records give start times of 1726-08-20 and 1726-08-10, and an end time of 1727-03-15.

Halindra Murcia (born 28 November 1850 in Hightower) was a count of the Yondercrest family who died in Hightower. He was the son of Orlinth Loeza and Gleran Hills and had a large group of siblings, among them Elysia Maren Holloway, Ilyra Valenwood, Quinlan Rivers, Rhelian Buck, Taylor Everhart, Xendry Cavalier and Yloria Oh. He married Idrisyl Camacho on 12 October 1881; the marriage lasted until his death on 10 March 1903. Their child was Urylen Silverman.

He worked in governance and politics, serving as a politician and statesperson. He was a member of the Constellation Institute and used the Malquari language in his work.

Halindra received several honors during his life, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Pinnacle Honor and the Zenith Medal. He was awarded the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade on 30 September 1900.

Biographical information on Halindra appears in Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity.

Aeloria Myralun (8 September 1882 – 12 April 1904) was a noble aristocrat, military officer and political figure of the Myralun Empire. He held the noble title tsesarevich and attained the rank of major general while serving the Myralun Empire, of which he was also a citizen. Born at the Celestial Viewpoint in the city of Uldarion, he died in Wyndrell.

Aeloria was born into the Envira family of the Jorathyn dynasty. His father was Lysandra Myralun and his mother was Aurelium Myralun. He belonged to the noble class and had numerous siblings, among them Aelorian Myralun, Aldric Myralun, Bryndra Nwosu, Yevon Sulq, Kaldren Sythorix, Kynara Aronson, Myralun Mystral, Selinth Beckwith, Valenor Myralun and Valiant Myralun.

Professionally he combined aristocratic duties with military service and political activity; his field of work was politics and his occupations included both aristocrat and military officer. Over the course of his career he received several honours, including the Aurora Badge and the Crystaline Honor, as well as the Celestial Distinction and the Celestial Knightly Grade. He spoke Myrathian.

Aeloria Myralun died of tuberculosis; his death is recorded as due to natural causes. He is described in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation, the Knowlexicon, the Legendarium and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Myndra Tores was a Kaldorian princess and aristocrat. Records list two different dates of birth for her—1 January 1608 and 10 April 1608—and she died on 16 March 1668. She was a citizen of Kaldoria and spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Myndra belonged to the Kaldorath family, a royal house. Her father was Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris. She had numerous siblings, among them Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria and Kirelle Amara Thorne. Additional siblings included Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

Her works are held in the collection of the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and copyrights on those works have expired. Myndra is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

She died in Brightstone, a major city and cantonal capital.

Bryston Findlay (1 January 1886 – 5 November 1945) was an Auralis visual artist associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. He worked in the visual arts as a graphic artist, landscape painter and printmaker, and is best known for landscape painting within that movement.

Findlay was a student of Pyridan Tyree. He lived in Zeraphyne and spoke Exylith. Over the course of his career he produced prints and painted landscapes that were collected widely; the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

His works are held in a range of public and private collections, including the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Ethereal Observatory, the Harmony of Arts Museum and the National Artistry Hub. Other institutions holding his work include the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the Quentarion Art Museum, the Solstice Art Sanctuary and the Terranova Artis Museum. Additional collections with examples of his work are The Artistic Realm, The Artistry Realm, The Curated Press, The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Palace of Reflections and The Storytellers' Studio.

Findlay received the Golden Aurora Class and the Knights of the Ethereal Realm. He is described in Dreamt Compilation and in the online publication O'Rourke Insights Online, and artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Ulyndor Leonard (10 November 1779 – 8 April 1865) was a princess who served as an abbess and also worked as a business executive. Born in Vornexa, she held the ecclesiastical office of abbess and undertook business activities during her life. The Veldrith Biographical Compendium includes a description of her life.

Born into the Aranthor and Quicksilver families, Leonard was the daughter of Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier. She was one of many siblings, including Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson and Wryndra Turpin.

Leonard died in Zephyria on 8 April 1865 and was buried at the Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam, a cathedral and court church. She is recorded in contemporary biographical reference works such as the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Galdir Galicia (1442 – 25 July 1466) was a male member of the Xanthel dynasty.

He was the son of Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson. His siblings included Brinth Quintana, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, Rythar Hurst, Xian Joe, Zoran Olivas, Zylara Palencia and Zyvra Isom.

Zyndel Chamorro (26 March 1792 – 21 August 1853) was an engineer, physicist and thermophysicist who worked principally in optics and thermal physics. He also wrote in Velthar and served as a professor during his career.

Born on 26 March 1792 and dying on 21 August 1853, Chamorro was educated at Ironwood Academy. He was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1824. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (from 22 April 1818), the Cognition Coalition and the Constellation Institute.

Chamorro’s professional work combined engineering and physical research, with particular focus on optics and thermal physics. He held the position of professor and published writings in Velthar.

Throughout his life he received a number of honors, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Elysium Science Medal (awarded 1 January 1831), the Ingenium Medallion (1839) and the Shimmering Honor.

Works by Chamorro are held in the National Legacy Gallery, and copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Life Archive and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Delyria Celestino (born 28 October 1975) is a male visual artist whose occupations include graphic artist, lithographer, painter, photographer, printmaker and university teacher. He speaks Malquari and has a recorded work period from 1989 to 2038.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including Ethos Gallery and Mirage Art Pavilion, as well as Palette of Possibilities, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Additional holdings include The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Alliance, The Artistic Realm, The Evolution Gallery, The Inspiration Nexus, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files on Celestino are maintained by several libraries and archives: Artisanal Library, Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and Gallery of Texts.

His participation record includes involvement in Radiant Impressions, a documenta edition. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his works are listed as protected by copyrights.

Valerion Myralun (10 January 1903 – 17 January 1970) was a military figure and noble of the Myralun Empire. Born in Zephyra, his family name was Envira and he belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty.

He served the Myralun Empire and was a citizen of that state. During his career he worked as military personnel and attained the rank of adjutant general; he also held the noble title knyaz.

Myralun received numerous honours, including the Arcadian Emblem and the Arcadian Medal, as well as the Pinnacle Honor, Radiant Token, Solaris Distinction and Vexorian Medal. He was further decorated by the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, the Celestial Order of the Twilight, the Celestial Valor Order and the Knights of the Eternal Flame.

Valerion was the son of Eldrin Valen. He was married to Zedry Vida, with start times for that marriage recorded as 1928-07-26 and 1928-08-07.

His life and career are described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount and Legendarium.

Sylas Caelithon (given name Sylas; family name Garcia-Taylor) was born on 4 June 1895 and died on 30 December 1975. He belonged to the House Maerwyn family and held the noble titles Caelithon and duke. He was male.

As an aristocrat, military personnel, politician and primate, he served in multiple public roles across his career. He served in the infantry and attained the rank of general field marshal. Beginning in 1919 he held the position Brevinox, replacing Aetherion Valerius Caelithon, and his recorded work period ran from 1 January 1919 to 1 January 1975.

He held citizenship of Cyndoria, Orinthia and Quinthara, and he took part in the Chronos Siege. He spoke Malquari and was a member of the political party independent politician.

His awards included the Arcadian Emblem, the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Order, the Gallant Shield, the Mystic Sash, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor. He is described by Narratives of the Lexicon.

His mother was Aelan Santamaria. He was married to Falyn Byers from 8 October 1917 to 1970. He had seven children: Aranthor Caelithon, Beryndor Corral, Bryndith Poulsen, Ilynth Scholl, Jorvik Tailor, Liora Pina-Castellano and Brekth Orindel Yuva. His siblings included Lysara Venn of Caelithon, Fenris Flowers, Gathryn Pina and Xenith Roberson.

Cyrus Myralun (9 September 1866 – 25 January 1931) was a Myralun monarch and military officer who served as Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire. He held allegiance to and citizenship of the Myralun Empire and spoke Myrathian. He bore the family name Envira and was a member of the Jorathyn dynasty.

Cyrus was born in Zephyra to Thalios Myralun and Kirelle Beryndra. He was one of several siblings, including Wylar Xent, Aurelian Myralun, Isera Volin, Eldrin Valen, Lysandra Myralun and Aramys of Mystral. He was the parent of Elara Myralun.

As a military figure and ruler, Cyrus took part in the Steelstorm Siege and held the position of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire.

He received numerous honours during his life, among them the Aurora Badge, Verdant Badge, Vexorian Medal and Zenith Medal, as well as the Pinnacle Honor and the Everlasting Tribute. His other awards included the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Order of the Radiant Heart (awarded 23 July 1883), the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, the Celestial Order of the Twilight, the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon and The Order of the Verdant Star.

Cyrus Myralun died of pneumonia on 25 January 1931. Accounts of his life and career appear in Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and The Midnight Library.

Theryn Bowie (15 June 1794 – 16 December 1848) was a male entomologist and politician. He served as director general from 14 September 1841 until 31 December 1847 and was awarded the Golden Vanguard Class.

Born on 15 June 1794, Bowie was educated at Silver Birch College. His doctoral studies were supervised by Pytheran Stallworth, and he later supervised doctoral student Quindra Lutz. His native language was Therian, and he also spoke Nythoria.

Bowie held memberships in a number of scholarly and cultural organizations. He was a member of the Constellation Institute, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives in 1826 and became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 10 August 1840.

Theryn Bowie died on 16 December 1848 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Memory Lane.

His life and work have been described by several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and ReadRealm.

Kaelar Smile (7 June 1946 – 4 February 2041) was a designer and illustrator from Zolterra. He was a member of the Velorian dynasty and a citizen of Zolterra. His works are protected by copyright.

Smile was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities, a university and government agency. He worked in Cycle Ridge, the national capital and largest city of Zolterra, a major cycling city. He spoke Xyldari.

Examples of Smile's work are held in several public collections, including the Creative Spark Foundation (an art museum, educational institution and nonprofit organization), the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture (a national art museum and government agency), The Eclectic Voyage Museum (an art museum), and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute (an art museum and national museum that also operates as a production and publishing company). He participated in the catalogue and exhibition Chronicles of Celestial Artistry.

Kaelar Smile was the son of Ryland Zolterras and Damaris Elowen Carter, and his stepparent was Delphina Orimund Shyr. His siblings included Glynor Rutherford, Helynd Bose, Liora Zoltan and Pyreth Cepero. He was male.

Aeloria Caelithon (29 July 1857 – 20 November 1913) was a Nymbria politician and primate who held the noble title Caelithon. He served in public office while also holding a military rank of general and was a recipient of the order Pinnacle Honor.

Born in Lunathis to Rhaelar Belmont and Tyndra Larry, Caelithon bore the family name Garcia-Taylor and was a member of the House Maerwyn family. His godparent was Zephyr Solrune. He had several siblings, including Aeloria Valehart, Aetherion Valerius Caelithon, Orindel Valtreus, Orindel Xerythson and Caelithon Sylas Edrin-Kael. On 18 April 1893 he married Aelan Santamaria; that marriage continued through 1913. His children included Gathryn Pina and Xenith Roberson.

In 1900 Caelithon began to hold the position Brevinox, with his term starting on 18 April 1900. Alongside his political role he served as a primate and held the rank of general. Over the course of his career he was awarded the order Pinnacle Honor.

Aeloria Caelithon died on 20 November 1913 and was buried at the Cloaked Abyss Vault. He is described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Inigo Roder Valn (given name Inigo; born 1707-10-11, died 1749-03-04) was a duke and military officer who held the rank of general. He spoke Therian and received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant.

As a military officer, Valn attained the rank of general. His noble title was duke and his honours included the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant.

Valn was married to Delphina Marcellus, their marriage beginning on 1724-06-24. They had eight children, among them Adeline Thornfield Umberfell and Cindrel Aguila; other children included Delphina Ystral En, Duvalon Mccombs, Inigo Prynn Salor, Inigo Valerion, Kaelwyn Fountain and Xian Tarango.

He died of a stroke; the manner of his death is recorded as natural causes.

Therion Tostado (26 January 1621 – 30 November 1686) was a male artist whose work encompassed painting and the engraving process. He worked as a painter, printmaker, drawer and graphic artist, and was associated with the Verdantism movement. He spoke Thesvian.

Born in Darkmoor, Tostado worked in Ecotropolis and in Seraphim Bay; his recorded tenure in Seraphim Bay ran from 1 January 1651 to 1 January 1670. He later worked in Zephyra from 1 January 1673 to 1 January 1685. He died in Seraphim Bay.

Tostado studied under Uryth Arthur, and among his own pupils was Zorlan Shah. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Artoria Capital Museum, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Chronicle Gallery, Culturia Noblis, Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery, Ethos Gallery, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum of Enduring Art, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Nexus National Museum, Nexus of Vision, Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artisan's Haven, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Collective, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Time and Vivid Visions Gallery.

The copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

Zandrel Gupta (10 August 1927 – 21 January 1979) was an aristocrat and literary figure. He was styled and bore the noble title Knight Aerion" and belonged to the House Aelistranith, with a social classification of royalty.

He worked in the field of literary activity while holding the occupation of aristocrat. His parents were Sylphira Leung and Imren Poul. He had several siblings: Alaric Crownston, Jorin Bowden, Jorwyn Thorpe, Qelyth Camacho, Silthar Oliva, Ulrith Gillett and Ylith Holder.

Gupta spoke and wrote in multiple languages, including Myrathian, Pyrathen, Therian, Thesvian, Velthar and Xarnum. Over the course of his life he received several honors: the Order of the Radiant Heart in 1948, as well as the Order of the Stalwart Heart and the Pinnacle Honor.

Nyssara Hilaire (31 July 1617 – 12 April 1687) was a politician who served as regent and bore the noble title of count. She was a member of the Kaldorath family.

Nyssara was born in Nextridge to Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris. She was one of many children in the Kaldorath household; her siblings included Bastian Everhart, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria and Kirelle Amara Thorne, as well as Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyvian Heredia, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

As a politician, Nyssara held the position of regent. Alongside her political role she held the hereditary noble title of count.

Nyssara was married to Liora Aelorian from 23 October 1635 until 9 August 1651. She died in Silvershore on 12 April 1687 and was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Zephyr Ulmaris (given names Sylas and Zephyr; 26 April 1822 – 24 March 1905) was a male military officer and ruler born in Celestrion, where he also died. During his career he served as military personnel and was a recipient of the Gallant Shield.

Ulmaris belonged to the Sablemoor family. His father was Jorian Bowens and his mother was Vespera Moonshadow. He had several siblings, among them Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex and Xendry Shields.

He spoke Malquari. His occupations are recorded as military officer and ruler, reflecting both his service in the armed forces and his role in governance.

Ulmaris is described in Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Xendry Cavalier (given name Elwood; 12 March 1860 – 12 December 1951) was a regent and military leader who held the position of regent, replacing Urylen Silverman. He served with the rank of general field marshal and was a member of the Constellation Institute. He spoke Malquari.

Born in Astral Springs, Cavalier was part of the noble family Yondercrest. His parents were Orlinth Loeza and Gleran Hills. He married Orindel Valtorian on 15 April 1883; their children included Elwood Oryn Fath and Pyris Ellington. He had several siblings: Elysia Maren Holloway, Halindra Murcia, Ilyra Valenwood, Quinlan Rivers, Rhelian Buck, Taylor Everhart and Yloria Oh.

Cavalier saw action in the Tempest of Steel. Over the course of his career he received numerous honors, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Celestial Distinction and Celestial Knightly Grade. He was also awarded a range of orders and chivalric distinctions, including the Circle of the Brave Lotus, Crystaline Honor, Ethos Token, Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, Knights of the Eternal Flame, Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, Order of the Radiant Heart, the Pinnacle Honor and the Zenith Medal.

He died in Hightower on 12 December 1951 of bronchitis. His life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Gelanthian Athletica (born 8 January 2026 in Aetherdon) is a Gelanthian princess, military officer, equestrian athlete and jockey, badminton player, fashion designer and writer. She is a citizen of Gelanthia and represents Gelanthia in sport. Athletica works in Aetherdon and was named after Kalyndra Ayoub. In 2058 she received the Order of the Dusk Rose.

Athletica belongs to the Graelith house and the Sylverian dynasty and is socially classified as royalty. Her father is Rhylaris Lisa and her mother is Elyndor Gulley. She has four siblings: Faryn Gastelum, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump and Jyris Palumbo, and other relatives include Elara Gelanthian and Ystara Michelle. Her stepparents have been Brendith Ransom (from 10 February 2040 to 11 December 2053) and Caelan Fierro (from 1 May 2058).
