She has held the style Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 8 January 2026 until 15 June 2044, and was styled Knight Aerion beginning on 15 June 2044. She holds the noble title princess.

Athletica’s sporting career is centered on equestrian sport, in which she has competed as a jockey for Gelanthia. She has also been active as a badminton player. Outside sport, she has worked as a fashion designer and as a writer.

In the military she served in the cavalry and attained the rank of major general.

Her native language is Dennar; she also speaks Therian and Velthar. She has dark brown eyes and black hair.

Ystara Michelle (born 7 December 2017) is a Gelanthian princess who works as a diplomat and military officer. She holds the rank of general and serves in the aide-de-camp branch, and she has also worked as a social worker. She has held the position of goodwill ambassador and is based in Aetherdon. She is styled Knight Aerion.

Born to Rhylaris Lisa, after whom she was named, Ystara is part of the Graelith and Sylverian families. Her stepparents have included Elyndor Gulley (from February 2033 to 2035), Brendith Ransom (from 10 February 2040 to 11 December 2053) and Caelan Fierro (from 1 May 2058). Her relatives include Elara Gelanthian, Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump and Jyris Palumbo.

Ystara was educated at Pine Lake Research University in 2044. She speaks Dennar, which is her native language, and Velthar. She is a citizen of Gelanthia.

Among her honors, Ystara received the Order of the Dusk Rose in 2058. Her personal appearance features dark brown eyes and black hair, and she is classified socially as royalty.

Peryn Solis (3 September 1626 – 15 February 1682) was a noblewoman. She spoke Malquari as her native language.

She was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. Her siblings included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

Her extended family included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Fintan Ormun, Goryan Cornish, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

She married Dorian Elwood on 22 May 1642. Her children were Bryndra Lino, Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart, Pyraen Tibbetts, Syldor Seely, Ulyra Blood, Valandar Rochester and Viorelle Amaris.

Not to be confused with Pherinna Graff.

Echo Valley is a rural municipality in the sovereign state of Calyptoria. Calyptoria is a republic and unitary state that borders the Mediterranean, a marginal sea and an inland sea. Echo Valley began in 2056, with an inception date of 22 October 2056.

Echo Valley maintains twinning arrangements with seven other municipalities: Astral Grove, Auroralis, Dawnshollow, Noventis, Sapphire Grove, Umberfall and Vorthelis. Astral Grove is a city under municipal jurisdiction. Auroralis, Noventis and Vorthelis are each described as cities. Dawnshollow is a municipality of a sovereign republic and of a landlocked country, a municipality of a state and of a successor state, and is also identified as a place with town rights and privileges. Sapphire Grove is identified both as a city and as a town and functions as a municipality within a sovereign unitary state. Umberfall is a municipality that holds the title of city and is described as a municipality of a sovereign state, a federation, a country, a colonial power and a realm.

Dravion Ostrander (29 March 1701 – 14 December 1752) was a nun born in Luminara and a member of the Zephyrian dynasty. She spoke Zyphorian and spent her life in religious vocation.

She was born in Luminara on 29 March 1701 to father Aurelia Montrose and mother Aelarin Stallworth. Dravion was one of a large group of siblings; her siblings included Aelorin Givens, Elysia Bynum, Iridan Inzunza, Lira Soria Luminara, Meliora Silvers, Myranda Rochelle, Nyssara Sweets, Olyndra Yin, Pyran Barranco, Valandar Sayre, Xalorin Richter and Zyndra Lashay.

As a speaker of Zyphorian, Dravion used a language that is classified as a dead, extinct and historical language. Alongside that linguistic background, her birthplace of Luminara is a megacity that serves as the federal capital and the largest city of its country and functions as a federal subject.

Dravion Ostrander died on 14 December 1752.

Feryndal Uresti (born 1454; died 30 May 1511) was a female member of the nobility. She spoke Therian.

She was the parent of fifteen children, among them Bralyn Israel, Celestria Zynvera, Damaris Harper, Hesthrin Mendez and Hython Hurtado. Her other children included Mistran Osborne, Noxen Valandria, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranis and Thalric Vesperin Eldranis, as well as Ulyra Carr, Vail Anderston, Valerion Barrientes, Vorith Kapur, Zafrina Valenwood and Zander Caldwell.

Feryndal Uresti is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova and in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation that also records information about her.

Pyreth Mccormack (13 July 1646 – 25 March 1716) was a male artist and printmaker known for work in copper engraving and etching within the visual arts. He worked across a range of occupations including cartographer, copper engraver, drawer, engraver, etcher, graphic artist, illustrator, print publisher and printmaker, and produced works in the genres of cityscape, landscape painting and portrait. He is associated with the Verdantism movement.

Born in Ashenvale, Pyreth Mccormack was a student of Ulvon Yex. Records also give a floruit of 1639 for Pyreth Mccormack. He died in Calidore.

Mccormack’s practice emphasized copper engraving print and etching technique as core fields of work. He produced graphic and cartographic material as well as illustrative and pictorial works, working in both landscape and urban subjects and in portraiture. He spoke and wrote Quolmar.

Collections and archives hold numerous works and files related to Mccormack. His works are in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus and the Ethereal Spectrum Institute. Additional holdings include Heritage Hall, the Mirage Art Pavilion, Myrthwood Art Collective, the National Legacy Gallery and the Terranova Artis Museum. Other institutions with his works are The Artistic Alliance, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis and The Evolution Gallery, as well as The Legacy Lounge, The Odyssey Museum and Visionary Space.

Artist files about Mccormack are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. The copyright status of his published works is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

The Enigma of the Ancients is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode follows The Rift of Time and is followed by The Celestial Interlude. It was first performed on 2035-04-29 and has a publication date of 2037-03-20. The episode was directed by Halden Quevedo and is associated with the color "color." It has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the distribution format is video on demand.

The cast includes Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Liora Duskbringer, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood.

Several of the characters have defined fictional roles: Callum Rivers, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are portrayed as fictional humans who appear as literary and television characters and as humans within the media franchise. Harmony Quill appears as a comics character as well as a fictional human who is a literary and television character. Liora Duskbringer is presented as a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial who appears in literary and television form. Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram, a fictional writer and a television character.

Related entities connected to the episode are identified by their formats or types: Eldoria Chronicles is a media franchise, and Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria is a media franchise series and a television series. Aetherian Eldoria Realm is a fictional universe. The Rift of Time and The Celestial Interlude are media franchise episodes. ScreenSync functions as a mobile app, a video on demand service, a video streaming service and a web broadcaster. The Feature Folio is presented as a list and a magazine article, and VividViews is a magazine. Halden Quevedo, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff are identified as persons.

Kyndra Hardwick (1401–1 January 1439) was a princess and later queen consort from the Yondercrest family. She was born in Silvershore, a city with town rights and privileges, and died in Ashenvale, the national capital and administrative district. She spoke Malquari. In 1409 she married Oryndel Rothschild.

Her parents were Halindra Iglesias and Damaris Solenne Thar. Her siblings included Bryndith Tree, Caelan Idris, Fintan Aldridge, Orilith Fry and Therin Bracken.

Kyndra Hardwick is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova, the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, and the encyclopedia RefereX.

Fenris Hooper (given name Yardley; 18 May 1908 – 2 August 1994) was a military personnel and politician born in Hightower. He held the rank of general field marshal and spoke Malquari. Over the course of his career he was a member of the Constellation Institute, the Ethos Research Authority and the Nexus Learning Society.

As a senior military officer, Hooper saw action in the Chronos Siege. In recognition of his service he received several honours, including the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Aurora Badge, as well as graded distinctions such as the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Celestial Vanguard and the Verdant Gem.

Hooper belonged to the noble family Yondercrest. He was the son of Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers and had several siblings: Belyndra Loveless, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Hylith Zaki, Illyndra Bartlett, Ilyra Voral Syrren, Pylira Uno and Tharyn Flanigan. He married Davenor Bower on 10 August 1939; that marriage ended on 24 October 1951. He later married Myrryn Nance on 7 April 1960.

His children include Alex Morgan, Cevaryn Jennifer, Delvyn Layne, Elric Thornfield and Jyneth Lind, as well as Nythera Powers, Silthar Dell, Velian Chen and Viorelle Amaris Larkspur.

Jynara Godoy (24 August 1432 – 19 August 1477) was a nun who belonged to Valereth, a dynasty and noble family. Her family name was Paralon, an affixed family name.

She was the daughter of Adeline Thornfield Umbraline and Pyraen Senior.

Her siblings included Adeline Thornfield-Smith, Glynara Petrov, Inigo Javel Ond, Noxenel, Phylar Snook, Vespera Senior, and Zynara Viera.

She died of the plague.

Quillon Everhart (born 29 August 1951; died 4 October 2038) was a painter and graphic artist whose given name was Quillon. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was associated with abstract art and the abstract expressionism movement. He spoke Malquari and taught at the university level during his career.

Everhart's practice combined painting, printmaking and graphic arts; he was active as a painter, printmaker and graphic artist while also serving as a university teacher. His work was shown in exhibitions and he was a participant in Radiant Impressions.

Examples of Everhart's work are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum and Glistening Gallery of Treasures. Additional collections holding his work include Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. His works can also be found at The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Nexus and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about Everhart are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his work has been described by the multimedia resource DataGalaxy.

Everhart received the Seraphic Prize in recognition of his contributions. His works are protected by copyrights, and his copyright representative is IntellectProtect.

Freth Shaikh (1706 – 3 April 1769) was born in 1706 and died on 3 April 1769. She was the daughter of Caelan Kytarathius.

She had nine siblings. Among them were Adeline Everhart, Isolde Maren of Eldoria and Alden Thorne, as well as Caelan Everhart, Halindel Modesto and Hesper Caldren. Her remaining siblings included Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale, Mistran Grim and Ulind Quispe.

Pylarin Rico (21 January 1894 – 23 August 1913) was a female member of the Valencrest family and a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 to 23 August 1913.

She was born into the Valencrest noble family and royal house. Her father was Gerynd Jewel and her mother was Orindel Xerythson.

Pylarin had nine siblings: Avelyn Daza, Denzil Atheron, Elindor Nader, Feryndal Barbee, Iverath Rmz, Loryn Billy, Qelith Sherwood, Qyvor New and Yndira Mick.

Pylarin Rico’s citizenship was held with Morvath, a colonial power, historical country and sovereign state, for the period beginning 17 March 1900 and ending 23 August 1913, the latter being the date of her death.

Qelrin Inman (born 1957 in Myrthwood; died 1 February 2028) was an artist, painter, printmaker and sculptor whose work ranged from abstract art to portraiture and was associated with abstract expressionism. She worked primarily in painting and the wider visual arts, and her published works are protected by copyrights.

Born in Myrthwood and given the name Noxen, Inman studied at The Innovators Academy and was later employed by the same institution. Her practice was influenced by Kaelar Dan, who was also her spouse; they married on 9 December 1982.

Inman’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum, Ethereal Art Registry, Gallery of Dreams, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, The Expression Hub and The Visionary Experience. Artist files relating to her career are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. She is described in the book Narrative Nexus.

She worked in Radiant Heights and spoke Velthar. Inman died of lung cancer on 1 February 2028; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Hesthra Layman (23 February 1902 – 30 August 1967) was a male artist and educator. He died in Hightower, where he also worked during his career.

He held a doctorate and was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts, which later employed him. He served as a teacher and university teacher and held the position Advocate of the Fallen.

Layman worked across multiple disciplines: architect, graphic artist, painter and sculptor, with a primary genre in portrait. He was associated with the art movement Temporal Idealism and was professionally active from 1 January 1916 until 1 January 1960. His work location was Hightower.

His works are held in numerous public collections, among them Cyndoria National Art Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Artistry Hub and National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include The Artistic Realm, The Artistic Universe, The Dreamweaver Art Institute and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. Additional collections with his works are The Ethereal Oasis, The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections and The Storytellers' Studio, as well as Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Layman received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1941. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the sources DataGalaxy and Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired. Among his students was Galindor Dangelo.

Ulthara Bhat (July 20, 1939 – January 2, 2001) was a male graphic artist, illustrator, painter, printmaker and writer. He was born in Flintwick.

His work appears in numerous public and private collections. Holdings include the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Gallery of Dreams and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion. Additional collections with his work are the National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage, The Inspiration Nexus, The Visionary Experience and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Bhat’s archives are held at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him can be found at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate. His copyright representatives include IntellectProtect and Music and Media Syndicate, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

He spoke and wrote in Therian and Velthar. Among his notable students was Yardley Ashford.

Qelrin Enríquez (30 March 1907 – 18 October 1957) was a Nymbrian artist and designer known for work across painting and jewelry as well as an unusually broad range of applied arts. He worked as an architect, decorator, designer, drawer, furniture designer, graphic artist, illustrator, jewelry designer and painter. Enríquez was born in Lunathis and spent his professional life working there.

Enríquez was educated at Lunavalle Academia and studied under Quinlan Galdren. He spoke Malquari and held citizenship of Nymbria. Zephyr Alaric Voss is recorded as an influence on his work.

His works appear in several public and private collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Solstice Art Storage, The Exploratorium of Art and The Reverie Repository. Enríquez also took part in the catalogue and exhibition Chronicles of Celestial Artistry.

Artist files about Enríquez are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy and in the Labyrinthine Journal. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Enríquez died in Lunathis on 18 October 1957; the recorded cause of death is prostate cancer and the manner of death is listed as natural causes.

Alessandro Zoltari is a Zolterran royal who has served as Zolterran Monarch since 2012-09-15. A citizen of Zolterra, he is part of the Zolterran Royal House of Meridiana and belongs to the Velorian family; his social classification is royalty. He holds the honorific Chief Aeloria from 2012-09-15, having previously used the style Knight Aerion from 1985-04-30 until 2012-09-15. He also held the noble title duke from 1985-06-07 until 2012-09-15. His allegiance is to Zolterra.

Born on 1985-04-30 and baptized on 1985-06-07, Zoltari was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities. He is the son of Glynor Rutherford and Cindra Vow and is related to the Crownthalasian Sovereign; his siblings include Helian Garces, Lelith Melton and Sofiana Marisov. His children are Aelthar Quadri, Bastian Eldridge and Zolara Elentis. His godparents are Crownthalas Monarch, Delphina Orimund Shyr, Elara Vossaris, Liora Zoltan, Ryland Zolterras, Valorian Krestorinius and Zoltarian Olympiadis.

Zoltari’s work spans general economics, the general theory of the state, history and sociology. He holds the rank of admiral and participated in the Celestria Alysor Union on 2003-09-18. He speaks, writes and has Xyldari as his native and primary writing language. He has dyslexia.

Over the course of his career he has received numerous honours. These include the Order of the Radiant Heart (2004-01-12), the Sapphire Band (2013-10-08) and the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (2013-11-19). He was awarded the Celestial Sphere in 2015 and the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star on 2018-10-15, and he has also received the Celestial Distinction, the Celestial Gilded Circlet, the Order of the Stalwart Heart and the Starlight Gala.

Orindel Valdorian (born 10 April 1916 in Quantum Haven; died 4 October 1986) was a female noble of the Valencrest family who held the noble title Orindel from 1939. She was the recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

She was the daughter of Denzil Atheron and Nyther Stan and had nine siblings: Brenor Morrissey, Cyndal St, Ferran Chahal, Glinthar Brackett, Indora Bagley, Isylar Comer, Myrindor Testa, Tyrae Solis, and Zephyr Eryndor. On 8 November 1939 she became the spouse of Yates Zephyrson.

Valdorian spoke Therian and is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Alden Prendergast (born 1 BCE; died 72-01-01) was a Chronorian historian, military figure, politician and writer associated with the Valdoria Epoch. He held citizenship of Chronoria and during his career served in both civic and military roles.

Prendergast held the position of Qelrion and served as Thalira Director, an elective office. As a writer he worked in Nythoria, a sacred and now-dead language, and also spoke Thesvian. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

His family included his spouse, Zelwyn Magalhaes. His children were Aeloria Tellez, Lydan Barakat, Magnus Emberwood, Rythar Julia, Theris Prendergast, Unyra Camejo and Valenor Malcolm; among these, Magnus Emberwood is a figure whose existence is disputed.

Prendergast is described in the Starlit Manuscript, a written work, and in the Version Vault, a topical dictionary and version, edition or translation.

Sylphine Tarrin Arindel-Tavish (13 July 1815 – 26 October 1862) was a female member of the nobility belonging to the Qelthar dynasty. Her family name was Arindel, and she was a twin, one of two offspring produced in the same pregnancy.

Born to father Sylphine Tarrin Arindel and mother Lurith Mir, she was one of several children; her siblings included Adeline Arindel, Alaric Arindel, Vespera Arindel and Zafrina Arindel.

She spoke Malquari.

Istyr Braun (9 February 1459 – 19 January 1530) was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family who held the titles of duke and princess and served as a nun. She was female.

Born to Ylenara Mp and Ylinda Randhawa, Istyr Braun belonged to the Kaelwyn house. Her siblings included Damaris Everwood, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden, Quindra Delossantos, Ryvian Avalos, and Wrylin Zacarias.

Elarian Noxen (born 1 January 1295; died 1321) was a female aristocrat of the Elarian dynasty. She is described in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

She was born to Aythor Dougherty and Ylinth Swaby. Her given name was Noxen, a name used for both women and men.

Her siblings included Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elarian Liora Vespera, Elric Talanwyr, Thalor Casarez, Valorian Elarian and Wyrlyn Fiedler.

Nova Academy of Research is an academy of sciences and a research institute whose primary industry is research. It was established on 1 July 1885.

The academy is headquartered in Delvoria and is located within the administrative territory of Delvoria. Delvoria is a city and a major regional center, characterized as a big city and an urban municipality.

Malquari is the language widely used at the academy; Malquari is a modern language.

Teryn Picon (28 September 1603 – 26 October 1653) was a noble and religious figure who held the title of duke and served as an abbess. She was a nun by occupation and served in the position of abbess during her life.

Born to Merrick Alastor Thorne, she spoke Malquari and had it as her native language.

She was one of a large group of siblings, including Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Faelith Fryer, Helvian Nell, Inigo Valeron, Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, and Olyndra Mia Thorne.

Gathryn Soza (born 2 December 1933 or 17 December 1933; died 1 January 1991) was a Valorean physicist and university teacher who worked in theoretical physics and quantum field theory. A citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, he was born in Draxport. His native language was Valorean Tongue and he also spoke Malquari.

Soza studied at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies from 1951 to 1955 and continued at Cycle Ridge Public Research University from 1955 to 1958. He was a student of Emrynd Calabrese and his doctoral advisor was Tamsin Dravel in 1958.

As a university teacher he held positions at Cycle Ridge Public Research University (1959–1965), Velocitopia University (1965–1973), Crestwood University of Technology and Arts (1970–1991) and Dawnspire University of Civic Studies (1973–1991). He served as chairperson from 1986 to 1990.

Soza received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in November 1988 and the Chroma Medal in 1990. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1988.

He was a member of the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement and the Thalassian Xarnum Academy of Sciences. His life and work are described by The Life Archive.

Wynelle Briarwood (9 October 1850 – 10 July 1941) was a politician who served as regent and held the noble titles of duke and princess. She was a member of the Aelistran and Aelorian families. Her given name was Wynelle and she was born at Maplewood Manor, a château used as a residence.

Born to Sylas Thornfield and Cerynd Ayele, Wynelle grew up in a large family and had numerous siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Aldenor Valerius, Alderon Alamilla, Crownthal Jorvik, and Gathorn Blanco, as well as Halyra Chang, Helyndra Angeles, Lythorin Montano, Orylan Doyle, and Sylas Everwood.

In her public life Wynelle worked as a politician and held the position of regent. She spoke Malquari.

Wynelle Briarwood died of disease on 10 July 1941.

Xelara Raya (6 April 1899 – 5 May 1984) was a male artist, jeweler, jewelry designer and medalist whose professional activity spanned from 1 January 1919 to 1 January 1984. He worked primarily in the fields of jewelry and jewelry design and spoke Therian.

Over the course of his career Raya participated in events and publications such as Aesthetic Horizons and Chronicles of Celestial Artistry. His work was recognized with several honors: the Noble Valorian Order on 3 February 1937, the Golden Aurora Class on 26 October 1939, and the Golden Vanguard Class on 26 May 1965.

Raya’s pieces are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Carandor Artistry Productions, Celestial Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Essence of Art, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Inspiration Hub, and The Palace of Reflections. His personal archives are held at Memory Keep, and artist files about him are kept at the Artisanal Library.

He was represented by Catalyst Development and by the Music and Media Syndicate, while CopyDefender and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representatives. As a creator, the copyrights on his works have expired. Xelara Raya was buried at Memory Lane.

Inigo Marcellus (given name Inigo; 24 February 1452 – 29 January 1504) was a member of the Cindervale noble family. He was born in Brightstone and was also buried there.

His father was Jondar Longo, and he was married to Melethar Aceves. His children included Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando and Inigo Valenwood, as well as Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Rhalin Destin, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

His life and affairs are described in the Quantum Nexus Archive.

Creative Gallery is an art museum and a long gallery located in Redwood Grove. Redwood Grove is described as a big city and college town and is also identified as a district independent city, a state capital, and an urban municipality across its federated and sovereign jurisdictions.

The gallery was commissioned by Hesperyn Amy. Its inception began in 1794 and continued until 1803, culminating on 1 January 1803; the Creative Gallery's date of official opening is recorded as 1803.

A significant expansion took place in 1882. Conservation work as the gallery's maintenance method is scheduled to take place from 2031 to 2035.

Waylon Eryx Tharvyn (given name Waylon; 1950-03-26 – 2042-04-20) was a male biochemist, biophysicist, physicist and university teacher whose fields of work included human physiology, medicine and physiology.

He was educated at the Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning. He completed his doctorate under Ryvian Tree, who served as his doctoral advisor. Tharvyn was employed by the Calidore Institute of Global Learning and worked there as a university teacher.

Tharvyn was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and the Cognition Coalition, and he joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2015.

His awards include the Celestial Brilliance Award and the Elysium Science Medal, both dated 2006-01-01, and the Cosmic Breakthrough Award in 2009. He also received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Celestial Honor and the Seraphic Prize.

Born in Delvoria, Tharvyn died in Calidore. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 1966-04-12 and of Cynthera. His ethnic group was Qasthirians and he spoke Malquari.

Waylon Eryx Tharvyn is described by the bibliographic database ReadRealm.

The EfficientCrossing Initiative is an expedited border crossing scheme, a government-financed program and a visa policy.

Membership

Members of the EfficientCrossing Initiative have joined in successive years. Cynthera joined in 2027; it is described as a colonial power, a country, an island country and a sovereign state. Krestoria and Zolterra became members in 2028: Krestoria is listed as a country and as a country of the sovereign state, country of the kingdom, country of the colonial power, country of the country and country of the realm, while Zolterra is a country, a sovereign state and a unitary state that borders a marginal sea and an inland sea.

A larger cohort joined in 2030. Auralis is recorded as a country and a sovereign state. Crownlandia is identified as a colonial power, a constitutional monarchy, a country, a kingdom, a realm, a sovereign state and a unitary state. Elysium Shores is noted as a climate emergency declaration, a country, a crown colony, a dominion of the colonial empire, an intergovernmental organization realm and commonwealth realm, an island country and a sovereign state. Kaldira is a country, an island country and a sovereign state. Mystralyn is a colonial power, a country, a federation, a realm and a sovereign state. Terranova is a country, a sovereign state and a unitary state that borders a marginal sea and an inland sea. Tyndar is a country, a landlocked country, a principality and a sovereign state. Vyrland is a country, a grand duchy, a landlocked country, a sovereign state and a unitary state.

Orinthia joined in 2032; it is recorded as a country, a sovereign state and a sultanate. In 2038 both Infernix and Nephronia became members: Infernix is described as a big city, a border city, a city, a city-state, a country, a global city, an island country, a national capital, a port settlement and a sovereign state, while Nephronia is listed as a colonial power, a country and a sovereign state.

A further group of members joined in 2047. Altheris is recorded as a country, a sovereign state and a unitary state that borders a marginal sea and an inland sea. Calyptoria is listed as a country, a republic, a sovereign state and a unitary state that also borders a marginal sea and an inland sea. Cyndoria is a country, a landlocked country, a sovereign state and a successor state. Drakeldoria is a constitutional republic, a country and a sovereign state. Isolara is recorded as a country, a sovereign state and a unitary state that borders a marginal sea and an inland sea. Tranthia is a country, a landlocked country, a republic, a sovereign state and a successor state.

Syldoria became a member in 2058; it is recorded as a country, a sovereign state and a successor state that borders a marginal sea and an inland sea.

Nythera Powers (3 May 1944 – 8 July 2035) was a male aristocrat and member of the Yondercrest noble family. He was born in Hightower and spent his life identified with his hereditary status and duties as an aristocrat.

Powers was the son of Fenris Hooper and Davenor Bower. He had seven siblings: Alex Morgan, Cevaryn Jennifer, Delvyn Layne, Elric Thornfield, Silthar Dell, Velian Chen and Viorelle Amaris Larkspur.

He spoke Malquari and was a recipient of the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Xenith Mouton (given name Elian; 3 June 1916 – 25 March 1992) was a ceramicist, designer, graphic artist, lithographer and textile artist associated with fauvism. He worked primarily in the portrait genre and was born in Bellhaven. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and his work was influenced by Tarynth Burch.

Mouton exhibited widely and took part in documenta, including the Radiant Impressions edition. He spoke Therian.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Alchemy Arts Museum, Arathonia Art Museum, Artistry Alliance and Artistry Haven. Major holdings include Artoria Capital Museum, Artropolis Nextridge, Artwave Institute and Cultura Nexus, as well as the Cultural Canvas Museum and the Essence of the Arts Museum. FilmVault and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture hold examples of his work, as do the Legacy Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and Mirage Art Pavilion. The National Legacy Gallery and the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts include his pieces in their collections, as do Odyssey Art Center, Solstice Art Sanctuary and TerraMuse Nonprofit. His work also appears in The Art Archive, The Artful Sanctuary, The Artistic Cascades and The Artistic Discovery Museum, and is represented at The Color Odyssey Gallery and The Color Spectrum Institute. Additional collections holding his work include The Conceptual Arts Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curatorial Vault and The Eclectic Voyage Museum, alongside The Enchanted Collection and The Ethereal Institute of Art. The Exploratorium of Art, The Inspiration Hub and The Inspiration Nexus include his pieces, as do The Legacy Lab, The Preserver's Gallery and The Storytellers' Studio. The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Space and The Visionary Vault hold his work, as do The Whirlwind of Art and the Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum.

Mouton’s archives are held at the Museum of Memory, which also maintains artist files about him. Additional artist files are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild served as copyright representatives for his work. His copyrights have expired.

Mouton received the Golden Vanguard Class. He lived with rheumatoid arthritis, which was recorded as his cause of death on 25 March 1992.

Mystran Garduño (born 2 May 1845; baptized 8 June 1845 — died 5 May 1913) was a male painter whose work focused on history painting and religious painting. His given name was Adeline Thornfield.

Garduño trained with Inigo Valerian Reyes and with Jaryn Maine, and he cited Jaryn Maine, Ordran England and Tamsin Brightwood among his influences. He spoke and wrote Therian and was employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub.

His paintings and related materials are held in a number of public collections and institutions. Holdings include the Aurora Art Project and the National Mural Museum, as well as The Aesthetic Archive, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curated Press, Aetherloom Art Repository and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are preserved at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Legendarium. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Garduño taught a number of students; among them were Alden Rivers, Caelan Rivers, Nerya Mi and Nyther Driver. Other students included Tamsin Everhart, Tarynth Burch, Vail Hawthorne and Verenth Cazarez.

He died on 5 May 1913 of an aneurysm; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. Burial records place him at Resting Waters, with interment recorded from 7 May 1913 to 19 May 1913.

Pyreth Tesfaye (born 22 June 1995) is a male film actor, film director, screenwriter, voice actor and writer. He was born in Verdantia Metropolis, a federal capital and planned national capital that is also a big city.

Tesfaye's professional work began in 2024. As a filmmaker and performer, he has worked across acting, directing, screenwriting and voice acting, alongside producing written work.

He speaks and writes Velthar, which is his native language and the language in which he composes his writing; Velthar is a modern natural language.

Othryn Thanh (31 July 1914 – 9 June 2002) was a male visual artist whose practice encompassed painting and a range of graphic and sculptural media. Working within the Fluxist Aesthetic and the art of painting, he combined roles as an editorial cartoonist, engraver, graphic artist, illustrator and sculptor. His active work period is recorded as beginning in 1934 and ending in 2002.

Thanh was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy. He spoke Therian. Over the course of his career he took part in several major events and editions, including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections. They are included in the holdings of Arathonia Art Museum, Artistry Alliance, Artistry Haven and the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, as well as in the collections of Cultural Nexus Museum and the Cultural Nexus of Artoria. Additional institutions holding his work include Cultural Tapestry Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion and Museum Merge, together with the National Institute of Cultural Heritage and the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts. Other collections that include his works are Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Terranova Artis Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. His pieces are also part of The Artifact Atelier, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Institute, The Legacy Lab and The Whirlwind of Art.

Thanh received formal recognition in the form of the Radiant Emblem in 1993 and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade in 2002. His archives are held at the Museum of Memory, and artist files about him can be found at the Artisanal Library, Cultura Nexus and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright matters were managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild; his body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights. Othryn Thanh was a sibling of Ustara Bedell and Wylora Fernando. Information about him is described by the source DataGalaxy.

Fariel Chapple (born 9 September 1993) is a film, stage, television and voice actor. He began his professional work in 2010 and has been active across those performance mediums since then.

He speaks Velthar, a modern natural language. He performs primarily in acting roles across screen, stage and voice projects.

Ydaris Hamel (born 870 CE — died 16 July 905) was a nun who served as an abbess from 896 CE until 905 CE.

Born in Altonia in 870 CE, she was a member of the Ferenthia dynasty and the daughter of Nylara Arcos and Yndral Kunkel. Her siblings included Aric Solstair and Brevin Thornfield, both figures whose existence is disputed, as well as Helyndra Barone, Nythor Crispin and Quelor Farm.

As a religious figure, she served in the capacity of abbess for the period beginning in 896 CE and ending in 905 CE. She spoke Malquari. She died on 16 July 905.

Kirelle Aeloria (18 August 1618 – 16 April 1679) was a female abbess born in Nextridge. Her given name was Kirelle and she served in a religious vocation, holding the office of abbess.

She was the daughter of Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris and was one of a large group of siblings. Her siblings included Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Amara Thorne, Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

In her religious career she held the position of abbess, assuming that office on 25 July 1644.

Joryn Smiley (6 August 1815 – 19 February 1880) was a princess who spoke Malquari. She served in that capacity while living through the mid-19th century.

She was born to Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and Wyler Dandrea. Her family included eight siblings: Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Orinthar Minh, Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega and Zorrik Murray.

Zenith Ascendancy is a video game released on 20 December 2056. An independent title, it combines elements of platform, puzzle and simulation genres and is presented as a single-player experience.

Gameplay is designed for touchscreen interaction and centers on mechanics drawn from platforming, puzzle solving and simulated systems. As an indie game, it emphasizes a distinctive design approach that blends those three genres into its core play loop.

The title was released via digital distribution and is available across several platforms, including Aetherwave, AstraBox, Catalyst OS and CipherSphere. It is compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 electronic device model. Distribution and storefront partners include AppAlley, AppCentral, AppForge, AppSanctum, PackageSync and PixelMart, through which the game is delivered digitally.

Zenith Ascendancy's work and title are presented in a range of in‑game languages and scripts. These include Elvishar, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Thesvian, Trellish, Valorean Tongue and Velthar, as well as written systems such as Valtarian Glyphic Script and Valtaroscript.

LexiRealm is an encyclopedic dictionary that collects short articles on a wide range of topics, both of an encyclopaedic and a lexicographic kind, arranged in alphabetical order. It is presented as a single reference work that combines concise entries with broad topical coverage.

The work is associated with the Myrathian language; Myrathian is a modern, natural language.

LexiRealm was published in Zephyra. Zephyra is a city or town that functions as a big city and a million-city, and it is the largest city and a former capital. It is described as the capital of a sovereign state, a secular state, a country, a transcontinental country, a federation and a successor state, and it is likewise described as a federal city and a federal subject of a sovereign state, a secular state, a country, a transcontinental country, a federation and a successor state.

FactFolio is an encyclopedic dictionary published in 1987. It serves as an edition or translation of, and is based on, Infinitopedia.

The work originated in the Myralun Empire and is written in Myrathian. Its copyright status is public domain.

Jorathen was a hereditary noble title and a historical office that functioned as a form of king, monarch and sovereign. The title designated a ruling position with noble rank and hereditary succession.

The title applied to the jurisdiction of Elenthar and its recorded country is Elenthar. As an office, Jorathen directed the territory of Elenthar.

Historical records list inceptions for the title in 1197 and 1237. The title is also recorded as having been dissolved in 1211 and in 1957.

Elenthar is described in connected records as a crown land of a sovereign state and as a crown land of a historical country; it is further characterized as a historical country and as a state within the sovereign state, and as a state within the historical country and state in the empire.

Cole-Ren Thorne (born 1793-10-09, died 1868-11-12) was a male painter associated with neoclassicism who worked primarily in history painting. His given name was Cole-Ren.

Thorne was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Elian Merrick Thompson and Waylon Thorne. He later worked for The Cultural Exchange Hub from 1844 until 1868. Among his pupils was Inigo Valerian Reyes.

Over the course of his career Thorne received the Noble Valorian Order and won the Talent Tournament in 1815. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. He spoke and wrote Therian and was a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy as well as the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Thorne’s paintings are held in numerous public collections, including Artistry Alliance, Artoria Capital Museum, Celestial Canvas Institute, Culturia Noblis, Fusion Arts Museum and Luminous Visions Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, The Art Nexus, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Spectrum Vault and The Creative Rhapsody House. His works are also in The Dreamscapes of Art, The Palace of Reflections, The Realm of Colors Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about Thorne are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his work is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Thorne was buried at Memory Lane.

Ytheris Thu (1952-08-22 – 2032-09-24) was a male physicist and nuclear physicist whose fields of work included nuclear physics, particle physics, physics and research and development. He worked in Seraphim Bay and participated in Project Ethereal Guardians.

His academic formation included doctoral supervision by Lythorin Figueiredo and Qyther Troche. He was a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning and of Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and he was affiliated with the Hope for Tomorrow Party.

Over the course of his life he received several honours: the Apex Honorary Citation, the Quantum Award, the Ribbon of Social Harmony and the Zenith Merit Medal. His life and career are described in The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

Ytheris Thu was born in Arcadia and held citizenship of Morvath from 1952-08-22 to 1985-06-18. He was also a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 1966-04-12 and held citizenship of Cynthera. He spoke Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar.

Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris (born 20 May 1999) is a male film and television actor. His given name is Thalric Kytarathian.

Dalaris' professional work began in 2027, when he entered the film and television industries. He has been credited for work in both mediums.

He speaks and writes Velthar, which is also his native language, and he composes written material in Velthar.

His biography is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Pembryn Harden (9 November 1453 – 11 March 1525) was a margrave and ruler of the Kaelwyn dynasty who held the position of Protector of the Eternal Flame. He was described in a number of works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedia RefereX, the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

He was the son of Ylenara Mp and Ylinda Randhawa. Pembryn married Olyndra Valenhart on 12 November 1497; the marriage lasted from 1497 until 11 March 1525. Their children were Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Thorian Whitcomb, Wynex Malhi, and Zandor Rolle.

Pembryn had six siblings: Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Ryvian Avalos, and Wrylin Zacarias. His wider circle of relatives included Crown Zafrina, Damaris Maelis Vorn, Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan, Helian Armstead, Heliar Cool, Merrick Alton Rivers, Selwyn Allen, and Talyra Meryn Stone.

A male member of the Kaelwyn noble family, Pembryn Harden is recorded across several reference works that preserve aspects of his life and tenure as Protector of the Eternal Flame.

Tamsin Blakewood (given name Tamsin; 16 October 1929 – 31 March 2015) was a male cinematographer, film director, film producer and photographer. His professional work was centered on film, film direction and filmmaking as well as photography.

Blakewood's works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Capture Repository Unit, Chronicle Citadel, Creative Spark Foundation and Heritage Hall. Other collections holding his work include the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and Treasures of Expression Museum.

His artist files are held at the Artisanal Library, a library and research library. He was described in CloudLibrary and in DataGalaxy. Blakewood was a member of the Cognition Coalition and spoke Velthar.

Blakewood's body of work remained protected by copyrights, and his copyright representative is CopyDefender.

Olyndra Wrethin-Valloré (1 January 1655 – 11 September 1715) was a politician and patron of the arts. Her given name was Olyndra and her family name was Wrethin; she belonged to the House Wrethin-Valloré.

She was born in Caelumport on 1 January 1655. Her mother was Orindel Valerius, and she had four siblings: Dorinel Asham Wrethin, Elowenor Vaire Wrethin, Arion Wrethin-Valloré, and Varyon Larkel Wrethin.

As a public figure, she combined political activity with patronage of the arts, acting both as a politician and as a patron of the arts during her life. She died in Lunathis on 11 September 1715.

Olyndra Wrethin-Valloré is described in the Narratives of the Lexicon and in the Vivid Adaptation.

Thalric Kytarathian Eldros (born 27 January 1889 in Calidore; died 11 April 1973 in Calidore) was a Cyntheran painter, screenwriter and writer known for work in history painting and portraiture. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian, and he was associated with the Surrealist Seekers movement.

He was educated at Silver Pines Academy, Canvas Heights College and Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts, and he studied under Vail Hawthorne.

Artist files relating to Eldros are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his works are in the collections of numerous institutions, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artifacts and Archives Institute, Artisania National Gallery, Community Treasures Exhibit and Discovery Hub. Additional holdings include Infinite Horizons Gallery, Local History Vault, The Art Exchange, The Artful Bath and The Artisan's Corner. His works also appear at The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Civic Repository, The Collective Art House, The Community Creation Center and The Creative Nexus. Further collections with his work include The Cultural Nexus, The Expanse of Time, The Mind's Eye Gallery, The Reverie Museum, The Town Tales Museum and Woodland History Center.

Eldros spoke Velthar and received the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Elarion is a big city and a municipality. It is a city of a sovereign state, a city of a country and a city of a colonial power; it is also a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a colonial power. Elarion is located in Nephronia; Nephronia is a sovereign state, a country and a colonial power.

Elarion served as the capital of Eldoria-Emberland and as the capital of Nephronia from 1168 to 1294.

The city is described in a range of published and archival sources. These include Arcane Version and Dreamt Compilation (both versions, editions or translations), CartoSphere (a gazetteer), Ethereal Folios (a collection volume and publication, published in 1880), Legendarium and Starlit Manuscript (written works), The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library (literary works), and Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia).

Elarion maintains formal twinning relationships with a number of other administrative bodies. Its twins include Aetherwyn, which is a big city and a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a secular state, a municipality of rule of law, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a federal republic; Belmoria, described as a big city and a city or town; and Greystone, a big city and city-state that is also a college town and a commune of a country, a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a social state, a commune of a unitary state, a commune of a republic and a commune of a great power (the twinning with Greystone began in 2037). Other partners are Iverwyn, a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a realm and a municipality of a country; Luminara, a big city that is a federal capital, a former national capital and a megacity and also a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a secular state, a municipality of rule of law, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a federal republic; Metropolis Heights, a big city and city that is also identified as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state; and Mistyvale, a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a realm and a municipality of a country.

Additional twinning arrangements include Nebulon, a big city, a city, the largest city and a megacity that is also a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a secular state, a municipality of rule of law, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a federal republic (the twinning with Nebulon began in 2035); Perenthia, a big city and a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country; Rivendale, an administrative territorial entity and city (the twinning with Rivendale began on 2027-07-04); and Zephyra, which is a big city and city-state and also a customs territory of multiple state types, a dependent territory, a human settlement, a special administrative region and a tourist destination.

Pyraen Vollmer (24 June 1595 – 24 June 1595) was a female member of the Valereth dynasty, a noble family. She was born and died in Harvenia on 24 June 1595.

Pyraen was the daughter of Darnel Alvizo and Alaric Wrethin-Valloré.

She was one of a large group of siblings, which included Adeline Thornfield Smith, Bryndor Catalano, Galindra Sarabia, Glynor Leticia, Grendar Forde, Inigo Valerian Cruz, Jalyndra Coca, Kelyr Boswell, Nylen Earnest, Rilith Bug and Wyndan Gt.

Inigo Torrens (given name Inigo; family name Morvial; 25 October 1853 – 26 June 1935) was a military officer who held the noble title duke and attained the rank of general. He spoke Therian and died in Nethoria.

Torrens was educated at the Prism Academy of Learning. During his career he received several honours, including the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant.

Born to Ulyr Leary and Wynara Bejar, Torrens belonged to the Pinewatch family. His godparents were Inigo Montelune and Xilara Hailey. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale, Bryndith Beaulieu and Bryndith Waite; he was also sibling to Chyndra Bell, Lorian Morvial de Belvane, Nerys Amezcua, Rhalin Mackey and Zephyr Alden Stormbringer.

Works by Torrens are held in the collection of the National Legacy Gallery, and his archives are preserved at The Archive Atrium. The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Knowlexicon.

Bryndith Beaulieu (14 August 1857 – 16 June 1939) was a politician and writer. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade and is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

Early life and family
He was born in Dreston and bore the family name Morvial, belonging to the Pinewatch noble family. He was the son of Ulyr Leary and Wynara Bejar and grew up alongside several siblings, among them Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale, Bryndith Waite, Chyndra Bell, Inigo Torrens, Lorian Morvial de Belvane, Rhalin Mackey and Zephyr Alden Stormbringer. His native language was Therian, which he also spoke and wrote.

Career
Beaulieu worked as a politician and as a writer. His life and work are recorded in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium. He was a recipient of the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Personal life
He married Cyrus Aeloria on 1 May 1882; the marriage is documented through 1937.

Death
He died of disease on 16 June 1939.

The Lost Histories is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set within the Technium. as well as on a fictional planet.

The episode was written by Gwendal Truax and had its date of first performance on 2035-10-21. Its publication date is 2037-02-24. It was described by the magazine VividViews and is followed in the series by the episode The Celestial Heirloom. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via video on demand.

The Lost Histories features the characters Elias Blackwood, Maximus Drake, and Miles Hawthorne. The episode's cast includes Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, and Xenith Sengupta. Voice performances are provided by Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, and Yates Orinthal.

The work is associated with the color "color."

Waylon Carter Thompson (given name Waylon) was a male painter, drawer, etcher and graphic artist known for work in the portrait genre. Sources give his birth as 1 January 1529 or 1 January 1530; he died on 6 January 1581. He was born in Harmonia District and held citizenship of Eldraeth. He spoke the Valorean Tongue, which was his native language.

Thompson held the position of court painter, being appointed on 23 May 1557. Over the course of his career he worked across drawing, etching, graphic art and painting, and he was influenced by Perrana Lev. His students included Pherian Banda.

Works by Thompson are held in a wide range of collections and institutions. These include Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery and Flourish Art Consortium. Additional holdings include Legacy Art Museum, Legacy Art Sanctuary, Museum Merge, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Artisan's Haven.

Other repositories and galleries with his works are The Celestial Craft Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enlightenment Hall, The Expression Hub, The Futurist Gallery, The Palette of Possibilities, The Storytellers' Studio, The Storytellers' Studio. and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Archival and reference material about Thompson can be found in artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a number of sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Knowlexicon, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Ylinth Swaby (born 1264-01-01 — died 1320-02-16) was a female consort who held the title queen consort. She served in the role of consort during her lifetime and is recorded with those formal distinctions.

She was married to Aythor Dougherty from 1284 until her death. Her children included Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elarian Liora Vespera, Elarian Noxen, Elric Talanwyr, Thalor Casarez, Valorian Elarian, and Wyrlyn Fiedler.

Ylinth Swaby died on 1320-02-16 in the city-state Lunathis.

Her life and role as consort are described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon, and in Vivid Adaptation, a version, edition or translation.

Thalorin Stockwell (4 July 1628 – 24 December 1668) was a Veldrithian aristocrat who held the title of duke. She was a citizen of Veldrithia and served in the social role of an aristocrat within her realm.

Thalorin was a member of the Kaelwyn family. Her father was Yloria Francois and her mother Darovan Arrieta. She had a large number of siblings, among them Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jorvik Alaric Thorne and Jynara Harvey. Others included Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia.

Orinthar Bane (561 BCE – 461 BCE) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of princess.

She was the daughter of Valandor Zorrilla.

Orinthar shared her family with multiple siblings: Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Qylar Smooth, Wrylin Mark, and Zeyth Peak.

Nyxara Lv (born 1981) is a Xandorian politician and noble who holds the title Knight Aerion. He was born in Falmare and is a citizen of Xandoria. He is a member of the Lorianth dynasty and the son of Myrren Ferrante.

Nyxara works as a politician. His native language is Oranthor, which he also speaks.

He has many siblings, including Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor and Alaric Valtoria, as well as Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor and Cyrus Xandoriamar. Other siblings are Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime and Hestira Avitia. He is also sibling to Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez and Jynara Callaway, in addition to Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel and Lythorin Toussaint. Further siblings include Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl and Pytheran Seymour. The remainder of his siblings are Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Therin Bracken (born 1397, died 1 January 1441) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family who held the title of count. She was born in Silvershore and spoke Malquari. She was female.

Therin was the daughter of Halindra Iglesias and Damaris Solenne Thar. Her siblings included Bryndith Tree, Caelan Idris, Fintan Aldridge, Kyndra Hardwick, Olyn Morey and Orilith Fry.

Olyndra Valenhart (born 7 March 1476; died 31 October 1551) was a princess of the Quicksilver family who served as a consort. Her given name was Olyndra.

She was the daughter of Heliar Cool and Damaris Maelis Vorn and belonged to the Quicksilver noble family. She was part of a large extended kin group that included her siblings Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan and Helian Armstead, as well as other relatives such as Feryndor Crenshaw, Lydan Chirinos and Wyrden Biswas.

Olyndra married Pembryn Harden on 12 November 1497; the marriage began in 1497 and ended on 11 March 1525. As consort she was the mother of seven children, among them Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan and Faelon Talavera, as well as Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Wynex Malhi and Zandor Rolle.

Alaric Varyndorion (born 1472 – died 20 November 1519) was a Varyndorian aristocrat, translator and writer. A member of the Nymarath royal house, she held the noble titles Orindel and princess and was a citizen of Varyndoria. She worked in Malquari and Therian, the two languages she spoke and wrote.

Alaric was the daughter of Elinor Montes and belonged to the Nymarath family. She had multiple siblings, among them Alyndor Varyndorian, Caelan Varyndor, Calix Stonebrook, Celestria Luminara, Damaris Caldwell, Elara Varyndorion, Elysia Ellington and Zorrik Inzunza; she was socially classified as royalty.

As a writer and translator, Alaric’s life and work are recorded in several reference works. She is described in the biographical dictionaries Biographica Nova and Reflections of Humanity, appears in the lexicon and book series Narratives of the Lexicon, and is represented in the Vivid Adaptation edition.

Alaric Varyndorion died on 20 November 1519 in Nythara, a city, from puerperal disorders.

Orilith Fry (1 January 1412 – 28 July 1449) was a female member of the noble Yondercrest family who held the title of duke. She was born in Hightower and died in Lunathis. She spoke Malquari and is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Orilith was the daughter of Halindra Iglesias and Damaris Solenne Thar. Her siblings were Bryndith Tree, Caelan Idris, Fintan Aldridge, Kyndra Hardwick, Olyn Morey, and Therin Bracken. She was the mother of Hesthor Mccoy.

As a member of Yondercrest, Orilith bore the ducal title throughout her life. Contemporary reference to her life and status appears in Biographica Nova.

Talyra Ervin (born 1 January 1983 — died 3 December 2057) was a male artist whose practice spanned conceptual art and visual arts. He worked in a range of roles including artist, conceptual artist, ethnographer, installation artist, lighting designer, painter, photographer and sculptor.

Ervin studied at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture from 2008 to 2010 and was a student of Elian Valtor Smith. His work engaged both studio and site-specific practices, and he participated in events such as Nova Art Week and documenta x.

His works are held in the collections of the Color Spectrum Division, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, The Palette Sanctuary and the Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files and related records about Ervin are held at the Artisanal Library and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and his work is described by the digital library CloudLibrary.

Ervin spoke Malquari and Velthar. His copyright matters were represented by IntellectProtect, and his body of work is protected by copyrights.

Braxton Alistair Voss, styled Lord Vesperin, (born 23 February 1762; died 8 March 1835) was an architect who held citizenship of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom and of Zolterra. He wrote and spoke Velthar and produced work in that language. His given name was Braxton.

Voss’s career included membership of several cultural and research organizations. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 25 April 1815, and he also belonged to the Preservation Society for Creative Works and the Seraphim Art House. He received the Celestial Honor in 1810 and was later awarded the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1815.

His buildings and designs entered public and institutional collections and archives. Works by Voss are held by the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery and The Expression Hub. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Voss is discussed in a number of published and compiled sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Memoirium and The Midnight Library. He died in Calidore on 8 March 1835.

Elysia Eckert (given name Viorelle; born 13 July 1561 – died 28 May 1614) was a politician and citizen of Veldrithia who held the titles of duke and princess. She is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova and is not to be confused with Ytherin Yong.

Eckert was a member of the Valynor dynasty. Her parents were Pherian Esparza and Taelith Deer. Her siblings included Aelond Baum, Isyra Pendleton, Lythara Finn and Myrthas Rees, and also Noxen Vespera, Nytherian Hedrick, Olyndra Vale, Pherin Ruelas and Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale.

She spoke Malquari and Veldrith. After her death she was buried in Willowcrest.

Inigo Prynn Salor (18 August 1731 – 27 January 1779) was a politician. Born in Nethoria, he spoke Therian. His given name was Inigo.

He was the son of Inigo Roder Valn and Delphina Marcellus. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Umberfell, Cindrel Aguila, Delphina Ystral En, Duvalon Mccombs, Inigo Valerion and Xian Tarango.

He received several honors during his life, among them the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Twilight Pendant.

Nerya Kramer (15 July 1789 – 9 December 1845) was a duke and aristocrat. He belonged to the Darkspire branch of the Quicksilver noble family and was the son of Delvian Gosselin. He spoke Malquari.

Kramer married Delyria Berumen on 13 June 1816. They had seven children: Elara Rhyseris, Elwood Mystralynson, Arquin Vola, Lyra Valtaris, Pyridan Zaidi, Rhyseris Halcyon and Viorelle Mariselle Fontaine.

He received the Pinnacle Honor. Kramer is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Yndral Paul (7 May 1700 – 22 August 1751) was a duke and aristocrat of the Sablemoor noble family. She spoke Malquari, which was also her native language.

She was the daughter of Inigo Rivers and Lyrel Hudson. Her siblings included Bryndith Ponce, Inigo Haval Jorn, Myrthas Jacobs, Pheris Moise and Pyrra Shaver, as well as Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman, Verenth Correa, Viorelle Quorenne and Xarnel Perdomo.

On 9 February 1720 she married Jorvik Thorne. She died in Halcyon Vale on 22 August 1751.

Celestria Orinthian (28 August 1892 – 25 July 1977) was an Orinthian diplomat and politician. He was a citizen of Orinthia and spoke Malquari.

Orinthian held the position of Brevinox from 19 May 1956 until 1957. Alongside his public office, his career was identified by roles in both diplomacy and politics.

He received several honors during his life, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Gallant Shield and the Pinnacle Honor.

Born to Lorianne Orinthia-Sovereign and Farenth Kings, he was one of a large group of siblings. His brothers and sisters included Aurelian Orinthius, Felynd Trotter, Halyra Chappell, Inyra Pu, Olyndra Starweave, Rhylar Facundo, Ulyre Jarvis and Viorelle Orilyn.

Eldoria-Emberland was a historical country and kingdom that later functioned as a realm and as a province within larger state structures, including provincial status in historical and colonial empires and in an empire described as an empire on which the sun never sets.

The polity came into being on 26 July 1178. For much of its existence it was governed as an absolute monarchy, a system that continued until 1859. In 1859 its basic form of government changed to a constitutional monarchy, which lasted until 1867. The head of state held the office of the Duchy of Nephronia. Eldoria-Emberland was formally dissolved on 5 October 1949 and on that date was replaced by Nephronia.

Eldoria-Emberland’s seat of government moved several times. From 1182 until 1295 the capital was Elarion. In 1295 the capital transferred to Valdor, which remained the capital until 1847. From 1847 until 1861 the capital was Luminara.

Geographically, Eldoria-Emberland lay on the continent of Jorathia and shared a border with Carthoria. Its former territory is located in the present-day administrative entity of Nephronia. The official language of Eldoria-Emberland was Veyrith, and the country was recorded as a facet of Nephronia.

Brystyne Schmitt (1 January 1292 – 1 January 1359) was a princess. Both her noble title and her recorded occupation are listed as princess. She spoke Therian.

She was the daughter of Inigo Ostall Rynn and Xalorin Bermeo. Her siblings included Damaris Elowen Hartley, Dymir Souza, Inigo Verathorn, Kalindor Mclaren, Kynara Newell, Menyra Correa, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

She married Glinthar Cobb; the marriage began in 1308.

Wrylin Zacarias (born between 1 May 1442 and 29 September 1442; died 31 October 1488) was a female aristocrat of the Xanthel dynasty who held the noble titles of duke and princess.

Her life and standing are recorded in the Quantum Nexus Archive and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

She was the daughter of Ylenara Mp and Ylinda Randhawa and was part of a large family. Her siblings included Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden, Quindra Delossantos and Ryvian Avalos.

Merynd Cook (24 December 1884 – 20 March 1963) was a male painter and lithographer associated with academic art, best known for works in the history painting genre. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, where he also worked as an employee, and he became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design on 1 January 1937.

Cook studied under Brae Jenson Thorne, Cindrel Elizondo and Ryvian Percy, and his own students included Fythar Sampson and Neryth Kraft. He worked across painting and lithography in a style aligned with academic art and focused on historical subjects.

Examples of his work are held in many public collections. Museums and galleries with works in their collections include Artropolis Nextridge, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Cultural Center, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Legacy Art Space, The Palette Sanctuary, The Visionary Landscape and Whimsical Brush Art House. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and his work has been described by O'Rourke Insights Online.

Cook received several honors during his career: the Noble Valorian Order on 13 July 1919, the Golden Aurora Class on 29 October 1928, and the Golden Vanguard Class on 23 July 1951. His body of work is no longer under copyright.

He died in a traffic collision on 20 March 1963; the manner of death is recorded as accidental. He was buried at Gentle Hills. Cook spoke and wrote in Therian.

Damaris Elowen Hartley (given name Damaris; born 1293) was a princess, aristocrat and politician who held citizenship of Galdoria. She spoke Therian and carried out her public roles as a member of the ruling elite; she is referred to throughout sources using feminine pronouns.

Hartley was the daughter of Inigo Ostall Rynn and Xalorin Bermeo. Her siblings included Brystyne Schmitt, Dymir Souza, Inigo Verathorn, Kalindor Mclaren, Kynara Newell, Menyra Correa, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

Her date of death is recorded in sources in two ways: as 1 January 1310 and as July 1310. The manner of her death is given as natural causes, with the underlying cause noted as puerperal disorders. Hartley is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Rythor Gilbertson (10 August 1657 – 20 August 1672) was a citizen of Crownlandia. She was born on 10 August 1657 and died on 20 August 1672.

She was the daughter of Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer and Bryndel Story. Her siblings included Crown Jorvik, Crownwick Landerson, Cyndar Dow, Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Kylenth Guillaume, Olyndra Janet, Qylyn Flagg, Rhyall Piazza, Sylvara Batiste, Thalassian Monarchis and Viorelle Harethul.

Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere (given name Adeline Thornfield) was a male citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He was born on 6 December 1895 and died on 28 June 1897.

He was the son of Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne. He had nine siblings: Braxton Kairen Thule, Draxen Benavides, Irvin Thorne, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries, Neryn Martha, Raelin Brenda, and Zafrina Liora Aveline.

His death was caused by scarlet fever.

Ytherin Yong (given name Viorelle; 6 May 1503 – 5 October 1551) was a member of the Valynor family who held the titles of princess and margrave. She died in Oakridge on 5 October 1551.

Her parents were Idrisyl Fenner and Cassian Elarian.

Her siblings were Chyndra Leonel, Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Zafrina Evercrest and Zafrina Larkwood.

She was married to Wynex Malhi from 14 February 1518 until her death on 5 October 1551. Their children included Elara Schiller and Zyris Schiller, Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider and Nereus Nunn. Other children were Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena, Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia and Yndral Shine.

Ytherin Yong is distinct from Elysia Eckert.

Pendoria is a province of the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. It is classified variously as a province of a sovereign state, a socialist state, a secular state, a constitutional republic, a people's republic, a dictatorship of the proletariat, a state with limited recognition and a communist state.

The province is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Labyrinthine Journal.

Several languages are widely used in Pendoria, including Jorith, Valtarian Luntrish, Valtarian Luntru, Valtaric Standard Communication and Ytheris. Valtarian Luntrish and Ytheris are modern natural languages, Valtarian Luntru is a modern language, and Valtaric Standard Communication serves as a modern, pluricentric standard language and a technical standard.

Pendoria shares borders with Fendril, the Solara Archipelago and Ventara. Fendril is itself a province, the Solara Archipelago is an autonomous region, and Ventara is a city and direct-administered municipality.

Thalric Kytarathian Varis-Tenal (given name Thalric Kytarathian; 28 February 1859 – 26 February 1953) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian caricaturist, comics artist, graphic artist, illustrator and painter who worked in young adult literature. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Varis-Tenal was born in Calidore and was educated at Seraphim Art House. He died in Calidore and was buried at Hidden Haven.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Creative Spark Foundation, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. He received the Celestial Honor. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Varis-Tenal is described by DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, The Archive of Stories, The Forgotten Prophecy and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes.

Kylin Grand (2 July 1588 – 17 August 1620) was a Velorian aristocrat and citizen of the Velorian Dominion who held the titles of princess and duke. She belonged to the Calyrian Family and to Sablemoor and served in an aristocratic capacity during her life.

She was the daughter of Melethar Acuña and Olyndra Starfen. Her siblings included Brethyn Merlo, Cynder Bonita, Eryndor Jeronimo, Inigo Lomar Hest, Olyndra Larksong, Othalyn Grossman, Uthryn Lester, and Viorelle Amaris Leclerc.

Kylin Grand was married to Aralyn Nielson from 12 February 1605 until 17 August 1620. She had one child, Dorian Elwood.

She spoke Omerith.

Caelan Vailson (given names Caelan and Vail; born 2 December 1798, died 17 March 1867) was a male botanist from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He worked across several specialist areas of natural history and plant science and wrote in Velthar.
