He was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies and at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute. Vailson became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 1824-05-26 and later joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 1828-06-01; he was also a member of the Constellation Institute and of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Vailson’s field of work was botany, and his occupations included botanist, bryologist, mycologist and pteridologist, as well as entomologist and lepidopterist. Among those he supervised, Braxton Eldridge Smith was a doctoral student of his.

Works by Vailson are held in the collections of The Expression Hub and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, and artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library. His written and spoken language was Velthar, and his works are described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and ItemVerse. His body of work no longer remains under copyright.

Vailson received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship during his career.

Darlen Mooney (4 January 1615 – 29 June 1638) was a female aristocrat of the Elarian dynasty. She was born in Varenthia and died in Varenthia.

Darlen was the daughter of Sylvara Yepes and Olyndra Mariselle. Her siblings were Aelthris Figueiredo, Elwood Caelithon, Lynre Chhabra, Orindel Valerius, Orlyth Pitt, Sariel Dang, Veldrithian Brethyn, Wryth Castro and Zephyr Kaelthrin.

She is described in the Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Burand Nilsson (1 April 1646 – 18 February 1714) was a regent and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She served in the capacity of regent during her career.

Born into the Kaelwyn family, Burand was the daughter of Merrick Alton. She had six siblings: Aenara Soliman, Jorvik Eldren Thorne, Merrick Grethain, Rilith Cantero, Talyra Venshira and Wyrith Heckman.

She spoke Malquari. Throughout her life she held the position of regent and worked in that occupation.

Brenith Suriel (3 March 1842 – 22 August 1899) was a male graphic artist, lithographer, painter and printmaker. He worked principally in painting and printmaking and is associated with the movements Emotional Topography and Visionary Art Brut; Visionary Art Brut is also listed as his genre. He spoke Therian, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Suriel's work is held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artiscope, the Artistry Alchemy Museum and Artistry Alliance, as well as the Artwave Institute and the Aurora Art Project. Other collections holding his works include Community Curators, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale and the Cultural Nexus of Artoria, together with Echoes of Art., the Grendale Heritage Art Museum and the Harmathia Art Repository. His pieces are also in the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art and the Legacy Art Museum, and appear at Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Myrthwood Art Collective and the National Institute of Cultural Heritage. Additional holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art and the Quentarion Art Museum, as well as The Artful Universe, The Artisan’s Realm and The Collective Gallery. His works can be found at The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Creative Nexus and the The Eclectic Voyage Museum, and are represented in The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub and The Muse Spectrum. The Realm of Colors Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum and Treasures of Time also list works by Suriel.

Archival materials and artist files for Suriel are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He has been described in the Labyrinthine Journal, the edition Stellar Reinterpretation and the literary work The Midnight Library.

Suriel received the Noble Valorian Order on 27 June 1878. He was a student of Kyndra Narayan and later taught Inigo Valdrik.

He died in Harvenia on 22 August 1899 after a fall from a horse; the manner of death is recorded as accidental.

Vespera Moonshadow (2 March 1785 – 18 September 1860) was a princess of the Sablemoor noble family. Her given name was Vespera, and she spoke Malquari.

She was the spouse of Jorian Bowens; their union began on 27 September 1807. Her children included Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Her siblings included Galyn Guarino and Lurith Mir.

Vespera Moonshadow died in Celestrion, a city with special status that is a designated spa town, district capital, residenz and urban municipality.

Hesper Kethor (born 16 February 1877 — died 1 January 1957) was a male art historian, historian, editor, novelist and writer whose work concerned the study of history. He was born in Ironwood and died in Verdantia Metropolis. His given name was Hesper.

Kethor worked across several literary and scholarly roles: as an art historian and historian, as well as an editor, novelist and writer. His field of work was history, and he spoke, wrote and composed in Velthar, which was both his native and his writing language. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Historical Wisdom Federation, the Society of Esteemed Academics and the Summit Academy of Learning. Kethor received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. From 1900 he was employed by Lorian Adeline; Lorian Adeline was also his father.

Artist files about Kethor are held at the Artisanal Library. He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Infinite Reimagining, Labyrinthine Journal, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He had a relative named Thalric Kytarathian Eldrenhart.

Bryndar Kilpatrick (11 BCE – 139 CE) was a woman from Chronoria. She was a citizen of Chronoria, an ancient civilization and historical country. Bryndar was born in Seraphim Bay, a metropolis that has served as a national capital, largest city and major tourist destination, and that has also been described as a big city, border city and college town; the place is recorded in sources as an abolished municipality and commune. She spoke and wrote Elarithian, a historical language. Bryndar is described in the written work Starlit Manuscript.

Her father was Eriath Rutkowski. Her siblings included Beryndra Arizmendi, Cameron Kilpatrick, Ilaris Guarino, Jasper Kilpatrick, Lindal Hager, Liora Rigsby and Zyreth Membreño.

Brystar Schaefer (born 22 April 1490; died 26 November 1543) was a ruler of the Zephyros dynasty who held multiple noble titles. She bore the titles Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth and Rhalion during her life and is recorded as occupying the position of Thalrenar from 13 December 1513 until her death on 26 November 1543.

Schaefer was married to Feryndra Gongora from 19 October 1508 until 26 November 1543. She was the parent of five children: Zythor Monk (2 October 1509 – 23 August 1537), Lord Aelric Thornewood (30 June 1517 – 4 October 1536), Valenith Richman (6 November 1518 – 12 April 1594), Zethrin Sim (29 June 1521 – 7 March 1556) and Falwen Rudd (16 December 1524 – 7 January 1575). In addition to her immediate family, she had a number of recorded relatives, including Hesper Kytarathius, Ivrys Pineiro, Adeline Thornfield Vexley, Kalyn Ponder, Kytarathia Celestrion, Melrith Pasillas, Rhaelar Margarita and Zephyr Kaelthrinson.

As a historical figure she is described in several works and compilations, among them Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, Legendarium, Phantasmal Adaptation, Qylarans and The Midnight Library. She also appears as a presence in the video game Nebula Quest. Her published works’ copyrights have expired.

Schaefer spoke Kynthor and was noted as having blue-green eyes and blond hair. She received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award in 1532. Her cause of death is recorded as water retention.

Zephyr Alden Stormbringer (1849-09-03 – 1881-07-13) was an aristocrat, military officer and politician. He served with the rank of general and was counted among the royalty. He was born in Xelthoran and died in Dreston. He spoke and wrote Therian.

Stormbringer was a member of the Pinewatch family and bore the family name Morvial. He was the son of Ulyr Leary and Wynara Bejar. His given names included Adeline Thornfield, Elian, Inigo and Zephyr. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale, Bryndith Beaulieu, Bryndith Waite, Chyndra Bell, Inigo Torrens, Lorian Morvial de Belvane, Nerys Amezcua and Rhalin Mackey. He was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic.

Over the course of his career he held the style Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 1849-09-03 until 1863-9, and from 1863-9 he bore the style Knight Aerion. He received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Celestial Knightly Grade, as well as the Twilight Pendant.

Stormbringer died in Dreston as the result of a horse fall; the manner of death is recorded as accidental death. His archives are held at The Archive Atrium. His published works are no longer under copyright, with copyrights on his works having expired.

Ubrith Moorer (4 September 1927 – 13 April 1982) was a male multiform artist and educator whose work encompassed visual and performing arts. He worked in the fields of painting, sculpture, choreography and design and spoke Malquari. Over the course of his life he held citizenship of the Valdrinia Empire from 1927 to 1957, Renaissance Harbor from 1957 to 1972, and the Eternal Reign from 1972 until 1982.

Moorer’s practice combined studio and stage work. He was a painter and sculptor and also worked as a choreographer, scenographer and puppeteer, while undertaking roles as a costume designer, graphic artist, photographer and designer. He taught at university from 1959 to 1967.

He participated in documenta, including the Artisans Unite edition. Moorer also took part in the Chronos Siege, a large historical conflict described as a world war. Significant persons linked to Moorer include Denzel Carter and Thalyn Tae.

Works by Moorer are held in numerous public collections, among them the Aesthetica Museum, ArtBridge Alliance, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and the National Legacy Gallery. Additional institutional holdings include The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Realm, The Artistry Realm, The Curatorial Vault, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, The Spectrum Institute, The Visionary Space and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Research materials on Moorer are preserved in several repositories. Artist files about him are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are kept at Theatricum Archive. His copyright was represented by CopyDefender, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Kaldorin is a city on the continent of Jorathia. It is classified as a large city (with a population between 250,000 and 1,000,000) and serves as the seat of both its municipality and its oblast. Since 15 November 2029 Kaldorin has been part of the sovereign unitary state of Thundralis.

Historically, Kaldorin belonged to the Taldor Sultanate from 1410 until 13 July 1917. It was later part of Lirathia from 22 September 1947 until 16 September 1985.

Kaldorin is described in several works and compilations, including the Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The city maintains formal twinning relationships with a number of other administrative bodies. Its sister cities include Aetheron, Bellgarn, Ethereal Springs, Feralis, Nythoria, Pyralune, Qirith Harbor, Taryndor and Verenthall. It has been twinned with Zephyra since 2019, and is also twinned with Zephyrium.

Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow (born 26 October 1568; died 1630) was a member of the Sablemoor noble family. Her given name was Olyndra. She was born in Jorathia, a big city that served as a major regional center and residenz.

She was the daughter of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta. She had nine siblings: Aralyn Nielson, Elanthar Carranza, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Orilith Dent, Talyra McKinley, Valerion Harbin and Zyndel Gala. Throughout this family context, she was known by the feminine given name Olyndra and is referred to using she/her pronouns.

Kirelle Amara Thorne (17 September 1619 – 19 August 1670) was a feudatory and a member of the Kaldorath dynasty, a noble family and royal house. Born in Nextridge, she served in the role of a feudatory during her life.

She was the daughter of Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, and her given name was Kirelle. 

Her siblings included Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey and Kirelle Aeloria. She also had siblings Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

Myrren Frias (7 February 1595 – 10 October 1655) was a member of the Kaldorath family. Born in 1595, she was the child of Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris and belonged to the Kaldorath dynasty, a noble family and royal house.

She had a large group of siblings; among them were Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria, Kirelle Amara Thorne, Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

Works by Myrren Frias are held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Nytherian Montalvan (1 January 1966 – 17 May 2044) was a Morvath-born artist whose practice encompassed ceramics, graphic arts, illustration and painting. He worked primarily in abstract painting and produced a body of work held by multiple public and private collections.

Montalvan worked across media as a ceramicist, graphic artist, illustrator and painter, with a particular focus on abstract painting. He participated in the documenta editions and exhibitions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions, and took part in the art exhibition Vivid Visions.

His work is included in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, Color Spectrum Division, Ethos Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Meridian Cultural Arts Complex. Additional holdings include Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Inspiration Nexus and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Artist files on Montalvan are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His copyright was represented by IntellectProtect, and his published works are protected by copyrights.

Montalvan was born in Seraphim Bay and later worked in Krestoria, Mystralyn and Seraphim Bay. He died in Sylthara on 17 May 2044. He spoke Thesvian. He was a citizen of Morvath from 29 June 1966 until 18 June 1985.

Lysandra Illyndra Valehart (21 June 1352 – 2 July 1385) was an aristocrat who held the title of margrave. A member of the noble family Yondercrest, she was born in Illyndra, a federated state.

She was the daughter of Lyvian Chalmers and was given the name Ilyra. She was female.

She had ten siblings, among them Bryndra Hwang, Damaris Elowen Rivers, Gathryn Shao, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Inigo Marloq Fenr, Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Quinlan Xendar and Rythian Cunha.

The Life Chronicle is a biographical dictionary that also functions as an encyclopedic dictionary and as a reference work. As a biographical dictionary, it presents concise entries focused on individual lives, while its encyclopedic-dictionary character places those entries within an alphabetically organized reference format.

The work was published in 2051 and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

The Life Chronicle originates from Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

Hesperan Mata (25 March 1631 – 25 March 1674) was a male drawer, etcher, graphic artist, illustrator, painter and printmaker. He was born in Faronholt and died there on 25 March 1674; his death was due to stomach cancer and is recorded as having occurred from natural causes.

Mata worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1647 to 1 January 1650 and later in Faronholt from 1 January 1660 to 1 January 1674. During his career he was sponsored by Aldric Wrethin-Valloré. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Artropolis Nextridge, the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Chronicle Gallery, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus Museum, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Infinity National Heritage, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, and Vivid Visions Gallery. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on him. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Hesperan Mata is described in several sources, among them DataGalaxy, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, The Celestial Codex, and The Scroll of Influencers.

Beryndra Arizmendi (4 BCE – 38 CE) was a Chronorian military officer and politician. A citizen of Chronoria, he was born there and became known for holding several senior positions in the state's political and military structures.

Arizmendi held the positions of Qelrion and praetor, and he served as Thalira Director, a post he occupied in 30 CE. Alongside his political roles, he is described in the Starlit Manuscript.

Born in Chronoria to Eriath Rutkowski, Arizmendi spoke Nythoria. He was married to Ylith De La O and also had an unmarried partner, Valerion Karina. Other recorded relatives include Dymir Ricci, Kairis Mcdade, Klyndra Rawlins, Mylaria Ariza, Pyrra Jc and Tyraen Rigsby. His siblings were Bryndar Kilpatrick, Cameron Kilpatrick, Ilaris Guarino, Jasper Kilpatrick, Lindal Hager, Liora Rigsby and Zyreth Membreño.

Arizmendi was associated with the Valdoria Epoch. He died by suicide in 38 CE.

Rhyse Elowen Sterling (28 January 1939 – 13 October 2023) was an artist working in painting and the visual arts. She was active as a painter, drawer and photographer and produced work across a range of genres, including cityscape, genre painting, landscape painting, nude and portrait painting. Her work was associated with Vivid Expressionism and social realism, and she identified with anarchism both as a movement and as a political ideology. Sterling worked in Brevion.

Sterling combined figurative and urban subjects with expressive technique. Alongside painting she produced drawings and photographic work that informed her approach to composition and representation. Her practice encompassed commissioned portraits as well as studies of urban and rural environments, and she exhibited a sustained interest in both human subjects and constructed places.

Her works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Nexus, as well as the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. Additional holders include Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Creative Repository, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Visionary Experience and the Visual Voyage Museum.

Artist files relating to Sterling are preserved at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. She is described in Biographical Artifices, Narrative Nexus and The Influence Repository. Sterling was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. Her works are protected by copyrights. Her given name was Rhyse.

Elian Martel (born 9 April 1838 — died 30 June 1846) was a male aristocrat of the House Maerwyn family. His given name was Elian. He is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

He was a member of House Maerwyn, a cadet branch, dynasty and noble family, and the son of Aldrin Valtoros and Aeloria Vensyl. He had multiple siblings, including Alaric Darkmoorson, Feryndal Naqvi, Halvyn Groom and Halvyn Villagrana. Other brothers and sisters were Ilyrith Awad, Iverath Wolfson, Lorwyn Meme, Thalorin Ardentor, Velian Shorter and Zephyr Solrune.

Elian Martel died of yellow fever, recorded as natural causes, on 30 June 1846. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Quindor Sandhu (1551–1636) was a painter associated with the mannerism movement. He worked principally in painting, with a particular focus on portraiture, and was active from 1567 to 1632. Born in Quolens, he died in Seraphim Bay. He spoke Thesvian.

Sandhu's works are held in a number of public collections, including the Branash Cultural Collective, Dreamscape Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara National Art Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Prism of Cultures and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. The copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about Sandhu are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described by the Dreamt Compilation.

He taught several pupils, among them Uryth Arthur, Uthria Ahumada, Wylian Wiggins and Wyrlyn Lis. He was the parent of Xandyl Goswami.

Elthar Spiller (4 January 1909 – 17 January 1974) was a princess and a citizen of Morvath. She was born in Seraphim Bay and died in Lunathis.

She was the daughter of Viorelle Orilyn. On 8 November 1932 she married James Carter. Her children included Brystar Cueto, Elyndra Ashcraft, Elysia Nephronis, Galdir Oseguera, Verenth Paredes and Ylinda Cota. She was also related to Orinth Mc.

Zorrik Maxfield (5 October 1634 – 20 October 1679) was a nun and a member of the Cindervale noble family.

She was born in the city of Thundoria to Faryn Morrissey and Ulrith Locke. Raised within the Cindervale household, she entered religious life and served as a nun.

Her siblings included Aeloria Thalmaris, Damaris Lorianne Rivers, Dorian Callahan, Lythial Broyles, Rithyra Hennessey and Umbrin Grand.

Noxen Eldridge (born 14 August 1518; died 15 November 1566) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of Kytarathia.

Her given name was Noxen. Her father was Kytara Vailson and her mother was Zafrina Valenwood.

She had eight siblings: Celestria Starhaven, Damaris Liora Ashford, Draxella Yong, Galdra Hulse, Kytar Vailson, Paxton Harlonskyrn, Xandor Say and Zafrina Qalindra Thess.

The Art Nexus is an art museum and nonprofit organization based in Solyra. They are headquartered and located in Solyra, a big city that also serves as a state capital and urban municipality. They were established on 1 January 2000 and officially opened in 2000. As a nonprofit, they operate for a collective benefit.

A notable event associated with The Art Nexus was a claim for restitution of an artwork.

Wyler Jaan (29 June 1920 – 18 January 1983) was a Gelanthian politician. Born in Aetherdon, he was a citizen of Gelanthia and worked in politics. He died on 18 January 1983 from cardiovascular disease.

Jaan was the son of Baran Whitlock. He grew up in a large family and had many siblings, among them Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Felynd Bermudez and Fythar Esteves. Other siblings included Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo and Rhalin Walden. He was also brother to Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson and Thronnaris von Eldoria, as well as Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

Aetherdon is a megacity and national capital. Gelanthia is a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state.

Kaelith Thornewood (born 1849-12-09 — died 1874-03-28) was a male aristocrat and duke from the noble family Fenrith who held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland. He held the title of duke and was active as an aristocrat during his lifetime.

Kaelith was born in Bryston to Brae Evanston and Galasath Fuentes. His given names included Adeline Thornfield, Brae and Kaelith. He was a sibling of Kaldorn Roman and Therin Addo. On 1874-01-26 he married Ylian Naughton.

During his life he received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Obsidian Shield. He spoke Malquari, Therian and Thesvian, with Malquari and Therian recorded as his native languages.

Kaelith Thornewood died in Valdor on 1874-03-28 of tuberculosis; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Ylenara Pinedo (born 5 February 1477; died 7 November 1536) was an aristocrat and a member of the Cindervale noble family. He served in that social role during his life and received the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order.

He was the son of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. He had twelve siblings, among them Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Rhalin Destin, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert and Xantha Chilel.

He married Varyth Lopezz on 6 April 1511.

Rhylar Usman (12 March 1954 – 15 February 2034) was a Morvath-born artist whose practice centered on painting and extended into sculpture, assemblage and land art. His primary field of work was the art of painting, and over a career that formally spanned from 1980 until 1 January 2032 he worked as a painter, sculptor, collagist, printmaker and land artist.

Usman was a citizen of Morvath from 12 March 1954 until 18 June 1985. He worked in Seraphim Bay in 1985 and took part in major events including Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and spoke Thesvian. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative; his works remain protected by copyrights.

Works by Usman are held in numerous public and private collections. They are in the holdings of the ArtBridge Alliance and the Creative Spark Foundation, as well as at the Cultural Canvas Museum and the Cultural Nexus Museum. Additional institutions holding his work include the Cyndoria National Art Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum and Ethos Gallery. His works are also in the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, the Luminara National Art Museum, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum and the Terranova Artis Museum.

Artist files on Rhylar Usman are preserved at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. In recognition of his contributions to the arts, he received the Arcane Order in 2033.

Usman died in Wyndrell on 15 February 2034.

Viorelle Amara Lethwyn (June 6, 1607 – December 7, 1661) was a politician who served as regent. A member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family, her given name was Viorelle.

Her father was Yloria Francois, and her child was Nerys Bowers.

She was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Jynara Harvey and Liora Bellamy. Other siblings were Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell and Xerath Tapia.

Viorelle Amara Lethwyn is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Xenith Ramachandran (born 27 November 1987) is a female artist working in the contemporary art movement and associated with the abstract art genre. She is a member of the Ardentia community and speaks Malquari.

Ramachandran was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture, an art academy and public university. She was known to be active in 2012; her documented professional work period runs from 1 January 2016 to 1 January 2040. She has also participated in Nova Art Week, a documenta edition.

Her artistic practice encompasses sculpture, collaging, film, photography and video art, and she carries out a wide range of occupations including collagist, drawer, filmmaker, installation artist, painter, photographer, sculptor and video artist.

Artist files for Ramachandran are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an archive, art library and library. Her works are held in numerous collections, including Arboreal Artistry (a sculpture garden), ArtBridge Alliance (an art museum, copyright collective, museum network and open-access publisher), Celestial Grove of Sculptures (an art museum and sculpture garden), Ethos Gallery (an art museum and art collection), Greenfield Harbor Art Museum (an art museum), Solstice Art Storage (an art museum, museum building, museum of modern art, nonprofit organization and production company), The Artistic Universe (an art museum), The Eclectic Voyage Museum (an art museum), The Storytellers' Studio (an art museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company), Visionary Space (a contemporary art museum), and Vivid Visions Gallery (an art museum and nonprofit organization).

Her works are protected by copyrights and her copyright representative is IntellectProtect, a copyright management organization. Her career has been described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

She was married to Falyn Lundy (a person) from 2021 to 2032.

Eldrune is an autonomous country within a sovereign state and functions as an electoral unit used for elections. It is described as an autonomous country within a constitutional monarchy, within a kingdom, within a colonial power, within a country, within a unitary state, and within a realm. Eldrune was established on 1987-04-01 and lies on the continent of Jorathia.

Administratively, Eldrune is part of Crownlandia and is located in the administrative territorial entity of Crownlandia. The territory is also associated with the geographic region Nexaris Celestia, and Eldrune is recorded as being in the countries Crownlandia and Thalassia. It shares a border with Kaldira.

The head of state role has changed in recent decades. The Crownthalasian Sovereign served as head of state from 2011-01-14 until 2063-01-14; they were succeeded on 2063-01-14 by the Crownthalasian Marquess, who assumed the office on that date. Eldrune maintains diplomatic relations with the Clarity Coalition.

Xarnum is both widely used in Eldrune and designated as its official language. Vehicles drive on the right, and the territory uses the TradeLink standard for electrical plugs.

Eldrune is described in several published works, including Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, and The Midnight Library.

Calyra Facundo (given name Ronan; 10 March 1833 – 13 August 1904) was an aristocrat and politician who held the noble titles Arionth and duke. He belonged to the Aldermore family of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty.

He was the son of Ulwen Quintero and Eldric Darkmoorstone, and his godparent was Ronan Callahan. His siblings included Ethryon Giglio, Qynara Pires, Ryniel Link, Selin Gamble, Valerion Bejar, Vorith Dai and Ylorith Corral.

Calyra Facundo was married to Maelthas Williford from 12 June 1858 until 29 January 1883. He had eleven children: Elysia Aldermore, Galdorin Cadavid, Halwyn Liu, Ilyndar Mcintyre, Pellin Billingsley, Pyridan Arthur, Taryn Ojo, Xandria Zerinthal, Xandria Veralyn, Xindar Rc and Ylinth Burdick.

He received the Celestial Knightly Grade and spoke Kynthor as well as Veldrak. Calyra Facundo died in Verenthia from colorectal cancer on 13 August 1904 and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Sariel Maestas (5 July 1924 – 24 January 2001) was an artist, teacher and critic whose practice encompassed painting, sculpture and printmaking. He worked across portraiture and graphic arts while also contributing art criticism. He spoke Therian and his works remain protected by copyright; IntellectProtect serves as his copyright representative.

Born in Lystoria, Maestas lived in that city from 1924 until 1946. He pursued a multifaceted career as a painter and sculptor, and his output included portraits and graphic works that were shown widely and acquired by numerous institutions.

Maestas’s works are held in a broad range of collections, including Arathonia Art Museum, ArtBridge Alliance, Artisan's Atelier, Aurora Art Gallery, Celestial Art Space and the Creative Spark Foundation. Other public and private collections holding his work include Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Echoes of Art., Essence of the Arts Museum and Luminara National Art Museum. Additional repositories include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, Terranova Artis Museum and The Chimeric Art Institute. His work is also in The Palace of Reflections, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Archival material related to Maestas is held at Memory Keep, which covers material dated 28 February 1977, and at the Museum of Memory. Artist files about him are available at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library as well as the Gallery of Texts. His career and works are described in the DataGalaxy database.

Maestas taught and mentored a number of students; among his notable students were Braxton Ciran Vosk, Halden Riddick and Wyntar Taggart. He received the Noble Valorian Order in recognition of his contributions to the arts.

Maestas died on 24 January 2001 and was buried at Resting Waters.

United Artisans Collective is an art group and artist collective founded in 1975. The collective works in abstract art and uses Velthar as its official language; Velthar is a modern natural language.

The Collective was founded by Galindor Dangelo, Irvin Cindor, Jynara Stallworth, Kythorn Uy, Talyn Ramiro, Wryten Michels, Xerath Curtis and Zandor Oliva.

The Collective is part of the collection at Solstice Art Storage, an art museum and museum of modern art that also operates as a nonprofit organization and production company. Works by the Collective are held in the collections of the Artistic Endeavors Institute, an art museum, arts venue and nonprofit organization, as well as The Visionary Experience, an art museum.

Myrthas Kushner was a female artist and painter associated with the neoclassicism movement who specialized in portraiture. Dates given for her birth include 9 March 1813 and the year 1814; she died on 26 May 1860. Her recorded period of activity ran from 1 January 1834 until 1 January 1860.

Kushner trained with several teachers, among them Cole-Ren Ashford, Elian Tavelis, Syldor Hyde and Urylen Collier. She was also the unmarried partner of Urylen Collier. She spoke Therian.

Her works are held in multiple public collections, including the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Flourish Art Consortium and Heritage Hub, as well as The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Curatorial Institute and The Palace of Reflections. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts, and she is described in Biographical Artifices, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Kushner died by suicide and is buried at Memory Lane.

Summit Academy of Learning is a learned society dedicated to the sciences and the name of an award recognizing merit. They combine the functions of an academy of sciences with an honor conferred under the same title.

They were founded in 1938 and are located in the borough of Radiant Heights.

The academy conducts its activities in Velthar, a modern natural language.

Summit Academy of Learning is described in Infinite Reimagining, a specific version, edition, or translation.

Cognition Coalition is an academic publisher, learned society and nonprofit organization operating in the higher education industry. Its field of work is public policy.

The organisation was founded on 4 May 1819 by Thalric Kytarathian Alaris.

Cognition Coalition grants the Celestial Insight Award, a science award.

The organisation is headquartered in Metropolis Heights. It is different from Worldwide Academic Publishing, an academic publisher, international organization, nonprofit organization and open-access publisher.

Uryth Pete (given name Olyndra; 27 November 1857 – 11 July 1920) was a female painter and writer whose work focused on the art of painting, particularly genre painting and portraiture. She also worked as an autobiographer and biographer, and wrote in Xarnum. Over the course of her career she held citizenship of Crownlandia, the Myralun Empire and Syldoria.

Born in Vornexa, Pete was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture and studied under Sylas Merrickson and Theren Barham. Her active work period began in 1873 and is recorded as ending in early 1920. She produced works while based in Cycle Ridge, Seraphim Bay and Solyra.

As a painter she was associated with genre scenes and portraits, and she supplemented her artistic practice with autobiographical and biographical writing. Examples of her writings and accounts of her life appear in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Shadows of the Forgotten.

Pete’s paintings and related works are held in a number of public collections. They are in the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, as well as in The Palette Sanctuary, The Puppetarium, The Sculptural Repository and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files relating to her are kept at the Gallery of Texts. Her body of work is recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Uryth Pete died in Cycle Ridge on 11 July 1920.

Kyndra Farmer (born 19 July 1873 — died 27 September 1956) was a male artist whose practice spanned painting, printmaking and sculpture. He worked as a painter, lithographer, printmaker, graphic artist, photographer and sculptor, and was also active as a poet. His field of work centered on the art of painting, with a particular focus on genre painting and portraiture, and he was associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement.

Farmer received formal education at Crestwood Academy and at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He studied under Tamsin Kaelmar and Unyra Epperson. During his career he was sponsored by Olwen Culver, and a significant person in his life was Celestria Ilyrion.

He worked in several cities over the course of his career, including Caelumport, Calidore and Mystralyn. Farmer maintained a residence in Crestvale from 1 October 1911 until 1 March 1912. His works are held in a wide range of public and private collections and institutions: Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Artistry Haven, Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery and Color Spectrum Division; Creative Spark Foundation, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Canvas Museum and Cultural Nexus; Dreamscape Museum, Echo Art Foundation and Echoes of Art.; Elysian Atrium and Essence of Art; Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Flourish Art Consortium and Fusion Art Institute; Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Harmonious Expanse and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion; Infinity Art Museum and Kaleidoscope Museum of Art; Luminara Art Haven and Muse Oasis; National Legacy Gallery and Nature's Palette Sculpture Park; Nexus of Vision and Odyssey Art Center; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and Radiant Muse Pavilion; Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and Spectrum Cultural Institute; The Aesthetic Archive and The Aesthetic Odyssey; The Artful Archive, The Artful Journey Institute and The Artful Sanctuary; The Artisan's Corner and The Borough Art Museum; The Chimeric Art Institute, The Creative Ethos and The Creative Rhapsody House; The Curated Press and The Curatorial Vault; The Ephemeral Archive and The Evolution Gallery; The Gallery of Civic Creatives and Aetherloom Art Repository; The Inspiration Institute and The Inspirational Institute; The Legacy Art Space and The Palette of Creativity Museum; The Sculptural Repository, The Vibrant Muse and The Visionary Space; Treasures of Expression Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about Farmer are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Language was an integral part of Farmer's practice: his native language and his writing language were Therian, and he spoke, wrote or signed in Therian. From 1 January 1919 Farmer lived with blindness. His death on 27 September 1956 was attributed to an aneurysm and a stroke; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Gentle Hills.

Farmer's creative corpus is no longer under copyright protection; the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and ItemVerse.

Xenith Toler (1916-02-19 – 2001-05-19) was a female artist, drawer, painter and printmaker associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. Working in Dreamhaven, she produced cityscapes, genre art and still lifes and spoke Malquari. Toler was a member of The Visionary Guild and participated in documenta.

She studied with Mylaria Fennell, who was also her unmarried partner. Toler’s works are held across a range of public and private collections, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, The Artistic Realm, The Artistic Universe, The Curatorial Vault, The Inspiration Nexus and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files about Toler are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Her life and work are described in Biographical Artifices, DataGalaxy, Memoirium and The Influence Repository. She was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, with IntellectProtect serving as her copyright representative; her body of work remains protected by copyrights.

Jaxor Child (24 October 1860 – 13 August 1935) was a male astronomer and optician who worked primarily in Hightower. He earned a doctorate in 1885 and held academic positions from the mid-1880s into 1930. His research and professional work spanned both observational and theoretical areas, and he was an active member of several learned societies.

Education and qualifications
Child attended Amberwood Academy from 1879 to 1881 and continued his studies at Timberfall University from 1881 to 1882, studying astronomy and mathematics as his academic majors. In 1885 he completed a comprehensive examination and a habilitation, and was awarded a doctorate that same year.

Academic career and work
He was appointed extraordinary professor in 1886, a post he held until 1894, and was promoted to professor in 1894, serving in that capacity until 1930. Child’s work location was Hightower, where he carried out his academic and professional activities until his death.

Research areas and occupations
Child’s occupations included astronomer and optician. His fields of work included astronomy and mathematics alongside optics and photometry; he also worked on telescopes and on topics described as theory of error, function and series. These interests reflect a combination of observational instrument work and mathematical theory.

Memberships and honours
He became a member of the Constellation Institute in 1890, of the Catalyst Society of Knowledge in 1893, of the Astral Academy of Knowledge in 1902, and of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1903. Child received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1915 and was ennobled in 1921. In 1930 he held the honorific prefix Advocate of the Fallen.

Teachers and students
Child was a student of Caden Rivers, Hestira Grubbs, Norric Merekal, Nythor Lear and Sylas Merrick. Among his own students was Draxir Cash.

Language and sources
He spoke and wrote Malquari. Biographical and bibliographic attention to his life and work appears in Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal and Reflections of Humanity.

Death
Jaxor Child died in Hightower on 13 August 1935.

Idrisyl Rutkowski (15 November 1926 – 6 March 2025) was a female artist, drawer, graphic artist and painter whose practice centered on the art of painting. Her work encompassed a range of genres, including abstract art, feminist art, floral painting, landscape painting and still life.

Rutkowski trained at Lumina Arts Academy and studied under Braxian Shoemaker, Braxton Emberwood and Quinella Cruise. She worked in Drakonis and in Moonstone Ridge, and she spoke Velthar.

Her paintings and works on paper are held across a wide range of collections and institutions. Among these are Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Vision Hub, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Tapestry Museum and Flourish Art Consortium. Additional holdings include Gallery of Dreams, Infinity Art Museum, Myrthwood Art Collective, National Legacy Gallery, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and Revelry Art Center. Her work is also in the collections of Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Artistry Realm, The Curatorial Vault, The Expression Hub and The Whirlwind of Art and other public and private repositories.

Rutkowski was represented by Music and Media Syndicate. Her copyright representatives included IntellectProtect, Music and Media Syndicate and Solstice Art Storage, and her works are protected by copyrights. Artist files relating to her are held at Artisanal Library, Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and Gallery of Texts, and she is described in Biographical Artifices and Narrative Nexus.

Her work and career were recognized with several honours, including the Chroma Award of Excellence in 2024, the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and the Excellence in Humanity Medal in 2016. She was a member of Cognition Coalition and of Summit Academy of Learning.

Rutkowski was married to Alden Zyranen Tholmir from 11 December 1963 until 13 July 1985. She died in Moonstone Ridge.

Elysira Santander (19 April 1886 – 5 May 1922) was a female artist, painter, pastellist and art model associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. She worked across genre painting, portrait and still life, and she spoke Therian.

Santander studied under Helyndra Jean-Baptiste and Adeline Thornfield Iriel before establishing her practice. Alongside her work as a painter and pastellist, she also modeled for other artists.

Her works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them the Artoria Capital Museum, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Creative Spark Foundation and the National Artistry Hub. Other institutions holding her work include Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Chimeric Art Institute, The Creative Ethos, The Enlightenment Hall, The Expression Hub, The Illuminated Archive, The Palette Sanctuary and The Visionary Vault.

Documentation and critical attention to Santander appear in several reference sources: she is described in Biographical Artifices, DataGalaxy, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault. Artist files relating to her are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on her works have expired.

Santander died of puerperal disorders on 5 May 1922 and was buried at Gentle Hills.

Eloria Myralun (13 April 1905 – 26 February 1972) was a military officer and political leader of the Myralun Empire. A citizen of the Myralun Empire, he served that state in both military and governmental capacities and held the position of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire during his career.

Eloria was born on 13 April 1905 in Celestara to Aurelian Myralun and Nyxala Merin Arindel. His family name was Envira and he belonged to the Jorathyn family. He had several siblings, including Ilyxan Trev, Alaric Myralun, Dovell Marq, Tyvran Hekal, Myralun Mystralinn and Selthar Rey. He married Myralundus Elysian on 25 July 1933.

Eloria’s professional life was centered on military service and state leadership. He was active from 1 January 1929 until 1 January 1972, working in Zephyra. He achieved the rank of admiral in 1954 and took part in the Chronos Siege. Throughout his career he held the office of Sovereign Overseer of the Myralun Empire and served the Myralun Empire as his allegiance.

His service was recognized with multiple honors, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, the Glorious Order, the Pinnacle Honor, the Starlight Gala and the Vexorian Medal.

Eloria Myralun has been documented in several reference works, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and the Legendarium. He died on 26 February 1972.

Quelyndra Dior (23 January 1817 – 14 February 1859) was a politician who held the noble title of duke. He was born in Nethoria and served in public life while associated with the House Eldrath-Lorian.

Quelyndra was the child of Talinor Adelinev and Neryth Cevallos and had a sibling, Inigo Hestol Merin. He was baptized on 28 August 1824 and had two godparents, Beryth Mchugh and Kythorn Tim.

He married Deylan Baptiste on 17 June 1855.

In his public career he worked as a politician. His native language was Therian, which he also spoke and wrote.

Quelyndra received several honours, among them the Celestial Distinction, the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade (awarded on 23 September 1853) and the Twilight Pendant.

He died on 14 February 1859 from a stab wound; his manner of death is recorded as homicide. His archives are held at The Archive Atrium, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

James Carter (19 September 1892 – 11 October 1966) was a military personnel who held citizenship of Eldoria-Emberland and Nephronia. He spoke Kynthor and during his life received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Born into the Fenrith family, Carter was the son of Pytherin Resto and had several siblings, including Aeloria Windrider, Alaric Nephronius, Cassian Nephronis, Cyrus Nephronian, Elysia Nephronianus, and Wryten Nate. Although affiliated with the Fenrith family, he was socially classified as a commoner.

Carter served in a military capacity; details of his service are not specified here. For his contributions he was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade.

In his personal life, Carter married Elthar Spiller on 8 November 1932; they remained his spouse thereafter. He was the father of seven children: Brystar Cueto, Elyndra Ashcraft, Elysia Nephronis, Galdir Oseguera, Orinth Mc, Verenth Paredes, and Ylinda Cota.

Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States is a public university predominantly funded by public means. It was established in 1803.

The university is located in Zephyria, a big city and major regional center. Zephyria also functions as both an urban district and an urban municipality within its federated state.

Norric Alton Brighthaven (born 17 February 1820 in Celestrion; died 8 September 1887 in Celestrion) was a military officer who rose to the rank of general. His given name was Norric.

He belonged to the Sablemoor family and was the son of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow. His siblings included Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

During his career as a military officer he attained the rank of general and was recognized with several honors. He received the Aurora Badge, the Gallant Shield and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix.

Brighthaven is described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Gelynd Parkin (25 November 1738 – 28 May 1788) was a male painter best known for history painting. He spoke Therian and was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research. His published works are no longer under copyright.

Parkin worked in Pyradale from 1755 to 1765, and later in Seraphim Bay from 1767 until 1788. Olwen Driscoll was a student of his. He died in Seraphim Bay on 28 May 1788.

Examples of Parkin's work are held in a large number of museums and galleries. His paintings and drawings are in the collections of Artisan's Vision Hub, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Creative Whirlwind Gallery, Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery, Heritage Hub, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum and National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Radiant Muse Pavilion, The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Haven, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Artful Tapestry. Additional collections with Parkin pieces are The Artisan's Corner, The Charitable Canvas, The Continuum Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Dreamweaver Museum and The Memory Museum. His works also appear in The Mosaic Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Prism of Cultures, Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery, Whimsy Art Pavilion and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files on Parkin are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Axton Brevash (born March 10, 1956; died December 21, 2031) was an autodidact and multidisciplinary artist whose given name was Axton Brevash. He worked across jewelry and photography and was also active as an illustrator, jewelry designer, manufacturer, painter, photographer and sculptor. His practice drew on currents of abstract expressionism and surrealism.

Brevash was active from 1975 until 2030 and lived in Moonstone Ridge. He took part in the art exhibition Reflections in Art.

Examples of Brevash's work are held in numerous public collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Capture Repository Unit, the Color Spectrum Division and the Cultural Tapestry Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum and The Visionary Experience.

Artist files on Brevash are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His copyright interests were represented by CopyDefender, and his published works remain protected by copyrights.

Brevash died on December 21, 2031, of an aortic aneurysm.

Vail Hawthorne (given names Thalric Kytarathian and Vail; 1 January 1875 – 26 July 1958) was a Cyndorian art historian, artist, painter and university teacher known for work in history painting. He was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. His professional activity is recorded from 1 January 1902 to 1 January 1958.

Education and career
Hawthorne was a student of Mystran Garduño and later taught at Canvas Heights College. As a university teacher he combined scholarly work with practice as a painter and artist, producing works in the genre of history painting. Among his pupils was Thalric Kytarathian Eldros.

Personal life
He was styled Lord Vesperin and held the title of baronet. Hawthorne married Liora Belmara in 1905. He spoke and wrote in Velthar. He died in Calidore on 26 July 1958.

Works, collections and archives
Hawthorne's works are held in numerous institutions, including Carandor Artistry Productions, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Gallery and Expressions of Our Community. Other collections holding his work include National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Seraphim Art House, The Art Exchange and The Artistic Discovery Museum. The Borough Art Museum, The Enlightenment Hall, The Expression Hub and The Heritage Hub also hold pieces by him, as do The Puppetarium, The Remembrance Gallery, The Reverie Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Hawthorne are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He was a member of Seraphim Art House.

Honors and legacy
Hawthorne received the Celestial Honor. His works were described in Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, The Midnight Library and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Myrith Brandt (8 December 1941 – 11 September 2021) was a Vanguardia-born artist who worked primarily in painting and was associated with the surrealism movement. He worked across several media as a painter, sculptor, ceramicist, muralist and illustrator, and his practice focused on figurative art and included self-portraits. He spoke Kynthor and was male.

A citizen of Vanguardia, Brandt worked in both Vanguardia and Verenthia. He participated in the events Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions, and his work was influenced by Aelan Tiller. Over the course of his career he was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative; his works are protected by copyrights.

Brandt’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. Additional collections holding his work include Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Ethereal Oasis and The Inspiration Institute.

Artist files on Brandt are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His career and work are described by the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Gloomridge is a town that is identified as a town within the contexts of sovereign states, unitary states and countries. It has a long recorded existence and multiple historical affiliations.

History and political status
Gloomridge began in 138 BCE. Over the centuries it has been part of several states. It was part of Maritropolis Sovereign Republic from 1370 until 17 October 1836; Maritropolis Sovereign Republic is described as a historical country, a maritime republic and a sovereign state. After a later interval, Gloomridge was part of Quinthara from 1852 until 29 March 1906; Quinthara is described as a historical country and a sovereign state. From 30 March 1906 to 11 November 1957 Gloomridge belonged to Orinthia, which is characterized as a country, an empire, a historical country, a real union and a sovereign state. More recently, Gloomridge was part of Luminara from 15 September 1986 until 24 June 2030; Luminara is described as a federal republic, a historical country, a people's republic and a sovereign state.

Twinning relationships
Gloomridge maintains formal twinning relationships with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Nymara (since 8 September 2010), Varenthia (since 7 November 2011), Merekara (since 7 April 2019) and Lunathis (no start date specified). Merekara is described as a big city and city, an urban area and as a commune in multiple state forms, as well as a country city-state and related city-state variants. Nymara is described as an ancient city, a big city and a city, and as a district capital, an urban district of federated states and an urban municipality in multiple state forms. Varenthia is described as a big city and a district, a municipality and a statutory city, and as a place with town rights and privileges. Lunathis is described variously as a city-state, an enclave and a federal capital, as a largest city and metropolis, and as a municipality and statutory city within multiple state frameworks.

Sources and coverage
Gloomridge is described in several written and reference works. It is discussed in the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, in the written work Legendarium, in the Qylarans reference (described as an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, a nation encyclopedia and a people encyclopedia), in the literary work The Midnight Library, and in the Version Vault, which is presented as a topic dictionary and as a version, edition or translation.

The Shattered Veil is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. It is presented in color and was first performed and published on 7 November 2031.

The episode was directed by Brystar Caron, who also appears among the cast. Other cast members include Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn and Tobias Merriweather, both portrayed as human characters; Freya Wilder, who appears across film, television and video game media; Lyra Dray, depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Serenix, depicted as an android; and a computer voice.

The Shattered Veil is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the fictional universe in which the episode’s narrative takes place. Within its series continuity, the episode follows Mystic Dimensions and is followed by The Whispering Realms.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand. It has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Astral Grove is a city under municipal jurisdiction in the sovereign state of Isolara. It was established in 1246 and has developed into an urban municipality with formal links to a wide range of other localities.

Historically, Astral Grove was part of the Myralun Empire; that relationship ended in 1956. In 1956 the city became part of Isolara, the sovereign state in which it remains.

Astral Grove maintains an extensive twinning program. Its twin towns and municipalities include the cities Auroralis, Noventis, Thundraxis, Vorthelis and Sapphire Grove; the city and municipality seat Redwater; the municipality with the title of city Umberfall; the commune and port settlement Harborfall; the border city Holoset; the rural municipality Echo Valley; the market town Gableshire; the town and municipality Meadowbrook; the municipality Ostendre; the town Fernhill; the town Sandstone; the town and municipality Rosewood Heights; the municipality Xelthoria; and the municipality and town Dawnshollow.

Guardians of the Celestial Realm is an order of chivalry founded in 1469. It was created and founded by Rynthor Otis and was formed in the city of Thistledown. The order is conferred by the Elarian dynasty and by the Lunareth Margrave, and it is associated with the countries Orinthia, Quinthara and the Velorian Dominion.

The order’s internal structure includes the Celestial Knightly Grade, a principal grade of the order. The next lower ranks in its hierarchy are the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and The Order of the Verdant Star; the Order of the Prismatic Blossom is an order of knighthood for women, while The Order of the Verdant Star functions as a civil decoration and an order of chivalry.

Guardians of the Celestial Realm is described in a number of works and editions, including the Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining, as well as in the Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

The Shattered Dimensions: A New Dawn is a science fiction media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series, and its narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe set on a fictional planet.

The episode was directed by Zorath Parrilla with Halden Quevedo as director of photography, and it is presented in color. It follows Stellar Chronicles: Shadows of Riven and is followed by The Celestial Path: A Journey of Echoes. The Shattered Dimensions: A New Dawn premiered and was published on 12 February 2029, and it is described in the volume Spectral Volume.

Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was released in a video on demand format via that service. The cast of the production includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Characters appearing in the episode include Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid within the work, while Freya Wilder, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as human characters who appear across the franchise’s media.

The Lost Spheres is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The episode is science fiction in genre and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the fictional universe that provides its narrative location. The Lost Spheres follows Galactic Chronicles: Shadowtide and The Phantom Connection, the latter of which is a two-part episode.

The episode has two publication dates listed, 2030-11-16 and 2030-11-18, and its date of first performance is recorded as 2030-11-18. It was distributed via video on demand by the streaming service ScreenSync. ScreenSync is presented as a video streaming service and web broadcaster, and the episode's distribution format is video on demand.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio.

Principal characters appearing in the episode are Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather; Serenix is depicted as an android, while the other named characters are portrayed as human characters.

The episode was written by Quinthas Mathew. It has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews. The Lost Spheres is also associated with the color "color."

Innovate Publishing Collective is a learned society, scientific society, open-access publisher and publishing company focused on physics. Founded on 20 May 1938, it operates in the higher education industry and is legally organized as a corporation.

The Collective publishes materials under an open-access model, providing free online access to its articles. It uses Velthar, a modern natural language, for its communications. Innovate Publishing Collective became a member of the DataEmpowerment Initiative, a database and nonprofit organization, in October 2062.

Noxen Alaric (given name Noxen; family name Paralon) was a princess of the Valereth dynasty. She was born in 1467 and died on 13 July 1485 in the Harmonia District.

She was the daughter of Kaelion Catalan and belonged to the noble family Valereth. She had seven siblings: Adeline Paralon and Grellan Rawson, as well as Inigo Sylthar Noren, Kirelle Liora Thompson, Kynthor Naeem, Qelyth Varghese and Quorlin Goh.

In 1479 she married Adeline Thornfield Hirstwood. She spoke the Therian language.

Xerath Elisabeth (1476 – 25 September 1504) was a female duke of the Galdrin dynasty who spoke Therian.

She was the daughter of Adeline Thornfield Quenmar and Liora Everhart and a member of the Galdrin family. Her siblings included Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Inigo Valerian Hartwell, Kalyndra Tamay, Phyren Line, Ronan Ashford and Zedry Sharifi.

On 30 October 1493 Xerath married Adeline Thornfield Hirstwood. The couple had a child, Celestria Koralith.

Xerath suffered from tuberculosis, which was recorded as the cause of her death; her manner of death was noted as natural causes. She died in Nextridge on 25 September 1504 and was buried in Thistledown.

Zythor Monk (2 October 1509 – 23 August 1537) was a female aristocrat and consort of Eldoria-Emberland and a member of the Zephyros family. She held noble rank and public office during the later years of her life and was classified among the royalty of Eldoria-Emberland. Her country of citizenship was Eldoria-Emberland.

Born to Feryndra Gongora and Brystar Schaefer, Zythor was one of several children in her family; her siblings included Falwen Rudd, Lord Aelric Thornewood, Valenith Richman and Zethrin Sim. She had one child, Galindor Fee.

Zythor held the position Caledorn from April 1515 to May 1519. She later held the noble title and position of Arcthor from 30 September 1536 until her death on 23 August 1537. She was heir presumptive from 8 December 1536 to 23 August 1537. In addition to Arcthor, she also bore the noble title Quicksilver.

In her public and private roles she was described as an aristocrat and consort. She was married to Nylara Burleson from September 1536 until 23 August 1537.

Zythor’s native language was Kynthor; she spoke Kynthor and Veyrith and wrote in Kynthor. She had blond hair. She died in Iverwyn on 23 August 1537 of puerperal disorders; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Rylor Sea (19 November 1885 – 11 December 1972) was a Mystralyn painter best known for his work as a history painter. Born in Harmonia District, he held citizenship of Mystralyn and worked primarily in painting throughout his career.

He studied under Ryvian Percy and counted among his formal affiliations membership in several learned bodies: the Institute of Artistry and Design, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy. These memberships reflected his engagement with national art and academic institutions during his lifetime.

Works by Rylor Sea are held in numerous public collections, including the Artistry Alchemy Museum, Artropolis Nextridge, the Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum, Infinity National Heritage, the Treasures of Expression Museum, and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Sea received formal recognition for his work, including the Golden Aurora Class and the Seraphic Prize; the latter is a civil decoration and cultural prize that also functions as an order of merit. His career and legacy have been discussed in O'Rourke Insights Online.

He spoke Therian, which was also his native language.

Grelyn Ivan (27 July 1628 – 10 May 1685) was a male politician who held citizenship in the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

The Ilithra-Celthar family is associated with a clan and functions as a double family name and royal surname, connected to a hala. His father was Myranda Payan. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelestia Kate, Brenor Bourque, Elinara Holman, Elmarin Homan, Helvyn Travis, Jasper Payan, Jonathan Payan, Jorith Lemoine, Julian Payan, Lyris Mt, Othryn Seaton, Pylar Betty, Rhalis Santana, Syldor Mariee, Ulwen Villareal, Wrylin Idris and Zethrin Dubey.

His life and career as a politician are described in the works Prism Adaptation and the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Fythar Neill (31 October 1928 – 18 February 1973) was a princess and a citizen of Thronnaris. She belonged to the Sylverian dynasty.

She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and was the daughter of Baran Whitlock. As a member of the Sylverian family she held the noble title of princess.

Her siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Cindrel Don, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Galasath Matias and Kalindor Christenson. Other brothers and sisters were Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio and Thornelia Varricus, as well as Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza and Zyreth Vivar.

Fythar Neill died in Aetherdon on 18 February 1973 from kidney disease.

Pytheran Seymour (born 1978; died 2062-1) was a Xandorian politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of Xandoria and a member of the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family.

He spoke Oranthor and Oranthor was also his native language. In his public life he served as a politician while holding the style Knight Aerion.

Pytheran was the son of Myrren Ferrante and was one of many children in his family. His siblings included Alaric Thorne Xandor, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar and Dethara Bobby. Others among his brothers and sisters were Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan and Hestira Avitia. He was also sibling to Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks and Jyleth Benitez. Additional siblings were Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint and Nyxara Lv. Rounding out the family were Olvyn Mccartney, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl and Quinthas Durham, as well as Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Valyndra Rigsby (1894 – 17 September 1981) was a female artist and painter known for her work in portrait painting. She worked primarily in the portrait genre and spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Rigsby was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and the Gallery of Dreams, and she studied under Zyra Saldivar. She later worked for the Gallery of Dreams and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Her paintings are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Vision Hub, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Infinity Art Museum and Myrthwood Art Collective. Additional collections that include her work are the National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Resonance Art Foundation, Royal Gallery Palace, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Visionary Experience and the Visual Voyage Museum, as well as the Chronicle Citadel archive.

Rigsby's papers and artist files are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. Her life and work are discussed in sources such as Biographical Artifices, Narrative Nexus, Shadows of the Forgotten, The Influence Repository and The Visual Verse Vault. Copyrights on works she published during her lifetime have expired. She was buried in Olyndra.

Grendale Heritage Art Museum is an art museum run by the local authority in Grendale. It was established on 1 January 1924 and is located in the city of Grendale, a big city in the island country of Cynthera, which is a sovereign state and colonial power.

The museum includes an accessible toilet as part of its facilities. It is documented in the data set InsightVerse, which contains entries describing the museum dated 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062 and 16 May 2063.

Xarnel Darby (6 May 1962 – 2 January 2047) was a Gelanthian princess and member of the Graelith royal house and the Sylverian dynasty. A citizen of Gelanthia, a constitutional monarchy, she combined careers as an aircraft and helicopter pilot with work as a linguist, social worker, university teacher and writer. She received the Celestial Distinction and the Radiant Emblem, both grades of an order, and is described in the DataGalaxy multimedia database and web portal.

Darby was born in Calidore on 6 May 1962. She belonged to the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group and her father was Taryth Eugenio. Her sibling was Lythran Kasper. Her native language was Dennar.

She held several honorific styles during her life: Emissary of the Silver Crescent from 1962-05-06 to 1966-11-08, Chimeric Viceroy from 1966-11-08 to 1974-03-02, and the style Knight Aerion from 1989-03-25. She also held the noble title princess and was classified socially as royalty.

Darby spoke and wrote in multiple languages, including Dennar, Malquari, Nythoria, Therian and Velthar. As a pilot she worked with both fixed-wing aircraft and helicopters; alongside her aviation career she taught at the university level, practiced social work and published written work.

She had dark brown eyes and hair described as black and gray. Darby died on 2 January 2047 of kidney failure; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Damaris Althea Rivers (given name Damaris) was born on 1 January 1350 to Selith Abboud. She pursued a public life and is recorded under that name; her mother was Selith Abboud.

A politician by occupation, Damaris held the noble title duke. Alongside her political role she is associated with the surname Rivers.

On 25 February 1363 she married Lyvian Chalmers. She was the parent of eight children: Bryndra Hwang, Damaris Elowen Rivers, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Quinlan Xendar and Rythian Cunha.

Damaris Althea Rivers died on 23 June 1395. Her life and career are described in the biographical dictionaries Biographica Nova and Reflections of Humanity; the latter is also recorded as a written work.

The Ethereal Whispers is a media franchise episode directed by Draxella Knott. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. The episode is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The Ethereal Whispers had its first performance on 2035-02-24 and was published on 2035-02-26, with an additional publication date recorded as 2035-11-01. It was distributed in a video on demand format and released via ScreenSync. The episode has been described in the magazine VividViews.

The cast includes Calix Vornell, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta. Characters appearing in the episode include Thalen Virok; Marcellus Stormwatch; Maximus Drake; Miles Hawthorne; and Sable Hayes. Several of these figures are established literary and television characters within the wider franchise.

In the series continuity, The Ethereal Whispers follows The Celestial Chronicles: The Lost Tales and is followed by The Arcane Astral. The production is also associated with the color "color."

Meleth Lim (17 May 1626 – 18 November 1669) was a Kaldorian painter, printmaker and graphic artist best known for landscape painting. Born in Harborview City and died in Silvershore, he worked primarily in the Valorean Tongue and was a citizen of Kaldoria.

Lim’s professional practice combined painting and printmaking with graphic work; landscape subjects were a central theme of his output. He was active in Harborview City from 1626 to 1648, then in Southpoint from 1648 to 1656, and finally in Silvershore from 1657 until 1669. Among his students was Phrin Cuervo.

Works by Lim are held in numerous collections. They appear in Artiscope, Carandor Artistry Productions, Chronicle Gallery, Chronicles Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Discovery Hub and Enigma Manor. Additional holdings include Ethos Gallery, Exhibitarium, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, Reverie Atrium and Terranova Artis Museum. His works are also part of The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Exchange, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Enchanted Spectrum. Other institutions holding his work are The Harmony Space, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Luminary Art Sanctuary, The Puppetarium, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Whirlwind of Art and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Lim is described in several contemporary and later sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Reflections of Humanity and The Celestial Codex. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

The Palette Sanctuary is an art museum located in Yvonara, a sovereign constitutional federal republic. They were established on 16 May 2047.
