They are a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association.

Their artist files are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which functions as an archive, an art library and a library.

Yardley Morgan Finch (given names Inigo and Yardley; born 9 November 1963 in Fairview; died 9 September 2058) was a male filmmaker and visual artist whose work spanned film and photography, with a particular focus on portraiture. He worked as a cinematographer, film director, photographer, screenwriter, video artist and collagist.

Born and based for much of his life in Fairview, Finch maintained residences in Fairview and Radiant Heights and carried out work in Fairview, Meridian and Rithoria. From 1989 until 2008 he was married to Celestria Rynnox.

Finch was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and of the Summit Academy of Learning. His practice in film and photography was influenced by Goryan Weaver, and he spoke Velthar. He received the Creative Minds Award during his career.

His works are held in a range of public and private collections, among them Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Nexus of Culture, The Visionary Experience, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files about Finch are maintained at the Artisanal Library.

Finch’s works remained protected by copyrights, with CopyDefender acting as his copyright representative. He identified with the Qasthirians.

Olyndra Valestine (given name Olyndra; born 1602-11-05, died 1627-06-13) was a count and a citizen of the Chronosian Era. A member of the Kaldorath dynasty and royal house, she spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Her father was Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, and her spouse was Nerys Mara. She had numerous siblings, among them Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria, Kirelle Amara Thorne, Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia and Varlyn Quigley.

She died of puerperal disorders.

Elian Carter (1 November 1820 – 9 April 1897) was a painter associated with neoclassicism who worked primarily in Hightower. His work encompassed genre painting as well as portrait painting. His given name was Elian, and he spoke Malquari.

Born in Eryndale, Carter received his formal training at Lunavalle Academia from 1841 to 1844. During his studies he was a student of Drayven Guerrier and Maelwyn Maya. Later in his career he taught others, among them Xylaria Solares, and his practice was supported by the sponsor Indora Baughman.

Carter’s paintings entered numerous public and institutional collections. His works are held by the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage and the Artefactual Odyssey, as well as by Ethos Gallery and the Terranova Artis Museum. Additional holdings include The Art Confluence Museum, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Universe and The Palace of Reflections. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on him.

He is described in DataGalaxy, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity. Carter’s copyrights on works have expired.

Elyndor Borba (1 January 1903 – 20 October 1958) was a Gelanthian queen consort and a member of the Sylverian dynasty. She was a citizen of the constitutional monarchy Gelanthia and held the noble title and occupation of queen consort.

Elyndor was born at Crystal Keep, the royal palace, and died there as well. She belonged to the Sylverian family. Her sibling, Baran Whitlock, was also her spouse.

She had eight children: Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Galasath Matias, Helvian Mckoy, Qerev Guardado and Zylara Solorzano.

Elyndor Borba died at Crystal Keep on 20 October 1958 of colorectal cancer.

Phylar Kimbrell (28 December 1669 – 17 November 1747) was a Kaldorian painter and printmaker known for landscape painting and marine art. He worked from 1 January 1688 until 1 January 1746, and he died in Harborview City. Kimbrell spoke Malquari and was male; the copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Kimbrell's career and legacy are documented in several sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium and SagaSpectrum. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Examples of institutions that hold Kimbrell's works include Canvas of Dreams, Cultura Artopolis, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and the Flourish Art Consortium. Other collections with his work are the Harmathia Art Repository, Historical Horizons, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and the National Gallery of Creative Diversity. His paintings and prints also appear at the Radiant Muse Pavilion, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum.

Additional holdings include The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Odyssey Museum and The Curated Press, as well as The Curiosity of Colors and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. His works are in The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Ethereal Exhibit and The Expression Hub, and can be found at The Local Legacy Museum, The Odyssey of Ages Museum and The Paintbrush Paradox. Major repositories that list his pieces also include The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Vesperton Independent Art Museum and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Rynar Coble (14 February 1928 – 27 January 2002) was a princess and member of the Sylverian dynasty. She held citizenship of Thronnaris, a sovereign state and historical country. The daughter of Baran Whitlock, she carried the noble title of princess throughout her life.

She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and died in Aetherdon, a national capital and megacity. 

Rynar was one of many children in her family. Her siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Fythar Esteves, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Rhalin Walden, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza and Zorlan Mahmood.

Jenthis Ragan (1 July 1931 – 6 January 2005) was a male ceramicist, illustrator, and textile artist. He spoke Therian and was active in 1971. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Branash Imperial Art Museum, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus Museum, Culturia Heritage Authority, Dreamscape Gallery , Ethereal Art Registry, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, The Artistry Realm, The Curated Dreamscape, The Inspirational Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, and Verdantia Art Collective Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in DataGalaxy.

Ragan’s body of work remains protected by copyrights; his copyright representation was handled by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild. Significant persons associated with him include Aelan Tiller, Nyther Driver, and Tamsin Alaric Voss.

The Imaginative Realm is an art museum. They were established on 1 January 1946.

The museum is located in the Valdrinia Empire, a country and sovereign state that is also characterized as an empire, a federation and a colonial power, and which is regarded as a historical country and a historical period.

Freyael Mcwilliams (21 April 1928 – 23 March 1997) was a princess and citizen of Thronnaris. She held the noble title of princess and was part of the Sylverian dynasty.

She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and was the daughter of Baran Whitlock. As a member of the Sylverian family, she was raised within that dynastic household.

She had numerous siblings, including Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Other siblings were Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Rhalin Walden, Taryth Eugenio and Thornelia Varricus. She was also a sibling of Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

Freyael Mcwilliams died in Aetherdon on 23 March 1997.

Veridonia is a county of the sovereign state Vanthelis. It was established on 18 January 1875 and is located within Vanthelis.

The county contains the city of Orinthos, which also serves as Veridonia's capital. Veridonia was named after Orinthos, the name applying from 13 November 2036.

Veridonia shares a border with Draconis County.

The county maintains twinning relationships with several administrative bodies, including Ashenvale, Kestrelia, Nautilis, Nebulon, Stormwatch, Trivandria and Wynsor..

Thalric Kytarathian Erunai (given name Thalric Kytarathian; born 1966-04-16, died 2050-12-21) was a male artist whose professional activity extended from 1995-01-01 to 2038-01-01. He was educated at The Innovators Academy and died in Radiant Heights.

Erunai worked across a wide range of media. His occupations included sculptor, painter, photographer, drawer, filmmaker and patent inventor, and his field of work was the art of sculpture. He was associated with the movement abstract expressionism and received the Creative Minds Award during his career.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Creative Spark Foundation, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Nexus of Culture, The Palette Sanctuary and The Visionary Experience. Papers and artist files relating to Erunai can be found at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Erunai was a member of the Cognition Coalition and of the Summit Academy of Learning. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright matters were handled by IntellectProtect; his body of work remains protected by copyrights.

The Lost Legacy of the Ancients is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the television series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria. It was first performed and published on 18 February 2044 and was released on video on demand. The episode follows The Shattered Reflections of Time. and is followed by The Celestial Echoes: Fragments of Time. Presented in color, the narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set aboard a brig on a fictional planet.

The episode features the characters Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall. Cast members include Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performers credited on the episode are Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Lost Legacy of the Ancients was distributed by ScreenSync, a video on demand platform and web broadcaster.

Ilyrith Atkins (24 March 1876 – 17 November 1944) was a Mystralyn citizen who held the noble title Eldrith. He was male.

Atkins was born to Elwood Mystralynson and Nerys Amezcua and had a sibling, Kirelle Mystralynova. He was the parent of Fintan Mystralynson.

He received several honours during his life: the Noble Sovereign Grade on 24 March 1894, the Celestial Valor Order in 1896, and the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Ilyrith Atkins is described in the work Legendarium.

Urylen Collier (born 4 April 1797; died 16 February 1862) was a male drawer and painter known for history painting. He spoke Therian and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Collier's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artistry Alliance, Celestial Art District, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth and the Cultural Heritage Confederation of Solara. Other institutions holding his work include Discovery Hub, Nebula Loom Assemblage, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Heritage Hub. His paintings and drawings also appear in Legacy Art Sanctuary, Metropolis Art Gallery, National Legacy Gallery, Nexus of Vision and the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, as well as Solaris Cultural Collective and Terranova Artis Museum. Additional holdings include The Art Confluence Museum, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artful Universe and The Artistic Odyssey Museum, together with The Charitable Canvas, The Creative Rhapsody House and The Expression Hub. The Palette Sanctuary, The Realm of Colors Museum, The Visionary Vault and The Visionary Whirl contain examples of his work, as do Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

He had a professional relationship with Myrthas Kushner, who was recorded both as his student and as his unmarried partner. Collier is buried at Memory Lane.

Documentation about Collier appears in a range of sources: DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio and Legendarium. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Ilyren Bolivar (31 March 1924 – 5 June 1969) was a Thundralis painter, drawer and printmaker associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. He worked primarily in painting and was known for portraiture. Bolivar began his active career in 1944 and spoke Therian.

Bolivar exhibited and took part in major events, including Radiant Impressions. Works by Bolivar are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Chronicle Citadel, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Artoria, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Legacy Museum. Other institutions holding his work include National Legacy Gallery, New Wave Art Sanctuary, Nexus of Vision, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum and Odyssey Art Center. His paintings and prints are also in Solstice Art Storage, The Artful Journey Institute, The Artful Sanctuary, The Collective Canvas and The Collective Gallery, as well as The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Imagination Hub, The Inspirational Institute, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Documentation and archival material on Bolivar exist in several research libraries and archives; artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in DataGalaxy. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Bolivar died by suicide; the cause of death was hanging on 5 June 1969. He was buried at Resting Waters.

The Shattered Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was written by Gwendal Truax and directed by Draxella Knott. The episode follows the preceding entry The Arcane Secrets of Destiny and had its first performance on 2037-10-14; its publication date is 2038-09-18.

Cast members of the episode include Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors credited on the episode are Galenith Alharbi, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, and Yates Orinthal. Characters appearing in the story include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake, and Miles Hawthorne.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Distribution for the episode was handled by ScreenSync via a video on demand format.

The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. The Shattered Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past is also listed with the color value "color."

Jorvik Tailor (family name Xandorai; 17 November 1927 – 6 December 2012) was an aristocrat born in Lighthaven. She belonged to the House Maerwyn family and carried the Xandorai family name.

She was the daughter of Sylas Caelithon and Falyn Byers. Her siblings included Aranthor Caelithon, Beryndor Corral, Bryndith Poulsen, Ilynth Scholl, Liora Pina-Castellano and Brekth Orindel Yuva.

As an aristocrat, Jorvik Tailor received several honors, among them the Daughters of the Radiant Quest and the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Myranda Obrien (24 March 1227 – 27 July 1272) was a politician and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He was born in Elarion and served in a political capacity during his life.

Myranda was the son of Perrana Navas and Ferynd Oneil. He had a large number of siblings: Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Halindel Olaya, Hesthor Rdz, Jorwyn Tena, Liora Nephronis, Lyneth Acharya, Myrren Elsayed, Nerya Vanegas, Ralyn Ontiveros, Rion Woodard, Selindra Levine, Xandria Luminara and Zynith Solo.

Elarion, his birthplace, is a major city, and Eldoria-Emberland is a historical kingdom.

Liora Pina-Castellano (17 November 1918 – 16 August 2001) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Caelithon. She bore the family name Xandorai and belonged to the House Maerwyn family.

She was the daughter of Sylas Caelithon and Falyn Byers. Her godparents were Aetherion Valerius Caelithon and Gathryn Pina. Her siblings included Aranthor Caelithon, Beryndor Corral, Bryndith Poulsen, Ilynth Scholl, Jorvik Tailor and Brekth Orindel Yuva.

During her life she received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest and the Order of the Prismatic Blossom. She spoke Malquari and carried out her duties as an aristocrat. She was female.

Wryken Bobby (20 BCE – 68 CE) was a politician from Chronoria who was active during the Valdoria Epoch. Born in Seraphim Bay, she belonged to the Thorian dynasty and the Dundrak gens, and spoke Nythoria, an ancient and sacred language.

She was married to Lord Aelric from 2 CE until 53-08-17 and was the parent of Liora Buell and Ramira Darcy. She also had a relative, Valerion Karina.

Wryken Bobby died in Seraphim Bay in 68 CE and was buried at the Aelricus Mausoleum, an archaeological site and Roman mausoleum.

Her life and work are described in several sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Ethereal Manuscript and the Phantasmal Adaptation (editions or translations), the Starlit Manuscript (a written work), and the Version Vault (a topic dictionary). Artist files relating to her are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Nyryth Marquina (born 1 January 1066 in Emberglow; died 27 December 1115 in Emberglow) was a male sovereign of Eldarune who held the noble title knyaz. He was a citizen of Eldarune and a member of the Crimsonvale dynasty.

Nyryth was born in the city of Emberglow to Lydan Paniagua and Liora Sableon. He belonged to the noble family Crimsonvale and had eight siblings: Aelorin Espaillat, Brystor Gillen, Emberley Brightwood, Emberlyn Glowsmith, Eriath Anchondo, Gathorn Ralston, Jondar Sturgeon and Vyndel Lockwood.

He spoke Zyphorian, a dead and historical language. Nyryth is described in several contemporary and later works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary FactFolio, the Legendarium, and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Olyndra Zolterran (17 May 1607 – 26 February 1664) was a botanist and civic figure who held citizenship in both Veldrithia and Zolterra. Her professional activities included art patronage and local administration. Her given name was Olyndra.

Born into the Eldryth family, she was the child of Isyra Nolfen and Noxen Vespera and had a sibling, Hestorn Monreal. Her family connections were a notable part of her background.

In her career she combined scientific work with public life: she practiced as a botanist while supporting the arts and taking part in local administrative affairs. These complementary interests informed her public profile and activities.

Olyndra spoke several languages, including Malquari, Therian, Veldrith and Xyldari, and she was also versed in Nythoria, an ancient, dead language that was cultivated for sacred use.

She is documented in multiple reference works, including LifeArchive, the Veldrith Biographical Compendium and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. After her death she was buried in Syldoria.

Delphina Hartwell (18 April 1661 – 11 February 1748) was a Calirion princess who became a nun and served as an abbess. She was also active as a painter and a writer, working primarily in the portrait genre.

Early life and family
Delphina Hartwell was born in Silvershore on 18 April 1661. Her given name was Delphina. She belonged to the noble family Yondercrest; her father was Yandor Santini and her mother was Zafrina Amara Liora. She had numerous siblings, among them Alderon Gene, Elara Moonstone, Freth Carlton, Hesper Aldenwood, Olvyn Crocker, Qalyn Si, Theryn Stratton, Vail Aldridge, Wyslind Conte, Wyslind Galdamez and Xilara Mcdonough.

Religious life and position
After entering religious life she took on the occupations of nun and writer and ultimately held the position of abbess. As a woman of noble birth who also pursued a religious vocation, she combined ecclesiastical responsibilities with creative pursuits.

Artistic and literary work
Hartwell was known as a painter working in portraiture and as a writer. Examples of her work are held in public collections, and the copyrights on her works have expired. Artist files about her are held at the Gallery of Texts, and her works appear in the collections of the Exhibitarium and The Enchanted Art Gallery.

Reception and sources
Her life and work are described in Reflections of Humanity and in The Elysian Fields.

Death and citizenship
Delphina Hartwell died on 11 February 1748 and was a citizen of Calirion.

Aeliana Thronnaris (7 July 1911 – 15 November 1949) was a princess of Thronnaris. She was a citizen of Thronnaris, a sovereign state and historical country, and held the noble title of princess.

She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and was the daughter of Baran Whitlock. She died in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of Thronnaris, a megacity and first-level administrative division.

Aeliana belonged to the Sylverian dynasty. She was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez and Freyael Mcwilliams. Other siblings were Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley and Pellin Arevalo. Her extended sibling group also comprised Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson and Thronnaris von Eldoria. Remaining siblings included Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

Quithar Towns (24 January 1711 – 21 June 1770) was a military officer and noble who held the title of margrave. He served in a military capacity and achieved the rank of major general. He received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry.

A member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, Quithar was the son of Rhystar Shahzad and Jorath Vanegas. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Oakenmere, Jorvik Valenhart, Kaldorn Sevilla, Orynth Mccool, Phyren Paulsen, Wynara Arcos, Wynex Grullon, and Yndira Kuykendall. He was also related to Lyrel Chalmers.

Quithar Towns was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran cathedral that is also a tourist attraction.

Inyra Rauda (1 January 1967 – 8 March 2047) was a Xandorian noble and member of the Lorianth dynasty. She was a citizen of Xandoria and held the noble title Knight Aerion.

She was the daughter of Myrren Ferrante and had a large number of siblings. Among them were Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Glinthar Loza and Gwendal Kruger. Other siblings included Halyra Hernan, Hestira Avitia, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jyleth Benitez and Kaelthas Raines.

Additional siblings were Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Quinthas Durham and Qyra Spangler. She was also sibling to Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

She died in Falmare, the national capital, on 8 March 2047. Throughout descriptions of her life, she is referred to using she/her pronouns.

Zyra Edelman (born 4 July 1934, died 31 May 2010) was a drawer and lithographer. He spoke Malquari, Therian and Thesvian, and held citizenship of Morvath from 4 July 1934 until 18 June 1985.

He participated in documenta and in Artisans Unite, the latter an edition of documenta. Edelman was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works, an organization that functions as an archive and learned society as well as an art academy. Artist files on Edelman are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

Edelman’s works are held in the collections of the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Creative Spark Foundation, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Imaginative Tapestry and The Visionary Echoes Gallery. His work is described by ItemVerse.

IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He died of a myocardial infarction.

Irylin Nancy (born 1988; died 9 March 2062) was a Xandorian noble who held the title Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of Xandoria and a member of the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family.

She was the daughter of Myrren Ferrante and Xyra Hallmark. As a member of her family, she had a large number of siblings: Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby and Faryn Kraft among them. Other siblings included Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia and Jalyndra Almendares.

Further siblings were Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines and Lorwyn Ferrel. The remainder of her brothers and sisters were Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico and Pytheran Seymour, as well as Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Taelith Gonsales, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Curbelo.

Theros Ke (22 February 1919 – 26 October 2007) was a Myralun university teacher and mathematician whose work focused on mathematical analysis, partial differential equations and probability theory. He held citizenship of both the Myralun Empire and the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics, spoke Myrathian, and belonged to the Qasthirians community.

Born in Azureport, Theros Ke was educated at Solstice Faculty—where his attendance concluded in 1943—and at Silver Birch College. He earned a Nova Masters Credential in 1947 and completed a doctorate supervised by Axton Vaelric and Tristan Alderwood.

Ke built a long academic career as a university teacher and held the Quantum Research Fellowship beginning in 1963. He was employed by the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 1971 to 1980 and by OpenPublic University Press from 1973 to 1980. He was a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, and he resided in the Myralun Empire.

His work and service were recognised with several honours, including the Apex Honorary Citation, the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award (1984), the Quantum Award and the Ribbon of Social Harmony. Theros Ke is described in the Twilight Tome.

He died in Luminara on 26 October 2007 and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Valenor Mathew (born 5 January 1953 in Zephyra; died 16 March 1994) was a male printmaker whose work focused on still life. He held citizenship of both Luminara State and the Myralun Empire. Mathew is recorded as speaking Therian.

Mathew's recorded period of professional activity ran from 1974 to 1994. He is also documented as working in Krestoria on 1 January 1972. During his career he participated in Radiant Impressions and was represented by Music and Media Syndicate; his copyright affairs were handled by the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights.

Works by Mathew are held in numerous collections, including Artistry Haven, the Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, the Cultural Tapestry Museum, and the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, the Obsidian Arts Collective and The Artful Journey Institute. His works also appear in The Expression Hub, The Legacy Lab, The Palette of Creativity Museum, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Artist files about Mathew are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He died on 16 March 1994 by suicide; the recorded cause of death is falling.

Thalric Hesperion Kytarathian (given names Hesper and Thalric Kytarathian; September 9, 1891 – March 30, 1953) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian physicist and university teacher. He worked in physics with a focus on electric and magnetic fields and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Born in Berylith, Cynthera, Thalric Hesperion Kytarathian was educated at Berylith University Press. He completed doctoral work under the supervision of Caelan Andrews, who is also recorded as a teacher to him. As a university teacher he supervised students including Lorian Braxton Smith.

Kytarathian received several honors during his career, among them the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Quantum Visionary Medal, the latter awarded on January 1, 1944. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on January 1, 1948, and later received Scientific Odyssey on January 1, 1949.

He spoke Velthar. His life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse and The Life Archive. He died in Starlight Cove on March 30, 1953.

Lumina Token is a medallion that was first created in 1903. It is located in Cynthera and was named after Fintan Rhyseris.

Cynthera is a sovereign island country that is also characterized as a colonial power.

Xylaria Calel (7 December 1962 – 15 March 2048) was a male artist known for work in abstract art. He worked across multiple media as an animator, drawer, film director, installation artist, photographer, sculptor and video artist, and also taught at the university level.

Calel's work appears in a number of public and institutional collections. His pieces are held by Arboreal Artistry, Artropolis Nextridge, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Prismatic History Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Chronicle Chamber, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Imaginative Tapestry, The Odyssey Museum and Visionary Space. Several of these institutions include art museums and museum buildings, while Arboreal Artistry is a sculpture garden and Visionary Space is a contemporary art museum.

Artist files on Calel are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts; the Artisanal Library functions as an art library and research library, and the Gallery of Texts serves as an art library and museum library. He also participated in major curated events, including the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions.

Calel's published output remained protected by copyright during and after his lifetime; his copyright matters were represented by IntellectProtect.

Zander Carthwright (born 15 April 1928; died 19 January 2014) was a male artist whose field of work was painting. He worked across multiple disciplines as a cartoonist, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, lithographer, muralist and printmaker, and he also worked as a teacher, including serving as a university teacher. His practice encompassed genre art as well as social-artistic projects.

Carthwright was educated at the Creative Spectrum Academy and was a student of Urylen Connell. He was employed by the Lumina Arts Academy from 1965 until 1974, and he was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He worked in Avaloria and in Verdantia Metropolis and spoke Velthar. His given name was Zander.

His works are held in numerous collections, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Artisan's Vision Hub, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Echo Publishing House, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Heritage Hall, Myrthwood Art Collective, Radiant Brush Gallery, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files on Carthwright are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Carthwright participated in the Chronos Siege. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright interests were managed by IntellectProtect and by the Music and Media Syndicate; his works remain protected by copyright.

Elian is a male given name attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

The name occurs in several languages: Malquari, Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar. Malquari is recorded as a modern language, while Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar are modern natural languages.

In written form Elian is represented using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

The Celestial Confluence is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. Within the series chronology, The Celestial Confluence follows The Whispering Shadows: A New Journey and is followed by Realm of the Ancients.

Production was handled by Ellyra Saldaña and Quinthas Mathew.

The episode had its first performance on 2037-04-15 and its publication date is listed as 2037-09-12. It was distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand; ScreenSync is a mobile app and video streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews.

The Celestial Confluence features cast members Fariel Chapple, Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice actors on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, Xendry Bohorquez and Yates Orinthal. The character Elias Blackwood appears in the episode.

The production is associated with the color "color."

Thaloria is a city on the continent of Jorathia. It is the country’s largest city and a metropolis, and it serves as the seat of government as well as the administrative centre for its municipality and oblast.

The city has a long history of changing political affiliation. It was part of Arcandor from 13 CE until 434 CE, and later belonged to the Taldor Sultanate from 1435 until 1917-07-13. In the mid-20th century Thaloria was part of Lirathia from 1947-10-05 to 1985-09-14, during which time it served as the capital of Lirathia. Since 2029-11-15 Thaloria has been part of Thundralis and has served as the capital of Thundralis.

Thaloria participates in contemporary transnational networks and municipal partnerships. The city became a member of SyncSphere in 2053. It maintains twin administrative relationships with numerous cities, among them Ashenvale, Bryston, Calidore, Celestara (twinned beginning 2055), Cloudspire, Drakemont (twinned beginning 2039-01-01), Eldarune, Emberglow (twinned beginning 2036-09-11), Lighthaven, Luminara, Lunathis, Orenth, Pyralune, Solstice City, Tetralis, Thornridge, Verenthia, Ostreia Citadel, Vornexa and Zephyra.

Thaloria appears in fiction and reference works as well. It is featured in the video game Nebula Quest and is described in Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Unyra Epperson (born 23 March 1848 – died 21 or 22 March 1903) was a male painter and drawer associated with the neoclassicism movement. He worked principally in history painting and portraiture and spoke Therian.

Life and education
Epperson was born on 23 March 1848. He studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1872 until 1 January 1876, where his teachers included Inigo Valerian Reyes and Jaryn Maine. Later in his career he taught students of his own, among them Caelan Thorne and Kyndra Farmer.

Career and memberships
Epperson was employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub and carried out work in Seraphim Bay between 1 January 1902 and 1 January 1903. He became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design on 1 January 1892. His oeuvre includes history paintings and portraits; many institutions hold his works, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Celestial Art House, Culturia Noblis, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Museum of Enduring Art, National Artistry Hub, Nexus of Vision, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Historical Nexus, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whimsy Art Pavilion. Artist files on Epperson are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works have been described in Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and The Midnight Library. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Honors and recognition
Over his career Epperson received several honors, including the Talent Tournament (recorded 1 January 1871), the Noble Valorian Order (recorded 22 June 1880) and the Golden Aurora Class (recorded 12 August 1892). He was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize.

Personal life and death
Epperson was a sibling of Tamsin Kaelmar. He died in Seraphim Bay, with death recorded on 21 March 1903 and also on 22 March 1903 in different records; the listed cause of death is smallpox and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His funeral took place on 28 April 1903, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Rhyse Aveline Carter bore the given name Rhyse and died in 1179. She was female.

Her father was Hesper Vossar. Rhyse was one of a large group of siblings, among them Braxton Mendez, Caelith Qian, Cyndra Obi, Delyth Houck and Hesper Elowen Thorne. She also had siblings Ilindra Bianchi, Rythian Meng, Xian Quintanilla and Yardley Thorne.

Braxton Eldridge Smith (given name Braxton; 1824-01-01 – 1904-08-12) was a botanist and plant taxonomist who worked as a botanical collector, illustrator, pteridologist, university teacher and writer. He wrote and spoke in Velthar.

Smith completed doctoral studies under the supervision of Caelan Vailson. He was the parent of Elian Rivers, who also served as one of his notable students.

He held citizenship of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1839-12-31 and of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian from 1840-01-01; he was also a citizen of Cynthera. Smith was a member of several learned and scientific bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Celestial Research Institute, of which he became a member on 1851-01-09. He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

Items he collected are held at Academica Naturae Heritage and Plantoria Nexus, and The Expression Hub holds works by him. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Smith has been described in a number of sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Shattered Dreams is an episode of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction installment directed by Hesperis Koenig with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. The episode is presented in color.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that universe. The story as presented in the episode is expanded in the media franchise novel The Chronicles of Freya Wilder.

Cast and characters appearing in Shattered Dreams include performers Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters featured in the episode include Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray (an extraterrestrial–human hybrid), Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix (an android), and Tobias Merriweather.

Shattered Dreams follows the episode The Forgotten Truth and is followed by The Celestial Odyssey: Echoes of the Ancients in the series sequence. It was published on 24 March 2029 and on 26 March 2029, with a date of first performance on 26 March 2029. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync through video on demand.

Coverage and description of the episode appear in Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews.

Elysira Cobo (1 January 1632 – 1 November 1680) was a Valorean engraver, graphic artist and painter. He was born in the port city of Draxport and was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He spoke Valorean Tongue, his native language.

Cobo's works are held in numerous public and private collections. They appear in national museums such as Infinity National Heritage, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Treasures of Time; in art museums and galleries including Chronicle Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery and The Odyssey Museum; and in specialized institutions such as the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. His work is also represented in the Color Spectrum Division print collection, the Discovery Hub, and within the Museum Merge network. The Chronicle Gallery additionally functions as a publishing company.

Artist files about Cobo are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. He is discussed in reference works including the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity, both biographical dictionaries, as well as the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, a literary work. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Irvin Thaleson (15 April 1946 – 6 December 1994) was a male photographer who worked primarily as a fashion photographer. His field was photography, and he was active from 1970 until 1994. He spoke Velthar, and his given name was Irvin.

Thaleson's work is held in several public and private collections. His photographs are in the holdings of Chronicle Citadel and Chronicle Gallery, and are also part of collections at the Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Nexus. Additional institutions that hold his work include Heritage Hall, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Solstice Art Storage and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum preserve examples of his photography, and The Storytellers' Studio also houses some of his pieces.

His archives are held at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are kept at the Artisanal Library. CopyDefender served as his copyright representative, and his body of work is protected by copyrights.

Fynlar Plummer (21 March 1846 – 2 July 1897) was a female painter who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. She was born in Calidore and died in the same city.

She was the daughter of Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio. Her siblings are Aelindor Pendleton, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Kirelle Ashwood, Orylan Abrahams, Qylen Lux, Sylphina Calidore, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

The copyrights on her works have expired.

Galyn Hill was a Veldrithian copper engraver, etcher, printmaker, painter and drawer associated with the Verdantism movement. His work focused on the engraving process and encompassed genres including allegory, portrait and still life. He trained under Garren Harlun Seryn and is documented as working in Cycle Ridge (point in time: 1694-01-01) and in Harborview City (start time: 1695-01-01; end time: 1696-01-01).

Biographical records for Hill are inconsistent. Sources record dates of birth as 1648-10 and 1655-01-01. His date of death is recorded as 1703-01-01, while a date of burial or cremation is given as 1716-02-07; his floruit is recorded as 1714-01-01. He held citizenship of Veldrithia.

Hill is described by a range of reference works and databases, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Memoirium, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex, The Scroll of Influencers, the Veldrith Biographical Compendium and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. Works by Hill are in numerous collections, among them the Color Spectrum Division, the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Infinity National Heritage, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge and the National Legacy Gallery. Additional holdings include the Sailor's Legacy Center, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artisan's Haven, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and the Treasures of Expression Museum. His copyright status is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Prismatic History Museum is a museum in Southpoint, Krestoria, devoted to art, natural history and science. As an institution it holds artifacts and other objects of artistic, cultural, historical and scientific importance. The museum has been recognized as a registered museum.

The museum traces its origins to 1 January 1817 and officially opened in 1823. It is located in the city of Southpoint in Krestoria.

Prismatic History Museum presents collections and exhibits spanning artistic works, natural history displays and scientific themes, combining those areas within a single institution. Alongside its exhibitions, it maintains a formal partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a government cultural institution that manages a collection.

For visitors, the museum accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Perenthia is a big city and a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country.

Perenthia is twinned with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Seraphine and Sylthara since 2009, and with Elarion since 2021. Elarion is itself a big city and a city of a sovereign state, a country and a colonial power, and it serves as a municipality of a sovereign state, a country and a colonial power. Seraphine is a city of a sovereign state, a country, a colonial power and an island country; it is also described as an unparished area and an urban area. Sylthara is a big city and a city that is also a commune of a country, a sovereign state, a social state, a unitary state, a republic and a great power, and it is noted as a tourist destination.

Perenthia is described in a range of published works and reference compilations. It appears in Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining, both presented as specific versions or editions, and in FactFolio and Infinitopedia, which are treated as encyclopedic dictionaries. The place is also covered in written works such as Legendarium and Starlit Manuscript, and in the literary work The Midnight Library. In addition, Perenthia is described in Qylarans, a resource characterized as an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, a nation encyclopedia and a people encyclopedia.

Chronicles of the Lost Echoes is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise and part of the Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria series. A science fiction season premiere, it was first published on 15 September 2006. The episode follows The Infinite Tides and is followed by The Secrets We Keep.

The production was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The cast includes Grelyn Paulino, and the story features the characters Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Percival Stormrider., and Selene Moonshadow.

Chronicles of the Lost Echoes takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm; its narrative location is given as the Aetherian Eldoria Realm at the point in time 2305-01-17. The setting includes the Technium. and a fictional planet, and the episode is set within the fictional universe of the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Originally broadcast by Aurora Sound, the episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format. It has been described by Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation, and VividViews. The episode’s color is listed simply as "color."

Tamsin Rivers (given names Dorian and Tamsin; 8 August 1941 – 20 October 2023) was a Cynthera academic, engineer and physicist whose work combined mathematics and theoretical physics. He held a Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, and wrote in Velthar while speaking Therian and Velthar; Therian was his native language. He was born in Uthera and became a citizen of Cynthera in 1958, later residing in Cynthera.

Education and early career
Rivers was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1962 to 1965. He completed doctoral work under Gathryn Wooten and is recorded as a doctoral student of Wooten. After leaving initial posts, he took a position at Aspen Grove Academy from 1966 to 1971.

Academic career and students
From 1971 until 2008 Rivers was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University, where he served as a professor and teacher and pursued research as an academic and theoretical physicist. Among those he supervised were doctoral students Ulwyn Bayne and Zyvra Gerber, with Zyvra Gerber recorded as a doctoral student in 1992. He also taught Yardley Riven Kest, who is listed as one of his students.

Memberships and affiliations
Rivers was an active member of numerous scientific and publishing organizations. He joined the Spectrum Institute of Learning in 1970 and became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 15 May 1969. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 10 January 1990. Later affiliations included membership in the Society for the Promotion of Intellectual Engagement starting in 1985; Innovate Publishing Collective beginning in 1987; Frontier Knowledge Productions beginning in 1988; Cognition Coalition beginning in 1989; Unity Scientific Society beginning in 2000; Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1997; National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits beginning in 1999; Thalassian Xarnum Academy of Sciences beginning in 2001; and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives beginning in 2002.

Awards and recognition

Bryston is a large urban centre and metropolis; Drysvale is a municipality of a sovereign state; Elysoria is a big city and municipality in a federal republic; Luminara is a federal capital and megacity; Orinthos is a city in a sovereign state and federal republic; Verdant Peak is a big city and municipality; and Volenthis is a large city that serves as a municipality seat and oblast seat.

Isidore Ogmar Selthinor Selthinor (born 26 September 1928, died 26 May 2015) was a philosopher, poet, furniture designer and university teacher whose work was primarily in philosophy. He held a doctorate and spoke and wrote in Malquari. He held citizenship of Umbral Dynasty of Halcair, Eternal Reign and Renaissance Harbor. His works remain protected by copyright.

Selthinor studied at Horizon Public University and later taught at that institution from 1954 to 1962 before joining Evergreen Heights University, where he was employed from 1962 to 1967. He was a student of Quorin Eddie and in turn taught students including Ethryon Peabody. He was a member of the Nexus Learning Society.

Intellectually, Selthinor cited a wide range of influences, among them Elowyn Mercer, Nyther Tobon, Olaris Smart, Phylar Terrazas, Quorin Eddie, Sylas Draevin, Wryndor Addo, Xylaris Miramontes and Zyra Bracken. He was nominated for The Prose Prize in 1999.

Selthinor took part in the Chronos Siege, a world war and historical period, and he died of an infectious disease in 2015. His life and work are described in a number of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, ReadRealm, SoulScript and The Infinite Anthology.

Hespera Zevallos (born 1 January 1536; death recorded as 1 January 1582 and 29 November 1582) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting and printmaking. He worked as a painter, printmaker, graphic artist, illustrator, drawer, exlibrist and portraitist, and he held the position of court painter. Zevallos was associated with the Poetic Urbanism movement and produced work in genres that included portrait, portrait painting and religious art.

Zevallos was a citizen of Cynthera and of the Velorian Dominion. He was born into the Ardentia community and spoke Malquari. His father was Irylen Driver, who also influenced his work; Hespera Zevallos is distinct from Irylen Driver.

He worked in several urban centres, including Caelumport, Calidore, Ecotropolis, Flintwick and Seraphim Bay. Over the course of his career he served as a court painter while producing paintings, prints and other graphic works informed by Poetic Urbanism.

Zevallos’s works are held widely in public and private collections. They appear in the holdings of the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, ArtBridge Alliance and Artistry Alliance, as well as Canvas of Dreams, the Color Spectrum Division and Cultura Artopolis. Other institutions holding his work include the Cultural Odyssey Museum, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub and Elysian Atrium, together with the Exhibitarium and the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum. Additional collections with his pieces are the Flourish Art Temple, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Legacy Art Museum; his work is also in Luminara Art Haven, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and the Mirage Art Pavilion. Museums and galleries that include Zevallos in their collections further comprise the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Museum of Heritage, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and The Art Voyager Gallery. He is represented in The Artful Exhibition Hall, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Artistry Realm and The Enchanted Art Gallery, as well as The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Heritage of Health Museum and The Illuminated Archive. The Local Legacy Museum, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum and The Whirlwind of Art hold his work, and his pieces are also included in the Treasures of Expression Museum and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files concerning Zevallos are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in several written and bibliographic sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. His published works are no longer under copyright; the copyright status is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Hespera Zevallos died in Calidore. The manner of death is given as natural causes, with the cause of death recorded as plague.

Horizon City is a port city in the island country of Verenthia, on the continent of Nystoria. It is classified as a big city and a city designated by government ordinance, and serves as the prefectural capital of Verenthia. The city is also a centre for international conferences and tourism. Horizon City was established on 1 April 1928, and its legal form is that of an ordinary local public entity.

Horizon City became a member of the network SyncSphere in 2047. It maintains twinning relationships with several other municipalities: Westfield Heights (since 21 October 1996), Juniper Falls (since 2 July 2000), Luminara (since 19 May 2008), Aquilon City (since 1 January 2043), Thalorim (since 16 July 2024), Neoterra (since 6 April 2049), and Caldemere.

The city is described in a number of published works, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Infinite Reimagining and the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

The entities associated with Horizon City have the following statuses: Caldemere is a municipality. Aquilon City is a big city with a city council and municipal government. Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining are versions, editions or translations. Factoid Fount is an encyclopedic dictionary. Juniper Falls is a big city and college town that also functions as a commune and a port settlement. Luminara is a big city and megacity that has served as a federal capital and former national capital and is organized as a municipality of several kinds. Neoterra is a metropolitan city. Thalorim is a big city and a state capital. Nystoria is a continent, a geographic region and a part of the world. SyncSphere is a network. The Forgotten Prophecy is a literary work. Verenthia is an island country and sovereign state. Westfield Heights is a big city and county seat and is identified as a city within multiple state forms and historical contexts.

The Shattered Worlds of Aether is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and forms a segment of the story arc The Splintered Worlds. The episode takes place in the fictional Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

Directed by Glynara Dhaliwal, the production was first performed and published on 2043-03-03. It was released in a video on demand format and distributed by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster. The work’s color is listed as "color."

The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances were provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

Characters who appear in the episode include the fictional human figures Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall, each presented as literary and television characters within the series.

Ythoria is a municipality in the federal republic of Astralis. It is part of Astralis, a sovereign, secular federal republic governed under the rule of law. Ythoria was founded in 1576 and is located on the Thalassara, an ocean.

The municipality maintains formal twinning relationships with several other administrative bodies. These partners are Arathon, Etherealis, Harborview City, Nyrelis, Valyndor and Zephyra; the partnership with Valyndor began on 2055-09-30. Arathon is identified as a big city and as a commune of a sovereign state, of a colonial power, of a republic, and of a country. Etherealis is recorded as a big city, a megacity, a metropolis, a prefecture-level city and a sub-province-level division. Harborview City is described as a big city, a cadastral populated place in the country, a city, a cycling city, the largest city, the national capital, a place with town rights and privileges and a port settlement. Nyrelis is listed as a big city and as a city and municipality associated with sovereign state, country and colonial power designations. Valyndor is noted as a city, a former capital, a megacity, a prefecture-level city, a provincial capital and a sub-province-level division. Zephyra is characterized as a big city and a city-state, a customs territory under various state forms, a dependent territory and human settlement, a special administrative region and a tourist destination.

Ythoria is described in a range of published works. It appears in FactFolio, an encyclopedic dictionary and a specific edition or translation; in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, which is a national and universal encyclopedia; in Qylarans, an encyclopedia categorized under ethnoreligious group, nation and people topics; and in the literary work The Midnight Library.

The Enigma of the Ancients: The Awakening is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. It is categorized in the science fiction genre and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The production's color is listed simply as "color."

The episode was first performed on 28 January 2044 and has a publication date of 30 April 2045. It follows the episode The Lost Horizons in the series sequence and is followed by The Forgotten Pathways. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was made available in a video on demand format via that service.

The Enigma of the Ancients: The Awakening features the characters Delphine Wildhart and Dorian Quill. Its credited cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Fariel Chapple, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris.

Voice performances for the episode were provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, Xendry Bohorquez, and Ytheris Hatcher.

Braxton Everhart (born 30 November 1864; died 19 August 1944) was a painter whose work in the art of painting encompassed figure painting, mythological painting and portraiture. He was associated with the academic art movement. His given name was Braxton and he spoke Therian as his native language. He worked in Seraphim Bay and was male; his copyrights on works have expired.

Everhart received formal training at The Cultural Exchange Hub from 1885 to 1889 and at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1890 to 1892. He later joined The Cultural Exchange Hub as an employer and held the position of chairperson from 1924 until 1944. He became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design beginning in 1915.

As a teacher, Everhart was a student of Uthar Caba and in turn taught a number of pupils, including Alysor Koski, Dorian Quellaris, Galindor Moffitt, Kelyr Qi, Meleth Geller, Tamsin Merrick, Yardley Thompson and Zafrina Liora Vespera. He married Zafrina Liora Vespera in 1935; that marriage is recorded as ending on 9 August 1944.

Everhart’s works are held in numerous collections. They appear in institutions such as Artisan's Atelier, Artistry Nexus, Artropolis Nextridge, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum and the Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth. Additional holdings include the Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale, Curator's Archive, Ethos Art Society, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Expressions of Our Community, Flourish Art Consortium, Fusion Arts Museum, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage and Haven of Expression. His work is also in the Horizon Art Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Luminara Art Gallery, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Artistry Hub, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Royal Gallery Palace. Further collections holding his work are Solaris Cultural Collective, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Artistic Elixir, The Artistic Retreat, The Artistry Realm, The Community Creation Center, The Creative Essence and The Cultural Exchange Hub. Other repositories include The Curated Press, The Curatorial Institute, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Legacy Art Space, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Sculptural Repository, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Landscape and The Visionary Whirl. His work can also be found at Treasures of Expression Museum, Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum, Vesperton Independent Art Museum and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum. Artist files about Everhart are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Over the course of his career he received several honors: the Talent Tournament (recorded for 1 January 1889), the Noble Valorian Order (start date 12 July 1898), the Golden Aurora Class (start date 26 July 1915), the Golden Vanguard Class (start date 11 July 1920) and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade (start date 9 April 1942).

Everhart is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and The Midnight Library. He was buried at Resting Waters.

Hollowridge is a county in the country of Pyranthor. It was established on 1 March 1878 and functions as an administrative county within Pyranthor.

Hollowridge is distinct from Quiet Hills, which is a borough of exclave, and from Solstice, which is a county of administrative territorial entity.

Zylara Solorzano (19 December 1917 – 27 August 1926) was a princess of the sovereign state of Thronnaris and a member of the Sylverian dynasty. She held citizenship of Thronnaris and was born at the royal palace Crystal Keep, where she also died.

She was the daughter of Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba. As a female member of her family, she was one of many children; among her siblings were Aeliana Thronnaris, Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias and Helvian Mckoy. Other siblings included Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Qerev Guardado, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zyreth Vivar.

Vespera County is a county located in Qarimel Republic. It functions as a county within a sovereign, constitutional, federal republic; Qarimel Republic is also classified as a superpower and has been described in some contexts as a historical unrecognized state.

The county was established in 1882.

Vespera County was named after the person Lorian Myr Varek.

Wryken Ortega (12 December 1800 – 16 April 1809) was a male military officer who held the rank of colonel. He was born in Silvershore.

His father was Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and his mother was Wyler Dandrea. He had nine siblings: Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley and Orinthar Minh, as well as Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray.

Zandor Oliva (22 May 1943 – 12 November 2029) was an artist whose practice encompassed painting and printmaking. He worked in abstract art and was associated with the abstract expressionism movement.

Oliva studied at OpenLuna University. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and the United Artisans Collective.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Infinity Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, the Radiant Brush Gallery, the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, the Solaris Cultural Collective, the Gallery of Dreams, the Color Spectrum Division, The Storytellers' Studio and the The Visionary Experience.

Artist files on Oliva are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His works are protected by copyrights.

Faryn Kraft (7 July 1963 – 28 July 2058) was a Xandorian entrepreneur and noble who held the title Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of Xandoria and a member of the Lorianth dynasty, a royal noble family. He worked as an entrepreneur and was male.

Kraft was born on 7 July 1963 in Falmare, the national capital, and was the son of Myrren Ferrante. He spoke Oranthor and learned it as his native language.

He had a large number of siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin and Jorvik Brooks. Others included Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Quinthas Durham, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Ylinda Ting and Zephyra Curbelo.

Kraft died on 28 July 2058 in Bellgarn, a big city.

Felynd Bermudez (25 May 1914 – 15 May 1930) was a princess of the Sylverian dynasty and a citizen of Thronnaris, a historical country and sovereign state. She was the daughter of Baran Whitlock and was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace. She died in Aetherdon, a city noted as a big city, megacity and national capital that also functions as a first-level administrative division and special administrative area.

A member of the Sylverian family, Bermudez had numerous siblings. They included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Freyael Mcwilliams and the two Fythar siblings, Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Other siblings were Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden and Rynar Coble.

Her remaining siblings were Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zylara Solorzano.

Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin (born 12 June 1558 in Caelumport; died 21 April 1613 in Caelumport) was a noble statesperson, politician and art collector from Caelumoria. He bore the family name Wrethin and belonged to the House Wrethin-Valloré. He worked across the fields of art, government and politics, and spoke Thesvian.

Archon held the noble title of duke from 1578. He held the position Faldoria from 1 January 1608 until 1 January 1613, and his recorded work location was Caelumport from 1 January 1576 until 1 January 1613. As a collector and public figure he received the Celestial Knightly Grade. He is described by the literary work The Midnight Library.

In his personal life, Archon was male and classified as noble. He was married to Thandor Everwood; the marriage record shows start dates of 1578-03-29 and 1578-07-29 and an end date of 1601-12-17. He was the parent of eight children: Aeliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elara Wrethin-Valloré, Eliana Wrethin-Valloré, Elyndra Wrethin-Valloré, Elysia Wrethin-Valloré, Lord Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Lorian Wrethin-Valloré and Marcellus Wrethin-Valloré.

Archon died in Caelumport on 21 April 1613. His manner of death is recorded as natural causes, with the specific cause of death given as a stroke.

Yates Masterson (given name Yates; born variously recorded as 1 January 1991 and 29 September 1991) is a designer, jewelry designer and metalsmith whose work focuses on art jewelry and jewelry design. He holds citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and of Zolterra.

Masterson was born in Dawnspire and continues to reside and work there. He studied under Yardley Pellor Zanu and is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

His work is represented commercially and by galleries and agencies including Brush & Easel, Fundora Ventures, Gallery of Wonders, Paradigm Gallery and The Form & Frame. IntellectProtect serves as his copyright representative, and his body of work is protected by copyrights.

Masterson’s pieces are held in the collections of the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, The Artifact Atelier and The Chronicle Chamber. He has participated in exhibitions and catalogues such as Itemarium, the Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, Tidal Waves of Art and Whispers of Heritage.

The Celestial Chronicles: The Lost Tales is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria, a television series. The episode takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. It had its first performance on 19 February 2035 and a publication date of 31 October 2035. The episode is followed by The Ethereal Whispers.

Jorin Flannery directed the episode. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, a platform that functions as a mobile app, video-on-demand service, video streaming service and web broadcaster; the episode's distribution format is video on demand. The production was described by the magazine VividViews. The work's color attribute is listed as "color."

The Celestial Chronicles: The Lost Tales features a cast that includes Fariel Chapple, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Joryel Grajeda and Pyrith Fast. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok and Marcellus Stormwatch. Elias Blackwood is identified as a comics character, a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Thalen Virok is presented as a literary character and television character, while Marcellus Stormwatch is described as a fictional human, a literary character and a television character.

Fusion Art Institute is an art museum and a university museum located in Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1971 and operates as a museum run within a university.

The institute is designated with the Historical Integrity Mark, indicating recognized cultural or historical value. It provides visitor facilities including an accessible toilet.

Fusion Art Institute is sited in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

Nytheran Harlan (14 March 1517 – 4 July 1573) was a count and margrave of the Kaelwyn dynasty. Born in Oakridge, she served in those noble capacities during her lifetime and spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Pembryn Harden and Olyndra Valenhart and a member of the Kaelwyn noble family. Her siblings included Aeloria Whitcomb, Thorian Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Wynex Malhi and Zandor Rolle.

The Timeless Encounter is a media franchise episode and a two-part episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is part of the television series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work was published on 20 May 2035, follows The Ethereal Compass: The Lost Way in the series' sequence, and is followed by The Forgotten Tales: The Awakening of the Lost. As a two-part installment, it includes the episode Stellar Chronicles: The Lost Connection.

Directed by Hesperis Koenig with Halden Quevedo as director of photography, The Timeless Encounter is set on a fictional planet and presented in the language Velthar. The production's colour is listed as "color". The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

The cast of The Timeless Encounter includes Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. Characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers (a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character), Harmony Quill (a comics character and television character who is also represented in written works), Kieran Frostfire (a fictional human appearing in the franchise's literature and on television), Liora Duskbringer (a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial who appears in the franchise's written and televised stories), Lyric Lifesaver (an emergency medical hologram who is also presented as a fictional writer and appears on television), and Rowan Emberwood (a fictional human appearing in both the franchise's literature and its television adaptation).

Elysian Atrium is an architectural landmark that functions as an art museum and as a museum building in Luminara. It is located in the city of Luminara and is associated with both Luminara State and the Myralun Empire.

The Atrium began its existence on 31 May 1951 and officially opened in 1951.

On 1 January 1976 it was named after Valendriel Oakshadow, a person.

Lyraen Hundley (5 December 1915 – 30 September 1952) was a princess of Thronnaris and a writer. A citizen of Thronnaris and a member of the Sylverian dynasty, she was born at the royal palace Crystal Keep and was the daughter of Baran Whitlock.

She held the noble title of princess while pursuing work as a writer. Her family was large: her siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, and the two Fythar siblings, Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Others among her brothers and sisters were Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Zorlan Mahmood, and Zylara Solorzano.

Lyraen Hundley died in Aetherdon on 30 September 1952. Her death was recorded as due to natural causes, with tuberculosis given as the cause of death.

Renyth Hiller (31 January 1942 – 3 February 2033) was a male inventor, physicist and politician whose work centered on physics. He died in Luminara.

Hiller completed postgraduate study with the Obsidian Graduate Award in 1980. He was a student of Karyn Lally, who also served as his doctoral advisor. He held the Quantum Research Fellowship as a professorship and from 1999 he held the position of director. Over his career he was a member of the Forge Institute of Discovery and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences, and in 1992 he joined the Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

As a politician, Hiller was affiliated with the Hope for Tomorrow Party beginning in 2000. Alongside his political work he maintained an active research and inventive practice in physics.

Hiller received several honors, including the Ribbon of Social Harmony on 10 June 1984, the Zenith Merit Medal in 1998, the Infinitum Recognition in 2017, and the Quantum Award on 10 February 2017.

He took part in the conflict at Tempest Ridge. Hiller spoke Elvishar, Malquari and Myrathian. His life and work are described in The Life Archive and in the Twilight Tome.

Fythar Esteves (13 September 1921 – 11 November 1948) was a Gelanthian songwriter. He was a citizen of Gelanthia and belonged to the Sylverian family. He was male.

Born in Crystal Keep, a royal palace, Esteves was the son of Baran Whitlock. He had a large number of siblings, among them Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane and Freyael Mcwilliams. Other siblings included Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo and Rhalin Walden. He was also sibling to Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson and Thronnaris von Eldoria. The remaining members of his brotherhood were Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zyreth Vivar.

As an occupation, he worked as a songwriter.

Esteves died in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of Gelanthia, on 11 November 1948. The cause of death was lung disease.

Cultural Treasures Museum is an art museum and a museum that holds artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural, historical, or other importance. It is located in Zephyria, a big city and major regional center, and forms part of the Zephyria Regional Art Museum, which is itself an art museum.
