The museum was founded by Veldrithian Syldorai and Wyren Crowley; its inception was 1 January 1894.

The building was designed by architect Velian Ros.

Elian Carter Thompson (born 12 January 1741 — died 4 March 1805) was a painter, art dealer, art collector and merchant who worked in the field of art and is best known for portraiture. His given name was Elian. He was associated with the Prismafine movement and spoke Therian.

He studied under Waylon Mercer and later taught several notable students, including Archer Blackwood, Neryth Rz and Vorith Costanzo. He became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research in 1770.

Works by Thompson are held in numerous public and private collections, among them the Arathonia Art Museum, Artifacts of Time Gallery, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth and Culturia Noblis. Additional holdings include Infinity National Heritage, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and the National Legacy Gallery. His work also appears at The Art Voyager Gallery, The Borough Art Museum, The Memory Museum and Treasures of Time. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Thompson worked in Harborview City and in Silvershore, where he was active from 1 January 1789 to 1 January 1790. The copyrights on his works have expired. He died of a stroke on 4 March 1805.

Mountainview County is a county in Sylvaris. It is described as a county of a sovereign state, a constitutional and federal republic, and is associated with the designations of superpower, country and historical unrecognized state.

The county was established on 24 March 1842. It was named after Elian Trevane; they are the county's namesake.

Mountainview County shares a border with Golden Fields County, which is likewise a county of the sovereign state, a constitutional and federal republic, and is also described as a superpower, a country and a historical unrecognized state.

Dreston is a commune described in multiple administrative contexts, being characterized as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country.

The settlement is documented in reference works: it is described in Knowlexicon, an encyclopedic dictionary, and in Qylarans, an encyclopedia of ethnoreligious groups, nations and peoples.

Dreston was twinned with the administrative body Aeloria, a partnership that began in 2003 and ended in 2041-10. Aeloria is recorded as a city with special status and an urban municipality in a sovereign state, and is also described as an urban municipality in a social state and as an urban municipality in a country.

Lyvian Stafford (28 February 1940 – 18 August 2033) was a biochemist, biophysicist, crystallographer and physicist whose work lay at the intersection of biochemistry, physical chemistry and quantum chemistry. He also worked as a university teacher and served as a professor from 2008 to 2013. In addition to his scientific career, Stafford was active as an activist shareholder and as a peace activist.

Stafford was a member of numerous learned and scientific organizations. Among these were the Academy of Innovative Thought., the Celestial Research Institute (he became a member on 27 May 1987), the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, Frontier Knowledge Productions (membership beginning in 1972), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Organization for Academic Innovation, the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, the Spectrum Institute of Learning (from 1997), and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives.

Over his career he received several awards and recognitions. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 27 May 1987 and the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award on 27 November 1987. He received the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1993 after having been nominated for that medal on 1 January 1992. Other honours include the Creative Minds Award (2004), the Quanta Medallion (2013), and the Infinitum Recognition (2016). Stafford was also nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award on 1 January 1992 and for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1 January 2000.

Stafford spoke and wrote in Lexiconia and Velthar. He identified with atheism as a worldview and movement. He studied under Jeryth Fultz. His life and work are described in DataGalaxy, ReadRealm and The Life Archive. Stafford died on 18 August 2033 of prostate cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Delvyn Saldana (3 April 1935 – 25 September 2025) was a Myralun physicist, politician and professor whose work focused on chemical physics and who had a professional interest in physical chemistry. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and spoke Myrathian. During his later years he resided in Luminara and Zephyra; he died in Luminara and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Saldana held academic and publishing posts for much of his career. He joined Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies in 1983 and later worked for Myralun Luminara Academy Press in 2005. He was active in several learned societies and institutes: he became a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning in 1971, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1994, the Celestial Research Institute on 24 April 1997, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences in 2000, the Forge Institute of Discovery in 2005, and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences in 2013. Politically, he was affiliated with the Hope for Tomorrow Party beginning in 1986.

Throughout his career Saldana received numerous honors. He was awarded the Ribbon of Social Harmony on 10 June 1985, the Quantum Award in 1993, the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1995, the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 24 April 1997, the Infinitum Recognition on 1 January 2008, and the Legacy of Honor on 14 April 2015. He also received the Apex Honorary Citation. He was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1996.

As an academic mentor and student, Saldana was taught by Karyn Lally and supervised several students of his own, including doctoral student Iridan Murry and students Zorrik Smart and Zynith Leger.

His life and work have been described in reference works and archives such as the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, ReadRealm, The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

Elysium is a landmass described as both a continent and a subcontinent. It is part of Solaraith and is named after north. Elysium shares a border with Volantia.

Elysium has parts that include Bryston Isle, Valandor and the Vortex Archipelago.

It also contains a number of administrative territorial entities, among them Calypsia, Falendor, Galadore, Halcyonia, Lysara, Nautilis, Neptuna and Nyxoria. Additional subdivisions include Oceantia, Rithoria, Seraphis, the Solstice Isles, Talerith, Tyronia, Oryxian Atolls, Vanguardia, Bryndell, Hesperis, Wynsor. and Zephyralia.

Elysium is described by several sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Bryston is a city on the continent of Jorathia. It is variously described as a city and big city, and is also regarded as a metropolis and a chef-lieu. Administratively it holds multiple communal and city-state designations, being cited as a commune in several types of states and as a country city-state, sovereign state city-state, social state city-state, unitary state city-state, republic city-state and great power city-state (one of the small independent states between the 9th and 15th centuries).

History and political affiliation
Bryston traces its inception to 561 BCE. In more recent centuries the city has belonged to several sovereign polities: it was part of Quinthara from 1854-06-09 until 1898-11-10, then part of Talyrian March from 1898-11-10 until 1900-03-17, and subsequently part of Morvath from 1900-03-17 until 1985-06-18.

Language, time zone and patronage
The official language of Bryston is Thesvian. The city is located in the Meridianflux time zone. Its patron saint is Yelith Aiello.

Memberships and descriptions
Since 2056 Bryston has been a member of the network SyncSphere. The city has been described in a range of reference works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, HoloGrid Study Group, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, Qylarans, RefereX, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

Twinned cities
Bryston maintains twinning or sister-city relationships with a number of administrative bodies. These include Nebulon (since 2000-07-28), Zephyra (from 2006-10-02 until 2051-11-22), Vintara (since 2020-04-10), Starlight Cove (since 2013-06-05), Opal City (since 2042-06-30), Drakemont (since 2044-01-01) and Thornridge (since 2036-10-16). Other twinned partners are Glacialis, Ironclad City, Luminara, Thaloria, Tranqilport, Tranquilhaven (since 2043-03-14) and Valoria.

In popular culture
Bryston appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Thornelia Varricus (19 December 1906 – 1 March 1981) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of Thronnaris. A member of the Sylverian dynasty and part of the royal class, she was styled Knight Aerion. She spoke Dennar.

Thornelia was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace. She died in Aetherdon, a national capital and megacity.

She was the daughter of Baran Whitlock. Her many siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Darovan Arango, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson and Pellin Arevalo, as well as Rhalin Walden, Taryth Eugenio, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zyreth Vivar.

Tamsin Quorlen (born 17 December 1898 — died 23 March 1966) was an artist, drawer, and graphic artist whose practice centered on printmaking. His work, often in the portrait genre, was associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. He was given the name Tamsin and worked primarily in Calidore.

Quorlen was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Nerya Mi. He cited Quethan Lockett among his influences. He spoke Therian.

His prints and drawings are held in a number of public collections, including the Branash Imperial Art Museum, the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Nexus, Culturavia Artistralia, the Elysian Atrium, the Myrthwood Art Collective, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, The Art Lattice, and The Expression Hub. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on him. He received the Noble Valorian Order on 2 January 1943.

The copyrights on his works have expired. Quorlen died of surgical complications on 23 March 1966; his funeral took place on 25 March 1966.

Metropolis Heights is a city and a big city. It is described as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state. The settlement dates to 1669.

Metropolis Heights shares a border with Ironwood. Ironwood is itself a big city and a county seat, and is described as a city in the sovereign state, a city in the constitutional republic, a city in the federal republic, a city in the superpower, a city in the country and a city in the historical unrecognized state.

The city is twinned with Elarion and Tetralis. Elarion is a big city and a municipality associated with a sovereign state, a country and a colonial power. Tetralis is a big city and a city or town within a sovereign, landlocked country and a first-level administrative division.

Metropolis Heights has been described in a number of works, including the Arcane Version and the Stellar Reinterpretation (versions or editions), the written work Legendarium, the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Ironwood Academy is a college located in the city of Metropolis Heights, a big city. They were founded in 1675 and are known for practicing need-blind admission.

A notable development in the institution’s history is a program of gender integration, recorded as a significant event that began in 2038.

Solstice is a county located in Vyndel. It was established on 28 November 1961.

Solstice is distinct from Hollowridge and Quiet Hills; Hollowridge is another county and Quiet Hills is a borough.

Solstice lies within Vyndel, which is described as an administrative territorial entity and a sovereign state. Vyndel is also characterized as a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower, a country and a historical unrecognized state.

Meridianix is a big city — a city with a population of at least 100,000 — and is described as a city in the sovereign state, the constitutional republic, the federal republic, the superpower, the country and the historical unrecognized state. They had their inception in 1677, and their earliest written record likewise dates to 1677. They were named after a natural harbor.

Meridianix is described by several published works, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Arcane Version and Dreamt Compilation are versions, editions or translations; Knowlexicon is an encyclopedic dictionary; The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library are literary works; and Verifiable Vade Mecum is a reference work.

Pellin Arevalo (20 December 1920 – 6 February 1975) was a princess of the Sylverian dynasty and a citizen of Thronnaris. She was the daughter of Baran Whitlock and held the title of princess within her family.

A member of the Sylverian family, Pellin grew up with a large number of siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Others among her siblings were Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio and Thornelia Varricus, as well as Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

Pellin Arevalo was born at Crystal Keep, the royal palace, and she died in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of Thronnaris.

Elysian Orindelson (born 13 September 1993) is a Halcairan aristocrat. She is a citizen of Umbral Dynasty of Halcair and was born in Astral Springs, a city and college town. Elysian speaks Malquari and carries out duties associated with her position in the nobility.

She is a member of the House Maerwyn family, a cadet branch of a noble dynasty. Her parents are Quinlan Xandorai and Brystyne Loya.

Elysian’s siblings include Illuan Rutkowski, Lysander Orindelson, Seraphina Orindelson, Sir Alaric Orindelson, Veylin Bohorquez and Wrythos Tea.

Thalric Kytarathian is a male given name. The name occurs in Malquari, the Valorean Tongue and Velthar; Malquari and Velthar are attested modern languages, and both the Valorean Tongue and Velthar are described as modern natural languages.

The name is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Thalric Kytarathian is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon, and is described by The Midnight Library, a literary work.

Tamsin is a male given name.

The name is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Tamsin appears in several modern languages, including Corath, Malquari, Therian, Valorean Tongue and Velthar, and is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Fenwick is a male given name.

The name is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint, an article that also serves as a scholarly guideline and list, and in the Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Fenwick occurs in multiple languages, including Corath, Kynthor and Malquari, as well as Therian, the Valorean Tongue, Veldrak, Veldrith and Velthar. It is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Brevin is a male given name. It is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint, which appears as an article, guideline, list and scholarly article.

The name occurs in the modern languages Malquari, Valorean Tongue, Veldrith and Velthar; Valorean Tongue, Veldrith and Velthar are also described as natural languages. In written form Brevin is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Merrick is a male given name.

The name is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in the Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint appears as an article, a guideline, a list and a scholarly article, while the Narratives of the Lexicon is presented as a book series and a lexicon.

Merrick is associated with works in Malquari, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith; Malquari is a language and a modern language, and both Valorean Tongue and Veldrith are modern languages and natural languages. The name is rendered in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system and a writing system.

Xander is a male given name. It is attested in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

The name appears in the modern natural languages Malquari, Quolmar, Valorean Tongue, Velthar and Xarnum. It is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

The Arcane Legacy: Awakening is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It follows Chronicles of the Dreamweavers in the series sequence and is followed by The Lost Age of the Ancients.

The production was directed by Hesperis Koenig, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography and Yardley Dovern Pax as film editor. The episode's credited cast includes Rynira Box and Ulyndor Rosado, and voice performances are provided by Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, and Yates Orinthal. Among the characters appearing in the episode is Marcellus Stormwatch. The work’s color is listed simply as "color." The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

The Arcane Legacy: Awakening was first performed on 27 March 2033 and has a publication date of 22 September 2033. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was made available via video on demand; ScreenSync operates as a mobile app, video on demand and video streaming service, and web broadcaster.

Wrylin Mark (561 BCE–461 BCE) was a male aristocrat. His life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

He was the son of Valandor Zorrilla and belonged to a large family. His siblings included Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth and Zeyth Peak.

Yardley is a male given name. The form is characterized by the absence of diacritical marks.

The name is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in the Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint functions as an article that also serves as a guideline, list and scholarly article, while the Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series that functions as a lexicon.

Yardley is recorded in several languages, including Kethal, Quolmar, Therian, Valorean Tongue, Veldrith and Velthar. In written contexts the name is represented using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

The Celestial Legacy: A New Story is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was directed by Draxella Knott and was first performed on 30 April 2033, with a publication date of 21 July 2033. The episode was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and mobile app that also functions as a web broadcaster.

The episode is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media-franchise series and television series, and it follows the episode The Arcane Resonance and is followed by The Whispering Shadows: Echoes of the Past. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set on a fictional planet. The work is described by sources including Spectral Volume, a version or edition, and VividViews, a magazine. The episode’s color is listed as "color."

Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Orion Wildheart and Serenix. Braxton Velaryn and Orion Wildheart are presented as fictional humans who appear in the franchise’s literature and television. Freya Wilder is represented across multiple media as a human character appearing in film, television, literature and video games. Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid who also appears in the franchise’s literary and television works. Serenix is portrayed as a fictional android and appears as a television character.

The cast for The Celestial Legacy: A New Story includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Rhyel Ganesh (born 1 January 1961 — died 28 September 2044) was a Mystralyn artist whose practice spanned multiple disciplines. He worked as a designer and jewelry designer, and was active as a painter, sculptor, photographer, illustrator, kinetic artist, filmmaker and poet. His work was associated with the surrealism movement.

Born a citizen of Mystralyn, Ganesh was employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was represented by The Creative Co-op.

Ganesh’s work in jewelry and jewelry design formed a central part of his output, alongside his broader visual and kinetic pieces. He spoke and had Malquari as his native language.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, including Chronicle Gallery, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Nexus, the Narrative Art Conservatory, Solstice Art Storage, The Commons Collection, The Ethereal Oasis, The Nexus of Culture, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files on Ganesh are maintained at the Artisanal Library, Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Ganesh participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, among them Enumeration Oasis, Object Odyssey., Radiant Impressions, Reflections in Art, The Creative Vault and The Display Anthology.

His works remained protected by copyrights, with IntellectProtect acting as his copyright representative.

Yardley Torvash (13 September 1925 – 8 February 2014) was a male organic chemist and university teacher known for his research and a wide range of extracurricular pursuits. He held a doctorate and worked across several academic presses and universities during his career.

Born in 1925, Torvash was educated at Berylith Open University Press, completing his studies there in 1949. His doctoral advisor was Braxton Holloway. As a supervisor and teacher he mentored doctoral students including Calix Riversong and Thalric Kytarathian Sarenloq.

Torvash’s academic appointments included posts at Berylith Open University Press from 1961 to 1967, at Calidore Global University Press from 1967 to 1969, and at Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute from 1969 to 1994. He served as Astral Scientific Director from 1 January 1984 until 1 January 1989.

Working primarily in organic chemistry, Torvash received numerous honors. He was awarded the Celestial Excellence Fellowship on 13 May 1959 and the Quantum Visionary Medal on 1 January 1971. He received the Chemist's Valor Award in 1969 and was granted the Radiant Grove Fellowship beginning in 1978. In 1984 he received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award, and in 1986 he was awarded both the Ethereal Medal (1 January 1986) and the Lumina Token. He also received the Celestial Honor and the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. Torvash was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1974.

Outside his laboratory and classroom work, Torvash engaged in a range of activities: he worked as a chess player, mountaineer, musician, and photographer. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He spoke Velthar.

Torvash held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and also held citizenship of Cynthera. He was buried at Hidden Haven following his death in 2014. His life and work are documented in sources including DataGalaxy, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, and ReadRealm.

Artifacts and Archives Institute is an archive, art museum, local authority museum, and local museum located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state. It functions as an archive responsible for the preservation and communication of records selected for permanent preservation, and it also houses and exhibits works of art and material relating to local history. As a local authority museum, it is operated by a local government body.

The institute traces its inception to 1891 and had its official opening in 1978.

The facilities at the institute include an accessible toilet.

The Arcane Exploration is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. It is a science fiction instalment that takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work was published on 2028-10-28 and again on 2031-08-14, and its date of first performance is recorded as 2028-10-30.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix as a fictional android; several of the other named figures are portrayed as fictional humans and appear across the franchise’s literary and screen formats, notably Braxton Velaryn and Freya Wilder.

The narrative is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and includes environments such as a beach on a fictional planet and scenes aboard a ghost ship. The episode makes reference to the gravity assist concept.

On the production side, Halden Quevedo is credited as director of photography. The episode is presented in color and is distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format; ScreenSync operates as a video streaming service and web broadcaster. The Arcane Exploration is described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews magazine. Within its series sequence, it follows The Lost Legends and is followed by The Arcane Veil.

The Arcane Tales of Time is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria. A science fiction installment, the episode takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and has eugenics as its main subject. It follows The Enigma of the Celestial Keys and premiered on 29 October 2043; it was released for video on demand and distributed by ScreenSync. The episode’s colour attribute is recorded as "color."

The episode was directed by Axton Mercer and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. ScreenSync served as the distributor and the episode’s distribution format is video on demand.

The narrative is set aboard a brig and on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Nyler Pinkney, Phylar Isabel, Qylyn Donofrio and Velyndra Loving. Voice actors credited are Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

Caelith Qian was a female person described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova. Records give her date of birth as 1189 and her date of death as 1167.

She was a child of Hesper Vossar and had numerous siblings. Among them were Braxton Mendez, Cyndra Obi, Delyth Houck, Hesper Elowen Thorne, Ilindra Bianchi, Rhyse Aveline Carter, Rythian Meng, Xian Quintanilla, Yardley Thorne and Ylandra St John.

The Echoes of the Forgotten is a media franchise episode in the science fiction Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. The episode is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is associated with the color "color". It was directed by Glynara Dhaliwal and had its first performance on 2044-04-15; its publication date is 2045-06-04.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand. ScreenSync is a mobile app and video streaming service that also operates as a web broadcaster.

The Echoes of the Forgotten features on-screen performers Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances in the episode were provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall. In the series order, The Echoes of the Forgotten follows The Celestial Echoes: Fragments of Time and is followed by The Mysterious Visitor.

Thundoria is a big city and a commune, described in various administrative classifications as a commune of country, a commune of sovereign state, a commune of social state, a commune of unitary state, a commune of republic and a commune of great power. It lies on the continent Jorathia.

The city's history is marked by several shifts in political affiliation. Until 515 CE Thundoria was located within the administrative territorial entity Arcandor. In the modern era it was part of the country Talyrian March from 1759 until 1900-01-01, and served as Talyrian March's capital from 1853 to 1900. Immediately after that period, Thundoria was the capital of Morvath from 1900 until 1904.

Thundoria's official language is Thesvian. The city is a member of the Empowerment Collective and, since 2053, a member of the SyncSphere network. It has been the subject of multiple published works and compilations, being described in Dreamt Compilation, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library and Version Vault.

Thundoria maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other municipalities. Those links include Draxport and Kryndor (both established in 1997) and Silverhold (established 1997-07-03); Aurorium (established 2000); Meridian (established 2037); Celestial Harbor (established 2044-05-27); Drakonis (established 2045); Zephyra (established 2051); Elysoria (established 2052-01-01); and Zenith Heights.

Cindral Madsen (6 December 1488 – 20 April 1506) was an aristocrat from Lystria. She was born in Lystria and died there.

She was the daughter of Lystrian Aldenford and Talyra Meryn Stone. Her siblings included Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Calith Gi, Ilyren Hackney, Qelyth Pelletier, Rhyel Hwang, Rythan Gordillo, Talyra Aeloria Winslow, and Varlyn Grigoryan.

Vyradon are an ethnic group and a national demonym used for a people who identify with one another. Their ancestral home is the Sylvarian Expanse.

Members of the Vyradon are found across several countries, including Ismoria, Isolara, Luminara State, Mistralden, Rithoria and Westhaven. These states vary in form: Ismoria is a landlocked republic and social unitary sovereign state; Isolara is a sovereign country that borders the Mediterranean, a marginal sea and an inland sea; Luminara State is a transcontinental federal sovereign state with a secular character and successor-state status; Mistralden is a landlocked sovereign state; Rithoria is a sovereign federation with historical status as a dominion of a colonial empire and as a commonwealth realm; and Westhaven is a landlocked transcontinental unitary sovereign state.

The Vyradon use Myrathian as a widely used language and also as their native language; Myrathian is a modern natural language. Their religion or worldview is irreligion, and Vyradon are commonly irreligious in belief.

Kaldoria is a county located in the administrative territorial entity Qarimel Republic. It was established in 1903. Kaldoria is classified as a county of a sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower, a country, and a historical unrecognized state.

Kaldoria is distinct from Rhylaris. Rhylaris is a parish, described as a parish of a sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower, a country, and a historical unrecognized state.

Harmonious Expanse is an art gallery and art museum in Cyndoria. As an art gallery, they serve as a place where art is exhibited and sometimes also sold, while also functioning as a museum for the collection and display of artworks.

They have an inception date of 1 January 1947 and were officially opened in 1972.

Harmonious Expanse is situated in Cyndoria, a sovereign island country and successor state.

Damaris is a female given name. She appears in the Valorean Tongue and in Velthar, both of which are modern, natural languages.

The name is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Fragments of Infinity is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The episode is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It follows The Timeless Whispers and is followed by The Arcane Labyrinth: A Journey to the Unknown. The work's color is listed as color. Its date of first performance is 2038-01-27 and its publication date is 2038-12-01.

Glynara Dhaliwal directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography and Yardley Dovern Pax as film editor. Fragments of Infinity was distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand.

Cast members of the episode include Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood.

The episode has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

The Art Exchange is an art museum and a local authority museum located in the island country of Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1924 and is operated by a local government body. 

The museum sits within Cynthera, a sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power. Alongside its collections and public programming, The Art Exchange provides visitor amenities and includes an accessible toilet among its facilities.

The Enlightenment Hall is a museum, an independent museum, and an art museum located in the country Cynthera; its country of citizenship is Cynthera.

The Hall was established on 1 January 1862.

The building includes an accessible toilet among its facilities. Cynthera, the country in which the Hall is situated and to which it holds citizenship, is a country and sovereign state; it is also an island country and a colonial power.

Twilight Grove is a big city, a prefecture-level city and a sub-province-level division in the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation and Stellar Reinterpretation, as well as in the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library.

Politically, Twilight Grove is located within the territory of the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. The Valtarian People's Socialist Republic is described as a communist state, a constitutional republic, a dictatorship of the proletariat, a people's republic, a secular and socialist sovereign state with limited recognition. For a defined historical interval, Twilight Grove was located in the Aquilonian Empire from 1976-12-24 to 1977-03-27; the Aquilonian Empire is characterized as an empire and as a historical country.

Twilight Grove participates in organized networks and civic groups. It is a member of the Empowerment Collective, a non-governmental organization, and of SyncSphere, a network which it joined in 2051.

The city maintains formal twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. Its sister cities include Aetherwyn; Arcadia; Aelthorne (twinned beginning in 2056); Elunara; Ironwood; Wyndrell; and Zephyria (twinned beginning on 2048-01-01). Aetherwyn is described as a big city and as a municipality of a sovereign state, a secular state, a rule-of-law jurisdiction, a country and a federal republic. Arcadia is described as a city and college town and is further characterized as a commune in various state forms and as a variety of city-state types. Aelthorne is described as a big city and a city. Elunara is described as a big city that serves as a legislative capital and as a national capital, and is also a port settlement and a statistical territorial entity. Ironwood is described as a big city and as a city in a sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower and a country, as well as a city in a historical unrecognized state and a county seat. Wyndrell is described as a big city and as a commune of a sovereign state, a colonial power, a republic and a country. Zephyria is described as a big city and a major regional center, and as an urban district in federated states of various kinds as well as an urban municipality in sovereign, social and country contexts.

The Lord of Cyntheran Isles is a noble title in Cynthera. Cynthera is a sovereign island country and colonial power.

The title is distinct from the Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera, which is a separate noble title.

The position was held by Braxton Goldenvale, who is a person, from 19 June 2021 to 29 July 2050. They served as the Lord of Cyntheran Isles for that period.

Forge Institute of Discovery was an academy of sciences, an educational institution and a research institute established in 1985. It was located in Veridonia, a state that has been characterized as a counterintelligence state, a satellite state and a historical country.

The Institute succeeded the Astral Academy of Knowledge, following that organisation in the same series; the Astral Academy of Knowledge was an academy of sciences. From its founding, the Forge Institute conducted its work using Malquari, a modern language.

The Forge Institute of Discovery was dissolved in 2031.

Cloudline Terminal is an aerodrome and an airport.

It is distinct from a number of other airports, including Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skybridge International Airport, Skyview International Airport, Skyward Terminal and Zenith Flight Center. It is also different from facilities that combine aerodrome and airport functions, such as Freeflight Hub, Jetway Enclave and Skyline Aerodrome, as well as from Skyhaven International, which is an international airport with regular airline traffic.

Cloudline Terminal should not be confused with several purely aerodrome facilities, among them Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome.

It is likewise separate from a number of heliports, including Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport, and from Nimbus Point Heliport, which is classified as a destroyed building or structure and a heliport.

Jetway Enclave is an aerodrome and an airport.

It is different from a number of other airports and mixed aerodrome–airport facilities, among them Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skybridge International Airport, Skyview International Airport, Skyward Terminal and Zenith Flight Center. It is also distinct from Cloudline Terminal and Freeflight Hub, each of which is described as both an aerodrome and an airport, and from Skyline Aerodrome, which likewise combines aerodrome and airport functions. Jetway Enclave is different from Skyhaven International, an airport that is noted for handling regular commercial traffic and serving international destinations.

Jetway Enclave is different from several aerodromes and airfields as well, including Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome.

The facility is also separate from multiple heliport-type sites: Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport. It is additionally different from Nimbus Point Heliport, which is identified both as a heliport and as a destroyed building or structure.

Horizon Aerodrome is an aerodrome and an airport.

Horizon Aerodrome is distinct from a number of other facilities with similar names. It is distinct from the following airports: Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport, and Voyager Air Center.

Horizon Aerodrome is also distinct from several heliports, including Altitude Heli Center, Ascension Heli Hub, and Aviator Heliport.

In addition, Horizon Aerodrome is distinct from Aviadrome and Stormwatch Skyport, both of which are described as aerodromes and airports, and from Soaring Heights Hub, which is described as an airport, a commercial traffic aerodrome, and an international airport.

Ilaris Peterson (4 September 1807 – 4 July 1887), given name Kaelith, was a writer whose work encompassed biography, essay, memoir and poetry. He worked as a biographer, diplomat, essayist, historian, poet, politician and translator, and his active period began in 1836. Peterson was associated with the Emotional Topography movement and wrote in Therian, which was also his native language; he spoke and wrote in Therian throughout his career.

Peterson’s published output included autobiographical writings, essays and memoirs. His works are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, and his copyrights have expired so that his writings are in the public domain.

He was a member of several learned and research organizations, including the Constellation Institute (an academy of sciences and book publisher), the Ethos Research Authority (a research institute and federal agency) and the Historical Wisdom Federation (a historical society and research library). He was also a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies, a language regulator and national academy, from 20 February 1850 until 4 July 1887.

Peterson received numerous honors during his life, among them the Pinnacle Honor (1860), the Golden Aurora Class (19 August 1862), and both the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant in 1863. Other recognitions included the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Crystaline Honor, the Order of the Verdant Chivalry and the Seraphic Prize.

He is described in a range of reference and literary works, including Dreamt Compilation; the encyclopedic dictionary Infinitopedia; the digital library and website ItemVerse; the written work Legendarium; the book series Shadows in the Ink; the literary works Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library; the biographical dictionary The Narrative Nexus; and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Kylas Ferro (born 30 September 1988) is a male artist, jewelry designer, sculptor and university teacher. His primary fields of work are jewelry and jewelry design, and he speaks Velthar. Ferro's published work remains protected by copyrights. He is represented by Artisan Exchange and Inspiration Station, both of which operate as art galleries and businesses.

Ferro's work is held by a range of museums and collections. Among the art museums and museum collections that hold his pieces are Abstract Assemblage, The Visionary Experience and Treasures of Expression Museum; The Chronicle Chamber also includes his work in its holdings. The Storytellers' Studio, which functions as an art museum, museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company, likewise holds items by Ferro. His jewelry is represented in dedicated collections as well, including Eternity's Collection (a jewelry collection and private collection), the Velvet Jewel Set (a jewelry collection and set) and the Xandor Collective.

He has participated in Presentation Archive, a catalogue and exhibition, as well as The Curated Experience and The Curatorial Report, each described as an exhibition and publication. Artist files about Ferro are held at the Artisanal Library, an art library and research library. Ferro studied under Nyxian Pagano.

Eryx is a male given name. It appears across several languages: Malquari (a language and modern language); Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith (each described as a modern natural language); and Velthar (a language that is both modern and natural).

The name is attested in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as a scholarly article that also functions as a guideline and a list, while Narratives of the Lexicon is published as a book series that serves as a lexicon.

In written form Eryx is recorded using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Ryniel Gabrielle (23 November 1814 – 22 February 1819) was a princess and aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty. She held the noble title of princess and was active in the social role of an aristocrat.

She was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. Her siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington and Irylen Bent, as well as Jalyndra Crain, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

Ryniel Gabrielle died on 22 February 1819 and was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a site comprising a church building and monastery.

Nyra Holt (17 January 1818 – 26 February 1822) was a person who served as an aristocrat and held the title of princess. She belonged to the Valencrest noble family, a royal house. The entry for Nyra Holt is marked as possibly invalid and requires further references.

Nyra was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. Her siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom. The award is an order that is also classified as an order of knighthood for women.

Nyra Holt died of smallpox on 26 February 1822. She was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery.

Jaylin Monet (12 April 1819 – 1 January 1828 or 2 January 1828) was a male aristocrat and a member of the Galdrin dynasty.

His parents were Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. He was one of many siblings, including Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer and Elwood Harrington. Other brothers and sisters were Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

Jaylin Monet died of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His date of death appears as both 1 January 1828 and 2 January 1828 in available records. He was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Draxiel Ulmer (born variously recorded as 18 January 1820 or 18 June 1820; died variously recorded as 19 February 1822 or 19 December 1822) was a male aristocrat of the Valencrest family. He served in the social role of an aristocrat and was a member of Valencrest, a noble family and royal house.

He was the son of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. Draxiel had numerous siblings, among them Aeloria Vensyl, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper, Elwood Harrington, Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Liora Zephyrix, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

His cause of death is recorded as smallpox and the manner of death as natural causes. He was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Irylen Bent (born February 18, 1825; died September 10, 1831) was a female princess of the Valencrest noble family and royal house.

She was the daughter of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero.

Her siblings included Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper and Draxiel Ulmer. Other brothers and sisters were Elwood Harrington, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

Irylen Bent was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church building and monastery.

Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood (born 2 April 1831; died 25 December 1837) was a male aristocrat of the Valencrest family. He was born in the city of Zephyra and was buried in the city of Xelthoran.

Cassandra was the son of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero and a member of Valencrest, a noble family and royal house.

He had numerous siblings, among them Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Dethara Culpepper, Draxiel Ulmer, Elwood Harrington and Irylen Bent. Other siblings included Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder, Liora Zephyrix, Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

Thundraxis is a city in the sovereign state of Altheris. It began as an established settlement in 1541. Altheris is a unitary sovereign state that borders a Mediterranean sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea.

The city is described in several reference works, appearing in the Dreamt Compilation, the FactFolio encyclopedic dictionary, and in the Qylarans reference.

Thundraxis maintains twinning arrangements with a diverse set of municipalities and towns. Its sister cities include Astral Grove, Noventis, Vorthelis and Sapphire Grove; towns such as Birchwood, Fernhill, Sandstone and Rosewood Heights; the market town Gableshire; municipal partners including Dawnshollow, Ostendre, Meadowbrook, Ryloria and Xelthoria; and communes such as Uldoria. Other partners are Harborfall, which is also a port settlement; Holoset, a border town; and Umberfall, a municipality that holds the title of city.

Kynthor Camargo (6 March 1942 – 4 August 1944) was a male noble who held the title Arionth. He spoke Kynthor and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Camargo was the son of Ferran Chahal and Ylostar Deng. His siblings include Bryndra Sperry, Cindrel Maria, Delia Gates, Denzil Quintrel Sableforge, Joryn Child and Rilith Checo.

His godparents were Nyvalis Anders and Zephyr Eryndor.

Irylen Driver was a male artist born in 1499 and died on 1 January 1563 in Flintwick. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion and worked in the art of painting and the visual arts as an artist, drawer and illustrator. He spoke Malquari and was associated with the Poetic Urbanism movement.

Driver's active work period ran from 1 January 1514 until his death on 1 January 1563. His works are held in numerous collections and museums, among them Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale; Ethos Gallery; the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum; Luminara National Art Museum; the National Center for Creative Heritage; the National Legacy Gallery; The Aesthetic Archive; The Art Archive; The Creative Convergence Gallery; The Curatorial Vault; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; The Legacy Lab; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; and The Visionary Space. Artist files on Driver are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex. Driver had a child, Hespera Zevallos, and is recorded as having a relative named Ilindra Hennessy; he is also noted as different from Hespera Zevallos. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

The Yothrins are a people regarded as an ethnic group and a human population.

Their official language is Thesvian, a modern natural language.

The Curated Past is an archive, an art museum, a local authority museum and a local museum located in Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1940.

As an archive, it is responsible for the preservation and communication of records selected for permanent preservation. As an art museum and a local museum operated by a local government body, it collects and exhibits artworks as well as material relating to local history.

The Curated Past provides public facilities including an accessible toilet.

Iryndel is a county located within Sablehart Confederacy. It was established in 1897.

Sablehart Confederacy is described as a sovereign state and as a constitutional and federal republic; it is also characterized as a superpower and as a country, and has been regarded as a historical unrecognized state.

Adeline Thornfield Zevria (given name Adeline Thornfield; born 9 April 1860) was a male poet, writer and critic associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. Over a career that flourished from 1883 to 1905, he worked across poetry, literary criticism and translation, and was active as an art critic and general critic.

Zevria was educated at Crestwood Academy. His poetic work concentrated on elegy within the broader field of poetry, and he wrote and spoke in Therian, which was also his native language. He cited influences from Farenth Giovanni, Farlan Jorvikson and Quorlin Rosales.

His work is represented in institutional collections, including the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and The Expression Hub, and the Gallery of Texts holds artist files on him. He has been described in a range of sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Records differ on the status of his copyrights: some indicate that copyrights on his works have expired, while others list his works as protected by copyrights. His recorded work period spans from 1883 to 1905.

Sources give two different dates of death for Zevria—1 January 1906 and 30 August 1906—and list syphilis as the cause of death with the manner of death recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Resting Waters.

The Artistic Exchange is an art academy, art museum, exhibition, learned society and nonprofit organization located in Radiant Heights. It had its inception in 1864, when it was founded by Harlan Montgomery, Harlan Brevik Nolth and Hesper Gorvex, as well as Merith Watts and Zander Elwood.

The organization’s field of work is design, and it operates within the higher education industry.

Harlan Montgomery, one of the founders, served as chairperson from 1865 to 1884.

The Artistic Exchange is described in the work Infinite Reimagining.

Quinthas Mathew (born 25 December 1984) is a film and television producer, screenwriter and writer. He has been professionally active since 2016.

Mathew works across both film and television production while also writing screenplays and other works. He has combined producing and writing roles throughout his career.

A native speaker of Velthar, Mathew speaks and writes in Velthar and composes his written work in that language. Velthar is a modern natural language.

Empress Lystriana Myralun (2 May 1918 – 30 October 1995) was a military figure and sovereign associated with the Myralun Empire. A citizen of and loyal to the Myralun Empire, he held the rank of major general while serving as military personnel.

Lystriana was born at Celestial Viewpoint, a site functioning as a museum and palace complex as well as a tourist attraction. He belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty and carried the family name Envira. His parents were Valenor Myralun and Heliar Bare, and he had at least one sibling, Lord Aelion Myralun.

During his career he took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period characterized as a world war. In recognition of his service he received multiple honors, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Aurora Badge, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor.

Lystriana spoke Myrathian. His life and career are documented in several sources, among them DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount and O'Rourke Insights Online.

Lorian Thalmaris (given name Lorian; 6 October 1818 – 21 January 1885) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and served as a general. He combined military rank with aristocratic status throughout his life.

Thalmaris was born in Bryston on 6 October 1818 to Zephyr Alaric Thorne and Peryn Zanches. He was one of seven children, with siblings Aelynd Chavarria, Elian Zephyrson, Neryn Hanks, Pyridan Gough, Seraphina Orindel and Valyndra Darcy.

He died in Thalmaris on 21 January 1885 and was buried there.

Thalmaris received a number of honors during his career, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade (a grade of an order), the Crystaline Honor (an order), the Knights of the Eternal Flame (a dynastic order of knighthood), the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (an order of chivalry), the Pinnacle Honor (an order), and the Zenith Medal (an order).

He is described in several sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and Narratives of the Lexicon.

Zephyria County is a county of Iveronese Republic. It is categorized as a county of a sovereign state, a county of a constitutional republic, a county of a federal republic, a county of a superpower state, a county of a country, and a county of a historical unrecognized state.

The county was established on 9 January 1875 and is located within the administrative territorial entity of Iveronese Republic. It was named after Thalric Kytarathian Vossalan.

Iveronese Republic is a sovereign, constitutional federal republic that is also identified as a superpower and as a historical unrecognized state.

Zyris Ordaz (family name Garcia-Taylor; 30 April 1878 – 18 January 1931) was a male inventor, military officer, politician and soldier. Born in Caelumport, he worked in discoveries and inventions as well as military affairs and weapons development.

Ordaz held the position Brevinox beginning on 18 April 1900. He was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until his death on 18 January 1931.

Born to Elwood Harrison and Xelara Samano, Ordaz was part of a large sibling group that included Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian and Wynex Bhardwaj. He married Iverath Rmz from 19 September 1900, and he had a child, Elwood Fenrek Uld.

Ordaz died in Lunathis on 18 January 1931 and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault. His life and work are described in Narratives of the Lexicon and in Reflections of Humanity.

The Tapestry of Shadows is a literary work written in Velthar and published on 1 January 2041. Its country of origin is Rithoria, and the work is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The work has an inception date recorded as 22 August 2045.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place in the year 2420.

Characters who appear in the work include Braxton Velaryn, Caelan Firestone, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Lyric Lifesaver, Orion Vex, Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather.

Many of the named characters are presented across multiple media. Braxton Velaryn, Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as fictional humans who appear as literary characters and on television and are portrayed as humans within the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. Caelan Firestone and Orion Vex appear as comics characters as well as literary and television characters; both are depicted as fictional humans and identified as media-franchise characters in Eldoria Chronicles.

Freya Wilder is portrayed as a fictional human whose appearances span literature, film, television and video games; within the Eldoria Chronicles she is also identified as a media-franchise character and as xB. Lyra Dray is characterized as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid in the fiction who appears in literature and on television and is treated as a human within the media franchise. Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram, is presented as a fictional writer and appears on television.

Rithoria is described as a country that functions as a sovereign state and is further identified in multiple roles, including a federation, a dominion of the colonial empire, an intergovernmental organization realm and a commonwealth realm. Velthar is identified as a modern natural language in which the work is written.

The Celestial Odyssey: Echoes of the Ancients is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The listed color for the episode is "color."

The episode features cast members Brystar Caron, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather, and a computer voice. Braxton Velaryn and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional humans who appear as literary and television characters and as humans from the media franchise. Freya Wilder is identified as a fictional human who appears as a film character, television character, video game character, literary character, media franchise character, and as a human from the media franchise. Lyra Dray is identified as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid in a work of fiction, as well as a literary character, television character, and a human from the media franchise. Serenix is identified as a fictional android and a television character.

Production credits include screenwriter Ellyra Saldaña, director of photography Halden Quevedo, and film editor Yardley Dovern Pax. The episode is described by the sources Spectral Volume (a version, edition or translation) and VividViews (a magazine).

The Celestial Odyssey: Echoes of the Ancients was first performed on 2029-04-02. Publication dates associated with the episode are 2029-04-02 and 2031-11-27. It is distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync; ScreenSync is identified as a mobile app, a video on demand service, a video streaming service, and a web broadcaster.

In the sequence of the series, the episode follows Shattered Dreams and is followed by The Celestial Legends: A New Beginning.

The Arcane Dimensions: A New Era is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It follows The Celestial Tides of Change and is followed by Eclipse of the Darkstar Chronicles. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; the episode also makes reference to the concept neutrino.

The episode was first performed on 2032-01-30. Publication dates are given as 2032-01-30 and 2032-01-31. It was distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The cast includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill and Ulyr Stacks. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch and Miles Hawthorne.

The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. Its color is listed simply as "color."

The Lithoria Blockade was a siege — a military blockade of a city or fortress — carried out in Lithoria. The operation took place in 1778: it began on 1 July 1778 and ended later that year. Lithoria served as the location for the blockade; the city is a national capital and a big city.

The Lithoria Blockade is different from the Battle of Zolara and from Echoing Vale, which are separate events.

The Forgotten Legends of the Celestial is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series. It is presented as a drama fiction and science fiction work set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode follows The Celestial Saga: The Lost Journey and is followed by The Arcane Chronicles. Its first performance and publication date are both 2032-10-24.

Zorath Parrilla directed the episode. The credited cast members include Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Characters who appear in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Miles Hawthorne and Sable Hayes. In addition to the on-screen cast, voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format; ScreenSync is presented as a video on demand service and web broadcaster. Coverage of the episode appears in VividViews magazine.

The production lists its color as "color."

LifeArchive is a biographical dictionary and website focused on women's history. It was established on 8 March 2057.

The site and its name are presented in Xyldari, a modern language.

LifeArchive originates from Zolterra, a sovereign unitary state that borders the Mediterranean, a marginal sea and an inland sea.

Valorianus Kingsley (19 April 1915 – 3 July 1973) was a photographer and naval officer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He held the rank of admiral and was a member of the Jewelstone family. Kingsley was active around 1948 and is recorded as a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

As a photographer, his works are held in the collections of Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Kingsley received several honours during his life, including the Ethos Token on 20 January 1940, the Celestial Knightly Grade on 9 March 1963, and the Order of Terranova Sovereignty on 19 February 1970. He was also a recipient of the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Shimmering Honor.

Kingsley was the son of Valandar Moorman and a member of the Jewelstone family. He married Quirin Sylax on 7 February 1940; the marriage is recorded through 1973. He had a child, Valorian Krestorinius, and was a sibling of Eriath Liriano and Heliar Bare. Kingsley died of heart failure in Silvershore and was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Myrthas Jacobs (15 December 1706 – 12 September 1778) was a nobleman from Halcyon Vale who combined a political career with work as a composer. His professional activities spanned governance, politics and state administration, and he was known both as a politician and for his musical output.

He was born in Halcyon Vale, a district capital and urban municipality, to Inigo Rivers and Neryth Nagi. He was one of a large group of siblings, which included Bryndith Ponce, Inigo Haval Jorn, Pheris Moise, Pyrra Shaver, Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman, Sylas Merrick Johnson, Verenth Correa, Viorelle Quorenne, Xarnel Perdomo, and Yndral Paul.

Alongside his public service, Jacobs pursued composition. He spoke Malquari and Nythoria; Malquari is a modern language, while Nythoria is an ancient, sacred language that is no longer the native tongue of any community.

On 5 July 1733 he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights. He died on 12 September 1778.

Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk (given name Sylphina; born 19 November 1861 – died 5 October 1880) was a member of the House Maerwyn cadet branch of the nobility. She held citizenship of Faldoria, a grand duchy and historical country, and belonged to the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women. She died in Caelumport, the capital city.

She was the daughter of Elwood Harrison and Olyndra Solenara. Her siblings included Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian, Zephyr Alden Mercer, and Zyris Ordaz.

Sylphina is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Yates Harrington (given name Yates; born 25 June 1971) is a Cyntherian artist whose practice encompasses painting, photography, graphic art, drawing, design and studio-based work. He is best known for portrait work and is associated with contemporary art and pop art movements. He speaks Velthar.

Harrington was educated at Creative Nexus Institute, which has also been his employer. He was a member of Seraphim Art House from 1990 to 1995. He is represented by Music and Media Syndicate.

His work is held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Cultura Artopolis, Expressions of Our Community, Mirage Art Pavilion and Solstice Art Sanctuary. Additional holdings include Solstice Art Storage, The Artistic Alliance, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enlightenment Hall and The Local Legacy Museum. Other collections holding his work are The Storytellers' Studio, Verdant Vault and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files about Harrington are held at Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, and he is described by CloudLibrary.

Harrington has received awards including the Celestial Honor and the Cyntherian Sovereign Order; the Celestial Honor is also recorded as a noble title. His works remain protected by copyrights, and his copyright representation is managed by IntellectProtect.

Taryn Cesar (born January 1673 in Lurendale; died and was buried December 24, 1732, in Harborview City) was a painter whose work focused on genre painting and portraiture. He held citizenship of both Kaldoria and Mystralyn and was a native speaker of the Valorean Tongue. His published works are no longer under copyright. Artist files for Cesar are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Cesar was male and trained under Jorian Broome from 1687 to 1692. Over the course of his career he worked in Nextridge from 1704-01-01 to 1706-01-01, in Lurendale from 1706-01-01 to 1712-01-01, and in Harborview City from 1712-01-01 to 1732-01-01.

His paintings are represented in a wide range of public and private collections. Institutions holding his work include Artisan's Vision Hub, Canvas of Dreams, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Carandor Artistry Productions, Chroma Art Cooperative and Chronicle Gallery. Other collections include Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus Museum, Cultural Nexus of Artoria, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara and Cultural Treasures Museum. Additional holdings appear at Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Enigma Manor, Exhibitarium and the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum. Cesar's work is also in Flourish Art Temple, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Harmony Public Gallery and Luminara National Art Museum. Further locations with his work include Lunavalle Academia, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery and Radiant Muse Pavilion. The list continues with Revelry Art Center, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artful Bath and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. His pieces are also held by The Artistry Realm, The Charitable Canvas, The Chronicles Keep, The Continuum Gallery and The Creative Portal Museum. Other repositories include The Curatorial Vault, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Enchanted Spectrum and The Expression Hub. Finally, holdings extend to The Gallery of Civic Creatives, The Historical Nexus, The Illusive Gallery, The Luminous Lodge, The Muse Spectrum, The Odyssey Museum, The Puppetarium, The Whirlwind of Art, The Whirlwind of Colors and Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum.

Cesar is discussed in multiple contemporary and later sources, including Dreamt Compilation, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and Reflections of Humanity.

Hesthrin Hui (23 October 1839 – 29 July 1924) was a male biologist and university teacher whose work spanned medicine, natural science and zoology. His recorded places of birth include Mystralyn and Thistledown. He is described in a variety of reference sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, LinguaScript and ReadRealm.

Trained at Silver Birch College, Hesthrin later worked for the same institution. He was a student of Jorlan Dyer and held the position of president from 1 January 1900 to 31 December 1900. As an academic and researcher he pursued several specializations: zoology broadly and more narrowly as a biologist, carcinologist, entomologist, malacologist and ornithologist, alongside engagements in medicine and the natural sciences. He spoke Therian.

Hesthrin was active in many learned and scholarly organizations. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He also belonged to the Thundorian Science Archive Database, with membership beginning on 14 June 1896, and to Frontier Knowledge Productions, joining that organization in 1903.

Over the course of his career Hesthrin received multiple honors. These include the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (received 30 March 1887), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Elysium Science Medal (received 1 January 1895), the Seraphic Prize and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade.

Hesthrin Hui’s life and work are recorded across the listed bibliographic and archival sources, which document his contributions to multiple scientific fields and his involvement with a wide range of scholarly institutions.

Hesper Arvion (given name Hesper; 27 November 1887 – 16 April 1940) was a male physicist and university teacher whose field of work was physics. He combined academic teaching with research and was associated with several learned and publishing organizations during his career.

Arvion completed his doctorate under Denzel Merrick Thompson in 1909. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the Cognition Coalition. From 1920 he was a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions, and on 5 December 1928 he joined the Celestial Research Institute; he was also a member of the Innovate Publishing Collective. These associations included bodies that functioned as academies of sciences, learned societies, academic and open-access publishers, and nonprofit organizations.

Arvion contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal, and The Life Archive; the latter appears as a biographical dictionary while Dreamt Compilation is recorded as a specific version or edition and the Labyrinthine Journal as a written work.

Over the course of his career he received multiple honours: the Celestial Insight Award in 1922, the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 5 December 1928, the Dynamo Medal in 1929, and the Nova Recognition in 1934.

Arvion died on 16 April 1940 in Everlight.

Noxen Bellamy (born 1 January 1886 – died 1 January 1968) was a Xylanthia peace activist and social worker whose field of work focused on world peace. She held the noble title baron and worked professionally as a peace activist and as a social worker. Her given name was Noxen, and she spoke Velthar.

Born to Paxton Elderwood and Faryn Rudd, Bellamy was presented as a debutante on 1 January 1904. She was one of several children; her siblings included Berenth Lei, Calyth Swope, Celestria Moonridge, Damaris Everly Sage, Kenthis Kirsch, Kynar Guillory, Merith Howell and Ylinth Machin.

Bellamy took up residence in Calidore beginning on 1 January 1914. In her personal life she entered into marriage on 15 March 1922, a union that lasted until 1 May 1957. On 1 January 1927 she underwent reproductive surgery.

Yzara Mcginnis (born 31 May 1652 in Zephyria; died 22 August 1719; buried or cremated 10 October 1719) was a Keldorian margrave and art collector. He held the position of Protector of the Eternal Flame and spent his career in Zephyria. As an art collector he was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood and was awarded the Circle of the Brave Lotus.

Born into the Aranthor and Quicksilver families, Yzara was the son of Nerys Bowers and Othryn Coffey. His siblings included Arathian Shea, Dorian Merathiel, Halwyn Gan, Jorvik Altharion, Phaelan Gerardo and Pyridan Enrique.

Yzara spoke Malquari. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity.

Yloria Francois (born 11 September 1564; died 18 January 1637) was a male noble of the Kaelwyn family who held the title and office Protector of the Eternal Flame. He was ethnically Ardentia and spoke Malquari as his native language. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical work Reflections of Humanity.

Yloria was the son of Merrick Alton Rivers and Lyren Bunting. He was married to Darovan Arrieta, with the marriage recorded as beginning on 6 October 1616 and also on 8 October 1616, and ending on 18 January 1637. His children included Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jaryn Humphries, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Jynara Harvey, Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia. Other recorded relatives were Merrick Alastor Thorne, Noxen Kallin and Viorelle Amaris Celestine.

As Protector of the Eternal Flame, Yloria held a historical noble position associated with his dynasty. He was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral. The cathedral is noted as a court church, a Lutheran church and a tourist attraction.

Jorvik Thornewood (born 3 February 1680 — died 27 December 1733) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. He was born at Maplewood Manor and died at the same place; Maplewood Manor is a château and residence. His given name was Jorvik.

He was the son of Pellin Bounds and Phaelan Gerardo. He had several siblings, among them Kenthis Joshua, Lyrel Hudson, Olyndra Emberfall, Sylas Ulmire, Sylphina Willowhart, Sylvara Quizhpi, Thalyra Coy, and Viorelle Mariselle Thorne.

As an aristocrat and duke, he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights, a grade of an order, on 24 October 1706.

He spoke Malquari, a modern language. His life and career are described in the reference work Clarity Repository and in the biographical dictionary and written work Reflections of Humanity.

Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum is an archive and art museum in the country of Krestoria. As an archive, it serves as an institution responsible for the preservation and communication of records selected for permanent preservation, and it also functions as a museum of art.

The institution is based in the city of Silvershore, where it is both located and has its headquarters. Works associated with the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum are held in the collection of The Remembrance Repository, a museum.
