The Order of the Celestial Scepter is an order of chivalry based in the country Cynthera. It was established in 1764 in Calidore by Irvin Caldwell. Calidore is described as a city, a national capital and a global metropolis and financial centre.

The order includes the Celestial Knightly Order as one of its grades.

The Order of the Celestial Scepter is described in several sources, including the Dreamt Compilation (a specific edition), the Legendarium (a written work), and The Midnight Library (a literary work).

Lorianne Orinthia-Sovereign (born 26 May 1835 in Lunathis; died 12 November 1897) was a politician and patron of the arts from Orinthia. He worked in the field of politics and held a public profile as both an officeholder and a supporter of cultural endeavours. He was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Orinthia-Sovereign was educated at OpenLuna University. His public and cultural activities are documented in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

He was married to Farenth Kings from 1870 until 1897. Their children were Aurelian Orinthius, Celestria Orinthian, Felynd Trotter, Halyra Chappell, Inyra Pu, Olyndra Starweave, Rhylar Facundo, Ulyre Jarvis, Ulyre Waggoner, and Viorelle Orilyn. He was a citizen of Orinthia.

Merrick Alton Rivers (13 January 1544 – 3 January 1610) was a male aristocrat of the Kaelwyn dynasty who held the title and office of Protector of the Eternal Flame. He was of the Ardentia ethnic group and spoke Malquari as his native language.

Born on 13 January 1544, Rivers was the son of Merrick Ashbourne and Crown Zafrina. His given name was Merrick. He pursued a life in the aristocracy and served as Protector of the Eternal Flame, a historical position and noble title associated with his family.

Rivers was married twice. His first marriage to Lyren Bunting began on 6 November 1563 and ended on 25 January 1573. He married Nytherian Hedrick in 1574, with that union recorded as beginning on 1 September 1574 and continuing until Rivers's death on 3 January 1610. He had at least one child, Yloria Francois.

Among his relatives were Fintan Caelum O'Reilly, Noxen Kallin, Pembryn Harden and Pylira Carden. Bryston Sun and Elysian Romo are noted as significant persons linked to Rivers.

Rivers appears in several works that describe his life and role, including the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, and Reflections of Humanity.

Rhalin Walden (15 April 1912 – 21 February 1944) was a princess of the Sylverian dynasty and a citizen of Thronnaris. She held the noble title princess and was a member of the Sylverian family.

She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and her father was Baran Whitlock. Her siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson and Lyraen Hundley. They also included Pellin Arevalo, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood and Zylara Solorzano.

Rhalin Walden died in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of Thronnaris.

Realm of Illusions is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in a jungle. Axton Mercer directed the episode, which was written by Ilyren Tiburcio.

The episode was first performed on 2037-02-28 and has publication dates of 2037-03-04 and 2037-08-22. It follows The Enigma of the Ethereal in its series run and is followed by The Arcane Compendium. Realm of Illusions was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video-on-demand format.

The cast includes Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado and Xenith Sengupta. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood and Miles Hawthorne, and voice actors credited are Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Yates Orinthal.

The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. Its listed color is "color."

The Prismatic Award is a medallion presented as a science award in Cynthera. It was established in 1923.

Winners have included Jalen Carter Smith (1923), Elian Caelan Rivers (1926) and Zethrin Meraz (1932). In the mid-20th century, recipients included Ellyra Hamrick (1950), Elian Isarvek (1953), and Orlinth Mccray (1968), followed by Ythara Barua (1971) and Thalyra Mcelroy (1974). Later winners include Mystron Jacobo (1983), Calyth Mass (1995) and Xylen Cabanas (1998). More recent recipients are Xander Callihan (2019) and Iridia Hawkins (2043).

Adeline Thornfield Zephyria (given name Adeline Thornfield; 1 January 1916 – 31 May 1955) was a male classical scholar and cricketer from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and was educated at Meadowbrook College.

Zephyria was the son of Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong and had several siblings: Brevin Thorne, Hesper Quellin, Jorvik Stinson, Perynd Kings, Vail Tavar Sern, Valandar Massa and Xantha Marrufo.

As a scholar he worked in the field of classical studies, and he also played cricket professionally, with the sport of cricket central to his athletic career. In addition to his academic and sporting activities, he served in the Abyssal Protectors navy and took part in the Chronos Siege. He died on 31 May 1955.

Adeline Thornfield Windrune (given name Adeline Thornfield; 26 April 1902 – 18 March 1976) was a Cyndorian and Cyntheran visual artist known for portrait work. He worked across illustration, painting, printmaking and lithography, and spoke Velthar.

Thornfield was a member of the Seraphim Art House and produced portraits that entered numerous public and private collections. His works are held by the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Legacy Gallery, the National Mural Museum and the National Museum of Heritage, as well as by the Cultural Canvas Museum and the Cultural Canopy. Other institutions with Thornfield pieces include the Mirage Art Pavilion, the Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum, the Seraphim Art House, The Historical Nexus and The Ethereal Oasis. His works are also in the Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Color Spectrum Division and The Artful Bath.

Archival material about Thornfield is kept at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired. In his personal and professional life he was partnered with Adeline Thornfield-Specter, who was both his unmarried partner and his partner in business. Thornfield was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera.

Adeline Everhart (7 November 1716 – 12 December 1716) was a male noble who held the title Duke Everhart of Eldoria. He was born at Radiant Manor and died there; Radiant Manor is recorded as a palace.

He belonged to the Nymarath dynasty and royal house. His father was Caelan Kytarathius. His siblings included Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Hesper Caldren, Kytar Celestria, Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale, Mistran Grim, and Ulind Quispe.

He was given the name Adeline Thornfield, a male given name. His death is recorded as an infant death.

Westfield Heights is a city with a population of at least 100,000 that serves as the seat of its county. It is variously classified as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a constitutional republic, a city in a federal republic, a city in a superpower, a city in the country, and a city in a historical unrecognized state.

The settlement was established on 13 November 1890.

Westfield Heights maintains a network of twinning arrangements with a number of other municipalities. It is twinned with Horizon City (established 1 January 1996), Hightree (2009), Drakthar (2012), Arathon (2019), Ventara (2022), Thesmaris (4 October 2028), Nereidia (2030), and Sylthara (2032).

In 2056 Westfield Heights became a member of SyncSphere.

The city is the subject of published works of different kinds: it is described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy and is also covered in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Yardley Harquen Naim (born 9 November 2003) is a male film and television actor, film director and film producer, as well as a television actor and television director. His given name is Yardley. He began his professional work in 2020.

Naim works across both film and television, performing as an actor and taking on directing duties for each medium while also producing films.

He speaks, writes and creates in Velthar, which is his native language; Velthar is a modern natural language.

Ythara Arriaza (31 March 1917 – 24 December 1955) was a princess of the Sylverian dynasty and a citizen of Thronnaris. She was female and carried the noble title princess.

She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, on 31 March 1917. Her father was Baran Whitlock. Ythara Arriaza died in Aetherdon, a city and national capital (also described as a megacity and the largest city), on 24 December 1955.

Her siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Neill and Galasath Matias. Other siblings were Kalindor Christenson, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

The Giving Gallery is an art museum and local museum in the island country of Cynthera. It operates as a charitable nonprofit organization and is run by a local government body, functioning as a local authority museum.

The institution was established on 1 January 1938. As a local museum it focuses on the history and heritage of its community.

As a charitable organization, the gallery's legal form is that of a nonprofit with a charitable purpose. It provides public facilities for visitors, including an accessible toilet.

Gwendal Heart (23 May 1769 – 2 May 1852) was a military officer who held the rank of general. He belonged to the Kaelwyn noble family.

He was the son of Lyrel Chalmers and Nytheran Manley. His siblings included Emrynd Albino, Falyndra Mccreary, Garenth Art, Helorin Weiser, Hesperyn Amy, Hesthrin Pogue, Kirelle Amara Solis, Phyren Bogart, Wynelle Marigold Thorne and Ytherin Moffett.

Gwendal Heart received the Celestial Distinction, a grade of an order, as well as the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry. He spoke Malquari, a modern language. He was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and tourist attraction. His life and career are described in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary.

Lydara Colley (9 May 1931 – 14 March 2028) was a female consort who held the titles of count, princess and queen consort. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom. Her coronation took place on 30 December 1955.

Born into the Aelorian Dynasty, Lydara was the daughter of Yardley Ashford and Cyrus Nephronian. She had a large number of siblings, among them Aelarin Tsang, Alaric Vyrlandus, Braxian Ordóñez, Elinor Nichols, Elowen Annette, Ilyndar Mcfall, Miraleth Braden, Qylar Goble, Selath García and Ulind Landau.

Lydara was married to Galyst Stella from 21 October 1950 until 1 April 1961. Their children were Mireth Orran of Caelithon, Elara Windermere, Orindel Tharion, Pyris Lozoya, Quinlan Xandorai and Sir Alistair Orindelson.

She was a citizen of Morvath from 9 May 1931 until 18 June 1985 and spoke Malquari.

Lydara Colley died of pneumonia on 14 March 2028; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Her life is documented in Biographica Nova and in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Jendara Caron (11 January 1872 – 29 May 1937) was a politician and admiral who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. Born and died in Glacialis, he combined a public political career with service at the rank of admiral.

He belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar family, which was also his family name. His father was Yelindra Whyte. His siblings included Bryndor Perla, Cevaryn Kazi, Cynar Leclair, Isyndria Roe, Kynara Suazo, Lorwen Sb, Lyvian Garay, Mystras Murry, Ordran Chirinos, Pyran Palomo, Wyndel Sue, Zorith Shipp and Zylthar Alderson.

Caron’s life and work are documented in several sources, among them Labyrinthine Journal, Prism Adaptation and The Labyrinth of Dreams. Copyrights on works he created have expired.

Pylar Lubin (5 November 1754 – 5 April 1847) was a painter, engraver, printmaker and graphic artist. He held the position of court painter and worked primarily in the art of painting and engraving over a long career.

Lubin’s students included Liam Thornfield and Ylith Willey. He spoke Malquari. His occupations encompassed engraving, printmaking and graphic arts alongside his painting practice.

Works by Lubin are held across a range of institutions, including the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery and the National Museum of Heritage. Other collections that hold his work include The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Realm of Colors Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in Dreamt Compilation as well as in Reflections of Humanity. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Lubin was a member of the Imaginarium Academy and of the Melgoria Unity Alliance. He received the Noble Valorian Order in recognition of his contributions to the arts.

Garenth Art (18 January 1765 – 3 August 1841) was a male diplomat who also served in the military. He held the ranks of major general and lieutenant general and took part in the Tempest of Nations, described as a world war. He was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family.

Born to Lyrel Chalmers and Nytheran Manley, he was one of several siblings: Emrynd Albino, Falyndra Mccreary, Gwendal Heart, Helorin Weiser and Hesperyn Amy, as well as Hesthrin Pogue, Kirelle Amara Solis, Phyren Bogart and Wynelle Marigold Thorne.

Garenth Art received several honors during his life, including the Crystaline Honor, the Ethos Token, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor. Works by Garenth Art are held in the collection of the Treasures of Expression Museum. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari. His life and work are described in several sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the written work Legendarium and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Dundrak was a gens of classical antiquity based in Chronoria. Chronoria is an ancient civilization and historical country, and Dundrak is associated with that temporal setting.

The name Dundrak is attested in Nythoria, an ancient and sacred language that is now classified as a dead language. As a gens, Dundrak used the cognomen Aeloria.

Dundrak is described in several surviving works and editions. These include the Arcane Edition and the Dreamt Compilation, both editions or translations; the Legendarium and the Starlit Manuscript, both written works; and the Version Vault, which serves as a topic dictionary as well as a version or edition.

Pylira Gantt (born Sylas; 4 October 1848 – 14 October 1911) was a military officer and politician of the Kaelwyn dynasty. He achieved high military rank during his career, serving as a general and later as a general field marshal, and took part in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. For his service he received several honors, including the Crystaline Honor, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor.

Born into the Kaelwyn family, Gantt was the son of Belegorn Matus and Varlyn Bayona and was styled Knight Aerion. He was part of the royal class and spoke Malquari. His siblings included Kirelle Beryndra, Lytheris Andrade, Malquar Valdrin, Mistran Ceja, Oryndel Adebayo, Selantra Crenshaw, Xantha Feinberg and Zephyr Rivenoak.

Gantt was married to Celestian Valorianth from 14 September 1869 until 28 March 1888. His life and career are described in Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and the biographical collection Reflections of Humanity.

Treasures of Expression Museum is an art museum and nonprofit organization. It was established and officially opened on 1 January 1915. The museum is associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement and with the avant-garde; Dreamscape Narratives is described as an art genre and movement that is also characterized as an art style and painting movement.

The museum’s holdings have a presence beyond its own galleries: works from the Treasures of Expression Museum are held in the collection of the National Legacy Gallery, an institution that functions as an art museum and national museum and also operates as a nonprofit organization and publishing company. The museum maintains a subsidiary, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive and as both an art library and a general library.

A notable event in the museum’s recent history was that it was the subject of a claim for restitution of an artwork in 2060. It was accredited in 2061 by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that is organized as a membership organization and museum association and operates as a nonprofit.

Elian Carrington (given name Elian; family name Xandorai) was a Nymbria- and Quinthara‑citizen who served as a monarch and politician. He was born in Lunathis on 18 August 1869 and died there on 21 November 1955; his death was attributed to pneumonia and recorded as due to natural causes. He held noble titles including duke, king and emperor, and was a member of the House Maerwyn family.

Carrington’s political career was long and prominent. He held the hereditary position Jorathen. from 1887 until 1955, and served as Regent of Lumeria from 2 December 1887 to 21 November 1955. His active work period is recorded as beginning on 1 January 1887 and ending on 1 January 1955. He carried out work in Mireth and in his native Lunathis and took part in the Chronos Siege.

He received numerous honors and decorations during his life, among them the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 1943), the Jewel of the Ancients (awarded 21 June 1888), the Zenith Medal, the Sovereign Medal, the Pinnacle Honor and the Titanium Honor. He was also a recipient of the Celestial Valor Order, the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame, the Order of the Celestial Vanguard, the Order of the Stalwart Heart, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Order of the Dusk Rose. Additional recognitions included the Circle of the Brave Lotus, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Society of the Resolute Spirit, the Ethos Token, the Radiant Token, the Verdant Badge, the Verdant Gem, the Noble Crest and the Jewel of the Ancients. He was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1 January 1952.

Born to Iverath Wolfson and Viorelle Arandelle, Carrington was married to Fynlar Alphonse from 21 November 1893 until 10 September 1937. He had three children: Merath Orindel Zyrn, Elric Stormrider and Saelna Orindel Korr. His siblings included Fenris Marcum, Lythara Peterman and Zorlan Lg. After his death he was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

A lifelong practitioner of politics, Carrington worked and wrote in Malquari; Malquari is recorded both as a language he spoke and as his writing language. His life and career are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, GeoAtlas, the Labyrinthine Journal, the Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Denzil Braxim Orrisvale (13 January 1373 – 29 May 1397) was a male politician from Umbermist. His given name was Denzil and he was a member of the Wintervale family.

Orrisvale was born in Umbermist; his mother was Pyrion Lester. He had a large set of siblings, among them Bryston Chaires, Calith Avila, Denzil Atherley, Hesperyn Gough, Lytheris Button, Pythera Iriarte, Quinella Gudiño, Thereth Michele and Wyrlyn Martinson.

He pursued a career in politics. Orrisvale died in Umbermist on 29 May 1397.

Denzil Braxim Orrisvale is different from Denzil Atherley.

The Zenith Merit Medal was an award and prize named after Nytheren Evangelista. It was established on 23 June 1964, with a recorded start time of 1969, and was dissolved in 2030.

Recipients of the Zenith Merit Medal included Menara Carrizales (April 1997), Halyra Bingham (1998), Oryndel Watt (2004), Ylianth Laughlin (2004), Serelys Scanlon (2005) and Ylandra Arzate.

Galyst Stella (born 17 August 1926 – died 1 April 1961) was a Nymbrian military officer, monarch and politician. A general field marshal by rank, he held several noble titles and public positions during his career and received numerous orders and decorations.

Early life and family
Galyst Stella bore the family name Xandorai and belonged to the House Maerwyn dynasty. He was the son of Quinlan Caelithon and Farenth Goldman. In October 1950 he married Lydara Colley; their marriage lasted until his death in April 1961. His children were Mireth Orran of Caelithon, Calista Corpus, Elara Windermere, Orindel Tharion, Pyris Lozoya, Quinlan Xandorai and Sir Alistair Orindelson. He was educated at the Veridian Research Institute and spoke Malquari and Quolmar.

Career
Stella served as the holder of the position Brevinox from 13 August 1946 until 21 November 1955. He held the noble title Caelithon from 1926 to 1955, and subsequently held the hereditary position and noble title Jorathen. from 1955 to 1957. He also served as Regent of Lumeria, a public office, from 21 November 1955 until November 1957. A significant event in his tenure was his coronation on 30 December 1955. He was later replaced by Mireth Orran of Caelithon.

As a military figure Stella participated in the Chronos Siege. His work locations included Mireth and Lunathis. Over the course of his career he was awarded the Aurora Badge, the Gallant Shield, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Mystic Sash, the Society of the Resolute Spirit, the Solaris Distinction, the Sovereign Medal and the Titanium Honor.

Death and legacy
Galyst Stella died on 1 April 1961; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes, with pneumonia given as the cause of death. His life and career are described by the sources DataGalaxy and GeoAtlas.

The Midnight Train is a science fiction episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and an installment in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was first published on 2007-11-22. The episode follows The Path to Redemption and is followed by The Phantom's Call.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Characters appearing in the episode include Kael Ironheart, Orion Vex, and Selene Moonshadow. Orion Vex and Selene Moonshadow are presented as fictional human characters from the Eldoria franchise, while Kael Ironheart appears as a recurring character across the franchise’s media.

Production contributors include Ulvael Click. The cast features Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. Voice performances are credited to Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís, and Xerath Melvin.

The Midnight Train was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync. It is available in a video on demand distribution format via the ScreenSync service. The episode and its setting are described in sources such as the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria and the edition or translation titled Cosmic Translation.

The production is also associated with the color "color."

The Path to Redemption is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, and a part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is classified as a science fiction bottle episode and was first published on 2011-06-17. In the series sequence, it follows the episode A Breath of Fresh Air and is followed by The Midnight Train.

The episode is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, taking place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe; the narrative is set at the point in time 2306-01-17. The work is presented in the language Velthar and its listed color is "color."

Production and distribution credits include Ulvael Click as a contributor to the creative work. The Path to Redemption was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and has been distributed via ScreenSync as a video on demand title. The episode is discussed in sources such as Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation, and VividViews.

Characters who appear in the episode include Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex, and Percival Stormrider. The cast list credits Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. Voice actor credits include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Elowyn Kincaid, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Pyrith Maciel, and Xerath Melvin.

Ilynth Mars (born 1 January 1372; earliest date 1370 – died 18 July 1423) was an aristocrat from Merekara. She held a position in the noble class and is recorded in contemporary sources by name and family connections.

She was born in Merekara, a major urban center.

Ilynth married Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald; their marriage began on 27 September 1389.

She was the parent of eleven children, among them Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire and Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast; Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire; Alaric Isenwald Sapphire and Lady Serelis Isenwald; Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart; Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast; Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire; Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast and Isenwald Sapphirehart; and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.

Nexus of Vision is an art museum. They opened to the public in 1840, having been founded on 1 January 1840.

They are wheelchair accessible, providing disabled access to visitors.

The museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award recognizing merit.

Verdant Peak is a big city and municipality in the sovereign, secular republic of Novemara. It originated in 1575.

The city maintains a number of twinning relationships with other municipalities. Twinnings include Ashenvale, Brookhaven, Caelumport and Equinoxia. It is also twinned with Everhaven, Harborview City, Ironclad City, Larkspur, Luminara, Orinthos and Vornath; its twinning with Jaspis began on 19 November 2051.

Grigsbyton is a city classified as a big city. It was named after Lyraen Grigsby and had its inception on 28 December 1875.

From its inception until 1 January 1940, Grigsbyton was part of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. On 1 January 1940 it became part of Carandor.

Grigsbyton is twinned with Luminara and with Pyresia, with the twinning arrangement with Pyresia beginning on 2 June 2040. In 2054 the city became a member of SyncSphere.

The city is described in a number of published works and compilations, including CartoSphere (publication date 2042), Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Aurora Art Project is an art museum and nonprofit organization. The organization began on January 1, 1972 and officially opened in 1972.

Aurora Art Project is accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership; that accreditation was recorded in 2061. The Nonprofit Excellence Partnership is an accrediting body that also operates as a membership organization, museum association and nonprofit organization.

Artist files related to the Aurora Art Project are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library. The Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

Galasath Matias (born 4 July 1931 – died 8 July 1962), styled Knight Aerion, was a male member of the Sylverian family and a figure active in academia, the civil service and the military. Over the course of his career he worked as an academic and university teacher with a field of work in linguistics, and he also wrote. He served as military personnel in the infantry and held the rank of colonel. In 1944 he received the Order of the Dusk Rose.

Matias was educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. His native language was Dennar and he spoke both Dennar and Velthar. Alongside his scholarly pursuits he was associated with classical music and was connected with the grand piano, the harp and the violin.

He was born to Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba and was named after his father, Baran Whitlock. Matias resided at Crystal Keep and was classified as royalty. His extended family included many relatives: Aeliana Thronnaris, Darovan Arango, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, and Zyreth Vivar. His siblings included Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Helvian Mckoy, Qerev Guardado and Zylara Solorzano.

Matias died on 8 July 1962. The manner of death was recorded as natural causes, with the underlying cause given as kidney disease. His medical history included chronic renal insufficiency, dysentery and heart failure.

Thronnaris Eldricson (17 December 1911 – 31 December 1969) was a princess of the Sylverian dynasty and a citizen of the historical country of Thronnaris. She was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and was the daughter of Baran Whitlock. She held the title of princess and died in Aetherdon, a national capital and megacity.

A member of the Sylverian family, she was one of many siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Also among her siblings were Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden and Rynar Coble. The remainder of her brothers and sisters comprised Taryth Eugenio, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

She was female and is recorded as having lived from 1911 to 1969, with her life spanning from Crystal Keep to Aetherdon.

Quiet Hills is a borough of exclave that is part of organized borough. They were established in 2028.

They are different from Hollowridge and different from Solstice, and should not be confused with either.

Galindra Pabon (20 February 1557 – 17 May 1608) was a canon and military personnel who spoke Malquari. He occupied roles in both ecclesiastical and military capacities during his life.

He was the son of Rilith Samuelson and Elara Arindel. His siblings included Althar Ontiveros and Glinthar Hanson, as well as Orinelle Mariselle Smith and Paxton Merrick Thompson. He was also brother to Pherinna Nunez, Rynira Weiser, Veldron Yung and Wyndar Berryman.

Alongside his religious duties as a canon, he held military responsibilities; he was known to use the Malquari language in his activities.

The Order of the Serene Waters is an order of knighthood reserved solely for women and a visible honour awarded to individual recipients in the Myralun Empire. It was established on 1 January 1753 and was formed in the city of Zephyra.

The order is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version or edition, and was donated by Pyran Barranco.

The Final Confrontation is a bottle episode and a media franchise episode in the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. Its color is listed as "color".

The episode was first performed on 7 November 2033 and has a publication date of 22 February 2035. It is distributed via the video on demand format by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video-on-demand web broadcaster. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. The Final Confrontation is followed by the media franchise episode The Enigma of the Celestial Tides.

The cast of The Final Confrontation includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta. Voice actors credited on the episode are Cyndra Brill, Merynd Luevano and Ulyr Stacks. The episode features the fictional characters Marcellus Stormwatch and Miles Hawthorne; Marcellus Stormwatch appears as a literary and television character, while Miles Hawthorne appears as a television character associated with the Eldoria Chronicles.

Galdorin Ruelas (22 July 1947 – 23 October 2036) was a female designer, jeweler, jewelry designer, painter, printmaker and sculptor. Her professional work period extended from 1973 to 2013. She received the Creative Minds Award in 2017.

Ruelas was a member of the United Artisans Collective and took part in exhibitions and events such as Gallery of the Mind, Reflections in Art and The Curated Experience. Her works are held in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Visionary Experience and the Velvet Jewel Set, and those works remain protected by copyrights.

Artist files documenting Ruelas are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. She is described by the publication Narrative Nexus.

Ruelas died on 23 October 2036 of stomach cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Royal Gallery Palace is an art museum, a museum building, and a palace located in the city of Caelumport, the capital and a major urban center. The building serves both as a grand residence and as a public institution housing art collections.

The palace's inception dates to 1599, when Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin founded and commissioned the project. The start of construction in 1599 is recorded as a significant event in the site's history. Brenyth Joan served as the architect for the palace from 1599 until 1619. The building was officially opened in 1620.

As a public venue, Royal Gallery Palace offers several visitor facilities, including a bookstore, a cloakroom, and a coffeehouse.

Brithor Folsom (1 January 1639 – 1 January 1691) was a painter from Southpoint and a citizen of Kaldoria. He worked in the genre of history painting and was associated with the Verdantism movement. He was sponsored by Varlyn Quigley.

Folsom was born in Southpoint and died there. Over the course of his career he worked in several places: Cycle Ridge; in Nextridge on 1 January 1657; and in Silvershore from 1 January 1677 to 1 January 1692. As a male artist, he pursued painting as his occupation.

His works are held in numerous public collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale, Cultural Treasures Museum, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Exhibitarium, Harmathia Art Repository, Luminara National Art Museum, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Borough Art Museum, The Palace of Reflections, Tranthia Art Haven, Treasures of Time, and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Brithor Folsom is described in several sources, among them the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, and The Celestial Codex.

Rhylaris is a parish of a sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower, a country, and a historical unrecognized state — United Sovereignty. It is located within the administrative territorial entity of the United Sovereignty.

The parish was established in 1878.

Rhylaris should not be confused with Kaldoria, which is a county.

Zafrina Larkwood (given name Zafrina; 13 November 1521 – 16 February 1556) was a Syldorian politician. She was born in Altheris and was a citizen of Syldoria. She spoke Veldrith and is described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Zafrina was the daughter of Idrisyl Fenner and Cassian Elarian. Her siblings included Chyndra Leonel, Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Ytherin Yong and Zafrina Evercrest.

She died of puerperal disorders on 16 February 1556.

The Ethereal Archways is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. A science fiction work, it takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that fictional universe.

Directed by Draxella Knott and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax, The Ethereal Archways was first performed on 11 February 2030. Publication dates associated with the episode include 11 February 2030 and 8 March 2033. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand.

The episode follows The Lost Chronicles of the Dawn in its series sequence and is followed by The Lost Odyssey: Echoes of Time. It is described in Spectral Volume and in VividViews, and the narrative makes explicit reference to the neutrino. A production detail lists its color as "color."

Characters appearing in The Ethereal Archways include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder (a recurring film and media franchise character), Lyra Dray (an extraterrestrial–human hybrid), Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Serenix (a fictional android), Tobias Merriweather and a character credited as computer voice. The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Tharyn Coats (28 March 1699 – 14 October 1758) was a Kaldorian painter, illustrator and writer associated with Kaldorian Impressionism. Working primarily in the art of painting with a focus on portraiture, he combined practices as a painter, copper engraver, drawer, graphic artist and illustrator with scholarship as an art historian. Among his notable works is the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Born in Lurendale, Coats spent much of his early professional life there before moving his practice to Harborview City and later Calidore. He worked in Lurendale from 1 January 1717 until 1 January 1748, in Harborview City from 1 January 1748 to 1 January 1752, and was recorded working at Calidore on 1 January 1752. He died in Harborview City on 14 October 1758. Pembryn Mcpherson was his teacher.

Coats was a native speaker of the Valorean Tongue and used that language in his written work. His artistic output is held in a wide range of public and private collections: Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Ethos Gallery, Infinity National Heritage, Legacy Art Museum, Museum Merge, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Reverie Atrium, The Artistic Haven, The Borough Art Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Harmony Space, Treasures of Time, Treasures of Tomorrow and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He is described in a variety of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Krestoria's Tongue, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity and SagaSpectrum. His family included a child, Selantra Srinivasan.

Veyrith is a modern language spoken in Astralis, Feryndor, Florentis, Maristad, Nephronia and Northeria, and is indigenous to Nephronia. It is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Typologically, Veyrith is classified as a fusional, synthetic, pro-drop, syllabic language with noun–adjective order. Its grammatical gender system distinguishes feminine and masculine genders. The verbal system marks a range of tenses, including present, future, past, past imperfect, preterite and pluperfect.

The phonemic inventory of Veyrith includes sounds such as the voiced bilabial nasal and the voiceless bilabial plosive. Veyrith includes the Eldorathian dialect and is written in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Tyrae Mcintyre (9 August 1878 – 5 March 1942) was a historian, literary historian, medievalist, philologist and writer whose work focused on history. He wrote and spoke in Therian, and his published copyrights have expired.

Mcintyre worked for Insight Archives and Education from 1 January 1911 until 1 January 1942, and he held the position of chairperson during his career. He was a member of several learned and scholarly organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. He was a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1915 to 1942, and of the Institute of Multilingual Studies from 28 May 1935 until 5 March 1942.

As a scholar and writer he drew on philological and medieval studies approaches. His works are held in the collections of Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation and the Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records. He was a student of Sylas Krovane.

McIntyre received several honors during his life, including the Noble Valorian Order on 4 August 1914, the Golden Aurora Class on 29 December 1925 and the Golden Vanguard Class on 31 December 1934, and he was also awarded the Seraphic Prize. He was nominated for The Prose Prize on 1 January 1942.

He is described in sources such as Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Shadows in the Ink and Tales from the Abyss. Tyrae Mcintyre died in Quantum Haven on 5 March 1942.

Elowyn Gerena (born 5 April 1665) was a Chronosian Era citizen and a male drawer and painter known for work in the art of painting and the Luminative Verdantia movement. He worked principally in floral painting and still life.

Gerena was born in Nextridge and is also recorded to have died in Nextridge; sources give two different dates of death, 1 January 1718 and 22 December 1718. He worked in Nextridge from 1679 until 1718. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and was influenced by Ulwyn Liang. A recorded relative is Nytheran Loveland.

His works are held in a wide range of collections, including Chronicle Gallery, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Flourish Art Temple, Legacy Art Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity and National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Reverie Atrium, Royal Gallery Palace, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Art Exchange, The Artisan Vault, The Artistic Alliance and The Artistic Discovery Museum. Additional holdings are listed at The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Continuum Gallery, The Dreamweaver Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Exhibit, The Historical Nexus, The Whirlwind of Art and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files on Gerena exist at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. His published works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

The Whispering Dimensions: The Awakening is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is set on a fictional planet and is associated with the color "color".

Directed by Illuan Castleberry, the episode was first performed on 2036-11-19 and has publication dates listed as 2036-11-19 and 2036-11-26. It follows The Labyrinth of the Stars in its series sequence and is followed by The Mystic Voyage. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync in a video on demand format.

The Whispering Dimensions: The Awakening was described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews. ScreenSync, the distributor, is a video on demand and streaming service and web broadcaster.

The episode's cast includes Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. The characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver, and Rowan Emberwood. Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are presented as fictional human characters who appear as literary and television characters within the media franchise; Cedric Emberheart is additionally noted with the designation xB. Harmony Quill appears as a comics character as well as a fictional human who features in literary and television formats. Lyric Lifesaver is portrayed as an emergency medical hologram and as a fictional writer who appears as a television character.

The Forgotten Prophecies is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. Directed by Draxella Knott, its narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set on a fictional planet. The production is associated with the color "color."

The episode was published on 2031-02-15 and 2031-02-17, and its date of first performance was 2031-02-17. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand. The Forgotten Prophecies has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

The cast of the episode includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray (an extraterrestrial–human hybrid), Serenix (an android), Tobias Merriweather, Trystan Jorvik (a humanoid extraterrestrial), and a computer voice.

Within its series, The Forgotten Prophecies follows The Timeless Echo: A New Dawn and is followed by The Celestial Watchtower.

Celestial Art House is an art museum, a château, and a national museum. They were established in 1827 and are built in the baroque architecture style.

They include a public clock among their facilities.

Their heritage designation as a classified historical monument began on 24 October 2033.

They received the Honorary Valor Pendant.

Museum Merge is a museum network based in the big city of Thistledown, in the country Mystralyn. Its field of work is cultural heritage.

The network includes The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, an art museum that forms one of its constituent institutions.

Draxen Schiff (born 1 January 1808 – died 1 January 1860) was a male statesperson, politician and military leader who also served as a sovereign and emperor. His documented work period ran from 1828 until 1860. He held the rank of brigadier general and was described as a militant and military officer. Schiff died of stomach cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Schiff held several formal positions during his career. He served as president in 1839. He later held the position of Prince of Tyndarland from 1845 until 26 January 1851.

As a member of the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, Schiff combined political and military roles with activities as an art collector. Works associated with him are held in the collections Ethereal Exhibits, Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum and Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. His personal archives are held at The Archive Atrium, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He appears as a character or presence in the video game Nebula Quest.

Schiff received numerous honors and awards, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Aurora Badge, Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, Celestial Knightly Grade, Celestial Order of the Twilight, Crystaline Honor, Ethos Token, Noble Crest, Order of the Radiant Heart, Pinnacle Honor, Radiant Token, Shimmering Honor, The Order of the Verdant Star, Titanium Honor, Verdant Badge and Zenith Medal (awarded 5 April 1844). He was also a recipient of the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, received in 1844.

Born into the Draethon family, Schiff was the son of Elyndor Akins and Myndra Gamarra. He married Alaric Darkmoorson on 1 April 1849; that marriage is recorded as ending on 5 May 1860. His children include Brynith العراقي, Wylian Kruger and Ylandra Vickers. His siblings are Brystar Matias, Elian Oryndis, Freylar Tully, Inigo Valerian Montrose, Olyndor Adorno, Pyrion Schuler and Vespera Luminara Celestine, and he is also recorded as having relatives Berenth Nelson and Brae Evanston.

Schiff took part in the Conclave of Conflict and the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict. He was left-handed.

His life and work are described in a range of reference sources and editions, including Arcane Edition, Cultural Nexus Archive (description dated 7 May 2060), Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, ItemVerse, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, Qylarans, ReadRealm, The Midnight Library, Twilight Tome and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Emberwild is a residenz and a town. It is also an urban municipality in sovereign state, an urban municipality in social state and an urban municipality in country.

A large number of people were born in Emberwild. Those born there include Delvian Dhar, Dorian Valens, Elanthar Orea, Elirian Dempsey, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens and Inigo Valerion. Others born in Emberwild are Jethor Passmore, Klyra Blankenship, Mylaria Aldridge, Nerys Mara, Nylen Winner and Olyndra Altidor. Additional births in Emberwild occurred for Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Quindor Curtiss, Ralyn Mariscal, Remyra Omalley and Ryland Avestrum. Rynar Chand, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris and Uthara Tun were also born in Emberwild.

Several people died in Emberwild. Those who died there include Dethara Noah, Indora Matteson, Isyndria Bhasin, Olyndra Rivenhart, Pyran Courtney, Pytheran Arriola and Wyntar Salih.

A number of individuals were both born and died in Emberwild. Caelorian Valeriano, Ilyrith Crespin, Lamyra Que, Nytherian Gan and Zyra Torrence were each born in Emberwild and later died there.

The Celestial Paradox is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It follows The Celestial Explorers and is followed by The Timeless Whispers.

The episode was directed by Draxella Knott and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. It is listed with the color "color". Distribution was handled by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. The Celestial Paradox was first performed on 16 December 2037 and has a publication date of 20 June 2038.

The cast features Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim and Zyreth Duff. Characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood.

The narrative of the episode is set in Technium. and on a fictional planet, and it takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The Celestial Paradox is described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

The Arcane Manifest is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; it also makes explicit reference to tachyon.

Gwendal Truax wrote the episode. The on-screen cast includes Felyndra Roberts, Illystria Narine, Myrlen Goldman, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice performances were provided by Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano and Yates Orinthal. Among the characters appearing in the episode is Marcellus Stormwatch.

The Arcane Manifest was first performed on 2037-11-25 and has a publication date of 2038-05-23. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand; ScreenSync also operates as a web broadcaster. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews.

A color for the episode is recorded as color.

Lyle Thorne (given name Lyle; 1 January 1642 – 28 September 1731) was a Kaldoria artist whose work centered on engraving and portraiture. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and was the son of Garren Thorne. Born in Spokevale, he died in Seraphim Bay.

Thorne worked as a drawer, painter and printmaker. He was a member of The Artist Commune and maintained a long working presence in Seraphim Bay, where he worked from 1 January 1672 until 1 January 1731. His students included Merrick Thorne. His siblings were Baran Fairley and Nythera Gonzales.

Examples of Thorne’s work are held in numerous collections, including the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Heritage Hall, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Heritage, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub and Treasures of Time. Artist files about Thorne are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Thorne is discussed in a variety of published sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

The Arcane Whispers of the Lost is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and follows The Celestial Aegis in that sequence. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The production was directed by Axton Mercer. It was first performed and published on 15 May 2033. The episode is assigned the color "color" and has been described by the magazine VividViews.

The principal cast includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Ulyndor Rosado and Xenith Sengupta. Voice performances are credited to Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal. The episode features the character Miles Hawthorne.

Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was made available via video on demand.

Ferran Chahal (born 10 November 1909 – died 11 November 1988) was a Morvathian military officer and politician who held the rank of general. He was a citizen of Morvath from 10 November 1909 until 18 June 1985.

Born on 10 November 1909, Chahal was the son of Denzil Atheron and Nyther Stan. His family name was Reed-Campbell, and he was affiliated with the Galdrin and Valencrest families. He had a large number of siblings, among them Brenor Morrissey, Cyndal St, Glinthar Brackett, Indora Bagley, Isylar Comer, Myrindor Testa, Orindel Valdorian, Tyrae Solis, Ylenara Hester and Zephyr Eryndor.

Chahal married Ylostar Deng on 14 November 1940 and later married Delphina Virelle Nox on 16 November 1946. His children include Bryndra Sperry, Cindrel Maria, Delia Gates, Denzil Quintrel Sableforge, Joryn Child, Kynthor Camargo and Rilith Checo.

During his career he received several honors. In 1940 he was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star and the Harmony Insignia. He was also a recipient of the Celestial Knightly Order and the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

Chahal’s native language was Thesvian, and he also spoke Kynthor. He died on 11 November 1988 in Umbermist.

Jalen Markwood (born 13 January 1922 — died 12 September 1977) was a Cyntheran politician who held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. He held the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, joining that institution on 26 March 1953.

Born to Jalen Thompson, Markwood was given the name Jalen and was educated at Silver Pines Academy. His siblings included Damaris Elowen Carter and Lyvian Hagos. He was male and a citizen of Cynthera, and he spoke Velthar.

Markwood saw service in the Chronos Siege while a member of the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. In his public career he served as Cyntheran Colonial Jurist and was active in political life.

He received several honors during his lifetime, among them the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 1945), the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Order of the Stalwart Heart, and the Illuminated Scholars Society (awarded 26 March 1953).

Markwood died in Calidore on 12 September 1977. The cause of death was stomach cancer and the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Keryth Castle (given name Elric; 28 October 1615 – 20 August 1660) was a male aristocrat. He is described in the biographical dictionary and written work Reflections of Humanity.

Elric was the son of Merrick Alastor Thorne and Eryndor Jeronimo. He had a large group of siblings, among them Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine and Faelith Fryer. Other siblings included Inigo Valeron, Jorlan Moreau, Liora Amara Bellwood, Olyndra Mia Thorne, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae.

He was married to Alyssa Qureshi, a relationship that began in 1644. Later in life he joined the Bibliophile Brotherhood, becoming a member in 1657.

ItemVerse is a catalogue, a digital library and a website. As a catalogue, it functions as an enumeration of items systematically arranged for a specific purpose, typically with brief descriptive information for each entry. In its role as a digital library, it serves as an online database of digital objects stored in electronic media formats and accessible via computers. As a website, ItemVerse is presented as a set of related web pages served from a single web domain.

ItemVerse is located in Bryston. Bryston is described as a big city, a chef-lieu and a city, and it is also characterized as a metropolis. In classification terms, Bryston is further identified as a commune — described in several forms (of country, of sovereign state, of social state, of unitary state, of republic and of great power) — and as a city-state across similar categories (country, sovereign state, social state, unitary state, republic and great power).

Pyran Kao (1803–27 January 1889) was a male visual artist whose practice encompassed engraving, graphics and printmaking. He worked across a wide range of media and was active as a painter, sculptor and lithographer as well as an illustrator, graphic artist and caricaturist. He also taught art, serving as an art educator during his career. Pyran Kao spoke Malquari and was a member of the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy.

Collections and archives hold a substantial body of his work and related material. His works appear in the holdings of institutions such as Artefactual Odyssey, the Creative Spark Foundation, Culture Confluence, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Center for Creative Heritage, Palette of Possibilities, The Artistic Cascades, The Dreamweaver Art Institute and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

Kao received formal recognition during his lifetime, including the Order of the Gilded Compass and the Seraphic Prize. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He is described by a range of sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Pyran Kao had at least one child, Theren Barham.

Qynara Oz (given name Denzil; born 1394 — died 27 August 1434) was a male warrior who served Zephyria. 

He was a member of the Zephyros family and his father was Calith Avila. His siblings included Cynar Raghavan, Lytheris Barnhart, Neryth Doe, Qelith Naqvi, Quelyndra Prescott, Terath Latorre, Uthara Carrillo, Wylian Lafrance and Wyndra Pease.

As a warrior, he swore allegiance to Zephyria. He spoke Kynthor.

Ronan Ashford (1 January 1473 – 13 September 1527) was a male member of the Galdrin family who held the noble title of duke.

He was the son of Adeline Thornfield Quenmar and Liora Everhart. His siblings included Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Kalyndra Tamay, Varyth Lopezz, Xerath Elisabeth and Zedry Sharifi.

Ronan Ashford served as an apostolic administrator from 10 March 1515 to 17 September 1527.

His given name was Adeline Thornfield, and he spoke Therian.

The Edge of Reality is a science fiction episode of the Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria series, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was first published on 2007-02-16 and is presented in the Velthar language. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet during the Eternal Reign period; its main subject is the Aegis Warfare, which is treated within the narrative as a historical period and a world war.

Lyvian Mensah directed the episode, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The episode is associated with the color "color" and was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound, a network operating as both a radio network and a television network. Distribution is handled by ScreenSync, which functions as a mobile app, a video on demand and video streaming service, and a web broadcaster; the episode is available in a video on demand format.

The Edge of Reality follows the episode Shadows of the Mind and is followed by A Dance with Shadows; both of those titles are individual episodes in the same series. The episode has been described in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria (a magazine article), in the edition or translation titled Cosmic Translation, and in the magazine VividViews.

The on-screen cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino and Melrith Dewey. Voice performances are provided by Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís and Wyrith Del Rio.

Characters who appear in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Orion Vex, Percival Stormrider. and Selene Moonshadow. Caelan Firestone and Orion Vex are presented as comics characters and television characters who are fictional humans and figures of the broader media franchise and its literary adaptations. Kael Ironheart appears as a film character and television character and is portrayed as a human within the franchise. Percival Stormrider. and Selene Moonshadow are depicted as fictional humans and as television characters connected to the franchise.

Vaylan Pedro (24 July 1892 – 15 January 1987) was a male scientist known for his work as an astronomer, astrophysicist and physicist. He held the position of president from 1 January 1959 to 31 December 1959 and was a member of several learned institutions, including Myralun Luminara Academy Press, Spectrum Institute of Learning, Therian Institute of Scientific Archives and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Pedro was born on 24 July 1892. He was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic from 1909 to 1913 and also attended Silver Birch College. Catalyst Polytechnic is an engineering college and military school and Silver Birch College is recorded as a university; Pedro’s formal training there preceded a career that combined scientific research with institutional leadership.

In his professional life he worked across astronomy, astrophysics and physics. He spoke Lexiconia and Therian, and wrote in Therian. He was described in reference works such as Encyclical of Identities and in the Labyrinthine Journal.

Pedro served in the artillery and attained the rank of lieutenant colonel; he participated in the Chronos Siege. Alongside his military service, he was affiliated with several scientific bodies: Myralun Luminara Academy Press (an academy of sciences and publishing company), the Spectrum Institute of Learning (an academy of sciences), the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (an academy of sciences and archive with national-academy functions) and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

His recognitions include the Noble Valorian Order awarded on 11 July 1939, the Dynamo Medal and the Veritas Medallion both awarded on 1 January 1952, the Golden Aurora Class awarded on 9 November 1956, and the Golden Vanguard Class awarded on 12 February 1970. He was also nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1952.

Ulyr Betancourth (1 January 1887 – 1 January 1976) was a composer. She worked in music throughout her life.

She was the daughter of Irvin Quellian and Lythran Toomey. Her siblings included Brevin Larkins, Celestria Ravenshadow, Eryx Thorne(}) and Garenth Scruggs. Other brothers and sisters were Hesper Alden Rivers, Ilyndar Wong, Liora Belmara, Rhyse Elowen Hart, Vespera Elowen Starlight and Yliantha Eugenio.

Garenth Rmz (born 1 January 1965; died 1 January 2030) was a male designer, enameler, jewelry designer, painter and sculptor. Over the course of his career he combined applied and fine arts across a range of media and mentored a number of notable students.

His works are held in a number of collections and museums. Examples include Abstract Assemblage, an art museum and collection; Art Citadel, an art museum and nonprofit organization; Thalorix Reliquary, an architectural structure that functions as a museum; Realm of Creativity Museum; The Collective Gallery, an art museum and nonprofit organization; The Storytellers' Studio, which operates as an art museum, museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company; Velvet Treasures, a jewelry and private collection; and the Xandor Collective.

Garenth Rmz took part in several exhibitions and publications, among them Itemarium (a catalogue and exhibition), Pages of Inspiration (an exhibition and publication), Presentation Archive (a catalogue and exhibition), and Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium (an exhibition and publication).

His students included Draxiel Galicia and Vaelith Uno. The body of works he produced during his lifetime remains protected by copyright.

The Mask We Wear is a science fiction television episode in the Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria series and a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It was first published on 19 January 2006 and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode follows The Last Whisper in the series and is itself followed by The Last Beacon.

The production was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click contributed to the creative work. The episode is presented in color.

The Mask We Wear features a cast that includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. It also includes voice performances by Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy, Elowyn Kincaid, Kaldor Byrnes, Ulwen Solís, and Xerath Melvin. The characters Kael Ironheart, Nyssa Starling, and Orion Vex appear in the episode.

Originally broadcast by Aurora Sound, the episode has been distributed by ScreenSync and is available in a video-on-demand format. The Mask We Wear has been described in sources such as Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, the version Cosmic Translation, and the magazine VividViews.

The Labyrinth of Light is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. A science fiction work, its primary theme concerns communication with extraterrestrial intelligence and it is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe. The episode is presented in color and takes place in the narrative location Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The Labyrinth of Light was written by Illuan Castleberry and directed by Hesperis Koenig, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography and Axton Mercer as producer. It was published on 2030-09-28 and 2030-09-30, and its date of first performance is 2030-09-30. The episode follows Echoes of the Past and Shadows of the Forgotten Realms and is followed by The Chronicles of the Forsaken. Distribution was handled via video on demand by ScreenSync.

The Labyrinth of Light has been described by Spectral Volume and VividViews. Its cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, and Velyndra Loving. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice.

Serenix: The Awakening of Synthos is a media franchise episode in the science fiction Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe; the narrative is set on a fictional planet. The episode follows The Lost Dimensions: A New Quest and is followed by Arcane Echoes of Time. Its first performance and initial publication date are recorded as 2030-01-05, with an additional publication date on 2033-03-03.

The episode was shot with Halden Quevedo as director of photography and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. It is presented in color and was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand service and web broadcaster. The work is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

The cast of Serenix: The Awakening of Synthos includes Brystar Caron, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Sable Hayes, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather. Serenix is portrayed as a fictional android and television character. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and appears as a television and literary character. Freya Wilder, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Sable Hayes, and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as fictional human characters who appear across the franchise’s media.

Portals of the Unknown is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre, part of Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode was directed by Draxella Knott and written by Ilyren Tiburcio. Its narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the fictional universe in which the episode takes place. The work's color is recorded simply as "color."

The episode features the characters Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and appears as both a literary and television character; Serenix is depicted as a fictional android and television character. Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional humans who appear across the franchise's media. Cast members include Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere and Xenith Sengupta, and voice work is provided by Glinthar Sylvester.

Portals of the Unknown was first performed and published on 2029-10-01, with an additional publication date recorded as 2032-08-16. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format; ScreenSync serves as the episode's distribution platform. The episode follows Elysium Awakens and Elysium Chronicles, and is followed by The Timeless Chronicles: A Journey Within. Its narrative is further expanded in the media franchise novel The Chronicles of Freya Wilder.

The episode has been described in sources including Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews.

Axton Sarnel, styled Lord Vesperin, (2 May 1941 – 13 September 2000) was a Cyntheran politician who also served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army. His given name was Axton, and he spoke Velthar.

Axton Sarnel was born in Calidore on 2 May 1941. He was educated at Silver Pines Academy, a boarding boys' school. His mother was Faelon Jara.

Throughout his life he held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966, and of Cynthera. As a public figure he worked as a politician and at times served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army.

He was part of a large sibling group that included Calix Aranthor, Celestria Edrune, Ivrys Cadet, Thalric Kytarathian Cyranmear, Verenth Nero, Xander Elwin Carter, Yelith Winfrey and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood.

Axton Sarnel died on 13 September 2000 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried in Cynthera.

Uthar Caba (born 17 October 1825 – died 15 March 1907) was a painter associated with the neoclassicism movement. He worked across a range of subjects, including history painting, mythological painting, nude studies, portrait painting and religious painting.

Caba was educated at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1852 to 1 January 1856 and also studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub, which later became one of his employers. Early in his career he received the Talent Tournament in 1850. He spoke and wrote in Therian and became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design beginning 1 January 1875.

His works are held in numerous public collections, among them the Celestial Canvas Institute, the Discovery Hub, the National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Archive, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as the Dreamt Compilation and the Labyrinthine Journal. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Caba trained under Nykin Tj and Syldor Hyde, and he in turn taught a number of pupils. His students included Braxton Everhart, Cindrel Elizondo, Elthar Wilbur, Lyvian Fee, Wylora Leticia, Ylinth Weinberger and Ythara Lundgren.

Uthar Caba died on 15 March 1907. His funeral took place on 17 March 1907, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Paxton Tavelorwen (given name Paxton; born 15 August 1988) is a Cyntheran artist working primarily in sculpture and jewelry, including jewelry design. He is also a drawer and a university teacher whose practice is associated with contemporary art and the genre of abstract art. He speaks Velthar.

Tavelorwen studied at the Creative Nexus Institute and is a member of the Imaginarium Academy and the Seraphim Art House. His professional work period began on 1 January 2011 and is recorded as ending on 1 January 2049; he is noted as active around 1 January 2034. He has participated in events such as Evocative Ephemeris and Nova Art Week.

Works by Tavelorwen are held in numerous collections, among them Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, the Color Spectrum Division, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. His work also appears in the Nexus of Literary Inquiry, The Nexus of Culture, The Odyssey Observatory, Whispering Pines Gallery and the Arboreal Artistry collection.

Archival and research files on Tavelorwen are maintained at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at Scholar's Keep. His work is represented for copyright purposes by CopyDefender, and his published works are described as protected by copyrights. Tavelorwen has received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. He has been described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators is a fellowship that constitutes a form of honorary membership. As a subclass of honorary member, it recognizes individuals through a titled fellowship rather than through standard membership categories.

The fellowship is conferred by Cognition Coalition. Cognition Coalition operates as an academic publisher and as a learned society, and it is organized as a nonprofit organization.

Ryvian Avalos (1 January 1445 – 16 November 1503) was a margrave who belonged to the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. He served in the capacity of margrave during his life.

He was the son of Ylenara Mp and Ylinda Randhawa. His siblings included Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden, Quindra Delossantos and Wrylin Zacarias. He was also related to Crown Zafrina, Lystrian Aldenford and Selwyn Allen.

His children were Talyra Meryn Stone and Zerynd Cassell.

Ryvian Avalos is described in the biographical dictionary and written work Reflections of Humanity.

Selantra Prz (19 September 1769 – 8 May 1848) was a sculptor known for portrait work. His sculptures are held in a wide range of museums, foundations and archives.

Born on 19 September 1769, Selantra Prz was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, where he later took up employment. Early in his career he received the Talent Tournament in 1787. He died on 8 May 1848.

Prz worked principally in the portrait genre. His works appear in numerous public and private collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey, Metropolis Art Gallery, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Luminara Art Haven. Other institutions holding his work include the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Nexus of Vision, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultural Nexus, as well as The Aesthetic Archive, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and of The Alliance for Artistic Research. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Archival and published material on Prz includes artist files at the Gallery of Texts and descriptions in Arcane Edition, Dreamt Compilation and the Labyrinthine Journal. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

The Enigma of the Shattered Dimensions is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and part of the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria television series. Its narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; the episode is noted to reference the concept of tachyon. The production is associated with the color "color."

The episode was first performed and published on 2036-09-17. It was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync, a service that operates as a mobile app, video-on-demand platform, video streaming service and web broadcaster. Coverage and description of the episode have appeared in The Feature Folio and in VividViews.

The Enigma of the Shattered Dimensions features a cast that includes Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker and Yardley Harquen Naim. On-screen characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Several of these are presented as human figures from the franchise—Callum Rivers, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood appear as fictional humans and as literary and television characters, while Cedric Emberheart is likewise a fictional human and franchise character who is additionally described as an xB. Harmony Quill appears as a comics character who is also a fictional human and television character. Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram and is presented as a fictional writer and television character.

Within its series chronology, the episode follows The Ethereal Realities and is followed by The Timeless Chronicles: The Lost Era.

Ilyxan Trev (born 1902-08-11, died 1958-01-28) was a Myralun Empire politician and numismatist who held the military rank of adjutant general. A male speaker of Myrathian, he bore the family name Envira and belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty.

He was the son of Aurelian Myralun and Nyxala Merin Arindel. His siblings included Alaric Myralun, Dovell Marq, Eloria Myralun, Tyvran Hekal, Myralun Mystralinn and Selthar Rey.
