He was married to Qelyth Camacho; the marriage is recorded with start times of 1939-01-01 and 1939-05-13 and an end time of 1958-01-01.

Ilyxan participated in the Chronos Siege. Over the course of his career he received numerous honours, including the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon, the Crystaline Honor, the Knights of the Eternal Flame, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star. His other recognitions included the Pinnacle Honor, the Radiant Token, the Solaris Distinction, the Starlight Gala and the Vexorian Medal.

He died on 1958-01-28 from a gunshot wound; the manner of death is recorded as homicide. Ilyxan Trev is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Olyndra Starfen (28 December 1565 – 20 May 1628) was a princess and margrave of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She held the titles of princess and margrave during her lifetime.

Her given name was Olyndra. She was the daughter of Wyrden Valdivia and belonged to the Kaelwyn family.

Olyndra was married to Melethar Acuña from 24 February 1583 until 28 December 1607.

She was the mother of nine children, among them Brethyn Merlo, Cynder Bonita and Eryndor Jeronimo. Her other children included Inigo Lomar Hest, Kylin Grand and Olyndra Larksong, as well as Othalyn Grossman, Uthryn Lester and Viorelle Amaris Leclerc.

Aeliana Vesperis (born 23 December 2014) is a Vesperian functionary who holds the military rank of general. He was born in Drakemont and is a citizen of Vesperia.

He was born to Alaric Vesperius. He has a number of siblings, among them Alaric Vesperian, Aurelia Vesperis and Aveline Vespera. Other siblings include Elara Vesperian, Elara Vesperion and Elara Vesperis, as well as Fynel Fountain and Liora Vesperian.

In his official capacity he has served as a functionary and holds the rank of general.

Aeliana Vesperis has received several honours, including the Harmony Insignia and the Noble Valorian Order. He is also a recipient of the Opal Honor, the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Order of the Gilded Compass, the latter received in 2014.

Alderon Khalil (26 June 1600 – 13 November 1662) was a female aristocrat of the Kaelwyn dynasty who held the titles of duke and princess. She served in an aristocratic capacity and was a speaker of Malquari.

Born to Yloria Francois, Alderon was a member of the Kaelwyn noble family. Her siblings included Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Jynara Harvey, Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia.

The Ethereal Visions: A New Dawn is a media franchise episode in the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series of the Eldoria Chronicles. It was directed by Zorath Parrilla and the screenplay was written by Ilyren Tiburcio. The episode’s central theme is terrorism, and its narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The episode was first performed on 21 November 2033 and was later published on 24 February 2035. It follows The Enigma of the Celestial Tides and is followed by The Shattered Harmony. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync through a video on demand format, and the work was described in the magazine VividViews. The episode is noted as having the color "color" and includes references to the neutrino.

Cast members include Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Thalyra Hannah, Xenith Sengupta and Zylara Zamudio. Voice actors on the production are Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood and Marcellus Stormwatch.

The Mirage of Time is a science fiction television episode from the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The work treats eugenics as its main subject and is presented in color. The episode began on 2005-09-07 and was published on 2006-02-16 and 2011-10-21.

The Mirage of Time was directed by Lyvian Mensah with Jorwen Huizar as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. Originally broadcast by Aurora Sound, the episode has also been distributed by ScreenSync and is available in a video on demand format.

Cast members of the production include Braxton Hale Thompson, Caelan Edran Solace and Grelyn Paulino. Voice actors who perform in the episode include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Pyrith Maciel and Xerath Melvin. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Orion Vex and Selene Moonshadow.

In the series sequence, The Mirage of Time follows The Forgotten City and is followed by The Shattered Mirror. The episode has been described in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, in the edition Cosmic Translation, and in VividViews.

The Door to Dreams is an episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is described as a science fiction bottle episode and follows the episode The Keeper of the Flame. The episode's narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm at the point in time 2305-01-17; it takes place on a fictional planet and is set in the Technium., a fictional artificial entity within that universe. Publication dates listed for the episode are 2006-11-17 and 2011-09-16. The work's language is Velthar. Original broadcast was on Aurora Sound, and distribution has been handled by ScreenSync via video on demand.

The Door to Dreams was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar credited as director of photography and Ulvael Click listed as a contributor to the creative work. The production's listed color is color. The episode is described by the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, by the translation Cosmic Translation, and by the magazine VividViews.

The episode's cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Melrith Dewey, and Mylaria Friedman. Voice actors associated with the episode include Brevin Alaric Thorne, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Pyrith Maciel, and Wyrith Del Rio. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Percival Stormrider., and Selene Moonshadow.

Eryndra Ferrari (born 1 January 1986) is an architect, artist, author, exhibition curator and jewelry designer. She works primarily in jewelry and jewelry design and was recorded as active in 2051. Her works published during her lifetime remain protected by copyright. She is represented by Boundless Brushworks, an art gallery and business, and by Paradigm Gallery.

She has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues. She took part in Gallery of the Mind and in Itemarium, a catalogue and exhibition, as well as Presentation Archive, another catalogue and exhibition. Her work was included in Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, an exhibition and publication, and in The Artistic Voyage, an art exhibition and travelling exhibition. She also participated in The Curated Experience, an exhibition and publication, and in Tidal Waves of Art, an exhibition and temporary exhibition.

Her pieces are held in numerous collections and institutions. These include the Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, an art collection; the Creative Nexus Institute, an art academy and public research university; and Eternity's Collection, a private jewelry collection. Works by Ferrari are also in Thalorix Reliquary, a museum and architectural structure, and in the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, an art museum and national museum. Additional holdings include The Artifact Atelier and The Collective Gallery, both art museums and nonprofit organizations; The Storytellers' Studio, which functions as an art museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company; and the Velvet Jewel Set and Velvet Treasures, both jewelry collections with Velvet Treasures described as a private collection.

Neryn Martha (2 March 1880 – 23 April 1890) was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. She was born in Cynthera and died in Xylanthia.

She was the daughter of Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne. Neryn was one of a number of siblings, including Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Draxen Benavides, Irvin Thorne, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries and Raelin Brenda.

Neryn suffered from tuberculosis, and the disease was given as the cause of her death. She died of natural causes in Xylanthia on 23 April 1890. As a female, she is referred to using she/her pronouns.

The Last Beacon is a science fiction episode of the television series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was first established on 7 September 2005 and has publication dates recorded as 26 January 2006 and 27 May 2011. The episode follows The Mask We Wear in the series sequence and is followed by Chronicles of the Unknown.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work makes use of the concept of gravity assist as a reference within its story world. The episode is presented in color and the language of the work is Velthar.

Lyvian Mensah directed the episode, with Jorwen Huizar credited as director of photography. Ulvael Click is listed among the contributors to the creative work. The Last Beacon was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and distributed by ScreenSync; it has been made available via video on demand.

The credited cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Irvin Hallowmere and Mylaria Friedman. Characters who appear in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex and Selene Moonshadow. The voice cast comprises Brevin Alaric Thorne, Elowyn Kincaid, Kairis Schechter, Kaldor Byrnes, Pyrith Maciel and Xerath Melvin.

The episode is described in the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria and in the edition or translation titled Cosmic Translation.

Elysoria is a big city and a municipality in the confessional state of New Providence. It is recognized as a city of a sovereign state, a city of a country, a city of a federal republic and a city of a nation, and it functions administratively as a municipality within those same categories.

Elysoria was established on 1891-08-05. The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the FactFolio and the literary work The Midnight Library; Dreamt Compilation and FactFolio are editions or reference works of different kinds, and The Midnight Library is a literary work.

Elysoria maintains a number of twinning arrangements with other municipalities and cities. Since 2027 it has been twinned with Aquilon City (a big city, city with a city council and municipality) and Drysvale (a municipality of a sovereign state, a realm and a country). From 2032 Elysoria has been twinned with Solstice Bay (a big city, port settlement and tourist destination) and Trivandria (a big city, border city, capital region, city and largest city). Novarun (a big city, city in a sovereign state/country/nation, legislature and port settlement) became a twin in 2033, and Primaris (a big city and city that is a federal capital, a federative entity across multiple state forms, largest city, megacity, metropolis and primate city) since 2035. In 2037 Brookhaven (a big city, city, federal capital and largest city), Noruclave (a big city, city and port settlement) and Lythoria (an administrative territorial entity, city and national capital) entered twinning agreements. Aetherwyn, a big city and municipality described across several state frameworks, has been twinned since 2045. Metropolisia (a big city and city) and Ironclad City (a big city, city and municipality within several state categories) established links in 2050, with Ironclad City’s arrangement recorded from 2050-08-04. Thundoria (a big city and commune across multiple state forms) became a twin in 2052. Ignisport (a big city and city) and Nexopolis (a big city and city described in many overlapping sovereign, constitutional, federal and independent city categories, including a historical unrecognized state) were twinned in 2056, with Nexopolis’s arrangement beginning in November 2056. Finally, Halcyon Bay (a city of republican significance, former national capital and largest city) was twinned from 2058-11-26.

The Arcane Chronicles: A New Dawn is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The story takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. Its first performance was on 2037-05-06 and its publication date is recorded as 2038-01-03. The episode is noted with the color "color" and is followed by the episode The Celestial Nexus: A New Era.

The episode's cast includes Hespera Coggins, Nylen Meraz, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Characters featured in the episode include Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood.

Cedric Emberheart is presented as a fictional human who appears in the franchise's written works and on television. Harmony Quill appears as a comics and literary figure who also appears on television. Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are portrayed as fictional humans across the franchise’s literary and television formats. Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram who also functions as a fictional writer and appears as a television character.

The Arcane Chronicles: A New Dawn was described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews. It was distributed by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and web broadcaster, and made available in a video on demand distribution format and via ScreenSync’s mobile app.

Viorelle Amaris Celestine (10 March 1524 – 24 May 1576) was a princess. She was born in Oakridge and her given name was Viorelle; she was female.

She was the daughter of Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong.

Her wider family included Lydan Chirinos, Merrick Ashbourne and Yloria Francois. Her siblings included Elara Schiller and Zyris Schiller, as well as Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena, Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood and Yndral Shine.

Miraleth Braden (23 July 1919 – 27 June 1998) was military personnel who belonged to the Aelorian Dynasty. He served as military personnel and saw action during the Chronos Siege, a world war and historical period, and was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order.

Braden was born to Yardley Ashford and Qelith Sherwood. He was one of a large group of siblings; his brothers and sisters included Aelarin Tsang, Alaric Vyrlandus and Elinor Nichols. Other siblings were Elowen Annette, Ilyndar Mcfall, Lydara Colley, Qylar Goble, Selath García and Ulind Landau.

Eriath Deboer (born 2001) is a female jeweler and jewelry designer. She works in the fields of jewelry and jewelry design and was active on 1 January 2036.

Deboer studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and was a student of Denzel Montgomery, Malachi Thorne, and Quinlan Hartwood. She is represented by the galleries Artisan Exchange and The Gallery Exchange.

Her work is held by museums and collections, including the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, and the Xandor Collective. She has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, among them the catalogue and exhibition Collection Conclave and the catalogue and exhibition Presentation Archive; the temporary exhibitions Evocative Ephemeris and The Quickening Exhibit; as well as the exhibitions The Collection of Curiosities. and The Curated Experience, the latter of which is also a publication.

Deboer received the Artistic Ambit Competition prize in 2037. She speaks Malquari, and her works are protected by copyrights.

Orinthal Series is a group of casts and a group of sculptures created by Kaelith Thornwood. The series was originated on 1 January 1916 in the Harmonia District and is executed in bronze with patina. Classified within the nude genre, the works are in the public domain.

The series depicts a variety of human forms and bodily details: it shows a man and a warrior, and includes representations of nudity and pubic hair. Specific anatomical and compositional elements depicted across the works include the armpit, back, navel, intergluteal cleft and a contrapposto pose; the series also incorporates imagery of major trauma.

Orinthal Series is part of the collections of the Jaspis Art Collective Museum and has been part of the National Artistry Hub collection since 1 January 2025. It has been located or exhibited at numerous institutions and venues, among them Arboreal Artistry; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Crestvale Collective Arts Museum; Dreamscape Museum; Harmonious Expanse; Horizon Ridge University Gallery; Jaspis Art Collective Museum; Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum; National Artistry Hub (from 1 January 2025); National Legacy Gallery; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; The Chroma Dreamscape; The Creative Ethos; The Eclectic Arts Pavilion; The Expression Hub; The Sculptural Repository; The Storytellers' Studio; and The Storytellers' Studio.. (The series was located at The Storytellers' Studio. from 1 March 1972 until 1 January 1986.)

Collective Canvas is an art museum and nonprofit organization operated for a collective benefit. It was founded on 1 January 1987 and officially opened in 1987.

Works by Collective Canvas are held in the collection of the Chronicle Gallery, which functions as an art museum and publishing company. Artist files about Collective Canvas are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that serves as an archive, art library and library.

Collective Canvas is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. The organization was designated with the Legacy Appreciation Badge, a heritage designation, beginning on 19 October 2043.

Lythara Townsend (25 June 1962 – 4 November 2033) was a male painter, sculptor, illustrator and graphic artist whose work was associated with abstract expressionism. He worked primarily in the art of painting while also producing illustration, graphic and sculptural work. Townsend received the Radiant Emblem and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Townsend's artistic practice was influenced by Aelath Thota and Glinthar Wilkinson, and his output combined painterly concerns with graphic and sculptural approaches. He took part in major contemporary presentations, including Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions.

His works are held in a wide range of public and institutional collections. Among them are Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation and the Color Spectrum Division. Additional collections holding his work include Cultura Nexus, the Cultural Tapestry Museum, Curator's Archive and Mirage Art Pavilion. Other repositories include Nexus National Museum, Radiant Brush Gallery, Solaris Cultural Collective and Solstice Art Storage. His pieces are also in Terranova Artis Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Enchanted Collection and The Inspiration Institute. The Inspiration Nexus, The Nexus of Culture and Vivid Visions Gallery likewise include his work in their holdings.

Archives and documentation on Townsend are maintained in several libraries and databases. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, and he is described in the DataGalaxy web portal. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate; his copyright was managed by IntellectProtect and by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights.

Townsend spoke Velthar. He died on 4 November 2033 of prostate cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Timeless Echoes: A Journey of Discovery is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and a part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Directed by Draxella Knott, it premiered on 13 February 2034, which is also its publication date. The episode is presented in color and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The narrative is set across several environments, including Technium. on a fictional planet, and within a temple. Characters that appear in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Marcellus Stormwatch, and Miles Hawthorne.

The Timeless Echoes: A Journey of Discovery features a cast that includes Calix Vornell, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Xenith Sengupta, and Zephyros Burk, with voice performances by Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, and Ulyr Stacks.

Distributed by ScreenSync, the episode was released via video on demand and was described by the magazine VividViews. In the series sequence, it follows The Eternal Chronicles and is followed by The Celestial Odyssey: A New Adventure.

The Lost Chronicles of the Dawn is a science fiction media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe and is associated with the color "color".

The production features cast members Brystar Caron, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Velyndra Loving. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Braxton Velaryn is presented as a human character appearing in literature and television; Freya Wilder appears across film, literature, television and video games as a human character; Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid in literature and television; Miles Hawthorne and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as human characters who appear in television and literary works; Serenix appears as an android character in television.

Halden Quevedo served as director of photography. The Lost Chronicles of the Dawn premiered on 2030-02-04; publication dates associated with the episode include 2030-02-04 and 2033-03-07. It was distributed by ScreenSync via a video on demand format. The episode has been described in Spectral Volume, an edition, and in VividViews, a magazine.

In the series chronology, The Lost Chronicles of the Dawn follows Arcane Echoes of Time and is followed by The Ethereal Archways.

Brynith Farfan (9 May 1646 – 1 September 1671) was a noble who held the title of count and belonged to the House Eldrath-Lorian, a dynasty and noble family. He was born in Harvenia and was part of the noble social class throughout his life.

His father was Jyris Dexter. He was one of a large set of siblings, which included Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Noxen Valeris, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

Farfan spoke Therian, a modern natural language. He received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, a grade of an order.

Julian Aldermore (31 January 1857 – 13 January 1900) was a count of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty who bore the family name Aldermore. He spoke Kynthor and is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Born in Verenthia, Aldermore was the son of Selin Gamble and Xerath Loya; his stepparent was Pytheran Cheney. His godparents were Chyra Mcallister and Vorith Dai.

Aldermore married Wyndra Casanova on 10 July 1889; the marriage is recorded through 1900. He died in Tranqilport on 13 January 1900.

During his life he received several honours, including the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Verdant Chivalry and the Twilight Pendant.

Olyndra Verathis (5 May 1526 – 7 February 1578) was a regent and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She was born in Oakridge and her given name was Olyndra.

She was the daughter of Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong and had numerous siblings. Among them were Elara Schiller and Zyris Schiller, as well as Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Pherian Aracena, Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia and Yndral Shine.

Her occupation and the position she held are both recorded as regent. Throughout accounts of her life she is referred to with she/her pronouns.

Thronnaris von Eldoria (17 March 1929 – 4 June 1971) was a princess of Thronnaris and a member of the Sylverian dynasty. A citizen of Thronnaris, she held the noble title of princess and was commonly referred to by her dynastic name.

She was born at Crystal Keep, the royal palace, and died in Aetherdon, a megacity that serves as the national capital and largest city. Throughout accounts of her life she is referred to with feminine pronouns.

Thronnaris was the daughter of Baran Whitlock. Her siblings included Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez and Freyael Mcwilliams. Other siblings were Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden and Rynar Coble. The remainder of her brothers and sisters comprised Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

Olyndra Mia Thorne (born June 13, 1600 — died November 14, 1644) was a female feudatory of the Xanthel dynasty. Her given name was Olyndra, and she served in the role of a feudatory within her family.

She was the daughter of Merrick Alastor Thorne. She had a large number of siblings; among them were Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine, Helvian Nell and Inigo Valeron. Other siblings included Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae.

She was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that is also a tourist attraction.

Braxton Tharen Ularis (given name Braxton Tharen; family name Ularis; 31 March 1863 – 8 September 1918) was a male artist active from 1884 to 1918. He worked as a drawer, graphic artist, lithographer, painter and sculptor, and was best known for portrait work. He studied at Ironwood Academy and was a student of Zander Delacroix; among his own students was Braxton Eldridge Mercer.

Artist files on Ularis are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His works are held in many public and private collections, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum, Echo Art Foundation, Gallery of Dreams, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium.

Copyrights on his works have expired. Ularis died on 8 September 1918; the manner of death is recorded as suicide, with drowning listed as the cause.

Zyvra Isom (born 1434; died 1 January 1486) was a politician of the Xanthel dynasty who held the noble title of duke and served as regent. She is recorded as having occupied the position of regent during her career.

She was born to Jorwyn Rebecca and Elysia Morgan Thompson and was a member of the Xanthel family. Her siblings were Brinth Quintana, Galdir Galicia, Karyth Gregorio, Nykin Basu, Rythar Hurst, Xantha Kannan, Xian Joe, Zoran Olivas and Zylara Palencia.

Her life and career are described in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium, a biographical dictionary.

Doryn Cortez (15 April 1721 – 8 February 1788) was a Kaldoria painter whose work focused on floral painting, landscape painting and still life. His field of work was the art of painting, and his body of work is now out of copyright: copyrights on works have expired. He is represented in numerous public and private collections.

Cortez was born in Harborview City and spent his career working there; he also died in Harborview City. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and spoke the Valorean Tongue. As a male painter, he is recorded in contemporary and later sources under his full name.

His works are held in a wide range of collections. Among them are the Branash Cultural Collective, the Canvas of Inspirations Museum, the Civic Visions Museum and the Creative Gallery. Further holdings include the Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, the Harmathia Art Repository, the Legacy Art Sanctuary and Lunavalle Academia. Other institutions with works by Cortez are the Mirage Cultural Center, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the National Legacy Gallery and the Prismatic History Museum. He is also represented at the Reverie Atrium, the Royal Gallery Palace, the Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. Additional collections holding his work include The Borough Art Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Dreamweaver Art Institute and The Enchanted Art Gallery. Works by Cortez appear in The Enchanted Spectrum, The Ephemeral Archive, The Ethereal Exhibit and The Ethereal Oasis. The Exploratorium of Art, The Expression Hub, The Giving Gallery and The Harmony Space also hold examples of his painting. The Historical Studio, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Odyssey Museum and The Palace of Reflections include his works in their collections, as do The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Space and The Whirlwind of Art. His paintings can also be found at Treasures of Time, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival and bibliographic references to Cortez include artist files at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in several written sources, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Krestoria's Tongue, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Legendarium and SagaSpectrum.

The Ethereal Whispers: A Journey to the Unknown is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. Presented as a disaster film and science fiction work, it is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The narrative takes place within that fictional universe and is set in the Technium and on a fictional planet. The episode's color is given as "color".

The episode was first performed and initially published on 2030-10-19; a further publication date is recorded as 2033-04-05. It follows the episode The Arcane Alchemy and is followed by The Forgotten Chronicles of Time. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync through video on demand.

The production was led by producers Axton Mercer, Illuan Castleberry and Quinthas Mathew, with a screenplay by Ilyren Tiburcio, Lyvian Mensah and Qyvor Ricketts.

The episode's cast includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Xenith Sengupta and Zylara Zamudio.

Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Sable Hayes, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and Trystan Jorvik. Several of these figures are presented with distinct fictional types: Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Serenix as a fictional android, and Trystan Jorvik as a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial. Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream, Sable Hayes and Tobias Merriweather appear as fictional human characters, with Freya Wilder additionally identified across film, literary, television and video game forms.

The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

The Celestial Echoes: Fragments of Time is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. It takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set aboard a brig and on a fictional planet, with its narrative later expanded in the written work The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars.

The episode was first performed and published on 2044-02-25. It follows The Lost Legacy of the Ancients and is followed by The Echoes of the Forgotten. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, released via video on demand through that platform.

The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters who appear in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall. Voice work for the production was provided by Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

The film editor for the episode was Yardley Dovern Pax. The work is also associated with the color "color."

Ronan Arkeddan Starfen (born Ronan Arkeddan Starfen; 22 September 1969 – 22 July 2037) was an author, writer, painter, illustrator and drawer. He worked in the Kynthor language and his career encompassed both written and visual practice. He participated in the events Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions.

Starfen's work is held in numerous public and private collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Cultural Canvas Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Essence of Form Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Visionary Space, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files on Starfen are maintained at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

His published body of work remains protected by copyright and his copyright is represented by CopyDefender.

Vorith Hurst (born between 1167 and 1174; died 1199) was a princess. She lived into 1199 and is recorded with a birth sometime between 1167 and 1174.

She was the daughter of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. Her siblings included Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran and Mystral Witherspoon, as well as Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino and Ulthir Whiteley.

Omerith is a modern natural language. It is found in the countries Carandor, Drakeldoria, Elysian Coast, Nymbrelia and Verenthia, and is indigenous to Verenthia.

Typologically, Omerith is an agglutinative, synthetic, pro-drop language that uses postpositions and typically places adjectives before nouns (adjective–noun order).

Omerith’s grammatical system includes nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, ablative and instrumental cases. The language marks present and past tenses and has a desiderative mood; it does not have grammatical agreement.

Omerith is written with hiragana, kanji and katakana. It is described in Arcane Edition, the Cultural Nexus Archive (entry dated 2060-05-07), Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia and Legendarium.

Ryland Zolterras (born Ryland; 11 November 1921 – 15 September 2012) was a Zolterran aristocrat, scholar and collector who served as Zolterran Monarch from 29 October 1989 until his death. A native Xyldari speaker, he wrote in Xyldari and was profiled in O'Rourke Insights Online.

Born into the Velorian family, Ryland was the son of Zoltarian Olympiadis. He was given the honorific style Knight Aerion at birth and held the title duke from 11 November 1921 until 29 October 1989. On 29 October 1989 he assumed the noble title Zolterran Monarch and the honorific prefix Chief Aeloria; he held the position of Zolterran Monarch until 15 September 2012. His country of citizenship was Zolterra and he was socially classified as royalty.

Educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities, Ryland pursued work across several scholarly fields. His occupations included anthropologist, classical archaeologist, botanist and art collector, and his fields of work were archaeology and botany. He held the military rank of lieutenant general. He was a member of the Ethos Research Authority and the Institute of Artistry and Design, and he belonged to the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1991 until 2012.

Ryland received numerous honors and awards during his life. Among them were the Order of the Radiant Heart (28 October 1942), the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame and the Knightly Sovereignty Grade (both 1 April 1944), and the Verdant Gem (1 April 1944). He also received the Order of the Dusk Rose (25 October 1950), the Apex Merit Prize (1962), the Collegiate Haven Excellence Award (1968), and the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (20 June 1964). Later recognitions included the Opal Crown (28 June 1993), the Celestial Sphere (1999), the Illuminated Scholars Society fellowship (21 May 1998), and the Emerald Circle (14 June 2005). Other honors recorded are the Celestial Order, the Celestial Order of the Twilight, the Glorious Order, the Noble Crest, the Pinnacle Honor, the Starlight Gala, the Verdant Badge and the Celestial Sphere.

In his personal life Ryland married Damaris Elowen Carter on 15 June 1944; that marriage ended on 1 May 1959. He later married Delphina Orimund Shyr on 3 November 1962; that marriage ended on 7 March 2004. He had five children: Glynor Rutherford, Helynd Bose, Kaelar Smile, Liora Zoltan and Pyreth Cepero. He had personal interests in fly fishing and tennis.

Ryland Zolterras died on 15 September 2012; the cause of death was pneumonia.

Valentina Zolterran (21 January 1868 – 8 December 1946) was a Zolterran Monarch and noble who held both sovereign and ducal positions during the first half of the 20th century. He served as Zolterran Monarch from 18 September 1911 until his death on 8 December 1946, and concurrently held the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 18 September 1911 to 7 June 1944. A holder of the noble title duke, he was also recorded with the military rank of admiral.

Born into the Velorian family, Valentina was the son of Allegra Zoltarra and Therin Addo. He had at least one sibling, Alessandro Zolterrius. Valentina married Istyr Ardila on 6 June 1896; that marriage is recorded as ending on 30 December 1952. He was the father of Galdanor Baggett, Nythor Brink, Phaelan Jim and Zoltarian Olympiadis. After his death, he was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

Valentina was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities and was an active member of scholarly organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press. His creative output is held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and the copyright status of his works is recorded as having expired.

Throughout his life he received numerous honors and orders. These include the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Ethos Token, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Knights of the Aetherial Realm, the Order of the Celestial Serpent, the Order of the Celestial Vanguard, the Order of the Gilded Compass and the Pinnacle Honor. He was also awarded the Jewel of the Ancients on 21 June 1888.

Valentina has been described in a variety of published and archival sources, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. He was a citizen of Zolterra.

Alessandro Zolterrius (born 3 May 1865, died 18 September 1911) was a Zolterran monarch, military leader and artist. A member of the Velorian family, he served as both king and duke while also working as a painter and a poet; he was male and is buried at the Celestial Citadel.

He held the position of Zolterran Monarch from 8 July 1898 to 18 September 1911, and simultaneously held the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom over the same period. As military personnel he attained the rank of general. His active work period ran from 1 January 1885 until 1 January 1911.

Zolterrius was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities and spoke Xyldari. His given name was Adeline Thornfield. His parents were Allegra Zoltarra and Therin Addo; he had a sibling, Valentina Zolterran, and a child, Liora Zoltan.

His artistic and literary works are held in the collections of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, and the National Legacy Gallery, and his copyrights have expired. He received several honors, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Pinnacle Honor. He is discussed in a number of sources, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Forgotten Prophecy and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Allegra Zoltarra (4 July 1838 – 8 July 1898) was a Zolterran composer and monarch. He held the hereditary Duchy of Auralis-Princedom and reigned as Zolterran Monarch from 8 March 1883 until his death on 8 July 1898. In addition to his royal duties he bore the noble title of duke and held the military rank of admiral.

Born into the Velorian family, Allegra was the son of Adel Zoltan. He became a citizen of Zolterra in 1849. Allegra was educated at Crestwood Academy and at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities. He married Therin Addo on 19 June 1862; the marriage continued until his death in 1898. He had two children, Alessandro Zolterrius and Valentina Zolterran.

As a composer Allegra’s works are held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He was a member of several learned bodies, joining the Celestial Research Institute on 21 December 1865, and also belonging to Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Allegra received numerous honours over his life, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Order of the Twilight, the Ethos Token, and the Pinnacle Honor. He was awarded the Illuminated Scholars Society fellowship on 21 December 1865. Later distinctions included the Jewel of the Ancients (21 June 1888), the Noble Sovereign Grade (20 October 1888), and memberships in the Knights of the Aetherial Realm. He was also a recipient of the Order of the Gilded Compass (2856), the Order of the Radiant Heart, and other awards.

Fluent in Exylith, Therian and Xyldari, Allegra has been described in a range of sources, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, The Midnight Library and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. He was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

Adel Zoltan (26 January 1802 – 8 March 1883) was a Zolterran military commander, politician and monarch from the Velorian dynasty. He was a citizen of Zolterra and his native language was Therian; he also spoke Xyldari. He was known by the given names Adeline Thornfield and Cole-Ren.

Adel Zoltan rose through a military career that began with the rank of sergeant in 1827. He was recorded as a colonel in 1832 and as a brigadier general in 1833, later attaining the rank of generalissimo in 1849. During his service he participated in the Conclave of Conflict.

In 1857 Adel Zoltan assumed both the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom and the position of Zolterran Monarch; he held both offices from 5 February 1857 until his death on 8 March 1883. He was a member of the Velorian family. His stepparent was Adelzo Thornfield, and he had a child, Allegra Zoltarra.

He received numerous awards and honors across his career, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Celestial Distinction, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Crystaline Honor, the Ethos Token, the Gallant Shield, the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Noble Crest, the Order of the Gilded Compass, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Pinnacle Honor and the Zenith Medal. The Order of the Gilded Compass was received on 21 August 1849.

Adel Zoltan is described in a range of sources, among them the Arcane Version, the Dreamt Compilation, the Infinitopedia, the Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. His personal archives are held at The Archive Atrium. He died of a stroke on 8 March 1883.

Adelzo Thornfield (given name Adeline Thornfield; 1787-10-07 – 1857-02-05) was a Zolterran Monarch who served as Zolterran Monarch from 1848-06-06 to 1857-02-05 and held the Duchy of Auralis-Princedom from 1853-11-14 to 1857-02-05. A career statesman and naval officer, he held the rank of admiral.

He was the son of Ryland Zolterra and Falyndra Mccreary, and was a sibling of Zolric Norra. He was the father of Adel Zoltan.

Thornfield received numerous honors during his lifetime, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Crystaline Honor, the Ethos Token (received on 1787-09-26), the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Pinnacle Honor.

Works by Thornfield are held in the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; the copyrights on his works have expired. He spoke Xyldari, and his life and work are described in Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Zolnorric Thalor (given name Norric; 1 November 1817 – 7 February 1876) was a Zolterran monarch who served as Zolterran Monarch from 29 March 1831 to 29 March 1848. He was a citizen of Zolterra and is recorded as male.

Born to Zolric Norra, Thalor was married to Liora Arindel; the start date of that marriage is reported as 6 October 1836 and also as 31 October 1836, with an end date of 7 April 1851. He had a child, Viorelle Zolterran.

Thalor’s recorded work period is given as beginning on 1 January 1739 and ending on 1 January 1838. Works by Thalor are held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and his published works are noted as having copyrights that have expired. His life and work are described in several sources, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, The Forgotten Prophecy and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

He received multiple honors during his life, among them the Crystaline Honor, the Ethos Token, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor. The Order of the Obsidian Phoenix is cited as an order of chivalry.

Thalor died of a stroke on 7 February 1876. He was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

Zolric Norra (given name Norric; 24 January 1785 – 29 March 1831) was a Zolterran politician who served as Zolterran Monarch from 12 February 1810 until 29 March 1831. He held Zolterra citizenship throughout his life.

Born to Ryland Zolterra and Falyndra Mccreary, he was the sibling of Adelzo Thornfield and the father of Zolnorric Thalor. As a male public figure, he combined political duties with involvement in learned institutions.

Norra’s occupation is recorded as politician, and he was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. Over the course of his life he received several honors, among them the Crystaline Honor, the Ethos Token (received on 17 April 1787), the Order of the Radiant Heart, and the Pinnacle Honor.

His creative and cultural legacy is preserved in several institutions. Works by Norra are held in the collections of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Terranova Artis Museum, and artist files relating to him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in such sources as Arcane Version and Dreamt Compilation, as well as in the literary works The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library; he is also documented in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Norra spoke and wrote in Therian and Xyldari. He died on 29 March 1831 of sepsis; his manner of death is recorded as homicide. He was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

Ryland Zolterra (given name Ryland; 14 May 1749 – 12 February 1810) was a Zolterran monarch who served as Zolterran Monarch from 25 March 1790 until his death on 12 February 1810. He was a citizen of Zolterra and spoke Xyldari.

Born at Maplewood Manor, Ryland married Falyndra Mccreary on 29 August 1783; their marriage continued until his death in 1810. They were the parents of Adelzo Thornfield and Zolric Norra. His works and legacy were later described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Reflections of Humanity, The Midnight Library and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

During his life he received several honours, including the Arcadian Emblem, the Ethos Token (received on 17 April 1787) and the Order of the Gilded Compass. His works are held in the collections of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Ryland Zolterra was buried at the Celestial Citadel.

Ytherin Skinner (1 January 1924 – 1 January 2016) was a Valorian designer and visual artist whose professional activity spanned from 1 January 1944 until 1 January 2016. He worked across multiple disciplines, most notably typography, and held occupations as an architect, ceramicist, cover artist, designer, graphic designer, industrial designer, photographer, postage stamp designer and typographer.

Skinner studied at Crestwood University of Technology and Arts. He took part in the exhibition or event Radiant Impressions during his career. For professional representation he was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative; his published works remain protected by copyrights.

The archives of Ytherin Skinner are held by several institutions, including Chronicle Gallery, Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum, Krestoria National Research Archive, The Artistry Archive, The Collective Gallery and The Creative Portal Museum.

Works by Skinner are held in numerous public collections. These include the Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum, Sailor's Legacy Center, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Luminara Atrium Museum, The Creative Portal Museum and The Reverie Repository.

He was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

Lysander Zoltari (born 7 December 1665 or 18 December 1665; died 1 January 1728 or 9 April 1728) was a Zolterran monarch, painter, philosopher, writer and art collector noted for her involvement in aphorism and politics. She served as Zolterran Monarch from 6 November 1671 until 6 June 1693 and wrote and painted in several languages, including Malquari, Therian, Thesvian, the Valorean Tongue and Xyldari.

Born into the Eldryth family, her father was Liora Zolterran. During her reign and after, she combined political activity with literary and artistic production, and her work shows the influence of Valyndra Rodas. As a collector she assembled works that are now held by the Color Spectrum Division, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, and the Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures.

Her life and output are documented across a range of sources, among them Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript, Phantasmal Adaptation, the Legendarium, The Midnight Library, the Clarity Repository and the Verifiable Vade Mecum. Her copyrights on works have expired, and she has been canonized as a saint.

She died at Seraphim Bay. She was non-heterosexual.

Liora Zolterran (born 19 December 1633 — died 16 November 1671) was a Zolterran king and military leader. He served as the Zolterran Monarch and was a citizen of Zolterra. He spoke Xyldari.

Liora held the position of Zolterran Monarch from 30 October 1650 until 6 November 1671. As monarch he bore the noble title of king while also serving in a military capacity.

He took part in the Sectarian Strife, a religious war, and was killed in action, dying in battle. He was buried at the Celestial Citadel, a church and heritage site.

Liora was a member of the Eldryth dynasty. His parents were Marcellus Zoltarelli and Wryten Obeng, and he had a child, Lysander Zoltari. He was also recorded with the given names Norric and Ryland.

He is described in a number of works and sources, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library, Whispers of Time and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive. He also appears in the video game Nebula Quest.

Marcellus Zoltarelli (4 October 1589 – 30 October 1650) was a Zolterran monarch who served as Zolterran Monarch from 22 March 1643 until 30 October 1650. A member of the Eldryth dynasty, he held citizenship of Zolterra and spoke Xyldari. He is described in the Arcane Version and the Dreamt Compilation, as well as in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

Born to Zolnorric Valtor and Lyneth Benz, Marcellus was male and part of a large family. His siblings included Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Aurelia Zoltan, Brendith Becker, Caspian Zolterrian, Isyra Nolfen, Loryn Aponte and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune. Marcellus was married to Wryten Obeng, the marriage beginning on 27 August 1631, and he had a child named Liora Zolterran.

During his career he is recorded with the occupation of monarch and formally held the position titled Zolterran Monarch between the stated start and end dates. The Arcane Version, the Dreamt Compilation and The Forgotten Prophecy provide contemporary or later descriptions of his life and rule.

Hestorn Monreal (born 20 June 1605 – died 30 April 1671) was a Veldrithian monarch and patron of the arts who held the title of king. A citizen of Veldrithia, he received the Celestial Knightly Grade and is recorded as having an active work period from 1 January 1626 to 1 January 1671.

Hestorn held a number of formal positions during his life. He served in the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 19 August 1626 until 19 April 1671. He also held the office of Zolterran Monarch between 17 November 1631 and 24 July 1638.

As a patron of the arts, Hestorn’s works are held in the collection of the Ethos Gallery. The copyrights on his works have expired. His life and activities are described in sources including the Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Hestorn belonged to the Eldryth dynasty. His parents were Isyra Nolfen and Noxen Vespera, and he had at least one sibling, Olyndra Zolterran. He was married to Veldrithian Brethyn from 31 May 1631 and later to Aelthris Figueiredo from 11 December 1644.

Hestorn died in Vornexa on 30 April 1671. The cause of death was a stroke, and the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Isyra Nolfen (20 December 1576 – 17 November 1631) was a Zolterran Monarch. He belonged to the Eldryth dynasty and was the son of Zolnorric Valtor and Lyneth Benz. He was a citizen of Zolterra. His siblings included Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Aurelia Zoltan, Brendith Becker, Caspian Zolterrian, Loryn Aponte, Marcellus Zoltarelli and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune.

He married Noxen Vespera in 1601. His child was Hestorn Monreal.

By occupation he was a monarch and he held the noble title Zolterran Monarch; he served as Zolterran Monarch from 30 September 1607 until his death on 17 November 1631.

He received the Twilight Pendant. Isyra Nolfen is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Aurelia Zoltan (13 December 1572 – 26 February 1616) was a Zolterran Monarch who worked in government and politics. He served as Zolterran Monarch and held the occupation of monarch during his career. He was a citizen of Zolterra.

Aurelia held the position of Zolterran Monarch from 29 September 1599 until 29 September 1607. His work was concentrated in the fields of government and politics.

He was a member of the Eldryth dynasty and the son of Zolnorric Valtor. His siblings included Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Brendith Becker, Caspian Zolterrian, Isyra Nolfen, Loryn Aponte, Marcellus Zoltarelli, and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune. Bryston Sun is recorded as a significant person linked to him.

Aurelia Zoltan died on 26 February 1616. His manner of death is recorded as homicide and the cause of death as poisoning.

He is described in several sources, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Zolnorric Valtor (given name Norric; 12 May 1535 – 29 September 1599) was a Zolterran Monarch and politician. He was a citizen of Zolterra and belonged to the Eldryth dynasty. He spoke Xyldari.

Educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities, Zolnorric held the position of Zolterran Monarch from 6 June 1562 until 29 September 1599. During his life he received the Twilight Pendant.

Zolnorric married Lyneth Benz; the marriage began on 11 October 1575. He was the parent of Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Aurelia Zoltan, Brendith Becker, Caspian Zolterrian, Isyra Nolfen, Loryn Aponte, Marcellus Zoltarelli and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune. Bryston Sun is recorded as a significant person linked to him.

Zolnorric is described in a number of works and compilations, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Jorvik Nareth Bolun (9 November 1605 – 8 November 1672) was a member of the Yewtree noble family who served in both ecclesiastical and secular offices, notably as diocesan bishop and as duke. He bore the given name Jorvik.

Bolun served as diocesan bishop from 21 January 1638 until 1664. He was also an elected bishop and served as a parish administrator at other points in his career.

In the secular sphere, he held the noble title of duke from 1 January 1650 until 1672.

A member of the Yewtree family, Bolun was the son of Theros Frimpong and Aveline Crownwood. His siblings included Gleran Villalpando, Ivrys Hornsby, Jaylin Marron, Nytheren Mohr, Pyraen Sy, Qyra Simone, Viorelle Thorne and Ydaris Berkowitz.

His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Rhyel Graves (born 8 March 1963; died 23 October 2052) was a Cyntheran artist and sculptor associated with contemporary art and known for work in abstract art and the art of sculpture. He spoke Velthar and worked primarily as an artist and sculptor throughout his career.

Graves was educated at Seraphim Art House; he was also a member of Seraphim Art House and belonged to the Cognition Coalition. His work was influenced by Hesper Alden Brightwood, and he took part in the Radiant Impressions exhibition.

His sculptures and related works are held in a number of public collections, including Cultural Nexus, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files on Graves are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Graves received several honours during his lifetime, among them the Celestial Honor (awarded 1 January 2026), the Harmony Cross (awarded 1 January 2039) and the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. His copyright was represented by CopyDefender, and his published body of work remained protected by copyrights.

He died in Calidore on 23 October 2052 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. Graves held citizenship of Cynthera and had held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966.

Mynel Galeano (12 February 1693 – 17 June 1721) was a princess. Her family name was Nyxmar. She was born and died in Halcyon Vale.

Galeano was female. She was the daughter of Elyndor Deshpande and Isylar Bastidas. Her siblings included Fintan Alaric Morrow, Jaylin Falconer, Jorvik Thorne, Neryth Nagi, Thalorin Marsden, Thalric Arion Kytarathian, Wryten Bartlett and Zynith Jhonson.

Halcyon Vale, the place of her birth and death, is a district capital and an urban municipality.

Sapphire Grove is a city and town that functions as a municipality within the unitary sovereign state of Terranova. It came into existence on 1 January 1971. The official language of Sapphire Grove is Seldim, a modern natural language.

Sapphire Grove maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other administrative bodies. Among these are Astral Grove, which is a city under municipal jurisdiction; the towns Birchwood, Fernhill and Sandstone; and Gableshire, a market town and civil parish. Dawnshollow, Ostendre and Rosewood Heights are all municipalities of various types, with Dawnshollow also noted as a place with town rights and privileges and Rosewood Heights described as a town as well. Harborfall is a commune and port settlement, while Holoset is identified as a border city and town. Thundraxis, Vorthelis and Astral Grove are listed as cities; Ryloria is a municipality of the country; Echo Valley is a rural municipality; Uldoria and Umberfall are communes and municipalities described by multiple administrative categories; and Xelthoria is a municipality associated with sovereign state, realm and country designations.

The Ethereal Expedition is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode was first performed and published on 2032-05-30. Its listed color is color.

Zorath Parrilla directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography and Illuan Castleberry credited as screenwriter. The work references the neutrino in its material. It is followed in the series by The Awakening: A New Dawn.

Cast members in the production include Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta, and Zephyros Burk. The character Thalen Virok appears in the episode. Voice actors credited for spoken roles include Idrisyl Pro, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks, and Yates Orinthal.

The Ethereal Expedition was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. Coverage of the episode appears in VividViews.

The Celestial Reflections is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode is assigned the color "color."

The episode features a cast that includes Lyris Cortés, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker and Zyreth Duff. Among the characters who appear are Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Harmony Quill is presented as a comics character who also appears as a television character; Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram and a fictional writer who appears on television. Cedric Emberheart is described as a fictional human, a literary and television character and is additionally noted as an xB. Callum Rivers and Rowan Emberwood are portrayed as fictional human characters who appear across the franchise.

Draxella Knott directed the episode. It was released and first performed on 2037-10-21, a date that is also given as its publication date. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync in a video on demand format; ScreenSync operates as a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

Within the series chronology, The Celestial Reflections follows The Labyrinth of Celestial Echoes and is followed by The Celestial Chronicles: A New Era. The episode has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

Belegorn Sievers (18 July 1703 – 6 April 1771) was a member of the noble family Yondercrest who held the title Protector of the Eternal Flame and served as bishop-elect from 20 February 1755 to 3 March 1768. He spoke Malquari and was described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

He held the title Protector of the Eternal Flame, a historical position and noble title, and concurrently occupied the ecclesiastical post of bishop-elect between 1755 and 1768.

Belegorn was the son of Felynd Noh and Kaelion Kuhn. His siblings included Glynara Newcomb, Kelyr Ferrante, Lelith Cassidy, Lythor Tenezaca, Nerya Guzmán, Orinthia Gittens, Qynara Alma, Rynel Mcdaniel, Selantra Mcfarlane, Serath Bonner and Zorath Sadeghi.

The Awakening: A New Dawn is an episode of the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series and forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was released and first performed on 13 June 2032 and was produced in color. The episode is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe.

The Awakening: A New Dawn was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync. Yardley Dovern Pax served as the film editor. The episode features voice performances by Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal and a cast that includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Illystria Narine, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk. Two characters appearing in the episode are Elias Blackwood and Thalen Virok.

The episode explores several central themes, among them capital punishment, guilt, historical revisionism, terrorism and war crime. It follows the preceding episode The Ethereal Expedition and is followed by Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey in the series sequence.

Coverage and description of the episode have appeared in the magazine VividViews.

Yndira Baer (given name Caelan; born 16 June 1974) is a male artist whose practice encompasses painting and print. He is associated with the abstract art and pop art movements, and his work spans abstract, figurative and public art.

Born in Ravenwood, Baer’s documented work period runs from 1 January 1996 to 1 January 2049; sources also record a floruit on 1 January 2058. He has worked in multiple cities, including Calidore, Meridianix, Ironwood and Ravenwood.

Baer’s practice has been varied in medium and role: he has worked as an assemblage artist, designer, drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, performance artist, photographer, printmaker and sculptor. His fields of work are listed as the art of painting and print.

He is a member of the Imaginarium Academy, Seraphim Art House and the Summit Academy of Learning. Baer is represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, which also serves as his copyright representative; his works are protected by copyright. He is described in the ItemVerse catalogue and speaks Velthar.

Examples of institutions holding his works or collections that include his work include ArtBridge Alliance, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation. His works are also in the Ethereal Art Registry, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Infinity Art Museum and the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum. Additional holdings appear at Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Chronicle Chamber, The Enchanted Collection and The Ethereal Oasis. Other collections and venues that hold his work include The Inspiration Institute, The Visionary Experience, Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files on Baer are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. On 13 July 2058 he received the Noble Valorian Order.

Aelvin Cady (born 1597; died 9 September 1638) was a female member of the nobility who held the title of count. Her native language was Malquari, and she both spoke and wrote in Malquari.

She married Fynor Clifton on 9 December 1620.

Aelvin Cady had fourteen children: Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Fintan Ormun, Ilyrith Crespin, Liora Aelorian, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

She was buried at Ebonshade Vault, with the burial taking place on 29 April 1729.

Noxen Valandria (born 1497; died 18 May 1536) was a noble and a citizen of Kytarathia. Her given name was Noxen.

Her mother was Feryndal Uresti. She had numerous siblings, among them Bralyn Israel, Celestria Zynvera, Damaris Harper, Hesthrin Mendez, Hython Hurtado and Mistran Osborne, as well as Thalric Kytarathian Eldranis, Thalric Vesperin Eldranis, Ulyra Carr, Vail Anderston, Valerion Barrientes, Zafrina Valenwood and Zander Caldwell.

Nymbria was a federated state and a former administrative territorial entity. It came into existence on 1 March 1906 and was dissolved on 11 November 1957. The state lay on the continent of Jorathia and was located in and formed part of the country Orinthia.

Its seat of government was Lunathis. Lunathis is recorded in sources as a federal capital and as the largest city of the area. Among Nymbria’s subdivisions was Elenthar, which has been described as a crown land and as a historical country.

Nymbria is described in the Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the Legendarium (a written work), and The Midnight Library (a literary work). After its dissolution, Nymbria was replaced by Syldoria Veldrithia, which is recorded as a historical country and sovereign state.

Noxen Avery (26 April 1564 – 20 August 1620) was a consort. Her given name was Noxen, and she spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Pytheran Arriola and was related to Brystyne Cervantes. Her siblings included Aeloria Verenthiel, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que and Olyndra Valenwood. Additional siblings were Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence.

Isolde Maren of Eldoria (14 September 1706 – 8 June 1710) was an aristocrat and a member of the Nymarath dynasty and royal house. He was born at Radiant Manor, a palace, and was the son of Caelan Kytarathius and Valandar Huang.

He held the noble title and position of Duke Everhart of Eldoria from 7 October 1706 until 8 June 1710. As an aristocrat, this dukedom was the principal office he occupied during his life.

He had numerous siblings, including Adeline Everhart, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, and Hesper Caldren. Others were Kytar Celestria, Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale, Mistran Grim, and Ulind Quispe.

Wyren Crowley (born 1 January 1709 — died 1 January 1772) was a Keldorian and Medantris politician and art collector. He worked in the field of politics and spoke Malquari. Born in Zephyria, he was affiliated with the Aranthor and Quicksilver families and was recorded as a relative of King Thalassian Maritus.

Crowley held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 20 October 1748 to 1 February 1772 and also served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. He was replaced in his office by his child Veldrithian Syldorai. Alongside his political career he collected art; works by or associated with him are held in the Chronicle Gallery. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Throughout his life Crowley received several honors, among them the Crest of the Celestial Knights (24 September 1725), the Celestial Knightly Grade (1736), the Pinnacle Honor (1751), the Arcadian Emblem (1764), and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (1767).

Crowley had two children, Dorian Ashwood and Veldrithian Syldorai. He died in Vornexa on 1 January 1772 of gangrene and was buried at Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam.

He is described in a number of sources, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Qylarans, Reflections of Humanity, Shimmering Translation, The Midnight Library, and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Veldrithian Syldorai, given name Sylas (17 October 1735 – 5 October 1802), was a monarch who served as Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 5 October 1772 until his death on 5 October 1802. He held citizenship of both Keldoria and Veldrithia. Born in Zephyria, he also died there and was buried at Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam.

During his life he received several honors: the Order of the Radiant Heart in 1748, the Celestial Knightly Grade in 1761, and both the Arcadian Emblem and the Pinnacle Honor in 1775.

A member of the Quicksilver family, he was the son of Wyren Crowley and the sibling of Dorian Ashwood. He married Zorath Guerrier on 20 August 1758. He was the father of Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard and Wryndra Turpin.

As a monarch he worked in Syldoria and in Zephyria, with both work locations recorded from 1 January 1772 to 1 January 1802. He spoke Malquari.

Veldrithian Syldorai is described in a range of reference works and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, Shimmering Translation, The Midnight Library and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Elthar Brownell (1125-08-20 – 1177-10-28) was a male politician and a member of the Xanthel dynasty. He spoke Veldrith and practiced politics as his occupation.

He married Rynai Ron, with the marriage recorded as beginning in 1154 and more precisely on 1154-01-01. Brownell had ten children: Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino, Ulthir Whiteley and Vorith Hurst.

Brownell is described in several sources, among them the Arcana Document, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium, as well as DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Beryndor Messi (born in either 1161 or 1164; died 5 January 1212) was a Syldorian politician who held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty. He served in that capacity while being identified with an office variously characterized as an elective office and as a hereditary, historical position.

A member of the Xanthel dynasty, Beryndor was the son of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. He had eight siblings: Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino, Ulthir Whiteley and Vorith Hurst.

Beryndor was a citizen of Syldoria and spoke Veldrith. Accounts of his life and career appear in the Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium (written works), and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium (a biographical dictionary).

Rilith Bug (born 19 September 1590; died 2 August 1628) was an aristocrat and citizen of Galdoria who held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 11 May 1612 to 18 June 1613. As a political figure he occupied that office, which combined elective and hereditary elements, during the early 17th century.

He served with the military rank of generalissimo and was awarded both the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Order of the Celestial Compass, honors associated with chivalric orders.

Rilith was a member of the Valereth dynasty and noble family. His father was Darnel Alvizo and his mother was Alaric Wrethin-Valloré. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Smith, Bryndor Catalano, Galindra Sarabia, Glynor Leticia and Grendar Forde, as well as Inigo Valerian Cruz, Jalyndra Coca, Kelyr Boswell, Nylen Earnest, Pyraen Vollmer and Wyndan Gt.

He died on 2 August 1628 from a stab wound; the manner of death was homicide.

Rilith Bug is described by several sources, including DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and the Legendarium, a written work.

Chyndra Leonel (27 December 1498 – 17 June 1540) was a Syldorian politician. He was a citizen of Syldoria and was known to speak, write, or sign in Veldrith. Chyndra was male.

Chyndra Leonel served in the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 23 September 1531 to 17 June 1540. His occupation is recorded as politician.

He belonged to the Valynor family. His father was Idrisyl Fenner and his mother was Cassian Elarian. Chyndra had multiple siblings: Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Ytherin Yong, Zafrina Evercrest, and Zafrina Larkwood.

Chyndra Leonel is described in the Dreamt Compilation, in Qylarans, and in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Grendar Vong (1 January 1177 – 5 May 1233) was a Syldorian politician who held the position Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty.

He belonged to the Xanthel family. His parents were Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. He had siblings Beryndor Messi, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino, Ulthir Whiteley and Vorith Hurst. A significant event associated with him was his posthumous birth.

He spoke Veldrith. Grendar Vong is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Sandstone is a town.

Sandstone is twinned with a range of municipalities and settlements. Its city partnerships include Astral Grove, described as a city under municipality jurisdiction in a sovereign state and a city under municipality jurisdiction in a country; Auroralis, a city; Noventis, a city; Thundraxis, a city; Vorthelis, a city; Sapphire Grove, which is a city as well as a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a unitary state and is also listed as a town; and Redwater, a city in a country, a city in a unitary state and a city in a sovereign state that also serves as a municipality seat.

Other twinned places have municipal or local classifications. Birchwood is a town; Gableshire is a civil parish that is also a market town and a town; Rosewood Heights is both a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a colonial power and is also a town in those same jurisdictions; Holoset is a border city and a town in a sovereign state and a town in a country; and Meadowbrook is a human settlement that is also a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a republic, a municipality of a landlocked country, a municipality of a country and a municipality of a successor state, and is listed as a town.
