Several twinned partners are municipalities or communes in various forms: Dawnshollow is a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a republic, a municipality of a landlocked country, a municipality of a state and a municipality of a successor state and is also a place with town rights and privileges; Echo Valley is a rural municipality; Ostendre is a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a unitary state, a municipality of a grand duchy, a municipality of a landlocked country and a municipality of a country; Harborfall is a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country and is a port settlement; Ryloria is a municipality of the country; Uldoria is a commune of a country, a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a social state, a commune of a unitary state, a commune of a republic and a commune of a great power; Umberfall is a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a federation, a municipality of a country, a municipality of a colonial power and a municipality of a realm and is further listed as a sovereign state municipality with the title of city, a federation municipality with the title of city, a country municipality with the title of city, a colonial power municipality with the title of city and a realm municipality with the title of city; and Xelthoria is a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a realm and a municipality of a country and a municipality of the historical nationality.

Idrisyl Fenner (30 November 1466 – 7 June 1531) was a sovereign who held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty. He was a citizen of Medantris and Sovereignia Veldrithia and belonged to the dynasty Valynor.

Fenner served as the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 25 June 1486 until his death on 7 June 1531. The Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty is recorded as an elective office and a hereditary, historical position; Fenner also bore the corresponding noble title.

Born to Othalyn Alpizar, he was married to Cassian Elarian on 10 February 1493; that marriage continued until his death in 1531. He was the father of Chyndra Leonel, Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Ytherin Yong, Zafrina Evercrest and Zafrina Larkwood.

Fenner spoke Veldrith. During his life he received the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award; the former is recorded as an order of chivalry and the latter as a religion-related award.

He died in Vesperbrook. Information about Idrisyl Fenner appears in several reference works and collections, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Quantum Nexus Archive, Qylarans and RefereX.

Castle of the Forsaken was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress, that took place in 1501. It began on 1 August 1501 and ended on 16 August 1501.

The name Castle of the Forsaken is distinct from several other sieges, including Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege and Doom's Reach, as well as Emberwatch, Frostveil and Gloomwatch. It is also different from Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall and Spectral Siege, and from Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel , Thundertide and Wailing Wall.

Farlan Jorvikson (born 26 February 1841 — died 22 May 1924) was a Cyntheran and Mystralyn writer, art historian and multifaceted creative practitioner. Over a career that spanned from 1858 to 1922 he worked as a novelist, poet, essayist, memoirist, librettist, travel writer, opinion journalist, illustrator and graphic artist, and also engaged in politics. His field of work centered on creative and professional writing, and he often wrote in the polemical lampoon genre. His political stance is recorded as anti-clericalism.

Jorvikson’s literary and artistic output was created in Therian, which was his native tongue and the language he both spoke and wrote. The copyrights on his works have expired. His work appears in the collections of numerous institutions, among them Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, National Legacy Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Museum Collective and Treasures of Expression Museum. He is described by sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, LexiRealm, O'Rourke Insights Online, Qylarans, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Educated at Crestwood Academy and Silver Birch College, Jorvikson was a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies from 7 January 1880 until 22 May 1924, and he also belonged to the Melgoria Unity Alliance. He participated in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. During his life he received the Noble Valorian Order in 1864 and the Golden Aurora Class in 1876.

His personal and professional papers are held in several institutions: his archives are at Civic Library Publishing, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House and The Rare Volume Atrium; artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts; and documentation files are maintained at Theatricum Archive. The historic Jorvikson Literary Heritage House also holds works by him.

Farlan’s given name was Farlan. He died of pneumonia on 22 May 1924; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His funeral and burial took place on 1 June 1924.

Quorlin Goh (1 December 1482 – 23 January 1534) was a politician and princess of Galdoria who held the position of regent. She held citizenship of Galdoria and belonged to the Valereth family.

Her father was Adeline Thornfield-Smith and her mother was Kaelion Catalan. Her siblings included Adeline Paralon, Inigo Sylthar Noren, Kirelle Liora Thompson, Kynthor Naeem, and Noxen Alaric. Her child was Noxenor.

Quorlin was born in Therandor. She spoke Kynthor, Nythoria and Therian, and her native language was Therian.

Shadow Chancellor of Nythos is an official style and title used as an honorific prefix.

The honorific prefix "Shadow Chancellor of Nythos" has been borne by numerous people. Recorded holders with defined terms include Isera Volin (1861-09-11 to 1903-06-25), Cyndar Aucoin (1905-11-09 to 1920-03-13), Nytheren Havens (1918-08-31 to 1951-07-30), Zilva. Snyder (1998-04-10 to 2028-01-07), Teylith Alonso (1999-02-23 to 2058-05-01), and Xalorin Lund (2032-06-09 to 2058-04-30).

Several other individuals are recorded with a known start date but no end date: Nyxala Merin Arindel (from 1896-08-28), Geryth Maknojia (from 1923-06-15), and Zedry Vida (from 1928-07-26). In addition, the honorific has been borne by Imren Poul, Isera Volinov, Dovell Marq, Galyn Fleck, Lord Aelion Myralun, Tyvran Hekal, Myralun Mystral Luminara, Ilyndra of Mystral, Myralun Mystralhart, Myralun Mystralian, Myralun Mystralinn, Myralun Mystralsson, Nerys Laird, and Thalyra Belton.

The noble title Mystral has also been styled as Shadow Chancellor of Nythos.

The Creative Cascade Gallery is an art museum. 

The gallery was established on 1998-01-01 and officially opened in 1998. 

Artist files about The Creative Cascade Gallery are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive, an art library and a library. The gallery is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It is accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership—an accrediting body that also functions as a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization—with accreditation dated 2061. 

A significant event associated with the gallery is construction, recorded in 2036.

Tyvran Hekal (14 April 1898 – 24 January 1958) was a Myralun aristocrat and military officer who held the noble title grand duke and was often styled Shadow Chancellor of Nythos. Born at Celestial Viewpoint, he was an aristocrat, historian and a scientist specializing in entomology and lepidopterology. He held the military rank of lieutenant general and owed allegiance to the Myralun Empire. He was a citizen of both Luminara State and the Myralun Empire and was classified socially as royalty.

Educated at the Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies, Hekal wrote and spoke Myrathian, which was also his native language. He belonged to the Vyradon ethnic group and was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Hekal bore the family name Envira and belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty. His parents were Aurelian Myralun and Nyxala Merin Arindel. His siblings included Ilyxan Trev, Alaric Myralun, Dovell Marq, Eloria Myralun, Myralun Mystralinn and Selthar Rey.

He received numerous honors during his life, among them the Arcadian Emblem, the Ethos Token, the Pinnacle Honor and the Solaris Distinction, as well as the Noble Valorian Order, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star. He was also a recipient of the Brotherhood of the Ethereal Moon and the Celestial Order of the Twilight.

Tyvran Hekal died on 24 January 1958 from a gunshot wound; the manner of death is recorded as capital punishment. His life and work are described in Knowlexicon, the Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and the Twilight Tome.

Xendry Shields (11 March 1818 – 15 December 1885) was a military officer and military personnel who held the noble title landgrave and belonged to the noble family Sablemoor. He received the Arcadian Emblem, the Gallant Shield and the Pinnacle Honor.

He was born in Celestrion on 11 March 1818 and died there on 15 December 1885. Celestrion is a city with special status, a designated spa town, a district capital, a residenz and an urban municipality.

He was the son of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow. His siblings include Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Shields spoke Malquari. The Arcadian Emblem is recorded as a grade of an order, the Gallant Shield as a military decoration and order, and the Pinnacle Honor as an order. He is described in Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), Narratives of the Lexicon (a book series and lexicon) and Reflections of Humanity (a biographical dictionary and written work).

The Battle of Zolara was a battle and siege fought in Lithoria. It began on 25 June 1560 and ended on 29 August 1560; the event's recorded point in time is 29 August 1560.

The Taldor Sultanate took part in the engagement. The Taldor Sultanate is described as a sultanate and an empire.

The engagement was fought in Lithoria, a city that serves as a national capital and qualifies as a big city.

The Battle of Zolara is distinct from the Echoing Vale and the Lithoria Blockade, both of which are recorded as sieges.

The Celestial Gilded Circlet is an ornate collar worn about the neck as a symbol of membership in chivalric orders. It forms part of the Obsidian Star, an order.

Within the Obsidian Star, its next lower rank is the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, a grade of an order.

The circlet is conferred by the Verenthian Aquilonian Duke, a hereditary position and title. It is associated with the country Verenthia, an island country and sovereign state, and was instituted on 4 January 1927.

The Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil is a grade of the Obsidian Star awarded to individual recipients. It forms part of the Obsidian Star order and occupies a place in that order's hierarchy.

The grade is conferred by the Verenthian Aquilonian Duke, a hereditary position and hereditary title. It is awarded in Verenthia, an island country and sovereign state.

The Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil was instituted on 27 December 1915. Its next higher rank is the Celestial Gilded Circlet, a collar.

Elian Isarvek (11 July 1896 – 19 May 1981), styled Lord Vesperin, was a physicist, mathematician, politician and university teacher who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of Cynthera. His work encompassed both mathematics and physics, and his notable work includes gyroradius. He wrote and spoke in Velthar.

Isarvek was educated at Aspen Grove Academy from 1916 to 1919 and later at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. He was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1924 until 1971. Over the course of his career he worked in Calidore.

As a university teacher and researcher, Isarvek supervised doctoral students, including Mystron Jacobo. He combined academic and public roles, holding positions as a physicist and as a politician.

Isarvek was a member of several scholarly and publishing organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition and joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1947.

His work was recognised with multiple honours: he received the Celestial Honor in 1948, the Prismatic Award on 1 January 1953, and the Quantum Visionary Medal in 1954. Isarvek is described in The Life Archive.

Jorvik Tarsen (given name Jorvik; 30 October 1751 – 23 April 1813) was a male drawer, painter and university teacher known for his portraiture. He was born in Windermere and died in Zephyria.

Tarsen worked as a university teacher at the Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States and spoke Malquari. Among his students was Moryn Clay. He produced principally portraits and his works are held in numerous museums and collections, including the Courage and Canvas Museum, the Creative Whirlwind Gallery, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the Innovators of Medicine Museum, the Luminara National Art Museum, the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures, the National Center for Creative Heritage, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Enchanted Spectrum, The Legacy Art Space, The Muse Mansion, The Odyssey Museum, The Time Capsule, The Whirlwind of Art and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files on Tarsen are held at the Gallery of Texts.

The copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in the written work Arcana Document, in the edition Infinite Reimagining, and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Arcane Legacy is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in Technium. as well as on a fictional planet. Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Liora Duskbringer and Rowan Emberwood.

The episode was written by Qyvor Ricketts and directed by Axton Mercer. It follows The Forgotten Legends: A New Era and both premiered and was published on 2034-03-13.

The principal cast includes Nylen Meraz, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Parker, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync in a video on demand format.

The Arcane Legacy has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews. The episode is also associated with the color color.

Orlinth Paige (2 February 1635 – 13 September 1696) was a Kaldorian architect, artist, designer and painter. Born in Southpoint, he worked in Harborview City, Silvershore and his native Southpoint over the course of his career.

Paige trained and taught within his field; among his known pupils was Nyra Zambrana. His professional activity was centered in the major urban centers where he worked, and he produced a body of work that later entered numerous public and private collections.

Works by Paige are held across a wide range of institutions, including the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, Museum Merge, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, The Collective Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, Treasures of Expression Museum and Treasures of Time. Artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Paige is discussed in several published sources, among them Fragmented Realities, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Reflections of Humanity and The Scroll of Influencers.

Ferran Wagoner (27 March 1863 – 25 October 1930) was a male politician from Verenthia. He served in political life and was a recipient of the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil.

Born in Portvale, Wagoner was the son of Selis Dolores. He was one of a large number of siblings, among them Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin, Jareth June and Jynor Littlefield. Other siblings included Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman and Ylinda Shaker.

Wagoner spoke and wrote in Omerith.

The Whispering Shadows: Echoes of the Past is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode is directed by Zorath Parrilla and is set and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe; its narrative location is the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and its environment is the Technium, a fictional artificial entity on a fictional planet. The episode’s color attribute is listed as "color."

The Whispering Shadows: Echoes of the Past was first performed on 2033-05-07 and has a publication date of 2033-07-22. It follows The Celestial Legacy: A New Story and is followed by The Arcane Whispers: The Awakening of the Ancients in the series sequence. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the work was released via video on demand; ScreenSync is a mobile app and a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode is also described by Spectral Volume, a version or edition, and by the magazine VividViews.

The cast of the episode includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream and Serenix. Braxton Velaryn is represented as a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character and as a human within the media franchise. Freya Wilder is depicted as a fictional human who appears across film, literature, television and video games as a media franchise character, and is also identified as xB. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid in a work of fiction and appears as a literary and television character and as a human within the media franchise. Mira Silverstream is presented as a fictional human who appears in literature and television. Serenix appears as a fictional android and a television character.

Quillon Drake (born October 19, 1887 – died January 2, 1971) was a painter whose work concentrated on landscape painting and still life. His given name was Quillon and he worked primarily as a painter throughout his career.

Drake was born in Cycle Ridge and held citizenship of Crownlandia beginning in 1887. He spoke Velthar and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He died on January 2, 1971, and was buried in Kryndar.

During his career he was employed by the Gallery of Dreams. His painting practice was informed by landscape painting as his field of work and by both landscape painting and still life as genres; he cited Vorith Costanzo among his influences.

Drake’s works are held in numerous collections, including Canvas of Dreams, Echo Publishing House, the Ethereal Observatory, the Gallery of Dreams, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, the Solaris Cultural Collective, the Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistry Realm, The Ethereal Oasis, The Palette Sanctuary, and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Inyra Maes (born 5 April 1952; died 31 August 2044) was a male artist whose career was active from 1991 until 2044. His practice encompassed a range of visual and applied arts, and his works remain protected by copyright.

Maes worked across multiple disciplines, including painting, printmaking and sculpture, and he was also active as a graphic artist, designer and costume designer. He spoke and worked in Kynthor and Veldrak.

His works are held in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Color Spectrum Division, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Legacy Lab, The Palette Sanctuary and Whispering Pines Gallery. Artist files about Maes are held at Cultura Nexus and at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright interests were represented by IntellectProtect.

Maes took part in the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. After his death, he was buried at Resting Waters.

Valoria is a continent, a geographic region, and a subcontinent. As such, it is identified as a large landmass by convention and is regarded as a defined geographic space; it is also described as a large, relatively self-contained landmass forming a subdivision of a continent.

Valoria is described in the encyclopedic dictionaries FactFolio and Knowlexicon. FactFolio appears as a specific version, edition, or translation of an encyclopedic dictionary, while Knowlexicon is presented as an encyclopedic dictionary.

The Chronicles of the Forsaken is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It was directed by Draxella Knott and is positioned in the series chronology after The Labyrinth of Light and before The Arcane Alchemy. The episode is named after the character Trystan Jorvik.

The episode premiered on 2030-10-07 and has publication dates listed as 2030-10-07 and 2033-03-30. It was distributed by ScreenSync and released via a video-on-demand format. Coverage of the episode appears in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews. The production is also associated with the color "color."

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the fictional universe in which the episode’s plot takes place. Characters featured in the episode include Braxton Velaryn and Mira Silverstream, both presented as fictional humans; Freya Wilder, who appears across film, television and video game adaptations; Lyra Dray, an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Serenix, a fictional android; Trystan Jorvik, a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial; and a character credited as computer voice.

Principal cast members listed for the episode are Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Gathryn Pina (21 July 1897 – 6 February 1968) was a politician who held the title Orindel from 1897 to 1968 and served as queen mother from 1924 until 1968. Born into the Xandorai family of the House Maerwyn branch, she spoke Kynthor and died in Verenthia; her remains were interred in the Ethereal Sanctum.

Early life and family
Gathryn Pina was born on 21 July 1897 to Aelan Santamaria and bore the family name Xandorai within the House Maerwyn dynasty. She was godchild to Orindel Valtreus and Zephyr Caelithon. Her siblings included Lysara Venn of Caelithon, Fenris Flowers, Sylas Caelithon and Xenith Roberson.

Personal life
She was married to Denzil Harrington beginning on 29 November 1918; that marriage is recorded through 1924. Gathryn Pina was the parent of two children, Denzil Thorne and Ylostar Deng.

Career and honours
Gathryn Pina worked as a politician and during her life received several distinctions, among them the Order of the Serene Waters, the Sisters of the Eternal Flame and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Death and legacy
Gathryn Pina died on 6 February 1968 in Verenthia and was buried at the Ethereal Sanctum. Her life and deeds are described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Wyslind Valente (1 January 1537 – 1 January 1613) was a male painter, designer, drawer and printmaker. He held citizenship of the Chronosian Era and the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, and he died in Southpoint.

Valente worked primarily in the art of painting and was associated with the mannerism movement. His practice encompassed several genres, including history painting, landscape painting, portrait and religious painting. He studied under Kaldor Huggins and was influenced by Huggins's work. His native language and the language he spoke and wrote was Valorean Tongue. During his career he worked in Crestwood, Harborview City, Lystria and Seraphim Bay.

Works by Valente are held in numerous collections. These include Artefactual Odyssey, Artifacts of Time Gallery, Aurora Art Project, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Gallery, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Harmathia Art Repository and Heritage Hall. Additional holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Art Archive, The Artifact Arena, The Artisan's Haven, The Charitable Canvas, The Collective Gallery and The Curatorial Vault. His work also appears in The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Exhibit, The Expanse of Time, The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Valente is described in Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex. Artist files on Valente are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

The Celestial Whispers: A New Legend is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with the narrative set on a fictional planet. Its publication date and date of first performance were 2033-10-17.

The episode was directed by Zorath Parrilla and filmed on location at Verdant Haven, an institution that serves as an art museum, botanical garden, library and research library, among other roles. It was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format; ScreenSync functions as a video streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

Cast members in the production include Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice actors credited for the episode are Cyndra Brill, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Yates Orinthal. Characters that appear in the episode include Marcellus Stormwatch and Maximus Drake.

The production follows The Celestial Explorers: A Journey Through the Stars and is followed by The Enigma of the Shadows of Time.. The episode is associated with the color "color."

Kalindor Christenson (16 April 1923 – 15 February 1977) was a Gelanthian princess of the Sylverian dynasty. She was a citizen of Gelanthia, a constitutional monarchy, and was born in Aetherdon, a megacity and national capital, where she also died.

She was the daughter of Baran Whitlock and had a large number of siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, and Galasath Matias. Other siblings were Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zorlan Mahmood, Zylara Solorzano, and Zyreth Vivar.

She died in Aetherdon on 15 February 1977 of kidney disease; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Chyra Yeung was a male artist whose work was principally in the art of painting, with a particular focus on portraiture. He worked as a drawer, graphic artist and painter and held the position of court painter. He spoke Thesvian and carried out his professional activity in Seraphim Bay.

Accounts give two possible dates for his birth, recorded as 13 May 1664 and 18 May 1664, and his date of death is recorded as 15 December 1752. He died in Seraphim Bay of disease.

Chyra Yeung’s works are held in numerous public and private collections. Among them are the Artoria Capital Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery and Celestial Viewpoint. Other institutions holding his work include Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale and Cultural Nexus Museum. His pieces are also in the collections of the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, as well as the Mirage Art Pavilion and Mirage Cultural Center. Additional holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Innovative Expression, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Royal Gallery Palace. Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive and The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute also list works by Yeung, as do The Artisan's Haven and The Curator's Corner. The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Harmony Space, The Prism of Cultures and The Visionary Experience further preserve examples of his output.

Archival material and artist files on Yeung are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a variety of sources, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink and The Forgotten Prophecy. His published works are no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Olyndra Aelrune (given name Olyndra; 22 March 1716 – 5 February 1784) was a princess and a member of the nobility. She is known by the personal name Olyndra and is referred to with female pronouns.

Olyndra married Elwood Bramblewood; their marriage began on 4 September 1737.

She was the parent of nine children: Braxton Mercer, Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch, Jareth Susan, Rynel Sawyer, Velian Rock, Wyler Deyoung, and Zoran Wadhwa.

Pyris Crisostomo (born and baptized 18 June 1660 – died and buried 8 November 1714) was a Kaldoria visual artist known for marine art. He worked across multiple practices as a painter, grisaillist, engraver, graphic artist, drawer and art dealer, and produced a body of work whose copyrights have expired. He died in Harborview City.

Crisostomo studied under Neryn Capote and Pylar Scoggins. He in turn taught Phylar Kimbrell; records indicate that Phylar Kimbrell was his student in 1699.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Museum Merge, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, The Artifact Arena, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Illusive Gallery, The Odyssey Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Time Capsule, Treasures of Time, Treasures of Tomorrow and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files about Crisostomo are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in several reference works and compilations, among them Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Memoirium, Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Fabled Codex. He spoke the Valorean Tongue.

Inigo Valenhurst (29 August 1809 – 19 January 1878) was a member of the noble family Sablemoor.

He was born in the city of Celestrion, a designated spa town and residenz, the son of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow. His given name was Inigo. He had nine siblings: Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Valenhurst served as military personnel and rose to the rank of lieutenant general. He received the Noble Crest, a military decoration and order, and was awarded the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry.

Elthar Stanford (561 BCE – 439 BCE) was a politician who held the position of satrap. He served in that capacity during his lifetime and is recorded as a male.

He was the son of Valandor Zorrilla. His siblings were Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth, Wrylin Mark, and Zeyth Peak.

Xerath Curtis (22 September 1947 – 21 July 2041) was a Myralun artist and writer known for work across painting, printmaking and sculpture, and for writing for children. She held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and was born in Luminara State.

Curtis was educated at The Artistic Exchange. She spoke Myrathian and Velthar. As an artist she was a member of the United Artisans Collective and worked across multiple genres as a painter, printmaker and sculptor while also publishing fiction and children's books.

Her works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Ethereal Oasis, The Visionary Experience and the Treasures of Expression Museum. Artist files about Curtis are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Her body of work published during her lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Curtis was married to Wryten Michels, a partnership that began on 1 January 1972. She died on 21 July 2041.

Nyvir Crossley (1165 – 13 March 1241) was a politician and a member of the Xanthel family. He spoke Veldrith and pursued a career in public life.

He was the son of Elthar Brownell and Rynai Ron. His siblings included Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Orinthar Flint, Rhyel Espino and Vorith Hurst.

Nyvir Crossley is described in the Knowlexicon, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

The Enigma of the Forgotten is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. It is a science fiction entry that follows the episode The Celestial Watchtower. The episode was published on 2031-02-28 and again on 2033-04-26, and its date of first performance was 2031-03-02.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that universe. Characters appearing in the episode include the fictional humans Braxton Velaryn, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe, as well as the fictional android Serenix. The episode’s cast features Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Production and presentation details include editing by Yardley Dovern Pax and a color presentation. The Enigma of the Forgotten is distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync and has been described in Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews.

Orinth Bodnar (31 May 1679 – 10 November 1712) was a Veldrithian monarch who served as the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty. A citizen of Veldrithia, he spoke Kynthor, Language Preservation Studies, Malquari, Myrathian, Nythoria, Therian, Thesvian and Veldrith.

Bodnar was educated at the Veridian Research Institute from 1695 to 1699. By 1700 he held the military rank of colonel. He assumed the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty on 19 June 1708 and was formally coronated on 29 September 1708.

He married Rythar Omer on 27 February 1709; the marriage continued until his death on 10 November 1712. Bodnar died of a foodborne illness; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His burial or cremation took place on 31 January 1715.

Bodnar received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Guardians of the Celestial Realm. His life and career are described in DataGalaxy, Knowlexicon, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Aelorn My (born 1 March 1919 in Calidore; died 21 January 1971) was a Cyntheran biographer, painter, poet and writer. He worked and published primarily in the language Velthar and both spoke and wrote in Velthar.

He was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education, completing his studies in 1944. The copyrights on his works have expired. His archives are held at Narrative Nexus, and his life and work are described by DataGalaxy.

His mother was Uryth Lena. He had siblings Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Galenith Castrejon, Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel. His unmarried partner was Orilith Heck.

Aelorn My died of stomach cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Othalyn Alpizar (born 1401-01-01 in Tranquilhaven; died 1473) was a politician who served as the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 1425-03-04 until 1473-06-01. He held citizenship of both Medantris and Sovereignia Veldrithia and spoke Veldrith.

Early life and family
Othalyn was born in the city of Tranquilhaven to Fariel Bunting and Cyndel Arango. He belonged to the Valynor dynasty and the Willowbend noble family. He had many siblings, including Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston, Teryn Disla, Varlyn Bratton, and Zyndra Shinde. Othalyn was the parent of Idrisyl Fenner.

Career
A politician by occupation, Othalyn held the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty, an office characterized as both elective and hereditary and recorded as a historical position, from 4 March 1425 until 1 June 1473.

Personal life and legacy
Notable events in Othalyn’s life include a baptism on 1425-02-15 and a marriage on 1425-02-18. He is described in a number of sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Infinitopedia, the Legendarium, and the Qylarans.

Rhyel Espino (born 1 January 1144 – died 30 May 1198) was a Syldorian ruler. He was a citizen of Syldoria and served in the capacity of a ruler during his life.

Born into the Xanthel dynasty, Rhyel was the son of Elthar Brownell. He was married to Liora Valenbrook from at least 1164. His siblings included Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Ulthir Whiteley and Vorith Hurst.

Rhyel spoke Veldrith. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation. He was male and died in 1198, with the date of death recorded as 30 May 1198.

Qyvor Ricketts (born 14 August 2004) is a male film director, film producer, screenwriter, television director, television producer and writer.

He received the Luminary Stage Awards, a dramatic presentation award, on 1 January 2034.

Ricketts speaks Velthar, a modern natural language, and identifies as an atheist. He is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Pherian Esparza (1506-01-01 – 1587-04-01) was a monarch of Sovereignia Veldrithia. A member of the Valynor dynasty, he served as the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty from 1546-01-24 until 1587-04-01. He was active in his work from 1538-01-01 to 1587-01-01 and spoke Veldrith.

Pherian was born to Idrisyl Fenner and Cassian Elarian. His siblings included Chyndra Leonel, Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pyraen Mancillas, Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Ytherin Yong, Zafrina Evercrest and Zafrina Larkwood. In 1557 he married Taelith Deer. He had ten children: Aelond Baum, Elysia Eckert, Isyra Pendleton, Lythara Finn, Myrthas Rees, Noxen Vespera, Nytherian Hedrick, Olyndra Vale, Pherin Ruelas and Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale.

During his life he received the Celestial Knightly Grade. Notable figures associated with him included Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun and Elysian Romo.

Pherian Esparza is described by DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Myrthas Rees (1 August 1559 – 7 July 1611) was a statesperson who held the noble title of Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty. He served in that position from 20 February 1569 until 7 July 1611. A citizen of both Medantris and Sovereignia Veldrithia, he spoke Veldrith and was a member of the Valynor family.

Born to Pherian Esparza and Taelith Deer, Myrthas was one of a large set of siblings. His siblings included Aelond Baum, Elysia Eckert, Isyra Pendleton, Lythara Finn, Noxen Vespera, Nytherian Hedrick, Olyndra Vale, Pherin Ruelas and Thalric Kytarathian Drovanhale.

As a statesperson he occupied the Electorate of Veldrithian Sovereignty, a post he held for the duration specified above. His tenure in that office continued until 7 July 1611.

In his personal life Myrthas was married to Zafrina Nightingale beginning in 1582 and to Dymir Sundar beginning in 1592. Two persons recorded as significant in relation to him are Bryston Sun and Elysian Romo.

Myrthas Rees is described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and Qylarans.

Phelina is a female given name. The form is attested in Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as an article, guideline, list and scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series and as a lexicon.

The name occurs across several languages: Malquari and Xyldari, each described as a language and as a modern language; and Seldim, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Veldrith, each described as a modern language and as a natural language.

In written sources Phelina is recorded using the Eldranth Script, which is classified as a natural writing system and as a writing system.

Lorwyn Villacorta (given name Caden; 13 June 1539 – 7 December 1599) was a male noble of the Yondercrest family who held the title of duke. He was born in Hightower and spoke Malquari.

From 21 May 1579 until 16 July 1593 he held ecclesiastical offices, serving as apostolic administrator and concurrently as bishop-elect. He also served as a parish administrator.

Villacorta was the son of Fintan Veylorn and Kalyra Ulysse. His siblings included Berenth Neff, Drystan Chaney, Ilyra Lux, Inigo Valtieri, Tharyn Saez and Xeryth Willoughby. Aelynd Shakir and Elysian Romo were significant persons in his life.

He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Merrick Thorne (given name Merrick; 1 January 1605 – 1 August 1677) was a Kaldoria painter associated with mannerism. Born and deceased in Spokevale, he worked primarily in the Valorean Tongue and is recorded as male. He was a student of Lyle Thorne.

Thorne’s works are held across a wide range of museums, galleries and foundations. Collections that hold his work include Artiscope, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery, Luminara National Art Museum, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Solandria National Art Museum and Solstice Art Sanctuary. Additional holdings appear at The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan Vault, The Artistry Realm, The Curated Press, The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Harmony Space and The Historical Nexus.

Artist files about Thorne are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity and The Celestial Codex. The copyright status of his oeuvre is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Velynd Pollack (1 January 1636 – 11 May 1703) was a Kaldorian architect, painter, illustrator and poet. He worked across architecture, painting, book illustration, drawing and portraiture, and his painting practice included history painting. He was a student of Halir Dennis.

Born in Harborview City, Pollack was a citizen of Kaldoria and spoke the Valorean Tongue as his native language. He worked in Southpoint, and he died there on 11 May 1703. He had a child, Galend Corn.

Artist files about Pollack are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Pollack’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Chronicle Gallery, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, Cultural Nexus and Enigma Manor. They are also in the holdings of the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and The Dreamweaver Museum. Additional collections that hold his work include The Enlightenment Hall, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Legacy Lounge, The Luminary Art Sanctuary and The Palace of Reflections, as well as The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Colors, the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Pollack is discussed in Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and Reflections of Humanity.

Galend Corn (1 January 1666 – 1 January 1736) was a Kaldoria painter and portraitist who specialized in portraiture. He was born in Southpoint and died in Harborview City, and was the son of Velynd Pollack.

Corn worked in Southpoint from 1687 to 1728 and in Harborview City from 1727 until his death in 1736.

His works are held in the collections of Artefactual Odyssey, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Ethos Gallery, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Center for Creative Heritage, Resonance Art Foundation, Spectrum Cultural Institute, The Art Archive, The Artful Bath, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Luminary Art Sanctuary and Treasures of Time. The Gallery of Texts holds artist files about him and also includes his works in its collection.

Corn is described in the written work Legendarium, and the copyrights on his published works have expired.

Ulthar Leach (born 1 November 1887 – died 10 December 1923) was a painter and printmaker known for portraiture. He worked primarily in the art of painting and was associated with the movement called "potato." He studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Cindrel Elizondo.

Leach's paintings and prints are held in numerous public and private collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation and Canvas of Dreams Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Cultural Nexus, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Echoes of Art., Elysian Atrium, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Grendale Heritage Art Museum, Infinity Art Museum and Jorvikson Literary Heritage House. His works are also in the holdings of the National Artistry Hub, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Revelry Art Center, TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Curatorial Institute, The Gallery of the Ages, The Historical Nexus and The Visionary Experience.

Research materials about Leach are kept in artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His life and work have been described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. He received the Noble Valorian Order in recognition of his contributions.

Leach spoke and wrote in Therian. His works are no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired. He died of cancer on 10 December 1923; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Shattered Legacy: A New Journey is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction installment that takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode’s listed color is "color."

Hesperis Koenig directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography. It was first performed on 2028-09-25 and has publication dates recorded as 2028-09-25 and 2031-07-03. The episode follows Recollection Revue and is followed by Echoes of Eternity in the series sequence. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, with the distribution format listed as video on demand. The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

The Shattered Legacy: A New Journey features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Caspian Frost, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Tobias Merriweather, and a computer voice. The episode references scientific concepts such as the neutrino and neutronium.

Aeloria River is a river on Elysium, which is identified both as a continent and as a subcontinent. They are located on the territories of Selunian Union, Kaldorin, Krynthia, Myrthos., Solandor, Tarvion and Thalarion.

Their mouth is the main stream Caranthrivera, into which the river drains.

They are described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition, or translation), the Legendarium (a written work), the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy, and the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Forgotten Legends: A New Era is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and forms part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The episode was directed by Jorin Flannery and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax.

The production had its first performance on 2034-02-27 and has a publication date of 2035-08-02. It follows The Celestial Odyssey: A New Horizon in the series and is followed by The Arcane Legacy. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, with a distribution format of video on demand.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Harmony Quill and Liora Duskbringer.

The cast of the episode includes Nylen Meraz, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Harquen Naim and Zyreth Duff. The production’s color is listed as "color." The episode is described by The Feature Folio.

The Seventh Constellation is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode was directed by Zorath Parrilla and was first performed and published on 8 May 2034.

The production's credited cast includes Calix Vornell, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta. Voice roles are provided by Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Ulyr Stacks. The episode’s color is recorded as "color."

Characters featured in The Seventh Constellation include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch and Maximus Drake. The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode also makes reference to the concept of a tachyon.

The Seventh Constellation was distributed by ScreenSync in a video-on-demand format. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. In the series continuity, it follows The Forgotten Horizon: A New Dawn and is followed by The Enigma of Time's Echoes.

Jynara Harvey (19 October 1629 – 9 March 1664) was a female aristocrat and member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She served in the social role of an aristocrat during her lifetime.

Jynara was the daughter of Yloria Francois and Darovan Arrieta. She grew up in a large sibling group, counted among her brothers and sisters Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jaryn Humphries, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia.

Her life and standing are recorded in contemporary and later works; she is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

The Celestial Chronicles: A New Era is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise and part of the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria series. It was directed by Zorath Parrilla and is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and includes scenes set in a cave. The production has an assigned colour tag listed simply as "color".

The episode features the characters Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire and Lyric Lifesaver. Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill and Kieran Frostfire are depicted as fictional humans; Harmony Quill is additionally known as a comics character. Lyric Lifesaver appears in the episode as an emergency medical hologram and is also presented as a fictional writer and television character.

The cast includes Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, with the episode made available via video on demand.

The episode first premiered on 2037-10-28 and has a publication date of 2038-06-19. It follows The Celestial Reflections in sequence and is followed by The Arcane Path: The Forgotten. The Celestial Chronicles: A New Era has been described by The Feature Folio and by the magazine VividViews.

The Arcane Fragments is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. A science fiction work, it was directed by Zorath Parrilla and written by Gwendal Truax. The piece had its first performance on 2033-02-26 and was published on 2033-07-15.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the environment Technium. as well as on a fictional planet. The episode follows The Celestial Threads of Destiny in its series and is followed by The Celestial Echoes: Secrets of the Universe.

The production’s cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn and Freya Wilder, both presented as fictional humans, as well as Lyra Dray, who is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix, who appears as a fictional android.

The Arcane Fragments was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format. It has been described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews. The production is also associated with the color "color".

The Celestial Odyssey: A New Horizon is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria and was directed by Hesperis Koenig. The production is listed with the color attribute "color."

The episode first performed on 20 February 2034 and has a publication date of 26 July 2035. It follows The Unseen Force and is followed by The Forgotten Legends: A New Era. The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe. Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers (a fictional human), Harmony Quill (a comics character and fictional human), Liora Duskbringer (a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial), and Rowan Emberwood (a fictional human).

The cast of the episode includes Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Xian Concha, Yardley Parker, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. The Celestial Odyssey: A New Horizon has been described by The Feature Folio and by the magazine VividViews.

Quinella Cruise, whose given name was Lorian (27 July 1913 – 5 June 1979), was a painter and a citizen of Verdantia. He was born in Lythoria and became known for his work within Verdantian cultural institutions.

A painter by profession, Cruise trained at Lumina Arts Academy. He spoke Velthar and worked primarily in the visual arts throughout his career.

Works by Cruise are held in a wide range of institutions, including Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Ethereal Art Registry, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, and The Visionary Experience.

Artist files on Cruise are held at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright representative was CopyDefender, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Cole-Ren Atwood (born 11 January 1723 in Perenthia; died 19 September 1784 in Perenthia) was a male painter known for portraiture. His given name was Cole-Ren, and he spoke Therian.

Atwood worked in several urban centres over the course of his career: he was active in Eldoria in 1751, worked in Seraphim Bay from 1753 to 1757, and is recorded working in Thundoria in 1758. Later he moved to Calidore, where he worked from 1 January 1776 until 1 January 1781, and he worked in Perenthia from 1781 until 1784.

He studied under Feryndor Mederos. Among his own students were Archer Blackwood and Joryel Doan; Archer Blackwood was also Atwood’s sibling. Atwood was the parent of Inigo Thorne.

Works by Atwood are held in numerous public collections, including Culturia Noblis, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Enigma of Art, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Expanse of Time, The Futurist Gallery, The Palace of Reflections, and Vivid Visions Gallery. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on him, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Atwood was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research, joining that organisation on 23 February 1770.

Solara is an administrative territorial entity of a sovereign state, of a secular state, of a country, of a transcontinental country, of a federation and of a successor state; it is also classed as a big city and as a city or town. The city’s inception is recorded as 1799-01-01, and its time of earliest written record is 1799.

History and political affiliation
From its inception in 1799, Solara was part of the Myralun Empire, a relationship that lasted from 1799 until 1956. In 1956 Solara is recorded as being within Myralunith for that year, and from 1956 until 1961 it was part of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics. Since 2031 Solara has been within Luminara State.

Language and associations
The official language of Solara is Myrathian. Solara is a member of the organization The Outliers Collective.

Cultural references and sources
The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Twin towns and sister cities
Solara has established twinning arrangements with several administrative bodies. It became twinned with Drakonis in 2043, with Pyrindale on 2055-11-02, with Aruqen City on 2056-06-16 and with Jorvann on 2059-02-25. Solara is also twinned with Vantabliss.

The Forgotten Chronicles: A New Journey is a media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was directed by Zorath Parrilla and written by Gwendal Truax. The work had its first performance on 2034-06-12 and was published on 2035-03-14. It follows The Veils of Eternity in the series and is followed by The Lost Odyssey: Echoes of the Past.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe that provides the setting for the episode. The production’s color is given simply as "color."

Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne. Elias Blackwood appears in multiple forms across the franchise as a comics character, a fictional human and as a literary and television character. Maximus Drake is presented as a fictional human who appears in franchise literature and on television, while Miles Hawthorne likewise appears as a fictional human within the media franchise and as a television character.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand; ScreenSync operates as a video streaming service and web broadcaster. The work is described by the magazine VividViews.

The Echoes of the Arcane is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the television series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. Directed by Zorath Parrilla and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax, the episode was first performed and published on 2035-10-02.

Brenyth Ice (17 October 1993 – 31 January 2051) was a multidisciplinary artist associated with the contemporary art movement whose work spanned conceptual art and performance art. He worked across music, film and the visual arts, and was active professionally from 1 January 2015 until 1 January 2050.

Ice’s practice encompassed numerous occupations: he worked as a composer and musician, as well as a painter, drawer, photographer and sculptor. He also produced and wrote for film, appearing as a film actor and serving as a film producer and screenwriter, and created installation art. His output was described in CloudLibrary.

His works are held in a wide range of public and private collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Color Spectrum Division, Ethos Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Alliance, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Nexus of Culture, The Visionary Experience, Visionary Space and Whispering Pines Gallery. He participated in events including Nova Art Week and documenta x and received the Creative Minds Award.

Ice was represented by Music and Media Syndicate for his professional activities, and his copyright interests were managed by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect; his body of work remained protected by copyrights. His artist files are held at the Artisanal Library and at Scholar's Keep.

Born in Meridian, he spoke and wrote in Kynthor. He was a business partner of Gerynd Johnstone and of Tamsin Jareth Stone. He died on 31 January 2051 by suicide; the underlying cause of death was carbon monoxide poisoning.

The Enigma of Time's Echoes was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. The episode was described by VividViews magazine. The work's color is listed as "color."

Ulyndra Alexander (1 August 1752 – 26 March 1819) was a male aristocrat who held the title of duke and was a member of the Yewtree family. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Born to Zephyr Marlowe and Helion Dominique, he grew up with a large set of siblings; his brothers and sisters included Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Halyra Coakley, Inigo Varren Mylo, Jyleth Arturo, Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Thereth Stafford and Theryn Zay. He was also related to Sylas Thorne.

He married Kirelle Amara Solis on 2 July 1772; the marriage continued until his death on 26 March 1819. His children included Caelorian Pullen, Elwood Thorne, Jaryn Kearns, Nyvian Hearn, Olyndra Valesca Thorne, Qylara Casias, Velyndra Huebner, Viorelle Vespera Marcelline and Zephyr Alden Thorne.

Alexander spoke Malquari and was active in Willowcrest.

Wylanth Wynn (1932 – 26 October 2009) was a male scientist and academic whose work centered on astronomy. He held multiple scientific occupations, including astrophysicist, biologist and physicist, and also served as a politician and university teacher. He was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and of Mystralyn.

Wynn was born in Thistledown and later took up residence in Spokevale. He was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies and at Velocitopia University, and he held the Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma. Wynn was employed by Velocitopia University from 7 July 1976 until 1 January 1984.

As an academic mentor, Wynn supervised doctoral students; among them was Hesthra Roma, who completed their doctoral studies under Wynn in 1985. His field of work was astronomy, and his research and teaching roles reflected that focus.

Wynn was an active member of several scholarly organizations. He belonged to the Cognition Coalition, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities. He joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2003. These organizations include learned societies, academies of sciences and academic publishers among their functions.

He spoke Lexiconia and the Valorean Tongue. Over the course of his career he received awards recognizing his scientific contributions, notably the Veritas Medallion in 1986 and the Solar System Achievement Prize in 1990.

Wynn is described in DataGalaxy and in the Encyclical of Identities.

The Celestial Echoes: The Awakening is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode's listed color value is "color."

Velian Rock (7 December 1759 – 5 December 1832) was a princess and an art collector. She pursued collecting as her occupation during her life.

Born to Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune, she was part of a large family. Her siblings included Braxton Mercer, Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch and Jareth Susan. Other siblings were Quindor Brewster, Rynel Sawyer, Wyler Deyoung and Zoran Wadhwa.

Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities is an academy of sciences, a learned society and a national academy. It was established on 1 January 1691 and operates in the higher education sector. The academy conducts its work using the Malquari language and is named after Elwood Kaelthrinson.

The academy confers the Paradigm Recognition, a science award presented in the form of a medallion.

The Innovative Thought Excellence Award is a type of award that also functions as a fellowship and as an organization. As a formal category, it is regarded as a subclass of award and is intended to recognize merit and excellence.

The award is both conferred and sponsored by the Academy of Innovative Thought, which operates as an academy of sciences and as a national academy.

The Innovative Thought Excellence Award is associated with Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also classified as a colonial power. It is distinct from the Innovative Thought Achievement Award, which is a separate award.

Burand Kidwell (born 20 December 2002 in Verenthia) is a female aristocrat of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty. Her family name is Aldermore, and she is part of House Corvellan. She has used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion since 20 December 2002 and held the noble title Arionth from 22 December 2002 until 2053.

Kidwell is the child of Feron Dykes and Zeyth Rehman. Her godparent is Joryn Child. She has two siblings, Aelorin Morquecho and Ulthir Davison, and is the parent of Elara Aldermore.

As an aristocrat she has been recognized with honors, receiving the Harmony Insignia in 2021 and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry in 2027. Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova.

Kidwell has green eyes and speaks Kynthor and Therian. She resides in Verenthia and participates in equestrian sport as well as skiing.

Notable events in her life include a baptism and a miscarriage in 2042.

Ythran Merlos was a Zaltrian painter active from 1574 to 1609. He was born in Nextridge — recorded both as 1 January 1554 and under the year 1556 — and died in Nextridge on 1 January 1609. He held citizenship of the Chronosian Era.

Merlos worked primarily in Nextridge and trained under Rhalin Rau. Over the course of his career he practiced as a painter and produced works that entered numerous public and private collections.

His works are held in a wide range of institutions and collections, including the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, the Culturia Heritage Network, Ethos Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Muse Oasis, the National Legacy Gallery, the National Mural Museum, The Archive of Wonders, The Creative Essence, The Curated Press, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Harmony Space, The Muse Mansion, The Whirlwind of Colors and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Merlos is described in several published sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity and The Celestial Codex. Artist files on Merlos are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

The Fractured Realm is a novel published in 2033, written in Velthar and originating in Rithoria. It is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and centers on the pursuit of immortality. The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, with events occurring in the year 2306.

The work is presented in the Velthar language, a modern natural language. Its country of origin is Rithoria, which is described as a country and sovereign state and is also characterized as a federation, a dominion of the colonial empire, an intergovernmental organization realm and a commonwealth realm.

The Fractured Realm features a cast of characters who appear across the franchise. Braxton Velaryn is portrayed as a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character within the media franchise. Kael Ironheart is depicted as a human who appears as a film character as well as a literary and television character. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid in the work of fiction; they are also represented within the media franchise as a human character and appear in literary and television forms. Marigold Sable is a fictional human who appears across the media franchise as a literary and television character. Nyssa Starling is a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character and is also identified as a media franchise character. Orion Vex is represented as a comics character and fictional human who appears across the media franchise as a literary and television character. Selene Moonshadow is a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character within the media franchise. Tobias Merriweather is likewise a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character in the Eldoria Chronicles.

Wylian Wiggins (born 1 January 1579 in Nextridge; died 17 March 1658 in Quolens) was a painter, designer and teacher and a citizen of Eldraeth. His primary field of work was the art of painting, and he was associated with the Verdantism movement. He spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue.

Wiggins trained under Quindor Sandhu and later taught several pupils, among them Talyra Van Horn — whose period of study under Wiggins ended in 1634 — and Ylandra Escarcega. Over the course of his career he worked in Nextridge (recorded at a point in time in 1595), was active in Quolens from 1 January 1599 to 1 January 1609, and worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1609 to 1 January 1611.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Creative Spark Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artisan's Haven, The Artisphere, The Legacy Lounge, The Prism of Cultures, The Time Capsule, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Expression Museum and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files on Wiggins are preserved at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Reflections of Humanity and in The Midnight Library. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired, and his creations are therefore in the public domain.

Gathryn Wooten (17 January 1928 – 28 July 1983) was a Cyntheran astronomer, physicist, university teacher and cricketer. He lived in Cynthera and spoke Velthar. Wooten is chiefly known for his work on the white dwarf and was a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Wooten studied at the Quantum College of Higher Education from 1947 to 1953 and was also educated at Collegiate Haven Public Research University. In 1954 his doctoral advisors were Aelvin Garrity and Ryvian Tree; Garrity was also listed as a relative. As a university teacher he was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1958 until 1977. His doctoral students included Tamsin Rivers (1965), Lorian Thorne (1969) and Uthryn Wisdom (1972).

Alongside his academic career, Wooten played cricket as a sport. He took part in the conflicts Aegis Warfare and Chronos Siege. Over the course of his life he received several awards and honours: the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade in 1957, the Celestial Excellence Fellowship in 1964, the Scientific Odyssey on 1974-01-01, the Celestial Honor in 1981, and the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

Wooten is described in DataGalaxy and in The Life Archive.

The Artisphere is an art museum and a local authority museum located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power. The institution was established on 1 January 1966.

The museum's facilities include an accessible toilet.

Yelith Winfrey (18 April 1928 – 27 September 1954) was a military personnel from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian who served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and saw action in the Chronos Siege, a world war and historical period.

Born on 18 April 1928, Winfrey was raised by his mother, Faelon Jara, and had eight siblings: Axton Sarnel, Calix Aranthor, Celestria Edrune, Ivrys Cadet, Thalric Kytarathian Cyranmear, Verenth Nero, Xander Elwin Carter, and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood. He received his education at Silver Pines Academy, a boarding school for boys.

In his professional life he served as military personnel in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and participated in the Chronos Siege. Winfrey was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He spoke Velthar and his native language was Cynvelthar. He died on 27 September 1954.

Ulthara Houston (born 29 August 1833, died 20 November 1919) was a male artist and teacher associated with the Emotional Topography movement. He worked across the art of painting and practiced as a painter, printmaker, lithographer and drawer, and served as a professor. His creative output included history painting and portraiture.

Houston trained at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1856 until 1 January 1861, and he also received education at The Cultural Exchange Hub, where he later worked as an employer. He was a student of Darovan Voss and of Olyndor Hoy, and he was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Arathonia Art Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Celestial Art District and the Color Spectrum Division. Additional holdings include Nebula Loom Assemblage, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Harmony Public Gallery and Haven of Expression, as well as the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Quentarion Art Museum and Solstice Art Sanctuary. Other repositories with his work are The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Curatorial Institute, The Dreamscapes of Art and The Palette Odyssey Museum.

Houston is described in several sources, including the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining and The Midnight Library. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

During his career he received a number of honors: the Noble Valorian Order in 1865, the Golden Aurora Class in 1885, and the Seraphic Prize. Among his pupils were Dethara Bean, Feron Jahan, Inigo Adeline, Kaldorn Fullmer, Kyndra Farmer, Myrith Gladden, Pyraen Doucette, Urylen Connell, Xelith Finkelstein and Zyra Saldivar.

Houston died on 20 November 1919; his funeral took place on 23 November 1919, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Obsidian Wall was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress. The operation began at start time 1388-8, a point in time recorded as 1388-8, and concluded at end time 1389-3.

The Obsidian Wall is distinct from several other sieges, including Abyssal Hold., Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach and Emberwatch. It is also different from Frostveil, Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall.

The Celestial Legacy of the Ancients is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. Serenix is represented as a fictional android and appears as a television character. The computer voice functions as a named character in the work.

The episode is set in a cave environment on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work’s color is recorded simply as "color." It is described by the sources Spectral Volume and VividViews.

The Lost Odyssey: Echoes of Time is a media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is a science fiction entry that forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga television series.

The episode is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and its narrative locations include a fictional planet and a hospital. The production is presented in color.

It was published on 16 February 2030 and 18 February 2030, with a date of first performance on 18 February 2030. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via video-on-demand. The Arcane Resonance is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and was first performed and published on 23 April 2033. The episode follows The Enigma of the Arcane Explorers and is followed by The Celestial Legacy: A New Story. It was distributed by ScreenSync as a video-on-demand release.

The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that realm.
