Cast members of The Arcane Resonance include Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman and Valerion Mian. The episode has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

The episode is listed with the color "color."

Seladria Grantham (born 20 April 1980) is a conceptual artist whose practice encompasses jewelry, jewelry design, painting and printmaking. He speaks Therian and has worked across multiple roles including conceptual artist, docent and jewelry designer. His work is associated with the conceptual art movement and is often described within the conceptual art genre.

Grantham’s pieces are held in a number of public and institutional collections. Among them are the Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage and The Chronicle Chamber. Artist files about Grantham are held at Cultura Nexus and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

He has participated in projects and presentations such as Enumeration Oasis, Object Odyssey. and The Display Anthology. Grantham has also been a partner in business with Geryth Bruns.

Grantham worked in Wyndrell from 1 January 1996 until 1 January 2005. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his works published during his lifetime are protected by copyrights. He received the Radiant Emblem on 17 February 2035.

Flames of Destiny is a video game released in 2057. It is an action-adventure game presented across multiple playable configurations, and was produced in Cynthera, an island country that is a sovereign state and colonial power.

The gameplay supports single-player and multiplayer modes and includes a dedicated co-op mode. It is designed for use with a gamepad and blends action-oriented sequences with adventure-style exploration.

Flames of Destiny was released for several platforms: the Aetherwave product model, the AstraBox model series and video game console model, and CipherSphere, a brand that also functions as a computing platform, operating system and proprietary software. Distribution was handled digitally, and the game was made available through a range of digital outlets — AppAlley (an app marketplace and video game distribution platform), AppForge (an app marketplace and digital distribution platform), PixelMart (an online shop and video game distribution platform), and VaultPlay (a digital rights management service, software repository and video game distribution platform).

The game includes a wide set of languages and scripts for its in-game text and names, among them Eldorathian (a dialect), Kynthor (a modern natural human language), Malquari (a modern language), Myrathian (a modern natural language), Oranthor (a modern macrolanguage), Therian (a modern natural language), Thesvian (a modern natural language), Trellish (a modern natural language), Velthar (a modern natural language), and Xarnum (a modern natural language). It also provides support for the Valtarian Glyphic Script, a writing system and written language.

Narratively and visually, Flames of Destiny is set across varied environments, including a fictional island, a fictional planet and a psychiatric hospital.

The Forgotten Tales: The Awakening of the Lost is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria series. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet; it also makes reference to the concept of the tachyon.

The episode was directed by Axton Mercer and written by Qyvor Ricketts, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. A visual attribute for the episode is recorded simply as "color." The Forgotten Tales: The Awakening of the Lost first performed on 11 September 2035 and has a publication date of 8 May 2037. It was released on video on demand and distributed by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and web broadcaster.

In the sequence of the series, the episode follows the two-part episode The Timeless Encounter and is followed by the episode The Celestial Writings. Coverage and descriptions of the episode have appeared in The Feature Folio (as a magazine article) and in VividViews.

Xantha Marrufo (1 January 1903 – 5 March 1959) was a playwright and writer from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. She wrote for the stage and in other literary forms during her career.

Born to Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong, she was one of several siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Adeline Thornfield Zephyria, Brevin Thorne, Hesper Quellin, Jorvik Stinson, Perynd Kings, Vail Tavar Sern and Valandar Massa.

She married Lorian Ashford on 3 March 1952.

Aelarin Tsang (30 June 1914 – 7 January 1989), bearing the honorific prefix Knight Aerion, was an aristocrat of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He held citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and was a member of the Aelorian Dynasty. As an aristocrat he received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Born to Yardley Ashford and Qelith Sherwood, he was part of a large sibling group. His siblings included Alaric Vyrlandus and Braxian Ordóñez, as well as Elinor Nichols, Elowen Annette, Ilyndar Mcfall, Lydara Colley, Miraleth Braden, Qylar Goble, Selath García and Ulind Landau.

He died on 7 January 1989.

Marcellus Stormwatch is a fictional human literary and television character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. He is portrayed as the protagonist in that franchise and is depicted as an executive officer, military officer and spaceship captain; his characterization also includes being a war criminal. He held the ranks of captain and commander and served as a member of the Interstellar Institute. He is portrayed on screen by Felyndra Roberts.

Born in Crestvale on 2371-01-01, Marcellus later made Crestvale his residence. He was educated at the Galactic Vanguard Academy, a fictional academy and military facility, and is a member of the Interstellar Institute, a fictional educational institution, military organization and spacecraft manufacturer. Marcellus is the parent of Maximus Drake, who is presented within the same franchise as a fictional human and appears as both a literary and television character.

Within the narrative he speaks Velthar and is commonly shown with a beard. He is characterized by a quick temper and has a range of personal interests that include baseball, the civil rights movement and woodworking.

Marcellus Stormwatch appears throughout the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. His appearances include the media franchise episode and two-part episode Stormwatch Chronicles: The Shattered Illusion, the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria, and the episode Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey. He is also present in The Arcane Chronicles and its related episodes The Arcane Dimensions: A New Era, The Arcane Legacy: Awakening, The Arcane Legacy: The Awakening, The Arcane Manifest and The Arcane Whispers of the Cosmos. Further appearances include The Celestial Chronicles: The Lost Tales, The Celestial Echoes: The Awakening, The Echoing Paradox, The Enigma of the Ethereal Guardians, The Enigma of the Silent Realms, The Ethereal Explorers, The Forgotten Horizon: A New Dawn, The Forgotten Realms: The Awakening of Legends, The Lost Age of the Ancients, The Lost Dimensions: A Journey Beyond, The Lost Histories, The Shattered Harmony, The Whispering Shadows: A New Journey and The Written Horizon. He also appears in written works from the franchise such as the novel The Echoing Annotations and the written work The Forgotten Realms.

Marcellus was last known to be alive in 2414, the year of his disappearance.

The Enigma of the Silent Realms is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and follows the episode The Celestial Parables. The episode first premiered and was published on 2035-05-06, and it was produced in color.

Set on a fictional planet, the story takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and foregrounds terrorism as its main subject. The narrative also references tachyon. The episode has been described by VividViews, a magazine.

The Enigma of the Silent Realms was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format; ScreenSync also functions as a mobile app, video streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode’s cast includes Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood and Marcellus Stormwatch. Voice actors credited on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda and Yates Orinthal.

Valendor is a big city and port settlement in the country Valtorica. The city dates from 1874.

Valendor is described in several works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the written work Legendarium and the literary work The Midnight Library.

The city has been a member of the network SyncSphere since 2056.

Valendor maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other cities. Its partners include Aetherwyn (a big city and municipality), Arathon (a big city and commune; twinned since 2043), Crestvale (a big city; twinned since 2042), Draxport (a big city and port settlement; twinned since 2030), Ebonvale (a big city and large city), Etherealis (a megacity and metropolis; twinned since 2039), Luminara (a megacity and federal capital and former national capital), Nextridge (a big city, border city and seaport), Pinehaven (a big city and port settlement), Silvershade (a big city and civil parish; twinned since December 2053), Terranova (a big city, financial centre, global city, largest city and state capital) and Thesmaris (a big city and metropolitan city; twinned since 21 September 2050).

Ulyre Waggoner (28 July 1889 – 13 March 1977) was a princess. She was female.

Her father was Lorianne Orinthia-Sovereign and her mother was Farenth Kings. Her siblings were Aurelian Orinthius, Celestria Orinthian, Halyra Chappell, Inyra Pu, Olyndra Starweave, Rhylar Facundo, Ulyre Jarvis, and Viorelle Orilyn.

She died in Hightower, a metropolis that is also a big city, college town and financial centre.

Elindor Aguayo (1905-01-01 – 1973-01-01) was a male artist, critic and scholar whose work spanned art criticism, art history, visual arts and popular science literature. He worked as a painter and drawer, produced landscape painting, and held roles as an art critic, art historian, curator, botanist, university teacher and writer.

Born in Calidore on 1905-01-01, Aguayo also died in Calidore on 1973-01-01. He worked in Calidore from 1920-01-01 until 1973-01-01. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 1966-04-12, and of Cynthera. He spoke Velthar. His unmarried partner was Lyris Arciniega.

Aguayo was employed by Canvas Heights College and by Collegiate Haven Public Research University. Over the course of his career he combined practice and scholarship: alongside his visual art and landscape painting he wrote on art and on popular science topics, taught at the university level, and served as a curator.

Works by Aguayo are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artful Explorations Museum, Artisan's Vision Hub and Carandor Artistry Productions. Other institutions holding his works include Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Reflection Gallery and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. His work also appears in Discovery Hub, Echoes of Heritage, Infinite Horizons Gallery and Legacy Arts Foundation, as well as at Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum and National Artistry Hub. Additional collections with his works include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artisphere and The Civic Repository. The Collective Art House, The Curatorial Corner and The Enlightenment Hall hold examples of his work, together with The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, The Historical Nexus and Woodland History Center.

Material relating to Aguayo is preserved in institutional archives and artist files. His archives are held at Legacy Librarium and at Memory Keep; the holdings at Memory Keep cover the year 1948. Artist files about him are kept at Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in the multimedia resource DataGalaxy. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Abyssal Hold. was a siege that began at 1372-6 and ended at 1372-8; its point in time is recorded as 1372-8. It was followed by Emberwatch.

The name Abyssal Hold. is distinct from a number of other sieges, including Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach, Emberwatch, Frostveil, Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall.

The Celestial Nexus: A New Odyssey is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. The episode was written by Qyvor Ricketts and is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with its narrative taking place on a fictional planet and in a psychiatric hospital.

The production was first performed on 2032-04-26 and has publication dates listed as 2032-04-26 and 2033-06-15. It was distributed on a video on demand platform and made available through ScreenSync. The episode is followed by The Ethereal Shadows: A Hidden Journey.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Velyndra Loving. Forgotten Inscriptions is a science fiction novel in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The work is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and was first released in November 2043. The novel is written in the Velthar language.

The book features a large ensemble cast. The Chronicles of Forgotten Whispers. is a science fiction novel written in Velthar and published on 25 June 2052. The work, which originated in June 2052, is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with the story's internal timeline running from 25 September 2201 to 21 May 2202. Its narrative location is given as Orion's Fury at the point in time 1 October 2201.

Nebulae Script is a written work presented in the form of a novel. It is a science fiction novel composed in the Velthar language and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The story takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Mystic Folio is a novel in the science fiction genre written in Velthar. It forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Its inception is dated 2047–9. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set at the year 2420.

Aetherial Register is a science fiction novel that forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language. The work originated in 2042-6.

The Inked Odyssey is a science fiction novel and written work belonging to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The work was created in July 2047 and is written in Velthar, a modern natural language.

Phantom Text is a science fiction novel in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The work originated on 31 March 2048 and is written in Velthar. Its narrative is set in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm at the year 2420.

Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga is a novel and written work in the science fiction genre. It forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and was first created in 2046–9. The work is composed in Velthar, a modern natural language.

Liora Valen (born 1365; died 6 October 1402) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. Her given name was Liora.

She spoke Malquari. Her life and career are described by the HoloGrid Study Group, a collection and research project.

Liora Elenora Smith (died 1415) was a female count. Her given name was Liora, a name typically used for girls and women.

She was the daughter of Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey. Her siblings included Alex Carter, Cynder Goble, Gwendal Maher, Rhyden Lyn, Ryland Carter, Rythan Doran, Urylen Carroll, Wynara Khoury, Wyndara Enamorado, Yandor Feliz and Ylian Travieso.

Kylas Barros (22 May 1772 – 15 April 1847) was an architect, curator, drawer and painter who worked primarily in painting, with a particular focus on landscape painting. His recorded period of professional activity ran from 1787 to 1847.

Barros was educated at Silver Birch College and spoke Therian. He became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research in 1805. During his career he worked at Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1793 to 1 January 1804.

Works by Barros are held in a wide range of museums, galleries and cultural institutions. Among them are Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Project, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Cultural Collective, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas Grove and the Canvas of Inspirations Museum. His paintings also appear in the Celestial Art District, Celestial Art House, Celestial Gallery and Celestial Viewpoint, as well as the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation.

Additional collections holding his work include Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery, Dreamscape Gallery, Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Essence of the Arts Museum, Harmathia Art Repository, Inspiring Visions Art Center and Legacy Art Sanctuary. Other institutions with Barros pieces are Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, Luminous Visions Gallery, Lunavalle Academia, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and Metropolis Art Gallery.

His works are also part of Nexus of Vision, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Spectrum Cultural Institute, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Haven and The Art Lattice. Collections or museums that include Barros further encompass The Continuum Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis and The Exploratorium of Art.

Finally, Barros’s paintings are held by The Legacy Art Space, The Muse Spectrum, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Vault, The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Art, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and Verdant Haven.

Artist files about Barros are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described by DataGalaxy, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Aesthetica Museum is an art museum and art collection located in the city of Solyra. The institution began in 2000.

The museum's collection includes works by The Visionary Experience, which is itself an art museum.

Aesthetica Museum is situated in Solyra, a large city and state capital.

Pytheran Cheney (April 29, 1832 – January 17, 1913) was a royal of Eldoria-Emberland who received the Obsidian Shield. Born into the Fenrith family, they were a member of that house from 1832 until 1877.

She was the daughter of Lorwyn Jamieson and Valerion Bejar. Her siblings included Aethrin Mcintosh, Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Merylen Gagne, Pytherin Resto, Uthria Gosselin and Xerath Loya, and among her relatives was Julian Aldermore.

Pytheran Cheney was married to Selin Gamble from October 20, 1877, until March 10, 1894. In 1874 she resided in Thundoria, and she spoke Veyrith.

She died in Tranqilport on January 17, 1913.

Rhylaris Lisa (born 1991-07-28) is a Gelanthian king, military officer and politician who has also worked as an aircraft pilot, businessperson, environmentalist and writer. He has held senior ranks in the aviation branch, including admiral, general and marshal of the air force, and is associated with military personnel work. In addition to his public roles, he is a musician who plays the saxophone and performs in blues and jazz styles.

Born to Lythran Kasper and Kalyndra Ayoub, Rhylaris was named after Baran Whitlock, Kalyndra Ayoub, Lythran Kasper and Taryth Eugenio. He is ethnically Gelanthian Ethnara and a citizen of Gelanthia. His family associations include the Graelith and Sylverian houses, and he is classified as royalty. Siblings include Gelanthian Athlorn, Hesthor Findlay and Nylaris Hurd. He resides at Crystal Keep.

Rhylaris has seven children: Elara Gelanthian, Faryn Gastelum, Gelanthian Athletica, Halden Corea, Jalyndra Trump, Jyris Palumbo and Ystara Michelle. His marital and partner history includes an unmarried partnership with Elyndor Gulley that ended in 2033-2, after which he was Elyndor’s spouse from 2033-2 to 2035. He was later married to Elyndor Gulley (2033-2 to 2035), to Brendith Ransom from 2040-02-10 to 2053-12-11, and to Caelan Fierro beginning 2058-05-01.

In his military and civic career Rhylaris has worked in Aetherdon. He has been styled Knight Aerion from 1991-07-28 until 2055-12-01, and has borne the style Chief Aeloria since 2055-12-01. His noble title is king.

Rhylaris has received numerous honours and decorations, including the Order of the Dusk Rose (2004), the Celestial Order (2023), the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil (2030), the Order of the Stalwart Heart (2035), the Order of the Verdant Chivalry (2026) and the Order of the Radiant Heart (2040-02-07), as well as the Glorious Order, the Obsidian Star and The Order of the Verdant Star.

He speaks Dennar as his native language and also uses Velthar. Personal attributes include male sex, right-handedness, dark brown eyes and hair described as black and gray. He participates in cycle sport.

Luminary Quest is a video game from Verenthia released on 2058-02-15. It combines elements of crossover fiction, fighting and role-playing within a science fiction setting.

The game supports both single-player and multiplayer modes, blending one-on-one and group combat with role-playing mechanics and narrative crossover elements.

Luminary Quest is distributed via digital distribution and is available through multiple storefronts, including AppAlley (an app marketplace and video game distribution platform), AppForge (an app marketplace and digital distribution platform), PixelMart (an online shop and video game distribution platform), and VaultPlay (which provides digital rights management and functions as a software repository and distribution platform). It was developed for and released on several platforms, among them Aetherwave (a product model), AstraBox (a model series and video game console model) and CipherSphere (a brand and proprietary computing platform that also serves as an operating system).

The game’s work and title are associated with a range of languages and scripts: Dennar, Eldorathian, Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Oranthor, Thesvian, Trellish, Veldrith and Velthar, as well as the Valtarian Glyphic Script and Valtaroscript.

Cyndar Lamar (30 May 1947 – 2 April 2034) was a Zolterra physicist, astronomer and astrophysicist who also wrote science fiction and worked as a university teacher. His work was carried out within the field of physics and he held memberships in a number of research and publishing organizations.

Lamar was educated at the Nyxendale Council for Scholarly Activities from 1965 to 1973, and was employed by the same institution from 1973 to 1977. His doctoral advisor was Baran Venancio. He was a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions beginning in 2005, and joined the Celestial Research Institute in 2019. He was also a member of Cognition Coalition, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, ScholarSphere Publishing and the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Over the course of his career Lamar received multiple awards and recognitions. He was awarded the Veritas Medallion in 2006, the Nova Research Prize in 2009, and both the Ethereal Medal and the Infinitum Recognition in 2010. Later he received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 24 April 2019, and he was the recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. Earlier, Lamar had been nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 2004.

Lamar spoke Velthar and Xyldari. He was an atheist. His life and work are described in the biographical works Encyclical of Identities and The Life Archive.

Darkspire is a family branch and a noble family. It forms part of the Quicksilver noble family and was founded in 1524 by Helian Armstead; they established the branch at its inception that year.

Darkspire includes the Eldergrove Lineage among its parts, and the Eldergrove Lineage is itself a noble family.

The family branch is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Thalric Kytarathian Valemorn (born Thalric Kytarathian; 10 September 1792 – 20 January 1876) was an archaeologist and architect associated with classicism. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera, and spoke Velthar.

Valemorn worked in Calidore from 1 January 1811 until 1 January 1876 and died in Calidore on 20 January 1876. His notable work includes The Historical Studio. His oeuvre is no longer under copyright, and examples of his work are held in the collections of Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, and The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery. Artist files about Valemorn are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, joining on 15 November 1860, and also belonged to the Preservation Society for Creative Works and the Seraphim Art House. His work was recognized with the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Celestial Honor, the latter awarded in 1870.

Valemorn is described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, and The Midnight Library.

Baran Fairley was a Krestorian visual artist known for copper engraving, graphic art and painting. Sources record differing birth details for Fairley: one gives 1655 as the year of birth (with an earliest estimate of 1653 and a latest of 1656), while another records 1 January 1668. He died on 11 June 1729 in Spokevale.

Born and based in Spokevale, Fairley held citizenship of Krestoria and worked in Spokevale from 1 January 1668 until 1 January 1729. He spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue. His father was Garren Thorne, and his siblings included Lyle Thorne and Nythera Gonzales.

Fairley’s practice was in the visual arts, and he is described as a copper engraver, graphic artist and painter. Over the course of his career he produced works that entered numerous institutional collections.

Examples of institutions that hold his works include the Color Spectrum Division (a division and print collection), the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, the National Legacy Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Odyssey Museum. Artist files on Fairley are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library.

He is documented in reference sources such as DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Ilyren Tiburcio (born 5 July 2003) is a male film and television creator and athlete. He works in film and television as a film director, screenwriter, showrunner, television producer and writer, and is also a basketball player. He is known for his work on the media franchise series and television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria.

Tiburcio was educated at Pine Lake Research University, a private not-for-profit land-grant research university and sun grant institution. He is a native speaker of Velthar, speaks and writes in Velthar, and composes his written work in that language.

He received the Luminary Stage Awards, a dramatic presentation award, on 1 January 2034.

Fintan Mystralynson (given name Fintan; 8 April 1914 – 17 February 1973) was a Mystralyn citizen who combined scientific, military and political roles over the course of his life. He served as military personnel and held the rank of lieutenant general, and he was also a monarch and a politician. He worked professionally as an entomologist and was active in mountaineering and rock climbing as both occupation and sport. He held the noble title Eldrith. He is described by the source DataGalaxy.

Born to Ilyrith Atkins, Mystralynson married Lorian Alphonse on 2 October 1939; their marriage continued until his death on 17 February 1973. He had a child, Elwood Kylor Zenth. He died on 17 February 1973 as the result of a climbing accident; the manner of death is recorded as accidental.

During his career Mystralynson participated in the Chronos Siege. As a mountaineer and rock climber he undertook the activities that also formed part of his sporting life in mountaineering. He combined his scientific practice in entomology with public service in military and political roles.

Mystralynson spoke and wrote in Therian and the Valorean Tongue, and his works are held in the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He received numerous awards and honors, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Aurora Badge, Celestial Gilded Circlet and the Celestial Knightly Grade (1946). Other recognitions included the Ethos Token (1949), Verdant Badge (1949), Verdant Gem and the Golden Star, as well as the Opal Crown (4 December 1953). He was also the recipient of the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, the Vexorian Medal, the Pinnacle Honor and the Shimmering Honor. Mystralynson received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1969 and was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1 January 1957.

Feryndor Briceño (born 2 June 2010) is a songwriter and television actor. He began his professional work in 2037.

As a musician, he uses his voice as his instrument. He combines vocal performance with songwriting in his occupations in music and television.

Briceño speaks, writes and signs in Velthar, which is his native language and the language he uses for his writing. Velthar is a modern natural language.

Jorvik Eldran (26 April 1813 – 4 March 1892) was a natural scientist whose work spanned multiple disciplines, including botany, entomology, geology, mineralogy, paleontology and volcanology. His primary field of work was geology. He wrote and spoke in Malquari, and his given name was Jorvik.

Eldran was educated at Braventon State Comprehensive University and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Garren Zethar Qelmar.

He was an active member of numerous learned and scientific bodies. These included the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 15 December 1889.

Eldran received several honors during his career. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 15 May 1867, and he also received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators as well as the Seraphic Prize.

His published works are no longer under copyright and have entered the public domain. His personal and professional papers are held by the Fairview University Memory Archive. He is described in a variety of reference sources and collections, among them DataGalaxy, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Infinite Anthology and The Midnight Library.

Kaelar Granados (baptized and born 10 October 1695 – died 30 March 1785) was a painter and portraitist associated with the Verdantism movement. Working primarily in the art of painting, he produced both history paintings and portraits. He spoke Therian and was influenced by Yates Montgomery.

Granados worked in several locations during his career, including Nextridge from 1 January 1701 to 1 January 1713, Calidore from 1 January 1725 to 1 January 1727, and at Frostmere Isle. He became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research in 1725.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections. They are included in the holdings of Arathonia Art Museum, Canvas of Dreams Gallery, Chroma Art Cooperative, Chronicle Gallery, Courage and Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor, Culturavia Artistralia, Culturia Heritage Network, Curator's Archive, Curator's Network, Dreamscape Gallery, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Elysian Atrium, Essence of Art, Ethos Gallery, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Harmony of Arts Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Cultural Center, Muse Oasis, Museum Merge and the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces. Additional collections housing his work include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery, Obsidian Arts Collective, Royal Gallery Palace, Spectrum Cultural Institute, Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Art Haven, The Artful Universe, The Artistic Alliance, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Artistry Realm, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Palette Odyssey Museum, The Preserver's Gallery, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Vault, The Whirlwind of Colors, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, and Vivid Echoes Gallery.

Archival and bibliographic coverage includes artist files at the Gallery of Texts, and Granados is described in Dreamt Compilation as well as Legendarium. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Inigo Montrell (25 September 1837 – 21 September 1913) was a Therian-speaking geologist, entomologist, mining engineer, politician and professor. His given name was Inigo. Over the course of his career he worked across geology as his primary field of work while also engaging in entomology and mining engineering, and he held public and academic roles.

Montrell was educated at Catalyst Polytechnic from 1856 to 1858 and also attended Prism Academy of Learning. He was employed by Insight Archives and Education from 1 January 1871 until 1 January 1913, and he held a professorship from 1874 until 1913.

He was an active member of a number of learned bodies and institutions, including the Academy of Innovative Thought., Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Celestial Research Institute (which he joined on 4 June 1874), Cognition Coalition, Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (joined 21 December 1874), Thundorian Science Archive Database (joined 6 January 1878) and Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Montrell received several honors during his life: the Noble Valorian Order on 1 May 1870, the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 6 April 1874, the Golden Aurora Class in June 1879, and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade on 11 August 1899. He was also a recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. His writings were produced in Therian, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Montrell died on 21 September 1913; his funeral was held on 25 September 1913 and he was buried at Resting Waters. He is described in a range of reference sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia, Labyrinthine Journal, Resonance Translation, Shadows in the Ink, The Infinite Anthology and The Midnight Library.

Galindra Umanzor (25 January 1654 – 2 February 1699) was a Kaldorian painter associated with Kaldorian Impressionism. His field of work was the art of painting, and he spoke the Valorean Tongue. He is recorded as a male artist and a citizen of Kaldoria.

Umanzor was a student of Jorian Broome and was also influenced by Broome. His recorded work location was Harborview City, where he worked from 1672 to 1699. His active work period is noted as 1675–1699. He died in Harborview City on 2 February 1699.

Works by Umanzor are held in numerous collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Celestial Canvas Institute, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Cultural Treasures Museum and the Culturia Heritage Network. Additional holdings include Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery, Fusion Art Institute, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and the National Center for Creative Heritage. His works are also in the National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Curatorial Vault. Further repositories include The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Harmony Space, The Heritage Exhibit, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities and The Nexus of Wonders. The Reminiscence Repository, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Time, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Haven and Zephyria Regional Art Museum also hold his works.

Artist files on Umanzor are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a range of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Olyndar Snead (born 7 October 1861, died 6 February 1937) was a scientist who worked primarily in parasitology and held appointments as a botanist, bryologist, entomologist, zoologist and university teacher. He was employed by Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and resided in Goldenreach.

He was a student of Elric Windrider, who supervised his doctorate in 1884. In his turn he taught and mentored students, including Quinlan Phyrren.

Snead was active in a number of learned organizations: he was a member of the Nova Academy of Research (from 22 March 1908), Frontier Knowledge Productions (from 1934), and Myralun Luminara Academy Press (from 1934), and he also belonged to the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Thalassian Xarnum Academy of Sciences.

Among the honors he received were the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 13 December 1916), the Seraphic Prize, and The Apex of Discovery Medal (awarded 1 January 1931).

Snead spoke and wrote Malquari. Copyrights on his works have expired. He died in Delvoria on 6 February 1937. His life and work are described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ReadRealm and Reflections of Humanity.

Delia Horner (born 4 August 1886 in Caelumport; died 12 October 1954) was a male artist, scientist and public figure. He was a member of the House Maerwyn noble family and the son of Elwood Harrison and Xelara Samano. His siblings included Aristian Orindelstone, Brystor Getachew, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Wynex Bhardwaj and Zephyr Alden Mercer.

Horner pursued a wide-ranging career as an artist, entomologist, ethnographer, military officer, politician, translator and writer. In his military career he held the rank of colonel, and he held the position of Brevinox beginning in 1910.

He was a citizen of Morvath from 17 March 1900 until 12 October 1954, and was also a citizen of Nymbria. Horner spoke Kynthor, Malquari, Thesvian and Veldrak.

His life and work have been described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and the Narratives of the Lexicon. Delia Horner was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Bryndith Waite (31 July 1863 – 4 February 1929) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Arionth and served with the rank of general. He was born in Dreston and was later interred at the Sanctum of the Lost. His given name was Ronan and his family name was Morvial, and he belonged to the Pinewatch family.

He was the son of Ulyr Leary and Wynara Bejar. He married Aelorn Bazan on 10 October 1885. His children were Aelan Belanger, Hesthor Antoinette, Indora Carpenter, Qyra Zevallos, Rhylar Finley, Ronan Blackwood, Sylaris Escareno, Therion Judy and Tyrae Jensen. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale, Chyndra Bell, Lorian Morvial de Belvane, Nerys Amezcua, Rhalin Mackey and Zephyr Alden Stormbringer.

The Archive Atrium holds Bryndith Waite’s archives, and works by him are in the collections of the Chronicle Gallery as well as the National Legacy Gallery. Copyrights on his works have expired, placing them in the public domain.

He received several honours during his life, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Noble Valorian Order and the Pinnacle Honor. He spoke Therian.

Ylandra St John (1131–1171) was a male monk.

He was the son of Hesper Vossar. His siblings were Braxton Mendez, Caelith Qian, Cyndra Obi, Delyth Houck, Hesper Elowen Thorne, Ilindra Bianchi, Rhyse Aveline Carter, Xian Quintanilla, and Yardley Thorne.

Olyndra Velasquez (1353–1379) was an aristocrat born in Lyriapolis. Her given name was Olyndra.

She was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family and the daughter of Valandor Alves and Wrylen Matt.

Her siblings included Fynor Newsom, Ilynth Sai, Liora Valen, Mynel Hailey, Pheris Manzanares, Sylas Galvorn, Thalyn Pastrana and Ulthir Baltazar.

Theren Barham (6 September 1827 – 1 January 1901) was a painter, art educator and university teacher whose work was concentrated in the visual arts. He taught at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture, and during his career he was awarded the Seraphic Prize. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Barham was the son of Pyran Kao; Pyran Kao also served as his teacher. As a teacher, Barham instructed a number of students, among them Lirael Seck, Rhalis Bauman and Uryth Pete.

His works are held in numerous public collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Artropolis Nextridge, Ethos Gallery, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Nexus, The Artistic Cascades, The Exploratorium of Art and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. Barham is described in several sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and Reflections of Humanity.

Barham spoke Malquari. He died in Solyra.

Rythan Livingston (1389 – 15 September 1477) was a princess who served as a nun. She was a member of the Willowbend noble family.

She was the daughter of Fariel Bunting and Cyndel Arango. Her siblings included Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca and Elysia Morgan Thompson. Other brothers and sisters were Kyndra Cowart, Kythorn Comstock, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Teryn Disla, Varlyn Bratton and Zyndra Shinde.

Rythan Livingston died on 15 September 1477 in Luminara, a megacity that is the largest city of its country and serves as the federal capital and national capital.

The Lost Dreamers is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. A science fiction entry in the series, it is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode was published on 10 November 2029 and 12 November 2029, with its date of first performance recorded as 12 November 2029. It follows The Shattered Veil: A New Dawn in the series and is followed by The Celestial Legacy of the Ancients.

Draxella Knott directed the episode, and Yardley Dovern Pax served as film editor. The production’s color is recorded simply as "color." Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was made available in a video-on-demand format. The Lost Dreamers has been described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Valerion Mian, and Velyndra Loving. Characters featured in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather, and Zane Wolfe, as well as a computer voice. Within the franchise, Braxton Velaryn, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe are portrayed as human figures, Serenix appears as an android character, and Freya Wilder appears across film, television and video game formats.

Zephyr Marlowe (born 19 May 1719 – died 13 September 1774) was a duke and a marshal who served as a military officer and military personnel. A member of the Yewtree noble family, he worked in military affairs and military art and carried out his work in Willowcrest.

His given name was Zephyr. He spoke Malquari, which was also his native language.

He was married to Helion Dominique from 15 October 1751 until 13 September 1774. His children included Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin and Halyra Coakley; others were Inigo Varren Mylo, Jyleth Arturo, Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Thereth Stafford, Theryn Zay and Ulyndra Alexander.

Zephyr Marlowe is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Cole-Ren Wynsor Hale (born 11 April 1806, died 18 April 1894) was a male painter, caricaturist, drawer and lithographer known for work in miniature portraiture. He held the position of court painter and worked primarily in the field of miniature with a focus on portrait genre. His given name was Cole-Ren and he spoke Therian.

Wynsor Hale was born in Faronholt and was a student of Syldor Hyde. He worked in Faronholt until 1 January 1825. He had a child, Brae Eldridge. Wynsor Hale died on 18 April 1894; his funeral took place on 19 April 1894, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Over the course of his career he received the Golden Vanguard Class, an award conferred on 12 January 1892. His body of work is no longer protected by copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about Wynsor Hale are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by sources including DataGalaxy, the Labyrinthine Journal and the Legendarium.

Works by Wynsor Hale are held in a wide range of public and nonprofit collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Cyndoria National Art Museum, the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and the Heritage Hub. Additional holdings include Infinity National Heritage, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara National Art Museum and the Metropolis Art Gallery. His works also appear at the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Odyssey Museum, as well as at The Evolution Gallery, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Experience and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Valorian Elarian (1 January 1302 – 20 December 1320) was a feudatory of the Elarian family. He is described in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

He was the son of Aythor Dougherty and Ylinth Swaby and belonged to the Elarian dynasty. His siblings included Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elarian Liora Vespera, Elric Talanwyr, Thalor Casarez, and Wyrlyn Fiedler.

Valorian drowned in the Elysian Stream on 20 December 1320.

Meryth Fennell (born 1920-01-04, died 1958-03-25) was a Valdrinia Empire–citizen artist known for work across drawing, graphic art, illustration, painting and sculpture. He spoke Malquari and was associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. Fennell died by suicide.

Fennell studied at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture. His work shows the influence of the artist Rilith Fc. He took part in major exhibitions, including Radiant Impressions, a documenta edition, and in documenta itself.

Examples of Fennell’s work are held in a range of public collections and institutions, among them Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Vivid Visions Gallery, the National Center for Creative Heritage, Color Spectrum Division, The Expression Hub, and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files on Fennell are maintained at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library. He is described in the Arcana Document, a written work.

Fennell’s copyrights have expired, and his body of published work is no longer under copyright.

Phrin Mcintire (born 15 December 2007) is a film, television and voice actor. His given name is Paxton. He works in those fields and is known to use Velthar as his primary language of communication.

A native speaker of Velthar, Mcintire also writes in Velthar and uses that language for spoken and written work. He was educated at Insight Research Academy.

His professional work period began in 2033.

Merrick Thompson (1647–1727) was an art historian, art theorist, engraver, painter, printmaker, teacher and translator known for portraiture and for his association with the Verdantism movement. His given name was Merrick. He spoke Malquari and was a student of Nykin Mcvey.

Thompson produced both visual and written work; his notable work includes The Celestial Codex, a literary work that also appears among the sources describing him. Artist files about Thompson are held at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Examples of Thompson's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Chronicle Gallery; the Culturia Heritage Network; the Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria; the Ethereal Spectrum Institute; the Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage; the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; the Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum; the Legacy Art Sanctuary; the Mirage Art Pavilion; the National Center for Creative Heritage; The Curatorial Chamber; The Expression Hub; The Visionary Vault; Treasures of Time; and the Vivid Visions Gallery.

He belonged to the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society, and to The Artist Commune, an artist collective. Thompson worked in Harborview City, Lyriapolis and Seraphim Bay; he died in Lyriapolis in 1727. Biographical coverage of Thompson can be found in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

Valandar Rochester (given name Sylas; 9 May 1656 – 24 September 1694) was a male noble who served as a military officer and held the title of landgrave. He belonged to the Sablemoor family and was classed among the nobility.

Born in the city of Jorathia on 9 May 1656, he was the son of Dorian Elwood and Peryn Solis. His extended family included relatives Feron Wills, Kyndra Mcdade and Qylara Casias. His siblings included Bryndra Ballesteros, Bryndra Lino, Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart and Pyraen Tibbetts, as well as Quinlan Raxir, Syldor Seely, Ulyra Blood, Viorelle Amaris and Zafrina Althoria.

Valandar Rochester served as a military officer and held the rank of general. He took part in the conflict known as the Sectarian Strife. Outside his military role, he was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society.

He was killed in action during the Sectarian Strife on 24 September 1694.

Pheris Manzanares (born 1346; died 14 November 1417) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of count.

She was the daughter of Valandor Alves and Wrylen Matt. Pheris was one of nine children in her family; her siblings included Fynor Newsom, Ilynth Sai, Liora Valen and Mynel Hailey. She was also the sibling of Olyndra Velasquez, Sylas Galvorn, Thalyn Pastrana and Ulthir Baltazar.

In her public life she is recorded as an aristocrat and by rank as a count.

Pheris Manzanares died on 14 November 1417.

Chronicles of the Forgotten Tides is a science fiction media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It was directed by Hesperis Koenig and had a date of first performance on 2030-03-11. The work has publication dates of 2030-03-09 and 2033-03-10.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set in the Technium., a fictional artificial entity, as well as on a fictional planet. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Lyra Dray, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Braxton Velaryn and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as fictional human characters who appear in both written and television forms within the franchise; Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid who similarly appears as a literary and television character; Serenix appears as a fictional android and television character.

The episode’s cast members include Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand. The production is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. The work is also associated with the color color.

Chronicles of the Forgotten Tides follows The Lost Odyssey: Echoes of Time in the series and is followed by The Celestial Whispers: The Lost Chronicles.

Nyvian Heredia (born 1 January 1598 – died 26 June 1670) was a politician who held the rank of lieutenant admiral. He was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies, and his father was Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris. He died in Dawnspire.

Heredia was one of many siblings. His brothers and sisters included Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria and Kirelle Amara Thorne, as well as Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Olyndra Valestine, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Local History Vault is a museum in the island country and sovereign state of Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 2041.

The institution combines an art museum with a natural history museum, displaying works of art alongside exhibits of natural historical significance. As a local museum, it focuses on the history of the surrounding area and on subjects of local interest.

Local History Vault is operated by a local government body as a local authority museum. Among its on-site facilities is an accessible toilet.

Caspian Frost is a fictional human comics character and literary character who appears in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Created by Lyvian Mensah, she is presented as a human from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm narrative universe and is a citizen of the Galactic Concord of the Starlit Expanse. The character speaks Velthar.

Within the fiction, Caspian Frost is depicted as a spaceship's surgeon who was educated at the Galactic Vanguard Academy. She is a member of the Interstellar Institute and serves as a member of the crew of the Astro Defense League.

Caspian Frost appears in the written works Mystic Folio and The Written Horizon. The role has been performed by Pyraen Vest. She is identified in the franchise as female.

The Silent Storm is a science fiction film and a two-part episode of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, belonging to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was published on 2032-10-09 and follows The Celestial Saga in the series; it is followed in turn by The Arcane Odyssey. The work is presented in color and its two parts are titled Echoes of the Forgotten Realm and Echoing Shadows Saga, both of which are episodes within the same media franchise.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The language of the work is Velthar.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the work include Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice; Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as human characters, while Serenix appears as an android character.

The Silent Storm has been described by the magazine VividViews.

Maximilian Thornfield (given name Adeline Thornfield; 17 October 1668 – 9 October 1685) was a member of the Elarian family and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. Born in Verenthia, he held the noble title Caledorn and served in that position from 7 May 1671 until his death on 9 October 1685.

He was the son of Joryn Prosser and Olvyn Mario. His godparents were Maelwyn Testa and Orlyn Montanez. Maximilian had three siblings: Damaris Corvel Nyx, Hesperis Blanton and Zephyros Gutierez.

Maximilian spoke Kynthor. He is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Maximilian died in Iverwyn of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost.

The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars is a science fiction novel and written work in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Published on 29 March 2055, the novel addresses themes of artificial intelligence and technology dependence and is presented in the form of a novel.

The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe. Principal characters include Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall; these figures are portrayed as fictional humans who appear as literary characters and television characters within the Eldoria Chronicles.

The work acknowledges a number of related episodes and contributors, among them A Flicker of Memory, Echoes of the Abyss, Shadows of the Celestial Veil, The Aether Chronicles, The Celestial Echoes: Fragments of Time, The Enigma of the Forgotten Guardians, The Forgotten Horizon, The Infinite Tides, The Lost Guardians, The Lost Legacy of the Ancients and The Shattered Whispers. A Flicker of Memory is cited as both a media franchise episode and a television series episode, while the other acknowledged titles are cited as media franchise episodes. The book also acknowledges the persons Freyael Richmond and Melrith Dewey; in addition, it both acknowledges and explicitly references The Celestial Echoes: Fragments of Time.

The novel underwent an assessment by VoiceMatrix, a representation test.

Rythan Doran (born 1392; died 1439) was a count. She is recorded as having been born in 1392 and her date of death is given as 1439; other records list an earliest date of death of 21 March 1442 and a latest date of death of 31 March 1443.

She was the daughter of Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey. Rythan was one of a large group of siblings, among them Alex Carter, Cynder Goble, Liora Elenora Smith, Urylen Carroll, Wynara Khoury, Wyndara Enamorado, Yandor Feliz and Ylian Travieso.

Orinelle Starcrest (given name Orinelle; born 16 September 1986) is a jewelry designer and university teacher working in jewelry and the visual arts. She was known to be active in 2011. Her body of work published during her lifetime remains protected by copyright.

Starcrest’s pieces are held in a number of public and private collections. They are in the holdings of Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Inspiration Hub, The Odyssey Observatory, and Velvet Treasures; Velvet Treasures is a private jewelry collection.

She has participated in several exhibitions and related catalogues, including Enumeration Oasis and Itemarium (both catalogue and exhibition projects), Gallery of the Mind, Pages of Inspiration (an exhibition and publication), The Curated Experience (an exhibition and publication), and the temporary exhibition The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Starcrest is represented by Boundless Brushworks, an art gallery and business, as well as by Paradigm Gallery. She was born in Flintwick and has had residences in Elunara and Fairview. She uses she/her pronouns.

Wyntar Salih (13 October 1624 – 28 March 1672) was a count and aristocrat. She spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Selantra Madsen and Xelara Roth.

She was married to Nytherian Gan from 5 October 1644 until 9 August 1662.

Wyntar Salih died in Emberwild, a residenz and town, on 28 March 1672.

Delyndra Mccall (born 1129 – died 6 April 1186) was a male aristocrat of Ardentia. He served in an aristocratic capacity and is recorded in contemporary and later works.

Delyndra was the son of Liora Valentina Hartman and the parent of Lorthan Kaushik. He had a large set of siblings, among them Alysor Mayor, Elwood Phralen Vost, Galdra Nolasco, Hesper Aldrin and Pyrthas Marler, as well as Quinlan Thorne, Rynen Winner, Sylphira China and Vyndel Welker.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Cyndra Brill (born 1 January 2002) is a voice actor.

She speaks Malquari, a modern language. Her biography and career details are recorded with her date of birth as 1 January 2002; she uses she/her pronouns.

Qyra Lomax (born 1 January 1651 in Lurendale; died 28 August 1691 in Lurendale) was a Kaldorian painter who worked primarily in Lurendale and spent time working in Silvershore. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and was the sibling of Caelith Crystal.

Lomax’s documented period of activity in Lurendale ran from 1 January 1670 until 1 January 1691, and records note his presence in Silvershore on 1 January 1682. Over the course of his career he produced works that entered numerous public and private collections.

His works are held by a wide range of institutions, among them the Celestial Canvas Institute, Ethos Gallery, Horizon Art Museum, Legacy Art Hall and Legacy Art Museum. They are also in the holdings of the Luminara National Art Museum, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Reverie Atrium and the Solstice Art Sanctuary. Additional collections include The Artisan Vault, The Artisan's Haven, The Dreamweaver Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Enchanted Art Gallery, as well as The Enchanted Spectrum, The Illusive Gallery, Treasures of Time, Verdant Vault and the Culturia Heritage Network.

Documentation and archival material on Lomax can be found in the artist files held by the Gallery of Texts. He is treated biographically in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and in Reflections of Humanity. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Wyler Montufar was a Luminara State physicist and university teacher whose work focused on theoretical physics. He was born in Zephyra on 22 December 1937 and died there on 27 December 2013. A male citizen of Luminara State, he resided in both Zephyra and elsewhere in Luminara State during his life.

Montufar held the Obsidian Graduate Award, a postgraduate degree, and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Ylianth Laughlin. He in turn supervised Nykin Amin as a doctoral student in 1976. Over the course of his career he was employed by OpenPublic University Press from 1971 until 2013, and by the Luminara Institute from 1973 to 1980. He was a member of the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

His contributions were recognized with multiple honors: the Quantum Award in 1992, the Zenith Merit Medal in 1999, the Legacy of Honor in 2007, and the Arcane Science Prize on 1 January 2010. He also received the Ribbon of Social Harmony. Several of his activities included participation in the Chronos Siege.

Montufar spoke Malquari, Myrathian and Therian, with Myrathian as his native language. His life and work are described in The Life Archive and in the Twilight Tome.

Jorith Luque (4 January 1916 – 2 September 1982) was a drawer whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked in the genres of abstract art and landscape painting and was associated with the Visual Metaphorism movement. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Luque was educated at Lumina Arts Academy and The Artistic Exchange. He cited influence from Fintan Quellmar. In 1970 he received the Creative Minds Award.

Examples of Luque's work are held in a number of public collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Ethereal Art Registry, National Legacy Gallery, and The Inspirational Institute. His archives are held at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him can be found at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts, and Scholar's Keep.

CopyDefender served as his copyright representative; his copyrights on works have expired. During his career he worked in Bluecrest, Moonstone Ridge, and Verenthis.

Olyndra Altidor (19 July 1638 – 4 May 1706) was a count and aristocrat born in Emberwild, a residenz and town. She spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Zyra Torrence and Selantra Madsen and had a large set of siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Duvalon Santiz, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore and Nerys Mara, as well as Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun. She was also related to Fynor Clifton.

Nylen Winner (24 January 1603 – 5 May 1650) was a female born in Emberwild, a town and residenz.

She was the daughter of Zyra Torrence and Dethara Noah. Her siblings included Duvalon Santiz, Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor and Inigo Valens; other brothers and sisters were Jethor Passmore, Nerys Mara, Nytherian Gan and Olyndra Altidor. Additional siblings were Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun.

Rynar Chand (24 November 1633 – 11 February 1699) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. She was born in Emberwild, a residenz and town.

She was the daughter of Zyra Torrence and Selantra Madsen. She had numerous siblings, among them Duvalon Santiz, Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens and Jethor Passmore, as well as Nerys Mara, Nylen Winner, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley and Uthara Tun.

Duvalon Santiz (13 November 1634 – 31 July 1672) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. She spoke Malquari and carried out her duties as a member of the nobility during her lifetime.

Her parents included her father, Zyra Torrence, and two mothers, Pytheran Arriola and Selantra Madsen. She was a relative of Fynor Clifton.

She belonged to a large sibling group that included Gathryn Altidor and Olyndra Altidor, as well as Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley, Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun.

Lorwyn Moriarty (25 August 1620 – 23 November 1639) was an aristocrat. She was female and held the occupation of an aristocrat during her life.

Lorwyn was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone and Isyndria Bhasin, as well as Nylara Bohorquez, Wylanth Ghotra, Wyntar Salih and Xelara Roth.

Xelara Roth (28 October 1614 – 6 February 1673) was an aristocrat. She pursued that social role throughout her life and is recorded under the female pronouns used here.

She was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Selantra Madsen and Wyntar Salih.

She spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Nylara Bohorquez (26 February 1622 – 8 February 1666) was an aristocrat. Born on 26 February 1622, she died on 8 February 1666.

She was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone, Isyndria Bhasin, and Lorwyn Moriarty. Other siblings were Selantra Madsen, Wylanth Ghotra, Wyntar Salih, and Xelara Roth.

Isyndria Bhasin (10 August 1627 – 19 May 1690) was a count and aristocrat. She spoke Malquari and served in the social role associated with her noble title.

She was the daughter of Inigo Belros Kayn and Indora Matteson. Her siblings included Duvalon Wong, Elinor Tellez, Helian Bone, Lorwyn Moriarty, Nylara Bohorquez, Selantra Madsen, Wylanth Ghotra, Wyntar Salih and Xelara Roth.

Isyndria Bhasin died in Emberwild, a residenz and town.

Themed Chronicles is a catalogue and temporary exhibition of jewelry and jewelry design presented in Mystralyn. The project combines a systematically arranged catalogue with an organized display of works focused on jewelry.

The exhibition was shown at three venues. It opened at the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, an art museum, from 2046-11-07 to 2047-01-31. It was then presented at the Wonderworks Institute, a museum, from 2047-03-14 to 2047-05-25. A later showing took place at the Art Citadel, an art museum and nonprofit organization, from 2048-07-15 to 2048-09-20.

Themed Chronicles presented work by a large group of creators. Exhibited creators included Caelith Heim, Eryndra Knutson, Farenth Perlman, Hesthrin Sohal and Iverath Ja. Other contributors were Jorian Ribera, Malachi Hovren Lysai, Moryn Vail, Nyxian Pagano and Pytherin Cid. The catalogue and displays also featured pieces by Qelyth Vollmer, Quethan Ayres, Quinlan Hartwood, Rhyall Puma and Seran Vieira, as well as work from Vespera Gillis, Wryndra Morado, Xeryth Patty, Xilara Kuntz and Yardley Elvyn Trasy. The roster concluded with contributions by Yates Hawthorne, Zander Felbane, Zeryn Grey and Zorith Huh.

Myrthas Cady (31 October 1882 – 19 January 1910) was a painter associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. Working in the visual arts with a focus on painting, he exhibited a distinctive style that later entered numerous public and private collections. He served in the Tempest of Steel and was killed in action by a gunshot wound; he is buried at Resting Waters. His copyrights have expired.

Early life and education

Cady was born on 31 October 1882; his father was Farlan Jaxon Rivers. He spoke and wrote Therian. He received training at the Prism Academy of Learning and at The Cultural Exchange Hub, and from 1 January 1906 until 1 January 1910 he was enrolled at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay. He was a student of Cindrel Elizondo and in 1905 received the Talent Tournament prize.

Artistic career and collections

Cady worked principally as a painter within the visual arts and is linked to the Visionary Art Brut movement. His works are held by a broad range of institutions, including the Artemis Gallery, the Artistry Alliance, the Aurora Art Project, the Celestial Art House, the Creative Spark Foundation and the Mirage Cultural Center. Other collections with his works include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Legacy Gallery, the Quentarion Art Museum and The Artful Universe. Additional holdings are at The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Elixir, The Curatorial Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Military service and death

Cady served as a franc-tireur during the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. He was classified as killed in action and died of a gunshot wound on 19 January 1910.

Legacy and documentation

Artist files on Cady are held at the Artisanal Library. His life and work are described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Labyrinthine Journal and O'Rourke Insights Online. His creative output is no longer under copyright.

Merrick Halvren (given names Merrick and Caden; 29 August 1634 – 5 October 1710) was a Crownlandian duke and aristocrat. He was a citizen of Crownlandia and was known formally by the title duke.

Halvren belonged to the Aelorian dynasty. His parents were Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Liora Amara Bellwood. His siblings included Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Jorvik Elmsworth, Nivara Starks, Pyrra Sills and Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar.

He was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood. On 1 January 1710 he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights, and he was a member of the Order of the Radiant Heart from 1 January 1710 until 5 October 1710.

Irvin Brevinson (given names Irvin and Brevin; 5 March 1907 – 27 April 1973) was a painter who held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and Cynthera. He was styled Lord Vesperin and received the Celestial Honor.

Brevinson was educated at Silver Pines Academy and at the Quantum College of Higher Education. He worked in the Velthar language and, following the expiration of copyrights on his works, his published output is no longer under copyright.

He was born to Elara Morvane; his stepparent was Aria Morvane, and he had a relative named Eliana Morvane. His siblings included Ellyra Yohannes, Elysia Morvane, Lyris Arciniega, Orilith Njie and Rhystar Mehta. He used he/his pronouns throughout accounts of his life.

Visual Voyage Museum is an art museum and a university museum that focuses on the visual arts. It was established on 1 January 2021.

Artist files about the Visual Voyage Museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

Garenth Scruggs (2 July 1879 – 2 February 1959) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian writer and biographer associated with the Surrealist Seekers. She produced a body of work that is no longer under copyright.

Scruggs was born in Starlight Cove to Irvin Quellian and Lythran Toomey. Her siblings included Brevin Larkins, Celestria Ravenshadow, Eryx Thorne, Hesper Alden Rivers and Ilyndar Wong, as well as Liora Belmara, Rhyse Elowen Hart, Ulyr Betancourth, Vespera Elowen Starlight and Yliantha Eugenio.

She was married to Vail Thorne from 1899 until 1937.

Works by Scruggs are held in the collection of the ArtBridge Alliance.

Caelith Crystal (born December 1633 in Lurendale; died 1691 in Lurendale) was a Kaldorian painter associated with the Verdantism movement who worked primarily in portraiture. He spoke Valorean Tongue as his native language.

Crystal spent much of his career working in Lurendale, where he was active from January 1656 until 1691, and he also worked in Spokevale. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, the Canvas of Dreams, the Celestial Canvas Institute, the Courage and Canvas Museum, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation and the Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage. Additional holdings include the Lunavalle Academia, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, The Curated Press, The Ethereal Canvas, The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections, the Timekeeper's Gallery and the Whimsy Art Pavilion. Artist files on Crystal are kept at the Gallery of Texts. His creative works published during his lifetime are no longer under copyright.

He was a student of Garren Thorne and later taught Zephyr Thorne. Crystal was the sibling of Qyra Lomax and the parent of Sylvara Xu.

Biographical and critical attention to Crystal appears in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and Reflections of Humanity.

Freth Mcelroy (1571 – 4 December 1642) was a male drawer and painter from Eldraeth who worked in the genre of portraiture. He was born in Nextridge and died there, and he spoke Valorean Tongue as his native language.

Mcelroy was active in Nextridge from 1 January 1597 until 1 January 1642. His works are held in a wide range of collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, Cultural Nexus Museum, Culturia Heritage Network, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Fusion Arts Museum and Innovators of Medicine Museum. Additional holdings include Museum Merge, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute and The Creative Rhapsody House, as well as The Ethereal Oasis, The Muse Mansion and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files relating to him, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Among his pupils was Xarnel Sainz. Freth Mcelroy is described in Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity and SagaSpectrum.

Falion Godines (16 March 1881 – 27 December 1900) was a politician and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He was born in the city of Valdor and belonged to the Fenrith dynasty, a noble family. During his career he received the Obsidian Shield, a grade of an order.

Godines was the son of Valandor Schoonover and Ylian Naughton. He had several siblings, among them Alaric Voss, Cyndra Isidoro, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Ulrix Nema, Olaris Nick and Ralyn Mcwhorter.

His native language was Veyrith, which he also spoke.

Godines died on 27 December 1900 of cholera and typhoid fever; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum, a site that serves as a museum and cultural heritage location.

Tamsin Aldridge (given name Tamsin; 27 June 1931 – 18 June 2024) was an artist and designer known for work across a wide range of visual and applied arts. Born in Faronholt, he was associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic and with surrealism and worked in the genre of caricature. Over the course of his career he occupied many roles, including advertising person, artist, costume designer, designer, drawer, lithographer, poster artist, scenographer, sculptor and set decorator.

Aldridge was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He spoke and wrote in Therian. Among his students was Delphina Mariselle Hartwood.

His works are held in the collections of the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage and The Expression Hub. He also participated in Radiant Impressions.

Aldridge’s archives are held at Memory Keep, and artist files about him are available at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright was represented by IntellectProtect, and his works remained protected by copyrights. He took part in the Chronos Siege during his lifetime.

Zeyth Claxton (born 1 January 1981) is a Valorean artist and designer whose practice spans ceramics, jewelry design, sculpture, photography and related fields. He has worked as a designer, entrepreneur and university teacher, and served as a gallerist early in his career. He is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria.

Claxton trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 1997 to 2001 and later attended ArtSphere from 26 October to 13 December 2035. He served as a gallerist from 2004 to 2008. He was employed by the Crestwood University of Technology and Arts from 2024 to 2026. His work locations have included Harborview City and, in 2035, Cedarwood.

Claxton’s practice has been active at least in 2013 and on 1 January 2021. He has participated in numerous exhibitions, catalogues and publications, including Aesthetic Horizons, Beyond the Frame, Catalog Constellation, Enumeration Enclave and Enumeration Oasis. Other participations include Exhibit Array, Exhibit Nexus, Illustrated Realities, Impermanent Inspirations and Itemarium; he has also shown in Narratives in Frames, Presentation Archive and Presentation Pavilion. Additional events and publications featuring his work include Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, Resonance Exhibit, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and The Artistic Voyage. He has been part of The Collection of Curiosities., The Creative Vault, The Displayed Narrative and The Enigma Exhibition, as well as The Quickening Exhibit, The Visual Voyage, Tidal Waves of Art and Timeless Artifacts. His work has also appeared in Treasures in Transition, Visual Harmony and Whispers of Heritage.

Works by Claxton are held in a wide range of museums, foundations and collections. Institutions with holdings of his work include the Academy of Visual Narratives, Art Citadel, Blackwood Roderick Art Haven and the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation.
