Other collections and museums that hold his work are the Creative Heritage Archive, Creative Spark Foundation, Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium and the Krishnamurthy Art Archive. National and regional museums with his work include the National Museum of Cultural Heritage and the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, and his pieces are also in The Artistic Alliance, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Inspiration Hub. The Odyssey Observatory, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time and Velvet Treasures hold examples of his work as well, along with the Wonderworks Institute and the Xandor Collective.

Claxton’s archives are held by the Krestoria National Research Archive and, from 2061, by The Odyssey Observatory. Artist files about him are held at ArtSphere and the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library.

For representation and rights, Claxton is represented commercially by Boundless Brushworks, Brush & Easel, Catalyst Development, Paradigm Gallery, The Scenic Studio and Visionary Vault. IntellectProtect acts as his copyright representative; his body of work published during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Claxton speaks Valorean Tongue, which is also his native language. He is married to Ulyr Rust; the marriage is recorded on 22 December 2005, and Ulyr Rust is also listed as a partner in business or sport.

Rythian Meng was a male individual whose recorded dates of death include 1 January 1140 and the year 1181.

He was a son of Hesper Vossar. His siblings included Braxton Mendez, Caelith Qian, Cyndra Obi and Ilindra Bianchi; he was also a sibling of Rhyse Aveline Carter, Xian Quintanilla, Yardley Thorne and Ylandra St John.

Talyn Ramiro (2 March 1943 – 22 December 2028) was a male artist working primarily in painting and illustration. He was associated with abstract expressionism and spent his career producing works in the field of painting. His published body of work remained protected by copyrights.

Ramiro worked as an artist, illustrator and painter. He received the Creative Minds Award in 2005. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and of the United Artisans Collective, and he took part in the Artisans Unite event.

His paintings and illustrations are held in numerous public and private collections, among them the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Canvas Museum and the Dreamscape Museum. Other institutions that hold his works include the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, the National Legacy Gallery, the Radiant Brush Gallery, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, the Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Visionary Experience.

Artist files documenting his career are kept at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Pact of Shared Commerce is a preferential trading area that was established on 19 April 2028.

Among its participants are Amethystia, Astralis, Auroria, Celestria, Drakeldoria, Jorvani, the Elysian Coast and Elysium. Other members include the Federation of Territorial Economies, Galatrix, Gelanthia, Infernix, Luminara, Lunethia, Meridia., New Providence and Novemara. The pact also counts Oceantia, Red Horizon, Solandria, Tarothia, Valdrem, Thundra, Trisandria, Vanguardia, Talvoria Republic, Ventoria, Talvorian, Vortune, Ythalia, Zephyralia and Zephyron among its participants. The Federation of Territorial Economies participates as a customs union and as an intergovernmental regional organization.

Vortune's participation in the Pact of Shared Commerce began on 19 April 2028.

Jorath Davidson (16 July 1525 – 29 September 1569) was a Caelumorian drawer and painter who worked in the art of painting. Born in Caelumport, he spent his career working in Caelumport and is recorded as a citizen of Caelumoria. His active work period is dated from 1 January 1540 to 1 January 1569.

Davidson trained under Pyrith Hampton and, in turn, taught artists including Phylar Shams. He worked professionally as a drawer and painter and spoke Thesvian.

Works by Davidson are held in numerous collections and institutions. His works appear in the holdings of Artisan's Vision Hub; Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation; Flourish Art Temple; Fusion Art Institute; Infinity Art Museum; Innovators of Medicine Museum; Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; Luminara National Art Museum; Museum Merge; Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures; Solstice Art Ensemble; The Artistic Odyssey Museum; The Charitable Canvas; The Historical Nexus; The Historical Studio; The Innovative Nook; The Palace of Reflections; The Reverie Museum; The Visionary Echoes Gallery; Valtaris Art & Culture Institute; Vivid Visions Gallery; and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about Davidson are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Davidson is described by a range of published and archival sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library, The Solstice Chronicles, and Verifiable Vade Mecum. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He died in Caelumport on 29 September 1569; his cause of death is recorded as the plague and his manner of death as natural causes.

The Town Tales Museum is an art museum and a local authority museum operated by a local government body. It is located in Cynthera, a country that is an island country and sovereign state and is also a colonial power. The museum was founded in 1948.

Among its visitor facilities, the museum includes an accessible toilet.

Yates Umbren (given name Yates; born 16 April 1960 — died 28 March 2043) was a Cyntherian film and stage professional whose career spanned from 1979 to 2043. He worked across film and television as an actor, voice actor and television actor, and was also a film director, film producer, producer, screenwriter, playwright and writer. He held the noble title of baron and was a citizen of Cynthera.

Umbren received multiple honours during his life, including the Celestial Honor, the Glorious Order and the Radiant Emblem. In 2014 he was awarded the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and his documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy and by The Archive of Stories.

In addition to his artistic career, Umbren served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and took part in the conflict known as Aegis Warfare. He spoke, wrote or signed several languages, among them Kynthor, Language Preservation Studies, Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar. He adhered to humanism and was associated with the sport of tennis.

Umbren died of heart failure; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Alden Merrick Thompson (born 1 January 1916) was an Orinthian artist and writer associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. He worked as an etcher, graphic artist, illustrator, painter, photographer and writer, and his practice spanned the fields of graphics, illustration and literature. His professional activity is recorded as beginning on 1 January 1937 and ending on 1 January 1998. His given name was Alden.

Thompson was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts. He counted Darian Morrow among his influences and was a member of the Nexus Learning Society. He spoke and wrote in Malquari and Quolmar. He also took part in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions.

Examples of Thompson's work are held in numerous public collections. Among them are the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the Mirage Art Pavilion and the National Legacy Gallery. His work is also in the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, the Terranova Artis Museum and The Artistic Universe, as well as The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Storytellers' Studio and the Vivid Visions Gallery. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files relating to him.

Thompson received the Sentinel's Honor on 1 January 1996. His copyrights are represented by IntellectProtect, and his works remain protected by copyrights. He is described in the databases and portals DataGalaxy and ReadRealm. Sources record two dates of death for Thompson, 1 January 1998 and 20 August 1998.

Delyth Ye (1504 – 1565-01-01) was a male drawer and painter from Ecotropolis who held citizenship of the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic. He worked principally in the art of painting, producing portraits over a career that began on 1519-01-01 and continued until 1565-01-01. He spoke and wrote in Thesvian.

Ye's works are held in numerous public and private collections. Among them are the Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum, the Chronicle Gallery and Cultural Nexus, as well as the Echo Art Foundation and Essence of Art. Additional repositories with works by Ye include The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Curatorial Vault. His pieces also appear at The Curated Press, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Space and Treasures of Time.

Documentation on Ye is preserved in both print and digital resources. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. The copyright status of his published works is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

Gryndell Archive Quarter is a big city, a city, a historic district and an urban area in Nymbrelia. The settlement began on 1573-03-23. It is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Gryndell Archive Quarter is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts and of The Outliers Collective. The Global Heritage Alliance for Arts is an international cultural association and international non-governmental organization, while The Outliers Collective is an organization.

Gryndell Archive Quarter maintains twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Utopis (start time 2023-01-03), Zephyrium (start time 2025-08-04), Primaris (start time 2026-06-17) and Portvale (start time 2026-09-19). Additional partnerships include Brevion (start time 2032-11-22), Olarith (start time 2035-03-23), Myrindale (start time 2037-06-21) and Luminara (start time 2042-10-10).

Aelan Tiller (31 December 1908 – 3 November 1993) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting, printmaking and graphic work. He lived and worked in Wyndrell and also worked in Calidore. Tiller spoke Therian, which was his native language, and held atheism as his worldview. He died in Wyndrell of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Tiller trained at the Creative Spectrum Academy and The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Lyvian Fee. He in turn taught Berenth Guillot. Cyndel Campbell is recorded as a significant person linked to him.

His occupations included painter, printmaker, lithographer, graphic artist, ceramicist and drawer. He worked across a range of genres, among them decoupage, figure painting, landscape painting, portrait painting and still life. His work is associated with the movements Dreamscape Narratives, fauvism and neo-impressionism. He participated in exhibitions and events such as Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta.

Memory Keep holds Aelan Tiller’s archives covering the period 1956 to 1977, and artist files about him are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described by the sources DataGalaxy and Quantum Translation.

Tiller’s works are held by numerous museums, galleries and foundations. These include Abstract Assemblage, Aesthetic Insights Press, Aesthetica Museum, Alchemy Arts Museum, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Haven , Artwave Institute, Aurora Art Project and Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Additional collections holding his work are Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Dreams, Civic Visions Museum, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Collective Canvas, Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Artopolis and Cultura Nexus. Other institutions that include his work are Cultural Nexus Museum, Discovery Hub, Dreamscape Museum and Echoes of Art.; still further holdings include Essence of Form Museum, Ethos Art Society, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum and Lystoria Artisphere Museum. His work also appears at Mirage Art Pavilion, Myrthwood Art Collective, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, National Museum of Cultural Heritage and National Sanctuary of Visual Arts. Additional repositories are Nature's Palette Sculpture Park, New Wave Art Sanctuary, Odyssey Art Center, Quentarion Art Museum, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Realm of Creativity Museum and Solaris Cultural Collective. Spectrum of Expression Gallery, TerraMuse Nonprofit, Terranova Artis Museum and a range of institutional archives and galleries also hold his pieces, including The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Art Archive, The Artful Journey Institute and The Artifact Atelier. His works are furthermore in The Collective Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Exploratorium of Art, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Historical Nexus, The Muse Spectrum, The Reverie Repository, The Spectrum Institute, The Visionary Sanctuary, The Visionary Whirl and The Whirlwind of Art, as well as in the Treasures of Expression Museum, Verdantia Art Collective Museum and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Tiller received the Noble Valorian Order. His copyright representation is recorded with IntellectProtect and Music and Media Syndicate. Records note that copyrights on his works have expired, and a public domain date of 2064-01-01 is also recorded.

Ulthar Mahler (born 1 January 1603) was a male designer and painter known for work in genre painting. He spoke Malquari, which was his native language, and his copyrights on works have expired.

Mahler was born in Hightower and also worked there during his career. He had documented periods of work in Ecotropolis from 1 January 1630 to 1 January 1645, and in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1630 to 1 January 1634. One of his known students was Micaiah Stormrider.

Examples of Mahler’s work are held in many public and institutional collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey; the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale; Cultural Nexus; Discovery Hub; Enchanted Brush Institute; Ethos Gallery; Flourish Art Temple; the National Center for Creative Heritage; National Legacy Gallery; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub; Radiant Pavilion; and Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum. His works are also in The Artisan’s Realm; The Artistic Discovery Museum; The Creative Convergence Gallery; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; The Ethereal Oasis; The Expression Hub; The Palace of Reflections; Tranthia Art Haven; Vivid Echoes Gallery; Vivid Visions Gallery; and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files on Mahler are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a number of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex, and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Sources give two different dates of death for Mahler, recorded as 1662 and 17 August 1664.

Ilynth Groom (16 May 1648 – 9 November 1680) was a military officer and politician who served as apostolic administrator from 1 March 1659 until his death on 9 November 1680. He achieved the rank of general and took part in the conflict known as Sectarian Strife, a religious war. He spoke Kynthor.

As a military officer and political figure, Groom combined service with administration; he held the position of apostolic administrator for the period beginning 1 March 1659 and ending on 9 November 1680.

Groom was born to Kalyn Ponder and Hylith Cordell. His godparents included Brethyn Okoro and Joryn Prosser; both Brethyn Okoro and Joryn Prosser are also listed among his siblings. His other siblings were Draxella Wingate, Kynthor Dana, Maelwyn Testa, Orlyn Montanez and Peryn Inzunza.

Ilynth Groom died in the Harmonia District and was buried in the Sanctum of the Lost. His life and career are described in the literary work Beneath the Starlit Sky, the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon, and the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Bibliophile Brotherhood is a literary society. It was founded by Inigo Valeron and began on 24 August 1656 in Windermere, a college town and medium regional center.

The organization is described in the written work Arcana Document and in the literary work The Elysian Fields.

Ferith Zermeno (6 March 1514 – 18 February 1603) was a Caelumorian engineer, general contractor, painter, sculptor and writer. He worked in genres associated with homoeroticism and was ethnically Yothrins. He spoke Thesvian.

Zermeno studied under Wyndan Byers. During his career he worked in Caelumport from 1 January 1568 until 1 January 1571, was active in Ecotropolis in 1568, and worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1571 to 1 January 1572.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Cynthera National Art Repository, Echo Art Foundation, Harmathia Art Repository, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, Luminara National Art Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion and Museum Merge. Additional holdings include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Prismatic History Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, Seraphim Art House, The Art Archive, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Haven, The Exploratorium of Art, The Historical Nexus, The Palace of Reflections, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum and The Visionary Experience. Artist files on Zermeno are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Ferith Zermeno is described in a range of sources and publications, among them DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, Qylarans, Tales from the Abyss, The Scroll of Influencers, The Solstice Chronicles and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

He died in Seraphim Bay on 18 February 1603 and was buried at the Basilica of the Sacred Lore.

Ethereal Art Registry is an art museum and a state agency of the sovereign state, the constitutional republic, the federal republic, the superpower, the country and the historical unrecognized state. It was established on 1 January 1956 and is located in Moonstone Ridge, on the continent and subcontinent of Elysium. Moonstone Ridge is a city in the sovereign state, the constitutional republic, the federal republic, the superpower, the country and the historical unrecognized state; it also serves as a county seat, a state or insular area capital and is a tourist city.

The Registry maintains works in the collection Ethereal Exhibits, which functions as both a collection and a museum. Artist files relating to the Registry are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

Ethereal Art Registry is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It was accredited in 2061 by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that operates as a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization.

Crownwick Landerson (2 February 1650 – 11 August 1672) was a priest who held citizenship of Crownlandia. He served in that religious capacity during his lifetime.

He was a member of the Aelorian family. He was the son of Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer and Wyrith Heckman.

He had ten siblings: Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Kylenth Guillaume, Olyndra Janet, Qylyn Flagg, Rhyall Piazza, Rythor Gilbertson, Sylvara Batiste, Thalassian Monarchis, and Uthria Danielson.

Rilith Fc (given name Irvin; 30 August 1905 – 18 February 1980) was a Mystralyn designer, drawer, painter and sculptor. Born in Cleanscape, he worked primarily in the genre of figurative art and was associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. He held the noble title of baron from 1970.

Throughout his career Rilith produced paintings, drawings and sculptures that reflected the principles of Temporal Idealism. He cited Dorian Everhart and Kaelith Thornwood among his influences. As a practitioner of several visual disciplines, he combined design and sculptural practice with drawing and painting.

Works by Rilith Fc are held in numerous collections, including Arboreal Artistry, Artropolis Nextridge, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Solstice Art Storage, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Inspiration Hub and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files on Rilith are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Rilith’s native language was Therian, which he also spoke and wrote. CopyDefender is listed as his copyright representative, although the copyrights on works published in his lifetime have expired.

Faelon Neely (31 July 1928 – 3 January 2011) was a Mystralyn drawer, graphic artist, illustrator, painter and printmaker. He was active in 1961.

A native Therian speaker, Neely also spoke Malquari and wrote in Therian. His works are held in the collections of the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Museum Merge, National Gallery of Creative Diversity and National Legacy Gallery, as well as The Artistry Realm, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Inspiration Hub and The Visionary Landscape.

Artist files about Neely are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts. He is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy and by the archival collection The Archive of Stories.

Neely’s body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights, and his copyright representative is IntellectProtect.

Aramys of Mystral (born 7 June 1865; died 1 January 1868) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title Mystral. She was a citizen of the Myralun Empire, a historical transcontinental sovereign empire.

A member of the Jorathyn dynasty, Aramys of Mystral was the daughter of Thalios Myralun and Kirelle Beryndra. Her siblings included Wylar Xent, Aurelian Myralun, Isera Volin, Cyrus Myralun, Eldrin Valen and Lysandra Myralun.

Yardley Xamar Tis (born 24 September 1794 – died 3 October 1869) was a painter known for portraiture. His given name was Yardley, and he worked primarily in the genre of portrait. He spoke the Therian language and, over the course of his life, produced works now held by numerous institutions.

Tis served as court painter from 15 October 1855 until 2 August 1869. In 1859 he was awarded the Noble Valorian Order. Among his students was Adeline Thornfield Mitchell. He is described in the written work Arcana Document, and artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in the collections of Aesthetic Insights Press, Artoria Capital Museum, Canvas of Dreams, Culturavia Artistralia and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional holdings include the Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Art Haven, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Luminous Lodge, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Experience and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Tis died by suicide on 3 October 1869 and was buried at Memory Lane. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Neryth Yeager (6 April 1522 – 7 April 1559) was a Velorian Dominion artist and architect. Born in 1522, he was of the Yothrins people and spoke Thesvian. Over the course of his career he worked as an architect, court painter, drawer, fresco painter, painter and sculptor. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Yeager worked in a range of genres, including allegory, history painting, mythological painting, portrait and portrait painting, as well as religious art. His documented work locations form a clear sequence: he worked in Sylthara from 1540 to 1541, in Nimbustown from 1542 to 1543, in Caelumport from 1543 to 1547, and in Seraphim Bay from 1547 until his death in 1559.

He was a student of Pherinna Goel, and his own pupils included Mynel Williams and Nyrian Blanco. Yeager received the Sacred Shield Fellowship during his lifetime.

Works by Yeager are held in many public and private collections, among them Artropolis Nextridge, Branash Cultural Collective, Canvas of Dreams, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Cultura Artopolis and the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara. Additional holdings include Cultural Treasures Museum, Culturia Heritage Network, Echo Art Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press. Other institutions with his works are Harmony Exhibit House, Historical Horizons, Legacy Art Sanctuary, Legacy Arts Foundation, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and the National Mural Museum. His pieces also appear in the National Museum of Innovative Expression, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Art Exchange, The Artistic Cascades, The Continuum Gallery and The Curator's Corner. Further collections holding his work include The Gallery of National Pride, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Historical Studio, The Odyssey Museum and The Palace of Reflections. His works are also in The Puppetarium, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Experience, The Whirlwind of Art, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdant Vault and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files on Yeager are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a number of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles.

Yeager died of heart failure on 7 April 1559 in Seraphim Bay. He is different from Elinor Antwi.

Jorian Broome (15 July 1645 – 1 January 1708) was a Kaldorian painter, printmaker, etcher, drawer and art collector associated with the Kaldorian Impressionism movement. His field of work was the art of painting and his creative output encompassed a wide range of genres, including genre painting, history painting, hunting still life, landscape painting, mythological art and mythological painting, portrait and portrait painting, religious painting, self-portrait, still life and vanitas. Broome’s works are no longer under copyright; copyrights on works he published in his lifetime have expired.

Born in Dawnspire, Broome studied at the Dawnspire University of Civic Studies from 1659 to 1660. He was a pupil of Olyn Yoon from 1660 to 1662, and he studied under Brynith Dalrymple during 1663; he also received instruction from Jaxira Soltero. Broome’s documented work period ran from 1664 until his death in 1708.

Broome’s professional activity included an early period working in Dawnspire from 1 January 1659 until 1 January 1663 and a later period based in Harborview City from 1 January 1670 until his death on 1 January 1708. Over the course of his career he combined making original paintings with printmaking and etching, and he was active as a collector.

As a teacher, Broome mentored numerous students. Among them were Celyndra Gallego (from 14 January 1667 to 1670), Galindra Umanzor (1673–1675), Zephyr Thorne (1675–1680), Taryn Cesar (1687–1691), Galindor Steve (1689–1691) and Pembryn Mcpherson (1692). Other students included Elarin Beats, Elyndor Lou, Garren Mirak Solenn, Iridia Trevizo, Lysira Schenk, Rylas Shafi and Valenith Brophy.

Broome’s works are held in a large number of institutions and collections. They appear in Aesthetic Insights Press, Branash Cultural Collective, Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Canvas of Dreams and Canvas of Illusions Gallery, as well as at the Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex and the Chronicle Gallery. Civic Library Publishing and the Creative Spark Foundation also hold his work, together with Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor, Cultural Odyssey Museum and Cultural Reflection Gallery. His work is represented in the Culturia Heritage Network, Discovery Hub and Nebula Loom Assemblage, and it is part of holdings at the Eldoria Art Museum of the Republic of Valtoria, Elysian Atrium and Essence of Art. Additional collections that include his work are Thalorix Reliquary, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Art Society and Ethos Gallery, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum and the Fusion Art Institute.

Further repositories and museums holding Broome’s work include Infinity National Heritage, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum and Legacy Art Sanctuary. His works are in Luminara Art Haven and Lunavalle Academia, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and Mirage Art Pavilion, as well as within Museum Merge and the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces. The Narrative Art Conservatory, National Center for Creative Heritage, National Gallery of Creative Diversity and National Institute of Cultural Heritage also preserve his art, alongside Nexus of Vision, Nostalgia Nook and the Sailor's Legacy Center.

Collections further holding Broome’s works include the Solandria National Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Ensemble and Spectrum Cultural Institute, as well as The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute and The Aesthetic Spectrum. His works appear at The Artful Exhibition Hall, The Artifact Arena, The Artisan Vault and The Artistry Realm, and are included in The Celestial Craft Gallery, The Chimeric Art Institute and The Creative Nexus. Other institutions holding his work are The Curiosity of Colors, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis and The Exploratorium of Art, plus The Expression Hub and The Futurist Gallery. The Harmony Space and The Heritage Exhibit, The Interestium and Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities keep examples of his work, as do The Nexus of Wonders, The Paintbrush Paradox and The Storytellers' Studio (as well as The Storytellers' Studio.). His work is also in The Verdant Gallery and The Visionary Experience, Tranthia Art Haven, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time and Treasures of Tomorrow.

Artist files on Broome are held at the Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep. He is described in a range of published and digital sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Legendarium, Qylarans, SagaSpectrum, The Celestial Codex, The Fabled Codex (published 1960), The Midnight Library and The Scroll of Influencers. Broome was a citizen of Kaldoria, spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue, and he died in Harborview City on 1 January 1708.

The Arcane Labyrinth: A Journey to the Unknown is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It follows the episode Fragments of Infinity in the series chronology.

The episode was first performed and published on 3 February 2038. It was distributed on a video on demand basis by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand and streaming platform.

Halden Quevedo served as director of photography for the production. The work’s color is listed simply as "color". Coverage and descriptions of the episode have appeared in The Feature Folio and VividViews.

Cast members of the episode include Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim and Ylostar Gaynor. Characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Several of these characters are presented as fictional humans and television characters, and Harmony Quill is also identified as a comics character. Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram and is additionally described as a fictional writer and television character.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Waylon Mercer was a Galdorian copper engraver, drawer, mezzotinter and printmaker known for work produced in the mid-18th century. His given name was Waylon. Sources record two possible dates of birth, 1 January 1712 and 11 June 1712, and two possible dates of death, 1 January 1772 and 8 May 1772; records also indicate he was active in 1771. He spoke and wrote in Therian and worked from Nythra Isle, dying in Harborview City.

Mercer trained and taught within the printmaking arts; among his students was Elian Carter Thompson. Over the course of his career he practiced copper engraving, mezzotint and related drawing and printmaking techniques.

Material relating to Mercer is preserved in a variety of libraries, archives and museums. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His works appear in numerous collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records, Harmathia Art Repository, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery, The Archive of Wonders, The Creative Portal Museum, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Visionary Experience and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

He is described in several published and digital sources, among them the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, DataGalaxy and ItemVerse. The copyrights on his works have expired, and his printed output is no longer under copyright.

Ulyndor Seaman (28 April 1712 – 4 May 1761) was a drawer, graphic artist and painter active from 1732 to 1761. He spoke Therian and was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research. His career and works have been described by DataGalaxy.

Seaman trained under Cole-Ren Aerbryn. He in turn taught students, among them Elthar Rivadeneira and Halindel Noah.

Works by Seaman are held in numerous collections and institutions. These include Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and National Legacy Gallery. Additional holdings are at Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files relating to Seaman are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyright on works published during his lifetime has expired.

Yelith Varney (given name Braxton; born 12 May 1906 in Thistledown; died 11 June 1995) was a Cynthera artist whose practice centered on painting and encompassed work as a graphic artist and photographer. He worked primarily in the art of painting and spoke Velthar.

Varney was a member of Seraphim Art House and produced work that entered numerous public and private collections. Among the institutions holding his work are ArtBridge Alliance, Artemis Gallery, Artisania National Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, and Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage. His works are also in Curator's Archive, Echoes of Heritage, Ethos Gallery, Harmony Exhibit House, and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional collections include Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Terranova Artis Museum, and The Artistic Discovery Museum. His work can be found at The Civic Repository, The Community Art Repository, The Creative Nexus, The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery, and The Ethereal Oasis. The Local Legacy Museum, The Puppetarium, The Remembrance Gallery and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute also hold examples of his work. As a member of Seraphim Art House, that institution likewise holds pieces by him.

Varney received honors during his career, including the Knights of the Ethereal Realm and the Lumina Token, the latter awarded in 1971.

Documentation and representation for Varney are maintained in a number of places. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and CopyDefender serves as his copyright representative; his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He is described in the database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Orylin Johal (8 June 1906 – 9 April 1998) was an architect, designer, urban planner and writer whose work was in the field of architecture. His notable work includes The Inspiration Institute. He was professionally active from 1932 until 1998.

Johal's built work and designs are held in a number of public and private collections. His works are in the collections of the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus and the National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative; his body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights. Johal was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Artist files about Johal are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at Scholar's Keep. He is described in reference sources such as CloudLibrary and DataGalaxy.

Johal's native language and the language he spoke and wrote was Velthar. He died in Eastwood City on 9 April 1998 from surgical complications.

Orilith Njie (1908-05-30–1936-7) was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian who spoke Velthar. She lived during the early 20th century and is recorded with those birth and death dates.

She was raised by her mother, Elara Morvane, and had Aria Morvane as a stepparent. Njie was part of a family that included several siblings: Ellyra Yohannes, Elysia Morvane, Irvin Brevinson, Lyris Arciniega and Rhystar Mehta. She also had a relative named Eliana Morvane.

Therin Fenner (born 1603 in Nextridge; died 1 January 1674 in Nextridge) was a graphic artist and painter who held citizenship of the Chronosian Era. He spoke Valorean Tongue, his native language, and his creative career was active from 1620 until 1674 in Nextridge.

Fenner worked in Nextridge from 1620 through 1674, and among his students was Halyra Peraza. The copyrights on his works have expired.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artoria Borderland Museum, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Culturia Heritage Network, Curiosities Art Museum, and Echoes of Art. Additional holdings include Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Narrative Art Conservatory, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Continuum Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Legacy Lounge, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Time, Vivid Echoes Gallery, and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Fenner is discussed in a range of published sources, including Fragmented Realities, Knowlexicon, Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Labyrinthine Journal, and Reflections of Humanity. The Gallery of Texts holds artist files relating to him.

Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan (born 31 July 1482; died 12 September 1539) was a politician and a duke of the Quicksilver family. He held the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order, and was known by the given name Fintan.

Born to Heliar Cool and Damaris Maelis Vorn, O'Sullivan was part of the Quicksilver noble family. His siblings included Helian Armstead and Olyndra Valenhart, and his extended family included relatives Pembryn Harden and Wyrden Biswas. He was the father of Valenith Whitaker.

His life and career are described in a variety of sources, including the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the written work Legendarium, the collection Quantum Nexus Archive, and the encyclopedia RefereX.

The Catalyst Society. is an organization that came into existence on 2042-07-31. Its headquarters have been located in Brightstone since 2042-07-31.

Brightstone is a big city and a college town. It is also described as a cantonal capital of a state, a cantonal capital of a landlocked country, a cantonal capital of a confederation, a cantonal capital of a federation, a cantonal capital of a sovereign state and a cantonal capital of a country. In addition, Brightstone is characterized as a city of a state, a city of a landlocked country, a city of a confederation, a city of a federation, a city of a sovereign state and a city of a country, and as a municipality of a state, a municipality of a landlocked country, a municipality of a confederation, a municipality of a federation, a municipality of a sovereign state and a municipality of a country.

Henris Ferdinand (born 13 April 1916 or 15 April 1916; died 1986 or 15 November 1986) was a male drawer, painter and sculptor who worked in figurative art. He spoke Malquari and was a member of the Imaginarium Academy.

He was educated at Creative Spectrum Academy. He also took part in the Chronos Siege.

His works are held in the collections of Arboreal Artistry, Artropolis Nextridge, Color Spectrum Division and the Creative Spark Foundation. Additional holdings include Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Palette of Possibilities and Solstice Art Storage, as well as The Artistic Cascades, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Ferdinand received The Imagination Medal on 1 January 1975. His archives are held at Memory Keep, and artist files about him are maintained by the Gallery of Texts. He is described by DataGalaxy.

CopyDefender served as his copyright representative, and copyrights on his works have expired.

He died of bladder cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Zorrik Smart (27 February 1943 – 18 December 2035) was a Luminara State and Myralun Empire citizen who worked as a physical chemist, physicist and politician. His research and professional interests lay in physical chemistry, physics and theoretical physics. He was born in Zephyra and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge.

Education and training
Smart attended Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1965 to 1967. He held the Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, and the Obsidian Graduate Award, a postgraduate degree. His doctoral work was supervised by Aelvin Garrity and Caelan Ralen Ivryk, and he was a student of Delvyn Saldana and Karyn Lally.

Career and memberships
Alongside his scientific work, Smart was active in public life. He became a member of the Myralun Luminara Academy Press in 1992 and joined the Hope for Tomorrow Party in 1995.

Honours and recognition
Smart received several honours during his life, including the Ribbon of Social Harmony, a civil decoration and socialist order of merit, on 1984-06-10; the Quantum Award, an order, on 1995-09-11; and the Infinitum Recognition, a medallion and science award, in 2021.

Personal background and legacy
A member of the Qasthirians, Smart spoke Malquari and Myrathian. His life and work are described in The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

Zeyth Peak (561 BCE – 421 BCE) was a satrap who also held the military rank of admiral. He was killed in action.

He was the son of Valandor Zorrilla. His siblings included Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford, Jordan Turner, Kelyr Swartz, Olyndra Pleitez, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth and Wrylin Mark.

He is described in the Starlit Manuscript, a written work.

Cole-Ren Draxford (born 17 September 1773, died 30 September 1820) was a drawer, etcher and painter best known for work in the portrait genre. His given name was Cole-Ren. He was active professionally from 1788 until 1820 and spoke Therian.

Draxford's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Celestial Gallery, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Elysian Atrium and Enchanted Brush Institute. Additional holdings include Ethos Gallery, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Museum Merge and National Legacy Gallery. His work also appears in the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He was a student of Neryth Rz and counted Liam Thornfield among his own students. Draxford was a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research. His life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation and in Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Bellia Bobadilla (born 17 March 1974 in Quolens) is a male drawer and photographer associated with the pop art movement. He works in media that bridge drawing and photographic practice and has been linked stylistically and critically to contemporary pop art currents.

Born in Quolens, Bobadilla speaks Therian and Thesvian. He cites Unyra Lott as an influence, and he participated in the art exhibition Documenta edition titled Radiant Impressions. His work has received official recognition in the form of the state order Everlasting Tribute.

Bobadilla's works are held in a number of public collections, including the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Artifact Atrium, The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, and The Memory Museum. Artist files about him are maintained at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts, and his career is described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

His copyright is managed by IntellectProtect and his works are protected by copyrights.

Lorwyn Funes (born 4 January 1923 in Myrthwood; died 18 July 1997 in Ironwood) was a painter, art critic and teacher whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked professionally as an art critic and painter while also teaching, and he was employed by Lumina Arts Academy.

Funes received training from Braxton Emberwood, Veldron Hinkle and Yardley Thompson, studying under each during his development as an artist. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Aurora Art Gallery, Canvas of Dreams, the Cultural Tapestry Museum and Infinity Art Museum. Additional collections that include his work are the Myrthwood Art Collective, Radiant Brush Gallery, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Curatorial Vault, as well as The Inspirational Institute, The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Expression Museum and Echo Publishing House.

Artist files about Funes are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His works are protected by copyrights. He spoke Velthar.

Olyndra Valehart (born 3 February 1606; died 14 November 1657) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title duke and was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family.

She was the daughter of Yloria Francois. She was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jaryn Humphries, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Jynara Harvey, Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn, and Xerath Tapia.

Her given name was Olyndra, a female given name.

Gwendal Bourne (1 April 1913 – 9 May 1966) was a male military officer and politician. He served as a member of the armed forces and attained the rank of general, and he took part in the Chronos Siege, a large-scale historical conflict.

Bourne was a member of the Yondercrest noble family. His parents were Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers. He had several siblings, among them Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Hylith Zaki, Illyndra Bartlett, Pylira Uno and Tharyn Flanigan.

Alongside his military career, Bourne was active in politics. He spoke Malquari.

Gwendal Bourne died on 9 May 1966 in Hightower, a metropolis that also functions as a major city, college town and financial centre.

The Splintered Worlds is a story arc that forms part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria television series. It is presented within the wider Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria media franchise series.

The Splintered Worlds comprises twelve parts, each presented as a media franchise episode. These parts are Aether Trails: Legends Reimagined; Chronicles of Aetheria; The Celestial Nexus: A Journey to the Unknown; The Celestial Secrets: A Tale of Heroes; The Chronicles of the Inbetween; The Forgotten Sanctum; The Labyrinth of the Timeless; The Shattered Realms: A New Tale.; The Shattered Whispers; The Shattered Worlds of Aether; The Timeless Realities: A Journey Through Time; and The Timeless Realm.

Theros Hall (4 January 1917 – 31 October 2000) was a Cynthera and Mistralith artist associated with post-impressionism who worked primarily in the portrait genre. He was a painter, muralist, etcher and drawer whose recorded period of activity runs from 1 January 1939 to 1 January 2000.

He was educated at Canvas Heights College, with recorded end times in 1933 and 1937, and was a student of Hesper Alden Brightwood. Over the course of his career he worked in Calidore and Ignisport, and his practice encompassed both easel painting and large-scale mural work.

His membership of Seraphim Art House is recorded with start dates in 1967 and 1979 and an end date of 1977. He is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Archival material on Hall is held at the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. Works by Hall are held in a wide range of institutions: the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage and ArtBridge Alliance; the Artifacts and Archives Institute and Artisania National Gallery; Carandor Artistry Productions and the Color Spectrum Division; the Creative Spark Foundation and the Cultural Canvas Museum; Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Reflection Gallery; Echoes of Heritage and Heritage Heart Museum; the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex and the Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum; Mirage Art Pavilion and Narrative Nexus; the National Museum of Heritage and the Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum; Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Seraphim Art House; Solstice Art Sanctuary and Solstice Art Storage; The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Civic Repository; The Community Creation Center and The Ethereal Dimensions Gallery; The Ethereal Oasis and The Mind's Eye Gallery; The Remembrance Gallery and the Treasures of Expression Museum; Treasures of Time and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute; the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and the Verdant Vault.

Hall received the Harmony Cross. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright is represented by CopyDefender. He spoke Velthar, and his recorded family includes a sibling, Liora Hallstone.

Solara Springs is a big city and a city or town. It was founded on 1 January 1687, and from that year it lay within Myralunara State until 22 October 1760.

Throughout its history Solara Springs has been part of several states. After leaving Myralunara State it became part of the Myralun Empire from 22 October 1760 to 1 March 1956. It was then in Myralunith from 2 March 1956 to 24 October 1956, and subsequently formed part of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 25 October 1956 until 29 December 1961. More recently, Solara Springs has been in Luminara State since 26 December 2030.

The city was officially named after Nytheren Evangelista on 9 May 1963. It is twinned with Silverbrook (since 8 September 2051) and with Jorvann (since 2054), and has been a member of the network SyncSphere since 2054.

Solara Springs is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the FactFolio (an encyclopedic dictionary), and the written work Legendarium. The city has received the Quantum Award, an order.

Ulyra Blood (1 August 1646 – 25 March 1697) was a naturalist, politician and writer from Jorathia. He combined scientific interests with public life and literary activity during his career.

Born in Jorathia, he belonged to the Sablemoor noble family and was the son of Dorian Elwood and Peryn Solis. He was one of many siblings, among them Bryndra Ballesteros, Bryndra Lino, Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart, Pyraen Tibbetts, Quinlan Raxir, Syldor Seely, Valandar Rochester, Viorelle Amaris and Zafrina Althoria.

He was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society. His life and work are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Delvyn Blaine (born 15 June 1623; died 9 June 1691) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of count. She is described in the biographical dictionary and written work Reflections of Humanity.

Born to Merrick Alastor Thorne and Eryndor Jeronimo, she was one of a large group of siblings. Her siblings included Darlen Vaz and Darovan Arrieta, as well as Faelith Fryer, Helvian Nell and Inigo Valeron. Other brothers and sisters were Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, Olyndra Mia Thorne and Unyra Jae.

Brenith Terrazas (1 January 1754 – 1 January 1819) was an aristocrat.

She was the daughter of Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune. Terrazas was part of a large family and had nine siblings: Braxton Mercer, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch, Jareth Susan, Quindor Brewster, Rynel Sawyer, Velian Rock, Wyler Deyoung, and Zoran Wadhwa.

Liora Solandrius (given name Kirelle; 18 September 1962 – 1 August 2055) was a royal citizen of Solandria and a member of the Aelorian Dynasty. She bore the honorifics Chief Aeloria and Knight Aerion and was commonly styled with those titles.

She was the daughter of Selath García. Liora was married to Elara Solandrin from 10 June 1987 until 1 August 2055, the latter date marking the end of the marriage upon her death. The couple had five children: Aeliana Solandrius, Aveline Solandria, Elysia Solandrian, Liora Solandrian, and Viorelle Solandria.

In her career she held the rank of lieutenant and took part in the Aegis Warfare, a world war and historical period.

Liora spoke, wrote, or signed multiple languages, including Corath, Therian, Thesvian, and Velthar.

The Remembrance Repository is a museum located in Krestoria. It was founded on 1989-10-04 and has received recognition as a registered museum.

The institution is a member of The Alliance of Ideas, having joined that cooperative and cultural association and network organization on 2059-01-01. It also maintains partnerships with both The Alliance of Ideas and the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, the latter being a government organization that functions as a cultural institution and a collection.

The Repository is described in the data set InsightVerse, with entries for the institution dated 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30 and 2060-08-03. For admissions and access it accepts the AccessCard, which serves as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

The Artifact Atrium is a museum located in Krestoria. They were established on 2043-12-16 and have received the registered museum designation.

They became a member of The Alliance of Ideas on 2059-01-01 and also maintain a partnership with The Alliance of Ideas. In addition, they have a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium; that consortium is a government organization that functions as a cultural institution and a collection.

For admission and concessions The Artifact Atrium accepts the AccessCard, which serves as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

The Artifact Atrium is described in the dataset InsightVerse on 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30 and 2060-08-03.

Darlen Penney (born 1985-08-30; baptized 1985-10-09) is a Crownlandian royal and philanthropist. She was born at Tranquil Keep and holds citizenship of Crownlandia. A member of House Aelistranith and the House of Eldoria-Mirathis, she is classified socially as royalty. Her hair color is blond, and she speaks Velthar and Xarnum.

The daughter of Crownthalas Monarch and Liora Zoltan, Penney is the sibling of Crownthalasian Sovereign and Maximilian Crownstone. She is the mother of Crownlandian Sovereign Realmington, Quinella Domínguez and Zenith Poon. Her listed godparents are Alaric Crownston, Alaric Crownstone, Alessandra Zoltani, Celestria Moonshadow, Crownthalas Jorvikson, Elara Vespera, Jorin Bowden, Pyreth Cepero, Ryland Zolterras and Valorian Krestorinius.

Penney has held the honorific prefix Knight Aerion from 1985-08-30 until 2003-09-18 and has borne the honorific prefix Chief Aeloria since 2003-09-18. She served as a consort from 2003-09-18 to 2012-06-01 and is also noted as a philanthropist. On 2003-09-18 she participated in the Celestria Alysor Union.

Her spouse was Alysor Wasson; their marriage is recorded from 2003-09-18 to 2062-01-10. Penney has received several honors, including the Order of the Celestial Serpent, the Order of the Radiant Heart (awarded on 1986-04-20) and the Starlight Gala. She is female.

The Apex of Discovery Medal is a cultural prize, an order conferred on individual recipients, and a science award. As a named honor, it combines elements of cultural recognition and scientific distinction while taking the visible form of an order presented to persons.

The medal had its inception in 2019 and was formed in Hightower. Hightower is described in related records as a metropolis and big city, and is also identified as a college town, district capital, financial centre and residenz. It is further listed as a type of local government and urban municipality in various administrative categorizations, and as an urban district of federated and free states as well as of a ward.

The Apex of Discovery Medal is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version, edition or translation.

Selorin Alegria, given name Olyndra (14 August 1766 – 1 January 1791), was a princess of the Galdrin dynasty and an aristocrat. She was born and died in Culturia Noblis. As a member of the nobility she also performed as a viol player and spoke Therian. Her life is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Selorin was the daughter of Inigo Valente and Dravion Appiah. Her godparents were Delphina Ystral En and Inigo Prynn Salor. She had a large number of siblings, among them Delphina Nereth Vale, Elanthar Gasca, Inigo Montale, Nylaris Prendergast, Peryn Harder, Tobias Winstone, Viorelle Mariselle, Xandor Lemons and Zyvra Smoot.

She died on 1 January 1791 in Culturia Noblis of smallpox; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Dorian Merathiel (born 28 March 1658; died 4 December 1720) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. His given name was Dorian. Born in Zephyria, he belonged to the Aranthor and Quicksilver families and served in the capacity of an aristocrat during his life.

He was the son of Nerys Bowers and Othryn Coffey. His siblings were Arathian Shea, Halwyn Gan, Jorvik Altharion, Phaelan Gerardo, Pyridan Enrique and Yzara Mcginnis.

Merathiel spoke Malquari and was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society. Throughout his life he combined his aristocratic status and ducal title with participation in that society.

The Ethereal Odyssey: Beyond the Echoes is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Produced by Gwendal Truax, the episode follows The Arcane Astral and is followed by The Celestial Balance. It was first performed on 2035-04-15 and published on 2035-11-04; distribution is via video on demand through ScreenSync.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet that includes a prison environment. Its principal themes concern imprisonment, psychological trauma and solitary confinement. The episode has been described in the magazine VividViews.

Cast members of the production include Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah and Vyndel Gibbs. Characters who appear in the episode include Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake, Miles Hawthorne and Sable Hayes. Voice actors associated with the episode are Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda and Yates Orinthal.

A technical attribute listed for the episode is its color, recorded simply as "color."

Jorvik Alaric Thorne (born 1 January 1620) was a margrave and political figure of the Kaelwyn family. He died in 1694; sources record dates of death as 1 January 1694 and 9 June 1694. His given name was Jorvik, and he was classified as noble.

Thorne was the son of Yloria Francois and Darovan Arrieta. He was one of a large set of siblings; among them were Alderon Khalil, Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jaryn Humphries, Jynara Harvey, Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa, Olyndra Valehart, Thalorin Stockwell, Tyndra Vigil, Viorelle Amara Lethwyn and Xerath Tapia.

In his professional life he worked in civil service, governance and politics, and served as a ruler. His occupations are recorded as politician and ruler, and his noble title was margrave. He was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood.

Thorne spoke and wrote Malquari, a modern language, and Nythoria, an ancient and sacred language that is now a dead language. Details of his life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Galindra Deoliveira (born 30 June 1537 in Oakridge; died 4 February 1602) was a citizen of Isolara and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. He was born in Oakridge and spent his life as a subject of Isolara.

He was one of the children of Wynex Malhi and Ytherin Yong. His siblings included Elara Schiller and Zyris Schiller, as well as Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena, Rhaelar Montez, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia and Yndral Shine.

Galindra is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. A significant person associated with him was Elysian Romo.

Bellia Courtney (28 September 1778 – 27 July 1851) was a noble politician who worked in military affairs and politics. He served as Protector of the Eternal Flame, a historical position and noble title, and carried out his work in Nymara. He was awarded the Shimmering Honor.

A member of the Quicksilver family, he was the son of Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier. His siblings included Adeline Thornfieldson, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard, and Wryndra Turpin.

Courtney spoke Malquari, Nythoria and Therian. His life and career are described in the Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Olyn Berlin was a painter and illuminator known for work in religious art. Sources record two different dates of birth for him—1426-01-01 and 1434—and give his date of death as 1494-02-18. His ethnicity is recorded as Yothrins, and he spoke Thesvian. He was male.

He trained under Idrisyl Mckoy and Xenith Usher, and he in turn taught Daryth Mahmood.

Berlin worked in Seraphim Bay from 1484 and also had a professional presence in Sylthara. His place of death is given as both Caelumport and Seraphim Bay.

Examples of Berlin’s work are held widely: Artistry Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Reflection Gallery, Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery, Echo Art Foundation, Ethos Gallery, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Royal Gallery Palace, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Art Haven, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Futurist Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum, Verdantia Art Collective Museum, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files on Berlin are held at the Gallery of Texts. His published works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Berlin is described in several reference sources, including DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library, and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Zandor Rolle (27 September 1507 – 26 February 1534) was a male military officer and ruler who held the noble title of margrave. He was born in Oakridge and died in Oakridge, and belonged to the Kaelwyn family.

He was the son of Pembryn Harden and Olyndra Valenhart. His siblings included Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Thorian Whitcomb, and Wynex Malhi.

As a military officer and ruler, he served in those capacities until he was replaced by Wynex Malhi, who was also one of his siblings. His life and career are described in the Quantum Nexus Archive.

Shadowed Alliances is a video game developed in Zolterra and published on 2057-08-01. An indie real-time strategy title, it is presented as a single-player experience and uses bird's-eye view game mechanics. The game is designed primarily for touchscreen input.

Shadowed Alliances runs on Catalyst OS, a mobile operating system and computing platform, and is available on several hardware platforms: Aetherwave, a product model; AstraBox, a model series and video game console model; and CipherSphere, a brand that serves as a computing platform and operating system and is distributed as proprietary software. Availability on CipherSphere began in 2057-10. The title is also compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 electronic device model.

Distribution is handled digitally: Shadowed Alliances is offered via digital distribution through AppForge, AppSanctum, GameCentral, PackageSync, PixelMart and VaultPlay.

The game's work or name is associated with multiple languages and language varieties, including Eldorathian, Kynthor, Language Preservation Studies, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Thesvian, Trellish and Velthar.

Rhaelar Montez (27 December 1520 – 21 September 1566) was a margrave and ruler born in Oakridge. He served as a ruler and held the noble title of margrave until his death in Falthoria.

Rhaelar was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. His father was Wynex Malhi and his mother was Ytherin Yong. He was related to Drystan Chaney and Lydan Chirinos, and had many siblings, including Elara Schiller, Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena, Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia, Yndral Shine and Zyris Schiller.

He married Berenth Neff on 25 August 1557; the marriage lasted until his death on 21 September 1566.

Rhaelar Montez is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Radiant Muse Pavilion is an art museum headquartered in Delvoria. It was established on 1 January 1887 and officially opened in 1887. The museum is located in the administrative territorial entity of Delvoria and maintains its main offices there.

Delvoria is a city and a big city, and it is identified as a major regional center. The locality also functions as both an urban district and an urban municipality.

Denzil Ashcroft (given name Denzil; 1183–1188) was a male noble and a member of the Wintervale family. He was the son of Denzil Thornton.

His siblings included Ivrys Baek, Mira Ashcroft, and Nytherian Hopkins, as well as Pyraen Ruiz, Qalir Villagrana, and Tyndra Echeverri. He was also sibling to Vilynd Luz, Waylindra Traylor, and Zyndra Lindstrom.

The Wintervale family is a royal house.

Ilyndor Good (given name Calix; born 1484-03-01) was a male painter, fresco painter and drawer from Caelumport. He belonged to the Yothrins and spoke Thesvian. His artistic practice encompassed allegory, history painting, mythological painting, portrait and religious painting. His active work period is recorded as beginning on 1499-01-01 and ending on 1549-01-01. Sources describe him in a number of compilations and catalogues, among them Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, ReadRealm, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. Reported dates of death include 1549-01-01 and 1549-05-16, and his place of death is given as Caelumport.

Ilyndor trained under Ryniel Crawley and Wyrden Rubino; Ryniel Crawley is also recorded as his employer. He in turn taught Mystron Selby. Over the course of his career he worked in several locations, including Arcadia, Caelumport, Lystria and Seraphim Bay.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, including Artistry Alliance, Branash Cultural Collective, Canvas of Dreams, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Fusion Art Institute, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Lunavalle Academia, and Ravenwood Collective Art Museum. Additional holdings and exhibition venues include Royal Gallery Palace, The Artful Tapestry, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Celestial Craft Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curated Press, The Innovative Nook, The Palace of Reflections, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files on Ilyndor Good are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts; these repositories are described respectively as an art library and research library, an archive and art library, and an art library and museum library. His published works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Rynira Cheong (10 July 1908 – 24 November 1977) was a Goldenreach nobleman, art collector, independent scholar and photographer. He held the noble title of duke and the military rank of general. His published works are recorded as having their copyrights expired.

Born in Zephyria, Cheong was a member of the Aranthor family. His parents were Pheris Dueñas and Alaric Voss. He had three siblings: Farenth Goldman, Fintan Valecrest and Ilyra Solene Thorne. He married Isylar Comer on 30 October 1945.

Cheong worked in Zephyria; records list his work location there with a start time of 1 January 1929 and an end time of 1 January 1877. Over the course of his life he combined his interests in collecting and scholarship with photography.

He received several honors, including the Aurora Badge, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star, the latter awarded in 1947. Cheong was a citizen of Goldenreach. He was buried at the cathedral Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam.

Narrative Nexus is an archive, library and museum located in Beltharis.

The institution was established in 1996 and is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association.

Fintan Marek O'Sullivan (born 27 April 1883, died 14 January 1959) was a male painter whose field of work was the art of painting, working primarily in the genre of history painting. His given name was Fintan.

He was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and later served as an employee there. He was a student of Jalen Carter Thompson and Rolyn Naik. He worked in Hightower and died there.

Works and archival material by and about O'Sullivan are held in a number of institutions. His paintings are in the collections of Aurora Art Gallery, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Glistening Gallery of Treasures, The Art Archive, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Harmony Space and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation and The Forgotten Prophecy.

He received The Apex of Discovery Medal, a cultural prize and science award, in 1945. Copyrights on his works have expired. He spoke Malquari.

Knights of the Eternal Flame is a dynastic order of knighthood distributed by the head of a former royal family. It was established in 1557 and is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

The order's grades include the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame. The next lower rank in its hierarchy is the Knights of the Ethereal Realm, which is itself a dynastic order of knighthood and an order of chivalry.

Bellia Feller (15 June 1409 – 1 March 1435) was a ruler. He was born in Ashenvale and spoke Malquari.

Early life and family
Bellia Feller was born to Alden Thornfield. He had seven siblings: Belyndra Joe, Damaris Rivenna Dorl, Freyael Welborn, Naryn Spurgeon, Oryndel Rothschild, Rhaelar Humes and Seraphina Lumeris.

Career
As a ruler, Bellia Feller used the Malquari language in his affairs.

Death and sources
Bellia Feller died on 1 March 1435. His life and role are described in RefereX, an encyclopedia.

Hesthrin Verde (1 January 1470 – 13 September 1545) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic citizen and an artist whose work centered on the art of painting. He worked across several media as a painter, illuminator, copper engraver, printmaker, sculptor and drawer, and was associated with the Ethereal Futurism movement. His work encompasses allegory, animal painting, history painting, mythological painting and religious painting. He spoke Thesvian and was of the Yothrins people.

Verde served as a court painter beginning in 1507 and carried out artistic work in a number of cities, including Merekara, Arcadia, Ecotropolis, Greystone, Lystria and Seraphim Bay. He was influenced by Nerya Reynaga. He died in Lystria on 13 September 1545.

Works by Verde are held in numerous collections and galleries. They appear in Abstract Assemblage, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Reflection Gallery and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. Additional holdings include the Echo Art Foundation, Heritage Hall, Museum Merge, Radiant Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and The Celestial Craft Gallery. Other institutions with his works are The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curiosity of Colors, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Evolution Gallery, The Futurist Gallery, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Storytellers' Studio., Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Archival and reference material on Verde is available in artist files at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. His known relatives include Avelyn Tostado, Bryndor Pence and Pyrith Fortune.

Yandor White was a male writer whose work spanned literature, theatre and military affairs. He worked as a novelist, playwright and poet and is also described simply as a writer. His literary output is associated with the mannerism movement and covers genres including poetry and tragedy. He wrote in Kynthor.

Born on 29 September 1586 and baptized on 9 October 1586, White's recorded date of death appears in different sources as 1 January 1655 and 22 April 1655; both dates are part of his surviving records. He died in Verenthia and his manner of death is recorded as natural causes. At one point he was detained at Cloudspire.

Over the course of his life he held a number of occupations: he served as a soldier in 1609 and worked as a tax collector in 1629, in addition to his literary career as a novelist, playwright and poet. His activities combined interests in theatre and military affairs alongside his literary production.

White's works are held in a number of collections and institutions, including Cultural Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery and The Museum Collective. Artist files about him are held at Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and documentation files relating to him are kept at Theatricum Archive. His published works are no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

He has been described or catalogued by a variety of sources, among them Cascade Collective, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, ReadRealm, Shadows in the Ink, Tales from the Abyss, The Elysian Fields and The Midnight Library.

Lythial Broyles (born 3 April 1625, baptized 12 May 1626–died 9 February 1644) was a noble who bore the family name Ilyndra and belonged to the Cindervale family. He received the Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame.

He was the son of Faryn Morrissey and Ulrith Locke. His siblings included Aeloria Thalmaris, Damaris Lorianne Rivers, Dorian Callahan, Orinthia Magdaleno, Rithyra Hennessey, Umbrin Grand, and Zorrik Maxfield.

He spoke Thesvian. He died in Aquilon and was interred at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Rynel Sawyer (born 2 August 1741; died 2 December 1808) was a male military officer and regent from the Velorian Dominion. He served as a general and held the position of regent during his career. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion, an empire and sovereign state.

As a military professional, Sawyer’s occupation is recorded as military personnel and his attained rank was general. For his service he received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry.

Sawyer spoke Malquari, a modern language.

He was the son of Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune. His siblings include Braxton Mercer, Brenith Terrazas, Elowen Millz, Elwood Finch, Jareth Susan, Quindor Brewster, Velian Rock, Wyler Deyoung and Zoran Wadhwa.

Sawyer is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Grand Cross of the Celestial Flame is a grade of an order bestowed upon an individual. The grade forms part of the Knights of the Eternal Flame and is also designated as a subclass of the Knights of the Eternal Flame.

The Knights of the Eternal Flame is a dynastic order of knighthood.

Hestira Avitia (born 1968 — died 2 November 2048) was a citizen of Xandoria who held the noble title Knight Aerion. She was born in 1968 and died in Falmare on 2 November 2048.

Hestira was a member of the Lorianth dynasty and the daughter of Myrren Ferrante.
