Born in Willowcrest, Thorne was the son of Ulyndra Alexander and Kirelle Amara Solis. His given name was Zephyr, and he spoke Malquari. He married Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore on 16 January 1803; the marriage continued until 10 November 1845.

Thorne took part in the Conclave of Conflict. Over the course of his life he received several honors, including the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, the Circle of the Brave Lotus, the Crystaline Honor and the Pinnacle Honor.

He belonged to a broad family network. His siblings included Caelorian Pullen, Jaryn Kearns, Nyvian Hearn, Olyndra Valesca Thorne, Qylara Casias, Velyndra Huebner and Viorelle Vespera Marcelline. Other relatives recorded in accounts are Adelzo Thornfield, Velun Pyr, Falyndra Mccreary, Hesperyn Amy, Irvin Caldwell, Irvin Pyrelan, Kaelar Trinidad, Nerya Kramer, Sylas Harkwood, Sylas Thorne and Zolric Norra.

Thorne is discussed in a number of works, appearing in Factoid Fount, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Holoset is a border city and a town in the sovereign state of Solandria.

Holoset is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation.

Holoset maintains twinning relationships with a number of other administrative bodies. Vorthelis (a city); and Xelthoria (a municipality of sovereign state, municipality of realm and municipality of country and a municipality of the historical nationality).

Xindar Mazariegos (4 February 1869, Zephyria — 14 August 1951) was a Goldenreach aristocrat. She died of a stroke on 14 August 1951, and her death was recorded as due to natural causes.

Her given name was Zafrina. She was a member of the Quicksilver family; her father was Zoran Morais and her mother was Kaelith Astran, who was a twin. Her siblings included Galindor Switzer, Olyndra Orindel, Orindel Thalorian, Pheris Dueñas, Pyraen Vargas and Viorelle Amarantha Liora. She spoke Malquari.

On 26 April 1910 she received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest.

Flourish Art Temple is an art museum and museum building located in the city of Seraphine in the country of Cynthera.

The institution was established on 1 January 1921.

It was granted the Historical Integrity Mark on 12 June 1989.

The building includes an accessible toilet for visitors.

Hesperan Sides (born 22 August 1788 or 28 August 1788; died 22 March 1871) was a Malquari-speaking polymath whose work spanned the sciences, the arts and public life. He worked in anatomy, geology, meteorology and physics and pursued a wide range of occupations including aphorist, art historian and theorist, autobiographer, composer, diplomat, librarian, librettist, mineralogist, novelist, philosopher, politician and statesperson, theatre manager, theologian, travel writer, writer and zoologist. He also wrote drama, lyric poetry and tragedy and produced literary and theatrical works in Malquari.

Early life and education
Sources record two dates of birth for Hesperan Sides, 22 August 1788 and 28 August 1788. He studied at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing from 1804 to 1807 and later attended Branash Imperial University of the Free Republic beginning in April 1809 through 1810. He was a student of Jorvik Larkwood and of Micaiah Thorne. Malquari was his native language and the language in which he both spoke and wrote.

Career and affiliations
Sides combined scientific research with literary and institutional roles. His scientific interests included anatomy, geology, meteorology and physics, and his occupations also encompassed mineralogy and zoology. In the arts and letters he worked as an art historian and art theorist, a theatre manager and a librettist, and he produced novels, autobiographical writing and travel literature as well as aphorisms and philosophical writing. He held the non-academic title Advocate of the Fallen and was active in public life as a diplomat, politician and statesperson. He was a member of several learned bodies and organizations, including the Academy of Natural Sciences, the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and he was associated with freemasonry.

Works, collections and sources
Examples of Sides's works are held in multiple collections: Chronicle Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artisan's Haven, The Curatorial Chamber, The Expression Hub and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are preserved at Theatricum Archive. He is described in a range of published and compiled sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinite Reimagining, ItemVerse, PersonaRecord, Reflections of Humanity, Stellar Reinterpretation and Tales from the Abyss. His creative output is noted as having copyrights that have expired.

Influences, awards and legacy
Sides acknowledged or was influenced by Berenth Salcedo, Braxton Eldridge, Draxen Schiff, Sylas Ulren, Theryn Heflin and Wyrden Dooley. His honours included the Celestial Distinction and the Golden Aurora Class; the Golden Aurora Class was conferred on 14 October 1847.

Death
Hesperan Sides died at Windermere on 22 March 1871 of a myocardial infarction, with the manner of death recorded as natural causes.

Arcthor is a title and position, a social role with an associated set of powers and responsibilities. It is classified among sovereign state noble titles, country noble titles, and colonial power noble titles, and represents a specific form of queen consort.

The title of Arcthor is associated with Eldoria-Emberland. Eldoria-Emberland is described as a historical country and kingdom that also functioned as a province within larger polities: as a province of a historical country, as a province of an empire (including a designation as a province of the empire on which the sun never sets), and as a province of the colonial empire. It is also characterized as a realm.

The Duchy of Nephronia was a hereditary, historical position established in 1178 and dissolved in 1949. The office existed from its inception in 1178 until its abolition in 1949, and its holders exercised authority under that title during that period.

The office applied to the jurisdiction of Eldoria-Emberland. Eldoria-Emberland has been described variously as a historical country and a kingdom, and has also been characterized as a province of the historical country, a province of the empire, a province of the empire on which the sun never sets, a province of the colonial empire, and a realm. The duchy was located within the country of Nephronia; Nephronia is identified as a colonial power, a country and a sovereign state.

The Duchy of Nephronia was classed as a subclass of king, monarch and sovereign, placing the title among roles associated with supreme or hereditary rulership.

The Whispering Labyrinth of Echoes is a science fiction episode in the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and forms part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was directed by Zorath Parrilla and first performed on 2029-04-30. Publication dates for the episode are recorded as 2029-04-28 and 2032-08-03. The work is distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format. Production details list the work's color simply as "color". The episode is described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that fictional universe.

Characters that appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Kethara Drune, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and a computer voice. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix appears as an android character. The credited cast members for the production are Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio.

In the sequence of the series, the episode follows The Celestial Legends: A New Beginning and is followed by The Ethereal Journey: Reflections.

Yates Caldwell (born 23 September 1822 in Solyra; died 6 March 1906) was a drawer, illustrator, painter and university teacher known for work in the portrait genre. His given name was Yates.

Caldwell was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture and was employed by Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts. He worked in Seraphim Bay and spoke Malquari. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design as well as the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement.

Works by Caldwell are held across a number of public collections, including Artropolis Nextridge, the Creative Spark Foundation, Culture Confluence, Ethos Gallery and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, The Art Nexus, The Artistic Cascades, The Expression Hub and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Caldwell received the Seraphic Prize and was awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1892. He is described in a range of sources, among them Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Xalorin Fontes (given name Ryland; 1 February 1883 – 18 May 1951) was a botanist, plant cell biologist and university teacher whose work was centered on cell biology. He held citizenship in the Myralun Empire, Syldoria and the Valdrinia Empire.

Fontes was employed by Synergy Knowledge Collective and worked in Jotunspire, where he also died. He was a member of several learned organisations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Constellation Institute. On 26 November 1930 he received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences and became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on the same date. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 3 December 1932 and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1937.

Across his career he contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab and was nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award on 1 January 1949. His published and archival presence is noted in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio and ReadRealm.

Born in Vornexa, Fontes spoke Malquari. He was male and is principally known for his work in plant cell biology within the broader field of cell biology.

Quinlan Yerenfell (7 May 1858 – 14 April 1944) was an astronomer who worked in the field of astronomy. He held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and the Valdrinia Empire and spoke Myrathian. Yerenfell was educated at OpenPublic University Press and his doctoral students included Isyndria Lamothe. His father was Sylas Verenthis.

Yerenfell belonged to numerous scholarly organizations. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Aurora Academy, and he joined the Celestial Research Institute on 27 November 1912. He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition and the Constellation Institute, as well as the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. His affiliation with Frontier Knowledge Productions began in 1922.

Among his honors, Yerenfell received the Veritas Medallion on 1 January 1889 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 27 November 1912. He was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize.

Biographical and reference works that describe Yerenfell include DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and the Encyclical of Identities.

Pylarin Mckelvey (18 March 1743 – 20 September 1766) was a male citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. The Aeloria Dynasty is described as a conquest dynasty and sovereign state that also functioned as a culture, a historical cultural region and divided region, an ancient civilization and historical country, a historical period, and a style.

He belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar family; Ilithra-Celthar is identified as a clan and a double family name that serves as a family name, hala and royal surname.

His father was Gleran Pires. His siblings included Hesperan Camara, Hesthra Deo, Merynd Alexandre, Olyndra Marchand, Pheris Keaton, Talyn Beats, Vesperyn Easton, Ylinda Christenson, Ylostar Mclean and Zyndel Nell; his father and all of these siblings are recorded as persons.

Hesthra Deo (5 January 1751 – 2 September 1809) was a politician who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar and belonged to the Ilithra-Celthar family.

He was the son of Gleran Pires and the parent of Orlyn Rosenblum. His siblings included Hesperan Camara, Merynd Alexandre, Olyndra Marchand, Pheris Keaton, Pylarin Mckelvey, Talyn Beats, Vesperyn Easton, Ylinda Christenson, Ylostar Mclean and Zyndel Nell.

Hesthra Deo is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

The Enigma of the Ethereal is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode was first performed on 2037-02-21 and has publication dates recorded as 2037-02-21 and 2037-02-25. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available by video on demand; ScreenSync operates as a video-on-demand mobile app and web broadcaster. The episode has been described in the magazine VividViews.

Principal cast members of the production include Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado and Xenith Sengupta. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano and Pyrith Fast.

Among the characters who appear are Elias Blackwood and Marcellus Stormwatch. Elias Blackwood is presented as a comics character who is a fictional human and appears across the franchise’s literary and television incarnations; Marcellus Stormwatch is likewise a fictional human who appears in the franchise’s literary and television works.

The Enigma of the Ethereal follows the episode The Lost Dimensions: The Awakening and is followed by the episode Realm of Illusions. The episode is associated with the color "color."

Olyndra Pleitez (561 BCE–461 BCE) was a male aristocrat. He is recorded as having been born in 561 BCE and to have died in 461 BCE.

He was the son of Valandor Zorrilla. His siblings included Bryndel Fritz, Cyndrel Sinha, Elthar Stanford and Jordan Turner, as well as Kelyr Swartz, Orinthar Bane, Qylar Smooth and Wrylin Mark.

Solstice Bay is a big city, a port settlement and a tourist destination. They are known for their role as a coastal urban center that attracts visitors.

Solstice Bay is described in several published sources: Dreamt Compilation, which is a version, edition or translation; Factoid Fount, which is an encyclopedic dictionary; and Legendarium, which is a written work.

Solstice Bay is twinned with a number of other cities. The partnership with Azureport began on 25 March 2032; Azureport is a big city and a metropolis, a port settlement and is also described as a city in a sovereign state, a city in a country, a city in a unitary state, a city in a republic, a city in a social state and a city in a territory. The twinning with Elysoria began on 1 January 2032; Elysoria is a big city and is described as a city of a sovereign state, a city of a country, a city of a federal republic, a city of a nation and a city of a confessional state, and it also functions as a municipality in those same categories. The partnership with Zephyra dates from 2004; Zephyra is a big city that serves as the capital of a sovereign state, a secular state, a country, a transcontinental country, a federation and a successor state, and is described as a city or town, a federal city and a federal subject of those same entities; Zephyra is also a former capital, the largest city and a million city. Solstice Bay established a twinning with Drakon City on 1 March 2035; Drakon City is a big city and is described as a city and as a populated place in a country, a sovereign state, a unitary state, a republic and a transcontinental country. Everlight is also a twin; Everlight is a big city described variously as a city in a sovereign state, a constitutional republic, a federal republic, a superpower, a country and a historical unrecognized state, and it is additionally described as an independent city in those same categories. Juniper Falls is a twin and is a big city and a college town; it is described as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country, and it is also a port settlement. Volenthis is another twin; Volenthis is described as a city in a country, a city in a unitary state and a city in a sovereign state, and it is a large city that serves as a municipality seat and an oblast seat.

Darian Rivers (11 December 1921 – 5 January 2009) was a physicist and theoretical physicist who worked as an academic and university teacher and wrote non-fiction. His given name was Darian. He belonged to the Qasthirians and followed the Veltharion worldview. He spoke Malquari and Velthar. Over the course of his career he held the position of professor.

Rivers was educated at ScholarQuest University from 1940 to 1943 and attended Fairview Comprehensive University in 1942. He was a student of Olyndor River and later supervised doctoral students of his own, including Sylas Cavorin (1961), Yardley Riven Kest (1966) and Farlan Montgomery (1970). Among his students were Paylan Anchondo and Paylan Carver.

He was a member of a number of scholarly organizations, including the Academy of Innovative Thought., the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. Rivers joined the Celestial Research Institute on 16 March 1978 and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1994.

Rivers received several awards and honors during his career: the Innovative Thought Excellence Award in 1976, the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence in 1987, the Chroma Medal in 1989, the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series in 1992 and the Nova Research Prize in 1993. He had been nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1987.

He participated in the Chronos Siege. Rivers held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera beginning in 1978.

Rivers is described in DataGalaxy, ItemVerse and The Life Archive.

The Celestial Alchemy is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The production's color is listed as "color". The episode had its first performance on 20 May 2037 and was published on 7 May 2038.

Hesperis Koenig directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand. The episode has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

Cast members include Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff.

Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers (a fictional human who appears in both literary and television formats), Cedric Emberheart (a fictional human and television character who is also represented in the franchise's literature), Harmony Quill (a comics character who also appears on television), Kieran Frostfire (a fictional human and television character), Lyric Lifesaver (an emergency medical hologram, fictional writer and television character), and Rowan Emberwood (a fictional human and television character).

In the series order, The Celestial Alchemy follows The Celestial Nexus: A New Era and is followed by The Labyrinth of Celestial Echoes.

Reflections of Humanity is a written work that takes the form of a biographical dictionary and an encyclopedia. The work is written in Malquari, a modern language, and was published in 1914.

The publication took place in Delvoria, a city and major regional center. Delvoria is regarded as a big city and functions as an urban district and an urban municipality.

Reflections of Humanity is in the public domain.

Vail Montrose (family name Dravon; born 23 June 1933, baptized 16 July 1933 – died 28 May 2011) was a Cyntherian aristocrat, military officer and monarch. He held dynastic and noble positions including Goldenvale Prince from 23 June 1949 until 20 January 1975, and both Grand Duke of Rithoria and the Federated Realms and the Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands from 20 January 1975 to 11 December 1975. His social standing was described as royalty.

Early life and family
Montrose was born on 23 June 1933 and was baptized on 16 July 1933. His mother was Celestria Moonshadow and his father was Irvin Thorne. He had several siblings: Celestria Valtaris, Hesper Thalorin, Irvin Talbot, Irvin Talmadge and Thalric Valorian Kytarathian. His given names included Axton, Fintan, Irvin, Jorvik and Vail, and his name was said to be inspired by Crownthal Jorvik, Fintan Farlanov, Fintan Rhyseris and Phineas Yonai. His godparents included Imren Poul, Alden Rhyseris, Celestria Lyraen, Crownthal Jorvik, Delphina Roselle Thorne, Elysia Crownhart, Elysia Thorne, Irvin Everhart, Vail Thorne and Valerius Aurelianus.

Titles, honorifics and official style
Over the course of his life Montrose held several honorific prefixes and styles. He bore the style Chimeric Viceroy from 23 June 1933 to 28 May 1937, Knight Aerion from 28 May 1937 until 20 January 1975, and Chief Aeloria from 20 January 1975 to 11 December 1975. Between 20 January 1975 and 11 December 1975 his official anthem was Chorus of the Stars.

Military career and public office
Montrose served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and took part in the Aegis Warfare and the Chronos Siege. In addition to his military role, he held public and hereditary offices including the Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands and the Grand Dukedom of Rithoria and the Federated Realms.

Memberships and honours
He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute. Montrose received numerous awards and honours over his career, among them the Opal Crown (1949), the Celestial Distinction (1951), the Knights of the Aetherial Realm (1953), the Apex Merit Prize (1 January 1960), the Lumina Token (1963), as well as the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, the Innovative Thought Achievement Award and the Order of the Celestial Vanguard.

Language and identity
Montrose belonged to the Luminara ethnic group. His native and principal writing language was Cynvelthar, and he also spoke and wrote Velthar. He held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and was also a citizen of Cynthera; his allegiances included service to Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and service to Cynthera.

Death
Vail Montrose died in Dreston on 28 May 2011. The manner of death was recorded as natural causes, with the specific cause listed as laryngeal cancer.

Darlen Balde (16 November 1703 – 26 December 1703) was a princess of the Galdrin dynasty who died in infancy.

She was the daughter of Inigo Thorne and Zephyros Gutierez. Her siblings included Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Delphina Balde, Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Alvren Kyl and Inigo Martinez. Elian Trevane (born 11 June 1780; died 17 June 1814) was a military physician and politician who took part in the Rithar Freedom Fighters. He spoke Velthar and is recorded as having begun his professional work period in 1814.

Early life and education
His given name was Elian. He was educated at Ironwood Academy, with his attendance at that institution ending in 1798.

Career
Trevane served as a military physician and was also active as a politician. He participated in the Rithar Freedom Fighters, a war of national liberation. His documented work period is listed as starting in 1814.

Sources
Elian Trevane is described in the Labyrinthine Journal and is cited in the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Aeliana is a female given name. It is attested in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

The name appears in Corath, Kynthor, the Valorean Tongue and Velthar, all of which are modern natural languages. In written form Aeliana is rendered using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Aeliana is the female version of the male given name Farlan.

Wyndra Pease (died 1482) was a nun who served as an abbess. She was a member of the Zephyros dynasty and the daughter of Calith Avila. As a woman, she carried out her religious vocation in leadership as abbess.

She was a sibling of Cynar Raghavan, Lytheris Barnhart, Neryth Doe, Qelith Naqvi, Quelyndra Prescott, Qynara Oz, Terath Latorre, and Uthara Carrillo.

Quelyndra Prescott (1439–1459) was a religious figure who served as an abbess. She held that office during her life and carried out duties associated with her position.

Born in 1439, Prescott was a member of the Zephyros dynasty and the daughter of Calith Avila. She died in 1459.

Her siblings included Cynar Raghavan, Lytheris Barnhart, Qelith Naqvi, Terath Latorre, Uthara Carrillo, Wylian Lafrance, and Wyndra Pease.

Vespera Lumira Ethys (born 1989) is a Cynthera installation artist, art educator and university teacher. Born in Grandview, she works in Calidore and speaks Velthar. Her given name is Vespera.

She is represented by Paradigm Gallery, and CopyDefender serves as her copyright representative. The works she published during her lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Examples of her work are held in public collections, including the Art Citadel and the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation. She has participated in a number of catalogues and exhibitions, among them Enumeration Oasis and Exhibit Nexus, as well as the temporary exhibition The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and the exhibition Treasures in Transition.

Obsidian Arts Collective is an art museum and nonprofit organization headquartered in Obsidian City. The organization was founded on 1 January 1970 and held its official opening on 22 January 1970.

Headquartered and located in Obsidian City, a big city, the Collective operates as a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. Its artist files are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that serves as an archive, art library and library.

In recognition of its cultural significance, the Collective was awarded the Legacy Appreciation Badge, a heritage designation, with that designation beginning on 19 March 2031. It was later accredited in 2061 by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that also functions as a membership organization, museum association and nonprofit organization.

Aelorn Jackson (born 23 June 1965) is a sculptor, illustrator, jewelry designer and university teacher whose work is centered on the art of sculpture. He began his professional practice in 1993 and was active as of 1 January 2029. He lives in Bryston and speaks Thesvian.

Jackson's works are held in a number of public and private collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Artropolis Nextridge, Celestial Grove of Sculptures, Creative Spark Foundation, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Solstice Art Storage, The Commons Collection and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. He is represented by The Palette Place, and his copyright interests are managed by CopyDefender; his body of work is protected by copyrights. His output is described in ItemVerse, and documentation and artist files relating to him are kept at Theatricum Archive, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts.

He has participated in a range of catalogues and exhibitions, among them Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Object Odyssey., Reflections in Art, Showcase Nexus, The Display Anthology and Vivid Visions. Jackson has received the Arcane Order and was awarded the Boundless Art Recognition on 1 January 2029. He works closely with Pherian Dove, who is both his sibling and his partner in business.

Ilyndor Neely (31 August 1818 – 2 April 1874) was a politician and member of the House Maerwyn noble family. Born in Caelumport, a major capital city, he was later recognized with the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order.

Neely was born to Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull and belonged to House Maerwyn, a cadet branch, dynasty and noble family. He was one of a large group of siblings, among them Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Calix Menard, Elian Merrickson, Elric Caelum, Eryndra Guizar, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni.

As a politician, Neely’s career is noted in contemporary sources. He died in Lunathis and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

His life and activities are described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Celestial Harvest is a video game announced on 2057-12-06 and published on 2058-10-25. It is classified as a science fiction role-playing game and is also described as an action role-playing game. The title is a single-player video game set on a fictional planet and in outer space.

The game incorporates multiple constructed in-world languages and scripts: the dialect Eldorathian; the languages Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Therian, Trellish, Veldrith and Velthar; and the writing system Valtaroscript as a written language.

Celestial Harvest was released for the Aetherwave, AstraBox and CipherSphere platforms. Aetherwave is presented as a product model, AstraBox as a model series and console model, and CipherSphere as a computing platform and operating system that is distributed as proprietary software.

Players interact with the game using a computer keyboard, computer mouse or a gamepad.

The title is distributed via digital distribution through a range of marketplaces and services, including AppAlley, AppForge, AppSanctum, GameCentral, PixelMart and VaultPlay. These services operate as app marketplaces or video game distribution platforms; AppForge also functions as a digital distribution platform, PixelMart as an online shop, and VaultPlay provides digital rights management and acts as a software repository.

Celestial Harvest is different from Quantum Duel.

Pythera Iriarte (1381–1415) was a female member of the Cimmerian dynasty and noble family. She was born in 1381 and died in 1415.

Her mother was Pyrion Lester. Pythera had several siblings: Bryston Chaires and Calith Avila, as well as Denzil Atherley and Denzil Braxim Orrisvale. She was also sibling to Lytheris Button, Quinella Gudiño, Thereth Michele, and Wyrlyn Martinson.

The Legacy Art Space is an art museum and a museum of the city of metropolis. It is also identified among museums of the city of tourist destination, museums of the city of global city, museums of the city of megacity, museums of the city of largest city, museums of the city of college town, museums of the city of big city, museums of the city of primate city and museums of the city of national capital.

The institution began in 1941.

The Legacy Art Space received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award, in recognition of its contributions.

The Legacy Lounge is a museum in Nextridge, Mystralyn. It began in 1916 and works in the areas of cultural heritage and performing arts.

The museum is located in the administrative territorial entity Nextridge, a city and seaport within Mystralyn.

The Legacy Lounge is described in the data set InsightVerse on the following dates: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

The Paper Pathway Award was a literary award presented as an award for best book by genre. It was presented to authors and literary associations in recognition of works within specific genres.

Winners of the Paper Pathway Award included Galenith Chohan (2010), Helvyn Haggard (2011), Freyael Richmond (2012), Jalen Carterson (2013), Halden Brown (2015), and Pyrra Mv (2017).

The award was replaced in 2019 by two successor prizes: The Literary Lantern, an award for best book (by genre), and The Narrative Jewel, a literary award.

Feryndra Wexler (1280–1329) was a member of the Wintervale family who held the titles of count and queen consort. She is described by DataGalaxy, Nebula Edition and The Midnight Library.

She was the daughter of Jorath Sher. Her siblings include Arlayn Quintanar, Beryndor Ok, Denzil Archer, Frenith Samuels, Kaelith Mckinney, Lysira Waldo, Melrith Fogel, Pylar Levin, Rhalin Mccormick, Wrythos Dorris and Zenith Dubon.

She is distinct from Lyra Kytara.

Ylorith Miguel (1610 – 6 March 1677) was a Kaldorian painter, drawer and architect known for portrait painting. He was born in Spokevale and died there; he spoke the Valorean Tongue. He was active around 1660 and his published works are no longer under copyright.

Trained by Drystan Valentin, he in turn taught Kylorin Edwin. Miguel worked in Crestwood, Seraphim Bay and Spokevale during his career.

Collections holding his works include Artifacts of Time Gallery, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub, Enigma Manor, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery, Infinity Art Museum and Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. Additional repositories and exhibitions with his works are the National Legacy Gallery, Sailor's Legacy Center, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Ensemble, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Collective Canvas. His paintings also appear in The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Interestium and The Palace of Reflections. Further holdings include The Visionary Space, The Whirlwind of Colors, Timekeeper's Gallery, Treasures of Time and The Visionary Space.

Artist files on Miguel are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in a number of written sources, among them Fragmented Realities; the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon; the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles; Reflections of Humanity; The Celestial Codex; and The Scroll of Influencers.

Selyndra Chauhan (born 1 January 1631 – died 26 August 1694) was a Kaldoria drawer, engraver and painter. He spoke the Valorean Tongue and held citizenship of Kaldoria. Chauhan died in Harborview City.

Chauhan's professional activity is recorded as beginning in 1651 and ending in 1694. He worked in Harborview City from 1651 to 1694, and among his pupils was Pylarin Mortimer.

His works are represented in numerous public and private collections. Examples include the Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, Krestorian Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Center for Creative Heritage, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Collective Gallery, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Expression Hub, The Historical Nexus, The Illusive Gallery, The Odyssey Museum, The Palace of Reflections, Treasures of Time and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files on Chauhan are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Chauhan is discussed in reference works such as Knowlexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon. His copyright status is recorded as "copyrights on works have expired."

Valdor is a national capital and big city on the continent of Jorathia. It functions as a municipality and as the principal city of the sovereign state and colonial power Nephronia, and it is located within Nephronia, of which it has been part since 1186.

The earliest written record of Valdor dates to 166 BCE. Valdor later served as the capital of the historical realm Eldoria-Emberland from 1294 until 1847, and it is also the capital of Nephronia.

Valdor maintains a range of international municipal partnerships. It is twinned with Quellwyn (since 2016), Verenthia (since 2018), Luminara (since 2020), Zephyra (since 2021), Dreamhaven and Lythoria (both since 2032), Orinthos (since 2026), Iskandor (since 2027), Quindale (since 2034), Emberglow (since 26 October 2039), Glacialis (since 2046), Tranquilburg (since 2024), and Nebulon (since 4 November 2061); it is also twinned with Solaris City.

Valdor has been described in several published sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, Qylarans, The Midnight Library and the Version Vault. The city is a member of the organization The Outliers Collective and appears as a location in the video game Nebula Quest.

Resonance Art Foundation is an art museum and nonprofit organization. It began in 1958 and officially opened on 1 January 1969.

The foundation is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association.

It is accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an organization that serves as an accrediting body, a membership organization, a museum association and a nonprofit organization; this accreditation is recorded for the year 2061.

Resonance Art Foundation received the Legacy Appreciation Badge, a heritage designation, beginning on 19 November 2013. Artist files about the foundation are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which functions as an archive, art library and library.

The Innovative Thought Achievement Award is an award conferred by Academy of Innovative Thought. The award is in Cynthera, a sovereign island country and colonial power.

The Innovative Thought Achievement Award is a subclass of the Innovative Thought Excellence Award and of honorary fellow; despite that classification, it is different from the Innovative Thought Excellence Award, which functions as an award, a fellowship and an organization.

The Academy of Innovative Thought is a national academy and an academy of sciences and serves as the granting body for the Innovative Thought Achievement Award.

Lysandra Wrethin-Valloré (19 March 1638 – 17 June 1705) was a male member of the House Wrethin-Valloré and a citizen of Faldoria. He bore the family name Wrethin and was born in Caelumport, where he also died.

He was the son of Elara Wrethin-Valloré and Aelan Catalan. His siblings were Maereth Valon Wrethin, Aeloria Wrethin-Valloré, Alaric Wrethin-Valloré, Aldric Wrethin-Valloré and Wrethin Valloré.

Zedry Nuñez (1230–1243) was a noble from Zephyria. She was a citizen of Zephyria and a member of the Cimmerian dynasty. Nuñez held the noble title Quicksilver, a title in the nobility of Zephyria.

Born in 1230 to Denzil Hallowfen Dray and Lyra Kytara, Nuñez belonged to the Cimmerian noble family. Her siblings included Althar Lennon, Hylith Fort, Olyndor Brewster, Olyndra Rowan, Rylas Qiu, Rythan Rosado, Terath Mcreynolds and Zephyra Rs.

Nuñez died in 1243 in Mistyvale, a municipality of Zephyria.

The Celestial Mirage is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode follows The Lost Dimensions: A Journey Beyond.

The Lost City of Aether is a science fiction episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, which is presented as a media franchise series and a television series. The narrative of the episode is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe. The episode is associated with the color "color."

Nerya Vanegas (1214–1265) was a male native of Eldoria-Emberland. He was born in Eldoria-Emberland and held citizenship of that historical country and kingdom.

Pylar Levin (1274–1274) was a female member of the Cimmerian dynasty and noble family. She was born in 1274 and died later that same year; her death was recorded as an infant death.

Aethrin Witter (4 June 1900 – 21 October 1900) died in infancy and was buried in the Sanctum of the Lost.

She was born to Ylinth Burdick and Nyrian Joyner. Her godparents were Aelorn Bazan and Bryndith Waite. Her siblings included Aldenric Caledorn, Beryth Greiner and Denzil Harrington, as well as Illystria Sharp, Nyvalis Anders, Unyra High and Uthar Bowles.

She was a recipient of the Daughters of the Radiant Quest and spoke Kynthor.

Norric Valenhart (born 12 March 1863; died 17 October 1926) was an engineer and physicist whose work focused on mechanics and physics. His given name was Norric, and he spoke Malquari.

Valenhart studied at Timberfall University from 1881 to 1885. He later worked for ScholarQuest University from 1889 to 1893. He completed doctoral work under the supervision of Caden Rivers. He supervised several doctoral students himself, including Isidore Valmont (1905), Fenwick Arlow (1914) and Ramira Brenner, and he taught Orathen Cowan beginning in 1908.

He was an active member of numerous scholarly organizations. Among these were the Catalyst Society of Knowledge and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, both from 1901; the Academy of Innovative Thought from 1907; the Cognition Coalition from 1909; and the Celestial Research Institute from 8 April 1914. Later memberships included Frontier Knowledge Productions from 1922 and the Thundorian Science Archive Database from 28 December 1923. He was also associated with the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement.

Valenhart received multiple awards during his career. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 8 April 1914, followed by the Paradigm Recognition on 1 January 1915. In 1916 he received the Chemist's Valor Award and the Nova Recognition, and he was awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1916. He was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize.

His life and work are described in a number of publications and resources, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Encyclical of Identities, Infinite Reimagining, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Life Archive.

Sylas Orinthal (27 January 1814 – 20 August 1893) was a male philosopher, university teacher and writer whose work addressed aesthetics, epistemology, metaphysics, natural philosophy and natural science. He held the position of professor and carried out his work in Hightower. His given name was Sylas, and he spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Orinthal was educated at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. Over the course of his career he was employed by Astral Springs State University, Bayview Comprehensive Institute. and the Synergy Knowledge Collective. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute and the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences. Among his doctoral students was Sylas Emberwood. Earlier in his formation, he was a student of Isyndria Meeks.

His thinking was informed by a number of contemporaries and predecessors, including Berenth Salcedo, Delyria De La Garza, Falion Iris, Hesperan Sides, Isyndria Meeks, Sylas Marwick, Talyra Sample, Xylaris Miramontes and Zyra Bracken. Orinthal combined his interests in philosophy and natural inquiry across the areas listed above.

Orinthal received several honors during his lifetime, notably the Seraphic Prize and The Apex of Discovery Medal, the latter awarded on 1 January 1892. Copyrights on his works have expired. His life and work are documented in a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, FactFolio, GeoAtlas, Infinite Reimagining, Infinitopedia, ItemVerse, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

The Celestial Odyssey: A New Legacy is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Within the series chronology, the episode follows Shadows of the Ethereal and is followed by The Forgotten Horizon: A New Dawn.

Production was directed by Felyndra Roberts, who also appears among the cast. The screenplay was written by Yardley Dovern Pax. Principal cast members include Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta. Voice roles are performed by Pyrith Fast and Ulyr Stacks. The episode features the character Miles Hawthorne.

The Celestial Odyssey: A New Legacy was first performed on 2034-04-24 and has a publication date of 2035-03-08. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews. The production’s credited color is listed as "color."

Galindor Steve (19 April 1672 – 25 February 1698) was a Kaldorian painter and printmaker associated with the Verdantism movement. His work focused on history painting and combined practices in both painting and printmaking.

Born in Harborview City, Galindor studied under Jorian Broome. He worked in Ecotropolis from 1694 to 1697, and he died in Ecotropolis in 1698.

Steve spoke the Valorean Tongue and produced a body of work that is now out of copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Examples of his works are held in numerous public collections, including Artefactual Odyssey, the Chronicles Museum and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. His works also appear within the Culturia Heritage Network and at institutions such as the Elysian Atrium and the Royal Gallery Palace, as well as The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. Additional collections holding his work include The Ethereal Canvas, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Storytellers' Studio, The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Time, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Galindor Steve is described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles.

The Enigma of Shadows is a science fiction media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the fictional universe where the narrative takes place. The episode is associated with the color "color" and references the concept of dark matter.

The episode was written by Ilyren Tiburcio and directed by Brystar Caron. It features Brystar Caron alongside Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio among its cast. The work was published on 2030-06-01 and again on 2033-03-23, with a date of first performance on 2030-06-03. Distribution is by ScreenSync and the distribution format is video on demand. The episode has been described by VividViews magazine.

Characters appearing in The Enigma of Shadows include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Sable Hayes, Serenix and a computer voice. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix appears as a fictional android; other characters such as Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder and Sable Hayes appear as human characters within the franchise.

In series continuity, The Enigma of Shadows follows The Lost Realm: A New Discovery and is followed by Chronicles of the Mystic Realms and Echoes of the Past, the latter being a two-part episode.

Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and addresses the subject of terrorism. Its date of first performance was 2032-06-20 and its publication date is recorded as 2033-05-29. The work is described by the magazine VividViews, and its color is listed in the metadata simply as "color."

The episode was written by Yardley Brackenridge and directed by Axton Mercer, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography. It is set across a number of environments within the narrative, including a fictional planet, a garden, a monastery and a shrine.

Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake, Miles Hawthorne and Sable Hayes. The on-screen cast members are Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk. Voice-only performances are provided by Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Ulyr Stacks.

Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey follows The Awakening: A New Dawn and is followed by The Ethereal Explorers. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

Garenth Buck (28 February 1823 – 26 January 1903) was a male Ardentian architect, painter and writer. He worked across architecture, the art of painting and literature, and wrote in the Malquari language. Born on 28 February 1823, he died in Hightower on 26 January 1903.

Buck's professional activity extended from 1 January 1839 until 1 January 1903. Over the course of his career he produced works now held in a number of public collections, including the Chronicle Gallery, Ethos Gallery, National Legacy Gallery, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Universe, The Palace of Reflections and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He was a member of several scholarly and artistic organizations, among them the Ethos Research Authority, the Institute of Artistry and Design and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. His contributions were recognized with awards including the Seraphic Prize and The Apex of Discovery Medal, the latter of which he received on 1 January 1892.

Copyrights on his works have expired. Buck is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Reflections of Humanity.

Deleth Lorenzo (born 25 January 1565, died 1 October 1625) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and at one time occupied the position of monarch. He was a citizen of Crownlandia and spoke Malquari.

Born to the Thalassian Sovereign Monarch, Deleth was a sibling of Thalassian Jorvikson. He fathered ten children: Hesperis Roden, Jareth Seibert, Jorvik Eldorian Steele, Liora Marcellus, Olyndra Faeloria, Qylara Heiser, Rolyn Short, Talyra Rehman, Thalyn Ferdinand and Wryten Obeng.

In his personal life, Deleth married Garenth Harrelson on 17 December 1603; that marriage lasted until 1 October 1625. Among the persons noted as significant in relation to him was Bryston Sun.

Deleth Lorenzo died at Maplewood Manor on 1 October 1625. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Dreamt Compilation is a specific version of a work presented as an encyclopedia and an encyclopedic dictionary. It was written in Myrathian, a modern natural language.

The edition was published in Zephyra on 1 January 1946. Zephyra is the capital and largest city of its country and served as the place of publication for this version.

Dreamt Compilation has its origins in both Luminara State and the Myralun Empire. Luminara State is a transcontinental sovereign federation and secular state, while the Myralun Empire is a historical transcontinental empire and sovereign state.

The work is in the public domain.

The Shattered Veil of Eternity is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and was first performed and published on 23 October 2034. The episode is presented in color.

Directed by Jorin Flannery, the production features cast members Illystria Narine, Myrlen Goldman and Ulyndor Rosado. Voice performances are provided by Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano and Pyrith Fast. The episode includes the characters Elias Blackwood and Maximus Drake, figures who appear across comics, written works and television within the Eldoria Chronicles.

The Shattered Veil of Eternity was released as a video on demand title and distributed by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and web broadcaster. It was described by the magazine VividViews. In series continuity, the episode follows The Arcane Whispers: Legends Untold and is followed by Enigma: The Lost Tales.

The Arcane Whispers of the Cosmos is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria, a television series, and was first performed and published on 1 January 2035. Presented in color, the episode is set on a fictional planet within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and centers on the theme of terrorism.

The episode was directed by Axton Mercer and written by Ellyra Saldaña and Yardley Brackenridge. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand; ScreenSync operates as a video streaming service and web broadcaster and is available as a mobile app. The episode has been described by VividViews magazine.

In the series chronology, The Arcane Whispers of the Cosmos follows The Forgotten Realms: The Awakening of Legends and is followed by The Timeless Enigma, both media franchise episodes in the same continuity.

Cast members include Myrlen Goldman and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors credited on the episode are Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Ulyr Stacks. The story features characters such as Elias Blackwood (a comics character who also appears on television), Thalen Virok (a literary character who appears on television), Marcellus Stormwatch (a fictional human appearing in literature and on television), Maximus Drake (a fictional human from the media franchise who appears in written works and on television) and Miles Hawthorne (a fictional human and media-franchise character who appears on television).

Halyra Coakley (born 1754-11-08, died 1836-01-13) was a princess who served as queen consort and worked in literary activity. She was a member of the noble Yewtree family and received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

Born in Willowcrest, Halyra's given name was Zafrina. She was the daughter of Zephyr Marlowe and Helion Dominique. Malquari was her native language, and she spoke both Malquari and Therian.

She had a large number of siblings; among them were Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Inigo Varren Mylo, Jyleth Arturo, Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Thereth Stafford, Theryn Zay and Ulyndra Alexander.

Halyra was married to Hesperyn Amy from 1772-06-12 until 1825-08-17. After her death she was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that is also a tourist attraction.

Her life and work are described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary.

Hesthor Titus, given name Vespera (4 April 1873 – 16 May 1929), was a female aristocrat who held the title princess and was styled Knight Aerion. She became princess on 24 August 1897 and carried the honorific prefix Knight Aerion during her life.

Hesthor was born in Hightower on 4 April 1873 to Elian Varros and Aelwen Prophete. She was part of a large sibling group that included Chyndra Helm, Fynlar Alphonse, Ilyra Calyss Veyran, Nylaris Sequeira, Teryn Sperling, Verenth Washington and Viorelle Edranix. She spoke Velthar.

As an aristocrat she received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, both orders of knighthood for women.

Hesthor Titus died in Altonia on 16 May 1929 from stomach cancer.

Alaric Orindelson (10 January 1897 – 13 April 1922) was a female writer who held the noble title Orindel. She was born in Caelumport and died in Quantum Haven.

She was the daughter of Zephyr Alden Mercer. Her siblings included Elian Caelithon, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

Alaric Orindelson was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

The Rift of Time is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode premiered and was published on 8 April 2035. It follows The Celestial Threads of Fate in the series and is followed by The Enigma of the Ancients. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and web broadcaster, and the episode was made available in a video on demand format. Yardley Dovern Pax served as the film editor.

The cast includes Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. The Rift of Time has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews. It is noted as having the color "color."

The Whispering Shadows: A New Journey is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is set on a fictional planet and is presented in color. Its date of first performance and publication date are both 2037-04-08.

Myrlen Goldman directed the episode and also appears among the cast. The production was distributed by ScreenSync as a video on demand release; ScreenSync is a mobile app, a video on demand and video streaming service, and a web broadcaster. The episode was described by the magazine VividViews.

The cast of The Whispering Shadows: A New Journey includes Fariel Chapple, Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Zephyros Burk; these individuals are persons who appear in the production. Voice actors on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, Xendry Bohorquez and Yates Orinthal; these performers are also persons.

Two characters who appear in the episode are Elias Blackwood and Miles Hawthorne. Elias Blackwood is a comics character and a fictional human who appears across written works and television within the franchise. Miles Hawthorne is a fictional human who appears as a television character and as a human within the media franchise.

In series chronology, The Whispering Shadows: A New Journey follows The Arcane Compendium and is followed by The Celestial Confluence; both neighboring entries are media franchise episodes. The episode belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and to the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria media franchise series, which is also a television series.

Merrick Solenvar (17 December 1929 – 18 July 1959) was a male military officer who held the rank of Elrith and served in the Chronos Siege. A member of the Kaelwyn family, his given name was Merrick and he spoke Malquari.

During his military career Solenvar participated in the Chronos Siege, a large-scale historical conflict. His service was recognized with several honors, including the Noble Crest, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

Solenvar was born into the Kaelwyn family to Yelith Rathore and Elara Sylphinus. He had four siblings: Alyndra Malquari, Jynara Weber, Sylas Arvonex and Tarynth Lathrop.

Solenvar died on 18 July 1959 in Redwood Grove. His manner of death was suicide by gunshot wound.

Thalorin was a country established in 1672 and dissolved on 1900-09-12. They were succeeded by several states following their dissolution, and during their existence they functioned as a distinct territorial and political entity.

They were governed as a constitutional monarchy and organized as a unitary state. Velthar served as both the language used across Thalorin and its official language.

The national anthem was Chorus of the Stars", a musical composition designated as the anthem; its start time is recorded as 2061-9. Internationally, Thalorin maintained diplomatic relations with several neighboring and regional powers, including Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom, Kytarathia and Nyxoria. Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian is recorded as a colonial power and historical sovereign state; the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom is noted as a historical kingdom and sovereign state; Kytarathia is described as a historical sovereign state; and Nyxoria is noted as a sovereign state.

Thalorin took part in armed conflicts recorded as the Rithar Freedom Fighters, a war of national liberation, and the Tempest of Nations, a war characterized as a world war.

After Thalorin's dissolution they were replaced by Falendor, Novemara, Nyxoria and Zephyralia. Among these successors, Falendor is identified as a republic, Novemara as a secular republic, and Nyxoria and Zephyralia as sovereign states.

Olyndra Orindel Vayen (given name Olyndra; 1 January 1918 – 30 May 2000) was female and held the noble title Orindel. She is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

She was the daughter of Zephyr Alden Mercer and Rhyse Darkmoor. Her siblings included Ilyra Ten of Caelithon and Elian Caelithon; other siblings were Alaric Orindelson, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

Melethar Grimaldo (given names Quinella and Wynelle; 12 April 1905 – 13 November 1968) was a princess and politician of the Kaelwyn dynasty. She was styled Knight Aerion and was classed as royalty.

Melethar was born in Redwood Grove and was baptized on 24 May 1905. Her parents were Malquari Valdrin and Elara Valtaris, and her godparent was Malquar Valdrin. She had five siblings: Draxen Blocker, Nyler Lupo, Rylor Koshy, Vaelith Mcmahan and Yelith Rathore.

As a politician, Melethar spoke Malquari.

Melethar Grimaldo died in Jotunspire of pneumonia. She was female.

Miraleth Sol (25 December 1500 – 8 December 1560) was a noble who held the title of queen consort. She served in the role of consort during her lifetime.

She was a member of the Darkspire family branch of the nobility. Miraleth was the daughter of Helian Armstead and Varlyn Vaught, and her siblings included Feryndor Crenshaw and Lydan Chirinos. A relative of hers was Zerynd Cassell. Her children included Crown Zafrina and Thalor Jorvistan.

Miraleth was married to Thaddeus Archemonta from 6 September 1517 until 20 February 1552. She spoke Malquari.

Pherian Palm (January 1, 1967 – January 1, 2054) was a Valorian artist working primarily in abstract art. He was known as an illustrator, photographer and textile designer, and was active around 2041.

Born a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Palm was educated at Crestwood University of Technology and Arts. He worked in Krestoria and spoke Valorean Tongue, which was also his native language.

Examples of his work are held by a number of cultural institutions and museums: Sculpted Dreams, a national museum and sculpture garden; Solstice Art Storage, a museum of modern art and nonprofit production company; The Chronicle Chamber; The Collective Gallery; The Enchanted Collection; Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities; and The Odyssey Observatory. He also participated in the temporary exhibition Impermanent Inspirations and in The Curatorial Report, an exhibition and publication.

Palm’s body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyright. His copyright representation was handled by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect. Information about him and his work is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Serath Bonner (born 5 July 1709 — died 15 September 1787) was a female politician and noble who held the title of duke and served as a regent. She was a member of the Yondercrest family and was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

She spoke Malquari and died in Darkmoor on 15 September 1787.

Serath Bonner was the child of Felynd Noh and Kaelion Kuhn and was the parent of Mylaria Bellinger. Her siblings included Belegorn Sievers, Calix Zepharon Kest, Glynara Newcomb, Lelith Cassidy, Lythor Tenezaca, Nerya Guzmán, Orinthia Gittens, Qynara Alma, Rynel Mcdaniel, Selantra Mcfarlane and Zorath Sadeghi.

Ulyr Scoggins (6 July 1783 – 8 December 1840) was a female aristocrat of the Galdrin dynasty. Born into a prominent family, she held the social rank of aristocrat throughout her life.

She was the daughter of Beryth Mchugh and Jynor Mulligan and was one of several siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Bryndra Tull, Fenwick Thorne, Phaelan Diop, Qyrian Harmon, Ronan Callahan, Ulwen Quintero and Ylindor Calvin.

Scoggins spoke Kynthor and received notable honors during her life. She was awarded the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, both orders of knighthood for women.

She died in Verenthia and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

The Celestial Saga is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, classified as science fiction. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with its narrative taking place in that fictional universe.

The story is presented on a fictional planet and in Technium., which is portrayed as an artificial entity. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn and Tobias Merriweather, both presented as human characters, Lyra Dray who appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix who appears as an android.

The Celestial Saga was written by Illuan Castleberry. Cast members credited for the episode are Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Publication dates are listed as 2032-10-02 and 2032-10-04, and the date of first performance is 2032-10-04. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format; ScreenSync functions as a video on demand service. The work is described by the sources Spectral Volume and VividViews. The Celestial Saga's color is listed as color.

In the series chronology, the episode follows The Ethereal Whispers: Secrets of the Ancients and is followed by Echoes of the Forgotten Realm and The Silent Storm.

Selinth Arrington (5 March 1762 – 14 January 1811) was a princess of the Quellhaven noble family and a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. She served as regent.

Born on 5 March 1762, Selinth was the daughter of Irvin Oathen and Vespera Ysindra Vaalor. Her family affiliation was with Quellhaven.

Her siblings included Alaric Thornewood, Elysian Valtaris, Fythar Rondon, Irvin Braxton Smith, Lurith Buck, Rhelian Ambrocio, and Ylenara Hinkle.

Selinth Arrington died in Aeloria on 14 January 1811.

Felynd Noh (born 1 January 1654, died 1 January 1729) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family who served as Protector of the Eternal Flame and worked as an art collector. He was a citizen of Calirion and spoke Malquari.

A member of Yondercrest, Noh married Kaelion Kuhn on 3 September 1692. His godparent was Kalyn Ponder. He was the father of Belegorn Sievers, Calix Zepharon Kest, Glynara Newcomb, Kelyr Ferrante, Lelith Cassidy, Lythor Tenezaca, Nerya Guzmán, Orinthia Gittens, Qynara Alma, Rynel Mcdaniel, Selantra Mcfarlane, Serath Bonner and Zorath Sadeghi.

Among his honors, Noh received the Celestial Knightly Grade. His life and career are described in Reflections of Humanity.

Noh died in Lunathis and was buried in Illyndra.

Ilyra Calyss Veyran (30 September 1882 – 18 June 1964) was an aristocrat who held the titles Radiant Count and princess and was a member of the noble family Yondercrest. She received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Born Ilyra to Elian Varros and Aelwen Prophete, Veyran was one of several children in her family. Her siblings included Chyndra Helm, Fynlar Alphonse, Hesthor Titus, Nylaris Sequeira, Teryn Sperling, Verenth Washington and Viorelle Edranix.

Veyran spoke Malquari. She was married to Avelyn Daza from 5 June 1900 until 8 June 1925.

She died in Hightower on 18 June 1964.

Sylphine Tarrin Arindel (14 February 1794 – 16 December 1840) was an aristocrat who bore the family name Arindel and belonged to the Qelthar dynasty. He married Lurith Mir on 15 July 1813, and his sibling was Elwood Arindel.

He was the parent of five children: Adeline Arindel, Alaric Arindel, Liora Arindel-Tavish, Vespera Arindel and Zafrina Arindel. One of his children, Liora Arindel-Tavish, was a twin.

Among recognitions he received were the Ethos Token and the Pinnacle Honor, both orders. He spoke Malquari. After his death he was buried at the Celestial Citadel, a church building that is also a cultural property, religious work of art and tourist attraction.

The Universal Peace Coalition is an intergovernmental organization composed primarily of sovereign states. It was established on 26 January 1992 and is registered in Mystralyn.

The Coalition's headquarters are located in Harmonia District, a metropolitan area. The organization is situated in Ostreia Citadel, a big city and enclave that is the largest city and a designated region of Mystralyn.

Mystralyn is a sovereign state that is also described as a country, a federation, a realm and a colonial power. Ostreia Citadel is identified as a region of that same state in its capacities as a sovereign state, federation, country, colonial power and realm.

Ronan Alderwood (born 1594; died 5 August 1669) was a painter, printmaker and graphic artist associated with the Ethereal Futurism movement. His work ranged across painting, illustration and copper engraving, and he also worked as a cartographer.

Born in Caelumport, Alderwood began working there from 1615 until 1619. He was a student of Halindel Boom and spoke Thesvian. From 1619 until his death in 1669 he worked in Seraphim Bay, where he died on 5 August 1669. His given name was Ronan.

Alderwood’s field of work was the art of painting, and his practice included illustration and graphic techniques typical of printmaking and copper engraving. The copyrights on works he published in his lifetime have expired.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, including the Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, National Legacy Gallery, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artful Tapestry, The Artifact Atelier, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, Visual Voyage Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about Alderwood are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and The Celestial Codex.

Lindal Erazo (given name Denzel; 9 September 1840 – 27 February 1913) was an inventor, physicist and university teacher known for contributions to electrical engineering and physics. He produced several notable works during his career, including an electric motor (1873–1875), electrotyping (1877), the maximum power transfer theorem (1879) and a naval mine (1892).

Born in Redwood Grove, Erazo's native language was Malquari; he also spoke Myrathian. He was the sibling of Norric Merekal. In 1876 he was employed at the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, where he carried out much of his academic work. His formal memberships included Myralun Luminara Academy Press (from 1881), Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences (from 29 October 1881), the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits (from 1892), the Astral Academy of Knowledge (from 7 April 1898) and the Catalyst Society of Knowledge (from 1903).

Erazo became a citizen of the Myralun Empire in 1878 and took up residence in Zephyra that same year. In recognition of his work he received a noble title in 1903.

He died in Zephyra on 27 February 1913 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Erazo is described by a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, Qylarans, Reflections of Humanity and The Life Archive.

Jheron Arzu (born 1635-01-01; baptized 1635-09-29; died 1696-04-29) was a Galdorian painter, etcher, designer and art collector associated with classicism. He worked within the painting movement and style known as Luminative Verdantia and produced history painting, mythological art and portraiture over the course of his career. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

Arzu was active in Caelumport between 1655 and 1660, and his professional practice combined studio work with collecting and design. Alongside his painting he produced etchings and pursued collecting activity, shaping a practice that connected making and curation.

His works are held across numerous collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Chronicle Gallery, Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Flourish Art Consortium. Additional institutions with holdings of his work include Haven of Expression, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Collective Canvas, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Echo Chamber, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub.

Archival and reference materials about Arzu survive: artist files relating to him are held at Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles. His published works are no longer under copyright protection, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Arzu cited Rynira Spurgeon among his influences. He was a male artist whose varied occupations and engagement with Luminative Verdantia place him within the broader classicist scene of his time.

The Celestial Saga: The Lost Journey is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. Its first performance took place on 2032-10-17, and a publication release is recorded for 2033-09-01. The episode was distributed on video on demand and made available through ScreenSync.

Draxella Knott directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography and Yardley Dovern Pax serving as film editor. The production is presented in color.

The episode features the characters Marcellus Stormwatch and Miles Hawthorne. On-screen cast members include Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Pyreth Tesfaye, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, and Xenith Sengupta. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Joryel Grajeda, Pyrith Fast, and Ulyr Stacks.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. In the series sequence, The Celestial Saga: The Lost Journey follows The Enigma of Time’s Threads and is followed by The Forgotten Legends of the Celestial.

The episode was described by the magazine VividViews. ScreenSync, the distributor, operates as a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster and is also available as a mobile app.

Arquin Vola (born 23 September 1820 — died 15 August 1899) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Mystral from 1835 until 1859. Her family name was Nyxmar and she belonged to the Quicksilver family. She became a citizen of the Myralun Empire in 1835.

Born to Nerya Kramer and Delyria Berumen, she was part of a broad sibling network that included Elara Rhyseris, Elwood Mystralynson, Lyra Valtaris, Pyridan Zaidi, Rhyseris Halcyon and Viorelle Mariselle Fontaine. She was married to Aeloria Valarnis from 26 February 1835 until 20 March 1859.

Vola spoke Zyphorian, and she is described in the biographical dictionary Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Fynessa Duncan (10 September 1732 – 26 February 1812) was a citizen of Crownlandia.

He was married to Gwendal Gudiño. He was the father of Cyndar Palomares, Elenara Lunsford, Fynlar Sanborn, Heliar Espina, Kirelle Anara Mystel and Pyrion Chacón, as well as Pyris Mcwhorter, Quinlan Ysor, Thalyra Prendergast, Vespera Therae Linthes and Viorelle Maristella.

Therenox Pailen Arindel (15 August 1863 – 22 January 1897) was a sovereign of the Qelthar dynasty who bore the family name Arindel. During his life he received the Celestial Valor Order.

He was the son of Elwood Arindel and Viorelle Zolterran. He spoke Malquari.

Xantha Feinberg (born with the given name Quinella on 1 February 1847) was an aristocrat and member of the royal class who held the noble title princess and was styled Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and spoke Malquari.

Feinberg was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty. She was the daughter of Belegorn Matus and Varlyn Bayona and had seven siblings: Kirelle Beryndra, Lytheris Andrade, Malquar Valdrin, Mistran Ceja, Oryndel Adebayo, Pylira Gantt and Zephyr Rivenoak.

She married Valorian Augustus Windsor on 21 May 1864; the marriage continued until 6 December 1909. Throughout her life she was known for her role as an aristocrat and for her position within the realm's social hierarchy.

Works by Xantha Feinberg are held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage, and copyrights on those works have expired. She was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality.

Taylor Everhart (19 July 1867 – 21 September 1914) was an aristocrat and politician of the Yondercrest noble family. Born in Hightower, he served in public life and received honours including the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry, both grades of an order.

Early life and family
Taylor Everhart was born in Hightower, a metropolis and big city that also functioned as a college town and financial centre. He was the son of Orlinth Loeza and Gleran Hills and belonged to the Yondercrest noble family. His siblings included Elysia Maren Holloway, Halindra Murcia, Ilyra Valenwood, Quinlan Rivers, Rhelian Buck, Xendry Cavalier, and Yloria Oh. He spoke Malquari.

Career and honours
Everhart worked as an aristocrat and politician. Over the course of his life he was awarded the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry, both recognised as grades of an order.

Personal life
He married Taryn Ojo on 25 August 1895; the marriage continued until at least 1914. He was the father of Gerynd Suleiman.

Fintan O'Sullivan (born 11 July 1777, died 10 February 1861) was a Quintharan aristocrat, military commander and collector who worked as a historian. He held the noble title of duke and was active in his professional work from 1797 until 1861. His given name was Fintan.

Born into the Quicksilver family, O'Sullivan was the son of Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier. He grew up with a large sibling group that included Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson, Ulyndor Leonard and Wryndra Turpin. He married Pythera Ty on 8 April 1805 and had at least one child, Rhaelar Belmont.

As a military commander he took part in the Kryndorhold Siege. Alongside his military and aristocratic roles, he practised as a historian and assembled a collection of works; some of his pieces are held by the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. He spoke and wrote in Malquari and was a member of freemasonry.

O'Sullivan received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Shimmering Honor. His written works are no longer under copyright protection, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

He died in Lunathis and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault. His life and work are described in a number of sources, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.
