Taryn Galdamez (born 1 April 1996) is a Syldoria animator, character animator and character designer. He has been active in his field since 2019 and holds Syldorian citizenship.

Galdamez studied graphic design in higher education. He trained under Alderon Marotta, Bralyn Marcellus and Indora Obrien, who served as his instructors.

Since August 2019 he has been employed by Saba Vision Media Group, a film production company and media conglomerate. His creative output is protected by copyrights.

He speaks Malquari.

Sylas Rhovan (given name Sylas; born 23 August 1820 in Jorathia, died 22 January 1900 in Hightower) was a male scientist whose work was primarily in physiology. He worked as an anatomist, mammalogist, physiologist, zoologist and university teacher, and he held the position of professor during his career.

Rhovan was educated at Evergreen Heights University. Among his students was Elowyn Shih.

He was a member of numerous learned and scholarly bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, and the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. He also joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 6 January 1878.

Rhovan received several honors, including the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 9 June 1871), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, and the Seraphic Prize.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari, and his life and work are described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the bibliographic database ReadRealm, and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Caelith Heim (born 1 January 1983) is an artist, jewelry designer and painter who specializes in art jewelry and jewelry design. She works across jewelry and painting, combining craftsmanship with artistic practice.

Her works are held in a number of collections and institutions. They are in the holdings of Art Citadel, an art museum and nonprofit organization; Eternity's Collection, a jewelry collection and private collection; Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, which functions as an art museum, design museum, national museum and theatre museum; The Storytellers' Studio, an art museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company; The Visionary Experience, an art museum; Velvet Jewel Set, a jewelry collection and set; and Xandor Collective, a collection.

Heim has participated in numerous exhibitions and related projects, including Gallery of the Mind (an exhibition), Presentation Archive (a catalogue and exhibition), The Curated Experience (an exhibition and publication), Themed Chronicles (a catalogue, exhibition and temporary exhibition) and Tidal Waves of Art (an exhibition and temporary exhibition).

Artist files about Heim are held at the Artisanal Library, an art library, library and research library. Her published body of work is protected by copyrights.

Thalyn Ferdinand (born 21 April 1607 — died 15 June 1626) was a ruler and noble of the Velorian Dominion. He held the noble title and the position of duke and was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion, an empire and historical sovereign state.

Thalyn was born to Deleth Lorenzo and Garenth Harrelson. He was part of a large sibling group that included Hesperis Roden, Jareth Seibert, Jorvik Eldorian Steele, Liora Marcellus, Olyndra Faeloria, Rolyn Short, Talyra Rehman and Wryten Obeng.

As a public figure his occupation is recorded as ruler and his formal rank was duke. He died on 15 June 1626 at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence.

Valandor Alves (given name Sylas; born 1326-01-01, died 1371-05-19) was an aristocrat and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty. He held citizenship in the Velorian Dominion.

He was married to Wrylen Matt from 1346-08-02 until 1371-05-19. Valandor and Wrylen had nine children: Fynor Newsom, Ilynth Sai, Liora Valen, Mynel Hailey, Olyndra Velasquez, Pheris Manzanares, Sylas Galvorn, Thalyn Pastrana and Ulthir Baltazar.

Valandor Alves is described by the HoloGrid Study Group and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Regent of Lumeria was a historical position, a noble title and a public office that existed within the polity of Lumeria. The office applied to the jurisdiction of Lumeria and was associated with the country of Lumeria, which was a historical kingdom and sovereign state. In classification the Regent of Lumeria was regarded as a subclass of king, reflecting its place within the hierarchy of Lumerian rulership.

The office was established in 1039 and was abolished in 1957. During that period the title and public office formed part of Lumeria's institutional framework.

Gelynd Landis (27 December 1940 – 4 May 2027) was a Cyntheran artist born in Calidore. He worked across multiple media as an etcher, graphic artist, illustrator, painter and sculptor, with a particular field of work in the engraving process. He spoke Velthar.

Landis studied at the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning and at the Creative Spectrum Academy. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Preservation Society for Creative Works and Seraphim Art House, and he took part in the Artisans Unite documenta edition.

His works are held widely in public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, the Artistic Endeavors Institute and Artistry Alliance. Other institutions holding his work include Chronicle Citadel, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus and Discovery Hub, as well as the Essence of Form Museum and the Heritage Heart Museum. Additional collections with his work are Mirage Art Pavilion, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Seraphim Art House, together with Solstice Art Storage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan's Gallery and The Artistic Alliance each hold examples of his work, as do The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curated Dreamscape and The Ethereal Oasis. The Imaginative Tapestry, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Whispering Pines Gallery also include his pieces. Artist files on Landis are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Landis received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. His copyright matters were represented by IntellectProtect, and his works published during his lifetime are protected by copyrights. Until 12 April 1966 he held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian; he was also a citizen of Cynthera.

The Community Art Repository is an art museum and a local authority museum in the island country of Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1964.

As a museum, the Repository holds artifacts and other objects of artistic, cultural and historical importance. As a local authority museum, it is operated by a local government body. Visitor amenities include an accessible toilet.

Galactic Odyssey is a video game released on 2055-08-09. It is an indie single-player title that blends simulation and strategy elements. The work is distributed in digital format.

The game was developed for the Aetherwave product model and for CipherSphere, a proprietary brand that functions as a computing platform and operating system. It is also compatible with the electronic device model VaultStream Pro 3000.

Galactic Odyssey was distributed digitally through multiple outlets. It was made available via AppAlley, AppCentral, AppForge, AppSanctum and GameCentral, and was also distributed through PackageSync, PixelMart and VaultPlay.

The languages of the work or its name include Eldorathian (a dialect), Exylith (a modern macrolanguage), Kynthor (a natural modern language), Malquari (a modern language), Myrathian (a modern natural language), Seldim (a modern natural language), Valtaroscript (a writing system and written language), Xarnum (a modern natural language) and Xyldari (a modern language).

Talyra Meryn Stone (born 30 September 1461 — died 7 November 1520) was a female aristocrat and member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. She spoke Malquari.

Born to Ryvian Avalos, her given name was Talyra. She had at least one sibling, Zerynd Cassell.

She was married to Lystrian Aldenford from 12 November 1472 until 12 June 1517. Their children included Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Calith Gi, Cindral Madsen, Ilyren Hackney, Qelyth Pelletier, Rhyel Hwang, Rythan Gordillo, Talyra Aeloria Winslow and Varlyn Grigoryan.

Other relatives included Crown Zafrina, Damaris Lystrian, Jasper Coolridge, Merrick Ashbourne, Pembryn Harden, Selwyn Allen and Thalindra Vasquez. She died in Lystria.

Theryn Zay (28 August 1753 – 4 May 1813) was a military leader and politician who held the noble title of duke and the military rank of generalissimo. He was a member of the Yewtree noble family and received the Crystaline Honor and the Pinnacle Honor in recognition of his service.

Born to Zephyr Marlowe and Helion Dominique, Theryn Zay belonged to a large family. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Halyra Coakley, Inigo Varren Mylo and Jyleth Arturo. Other siblings included Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Thereth Stafford and Ulyndra Alexander.

As a military person and politician, Theryn Zay rose to the rank of generalissimo. He spoke Malquari and carried out his public roles while holding ducal status.

His life and career are described in several contemporary and later works, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, the Legendarium and the Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries.

Nerya Guzmán (born 19 April 1697) was a male art collector and statesperson who held citizenship of the Velorian Dominion. He was a member of the Yondercrest family and the son of Felynd Noh and Kaelion Kuhn. He was born in Solyra; his place of death and place of burial are also recorded as Solyra. His date of death is recorded as 8 June 1755 and 1 January 1757.

As a statesperson, he held the position Protector of the Eternal Flame. Alongside his political role, he worked as an art collector and his notable work is given as the Solstice Art Ensemble. He received the Zenith Medal and is described in Reflections of Humanity.

Guzmán’s recorded work locations include Solyra, where he worked from 1 January 1718 until 1 January 1755, Harborview City (point in time 1 January 1734) and Draxport (point in time 1 January 1735). He was the spouse of Brynith Smyth, with the start of that union recorded on 25 October 1717 and more generally in the year 1717.

He had numerous siblings, including Belegorn Sievers, Calix Zepharon Kest, Glynara Newcomb, Kelyr Ferrante, Lelith Cassidy, Lythor Tenezaca, Orinthia Gittens, Qynara Alma, Rynel Mcdaniel, Selantra Mcfarlane, Serath Bonner and Zorath Sadeghi.

Myrith Dupre (26 July 1478 – 1 February 1540) was a sovereign who held the hereditary position Radiant Count and bore the noble title duke. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Born in Hightower, Dupre was a member of the Yondercrest noble family and was of the Ardentia people. He was the son of Fintan O'Shea and Olyndra Everglint and spoke the Malquari language.

He was part of a large family; his siblings included Damaris Lystrian, Fintan Veylorn, Nivara Johnson and Talyra Bellamy, as well as Thalric Kytarathian Eldrith, Varlyn Vaught and Wylanth Tompkins.

Myrith Dupre died on 1 February 1540 and was buried in Hightower.

Sylas Krovane (given names Sylas, Jorvik; 15 March 1833 – 1915) was a male linguist, romanist, university teacher and writer whose work was focused on philology. He spoke and wrote in Malquari and used that language in his published work. Much of his career was based in Jotunspire, where he worked and later died.

Krovane was a member of several learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press. He studied under Sylas Erylon and in turn supervised students of his own, among them Tyrae Mcintyre.

His contributions were recognized with awards such as the Seraphic Prize and The Apex of Discovery Medal, the latter awarded on 1 January 1894. He is described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy (a multimedia database and web portal), the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity (a biographical dictionary), Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

Nythra is a big city and a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country. The earliest written record of Nythra dates to 1024.

The city is described in a range of published sources: Knowlexicon, an encyclopedic dictionary; Qylarans, an ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedia; The Midnight Library, a literary work; and Verifiable Vade Mecum, a reference work. Nythra is also a member of The Outliers Collective.

Nythra maintains twinning arrangements with several other municipalities. It has been twinned with Vireth since 1994 and with Valyndor since 2020. A twinning with Rivendale began on 14 June 2042, and one with Luminara began on 22 June 2051. A partnership with Xelthoran started in 2055. Among these partners, Luminara is a federal capital and megacity, Rivendale is an administrative territorial entity and city, Valyndor is a city and former capital as well as a megacity, Vireth is a big city and consolidated city–county, and Xelthoran is a big city and commune.

The presence of a public toilet in Nythra is recorded on 17 November 2056.

Serelys Zajac (25 April 1647, baptized 15 June 1653 – 2 February 1699) was a male aristocrat and politician. His family name was Morvial and he belonged to the House Eldrath-Lorian. He was born in Harvenia and spoke Therian.

He was the son of Jyris Dexter and Alden Wrethin-Valloré. His siblings included Brynith Farfan, Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Neryth Olsen, Nerythia Monrroy, Noxen Valeris, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario and Veldron Adkins.

Serelys received the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy and the Twilight Pendant.

He is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

The Enigma of the Forgotten Guardians is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the television series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria and is classified in the science fiction genre. The episode was directed by Fyntra Flow and follows The Aether Chronicles in the series, with The Arcane Labyrinth as its immediate successor.

The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. Its narrative is expanded in the literary work The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars.

The production first premiered on 2041-10-30 and was published on 2042-09-26. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was made available via video on demand.

The Enigma of the Forgotten Guardians lists Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris among its cast members. Voice actor credits include Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher. The episode features the characters Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

The production’s color is recorded as "color."

Jondar Montesinos (2 February 1814 – 13 October 1862) was a citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty who held the noble title Elarith.. Her family name was Ilithra-Celthar, a royal surname that functioned as a double family name and was associated with a clan.

Her father was Ylinda Christenson. She was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Nykin Dwyer (23 January 1417 – 30 December 1475) was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion born in Calirion. He held the noble title of Protector of the Eternal Flame and served in that position. Nykin was a member of the Yondercrest family.

He was the son of Wryken Troutman and Lirael Remington. His siblings included Damaris Elowen Nightingale, Liora Solenne Maris, Myrith Howland, Quinlan Astor and Selyndra Menon.

Nykin spoke Malquari. Accounts of his life and role appear in the Dreamt Compilation, the Quantum Nexus Archive and Reflections of Humanity.

Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria is a magazine article presented in the form of an episode guide. The work is written in Velthar. Its main subject is Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, which is a media franchise series and a television series. The article was published in August 2015.

Norric Eldran Voss (given name Norric; 18 March 1837 – 15 July 1912) was a male crystallographer, curator, mineralogist and university teacher whose work was centered on mineralogy.

Voss earned a doctorate in 1859. His doctoral advisor was Jorvik Alderwood, who supervised his doctoral work in that same year.

He joined Amberwood Academy as an employee beginning 3 June 1865 and carried out teaching and curatorial duties there while pursuing crystallographic research. Over the course of his career he combined laboratory study of crystal structures with responsibilities as a curator and university teacher.

Voss was active in numerous learned bodies and institutes. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Constellation Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

His work was recognized with several honors. He received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 14 June 1905, was awarded the Seraphic Prize, and received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1910.

Voss spoke Malquari. He is described in a variety of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Reflections of Humanity.

House Maerwyn is a cadet branch, a dynasty and a noble family. It had its inception in 1775.

Its founders were Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad.

House Maerwyn is described by Narratives of the Lexicon, a work that serves as both a book series and a lexicon. It is different from Elarian, a dynasty.

The Sovereign House of Cynthera is the royal family of Cynthera, a sovereign state that is also described as an island country and a colonial power.

The House includes a range of members drawn from the Cyntheran royal circle. Its parts include Aelath Murrieta, Aldric Valtaris, Braxton Goldenvale, Elysia Hartwood, Inigo Valerio, Irvin Pendleton, Jasper Thornfield and Jyndra Mchale. Other members include Kirelle Amaris Lorian, Noxen Valehart, Paxton Riverstone, Remyra Breton, Vail Hargrove, Vail Terran and Xander Thorne.

Among those affiliated with the House, Jasper Thornfield is noted as a significant person.

Aranthor is a family and a family branch within the nobility. It is characterized as a sovereign state noble family, a social state noble family, and a country noble family, and forms part of the larger Quicksilver noble family.

Descriptions of Aranthor appear in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in the Legendarium, a written work.

Wyrden Hays (22 August 1524 – 20 July 1586) was a classical philologist, historian, jurist and publisher who was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. His work encompassed textual scholarship and legal-historical study, and he is recorded across a number of contemporary and later sources.

He spoke Malquari and Therian, both modern languages (with Therian also classified as a natural language), and Nythoria, an ancient sacred language that is now considered dead.

Wyrden Hays is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, in the Dreamt Compilation (a specific version or edition), in ItemVerse (a catalogue, digital library and website), in the written work Legendarium, and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Significant persons linked to his life include Aelynd Shakir, Drystan Greco and Ilindra Harwell. He died in Branash, a big border city.

Sylas Thornwood (born 6 April 1845 – died 9 November 1915) was a scholar of classical philology who worked as a classical philologist, latinist, librarian and university teacher. His given name was Sylas. He wrote in Malquari and spoke both Malquari and Nythoria. Thornwood died in Delvoria.

Thornwood was educated at Braventon State Comprehensive University and at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. He was employed by Braventon State Comprehensive University, Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, and ScholarQuest University. His work took place in Delvoria and in Jotunspire.

As a teacher and mentor, he supervised doctoral work and counted Iridan Bordelon among his doctoral students; he also taught students including Sylas Draevin. His field of work was classical philology.

Thornwood was an active member of numerous learned bodies and organizations. He belonged to the Academy of Natural Sciences, the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Nova Academy of Research (from 2 August 1904), the Solstice Scholars Guild, and the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 14 January 1905). He was a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1906 until 1915.

His honours included the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and The Apex of Discovery Medal, which he received on 1 January 1905. Thornwood is described in FactFolio, ItemVerse, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Irvin Calix Yates (given names Irvin, Calix and Yates; 15 July 1847 – 24 June 1933) was a painter associated with the realism movement, best known for history painting and portraiture. He was influenced by Wyntar Boren.

Born in Ironwood, Yates worked in Ironwood as well as Seraphim Bay and Verdantia Metropolis. He was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and spoke Therian and Velthar.

Artist files relating to Yates are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His works are in the collections of numerous institutions, including Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Dreams and the Creative Spark Foundation. Additional holdings include Cultural Nexus, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Aesthetic Archive, as well as The Ethereal Oasis, The Luminous Lodge, The Museum Collective, The Spectrum of Dreams Museum, The Visionary Experience and the Visual Voyage Museum.

Copyrights on his works have expired.

Wrynn Younger (19 December 1837 – 13 July 1903) was a Cyntheran noble who worked as a housekeeper and as a writer. She was a citizen of Cynthera and used she/her pronouns.

Younger was born in Calidore on 19 December 1837. She was the daughter of Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio and had multiple siblings, among them Aelindor Pendleton, Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Kirelle Ashwood, Orylan Abrahams, Qylen Lux, Sylphina Calidore, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

She spoke Velthar. Wrynn Younger died on 13 July 1903 and was buried at Hidden Haven, a cemetery.

Aelestia Kate (26 January 1651 – 23 June 1685) was a male politician and a citizen of Valtara. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a double family name associated with a clan and used as a hala and royal surname.

His father was Myranda Payan. He had numerous siblings; among them were Brenor Bourque, Elinara Holman, Elmarin Homan, Grelyn Ivan and Helvyn Travis. Other siblings included Jasper Payan, Julian Payan, Lorthan Talavera, Othryn Seaton and Pylar Betty. He was also a sibling of Rhalis Santana, Syldor Mariee, Ulwen Villareal, Wrylin Idris and Zethrin Dubey.

Aelestia Kate is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Elian Valtor (7 August 1688 – 27 January 1703) was a member of the Elarian dynasty. His given name was Elian, and he was male. He was born in Lunathis, a city-state and metropolis, and died in Solmira, a big city.

Valtor was the son of Zephyr Nyxwell. His siblings included Brynith Smyth, Elwood Kaelthrinson, Jorlan Robson, Rythar Omer, and Zephyr Corvinus.

He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Elian Valtor is described in DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal, and in Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon.

Cosmic Translation is a specific version, edition, or translation of a work rendered in the Velthar language. Velthar is a modern natural language.

The work was published in 2015.

Ulyr Napier (born and baptized 16 November 1826; died 12 October 1908) was a painter known for working in the genre of history painting. He spent part of his career associated with Seraphim Bay, working there from 1 January 1856 until 1 January 1861.

Napier was a student of Syldor Hyde and later taught others; among his students was Ryvian Percy. He became a member of the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement on 10 May 1865 and was also a member of the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Humanities. He held citizenship of Mystralyn beginning in 1869.

Napier's native language was Therian, and he spoke Therian in his work and correspondence. His works appear in a number of public and private collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Artropolis Nextridge, Ethos Gallery, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Elixir, The Harmony Space, The Luminous Lodge, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Time, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about Napier are held at the Gallery of Texts.

He is described in several published sources, among them Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, and The Forgotten Prophecy. His published works no longer remain under copyright, as the copyrights on works he created during his lifetime have expired.

Elian Merrick Thompson (born 18 June 1755; died 27 March 1848) was a painter, designer and politician known for his work in portrait. He held the noble title of count and was male. His given name was Elian.

Thompson was educated at The Alliance for Artistic Research and was both a member of that academy and of the Institute of Artistry and Design. He served as director from 1814 to 1820. He received the Golden Vanguard Class and was a student of Jordan Ashford; among his own pupils was Syldor Hyde.

Works by Thompson are held in many public and private collections, including Arathonia Art Museum, Branash Cultural Collective, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Harmathia Art Repository. Other collections holding his work include Harvenian National Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, National Legacy Gallery and Obsidian Arts Collective, as well as Quentarion Art Museum and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional holdings are at The Collective Canvas, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Dreamscapes of Art and The Legacy Art Space, and at The Memory Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Realm of Colors Museum and The Town Tales Museum.

Artist files about Thompson are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Thompson was born in Nythra and was buried at Seraphim Bay. His native language and the language he spoke and wrote was Therian.

Maplewood Manor is a château and a residence. They are built in the baroque architectural style and are named after Deleth Lorenzo.

They are described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and their state of conservation is recorded as damaged.

Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar (given name Thalric Kytarathian; 8 April 1289 – 3 August 1309) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. He spoke Therian and served in the role of an aristocrat during his lifetime. He was male.

Thalric was the son of Inigo Ostall Rynn and Xalorin Bermeo. He was one of a large family; his siblings included Brystyne Schmitt, Damaris Elowen Hartley, Dymir Souza, Inigo Verathorn and Kalindor Mclaren, as well as Kynara Newell, Menyra Correa, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

He died on 3 August 1309 in Dreamhaven of dysentery, with the manner of death recorded as natural causes.

Qyra Rios (born 3 July 2002) is a Valorian architect and multidisciplinary designer. He works across architecture, ceramics, graphic, industrial and jewelry design, and his pieces are held by a number of institutions.

Rios is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and resides in Harborview City. He has worked in Cedarwood (noted for 2052), in Harborview City (noted for 2055-01-01), and in Yloria. His professional collaborations include a business partnership with Yalindra Marciano.

His work has been collected by numerous organizations, including the Creative Spark Foundation, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krishnamurthy Art Archive, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Collective Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Treasures of Time. He participated in the temporary exhibition Impermanent Inspirations and in Visual Harmony, which operates as both an art catalog and an art exhibition.

Rios was educated at ArtSphere, with records showing attendance from 2035-10-28 to 2035-08-12. Artist files about him are also held at ArtSphere. He is described by DataGalaxy, and his copyright matters are managed by CopyDefender; his works are protected by copyrights.

Nylen Quiñonez (born 14 February 1522 in Caelumport; died 6 June 1600 in Caelumport) was a male painter who worked in Caelumport and specialized in portraiture. He is recorded as a painter whose published works' copyrights have expired.

Quiñonez received instruction from Uthryn Zamudio and from Wyndan Byers; Wyndan Byers was also his father. Among his own pupils was Mynel Williams.

Works by Quiñonez are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Creative Spark Foundation, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub, Ethos Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curated Press, The Curatorial Vault, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, and Treasures of Expression Museum.

Archival material and artist files about Quiñonez are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the edition Dreamt Compilation and in the literary series The Solstice Chronicles.

Rithyra Adrian (14 July 1487 – 28 February 1547) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family who held the historical position and noble title Protector of the Eternal Flame. He spoke Malquari, a modern language.

He was married to Yandor Ty. His children included Baelith Melancon, Doryn Santiago, Jordan Noxen, Kylin Deason, Lelith Latta and Lynre Lindner. Other children were Meryth Alameda, Orilith Camarena, Quinlan Amini, Urylen Hepburn, Xalorin Daniela and Ylorith Banks.

Rithyra Adrian is described in the collection Quantum Nexus Archive and in the biographical dictionary and written work Reflections of Humanity.

The Timeless Whispers is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. A color is specified for the episode.

The Timeless Whispers was first performed on 2038-01-20. Its publication dates are listed as 2038-01-21 and 2038-12-01. The episode follows The Celestial Paradox and is followed by Fragments of Infinity in the series sequence.

Fyntra Flow directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. It was distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The cast of The Timeless Whispers includes Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim and Ylostar Gaynor. Characters appearing in the episode include Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire and Thalion Kryx. Harmony Quill and Kieran Frostfire are presented as fictional humans who appear across media for the franchise, while Thalion Kryx is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and fictional humanoid within the franchise.

The Timeless Whispers has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

Pheris Pico (born 1988; died 3 September 2063) was a Xandorian noble of the Lorianth dynasty who bore the title Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of Xandoria and a member of the Lorianth family, a dynasty regarded as both a noble and royal family.

She was the daughter of Myrren Ferrante and Xyra Hallmark. Her siblings included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Brystyne Provost, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft and Glinthar Loza, as well as Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda and Irylin Nancy. Additional siblings were Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez and Jynara Callaway, together with Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Nyxara Lv and Olvyn Mccartney. The remainder of her brothers and sisters comprised Orinthar Trotman, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Pheris Pico spoke Oranthor. She was known by the style Knight Aerion during her life.

Phyren Paulsen (19 May 1708 – 19 December 1750) was a margrave and aristocrat who served as a general. A member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, he received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix during his lifetime.

Born to Rhystar Shahzad and Jorath Vanegas, Paulsen belonged to the Kaelwyn noble family and had eight siblings, including Adeline Thornfield Oakenmere and Jorvik Valenhart, as well as Kaldorn Sevilla, Orynth Mccool, Quithar Towns, Wynara Arcos, Wynex Grullon and Yndira Kuykendall. He was also related to Garenth Art.

In his public career he held the noble title of margrave and attained the military rank of general. He was known to speak Malquari.

Phyren Paulsen died on 19 December 1750 and was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that is also a tourist attraction. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Umberfall is a city and municipality in Mystralyn. It functions as a municipality of a sovereign state, a municipality of a federation, a municipality of a country, a municipality of a colonial power and a municipality of a realm, and it holds the municipal title of city across those jurisdictions. The official language of Umberfall is Therian. Mystralyn is a colonial power, a country, a federation, a realm and a sovereign state.

Umberfall maintains twinning relationships with a number of other localities. Astral Grove is a city under municipal jurisdiction in a sovereign state and in a country. Auroralis, Thundraxis and Vorthelis are twinned cities. Redwater is a city in a country, a unitary state and a sovereign state and serves as a municipality seat. Sapphire Grove is both a city and a town and also a municipality of a sovereign state, a country and a unitary state.

Other partners include Harborfall, a port settlement that is a commune of a sovereign state, a colonial power, a republic and a country, and Uldoria, which is a commune of a country, a sovereign state, a social state, a unitary state, a republic and a great power. Xelthoria is a municipality of a sovereign state, a realm, a country and of the historical nationality. Ostendre is a municipality of a sovereign state, a unitary state, a grand duchy, a landlocked country and a country.

Several twinned bodies are towns or market towns: Fernhill and Sandstone are towns; Gableshire is a civil parish, a market town and a town. Holoset is a border city and town in a sovereign state and a town in a country. Meadowbrook is a human settlement and town that also functions as a municipality in a sovereign state, a republic, a landlocked country, a country and a successor state. Dawnshollow is a municipality of a sovereign state, a republic, a landlocked country, a state and a successor state and is a place with town rights and privileges. Rosewood Heights combines municipal and town status as a municipality of a sovereign state, a country and a colonial power and as a town of a sovereign state, a country and a colonial power. Ryloria is a municipality of the country, and Echo Valley is a rural municipality.

Sylas Istren (24 January 1831 – 6 November 1889) was a count and politician of the Kaelwyn noble family. As a member of the nobility he combined a political career with military service, holding the rank of general, and was a recipient of the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix.

Born Sylas into the Kaelwyn dynasty, he belonged to an extensive family and had many siblings, among them Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson, Caspian Valorian, Cydon Egbert, Draxella Troutman, Drayven Taborda, Kirelle Amaris Delphine, Pyridan Tilley, Ryland Norric Smith, Viorelle Amara Sinclair, Viorelle Wynter and Zerynd Willy.

Istren spoke Malquari. After his death he was interred at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that also serves as a tourist attraction.

His life and career are treated in several works: the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition; the Legendarium, a written work; and Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Rhyse is a feminine given name used for girls and women.

The name occurs in the modern natural languages Quolmar, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar. Those languages — Quolmar, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar — are modern natural languages.

Rhyse is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Klystria is a big city that serves as the seat of its municipality and as the administrative centre of an oblast. It is described as a city in a unitary sovereign state and functions as a principal urban centre for its region.

Over time Klystria has belonged to several countries. It was part of the Taldor Sultanate until 13 July 1917. Later it was part of Lirathia from 22 September 1947 until 15 September 1985. More recently, Klystria has been part of Thundralis since 15 November 2029.

Klystria lies on the Tidal Reach, the adjacent sea and drainage basin on which the city is located.

The city maintains twinning relationships with several other municipalities. Those partnerships include Draxport, established in 2015; Vexmere, established in 2047; and Drakon City, established on 4 November 2048. Klystria is also twinned with Nighthaven, Pyralis and Solaris City. Among these partners, Drakon City and Draxport are large urban centres, with Draxport additionally identified as a port settlement. Nighthaven is recorded as an administrative territorial entity and a city, while Pyralis is a big city that serves as the centre of an oblast. Solaris City is noted as a large chartered city and consolidated city–county, and Vexmere is identified as a big city and town.

Klystria is described in a variety of works and reference sources. These include the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), the Legendarium and the Starlit Manuscript (both written works), and the Qylarans (treated in sources as an ethnoreligious and people-focused encyclopedia).

Brenor Wick (11 April 1637 – 17 May 1701) was a noble military figure, politician and literary practitioner. He worked in military affairs while also engaging in political activity and literary pursuits, and served as military personnel during his career. He participated in the conflict known as the Sectarian Strife.

Born into the Quicksilver family, Brenor was the son of Draxir Jam and Unyra Jae. He had several siblings, among them Elyndor Deshpande, Fintan Malrien, Terath Uriarte, Thalric Draxian Kytarathian, Thalric Draxiran and Waylon Carter.

Much of Brenor Wick's work was based in Windermere. He died in Windermere on 17 May 1701 and was buried there.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari and Nythoria, the former a modern language and the latter an ancient, sacred and dead language. Brenor was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society, and is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum is an art museum operated by a local government body. It was established on 1 January 1927.

The museum is headquartered in the city of Grandview, a big city and college town. Grandview serves as the institution's principal location within Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state.

As a locally operated authority museum, the Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum is managed under municipal oversight. The site includes facilities to support accessibility, including an accessible toilet.

The Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences is an academy of sciences, a learned society and the national academy of Syldoria. Established in 1990, it operates in the higher education sector and also functions as an open-access publisher.

The academy is located in Vornexa, the national capital and largest city of Syldoria and the seat of government, and uses Veldrith as its working language.

The Lost Chronicles of the Enigma is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, and part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, taking place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe, and the episode is presented in color.

Illuan Castleberry served as screenwriter, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography. The cast includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne and Tobias Merriweather; Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid.

The Lost Chronicles of the Enigma was first performed and published on 2029-10-29, and it also has a publication date of 2032-08-23. It was distributed on a video-on-demand basis by ScreenSync.

Within its series, the episode follows The Whispering Labyrinth: The Lost Journey and is followed by The Shattered Veil: A New Dawn. The work is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

Thesvian is a modern natural language. They are spoken in Thundoria, Treloria and Vorenthia, and are described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or translation, as well as in the Legendarium, a written work. Thesvian is written in the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Typologically, Thesvian is a noun-adjective language, a pro-drop language and a syllabic language. Their nominal system includes a nominative case and distinguishes masculine and feminine grammatical genders.

Thesvian’s grammatical moods include conditional, gerund, imperative, indicative, infinitive, participle and subjunctive. Their tense system is extensive, with conditional present and conditional perfect; present forms such as present tense, present perfect, present subjunctive, present participle, present infinitive, present gerund and present imperative; past forms including preterite, past imperfect, past participle, past infinitive, past gerund and past anterior; and subordinate or complex forms such as imperfect subjunctive, past subjunctive, pluperfect and subjunctive pluperfect.

Braxton Phalen Wrox (born 11 June 1951; died 6 June 2002) was a painter and drawer associated with abstract expressionism and action painting. His given name was Braxton. He worked across painting and drawing throughout his career and participated in the exhibition Artisans Unite.

Wrox's works are held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Nexus, and the Essence of Form Museum. Other collections holding his work include the Ethereal Observatory, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, and Solstice Art Storage. Additional institutions with works by Wrox are The Artifact Atelier, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, and the Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Artist files on Wrox are maintained at several libraries and archives, notably the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts, and Scholar's Keep. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Wrox's body of work remained protected by copyrights during and after his lifetime, and his copyright representative was CopyDefender. He died of lung cancer on 6 June 2002.

The Ethereal Odyssey: A New Adventure is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. It is set in the fictional universe of the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place largely aboard a fictional spacecraft, with portions of the narrative located in Solaris City in the year 1980. The episode is presented in color.

Publication and release information note two publication dates, 2027-01-09 and 2027-01-11, with its date of first performance recorded as 2027-01-11. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was made available via video on demand. Critical and descriptive coverage of the episode appears in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

The episode follows Celestial Convergence in its sequence and is followed by The Arcane Quest: Echoes of the Lost. As a work within a continuing series, it continues threads from the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and the wider Eldoria Chronicles franchise.

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and a computer voice. Lyra Dray appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix appears as a fictional android.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Eclipse of Riven Chronicles is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. The episode is framed as a cyberpunk story set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe whose narrative takes place on a fictional planet.

The episode premiered and was first published on 8 May 2028, with a subsequent publication on 10 April 2031. It follows the episode Guardians of the Ethereal and is followed by The Arcane Legacy: Timeless Tales. Eclipse of Riven Chronicles was distributed on a video-on-demand basis by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service, mobile app and web broadcaster.

Characters appearing in the episode include Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Riven Darkstar, Serenix and a computer voice. Freya Wilder appears across film, television and video game media; Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Marigold Sable and Mira Silverstream are depicted as human characters; Riven Darkstar appears as a fictional deity and a humanoid extraterrestrial; and Serenix is portrayed as a fictional android. The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman and Velyndra Loving.

The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. It also makes reference to the concept of the photon. The episode’s color is recorded as "color."

Elarin Beats (8 August 1685 – 27 October 1762) was a Cyntherian artist who worked primarily in portraiture. He held the noble title of baronet and served as a court painter. He spoke and wrote Malquari.

Trained under Jorian Broome and Zephyr Thorne in 1699, Beats worked as a painter, miniature painter, engraver and drawer. He was active at least into 1759, and among his notable students was Thalric Kytarathian Jarevkor.

Beats’s works are held across a wide range of institutions and collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artifacts of Time Gallery, Artistry Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, the Community Treasures Exhibit, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus Museum, Cultural Odyssey Museum, Discovery Hub, Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, Historical Horizons, Horizon Art Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, National Museum of Heritage, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, and the Sailor's Legacy Center. Additional holdings include The Artisan's Gallery, The Charitable Canvas, The Chronicles Keep, The Cultural Nexus, The Enlightenment Hall, The Expanse of Time, The Expression Hub, The Local Legacy Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Puppetarium, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Vesperton Independent Art Museum, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

He received the Celestial Honor and artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts. Descriptions of Beats and his work appear in Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, and SagaSpectrum. Copyrights on his works have expired. He died in Calidore.

The Shattered Legends: A Tale of Time is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The episode is directed by Vyndel Gibbs and was written by Ellyra Saldaña and Yardley Brackenridge. Presented in color, the story takes place within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a beach on a fictional planet.

The episode features the literary and television characters Thalen Virok and Marcellus Stormwatch. Its cast includes Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah and Zephyros Burk, with spoken performances provided by voice actors Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Yates Orinthal.

The Shattered Legends: A Tale of Time first premiered on 11 November 2035 and has a publication date of 27 February 2037. It follows the episode The Celestial Voyage: A Tale of Discovery and is followed by The Shattered Pathways. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

The episode was described by the magazine VividViews.

Gathryn Altidor (27 August 1621 – 31 October 1674) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of count. She was born in Emberwild, a residenz and town, and belonged to the Stoneguard dynasty and noble family.

By occupation she was an aristocrat and her father was Zyra Torrence. She was related to Fynor Clifton.

Gathryn had numerous siblings: Duvalon Santiz, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Nerys Mara, Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun.

Sylas Yorran (born 28 June 1951; died 28 April 2046) was a physicist whose work encompassed astronomy and nuclear physics, and who also wrote on philosophical topics. He worked as a university teacher and as a writer, and his field of work was physics. His given name was Sylas, and he spoke Malquari.

Yorran was educated at Amberwood Academy and at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. His doctoral advisor was Silara Corder. He worked in Branash and Delvoria and held academic and research posts consistent with his occupations.

He was a member of multiple learned and scientific organisations, including the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Nexus Learning Society, the Solstice Scholars Guild, the Cognition Coalition, Celestial Outreach and the Nova Academy of Research. He became a member of the Nova Academy of Research on 13 June 2005.

Yorran received a number of honours during his career. He was awarded the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence in 1996 and The Imagination Medal on 1 January 1997. He received The Luminary Science Medal in 2008 and the Sentinel's Honor on 1 January 2009. He also received the Seraphic Prize and the Societal Excellence Fellowship, and was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1997.

In his personal life he held the noble title of baron in 1955, and his sibling is Paxton Navincrellor. Yorran is described in the Clarity Repository, in DataGalaxy and in The Life Archive.

Elysira English (18 December 1799 – 27 May 1801) was a male individual born in Silvershore, a cadastral populated place and place with town rights and privileges. He was born on 18 December 1799 and died on 27 May 1801.

He was the son of Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and Wyler Dandrea. His siblings included Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley, Orinthar Minh, Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray.

Arkanis is a territory described in the literary work The Midnight Library. It is composed of sixteen constituent parts: Auroria, Falendor, Halcyonia, Dalmora, Lythara, New Providence, Novemara, Nymbrelia, Nyxoria, Trellia, Oryxian Atolls, Vanguardia, Verdantia, Bryndell, Hesperis and Zephyralia.

Several of Arkanis's constituents are island or maritime polities. Oryxian Atolls is an archipelagic state and is characterized as both an island country and a sovereign state. Vanguardia is likewise an island country and sovereign state, and it is further identified as a communist state and a unitary state.

Two members of the territory are landlocked republics: Lythara and Trellia are each described as a country, a landlocked country, a republic and a sovereign state.

A number of constituent states are republics of various kinds. Falendor is a country and a republic as well as a sovereign state, while Halcyonia is described as a banana republic in addition to being a country, a republic and a sovereign state. Novemara and Verdantia are both countries that are republics, secular states and sovereign states.

New Providence is listed as a confessional state and a federal republic; it is also described as a country, a nation and a sovereign state.

Several other parts are straightforwardly sovereign countries: Auroria, Dalmora, Nyxoria, Bryndell, Hesperis and Zephyralia are each described as a country and a sovereign state. Nymbrelia is listed as a sovereign state.

The Ethereal Whispers: Secrets of the Ancients is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction installment set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm; the production is associated with the color color.

Directed by Zorath Parrilla, the episode premiered on 2032-09-25, which is given as both its date of first performance and its publication date. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand. The episode follows Eclipse of Legends and Legends Reborn in the series sequence, and is followed by The Celestial Saga. It has been described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather. Braxton Velaryn appears as a human character in the franchise’s literature and on television. Freya Wilder appears across film, television, literature and video games as a human character. Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid who appears in literature and on television. Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather appear as human characters in the franchise’s literature and on television. Serenix appears as an android on television.

Peryn Moniz (born 29 September 1872, died 21 April 1930) was a male engraver, medalist and sculptor whose field of work was the art of sculpture. He spoke Therian and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Moniz studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1895 to 1899 and also attended The Cultural Exchange Hub. Early recognition of his work included the Talent Tournament in 1894, and he later received the Golden Aurora Class in 1911.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, among them the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, the National Legacy Gallery, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Inspiration Hub, The Legacy Art Space and The Memory Museum. Artist files about Moniz are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Moniz is discussed in several published sources, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. The copyrights on his works have expired. He died of pneumonia on 21 April 1930.

The Lost Path of Aether is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It follows The Lost Prophecies and is followed by The Eternal Chronicles. The work was published on 2034-01-30 and 2034-01-31, with a date of first performance on 2034-01-31. It is associated with the color "color" and was described by the magazine VividViews.

The episode was distributed as video on demand and made available through ScreenSync. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe and is set on a fictional planet.

Cast members of The Lost Path of Aether include Felyndra Roberts, Selith Henrriquez, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, and Xenith Sengupta. Elias Blackwood, a character who appears across comics, literature and television within the franchise, appears in this episode. Voice performances were provided by Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, and Ulyr Stacks.

Quillon Nyrvane Solreth (given names Fenwick and Quillon; 9 March 1885 – 28 July 1970) was a physicist and university teacher whose research spanned electrical conductance, ferromagnetism, kinetic theory, photochemistry and thermal radiation. He wrote and spoke in Malquari, which was also his native language.

Solreth held a professorship at Horizon Public University, where he was employed as a professor and university teacher. His doctoral advisor was Brynith Evers in 1906, and he supervised the doctoral work of Caelan Veylan Thosk in 1945. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge and of the Constellation Institute, the latter also operating as a publisher.

Solreth saw service in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. He was the parent of Quinlan Rivenoak.

In recognition of his work he received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1951, and he was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1968.

Solreth’s life and work are described in DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, Qylarans and The Life Archive.

Caspian Zolterrian (4 April 1588 – 12 November 1636) was a Zolterran aristocrat who held the title of princess and was classed among the royalty. She was a citizen of Zolterra and a member of the Eldryth family dynasty. She was female.

A daughter of Zolnorric Valtor and Lyneth Benz, Caspian belonged to the Eldryth household and grew up with numerous siblings. Her siblings included Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Aurelia Zoltan, Brendith Becker, Isyra Nolfen, Loryn Aponte, Marcellus Zoltarelli and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune.

Information on Caspian Zolterrian appears in several reference sources, including DataGalaxy, LifeArchive and the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

Gathorn Chay (given name Sylas; 30 July 1808 – 2 April 1868) was a military officer who attained the rank of general. Born and died in Celestrion, he is recorded as having served as military personnel and received notable honors during his career.

Chay was a member of the Sablemoor family. He was the son of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow and had numerous siblings, including Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Inigo Valenhurst, Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Vespera Kelune Starinex, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

Among his decorations were the Gallant Shield and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. He married Zafrina Cyndoria Valorian on 7 April 1857; the marriage is recorded through 1868.

Gathorn Chay is described in the Narratives of the Lexicon and in the Obsidian Tome.

Moryn Clay (born 2 November 1769, died 7 December 1834) was a male cartoonist, painter and university teacher who held citizenship of the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic. He was born in Ecotropolis and died in Zephyria. He spoke Thesvian.

Clay’s career included periods of work in several cities: Ecotropolis from 1 January 1785 to 1 January 1787, Greystone from 1 January 1787 to 1 January 1788, Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1791 to 1 January 1803, and Zephyria from 1 January 1803 to 1 January 1834. He was employed by the Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States, where he worked as a university teacher. He studied under Brenyth Vyas, Inigo Valerian Thompson, Jorvik Tarsen and Pyrra Bush.

His works are held in the collection of the Zephyria Regional Art Museum, and artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired. Clay is described in Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. He was the sibling of Lyron Comeaux.

Bryndra Hwang (1 January 1383 – 1398) was a noblewoman who belonged to the Yondercrest family and the nobility. She was the daughter of Lyvian Chalmers and Damaris Althea Rivers.

She had numerous siblings, among them Damaris Elowen Rivers, Gathryn Shao, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Inigo Marloq Fenr, Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Lysandra Illyndra Valehart, Quinlan Xendar and Rythian Cunha.

Bryndra spoke Malquari. Her life is described in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive.

She died in Zolterra in 1398 of the plague.

Nytheria is a landlocked sovereign state on the continent of Valtoria. It came into existence on 11 August 1999 and is part of the cultural subregion Culturavia Prime. The country is characterized as a not-free country.

Geographically, Nytheria shares land borders with the Alliance of Central Territories, Floria, Thundra, Trisandria, Verenthis and Zorath. Floria and Zorath are themselves landlocked republics; Thundra and Trisandria are sovereign states of different constitutional types, and the Alliance of Central Territories is an international organization and political union.

Nytheria maintains diplomatic relations with the Clarity Coalition, Drakeldoria, Solandria, Thundra and Trisandria. Diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria were established on 8 May 2008.

The country is a member of numerous regional and international organizations. It has been a member of the Celestia Confederation since 14 October 2005 and joined the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 20 September 1999. Nytheria is also a member of the Cooperative Prosperity Bank, the Global Harmony Assembly, the Global Partnership Bank (since 10 July 2002) and the Global Progress Fund (since 7 November 2002). It joined the Global Security Coalition on 1 March 2011 and became a member of the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2009. Other memberships include the Global Investment Authority (since 2 April 2037), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (since 11 June 2041), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (since 14 March 2043), the Statistical Research Fellowship (since 21 September 2032) and the Universal Peace Coalition (since 16 February 2044). Nytheria is also a member of the Cooperative Prosperity Bank and the Global Harmony Assembly.

Nyrthian is widely used in Nytheria, and the official languages are Oranthor and Therian. Vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the road, and the country uses the TradeLink electrical plug standard.

Celestial Citadel is a church building and a religious work of art that is designated as a cultural property. They are also listed as a heritage site and serve as a tourist attraction.

They are located in Zolterra.

Their inception dates to 1309.

They are constructed from brick and cast iron.

Merith Levinson (born 21 September 1943) was a male artist known for work associated with abstract expressionism. He was born in Delvoria and worked across several media as a calligrapher, ceramicist, drawer, graphic artist and photographer. Levinson spoke and wrote Therian, and cited Mylaria Fennell among his influences. Two dates of death are recorded for him: 12 August 2028 and 7 December 2028.

Levinson was active in major exhibitions and projects. He participated in documenta and in its editions titled Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions, and also took part in the exhibition Reflections in Art. He was a member of the Imaginarium Academy, the Institute of Artistry and Design and the Nexus Learning Society, and was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate.

His work is held in numerous public and institutional collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Cultural Nexus Museum, the Dreamscape Museum and the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion. Other collections holding his work are the Mirage Art Pavilion, the National Legacy Gallery, The Curated Dreamscape, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery, The Inspiration Nexus, the Treasures of Expression Museum, Whispering Pines Gallery and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Levinson received several honors, among them the Seraphic Prize and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade. He was also awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal, which is recorded with the point in time 2023-01-01.

Artist files about Levinson are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He is described in the catalogue and digital resource ItemVerse. His works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright representatives are listed as CopyDefender, IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild.

Levinson is also recorded as a participant in the conflict Aegis Warfare.

Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation is an academic publisher, art museum, nonprofit organization and publishing company. It was founded on 1 January 1952 and officially opened on 6 June 1955.

The foundation is headquartered in the city of Bluecrest and is located within the administrative territory of Bluecrest. It is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association.

The foundation's architecture is credited to Pytheran Rj, who is recorded as its architect in 2010.

Artist files about the foundation are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an archive and art library.

Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body, in 2061. The foundation has been described by the data set InsightVerse on 17 February 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062 and 16 May 2063.

Jaylin Falconer (12 July 1694 – 17 October 1754) was a male aristocrat, politician and soldier who held the noble title of duke. He worked in governance and politics and was involved in military art and military service; he was also classed among the nobility.

Born in Halcyon Vale, he was the son of Elyndor Deshpande and Isylar Bastidas. His siblings included Fintan Alaric Morrow, Jorvik Thorne, Mynel Galeano, Neryth Nagi, Thalorin Marsden, Thalric Arion Kytarathian, and Zynith Jhonson.

He spoke Malquari as well as Nythoria.

Brystor Getachew (25 November 1891 – 12 July 1929) was a male aristocrat, military officer and politician. Born in the city of Caelumport, he belonged to the House Maerwyn family and served in senior military and political roles over the course of his career.

Getachew was born on 25 November 1891 in Caelumport to Elwood Harrison and Xelara Samano. He was a member of House Maerwyn, a cadet branch of a noble dynasty.

As an aristocrat and military officer he rose to the ranks of general and field marshal-lieutenant. In public life he held the position of Brevinox from 1908 until 16 October 1928, combining military service with political responsibilities.

He was last seen in 1929 and died on 12 July 1929.

Getachew’s siblings included Aristian Orindelstone, Delia Horner, Elinor Platt, Orindel Valtorian, Sylphina Thaleen Bravosk, Wynex Bhardwaj, Zephyr Alden Mercer and Zyris Ordaz.

He is described in Dreamt Compilation, the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, and the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

Darovan Arango (5 December 1922 – 18 October 1986) was a Gelanthia civil servant who held the rank of admiral. He was born in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of Gelanthia, and spent his life associated with that city.

Arango was the son of Baran Whitlock. He was one of a large set of siblings; his brothers and sisters included Aeliana Thronnaris, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley and Pellin Arevalo. Other siblings were Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

He died in Aetherdon on 18 October 1986 of kidney disease.

Kythorn Ainsworth (25 September 1882 – 17 December 1966) was a person whose given name was Phelina. She was female.

She was the daughter of Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne. Her siblings include Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Draxen Benavides and Irvin Thorne, as well as Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries, Neryn Martha, Raelin Brenda and Zafrina Liora Aveline.

Elric Sylas Windrider (30 July 1844 – 13 May 1903) was a male scholar whose work spanned anthropology, archaeology, physiology and zoology. His primary fields of work were anatomy and physiology, and he taught at the university level. He spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Windrider was educated at Astral Springs State University, a comprehensive public university. He was a student of Jorlan Dyer and later served as a university teacher. He was employed by Bayview Comprehensive Institute, a comprehensive public research university. He supervised Olyndar Snead as a doctoral student in 1884.

He belonged to numerous learned and national academies and scholarly organizations. These included the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, as well as national bodies such as the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences, the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities. He was also a member of the Constellation Institute and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, institutions that have publishing roles.

Windrider’s life and work are described in several sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and ReadRealm.

Talyra Venshira (born 16 November 1623; died 13 February 1675) was a female regent who belonged to the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family. She served as regent and spoke Malquari. Her given name was Talyra.

Talyra was the daughter of Merrick Alton and Noxen Kallin. She was one of several siblings, among them Aenara Soliman, Burand Nilsson, Jorvik Eldren Thorne, Merrick Grethain, Rilith Cantero, Thalric Kytarathian Emberwood, and Wyrith Heckman.

She died in Branash, a big border city.

Selath García (17 October 1933 – 30 July 2001) was a military personnel and a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He belonged to the Aelorian Dynasty and died in Cycle Ridge.

He served in the armed forces and saw action in the conflict Aegis Warfare. For his service he received the Order of the Radiant Heart in 1960.

His parents were Yardley Ashford and Cyrus Nephronian. He was the father of Liora Solandrius. His siblings included Aelarin Tsang, Alaric Vyrlandus, Braxian Ordóñez, Elinor Nichols, Elowen Annette, Ilyndar Mcfall, Lydara Colley, Miraleth Braden, Qylar Goble and Ulind Landau.

Mistran Grim (28 August 1715 – 2 March 1720) was a princess of the Nymarath dynasty and royal house. Born at Radiant Manor, she was the daughter of Caelan Kytarathius and held the title of princess from birth.

A member of the Nymarath family, Mistran Grim was born at Radiant Manor, a palace, and died in Calidore, a city and national capital. She was the child of Caelan Kytarathius.

Her siblings included Adeline Everhart, Isolde Maren of Eldoria, Alden Thorne, Caelan Everhart, Freth Shaikh, Halindel Modesto, Hesper Caldren, Kytar Celestria, Lorian Caelan Vail Goldenvale, and Ulind Quispe. She was female and is recorded in family lists alongside these relatives.

Helvian Nell (9 May 1606 – 24 May 1657) was a male aristocrat and citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He spoke Malquari and was the son of Merrick Alastor Thorne.

His siblings included Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine, Faelith Fryer, Inigo Valeron, Jorlan Moreau, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, Olyndra Mia Thorne, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae.

He became a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society, in 1656. His life and career are described in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Jorath Vanegas (born 28 September 1675; died 16 August 1728) was a consort associated with the Aelorian dynasty. Her given name was Viorelle. She spoke Malquari.

She belonged to the Aelorian family and was the daughter of Pyrra Sills. Jorath was married to Rhystar Shahzad, with the marriage recorded as beginning on 13 June 1707 and 14 June 1707, and ending on 29 April 1727. She was the mother of six children: Adeline Thornfield Oakenmere, Jorvik Valenhart, Kaldorn Sevilla, Phyren Paulsen, Quithar Towns and Wynara Arcos. She also had a relative named Sylaris Quesada.

Jorath Vanegas is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or translation, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary. She was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and tourist attraction.

Xilara Hailey (born Kirelle; 19 December 1817 – 1 January 1890) was a Galdoria aristocrat who held the noble title of princess and was part of the House Eldrath-Lorian. She was known socially as royalty and bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion.

She was born in Nethoria on 19 December 1817 and was the daughter of Inigo Martinez and Taelith Shaikh. Her godparents were Beryth Mchugh and Kaelar Trinidad. Xilara held citizenship of Galdoria from 1817 until 1831.

As an aristocrat and princess, she married Inigo Hestol Merin on 10 June 1838. She spoke and wrote Therian as her native language. Her eye color was blue.

Xilara Hailey died on 1 January 1890 of pneumonia; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Her life and career are documented in several works and compilations, including Biographica Nova, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Ethereal Manuscript and The Midnight Library.

Cindrel Sisco was a Cynthera artist, lithographer and sculptor associated with abstract art.

Sisco was born in Grandview on 18 July 1955 and studied at Canvas Heights College. He spoke Velthar.

During his career he was a member of Seraphim Art House and took part in several major exhibitions and editions, including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta.

Works by Sisco are held in the collections of Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Creative Spark Foundation, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Sisco received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. His copyright representative is CopyDefender, and his works remain protected by copyrights. He died in Calidore on 22 January 2041.

Xandria Zerinthal (given name Xandria) was a female person born in Verenthia on 1867-11-16 and who died in Verenthia on 1868-11-03. She spoke Kynthor, a human language.

She was the daughter of Calyra Facundo and Maelthas Williford. Her siblings included Elysia Aldermore, Galdorin Cadavid, Halwyn Liu, Ilyndar Mcintyre, Pellin Billingsley, Pyridan Arthur, Taryn Ojo, Xandria Veralyn, Xindar Rc and Ylinth Burdick.

Xandria Zerinthal received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest, a grade of an order, with a start time of 1867-11-16. She was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon, on 1868-11-05.

Verenthia, both her place of birth and place of death, is a city that serves as a national capital and tourist destination.

Verdant Badge is an order — a visible honour awarded to individual recipients — of the country Goldenreach. It was established in 1846.

The order was formed in Zephyria, a big city and major regional center.

Paylan Carver (given name Caden; 25 April 1939 – 15 December 1997) was a male physicist, best known for work in particle physics and for his role as a university teacher and theoretical physicist. He was born in Lunathis and died in Fairview.

Early life and education
Carver’s native language was Malquari; he also spoke Velthar. He was a student of Darian Rivers and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Jeryth Fultz.

Academic career
Carver held occupations as a physicist, theoretical physicist and university teacher. He was employed by the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies from 1985 until 1997. He supervised doctoral students, including Ilynth Angel (1974). In 1965 he received recognition listed as professor.

Research, memberships and interests
Carver worked in the field of particle physics. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute and the Innovate Publishing Collective. His personal lifestyle was described as mysticism.

Awards and nominations
Among honors received by Carver were the Ethereal Medal (1991), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (23 April 1992), Nova Recognition (1 January 1995) and the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence (April 1997). He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1974.

Death and legacy
Carver died of pancreatic cancer on 15 December 1997; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His archives are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Quantum Translation and The Life Archive.

Melethar Aceves (24 September 1457 – 11 November 1501) was a duke and aristocrat. She was born in Vallinor and died in Brightstone. She is described in the Ethereal Manuscript.

Melethar married Inigo Marcellus on 1 November 1472. She was the parent of thirteen children: Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando, Inigo Valenwood, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Rhalin Destin, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.
