Born in the big city of Vallinor, Melethar carried the noble title duke during her life and pursued the occupation of aristocrat. She died in Brightstone, a large city that serves as a cantonal capital.

Jorvik Valenhart (24 May 1716 – 3 September 1773) was a margrave and military officer who held the rank of general. He was a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty, a noble family, and during his career received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry.

He was the son of Rhystar Shahzad and Jorath Vanegas. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Oakenmere, Kaldorn Sevilla, Orynth Mccool, Phyren Paulsen, Quithar Towns, Wynara Arcos, Wynex Grullon and Yndira Kuykendall.

Valenhart spoke Malquari. He was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that also serves as a tourist attraction.

Ylinda Shaker (19 June 1901 – 13 July 1962) was a Verenthia politician who held the noble title of count. He was a citizen of Verenthia and served in public life as a politician.

He was the son of Selis Dolores and belonged to the kazoku social class. He had numerous siblings, including Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin, Jareth June, Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Xeryn Kingston and Xylara Furman.

He spoke and wrote Omerith, using that language for his written work.

The Hidden Path is a media franchise episode and a television series episode in the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria, part of the Eldoria Chronicles. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

It was directed by Hesperis Koenig and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. The Hidden Path was first performed on 2034-02-06 and has publication dates recorded as 2034-02-06 and 2035-07-12. In the series sequence, the episode follows Whispers in the Dark and is followed by The Unseen Force.

The production was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format; ScreenSync is a mobile app and a video on demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The episode has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews; The Feature Folio appears as a list and magazine article, and VividViews is a magazine.

The cast of The Hidden Path includes Phrin Mcintire, Xian Concha, Yardley Harquen Naim and Ylostar Gaynor. Characters appearing in the episode include Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Harmony Quill is presented as a comics character, a fictional human and both a literary and television character. Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are portrayed as fictional humans and television characters. Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram, a fictional writer and a television character.

The episode references neutronium. The Hidden Path is associated with the color color.

Jorvik Alderwood (born 26 February 1819; died 1 October 1895) was a Velorian Dominion citizen who worked as a crystallographer, mineralogist, physicist and university teacher. His given name was Jorvik. He held the rank of full professor and carried out his work in Delvoria.

Alderwood was born in Delvoria, a major regional center and big city, and was educated at the Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, a public comprehensive university and open-access publisher. His doctoral advisor was Garren Zethar Qelmar.

Over the course of his academic career Alderwood was employed by the Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and by Luminara College. His fields of work included crystallography, mineralogy and physics, and he supervised doctoral students including Norric Eldran Voss in 1859 and Caden Rivers in 1864.

He was a member of several learned bodies, among them the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, as well as the Constellation Institute, an academy of sciences that also functions as a book publisher, and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, a national academy and learned society. Alderwood received the Seraphic Prize, a civil decoration that serves as a cultural prize, order of merit and science award.

Alderwood spoke Malquari. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary.

Kalyra Painter (17 April 1918 – 2 March 1957) was a male aristocrat born in the city of Lyrisport. Born and resident in Lyrisport, he died in Lunathis, a city-state and federal capital.

He was the son of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. His siblings included Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Qeryth Wooten, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai and Zethrin Kantor.

Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture is an art academy specializing in art and a public university predominantly funded by public means. They were founded in 1801.

The university is based in the city of Solyra, where they maintain their headquarters and are located within the city's administrative territory. Solyra is a big city and serves as a state capital.

Zorlan Mahmood (27 June 1917 – 4 January 1934) was a Gelanthia citizen and a member of the Sylverian family. He was born at Crystal Keep, a royal palace, and was the son of Baran Whitlock.

He had a large number of siblings, among them Aeliana Thronnaris, Belwyn Mcghee, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez and Freyael Mcwilliams, as well as Fythar Esteves and Fythar Neill. Other siblings included Galasath Matias, Kalindor Christenson, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Rynar Coble, Taryth Eugenio, Thronnaris Eldricson, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza and Zyreth Vivar.

He died in Aetherdon, a large city and national capital, on 4 January 1934. The cause of death was typhoid fever and the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Helvian Mckoy (8 February 1920 – 22 November 1926) was a male citizen of Gelanthia and a member of the Sylverian family.

He was born in Crystal Keep and died in Aetherdon.

Mckoy was the son of Baran Whitlock and Elyndor Borba. His siblings were Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Delwyn Villafane, Qerev Guardado and Zylara Solorzano.

Daryth Tamayo (7 January 1891 – 3 July 1968) was a painter and photographer known for work in genre painting and portraiture. He spoke Therian and worked across both painting and photographic media during his career.

Tamayo was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Cindrel Elizondo and Nerya Mi. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design, Seraphim Art House, and the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy. During his career he received the Talent Tournament.

His works are held in a wide range of collections, including Cyndoria National Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. Other institutions with holdings include Abstract Assemblage, Creative Spark Foundation, Elysian Atrium, Essence of Art, Seraphim Art House, Terranova Artis Museum and The Art Haven. Additional repositories that hold his work include The Artistic Elixir, The Curated Press, The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Palace of Reflections and The Visionary Landscape. Artist files about Tamayo are kept at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Tamayo has been described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and O'Rourke Insights Online.
Resonance Translation is a translation of a work into the Myrathian language. Myrathian is a modern natural language. The translation was published in 1975.

Liora Solandrian (born 26 March 1988) is a diplomat who holds citizenship of both Cynthera and Solandria. She is of royal social classification and is styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. Liora is employed by the Council of Allied Sovereignties and is a recipient of the Noble Valorian Order.

She was educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute. As part of her public and ceremonial roles, she participated in the Celestria Alysor Union on 18 September 2003.

Her father is Elara Solandrin and her mother is Liora Solandrius. Her godparents are Alysor Wasson and Bastian Verenthia. She has four siblings: Aeliana Solandrius, Aveline Solandria, Elysia Solandrian and Viorelle Solandria.

Liora speaks Corath, Therian, Thesvian and Velthar. She has strawberry blond hair and participates in equestrian sport. She is described in Biographica Nova.

Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere (16 January 1774 – 28 November 1827) was a governor and military officer who held the rank of general field marshal. He spoke Malquari and Therian, and his given name was Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere.

He was married to Wyler Dandrea from 5 March 1799. The couple had ten children: Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley and Orinthar Minh, as well as Othalyn Roma, Sylas Sarnel, Wryken Ortega, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray.

Fallowmere is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Grellan Flaco (born 1958-08-09 in Ecotropolis; died 2045-10-25 in Ecotropolis) was a Thesvian-speaking artist. He worked across multiple media as an artist, drawer, graphic artist, lithographer, painter and printmaker, and also served as a partisan. He was active in 1998.

Flaco held citizenship of Morvath from 1958-08-09 to 1985-06-18. Over the course of his career he participated in Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Ethos Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Solstice Art Storage, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Institute and The Inspiration Nexus.

He received the Arcane Order. His body of work remains protected by copyrights and his copyright representative is CopyDefender. Artist files on Flaco are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts.

Fynor Vásquez (17 August 1962 – 14 August 2041) was a male artist whose work spanned visual arts, literature and music. He was associated with the pop art movement and worked in painting and sculpture, and his creative output included jazz and poetry.

Vásquez's visual practice encompassed painting, sculpture, photography, drawing and design. He also wrote poetry and other texts, and performed as a musician: he was a jazz musician and saxophonist who played the saxophone, and jazz figures among his primary genres and fields of work. He spoke Velthar.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Artemis Gallery, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance, Chronicle Citadel, Creative Spark Foundation, National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. He participated in the exhibition Radiant Impressions, a documenta edition.

Artist files about Vásquez are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright representatives included CopyDefender, IntellectProtect and Music and Media Syndicate; his works remain protected by copyrights.

Qylen Marques (born Inigo; 13 May 1833 – 20 March 1874) was a painter associated with the Emotional Topography movement. He was a member of the Imaginarium Academy and worked primarily in Seraphim Bay. He spoke and wrote Therian.

Born Inigo in 1833, Marques trained under Syldor Hyde and Wyntar Boren. He worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1857 until 1 January 1870. During his career his paintings were acquired by a wide range of institutions; holdings include the Arathonia Art Museum, the Artistry Alliance, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, the Harmathia Art Repository and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional collections with his work are the Solaris Cultural Collective, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Expression Hub, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Memory Mosaic, Treasures of Expression Museum and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files on Marques are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Marques died by suicide on 20 March 1874 in Ecotropolis; the recorded cause of death was exsanguination. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Vortex Archipelago is an archipelago and geographic region located on the Valandor subcontinent and forming part of the larger Solaraith supercontinent. It occupies a maritime area alongside the Syrenthia Estuary but is distinct from the estuary itself.

The archipelago shares a border with Volantia. Administratively and politically, the Vortex Archipelago comprises a number of island countries and states among its constituent parts. These include Calypsia, a sovereign island country; Galadore, an archipelagic sovereign monarchy; Nautilis, an archipelagic state that is also an administrative territorial entity; Oceantia, a unitary archipelagic sovereign state; Seraphis, an archipelagic sovereign state; the Solstice Isles, an island country and sovereign state; Talerith, a sovereign island country; Tyronia, an island country and sovereign state; Oryxian Atolls, an archipelagic sovereign state; Vanguardia, a communist, unitary island sovereign state; and Wynsor., a sovereign island country.

Geographically, the archipelago is situated in or next to the Syrenthia Estuary and forms part of the maritime and insular landscape of Valandor within Solaraith.

Crown Zafrina (given name Zafrina; born 24 June 1524 — died 10 June 1594) was a royal consort of Crownlandia and a member of the Aelorian dynasty. She served as a royal consort and was a citizen of Crownlandia, a kingdom and constitutional monarchy that is also described as a colonial power, sovereign state, realm, country and unitary state.

Zafrina was the daughter of Thaddeus Archemonta and Miraleth Sol and had at least one sibling, Thalor Jorvistan. She was also related to Ryvian Avalos and Talyra Meryn Stone.

On 10 April 1541 Zafrina married Merrick Ashbourne; that marriage continued until 11 July 1574. She had a child, Merrick Alton Rivers.

She spoke Malquari, a modern language. Zafrina died on 10 June 1594 and was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that is also a tourist attraction.

Zafrina is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Fintan Aldridge (1 January 1407 – 21 January 1436) was a regent and noble who held the title of duke and the position of Radiant Count. His given name was Fintan, and he belonged to the Yondercrest family and to the Ardentia people. He spoke Malquari.

Born to Halindra Iglesias and Damaris Solenne Thar, he was one of several children. His siblings included Bryndith Tree, Caelan Idris, Kyndra Hardwick, Olyn Morey, Orilith Fry and Therin Bracken.

In his public role as a regent he served as Radiant Count and bore the noble title duke. He was a recipient of the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Fintan Aldridge is described in Reflections of Humanity.

Pluralingua is a modern language, a pluricentric language variant (an officially regulated variety of a pluricentric language), and a standard variety. It is used across Cyndoria, Merithia, the Quolmaris Republic, Solandria and Tranthia, and is indigenous to Lunathis.

Typologically, Pluralingua is a fusional, pro-drop, stress-timed language that favors an adjective–noun order while allowing relatively free word order. These characteristics inform both its syntax and prosody.

Grammatically, Pluralingua marks a set of seven cases—nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, instrumental, locative and vocative—and distinguishes four genders: feminine, masculine animate, masculine inanimate and neuter. Verbal morphology encodes three basic tense distinctions: present, past and future.

Narratives of the Lexicon is a book series and lexicon presented as a biographical dictionary devoted to biographies. Written in Malquari, it was first published in Lunathis in 1895 and the series ran from 1895 until 1930. The work is in the public domain.

The series is organized into multiple volumes and comprises a range of reference forms, including biographical articles and encyclopedia articles, supported by cross-references. Genealogical tables appear both as parts of the work and as illustrative content, and the series also includes a list of genealogical tables and a postface.

Front and back matter within the series contains a preface and various registers of persons, among them a general register of persons as well as registers organized by country of birth and by occupation or position. The work is associated with the country of Quinthara and was published in Lunathis.

Wylora Leticia (15 March 1868 – 23 July 1944) was a painter associated with the Temporal Idealism movement. Working principally in visual arts, he specialized in portraiture and maintained an active professional career from 1 January 1895 until 1 January 1944.

Early life and education
Leticia was born on 15 March 1868. His native and principal language was Therian. He trained under Elena Venturi from 1 January 1887 to 9 January 1890 and then under Uthar Caba from 9 January 1890 to 1 January 1897. He studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1898 to 1 January 1902 and also attended The Cultural Exchange Hub.

Career
As a painter working within visual arts and the portrait genre, Leticia was active across the late 19th and early 20th centuries and became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design on 1 January 1928. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Abstract Assemblage; Artefactual Odyssey; Artemis Gallery; Artistry Alliance; Canvas Grove; Canvas of Dreams Gallery; Canvas of Inspirations Museum; Celestial Art Space; Cultura Nexus; and Curator's Archive. Additional institutions holding his work include the Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation; Ethos Gallery; Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press; Haven of Expression; Heritage Hub; Institute of Fine Arts and Culture; Jorvikson Literary Heritage House; Kaleidoscope Museum of Art; Mirage Cultural Center; Myrthwood Art Collective; and the National Legacy Gallery. His work also appears in the collections of Quentarion Art Museum; Revelry Art Center; Royal Gallery Palace; Solaris Cultural Collective; Solstice Art Sanctuary; TerraMuse Nonprofit; The Artisan’s Realm; The Creative Rhapsody House; The Curated Press; The Dreamscapes of Art; The Memory Mosaic; The Visionary Landscape; Valtaris Art & Culture Institute; and Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Honors and recognition
Leticia received several awards and honors during his career, beginning with the Talent Tournament (1 January 1897). He was awarded the Noble Valorian Order on 1 November 1912, the Golden Aurora Class on 11 July 1917, the Golden Vanguard Class on 2 July 1937, and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade on 19 May 1942.

Legacy and documentation
Artist files on Leticia are held at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described in sources including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, LinguaScript, and O'Rourke Insights Online. Copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Aeliana Solandrius (born 1 January 1992 in Havencrest) is a citizen of Solandria who is a member of the country's royalty and a socialite. She is styled with the honorific prefix Knight Aerion" and speaks Corath, Cynvelthar and Therian.

She is the daughter of Elara Solandrin and Liora Solandrius. Her siblings are Aveline Solandria, Elysia Solandrian, Liora Solandrian and Viorelle Solandria.

Aeliana is described in the biographical dictionary Biographica Nova.

Vesperin Solan Arindel (13 November 1492 – 19 March 1566) was a male noble of the Qelthar family. His family name was Arindel, and he spoke Malquari.

He served as a ruler and held the noble title margrave.

He married Ulwyn Rey on 19 December 1507. Vesperin Solan Arindel was the parent of nine children: Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elric Arindel, Elysia Arindel, Jasper Arindel and Thalindra Arindel, as well as Galen Blythe, Iverath Solano, Kelyr Voigt and Ulyra Gibson.

Vesperin Solan Arindel is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage is an archive, art museum and library that also serves as the national library of Cynthera. It is a government-sponsored body with support from the executive branch. The institute was established in 1946.

The institute is located in Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The institute has been described by the data set InsightVerse on several occasions: 31 October 2058, 30 April 2059, 3 August 2060, 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062, and 16 May 2063.

Mistralith, which appears in the institute’s name, is an administrative region and is also recorded as a constituent country of a sovereign state. It is additionally described as a country and as a sporting nation.

Thalric Kytarathian Althorian (born 23 December 1909, died 1 October 1992) was a male creative practitioner whose work was associated with modernism and the genre of landscape painting. His given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He worked as an architect, drawer and photographer and was active professionally from 1924 to 1989. He was a student of Zander Thaloren and in 1945 he worked in Harborview City.

He was educated at the Gallery of Dreams and at Lumina Arts Academy, and he spoke the Velthar language. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition and of the Summit Academy of Learning. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative; the copyrights on his works have expired. He is described by DataGalaxy.

Works by Thalric Kytarathian Althorian are held in a number of collections, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Aurora Art Gallery, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Tapestry Museum and the Ethereal Art Registry. Other institutions that hold his work are the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Curatorial Vault, The Evolution Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Collective and the Visual Voyage Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep.

The Heritage Exhibit was an art museum and memory institution located and headquartered in Fairview. It was established on 1 January 1999 and officially opened in 1999.

As a memory institution, it had curatorial care over a collection and its stated mission was to preserve that collection for future generations. The Heritage Exhibit ceased operations on 31 May 2054.

Olyndra is a female given name attested in reference works and literary lexica. It is recorded in the Academic Reference Blueprint and in Narratives of the Lexicon. The Academic Reference Blueprint is presented as an article, guideline, list and scholarly article, while Narratives of the Lexicon appears as a book series and as a lexicon.

The name occurs across a range of languages, including Quolmar, the Tethyrian Language, Thesvian, the Valorean Tongue, Veldrak, Veldrith, Xarnum, Xyldari and Zentari. These languages are described variously: many are identified as both modern and natural languages; Veldrak and Xyldari are presented as languages and modern languages; the Tethyrian Language is additionally noted as a specialty.

Olyndra is recorded in the Eldranth Script and is written using that script, which is a natural writing system.

Delvyn Llano (30 April 1965 – 10 May 2055) was an installation artist, jewelry designer, painter, printmaker and sculptor whose work operated at the intersection of jewelry and jewelry design and engaged with abstract art, minimalism and conceptual art. His practice combined small-scale crafted objects with larger sculptural and installation approaches, reflecting the aesthetic concerns of abstract and conceptual movements.

Given names associated with Llano include Adeline Thornfield and Fintan. He worked primarily in the languages of Therian and exhibited widely; among his participations were The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, a temporary exhibition, and The Display Anthology, an exhibition and publication.

Llano’s works are held in numerous public and private collections. Institutions holding his pieces include the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Dreamscape Museum, the Mirage Art Pavilion, the Nexus of Literary Inquiry, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Chronicle Chamber, The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and The Memory Museum. Several of these institutions combine museum, research and library functions, and the Nexus of Literary Inquiry also serves as a research institute and specialized archive.

Artist files relating to Llano are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts; both institutions function as art libraries and research resources, and the Gallery of Texts also serves as a museum library. For copyright matters his interests were represented by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild, with his body of work described as protected by copyrights.

He produced work across multiple media and scales, moving between intimate jewelry and expansive installations, and his output reflected the formal restraint of minimalism alongside conceptual approaches to material and space.

Aelindor Pendleton (18 February 1841 – 17 May 1895) was a naval officer from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, a colonial power and sovereign state. He entered the Abyssal Protectors—the navy—on 26 May 1853 and served as a naval officer. During his service he took part in the Conclave of Conflict.

Pendleton was the son of Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio. He had ten siblings, including Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Kirelle Ashwood and Orylan Abrahams. His other siblings were Qylen Lux, Sylphina Calidore, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

Ilynth Currie (9 December 1838 – 30 October 1893) was a military officer who served Cynthera and attained the rank of lieutenant general in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army.

Born in the city and national capital Calidore, Currie was the son of Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio. His siblings included Aelindor Pendleton, Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Kirelle Ashwood and Orylan Abrahams, as well as Qylen Lux, Sylphina Calidore, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

Currie held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and had been a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom until 1 January 1840. His allegiance was to Cynthera.

As a career military officer, he served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and rose to the rank of lieutenant general.

Wylen Renner (5 January 1939 – 15 January 1994) was a painter, sculptor, illustrator and drawer whose work was principally concerned with the art of painting. He worked within a surrealist movement and is associated with abstract art.

Renner was influenced by Aelan Sutherland. Over the course of his career he produced drawings, illustrations, paintings and sculptures; his career and works are described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy, and artist files on him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in many public and private collections, including the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Canvas of Illusions Gallery and the Color Spectrum Division. Other collections holding his work are Cultural Nexus, the Cultural Nexus of Artoria, the Dreamscape Museum, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics and the Essence of Form Museum. The National Museum of Cultural Heritage, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum and Solaris Cultural Collective also include his works, as do Solstice Art Storage and the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum. Additional holdings include The Artful Journey Institute, The Artifact Atelier, The Echo Chamber, The Expression Hub and The Inspiration Institute, as well as The Palette of Creativity Museum and The Realm of Colors Museum. His works are further represented in the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and the Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

He spoke Therian and Velthar, and he was married to Tyrian Balcazar. Renner died of a myocardial infarction on 15 January 1994; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His oeuvre remains protected by copyrights and is represented by IntellectProtect and the Music and Media Syndicate.

Delyth Houck (1089 – 25 November 1159) was a person. She was the daughter of Hesper Vossar.

Her siblings included Braxton Mendez, Caelith Qian and Cyndra Obi. Other siblings were Hesper Elowen Thorne, Ilindra Bianchi and Rhyse Aveline Carter, as well as Rythian Meng, Xian Quintanilla, Yardley Thorne and Ylandra St John.

Wrylen Matt (died 1387) was a woman. She was married to Valandor Alves.

She had nine children, among them Fynor Newsom, Ilynth Sai, Liora Valen and Mynel Hailey. Her other children included Olyndra Velasquez, Pheris Manzanares, Sylas Galvorn, Thalyn Pastrana and Ulthir Baltazar.

Eriath Tripp (23 September 1798 – 7 March 1841) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title duke and belonged to the House Eldrath-Lorian. She was born in Nethoria and died in Zephyra.

Tripp was the daughter of Inigo Montale and Rynira Shams. Her godparents were Delphina Nereth Vale and Inigo Martinez. She married Rynthor Lowe on 6 September 1814.

Her family circle included numerous siblings, among them Talinor Adelinev, Elirian Bunker, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Montelune, Inigo Montale, Inigo Valerian Thorne, Pyrion Cipriano and Ulyndra Cahill. As an aristocrat she spoke Therian.

Eriath Tripp died of an infectious disease in Zephyra on 7 March 1841.

Elysian Thornehart (15 August 1614 – 21 November 1621) was a noble of the Elarian dynasty who held the title and office of Caledorn. He was born in Verenthia and died there on 21 November 1621; his death was attributed to smallpox and recorded as due to natural causes. He was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

A member of the Elarian family, he was the son of Rhaelar Margarita and Olyndra Valemont. His godparents were Aethrin Amber and Rhalin Jacquez; Aethrin Amber also appears among his siblings. His brothers and sisters included Aelarin Nickel, Aethrin Amber, Aldric Fenwyn, Aldric Thornewood, Kalyn Ponder, Terath Latta and Ulrith Locke.

Thornehart spoke Kynthor. Verenthia, his birthplace and place of death, is a city that serves as a national capital and a tourist destination.

Merrick Alastor Thorne (21 October 1575 – 6 December 1625) was a ruler and citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He was given the names Caden and Merrick and spoke Malquari.

He was married to Eryndor Jeronimo from 9 January 1610 until 6 December 1625. His known relatives included Pylira Carden and Yloria Francois. He was the father of Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine, Faelith Fryer, Helvian Nell, Inigo Valeron, Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, Olyndra Mia Thorne, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae.

Thorne is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary.

Arcane Legends is a video game from Verenthia. It is described as a role-playing game and specifically as a turn-based role-playing game presented in a single-player format. The title was announced on 2058-08-29 and has publication dates of 2059-01-16 and 2060-03-02.

The game was released for the AstraBox and the CipherSphere platforms. AstraBox is a model series and video game console model, while CipherSphere is a computing platform and operating system released as proprietary software. Arcane Legends is distributed by digital distribution and is available through AppAlley, AppForge, PixelMart and VaultPlay. AppAlley and AppForge operate as app marketplaces, PixelMart functions as an online shop and video game distribution platform, and VaultPlay serves as a digital rights management service, a software repository and a video game distribution platform. Arcane Legends is also compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 electronic device model.

Arcane Legends supports interaction via a computer keyboard, a computer mouse and a gamepad. The work is associated with the languages Omerith and Velthar.

The narrative of Arcane Legends is set in Celestport, Verenthia and Vintara. The cast of characters includes Kael Starwhisper, Kaelin Stormforge, Lucian Rook, Lyra Ysolde, Mira Dawnshadow, Orion Brightforge, Orion Vale, Raine Nightfall and Thorne Wilder. Among these, Lucian Rook, Orion Vale and Thorne Wilder are presented as vigilante figures.

Mythical Crusade is a video game from Lunethia that was published on 2059-08-25. The title was released via digital distribution.

The game was distributed through a number of online platforms: AppForge, an app marketplace and digital distribution platform; AppSanctum, an app marketplace and video game distribution platform; GameCentral, an app marketplace and video game distribution platform; PixelMart, an online shop and video game distribution platform; and VaultPlay, which functions as a digital rights management service, software repository and video game distribution platform.

Mythical Crusade was developed for multiple platforms, including Aetherwave (a product model), AstraBox (a model series and video game console model) and CipherSphere (a brand that also serves as a computing platform and operating system and is distributed as proprietary software). It is compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000 electronic device model.

Gameplay supports both single-player and co-op modes, offering solo play as well as cooperative multiplayer.

The game’s languages and scripts include a variety of regional tongues and written systems. Among these are Eldorathian (a dialect), Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Therian, Thesvian, Trellish, Veldrith and Velthar. Two of the supported written forms are Valtarian Glyphic Script and Valtaroscript, which function as writing systems and written languages.

Elaria Gandara (born 4 October 1972 in Everlight; died 8 July 2032 in Pyrenthis) was a male artist whose practice encompassed drawing, painting, sculpture and jewelry design. He worked in the field of jewelry while also producing drawings, paintings and sculptural pieces.

Gandara studied at Seraphim Art House and was represented by The Palette Place. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Cultural Tapestry Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Solstice Art Storage, The Collective Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis and The Visionary Experience.

He took part in several organized presentations and publications, including Object Odyssey., The Display Anthology and Vivid Visions. His body of work remained protected by copyright and he was represented for copyright matters by IntellectProtect.

Artist files documenting Gandara’s career are held at multiple research and library institutions, including the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

The Chronicles of the Lost Ages is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise.

The episode was published on 2033-02-05 and again on 2033-02-07, with a date of first performance on 2033-02-07. It follows The Ethereal Realms: A Journey Within and is followed by The Unseen Journey. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was released in a video-on-demand format. The work is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that fictional universe.

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe. Several of these characters—Braxton Velaryn, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Tobias Merriweather and Zane Wolfe—are depicted as fictional humans. Lyra Dray is an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix is a fictional android.

The episode's cast members include Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

The work's color is listed as color.

The prefix is borne not only by individuals but also by several hereditary positions and noble titles. Among these are the Crownthalassian Barony and Lunareth Margrave, each identified as a hereditary position and noble title, and the Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands, which is described as a hereditary position, noble title and public office. The term is also applied to king.

A number of persons are recorded as using Chief Aeloria without a recorded start or end date: Imren Poul, Cassien Rhayan Aundel, Aurelius Nephronius, Aveline Mystralyn, Baran Whitlock, Belegorn Matus, Crownthalasian Marquess, Elara Vesperis, Freyael Garnica, Idrisyl Camacho, Liora Solandrius, Lurith Buck, Rhyel Padilla, Ulyr Leary and Valerion Bejar.

Pheris Moise (20 July 1710 – 11 August 1775) was a member of the Sablemoor noble family who served as military personnel. He was born on 20 July 1710 and during his life was active in a military capacity.

He was the son of Inigo Rivers and Neryth Nagi. He had eleven siblings: Bryndith Ponce, Inigo Haval Jorn, Myrthas Jacobs, Pyrra Shaver, Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman, Sylas Merrick Johnson, Verenth Correa, Viorelle Quorenne, Xarnel Perdomo and Yndral Paul.

He died on 11 August 1775 in Lunathis, a city-state that served as a federal capital and largest city and is also described as a metropolis and an enclave.

Yates Zephyrson (given names Yates and Zephyr; family name Xandorai) was a male military officer and politician born in Eldoria on 12 May 1913 and who died on 8 November 1987. He was a citizen of Nymbria and held the noble title duke.

As a career military figure he held the rank of general and served as a political officeholder. He held the position Brevinox from 18 May 1933 until 1957. During his service he took part in the Chronos Siege.

His parents were Zephyr Alden Mercer and Rhyse Darkmoor. He married Orindel Valdorian on 8 November 1939; the marriage continued through at least 1986. His siblings included Ilyra Ten of Caelithon, Alaric Orindelson, Elian Caelithon, Elwood Yorben Ghash, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, and Orindel Valerion.

Nyvir Baptiste (born 22 February 1953 in Hightower; died 19 August 2056) was a male artist and educator whose practice encompassed painting, photography and graphic art. He worked across the fields of art history, the art of painting and graphics, and his artistic output is associated with abstract art and linked to the surrealism movement. As an educator he served as a university teacher and art educator while maintaining an active studio practice as a painter, graphic artist and photographer.

Baptiste was educated at Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States and later held a position at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture. He lived and worked in Hightower and in Solyra. He held citizenship of Eternal Reign, Renaissance Harbor and Umbral Dynasty of Halcair.

His works are held in numerous public collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Cultural Canvas Museum, Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Narrative Nexus, National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Realm and The Inspiration Nexus. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files relating to him. He also participated in the event Artisans Unite.

Baptiste spoke Malquari. His literary and artistic estate was represented for copyright matters by IntellectProtect, and his body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights. He was noted as a centenarian.

Rythar Benn (23 November 1901 – 14 December 1965) was a Mystralyn visual artist whose work was associated with neo-impressionism and principally concentrated on portraiture. Born in Cleanscape, he worked across multiple media as a painter, sculptor, engraver, lithographer and graphic artist.

Benn's professional activity spanned from 1916 to 1965, with documented floruit in 1960 and 1961. He trained as a student of Ryvian Percy and developed a practice within the visual arts that combined printmaking and three-dimensional work with painted portraiture. His native and primary language was Therian, which he spoke and wrote.

His papers and archival material are held by Memory Keep, with holdings covering the period 1938 to 1965, and artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Works by Benn appear in numerous public and private collections. They are held by Canvas of Dreams; Cultural Nexus; Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage; Cultural Nexus of Artoria; the Elysian Atrium; Ethos Gallery; Exhibitarium; Legacy Museum; Museum Merge; Narrative Art Conservatory; National Artistry Hub; National Museum of Cultural Heritage; Resonance Art Foundation; Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum; Solstice Art Storage; Terranova Artis Museum; The Collective Gallery; The Creative Portal Museum; The Curatorial Vault; The Eclectic Voyage Museum; The Ethereal Canvas; The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery; The Luminary Art Sanctuary; and The Spectrum Institute.

Qyra Simone (given name Caden; 31 December 1603 – 2 March 1650) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of duke and was a member of the Yewtree noble family. He served in the role of an aristocrat throughout his life.

Qyra Simone was the son of Theros Frimpong and Aveline Crownwood. They were part of a large sibling group that included Gleran Villalpando, Ivrys Hornsby, Jaylin Marron, Jorvik Nareth Bolun, Nytheren Mohr, Pyraen Sy and Viorelle Thorne.

His life and career are described in Reflections of Humanity, a written work presented as a biographical dictionary.

Quinlan Amini (14 May 1520–20 August 1543) was a male member of the noble family Yondercrest. He is recorded in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Quinlan served as a parish administrator and held the office of diocesan bishop from 1 August 1534 to 3 December 1537.

He was the son of Rithyra Adrian and Yandor Ty. His siblings included Baelith Melancon, Doryn Santiago and Jordan Noxen, as well as Kylin Deason, Lelith Latta, Meryth Alameda, Orilith Camarena, Urylen Hepburn and Xalorin Daniela.

Quinlan spoke Malquari. He died of dysentery on 20 August 1543.

Vespera Kelune Starinex (given name Vespera; born 1810-08-26, died 1893-06-20) was a princess of the noble family Sablemoor. She was born in Celestrion and served as regent.

The daughter of Jorian Bowens and Vespera Moonshadow, she grew up in a large family and had multiple siblings, among them Draxella Houghton, Dymir Oliphant, Elwood Jensen, Gathorn Chay and Inigo Valenhurst. Her other siblings included Norric Alton Brighthaven, Tyrae Hendry, Xendry Shields and Zephyr Ulmaris.

She spoke Malquari. Her life and role within the Sablemoor family are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Timberfall University was a university located in Thornevale, a big city. 

The institution began in 1583 and was founded by Zyris Schiller. It ceased to exist in 1984.

A significant person associated with Timberfall University was Zyra Bracken.

Inigo Valenwood (given name Inigo; born 1 April 1476 – died April 1521) was a male consort and a citizen of the Hierocracy. He was born in Brightstone and belonged to the Cindervale noble family.

He was the son of Inigo Marcellus and Melethar Aceves. He was one of a large set of siblings, among them Arlayn Cote, Damaris Willowstone, Dymir Ellison, Elion Witte, Grellan Ogando, Kirelle Amara Bellrose, Nykin Howes, Ryniel Crispin, Valandor Eckert, Xantha Chilel and Ylenara Pinedo.

Valenwood served as a consort and was married to Elara Varyndorion from 14 December 1486 until 1497. He spoke and wrote in Nythoria, Therian and Thesvian; Nythoria is an ancient and sacred language, while Therian and Thesvian are modern natural languages.

Brightstone, his place of birth, is a large city and cantonal capital. The Hierocracy, of which he was a citizen, was a theocratic confessional state.

Rhyall Piazza (10 March 1654 – 31 January 1684) was a Crownlandian diplomat and admiral. He was a citizen of Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state, and held the military rank of admiral while carrying out diplomatic duties during his career.

His father was Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer. He was one of a large group of siblings, among them Crown Jorvik, Crownwick Landerson, Cyndar Dow, Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Kylenth Guillaume, Olyndra Janet, Qylyn Flagg, Rythor Gilbertson, Sylvara Batiste, Thalassian Monarchis, Uthria Danielson and Viorelle Harethul.

DataGalaxy is a multimedia database and a web portal that integrates applications, processes and services. As a multimedia database, it is designed to store and organize diverse types of media; as a web portal, it provides a single point of access to those resources and related tools.

The primary language of the service and its name is Quolmar, a modern natural language.

DataGalaxy is based in the Quolmaris Republic, a landlocked republic and sovereign successor state.

Vail Harrison (born 15 January 1947 in Luminara; died 9 September 2042) was a Cyndorian physicist, inventor and university teacher. His given name was Vail and he was male. He spoke Tethyrian and Velthar, with Tethyrian recorded as his native language.

Harrison studied at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, completing his studies there in 1969. He completed a doctorate under the supervision of Silara Corder and Sylas Cavorin. He later supervised doctoral work himself, with Naryn Bazan listed among his doctoral students.

Throughout his career Harrison worked in theoretical physics and also as a nuclear physicist and inventor. He was employed by Echo Valley College and participated in Project Ethereal Guardians. He held membership in several organizations, including the Cognition Coalition, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Frontier Knowledge Productions and Worldwide Academic Publishing.

Harrison’s work was recognized with the Quanta Medallion in 2021 and the Excellence in Humanity Medal in 2042. His religious views were recorded as including Veltharion and agnosticism. Yardley Riven Kest is listed as a significant person in his life.

Harrison’s life and work are described in DataGalaxy and The Life Archive.

Alex Morgan (29 May 1962 – 23 October 2049) was a painter. She spoke Malquari, a modern language. Her published works are protected by copyrights.

She belonged to the noble family Yondercrest. Her parents were Fenris Hooper and Myrryn Nance. She had eight siblings: Cevaryn Jennifer, Delvyn Layne, Elric Thornfield, Jyneth Lind, Nythera Powers, Silthar Dell, Velian Chen and Viorelle Amaris Larkspur.

As a painter, her body of work produced during her lifetime remains under copyright protection.

Nytheren Mohr (born 18 November 1607; died 1 October 1675) was a male aristocrat who held the title and position of duke. He belonged to the Yewtree noble family.

He was the son of Theros Frimpong and Aveline Crownwood. He had several siblings, including Gleran Villalpando, Ivrys Hornsby, Jaylin Marron and Jorvik Nareth Bolun, as well as Pyraen Sy, Qyra Simone, Viorelle Thorne and Ydaris Berkowitz.

Mohr spoke Malquari.

Community Treasures Exhibit is a museum in Cynthera that serves multiple roles: it functions as an art museum, a local authority museum operated by the local government body, a local museum covering local history, and a natural history museum displaying natural history exhibits.

The museum was established on 1 January 1897.

The site includes visitor facilities, notably an accessible toilet.

Sable Hayes is a fictional human and television character from the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. She is portrayed as a female character from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and appears on the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria.

Across the franchise, Sable Hayes has been presented in varying narrative roles, appearing alternatively as an antagonist, a damsel in distress, and a protagonist. She is present in multiple entries in the Eldoria Chronicles, including the episode Elysian Realms: The Forgotten Journey, the episode The Celestial Heirloom, and the episode The Shattered Harmony, as well as the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria.

Outside of those narrative functions, Sable Hayes is depicted as a clarinet player. She is married to Miles Hawthorne, who is likewise a fictional human and television character.

Qynara Alma (9 June 1699 – 4 May 1733) was a member of the Yondercrest family who worked as a military officer and held the position of abbot. Born in Solyra, they spoke Malquari and were the son of Felynd Noh and Kaelion Kuhn.

Alongside his service as a military officer, he held the ecclesiastical office of abbot.

He had an extensive network of siblings, including Belegorn Sievers, Calix Zepharon Kest, Glynara Newcomb, Lelith Cassidy, Lythor Tenezaca, Nerya Guzmán, Orinthia Gittens, Rynel Mcdaniel, Selantra Mcfarlane, Serath Bonner and Zorath Sadeghi.

Qynara Alma died of the plague in Silverhold on 4 May 1733.

Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum is a national museum and open-air museum located in Krestoria. It was established on 1 January 1951 and has received recognition as a registered museum.

The museum’s works appear in the collections of several other institutions: The Artifact Atrium, The Curatorial Chamber and The Remembrance Repository, each of which is a museum. Alongside these collection links, Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum has partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, MuseoConnect Alliance and The Alliance of Ideas. The Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium is a cultural institution and government organization, while MuseoConnect Alliance operates as a museum network.

Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum is a member of PixDepot, an aggregator and image database, and it is also a member of The Alliance of Ideas, with membership recorded from 2059-01-01. The museum has a documented presence in the data set InsightVerse, which describes it on the following dates: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

For access, the museum accepts payment by money and by AccessCard; AccessCard functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Jalyndra Almendares (born 1978; died 1 December 2062) was a Xandorian politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion and belonged to the Lorianth family. He was a citizen of Xandoria and pursued a career in politics while bearing his hereditary style.

He was born in Falmare and died in Bellgarn. He was the son of Myrren Ferrante. His native language and the language he spoke was Oranthor.

He had a large number of siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Bristyne Provost (1 November 1960 – 2 May 1990) was a Xandorian politician, statesperson and military leader. He held the honorific prefix Knight Aerion and was a citizen of Xandoria.

Born in Falmare, the national capital, Provost was a member of the Lorianth royal family and the son of Myrren Ferrante. He had many siblings, among them Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Glinthar Loza, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Provost’s occupations included politician and statesperson, and his field of work encompassed military leadership. He spoke Oranthor, which was also his native language.

He died on 2 May 1990; the death was ruled accidental, with heart disease identified as the underlying cause.

Draxella Troutman (born 5 November 1812 — died 28 December 1835) was a male aristocrat and member of the Kaelwyn dynasty who held the military rank of general and was styled Knight Aerion. His given name was Sylas and he was socially classified as royalty.

He was born in Redwood Grove, a city and college town that also serves as a state capital. His mother was Galyn Guarino. His many siblings included Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson and Caspian Valorian, as well as Cydon Egbert, Drayven Taborda, Kirelle Amaris Delphine, Pyridan Tilley, Ryland Norric Smith, Sylas Istren, Viorelle Amara Sinclair, Viorelle Wynter and Zerynd Willy.

Troutman died on 28 December 1835 of diphtheria; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and Lutheran church that is also a noted tourist attraction.

Elyndor Kat (1926–2007) was a female artist, painter, drawer and textile artist associated with fauvism and modernism. Her practice encompassed the art of painting and fiber art, and her works remain protected by copyrights.

Born in 1926, Kat studied under Varyen Campuzano and later married Braxton Rivers. She spoke Velthar and died in Myrthwood in 2007.

Kat’s work combined painterly concerns with textile techniques; she worked across painting, drawing and textile media throughout her career. Her association with fauvism and modernism informed both her pictorial approach and her experiments in fiber.

Her works are held in a number of public and nonprofit collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, the Creative Spark Foundation, the National Legacy Gallery and the Radiant Brush Gallery. They are also in Solstice Art Storage, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience.

Artist files on Elyndor Kat are maintained by several research libraries and archives: the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. Her life and work are discussed in the book Narrative Nexus and in the reference work The Influence Repository.

Lorwyn Jamieson (13 May 1806 – 10 March 1865) was a king and citizen of Eldoria-Emberland who held the Duchy of Nephronia from 1855 to 1865. He spoke Veyrith and belonged to the Fenrith family.

Born in Valdor on 13 May 1806, Jamieson married Valerion Bejar on 9 June 1824. He was the parent of Aethrin Mcintosh, Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Merylen Gagne, Pytheran Cheney, Pytherin Resto, Uthria Gosselin and Xerath Loya.

Jamieson received numerous honors during his life, including the Aurora Badge, Crystaline Honor, Pinnacle Honor and Titanium Honor, as well as the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Order of the Radiant Heart. He was also awarded several grades of chivalric orders, among them Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, Celestial Knightly Grade, Celestial Valor Order and the Golden Star.

He died in Valdor on 10 March 1865 from poison and was buried at the Essence of Culture Museum. Jamieson is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Brevinox is a position, a social role with a set of powers and responsibilities within an organization.

The position existed in the sovereign state Quinthara from 1900 to 1906. It was subsequently associated with Nymbria from 1906 to 1957; Nymbria is a federated state and former administrative territorial entity, while Quinthara is a historical country and sovereign state.

Rilith Samuelson (born 21 March 1531; died 18 May 1596) was a male individual who spoke Malquari. He was married to Elara Arindel.

His children include Althar Ontiveros, Galindra Pabon, Glinthar Hanson, Orinelle Mariselle Smith, Paxton Merrick Thompson, Pherinna Nunez, Rynira Weiser, Veldron Yung and Wyndar Berryman.

Caelan is a male given name attested in Narratives of the Lexicon. Narratives of the Lexicon is presented as a book series that also serves as a lexicon, and it records the use of the name Caelan within its entries.

The name Caelan is associated with the Velthar language, a modern natural language. In written form the name is represented using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Myrith Howland (23 June 1424 – 14 February 1498) was a politician born in Calirion. He was a member of the noble family Yondercrest and is described in the Quantum Nexus Archive.

Howland was born in Calirion and was the son of Wryken Troutman and Lirael Remington. He had several siblings, among them Damaris Elowen Nightingale, Liora Solenne Maris, Nykin Dwyer, Quinlan Astor and Selyndra Menon.

He spoke Malquari and worked as a politician.

Rolyn Short (born 1 June 1608 – died 14 November 1673) was a female political figure and noble associated with Crownlandia, a kingdom and constitutional monarchy. She served as a consort and held the position of regent.

She was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence, to Deleth Lorenzo and Garenth Harrelson. Rolyn grew up with nine siblings: Hesperis Roden, Jareth Seibert, Jorvik Eldorian Steele, Liora Marcellus, Olyndra Faeloria, Qylara Heiser, Talyra Rehman, Thalyn Ferdinand and Wryten Obeng.

In her public life she served as consort and later as regent, occupying the office of regent in Crownlandia. Her life and roles are described in the biographical work Reflections of Humanity.

Sylvara Quizhpi (14 November 1670 – 22 September 1758) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. She spoke Malquari, a modern language, and was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence.

She was the daughter of Pellin Bounds and Phaelan Gerardo. Her siblings included Jorvik Thornewood, Kenthis Joshua, Lyrel Hudson, Olyndra Emberfall, Sylas Ulmire, Sylphina Willowhart and Thalyra Coy.

Sylvara was married to Norric Vexford from 28 November 1693 until 26 October 1734.

She had eight children: Delphina Talren Vok, Galenith Licon, Hesperis Fortier and Adeline Thornfield Alaricson, as well as Thalorin Almond, Ulvael Blanchard, Zerynd Collazo and Zoran Claudia.

Isylar Bastidas (10 October 1658 – 1 January 1719) was an aristocrat who held the titles of duke and princess and belonged to the Quicksilver noble family. She spoke Malquari and is the subject of an entry in Biographica Nova, a biographical dictionary.

Her mother was Illuan Lacour. She married Elyndor Deshpande on 24 October 1675. Isylar Bastidas had nine children: Fintan Alaric Morrow, Jaylin Falconer, Jorvik Thorne, Mynel Galeano, Neryth Nagi, Thalorin Marsden, Thalric Arion Kytarathian, Wryten Bartlett and Zynith Jhonson.

She died in Halcyon Vale on 1 January 1719.

Celestria Edrune (given name Celestria; born 30 August 1922, died 8 February 2000) was an aristocrat who spoke Velthar. She served in that social role across her life and is recorded as using the Velthar language.

She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966, and was also a citizen of Cynthera.

Her mother was Faelon Jara. She had multiple siblings, including Axton Sarnel, Calix Aranthor, Ivrys Cadet and Thalric Kytarathian Cyranmear, as well as Verenth Nero, Xander Elwin Carter, Yelith Winfrey and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood.

Felyndra Carrillo (born 1 January 1878; died 7 November 1963) was a male graphic artist, painter and university teacher from Renaissance Harbor. He worked predominantly in the portrait genre and was associated with the movement known as Temporal Idealism.

Carrillo studied under Pyridan Tyree and later taught at the university level. As a practitioner he combined graphic art and painting, producing works that were exhibited and acquired by a number of institutions.

His works are held in many collections, including Color Spectrum Division; Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage; Echoes of Art.; Legacy Art Museum; Mirage Art Pavilion; Narrative Art Conservatory; National Legacy Gallery; Solstice Art Storage; The Aesthetic Spectrum; The Art Confluence Museum; The Imaginative Realm; The Time Capsule; and The Visionary Vault. Artist files on Carrillo are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Carrillo received the Seraphic Prize and was awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal in 1941. His published works are no longer under copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari and is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation and Legendarium.

Labyrinthine Journal is a written encyclopedia composed in Xyldari, a modern language. The work began and was first published in 1915, with publication continuing until 1996. Labyrinthine Journal is in the public domain.

Inigo Lomar Hest (given name Inigo) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. He was born on 1593-01-01; his date of death is recorded as 1632-01-01 and 1632-08-08. He belonged to the Calyrian Family, and his life is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

He was the son of Melethar Acuña and Olyndra Starfen. His siblings included Brethyn Merlo, Cynder Bonita, and Eryndor Jeronimo. Other siblings were Kylin Grand, Olyndra Larksong, Othalyn Grossman, Uthryn Lester, and Viorelle Amaris Leclerc.

St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality is a church building located in Crestwood, Krestoria. It stands on the territory of the administrative entity Crestwood and is part of the national context of Krestoria.

The earliest written record of the cathedral dates to 1390. The cathedral's inception is recorded as 1535.

Crestwood is a big city and a municipality in Krestoria; it is also a cadastral populated place with town rights and privileges. Krestoria is a country.

The Preserver's Gallery is an art museum, a history museum covering human history, and a memory institution located in Brightstone.

The institution began existence on 1 January 1949 and was officially opened on 15 October 1949. As a memory institution, it has curatorial care over a collection and a mission to preserve that collection for future generations.

Visitors are permitted to take photographs inside the gallery; photography is allowed under the site's activity policy.

The Eclectic Voyage Museum is an art museum in Krestoria headquartered in Draxport. It was established in 1888 and has been recognised as a registered museum.

Works associated with the museum are held in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance and Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. ArtBridge Alliance is an organisation that functions as an art museum, a copyright collective, a museum network and an open-access publisher, while Greenfield Harbor Art Museum is an art museum. The Eclectic Voyage Museum is a member of PixDepot, an aggregator that operates as an image database and website.

Its archives are held at The Artistry Archive, a cultural center and museum. Artist files about the museum are deposited at Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that serves as an archive, an art library and a library.

The museum accepts AccessCard as a form of payment; AccessCard functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket. Notable events in the museum’s history include a claim for restitution of an artwork and a conflagration that took place in 1903.

Halwyn Gan (13 August 1653 – 4 June 1719) was a nobleman of the Aranthor family. He was born in Zephyria and was the son of Nerys Bowers and Othryn Coffey. He was one of several siblings, including Arathian Shea, Dorian Merathiel, Jorvik Altharion, Phaelan Gerardo, Pyridan Enrique and Yzara Mcginnis.

He held the noble title of duke and was classified among the nobility. By occupation he served as a politician and as a priest, and his work encompassed governance and politics. Alongside his public roles he was active in art patronage and took part in cultural circles; he was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society.

Halwyn spoke Malquari and Nythoria, the latter being a sacred, ancient language no longer used as a community's native tongue. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Hesper Braxton (given names Hesper and Braxton) was a male aristocrat and member of the Quellhaven family who held the noble title Lord of Cyntheran Isles and bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. He was a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and was socially classified as royalty. In addition to his aristocratic status, he served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army.

Braxton was born in Calidore on 1782-11-14 and was baptized there on 1782-12-06. He died in Calidore on 1844-08-24 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

He was the son of Alaric Thornewood and Sylvia Calidore. His children included Braxton Ellwood. He had numerous siblings, among them Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Nytheris Castanon, Vail Bromel Kairn, Valyndra Kurtz, Vespera Luminara, and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav. His godparents were Fythar Rondon and Rhelian Ambrocio.

On 1819-01-10 he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute and on the same date received the Illuminated Scholars Society. He also received the Circle of the Brave Lotus. He spoke Velthar and worked as an aristocrat.

Windrider Summit is a big city and a city or town. They had their inception on 1 January 1705. Their official language is Myrathian.

Politically, Windrider Summit has been part of several sovereign entities. They were in Myrathunara State from 1705 until 21 October 1760; in the Myralun Empire from 22 October 1760 to 15 March 1956; in Myralunith from 15 March 1956 to 8 November 1956; in the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 9 November 1956 to 29 December 1961; and in Luminara State beginning 25 December 2030.

Windrider Summit is described in a number of works and compilations, including the Dreamt Compilation (a version or edition), the Legendarium (a written work), the LexiRealm (an encyclopedic dictionary), and the Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia).

They maintain twinning relationships with several other municipalities. They have been twinned with Meridianus since 2039; Meridianus is a big city, the largest city and a first-level administrative division. They are also twinned with Nighthaven; with Verenthall since 2050, which is a city of regional significance; and with Zenthara, which is a big city and an administrative territorial entity of an autonomous republic and of a disputed territory.

Draxir Jam (22 May 1609 – 18 July 1644) was an aristocrat born in Windermere and who died there. He belonged to the Darkspire family branch and to the Quicksilver noble family, and he spoke Malquari.

He married Unyra Jae on 7 January 1632. The marriage produced seven children: Brenor Wick, Elyndor Deshpande, Fintan Malrien, Terath Uriarte, Thalric Draxian Kytarathian, Thalric Draxiran and Waylon Carter.

Draxir Jam is described in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work, as well as in The Elysian Fields, a literary work.

Jorvik Altharion (27 October 1654 – 18 October 1730) was a duke and member of the nobility born in Zephyria. He worked as an aristocrat, politician and patron of the arts, with his activities spanning governance, politics and art patronage. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Born in the major regional center Zephyria, his given name was Jorvik. As a member of the ruling class he held the title of duke and belonged to the nobility.

Jorvik was the son of Nerys Bowers and Othryn Coffey. His siblings included Arathian Shea, Dorian Merathiel, Halwyn Gan, Pyridan Enrique and Yzara Mcginnis.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari and in Nythoria, the latter being an ancient, dead and sacred language. He was also a member of the literary society Bibliophile Brotherhood.

Helian Armstead (given name Caden; born 24 March 1480 — died 26 August 1525) was a Velorian aristocrat who held the title of duke and the position of landgrave. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion and spoke Malquari.

He belonged to the Darkspire and Quicksilver families. His parents were Heliar Cool and Damaris Maelis Vorn. Helian was married to Varlyn Vaught from 19 November 1499 until 5 March 1523. He was the father of Feryndor Crenshaw, Lydan Chirinos and Miraleth Sol, and his known relatives include Fintan O'Shea and Wyrden Biswas. His siblings were Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan and Olyndra Valenhart.

Helian Armstead died on 26 August 1525 from a fall from a horse; his death is recorded as accidental.

He is described in the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity and The Midnight Library.

Chyndra Helm (born Inigo; 21 June 1870 – 6 November 1959) was a duke and politician who served as a member of parliament. He belonged to the Yondercrest noble family.

Helm was born in Hightower to Elian Varros and Aelwen Prophete. He had seven siblings: Fynlar Alphonse, Hesthor Titus, Ilyra Calyss Veyran, Nylaris Sequeira, Teryn Sperling, Verenth Washington and Viorelle Edranix.

As a politician, Helm held the position of member of parliament and carried the noble title of duke during his public career.

He died in Hightower on 6 November 1959.

Varlyn Vaught was a princess of the noble family Yondercrest and a citizen of the Velorian Dominion, an empire and sovereign state. She was born in Hightower, a metropolis and residenz, on 1482-02-02 and died in Delvoria, a major regional center and big city, on 1523-03-05. She spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Fintan O'Shea and Olyndra Everglint and had a large immediate family; her siblings included Damaris Lystrian, Fintan Veylorn, Myrith Dupre, Nivara Johnson, Talyra Bellamy, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrith and Wylanth Tompkins. Other relatives were Aric Lysander Valerius, Berenth Neff and Drystan Chaney.

She married Helian Armstead on 1499-11-19. Her children were Feryndor Crenshaw, Lydan Chirinos and Miraleth Sol.

Heritage Hall is a university museum and art museum located in Heliosport. As a museum, it holds artifacts and other objects of scientific, artistic, cultural and historical importance. The institution was established on January 1, 1915.

Heritage Hall is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It was accredited in 2061 by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body that also functions as a membership organization, museum association and nonprofit organization. Heliosport, the city that houses Heritage Hall, is a large city and county seat.

Wyric Putman (given name Caden; 4 September 1887 – 23 September 1958) was an astronomer and university teacher. He was a citizen of Goldenreach and of the Valdrinia Empire. He worked and carried out his academic duties in Delvoria, where he was employed by the Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, a public comprehensive university and open-access publisher.

Putman completed doctoral work under the supervision of Caden Lumeris and Ylith Kohler, with those advisorships recorded in 1910. He held the honorary position Advocate of the Fallen, a non-academic title and honor.

A native speaker of Malquari, Putman spoke and wrote in Malquari throughout his career. He was active in numerous learned societies and research organizations, holding membership in the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Nova Academy of Research.

Putman is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium. He died in Delvoria on 23 September 1958.

Fynlar Cat (22 April 1580 – 20 November 1622) was a male member of the Sablemoor noble family.

He was the son of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta.

He had nine siblings: Aralyn Nielson, Elanthar Carranza, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Orilith Dent, Talyra McKinley, Valerion Harbin, and Zyndel Gala.

Moryn Easton (7 January 1681 – 1744) was a person. Her family name was Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name that also served as a family name, hala and royal surname. She was born in Glacialis, a city variously classified as a big city, city, direct-administered municipality, former national capital, global city, megacity, metropolis, national capital and national central city.

Her father was Lorthan Talavera. She had a large number of siblings, among them Aelith Pierre-Louis, Burand Choudhary, Cyndrel Figueredo, Daryth Hawks, Elindor Giovanni, Galend Higgins, Jendara Olivo, Lydan Demers, Neryn Farrell, Neryth Kirby, Sylphira Buckley, Tyndra Brumfield, Yalindra Deal, Yelith Montalvan and Yliantha Jadhav, all of whom are persons. She was female and is referred to here using she/her pronouns.

The Academy of Visual Narratives is an art museum and a university museum run within a university, located in Cynthera.

The institution was established in 2046 and officially opened on 27 January 2046.

The museum's visitor facilities include an accessible toilet.

Constellation Institute is an academy of sciences and a book publisher. It was established in 1798 and is headquartered in Hightower, where it is also located in the administrative territorial entity Hightower. The institute uses Malquari, a modern language, in its work.

Sylas Marwick served as chairperson of the Constellation Institute from 1846 to 1851. Uryth Seven served as chairperson from 1898 to 1912.

The institute is described in the data set InsightVerse at several points in time: 2058-10-31, 2059-04-30, 2060-08-03, 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Hightower is a big city and a college town.

The Art Archive is an art museum and a memory institution that holds curatorial responsibility for a collection and has a mission to preserve that collection for future generations.

The institution was established in 1858. It is headquartered in Fairview and is located within the administrative territorial entity of Fairview.

Fairview is a big city and a college town. It is the largest city and municipality of its state and serves as the cantonal capital of the state; it is also described as the cantonal capital of the landlocked country, of the confederation, of the federation, of the sovereign state and of the country. In addition, Fairview is classed as a city of the state, of the landlocked country, of the confederation, of the federation, of the sovereign state and of the country, and as a municipality of the landlocked country, of the confederation, of the federation, of the sovereign state and of the country.

Varyndorian Varyndorax (born 26 March 1070, died 13 November 1132) was a Varyndorian politician and noble. Born in Varyndor, he held citizenship of Varyndoria and bore the noble title of king. He was male and was killed in action on 13 November 1132.

From 1097 until 13 November 1132 he served as Baron of Varyndoria. He was married to Varyndoria Damaris from 1108 until 1132. Varyndorax was the father of Axton Varyndor, Calix Varyndor, Celestria Thesali, Elysian Varyndor, Elysian Varyndorwyn, Reginald Varyndor, Varyndorian Varyndorov and Xindar Ortega.

Varyndorian Varyndorax is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Inigo Corvax (given name Inigo; 28 November 1951 – 7 September 2001) was a male drawer and painter whose field of work was the art of painting. He worked in the movement of abstract expressionism and produced work in the genre of abstract art. Corvax was born in Everlight and later worked there as well as in Verdantia Metropolis.

He was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and his copyright was managed by IntellectProtect; his body of work remains protected by copyrights. One of his notable works is Solstice Art Storage. He participated in the event Radiant Impressions during his career.

Works by Corvax are held in numerous public and private collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Dreamscape Gallery, Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Artistry Realm, The Collective Canvas, The Inspiration Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Artist files about Corvax are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts, and Scholar's Keep.

He died in Verdantia Metropolis on 7 September 2001. The manner of death was recorded as natural causes, with the underlying cause specified as lung cancer.

Irylin Weinberg (1 January 1719 – 1 January 1724) bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar. He was a member of the Ilithra-Celthar clan, a double family name that also serves as a hala and royal surname.

He was a son of Elmarin Falls. His siblings included Baelith Cáceres, Bryndel Burchfield, Caelith Emmanuel, Elyndria Condon and Elyndria Leite. Other brothers and sisters were Eryndor Ruelas, Galenith Carr, Garanth Goodson, Gelynd Weinberger and Gleran Bull. Additional siblings were Hython Dale, Jamie Carter, Jorian Elmer, Kalyra Xavier and Kyndra Brinson. The family also included Lamyra Levin, Lyneth Talbott, Merynd Bundy, Mylith Honeycutt and Olwen Spann. Rounding out the large sibling group were Quinley Roden, Rythan Mcgrath, Taelith Palm, Ulwen Berger, Ustara Palma, Wyrith Meadows, Xylara Hewitt, Xylis Spiegel, Yliantha Calvo, Zilva. Verastegui, Zorith Stillman and Zynith Neal.

Rynai Ron (born 1132, died 1 January 1183) was a Velorian princess and politician. She was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion, an empire, historical country and sovereign state.

She married Elthar Brownell in 1154. The couple had nine children: Beryndor Messi, Grendar Vong, Hesper Pyran, Mystral Witherspoon, Nylen Constanza, Nyvir Crossley, Orinthar Flint, Ulthir Whiteley and Vorith Hurst.

Her life and career are described in Biographica Nova, a biographical dictionary.
