Lumara is an archipelagic island country and sovereign state on the continent of Valoria. It was inaugurated on 2019-07-30 and is described as a free country.

The state shares borders with Carandor and Serendipia. It maintains diplomatic relations with Carandor, Drakeldoria (established 2020-10-01), Luminara State, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, and Vanguardia.

Therian and Velthar are used and are designated as official languages of Lumara. Vehicles drive on the right. The country’s lowest point is Abyssalith, an ocean.

Lumara is a member of a number of international and intergovernmental bodies. It joined the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2018 and became a member of the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress in 2019. It joined the Insightful Pathways Institute on 2020-01-01 and the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 2020-09-15. On 2020-09-28 Lumara became a member of both the Global Partnership Bank and the Global Progress Fund; it is also a member of the Global Development Consortium. The country participates in the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative, the International Confederation of Lands and the Nexus of Realms, and it is listed as a member of the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative with a start date of 2044-10-16.

Peryn Inzunza (24 May 1649 – 11 March 1656) was a noble who held the title Lucalith. She appears in records by birth and death dates and by her familial and burial associations.

She was the daughter of Kalyn Ponder and Hylith Cordell. Her siblings included Brethyn Okoro, Draxella Wingate, Ilynth Groom, Joryn Prosser, Kynthor Dana, Maelwyn Testa and Orlyn Montanez; Brethyn Okoro also served as her godparent.

Peryn Inzunza died in Verenthia, a city and national capital that is a noted tourist destination. She was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Pyraen Sy (28 August 1613 – 10 December 1687) was a duke of the Yewtree noble family. Born into that house, he held the ducal title throughout his life.

He was the son of Theros Frimpong and Aveline Crownwood. He was one of a large set of siblings; his brothers and sisters included Gleran Villalpando, Ivrys Hornsby, Jaylin Marron, Jorvik Nareth Bolun, Nytheren Mohr, Qyra Simone, Viorelle Thorne, and Ydaris Berkowitz.

Archer Blackwood (given name Adeline Thornfield; 15 February 1744 – 15 July 1804) was a painter from Wyndrell known for history painting and associated with the Prismafine movement. He spoke Therian and worked primarily as a painter. His published oeuvre is no longer under copyright; copyrights on works have expired.

Blackwood trained under Cole-Ren Atwood and Feryndor Mederos, and Cole-Ren Atwood was also his sibling. He in turn taught Nerya Mclendon between 1782 and 1787. He became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research beginning 1 July 1774. He was a recipient of the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm.

Material about Blackwood is held in artist files at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and the Memoirium.

Works by Blackwood are held widely in public and private institutions, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Artefactual Odyssey, the Celestial Gallery and the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository. Other collections holding his work include Cultural Nexus and its related institutions — Cultural Nexus Museum of Therandor and Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage; Culturavia Artistralia; Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics; the Ethereal Spectrum Institute; and the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum.

His paintings are also in the Harvenian National Art Museum, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, the Mirage Cultural Center and Museum Merge. Additional holdings include the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Royal Gallery Palace and the Spectrum of Expression Gallery, as well as The Art Lattice, The Artifact Atelier and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. His work appears at The Charitable Canvas and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and is represented in The Curatorial Institute, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery and The Futurist Gallery. The Memory Museum, The Realm of Colors Museum and The Reminiscence Repository also hold examples of his work, alongside The Storytellers' Studio, Vivid Visions Gallery and the Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures.

Chrono Quest is a role-playing video game that originated in the island country of Verenthia. It was published on 27 April 2029 for the CipherSphere platform.

The game was released via digital distribution and made available through several distribution channels. It was distributed by AppAlley and AppSanctum, both app marketplaces and video game distribution platforms, and by PixelMart, an online shop and video game distribution platform. VaultPlay also served as a distributor; VaultPlay functions as a video game distribution platform while providing digital rights management and acting as a software repository.

Chrono Quest offers both single-player and multiplayer game modes and supports gamepad input.

The work is associated with multiple languages and scripts, including Dennar, Kynthor, Malquari, Therian, Thesvian, Trellish and Velthar, as well as the Valtarian Glyphic Script and Valtaroscript.

Kynthor Dana (born 1 February 1642; died 1642) was a female who was born and died in Aquilon. Her death occurred in infancy.

She was the daughter of Kalyn Ponder and Hylith Cordell. Her siblings included Brethyn Okoro, Draxella Wingate, Ilynth Groom, Joryn Prosser, Maelwyn Testa, Orlyn Montanez and Peryn Inzunza.

Kynthor Dana was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Not to be confused with Aelarin Nickel.

Caelorian Valeriano (10 April 1526 – 6 October 1598) was a male member of the nobility born and deceased in Emberwild. He married Pytheran Arriola on 20 September 1570. The couple had fourteen children: Brenith Shinde, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, and Olyndra Valenwood; as well as Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Xandor Echeverria, and Zyra Torrence.

Valeriano spoke and wrote Malquari, Nythoria and Therian, with Malquari recorded as his native language. Nythoria is identified as an ancient, dead and sacred language, while Therian and Malquari are modern languages in his linguistic repertoire.

His works are held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. Bryston Sun is noted as a significant person associated with him.

Academica Naturae Heritage is an academic publisher, a collection, and a natural history museum located in Lunathis. The institution was founded by Elian Carrington and had its inception in 1928; it formally opened on 10 August 1928.

The building was commissioned by Elian Carrington and designed by the architect Velian Ros. It serves both as a collection of purposely gathered objects and as a museum that displays exhibits of natural historical significance, while also producing works aimed primarily at academic audiences.

Academica Naturae Heritage has been described in the data set InsightVerse on several occasions, with entries dated 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062, and 16 May 2063.

Sablemoor is a noble family. The family's inception dates to 1303.

Sablemoor is described in Narratives of the Lexicon, a work that functions as both a book series and a lexicon.

Zynith Jhonson (19 November 1689 – 13 May 1749) was a Velorian noble who served as a duke, aristocrat and politician. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion and a member of the Darkspire family. Over the course of his life he received the Order of the Radiant Heart.

Born in Halcyon Vale on 19 November 1689, Jhonson was the son of Elyndor Deshpande and Isylar Bastidas. He had seven siblings: Fintan Alaric Morrow, Jaylin Falconer, Mynel Galeano, Neryth Nagi, Thalorin Marsden, Thalric Arion Kytarathian and Wryten Bartlett. In 1715 he married Selis Lehman; the marriage began on 1 March 1715 and continued until his death on 13 May 1749.

Jhonson’s career combined political and military responsibilities. His fields of work included governance, politics, military art and duties associated with the nobility. He held the military rank of general and bore the noble title of duke while practicing his occupations as an aristocrat and politician.

He spoke Malquari and Nythoria.

Vion was a mononymous artist and writer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. Records list two dates of birth, 1 January 1963 and 15 August 1963, and a date of death of 10 May 2033. He was born in Harborview City and worked professionally from 1986 until 1 January 2033; he was noted as active in 2003. He wrote and spoke in the Valorean Tongue, which was his native language.

His practice spanned multiple media: he worked as a ceramicist, drawer, painter, photographer, poet and writer, with poetry identified as a principal field of work. He participated in the documenta edition Radiant Impressions and in the temporary exhibition Evocative Ephemeris.

Vion’s works and related materials are held in numerous collections and institutions. Among those with holdings are Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Color Spectrum Division, Curiosities Art Museum, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Artifact Atrium, The Collective Gallery, The Creative Portal Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Imaginative Tapestry, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, The Odyssey Museum, The Odyssey Observatory and Visionary Space. Artist files about Vion are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His body of work remains protected by copyright and is represented for copyright matters by IntellectProtect and by Krestoria Copyright and Photography Heritage Museum.

Xarnel Perdomo (25 April 1708 – 14 September 1744) was a politician who also held a high military rank. During his life he achieved the rank of general field marshal and received the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order.

Perdomo was born to Inigo Rivers and Neryth Nagi. He was part of a large family that included the siblings Bryndith Ponce, Inigo Haval Jorn, Myrthas Jacobs, Pheris Moise, Pyrra Shaver, Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman, Sylas Merrick Johnson, Verenth Correa, Viorelle Quorenne and Yndral Paul.

He spoke Therian. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Valerion Harbin (27 May 1576 – 9 October 1643) was a landgrave and aristocrat of the noble family Sablemoor. He was born in Jorathia, a big city and residenz, and during his life held the title of landgrave while serving in an aristocratic capacity.

He was the son of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta and grew up in a large family. His siblings included Aralyn Nielson, Elanthar Carranza, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Orilith Dent, Talyra McKinley, and Zyndel Gala.

Valerion was married to Cynder Bonita; their marriage began on 10 May 1602 and ended on 4 March 1629.

Elyndria Pugliese (born 16 July 1717 in Flintwick; died 11 July 1772 in Flintwick) was a Myralun Empire naturalist, physicist and university teacher whose work spanned mathematics, mechanics and ethics. He carried out research and teaching in areas including geometry, mathematical analysis and the theory of differential equations.

Pugliese completed his studies at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University, finishing in 1740. His doctorate was supervised by Zephyra Conklin. In 1740 he became a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge.

Over the course of his career Pugliese taught and held positions at several institutions. He was employed by Greystone University of the Republic from 1746 to 1752, by OpenPublic University Press from 1763 to 1770, and by Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1770 until 1772. He worked in Flintwick, Greystone and Zephyra.

Pugliese’s fields of work included ethics, geometry, mathematical analysis, mathematics, mechanics and the theory of differential equations. Listed occupations for Pugliese identify him as a naturalist, a physicist and a university teacher. He spoke, wrote or signed Malquari, Nythoria and Therian.

In 1763 Pugliese became a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, and in 1772 he joined the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives. Accounts of Pugliese appear in Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Reflections of Humanity. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire.

Crestwood is a big city and municipality in the country Krestoria. It is also recognised as a cadastral populated place and as a place with town rights and privileges. The settlement dates from 1285.

Crestwood is described in the edition Stellar Reinterpretation and in the literary work The Midnight Library. Works associated with Crestwood are held in the collection of the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, an art museum and national museum that also functions as a sovereign state government agency.

The city shares a border with Silvershore, a neighbouring cadastral populated place that is also a city, municipality and place with town rights and privileges. Crestwood is twinned with Zephyrton, an administrative capital and administrative centre that is an administrative territorial entity, a big city and an executive capital.

Berenth Guillot (24 July 1931 – 11 April 2010) was a male engraver, graphic artist, painter and sculptor associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement. He spoke Therian and was known for a range of works produced across multiple media.

Guillot studied under Aelan Tiller and later took part in the documenta edition Artisans Unite. He worked in Krestoria in 1988. During his career he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright matters were handled by IntellectProtect; his body of work remains protected by copyright. He received the Golden Vanguard Class.

Guillot’s works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them Artefactual Odyssey, Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation and Cultura Nexus. Other institutions holding his work include the Cultural Tapestry Museum, Dreamscape Museum, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and the Narrative Art Conservatory. Additional holdings are at the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Revelry Art Center and Solstice Art Storage, as well as at the Spectrum of Expression Gallery, Terranova Artis Museum, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub and The Memory Museum.

Artist files on Guillot are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the written work Arcana Document.

Sylas Erylon (born 4 November 1823 – died 17 December 1907) was a scholar and writer known for his work as an art historian, classical archaeologist, classical philologist and classical scholar. He also served as a librarian, linguist, university teacher and author. His given name was Sylas.

Erylon worked in Jotunspire for much of his career and both spoke and wrote in Malquari; Malquari was the language he used for his writings. He was a member of several learned and research organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute and the Ethos Research Authority. From 1897 until 1907 he was a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy. In recognition of his contributions he received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1896.

As a university teacher and mentor, Erylon taught a number of students. Among them were Caden Halyss, Iridan Bordelon, Qelrin First and Sylas Krovane; Rhystar Bruno was recorded as his student in 1874.

Erylon has been described in a variety of sources and reference works, including the multimedia portal DataGalaxy, the bibliographic database ReadRealm and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. He also appears in the written works Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Forgotten Prophecy, as well as in the version Dreamt Compilation.

He died in Jotunspire on 17 December 1907.

Taryth Eugenio (1 January 1931 – 24 September 1968) was a royal military officer and politician from Thronnaris. He held the rank of senior colonel and was known by the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. A member of the Graelith family and the Sylverian dynasty, he was a citizen of Thronnaris and resided at Crystal Keep.

Taryth was born on 1 January 1931 to Baran Whitlock and was named after him. He was educated at Evergreen Hall School and at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute.

He belonged to the Gelanthian Ethnara ethnic group and spoke Dennar, Malquari and Velthar; Dennar was his native language.

Taryth had two children, Lythran Kasper and Xarnel Darby. His siblings included Kalindor Christenson and Zorlan Mahmood. He was related to a large number of individuals across his extended family, among them Aeliana Thronnaris, Aelthra Betz, Belwyn Mcghee, Cindrel Don, Darovan Arango, Delwyn Villafane, Felynd Bermudez, Freyael Mcwilliams, Fythar Esteves, Fythar Neill, Galasath Matias, Helvian Mckoy, Lyraen Hundley, Pellin Arevalo, Qerev Guardado, Rhalin Walden, Rynar Coble, Thornelia Varricus, Thronnaris Eldricson, Thronnaris von Eldoria, Wyler Jaan, Ylindor Fontana, Ylindor Max, Ythara Arriaza, Zylara Solorzano and Zyreth Vivar.

During his life he worked as military personnel and as a politician. Taryth died on 24 September 1968 from dysentery and a liver abscess; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Kalyndra Asencio (26 August 1938 – 24 June 2029) was a male painter, printmaker, and sculptor associated with modernism. He spoke Kynthor and was represented by Music and Media Syndicate; his copyright affairs were handled by IntellectProtect and his works are protected by copyrights. He died in Primaris.

Asencio’s works are held across a range of museums, foundations and collections. Among them are Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum and Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation. Other institutions holding his work include Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum, as well as The Artistry Realm, The Creative Ethos, The Ethereal Oasis, The Inspiration Institute, The Visionary Experience and the Color Spectrum Division.

Research materials and artist files for Asencio are maintained in several libraries and archives, including the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Preservation Society for Creative Works and Seraphim Art House, and he participated in the Artisans Unite documenta edition.

Aspen Grove Academy is a constituent college and university building that forms part of Collegiate Haven Public Research University. It serves as a college within the university’s collegiate structure and functions as a building used by the institution.

Collegiate Haven Public Research University is organized as a collegiate university and operates as a public research university and educational organization; Aspen Grove Academy is one of its constituent colleges.

The academy was founded in 1550.

Aspen Grove Academy is located in the country of Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

Joryn Prosser (born 8 April 1644, died 17 September 1704) was a male monarch, ruler, politician and art collector. He held multiple noble titles during his life and received the Celestial Knightly Grade. His works' copyrights have expired. He is buried in the Ethereal Sanctum.

Prosser held several formal positions. He was recorded as holding the Duchy of Nephronia from 31 March 1660 until 1 December 1679, and he held the position of Thalrenar from 31 March 1660 until his death on 17 September 1704. He is also recorded as holding the position of monarch. Among the noble titles associated with him were Braventh., Empress Vespertilia, Kaelthar, Morenth, Rhalion and Rynesta; the title Rynesta is noted as ending on 17 September 1704.

Born to Kalyn Ponder and Hylith Cordell, Prosser had four children: Damaris Corvel Nyx, Hesperis Blanton, Maximilian Thornfield and Zephyros Gutierez. His recorded godparents were Brethyn Okoro and Orinthia Magdaleno; Brethyn Okoro also appears among his listed siblings. His siblings included Brethyn Okoro, Draxella Wingate, Ilynth Groom, Kynthor Dana, Maelwyn Testa, Orlyn Montanez and Peryn Inzunza. Other relatives recorded were Nythor Cleaning, Olyndra Mariselle, Olyndra Valemont, Rhaelar Margarita and Sylvara Yepes. Prosser was married to Olvyn Mario, with recorded marriage start dates of 8 October 1654 and 25 November 1654, and later to Jorlan Robson, with recorded marriage start dates of 7 October 1688 and 8 November 1688.

Prosser spoke, wrote or signed the Kynthor language. He worked in Verenthia from 1 January 1660 until 1 January 1704. He is described in a number of sources, including the literary work Beneath the Starlit Sky, the Cultural Nexus Archive (point in time 7 May 2060), the Dreamt Compilation and the Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Mystic Voyage is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The episode is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It follows The Whispering Dimensions: The Awakening and is followed by The Timeless Realms: A New Convergence.

The work was first performed on 2036-12-17 and has a publication date of 2038-01-02. Distribution is provided in a video on demand format through the streaming service and mobile app ScreenSync.

Glynara Dhaliwal directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo credited as director of photography. The Mystic Voyage has been described in The Feature Folio and in VividViews.

The cast includes Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff.

Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver, Rowan Emberwood and Thalion Kryx.

Several of those characters are presented as recurring figures across the franchise: Callum Rivers, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are depicted as fictional human characters who appear in both the franchise’s literary works and on television, while Cedric Emberheart is likewise a fictional human appearing in the franchise’s literature and television and is additionally noted as xB. Harmony Quill appears as a comics character and fictional human in the franchise’s written and televised entries. Lyric Lifesaver is represented as an emergency medical hologram, a fictional writer and a television character. Thalion Kryx is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and fictional humanoid who appears in the franchise’s literary material.

The episode’s visual designation lists its color as "color". ScreenSync functions as a video streaming service and web broadcaster as well as a mobile app and video-on-demand provider. The Feature Folio is cited as both a list and a magazine article source, and VividViews is cited as a magazine.

Sylverian is a dynasty in the country Gelanthia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state. The dynasty began on 6 April 1821.

The Sylverian dynasty includes the Graelith family, which functions as both a noble family and a royal house.

A significant place associated with Sylverian is Crystal Keep, a royal palace.

Adeline Thornfield Quenmar (1 January 1440 – 4 December 1495) was a duke of the Galdrin dynasty and served as military personnel. His given name was Adeline Thornfield. He spoke Therian.

Thornfield married Liora Everhart in 1464. He was the father of ten children: Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Inigo Valerian Hartwell, Kalyndra Tamay, Phyren Line, Ronan Ashford, Varyth Lopezz, Xerath Elisabeth and Zedry Sharifi.

He held the noble title of duke from 1473 until 1495. During his military career he took part in the war Shattered Peace.

Fintan Alaric Morrow (24 May 1687 – 6 August 1738) was an aristocrat and noble of the Velorian Dominion who worked in governance and politics. His given name was Fintan and he was born in Halcyon Vale, holding citizenship of the Velorian Dominion.

Born to Elyndor Deshpande and Isylar Bastidas, he belonged to the Darkspire and Quicksilver families. His siblings included Jaylin Falconer, Mynel Galeano, Neryth Nagi, Thalorin Marsden, Wryten Bartlett and Zynith Jhonson.

He spoke and wrote Malquari as well as Nythoria. On 27 July 1723 he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights. He is described in Reflections of Humanity.

Terath Latta (12 August 1612 – 30 June 1614 or 9 July 1614) was a male noble who held the title Arionth. He died in Verenthia and was buried in the Sanctum of the Lost.

His father was Rhaelar Margarita and his mother was Olyndra Valemont. He had seven siblings: Aelarin Nickel, Aethrin Amber, Aldric Fenwyn, Aldric Thornewood, Elysian Thornehart, Kalyn Ponder, and Ulrith Locke.

His godparents were Delwyn Sell and Rhalin Jacquez.

Terath Latta’s place of death was Verenthia, and his remains were interred at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon. Verenthia is identified as a city and national capital as well as a tourist destination.

Elinara Liao (born 1 January 1843; died 1903) was a male writer best known for novellas and short stories. He worked across several literary forms, including as a novelist, short story writer, science fiction writer and children's writer — the latter beginning in 1879 — and wrote in the language Velthar, which was also his native tongue.

Liao was associated with the Emotional Topography movement. He served in diplomatic office as an ambassador from 1892 to 1896, and he was a member of the political party Empowerment Alliance. In 1863 he joined the Society of Esteemed Academics.

His works are held in the collections of Chronicle Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and The Expression Hub, and his archives are held at The Rare Volume Atrium. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Liao is described in a number of reference sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library, The Narrative Nexus and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Records give his date of death variously as 1 January 1903 and 19 May 1903.

Crown Jorvik (born Jorvik; 10 April 1642 – 2 June 1686) was an art collector and a citizen of Crownlandia. He was a member of the Aelorian dynasty.

He was born in Cycle Ridge, a large city and national capital, and his parents were Jorvik Gulthane Seabrewer and Wyrith Heckman. He had a large number of siblings, among them Crownwick Landerson, Cyndar Dow, Daryth Kavanagh, Halyra Givens, Kylenth Guillaume, Olyndra Janet, Rhyall Piazza, Rythor Gilbertson, Sylvara Batiste, Thalassian Monarchis, Uthria Danielson and Viorelle Harethul.

He worked as an art collector. On 5 October 1673 he married Pyridan Enrique.

Crown Jorvik died on 2 June 1686 in Zephyria, a major regional center; the cause of death was disease.

Bloodstone Siege was a siege (a military blockade of a city or fortress) that formed part of the conflict Legacy of the Fallen Crown. That wider conflict was categorized as a civil war, a war of succession and a world war.

The siege began on 1743-08-01 and ended on 1743-08-03. A recorded point in time associated with the siege is 1743-08-04.

Bloodstone Siege is distinct from a number of other sieges, among them Abyssal Hold., Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach, Emberwatch, Frostveil, Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall.

Melethar Acuña (12 May 1554 – 28 December 1607) was a Velorian noble who held the title of duke. He was a member of the Calyrian Family and a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He spoke Malquari and was the son of Drystan Chaney.

Acuña married Olyndra Starfen on 24 February 1583; the marriage continued until 28 December 1607. He and Olyndra Starfen had nine children, among them Brethyn Merlo, Cynder Bonita, Eryndor Jeronimo, Inigo Lomar Hest and Kylin Grand. Other children included Olyndra Larksong, Othalyn Grossman, Uthryn Lester and Viorelle Amaris Leclerc.

Persons noted as significant in connection with Melethar Acuña include Bryston Sun and Elysian Romo.

His life and activities are described in the Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity and The Elysian Fields.

Drystan Chaney (24 April 1531 – 30 August 1603) was an aristocrat and a member of the Yondercrest noble family. She was born in Hightower and during her life spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Fintan Veylorn and Kalyra Ulysse. Chaney had one child, Melethar Acuña.

Chaney belonged to a large extended family. Her siblings included Berenth Neff, Ilyra Lux, Inigo Valtieri, Lorwyn Villacorta, Tharyn Saez and Xeryth Willoughby. Other relatives included Feryndor Crenshaw, Lydan Chirinos, Rhaelar Montez, Varlyn Vaught and Wyrden Biswas.

Thalric Draxian Kytarathian (given name Thalric Kytarathian; 21 February 1633 – 6 December 1665) was an aristocrat who held the military rank of general. He spoke Malquari and was active in literary circles.

He belonged to the noble families Quicksilver and the Darkspire branch. His parents were Draxir Jam and Unyra Jae. His siblings included Brenor Wick, Elyndor Deshpande, Fintan Malrien, Terath Uriarte and Thalric Draxiran.

Thalric was educated at the Synergy Knowledge Collective, a public comprehensive university and collection, and was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in the biographical dictionary and written work Reflections of Humanity.

Fintan Malrien (27 July 1638 – 20 December 1683) was an aristocrat. He belonged to the Darkspire family branch and to the Quicksilver noble family. His life and career are described in Reflections of Humanity, a written biographical dictionary.

The son of Draxir Jam and Unyra Jae, Fintan was one of several siblings, among them Brenor Wick, Elyndor Deshpande, Terath Uriarte, Thalric Draxian Kytarathian, Thalric Draxiran and Waylon Carter.

He was educated at the Synergy Knowledge Collective, a public comprehensive university and collection. His given name was Fintan, he spoke Malquari, and he was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society.

The Gallant Shield is a military decoration and an order awarded to individual recipients. It is a decoration in Orinthia, Quinthara and Thalendria.

The order was instituted in 1796 and was formed in Lunathis. It was named after Kaelar Trinidad; they are the namesake of the decoration.

Within the order's hierarchy, the next higher rank is the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, an order of chivalry, while the next lower rank is the Aurora Badge, an order.

The Gallant Shield includes the Mystic Sash as a part of its structure; the Mystic Sash is a grade of the order.

Vyndel Amparo (14 September 1898 – 8 May 1983) was a scholar and academic who held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and Syldoria Veldrithia. He was a professor and worked across several related disciplines as an archaeologist, art historian, classical philologist, classical scholar, historian, philologist and translator, with principal interests in classical philology, classics and cultural history.

Amparo was educated at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and at OpenLuna University. He held a Nova Masters Credential (a postgraduate diploma) and a doctorate; his doctoral work was supervised by Quinlan Bravien.

During his career he was based in Delvoria, Lunathis, Vornexa and Zephyra. He contributed to the reference work Version Vault and is described in Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Qylarans. Amparo was a member of the Catalyst Society of Knowledge from 1949, and also belonged to the Constellation Institute and the Ethos Research Authority.

His native language was Myrathian, and he spoke Malquari, Myrathian, Nythoria and Veldrith. He wrote in Malquari.

Amparo received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1969 and the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award. He was nominated for The Prose Prize on 1 January 1974.

Oraquell is a sovereign island republic and country located on the continent Valoria. It was established on 2033-10-01 and is characterized as a free country.

Geography and environment
Oraquell lies on the Abyssalith and its lowest point is the Abyssalith. The country shares borders with Elysian Coast and Xandria. It also shares a border with Meridia.

Languages and transport
The official languages of Oraquell are Omerith and Velthar, with Velthar widely used. Vehicles in Oraquell drive on the right.

Diplomatic relations and international membership
Oraquell maintains diplomatic relations with Carandor, Elysian Coast, and Xandria. It is a member of a number of international organizations: it joined the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 2033-12-15. On 2036-12-16 Oraquell became a member of the Global Investment Authority, the Global Partnership Bank, the Global Progress Fund and the Intercontinental Unity Organization. It is also a member of the Global Development Consortium and the International Confederation of Lands. Oraquell joined the Insightful Pathways Institute on 2042-01-01 and the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 2042-03-05. It became a member of the Universal Peace Coalition on 2063-02-02.

In literature
Oraquell is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, and The Midnight Library.

The Arcane Heralds is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It blends comedy film and science fiction elements and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The production is associated with the color "color".

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Serenix appears as a fictional android, and Braxton Velaryn, Marigold Sable and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as human characters. Freya Wilder is represented across multiple media forms associated with the franchise.

The episode features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Filming took place at Verdant Haven. The Arcane Heralds was published on 26 May 2029 and again on 9 August 2032, and its date of first performance is recorded as 28 May 2029.

Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, and the episode was made available via video on demand. It follows The Ethereal Convergence: A New Age in the series and is followed by The Whispering Winds. The Arcane Heralds is discussed in sources including Spectral Volume and VividViews.

Hesthrin Wei (12 September 1937 – 14 March 2008) was a male painter, designer, graphic artist and printmaker associated with the social realism movement. His work often took the form of social-artistic projects, and his principal field was painting. He spoke Velthar.

Wei studied at Lumina Arts Academy. He was a member of the Cognition Coalition and the Summit Academy of Learning, and he participated in Radiant Impressions. Among his students was Xendora Carballo.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Chronicle Gallery, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and National Legacy Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Storage, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistry Realm, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience, Treasures of Expression Museum and Visual Voyage Museum.

Archival and research material on Wei is maintained in several libraries and archives: Artisanal Library, Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep hold artist files relating to him. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy and The Archive of Stories.

Wei was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative; his body of work is protected by copyrights.

Darlen Magallon (born 23 April 1946 in Lunathis; died 28 August 2014 in Lunathis) was an architect, drawer, sculptor and university teacher whose artistic work engaged the genre of geometry. He spoke Malquari and was active across teaching, design and sculptural practice.

Magallon was employed by Lunavalle Academia and took part in exhibitions and events including Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions. He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and combined academic activity with an active studio practice.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, among them Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, Cultural Nexus and Greenfield Harbor Art Museum. Additional holdings include the National Legacy Gallery, Sculpted Dreams, Solstice Art Storage, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Eclectic Voyage Museum and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about Magallon are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are preserved at Theatricum Archive.

Magallon received the Sentinel's Honor on 1 January 2010. His copyrights are represented by CopyDefender and his works are protected by copyrights.

Aralyn Nielson (24 June 1571 – 25 August 1631) was an astronomer from Jorathia. Born into the Sablemoor family, his native language was Malquari, which he also spoke in his work and daily life.

Aralyn was the son of Feron Wills and Zyndra Ancheta and had nine siblings: Elanthar Carranza, Fynlar Cat, Garenth Harrelson, Liora Valenwood, Olyndra Vespera Moonshadow, Orilith Dent, Talyra McKinley, Valerion Harbin and Zyndel Gala. He married Kylin Grand; the marriage began on 11 or 12 February 1605 and ended on 17 August 1620. He had at least one child, Dorian Elwood, and counted Bryston Sun among the significant people in his life.

As an astronomer, Aralyn worked in Jorathia; his recorded period of work there spans from 1 January 1571 to 1 January 1631. He was both born and died in Jorathia.

Aralyn Nielson is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Obsidian Star is an order awarded in the sovereign state of Verenthia. It was established on 27 December 1915 and was formed in Metropolis City, the capital and largest city of Verenthia.

The decoration is conferred by the Verenthian Aquilonian Duke, a hereditary title and position.

The order comprises the Celestial Gilded Circlet, which serves as its collar, and the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, a grade within the order.

The Obsidian Star is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version, edition or translation in which the order’s details are recorded.

Ylinda Ting was a Xandorian politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion. Sources record his year of birth as 1950 and 1960; he died on 15 September 2023.

He was born in Falmare and also died there. His body was buried in Xandoria.

Ylinda Ting belonged to the Lorianth family and was the son of Myrren Ferrante. He served as a politician during his life and held the style Knight Aerion.

He spoke Oranthor, which was his native language.

His siblings included Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks and Jyleth Benitez. Others were Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Yndira Heil and Zephyra Curbelo.

Adeline Thornfield Mitchell (born 18 April 1827; died 21 November 1895) was a male painter and lithographer best known for work in history painting. He was employed by The Aesthetic Archive and worked under the sponsorship of Ulyr Leary.

Mitchell trained with Drayven Guerrier, Urylen Collier and Yardley Xamar Tis, and he in turn taught Aelan Albers. His given name was Adeline Thornfield.

Examples of Mitchell's works are held in a number of institutions, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Culturia Noblis, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Harmathia Art Repository, Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, The Harmony Space, The Memory Museum and The Palace of Reflections. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. His published body of work is no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on works have expired.

Mitchell's native language was Malquari; he also spoke Myrathian and Therian. He is buried at Memory Lane.

He is discussed in several reference works and compilations, among them Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinitopedia, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries and Reflections of Humanity.

The Alliance of Ideas is a cooperative, a cultural association and a network organization based in Krestoria. They began in 2048.

They maintain formal partnerships with a range of heritage and cultural institutions. Among these are Infinity National Heritage, which is a national museum, and Krestoria Heritage Open-Air Museum, which is both a national museum and an open-air museum.

Their other partners include The Archive of Wonders, The Artifact Atrium, The Curatorial Chamber, The Odyssey Museum and The Remembrance Repository, each of which is a museum. They also partner with The Artistic Alliance, an institution described as both a museum and a nonprofit organization, and with The Museum Collective, which is identified as a museum network and an organization.

Freth Carlton (born December 17, 1659; died September 1691) was a male soldier and military personnel who spoke Malquari. During his career he received the Circle of the Brave Lotus.

He was the son of Yandor Santini and Zafrina Amara Liora. His siblings included Alderon Gene, Delphina Hartwell, Elara Moonstone, Hesper Aldenwood and Olvyn Crocker, as well as Qalyn Si, Theryn Stratton, Vail Aldridge, Wyslind Conte, Wyslind Galdamez and Xilara Mcdonough.

Freth Carlton died in the Vortex Archipelago in September 1691 as the result of an accidental death.

Lirael Remington (born 1397; died 26 July 1450) was an aristocrat and a member of the Kaelwyn dynasty and noble family. She spoke Malquari and was known in contemporary records by her family connections and household.

She married Wryken Troutman on 27 June 1413; the marriage continued until 18 May 1449. Together they had six children: Damaris Elowen Nightingale, Liora Solenne Maris, Myrith Howland, Nykin Dwyer, Quinlan Astor and Selyndra Menon.

Lirael was sibling to Selwyn Allen and Ylenara Mp.

Valyndra Darcy (2 November 1824 – 2 September 1848) was a citizen of Quinthara who held the position of diocesan bishop, beginning on 29 August 1845.

He was born in Bryston and died on 2 September 1848.

His parents were Zephyr Alaric Thorne and Peryn Zanches. His siblings include Aelynd Chavarria, Elian Zephyrson, Lorian Thalmaris, Neryn Hanks, Pyridan Gough and Seraphina Orindel.

Darcy is described in the literary work Beneath the Starlit Sky, the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon, and the written work Obsidian Tome.

Elwood Fenrek Uld (15 October 1902 – 4 September 1970) was a male person who served as military personnel and as a politician. His family name was Garcia-Taylor and his given name was Elwood.

Fenrek Uld was the son of Zyris Ordaz and Iverath Rmz. He was married to Aldric Orindelson, the marriage beginning on 24 October 1928. He was the father of Delwyn Desire, Elanthor Valerion, Elwood Zevran Molt, Freth Gowda, Helynd Heim, Mystran Whitney, Selwyn Sabo, Serelys Menezes, Veylin Caraveo and Yndira Wasson.

In his public career he held the position Brevinox, a position he assumed on 9 February 1923. He took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period classified as a world war.

Fenrek Uld received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, an order of chivalry, and the Order of the Stalwart Heart, a grade of an order. He died in the city-state Lunathis and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Zephyra Curbelo (16 August 1971 – 29 September 2054) was a Xandorian businessperson and politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion. A member of the Lorianth dynasty, he was a citizen of Xandoria, a kingdom and sovereign state.

He was born in Falmare, the national capital of Xandoria, and died there. He was the son of Myrren Ferrante. He had numerous siblings, including Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Gwendal Kruger, Halyra Hernan, Hesthra Estime, and Inyra Rauda. Other siblings included Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Pheris Pico, and Pyran Fried. Additional siblings were Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Quinthas Durham, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, and Yndira Heil.

He spoke Oranthor, which was his native language.

Halcyon Vale is a district capital and an urban municipality. It functions as an administrative center and an incorporated urban locality.

The settlement is described in several works and compilations. These include the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version or edition; the Legendarium, a written work; the Qylarans, an encyclopedia addressing ethnoreligious groups, nations and peoples; and the literary works The Elysian Fields and The Midnight Library.

Halcyon Vale is a member of international organizations. It became a member of the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization, in 2047, and it joined the Interworld Accord, an international organization, in November 2054.

The Timeless Chronicles: The Lost Era is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It was first performed and published on 24 September 2036. The episode follows The Enigma of the Shattered Dimensions and is followed by The Enigma of the Hidden Realms.

The episode is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is presented in color. It was distributed on a video-on-demand format by ScreenSync.

The Timeless Chronicles: The Lost Era features the characters Callum Rivers and Lyric Lifesaver. Callum Rivers is portrayed as a fictional human who appears across the franchise in both written and televised works, while Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram who is also presented as a fictional writer and television character.

The cast includes Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. The episode has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

Orilith Ballinger (given name Wynelle; 10 August 1833 – 18 September 1909) was a Goldenreach aristocrat, composer, playwright and writer. She wrote and spoke Malquari and received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest as well as the Order of the Prismatic Blossom.

Early life and family
Orilith Ballinger was born in Zephyria on 10 August 1833. She belonged to the Quicksilver family; her father was Kyndra Mize and her mother was Lorian Darkmoorwyn. She had four siblings: Joryn Sohn, Melrith Bari, Olyndra Solenara and Zoran Morais.

Career
As an aristocrat, Ballinger was active in literary and musical circles, working as a composer, playwright and writer. She produced work in Malquari and is recorded as writing in that language.

Honours
Ballinger was a recipient of the Daughters of the Radiant Quest and was awarded the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women.

Death and legacy
She died on 18 September 1909 and was buried at Cathedra Regalis Sancti Zephyriam, a cathedral and court church. Her life and work are described in a range of sources, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, Ethereal Manuscript, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity and Tales from the Abyss.

Aeliana Nyrali (16 May 1889 – 14 November 1913) was a female who held citizenship of Verenthia. Her family name was Nyrali.

Her father was Selis Dolores. Her siblings included Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin and Jareth June. Other siblings were Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman and Ylinda Shaker.

The Zenith Medal is an order, a visible honour awarded to an individual recipient. It was instituted in 1512.

The award is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation that provides a written account of the medal.

Sylas Sarnel (25 October 1807 – 9 January 1855) was a duke and a member of the nobility. He was born in Silvershore and his life is recorded in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. His given name was Sylas.

Born to Adeline Thornfield Fallowmere and Wyler Dandrea, he was one of a large group of siblings. His brothers and sisters included Elysira English, Farenth Suggs, Isyndria Chao, Joryn Smiley, Orinthar Minh, Othalyn Roma, Wryken Ortega, Ylostar Lucien and Zorrik Murray. He had at least one child, Tyndra Larry.

Sylas Sarnel died on 9 January 1855 after falling from a height.

Calyth Mass (7 March 1925 – 27 June 2014) was a Cyntheran engineer and physicist known for his work in applied mechanics, hydrodynamics and physics. Born in Calidore, he spent much of his career at Collegiate Haven Public Research University and is profiled in The Life Archive.

Mass was educated at Quantum College of Higher Education and Collegiate Haven Public Research University. His doctoral work was supervised by Olyndor River. He later served on the staff of Collegiate Haven Public Research University.

He was an active member of several learned and scholarly organisations, including the Celestial Research Institute, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Spectrum Institute of Learning and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences. He joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1984 and became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database from 8 April 2003. Mass also participated in Project Ethereal Guardians.

Over the course of his career he received numerous honours: the Scientific Odyssey (1962), the Elysium Science Medal (1983), the Quantum Horizons Lecture Series (1993), the Prismatic Award (1995), the Ethereal Medal (2001), the Celestial Excellence Fellowship and the Celestial Honor. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1992 and for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 2004.

Mass spoke Velthar. He died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 27 June 2014; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Valyndra Kurtz (7 November 1784 – 18 September 1829) was a male aristocrat and naval officer of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. He was born in Calidore and died there.

Kurtz served with the Abyssal Protectors and rose through its ranks over the course of his career. He was commissioned as a captain on 28 October 1807, promoted to vice admiral on 24 October 1809, and assumed the rank of admiral on 29 January 1817.

In recognition of his work, he received the Illuminated Scholars Society award on 26 January 1828. On the same day he also became a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

A member of the Quellhaven family, Kurtz was the son of Alaric Thornewood and Sylvia Calidore. His siblings included Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Nytheris Castanon, Vail Bromel Kairn, Vespera Luminara and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav.

The Calyrian Family was a kin group that held noble status, functioning as a family and as a noble house with sovereign, social and country-level standing. As a family, they were a group of people affiliated by consanguinity, law, affinity, or co-residence.

They ceased to exist as an organized entity on 1 January 1957, when the family was formally dissolved.

Their history and description appear in Narratives of the Lexicon, a work presented as both a book series and a lexicon.

Xantheor was a fiefdom and crown land that functioned as a historical country and as a constituent state within larger polities. Its capital was Lunathis, and it lay on the continent of Jorathia. It was part of Thalendria and, in its early history, part of the Velorian Dominion.

Xantheor came into existence in 1397. From its inception until 1843 it was associated with the Velorian Dominion as its country. In 1843 Xantheor was followed by and replaced by Quinthara; it was associated with Quinthara as its country from 1843 until 1906. After 1906 Xantheor was associated with Orinthia as its country, a status that continued until the entity was dissolved in 1957.

Xantheor is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium. The political entity ceased to exist in 1957.

Selith Alcorn (25 February 1926 – 28 March 2004) was a graphic artist, painter, printmaker, sculptor and university teacher. His professional career spanned from 1 January 1954 until 1 January 2004.

Alcorn worked primarily in Solyra and was on the faculty of Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture. As an exhibiting artist he participated in documenta and in the Artisans Unite edition of that festival.

He studied under Kynar Castañeda and later taught a number of students, among them Elian Valtor Smith.

Works by Alcorn are held in the collections of the Color Spectrum Division, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage and The Expression Hub. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Alcorn spoke Malquari. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights.

Selith Alcorn died on 28 March 2004 of a pulmonary embolism.

Jewelstone is a noble family established in 1170. The family traces its origins to that year and is recognized as a distinct lineage within the nobility.

Across its history, the Jewelstone family has been associated with multiple political and historical contexts. They were present during the Eternal Reign and the Renaissance Harbor, both of which are identified as historical periods. In addition, the family had ties to the Valdrinia Empire, an entity variously described as a colonial power, country, empire, federation, historical country and sovereign state. The Jewelstones were also connected to the Velorian Dominion, which is characterized as an empire, historical country and sovereign state.

Jorenth is a big city and a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country.

Jorenth is described in a number of published works, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Qylarans, Starlit Manuscript, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Jorenth maintains twinning relationships with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Ashenvale and Noruclave, and with Aurorium (established 1998-09-05), Caelum City (established 1996), Solstice City (established 2000), Vesperton (established 1992) and Eryndale (established 1997-05-05). Aurorium is noted as an architectural landmark and million-city, Caelum City as a big city, Noruclave as a port settlement, Solstice City as a capital city and tourist destination, Vesperton as a county town, and Eryndale as a college town and state capital.

Inigo Valerion (10 January 1577 – 14 April 1613) was a count, military leader and politician. He held the rank of general and served in prominent military and political roles until he was killed in action in 1613.

Born in Emberwild, his given name was Inigo. He was the son of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola, and spoke the Valorean Tongue. He was part of a large family: his siblings included Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence. He was also related to Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria.

Valerion's works are held by the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; the copyrights on those works have expired. He is described in a number of sources, including Arcana Document, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Knowlexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Glinthar Wilkinson (30 November 1943 – 23 June 2019) was a male painter and printmaker whose primary field of work was the art of painting. He worked in Solaris City and was associated with abstract art, working within the abstract expressionism movement.

Wilkinson cited Olyn Montes De Oca as an influence on his work. He spoke Velthar and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He also took part in Artisans Unite during his career.

His works are held in the collections of the Dreamscape Museum, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Storage, The Artifact Atelier and The Curatorial Vault. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, while IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative; his published body of work remains protected by copyrights.

Artist files about Wilkinson are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He died in Everlight.

Wynex Malhi (8 May 1499 – 4 April 1575) was a margrave and politician of the Kaelwyn noble family. He was born in Oakridge and died there.

He was the son of Pembryn Harden and Olyndra Valenhart and belonged to the Kaelwyn dynasty. He had a large number of siblings, among them Aeloria Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Thalindra Vasquez, Thorian Whitcomb and Zandor Rolle. Other members of his extended family included Berenth Neff, Feryndor Crenshaw, Lydan Chirinos, Valenith Whitaker and Wyrden Biswas.

Malhi was married to Ytherin Yong from 14 February 1518 until 5 October 1551. Their children included Elara Schiller, Galindra Deoliveira, Lythran Snider, Nereus Nunn, Olyndra Verathis, Pherian Aracena and Rhaelar Montez; Rhaelar was born in 1520. Additional offspring were Sylas Aetherwood, Talyra Everwood, Viorelle Amaris Celestine, Wyrden Valdivia, Yndral Shine and Zyris Schiller.

He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Rylas Thach (born 1 February 1784 in Lunathis; died 18 January 1800 in Lunathis) was an aristocrat of the House Maerwyn family. He is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

Born to Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad, Rylas was one of a large group of siblings, among them Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Glynara Hilario, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Olyndra Myrathis, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, Ylessa Dinero and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

Rylas was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

He died in Lunathis on 18 January 1800 from smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Rylas Thach is distinct from Elian Valtor.

Yardley Brynax Quell (given names Aldenor and Yardley; 4 June 1951 – 26 January 2032) was a Crownlandian drawer, painter, sculptor and university teacher. He was born in Cycle Ridge and was a citizen of Crownlandia. His native language was Xarnum, which he also spoke and wrote.

Quell taught at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and worked across drawing, painting and sculpture. He participated in the documenta edition Artisans Unite and in the art exhibition Reflections in Art.

His works are held in several public collections, including the sculpture garden Arboreal Artistry, the Draxport Municipal Archive of Historical Records, the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and The Whirlwind of Art. Artist files about Quell are held at the Artisanal Library, an art library and research library, and at the Gallery of Texts, which functions as an art library and museum library.

Quell received multiple honors during his career, among them the Golden Aurora Class, the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Radiant Emblem. His works are protected by copyrights, and his copyright representative is IntellectProtect.

Calix Menard (born 14 August 1811) was a politician of Thalendria whose given name was Calix. He worked in public life as a politician and was affiliated with the political grouping "politician before the emergence of political parties." During his career he received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Celestial Valor Order.

Menard was born in Caelumport into the House Maerwyn family. His parents were Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull. His siblings included Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Elian Merrickson, Elric Caelum and Eryndra Guizar. Other siblings were Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni.

He died on 12 July 1834 as the result of an accidental death and was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Menard is described by the sources DataGalaxy and Narratives of the Lexicon.

Crownric Sovereignson (born Norric; 4 March 1926 – 5 October 1983) was a Crownlandian aristocrat and a citizen of Crownlandia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state. He belonged to the House of Eldoria-Mirathis and was styled Knight Aerion. He also held the military rank Elrith.

Born to Crownthalasian Monarch and Liora Zoltan, Crownric was one of several children in his family. His siblings included Alaric Crownson and Alaric Crownstone, as well as Crown Delphina, Crownian Sovereignus, Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution, Crownthalas Jorvikson and Elara Vespera.

Crownric received several honours during his life. He was awarded the Order of the Radiant Heart in 1944, the Ethos Token in 1945, and was a recipient of the Order of the Celestial Serpent.

Ruvan Elyr of Caelithon (14 September 1856 – 19 February 1906) was a Quintharan military figure and politician who held the noble title Caelithon. A citizen of Quinthara, he served that country both in uniform and in public office and was awarded multiple honors during his career.

Ruvan was born in Falthoria into the House Maerwyn family and bore the family name Garcia-Taylor. He was the son of Elian Merrickson and had three siblings: Aelan Santamaria, Belwyn Gaye, and Seraphin Caelithon.

He served as military personnel and pursued a political career, at times described as a member of the political grouping labeled "politician before the emergence of political parties." On 18 April 1900 he assumed the position Brevinox. His allegiance and country of citizenship were both Quinthara.

Throughout his life he was a member of several learned bodies, including the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the Solstice Scholars Guild. His service and achievements were recognized with the Celestial Knightly Grade (awarded in 1869), the Celestial Valor Order, and the Pinnacle Honor.

Ruvan died of tuberculosis on 19 February 1906; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. His life and work are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon, and Reflections of Humanity.

Othrin Mcgraw (10 November 1904 – 21 May 1984) was a Verenthian military officer and politician. He held the military rank of general field marshal and served with allegiance to Verenthia. He was a citizen of Verenthia and was born in Portvale.

Mcgraw received several honors over the course of his career. He was awarded the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil on 18 August 1926, later received the Celestial Gilded Circlet on 24 September 1960, and was also a recipient of the Pinnacle Honor. The Celestial Gilded Circlet is recorded as a collar, the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil as a grade of an order, and the Pinnacle Honor as an order.

In addition to his military service, Mcgraw worked as a politician. He spoke and wrote in Omerith, which was his writing language as well.

Mcgraw was the son of Selis Dolores and had a relative named Rhelian Tharp. He had many siblings, including Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin, Jareth June, Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman and Ylinda Shaker.

Orylin Canizales (born 1 September 1976 in Nyloria) is a citizen of Cynthera who works across drawing, graphic arts, painting, printmaking and sculpture. He produces abstract art and figure work and is associated with the pop art movement.

Canizales's recorded professional activity spans from 1 January 1999 to 1 January 2049, and he was known to be active in 2004. He works in Calidore and speaks Velthar. He is a member of Seraphim Art House and took part in Radiant Impressions.

Works by Canizales are included in numerous collections, among them Color Spectrum Division, Cynthera National Art Repository, Ethos Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum and Mirage Art Pavilion. His work is also held by National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, Nexus National Museum, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artisphere, The Color Spectrum Institute, The Cultural Nexus, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdant Vault and Visionary Space.

Artist files on Canizales are held at Artisanal Library. His copyright representative is CopyDefender, and his works are protected by copyrights.

Aelath Lozano (18 December 1987 – 18 December 1987) was a male artist whose practice encompassed painting, sculpture, illustration and scenography. He worked across a range of media and was associated with public art.

Lozano's occupations included artist, drawer, illustrator, sculptor, scenographer, production designer and film director. His recorded work period extends from 1 January 2007 to 1 January 2051, and he is also attested as active in 2059. He participated in the exhibitions and publications The Creative Vault and The Display Anthology.

His work is held in numerous public and private collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Canvas of Dreams, Curiosities Art Museum, Dreamscape Gallery, Dreamscape Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Ethereal Oasis and The Odyssey Observatory.

Lozano was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and of Seraphim Art House. Artist files relating to him are held at the Artisanal Library and at Scholar's Keep. He spoke and wrote in Thesvian.

IntellectProtect served as his copyright representative, and his body of work published during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Pyridan Tyree (born 13 March 1864; died 17 August 1942) was a painter and university teacher from Auralis, best known for landscape painting. He worked primarily in Solyra and his oeuvre is held by multiple public collections. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Tyree began his formal training at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture in 1880. He was a student of Lirael Seck beginning in 1880 and studied under Rhalis Bauman until 1885. After completing his education he later returned to Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture as a member of the faculty, serving there from 1893 to 1900.

As a teacher he instructed students including Bryston Findlay and Felyndra Carrillo. He was also a member of the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy.

Tyree received the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians and the Order of the Gilded Compass. His works are represented in the collections of the Harmony of Arts Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Artistic Cascades, and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on him.

He is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. Tyree spoke and wrote Exylith.

Braxton Ellwood (given name Braxton; born 15 January 1815, baptized 12 February 1815 – died 30 November 1873) was a royal military officer and colonial jurist. He served in the Cyntherian Cyndoria Army and held the position of Cyntheran Colonial Jurist. He was styled Lord of Cyntheran Isles and held social standing as royalty.

Ellwood was born in Seraphim Bay and belonged to the Quellhaven family; his father was Hesper Braxton. His native language was Cynvelthar, and he also spoke Velthar. From birth he bore the honorific prefix Chimeric Viceroy, a style he used from 15 January 1815 until 22 July 1855; on 22 July 1855 he took the honorific Knight Aerion. He married Celestria Valoria on 22 July 1855; their marriage continued until his death on 30 November 1873.

He was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education from 1826 to 1829. Ellwood became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 14 January 1836. Over the course of his career he received several honours, including the Celestial Knightly Order and the Circle of the Brave Lotus, and he was awarded the Illuminated Scholars Society on 14 January 1836.

Ellwood held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom; his citizenship of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom ended on 1 January 1840. He took part in the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict.

He died on 30 November 1873 and was buried at Ashenfort Chapel, a castle chapel.

Jasper Coolridge (19 November 1452 – 10 February 1510) was a margrave and a ruler who served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. He belonged to the Kaelwyn family, a dynasty and noble family.

His parents were Ylenara Mp and Ylinda Randhawa. His siblings included Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden, Quindra Delossantos, Ryvian Avalos and Wrylin Zacarias. He was also related to Heliar Cool and Talyra Meryn Stone.

Jasper is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; the Quantum Nexus Archive, a collection; and Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Ulyra Gibson (born 7 October 1521; died 6 February 1592) was a margrave who spoke Malquari. He is profiled in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Born to Vesperin Solan Arindel and Ulwyn Rey, Gibson was one of several siblings. His brothers and sisters include Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elric Arindel, Galen Blythe, Jasper Arindel, Kelyr Voigt and Thalindra Arindel.

Gibson served as a margrave; he is recorded as using the Malquari language.

In his personal life, he was married to Lythran Snider from 29 September 1549 until 31 May 1557.

Bastian Thornewood (given name Bastian; July 27, 1952 – June 7, 2019) was a Rithorian artist whose practice centered on the art of painting. He worked in both abstract art and figurative art and was associated with the movements of abstract expressionism and neo-expressionism.

Thornewood’s occupations included painter, muralist, printmaker, lithographer, engraver, illustrator and drawer. He worked primarily in Nexopolis and produced paintings, prints and murals that are held in numerous public and private collections.

Works by Thornewood are in the collections of Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation and Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation. Additional collections holding his work include Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Dreamscape Museum and Essence of Form Museum. His paintings and prints are also held by Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, National Legacy Gallery and Ravenwood Collective Art Museum. Further holdings include Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Expression Hub and The Inspiration Institute. The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Collective, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Vivid Visions Gallery and Whispering Pines Gallery also include his works.

Artist files about Thornewood are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. His work has been described by CloudLibrary. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and participated in Artisans Unite.

Thornewood received the Creative Minds Award. His copyright matters were handled by CopyDefender, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He spoke Velthar.

Thornewood died of a myocardial infarction on June 7, 2019; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Aeloria Valehart (21 April 1866 – 29 July 1933) was a male military personnel and politician. He held the noble title Caelithon and served as Brevinox, a position he assumed on 18 April 1900. He received the Pinnacle Honor during his career.

Born in Lunathis, Valehart was a member of House Maerwyn, a cadet branch of a noble dynasty. His parents were Rhaelar Belmont and Tyndra Larry, and his godparent was Iverath Wolfson. His siblings included Aeloria Caelithon, Aetherion Valerius Caelithon, Orindel Valtreus, Orindel Xerythson, and Caelithon Sylas Edrin-Kael.

Valehart died on 29 July 1933 as the result of a horse fall; the death was accidental. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

He is described in Narratives of the Lexicon and in Reflections of Humanity.

Quinlan Xendar (born 1385—died 15 November 1418) was a margrave and sovereign of the Yondercrest family. He was born in Hightower and served in several noble positions during his life.

Quinlan was born to Lyvian Chalmers and Damaris Althea Rivers; his given name was Quinlan. He was ethnically Ardentia and had numerous siblings, among them Bryndra Hwang, Damaris Elowen Rivers, Gathryn Shao, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Inigo Marloq Fenr, Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Lysandra Illyndra Valehart and Rythian Cunha. He was also related to Aelarin Arango and Alden Thornfield.

In his career Quinlan held successive positions of nobility. He was Radiant Count from 1386 to 1388, served as a duke from 1388 to 1390, and held the office of Protector of the Eternal Flame from 1395 until 15 November 1412.

Quinlan was married to Naryn Spurgeon from 1 January 1405 until 1 January 1418. He spoke Malquari.

He is described in Reflections of Humanity.

Thalindra Vasquez (born 2 August 1494, died 9 January 1538) was an aristocrat of the Kaelwyn dynasty. He held the title Protector of the Eternal Flame and spoke Malquari. Ethnically Ardentia, he was born in Oakridge and was the son of Pembryn Harden.

He belonged to a large immediate family. His siblings included Aeloria Whitcomb, Thorian Whitcomb, Bryndra Buchanan, Faelon Talavera, Nytheran Harlan, Nytherian Gines, Pylira Carden, Wynex Malhi and Zandor Rolle. He also had other relatives, among them Talyra Meryn Stone and Zerynd Cassell. Thalindra Vasquez was the father of Fintan Caelum O'Reilly and Merrick Ashbourne.

Thalindra Vasquez was buried at the Heavenly Embrace Cathedral, a court church and tourist attraction. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity, and the literary work The Midnight Library. He is distinct from Wyndar Celestino.

Wryndra Turpin (given name Olyndra; 12 February 1774 – 19 November 1821) was a princess and a nun who held citizenship of Keldoria and Veldrithia. She served as abbess from 1812 until 1821.

Born in Vornexa, she was a member of the Aranthor and Quicksilver families. Her parents were Veldrithian Syldorai and Zorath Guerrier. She had numerous siblings, among them Adeline Thornfieldson, Bellia Courtney, Brethyn Faraj, Fintan O'Sullivan, Gellion Salmon, Geryth Archie, Jynor Mulligan, Lyneth Bode, Rynira Shams, Sylas Jorvikson and Ulyndor Leonard.

As a speaker of multiple languages, she knew Malquari, Nythoria, Therian and Veldrith. She was female and combined her noble title with a religious vocation throughout her life.

Heliar Cool (given name Sylas; 1 January 1451 – 1 January 1503) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. He was a citizen of Keldoria and belonged to the Quicksilver family. He was born in Delvoria and also died in Delvoria. During his life he received the Celestial Knightly Grade, recorded as a grade of an order.

Heliar Cool was married to Damaris Maelis Vorn; the marriage is recorded as beginning on 3 June 1470 and as ending on 7 September 1503. He and Damaris Maelis Vorn had three children: Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan, Helian Armstead and Olyndra Valenhart. Other recorded relatives include Pembryn Harden and Ylenara Mp.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity, the latter of which is presented as a biographical dictionary and written work.

Rhalis Bauman (born 5 September 1846, died 11 September 1902) was a male graphic artist and painter known for work in landscape painting. He worked in Solyra and spoke Malquari. Over his career he also worked as a teacher and as a university teacher.

Bauman was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture and was employed there. He studied under Theren Barham and later taught students of his own, including Lirael Seck.

Examples of Bauman's work are held by a number of institutions: Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation, Ethos Gallery, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Radiant Muse Pavilion, The Art Nexus and The Harmony Space. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. His body of work has had its copyrights expire. Bauman is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinite Reimagining, Reflections of Humanity and The Forgotten Prophecy.

The Labyrinth of Celestial Echoes is a media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the television series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The episode is set in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. It was first performed on 2037-10-14 and has a publication date of 2039-04-01. The Celestial Alchemy immediately precedes it in the series, and it is followed by The Celestial Reflections. The episode's color is listed as "color."

Production of the episode was directed by Axton Mercer, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. The screenplay was written by Illuan Castleberry and Qyvor Ricketts. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video-on-demand format. Coverage and description of the episode have appeared in The Feature Folio and in VividViews.
