The episode's credited cast includes Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim and Ylostar Gaynor. Characters appearing in the episode include Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Harmony Quill is presented as a comics character and television character depicted as a fictional human from the media franchise; Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are likewise fictional human characters who appear as literary and television characters. Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram and is portrayed as a fictional writer and television character.

The Celestial Whispers: The Lost Chronicles is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction work set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is presented in color. The narrative takes place on a fictional planet and aboard a ghost ship within that fictional universe.

Production was directed by Draxella Knott with Yardley Dovern Pax credited as film editor. The work was first performed on 2030-03-18 and has publication records for 2030-03-18 and 2033-03-11. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, with a video on demand release format. The episode follows Chronicles of the Forgotten Tides in its series and is followed by The Forgotten Realms of Aether. It is described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

The principal cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, Xenith Sengupta, and Zylara Zamudio. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, and Ulyr Stacks.

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Sable Hayes, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather. Several of these characters are depicted as human, including Braxton Velaryn, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Sable Hayes, and Tobias Merriweather; Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix appears as a fictional android. Freya Wilder is a character associated with multiple media forms within the franchise.

Eryx Valorian (given names Eryx and Paxton; 31 May 1899 – 22 January 1981) was a Cyntheran artist known for work in genre art and associations with the post-impressionism movement. He worked as an artist, drawer, painter and photographer, and produced work in and wrote in Velthar. Valorian studied under Caelan Rivers and cited Kyndra Farmer among his influences.

Valorian’s career included distinct periods working in different cities. He worked in Krestoria on 1 January 1926, in Ecotropolis from 1 January 1933 to 1 January 1943, and in Calidore from 1 January 1943 until 1 January 1981. He was a member of Seraphim Art House and was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artistry Alliance, Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus Museum, Cultural Reflection Gallery, Cultural Saloon and Discovery Hub. Additional holdings include Dreamscape Gallery, Echoes of Heritage, Fusion Art Institute, Harmony Exhibit House, Heritage Heart Museum, Legacy Arts Foundation and Local History Vault. Valorian’s work is also in the Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, Mirage Art Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artisan's Gallery, The Artisphere and The Artistic Discovery Museum. Other collections holding his pieces are The Civic Repository, The Collective Art House, The Community Art Repository, The Expression Hub, The Town Tales Museum, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vesperton Independent Art Museum and Woodland History Center.

Artist files about Valorian are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy. Copyrights on his works have expired; copyright representation has been associated with CopyDefender and IntellectProtect.

Valorian was born in Hightower and died in Seraphine. He was male and was married to Braxian Grabowski from 1965 until 1981.

Valtarian Luntru is a modern language belonging to the Luntru language group. It is classified typologically as a tonal language.

Geographic distribution of Valtarian Luntru includes presence in the countries Lunethia, Orinthia and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. The language is indigenous to several places and communities, including Fendril, Mercuria, the Solara Archipelago, Tharavon and Zephyra.

Valtarian Luntru is written in two scripts: the Valtarian Glyphic Script and Valtaroscript, both of which are writing systems used for the language.

Selath Belton (23 June 1947 – 20 March 2014) was a male member of the Galdrin dynasty who held the noble title Arionth. He received the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Harmony Insignia, both grades of an order.

Belton was born on 23 June 1947 and baptized on 29 June 1947. He was the son of Denzil Thorne and Elara Aeliana Valtaris. His godparents were Nyvalis Anders and Xendry Cavalier. He had several siblings, among them Caledorn Denzil Ravenshire, Lelith Marston, Lytheris Karimi, Rythor Pickering and Vorith Mcclanahan.

He spoke Kynthor and lived with a deaf-mute medical condition. 

Belton died on 20 March 2014 as a result of falling from height and was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Wailing Wall were a military blockade of a city or fortress that began in May 1505 and ended on 26 July 1506. They occupied that period as an organized siege operation.

They were different from several other named sieges, including Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege and Castle of the Forsaken, as well as Doom's Reach, Emberwatch, Frostveil and Gloomwatch. Other distinct comparators include Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel and Thundertide.

Myrren Schofield (27 February 1940 – 6 August 2019) was a Morvath-born artist whose work was associated with modern art. He worked primarily in the art of sculpture and was also active as a lithographer. Over the course of his career he produced work in the genres of figurative art, nude and portrait.

Schofield was a member of the Cognition Coalition and the Nexus Learning Society. He participated in several notable exhibitions and editions, including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta. His work locations included Caelumport and Thundoria, where he carried out much of his professional practice.

His works are held in a wide range of collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance and Dreamscape Museum. Additional institutions holding his work include Ethos Gallery, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Infinity Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Evolution Gallery and The Inspiration Nexus. Artist files on Schofield are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the catalogue ItemVerse.

Schofield received the Seraphic Prize. His copyright was represented by IntellectProtect, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He spoke and wrote in Thesvian, which was also his language of writing. From 27 February 1940 until 18 June 1985 he held citizenship of Morvath.

Soren Valq (1 January 1930 – 18 July 1957) was a male military officer, military personnel and politician of the Myralun Empire. He bore the family name Envira, belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty and held the noble title knyaz; he was also socially classified as noble.

He served the Myralun Empire and was a citizen of that state. Working in military service, he rose to the rank of Elrith and took part in the Chronos Siege. For his service he received the Pinnacle Honor and the Vexorian Medal.

Soren was born in Zephyra and spoke Myrathian. His father was Elara Myralun and his mother was Jaryn Candela. He was a sibling of Aldren Myralun, Calyndra Myralun, Cyralun Varethian and Zalet Horyn. He died by homicide on 18 July 1957.

Kyndra Narayan (1824-01-30 – 1900-09-28) was a male painter known for portrait work. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and received recognition including the Golden Aurora Class and the Talent Tournament.

Narayan studied at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1850-01-01 to 1851-01-01 and also trained at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He was a student of Syldor Hyde, who likewise influenced his artistic development.

His paintings are held in numerous public collections, among them the Fusion Arts Museum, the Harmathia Art Repository, the Realm of Creativity Museum, The Cultural Exchange Hub, The Curatorial Institute, The Memory Museum, and The Visionary Whirl. Artist files relating to his career are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and the Legendarium. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Narayan spoke Therian. His known students include Brenith Suriel and Elthar Wilbur.

Aelvin Gz (23 October 1883 – 4 December 1939, Astral Springs) was a male drawer, graphic artist and painter known for portraiture and for his association with the Ethereal Canvas movement. He spoke Malquari.

He studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and later worked for the same institution. Early in his training he was a student of Jalen Carter Thompson.

His paintings and graphic works are represented in numerous public collections. Examples include the Cyndoria National Art Museum, the National Center for Creative Heritage, the Radiant Muse Pavilion, and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional holdings are held by The Aesthetic Archive, The Artistic Realm, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Exploratorium of Art, The Expression Hub, The Palace of Reflections, The Storytellers' Studio, and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files about Aelvin Gz are held at the Gallery of Texts. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Karyth Diop (15 May 1886 – 13 August 1968) was a Cynthera biologist and zoologist who also worked as a botanist, scientific illustrator and writer. His primary field of work was zoology, and he spoke and wrote in Velthar. He was born and died in Calidore.

Diop was educated at Meadowbrook College and was employed by the Calidore Institute of Global Learning. Over the course of his career he was influenced by Zander Hesperfield and held memberships in a number of learned bodies, including the Aurora Academy, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the Spectrum Institute of Learning and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1942.

As a writer and contributor, Diop contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. He is described by ItemVerse and in the literary work Tales from the Abyss. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Diop received several honors during his life: the Quantum Visionary Medal (1924), the Elysium Science Medal (1952), the Quantum Scholar Recognition (1959) and the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

Irvin Helvorn (1 January 1864 – 1 January 1933) was a painter who specialised in landscape painting. He worked in Calidore, Draxoria, Ironwood and Seraphim Bay, and his body of published work is noted as having copyrights that have expired. His given name was Irvin.

Helvorn's field of work is recorded as the art of painting, with a particular focus on landscape painting, and his genre likewise is listed as landscape painting. He spoke Velthar. Among his students was Inigo Uvan Dresk. Helvorn is described in the Arcana Document as well as the Dreamt Compilation.

Artist files about Helvorn are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. Works by Helvorn are included in numerous collections and museums, among them the Artisan's Vision Hub, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, the Canvas of Dreams, the Celestial Grove of Sculptures, the Chroma Art Cooperative, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Canvas Museum, and the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara. His paintings also appear in the collections of the Essence of Form Museum, the Ethereal Observatory, the Flourish Art Consortium, the Horizon Ridge University Gallery, the Infinity Art Museum, the Jaspis Art Collective Museum, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, and the Obsidian Arts Collective.

Further holdings of Helvorn's work include the Radiant Brush Gallery, the Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, the Realm of Creativity Museum, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, the Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artistic Exchange, The Chroma Atelier, The Creative Cascade Gallery, The Ethereal Oasis, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and the Verdantia Art Collective Museum.

Cedric Emberheart is a fictional human character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise who appears in both written works and television. She originates from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is described in sources as xB. Cedric was born on 24 June 2387 and is portrayed by Lyris Cortés.

Physically, Cedric is depicted with blue eyes and blond hair; portrayals show her hair as shoulder-length or worn up, and she is also depicted with hair loss. She is frequently shown wearing a catsuit and is musically accomplished, playing the piano.

Within the setting, Cedric is a member of the crew of the Ethereal Shipbuilders and is affiliated with the Interstellar Institute. Significant associates in her story include Flux, Freya Wilder, Garrick Shadowbrook, and Harmony Quill. She is represented as bisexual.

Cedric appears across a range of franchise works. She is present in written works such as Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions, Nebulae Script, Phantom Text, Shadowed Annals, The Written Horizon and Threads of Time, in media franchise novels including The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Inked Odyssey and The Serpent's Compendium, and in the two-part episode The Ascendant Quest.

Ustara Bedell (5 November 1915 – 9 October 1957) was a painter and sculptor associated with the Fluxist Aesthetic. He participated in documenta and his work was affected by the Chronos Siege.

Born 5 November 1915, Bedell was educated at Silver Birch College. He spoke Therian. He had two siblings, Othryn Thanh and Wylora Fernando.

Bedell’s paintings and sculptures are held in numerous public and private collections, including Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository and the Creative Spark Foundation. Other institutions holding his work include Cultural Nexus, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, National Legacy Gallery, National Museum of Cultural Heritage and Solstice Art Storage, as well as The Expression Hub, The Inspiration Institute and Treasures of Expression Museum. The copyrights on his works have expired.

His archives are held at the Museum of Memory, and artist files about him are located at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described by the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Bedell died in Quantum Haven on 9 October 1957 of typhus.

Calyndra Myralun (23 April 1942 – 7 November 1977) was a Myralun aristocrat who held the noble title knyaz. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire, a transcontinental sovereign state and historical empire. Born in Zephyra, a million-city and former capital, Calyndra bore the family name Envira and was a member of the Jorathyn dynasty.

He was the son of Elara Myralun and Jaryn Candela. His siblings included Soren Valq, Aldren Myralun, Cyralun Varethian and Zalet Horyn.

Quillon Thorne (given names Denzel and Quillon; 9 October 1891 – 15 July 1958) was a Valdrinia Empire biochemist and university teacher who worked in the field of chemistry. He held the academic degree of professor, spoke Malquari, and was widely described in reference works and compilations including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Labyrinthine Journal, Legendarium and the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Thorne’s academic career included appointments at Astral Springs State University, Bayview Comprehensive Institute and Branash Imperial University of the Free Republic. He worked in Hightower and his doctorate was supervised by Ilindra Sharon. Among the students he supervised was Quinlan Rivenoak.

He was an active member of numerous learned societies and academies. These included the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 1 June 1938), the Cognition Coalition, Frontier Knowledge Productions (membership beginning in 1943), Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment.

Thorne received several awards over the course of his career. He was awarded Paradigm Recognition and The Apex of Discovery Medal in 1937, the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1941, and both the Arcane Science Prize and the Celestial Brilliance Award in 1948. He also received the Seraphic Prize. He was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1941 and for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award on 1 January 1948.

Thorne produced work that is no longer protected by copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired. He died of natural causes on 15 July 1958.

Carandor Artistry Productions is an art museum and production company. It was founded by Fintan Farlanov and had its inception on 1 January 1920.

The organisation is headquartered in the city of Grigsbyton, a big city. From its inception until 1 January 1940 it was located in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian; on 1 January 1940 its national affiliation changed and it has been in the country of Carandor since that date.

Veldron Hinkle (born 1898 in Havencrest; died 13 December 1962) was a male visual artist whose work encompassed painting and graphic practices. Sources give two dates of birth for Hinkle—1 January 1898 and 20 November 1898—and his recorded date of death is 13 December 1962.

Hinkle's recorded work period runs from 1 January 1918 to 1 January 1962. During his career he worked in Auralis and Hightower and practiced across several related fields: painting, graphics, and the wider visual arts. His occupations included graphic artist, illustrator, lithographer, poster artist, printmaker and sculptor. He produced genre art, notably nudes and still lifes. Among his students was Lorwyn Funes.

Hinkle's works are held in numerous public and institutional collections. Examples include the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, the Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, The Ethereal Oasis, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Legacy Art Space, the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Whimsical Brush Art House. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are kept at the Theatricum Archive. He is described by DataGalaxy. His copyrights as a creator are recorded as having expired.

Hinkle spoke and wrote Therian and also used Quolmar; his native language and his writing language are recorded as Therian.

Glinthar Cobb (23 October 1294 – 25 June 1314) was a member of the Wintervale royal house. He was born in Aquilon and spoke Kynthor.

He was the son of Denzil Archer and Jynara Valladares. He had eight siblings: Brethyn Taboada, Caelan Mavren Osk, Fythar Ferrufino, Goryan Patrice, Lamyra Sandler, Liora Ferrufino, Uthria Chia and Vespera Zavala. In 1308 he married Brystyne Schmitt.

Aldren Myralun (27 November 1931 – 12 October 1953) was a Myralun poet and noble who held the title of knyaz. He served as a cornet in the cavalry and held allegiance to the Myralun Empire. A citizen of the Myralun Empire, he wrote in Myrathian and was awarded the Pinnacle Honor.

Born in Zephyra to Elara Myralun and Jaryn Candela, Aldren belonged to the Jorathyn dynasty and used the family name Envira. He was one of several siblings, including Soren Valq, Calyndra Myralun, Cyralun Varethian and Zalet Horyn.

Aldren took part in the Chronos Siege and was killed in action; he died in Tranquilhaven. His military service was carried out in the cavalry at the rank of cornet.

He is described in Knowlexicon.

The Enigma of the Lost Realms is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It was directed by Axton Mercer and first premiered on 2037-12-02, with a publication date of 2038-06-20. The work is distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync. The episode is also described with the color "color."

The episode's cast includes Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Characters appearing in the episode include Cedric Emberheart, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Cedric Emberheart and Rowan Emberwood are presented as fictional human characters who appear in both written and televised forms, while Lyric Lifesaver is depicted as an emergency medical hologram and is also identified as a fictional writer and television character.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. In series continuity, the episode follows Fractured Time: Echoes from the Past and is followed by The Celestial Explorers, both of which are media franchise episodes.

ScreenSync, the distributor, operates as a mobile app and a video streaming service that provides video on demand and web broadcasting. The Enigma of the Lost Realms has been described in The Feature Folio, presented as a list and magazine article, and in VividViews, a magazine.

Moryn Swift (24 November 1953 – 25 April 2042) was a male architect and artist whose work centered on sculpture and encompassed abstract and public art. He worked across multiple visual disciplines as an architect, artist, drawer, graphic artist, painter and sculptor, and was associated with the abstract art movement.

Born in Calidore, Swift participated in the documenta festival, including the Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions editions. His sculptures and other works are held in the collections of Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Artropolis Nextridge, Color Spectrum Division, the National Legacy Gallery, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Solstice Art Storage, The Evolution Gallery and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Swift was a member of the Seraphim Art House and received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order. He spoke Velthar and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966, as well as citizenship of Cynthera.

His works remain protected by copyright and are represented by CopyDefender. Artist files about Swift are held at the Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep.

Kaelith Vorenstal (given name Kaelith) was a male artist, painter and author born on 29 April 1921. Records list two dates of death, 30 January 1999 and 1 February 1999. He spoke Therian.

Vorenstal’s fields of work included the Fluxist Aesthetic, the art of painting and the visual arts. He was associated with movements including the Fluxist Aesthetic, abstraction and fauvism, and worked across painting and related visual practices in addition to authorship.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections. Among the museums and institutions that include Vorenstal’s work are Arathonia Art Museum, Artistry Alliance, Cultura Nexus, Curator's Archive, Echoes of Art., Glistening Gallery of Treasures, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Nexus of Literary Inquiry, The Aesthetic Archive, The Chroma Atelier, The Collective Gallery, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Color Spectrum Institute, The Expression Hub, The Storytellers' Studio and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Artist files about Vorenstal are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library and museum library, and at Scholar's Keep, an academic library and library building. He also participated in major events, including Artisans Unite and documenta.

Vorenstal was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright representative was the Intellectual Harmony Guild. His body of work published during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Quinlan Astor (born 24 August 1429; died 5 July 1500) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family who held the position of regent. He spoke Malquari and was known by the given name Quinlan, a male given name.

He was the son of Wryken Troutman and Lirael Remington. He had five siblings: Damaris Elowen Nightingale, Liora Solenne Maris, Myrith Howland, Nykin Dwyer, and Selyndra Menon.

Quinlan Astor is described in the collection Quantum Nexus Archive and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Therin Ontiveros (1599-01-01 – 1674-05-17) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic painter working in the visual arts. He spoke Thesvian and is recorded as male. His body of work is no longer under copyright; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Ontiveros was born in Ecotropolis and died there. His father was Rythian Pfeiffer. Over the course of his career he worked in Crankton, Ecotropolis and Lystria.

Collections and archives hold numerous examples of his work. Works by Therin Ontiveros are in Artefactual Odyssey, Aurora Art Gallery, Branash Cultural Collective, Canvas of Dreams, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Reflection Gallery, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Echo Art Foundation and Ethos Gallery. Additional holdings include Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Historical Nexus and The Prism of Cultures, as well as The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Whirl, Tranthia Art Haven and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the web portal DataGalaxy. Records also indicate that Therin Ontiveros is different from Rythian Pfeiffer.

Hesperis Roden (born Sylas; 1 September 1618 – 3 September 1673) was born at Maplewood Manor, a château and residence. He spoke Malquari, a modern language.

He was the son of Deleth Lorenzo and Garenth Harrelson. His siblings included Jareth Seibert, Jorvik Eldorian Steele, Liora Marcellus, Olyndra Faeloria, Qylara Heiser, Rolyn Short, Talyra Rehman, Thalyn Ferdinand and Wryten Obeng.

Hesperis Roden is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity, a written work that records details of their life.

Chyndra Dor (19 November 1939 – 15 October 2019) was a Myralun physicist, mathematician, university teacher and politician. He was a citizen of the Myralun Empire and worked primarily in mathematics and the calculus of variations. Born in Velarune, he died in Luminara. His native language was Myrathian and he spoke Myrathian.

Dor was educated at Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1960 to 1965 and attended Silver Birch College in 1966. He held an Obsidian Graduate Award. As an academic and teacher, he was employed by the Spectrum Institute of Learning from 1978 to 1988, by Luminara State University of Transcontinental Studies from 1988 to 1996, and by the Myralun Luminara Academy Press from 1996 to 2014.

He supervised doctoral students, including Olyndra Sprague (1976) and Feryth Kohler (1977). In addition to his university posts, Dor was a member of a number of learned and research organizations: the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. He was also a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party.

Dor received numerous honours over his career. He was awarded the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1984, 1987, 1993 and 1995, and received the Apex Honorary Citation in 1985 and 1988. He won the Quantum Award several times, in 1992, 1995, 1999, 2006 and 2014, and he received the Zenith Merit Medal in 1997. Other recognitions included the Legacy of Honor (2006), the Golden Vanguard Class (2010) and the Infinitum Recognition (2016-01-01).

Biographical information on Dor appears in SoulScript.

The Lost Horizons is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. It is a science fiction work that takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The production is presented in color and makes reference to the observer effect.

Fyntra Flow directed the episode. Its date of first performance was 2044-01-21, and its publication date is 2045-04-23. The Lost Horizons was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand; ScreenSync operates as a video-on-demand and streaming service and is available as a mobile app and web broadcaster.

Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall. Cast members are Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice actors credited on the episode include Garanth Smit, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Lost Horizons is followed in the series by the episode The Enigma of the Ancients: The Awakening.

Delvyn Layne (8 May 1940 – 1 January 1953) was a royal prince. He was born in Upland, a college town and district capital that also serves as a major regional center and urban municipality.

He was the son of Fenris Hooper and Davenor Bower. His siblings included Alex Morgan, Cevaryn Jennifer, Elric Thornfield, Jyneth Lind, Nythera Powers, Silthar Dell, Velian Chen, and Viorelle Amaris Larkspur.

Pylira Uno (6 July 1911 – 10 June 1993) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family. She spoke Malquari and was married to Zephyr Eryndor from 31 May 1936 until 1993.

Pylira was the daughter of Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers. Her siblings included Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Hylith Zaki, Illyndra Bartlett, and Ilyra Voral Syrren.

Pylira Uno died on 10 June 1993.

Ythira Selby (born 1718-01-27, died 1791-01-26) was a male painter who worked primarily in portraiture. His father was Nerya Jaime.

He spoke Therian. Selby became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research on 1747-07-28. He held the position of director from 1777 to 1790 and worked in Seraphim Bay from 1777-01-01 until 1791-01-01. He died in Seraphim Bay on 1791-01-26.

Selby's works are held in the collections of many institutions, including the Artoria Capital Museum, the Aurora Art Project, the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, the Celestial Canvas Institute and the Celestial Gallery. Additional holdings include the Cultural Nexus, the Discovery Hub, the Enchanted Brush Institute, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum and the Fusion Art Institute. His works are also in the collections of the Haven of Expression, the Heritage Hub, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and the Spectrum of Expression Gallery. Other repositories that hold his work are The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Artistic Odyssey Museum and The Curatorial Institute. The Evolution Gallery, The Memory Mosaic, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and the Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum likewise include his works in their collections.

Artist files about Selby are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described by the Dreamt Compilation. As a creator, his copyrights on works have expired.

Damaris Lystrian (given name Damaris; 10 January 1481 – 23 October 1518) was a politician and member of the Yondercrest noble family. She was born in Hightower, a major city and college town, and died in Lystria, a commune.

Early life and family
Damaris was the daughter of Fintan O'Shea and Olyndra Everglint. She was part of the Yondercrest family and had several siblings: Fintan Veylorn, Myrith Dupre, Nivara Johnson, Talyra Bellamy, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrith, Varlyn Vaught and Wylanth Tompkins. She was also related to Talyra Meryn Stone.

Career and language
Damaris worked as a politician. She spoke Malquari.

Personal life and health
She married Aric Lysander Valerius on 10 May 1502; that marriage ended on 14 October 1518. Damaris was female and lived with abnormal kyphosis.

Thalyn Tae (22 January 1928 – 31 August 1994) was a male artist and educator known for work in abstract art. He worked as a designer, drawer, graphic artist, graphic designer, painter, typographer and university teacher over a career that spanned from 1944 to 1994.

Tae participated in several notable exhibitions and editions, including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta. His work is held in numerous public and private collections, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Color Spectrum Division, Creative Spark Foundation and Essence of Form Museum. Additional repositories of his work include Ethos Gallery, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, National Museum of Cultural Heritage, The Aesthetic Spectrum and The Artistic Realm. Other collections and institutions holding his pieces are The Artistry Realm, The Curatorial Vault, The Inspiration Nexus, Verdant Vault and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Archival material and artist files for Tae are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. His published works remain protected by copyrights; his copyright representatives are IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective.

Tae spoke Malquari. Significant persons associated with him include Denzel Carter and Ubrith Moorer, and he was sponsored by Ryland Tharim Kove.

Alden Marwood (given name Alden; born 1 July 1840 – died 21 April 1916) was an anatomist, physiologist and university teacher whose work focused on physiology. He held citizenship of Goldenreach and the Myralun Empire. Marwood was born in Delvoria and carried out his professional work there.

Marwood was educated at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. He was employed by Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and by Braventon State Comprehensive University, and he held the position of rector. Among his doctoral students was Denzel Afton.

He was a member of several learned organizations, including the Constellation Institute, the Nova Academy of Research (membership beginning 24 February 1888) and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities (membership beginning in 1913). Marwood spoke Malquari.

Marwood is described in a range of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Labyrinthine Journal, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, ReadRealm and Reflections of Humanity.

Hesthra Berndt (5 June 1795 – 29 July 1871) was a count and a male political figure whose professional work was connected with chemistry. He spoke and wrote Therian, which was his native and primary writing language, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Berndt pursued scholarly work in chemistry and completed a doctorate under the supervision of Pytheran Stallworth. Alongside his scientific background, he worked as a politician and held the position of president from 1841 to 1842.

He was active in a number of scholarly and publishing bodies. Berndt was a member of the Academy of Natural Sciences, the Celestial Research Institute, the Constellation Institute, the Guild of Intellectual Pioneers, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (which he joined on 20 November 1822), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Berndt received several honors during his lifetime. He was awarded the Twilight Pendant in 1826. Later, he received the Celestial Distinction on 22 May 1864 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 9 June 1864; the Celestial Distinction and Twilight Pendant are grades of an order, and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences is a fellowship.

His life and work are discussed in multiple sources, including the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Thalric Valenor Kytarathian (born 25 March 1584; died 9 October 1661) was an aristocrat and a citizen of Crownlandia. He was a member of the Aelorian dynasty, and his given name was Thalric Kytarathian. He spent his life in the role associated with his social rank and belonged to a prominent family.

He was the son of Thalassian Jorvikson and had at least two siblings, Aveline Crownwood and Thalassian Sovereighn. He married Tharyn Rhodes on 19 August 1607 and later married Liora Amara Bellwood on 14 February 1627.

Thalric was the father of thirteen children. Among them were Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Helian Cates and Jorvik Elmsworth. His other children included Merrick Halvren, Nereus Oswald, Nivara Starks, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar and Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood.

In recognition of his standing he received the Crest of the Celestial Knights in 1619. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Lythara Mattison was a male jewelry designer, silversmith, and university teacher whose recorded life dates include two differing entries for birth — 1969-01-01 and 1969-06-27 — and two differing entries for death — 2014-01-01 and 2014-12-20. 

Mattison worked at the intersection of education and applied arts, with fields of work noted as education, jewelry, and jewelry design. He was employed by the Valor Brigade from 1992 to 1994. 

He took part in a number of exhibitions and related catalogues, including Aesthetic Horizons, Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Itemarium, Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, and The Curated Experience. Several of these projects also functioned as published catalogues or publications in addition to exhibitions.

Works by Mattison are held in multiple institutions and collections. His pieces appear in the Creative Heritage Archive, Thalorix Reliquary, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Palace of Reflections, Treasures of Expression Museum, Velvet Jewel Set, Velvet Treasures, and the Wonderworks Institute. Artist files about him are kept at the Artisanal Library, an art library and research library.

Mattison’s body of work published during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights.

Ytherin Bateman (6 February 1918 – 10 January 1988) was a male painter, printmaker and teacher associated with the post-impressionism movement. He worked primarily in portraiture and is recorded as speaking and writing Therian. Bateman was a student of Kaldorn Fullmer and counted Brenar Pedroza, Tamsin Alaric Voss, Tamsin Sterling and Therin Harman among his influences.

Bateman was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He participated in the Artisans Unite edition and taught as part of his practice. His archives for the period 1956 to 1977 are held at Memory Keep, and artist files about him are held by the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy.

Works by Bateman appear across a wide range of public collections. They are held by ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Haven, Artoria Borderland Museum, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Nexus of Artoria, Cultural Reflection Gallery and Echoes of Art.. Additional holdings include Essence of the Arts Museum, Harmony of Arts Museum, Legacy Museum, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, National Artistry Hub and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. His work is also in the collections of Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Art Archive, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Ethereal Institute of Art and The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery. The Historical Nexus, The Muse Spectrum, The Whirlwind of Colors and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute likewise hold his work.

Bateman received the Everlasting Tribute. IntellectProtect is listed as his copyright representative, and his published works are recorded as having had their copyrights expire. He was born in Bellhaven and was buried at Resting Waters.

Nyvir Depaz (21 December 1943 – 4 March 2040) was a male artist known for work in abstract art. Over a career that stretched from 1 January 1958 until 1 January 2040, he worked as a drawer, lithographer and stained-glass artist and was active in multiple international exhibitions.

Depaz trained at Creative Spectrum Academy, Silver Birch College and The Cultural Exchange Hub. His practice was associated with the abstract art movement and he participated in documenta, including the documenta editions Artisans Unite and Radiant Impressions.

His works are held in a number of public collections and museums, among them the Color Spectrum Division, Cultura Nexus, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Collection, The Legacy Lab and The Whirlwind of Art. Archival material and artist files relating to Depaz are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Depaz received the Radiant Emblem, a grade of an order, in 2019. His published works remain protected by copyrights and his copyright is represented by IntellectProtect. He is described by DataGalaxy, and he spoke Therian.

Sylas Everhart (14 May 1820 – 14 June 1912) was a historian, jurist, politician, university teacher and writer. He held a doctorate and wrote in Malquari; he also spoke Malquari. His given name was Sylas.

Everhart was educated at Braventon State Comprehensive University and later worked at Luminara College and at ScholarQuest University. He was a member of several learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute and the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences. He became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 19 February 1876.

He received the Seraphic Prize and was awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1892.

His life and work are described in a range of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library.

Urylen Connell (28 March 1877 – 23 March 1960) was a male painter, illustrator, sculptor and teacher associated with the academic art movement. His primary field of work was the art of painting, and his practice included history painting as a central genre.

Connell was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Ulthara Houston. As a teacher, he took on pupils including Ulthara Clough and Zander Carthwright. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and of Seraphim Art House.

Works by Connell are held in a wide range of public and private collections. Among these are the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and the Royal Gallery Palace, as well as the Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Project, Enchanted Brush Institute and Nexus of Vision. Additional holdings include The Dreamscapes of Art, The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Palace of Reflections, The Realm of Colors Museum, The Visionary Experience, The Visionary Landscape and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

Artist files on Connell are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. Connell spoke Therian. The copyrights on works he created have expired.

Kaelith Escobedo (given name Inigo; 24 December 1958 – 25 October 2061) was a male visual artist best known for his work in painting and abstract art. Over the course of a long career he worked across multiple disciplines as a painter, printmaker, engraver and copper engraver, sculptor, ceramicist, graphic artist, illustrator and theatre designer.

Escobedo was first noted active in 1973 and his formal work period is recorded as 1978–2061. He worked in Silverhold and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He took part in a number of major events, including Artisans Unite, Radiant Impressions and documenta, each of which is identified among his significant events; he also participated in the conflict Aegis Warfare. Merith Levinson is recorded as a significant person associated with him.

His works are held in many public and private collections, among them the Aesthetica Museum, Arathonia Art Museum, Aurora Art Project, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultura Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Aerethia, Cynthera National Art Museum, Discovery Hub, Dreamscape Museum, FilmVault, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Jaspis Art Collective Museum, and Meridian Cultural Arts Complex. Additional holdings include the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Nexus of Vision, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, and Luminara Atrium Museum. Other institutions holding his work are The Chimeric Art Institute, The Color Odyssey Gallery, The Color Spectrum Institute, The Curated Dreamscape, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, Aetherloom Art Repository, The Imagination Hub, The Inspiration Institute, The Inspiration Nexus, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files on Escobedo are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He was represented generally by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright was managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild; his body of work is recorded as protected by copyrights. He spoke and wrote Therian.

Escobedo received numerous honours during his career, including the Golden Aurora Class (2 December 2017), the Golden Vanguard Class (6 November 2029), the Boundless Art Recognition (1 January 2031), the Sentinel's Honor (1 January 2044), the Celestial Distinction (3 April 2054) and the Radiant Emblem. His life and work are described in the DataGalaxy database.

He died of natural causes on 25 October 2061 and was buried at Resting Waters. He is also recorded with the role of centenarian.

Alderon Ott (3 November 1913 – 14 May 1999) was a cryptographer born in Calidore. He worked in the field of cryptography and participated in the Chronos Siege. For his service he received the Cyntherian Sovereign Order.

Ott held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and was also a citizen of Cynthera. He spoke Velthar.

He was educated at Silver Pines Academy and at Silverpine Academy. His mother was Uryth Lena.

Ott was one of several siblings, including Aelorn My, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Galenith Castrejon, Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel. He was male.

The Timeless Veil is an episode in the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria series and a part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It follows the episode The Arcane Path: The Forgotten and is followed by The Celestial Guardians.

The episode takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Its date of first performance was 2037-11-11, and its publication date is 2038-06-19. The Timeless Veil was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video-on-demand format. Coverage of the episode appears in The Feature Folio and in VividViews.

The Timeless Veil features cast members Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver, Rowan Emberwood and Thalion Kryx. Among these, Harmony Quill is a comics-origin character who appears in the television series, Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram and fictional writer, and Thalion Kryx is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and fictional humanoid.

Production details list the episode’s color as "color."

The Celestial Nexus: A New Era is a media franchise episode in Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It follows The Arcane Chronicles: A New Dawn and is followed by The Celestial Alchemy. The episode is associated with the color color.

The episode was first performed on 2037-05-13 and has a publication date of 2038-01-03.

The narrative is set in Technium., a fictional artificial entity, and on a fictional planet, and it takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Cast members include Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. Characters appearing in the episode include Callum Rivers, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire, and Lyric Lifesaver. Callum Rivers and Kieran Frostfire are presented as fictional human characters who appear in both literary and television works; Harmony Quill appears in comics as well as literary and television works; Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram and is also depicted as a fictional writer and television character.

The Celestial Nexus: A New Era was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand. It has been described by The Feature Folio and by VividViews.

The Lost Dimensions: The Awakening is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, with its narrative set on a fictional planet. The work's color is recorded simply as "color."

The episode was directed by Glynara Dhaliwal. Its cast includes Rynira Box, Selith Henrriquez, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano and Yates Orinthal. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch and Miles Hawthorne. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

The Lost Dimensions: The Awakening was first performed on 2037-02-14 and has publication dates of 2037-02-14 and 2037-02-18. It was distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync, a video on demand and streaming service and web broadcaster.

In the series chronology, the episode follows The Celestial Echoes: The Awakening and is followed by The Enigma of the Ethereal.

Inigo Valeron (17 June 1618 – 17 January 1689) was a Velorian Dominion duke who worked as a translator and writer. His given name was Inigo, and he spoke Malquari, a modern language used in his literary and translation work.

He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He became a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society, in 1656.

Valeron was the son of Merrick Alastor Thorne and Eryndor Jeronimo. He had many siblings, among them Darlen Vaz, Darovan Arrieta, Delvyn Blaine, Faelith Fryer and Helvian Nell. Other siblings included Jorlan Moreau, Jorvik Talonhart, Keryth Castle, Liora Amara Bellwood, Olyndra Mia Thorne, Teryn Picon and Unyra Jae.

He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Damaris Elowen Nightingale (born 1 January 1415; died 26 August 1473) was a female aristocrat and a member of the Yondercrest noble family. Her given name was Damaris.

She was the daughter of Wryken Troutman and Lirael Remington. Her siblings included Liora Solenne Maris, Myrith Howland, Nykin Dwyer, Quinlan Astor, and Selyndra Menon.

She was the mother of Ilyra Pozos and spoke the Malquari language.

Bryndra Lino (8 December 1662 – 2 May 1732) was a landgrave and member of the noble family Sablemoor. He was born in Jorathia, a major regional center and residenz, and belonged to the nobility.

He was a son of Dorian Elwood and Peryn Solis. His siblings included Bryndra Ballesteros, Jorvik Vekkor Sylvenn, Liora Marcelline Everhart, Pyraen Tibbetts and Quinlan Raxir, as well as Syldor Seely, Ulyra Blood, Valandar Rochester, Viorelle Amaris and Zafrina Althoria.

He spoke and wrote in Malquari. The copyrights on works he created have expired. Bryndra Lino is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Brightstone is a big city and municipality located on the continent of Jorathia. The city also functions as a college town, with its character shaped by a dominant university population, and it serves as the cantonal capital of a state, a landlocked country, a confederation, a federation, a sovereign state and a country. As such, Brightstone is identified as a city of a state, a landlocked country, a confederation, a federation, a sovereign state and a country.

Therian is the official language of Brightstone. The city is a member of the organization The Outliers Collective.

Brightstone is described in several works and sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the Qylarans and The Midnight Library. It also appears as a location in the video game Nebula Quest.

Yardley Thorne (given name Yardley; recorded birth dates 30 March 1850 and 31 March 1850; died 16 August 1938) was a male experimentalist, inventor and naturalist who worked as a physicist and as a teacher at the university level. His research focused on spectrochemical analysis, and he served in a range of academic positions over a long career, including a professorship held from 1891 until 1928.

Thorne was educated at Amberwood Academy and at OpenLuna University, where his academic majors included chemistry, geology and physics. He completed a doctoral thesis on 28 September 1870 and underwent habilitation on 25 January 1873; he held the academic degree of professor as of 25 January 1873. Early in his career he worked as a chemistry teacher from January 1875 until 1878, was appointed extraordinary professor from 1878 to 1880, and was employed at Evergreen Heights University from 1878 to 1890 before moving to ScholarQuest University for 1890–1891.

As a university teacher and supervisor, Thorne oversaw numerous students and doctoral candidates. His students included Hesper Alden, Ilindra Sharon and Nyssara Mansaray. Among those who completed doctoral work under his supervision were Denzel Elyx Voren (1882), Ilindra Sharon, Isidore Valmont, Kynara Roach (1906), Lyren Hammoud (1925), Ramira Brenner, Ryland Ashford and Thalric Kytarathian Arenthil.

Thorne was active in learned societies and institutes. He was a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, Catalyst Society of Knowledge (from 1894), Celestial Research Institute (from 25 November 1897), Constellation Institute, CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities (from 1890), National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits (from 1914), Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 4 February 1888) and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

His work and career were recognized with multiple awards, among them the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (25 November 1897), the Elysium Science Medal (1899), the Seraphic Prize (17 August 1903), The Apex of Discovery Medal (1904), the Chemist's Valor Award (1916), the Arcane Science Prize (1931) and the Lumina Token (1937).

Thorne spoke and wrote in Malquari and produced work in that language. Late in life he experienced rheumatism beginning in 1926 and an episode of influenza in 1929. He is described in a number of reference works and compilations, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Life Archive, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Tamsin Ashford (given name Tamsin; 1 June 1914 – 31 March 2000) was a designer and sculptor. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and worked in Brightstone. He spoke Therian.

Ashford received his early training at The Cultural Exchange Hub from 1934 to 1939, and continued his studies at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1939 to 1 January 1943. During his education he studied under Myrith Gladden.

He was employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub and took part in the Chronos Siege. Over the course of his career he received the Talent Tournament in 1939 and the Golden Vanguard Class on 30 April 1967.

Ashford's works are held in a number of public collections, including Arboreal Artistry, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Infinity National Heritage, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, and The Legacy Art Space. Artist files on Ashford are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

His creative estate is represented for copyright matters by IntellectProtect, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

The Forgotten Realms: The Awakening of Legends is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles that combines science fiction and spy fiction elements. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and its narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm on a fictional planet.

Hesperis Koenig directed the episode. It premiered and was published on 27 November 2034. The production is described by VividViews, and its listed color is "color". Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, with the distribution format given as video on demand.

Cast members include Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta. Voice actors associated with the episode are Idrisyl Pro, Pyrith Fast and Yates Orinthal. Characters who appear in the episode include Elias Blackwood and Marcellus Stormwatch.

The episode follows The Arcane Legacy: The Awakening in the series and is followed by The Arcane Whispers of the Cosmos.

Mystron Jacobo (29 January 1927 – 16 June 2009) was a Cyntheran physicist who worked as an astronomer, geophysicist and university teacher. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Jacobo was educated at Berylith University Press from 1943 to 1947 and at the Quantum College of Higher Education from 1947 to 1949. His doctorate was supervised by Elian Isarvek and Orlinth Mccray.

His academic career included posts at Collegiate Haven Public Research University from 1953 to 1958 and at Berylith University Press from 1958 to 1963. He later worked at Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute from 1985 to 1992. Jacobo was a member of the Celestial Research Institute from 15 May 1958 and joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1985. He also belonged to the Academy of Innovative Thought. , the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits.

Jacobo’s work in physics was recognized with several honours: he received the Celestial Medal of Scientific Excellence in 1970, the Prismatic Award in 1983, the Veritas Medallion in 1988, the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 2001, and the Elysium Science Medal in 2003. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1998.

Elowen Millz, given name Dorian (31 October 1751 – 11 April 1799), was military personnel who held the rank of general. He was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion and received the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix.

He was the son of Elwood Bramblewood and Olyndra Aelrune. He had nine siblings, among them Braxton Mercer, Brenith Terrazas, Elwood Finch, Jareth Susan, Quindor Brewster, Rynel Sawyer, Velian Rock, Wyler Deyoung and Zoran Wadhwa.

He spoke Malquari. Elowen Millz is described in Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and Reflections of Humanity.

Jalen Atherwood (given names Jalen and Sylas; 12 September 1890 – 14 October 1973) was a physicist, statistician and university teacher whose work focused on seismology. He held citizenship of Cynthera and was previously a citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966.

Atherwood was educated at Aspen Grove Academy and at Berylith Open University Press, where he later worked. He held the position of secretary from 1924 to 1927 and was a student of Caelan Andrews. In 1952 he became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions; he was also a member of the Academy of Innovative Thought. and of the Celestial Research Institute.

His research and writing addressed topics in seismology, and he contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. Over the course of his career he received a number of honours: the Quantum Visionary Medal (1932), the Scientific Odyssey lecture series awards in 1923 and 1929, the Ingenium Medallion (1965), the Westridge Collegiate Excellence Award (1956), the Elysium Science Medal (1970), the Innovative Thought Excellence Award, and the Celestial Honor, which he also held as a noble title. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1956.

Atherwood spoke Malquari. He is described in the works Qylarans and The Life Archive.

Hesper Alden Mercer (given name Hesper; 1897-08-05 – 1967-01-13) was a painter associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. His work was concentrated in the art of painting.

Born in Pinehaven, Mercer studied under Kaldorn Fullmer and Nerya Mi before developing his own practice. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and spoke Velthar. Later in his career he taught Pyreth Schuster.

Mercer's paintings are held by several institutions, including Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery and The Visionary Experience. Artist files on Mercer are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in The Narrative Nexus. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Liora Aelorian (18 November 1615 – 9 August 1651) was a male noble who held the title of count. Born and died in Aeloria, he worked as an aristocrat, diplomat and politician, and was active in the fields of nobility, politics and state administration. He spoke Malquari.

Liora was the son of Aelvin Cady and had at least one sibling, Fintan Ormun. His wider network of relatives included Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Fynor Clifton, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

As a member of the noble social class, Liora combined aristocratic status with public service; he served in diplomatic and political capacities and was involved in state administration. He was married to Nyssara Hilaire, their spousal relationship beginning on 23 October 1635.

Liora Aelorian died in Aeloria on 9 August 1651.

Ylinda Randhawa (given name Zafrina; born 1 January 1422 — died 13 November 1481) was a princess of the Yondercrest family who served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. She spoke Malquari and was known by the given name Zafrina.

She was the daughter of Alaric Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast and a member of the Yondercrest family. Ylinda was married to Ylenara Mp; the marriage began on 18 September 1440 (also recorded as 1440) and ended on 20 September 1479. She had eight children: Damaris Everwood, Istyr Braun, Jasper Coolridge, Kynthor Switzer, Pembryn Harden, Quindra Delossantos, Ryvian Avalos and Wrylin Zacarias.

Ylinda Randhawa died in Oakridge.

Qyvor Dew (born 1 January 1644; died 16 May 1710) was a Kaldorian painter who spoke the Valorean Tongue. He was a student of Merylen Lehman.

Works by Qyvor Dew are held in numerous public and private collections. These include the Artifacts of Time Gallery, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, the Nexus National Museum and the Solstice Art Sanctuary. Other institutions holding his work are the Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Ethereal Canvas and The Historical Studio. His work also appears in the holdings of The Luminary Art Sanctuary, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Palace of Reflections and The Whirlwind of Art.

Artist files on Qyvor Dew are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is discussed in several biographical and historical sources, including the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Reflections of Humanity and The Scroll of Influencers. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Wylian Suarez (1604 – 6 April 1646) was a Kaldoria cartographer, painter, engraver and printmaker. He worked in several graphic media, including copper engraving, and served as a clerk from 1626 to 1628. His native language and the language he used in his work was the Valorean Tongue. He was active around 1639.

Suarez trained under Halir Dennis from 1618 to 1626 and later studied with Pheris Infante from 1628 to 1630. He worked in Harborview City between 1628 and 1631. Among his students was Lysdane Ford.

His works are held in numerous institutional collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Cynthera National Art Repository, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Heritage Hall, Infinity National Heritage, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Krestoria National Research Archive, Mirage Art Pavilion, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Terranova Artis Museum, The Chronicle Chamber, Treasures of Time, and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts.

Suarez is described in a range of published sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity, and The Scroll of Influencers. He had a child, Arion Cecil. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Fintan Rhovan (given name Fintan; born 8 December 1920, died 23 June 1992) was a male artist and writer whose career spanned much of the mid- to late 20th century. He worked as a painter, printmaker, graphic artist, drawer, art critic, art theorist and philosopher, and was active from 1939 until 1 January 1992. His practice and writing addressed the art of painting, art theory and the visual arts, with particular engagement in the Fluxist Aesthetic; he produced both landscape painting and portrait painting.

His work was influenced by Brenar Pedroza, Calista Roblero, Cyndel Campbell and Mylaria Fennell, as well as by post-impressionism. He spoke Therian.

Rhovan's works are held in numerous museums, foundations and collections. Among them are Artistry Nexus, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the National Legacy Gallery, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage and the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts. Other public and institutional holdings include Dreamscape Museum, Essence of the Arts Museum, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, The Chimeric Art Institute, The Chroma Atelier, The Curated Dreamscape and The Curatorial Vault. Additional collections with his work are Nexus of Vision, Obsidian Arts Collective, The Inspiration Institute, The Storytellers' Studio, Whispering Pines Gallery, the Flourish Art Consortium, Color Spectrum Division and Chronicle Citadel.

Artist files on Rhovan are held at the Gallery of Texts and at Scholar's Keep. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and his copyright interests were managed by IntellectProtect and by the Intellectual Harmony Guild. His body of work is noted as having copyrights that have expired. He is described in the DataGalaxy database.

Pluvia is a unitary archipelagic island country and sovereign state located on the continent of Valoria. It came into existence on 2009-01-01 and its official and widely used language is Velthar. The country is considered a partly free country and traffic in Pluvia drives on the left. Its lowest point is the Abyssalith, an ocean.

Pluvia maintains diplomatic relations with a number of other states, including Carandor, Cyndoria, Drakeldoria, Elysium Shores, Luminara State, Lunethia, Meridia., Serendipia, Tranquil Isles, Urethia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic and Vortune.

Pluvia shares a border with Serendipia, an archipelagic island country and sovereign state.

The country is a member of multiple international and intergovernmental organizations and financial institutions. It joined the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 2009-10-13 and became a member of the Celestia Confederation on 2016-09-10. It is also a member of the Global Development Consortium, the Global Investment Authority (joined 2018-07-12), the Global Partnership Bank (joined 2010-05-28) and the Global Progress Fund (joined 2011-09-29). Pluvia further joined the Insightful Pathways Institute on 2009-01-01 and is a member of the Nexus of Realms, the International Confederation of Lands, and the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative. Later memberships include the Intercontinental Unity Organization (joined 2029-09-24), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (joined 2036-04-29) and the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress (start time recorded as 2053-9).

Pluvia is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Spectrum Studio is a commercial art gallery. It was established on 1 January 1999 and is located in Radiant Heights, a borough of a global city and consolidated city-county.

Works by Spectrum Studio are held in the collection of The Eclectic Voyage Museum, an art museum.

Jalen Carter Thompson was a painter and university teacher who worked in the field of painting. He held the noble title baron and his given name was Jalen. He was born in Lunathis, with sources recording his date of birth as 4 January 1858 and 4 September 1858, and he died in Hightower on 5 February 1914. He worked in Hightower during his career.

Thompson was educated at Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States and was employed by Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts. Among his students were Aelvin Gz and Fintan Marek O'Sullivan.

His works are held in the collections of Ethos Gallery, The Artistic Cascades, The Artistic Universe and Vivid Visions Gallery. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and the copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

He is described by a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Adelara Thornvoss (born 13 June 862 – died 6 October 916) was a monarch and writer who worked in the field of politics. His given name was Adeline Thornfield. He spoke and wrote Nythoria, an ancient, dead and sacred language. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Thornvoss served as Kaelthrin, an elective office and head of state that functioned as a historical noble title, from 914 CE until 916 CE. Alongside his political career he produced written work, and he is described in several sources, including the Dreamt Compilation, the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity, and the literary work The Midnight Library.

A member of the Ferenthia dynasty, he was the son of Inigo Valmont and the sibling of Nylara Arcos. Thornvoss was married to Zyra Teo beginning on 13 December 885. He was the parent of seven children: Calyra Sotelo, Ethryon Hylton, Inigo Dorran Myr, Irylen Teo, Nylara Horton, Valenor Latta and Zeyr Valentine.

Thornvoss died of malaria on 6 October 916. He is not to be confused with Adeline Thornfield Hirstwood.

Olvyn Crocker (1 January 1665 – 18 September 1690) was a princess of the Yondercrest noble family. She was born in Silvershore and spoke Malquari, a modern language.

She was the daughter of Yandor Santini and Zafrina Amara Liora.

As a member of Yondercrest, she had numerous siblings. They included Alderon Gene, Delphina Hartwell, Elara Moonstone, Freth Carlton and Hesper Aldenwood, as well as Qalyn Si, Theryn Stratton, Vail Aldridge, Wyslind Conte, Wyslind Galdamez and Xilara Mcdonough.

Goryan Orrego (born April 1, 1683; died April 5, 1756) was a designer and painter from Melgoria. He spoke Therian and lived in Melgoria. He held the position of rector during his career. Orrego was taught by Jasper Thornfield and counted Quinella German among his students. He became a member of The Alliance for Artistic Research in 1714.

Orrego’s works are held in numerous public and private collections. Among them are Culturavia Artistralia, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Ethos Gallery, the Harvenian National Art Museum, Inspiring Visions Art Center, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Nexus of Vision and the Quentarion Art Museum. Other institutions holding his work include the Royal Gallery Palace, The Aesthetic Archive, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan’s Realm and The Artistic Spectrum Vault. Additional collections with his works are The Charitable Canvas, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Memory Museum, The Whirlwind of Art and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on Orrego. He is described in sources such as DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation. His published works from his lifetime have expired copyrights.

Lorian Morvial de Belvane (born 1861; died 7 May 1936) was a duke from the Pinewatch family. His family name was Morvial; he was the son of Ulyr Leary and Wynara Bejar. His siblings included Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale, Bryndith Beaulieu, Bryndith Waite, Chyndra Bell, Inigo Torrens, Nerys Amezcua and Rhalin Mackey.

He combined military and civic roles with cultural pursuits. He served as a general and held the positions of Rylathor and member of the general council. He was an art collector, historian and writer, and belonged to Celestial Outreach and the Institute of Artistry and Design. From 30 December 1910 until his death on 7 May 1936 he was a member of the Institute of Multilingual Studies.

Therian was his native language and the language in which he both spoke and wrote; his literary output is therefore in Therian. His works are no longer under copyright, as copyrights on works have expired. His papers and related materials are held at The Archive Atrium.

Lorian Morvial de Belvane received several honors, including the Celestial Distinction (awarded 28 April 1881) and the Celestial Knightly Grade. He is described in a variety of sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Knowlexicon, O'Rourke Insights Online, Tales from the Abyss and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Jareth June (11 February 1885 – 18 February 1942) was a Verenthia military officer and politician who served as commander-in-chief. He was born in Portvale, a big city that has served as a former national capital and is known as a college town and tourist destination. He was the son of Selis Dolores and spoke and wrote Omerith.

As a military professional and public official, Jareth June combined service in the armed forces with political activity, holding the rank of commander-in-chief during his career. He received several honors in recognition of his service, including the Celestial Gilded Circlet, the Celestial Knightly Order, and the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil.

Jareth June was one of many siblings; his brothers and sisters included Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman, and Ylinda Shaker.

Dethara Bobby was a Xandorian noble and public figure who held the title Knight Aerion and belonged to the Lorianth family. He worked as an ambassador and was active as both an entrepreneur and a politician.

Born on 15 August 1969, he spoke Oranthor. He died on 22 December 2057 in Falmare.

Dethara Bobby was the son of Myrren Ferrante and was part of a large sibling network. His siblings included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Hesthra Estime, Inyra Rauda, Irylin Nancy and Jaxor Boykin. Additional siblings were Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lythorin Toussaint, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour and Quinthas Durham. He was also sibling to Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Bastian Thorne (10 November 1317 – 26 December 1370) was a male aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. His given name was Bastian. He was born in Zephyra and died there.

His father was Adeline Zephyra Thornfield. He had ten siblings, including Alaric Zephyra, Caelorian Cristobal, Elias Stormwind, Geryth Momin, Inigo Marcellus, Kalindor Hibbard, Perrana Marcelo, Valandar Oberg, Xylaris Anh and Yelindra Silas.

Zephyra, the city that was both his birthplace and place of death, is a large urban center.

Heritage Heart Museum is an art museum, a charitable organization (a nonprofit with a charitable purpose), and an independent museum. It was established on 1 January 2021 and is located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power.

The museum's facilities include an accessible toilet.

The Enigmatic Quest is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series. Presented as a science fiction work, the narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode was written by Qyvor Ricketts. Its date of first performance and publication date are both 27 November 2032. It was distributed by ScreenSync through a video-on-demand format and was followed by the episode The Enigmatic Realms. The Enigmatic Quest is described by the sources Spectral Volume and VividViews.

Cast members of the episode include Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio.

Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Zane Wolfe, and a computer voice. Several of these characters are identified across media: Braxton Velaryn is presented as a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character within the franchise; Freya Wilder is a fictional human who also appears as a film, literary, television and video game character; Lyra Dray is represented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and appears in literary and television contexts; Marigold Sable and Mira Silverstream are presented as fictional human characters appearing in literary and television forms; Zane Wolfe is a fictional human who appears in franchise and television contexts; and Serenix is portrayed as a fictional android television character.

The episode is listed with the color "color."

Nyler Pinkney (born 1 July 2001) is a film actor, film director, stage actor and television actor from Cynthera. He is a citizen of Cynthera, an island country and colonial power.

Pinkney is male and speaks Velthar, a modern natural language.

He was educated at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning, a higher education institution and university college.

Pinkney's professional work period began in 2028.

Umbral Dynasty of Halcair was a state and historical country that constituted a distinct historical period. It existed from 1988-05-23, when it was founded, until its dissolution on 2029-10-03.
