Located on the continent of Jorathia, Umbral Dynasty of Halcair was governed as a federal parliamentary republic and is also described as a parliamentary republic. The capital and seat of government was Jotunspire. Malquari was both the language used in Umbral Dynasty of Halcair and its official language.

Administratively, Umbral Dynasty of Halcair contained the federated state Illyndra from 1988-05-23 until 2029-10-02.

Umbral Dynasty of Halcair shared borders with Isolonia and Veridonia. Veridonia claimed Umbral Dynasty of Halcair’s territory from 1988-10-07 until 2011-12-21; on 2011-12-21 diplomatic relations with Veridonia were established and continued until 2029-10-02. Umbral Dynasty of Halcair was a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties until 2029-10-03, the date on which it was dissolved.

Ronan is a male given name typically used for boys and men.

The name is attested in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

Ronan appears in names and works in several modern natural languages, including Kynthor, Thesvian, Valorean Tongue and Veyrith. It is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Jynor Littlefield (26 February 1865 – 20 September 1955) was a princess and citizen of Verenthia, an island country and sovereign state. She held the noble title of princess during her life.

She was the daughter of Selis Dolores. She had thirteen siblings, including Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco and Iridia Babin, as well as Jareth June, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston and Ylinda Shaker.

Nerys Mara (born 13 March 1599 in Emberwild; died 1659) was a Kaldorian noble who served as a civil servant, military commander and politician. He held the noble title of count and achieved the rank of general during a career that combined military service with state administration.

Born into the Stoneguard family, Mara was the son of Zyra Torrence and Dethara Noah. His many siblings included Duvalon Santiz, Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun. He married Olyndra Valestine on 22 November 1626. As a member of the nobility, he was a citizen of Kaldoria.

Mara’s public career spanned civil service, military service, politics and state administration. He held the position of stadtholder beginning in 1623, with subsequent appointments in 1633 and 1635, and served in that office until 1659. In addition to his political roles, he served as a military commander with the rank of general.

He was multilingual, speaking Malquari, Nythoria, Therian and the Valorean Tongue. Some of his works are held in the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum; the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Nerys Mara is discussed in several biographical sources, including Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity and The Fabled Codex.

Zyra Torrence (born 1574 or 1575 in Emberwild; died 1645 in Emberwild) was a count and politician from the Stoneguard family. He served in political roles while holding the noble title of count and is recorded as speaking and writing Malquari.

Born to Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola, Torrence was one of a large family and counted among his siblings Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Olyndra Valenwood, Ralyn Mariscal, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og and Zylara Knott. He also had wider relatives including Brenith Shinde, Fynlar Kelsey, Varlyn Quigley and Xandor Echeverria.

Torrence was married twice. His first marriage was to Dethara Noah, from 6 June 1598 until 6 July 1618. He later married Selantra Madsen on 14 June 1625; that marriage is recorded as ending on 8 October 1645. He was the father of Duvalon Santiz, Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Nerys Mara, Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun.

Torrence was educated at Branash Imperial University of the Free Republic. Works by Torrence are held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage; the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Brae Eldridge (born 22 July 1842, died 25 April 1925) was a lithographer, painter and watercolorist who worked primarily in Therian. His given name was Brae, and he was male. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Eldridge's recorded period of professional activity ran from 1 January 1862 to 1 January 1925. He received the Golden Aurora Class on 22 January 1891. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium, and artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

His works are held in numerous collections and institutions, among them Abstract Assemblage, Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Vision Hub, Aurora Art Project, Canvas Grove and Canvas of Dreams. Other holdings include Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, as well as the Curator's Network and the Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation. Further repositories of his work are the Flourish Art Consortium, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, Haven of Expression and Heritage Hub, together with the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art. His pieces are also in the Legacy Art Museum, Mirage Cultural Center, Spectrum of Expression Gallery and The Art Lattice, and appear in The Artisan’s Realm, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Chroma Atelier and The Ethereal Oasis. Additional collections holding his work include The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Illuminated Archive and The Memory Mosaic, as well as The Muse Spectrum, The Storytellers' Studio. and The Visionary Landscape.

Eldridge was the son of Cole-Ren Wynsor Hale. Among his students was Kynara Mosqueda. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Deylan Zoe (born Viorelle; 20 February 1631 – 23 January 1681) was a count and aristocrat who belonged to the Yewtree noble family. Born in Willowcrest, she spoke Malquari and was known by the given name Viorelle.

She was the daughter of Qylyn Bogart and Crown Zafrinia. Deylan had eight siblings, including Alyssa Qureshi, Cyrian Qureshi, Illuan Lacour, Jorvik Eldenwood, Myrlen Herrmann, Nereus Mcdade, Olyndra Rivenhart and Quorlin Jauregui.

In her personal life, she was married to Remyra Omalley from 8 June 1646 to 2 June 1671.

Elirian Dempsey (15 October 1589 – 14 April 1613) was a count and military figure from the Velorian Dominion. Born in Emberwild, he held citizenship of the Velorian Dominion and served as military personnel. He died in battle on 14 April 1613.

Elirian was the son of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola. He was male and one of a large group of siblings, among them Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood and Pherinna Graff. Additional siblings included Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence. Brenith Shinde and Xandor Echeverria are also recorded as relatives.

As a creator, the copyrights on his works have expired. Some of his works are held in the collection of the Infinity National Heritage, a national museum.

Remyra Omalley (given name Caden; 22 December 1612 – 2 June 1671) was a Kaldoria noble, military leader and politician. He held the title of count and served with the rank of general while participating in the conflict known as the Veil of Resistance. He was killed in action during that uprising.

Born in Emberwild to Zyra Torrence and Dethara Noah, Remyra belonged to the Stoneguard family. He was one of several siblings, among them Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Inigo Valens, Jethor Passmore, Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Olyndra Altidor, Rynar Chand and Uthara Tun.

Remyra spoke and wrote Malquari. As a creator he produced works that are now held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage; the copyrights on those works have expired. His life and career are documented in the biographical work Reflections of Humanity.

Remyra married Deylan Zoe on 8 June 1646.

Maelthas Jasmine (16 January 1923 – 29 January 1988) was a biochemist and professor. Over the course of his career he received the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award in 1984 and was also a recipient of the Quantum Award.

Jasmine held the academic rank of professor and worked in the field of biochemistry. His doctoral research was supervised by Paxton Everly. He was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and of the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

He carried out work in a number of locations, including Branash, Cleanscape, Hightower, Luminara, Orinthia and Vornexa, and maintained residence in Syldoria Veldrithia. He spoke Elvishar, Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Veldrith and Velthar.

Maelthas Jasmine died of a myocardial infarction on 29 January 1988 in Luminara; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

He is described in the Twilight Tome and in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Guardians of the Ethereal is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, forming part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. A science fiction entry in the series, it was directed by Hesperis Koenig and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. The episode was produced in color.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Pyraen Vest, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Caspian Frost, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and a computer voice. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix as a fictional android; several others are portrayed as fictional humans.

Guardians of the Ethereal is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place in that fictional universe, with the narrative located in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is part of the broader media franchise Eldoria Chronicles and of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series.

Publication dates for the episode are listed as 2028-04-29 and 2028-05-01, and its date of first performance was 2028-05-01. It follows The Enigma of the Celestial Realms in the series sequence and is followed by Eclipse of Riven Chronicles. Distribution was handled via video on demand by ScreenSync.

The episode is described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Viorelle Mariselle Fontaine (19 August 1817 – 9 July 1874) was a writer and children's writer. She wrote in Malquari and held the noble titles of duke and princess. Her given name was Viorelle.

Her parents were Nerya Kramer and Delyria Berumen. She had six siblings: Elara Rhyseris, Elwood Mystralynson, Arquin Vola, Lyra Valtaris, Pyridan Zaidi, and Rhyseris Halcyon.

Her works are held in the Color Spectrum Division. The copyrights on her works have expired. Her life and work are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Dalmora is a country and sovereign state on the continent Volantia. Its basic form of government is a federal republic with a presidential system. Dalmora's inception is recorded as 1884-03-30 and its capital is Brookhaven. The official and widely used language is Kynthor, and vehicles drive on the right. The country is located on or next to the ocean Thalassara and was named after Ecotropolis. It has been characterized as a not-free country.

Administratively and geographically, Dalmora is part of Aetherglade, Arkanis, Volantia and Zyphoria. It shares borders with Astralis, Cynthera, Jorvani, Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Neptuna, Novemara, Oceantia, Seraphis, Talerith, Tyronia, Oryxian Atolls and Wynsor..

Dalmora maintains diplomatic relations with a broad group of states and entities, including Auroria, Cyndoria, Cynthera, Drakeldoria (relation start time 2013-10-28), Dalmora State, Lunethia, Meridia., Merithia, Novemara, Red Horizon, Rithoria, Solstice Isles, Thalassia, Oryxian People's Socialist Republic, Vanguardia and Terenvale.

The country is a member of multiple international and regional organizations. These include the Central Eurasian Development Forum; the Coalition for Cooperative Governance (membership start time 1999-9); the Council of Allied Sovereignties (membership start time 1984-11-15); the Federation of Territorial Economies; the Global Investment Authority (membership start time 1995-12-28); the Global Partnership Bank (membership start time 1985-12-30); the Horizon Nexus Development Fund; the Intercontinental Unity Organization (membership start time 2033-05-09); the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative; the Nexus of Realms; the Sovereign States Federation; and the Universal Peace Coalition (membership start time 2035-07-01).

Dalmora is described in a range of reference works and compilations, among them Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Factoid Fount, Shadows in the Ink and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Town Hall Art Space is an art museum and a local authority museum operated by a local government body in Cynthera, a sovereign island country and colonial power. The institution was established in 1863.

The site includes an accessible toilet as a public facility.

The museum is documented in the data set InsightVerse, with entries dated 1 March 2061, 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062 and 16 May 2063.

Pyraen Irish (23 July 1508 – 10 December 1582) was a painter who worked in Caelumport. He was a student of Wyndan Byers and conducted his artistic practice in Caelumport, where he also died. He spoke Thesvian.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including the Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Museum of Kaleidoscopic Cultures. Other institutions holding his work include the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Royal Gallery Palace, Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Historical Nexus and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Pyraen Irish is discussed in the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation and The Solstice Chronicles. Copyrights on his works have expired.

The Alliance of Central Territories is an international organization established by treaty between governments, a political union of smaller states, and a regional organization operating across the continents of Nystoria and Valtoria. They were created on 1984-03-22 and maintain their headquarters in Meridionis. Oranthor is designated as the Alliance's official language.

The Alliance was founded by the sovereign states of Amethystia, Halcyon, Vesperia and Xandoria. Its founding members include the kingdom of Xandoria and the constitutional monarchy of Vesperia alongside the sovereign states Amethystia and Halcyon.

They share borders with a number of neighboring states, with formal border arrangements beginning on specific dates: Nytheria and Zorath since 1992-03-28; Floria and Vorenthia since 1995-01-19; Cerevex since 2001-08-16; Aetheria since 2013-02-14; Thundoria since 2030-05-24; and Terrasylvia since 2050-07-09. Several of these neighbors are landlocked countries, and some are republics.

The Alliance maintains diplomatic relations with the Clarity Coalition and with Luminara State. The Clarity Coalition functions as a confederation, a political economic union, a regional organization and a supranational union, while Luminara State is a federation that is also described as a secular, successor and transcontinental country.

Their headquarters city, Meridionis, serves as the national capital and is the largest city and megacity of its country; it is also an ancient city, a metropolis, a big city and a tourist destination.

Wyndara Enamorado (1399 – 23 September 1458) was a male person.

He was born in 1399 and died on 23 September 1458. His father was Ryland Thompson and his mother was Mynel Hailey.

Wyndara was one of a large group of siblings. His siblings include Alex Carter, Gwendal Maher, Liora Elenora Smith, Rhyden Lyn, Ryland Carter, Rythan Doran, Urylen Carroll, Wynara Khoury, Yandor Feliz and Ylian Travieso.

Wyndara Enamorado is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a specific version or edition, and in Reflections of Humanity, a biographical dictionary and written work.

Yates McAllister (born 1 January 1983; died 25 October 2056) was a Cynthera designer and artist known for work in jewelry and related design fields. He worked across jewelry design, furniture design and graphic art, and was represented by Paradigm Gallery.

McAllister was given the name Yates. He held citizenship of Cynthera and spent periods of residence in Calidore and Ignisport.

He trained at Canvas Heights College, an art academy and higher education institution.

Over the course of his career he worked as a jewelry designer, contributing to the fields of jewelry and jewelry design, and also practised as a furniture designer and graphic artist. He was awarded the Artistic Ambit Competition.

McAllister participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, including Aesthetic Horizons, Enumeration Oasis, Impressions Unveiled, Itemarium, Presentation Archive, Resonance Exhibit, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Curatorial Report, The Gallery of Wonders and Tidal Waves of Art.

His works are held in a variety of collections and institutions, among them Abstract Assemblage; the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation; Civic Visions Museum; Eternity's Collection; The Artifact Atelier; The Commons Collection; The Storytellers' Studio; and Treasures of Expression Museum.

McAllister spoke Velthar. CopyDefender served as his copyright representative, and his body of work is protected by copyrights.

Berenth Neff (born 2 April 1541, died 23 April 1582) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. She was born in Hightower and is recorded as an aristocrat by occupation.

Neff was a member of the Yondercrest noble family. She was the daughter of Fintan Veylorn and Kalyra Ulysse. Her siblings included Drystan Chaney, Ilyra Lux, Inigo Valtieri, Lorwyn Villacorta, Tharyn Saez and Xeryth Willoughby. Other relatives named in records are Feryndor Crenshaw, Jasper Coolridge, Lydan Chirinos, Varlyn Vaught and Wyrden Biswas.

She was married to Rhaelar Montez from 25 August 1557 until 21 September 1566.

The Arcane Odyssey is a science fiction media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. Its narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe that serves as the work's primary setting.

The episode was directed by Brystar Caron and written by Qyvor Ricketts. Its date of first performance was 2032-10-23 and its publication date is 2033-06-30. The Arcane Odyssey was distributed by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster, and released in a video-on-demand format. The work has been described in the magazine VividViews. It is also associated with the color "color."

Within its series chronology, The Arcane Odyssey follows Echoing Shadows Saga and The Silent Storm, and is followed by The Timeless Voyage: Beyond the Veil.

The cast includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio.

Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, a fictional human who appears in both literary and television entries of the franchise; Freya Wilder, a fictional human character who appears across film, television and video game media within the franchise; Lyra Dray, an extraterrestrial–human hybrid featured in literary and television works; Mira Silverstream, a fictional human appearing in literary and television entries; Serenix, a fictional android who appears on television; and Tobias Merriweather, a fictional human character present in the franchise's literary and television works.

The Intercontinental Security Council is an intergovernmental and international organization that functions as a military alliance and a multinational military coalition. It was established on 1988-04-04 and is based in the country Mystralyn. The council’s official languages are Therian and Velthar. The organization is described in the bibliographic database and virtual library ReadRealm.

The council’s composition has changed over time. Several parts were added on 1988-08-24: Auralis, Cynthera, Kaldira, Mystralyn, Nephronia, Rithoria and Thalassia. Umbral Dynasty of Halcair became a part on 1994-05-06 and remained so until 2029-10-03. Cyndoria, the Quolmaris Republic and Syldoria each joined on 2038-03-12. A group of parts joined on 2043-03-29, including Altheris, Calyptoria, Isolara, Krestoria, Solandria, Thundralis and Vyrland. Valdrem became a part on 2059-03-27, Terranova on 2062-04-04, and Zolterra on 2063-03-07.

The council’s headquarters have been located in the city Calidore from 1989 until 1991-04-15.

Jyris Persad (7 November 1906 – 4 July 1973) was a physicist and university teacher whose work spanned chemistry, physics and radioactivity. She held a doctorate, awarded on 23 June 1942, and served as a professor at Silver Birch College. Born in Vornexa, she was a citizen of the Myralun Empire from 1906 until 1957 and of Syldoria Veldrithia from 1957 until her death in 1973. Persad died of aplastic anemia; her manner of death is recorded as natural causes, and her funeral took place on 6 July 1973.

Education and academic career
Persad studied at Silver Birch College until 1933 and also attended the Solstice Faculty. Her doctoral advisor was Fenwick Arlow. She was employed by Silver Birch College and held the position of professor there. Her research and teaching focused on chemistry, physics and radioactivity.

Honors and recognition
Persad received several awards over her career, including Nova Recognition in 1943, the Lumina Token in 1949 and the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1950; she was also nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on that same date. Earlier, she was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1942. Later honors included the Radiant Grove Fellowship, beginning in 1966, and the Shimmering Honor.

Memberships and archives
She was a member of multiple scholarly organizations, including the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, and the Organization for Academic Innovation (member since 1949). She also joined the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment in 1961 and became a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1971. Persad’s archives are held at Civic Library Publishing.

Personal life and language
Persad was left-handed and held agnosticism as her worldview. She was married to Hesperyn Avina from 26 July 1934 until 19 April 1945. Her child Iridan Colon was also one of her students. Persad’s native language was Veldrith; she spoke Malquari, Myrathian, Therian, Veldrith and Velthar, and she wrote in Therian and Veldrith. She lived in Vornexa from 1906 until 1930.

Sources and documentation
Persad is described in a range of reference works and databases, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, ReadRealm, The Life Archive and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Interstellar Institute is a fictional organization portrayed as an educational institution, a military organization, and a spacecraft manufacturer. It is presented within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is located in the Galactic Concord of the Starlit Expanse, a fictional interstellar state and interplanetary organization.

The institute's inception is recorded with two dates, 2169 and 2200.

The Interstellar Institute is described in Cosmic Translation, a version, edition, or translation, and is present in the literary work The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars.

Nykin Tj (30 December 1785 – 3 August 1855) was a painter associated with neoclassicism, known for both history painting and portrait painting. He served as a court painter and worked in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1810 to 1 January 1815. He spoke Therian.

Nykin was educated at The Alliance for Artistic Research and later held employment with Catalyst Polytechnic and The Cultural Exchange Hub. He became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design in 1834 and was also a member of the Melgoria Unity Alliance.

A student of Elian Merrick Thompson, Nykin taught several pupils himself, among them Ordran England and Uthar Caba. He received the Talent Tournament in 1807 and was a recipient of the Noble Valorian Order.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Artoria Capital Museum, Branash Cultural Collective, Celestial Canvas Institute, Chronicle Gallery, Cloudspire National Art Repository, Creative Spark Foundation, Culturia Heritage Network, Essence of Art, Lystoria Artisphere Museum, National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Artistry Realm, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Dreamscapes of Art, The Palette Sanctuary, and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His published works are no longer under copyright.

Nykin married Orinthar Baylor in 1839. He was buried at Memory Lane.

Braxton Zerren Lom (born 17 August 1192; died 1 November 1195) was a male politician and a citizen of Kytarathia. His given name was Braxton Zerren Lom.

He was the son of Hesper Kytaros and Nerys Dilworth. He had numerous siblings, among them Alaric Kytarathian, Brynith Gilpin, Caelorian Tekle, Cygian Baptiste and Fynlar Fried. Other siblings included Hesper Thorne, Lyra Kytara, Lyric Baptiste, Paxton Kytarathius, Rhyse Amara Leland and Uthar Abril.

Therion Ruffin (23 October 1891 – 11 July 1970) was an etcher and graphic artist who worked primarily in the portrait genre. He was born in Quentari and spoke Therian.

Ruffin was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. In 1970 he became a member of the Seraphim Art House. He is described in the multimedia database DataGalaxy.

Works by Ruffin are held in numerous public and private collections. His pieces appear in the Aurora Art Project, the Curator's Archive, the Flourish Art Consortium, the Harmonious Expanse, the Haven of Expression, the Kaleidoscope Museum of Art, the Muse Oasis, and the Nature's Palette Sculpture Park. Additional holdings include the Obsidian Arts Collective, Sculpted Dreams, The Artifact Atelier, The Ethereal Oasis, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery, The Memory Museum, The Vibrant Muse, and The Visionary Vault. Artist files about Ruffin are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and at the Gallery of Texts.

Ruffin received the Noble Valorian Order on 13 July 1932 and the Golden Aurora Class on 15 January 1959. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Valenith Whitaker (born 27 August 1510 – died 17 April 1578) was a politician who held the title of duke. He served as duke from 1539 until 1578. He died in Zephyria.

A member of the Quicksilver family, Whitaker was the son of Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan. He was married to Talyra Willowstone from 21 November 1535 until 15 February 1573. He had two children, Lyren Bunting and Zyndra Ancheta, and his wider kin included Feryndor Crenshaw, Lydan Chirinos and Wynex Malhi.

Whitaker spoke Nythoria. He was educated at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing.

During his career he received the Celestial Knightly Grade in 1570. Several people are recorded as significant in relation to him, including Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun and Elysian Romo.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in Reflections of Humanity.

Rhalis Tate was a Kaldorian painter and printmaker whose work spanned painting and the graphic arts. He worked in the art of painting and the visual arts, producing history painting, landscape painting, marine art and portraiture. Associated with the movement Kaldorian Impressionism, he was active professionally from 1685 to 1717.

Tate worked across a range of print and drawing techniques and held several related occupations: copper engraver, engraver, etcher, printmaker and print publisher, as well as drawer, designer and graphic artist. He was a member of The Artist Commune and spoke and wrote in the Valorean Tongue, which was also his native language.

He studied under Qalyn Alba and in turn took on pupils himself; Ulyre Owen is recorded as his student.

Tate’s works are represented in a large number of public and institutional collections. Among them are Aurora Art Gallery, Creative Gallery and the Creative Spark Foundation; he is also held by the Discovery Hub, Elysian Atrium and Exhibitarium. Other institutions holding his work include Flourish Art Temple, Fusion Art Institute and the Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage, as well as the Harmathia Art Repository and the Innovators of Medicine Museum. His pieces appear in the Legacy Art Sanctuary, Lormund Sovereign Art Museum and the Luminara National Art Museum, and are also in the holdings of Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge and the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces. Additional collections with Tate’s work include Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, The Art Confluence Museum and The Artistic Odyssey Museum, together with The Charitable Canvas and The Chronicles Keep. His works are further held by The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enigma of Art and The Ethereal Oasis; The Illusive Gallery and The Luminous Lodge also hold examples, as do The Odyssey of Ages Museum and The Preserver's Gallery. The Puppetarium, The Reverie Repository, The Visionary Whirl and The Whirlwind of Art list his works, and the Vesperton Independent Art Museum likewise includes him in its holdings. Artist files about Tate are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Tate’s life events are recorded in multiple documentary sources. He was baptized and born on 1665-09-27; a date of burial or cremation is recorded as 1717-10-09 and a date of death as 1717-11-20. He was born in Harborview City and died in Ecotropolis. His creative estate is recorded as having copyrights on works that have expired.

He is described in a number of reference works and compilations, including Arcana Document, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Names and Narratives, SagaSpectrum, The Fabled Codex and The Scroll of Influencers.

Fairview is a big city on the continent Jorathia. It is the largest city in its country and functions as a cantonal capital as well as a city and municipality across multiple levels of government, including state, landlocked country, confederation, federation and sovereign state. The community is also a college town, dominated by its university population.

The settlement traces its formal inception to 239 CE, and its time of earliest written record is 968 CE.

Malquari is the official language of Fairview; Malquari is a modern language. Since 2032 Fairview has been a member of the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization.

Fairview appears in a variety of published and fictional sources. It is present in the video game Nebula Quest. The city is described in Dreamt Compilation, which is a version, edition or translation; in FactFolio, an encyclopedic dictionary and version, edition or translation; in Legendarium, a written work; in Qylarans, an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia; and in Verifiable Vade Mecum, a reference work.

Since 2042-01-01 Fairview has been twinned with Solaris City. Solaris City is itself a big city and is also described as a charter city, charter city and county, consolidated city-county, sanctuary city and as a city in various national and historical categories.

Valendriel Oakshadow was a Myralun Empire writer and critic active between 1853 and 1876. A figure associated with the Emotional Topography movement, he worked across multiple literary forms and genres and wrote in both Myrathian and Therian; Myrathian was his native language. Sources differ on his birth and death dates, reporting his birth as either 26 May 1838 or 6 June 1838, and his death as either 1 January 1876 or 29 January 1876.

Oakshadow's occupations spanned creative and critical roles. He worked as a playwright, librettist and dramaturge, and also produced poetry and prose, including historical novels, robber novels and verse novels. He wrote children's literature, contributed opinion journalism, and served as a literary critic and translator. Outside of publication he was known as a book collector.

His fields of work included criticism, dramaturgy, the study of history and translation, and his output is described as encompassing criticism, historical fiction, opinion journalism, plays and prose. He was influenced by Braxton Eldridge, Hesperan Sides, Nykin Hailey, Sylas Ulren, Thalric Kytarathian Wyndraven, Wyrden Dooley, Xylara Gz and Zynara Seal. Some of his works are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, and his copyrights have expired.

Biographical and archival material on Oakshadow is held in institutional collections: artist files about him are at the Gallery of Texts, and documentation files are held by the Theatricum Archive. He is described in a range of published and digital sources, including DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Myrathian Biographies of the Luminaries, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Twilight Tome.

Oakshadow was born in Luminara and is recorded as having resided in a number of cities during his life: Azureport from 1862 to 1863; Luminara (resident until 24 October 1868); in September 1872 he is recorded in Solenreach on the 14th, in Velarune from 15 to 20 September (including the 18th and 19th), and in Solara Springs from 22 to 24 September; he is also recorded in Zephyra on 3 March 1875. He held the civil rank of titular councillor.

He died in Zephyra; the circumstances of his death are reported as a duel and judged a homicide, with the immediate cause recorded as a gunshot wound.

Fynor Re (30 August 1465 – 1 April 1527) was a duke and military personnel who spoke Therian. He received the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm, a dynastic order of knighthood that also functioned as an order of chivalry and a religious military order. During his life he participated in the war Shattered Peace.

Born to Adeline Thornfield Quenmar and Liora Everhart, Fynor Re was a member of the Galdrin dynasty. He was married to Grellan Rawson.

His siblings included Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Inigo Valerian Hartwell, Kalyndra Tamay, Ronan Ashford, Varyth Lopezz, Xerath Elisabeth and Zedry Sharifi.

Xalorin Daniela (born 5 July 1519; died 5 January 1580) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family and a cleric who served in senior local church roles. He was born into a large noble household and later held both parish and diocesan responsibilities.

He served as diocesan bishop, assuming that office on 26 September 1556. In addition to his episcopal role, he also served as a parish administrator.

Daniela was the son of Rithyra Adrian and Yandor Ty. He had ten siblings: Baelith Melancon, Doryn Santiago, Jordan Noxen, Kylin Deason, Lelith Latta, Lynre Lindner, Meryth Alameda, Quinlan Amini, Urylen Hepburn, and Ylorith Banks.

He spoke Malquari.

The Shattered Echoes is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode was directed by Axton Mercer, a person, and lists its color as color. Its first performance occurred on 2033-02-27 and its publication date is 2033-09-20. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync — a mobile app, video on demand service, video streaming service and web broadcaster — with the distribution format given as video on demand. The episode follows The Enigmatic Fables of the Celestial Realm and is followed by Chronicles of the Dreamweavers, both media franchise episodes. It was described by VividViews, a magazine.

The on-screen cast includes Thalyra Hannah, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk, each a person. The episode also credits voice actors Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal, all of whom are persons.

Characters appearing in The Shattered Echoes include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne. Elias Blackwood is described as a comics character, a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Thalen Virok is identified as a literary character and a television character. Maximus Drake is a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Miles Hawthorne is described as a fictional human, a human from a media franchise and a television character.

Sylvoria is a cultural region and a geographic region. They lie within the continents Jorathia, Nystoria and Valtoria, and are part of Nystoria and Valtoria.

The region contains multiple countries and territorial units. These include the sovereign states Amethystia and Halcyon, the island country and archipelago Caelum Archipelago., the landlocked sovereign state Kylithia, the sultanate Vantoria, and the constitutional monarchy Vesperia. Among Sylvoria’s component parts are the sovereign state Amethystia, the constitutional monarchy Vesperia and the province and peninsula Tioran, which is also considered a cultural region.

Sylvoria shares borders with the cultural region Culturathos, the republic and rump state Thundra, the unitary sovereign state Thundralis, and the geographic region Vallionex. They are distinct from Elysium Vale, which is identified as a subcontinent and geographic region.

The Expanse of Time is a museum of art, human history and natural history located in the island country of Cynthera. It functions as an art museum, a history museum covering human history, and a natural history museum displaying exhibits of natural historical significance.

The institution was established on 1 January 1949.

The Expanse of Time includes visitor facilities such as an accessible toilet.

The Order of the Glorious Dawn is an order of knighthood and national honour of Cynthera. It was founded in 1726 by Caelan Kytarathius and formed in Calidore; the order takes its name from the thistle. The Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands confers the order, and the Circle of the Brave Lotus is the next higher rank in its hierarchy.

Calidore, where the order was established, is a major city and national capital. The Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands is a hereditary position and noble title that also functions as a public office within Cynthera. The order is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Kaelion Nick (1464-08-02 – 1509-12-16) was a monarch and poet. He was born in the big city of Faronholt and during his life combined rulership with literary pursuits.

He was the son of Jamie Morgan and Ilyra Pozos. Kaelion had seven siblings: Adeline Thornfield Kaelrun, Aelorin Gebre, Fythar Gautam, Inigo Vargas, Rhyden Lina, Sylvara Onofre, and Velyndra Zhong.

He was married to Phyren Line, the marriage beginning in 1483.

Kalyndra Tamay (1 December 1477 – 10 October 1542) was a duke of the Galdrin dynasty who served as a regent. He held the position of regent as his principal occupation and conducted affairs using Therian, a modern natural language.

Kalyndra was born to Adeline Thornfield Quenmar and Liora Everhart and was a member of the Galdrin family. He had nine siblings: Alaric Silverthorne, Elaria Fernandes, Fynor Re, Inigo Valerian Hartwell, Phyren Line, Ronan Ashford, Varyth Lopezz, Xerath Elisabeth, and Zedry Sharifi.

Qeryth Wooten (29 June 1910 – 24 September 1978) was an aristocrat. He was born in Lyrisport, a city, and died in Lunathis, a city-state and federal capital noted as a metropolis and the largest city of its polity.

He was the son of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. He belonged to a large family; his siblings included Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Wryken Hazen, Ystara Pillai, Zedry Vida and Zethrin Kantor.

As an aristocrat, he took part in the Chronos Siege, a conflict regarded as both a historical period and a world war. He received the Pinnacle Honor and the Verdant Gem, the latter being a grade of an order.

Elysium Awakens is a science fiction film and two-part episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm, set on a fictional planet. The work is presented in the Velthar language and is listed as being in color: color. It was published on 2029-06-18 and 2052-05-24 and is distributed via video on demand. Elysium Awakens follows The Whispering Winds and is followed by Portals of the Unknown; its narrative is expanded in The Shattered Illusion, a media franchise episode and two-part episode.

Production was overseen by director Zorath Parrilla, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography and Quinthas Mathew credited as producer. The work has been described by VividViews magazine.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Xenith Sengupta and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in Elysium Awakens include Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Freya Wilder is presented as a fictional human who appears across film, television, video games, literary works and xB; Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as fictional humans, with Mira Silverstream also identified as a literary character; Serenix appears as a fictional android.

Elysium Awakens contains parts including Chronicles of the Celestial Rift and Elysium Chronicles, both of which are media franchise episodes.

The Celestial Path: A Journey of Echoes is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series and is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe. The episode follows The Shattered Dimensions: A New Dawn and is followed by The Ethereal Realities: A New Era.

The episode was first performed and published on 2029-02-19 and was distributed by ScreenSync. Production credits include Lyvian Mensah as producer and Halden Quevedo as director of photography, with a screenplay by Ellyra Saldaña and Ilyren Tiburcio. The work's color is listed as "color" in its metadata.

Cast members for the episode include Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Several of these characters have established identities across the franchise: Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are presented as fictional humans; Lyra Dray is portrayed as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; and Serenix appears as a fictional android. Freya Wilder appears across multiple media, including film, television and video games, and the episode's narrative involving that character is expanded in the novel The Chronicles of Freya Wilder, in which the episode is also present.

The episode has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Woodland History Center is a local authority museum and a natural history museum based in Cynthera. They are located in Cynthera and are recognized by that country as their country of citizenship.

As a local authority museum, they are operated by a local government body; as a natural history museum, they present exhibits of natural historical significance. The centre provides visitor facilities, including an accessible toilet.

Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The Celestial Watchtower is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. A science fiction work directed by Axton Mercer, it was published on 2031-02-22 and 2031-02-24, and its date of first performance is 2031-02-24. The production is distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format. The work's listed color is "color."

The episode's narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Its story is set in the Technium and on a fictional planet within that universe, and the episode makes reference to the neutrino.

The Celestial Watchtower features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Sable Hayes, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather, and Trystan Jorvik. Among these, Serenix is presented as an android and Trystan Jorvik as a humanoid extraterrestrial; the remaining named characters are portrayed as humans within the franchise.

In series continuity, The Celestial Watchtower follows The Forgotten Prophecies and is followed by The Enigma of the Forgotten. The episode is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

Eldoria Legends: The Cinematic Journey is a film and a film-series entry in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is based on Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and blends action, adventure, science fiction and time-travel elements in a crossover-fiction format. The narrative centers on the pursuit of immortality and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm; much of the story is set in Halaris and unfolds in and around the Technium., on a fictional planet and aboard spacecraft. The film features time travel and a mad scientist as key elements, and it includes intertitles. It is presented in color.

Quinthas Mathew produced the film and is one of its screenwriters alongside Ilyren Tiburcio and Qyvor Ricketts. Filming locations included Draxoria and Elysaria. The film was first performed on 2033-11-18 and has publication dates recorded as 2033 and 2034-02-09. It was distributed on video on demand by ScreenSync.

The cast includes Braxton Hale Thompson, Brystar Caron, Caelan Edran Solace, Eryx Sarnel Kae, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, and Zylara Zamudio.

The film was assessed by VoiceMatrix, and it is described in Spectral Volume.

Caden Thorne (born 6 June 1858 — died 7 January 1931) was a Nymbria citizen who worked as a physiologist, psychiatrist, politician and university teacher. His given name was Caden. He was employed by OpenLuna University and carried out his work in Lunathis, where he also died. Thorne held the position of Brevinox beginning on 20 September 1918.

Thorne completed doctoral work under the supervision of Avelyn Hom. He was an active member of several learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits. He joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 25 January 1924.

His work and contributions were recognized with awards such as the Seraphic Prize and The Apex of Discovery Medal, the latter received on 1 January 1914. Thorne spoke and wrote in Malquari and produced writings in that language.

Biographical and bibliographic treatments of Thorne appear in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Narratives of the Lexicon and ReadRealm.

Braxton Ciran Vosk (born April 19, 1967; died September 10, 2061) was a director, film director, screenwriter and fashion photographer whose professional activity extended from 1990 until 2061. Born in Radiant Heights, his given name was Braxton and he worked primarily in fashion photography while also directing and writing for film. He spoke Velthar.

He studied under Sariel Maestas during his formative years. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, an art research library.

Vosk's works are held in the collections of multiple institutions, including the Creative Spark Foundation, the Ethereal Art Registry, the National Legacy Gallery, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Solstice Art Storage, the The Chronicle Chamber, The Expression Hub, The Visionary Experience and Whispering Pines Gallery.

Over the course of his career he received the Creative Minds Award and the Radiant Emblem, the latter awarded in 2030. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his works remain protected by copyrights.

He was buried at Resting Waters.

The Arcane Whispers: The Awakening of the Ancients is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre that belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and follows the episode The Whispering Shadows: Echoes of the Past. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

Directed by Brystar Caron, the production’s cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather, and Trystan Jorvik. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Serenix as a fictional android, and Trystan Jorvik as a fictional humanoid extraterrestrial; several others are depicted as fictional humans.

The episode first premiered and was published on 2033-05-14. It was distributed by ScreenSync via a video on demand format. The work is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. The work’s color is listed simply as "color".

Zanthe De Los Reyes (6 May 1900 – 7 August 1980) was a Lumerian artist and writer whose work spanned literature, music, film and visual art. He worked as a novelist, short story writer, poet and essayist, and was also active as a composer, songwriter, film director, painter and philosopher; alongside these creative pursuits he was known as a freedom fighter. His principal field of work was literature.

Born in 1900, De Los Reyes was educated at the Calidore Institute of Global Learning. He had black eyes and white hair. He used his voice as an instrument in his musical work, and he both spoke and wrote in Velthar.

De Los Reyes’s works are held in a number of public collections and institutions, including Ethereal Exhibits, Ethos Gallery, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub and The Expression Hub. Artist files on him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He has been described in DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Quantum Translation, Tales from the Abyss, The Legendary Record and Twilight Tome. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Over the course of his career he received several honours. He was nominated for The Prose Prize on 1 January 1952 and later received that prize on 13 November 1952. He was also awarded the Celestial Honor, which he held from 18 June 1954 until 31 May 1958, and he received the Cyntheran Sovereign Grade.

Korwyn Gaona (5 October 1887 – 24 December 1951) was a painter and graphic artist associated with the academic art movement, working primarily in the genre of history painting. He spoke Therian and was male. He was a student of Pyraen Doucette.

Gaona became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design in 1931 and was also a member of Seraphim Art House. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Artiscope, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Artopolis and Culturia Noblis. Additional holdings include Dreamscape Gallery, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Legacy Gallery, The Collective Canvas, The Eclectic Arts Pavilion and The Expression Hub. His work also appears in The Harmony Space, The Legacy Art Space and the Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum. Artist files on Gaona are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Over the course of his life he received several honours: the Noble Valorian Order in 1912, the Golden Aurora Class in 1920, the Golden Vanguard Class in 1936 and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade in 1949. He took part in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Gaona is described in a number of reference works and publications, among them Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online and Verifiable Vade Mecum. He is buried at Memory Lane.

Inigo Varren Mylo (born 25 September 1757 in Willowcrest; died 12 May 1827) was a duke who served the Velorian Dominion as a military officer and politician. He attained the rank of general field marshal during his service and held political office alongside his military career.

Born to Zephyr Marlowe and Helion Dominique, he belonged to the Yewtree family. His given name was Inigo. His siblings included Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Halyra Coakley, Jyleth Arturo, Kyndra Mcdade, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Thereth Stafford, Theryn Zay and Ulyndra Alexander.

He spoke Malquari. Among his honors, he received the Pinnacle Honor. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Selis Dolores (19 November 1841 – 7 September 1911) was a citizen of Verenthia, an island country and sovereign state. Born on 19 November 1841 and dying on 7 September 1911, he was active in Verenthia throughout his life.

He was the father of fifteen children, including Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin and Jareth June. His other children were Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman and Ylinda Shaker.

Silthar Dell (28 March 1961 – 14 February 1997) was a male individual who spoke Malquari and was a recipient of the Zenith Medal, an order.

He was the son of Fenris Hooper and Myrryn Nance. He had seven siblings: Alex Morgan, Cevaryn Jennifer, Delvyn Layne, Elric Thornfield, Jyneth Lind, Nythera Powers, and Velian Chen.

Dell died on 14 February 1997 in an accidental traffic collision.

Brenor Mcclintock (19 April 1890 – 24 May 1915) was a Verenthian naval officer who held the rank of admiral. He was a citizen of Verenthia, an island sovereign state, and was born in the city of Portvale.

Mcclintock was born on 19 April 1890 in Portvale, a big city that served as a former national capital and is known as a tourist destination. His father was Selis Dolores, and his extended family included Rhelian Tharp. He was one of many siblings; among them were Aeliana Nyrali, Celyndra No, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin, Jareth June, Jynor Littlefield, Lynre Robert, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman and Ylinda Shaker.

During his career he attained the rank of admiral in Verenthia's forces. Brenor Mcclintock died on 24 May 1915.

Aurelia Vesperis (born 23 April 2007) is a princess of Vesperia and serves as a diplomat. She is a citizen of Vesperia and was born in Drakemont. She is female.

Her father is Alaric Vesperius. She has several siblings, including Aeliana Vesperis and Alaric Vesperian. Other siblings are Elara Vesperian, Elara Vesperion and Elara Vesperis, as well as Fynel Fountain and Liora Vesperian.

Elara Vesperion (born 13 February 1995 in Drakemont) is a princess and citizen of Vesperia, a sovereign state and constitutional monarchy. She received the Opal Honor, a civil decoration and order.

She was born in Drakemont, a city, and is the daughter of Alaric Vesperius. Her siblings include Aeliana Vesperis, Alaric Vesperian, Aurelia Vesperis, Aveline Vespera, Elara Vesperian, Elara Vesperis, Fynel Fountain and Liora Vesperian. She is female.

Lyrel Irons (7 August 1930 – 3 November 1972) was an aristocrat who held citizenship of the Aquilonian Empire and Verenthia. A member of the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles, she spoke Omerith.

She was the daughter of Xerath Amini and Elthar Barbour. She had numerous siblings, among them Alderon Cifuentes, Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Hesthra Uribe, Lythor Sorrentino, Nyryth Villeda, Nytheren Havens, Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Xendry War, Xilara Bustamante and Zylara Cho, as well as Corwin, who was stillborn.

Liora Vesperian (born 9 February 2025) is a princess of Vesperia. She is a citizen of Vesperia and was born in Drakemont, a big city. She is female.

Liora is the daughter of Alaric Vesperius. Her siblings include Aeliana Vesperis, Alaric Vesperian, Aurelia Vesperis, Aveline Vespera, Elara Vesperian, Elara Vesperion, Elara Vesperis, and Fynel Fountain.

She was educated at the Horizon of Knowledge Institute and at the Insight Research Academy. The Horizon of Knowledge Institute is an ancient public university that also functions as an open-access publisher, while the Insight Research Academy is an organization that serves as a public research university, university and university campus and as a public educational institution.

Elara Vesperian (born 23 April 2007) is a Vesperian princess and aristocrat. She is a citizen of Vesperia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state. Elara was born in Drakemont, a city and big city, and carries the noble title of princess while working as an aristocrat.

Elara is one of the children of Alaric Vesperius. Her siblings include Aeliana Vesperis, Alaric Vesperian, Aurelia Vesperis, Aveline Vespera, Elara Vesperion, Elara Vesperis, Fynel Fountain, and Liora Vesperian.

She uses she/her pronouns.

Belegorn Zhang, given name Harlan (30 November 1874 – 21 April 1949), was a male writer whose work ranged across historical fiction and shorter forms. Over a career that began in 1903 and continued until 1949, he worked in many literary roles: novelist, children's writer, travel writer, autobiographer and aphorist, as well as a humorist, opinion journalist and prose writer. He also taught. Much of his published output is no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Zhang wrote in and spoke Malquari and Velthar, and his surviving work is recorded as being written in those languages. His papers and archives are held by the Narrative Nexus, an archive, library and museum, and by The Rare Volume Atrium, an academic archive, academic library, library building and rare book library. Examples of institutions that hold his works in their collections include the Chronicle Gallery and the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum.

He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and described in a variety of sources. Editions and versions such as Arcane Version and Infinite Reimagining, reference works and compilations including Verifiable Vade Mecum and The Narrative Nexus, and publications and projects such as Cascade Collective, Knowlarium, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library have all described him. He is also present in the literary work The Chronicles of Freya Wilder.

Personal details recorded about Zhang include that he held an atheistic worldview and was noted for a walrus moustache. He died on 21 April 1949 from a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Brithor Valentine (born 1 January 1609 in Nextridge; died 9 August 1673 in Nextridge) was a copper engraver, drawer and publisher whose field of work centered on the engraving process. A citizen of Eldraeth, he worked in Nextridge as well as in Caelumport and Ecotropolis. He produced a body of work that is no longer under copyright, as copyrights on his works have expired.

Valentine’s works appear across a range of public and institutional collections. They are held by Artropolis Nextridge, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Ethereal Oasis and Vivid Visions Gallery; by larger institutions such as the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the National Legacy Gallery; and by organizations including the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Color Spectrum Division, Museum Merge and The Legacy Lounge.

Archival and reference material on Valentine can be found at the Gallery of Texts, which maintains artist files about him. He is also described in several published sources and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Reflections of Humanity and The Scroll of Influencers.

The Chronicles of the Celestial Veil is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode was directed by Calix Vornell and written by Ellyra Saldaña.

The on-screen cast includes Fariel Chapple, Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Selith Henrriquez, Vyndel Gibbs and Zephyros Burk. Voice performances are provided by Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano and Pyrith Fast.

The episode premiered on 13 May 2037 and was later published on 17 October 2037. It was distributed by ScreenSync via video on demand.

In the series continuity, The Chronicles of the Celestial Veil follows The Timeless Whispers: Echoes from Beyond and is followed by The Lost Echoes of the Ethereal. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews. Its colour is listed as "color."

Chronicles of the Dreamweavers is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe. The narrative is set on a fictional planet. Within the series chronology, the episode follows The Shattered Echoes and is followed by The Arcane Legacy: Awakening.

The episode was first performed and published on 2033-03-20. It was distributed by ScreenSync, a video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster, and made available in a video-on-demand format. The work is described by the magazine VividViews and is associated with the color "color."

The production's cast includes Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta. Voice actors credited on the episode include Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal.

Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, who is presented as a comics character and television character and described as a fictional human and a human from the media franchise; Thalen Virok, a literary and television character; and Marcellus Stormwatch, a fictional human who appears as a literary and television character.

The Lost Dimensions: A Journey Beyond is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was directed by Draxella Knott and premiered on 2032-05-09, the same date as its publication. The episode is followed by The Celestial Mirage. The production is set on a fictional planet and takes place within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The listed color for the production is "color."

The episode addresses themes of forced displacement and progress. It has been described in the magazine VividViews.

The Lost Dimensions: A Journey Beyond was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand. ScreenSync is presented as a mobile app and a video streaming service that also functions as a web broadcaster.

Cast and characters appearing in the episode include actors Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Selith Henrriquez, Ulyndor Rosado, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk, with voice performances by Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda and Merynd Luevano. Characters featured in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne. Elias Blackwood appears as a comics character, a literary character and a television character, and is depicted as a fictional human associated with the media franchise; Thalen Virok is presented as a literary character and a television character; Maximus Drake is portrayed as a fictional human who appears in literary and television forms within the franchise; and Miles Hawthorne is depicted as a fictional human and a television character within the media.

Yardley Thompson (born 24 June 1904 in Ravenwood; died 12 July 1968) was a painter associated with the Ethereal Canvas movement. Given the name Yardley, he worked across a range of subjects and styles, producing cityscapes, figures, genre paintings, landscapes and portraits. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning and made his career chiefly in Harborview City, Moonstone Ridge and Southpoint.

Thompson studied at the Creative Spectrum Academy and at the Gallery of Dreams, and he was a student of Braxton Everhart, Yardley Prescott, Zander Thaloren and Zander Caelthorn. In turn, he taught Thalric Vyndorathian and Vail Theren Basqor.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections. These include Aesthetic Insights Press, ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation and Canvas of Dreams. Additional holdings encompass Canvas of Illusions Gallery, the Creative Spark Foundation, Crestvale Collective Arts Museum, Cultural Canvas Museum and the Cultural Tapestry Museum. Other institutions with his works are Dreamscape Museum, Echo Publishing House, Ethereal Art Registry, Gallery of Dreams and Horizon Ridge University Gallery. Luminara Art Gallery, National Legacy Gallery, Nexus National Museum, Radiant Brush Gallery and Ravenwood Collective Art Museum also hold examples of his work, as do Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum and The Artistic Exchange. The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Expression Hub, The Spectrum of Dreams Museum, The Visionary Collective and The Visionary Experience further include his paintings in their collections.

Thompson’s archival and research materials are preserved at The Rare Volume Atrium, and artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts. He spoke the Velthar language. As a creator his copyrights on works have expired. He is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Thompson died of prostate cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Lyris Gerson (born 1 January 1692 — died 13 September 1775) was a Kaldoria painter best known for landscape painting. He worked primarily in the art of painting with a particular focus on landscapes, and his occupation is recorded as painter. A citizen of Kaldoria, he lived and worked in Seraphim Bay and died there.

Gerson studied under Garenth Neil, Nyra Zambrana and Pytheran Lazo, and he was a member of The Artist Commune. His professional activity centered on Seraphim Bay, where he carried out much of his work.

His works are held widely in public and institutional collections. They appear in museums and collections such as Artefactual Odyssey, the Cultural Canvas Museum, the Culturia Heritage Network, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Ethos Gallery. Additional holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, The Art Exchange, The Artisan's Haven, The Curated Press and The Curatorial Vault. Other institutions with works by Gerson are The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Harmony Space, Town Hall Art Space, Treasures of Time and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Gerson is described in the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His body of published work is no longer under copyright, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

The Celestial Odyssey: A New Adventure is a media franchise episode belonging to the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria and follows the episode The Timeless Echoes: A Journey of Discovery. The piece was first performed on 2034-02-20 and has a publication date of 2035-03-04. The screenplay was written by Ellyra Saldaña and the episode was directed by Vyndel Gibbs.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode features the characters Marcellus Stormwatch and Miles Hawthorne; Marcellus Stormwatch is presented as a fictional human who appears in both written works and television, while Miles Hawthorne is a fictional human who appears across the media franchise and as a television character.

The cast includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Vyndel Gibbs, and Zephyros Burk, and the voice cast includes Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, and Ulyr Stacks.

The episode is distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync, a mobile app and video-on-demand streaming service and web broadcaster.

The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews. The production is associated with the color "color."

Pylar Hester (27 December 1800 – 10 August 1869) was a person who served as military personnel and as a politician. He held the noble title of duke and attained the military rank of general.

He participated in the Conclave of Conflict, a series of wars.

A member of the Calyrian Family, he was the son of Sylas Wrynsel and Wynelle Mistral; his given name was Sylas. He spoke Malquari. His siblings included Calix Merriden, Gellion Xue, Irylin Collazo, Mylaria Enamorado and Orinthia Club, as well as Peryn Frimpong, Sylas Harkwood, Verenth Jj and Zephyr Alaric Stormwind.

Thalric Kytarathian Emberwood (16 December 1616 – 2 March 1663) was a margrave and served as a ruler. 

His given name was Thalric Kytarathian, and he spoke Malquari. He was male.

Born to Merrick Alton and Noxen Kallin, he had several siblings, among them Aenara Soliman, Burand Nilsson and Jorvik Eldren Thorne. Other siblings included Merrick Grethain, Rilith Cantero, Talyra Venshira and Wyrith Heckman.

He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Eclipse of the Darkstar Chronicles is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It follows the episode The Arcane Dimensions: A New Era and had its first performance on 2032-02-06. The work was published on 2032-02-07 and again on 2033-02-27.

Yardley Brackenridge directed the episode, and Yardley Dovern Pax served as film editor. It was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. The production is described by the magazine VividViews and makes use of technobabble. The work’s color is listed as "color."

The cast includes Calix Vornell, Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs and Zephyros Burk.

Characters who appear in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch, Miles Hawthorne and Riven Darkstar.

Voice performances were provided by Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal.

The story is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Qalir Olivar (25 April 1863 – 22 September 1927) was a painter known for portrait work and associated with the Visionary Art Brut movement. He worked primarily in the art of painting and produced numerous portraits that are held by a range of cultural institutions.

Olivar received his formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay from 1889 to 1893 and was also educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He later held a professorship at both Creative Spectrum Academy and The Cultural Exchange Hub, and he held a position at Creative Spectrum Academy. From 1924 to 1927 he served as a teacher.

During his career Olivar was employed by The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. His works are represented in many collections, including Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Creative Spark Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Harmony of Arts Museum, National Artistry Hub, The Aesthetic Archive, The Gallery of the Ages, The Memory Museum, and The Palace of Reflections. Artist files about Olivar are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Olivar received the Talent Tournament prize in 1888 and was awarded the Noble Valorian Order on 12 August 1904. He was a student of Tamsin Brightwood and taught several pupils, among them Dorian Quellaris, Tamsin Merrick and Yardley Prescott. He spoke and wrote in Therian.

He is described in sources such as the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and O'Rourke Insights Online. Copyrights on his works have expired. Olivar died of hypostatic pneumonia on 22 September 1927; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes and he was buried at Gentle Hills.

Yelith Montalvan (born 1 January 1664) is a female noble who holds the title Elarith.. Her family name is Ilithra-Celthar, a name that serves as a clan designation and a double family name and is regarded as a hala and royal surname.

She is a daughter of Lorthan Talavera. Her siblings include Aelith Pierre-Louis, Burand Choudhary, Elindor Giovanni, Jendara Olivo, Kenthis Ulrich, Lydan Demers, Menyra Defreitas, Myrindor Tam, Myrith Eddie, Mystral Gilbertson, Neryn Farrell, Sylphira Buckley, Thalorin Baskin, Tyndra Brumfield, Yalindra Deal and Yliantha Jadhav.

Tyndra Brumfield (20 January 1681 – 22 August 1695) was a member of the Ilithra-Celthar clan, a double family name and royal surname. He is recorded with the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

His father was Lorthan Talavera. His siblings included Aelith Pierre-Louis, Burand Choudhary, Cyndrel Figueredo, Daryth Hawks, Elindor Giovanni, Jendara Olivo, Kenthis Ulrich, Lydan Demers, Menyra Defreitas, Moryn Easton, Myrith Eddie, Mystral Gilbertson, Neryn Farrell, Thalorin Baskin, Yalindra Deal and Yliantha Jadhav.

Tyndra Brumfield is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

The Enigma of Aetherial Paths is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, presented as part of the television series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction instalment set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe. The episode is associated with the color color.

The episode was published on 2030-04-20 and 2030-04-22, and its date of first performance is 2030-04-22. It follows The Shattered Echoes: Legends Untold in the series and is followed by The Shattered Echoes of Time. The Enigma of Aetherial Paths was distributed as a video on demand release through ScreenSync and has been described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

Zorath Parrilla directed the episode, with Halden Quevedo serving as director of photography. The cast of the episode includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the story include Braxton Velaryn and Tobias Merriweather, who are depicted as humans; Lyra Dray, who appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Serenix, who appears as an android; and a computer voice.

Uryth Osborne (born 1 April 1805, died 16 March 1876) was a painter, art educator, collector and philanthropist known for his work in portraiture. He worked in both Caelumport and his native Nythra, and he served as a director from 1864 to 1876. He spoke Therian.

Born and died in Nythra, Osborne received his artistic education at The Alliance for Artistic Research and was taught by Syldor Hyde. His practice centered on the art of painting with a particular focus on portraits, and alongside his studio work he was active as an educator, collection builder and supporter of the arts.

Osborne's paintings and related works are held by numerous institutions. Examples include Abstract Assemblage, Arathonia Art Museum, Artefactual Odyssey, the Museum of Enduring Art, the Realm of Creativity Museum and the Whimsy Art Pavilion. Other public and private collections holding his work are Aesthetic Insights Press, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the National Legacy Gallery and Vanguardia Art and National Heritage Museum. His works also appear in The Artful Tapestry, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Elixir, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curatorial Institute, The Harmony Space and The Palette Sanctuary.

Osborne received recognition during his lifetime, including the Golden Aurora Class and the Talent Tournament. Artist files on him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation and ItemVerse. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Valtaric Standard Communication is a modern, pluricentric standard language and a technical standard. Typologically, it is classified as an isolating language.

The variety is indigenous to several places, specifically Mercuria, Pendoria, the Solara Archipelago and Zephyra. Mercuria functions as a big city and city-state, a dependent special administrative region and global metropolis, and is also described as a customs territory under multiple forms of sovereign administration. Pendoria is a province-level territory, identified as a province within a range of state types. The Solara Archipelago is an autonomous region. Zephyra appears as a big city and city-state that is a dependent special administrative region and human settlement, a tourist destination, and also operates as a customs territory under various state arrangements.

Valtaric Standard Communication is present across a number of countries. It is used in the Elysian Coast, an archipelagic state and sovereign country; in Infernix, which is simultaneously a city, big city, border city, city-state, island country, national capital, port settlement, global city and sovereign country; and in Lunethia, a sovereign federation that is a member state of intergovernmental, geopolitical, regional and confederational organizations. It is also found in Meridia., an archipelagic island country and sovereign unitary state that is a constitutional republic with a presidential system and has been described as a historical unrecognized state; in Orinthia, a sovereign country organized as a sultanate; and in the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, a sovereign people's republic and state with limited recognition that is described as a socialist and communist state, a constitutional republic, secular in character, and organized under the doctrine of a dictatorship of the proletariat.
