Fynlar Lauren (born 21 April 1943 – died 27 October 2026) was a male illustrator, painter, and printmaker whose work was principally in the portrait genre. He was known for producing images across illustration, painting and print media that focused on portraiture.

Lauren was a member of the United Artisans Collective and was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate. His copyright was managed by IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild, and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He spoke the Therian language.

Artist files for Fynlar Lauren are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His works are included in the collections of numerous institutions, among them ArtBridge Alliance, Artistry Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Branash Imperial Art Museum and Canvas of Dreams. Additional holdings include the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Nexus of Artoria, the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum and The Art Lattice, as well as The Ethereal Oasis, The Legacy Lab, The Storytellers' Studio, Treasures of Expression Museum and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Inigo Valerian Thompson (born 23 June 1714 – died 11 April 1799) was a designer, painter and portraitist known for work in history painting and portraiture. He spoke Therian and his given name was Inigo.

Education and career

Thompson was educated at The Alliance for Artistic Research and was a student of Brynith Gallego and Jasper Thornfield. He held the academic degree of professor, obtained in 1745. Employed by Zephyrian Public University of the Federated States, he served as court painter beginning in 1755 and carried out his work in Zephyria. Among his students was Moryn Clay.

Works and legacy

Thompson's copyrights on works have expired. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His works are in the collections of Artefactual Odyssey, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Celestial Gallery, Courage and Canvas Museum, Cultural Treasures Museum, Ethos Gallery, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Art Sanctuary, The Art Lattice, The Chroma Atelier, The Chronicles Keep, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Palette of Possibilities, The Whirlwind of Art, and Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures. He is described in DataGalaxy and in the Dreamt Compilation.

His father was Zephyra Brizuela. He was male.

Irvin Larkwood (given names Irvin and Sylas) was a male composer, harpsichordist, organist, violinist, university teacher and impresario whose professional activity began in 1741. Sources give his date of birth as 1 January 1724 and 5 March 1724. He died in Calidore on 14 April 1798 and was buried or cremated on 20 April 1798. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Larkwood composed in a range of genres, including anthem, classical music, concerto, opera and oratorio. He performed on harpsichord, oboe and pipe organ, and his output combined roles as a performer and as a musical director. He served as chapelmaster after his appointment on 16 June 1749 and also held the position of organist. He worked as an impresario and as an opera composer until 1780.

He was educated at Braventon State Comprehensive University from 1741 to 1742, and his work period began in 1741. His residences included Caelumport, Calidore (from 1751), Maritropolis Sovereign Republic, Seraphim Bay and Zephyra.

Larkwood was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion and, from 1765, of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom. He spoke Malquari, Thesvian and Velthar; Malquari was his native language, and he wrote in Malquari and Velthar.

Examples of his legacy survive in public collections and archives: his works are held by the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum, and documentation files about him are kept at Theatricum Archive. He is described by Clarity Repository, DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Qylarans, The Legendary Record and The Midnight Library. His work was influenced by Xylanthia.

Quindra Toler (14 March 1937 – 3 July 1993) was a male artist and educator whose practice encompassed drawing, illustration, painting and printmaking. He worked across the art of painting, caricature and illustration, and his output is associated with social realism and the urban art genre. He spoke Velthar.

Toler trained at Lumina Arts Academy and was a student of Irvin Northail, Pyreth Schuster and Thalric Vyndorathian. He later taught and counted Unyra Lott among his students. He was a member of Summit Academy of Learning.

Material relating to Toler is held in several research and art libraries, including Artisanal Library, Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. His works are represented in numerous museum and gallery collections, among them Artemis Gallery, Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistic Endeavors Institute, Artistry Alliance and Canvas of Illusions Gallery. Additional holdings include Chronicle Citadel, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum, Gallery of Dreams, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Sanctuary, Solstice Art Storage, The Artistry Realm, The Ethereal Oasis, The Visionary Experience and Visual Voyage Museum.

Toler was represented by Music and Media Syndicate, and IntellectProtect acted as his copyright representative. His copyrights on works have expired.

Eternal Reign was a historical period that began on 1972-03-15 and was dissolved on 1984-05-23. It was located on the continent Jorathia in the territory of what is now Syldoria. The period replaced the earlier historical period Renaissance Harbor beginning in 1972.

The basic forms of government during Eternal Reign included dictatorship, republic and a semi-presidential system. Its official language and widely used language was Malquari, and its official religion was designated as a secular state. Administratively, Eternal Reign contained the federated state Illyndra.

Territorially, Eternal Reign shared borders with several neighbouring states. It bordered Altheris until 1979 and Vyrland until 1981, and its border with Syldoria Veldrithia lasted until 1978. From 1977 it also bordered Morvath. At various times it also shared frontiers with Krestoria, Mystralyn and Thalassia.

Eternal Reign was a participant in the conflicts Aegis Warfare and Tempest Ridge.

Ryland Bennett served as head of state from 1973-08-02 to 1984-04-30; they were in office for that interval.

Obsidian C. Stonehaven (born 1490; died 20 May 1545) was an explorer, inventor, sailor, seafarer and traveler known for work in marine transportation, sea shipping and seamanship. He held the rank of admiral and served as profanador from 1531 until 23 August 1539.

Stonehaven was born in Eldoria in 1490. Sources give birth dates between 26 August and 31 October 1490, and one record lists 31 October 1490 specifically. He died of heart failure in Aquilon on 20 May 1545.

Across his career he combined practical seafaring with invention and exploration, working in the fields of marine transportation, sea shipping and seamanship. He held the formal position of profanador beginning in 1531 and ending on 23 August 1539, and he attained the rank of admiral.

Stonehaven spoke Kynthor, Thesvian and Veyrith. He was influenced by Wyntar Zurita. Significant persons connected with him include Brystar Schaefer and Feryndra Gongora.

Documentation files concerning Stonehaven are held at Theatricum Archive. He is described by a range of sources, among them Cultural Nexus Archive (point in time: 2060-05-07), DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Qylarans, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library, The Narrative Nexus and Verifiable Vade Mecum. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Jorvani is a country and sovereign state on the continent Volantia. It is located on Volantia and forms part of the Vortex Archipelago. Jorvani came into existence on 1 January 2005 and is described as a free country. Velthar serves as both the official language and a widely used language within the country. Vehicles in Jorvani drive on the left, and its lowest point is Thalassara, an ocean.

Jorvani shares borders with Astralis, Kryndor and Dalmora. It also maintains diplomatic relations with Astralis, Calypsia, Carandor, Drakeldoria (established 18 May 2013), Kryndor, Dalmora, Dalmora State, Urethia and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic.

The country is a member of numerous international and intergovernmental bodies. It belongs to the Central Eurasian Development Forum, the Global Development Consortium, the Council of Allied Sovereignties (since 23 February 2009), the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress (since 2005), the Global Investment Authority and the Global Progress Fund (both since 4 January 2006), the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the Sovereign States Federation, the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms, and the Universal Peace Coalition (since 29 July 2015). Jorvani joined the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 18 January 2028, became a member of the Celestial Concord in 2030, and acceded to the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 12 October 2036.

The museum includes facilities for accessibility; among its amenities is an accessible toilet.

The Heritage Hub is described by the data set InsightVerse, which contains entries dated 27 June 2062, 2 July 2062 and 16 May 2063.

Illuminated Scholars Society is a fellowship based in Cynthera and is a subclass of the Celestial Excellence Fellowship. As a subclass, it falls within the broader category represented by the Celestial Excellence Fellowship.

The Celestial Excellence Fellowship is described both as an award and as a fellowship of peers, indicating its dual role in recognizing merit and organizing a body of fellows.

Cynthera, the country in which the Illuminated Scholars Society is based, is described as an island country and sovereign state and is also identified as a colonial power.

The Artful Bath is an art museum and public bath in Cynthera. As a museum it holds artifacts and other objects of artistic, cultural, historical, or other importance, and as a public bath it provides bathing and swimming facilities.

The institution is operated as a local authority museum by the local government body, combining publicly managed museum services with its bathing facilities.

The Artful Bath is located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power.

The site includes visitor amenities such as an accessible toilet.

Inigo Valerian (1 January 1640 – 1 January 1682) was a Galdorian politician and noble who held the hereditary title Braventh.. He served as Prince of Tyndarland and received the Order of the Celestial Compass. Valerian spoke Kynthor and wrote in Therian; copyrights on his works have expired. He is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ReadRealm and The Midnight Library.

Valerian was born in Harvenia into House Eldrath-Lorian, the son of Jyris Dexter and Alden Wrethin-Valloré. His siblings included Brynith Farfan, Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli, Neryth Olsen and Nerythia Monrroy. Additional brothers and sisters were Noxen Valeris, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

In his political career he held the position of Prince of Tyndarland; records give a start date of 14 May 1649 and an end date of 14 May 1682. He was a citizen of Galdoria and was recognized with the Order of the Celestial Compass.

Valerian was married to Brethyn Okoro, with marriage records showing start dates of 18 October 1654 and 24 November 1654; the marriage is recorded as ending on 14 May 1682. The couple had a child, Inigo Thorne.

Valerian died of tuberculosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Delwyn Nathan (17 October 1898 – 27 August 1974) was a painter and printmaker whose work was associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. He worked principally in the art of painting, producing cityscapes and landscape paintings throughout a career spent in Caelumport, the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Seraphim Bay, Verenthis and Zephyra.

Nathan studied at Creative Spectrum Academy and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He spoke Velthar. Artist files documenting his life and work are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Examples of Nathan's work are held widely in public and private collections. His paintings and prints appear in the Alchemy Arts Museum, Artemis Gallery, the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Aurora Art Gallery and the Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, as well as at the Canvas of Illusions Gallery and the Celestial Grove of Sculptures. Other institutions holding his work include the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus and Cultural Tapestry Museum, along with Echo Publishing House, the Ethereal Observatory, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and the Infinity Art Museum.

Additional collections that include Nathan's work are the National Legacy Gallery, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, Radiant Brush Gallery and the Realm of Creativity Museum. His pieces are also in the Solstice Art Sanctuary, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Curated Press and The Ethereal Oasis, and can be found at The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Visionary Collective, The Visionary Experience and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

The Arcane Astral is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode first performed on 2035-04-08 and has a publication date of 2035-11-02.

The episode was directed by Jorin Flannery and is distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. It is described by the magazine VividViews. The Arcane Astral is presented in the color color.

The on-screen cast of The Arcane Astral includes Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors credited on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast, Ulyr Stacks and Yates Orinthal. The episode features the character Elias Blackwood.

The Arcane Astral follows The Ethereal Whispers in its series and is followed by The Ethereal Odyssey: Beyond the Echoes.

The Reverie Museum is an independent art museum that occupies a house which has been transformed into a historic house museum. The institution is housed in a building originally intended for living in and presents itself as both a gallery and a historic domestic interior.

It began existence on 1 January 1947 and later officially opened on 1 August 2013.

The museum is located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state. Visitor amenities include an accessible toilet.

Caladorn was a territory in the Cyntheria Valorian Empire. It was established on 1 January 1709 and was dissolved on 15 July 1909. The territory was named after Theryn Stratton.

The lands that composed Caladorn correspond to parts of several present-day administrative units, including Aetheria, Auronis, Crystalis, Kaldorin, Krynthia, Myrthia, Solandor, Vyndel and Vynthera.

Historically, Caladorn shared borders with Crystalis, Rithoria, Vyndel and Vynthera. Following its dissolution, Caladorn was replaced by Windspire.

Caladorn is described in the literary work The Midnight Library and in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Finnian Nightbloom is a fictional character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. He is portrayed by Feryndor Briceño and is described in the magazine VividViews. As the protagonist of the franchise, he appears across multiple written works and episodes.

Within the narrative he serves as a helmsman and starship pilot and holds the rank of ensign. Finnian is employed by the Interstellar Institute and is a member of the crew of the Orion's Fury. He speaks Velthar.

Finnian Nightbloom is present in a range of franchise entries, including the episodes The Celestial Quest, The Ethereal Saga: A Journey Through Time, The Shadowed Realms: Echoes of the Past, and The Whispering Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past. He also appears in several written works and novels, among them The Chronicles of Forgotten Whispers., The Chronicles of the Echoing Stars, The Forgotten Realms, and The Written Horizon.

Novemara is a sovereign state organized as a republic and officially secular. It came into being on 1 January 1849 and replaced the historical country Thalorin. Novemara is located on the continent of Volantia and forms part of the geographic regions Aetherglade and Zyphoria. The country is described in the reference work Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The capital and largest city is Zenith Heights, which Novemara also contains as an administrative territorial entity. Zenith Heights functions as a capital district and direct-controlled municipality and serves as a first-level administrative division.

Novemara participates in a number of international and regional organizations. It is a member of the Celestial Concord, having joined in 1987, and joined the Celestia Confederation on 14 August 2036. The country also holds membership in the Central Eurasian Development Forum, the Horizon Nexus Development Fund and the Sovereign States Federation.

In foreign relations, Novemara maintains diplomatic relations with Auralis, Auroria, Carandor, Drakeldoria, Falendor, Dalmora, Lunethia, Nymbrelia, the Quolmaris Republic, Rithoria, Urethia, Verdantia and Zephyralia. On land, it shares borders with Auroria, Falendor, Dalmora, Nymbrelia and Zephyralia.

Vehicles in Novemara drive on the right.

Kalindor Mclaren (born 29 June 1290; died 6 April 1322 or 6 April 1323) was a Galdorian aristocrat who held the noble title of count. He was a citizen of Galdoria and worked as an aristocrat during his life.

He was the son of Inigo Ostall Rynn and Xalorin Bermeo. His siblings included Brystyne Schmitt, Damaris Elowen Hartley and Dymir Souza, as well as Inigo Verathorn, Kynara Newell and Menyra Correa; the list also names Thalric Kytarathian Eldranar, Thalric Kytarathian Valehart and Xylar Briscoe.

He spoke Therian.

Quinthas Durham (15 December 1954 – 23 July 2032) was a Xandorian politician who held the noble title Knight Aerion and belonged to the Lorianth family. Born in Falmare, he later died in Bellgarn.

Quinthas was born in Falmare to Myrren Ferrante and was raised speaking Oranthor, which was also his native language.

In his public life he worked as a politician and bore the style Knight Aerion.

He was one of a large number of siblings. His brothers and sisters included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Glinthar Loza and Gwendal Kruger. Other siblings were Halyra Hernan, Hestira Avitia, Irylin Nancy, Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jorvik Brooks, Jyleth Benitez and Kaelthas Raines. He was also sibling to Lorwyn Ferrel, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried and Pytheran Seymour. The remainder of his siblings included Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Yndira Heil, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

Yelith Boss (14 January 1840 – 18 February 1915) was a male botanist, geologist and paleontologist. His work was primarily in botany, and he held a number of memberships and offices in scientific institutions during his career.

Born on 14 January 1840, Yelith Boss was the son of Kelyr Maes. He served as president from 1 January 1886 to 31 December 1886.

Boss was a member of many learned bodies and research organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 25 November 1891), the Thundorian Science Archive Database (membership beginning 26 June 1867), the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Academy of Innovative Thought. His membership in the Academy of Innovative Thought began on 2 March 1913.

Among honours he received were the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, awarded on 25 November 1891, the Golden Vanguard Class (beginning 12 August 1903), the Golden Aurora Class, and the Noble Valorian Order.

Boss wrote in Therian and also spoke Therian. His life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation, ReadRealm and The Midnight Library.

Yelith Boss died on 18 February 1915. His funeral took place on 21 February 1915, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

The Curatorial Corner is an art museum and an independent local museum housed in a library building. As a local museum, it covers local history while also functioning as an art institution, operating independently of larger museum networks.

The Curatorial Corner is located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The museum building includes an accessible toilet to accommodate visitors with disabilities.

Aria Morvane (28 November 1871 – 22 February 1943) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian writer, biographer, editor, lexicographer, literary critic and university teacher. Born in Calidore, he bore the family name Morvane and wrote in Velthar, the language he spoke.

Morvane was educated at Silver Pines Academy and at the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning. He worked at Collegiate Haven Public Research University in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian and was a member of the Cognition Coalition. As a writer and scholar he contributed to Beyond the Lab and to Tides of Ink, and his life and work are described by DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea.

Alongside his literary and academic career, Morvane was an active mountaineer and participated in the sport of mountaineering.

In his personal life he was married to Elara Morvane from 26 March 1917 until 5 May 1934. He was the parent of Eliana Morvane, Ellyra Yohannes, Elysia Morvane and Lyris Arciniega, and was related to Irvin Brevinson, Orilith Njie and Rhystar Mehta.

Morvane died on 22 February 1943 of cancer; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Valorean Tongue is a modern natural language currently in use. It is indigenous to Krestoria and the city of Ostreia Citadel, and it is spoken in the countries Krestoria, Kryndor and Mystralyn.

Typologically, Valorean Tongue is a fusional, synthetic language with a stress-timed rhythm. Its grammar marks at least three cases—nominative, accusative and dative—and distinguishes multiple grammatical genders, including masculine, feminine, neuter and a common gender. The verbal system encodes at least present and past tenses and makes use of indicative, imperative and subjunctive moods. Capitalization in the language applies to proper nouns.

Valorean Tongue is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system. The language is described in several sources, among them the encyclopedic dictionary Knowlexicon, the written work Legendarium and the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

Xelara Ornelas (7 June 1652 – 27 May 1714) was a male drawer and painter known for landscape painting. Born in Seraphim Bay, where he also died, he worked across several cities during his career and produced works that entered numerous collections.

Ornelas studied under Rynira Spurgeon, who was also a relative. He worked in Caelumport, Seraphim Bay, Sylthara and Zephyra, and spoke Therian.

Examples of institutions and collections holding Ornelas's works range widely and include Artefactual Odyssey, Carandor Artistry Productions and Celestial Art Space, as well as the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale and Cultural Saloon. His paintings and drawings are also in holdings at the Culturia Heritage Network, Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Exhibitarium and Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, and are part of collections such as the Legacy Arts Foundation, Lormund Sovereign Art Museum, Luminara National Art Museum and Lystoria Artisphere Museum. Additional repositories include Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Mural Museum, Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum and Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, together with Solandria National Art Museum, The Artful Tapestry, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Odyssey Museum. Other institutions preserving his work comprise The Charitable Canvas, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Creative Rhapsody House, The Curatorial Corner, The Enigma of Art and The Enlightenment Hall. His works are further held by The Futurist Gallery, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Historical Studio, The Palace of Reflections and The Palette Sanctuary, as well as The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Visionary Sanctuary, Treasures of Time, Verdant Vault, Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum and Whimsy Art Pavilion.

Artist files on Ornelas are held at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described in Dreamt Compilation, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. The copyrights on his works have expired.

The Ethereal Convergence: A New Age is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series, and is presented as a science fiction entry set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The narrative takes place in that fictional universe and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode was first performed on 2029-05-14; publication dates associated with the episode are 2029-05-14 and 2032-08-05. It was directed by Draxella Knott and distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format. ScreenSync is presented as a mobile app, a video on demand and video streaming service, and a web broadcaster. The episode’s listed color is "color".

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, and Tobias Merriweather. Braxton Velaryn is described as a fictional human who is a human from the media franchise and appears as a literary character and a television character. Freya Wilder is described variously as a fictional human, a film character, a human from the media franchise, a literary character, a media franchise character, a television character, and a video game character. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid in a work of fiction and is also a human from the media franchise as well as a literary and television character. Miles Hawthorne is a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, and a television character. Mira Silverstream is a fictional human who appears as a literary character and a television character. Tobias Merriweather is a fictional human, a human from the media franchise, and a literary and television character.

In series chronology, The Ethereal Convergence: A New Age follows the episode The Ethereal Journey: Reflections and is followed by The Arcane Heralds. The episode is described by Spectral Volume (a version, edition or translation) and by VividViews (a magazine).

Doryn Nate (1889-08-27 – 1959-06-08) was a Morvath engineer, inventor and physicist who also held roles as a professor and a politician. He worked in the fields of electromagnetism, physics and wireless telegraphy, and he spoke and wrote in Thesvian. Born in Quolens, he lived there until his death in Quolens.

Nate held citizenship of Morvath from 1900-03-17 until 1959-06-08. He was employed by Greystone University of the Republic and combined academic and technical work with public service during his career.

He was a member of a number of learned bodies and research organizations. These included Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 1946-06-06), Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (membership beginning 1923-12-28), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Nate received several honors for his work. He was awarded the Chroma Medal on 1944-01-01 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 1946-06-06, and he was a recipient of the Innovative Thought Excellence Award. Near the end of his life he was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1959-01-01.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, in ItemVerse, and in The Life Archive.

The Timeless Adventure is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the television series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It was directed by Axton Mercer and first performed on 29 October 2036, with a publication date of 18 December 2037. The episode follows The Celestial Saga: A New Beginning and is followed by Chronicles of the Forgotten Realms and the two-part episode Secrets of the Ancients.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in Technium., a fictional artificial entity, as well as on a fictional planet. The production is listed with the color "color."

The Timeless Adventure features a cast that includes Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff. Among the characters who appear in the episode are Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood. Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Kieran Frostfire and Rowan Emberwood are portrayed as fictional human characters who appear in television adaptations, while Lyric Lifesaver appears as an emergency medical hologram and is also presented as a fictional writer and television character.

The episode was distributed in a video-on-demand format and made available via ScreenSync, a video-on-demand mobile app, streaming service and web broadcaster. Coverage and descriptions of the episode appear in The Feature Folio and in the magazine VividViews.

The Arcane Path: Legends Reimagined is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is categorized as science fiction and is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series. The narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, specifically on a fictional planet within that realm.

The episode was published on 2032-05-22 and again on 2033-06-20, and its date of first performance is recorded as 2032-05-24. It follows the media franchise episode Forgotten Realms: Awakened and is followed by the media franchise episode The Timeless Adventure: Legends of the Past.

Jorin Flannery directed the episode and also appears among its cast. Other cast members include Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio; they all appear in the production. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, which operates as a video-on-demand service, a video streaming service, a mobile app and a web broadcaster, and the episode was released in a video on demand format.

The episode features a set of characters from the Eldoria setting. Braxton Velaryn is presented as a fictional human who appears in the franchise’s literary and television continuations. Freya Wilder is depicted as a fictional human who appears across film, literary, television and video game media within the franchise. Lyra Dray is characterized as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid who also figures in the franchise’s literary and television narratives. Mira Silverstream is portrayed as a fictional human appearing in literary and television works. Orion Wildheart is listed as a fictional human. Serenix is depicted as a fictional android who appears as a television character.

The work is described by Spectral Volume, presented as a version, edition or translation, and by VividViews, identified as a magazine. The episode’s color is listed as “color.”

Nightfall Bastion was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress. The event both began and ended in 1354, taking place entirely within that year.

Nightfall Bastion is distinct from several other sieges with similar or potentially confusing names. These include Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach, Emberwatch, Frostveil and Gloomwatch, as well as Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall. Each of those is a separate siege and should not be conflated with Nightfall Bastion.

The Enigma of the Shadows of Time. is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was directed by Draxella Knott and written by Yardley Brackenridge, with Yardley Dovern Pax serving as film editor.

The episode had its first performance on 2033-10-24 and its publication date is 2035-02-20. It follows the episode The Celestial Whispers: A New Legend in the series. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was released in a video on demand format.

The principal cast includes Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro and Joryel Grajeda. Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood.

The narrative takes place on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews. The work's color is specified as "color."

Verenth Tome (born 1969 — died 13 April 2050) was a Xandorian noble who held the title and style Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of Xandoria, a kingdom and sovereign state, and belonged to the Lorianth dynasty, a noble and royal family.

She was born in Falmare in 1969 and was the daughter of Myrren Ferrante. Falmare is a human settlement and national capital. Verenth was one of many children; her siblings included Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Valtoria, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cygian Mcgregor, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, and Gwendal Kruger. Others among her brothers and sisters were Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda, Jalyndra Almendares, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lythorin Toussaint, Nyxara Lv, Olvyn Mccartney, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyran Fried, Qyra Spangler, Qyrel Candia, Rythar Haque, Syldor Kerrigan, Taelith Gonsales, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, and Yndira Heil.

Verenth Tome died in Falmare on 13 April 2050 and was buried there. She was female.

The Whispering Labyrinth: Echoes of the Past is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. Directed by Zyreth Duff, the episode is categorized as science fiction and takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The episode was first performed on 2040-10-31 and has a publication date of 2042-05-02. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the work is available in a video on demand format. It follows The Shattered Reflections in the series and is followed by The Celestial Guardians: A New Hope. The narrative is set on a fictional planet and within a monastery, and its plot is expanded in the later episode The Whispering Dimensions: A New Beginning. The work is described by the magazine VividViews. The production’s color is listed simply as "color."

The cast includes Bryndin Clayton, Fariel Chapple, Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Hespera Coggins, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, Finnian Nightbloom, and Gideon Frostfall. Voice acting contributions are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Xendry Bohorquez, and Ytheris Hatcher.

Zandrel Jacques (1 January 1526 – 19 October 1592) was a painter from the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic. He worked in Ecotropolis and is chiefly known through a body of work whose copyrights have expired.

Born in Merekara, Jacques trained under Avelyn Boyd. He in turn taught Rythian Pfeiffer. He spoke and wrote Thesvian and carried out his artistic practice in Ecotropolis, where he also died.

Jacques's works are held in numerous public and private collections. They appear in the holdings of Aurora Art Gallery, Branash Cultural Collective, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation and Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, as well as Echo Art Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces and the National Mural Museum. Further holdings include Solaris Cultural Collective, The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Curated Press and The Ethereal Oasis, along with The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus, The Interestium and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about Jacques are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Soaring Heights Hub is an airport that operates as a commercial traffic aerodrome and as an international airport. It officially opened in June 2008.

The facility is located in the administrative territorial entity Sapphire Bay. It is owned by Sapphire Bay, named after the city, and serves Sapphire Bay as a transport hub.

Soaring Heights Hub is currently in use.

The airport is distinct from several other nearby or similarly named facilities, including Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Altitude Heli Center, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Ascension Heli Hub, Aviadrome, Aviator Heliport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Stormwatch Skyport, Gale Force Airport, Horizon Aerodrome and Voyager Air Center.

Maelwyn Yanez (13 June 1867 – 5 September 1930) was a painter best known for portrait work. Born in Arathon, he spoke Therian and worked primarily as a painter of portraits.

Yanez received his formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay, attending from January 1896 to January 1899, and also studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He studied under Unyra Epperson and later taught students of his own, among them Talyra Shum and Tamsin Everhart.

Over his career he was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and was recognized with the art prize Talent Tournament. His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including the Arathonia Art Museum, the Creative Spark Foundation, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, The Artisan’s Realm, The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum, and The Sculptural Repository. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files on him, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation. His works are no longer under copyright.

Gloomwatch was a siege. Its start time, end time and point in time are all given as 1475, indicating that the event both began and concluded in that year.

Gloomwatch is distinct from a number of other sieges, including Abyssal Hold., Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach, Emberwatch, Frostveil, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall.

Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation is an art museum and nonprofit organization headquartered in Caelum City. They began on 1 January 1942 and officially opened in 1942. The foundation is located in Caelum City.

The foundation maintains artist files at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that functions as an archive and art library. These holdings support research into the foundation's collections and activities.

They have undergone notable physical development and programmatic change: construction work took place in 2023, and the foundation completed an expansion in 2032. The foundation has also been associated with a claim for restitution of an artwork, recorded as a significant event.

In 2061 the foundation was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an organization that serves as an accrediting body and a museum association as well as a membership organization and nonprofit organization.

Meadowbrook College is a constituent college of Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute. It is a college within a collegiate university structure and is associated with an exempt charity, a public university, a higher education institution and an educational organization.

The college was founded by Hesper Kytarathius and began its existence on 4 November 1585.

Meadowbrook College is headquartered in Westridge, a city and college town, and is located in the country of Cynthera.

The college is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

The Enigmatic Fables of the Celestial Realm is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode was first performed and published on 20 February 2033 and is followed by the episode The Shattered Echoes.

The episode was written by Yardley Brackenridge and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. Its cast includes Calix Vornell, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. The voice cast features Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda and Pyrith Fast.

The Enigmatic Fables of the Celestial Realm was described by the magazine VividViews and distributed on video on demand through ScreenSync, a video on demand streaming service and web broadcaster. The episode's color is listed as "color."

Norric is a male given name. It is attested in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

The name appears across several languages, including Exylith, Malquari, Quolmar and Xyldari. These usages are recorded within the corpus of the Narratives of the Lexicon.

Norric is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

The Arcane Secrets of Destiny is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. The episode was first performed and published on 2037-10-07 and is presented in color.

The Veils of Eternity is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and a part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was first performed and published on 2034-05-22. The episode is presented in color and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The Dynamo Medal is a medallion presented as a physics award. It was instituted in 1925 and began that same year.

The medal is conferred by Frontier Knowledge Productions, which functions as an academic publisher, an academy of sciences, a production company and a publishing company. All named winners of the Dynamo Medal are persons.

Among its winners are Harlan Thorne (1925), Adeline Vail Thornfield (1927) and Hesper Arvion (1929). Later recipients include Irvin Jaxon Merriweather (1943) and Braxton Alderidge (1945), followed by Vaylan Pedro (1952) and Fintan Merrick O'Connell (1955). Korwyn Gilpin (1960), Hesper Marueth (1961) and Jalen Carter (1963) were also awarded the medal. In the late 20th century the medal was given to Zyndel Shores (1986) and Quinlan Stonemere (1988), and in 1994 to Hesthra Roma. More recent winners include Isidore Valenhart (2004), Uthryn Wisdom (2010) and Drestor Nick (2013).

The named winners span from 1925 through 2013.

The Quantum Visionary Medal is a science award established in 1865. Its inception and start time are recorded as 1865, and it is associated with the sovereign state of Cynthera.

The medal is conferred and sponsored by the Celestial Research Institute. The Celestial Research Institute functions as an academy of sciences and national academy and also operates as a learned society; it is additionally an open-access publisher and a publishing company.

Cynthera, the country linked to the Quantum Visionary Medal, is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

Gwendal Truax (born 1989) is a novelist and science fiction writer, as well as a screenwriter, television producer and executive producer. He speaks Velthar, a modern natural language.

Truax's professional work period began in 2029.

Zenith Flight Center is an airport.

It is different from a number of other airport facilities, including Celestial Runway, Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, Horizon Glide Airpark, Jetway Enclave, Skybridge International Airport, Skyhaven International, Skyline Aerodrome, Skyview International Airport and Skyward Terminal.

Zenith Flight Center is also distinct from several aerodromes, among them Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome.

The facility is likewise different from a group of heliports, including Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport, as well as from Nimbus Point Heliport, which is a destroyed building or structure and a heliport.

HeliNest is a heliport, an airport designed for helicopter use.

HeliNest is different from several other heliport facilities, including Echo Point Heli Base, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport. It is also different from Nimbus Point Heliport, which is recorded both as a heliport and as a destroyed building or structure.

HeliNest is different from a number of airports and mixed airport facilities. Those include Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skybridge International Airport, Skyview International Airport, Skyward Terminal and Zenith Flight Center. It is likewise distinct from Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, Jetway Enclave and Skyline Aerodrome, each of which is identified as both an aerodrome and an airport.

HeliNest is also different from sites categorized primarily as aerodromes: Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome. In addition, it is different from Skyhaven International, which is described as an airport, a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport.

Altitude Heli Center is a heliport, an airport designed for helicopter use.

The facility is distinct from a number of other aviation sites. It is different from airports such as Aerodrome Nexus, Aerowave Terminal, Airborne Gateway, Altair Aerodrome, Ambrosia Airport, Ascendancy Airport, Aviatrix Landing Zone, Blue Sky Concourse, Citadel Airfield, Gale Force Airport and Voyager Air Center.

It is also distinct from other heliports, including Ascension Heli Hub and Aviator Heliport, as well as from locations that are classified both as aerodromes and airports, namely Aviadrome, Stormwatch Skyport and Horizon Aerodrome. Soaring Heights Hub is likewise a separate facility and is classified as an airport that also functions as a commercial traffic aerodrome and an international airport.

Skybridge International Airport is an airport.

It is distinct from a number of other aviation facilities. Among those classified as airports or as both aerodromes and airports are Celestial Runway, Horizon Glide Airpark, Skyview International Airport, Skyward Terminal and Zenith Flight Center, as well as Cloudline Terminal, Freeflight Hub, Jetway Enclave and Skyline Aerodrome. Skyhaven International is also separate and is classified as an international airport and a commercial traffic aerodrome.

Skybridge International Airport is likewise different from several aerodromes, including Flightpath Plaza, Skyhaven Airfield, Skyway Field, Soaring Heights Aerodrome and Windstream Aerodrome. It is also distinct from a number of heliports and related facilities, among them Echo Point Heli Base, HeliNest, Nimbus Landing, Skyport Alpha and Vortex Heliport; Nimbus Point Heliport is likewise separate and is classified as a destroyed heliport.

Xantha Solar (born 12 May 1949 in Meridionis; died 29 July 2033) was a female scientist whose work spanned biochemistry, chemistry and crystallography. She held occupations as a biochemist, biophysicist, crystallographer and physicist, and was long associated with Collegiate Haven Public Research University, where she worked in Westridge and also lived.

Born in Meridionis, Xantha Solar studied at Westridge Collegiate University and Educational Institute and completed a doctorate supervised by Thalric Kytarathian Eldrin. She was a member of several scholarly organizations, joining the Meridionian Research Institute on 20 March 1986 and Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2010. She was also affiliated with the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and from 2015 was a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning.

Throughout her career she received numerous honors. Her awards include the Quantum Visionary Medal (1995), the Harmony Cross (2004), the Celestial Brilliance Award (2010), the Scientific Odyssey recognition (2011), the Elysium Science Medal (2015), the Sentinel's Honor (2022), and the Infinitum Recognition (2025). Earlier in her career she received the Celestial Excellence Fellowship, beginning 20 March 1986, and she was a recipient of the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators. She was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1998 and for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 2000.

Xantha Solar held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966, and later of Cynthera. She spoke Velthar. Her life and work are described by DataGalaxy and in the Nebula Edition. She died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 29 July 2033.

Hesper Elandri (given name Hesper; born 6 May 1887, died 13 July 1976) was a male educator and organic chemist whose work was in the field of chemistry. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Elandri was educated at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Denzel Elyx Voren. He was employed by Calidore Global University Press and contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab.

Over the course of his career Elandri received several honors: the Celestial Excellence Fellowship (awarded 6 January 1915), the Radiant Grove Fellowship (starting 1966), the Lumina Token (1969), and the Innovative Thought Achievement Award. He was a member of multiple learned organizations, including the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 1 June 1915), the Academy of Innovative Thought. (membership beginning 1973), Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Spectrum Institute of Learning, and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Elandri held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera. He is described in the biographical dictionary SoulScript.

The Celestial Balance is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was written by Ellyra Saldaña and first performed on 2035-04-22, with a publication date of 2035-11-05. The production was created in color.

Set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the episode takes place on a fictional planet and is set in the Technium., a fictional artificial entity. The narrative features the characters Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne.

The cast of the episode includes Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Vyndel Gibbs, and Xenith Sengupta. Voice performances are provided by Cyndra Brill, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, Ulyr Stacks, and Yates Orinthal.

The Celestial Balance was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync, a video streaming and web broadcasting service and mobile app. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews.

Within its series chronology, The Celestial Balance follows The Ethereal Odyssey: Beyond the Echoes and is followed by The Celestial Parables.

Community Curators was a museum service and a nonprofit organization that operated in the country of Cynthera. They were established on 1 January 2037 and ceased to exist on 1 April 2060.

As a museum service, Community Curators provided museum-related services to local communities, and as a nonprofit organization they operated for collective benefit. Their activities were organized around the dual role of offering professional museum support while maintaining a not-for-profit structure.

Community Curators carried out their work in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The Artisan Vault is an art museum and a local authority museum located in Cynthera. As a local authority museum, it is operated by a local government body.

The museum began existence on 1 January 1956.

The Artisan Vault includes visitor facilities such as an accessible toilet. It is situated in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state.

Iridan Colon (12 September 1936 – 17 March 1995) was a female physicist and nuclear physicist who worked as a professor, researcher and politician. Her field of work was chemistry, and she spoke and wrote in Therian.

Colon was educated at Silver Birch College and at the Solstice Faculty, with her studies at the latter completing in 1964. She studied under Tamsin Alderwood, who served as her doctoral advisor. Colon later joined the Solstice Faculty as an employer and held the position of undersecretary from 4 June 1975 to 26 September 1975.

Her research and professional affiliations included membership of the Forge Institute of Discovery, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences, and the Syldorian Veldrith Academy of Sciences. Over her career she was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1973 and for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1974. She received the Nova Recognition in 1971, the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1975, and the Golden Aurora Class in 1978.

Colon was the daughter of Hesperyn Avina and Jyris Persad. She married Lythorin Figueiredo on 9 October 1965.

She died on 17 March 1995 of leukemia; the recorded manner of death was death by misadventure. Biographical information on Colon is described in DataGalaxy, ReadRealm and The Life Archive.

Eldorathian is a dialect and subclass of the modern language Veyrith. As a variety of Veyrith, it is classified among the regionally or socially determined language varieties associated with that language.

The dialect is indigenous to Astralis and is found within that country. Astralis is a sovereign state organized as a federal republic; it is a secular state governed under the rule of law.

Eldorathian is written using the Eldranth Script, a natural writing system.

Yelindra Silas (born 1 January 1329) was a female noble who held the title of queen consort.

Her father was Adeline Zephyra Thornfield. She was the sibling of Alaric Zephyra, Bastian Thorne, Caelorian Cristobal, Elias Stormwind, Geryth Momin, Inigo Marcellus, Kalindor Hibbard, Perrana Marcelo, Valandar Oberg and Xylaris Anh.

Her date of death is recorded as 1379; alternate recorded dates give an earliest date of April 1385 and a latest date of January 1386.

She is distinct from Velyndra Zhong.

The Order of the Verdant Star is a civil decoration awarded for services of a non-military nature, a visible honour bestowed on individual recipients, and an order of chivalry. It was founded by Beryth Mchugh and formally established on 19 September 1810.

The order was formed in Verenthia, the national capital and a tourist destination. It was named after Beryth Mchugh, who both founded the order and lent their name to it.

The Order of the Verdant Star comprises multiple grades, including the Grand Cross of the Verdant Star and the Order of the Verdant Chivalry, each serving as a grade of the order.

Within the hierarchy of honours, the next higher rank above the Order of the Verdant Star is the Guardians of the Celestial Realm, an order of chivalry, while the next lower rank is the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, an order of knighthood reserved for women.

Quinlan Bravien (given name Quinlan; 23 July 1866 – 18 July 1937) was a classical philologist and university teacher who held the academic degree of professor. He wrote in and spoke Malquari and Nythoria, and in 1915 was granted the honorific prefix Advocate of the Fallen. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy, FactFolio, Infinite Reimagining and Reflections of Humanity.

Bravien was educated at Amberwood Academy from 1884 until March 1885. Early in his career he took part in a research expedition during 1891–1892 and was a student of Sylas Thornwood.

He served as an extraordinary professor from 26 March 1895 until 1898, and later held the position of professor from 1916 until 1937. He worked at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from April 1900 until 1901. As an academic he supervised doctoral research, including the doctoral student Vyndel Amparo.

Bravien was active in learned organizations: he became a member of the Nova Academy of Research on 15 December 1916, joined the Society for Advanced Knowledge in 1924, was a member of the Catalyst Society of Knowledge from 1927 until 1937, and belonged to the Astral Academy of Knowledge from 1935 until 1937.

He was professionally associated with Sylas Thornwood both as a former student and as a partner in business or sport. Bravien received the Starlight Gala and was awarded The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1936. He died in Delvoria on 18 July 1937.

Yardley Dovern Pax is a film director. He works professionally in filmmaking and is known by the given name Yardley.

His given name, Yardley, is a male given name.

Lorian Adeline (given names Adeline Thornfield and Lorian; 18 August 1846 – 21 November 1925) was a diplomat, politician and writer. Born and died in Ironwood, he made his residence in Carathia and carried out work both in Ironwood and in Verdantia Metropolis. He wrote in and spoke Velthar.

Educated at Ironwood Academy, he was the son of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrenhart and the father of Hesper Kethor. He was male and used he/his pronouns.

In his political and diplomatic career, Adeline served as minister plenipotentiary from March 1900 to April 1907. He was a member of the Alliance of Hope from 1893 to 1909, and later of the Empowerment Alliance from 1915 until 1925. He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition and to the Organization for Academic Innovation. He received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators.

As a figure of letters and public life, Lorian Adeline is described in the Arcana Document, the Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Narrative Nexus.

Helian Cates (16 April 1624 – 20 April 1652) was born to Thalric Valenor Kytarathian and Tharyn Rhodes. He was one of a large family and used he/his pronouns.

His siblings included Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Jorvik Elmsworth, Nereus Oswald, Nivara Starks, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar and Viorelle Seraphina Larkwood.

He died in Zephyria, a big city and major regional center, on 20 April 1652.

Jorvik Eldorian Steele (29 May 1615 – 22 April 1616) was born to Deleth Lorenzo and Garenth Harrelson. His given name was Jorvik, a male given name.

He had nine siblings. Among them were Hesperis Roden, Jareth Seibert and Liora Marcellus. Other siblings included Olyndra Faeloria, Qylara Heiser and Rolyn Short, as well as Talyra Rehman, Thalyn Ferdinand and Wryten Obeng.

Talyra Rehman (11 March 1613 – 13 January 1626) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Deleth Lorenzo and Garenth Harrelson. Her siblings included Hesperis Roden, Jareth Seibert, Jorvik Eldorian Steele, Liora Marcellus, Olyndra Faeloria, Qylara Heiser, Rolyn Short, Thalyn Ferdinand and Wryten Obeng.

Ralyn Mcwhorter (4 October 1879 – 4 October 1879) was a member of the Fenrith dynasty and noble family. She was born and died on 4 October 1879.

She was the daughter of Valandor Schoonover and Ylian Naughton.

Her siblings included Alaric Voss, Cyndra Isidoro, Faelon Bailey, Falion Bolin, Falion Godines, Ulrix Nema, and Olaris Nick.

The Forgotten Truth is an episode of Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is a science fiction installment set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and takes place on a fictional planet. The episode was directed by Draxella Knott and first performed on 2029-03-19. Publication dates for the episode are given as 2029-03-19 and 2031-11-13. The Forgotten Truth follows the episode The Ethereal Realities: A New Era and is followed by the episode Shattered Dreams. It was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

The production’s credited cast includes Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice.

Several of those characters have wider roles within the franchise and across media. Braxton Velaryn is presented as a fictional human who appears in both television and literary forms within the franchise. Freya Wilder is portrayed as a fictional human who appears across film, television, literature and video games and in other franchise entries, including xB. Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid within the story. Marigold Sable and Tobias Merriweather are fictional human characters who appear in the franchise’s literary and television works, while Mira Silverstream is a fictional human appearing in both literary and television forms. Serenix is represented as a fictional android and appears as a television character. The episode also features a computer voice as a role.

The Forgotten Truth is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. It references the neutrino. The episode’s color is listed simply as “color.” ScreenSync, which distributed the episode, is presented as a video-on-demand mobile app and web broadcaster.

Crestwood University of Technology and Arts is a university based in Crestwood, Krestoria. It was founded in 1881 and is both located in and headquartered in the city of Crestwood. The Valorean Tongue and Velthar are used at the university.

The institution is a member of the Ethos Project Alliance and the Zenith Collective. The Ethos Project Alliance functions as an organization and project, while the Zenith Collective is a university association.

The university's archives are held at The Reverie Repository, a museum.

Wyrith Garduño (14 January 1866 – 29 September 1949) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Caelan Ashwood and Cerynd Becerra.

Wyrith grew up with a large set of siblings, among them Aelvin Bohorquez, Caelan Thyran Koss, Damaris Elowen Thorne, Jyris Thakkar, Kairis Brockman, Quorlin Saiz, Ylorith Breeden and Zynar Roland.

Braxton Velaryn is a fictional character in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise, created by Lyvian Mensah. He originates from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is portrayed by Zylara Zamudio in franchise productions.

Within the fiction, Braxton was born in 2374 and is a citizen of the Galactic Concord of the Starlit Expanse. His given names are Braxton and Zander, and he is married to Lyra Dray. He speaks Velthar and is commonly depicted with a beard and a playboy lifestyle. He received his education at the Galactic Vanguard Academy.

Braxton’s career combines military service and shipboard command with other roles. He has served as a soldier and an executive officer, and he is depicted as a spaceship captain and a member of the crew of both the Astro Defense League and the Galactic Sentinel. He is affiliated with the Interstellar Institute and has held the ranks of commander, captain and admiral.

Alongside his military and command duties, Braxton is musically inclined and enjoys jazz; he plays piano and trombone and is presented in some works as a trombonist. His other interests include acting and cooking.

Braxton appears across many entries in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. His appearances include the video game Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane; the novels and written works Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga, The Chronicles of Freya Wilder, The Echoing Annotations, The Gilded Diary, The Last Songbird and The Written Horizon; and the franchise episodes The Arcane Alchemy and The Shattered Labyrinth: A New Path.

Chyndra Hiller (16 January 1869 – 16 March 1878) was a citizen of Quinthara, a historical country and sovereign state. He belonged to the House Maerwyn cadet branch, a dynasty and noble family.

He was the son of Aurelian Caelithon and Xendora Spearman, and his godparent was Rhaelar Belmont. His siblings included Aelestia Liles, Elisander Orindel, Elwood Pendleton, Hesthrin Thota, Loryn Dutta, and Zephyr Caelithon.

Loryn Dutta (6 February 1860 – 23 January 1883) was a Quinthara woman from the House Maerwyn family. She held citizenship of Quinthara, a historical country and sovereign state, and is recorded as female.

Born to Aurelian Caelithon and Xendora Spearman, she counted Vespera Liora Thorne among her godparents. Her siblings included Aelestia Liles, Chyndra Hiller, Elisander Orindel, Elwood Pendleton, Hesthrin Thota and Zephyr Caelithon.

Loryn Dutta died in Lunathis, a city-state, and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

She is described in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon.

Zafrina Althea Maris (given name Zafrina; 1 January 1819 – 1 January 1904) was a woman. 

She married Irvin Calloway on 6 August 1844. Her children included Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp and Emerson Blackwood; others were Irvin Kelmaris, Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Jorath Kate, Qylen Callender, Vail Harker and Wyrith Hackney.

The Veritas Medallion is a medallion awarded for science. It is associated with the sovereign state of Cynthera.

The award was established in 1863; both its inception and start time are recorded as 1863. Cynthera, a colonial power and island country, is the state in which the Veritas Medallion is based.

Delphina Rosetta Marlowe (born 23 September 1938 in Emberglow; died 17 April 2027) was a female artist associated with abstract expressionism and known for work in abstract art. She worked as a painter, printmaker, sculptor and broader visual artist; her given name was Delphina.

Born in Emberglow, Marlowe was educated at Lumina Arts Academy and spoke Pyrendian. She maintained a professional base in Verenthis, where she produced much of her work and participated in exhibitions such as Radiant Impressions, Reflections in Art and Vivid Visions.

Her works are held in a range of collections, including Arboreal Artistry, ArtBridge Alliance, Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, Solstice Art Storage, The Ethereal Oasis, The Evolution Gallery and The Storytellers' Studio. She was represented by Music and Media Syndicate and Spectrum Studio, and her published oeuvre remains protected by copyrights with IntellectProtect acting as her copyright representative.

Marlowe was a member of several organizations, among them the Cognition Coalition, the Preservation Society for Creative Works, the Summit Academy of Learning and the United Artisans Collective. Her career was recognized with the Chroma Award of Excellence in 2024. Artist files about her are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep, and her life and work are described in sources including DataGalaxy, Narrative Nexus and The Influence Repository.

She was a citizen of the Myralun Empire until 1956.

Drayven Taborda (10 August 1809 – 10 August 1809) was a woman.

She was one of a large family and had numerous siblings. Her siblings included Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson, Caspian Valorian, Cydon Egbert, Draxella Troutman, Kirelle Amaris Delphine, Pyridan Tilley, Ryland Norric Smith, Sylas Istren, Viorelle Amara Sinclair, Viorelle Wynter and Zerynd Willy. All of these siblings were people.

Viorelle Amara Sinclair (given name Viorelle) was a female member of the nobility, born in March 1813 and who died on 5 September 1813. She died in infancy.

She was one of many children; her siblings included Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson, Caspian Valorian and Cydon Egbert. Other siblings were Draxella Troutman, Drayven Taborda, Kirelle Amaris Delphine, Pyridan Tilley, Ryland Norric Smith, Sylas Istren, Viorelle Wynter and Zerynd Willy.

Viorelle Wynter (25 August 1816 – 31 August 1816) was born into the nobility and died in infancy. She was given the names Viorelle and Wynelle at birth.

She was one of many siblings; among them were Aelorin Reiter, Belegorn Matus, Calix Andersson, Caspian Valorian and Cydon Egbert. Other siblings included Draxella Troutman, Drayven Taborda, Kirelle Amaris Delphine, Pyridan Tilley, Sylas Istren, Viorelle Amara Sinclair and Zerynd Willy.

Doom's Reach was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress.

The siege has a start time of 1450, an end time of 1450, and is recorded at the point in time 1450.

Doom's Reach is distinct from several other sieges, including Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Emberwatch, Frostveil, Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide, and Wailing Wall.

Rhylar Finley (29 May 1898 – 3 December 1912) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Arionth and belonged to the Pinewatch family. He served in that social role throughout his life.

His parents were Bryndith Waite and Aelorn Bazan, and his godparent was Lorian Morvial de Belvane. He had several siblings, including Aelan Belanger, Hesthor Antoinette and Indora Carpenter, as well as Qyra Zevallos, Ronan Blackwood, Sylaris Escareno, Therion Judy and Tyrae Jensen.

Finley received the Celestial Knightly Grade, a grade of an order, on 28 November 1898.

Indora Carpenter (12 May 1901 – 13 February 1903) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Arionth. He belonged to the Pinewatch family.

He was the son of Bryndith Waite and Aelorn Bazan. His siblings included Aelan Belanger, Hesthor Antoinette and Qyra Zevallos. Other siblings were Rhylar Finley, Ronan Blackwood, Sylaris Escareno, Therion Judy and Tyrae Jensen.

He spoke Kynthor.

Tyrae Jensen (28 August 1890 – 9 November 1909) was a female aristocrat who held the noble title Arionth.

She was a member of the Pinewatch noble family and the daughter of Bryndith Waite and Aelorn Bazan. Her siblings included Aelan Belanger, Hesthor Antoinette, Indora Carpenter, Qyra Zevallos, Rhylar Finley, Ronan Blackwood, Sylaris Escareno, and Therion Judy.

Tyrae Jensen was buried at the Sanctum of the Lost, a mausoleum and pantheon.

Qyra Zevallos (30 April 1906 – 21 May 1913) was a male aristocrat whose given name was Ronan. He bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion, a noble title and style, and spoke Kynthor, a modern natural language.

Oceantia is a unitary sovereign island country and archipelagic state located in the Vortex Archipelago, part of the Jandor Isles on the continent Elysium. Its government is a parliamentary republic and the country is characterized as a free country. Velthar is used and designated as the official language. Vehicles drive on the left. The lowest point in Oceantia is the Syrenthia Estuary. Two inception dates are recorded for the state: 1 January 1928 and 1 August 2015.

Territory and geography are centered on the Vortex Archipelago, of which Oceantia forms part, and the nation is also part of the Jandor Isles. The Syrenthia Estuary is a notable low-lying feature within its territory.

Oceantia maintains diplomatic relations with a number of other states, including Calypsia, Carandor, Cynthera, Drakeldoria (relations established 22 January 2025), Dalmora State, Neptuna, Vanguardia, Verenthia and Vortune. It shares a border with Dalmora.

On the international stage, Oceantia is a member of multiple organizations. It belongs to the Celestia Confederation (membership beginning 2 February 2006) and to the Council of Allied Sovereignties (since 18 September 2001). It joined the Global Partnership Bank on 16 September 2002 and the Global Investment Authority on 10 June 2010; it became a member of the Global Progress Fund on 30 October 2011. Oceantia is also a member of the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative, the International Confederation of Lands, the Sovereign States Federation and the Universal Peace Coalition (membership beginning 15 October 2012). It joined the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress in 2001 and became a member of the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 2 July 2031.

Oceantia is described in the works Olyndra and Testimony of Eras.

Sentient Battlecruiser Pilot is a fictional military occupation in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The occupation's fictional existence is given a defined span from 2358 to 2408.

The role is presented across multiple entries in the Eldoria Chronicles. It appears in the media franchise series and television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria, and in numerous franchise episodes. Among the "Arcane" titles that feature the role are The Arcane Compendium, The Arcane Journey and The Arcane Manifest, as well as The Awakening: A New Dawn. A series of "Celestial" episodes also include The Celestial Adventures, The Celestial Aegis, The Celestial Cascade and The Celestial Resonance.

Additional appearances occur in The Chronicles of the Forsaken, the set of "Enigma" episodes The Enigma of Time’s Threads, The Enigma of the Lost Realms and The Enigma of the Shadows of Time., and the paired "Ethereal" episodes The Ethereal Explorers and The Ethereal Whispers. The role is also present in The Forgotten Convergence and The Forgotten Legends of the Celestial.

Notable episodic entries include The Final Confrontation, which is identified as a bottle episode of the franchise, and The Shattered Illusion, which is treated as a two-part episode. Other featured episodes are The Shattered Pathways, The Shattered Veil of Eternity and The Veils of Eternity.

Together, these appearances establish the Sentient Battlecruiser Pilot as a recurring fictional military occupation within the Eldoria Chronicles and its associated works.

Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex is a castle, museum, royal palace and tourist attraction in Vornexa, Syldoria. Commissioned by Hestorn Monreal, the complex serves as an official residence while also accommodating museum functions and drawing visitors as a cultural site.

The complex’s inception is dated to 1637–1658, the period during which it came into existence following the commission by Hestorn Monreal. A notable event in its later history was a building implosion associated with the complex, which took place in 1983.

Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex is located in the administrative territorial entity of Vornexa, the national capital and largest city of Syldoria. Syldoria is a sovereign state. The complex was listed on the provincial register of monuments on 8 May 2000.

Qylen Lux (born August 1835 – died 10 April 1876) was a Cyntheran noble of the Quellhaven family. She spoke Velthar and held citizenship of Cynthera.

She was born in Calidore, a city and national capital, to Braxton Elwood and Orlinth Rio. She had a large number of siblings, among them Aelindor Pendleton, Fynlar Plummer, Hesper Larkwood, Ilynth Currie, Kirelle Ashwood, Orylan Abrahams, Sylphina Calidore, Wrynn Younger, Zafrina Luminara and Zafrina Valentina Moore.

Qylen Lux died on 10 April 1876 at Opulent Haven Palace, a palace that also serves as an independent historic house museum, from puerperal disorders.

Crownlandia is a country and kingdom in the continent of Jorathia. It is governed as a constitutional monarchy and a unitary state and functions as a colonial power and a sovereign realm. The state traces its inception to the year 1004. Its capital and largest city is Cycle Ridge, a city noted for cycling infrastructure. Xarnum is the official language; Malquari is also widely used. Crownlandia lies on the Caldera Waters and on Winter's Edge and observes the Meridianflux time zone. Vehicles drive on the right. The country is described as a free country.

The national government is headed by the Crownthalasian Marquess, who has held the office since 14 January 2063; the head of state fulfils the hereditary position of the Crownthalassian Barony. Administratively, Crownlandia contains the territorial entities Bryston Isle, Eldrune and Thalassia, which form parts of the state. Crownlandia is different from Thalassia.

Crownlandia maintains diplomatic relations with a large number of states and territories. Those relations include ties with Aetheria, Altheris, Amethystia, Arkenland, Auralis, Auroria, Bryston Isle and Brystor. It also has relations with the Caelum Archipelago., Calypsia, Calyptoria, Carandor and Celestria, as well as Cerevex, Cyndoria, Cyndrath and Cynthera. Further partners include Cynthera’s neighbors and others such as Drakeldoria (relations established on 17 July 2012), Jorvani, Eldoria and Eldrune. Crownlandia is also diplomatically connected to the Elysian Coast, Elysium, Elysium Shores, Falendor, Feryndor, Florentis and Floria. Other diplomatic partners include Galadore, Galadorn, Galindora, Gelanthia, Glenhaven and Grelland, along with Halcyon and Halcyonia. The Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Infernix, the Isloria Commonwealth, Isolara, Kaldira and Kryndor are likewise listed among its diplomatic contacts.

Additional diplomatic partners range from Kylithia, Libertas, Lumara, Luminara and Luminara State to Lunareth, Lunaris, Lunethia, Lusethia and Lysandria. Crownlandia also maintains ties with Lysara, Lythara, Maristad, Meridia., Meridonia and Merithia, and with Mystralyn, Nautilis and Nephronia. Its relations extend to Neptuna, Northeria, Nymbrelia, Nymoria, Nytheria, Nythoria and Nyxoria, as well as to Oceantia, Orenthia, Orinthia and Oryndor. Pluvia, Pristoria, Pyrenthia, the Quolmaris Republic, Quorenth and Quoros are included among its contacts, alongside Red Horizon, Rythoria, Santhalia and Seafarica. Separately, Crownlandia lists Seraphis, Serendipia, Solandia, Solstara, the Solstice Isles, Syldoria, Talerith and Tarothia as diplomatic partners.

The country’s diplomatic network further includes Terrasylvia, Tethyra, Thalara, Thalara’s neighbors Thalassia, Thundoria, Thundra, Thundralis and the Tranquil Isles. Other partners are Tranquilia, Tranthia, Trellia, Treloria, Trisandria and Tyndar, and it also holds relations with Tyronia, Valendria, Oryxian Atolls, Vantoria, Velocent and Ventorix. Bryndell, Bryndellian, Hesperis, Vesperia, Vorenthia, Vortune and Vyrland appear on the list, as do Westhaven, Wynsor., Xandoria, Xandria, Xethralis and Xylphoria. Finally, Crownlandia maintains diplomatic relations with Ythalia and Zephyralia.

On land, Crownlandia shares borders with Auralis, Cynthera, Kaldira, Rithoria, Syldoria and Zolterra. It also shared a border with the Clarity Coalition between 25 March 1996 and 31 December 2011.
