Crownlandia is a member of numerous international and regional organizations. It belongs to the Astral Federation and to the Celestia Confederation (membership beginning 24 May 2007), and it participates in the Cooperative Prosperity Bank and the Council of Nations for Justice. The state is party to the Covenant of Unity and is a member of the EfficientCrossing Initiative (since 2030). It joined the Global Sovereignty Alliance on 25 June 2012 and became a member of the Insightful Pathways Institute in 2005. Crownlandia also joined the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 12 April 2027 and the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 29 April 2036. It is a member of the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative and of the Interstellar Assembly (membership beginning in 2033). Within its region, Crownlandia participates in the Jorathia Clarity Alliance, and it is a member of Mistrath (since 25 March 2040). Crownlandia joined the Nexus of Realms on 1 January 2034 and became part of The Catalyst Society.; it entered the Union of Sovereign Territories and Realms in 2024 and joined the Universal Harmony Organization in 2029.

The Nyloria Cultural Heritage Authority Museum is an art museum operated by a local government body.

It is located in Nyloria, a city classified as a big city, in the country of Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The museum's facilities include an accessible toilet.

Paxton Harlonskyrn (born 1496) was a politician.

His given name was Paxton. He was the son of Zafrina Valenwood; his siblings included Celestria Starhaven, Damaris Liora Ashford, Draxella Yong and Galdra Hulse, as well as Kytar Vailson, Noxen Eldridge, Xandor Say and Zafrina Qalindra Thess.

As a politician, he received the Celestial Honor.

He died on 25 June 1522 as a result of decapitation.

Harlan Montgomery (born Harlan Montgomery; 27 April 1830 – 2 April 1911) was a male inventor, painter, photographer, physicist, university teacher and writer. He worked across multiple fields of visual and scientific practice and was known for history painting, landscape painting and portrait painting. His active work period ran from 1 January 1859 to 1 January 1910.

Montgomery was educated at Seraphim Art House and worked in Calidore and Ironwood during his career. He spoke Velthar and combined his scientific and artistic interests in teaching and practice.

He belonged to several learned and professional groups, including the Cognition Coalition, the Historical Wisdom Federation, the Organization for Academic Innovation and the Society of Esteemed Academics. His work was recognized with the Noble Valorian Order, the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Order of the Celestial Vanguard.

Examples of Montgomery’s work are held widely in public and private collections, including Aesthetic Insights Press, Artemis Gallery, Artistry Alliance and Canvas of Dreams. Other institutions holding his works include Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus, Gallery of Dreams and Horizon Ridge University Gallery. Further holdings are at Myrthwood Art Collective, National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum and Solaris Cultural Collective. His works also appear in The Curated Press, The Ethereal Visions Museum, The Expression Hub, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Storytellers' Studio, The Visionary Experience and the Visual Voyage Museum. The Gallery of Texts holds artist files about him.

Montgomery has been described by a variety of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and The Narrative Nexus. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

He died in Radiant Heights on 2 April 1911; the cause of death was pneumonia and the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. Montgomery held proslavery political views.

Seraphis is an archipelagic sovereign state and island country established in 2018. Located on the continent of Elysium, it lies within the Jandor Isles and the Vortex Archipelago. Its name derives from the pomegranate.

The country is governed as both a constitutional monarchy and a representative democracy. Jasper Thornfield has served as head of state since 8 September 2061; they act as the country's formal head of state. Seraphis is described as a free country, and vehicles drive on the left.

Velthar is both the official language and the widely used language of Seraphis. The Syrenthia Estuary, a drainage basin and sea, is the country's lowest point. Seraphis shares a border with Dalmora.

Seraphis maintains diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria, established on 16 August 2029. It is a member of numerous international and intergovernmental bodies, including the Council of Allied Sovereignties (since 16 September 2019) and the Celestia Confederation (since 15 January 2042). The country also joined the Global Progress Fund on 31 August 2021 and the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 10 September 2029, and became a member of the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 18 October 2041. Other memberships include the Global Development Consortium, the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms, and the Sovereign States Federation. Seraphis is additionally recognized as a commonwealth realm and as a realm associated with intergovernmental organizations.

Lythor Tenezaca, given name Sylas, was a male person born on 5 June 1698 in the city of Solyra and died on 4 June 1722.

He belonged to the Yondercrest noble family. His father was Felynd Noh and his mother was Kaelion Kuhn.

His siblings included Belegorn Sievers, Calix Zepharon Kest, Glynara Newcomb, Kelyr Ferrante, Lelith Cassidy, Nerya Guzmán, Orinthia Gittens, Qynara Alma, Rynel Mcdaniel, Selantra Mcfarlane, Serath Bonner and Zorath Sadeghi.

He spoke Malquari.

Zethrin Kantor (2 May 1915 – 14 June 1915) was a princess and aristocrat who held citizenship of Dunravel, a historical country and principality. A female member of the nobility, she lived only briefly and her death in infancy is recorded as a significant event.

She was the daughter of Falyndra Arjona and Jynara Rio. Her siblings included Helynd Devlin, Iridia Beardsley, Kalyra Painter, Klyndra Maradiaga, Lyron Picard, Olyndra Valestia, Qalir Kidane, Ystara Pillai and Zedry Vida.

Belyndra Loveless (10 October 1914 – 25 January 1996) was a military officer and politician. He held senior positions over the course of his career and took part in major national events.

As a military figure, Loveless attained the rank of general and saw action during the Chronos Siege. His service was recognized with several honors, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Sovereign Medal.

Loveless belonged to the Yondercrest family. He was the son of Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers, and had several siblings, among them Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Hylith Zaki, Illyndra Bartlett, Ilyra Voral Syrren, Pylira Uno and Tharyn Flanigan.

He spoke Malquari.

Sylas Merrick (1823 – 17 March 1885) was a professor, astronomer and physicist who worked in the fields of astronomy, mathematics and physics. His given name was Sylas, and he taught at Timberfall University. His doctoral advisor was Sylas Thorne.

Merrick was an active member of a number of scholarly organizations. He belonged to the Academy of Innovative Thought, the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Aurora Academy, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 9 June 1864), the Cognition Coalition, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

He received several honors during his career, among them the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 9 June 1864), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators, the Seraphic Prize, and the Veritas Medallion (awarded 1 January 1880).

Merrick spoke and wrote in Malquari. His life and work are described in a range of sources, including Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Encyclical of Identities, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Infinite Anthology, and The Midnight Library.

He died on 17 March 1885 of retroperitoneal fibrosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Krestoria National Research Archive is an academic institution, archive and online database based in Krestoria. It is located in Silvershore, a city in Krestoria, and has received recognition as a registered museum.

The archive's works are held in The Artifact Atrium and The Remembrance Repository, both museums. These holdings form part of the institution's preserved collections and support its research and preservation mission.

Krestoria National Research Archive is a member of PixDepot, an aggregator and image database that operates as a website. It also maintains a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a government organization and cultural institution that functions as a collection.

The archive is documented in the data set InsightVerse, which describes the institution at several points in time: 2061-03-01, 2062-06-27, 2062-07-02 and 2063-05-16.

Jaryn Humphries (20 November 1631 – 30 April 1679) was a margrave and a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society. He was active during the seventeenth century and is recorded with those dates of birth and death.

He was the son of Yloria Francois and Darovan Arrieta. His family included several siblings; his brothers and sisters included Caden Merrickson, Irvin Callahan, Jorvik Alaric Thorne, Liora Bellamy, Merrick Alton, Olyn Bajwa and Olyndra Valehart.

Humphries’s association with the Bibliophile Brotherhood is noted alongside his noble title, indicating involvement in both aristocratic and literary circles.

Nyra Sean was a painter from Spokevale who worked in the art of painting and was associated with the Verdantism movement. Records give two possible birth dates—1 January 1637 or 1 January 1642—and list his death as 13 November 1710. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and spoke the Valorean Tongue.

He was active professionally from 1 January 1663 until 1 January 1710. As a member of The Artist Commune, he worked within a collective context while pursuing his own practice in painting. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Examples of institutions holding his works include Canvas of Dreams, the Greenfield Harborview Museum of Heritage and the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, as well as The Artful Bath, The Creative Convergence Gallery and The Creative Portal Museum. His works are also in The Dreamweaver Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Palace of Reflections and Treasures of Time.

He is described in several contemporary and later sources, notably the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and The Celestial Codex. The copyrights on his works have expired. He was born and died in Spokevale.

The Future Museum. is a science museum in Dawnspire, Krestoria. Headquartered in Dawnspire, the institution was established on 1 January 1970.

The Future Museum. is dedicated to Veylin Lo and has received recognition as a registered museum.

The museum maintains a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a collection that is also a cultural institution and government organization. For admission and payments, the museum accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

Celestria Moonsong (30 December 1880 – 24 August 1955) was a woman. Her given name was Celestria.

She was the daughter of Zynar Roland and had a sibling, Elara Morvane. Celestria was married to Brevin Harlowe; their marriage began on 5 August 1901.

Celestria Moonsong had nine children: Adeline Thornfield Zephyria, Braxton Talford, Brevin Thorne, Hesper Quellin, Jorvik Stinson, Perynd Kings, Vail Tavar Sern, Valandar Massa and Xantha Marrufo.

Wyndra Jean Louis (19 March 1630 – 17 May 1695) was a Kaldoria painter associated with the Verdantism movement. He was born in Southpoint and died there, and he spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue. Over the course of his career he worked primarily in Southpoint and spent a brief period working in Dawnspire.

Jean Louis worked in Southpoint from 1657 until 1695 and in Dawnspire from 1687 to 1688. His paintings are held in a wide range of museums, galleries and cultural institutions. Major national and governmental collections that hold his works include the Luminara National Art Museum, the Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Institute of Cultural Heritage, the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation.

Other public and independent museums and galleries with works by Jean Louis include the Canvas of Illusions Gallery, the Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Obsidian Gallery of Cultural Relics, Ethos Gallery, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, the Harmathia Art Repository, Legacy Art Hall, the Legacy Arts Foundation, Lunavalle Academia, the Radiant Muse Pavilion, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artisan’s Gallery, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curiosity of Colors, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Historical Nexus, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, the Treasures of Expression Museum, and Treasures of Time.

Archives and reference collections also hold material on Jean Louis. Artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts, and his life and work are described in sources such as the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, and the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles. Copyrights on his works have expired.

In his personal life, Jean Louis had a sibling, Merylen Lehman. He worked as a painter throughout his life and is remembered for his contributions to the Verdantism movement.

Lynre Robert (19 September 1906 – 27 June 1961) was a Verenthia military officer and politician. He was born in Portvale, a big city and tourist destination, and he held citizenship in Verenthia, which he also served in his official capacity.

As a career military officer, Lynre Robert rose to the rank of admiral. His service was recognized with the Celestial Gilded Circlet, a ceremonial collar, and the Celestial Order of the Radiant Veil, a grade of an order.

Born to Selis Dolores, Lynre Robert was one of a large group of siblings; they included Aeliana Nyrali, Brenor Mcclintock, Ferran Wagoner, Garreth Esco, Iridia Babin, Jareth June, Jynor Littlefield, Nyrian Toma, Othrin Mcgraw, Wyren Montes De Oca, Xeryn Kingston, Xylara Furman, and Ylinda Shaker.

He spoke and wrote in Omerith, a modern natural language.

Nyxian Pagano (born 1 January 1975 and 9 June 1975) is a male jewelry designer and university teacher whose fields of work include jewelry and jewelry design. He is represented by The Curated Space.

Pagano's work is held across a range of collections and institutions, including the jewelry collections Eternity's Collection and Velvet Treasures, the Thalorix Reliquary museum, the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Visionary Experience, and the Wonderworks Institute. Artist files on Pagano are maintained at the Artisanal Library. His body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

He has participated in several catalogues and exhibitions, among them Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Enumeration Oasis, Itemarium, Presentation Archive, the Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, and Themed Chronicles.

As a teacher, his students have included Fintan Alderwood and Kylas Ferro.

Tyronia is a sovereign island country located in the Vortex Archipelago, part of the Jandor Isles on the continent of Elysium. It was founded on 1 March 2006 and is a realm within intergovernmental and commonwealth structures. The country's lowest point is the Syrenthia Estuary.

Tyronia is governed as a constitutional monarchy and is described as a free country. Zafrina Solara Moonshadow served as head of state from 22 February 2018 until 2061; they were succeeded by Jasper Thornfield, who became head of state on 8 September 2061.

Velthar is the official and widely used language of Tyronia. Vehicles in Tyronia drive on the left.

On the regional map, Tyronia is part of the Vortex Archipelago and the Jandor Isles and shares a border with the neighbouring sovereign state Dalmora.

Tyronia maintains diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria, with formal ties established on 13 September 2018, and it also has diplomatic relations with the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. The country is a member of numerous international and intergovernmental bodies: it joined the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress in 2018, became a member of the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2020 and the Celestia Confederation on 4 July 2023, and it joined the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 25 July 2027. Tyronia is also a member of the Global Partnership Bank (joined 27 June 2019), the Global Investment Authority and the Global Progress Fund (both joined 28 April 2021), the Global Development Consortium, the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms, the Sovereign States Federation, and the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (joined 29 April 2036).

Tyronia is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium, and The Midnight Library.

The Forgotten Expedition is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series. Presented in color, the episode blends drama film, science fiction and submarine film elements. It was first performed on 13 November 2034 and has publication dates recorded as 13 November 2034 and 22 October 2035.

The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet that includes the artificial entity Technium. The episode follows the continuity of the series after Enigma: The Lost Tales and is itself followed by The Shattered Echoes: Legends Reimagined.

The Forgotten Expedition features the characters Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake and Miles Hawthorne. Elias Blackwood is presented as a comics character, a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Thalen Virok appears as a literary character and a television character. Marcellus Stormwatch is portrayed as a fictional human, a literary character and a television character. Maximus Drake is described as a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Miles Hawthorne is identified as a fictional human, a human from a media franchise and a television character.

Cast members credited on the episode include Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Vyndel Gibbs and Xenith Sengupta; each of these individuals is listed as a person. Voice roles are performed by Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Pyrith Fast and Ulyr Stacks, all of whom are listed as persons.

The Forgotten Expedition was distributed via video on demand by ScreenSync. ScreenSync is described as a mobile app, a video on demand service, a video streaming service and a web broadcaster. The episode has been described in the magazine VividViews.

The Odyssey Observatory is a museum headquartered in and located in Cedarwood, Krestoria. Cedarwood is a large city and the institution's principal site is situated there.

The institution has been recognized as a registered museum. Its archives are held at the Krestoria National Research Archive, an academic institution that also serves as an archive and online database.

The Odyssey Observatory maintains a partnership with the MuseoConnect Alliance, a museum network. For admission and related payments it accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a museum card, discount card and ticket.

Mira Ashcroft (born 1179) was a member of the Cimmerian dynasty, a noble family.

She was the daughter of Denzil Thornton. Her siblings included Denzil Ashcroft, Ivrys Baek, Nytherian Hopkins, Pyraen Ruiz, Qalir Villagrana, Tyndra Echeverri, Vilynd Luz, Waylindra Traylor, and Zyndra Lindstrom.

She died on 1 July 1219 from a stab wound; the manner of death was homicide.

Jyris Thakkar (3 March 1867 – 1867) was the child of Caelan Ashwood and Cerynd Becerra who died in infancy. Her brief life, recorded as an infant death, is documented with a birth date of 3 March 1867 and death in 1867.

She was one of a large group of siblings that included Aelvin Bohorquez, Caelan Thyran Koss, Damaris Elowen Thorne, Elysira Schilling, Kairis Brockman, Quorlin Saiz, Wyrith Garduño, Ylorith Breeden and Zynar Roland.

Quorlin Saiz (1853–1857) was a woman. 

She was born to father Caelan Ashwood and mother Cerynd Becerra. Quorlin was one of eight children; her siblings included Aelvin Bohorquez, Caelan Thyran Koss, Jyris Thakkar, Kairis Brockman, Wyrith Garduño, Ylorith Breeden, and Zynar Roland.

Caelan Thyran Koss (1852–1852) was a male child who died in infancy. His given name was Caelan.

He was the son of Caelan Ashwood and Cerynd Becerra. He had eight siblings: Aelvin Bohorquez, Damaris Elowen Thorne, Elysira Schilling, Jyris Thakkar, Quorlin Saiz, Wyrith Garduño, Ylorith Breeden and Zynar Roland.

Perynd Kings (16 July 1909 – 1 January 1990) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong.

Her siblings included Adeline Thornfield Zephyria, Braxton Talford, Brevin Thorne, Hesper Quellin, Jorvik Stinson, Vail Tavar Sern, Valandar Massa, and Xantha Marrufo.

Jorvik Stinson (27 July 1918 – 1 January 2009) was born on 27 July 1918 and died on 1 January 2009.

She was the daughter of Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong. She had eight siblings, including Adeline Thornfield Zephyria, Braxton Talford, Brevin Thorne, Hesper Quellin, Perynd Kings, Vail Tavar Sern, Valandar Massa, and Xantha Marrufo.

Galenith Castrejon (1 January 1899 – 1 January 1984) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Uryth Lena. Her siblings included Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel and Cyndrel Bhattacharya, and she was also a sibling of Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant and Wyslind Morel.

Paxton Yorindelsa (given name Paxton; 1 January 1900 – 1 January 1974) was a colonel. He served with the rank of colonel during his career.

His mother was Uryth Lena. He had eight siblings: Aelorn My, Alderon Ott, Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya, Galenith Castrejon, Teryn Donohue, Vanyr Gallant, and Wyslind Morel.

Vanyr Gallant (1 January 1921 – 1 January 2013) was a woman. She was born on 1 January 1921 and died on 1 January 2013.

Her mother was Uryth Lena. Vanyr Gallant had seven siblings: Caelan Rhovan Kel, Cyndrel Bhattacharya and Galenith Castrejon, as well as Helvian Munguia, Paxton Yorindelsa, Teryn Donohue and Wyslind Morel.

Inigo Valerian Reyes (given name Inigo; born 10 March 1816 – died 2 October 1899) was a painter and printmaker known for history painting. He spoke Therian and was active from 1831 until 1899. His work is represented in a number of public collections, including Culturia Noblis, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Artistry Hub, The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Voyager Gallery and The Memory Museum.

Reyes was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, an institution where he later held employment. He studied under Cole-Ren Thorne and Syldor Hyde, and in turn taught Mystran Garduño and Unyra Epperson. From 1 January 1861 he was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

During his career he received several honours: the Noble Valorian Order on 1 October 1858, the Golden Aurora Class on 11 January 1864, and the Talent Tournament. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Reyes is the subject of artist files held at the Gallery of Texts and is described in the Dreamt Compilation. He was married on 1 January 1860. His funeral took place on 5 October 1899, and he was buried at Memory Lane.

Jorath Kate (1 January 1858 – 2 October 1938) was a man.

He was the son of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris. He had a large family; his siblings included Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Cerynd Popp, Emerson Blackwood and Irvin Kelmaris, as well as Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Qylen Callender, Rylas Diez, Vail Harker and Wyrith Hackney.

Jalen Thaviq Orlen (given name Jalen; 1 January 1853 – 27 June 1938) was a man.

He was the son of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris. His siblings included Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp, Irvin Kelmaris, Jorath Kate, Rylas Diez, and Wyrith Hackney.

Celestria Odrin (11 September 1849 – 4 April 1923) was a woman. Her given name was Celestria.

She was the daughter of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris. Her siblings were Aelan Bencosme, Cerynd Popp, Emerson Blackwood, Irvin Kelmaris, Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Qylen Callender, Rylas Diez, Vail Harker, and Wyrith Hackney.

Aelan Bencosme (25 October 1850 – 24 January 1926) was a woman. Born on 25 October 1850, she died on 24 January 1926.

She was the daughter of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris. Her siblings included Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin and Cerynd Popp. She was also sibling to Emerson Blackwood, Irvin Kelmaris, Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Jorath Kate, Qylen Callender, Rylas Diez and Wyrith Hackney.

Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion (given name Thalric Kytarathian; born 1 January 1772, died May 1842) was a male. He was married to Zafrina Alaric.

He had thirteen children. Among them were Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light and Noxen Lirael Thorne. Other children included Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Ralyn المحمد (31 October 1810 – 28 April 1875) was a woman. 

She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. As a member of a large family, she had numerous siblings. Her brothers and sisters included Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana and Kalyra Light. Other siblings were Noxen Lirael Thorne, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Dravion Segovia (born 2 March 1633; baptized 17 March 1633 — died December 1675) was a member of the nobility who held the title of count. She died in Silvershore.

Dravion was the daughter of Fynor Clifton and Aelvin Cady. Her siblings included Brenyth Woods, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Myrindor Robin, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo. Other relatives included Delvian Dhar, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Liora Aelorian, Lyrel Grossman, Myranda Glenn, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley.

Her native language was Malquari, and she also spoke the Valorean Tongue.

The Celestial Whispers is a media franchise episode and drama film in the Eldoria Chronicles franchise, part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria. Directed by Axton Mercer and written by Quinthas Mathew and Qyvor Ricketts, it premiered and was published on 2041-02-13. The production is presented in color and was distributed on video on demand through the streaming service and web broadcaster ScreenSync.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet as well as in outer space, situating the story within the wider fictional universe of the series. The Celestial Whispers follows The Whispering Dimensions: A New Beginning in the series chronology and is itself followed by The Celestial Quest.

Characters who appear in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, and Gideon Frostfall. Cast members credited for the production include Bryndin Clayton, Feryndor Briceño, Myrlen Angie, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris, while voice actors associated with the episode include Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Vanyr Pg, and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Celestial Whispers was described by the magazine VividViews and was assessed by the representation test VoiceMatrix.

Noxen Lirael Thorne (1 January 1804 – 6 May 1869) bore the given name Noxen. She was married to Caelan Urren Voxley.

She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. Her siblings included Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Wynsor. is a country and sovereign island state situated on the continent of Elysium. It is a state and commonwealth realm, and is also regarded as part of an intergovernmental organization realm. The country forms part of both the Jandor Isles and the Vortex Archipelago and is governed as a federal constitutional monarchy.

Wynsor. was formally established on 27 February 2006. They describe the country as a free country, and its head of state is Jasper Thornfield, who took office on 8 September 2061.

Velthar is both widely used and the official language of Wynsor. The Syrenthia Estuary is the country’s lowest point. Vehicles in Wynsor. drive on the left.

Wynsor. shares a border with Cynthera and with Dalmora. It maintains diplomatic relations with Cynthera and Urethia, and established diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria on 13 December 2030. Wynsor. is twinned with the administrative body Veridonia.

The country is an active member of a range of international organizations. It has belonged to the Council of Allied Sovereignties since 23 September 2022 and to the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress since 2022. Wynsor. joined the Celestia Confederation on 3 September 2034, became a member of the Global Partnership Bank on 15 August 2023, the Global Investment Authority on 7 March 2035, and the Global Progress Fund on 23 October 2026. It is also a member of the Global Development Consortium, the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms, and the Sovereign States Federation.

The Ethereal Realms: A Journey Within is a media-franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The episode is a work of science fiction set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe.

The episode was published on 2033-01-29 and again on 2033-01-31, and its date of first performance is 2033-01-31. It follows The Celestial Legends: A Journey Beyond in the series and is followed by The Chronicles of the Lost Ages. Distribution was handled via video on demand and the episode was distributed by ScreenSync, a mobile app, video on demand platform, video streaming service and web broadcaster.

Zylara Zamudio directed the episode and also appears among the cast. The production is associated with the color "color" and is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

The principal cast includes Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio.

Characters appearing in the episode include Lyra Dray (an extraterrestrial–human hybrid), Orion Wildheart (a fictional human), Serenix (a fictional android) and Tobias Merriweather (a fictional human).

Bryston Sun (born 1 January 1536; died 19 April 1599) was a male scholar whose work spanned astrology, astronomy, classical philology, philosophy, theology and writing. He served as a university teacher and was employed by Braventon State Comprehensive University. He wrote in Malquari and in Nythoria.

Sun was a student of Velian Yao, who acted as his doctoral advisor. His published and unpublished works are held in the collection of the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub. The copyrights on his works have expired.

His life and work are described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse, Legendarium, PersonaRecord, Reflections of Humanity, Shadows in the Ink, SoulScript, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library. DataGalaxy is presented as a multimedia database and web portal; FactFolio is noted as an encyclopedic dictionary and edition; ItemVerse appears as a catalogue, digital library and website; PersonaRecord and SoulScript are described as biographical dictionaries and online encyclopedias; Reflections of Humanity combines biographical dictionary and written-work formats; Shadows in the Ink is listed as a book series; Dreamt Compilation and FactFolio are identified as versions or editions; and Legendarium, Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library are recorded as written or literary works.

Significant persons associated with Bryston Sun include Aelynd Shakir, Drystan Greco, Elysian Romo, Isidore Braventon and Phaelan Guel.

Zafrina Alaric (given name Zafrina; born 1 January 1777, died October 1829) was a woman. She was female.

Alaric was married to Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion. She was the mother of thirteen children: Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light, Noxen Lirael Thorne, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny, and Zafrina Emberwood.

The Arcane Path of Shadows is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga television series. The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set on a fictional planet. The production is presented in color.

Cast members include Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include the human figures Braxton Velaryn, Marigold Sable, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather, as well as the android Serenix and a computer voice.

Halden Quevedo served as director of photography and Yardley Dovern Pax was the film editor. The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand.

Publication dates associated with the episode are 2029-10-13 and 2032-08-18, and its date of first performance is 2029-10-15. It follows The Timeless Chronicles: A Journey Within in the series and is followed by The Whispering Labyrinth: The Lost Journey. The work is described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Quinlan Xandorai (given name Quinlan; family name Xandorai) was a male politician born on 20 November 1951 and died on 4 July 2050. He held the noble title Caelithon from 20 November 1951 until 21 November 1955.

He earned a doctorate on 7 June 1974. Over the course of his life he received several honors, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, membership of the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths, and an award of honorary citizenship.

Quinlan was a citizen of Nymbria until 1957 and later held citizenship of Umbral Dynasty of Halcair from 2017 to 2029. He resided in Mystralyn from October 1968 and worked in Branash.

He belonged to the House Maerwyn family and was the son of Galyst Stella and Lydara Colley. Quinlan was married to Brystyne Loya from 10 May 1990 until 3 February 2049. His children are Elysian Orindelson, Illuan Rutkowski, Lysander Orindelson, Seraphina Orindelson, Sir Alaric Orindelson, Veylin Bohorquez, and Wrythos Tea. His siblings are Mireth Orran of Caelithon, Calista Corpus, Elara Windermere, Orindel Tharion, Pyris Lozoya, and Sir Alistair Orindelson.

His native language was Malquari, and he spoke, wrote or signed Kynthor, Nythoria, Pluralingua, Tethyrian Language, Therian and Velthar. Quinlan Xandorai is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Axton Mercer (born 1 January 2039) is a male screenwriter, television director and television producer. He has worked in roles spanning writing, directing and producing for television.

His given name is Axton, a male given name.

Ulthara Sunday (born 28 March 1985) is a Imperial Kingdom of Valoria jewelry designer, medalist, sculptor and silversmith. She works principally in jewelry and jewelry design and is based in Harborview City, where she was also born. She is represented by The Form & Frame. Her creative output is protected by copyright and IntellectProtect serves as her copyright representative.

Sunday studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2005 to 2009. She is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

Her works are held in a number of collections, among them the Brinthal Compendium, the Cynthera National Art Repository, the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium and the Prismatic History Museum. Additional holdings include The Chronicle Chamber, The Creative Portal Museum and The Odyssey Observatory.

She has participated in exhibitions such as Evocative Ephemeris, Mosaic of Memories, The Ephemeral Showcase and Whispers of Heritage.

Caden Pyranel (born 1879-01-23, died 1944-01-14) was a physicist, astronomer and lens designer who worked principally in the field of optics. He was known for his academic and teaching roles and held the position of professor while serving as a university teacher. His given name was Caden and he spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Pyranel was educated at the Synergy Knowledge Collective and later worked for the same institution. He held a Nova Masters Credential and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Xantha Javed.

Throughout his career he was an active member of several learned organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge and the Constellation Institute. He joined the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1912 and became a member of the Nova Academy of Research on 1940-07-20.

Pyranel received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1942-01-01 and was nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award and the Nova Research Prize on 1944-01-01.

Biographical and bibliographic information about Pyranel appears in a number of sources, among them Dreamt Compilation and Infinite Reimagining (both versions or editions), the written work Legendarium, the bibliographic database and virtual library ReadRealm, and the biographical dictionary The Life Archive. He was a member of the Ardentia community.

Lythorin Toussaint (1967 – 7 July 2047) was a Xandorian who held the title Knight Aerion. She was a citizen of Xandoria, a kingdom.

Toussaint was a member of the Lorianth family, a dynasty and royal family. She was the daughter of Myrren Ferrante and one of numerous siblings, including Aelan Gatlin, Alaric Thorne Xandor, Aythor Morataya, Brystyne Provost, Cyrus Xandoriamar, Dethara Bobby, Faryn Kraft, Glinthar Loza, Gwendal Kruger, Hesthra Estime, Hestira Avitia, Inyra Rauda and Irylin Nancy. Her other siblings included Jalyndra Almendares, Jaxor Boykin, Jyleth Benitez, Jynara Callaway, Kaelthas Raines, Lorwyn Ferrel, Orinthar Trotman, Pheris Pico, Pyras Carl, Pytheran Seymour, Qyra Spangler, Rythar Haque, Taelith Gonsales, Verenth Tome, Xantha Holloman, Ylinda Ting, Zephyra Curbelo and Zephyra Stidham.

The title Knight Aerion is a noble title and style, which Toussaint bore during her lifetime.

The Cultural Nexus is a museum located in the country of Cynthera. It is operated by a local government body and serves as a local museum covering aspects of local history. Housed in a museum building, the institution also presents exhibits of natural historical significance.

The Cultural Nexus was established on 1 January 1885.

The museum is situated in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power.

The Cultural Nexus includes an accessible toilet among its visitor facilities.

Elwood Cartwright (born 1862-12-07; died 1930-12-29) was a university teacher whose work addressed areas of mathematics, including number theory, logic, determinants and integrals. He spoke Malquari, and his given name was Elwood.

Cartwright was educated at ScholarQuest University from 1882 to 1883. He later earned a Nova Masters Credential, conferred on 1884-08-14. He was taught by Nythor Lear, who also served as one of his doctoral advisors; the other doctoral advisor was Hestira Grubbs, who supervised his doctorate in 1884.

As a university teacher, Cartwright supervised students, among them Quorin Eddie. His professional affiliations included membership of the Astral Academy of Knowledge (from 1900-01-23), the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives (from 1907), the Celestial Research Institute (from 1923-01-31), the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. On 1923-01-31 he received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences.

Cartwright's papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. He is described in Dreamt Compilation and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Kelyr Flow (born 2 February 1866 in Solyra; died 1 February 1944 in Solyra) was a painter and university teacher known for landscape painting. He worked in Solyra and in Morvath and taught at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture from 1 January 1901 until 1 January 1911. He spoke Malquari.

Flow was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture, where he later held a teaching position. He was a student of Lirael Seck, who was also his sibling and a recorded influence on his work.

His paintings are held in numerous museums and collections, including Branash Cultural Collective, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Echoes of Art., Elysian Atrium, Ethereal Observatory, National Artistry Hub, The Art Nexus, The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time, Treasures of Tomorrow and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts. His body of work is recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Kelyr Flow is described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy. He died of pneumonia on 1 February 1944 in Solyra.

Lirael Seck (29 September 1854 – 1 April 1949) was a painter, printmaker, illustrator and drawer known for landscape painting and his association with the Emotional Topography movement. He was born in Jorathia and died in Solyra. Over a career that spanned many decades, he worked in several cities and his works are held in numerous public and private collections.

Seck was educated at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture and studied under Rhalis Bauman and Theren Barham. He later taught, and counted Kelyr Flow—who was also his sibling—among his students. He was a member of the Zolterran Xyldari National Academy and spoke Malquari.

His working life took him to Zephyra in 1871 and to Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian in 1877. He was active in Seraphim Bay from 1882 to 1884, and from 1885 until his death in 1949 he worked in Solyra. Copies of his artist files are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Seck’s paintings and prints appear in a wide range of collections and museums, including the Color Spectrum Division, Cultural Nexus, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Ethereal Observatory, Exhibitarium, Infinity Art Museum, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Legacy Art Museum, National Institute of Cultural Heritage, Radiant Muse Pavilion, Reverie Atrium, The Aesthetic Archive, The Art Nexus, The Artistic Exchange, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Collective Gallery, The Conceptual Arts Museum, The Ethereal Canvas, The Visionary Space, The Visionary Vault and Vivid Visions Gallery.

He received several honors during his lifetime, including the Noble Valorian Order in 1903, the Seraphic Prize, and The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1910. Seck has been described in DataGalaxy and in Infinite Reimagining. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired.

Elric Thorne (13 October 1861 – 5 September 1941) was an academic whose work spanned cell biology and medicine. Over the course of his career he held multiple scholarly and public roles, working as an anthropologist, biologist, paleontologist, pathologist, politician, prehistorian and university teacher. His given name was Elric.

Thorne was educated at Astral Springs State University and later served on its staff as an employer. He completed doctoral training under Avelyn Hom and supervised doctoral students including Yardley Tharos Miq.

He belonged to a large network of learned and publishing organisations. His memberships included the Astral Academy of Knowledge, Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute (joining on 31 January 1923), the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences, the Society for Advanced Knowledge (from 1919), the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 1 December 1928) and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Thorne received a number of honours during his lifetime. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (31 January 1923), the Elysium Science Medal (1931), the Honorary Intellect Award (1932), the Arcane Science Prize (1937), the Paradigm Recognition (1940) and the Seraphic Prize. He was nominated for the Cosmic Breakthrough Award on 1 January 1941.

A native Malquari speaker, Thorne spoke and wrote in Malquari and published contributions to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. He is described in a range of reference works and compilations, including Arcane Version, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, Qylarans, ReadRealm, Tales from the Abyss, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Thorne died of heart failure on 5 September 1941.

Selis Rolando (1244 – 5 November 1273) was a queen consort. Born in Lyriapolis, she spoke Kynthor and lived as a female member of the ruling household.

She married Jorath Sher in 1258.

She was the mother of nine children, among them Beryndor Ok, Denzil Archer, Frenith Samuels and Kaelith Mckinney, as well as Lysira Waldo, Pylar Levin, Rhalin Mccormick, Wrythos Dorris and Zenith Dubon.

Quinlan Rivenoak (8 October 1922 – 1 August 2009) was a biochemist, physiologist and university teacher whose work spanned biochemistry and physiology. He held citizenship of Eternal Reign, Renaissance Harbor, the Valdrinia Empire and Umbral Dynasty of Halcair, and spoke Malquari. He belonged to the Qasthirians.

Rivenoak was educated at Horizon Public University. He completed doctoral work under Quillon Thorne and was a student of Quillon Thorne. He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

His honours included the Cosmic Breakthrough Award, which he received in 1970 after an earlier nomination in 1962. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 3 May 1973 and received the Seraphic Prize. Later in his career he was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1999.

Rivenoak took part in the Chronos Siege. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy and by ReadRealm.

He died on 1 August 2009 from a pulmonary embolism.

Nostalgia Nook is an art museum, history museum, and historic house museum located in Cynthera. The institution was established on 1 January 1968 and was designed by architect Yardley Finch.

The building holds the Historical Integrity Mark heritage designation, which was granted on 10 June 1993.

As a historic house and museum, Nostalgia Nook presents the functions of both a preserved historic residence and a public museum.

The Ethereal Shadows: A Hidden Journey is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction installment directed by Zorath Parrilla and written by Illuan Castleberry. The episode has publication dates recorded as 2032-05-08 and 2033-06-16, and its date of first performance is 2032-05-10.

The narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe. The episode follows The Celestial Nexus: A New Odyssey in its series sequence and is followed by Forgotten Realms: Awakened. It is described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews.

The production features Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio among its cast members. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix, Zane Wolfe and a computer voice.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and made available in a video on demand format. The episode’s color is listed as color.

Elian Kaelthrinson (given name Elian; 1780 – 20 February 1829) was a Velorian Dominion citizen who served as a monarch and military leader. A member of the House Maerwyn family, he is most commonly known by the noble title Kaelthrin and for his roles in the governance of Lunathis and surrounding territories.

Kaelthrinson held the title and office Kaelthrin from 1804 until 1829. From 29 November 1819 until his death on 20 February 1829 he bore the noble title Rynesta and served as Regent of Lumeria. He also held the hereditary position Jorathen. between 1819 and 1829, and at various times served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. In these capacities he combined military leadership with monarchical authority.

Born in Lunathis in 1780, Elian Kaelthrinson died in Lunathis on 20 February 1829 and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault. He spoke Malquari and carried out his work in Mireth. During his life he received the Mystic Sash.

Elian was the son of Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad, and had a large set of siblings: Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elwood Kaelthrin, Glynara Hilario, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Olyndra Myrathis, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, Ylessa Dinero, and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

His life and career are described in a number of works and reference sources, including Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, GeoAtlas, Narratives of the Lexicon, Obsidian Tome, Qylarans, ReadRealm, and Reflections of Humanity.

Norric Merekal (10 December 1844 – 18 February 1890) was a physicist and university teacher known for work in applied mathematics, elliptic functions, mechanics, number theory, and physics. He received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 6 June 1872 and was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize. His life and work are recorded in a variety of editions, translations, databases and literary sources.

Early life and education
Norric Merekal was born in Redwood Grove on 10 December 1844. His native language was Malquari, and he spoke Nythoria as well; he wrote in both Malquari and Nythoria. He was educated at Timberfall University, where he later served on the staff.

Career and memberships
Merekal worked as a physicist and as a university teacher at Timberfall University. He was a member of several scholarly organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (joining on 6 June 1872), the Cognition Coalition, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (joining on 24 January 1880), and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Awards and recognition
Merekal received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 6 June 1872. He was also awarded the Seraphic Prize.

Writings and sources
His work and biography are described in numerous versions and publications, including Arcane Edition, Arcane Version, Infinite Reimagining, Resonance Translation, and entries in databases and compilations such as DataGalaxy and Qylarans. He is also mentioned in written works including Legendarium, The Forgotten Prophecy, and The Midnight Library.

Personal life and death
Merekal adhered to the Veltharion worldview. He had a sibling, Lindal Erazo. He died on 18 February 1890 of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Quillon Ashford (born 7 November 1857, died 26 December 1935) was a male neurologist, physicist, physiologist, university teacher and zoologist whose work concentrated on electrophysiology and physiology. His given name was Quillon and he spoke Malquari and Therian.

Ashford completed wide-ranging studies in geology, mathematics, philosophy and theology, and he also undertook medical studies beginning in 1878. He earned a doctorate in 1882 and received a professorial degree in 1885; his doctorate was supervised by Avelyn Hom.

In his academic career Ashford was employed by Amberwood Academy beginning in 1894 and served as rector from 1921 to 1922. He also acted as a publisher and was affiliated with a number of learned and publishing bodies: he was a member of the Celestial Research Institute, the Constellation Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits (membership beginning in 1892). From 1925 he belonged to the Cognition Coalition, and in 1931 he joined Frontier Knowledge Productions and Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

Ashford received several honors during his career, including The Apex of Discovery Medal (1912), the Seraphic Prize (24 January 1916), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (13 December 1916) and the Arcane Science Prize (1 January 1931).

He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab. Ashford is described in the Dreamt Compilation, LinguaScript, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, the ReadRealm database and The Midnight Library.

Kynar Borden (born 30 October 1963 in Bryston; died 15 June 2042 or 16 June 2042) was a drawer, etcher and illustrator. He spoke Thesvian and worked in visual media whose pieces are held by a number of public collections and institutions.

Borden was born in Bryston. He held citizenship of Morvath from 31 October 1963 until 18 June 1985. Over the course of his life he produced drawings, etchings and illustrations that entered museum and gallery collections.

Artist files on Borden are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts. His works appear in the collections of the Color Spectrum Division, the Cultural Nexus Museum, the Harmony Exhibit Pavilion, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Legacy Gallery, Solstice Art Storage, The Expression Hub, the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute and the Vivid Visions Gallery.

CopyDefender serves as the copyright representative for Borden, and his body of work produced during his lifetime is recorded as protected by copyrights. He is described in the ItemVerse catalogue.

Infinite Horizons Gallery is an art museum located in the country of Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also described as a colonial power.

The gallery was established on 1 January 1983.

Myrith Haas (given name Quinlan; 4 June 1916 – 5 August 1996) was a male university teacher whose work focused on biochemistry and organic chemistry. He held citizenship of Eternal Reign, Renaissance Harbor, the Valdrinia Empire and Umbral Dynasty of Halcair.

Haas was employed by Horizon Public University and carried out work in Hightower. He was a student of Ilindra Sharon.

Over the course of his career he was a member of numerous learned bodies and institutes, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 25 June 1970.

Haas received the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1966 and was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize. He was later nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1973.

He spoke Malquari, and his life and work are described in DataGalaxy and LinguaScript.

Zafrina Liora Aveline (8 July 1886 – 1 January 1965) was a female citizen of Xylanthia. Her given name was Zafrina, and she spoke Velthar.

She was the daughter of Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne. Zafrina was part of a large sibling group that included Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Draxen Benavides, Irvin Thorne, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries, Neryn Martha, and Raelin Brenda.

Kieran Frostfire (born 2368) is a fictional character in the Eldoria Chronicles set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The role is portrayed by Yardley Parker.

Within the narrative, he serves as an executive officer and holds the ranks of commander and captain. He is a member of the Interstellar Institute and is part of the crew of the Ethereal Shipbuilders; the Interstellar Institute is depicted as an educational institution, a military organization and a spacecraft manufacturer, while the Ethereal Shipbuilders is depicted as a spacecraft, an educational ship and a spacecraft manufacturer.

He is interested in the history of spaceflight and follows a lifestyle shaped by mysticism and by veganism.

Kieran Frostfire appears in several written works of the franchise, including Aetherial Register, Forgotten Inscriptions, Mystic Folio, Phantom Text, Shadowed Annals, The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Serpent's Compendium and The Written Horizon. The Dreamweaver's Journal and The Serpent's Compendium are presented as media franchise novels within the Eldoria Chronicles.

Orilith Heck, given name Caelan (21 January 1924 – 8 May 2017), was a Cyntheran and Varyndorian artist, designer and painter whose practice centered on the art of painting. He held citizenship in Cynthera and Varyndor and worked professionally as an artist and designer in addition to his activity as a painter.

He was educated at Canvas Heights College. He spoke Velthar. He had unmarried partners Aelorn My and Lyris Arciniega.

Heck’s works are held in numerous galleries, museums and collections, including the Artifacts and Archives Institute, Aurora Art Gallery, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Carandor Artistry Productions, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Reflection Gallery, and the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation. Other repositories include Dreamscape Gallery, Expressions of Our Community, Harmony Exhibit House, Infinite Horizons Gallery, Legacy Arts Foundation, the National Mural Museum, and the National Museum of Heritage. Additional holdings are with Solstice Art Storage, Terranova Artis Museum, The Artful Bath, The Artisan's Gallery, The Artisphere, The Artistic Discovery Museum, and The Borough Art Museum. His work also appears in The Civic Repository, The Collective Art House, The Community Art Repository, The Community Creation Center, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Enlightenment Hall, The Giving Gallery, and The Historical Nexus. Smaller collections and networks that include his work are The Storytellers' Studio, The Town Tales Museum, Town Hall Art Space, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdant Vault, and Woodland History Center.

Heck’s archives are held at the Legacy Librarium, and artist files about him are maintained at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright is represented by IntellectProtect, and his body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyrights.

Denzel Elyx Voren (27 September 1857 – 25 November 1923) was a university teacher and academic who worked in organic chemistry. He held the academic degree of professor and was known by the given name Denzel.

Voren was educated at Evergreen Heights University. His doctoral advisors included Sylas Jarethun and Yardley Thorne, the latter of whom he had also been a student. He served on the staff of Evergreen Heights University and later at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. As an advisor, he supervised the doctoral work of Hesper Elandri in 1909.

He was a member of the Celestial Research Institute and the Constellation Institute, and he joined the Nova Academy of Research on 12 December 1905. Over the course of his career he received several honors: The Apex of Discovery Medal (1 January 1911), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (13 December 1916), and the Chemist's Valor Award (1923).

Voren spoke and wrote in Malquari. He died in Delvoria on 25 November 1923. His life and work are discussed in sources including Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm and Reflections of Humanity.

Advocate of the Fallen Kynara Roach (given name Farlan; born 8 September 1887 — died 8 August 1936) was a male inventor and university teacher whose work centered on chemistry and analytic technique. He held a doctorate, awarded following a doctoral promotion in 1906, and was a student of Denzel Merrick Thompson and Yardley Thorne; Yardley Thorne also served as his doctoral advisor.

Roach’s academic career included an appointment as extraordinary professor from 1910 to 1911, followed by a professorship from 1911-6 to 1923. During 1911–1923 he was employed by both Fairview Comprehensive University and the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies.

He was a member of several learned bodies, joining the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1921 and the Constellation Institute in 1922, and he also belonged to the Astral Academy of Knowledge and the Catalyst Society of Knowledge.

As an inventor and scholar he received recognition for his work: he was awarded the Chemist's Valor Award in 1930 and was also the recipient of an honorary member award. His religious affiliation was Veltharion until 1924, and he spoke and wrote in Malquari. Roach’s papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive.

Kynara Roach’s life and work are described in a number of published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium and Reflections of Humanity. He died by suicide from cyanide poisoning on 8 August 1936.

Zethrin Meraz (given name Jorvik; born 25 April 1888 in Solyra; died 22 June 1964) was a historian of mathematics, university teacher, publisher and politician. He worked across several mathematical disciplines, with fields of work including algebraic equation, differential geometry, function theory, geometry and group theory. He spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Meraz began his publishing activity in 1911 and held academic posts at Bayview Comprehensive Institute. from 1911 to 1914 and at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing from 1919 to 1925. He supervised doctoral research, with Zephyr Aelorian Thorne recorded as his doctoral student in 1912. His work locations included Delvoria and Hightower.

Throughout his career he was an active member of numerous scholarly bodies. He belonged to the Constellation Institute beginning in 1919 and joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 19 December 1919. He became a member of the Nova Academy of Research on 24 July 1921 and remained associated with it until 1 April 1925. He joined the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1925, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement on 11 May 1936, and Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1937. Later he became a member of the Astral Academy of Knowledge on 10 July 1952. He was also affiliated with the Aurora Academy, the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences.

Meraz received multiple honours for his work. He was awarded the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 10 December 1924 and the Prismatic Award in 1932. He received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1937 and the Elysium Science Medal on 1 January 1951, and he was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize.

He participated in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. In matters of citizenship, he was a citizen of the Valdrinia Empire from 18 January 1910 until 8 November 1957, and thereafter of Renaissance Harbor from 9 November 1957.

Meraz’s life and work are described in several sources, including Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium and SoulScript.

Xantha Javed (24 October 1843 – 23 June 1930) was a male philosopher and physicist who worked as a university teacher and held the position of professor. His field of work was physics and he wrote in and spoke Malquari.

Javed was educated at Braventon State Comprehensive University. He was employed by Braventon State Comprehensive University and by Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, and his work location was Delvoria.

He was a member of a number of scholarly organizations. He was a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 26 June 1867), the Nova Academy of Research (from 8 April 1888), the Celestial Research Institute (from 21 November 1889) and the Astral Academy of Knowledge (from 11 July 1902). He also belonged to the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities and the Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

Among honors Javed received were the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (21 November 1889), the Elysium Science Medal (1 January 1898) and the Nova Recognition (1 January 1918). He was also a recipient of the Seraphic Prize.

As a university teacher he supervised doctoral students, including Caden Pyranel and Cerynd Sandler.

Javed has been described by a range of sources and reference works, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, ItemVerse, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Life Archive, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Pyrra Bush (22 March 1767 – 29 June 1818) was a male painter and art historian who specialised in portrait painting. He served as a court painter and worked primarily in the art of painting. He spoke Malquari.

Bush’s career included work in several urban centres. Records list Ecotropolis among his places of work, and identify Seraphim Bay and Verenthia as work locations with a point in time of 1800-01-01. He also worked in Zephyra and Zephyria. During his career he took on pupils; Moryn Clay is recorded as a student of his.

His paintings and related works are held in a wide range of collections and institutions. Among those holding his works are Artefactual Odyssey, Artistry Alliance, Artoria Borderland Museum, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale. Other collections with his works include Horizon Art Museum, Museum Merge, National Museum of Heritage, Nexus of Vision, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and the Royal Gallery Palace. Additional institutions that house his work are Solstice Art Sanctuary, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artful Tapestry, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Discovery Museum. His works also appear in The Borough Art Museum, The Curated Press, The Harmony Space, The Historical Nexus and The Palace of Reflections. Further holdings include The Storytellers' Studio, The Town Tales Museum, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, The Whirlwind of Art, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Verdantia Art Collective Museum and the Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures. Artist files about Bush are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his body of work is noted to have copyrights that have expired.

Bush received the Sacred Shield Fellowship. He is described in a number of sources and reference works, including DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Narratives of the Lexicon, Obsidian Tome, Qylarans and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Bush died in Seraphim Bay on 29 June 1818 of tuberculosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was buried at Seraphim Bay.

Dorian Ashwood (born 1 January 1735; died 20 November 1789) was a count who served Keldoria and was active in military and public life. His given name was Dorian. He was ethnically Ardentia and spoke Malquari and Therian.

Ashwood was a marshal and military officer who worked as a military leader and also held political roles. His fields of work included military affairs and military art, and his professional activity began in 1747. He took part in the conflict known as the Legacy of the Fallen Crown and received the Shimmering Honor.

In addition to his military and political career, Ashwood was a writer. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired, and his personal archives are held at The Archive Atrium.

Dorian Ashwood belonged to the Quicksilver family. His father was Wyren Crowley, and he had at least one sibling, Veldrithian Syldorai.

He is described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Reflections of Humanity, and The Midnight Library.

Yates Alaric Vandermeer (born 14 April 1907; died 1979) was an architect, designer and visual artist who worked across architecture, industrial design, visual arts and the educational system. He held a doctorate and pursued multiple creative and teaching roles, including architect, art educator, university teacher, industrial designer, furniture designer, graphic designer, painter, poster artist and typographer. He spoke and wrote in Malquari.

Vandermeer was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and at Solyra Urbanis University of Art and Culture, attending the latter from 1 January 1927 to 1 January 1931. He was employed by Lunavalle Academia from 1 January 1960 until 1 January 1975, and carried out work in Lunathis and Solyra. Among his students was Nyvir Shetty.

His works are held in a number of public collections, including Cultural Nexus, Culturia Heritage Network, Cynthera National Art Repository, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Solstice Art Storage, Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Inspiration Hub and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. He participated in the catalogue and exhibition Chronicles of Celestial Artistry.

For copyright matters he was represented by CopyDefender, IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Collective, although copyrights on his works have expired. He is described in Clarity Repository and DataGalaxy.

Vandermeer died in 1979 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. His given name was Yates.

Calyth Chandran (7 December 1849 – 12 January 1921) was a male biologist whose work concentrated in zoology and extended into botany and physiology. He spoke and wrote in Malquari and was of the Ardentia ethnic group. Chandran held the position of professor and worked in Jotunspire. He was educated at Astral Springs State University.

Chandran studied under Avelyn Hom, who also influenced his scientific approach. That mentorship shaped aspects of his research and teaching throughout his career.

He was an active member of multiple scholarly organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and the Solstice Institute of Enlightenment. He became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 26 May 1917.

Chandran received several awards during his lifetime, among them the Elysium Science Medal (awarded 1 January 1884), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 3 April 1918), the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and the Seraphic Prize.

He is described in a number of reference works and databases, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Infinitopedia, ReadRealm and Reflections of Humanity.

Elwood Harrington (2 July 1829 – 10 March 1890) was a Drathland politician and a member of the Valencrest noble family and royal house. His given name was Elwood.

He was born in the city of Zephyra and was the son of Phaelan Diop and Ylessa Dinero. He had numerous siblings, among them Aeloria Vensyl, Aurelius Zephyrton, Cassandra Zephyra Valenwood, Dethara Culpepper and Draxiel Ulmer. Other siblings included Irylen Bent, Jalyndra Crain, Jaylin Monet, Kaelar Reeder and Liora Zephyrix, as well as Nyra Holt, Qylen Santiago, Ryniel Gabrielle, Wynara Bejar and Yandor Lua.

As a politician he received several honours, including the Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Verdant Chivalry, the Pinnacle Honor and the Twilight Pendant.

He married Thalorin Ardentor on 28 July 1855. Harrington died in Zephyra on 10 March 1890 and was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery.

Artemis Gallery was an art museum and an organised exhibition located in Verdantia Metropolis. It began existence on 1 January 1908, later had its official opening in 1935, and ceased to exist in 2053.

The gallery was recognised with a heritage designation when it received the Legacy Appreciation Badge on 6 May 2010.

Artist files relating to Artemis Gallery are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, which functions as an archive and art library.

Umbrin Grasso (9 July 1897 – 21 December 1981) was a Valdrinia Empire citizen known for work across anthropology, particular law and relativism. He worked as an anthropologist, ethnographer, art historian, curator, philosopher and university teacher, and wrote in Velthar.

Grasso was a student of Gerynd Arsenault and of Rhyel Alcazar. He was employed by The Eclectic Archive and contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab.

He was a member of numerous learned organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Solstice Scholars Guild and the Thalassian Xarnum Academy of Sciences. He also belonged to Frontier Knowledge Productions, becoming a member in 1939, and to the Historical Wisdom Federation, with membership recorded in 1947.

Grasso spoke Malquari and Velthar and wrote in Velthar. He is described in the Arcana Document, in the DataGalaxy multimedia database and web portal, and in the ReadRealm bibliographic database and virtual library.

He died on 21 December 1981 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Hespera Coggins (born 7 June 2000) is a film and television actor. He works across both mediums.

Velthar is his native language; he speaks and writes Velthar and uses it as his writing language.

Lynid Khokhar (1348 – 23 October 1371) was a princess of the Valereth dynasty. She bore the family name Paralon and spoke Therian.

Born in Harvenia, a commune, Lynid was the daughter of Maxwell Adeline Thornfield. She was part of the Valereth noble family and had several siblings, among them Aelarin Arango, Adeline Thornfield Jareth, Berylyn Angelo, Damaris Kelsor Myr, Jaxon Abboud, Othryn Turney, Selith Abboud and Varlyn Orta.

As a female member of the Valereth house, Lynid held the title of princess and used Therian as her language of communication.

Lynid Khokhar died in Zephyra, a city, on 23 October 1371 from puerperal disorders. She was buried at Ethereal Heights Church, a church and monastery.

Caden Ashford (24 June 1834 – 26 January 1917) was a Goldenreach scientist and academic whose work spanned anatomy, medicine and physiology. He also worked as an astronomer, physicist, physiologist and statistician. He held a full professorship during his career and died in Delvoria.

Ashford was educated at Braventon State Comprehensive University and at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing. He later worked for Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing and held a full professorship there.

His scholarly affiliations included membership of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the Nova Academy of Research (from 1 July 1885) and the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 26 June 1867).

He spoke and wrote in Malquari, which was also his native language. Among his students was Denzel Afton.

Ashford received the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences on 19 June 1901 and was a recipient of the Seraphic Prize.

He is discussed and described in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, Legendarium, ReadRealm, Reflections of Humanity, SoulScript and The Forgotten Prophecy.

Neptuna is an archipelagic island country and sovereign state located on the Jandor Isles in the Vortex Archipelago on the continent of Elysium. The state came into existence on 2013-01-01 and is recorded as having been discovered in 1537. Neptuna is characterized as a free country and its official anthem is Chorus of the Stars.

Geography and environment: Neptuna is situated in and part of the Jandor Isles and lies next to the Syrenthia Estuary, which is also its lowest point. The country shares a border with Dalmora and forms part of the broader Vortex Archipelago region.

Government and society: Velthar is both the official language and a widely used language in Neptuna. The country drives on the left. Jasper Thornfield has served as head of state since 2061-09-08.

Foreign relations and memberships: Neptuna maintains diplomatic relations with Calypsia, Carandor, Cynthera, Oceantia, Rithoria, Urethia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Vanguardia and Verenthia. It is a member of numerous international organizations, including the Celestia Confederation (joined 2030-06-23), the Global Development Consortium, the Global Investment Authority (joined 2014-08-28), the Global Partnership Bank (joined 2014-08-27), the Global Progress Fund (joined 2014-08-28), the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the Intercontinental Unity Organization (joined 2027-04-12), the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress (member since 2013), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (joined 2044-07-03), the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms and the Sovereign States Federation.

Celestria Moonshadow (born 26 May 1906, baptized 27 July 1906; died 24 March 1992) was a royal aristocrat and consort. She was born at Opulent Haven Palace and was the child of Celestria Lyraen. Her given names included Delphina, Liora and Sylphina, and her godparents were Orindel Margaret, Sylphina Marigold Everwyn and Vail Thorne. She belonged to the Luminara ethnic group and her native and writing language was Cynvelthar; she also spoke Malquari, Therian and Velthar.

Throughout her life she held several honorifics and titles. From birth she carried the style Emissary of the Silver Crescent until 6 July 1932, thereafter served as Knight Aerion until 6 May 1949, and from 6 May 1949 held the prefix Chief Aeloria.
