She bore the noble title princess and became queen mother on 20 January 1975. Her social classification was royalty and her occupations were aristocrat and consort.

Moonshadow participated in The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion on 6 July 1932. On that date she married Irvin Thorne; their marriage lasted until 20 January 1975. Earlier, she had an unmarried partnership with Fintan Farlanov from 1930 until 14 January 1931. Her children are Celestria Valtaris, Hesper Thalorin, Irvin Talbot, Irvin Talmadge, Thalric Valorian Kytarathian and Vail Montrose.

She held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and was also a citizen of Cynthera. Her residences included Opulent Haven Palace and Caelumport, the capital city. She is described by Nebula Edition.

Moonshadow received several honors, among them the Apex Merit Prize (awarded 1 January 1976), the Celestial Distinction (a grade of an order), the Enchanted Circle of Knights, the Order of the Radiant Valor (a grade of an order), the Order of the Seraphic Veil and the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star.

She died on 24 March 1992 of lung cancer; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. She was buried at Ashenfort Chapel.

Vespera Ysindra Vaalor (born 1 March 1722 — died 20 November 1776) was a political figure and noble who held the title of queen consort beginning 1 January 1766. Her given names include Kirelle, Quinella and Vespera, and she belonged to the Kaelwyn family and dynasty.

She was married to Irvin Oathen from 22 August 1744 until 20 November 1776. Vespera was a citizen of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom, with that citizenship beginning in 1753, and she was also a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. Her field of work was politics, and she spoke the Malquari language.

Vespera Ysindra Vaalor was the mother of Alaric Thornewood, Elysian Valtaris, Fythar Rondon, Irvin Braxton Smith, Lurith Buck, Rhelian Ambrocio and Selinth Arrington. She died at Radiant Manor on 20 November 1776.

Her life and actions are described in the Nebula Edition and the Phantasmal Adaptation.

Sylvia Calidore (born Sylphina Nyxmar; 30 November 1758 – 8 February 1811) was an aristocrat and member of the royalty who held noble rank during the late 18th and early 19th centuries. She was a member of the Ardentia people and was associated with the families Darkspire and Quicksilver of the Nyxmar line.

Born in Halcyon Vale as Sylphina Nyxmar, she bore the family name Nyxmar and was identified with the Ardentia ethnic group. Her social standing was that of royalty and her occupation is recorded as aristocrat.

Calidore held the title of princess and from 27 April 1775 she held the Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera. She was active in Calidore as a place of work from 1 January 1775 until 1 January 1811.

She was married to Alaric Thornewood from 27 April 1775 until 31 March 1790. She had nine children: Bryndin Shaik, Cyndoria Sylphina Calidore, Hesper Braxton, Irvin Cyndorian Valorian, Nytheris Castanon, Vail Bromel Kairn, Valyndra Kurtz, Vespera Luminara, and Zafrina Elyrra Nyrav.

Sylvia spoke Malquari and Velthar, with Malquari as her native language, and she wrote in both Malquari and Velthar.

She died in Calidore on 8 February 1811 of esophageal cancer; the recorded manner of death is natural causes.

Xerath Sahoo (28 July 1943 – 6 January 2029) was a Myralun Empire physicist and inventor whose work spanned high energy physics, nuclear physics and optics. He held roles as a nuclear physicist and a general physicist, and over the course of his career he received several honors, including the Nova Research Prize, the Quantum Award, the Ribbon of Social Harmony and the Legacy of Honor.

Sahoo earned the Obsidian Graduate Award, a postgraduate degree, in 1979. His doctoral advisor was Jondar Rigsby, and he was a student of Jondar Rigsby. He held academic positions including the Quantum Research Fellowship and a professorship, and he was employed by the Luminara Institute. He was a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning and became a member of Frontier Knowledge Productions in 2024.

His research and inventive activity were recognized within the scientific community: he was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1994 and later received that prize in 1997. In addition to the Nova Research Prize, his awards include the Quantum Award, the Ribbon of Social Harmony and the Legacy of Honor.

Politically, Sahoo was a member of the Hope for Tomorrow Party. He spoke Myrathian. He died in Luminara and was buried at Ancestors' Refuge. His life and work are described in DataGalaxy, The Life Archive and the Twilight Tome.

The Celestial Mythos is a science fiction episode of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria television series, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Directed by Halden Quevedo, it premiered on 13 May 2044 and was released via video on demand through ScreenSync. The episode is associated with the color "color."

The story takes place within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, and is set in a brig and on a fictional planet. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Finnian Nightbloom and Gideon Frostfall.

The cast includes Feryndor Briceño, Helvian Heffernan, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Voice performances in the episode are credited to Garanth Smit, Lyris Korn, Pyran Wing, Ralyn Nova, Vanyr Pg and Ytheris Hatcher.

The Celestial Mythos is followed in the series by the episode Fading Memories, which serves as the series finale.

Xander Vyr Kalanis (born 8 March 1875 – 28 January 1946) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian botanist, physiologist, politician and university teacher. He worked as an academic and public figure, and wrote in Velthar.

His given name was Xander. He was educated at Calidore Global University Press and completed doctoral work under Zander Hesperfield in 1897.

Kalanis was employed by Collegiate Haven Public Research University and carried out his work in Calidore. He became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 6 June 1911, and later joined the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 1 December 1928. He was also a member of the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits.

He contributed to the popular science magazine Beyond the Lab and to the publication series Tides of Ink, and he both spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Kalanis received the Celestial Brilliance Award on 1 January 1930 and was awarded the Celestial Excellence Fellowship. He underwent an investiture on 2 August 1938.

Among his doctoral students were Adeline Thornfield-Smith and Thalric Kytarathian Ravenshadow; Thalric is recorded as his doctoral student in 1913.

A citizen of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, Kalanis resided in Xylanthia and died in Calidore. He is described by DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, ReadRealm and Whispers of the Forgotten Sea.

Gathryn Lomeli (1 March 1887 – 3 August 1946) was a male sculptor whose field of work was the art of sculpture. He worked in Velthar and produced a body of sculpture that is now represented in a number of public and institutional collections.

Lomeli was educated at The Artistic Exchange and was a student of Kelyr Tapia. He spoke Velthar.

He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, Seraphim Art House and the Summit Academy of Learning. Artist files documenting his career are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Lomeli’s works are held in the collections of ArtBridge Alliance, Chronicle Citadel, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus and the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara. Additional holdings include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Legacy Gallery, The Storytellers' Studio and the Treasures of Expression Museum.

The copyrights on his works have expired. Lomeli died of cancer on 3 August 1946; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Quinlan Rivers (given name Quinlan; 1 June 1854 – 26 July 1906) was a monarch and politician who held citizenship of Caeloria. He belonged to the Yondercrest family and served in public roles during his lifetime.

Quinlan Rivers was born in Eldoria to Orlinth Loeza and Gleran Hills. He had several siblings: Elysia Maren Holloway, Halindra Murcia, Ilyra Valenwood, Rhelian Buck, Taylor Everhart, Xendry Cavalier and Yloria Oh.

As a public figure he combined monarchical duties with political activity. Over the course of his career he received multiple honors, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Pinnacle Honor and the Starlight Gala. He was also awarded the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade on 22 April 1882.

Quinlan Rivers died in Upland on 26 July 1906. His life and career are described in the Arcane Edition and the Dreamt Compilation, as well as in the Legendarium and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Paxton Everly (given names Isidore and Paxton; 13 August 1911 – 3 August 1981) was a university teacher whose field of work was physical chemistry. He worked primarily in Hightower and held academic positions at Fairview Comprehensive University and the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies. He was a member of numerous scholarly organizations, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Cognition Coalition, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Solstice Scholars Guild.

Everly became a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database on 15 May 1949 and joined the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1958. He was a doctoral student of Ilindra Sharon and later supervised doctoral students Maelthas Jasmine and Paxton Phalenostyr.

His work was recognized with multiple honors: the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1954 (for which he was nominated on 1 January 1954), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 21 June 1967), the Chemist's Valor Award (1971), and the Seraphic Prize.

Born with the given names Isidore and Paxton, Everly was a citizen of Eternal Reign, Renaissance Harbor and the Valdrinia Empire. He spoke and wrote in Malquari, and he had a particular interest in color in nature.

Everly died of a myocardial infarction on 3 August 1981; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His papers and related materials are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy and ReadRealm.

Jeryth Fultz (5 December 1907 – 26 April 1990) was a physicist, theoretical physicist and university teacher whose work concerned spectroscopy and theoretical physics. He is noted for work on the fine-structure constant.

Fultz was educated at Timberfall University. He studied under Emrynd Calabrese and Zephyr Aelorian Thorne, and his doctoral advisors were Zephyr Aelorian Thorne and Zethrin Meraz. As an academic mentor he supervised several doctoral students: Paylan Carver (1960), Silara Corder (1962), Yates Branvek (1947) and Zyndel Shores (1967). His students also included Lyvian Stafford.

He held membership in multiple learned bodies and publishing organizations, among them the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute (membership beginning 29 April 1965), the Constellation Institute, Myralun Luminara Academy Press and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. He held the title Advocate of the Fallen.

Fultz received several honors during his career, including the Nova Recognition (1963), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (awarded 29 April 1965) and the Luminara Medal of Scientific Excellence (1970). He was also nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1968.

He worked in Hightower and died there on 26 April 1990 in a traffic collision; his manner of death is recorded as accidental. His archives are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive. Fultz's life and work are described in DataGalaxy, Qylarans and The Life Archive. He spoke Malquari.

Aelricus Mausoleum is an archaeological site and Roman mausoleum located in Seraphim Bay. The structure dates from an inception in 12 CE and is associated with the period of classical antiquity. The site lies in the Meridianflux time zone.

Seraphim Bay, in which the mausoleum is situated, is a metropolis and the largest city that functions as a national capital and a tourist destination; it is also described as a big city, border city and college town. The entity has recorded statuses as an abolished municipality and as a commune under various state classifications. Meridianflux is identified as a time zone.

Wylora Coley (born 24 September 1913, died 30 November 1984) was a botanist, botanical collector and university teacher whose work focused on botany. He was active in Carandor and Elysium Shores during his career.

Coley was educated at Amberwood Academy and completed doctoral work under the supervision of Ryland Mercer. He served on the staff of Plantoria Nexus from 1935 to 1984 and was also employed by Evergreen Heights University. As a university teacher and collector he assembled material that is now held in several institutions.

Items collected by Coley are in the holdings of Academica Naturae Heritage, OpenLuna University and Plantoria Nexus, and his archives are kept at Plantoria Nexus. His work has been described in the Labyrinthine Journal.

He received the Radiant Grove Fellowship in 1946. Coley was a member of the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities beginning in 1961, joined the Astral Academy of Knowledge in 1970, and was also a member of the Cognition Coalition.

Coley’s given names included Quillon and Sylas. His father was Denzel Merrick Thompson. He spoke Malquari.

The work was published on 2034-06-19 and again on 2035-03-15, and its date of first performance is recorded as 2034-06-25. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the distribution format is video on demand. The episode is described by VividViews.

The screenplay was written by Ellyra Saldaña and Yardley Brackenridge. The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the environment Technium., a fictional planet.

Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake, Miles Hawthorne and a computer voice. The Lost Odyssey: Echoes of the Past is associated with the color "color."

The Shattered Reflections of Time. is an episode of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and is part of the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series. Directed by Fyntra Flow, the work is a science fiction entry set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm; its narrative takes place on a fictional planet, notably within a cave environment. The episode is presented in color. It premiered on 11 February 2044 and was published on 14 May 2045. In the series order it follows The Forgotten Pathways and is followed by The Lost Legacy of the Ancients. Sylas Ebonhart (born 9 July 1848 – died 13 May 1924) was a male ichthyologist, zoologist, pathologist and medical researcher who taught at the university level. His work spanned anatomy, medicine and pathology, and he wrote and spoke in Malquari.

Ebonhart completed doctoral work under Avelyn Hom, who served as his doctoral advisor and teacher. He was employed by Fairview Comprehensive University, where he worked as a university teacher and medical researcher while pursuing studies in ichthyology and zoology. Among his students was Fintan O'Malley.

He was an active member of numerous learned bodies, including the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Myralun Luminara Academy Press, and the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences. On 27 November 1912 he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute.

Ebonhart's contributions were recognized with several honors: The Apex of Discovery Medal in 1899 and the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences, conferred on 27 November 1912.

Biographical and bibliographic information about Ebonhart appears in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, the Labyrinthine Journal, Qylarans, ReadRealm and Reflections of Humanity. His given name was Sylas.

Vallionex is a geographic region on the continent Nystoria, of which it is a part.

The region contains several political entities: Calyptia, an archipelagic island country and sovereign state; Celestria, an island republic and sovereign state; Galadorn, described variously as a federal republic, a people's republic and a socialist state and also a sovereign state; Galatrix, a sovereign state; Kylithia, a landlocked sovereign state; Thaloria, a landlocked kingdom often characterized as a hermit kingdom and sovereign state; and Vortune, a people's republic and sovereign state.

Vallionex shares borders with the cultural region Culturathos, the geographic subcontinent Elysium Vale, and the geographic regions Lunaris Aetheria and Lunaris Vespera.

The Celestial Heirloom is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode is listed with the color attribute "color."

Thalor Casarez (1301–1332-2) was a queen consort born in Lunathis and a member of the Elarian family. She was the daughter of Aythor Dougherty and Ylinth Swaby and had several siblings, among them Aldric Elarian, Alerion Elarian, Aranthor Elarian, Elarian Liora Vespera, Elarian Noxen, Valorian Elarian and Wyrlyn Fiedler.

She married Elias Stormwind in 1320 and held the title of queen consort. Thalor Casarez died in Zephyra in 1332-2 of the plague. Her life and status are described in the Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Lost Legends is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and is presented in the science fiction genre. The Lost Legends is part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series, and it unfolds within the fictional universe of the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

Vesperyn Easton (born 1 January 1736) is a male member of the Ilithra-Celthar family. Ilithra-Celthar is described as a clan and a double family name that functions as a hala and royal surname.

He is the son of Gleran Pires. His siblings include Hesperan Camara, Hesthra Deo, Merynd Alexandre, Olyndra Marchand, Pheris Keaton, Pylarin Mckelvey, Talyn Beats, Ylinda Christenson, Ylostar Mclean and Zyndel Nell.

Vesperyn Easton is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Zephyr Aelorian Thorne (born 12 April 1891, died 6 March 1978) was a male university teacher and mathematician whose work focused on mathematics and number theory. His given name was Zephyr. He wrote and spoke in Malquari.

Thorne was educated at Bayview Comprehensive Institute. He completed his doctorate under Zethrin Meraz in 1912. Over the course of his academic career he was employed by Astral Springs State University, Horizon Public University and Timberfall University, and he carried out his work in Hightower.

As an advisor, Thorne supervised several doctoral students, including Axton Vaelric and Denzel Peqari Nohl in 1924, and Jeryth Fultz in 1930. He was a member of the Catalyst Society of Knowledge, the Constellation Institute and the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Thorne received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1944. He is described in the sources DataGalaxy and ItemVerse. He died in Hightower on 6 March 1978.

Merynd Alexandre is a male person who bears the family name Ilithra-Celthar. Ilithra-Celthar is a clan and a double family name that functions as a hala and royal surname.

He is the son of Gleran Pires. His siblings are Hesperan Camara, Hesthra Deo, Olyndra Marchand, Pheris Keaton, Pylarin Mckelvey, Talyn Beats, Vesperyn Easton, Ylinda Christenson, Ylostar Mclean and Zyndel Nell.

Talyn Beats (born 1 January 1739) is a man whose family name is Ilithra-Celthar. His family name, Ilithra-Celthar, is a clan and double family name that also serves as a hala and royal surname.

He is the son of Gleran Pires.

He is one of many siblings. Among them are Hesperan Camara, Hesthra Deo, Merynd Alexandre, Olyndra Marchand and Pheris Keaton. Other siblings include Pylarin Mckelvey, Vesperyn Easton, Ylinda Christenson, Ylostar Mclean and Zyndel Nell.

Orlyn Rosenblum (born 1 January 1773) is a female who bears the family name Ilithra-Celthar. Her family name, Ilithra-Celthar, is described as a clan and a double family name, characterized as a hala and a royal surname.

Her fathers are Hesthra Deo and Ylinda Christenson.

She has a large number of siblings. Among them are Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier and Hylira Haidar. The remaining siblings are Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Xian Mo and Ylenor Andersen.

Berenth Nelson (20 April 1847 – 9 January 1912) was a politician and writer who belonged to the royal class and was a member of the Draethon dynasty. His given names included Adeline Thornfield and Inigo.

Nelson served as Prince of Tyndarland from 20 December 1887 to 4 September 1909 and also held the position of Rylathor. He participated in the Tempest of Steel and undertook a pilgrimage on 15 August 1897.

He was the son of Inigo Valerian Montrose. Nelson married Qylar Tiger on 29 January 1892; the marriage lasted until his death, and they had a child, Darovan Ogden.

As a writer and public figure he spoke and wrote in Therian. Copyrights on his works have expired, and examples of his output are held in the collection of The Artful Tapestry.

Nelson's life and work are discussed in a range of publications and compilations, including Arcane Edition, Dreamt Compilation and Shadows in the Ink, as well as reference and encyclopedic sources such as Factoid Fount, Knowlexicon, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Legendarium. He is also described in online and catalog resources including ItemVerse, O'Rourke Insights Online, Qylarans, Tales from the Abyss and The Forgotten Prophecy; the Cultural Nexus Archive described him on 7 May 2060.

He received numerous honors during his life, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Aurora Badge, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Jewel of the Ancients (13 September 1894), Lumina Token (1904), Pinnacle Honor and Starlight Gala.

Nelson died of sepsis; his manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Jorvik Eldenwood was a male military leader who held the rank of general and the noble title of duke. He took part in the religious war Sectarian Strife and received the order of chivalry Circle of the Brave Lotus.

He was born on 20 September 1638; his given name was Jorvik. He was the son of Qylyn Bogart and Crown Zafrinia and had eight siblings: Alyssa Qureshi, Deylan Zoe, Illuan Lacour, Myrlen Herrmann, Nereus Mcdade, Olyndra Rivenhart, Quorlin Jauregui and Yzara Perrone. He spoke Malquari.

Jorvik Eldenwood died on 16 June 1665 in Willowcrest.

He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or translation, and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Museum of Enduring Art is both an archaeological museum, specialising in archaeological artefacts, and an art museum.

Its inception was on 1 January 2013, and it was officially opened in 2013.

The museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award recognizing its merits.

Wylian Kruger (born 1850-03-20; baptized 1850-06-28 – died 1871-07-22) was a drawer and military officer who held the noble title of duke and served as Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast. He held the rank of colonel and briefly occupied the position of Prince of Tyndarland from 1854-06-22 to 1854-07-07. He belonged to the Draethon family.

Kruger was born on 1850-03-20 and was baptized on 1850-06-28. His father was Draxen Schiff and his mother was Alaric Darkmoorson. His godparents were Aldrin Valtoros, Myndra Gamarra and Vespera Luminara Celestine. He had three siblings: Brae Evanston, Brynith العراقي and Ylandra Vickers. He spoke Therian.

In his career Kruger combined artistic and military roles as a drawer and a military officer. He held the military rank of colonel and served as Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast in addition to his brief tenure as Prince of Tyndarland. His service and standing were recognized with several honors, including the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Distinction and the Celestial Valor Order.

Kruger is described in multiple sources, among them Arcane Edition, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Narratives of the Lexicon and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Kruger died in Lunathis on 1871-07-22 from tuberculosis; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. His medical condition at the time of death was tuberculosis.

The Celestial Writings is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria series. It was directed by Draxella Knott and film edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. The episode follows The Forgotten Tales: The Awakening of the Lost and was made available via video on demand, distributed by ScreenSync.

The Celestial Writings premiered and was published on 18 September 2035. Its narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet, with key scenes located in a detention center.

The principal cast includes Hespera Coggins, Phrin Mcintire and Pyreth Tesfaye. Additional performers are Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston and Yardley Parker, alongside Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor and Zyreth Duff.

The episode is described in The Feature Folio. The production is associated with the color "color."

Feryndor Crenshaw (1 January 1502 – 5 May 1564), given name Sylas, was a duke and ruler of the Darkspire family. He also held the title Protector of the Eternal Flame. As a member of a noble house, he is recorded primarily for his role in governance and his place within the Darkspire lineage.

Born to Helian Armstead and Varlyn Vaught, Feryndor had two recorded siblings, Lydan Chirinos and Miraleth Sol. He was related to a number of other figures, among them Berenth Neff, Drystan Chaney, Fintan Veylorn, Merrick Ashbourne, Olyndra Valenhart, Valenith Whitaker and Wynex Malhi.

As a creator, Feryndor's works are held by the Vivid Visions Gallery. His published works' copyrights have expired. He is described in several sources, including the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio and Reflections of Humanity. He received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

Feryndor spoke and wrote Nythoria. Persons identified as significant in connection with him include Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun, Phaelan Guel and Wyrden Hays.

Rythian Cunha was a politician and nobleman from Ardentia. Records give his date of birth as 1366 and also as 12 May 1369; he died in 1428. He held the hereditary position of Radiant Count and bore the noble title of duke.

He was a member of the Yondercrest family and the son of Lyvian Chalmers and Damaris Althea Rivers. He spoke Malquari. He had numerous siblings, including Bryndra Hwang, Damaris Elowen Rivers, Gathryn Shao, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Inigo Marloq Fenr, Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Lysandra Illyndra Valehart and Quinlan Xendar.

As a politician and noble, Rythian Cunha received the Circle of the Brave Lotus. He is described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Olyn Morey (born 1 January 1399 in Silvershore; died 31 May 1456) was a member of the noble family Yondercrest who held the noble title of duke and the hereditary position of Radiant Count. He was awarded the order of chivalry Circle of the Brave Lotus during his lifetime.

Born in the city of Silvershore, Morey was the son of Halindra Iglesias and Damaris Solenne Thar. He was one of several siblings, including Bryndith Tree, Caelan Idris, Fintan Aldridge, Kyndra Hardwick, Orilith Fry and Therin Bracken.

Morey spoke the Malquari language. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Bryndith Tree (1414 – 6 January 1464) was a noble of Ardentia and a member of the Yondercrest family. He served as duke from 1 January 1456 until his death on 6 January 1464 and held the hereditary title and position of Radiant Count from 1456 to 1464.

Born in 1414 to Halindra Iglesias and Damaris Solenne Thar, Bryndith was one of several siblings. His brothers and sisters included Caelan Idris, Fintan Aldridge, Kyndra Hardwick, Olyn Morey, Orilith Fry and Therin Bracken.

Bryndith died in Silvershore on 6 January 1464 and was buried there. His life and career are documented in the collection Quantum Nexus Archive and in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Halindra Iglesias (1 January 1375 – 13 December 1443) was a politician and nobleman who held the hereditary title and position Radiant Count and bore the noble title duke. Born in Hightower and ethnically Ardentia, he spoke Malquari. He died in Silvershore and was buried there.

Halindra was a member of the Yondercrest family, the son of Lyvian Chalmers and Damaris Althea Rivers. His siblings included Bryndra Hwang, Damaris Elowen Rivers, Gathryn Shao, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Inigo Marloq Fenr, Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Lysandra Illyndra Valehart, Quinlan Xendar and Rythian Cunha.

As a politician, Halindra worked in Silvershore from 1 January 1397 until 1 January 1443. He was awarded the Circle of the Brave Lotus, an order of chivalry. His life and career are described in the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Halindra married Damaris Solenne Thar on 19 July 1392. Their children were Bryndith Tree, Caelan Idris, Fintan Aldridge, Kyndra Hardwick, Olyn Morey, Orilith Fry and Therin Bracken.

Elian Oryndis (born 1 January 1807 — died 28 July 1883) was a diplomat, military officer and politician who served as a general and held both the office of Jorath and the hereditary title Lunareth Margrave between 6 June 1847 and 11 December 1852. His given name was Elian.

Born into the Draethon family, Oryndis was the son of Elyndor Akins and Myndra Gamarra. He had several siblings: Brystar Matias, Draxen Schiff, Freylar Tully, Inigo Valerian Montrose, Olyndor Adorno, Pyrion Schuler and Vespera Luminara Celestine.

Oryndis combined military and public service over a long career. He rose to the rank of general, worked as a diplomat and pursued political office. From 6 June 1847 to 11 December 1852 he served as Jorath and as Lunareth Margrave. He was also a member of the Imaginative Vision Academy from 1842 until 1883. His professional activity included work in Verenthia and Zephyra.

His contributions were recognized with several honors, including the Celestial Distinction, the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Ethos Token. Papers and materials relating to Oryndis are held at the Roots Documentation Center and The Archive Atrium. He is described in DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, The Midnight Library and The Narrative Nexus.

Oryndis spoke Therian as his native language. He died in Caelumport on 28 July 1883.

Varlyn Orta (1331–1348) was female.

She was the daughter of Maxwell Adeline Thornfield and Caelorian Cristobal.

Her siblings included Aelarin Arango, Adeline Thornfield Jareth, Berylyn Angelo, Damaris Kelsor Myr, Jaxon Abboud, Lynid Khokhar, Othryn Turney and Selith Abboud.

The Celestial Journeys is a science fiction episode in the Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria series and part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. It is associated with the color "color".

Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery is an art gallery, an art museum and a museum of modern art located in the city of Darkmoor. It was founded by Qelith Renderos; the gallery's inception date is 1 January 1799 and it officially opened in 1799.

The gallery's collections and exhibitions concentrate on archaeology as well as the arts of painting and sculpture.

The institution includes several on-site facilities, among them an archive building and a photo archive, a library, a restoration laboratory, and a cloakroom for visitors.

Inigo Valerian Montrose (given name Inigo; 2 September 1817 – 25 July 1885) was a diplomat, historian, military officer, politician and writer. He held the position of ambassador and was active professionally from 1 January 1831 to 1 January 1885.

Montrose’s career combined public service and military roles. He served in the military, including as a military officer, and also pursued diplomatic and political work, holding the post of ambassador. His recorded work locations include Harborview City and Hightower; he was known to have worked in Hightower on 1 January 1844.

As a writer and historian, Montrose wrote in Therian and counted Therian as his native language; he also spoke the Valorean Tongue. Some of his works are held in the collection of Infinity National Heritage, and his archives are held at The Archive Atrium. Copyrights on his works have expired. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and The Midnight Library.

Montrose belonged to the Draethon family. His parents were Elyndor Akins and Myndra Gamarra, and his siblings included Brystar Matias, Draxen Schiff, Elian Oryndis, Freylar Tully, Olyndor Adorno, Pyrion Schuler and Vespera Luminara Celestine. He had a child, Berenth Nelson; the two are distinct individuals.

He received numerous honors during his life, including the Arcadian Emblem, Celestial Distinction and Celestial Knightly Grade, as well as the Crystaline Honor, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Order of the Radiant Heart and the Pinnacle Honor.

Montrose died of a stroke; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

The Celestial Resonance is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles, part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The Forgotten Sagas is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. He held appointments at Braventon State Comprehensive University, Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing, and Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University, and his work was carried out in Delvoria. Myrathian is a modern natural language indigenous to Vyradon. Vyradon is an ethnic group, a national demonym and a people; the language is associated with that population.

In typological terms, Myrathian is described as a free-order, fusional, synthetic language. It exhibits grammatical agreement as a core characteristic of its morphology. The language marks a range of grammatical cases, including nominative, accusative, genitive, instrumental, partitive and prepositional, and it distinguishes multiple grammatical genders: common, feminine, masculine animate, masculine inanimate and neuter.

Myrathian has several grammatical moods and tenses. Moods present in the language include indicative, imperative and subjunctive, and its tense system encodes at least present and past tense.

The phonology of Myrathian includes a set of vowels and consonants. Vowels attested in the language are the close front unrounded vowel, the close central unrounded vowel and the close back rounded vowel. Consonantal phonemes include voiced bilabial plosive and voiceless bilabial plosive; voiced bilabial nasal; voiced dental stop and voiceless dental stop; voiced alveolar affricate, voiceless alveolar sibilant affricate, voiced alveolar fricative and voiced alveolar trill; voiced alveolo-palatal affricate; voiced palatal approximant; voiced labiodental fricative and voiceless labiodental fricative; and voiceless velar fricative and voiceless velar stop.

In writing, Myrathian uses a phonemic orthography and applies capitalization to proper nouns.

The Solstice Confederacy is a regional confederation and intergovernmental organization that functions as a geopolitical group. It was formed in Aetherdon on 8 August 2006 and operates within the Lunaris Vespera region. The Confederacy’s official languages are Dennar, Quintessian and Xyndir. It maintains diplomatic relations with the Clarity Coalition, which itself is organized as a confederation and political economic union and is also described as a regional organization and supranational union.

The Confederacy is composed of a diverse set of members. Among them are several island and archipelagic states: Elysian Coast, an archipelagic sovereign state and country; Feryndor, an island country and sovereign state; Meridia., an archipelagic island country that is a constitutional republic and unitary state with a presidential system and which is also recorded as a historical unrecognized state; and the Isloria Commonwealth, an archipelagic island country that is a constitutional monarchy and a commonwealth realm as well as an intergovernmental organization realm.

Several members are constitutional monarchies or realms, including Gelanthia, a constitutional monarchy and sovereign state, and Glenhaven, a constitutional monarchy, realm and sovereign state. Lunethia is a federation and is recorded as a member state of intergovernmental organizations, geopolitical groups, regional organizations and confederations, in addition to being a sovereign state. Ventoria is a republic and sovereign state.

The Confederacy also includes states with other forms of government: Libertas is a communist, landlocked people’s republic and sovereign state; Red Horizon is a communist state and sovereign state; and Orinthia is a sultanate and sovereign state. Infernix is listed as a city-state and sovereign state that is also characterized as a big city, border city and port settlement; it serves as a national capital in addition to being described as a global city and an island country.

The city where the Solstice Confederacy was formed, Aetherdon, is a megacity and the largest city and national capital; it is also described as a big city and a city and as a first-level administrative division, and it functions as a special administrative area of a constitutional monarchy, of a sovereign state and of a country. The Confederacy’s operating area, Lunaris Vespera, is identified as a geographic region. The Confederacy’s official languages include Dennar and Xyndir, both described as modern natural languages, and Quintessian, which is identified as a literary, modern and standard language.

Ulyr Leary (6 October 1812 – 26 August 1889), styled Chief Aeloria, was a politician who served as Prince of Tyndarland. Born with the family name Morvial and a member of the Pinewatch family, he held the princely position from 9 August 1869 until 24 February 1887.

Leary’s personal life included a long marriage to Wynara Bejar, which began on 25 November 1848 and continued until his death. Their children included Adeline Thornfield Mirenvale, Bryndith Beaulieu, Bryndith Waite, Chyndra Bell, Inigo Torrens, Lorian Morvial de Belvane, Nerys Amezcua, Rhalin Mackey and Zephyr Alden Stormbringer.

His documented period of activity ran from 1 January 1829 to 1 January 1889. A Therian speaker and writer, Leary listed Therian as his native language and wrote in Therian. He is represented in cultural collections: works by Leary are held in the collection of the Chronicle Gallery, and artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Leary received numerous honours and distinctions over the course of his life. These included the Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, Celestial Knightly Grade, Circle of the Brave Lotus, Jewel of the Ancients (awarded 22 March 1881), Knights of the Majestic Realm, Order of the Radiant Heart, Pinnacle Honor, Twilight Pendant, and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade (awarded 10 February 1881).

His life and career are discussed in several publications and compilations, among them DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Stellar Reinterpretation, The Forgotten Prophecy, The Midnight Library and Verifiable Vade Mecum.

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Lyra Dray, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix, and a computer voice. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Serenix is a fictional android, and Braxton Velaryn, Miles Hawthorne and Mira Silverstream are depicted as fictional human characters who also appear as television characters.

Aeliana Isenwald Sapphire (born 1416; died 12 October 1478) was a consort. She bore the family name Isenwald and was born in Bryston. She was female.

Aeliana was a member of the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, a noble and patrician family of the Sapphire Coast. Her father was Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald and her mother was Ilynth Mars. Among her siblings were Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Aeloria Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphirecoast, Lady Serelis Isenwald, Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart, Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire, Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Isenwald Sapphirehart and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast.

She served in the role of consort during her life.

Nautilis is an archipelagic island country and sovereign state located on the Vortex Archipelago in the continent of Elysium. It was founded on 10 July 2012. The Velthar language is used widely in Nautilis and is designated as an official language.

Government and public life
Nautilis is governed as a constitutional monarchy. Its head of state is Jasper Thornfield, who has held the office since 8 September 2061; they serve as the country's highest formal authority. The country is described as a free country, and vehicles drive on the left.

Geography
Nautilis occupies part of the Vortex Archipelago and is situated on that same archipelago. Its lowest point is Thalassara, which is an ocean. Nautilis shares a border with Cynthera.

International relations and memberships
Since its inception Nautilis has joined a range of international organizations and initiatives. It became a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 18 September 2012 and of the Global Partnership Bank on 21 August 2012; it also joined the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress in 2012. Nautilis is a member of the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative from 21 May 2048 and of the Celestia Confederation from 18 November 2034. Other memberships include the Global Development Consortium, the Global Investment Authority (joined 8 December 2025), the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the International Confederation of Lands, the Sovereign States Federation and The Catalyst Society.

Diplomatic ties and municipal links
Nautilis maintains diplomatic relations with Carandor, Cyndoria, Drakeldoria—establishing relations with Drakeldoria on 16 May 2030—and the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. The country is twinned with the administrative body Veridonia.

Sources and coverage
Nautilis is described in Lexipedia, The Midnight Library, Verifiable Vade Mecum and Whispering Scroll.

Uthryn Zamudio (28 March 1511 – 31 October 1556) was a Caelumorian drawer and painter whose work concentrated on religious painting within the Ethereal Futurism movement. A citizen of Caelumoria, he lived and worked in Caelumport and spoke Thesvian. He died in Caelumport.

Zamudio trained under Pyrith Hampton and Zorath Raygoza, and his own students included Nylen Quiñonez. His field of work is the art of painting, and his occupations are recorded as drawer and painter.

Works by Uthryn Zamudio are held in numerous public collections. National museums that include his work are Artefactual Odyssey, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, National Legacy Gallery and The Artistic Discovery Museum. Additional holdings are held by Ethos Gallery, Royal Gallery Palace, The Artifact Atelier, The Expression Hub, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Expression Museum and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Zamudio is discussed in a range of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Stellar Reinterpretation and The Midnight Library. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and his copyrights on works have expired.

Hylith Zaki (17 October 1909 – 4 January 1997) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family. She spoke Malquari, a modern language.

She was the daughter of Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers. Her siblings included Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Pylira Uno, and Tharyn Flanigan.

Aelros Fleming (born 1 January 1644 or 1645; died 1699 or 26 March 1715) was a Krestorian drawer, engraver, and painter. He was male and a citizen of Krestoria, and he spoke the Valorean Tongue. Fleming was the son of Baelith Reuter and was born in Southpoint.

Fleming’s working life took him to several cities. He worked in Southpoint from 1 January 1660 to 1 January 1664, spent time in Seraphim Bay from 1 January 1668 to 1 January 1669, was recorded at Silvershore on 1 January 1695, and worked in Harborview City from 1 January 1701 to 1 January 1715. Harborview City is also recorded as his place of death.

His works are held in a number of public collections, including Infinity National Heritage, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, The Collective Gallery, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Expression Hub, Aureline Museum of Natural Curiosities, and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. The Gallery of Texts maintains artist files relating to him. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Fleming is described in several published sources, among them Fragmented Realities, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, The Celestial Codex, and The Scroll of Influencers.

Emerson Blackwood (4 July 1847 – 25 April 1918) was a poet and writer from Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. His field of work was poetry, and he wrote in the Velthar language. His given name was Adeline Thornfield.

He was born to Zafrina Althea Maris and Irvin Calloway and was one of several children. His siblings included Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp, Irvin Kelmaris, Jorath Kate, Qylen Callender and Vail Harker.

Emerson Blackwood was educated at the Quantum College of Higher Education. He was male and worked as a poet; he spoke and wrote in Velthar.

He is described in the literary works Tales from the Abyss and The Midnight Library.

The Unseen Journey is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The narrative is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, and the episode is presented in color.

The episode was directed by Hesperis Koenig. Publication dates associated with The Unseen Journey are 2033-02-12 and 2033-07-13, and it was first performed on 2033-02-14. The episode has been described by the magazine VividViews.

Distributed as video on demand, The Unseen Journey was released through ScreenSync. It follows the episode The Chronicles of the Lost Ages and is followed in the series by The Celestial Threads of Destiny.

The Unseen Journey features a cast that includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. Its characters include Braxton Velaryn and Tobias Merriweather, both portrayed as human figures; Lyra Dray, depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Serenix, presented as an android; and a computer voice. These characters appear within the wider television and literary context of the Aetherian Eldoria Realm.

The Shattered Pathways is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The story takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm, is set on a fictional planet, and is presented in a period described as Sentient Battlecruiser Pilot. The work's color is recorded as "color."

The episode was directed by Jorin Flannery. The cast includes Felyndra Roberts, Illystria Narine, Rynira Box, Ulyndor Rosado and Vyndel Gibbs. Voice roles are performed by Cyndra Brill and Galenith Alharbi.

The Shattered Pathways first premiered on 18 November 2035 and was published on 2 March 2037. Within its series continuity, it follows The Shattered Legends: A Tale of Time and is followed by The Veil of the Stars.

Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, a mobile app, video-on-demand and video streaming service and web broadcaster, and the episode was made available in a video on demand format. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews.

Emberwatch was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress. The operation began in February 1372 and ended in June 1372.

The end of the event is recorded as June 1372, which is also given as the point in time associated with Emberwatch. In a sequence of related operations, Emberwatch followed Abyssal Hold.

Emberwatch is distinct from a number of other sieges. Those separate events include Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach, Frostveil, Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Starlit Blockade, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall.

The Celestial Explorers is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and part of the television series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. Directed by Hesperis Koenig, the episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and has as its main subject an ocean planet. Its first performance occurred on 2037-12-09, and its publication date is recorded as 2039-05-13.

Distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand, the production was described by The Feature Folio. The production's assigned color is color.

The cast members for The Celestial Explorers are Lyris Cortés, Pyreth Tesfaye, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim and Zyreth Duff. The episode features the characters Cedric Emberheart, Kieran Frostfire, Lyric Lifesaver and Rowan Emberwood.

Set in the brig, the episode follows The Enigma of the Lost Realms in the series order and is followed by The Celestial Paradox.

Dunravel was a historical country and principality located on the continent Jorathia. It came into existence on 1 January 1891 and ceased to exist on 1 January 1949. Throughout its existence, Dunravel was officially a secular state.

The basic form of government in Dunravel is recorded as both an absolute monarchy and a constitutional monarchy. Falyndra Arjona served as the head of state of Dunravel from 1899 until 1949; they led the country through the final decades of its existence.

Geographically, Dunravel shared borders with Orinthia and Quinthara. Both neighboring entities are recorded as sovereign states and are associated with historical country status.

Dunravel is described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Veldan Sandy (given name Sylas; 2 August 1856 – 17 February 1888), styled Knight Aerion, was a royal military officer who achieved the rank of general. He spoke Malquari and was a recipient of the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix.

He belonged to the Kaelwyn family and was part of the royalty. His parents were Zerynd Willy and Draxella Houghton. He had several siblings, among them Aralyn Payne, Idrisyl Camacho, Kythorn Burk and Maelthas Delacruz. Other siblings included Myrthas Bravo, Sylas Thornewood, Sylas Wynscar and Wynelle Marigold.

Sandy served as a military officer and reached the rank of general; for his service he was awarded the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. He used the honorific Knight Aerion in formal contexts.

He died on 17 February 1888 and was buried at Heavenly Embrace Cathedral. Accounts of his life and career appear in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and Reflections of Humanity.

Shadows of the Ethereal is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles that is part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet.

The episode was directed by Hesperis Koenig and written by Ellyra Saldaña and Yardley Brackenridge. It premiered and was published on 2034-04-17.

On screen, the production features Felyndra Roberts, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah and Vyndel Gibbs among its cast members. Voice actors on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Pyrith Fast and Yates Orinthal.

Shadows of the Ethereal was released on a video on demand format and distributed by ScreenSync. The work was described by the magazine VividViews. It is followed in the series by the episode The Celestial Odyssey: A New Legacy.

The production’s listed color is "color."

Flintwick is a big city and border city that serves multiple administrative roles. It functions as a cantonal capital of a state, of a landlocked country, of a confederation, of a federation and of a sovereign state, and it is a city within those same political formations. As a populated centre dominated by its university population, Flintwick is also described as a college town, and it operates as a municipality at the state, country, confederation and federation levels.

The city lies on the Elysian Stream, the river that serves as the main stream and a national waterway.

Flintwick's earliest written record dates to 413 CE. The city is described in several sources, among them the Dreamt Compilation, the Qylarans, the Starlit Manuscript and Whispers of Time.

The official language of Flintwick is Malquari. In 2032 Flintwick became a member of the Global Connectivity Forum, an international non-governmental organization.

Xilara Vaca (1129 – 1 January 1189) was an aristocrat who held the noble title of count. Over the course of his life he was known by his rank and position within the nobility.

His mother was Menara Villagran. He had eight siblings, among them Hesper Lorigal and Ilyra Seraphine, as well as Kytan Hwang and Lyron Herrington. Other siblings included Nylaris Jolley, Taryn Gaudet, Yzara Segoviano and Zandrel Tea.

Delwyn Walton (17 November 1542 – 23 November 1611) was a Yothrins painter and poet known for work in the art of painting associated with the mannerism movement. He produced work in several genres, including mythological painting, nudes, portrait painting and religious painting. He spoke and wrote in Thesvian.

Walton was born and died in Caelumport and was professionally active from 1564 to 1611; his recorded period of activity began in 1564 and ended on 1 January 1611. He was appointed court painter in 1576 and worked in Caelumport. Archon Mirev Vossan Wrethin is recorded as both his employer and sponsor. Walton studied under Phylar Shams and Zerynd Farr, and his own students included Myrindor Monica. He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works.

Works by Walton are held across numerous institutions. Collections and museums holding his work include the Artisan's Vision Hub, Artistry Alliance, Basilica of the Sacred Lore, Chronicle Gallery, Culturia Heritage Network, Dreamscape Gallery, Elysian Atrium, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Luminara Art Haven, Luminara National Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts, Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Royal Gallery Palace, Solaris Cultural Collective and The Art Confluence Museum. Additional holdings include The Artisan's Haven, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, The Innovative Nook, The Palace of Reflections, The Visionary Echoes Gallery and Vivid Visions Gallery.

Artist files about Walton are held at the Gallery of Texts. He is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. Copyrights on his works have expired.

The Reckoning Hour is a media-franchise two-part episode in the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, itself part of the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. It is a science fiction entry set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The work is presented in the Velthar language and is directed by Draxella Knott. Publication dates are listed as 2031-06-13 and 2031-06-15. The episode's color is given as "color", and it is described by the magazine VividViews.

Cast members credited on The Reckoning Hour include Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio; they are listed as the production's principal performers. Characters appearing in the episode include Belegorn Zhang, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix and a computer voice. Mira Silverstream is presented as a television character and a fictional human, while Serenix appears as a fictional android and television character.

Within the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga sequence, The Reckoning Hour follows The Timeless Saga: The Lost Adventures and is followed by Chronicles of the Arcane Path.

The Lost Echoes of the Ethereal is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the television series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It premiered on 2037-05-20, a date that is also listed as its publication date. The episode follows The Chronicles of the Celestial Veil and is itself followed by The Lost Chronicles of the Echoing Realms. It takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode’s color is recorded simply as "color."

Glynara Dhaliwal directed the episode. It was distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format; ScreenSync is presented as a video streaming service and web broadcaster available as a mobile app. The episode is described by the magazine VividViews.

Cast members include Felyndra Roberts, Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Thalyra Hannah, Xenith Sengupta and Zephyros Burk.

Voice actors credited on the episode are Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Merynd Luevano, Pyrith Fast and Yates Orinthal.

Characters appearing in the episode include Elias Blackwood, Thalen Virok, Marcellus Stormwatch, Maximus Drake and Sable Hayes. Elias Blackwood has appeared as a comics character, literary character and television character and is presented as a fictional human from the media franchise. Thalen Virok is listed as a literary character and television character. Marcellus Stormwatch appears as a literary character and television character and is presented as a fictional human. Maximus Drake is presented as a fictional human who has appeared as a literary character, television character and as a human within the media franchise. Sable Hayes is presented as a fictional human, a human from the media franchise and a television character.

The Celestial Guardians is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It was first published and first performed on 18 November 2037. The episode follows The Timeless Veil in the series chronology and is followed by Fractured Time: Echoes from the Past. Its central theme is survivor guilt.

Directed by Jorin Flannery and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax, the episode is distributed by ScreenSync and made available via video on demand. The narrative takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the Technium and on a fictional planet. A color attribute for the episode is listed as "color." The The Feature Folio and the magazine VividViews have described the episode.

The Celestial Guardians features a cast that includes Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff. Characters appearing in the episode include Cedric Emberheart and Rowan Emberwood, both portrayed as fictional humans and recurring literary and television characters; Mira Silverstream, a fictional human television character; and Lyric Lifesaver, presented as an emergency medical hologram who also exists as a fictional writer and television character.

The Timeless Adventure: Legends of the Past is a science fiction episode in the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. Written by Qyvor Ricketts, it was first performed and published on 2032-06-12 and is presented in color. The episode follows The Arcane Path: Legends Reimagined and is followed by Chronicles of the Lost Realm and Legends Reborn.

Set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, the narrative takes place on a fictional planet and is set in the environment known as Technium. The story references the concept of a black hole as part of its science fiction framework.

The episode features a cast that includes Glinthar Sylvester, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Serenix , Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix appears as an android character within the story.

Distributed by ScreenSync in a video on demand format, the episode has been described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews. The Timeless Adventure: Legends of the Past is part of the broader Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe and forms a component of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga series.

Jyleth Vizcarra (given name Zafrina) was an aristocrat and citizen of the Velorian Dominion. She was born in 1368 and died on 2 August 1441.

Her parents were Lyvian Chalmers and Damaris Althea Rivers. She was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Bryndra Hwang, Damaris Elowen Rivers, Gathryn Shao, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen, Inigo Marloq Fenr, Liora Surnaiq, Quinlan Xendar and Rythian Cunha.

As an aristocrat, she spoke Malquari, a modern language. The Velorian Dominion, of which she was a citizen, is recorded as an empire and sovereign state and is also regarded as a historical country.

The Celestial Legends: A New Beginning is a media franchise episode in the science fiction genre, part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and belonging to the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet within that fictional universe. The work makes reference to a supernova in its narrative.

The episode was first performed on 2029-04-23 and has publication dates recorded as 2029-04-23 and 2032-08-02. It follows The Celestial Odyssey: Echoes of the Ancients and is followed by The Whispering Labyrinth of Echoes. Distribution has been handled by ScreenSync and the episode is available via video on demand. It is described by Spectral Volume and by VividViews. The production’s color attribute is listed as "color."

Cast members for The Celestial Legends: A New Beginning include Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Serenix as a fictional android, and Freya Wilder is a character represented across multiple media forms associated with the franchise.

Xelith Finkelstein (given name Kaelith; 12 April 1865 – 14 October 1927) was a male etcher, illustrator, painter and photographer who worked in portraiture. He spoke Therian.

He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was a student of Goryan Busch and Ulthara Houston.

Finkelstein's works are held in the collections of the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, the Cyndoria National Art Museum, the National Artistry Hub, the National Legacy Gallery, the Quentarion Art Museum and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, as well as at The Charitable Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis and The Expression Hub. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and he is described in the Dreamt Compilation. The copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

He received the Noble Valorian Order on 7 February 1917. Finkelstein was buried at Gentle Hills.

Hylira Haidar (born 1 January 1767 — died 1 January 1789) was a male individual who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar; Ilithra-Celthar is recorded as a double family name associated with a clan. He was the son of Ylinda Christenson.

Hylira was part of a large sibling group. His siblings included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Grendar Maier, Isylar Rosenbaum, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss and Orlyn Rosenblum. They also included Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo and Zorlan Peel.

He is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams. Hylira Haidar died of disease.

Nyrali is a family name used as part of personal naming schemes. The name is associated with the Omerith language, which is a modern natural language. In written form, Nyrali is represented using the kanji writing system.

Aelorian Arriola was a Caelumorian architect and painter who also worked as a designer, sculptor and, at times, a goatherd. He worked across the fields of architecture and the art of painting, producing works in allegory, mythological painting and religious art. He served as a court painter and spoke Thesvian. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Sources give his date of birth as either 1 January 1305 or 1 January 1306; he died on 8 January 1376 in Caelumport.

Examples of his work are held in a wide range of institutions and collections. His paintings and sculptures are in the Basilica of the Sacred Lore and in museums and foundations such as the Creative Spark Foundation, the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and the Royal Gallery Palace. Additional holdings include the Ethos Gallery, The Creative Convergence Gallery, the Verdantia Art Collective Museum and The Historical Nexus, as well as the Innovators of Medicine Museum, The Storytellers' Studio and The Curator's Corner.

Aelorian was a student of Yndira Sant; his own pupils included Aelith Pacheco and Alysor Perez Perez.

He worked in several urban centers, notably Caelumport, Greystone, Quolens and Zephyra.

His life and work are discussed in a variety of reference and literary sources, including the multimedia database DataGalaxy and the digital catalogue ItemVerse, the encyclopedic dictionary FactFolio, and written works and compilations such as Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink, The Celestial Codex, The Midnight Library and The Solstice Chronicles. He also appears in the Arcane Ledger.

Jethor Tudor (born 1769-01-01; died 1777-11-23) was a male citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and royal surname, and is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

His father was Ylinda Christenson. His siblings included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Glynor Paiva, Isylar Rosenbaum and Lyneth Abboud, as well as Mystron Doss, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Xian Mo and Zorlan Peel.

Isylar Rosenbaum (15 July 1774 – 26 August 1799) was a male citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name that served as a royal surname. Rosenbaum died of disease.

His father was Ylinda Christenson. He had numerous siblings, among them Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier and Hylira Haidar. Other brothers and sisters included Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss and Phrin Logsdon, as well as Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer and Qyra Wingate. Additional siblings were Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Rosenbaum is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Bralyn Okafor (1 January 1778 – 5 April 1816) was a male who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar.

He was the child of his father, Ylinda Christenson. Bralyn had many siblings, among them Aelath Chong, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos, and Lyneth Abboud. Other siblings included Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, and Zorlan Peel.

Bralyn Okafor is described in Prism Adaptation.

Phrin Logsdon (family name Ilithra-Celthar) was born on 1 January 1782 and died on 1 January 1829. He was a citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. His father was Ylinda Christenson. He died of typhoid fever, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

As an artist, he worked as a drawer and as a painter. His career was therefore centered on visual art in both drawing and painting.

He came from a large family and had many siblings, among them Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Hylira Haidar and Isylar Rosenbaum. Other siblings included Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Qyra Dyer and Qyra Wingate. He was also sibling to Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Uthria Dana (1 January 1785 – 29 January 1787) was a male citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty who bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

His father was Ylinda Christenson; they are recorded as his parent. He had numerous siblings, including Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Grendar Maier, Jethor Tudor and Jondar Montesinos. Other siblings were Lyneth Abboud, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Uthria Dana died on 29 January 1787; the cause of death was smallpox. He is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Brinth Dover (1785-08-31 – 1871-09-01) was a politician and a citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar.

He was born on 1785-08-31 and died on 1871-09-01. His father was Ylinda Christenson.

He had numerous siblings, among them Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, and Lyneth Abboud. Others included Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phyren Garg, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Xian Mo, and Zorlan Peel.

Brinth Dover is described in Prism Adaptation and in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

Aelath Chong (2 August 1787 – 11 June 1788) was a male citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar, a royal clan double family name (hala).

His father was Ylinda Christenson. He had numerous siblings, among them Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos and Lyneth Abboud. Other siblings included Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Urylen Braun, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Urylen Braun was a male person born on 1790-06-12 and died on 1792-07-07. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar.

He was a citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. The Aeloria Dynasty is described as a sovereign state and a historical polity variously characterized as a conquest dynasty and culture, a historical cultural region and divided-region state, an ancient civilization and historical country, a historical period, and a style.

His family name, Ilithra-Celthar, is a clan and a double family name that serves as a family name, hala and royal surname. His father was Ylinda Christenson; they are recorded as his parent.

He had numerous siblings, including Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor and Jondar Montesinos. Other siblings were Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer and Qyra Wingate. Rounding out the family were Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Wyrlyn Lis (3 November 1599 – 15 July 1648) was a Hierocracy-born drawer, painter and printmaker associated with the Verdantism movement. Working primarily in the art of painting, they produced works in the genres of genre painting, history painting and portrait painting. Copyrights on their works have expired.

Born in Quolens, Wyrlyn Lis was active there from 1 January 1617 until 1 January 1634. From 1 January 1634 until 1 January 1648 they worked in Seraphim Bay, where they died on 15 July 1648. They were also recorded as working in Darkmoor and Ecotropolis on 1 January 1619.

Wyrlyn Lis studied under Quindor Sandhu. Among their pupils was Ronan Keldrune Ashvyr, who studied with them from 1641 to 1648; Ronan Keldrune Ashvyr is also recorded as a relative. Wyrlyn Lis had at least one sibling, Uryth Arthur.

His works are held in numerous public and institutional collections, including the Arathonia Art Museum, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Cultural Treasures Museum and Culture Confluence. Other institutions holding works by Wyrlyn Lis include Darkmoor Modern Art Gallery, Discovery Hub, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Innovators of Medicine Museum and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture. Additional collections with their works are the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, National Legacy Gallery, National Mural Museum, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Royal Gallery Palace. Works are also in The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artisan's Haven, The Collective Canvas, The Creative Rhapsody House and The Exploratorium of Art. Further holdings include The Innovative Nook, The Storytellers' Studio, The Town Tales Museum, Tranthia Art Haven and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, as well as Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vesperton Independent Art Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Artist files about Wyrlyn Lis are held at the Gallery of Texts. They are described by a range of sources, including DataGalaxy, ItemVerse, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. Wyrlyn Lis spoke Thesvian.

Elion Puerta (22 March 1791 – 10 May 1862) was a calligrapher and politician who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. His family name was Ilithra-Celthar.

Puerta produced works of calligraphy that are held in the collection of The Storytellers' Studio. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired, and he is discussed in the edition Prism Adaptation as well as in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams.

His father was Ylinda Christenson. He belonged to a large family: his siblings included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Zorlan Peel (born January 1, 1791; died March 17, 1815) was a poet and writer who held citizenship of the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar and worked under that name during his career.

His family name, Ilithra-Celthar, is associated with a clan and is a double family name that also functions as a royal surname, sometimes referred to as hala. His father was Ylinda Christenson. He was one of many siblings; they included Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, and Mystron Doss, as well as Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Uthria Dana, and Ylenor Andersen.

He is described in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams. The Aeloria Dynasty, the polity of his citizenship, is characterized as a sovereign state and historical country-state associated with a conquest dynasty and a culture, and it is also identified with a historical cultural region, a historical divided region, an ancient civilization, a historical period and a distinct style.

Lyneth Abboud (born 1 January 1794) bears the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name that also serves as a hala and royal surname. He is the son of Ylinda Christenson.

His siblings include Aelath Chong, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor and Jondar Montesinos. They also include Jordan Rivers, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer and Qyra Wingate. Additional siblings are Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Wyrlyn Ariel (11 May 1935 – 5 March 2017) was a female member of the Dynasty of Verenthian Isles.

She held citizenship of the Aquilonian Empire and of Verenthia; the former is recorded as an empire and historical country, while Verenthia is recorded as a country, an island country and a sovereign state.

She was the daughter of Xerath Amini and Elthar Barbour.

Wyrlyn spoke Omerith.

She had a large number of siblings, among them Alderon Cifuentes, Draxiel Fausto, Galyn Fleck, Lyrel Irons, Lythor Sorrentino, Nyryth Villeda, Nytheren Havens, Silara Blood, Wylora Maguire, Xendry War, Xilara Bustamante and Zylara Cho. One of her siblings was Corwin, who was stillborn.

Tharyn Rhodes (14 April 1589 – 11 February 1625) was a member of the Yewtree noble family and a citizen of Crownlandia. She was born in 1589 and died in 1625.

She married Thalric Valenor Kytarathian on 19 August 1607.

Tharyn Rhodes was the mother of eleven children: Caelan Oz, Calix Whitaker, Freyael Hammoud, Helian Cates, Jorvik Elmsworth, Nereus Oswald, Nivara Starks, Olyndra Valeska, Ordran Scribner, Pyrra Sills and Thalric Kytarathian Eldranthar.

The Civic Repository is an art museum and public library housed in a library building; it functions as a museum and is operated as a local authority museum.

It is located in the country Cynthera. The institution was established in 1922 and officially closed in 2053.

The building includes visitor facilities, among them an accessible toilet.

The Union of Sovereign Territories and Realms is an international organization established by treaty between governments. It began on 1 January 2024 and is named after Carandor.

The union was founded by Carandor, the Clarity Coalition, Cynthera, Elysium Shores, Krestoria, Mystralyn, Rithoria, Thalassia, Verenthia and Vyrland.

The union comprises the following territories and realms as constituent parts: Altheris, Auralis, Calyptoria, Carandor, Cyndoria, Cynthera, Drakeldoria, Elysium Shores, Isolara, Kaldira, Krestoria, Nephronia, New Providence, Quolmaris Republic, Rithoria, Solandria, Syldoria, Thalassia, Thundralis, Verenthia and Zolterra.

The founders and members are diverse in constitutional form and status.
