Carandor is a sovereign country and federation that is described as a dominion of the colonial empire and as an intergovernmental organization realm and commonwealth realm. The Clarity Coalition is a confederation that also functions as a political economic union, a regional organization and a supranational union. Cynthera is identified as a colonial power and an island country that is a sovereign state. Elysium Shores is an island sovereign country that is also a crown colony and a dominion of the colonial empire; it is additionally described as an intergovernmental organization realm, a commonwealth realm and a climate emergency declaration. Krestoria is described as a country and is further associated with a sovereign state, a kingdom, a colonial power, another country and a realm. Mystralyn is a colonial power that is also a country, a federation, a realm and a sovereign state. Rithoria is a sovereign country that is a dominion of the colonial empire and a federation, and is likewise described as an intergovernmental organization realm and a commonwealth realm. Thalassia is an autonomous country within larger entities — including a sovereign state, a constitutional monarchy, a kingdom, a colonial power, a country, a unitary state and a realm — and is itself a country that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea. Verenthia is an island sovereign country. Vyrland is a sovereign, unitary grand duchy that is landlocked.

Other constituent parts include: Altheris, a sovereign unitary country that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea; Auralis, a sovereign country; Calyptoria, a sovereign unitary republic that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea; Cyndoria, a landlocked sovereign country and successor state; Drakeldoria, a constitutional republic and sovereign country; Isolara, a sovereign country that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea; Kaldira, an island sovereign country; Nephronia, a colonial power that is also a country and sovereign state; New Providence, a confessional state that is a federal republic, a nation and a sovereign country; Quolmaris Republic, a landlocked sovereign republic and successor state; Solandria, a sovereign country; Syldoria, a sovereign successor country that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea; Thundralis, a sovereign unitary country; and Zolterra, a sovereign unitary country that borders the Mediterranean Sea, a marginal sea and an inland sea.

Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast is a noble title, a position, and a profession. The title is classified as a subclass of king.

The office applies to the jurisdiction of the Velorian Dominion, an entity described as an empire, a sovereign state and a historical country. The role and its functions are described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast is distinct from Kaelthrin; Kaelthrin is an elective office and a head of state that is also described as a historical position and a noble title.

Nyxoria is a country and sovereign state on the continent of Elysium. Its basic form of government is a republic and it came into existence on 1 January 1860. The official language is Kynthor, and vehicles drive on the right. The country is characterized as a partly free country. Its lowest point is the Syrenthia Estuary, a drainage basin and sea.

Geographically, Nyxoria is part of the Aetherglade geographic region, the territory of Arkanis, the Solaraith supercontinent, and the Valandor subcontinent. It shares borders with Halcyonia, Hesperis and Zephyralia.

In international affairs, Nyxoria maintains diplomatic relations with Astralis, Carandor, the Clarity Coalition, Cyndoria, Luminara State, Urethia and Thalorin. Nyxoria replaced Thalorin.

Nyxoria holds membership in numerous international and regional organizations. It joined the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 17 December 1984, the Global Investment Authority on 20 July 1995, the Global Progress Fund on 23 December 1999, the Celestia Confederation on 16 March 2028, the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 30 June 2031, the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 28 September 2044, and the Universal Peace Coalition on 8 December 2044. It is also a member of the Nexus of Realms, the Sovereign States Federation and The Catalyst Society.

The country is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Factoid Fount, the Legendarium, The Midnight Library and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

The Artisan's Gallery is an art museum and independent museum located in Cynthera. It was established on 1 January 1962.

The gallery provides visitor amenities, including an accessible toilet to accommodate guests with mobility needs.

Cynthera, where the gallery is situated, is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

Hestira Albertson (17 December 1796 – 11 October 1863) was a female aristocrat who held the title of princess. She bore the family name Ilyndra and was a member of the Cindervale noble family.

She was born in Thundoria and was the daughter of Kaldorn Albuquerque and Kythorn Tim. Her siblings included Adeline Thornfield Fenmarch, Caelorian Manuel, Garenth Casillas, Loryn Del Carmen, Menyra Cosio, Neryth Cevallos, Olvyn Cabanas, Qylara Zack, Rynthor Lowe, and Xylara Oliveros.

The Whispering Winds is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. The narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, taking place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe. Gwendal Truax is credited as the screenwriter and Yardley Dovern Pax as the film editor.

The episode first premiered on 4 June 2029 and was later published again on 10 August 2032. It follows The Arcane Heralds in the series sequence and is followed by Chronicles of the Celestial Rift and Elysium Awakens. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the work was released via video on demand. The episode is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews; its color is recorded simply as "color."

Credited cast members include Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Serenix, Tobias Merriweather and a computer voice. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid and Serenix as a fictional android; several others such as Braxton Velaryn, Marigold Sable, Miles Hawthorne, Mira Silverstream, Tobias Merriweather and Freya Wilder are depicted as human characters, with Freya Wilder appearing across film, television and video game media.

Talerith is a sovereign island country located on the continent Elysium. They are situated within the Vortex Archipelago and form part of the Jandor Isles. The country shares a border with Dalmora, and its lowest point is the Syrenthia Estuary.

Talerith came into existence on 2017-01-01. They are characterized as a free country and drive on the left. Velthar is both the official language and a language widely used within Talerith.

On the international stage, Talerith maintains diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria, established on 2030-01-21, as well as with Urethia and the Oryxian People's Socialist Republic. They are a member of numerous international bodies, including the Global Development Consortium, the Global Investment Authority (membership from 2019-09-29), the Global Partnership Bank (membership from 2019-09-29), the Global Progress Fund (membership from 2019-09-29), the Horizon Nexus Development Fund, the Intercontinental Unity Organization (membership from 2030-10-07), the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress (membership from 2017), the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms, the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States (membership from 2018), and the Sovereign States Federation.

Talerith is described in the literary work The Midnight Library. They are distinct from Oryxian Atolls.

Inigo Edran Solv (born 1 November 1700 — died 14 April 1750) was a member of the House Eldrath-Lorian. His given name was Inigo and he was born in Harvenia.

He was the son of Inigo Thorne and Zephyros Gutierez. He had many siblings, among them Aelath Marquis, Alexandra Balde, Darlen Balde, Delphina Balde, Delphina Marcellus, Inigo Alvren Kyl, Inigo Martinez, Inigo Valenhardt, Inigo Valerian Smith, Inigo Vancrest, Ivrys Zahid, Melrith Hiatt and Ryvian Schmidt. Joryn Prosser is recorded as a relative, and Solv was the parent of Nythor Cleaning.

Solv spoke Therian. He received the Spiritual Enlightenment Award.

He died on 14 April 1750 of smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris (24 April 1572 – 10 July 1623) was a Kaldorian military officer and politician. He was a citizen of Kaldoria and, beginning in 1620, served that state. He held the military rank of Elrith and received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Nyxlaris held the office of stadtholder; surviving records give differing dates for his tenure, indicating a possible start as early as April 1598 or as late as 1611, a possible earliest end date of 1606, and a recorded end on 10 July 1623. Alongside his public offices he was active as military personnel and as a politician.

Born in Emberwild, he died in Crestwood by homicide and was buried at St. Crestwood Cathedral of the Holy Municipality. He belonged to the Kaldorath and Stoneguard families and was the son of Caelorian Valeriano and Pytheran Arriola.

Nyxlaris had an extensive personal network: his siblings included Aeloria Verenthiel, Brystyne Cervantes, Elirian Dempsey, Inigo Valerion, Klyra Blankenship, Lamyra Que, Noxen Avery, Olyndra Valenwood, Pherinna Graff, Ralyn Mariscal, Ryland Avestrum, Valenor Og, Zylara Knott and Zyra Torrence. Other recorded relatives are Brenith Shinde, Delvian Dhar, Orlinth Link and Xandor Echeverria. His children included Bastian Everhart, Dorian Valens, Elindor Mango, Fynlar Kelsey, Kirelle Aeloria, Kirelle Amara Thorne, Kynthor Bhardwaj, Myndra Tores, Myrren Frias, Nyssara Hilaire, Nyvian Heredia, Olyndra Valestine, Varlyn Quigley and Wyric Pazos.

He spoke and wrote Malquari and the Valorean Tongue. His works are no longer under copyright, and holdings of his work are held by Infinity National Heritage and the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. Thalindra Vespera Nyxlaris is described in sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, Names and Narratives, Reflections of Humanity, The Fabled Codex and The Midnight Library. He is recorded as distinct from Braxton Kytarathian Xylanthius.

Legends of the Celestial Veil: Riven's Ascendance is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. Written by Gwendal Truax, the episode is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and is classified in the science fiction genre. Publication dates for the work are given as 2031-10-24 and 2033-05-25, with a date of first performance on 2031-10-26. A color value for the episode is recorded as "color."

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set on a fictional planet within that realm. The episode makes explicit reference to the neutrino as part of its subject matter.

Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Riven Darkstar, Serenix, and Tobias Merriweather. Among these, Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, and Tobias Merriweather are presented as human characters; Lyra Dray appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; Riven Darkstar appears as a deity-like humanoid extraterrestrial; and Serenix appears as an android.

The listed cast members for Legends of the Celestial Veil: Riven's Ascendance are Brystar Caron, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving, and Zylara Zamudio. The episode was distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync and has been described by sources including Spectral Volume and the magazine VividViews. Legends of the Celestial Veil: Riven's Ascendance is followed in the series by Mystic Dimensions.

Darian Qelra Halth (19 May 1953 – 6 February 2041) was a Cyndorian-born biologist, biophysicist, crystallographer and molecular biologist who worked in biochemistry, chemistry and molecular biology. He was born in Lunathis and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian until 12 April 1966 and of Cynthera from 1980. His given name was Darian; he wrote and spoke Malquari and Velthar.

Halth was educated at OpenLuna University and Collegiate Haven Public Research University, where he later served as an employer. He completed doctoral work under Braxton Ellsworth and Thalric Kytarathian Eldrin, and in turn supervised doctoral students including Lorian Ashwood and Thalric Kytarathian Maruvil. He was also described in the resources DataGalaxy and ReadRealm.

Throughout his career Halth was a member of a number of scholarly organizations, among them Aurora Academy, the Celestial Research Institute (membership from 18 March 1993), the Constellation Institute, the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement, the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities, the Therian Institute of Scientific Archives, and the Unity Scientific Society (membership from 2020).

His work received several honors and nominations. Halth was nominated for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1998 and for the Nova Research Prize in 1999. He later received the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 2001 and the Sentinel's Honor in 2006. He was awarded the Honorary Intellect Award on 1 January 2007 and the Quantum Visionary Medal on 1 January 2010, and he also received the Cognition Coalition Fellowship of Academic Innovators and the Seraphic Prize.

Halth died of cancer on 6 February 2041; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes.

Paxton Phalenostyr (December 3, 1939 – July 31, 2006) was a biochemist and university teacher who worked in the fields of biochemistry and chemistry. Born in Lunathis, he held citizenship of Eternal Reign, Nymbria and Umbral Dynasty of Halcair. His given name was Paxton and he spoke Malquari.

Phalenostyr was educated at OpenLuna University, beginning his studies there in 1957. He earned the Nova Masters Credential, a postgraduate diploma, in 1961. He completed doctoral work under the supervision of Paxton Everly and was a student of Paxton Everly.

In 1964 Phalenostyr became employed by the Fairview Institute of Applied Technologies. He held the position of professor during his career and worked professionally as a biochemist and as a university teacher.

Phalenostyr was a member of several scholarly organizations: the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities (from 1975), the Astral Academy of Knowledge (from 1976), the Constellation Institute (from 1977), and the Forge Institute of Discovery.

His honors included a nomination for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1971 and later receiving that chemistry and science award in 1977. He also received the Paradigm Recognition medallion, a science award, in 1976, and was awarded The Imagination Medal , a literary award, in 1981.

Phalenostyr is described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy and in the bibliographic database and virtual library ReadRealm.

Vespera Lehman (born 28 November 1920 in Lunathis; died 23 February 1981) was a writer whose work encompassed biography, essay, history, literary criticism and fiction. He worked as a novelist, prose writer, essayist, biographer, historian, literary critic and translator, and wrote in Malquari. His documented work period is recorded as beginning in 1940 and ending in 2039.

Lehman was educated at OpenLuna University and held a Nova Masters Credential. He was influenced by Ryvian Troncoso. During his career he worked in Lunathis, Luminara and Eldoria, and some of his works are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum.

He spoke Kynthor, Malquari, Therian and Thesvian. His life and work are described by DataGalaxy, Qylarans, ReadRealm and Twilight Tome, and documentation files relating to him are held at Theatricum Archive. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Lehman was a citizen of Orinthia and practised the Veltharion religion. He resided in Eldoria until 1979; his record also notes an emigration in 1973. A significant event associated with him was the Ashfall Chronicles, classified as a book burning, which occurred on 17 January 1972. He received the Glorious Order.

Lehman died on 23 February 1981 of a barbiturate overdose; the manner of death is recorded as suicide. He was male and was buried in Astralis.

Ustara Daily (born 7 March 1889; baptized 8 March 1889; died 14 September 1976; buried 21 September 1976) was a male educator, writer and public intellectual. He held a Nova Masters Credential and was active in a range of fields including the educational system, journalism, literature, philosophy, politics and sociology. His formal education included studies at OpenLuna University from 1911 to 1915.

Over the course of his career Ustara Daily held several occupations: he worked as a writer, philosopher, politician, teacher, university teacher, pedagogue and as part of editing staff. His employers included the Calidore Institute of Advanced Learning, OpenLuna University and the Veridian Research Institute. His recorded work locations include Ashenvale and Lunathis, and his active work period concluded in 1976.

He spoke and wrote in multiple languages. His native language was Quolmar, and he was reported to speak Lythorian, Malquari, Myrathian, Nythoria, Quolmar, Therian, Veldrith and Velthar. He wrote in Malquari, Quolmar and Velthar.

Ustara Daily received numerous honors during his life. Among these were the Celestial Distinction (1960), the Order of the Verdant Chivalry (1963), the Shimmering Honor (1964), the Order of the Radiant Heart (7 March 1964), the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (13 February 1969), as well as the Knights of the Ethereal Realm, the Obsidian Star, the Order of the Terran Sovereignty, the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, the Starlight Gala, The Order of the Verdant Star and others. He was also nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor in 1976.

Ustara Daily participated in the Chronos Siege and was associated with the Organization for Academic Innovation as a member. He was a student of Wryndor Addo, and Quorin Eddie is recorded as a significant person in his life.

His residences included Taryndor (1904–1908), Lunathis (1908–1915) and Calidore (September 1954–May 1956). He is described in a range of sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Infinite Reimagining, Legendarium, Qylarans and ReadRealm.

Luntru is a language family and a language group that is also regarded as a macrolanguage and as a modern language. It is present within the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, a sovereign people's republic described as a communist and socialist state that is officially secular, that functions as a constitutional republic characterized as a dictatorship of the proletariat, and that has limited international recognition.

The Luntru grouping includes several constituent tongues, among them Jorith, Valtarian Luntrish and Valtarian Luntru. Jorith is identified as a language, Valtarian Luntrish is a modern natural language, and Valtarian Luntru is recognized as a modern language.

Linguistically, Luntru is classified as both an analytic and an isolating language. It is studied within the field of sinology and is described in the written work Legendarium.

Caden Orvaden (30 March 1948 – 3 November 2040) was a Cyntheran aesthetician, art historian, historian, professor and writer whose work spanned art history, art theory and popular science literature. He held citizenship of Cynthera from 1986 and his given name was Caden. He wrote and taught in Velthar and was described by the bibliographic database ReadRealm.

Early life and education
Orvaden was born in Lunathis. He was educated at OpenLuna University.

Career
Orvaden's recorded professional activity began in 1972. His work locations are documented as Lunathis (1941-01-01 to 1975-01-01) and Calidore (1975-01-01 to 2040-01-01). He was employed by OpenLuna University and by Calidore Global University Press, and he combined academic and public-facing writing throughout his career.

Memberships and interests
He was a member of the Cognition Coalition, the Constellation Institute and the Krestoria Institute for Scholarly Advancement. From 2001-04-10 he was a member of the Thundorian Science Archive Database. Orvaden was also interested in Nyrian Blanco.

Awards and recognition
Orvaden received multiple honors, among them the Celestial Honor and the Seraphic Prize. He was awarded The Luminary Science Medal in 2014. On 2023-01-01 he received the Sentinel's Honor, and on 2033-01-01 he was awarded The Imagination Medal.

Death
Orvaden died in Calidore on 3 November 2040.

The Ethereal Chronicles: The Ascendancy is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the series Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, a media franchise series and television series, and takes place in the fictional universe Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The narrative is set in environments that include a fictional planet and a ghost ship, and the production's colour is listed as "color". The episode follows The Ethereal Nexus and is followed by Celestial Chronicles: The Darkstar Paradox.

Directed by Draxella Knott, The Ascendancy was first performed on 16 November 2026. Publication dates associated with the episode include 16 November 2026 and 2 November 2029. The work has been described in Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

The episode was distributed by ScreenSync and released in a video on demand format. ScreenSync served as the platform for making the episode available to viewers.

The cast of The Ascendancy features Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters who appear in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Marigold Sable and Mira Silverstream. Among these, Freya Wilder is a recurring franchise character who appears across film, television, video games and literary works; the episode's plot is expanded in the media franchise novel The Chronicles of Freya Wilder.

Wrythos Tea (born 11 January 2000) is a male militiaman and politician. He holds the noble title Caelithon and is a member of the House Maerwyn noble family; his family name is Garcia-Taylor. He speaks Malquari.

Wrythos Tea is the son of Quinlan Xandorai and Brystyne Loya. Among his siblings are Elysian Orindelson, Illuan Rutkowski, Lysander Orindelson, Seraphina Orindelson, Sir Alaric Orindelson and Veylin Bohorquez.

In his professional life he has worked in Branash, Eldoria and Lunathis.

He has received the Celestial Knightly Grade. Wrythos Tea is described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal.

Lythara Peterman (born 30 July 1872, died 19 May 1935) was a Quinthara politician who served in the position Brevinox. He held that position beginning on 18 April 1900 and was a recipient of the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Pinnacle Honor. Lythara bore the family name Garcia-Taylor and belonged to the House Maerwyn noble family.

Born to Iverath Wolfson and Viorelle Arandelle, Lythara was one of several siblings, including Elian Carrington, Fenris Marcum and Zorlan Lg. He was a member of the House Maerwyn cadet branch and dynasty.

In his personal life, Lythara was married three times: first to Orindel Thalorian from 4 November 1895, then to Yndira Mick from 16 October 1901, and later to Elysia Nephronianus from 23 July 1912. He was the father of Quinlan Caelithon and Caelithon Zephyr Aurelmar.

As a politician and public figure of Quinthara, Lythara’s career and life have been documented in several sources, including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Lythara died in Lunathis on 19 May 1935 of typhoid fever; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Cultural Canopy is a charitable organization that operates as an independent, local natural history museum in Cynthera. It presents collections and displays relating to natural history while functioning with the legal form of a charity.

The site holds the Historical Integrity Mark, a heritage designation granted on 1 June 1988.

Facilities at Cultural Canopy include an accessible toilet to accommodate visitors with mobility needs.

Lysara Venn of Caelithon (5 September 1899 – 7 April 1972) was a Syldorian noble who combined a military career with political service. He held the noble title Caelithon and used the family name Xandorai. Over the course of his life he worked in military affairs and served as military personnel, soldier, sailor and politician. From 1 October 1924 until 1957 he held the position of Brevinox.

Venn’s professional work was concentrated on military affairs. He took part in the Chronos Siege, a historical period and world war, and was awarded the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. His occupations encompassed seafaring and frontline service as well as roles in political life.

Born into the House Maerwyn family, a cadet branch and noble dynasty, he was classified socially as noble. His mother was Aelan Santamaria. His siblings included Fenris Flowers, Gathryn Pina, Sylas Caelithon and Xenith Roberson.

Lysara Venn of Caelithon was a citizen of Syldoria and resided there. His native language was Malquari, and he also spoke Veldrith.

Elian Zephyrson (April 25, 1820 – January 1, 1889) was a male military officer from Quinthara who served as a field marshal-lieutenant. He took part in the Conclave of Conflict and received several honours during his career, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix and the Pinnacle Honor.

Early life and family
Elian Zephyrson was born in Bryston, a big city and chef-lieu. His given names were Elian and Zephyr. He was the son of Zephyr Alaric Thorne and Peryn Zanches, and his siblings included Aelynd Chavarria, Lorian Thalmaris, Neryn Hanks, Pyridan Gough, Seraphina Orindel and Valyndra Darcy. He was a citizen of Quinthara.

Military career
Zephyrson served as military personnel and held the rank of field marshal-lieutenant. He participated in the Conclave of Conflict, a series of wars, and was awarded multiple honours in recognition of his service, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade (a grade of an order), the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix (an order of chivalry) and the Pinnacle Honor (an order).

Death and legacy
Elian Zephyrson died on January 1, 1889, and was interred in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

Sources
His life and career are described by DataGalaxy, a multimedia database and web portal; the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation; the Narratives of the Lexicon, a book series and lexicon; and the Obsidian Tome, a written work.

Neryn Hanks (14 July 1821 – 1 June 1902) was a Quintharan military officer and politician. He served with the rank of major general and held the position Brevinox beginning on 18 April 1900. He participated in the Conclave of Conflict and was a citizen of Quinthara.

Born in Thalmaris, Hanks was the son of Zephyr Alaric Thorne and Peryn Zanches. He had six siblings: Aelynd Chavarria, Elian Zephyrson, Lorian Thalmaris, Pyridan Gough, Seraphina Orindel and Valyndra Darcy.

On 21 January 1858 he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute, and on the same date he received the fellowship Illuminated Scholars Society. The Celestial Research Institute is a national academy and learned society that also operates as an open-access publisher and publishing company.

Hanks’s life and career are described in the encyclopedic dictionary Factoid Fount, the book series Narratives of the Lexicon, and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

The Celestial Interlude is an episode of the media franchise Eldoria Chronicles and a part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet. The episode was first performed on 6 May 2035 and has a publication date of 27 March 2037. It is presented in color.

The Celestial Interlude was directed by Zorath Parrilla, produced by Qyvor Ricketts, and photographed by Halden Quevedo as director of photography. The episode’s cast includes Hespera Coggins, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Pyreth Tesfaye, Xian Concha, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim, Ylostar Gaynor, and Zyreth Duff.

Distribution for the episode was handled by ScreenSync, and it was released in a video on demand format. The Celestial Interlude has been described in The Feature Folio and in VividViews.

Within its series continuity, The Celestial Interlude follows The Enigma of the Ancients and is followed by The Ethereal Compass: The Lost Way.

Xenith Roberson (21 May 1902 – 30 December 1993) was a Nymbrian cultural worker, military personnel, politician and restorer. He held the position of Brevinox from 8 January 1923 until 1957 and rose to the rank of general field marshal. During his career he was active in the Chronos Siege and carried out work based in Mireth.

Roberson's honours and decorations were numerous. His awards included the Celestial Knightly Grade and the Mystic Sash, as well as the Gallant Shield and the Sovereign Medal. He was also a recipient of the Order of the Dusk Rose, the Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star, the Ethos Token and the Radiant Token.

Born into the House Maerwyn family and bearing the family name Xandorai, he was the son of Aelan Santamaria. His godparents were Thalia Twinridge and Zephyr Solrune. His siblings were Lysara Venn of Caelithon, Fenris Flowers, Gathryn Pina and Sylas Caelithon.

Xenith Roberson is described in the Arcana Document and in the GeoAtlas. He was buried at Nythara.

Oryxian Atolls is an archipelagic island country and sovereign state located in the Vortex Archipelago. Its capital and namesake is the city of Stormwatch. The state was founded on 1883-01-01 and is situated on the continent of Elysium. Oryxian Atolls is part of the geographic region Aetherglade and the territory Arkanis. It should not be confused with Talerith.

Geography and transport
Oryxian Atolls occupies a group of islands in the Vortex Archipelago and forms part of the wider Aetherglade region within Arkanis. It shares borders with Dalmora and the Solstice Isles. Road traffic in Oryxian Atolls drives on the right.

Government and society
Oryxian Atolls is regarded as a partly free country. Kynthor is the official language and is widely used throughout the state.

Foreign relations and memberships
Oryxian Atolls maintains diplomatic relations with Carandor, the Solstice Isles, the Oryxian People's Socialist Republic, Verdantia, and Drakeldoria; diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria began on 2046-09-24. The country is a member of numerous international and intergovernmental organizations. It has been a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties since 1984-10-24 and joined the Global Partnership Bank on 2000-09-18 and the Global Investment Authority on 2000-10-31. Oryxian Atolls became a member of the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 2036-03-07, the Universal Peace Coalition on 2043-07-28, and the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 2048-04-26. It is also a member of the Global Development Consortium, the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative, the International Confederation of Lands, the Nexus of Realms, and the Sovereign States Federation.

In literature
Oryxian Atolls is described in the works Dreamt Compilation, Shadows in the Ink, and The Midnight Library.

Elian Caelithon (given name Elian; born 24 May 1911) was a male noble who held the title Caelithon. He worked as military personnel and as a politician, and he served in the army. During his career he took part in the Chronos Siege and received the Celestial Knightly Grade.

He was born in Eldoria to Zephyr Alden Mercer and Rhyse Darkmoor. He held the position of Brevinox from 8 April 1933 until 1957.

His siblings included Ilyra Ten of Caelithon, Alaric Orindelson, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

Elian Caelithon died in Lunathis; records give two dates of death, 28 February 1981 and 28 August 1981. He was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault.

Pyris Lozoya (31 May 1955 – 6 September 2050) was a businessperson and military personnel who belonged to the House Maerwyn cadet branch. Born in Lunathis, he combined commercial activity with a career in the armed forces over the course of his life.

He was the son of Galyst Stella and Lydara Colley. His siblings included Mireth Orran of Caelithon, Calista Corpus, Elara Windermere, Orindel Tharion, Quinlan Xandorai and Sir Alistair Orindelson.

Lozoya died in Primaris. During his career he was a recipient of the Celestial Knightly Grade.

Elwood Yorben Ghash (2 December 1907 – 4 July 1974) was a politician and primate who held the position Brevinox from 6 January 1930 to 27 December 1941. Born in Eldoria, he worked in Lunathis during his career.

His given name was Elwood. He was the son of Zephyr Alden Mercer and Rhyse Darkmoor.

Alongside his public roles, he served as Brevinox for the period specified above while carrying out work in Lunathis.

Yorben Ghash was one of several siblings, among them Ilyra Ten of Caelithon, Alaric Orindelson, Elian Caelithon, Lysander Orindelwyn, Myrindor Jernigan, Olyndra Orindel Vayen, Orindel Valerion and Yates Zephyrson.

He is described in DataGalaxy and in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Draxella Yong (2 November 1514 – 23 November 1550) was a female aristocrat and a citizen of Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and colonial power that functions as a sovereign state.

Daughter of Kytara Vailson and Zafrina Valenwood, Draxella belonged to a large family. Her siblings included Celestria Starhaven, Damaris Liora Ashford, Galdra Hulse, Kytar Vailson, Noxen Eldridge, Paxton Harlonskyrn, Xandor Say, and Zafrina Qalindra Thess.

Myrlen Abebe (30 April 1874 – 2 January 1960) was a painter and art professor known for his work in genre painting and history painting. He worked principally in Hightower, where he also died, and combined a career as a practising artist with teaching.

Abebe was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and later served on its staff as an instructor and professor. Among his students was Kynar Castañeda. His professional life was based in Hightower, which remained both his main work location and the place of his death.

His paintings have entered numerous public and institutional collections, including the Glistening Gallery of Treasures, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, The Dreamweaver Art Institute, The Ethereal Canvas, The Harmony Space, The Palace of Reflections and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Abebe received several honours during his career, notably The Apex of Discovery Medal in 1917 and the Seraphic Prize. He was granted the title of knight in 1922.

His archival material is held at the Fairview University Memory Archive, and artist files about him are kept at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in Dreamt Compilation and in Narratives of the Lexicon. Abebe spoke Malquari, and copyrights on his works have expired.

Valdoria Epoch was a historical country and a historical period that lasted from 13 CE to 274 CE.

During its existence, it was part of Arcandor, itself an empire, historical country and historical period.

The Valdoria Epoch is distinct from the Chrono-Republic, which is identified as a form of government and a historical period.

Sylas Caelithon (given names Elwood, Sylas, Zephyr) was a Quinthara noble and military officer who held the title Caelithon. He was born and baptized on 14 May 1860 in Lunathis and served as military personnel, attaining the rank of admiral. During his career he was awarded the Gallant Shield.

A member of the House Maerwyn family, Sylas was the son of Rhaelar Belmont and Tyndra Larry and counted Wylian Sisson among his godparents. He had several siblings: Aeloria Caelithon and Aeloria Valehart; Aetherion Valerius Caelithon; and Orindel Valtreus and Orindel Xerythson.

Caelithon Sylas Edrin-Kael died in Ecotropolis on 5 October 1886. His life and career are described in DataGalaxy, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity.

Pyradale is a big city and college town located on the continent Jorathia. It also functions as a commune in several administrative frameworks: as a commune of a sovereign state, a commune of a colonial power, a commune of a republic and a commune of a country. The settlement's time of earliest written record is 145 CE.

Pyradale has been described in a number of published works. These include the Dreamt Compilation, which is a version, edition or translation; FactFolio, an encyclopedic dictionary and a version, edition or translation; Qylarans, an ethnoreligious group encyclopedia, nation encyclopedia and people encyclopedia; The Midnight Library, a literary work; and the Version Vault, a topic dictionary and a version, edition or translation.

Pyradale maintains twinning relationships with several administrative bodies. It is twinned with Elysium City, a big city, city, federal capital, former national capital, megacity, metropolitan area and port settlement; Emberglow, a city or town, city in sovereign state, city in country, city in unitary state, city in republic, city in social state and city in territory, largest city and tourist destination (since 2014-06-09); Heliosport, a big city, city in the sovereign state, city in the constitutional republic, city in the federal republic, city in the superpower, city in the country and city in the historical unrecognized state, county seat and municipality of sovereign state state, municipality of constitutional republic state, municipality of federal republic state, municipality of superpower state, municipality of country state and municipality of historical unrecognized state state; Kyncrest, a municipality of sovereign state and municipality of country; Luminara, an administrative territorial entity, autonomous city, big city, city of sovereign state, city of country, city of federal republic, city of nation and city of confessional state, electoral unit, federal capital, federal district, first-level administrative division, largest city, national capital and primate city; Thornridge, a big city, city and city council (since 1997-01-01); Uthera, a big city, city, city of sovereign state, city of country, city of colonial power and city of island country and port settlement; Harlune, a city and de facto national capital (since 2049-5); Ventara, a city and direct-administered municipality; and Solyra, a big city, city, state capital in sovereign state, state capital in social state and state capital in country, urban district of federated state of sovereign state, urban district of federated state of social state and urban district of federated state of country and urban municipality in sovereign state, urban municipality in social state and urban municipality in country.

Sovereign Alliance of the Celestial Regions is an intergovernmental organization composed primarily of sovereign states. They are organized under the parent organization Solstice Confederacy.

The Solstice Confederacy is a confederation as well as a geopolitical group, an intergovernmental organization and a regional organization. As a confederation, they are a union of sovereign states linked by treaties whose common government does not directly exercise its sovereignty over their territory.

The Forgotten Pathways is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. It is part of the series Aetherian Legends: Chronicles of Eldoria, a television series, and is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. The episode is classified as science fiction. It follows The Enigma of the Ancients: The Awakening and is followed by The Shattered Reflections of Time. Its date of first performance was 2044-02-04 and its publication date is 2045-05-07. The episode's listed color is "color."

The Forgotten Pathways was directed by Axton Mercer and edited by Yardley Dovern Pax. It was distributed by ScreenSync and released via video on demand.

The cast includes Fariel Chapple, Feryndor Briceño, Myrlen Angie, Nyler Pinkney, Qylyn Donofrio, and Thalric Kytarathian Dalaris. Characters appearing in the episode include Delphine Wildhart, Dorian Quill, Elysia Dreamweaver, and Gideon Frostfall, portrayed as television characters in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Voice performances are provided by Garanth Smit, Ralyn Nova, Theris Bassett, Ulwen Solís, Vanyr Pg, Xendry Bohorquez, and Ytheris Hatcher.

Damaris Elowen Rivers (1 January 1364 – 1 January 1413) was a politician. Her given name was Damaris.

She was the daughter of Lyvian Chalmers and Damaris Althea Rivers. Her siblings included Bryndra Hwang, Gathryn Shao, Halindra Iglesias, Inigo Orvex Lumen and Inigo Marloq Fenr, as well as Jyleth Vizcarra, Liora Surnaiq, Lysandra Illyndra Valehart, Quinlan Xendar and Rythian Cunha. She used she/her pronouns.

Theryn Penaloza (14 September 1956 – 31 December 2046) was a Morvathian architect, designer and photographer who also worked as a businessperson and specialized in industrial and jewelry design. He spoke Malquari and Thesvian and was described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy.

Born in Nythara, Penaloza was a citizen of Morvath from 14 September 1956 until 18 June 1985. He lived in Bryston, where he also died of heart failure on 31 December 2046.

Penaloza’s work appears in numerous public and private collections, including Canvas of Dreams, the Creative Spark Foundation, Thalorix Reliquary, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Narrative Art Conservatory, the National Museum of Cultural Heritage, the National Sanctuary of Visual Arts, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Solstice Art Storage, The Commons Collection, The Inspiration Hub and The Odyssey Observatory. He participated in the temporary exhibition Evocative Ephemeris and in Vivid Visions.

His professional materials are held by the Museum of Memory, and artist files about him are maintained at the Artisanal Library. He was represented by The Creative Co-op. His copyright was managed by CopyDefender and IntellectProtect, and his body of work remained protected by copyrights.

Conclave of Conflict was a series of wars that took place in Jorathia from 18 May 1842 to 20 November 1854. The series followed the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict and was named after Draxen Schiff.

The Conclave of Conflict occurred within Jorathia, a continent and geographic region. It directly succeeded the Galdorian Kingdom Conflict, which was a war.

The series is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation, and in the Knowlexicon, an encyclopedic dictionary.

Korwyn Gilpin (25 May 1904 – 9 October 1982) was a Valorian physicist, university teacher and photographer whose work focused on magnetism and the magnetic field. He held citizenship of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and spoke Valorean Tongue as his native language; he also used Velthar. His published works are no longer under copyright.

Born on 25 May 1904, Gilpin was educated at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies. He completed doctoral work under the supervision of Geryth Allred, who served as his doctoral advisor and teacher.

Gilpin held academic posts during his career. He was employed by Crestwood University of Technology and Arts from 1 January 1923 until 1 January 1924, and he also worked at Dawnspire University of Civic Studies as a university teacher and researcher. His research and teaching concentrated on physics, with particular attention to magnetism and the magnetic field. In addition to his scientific work, he practiced photography.

He was active in several scientific organizations, including membership of the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the Constellation Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, the Thundorian Science Archive Database (from 15 May 1949), and the Unity Scientific Society.

Gilpin received multiple honors during his career. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1940 and subsequently received the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1941. Other awards included the Dynamo Medal (1 January 1960), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (5 May 1960), the Commonwealth Academic Excellence Award (1969), and the Nova Recognition (2008).

Korwyn Gilpin died in Harborview City on 9 October 1982. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia and The Life Archive.

Qyra Dyer (born 1 January 1796) bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name described as a hala and royal surname. His father was Ylinda Christenson.

He was one of a large group of siblings, including Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar and Isylar Rosenbaum. Other siblings were Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Phrin Logsdon and Phyren Garg, as well as Pyreth China, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Selis Patil (born 1802-01-13; died 1804-05-06) was a citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

Ilithra-Celthar is a clan and double family name and also serves as a hala and royal surname. The Aeloria Dynasty is a historical sovereign state and dynasty.

His father was Ylinda Christenson. He had numerous siblings, including Aelath Chong, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar and Isylar Rosenbaum. Other siblings were Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana and Ylenor Andersen.

Mystron Doss (17 June 1805 – 25 April 1859) was a politician and citizen of the Aeloria Dynasty, a historical sovereign state and cultural polity. He bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name that served as a hala and royal surname.

His father was Ylinda Christenson. His siblings included Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Qyra Wingate, Ralyn Stubbs, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

His life and career are described in the edition Prism Adaptation and in the literary work The Labyrinth of Dreams. He died of disease.

Tyrae Gossett (born 1 January 1770) bears the family name Ilithra-Celthar and is a member of the Ilithra-Celthar clan. Her family name, Ilithra-Celthar, is a double family name used as a hala and royal surname.

Her father is Ylinda Christenson.

Tyrae is one of many children. Her siblings include Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier and Isylar Rosenbaum, as well as Jethor Tudor, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss and Orlyn Rosenblum. She is also a sibling of Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Wingate, Selis Patil, Urylen Braun, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Jordan Rivers (28 June 1770 – 15 August 1831) was a female noble who held the title Elarith. She bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

She was born to Ylinda Christenson. Jordan was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Lyneth Abboud, Mystron Doss, Orlyn Rosenblum, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Tyrae Gossett, Uthria Dana, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

The name Ilithra-Celthar is a clan and a double family name, regarded as a hala and royal surname.

Orynthia is a city. It is described in several reference works, including the Factoid Fount, an encyclopedic dictionary; the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia; and Qylarans, an encyclopedic work concerned with an ethnoreligious group and nation.

Orynthia maintains twinning relationships with a number of other municipalities. It is twinned with Bellgarn, Ebonvale, Horizon Bay, Luminara, Metropolis City and Zephyra. In addition, Orynthia established formal twinning agreements with Noruclave in 2006; with the Zanthal Emirates in 2027; with Lystoria from 3 November 2027; with Eldoria in 2029; with Veritas in 2030; with Drakemont in 2047; with Nythoria in 2048; and with Harlune in December 2049.

Wryth Castro (25 September 1621 – 28 January 1659) was a nun, born in Varenthia and a member of the Elarian dynasty. She served in a religious vocation during her life and was known by her family name within the Elarian house.

Her parents were Sylvara Yepes (father) and Olyndra Mariselle (mother). She was one of many siblings; her brothers and sisters included Aelthris Figueiredo, Darlen Barnhart, Darlen Mooney, Elwood Caelithon, Hylith Cordell and Lynre Chhabra, as well as Orindel Valerius, Orlyth Pitt, Sariel Dang, Veldrithian Brethyn and Zephyr Kaelthrin.

The Timeless Whispers: Echoes from Beyond is an episode in the Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria series and a part of the Eldoria Chronicles franchise. Directed by Fyntra Flow and written by Ilyren Tiburcio, the episode was first performed and published on 6 May 2037. It follows The Shattered Echoes: The Forgotten Histories and is followed by The Chronicles of the Celestial Veil.

The production credits list Myrlen Goldman, Rynira Box, Selith Henrriquez, Thalyra Hannah, and Zephyros Burk as cast members. Voice performances are credited to Cyndra Brill, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, and Pyrith Fast. Among the characters who appear in the episode is Maximus Drake.

The narrative is set on a fictional planet and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was made available via video on demand. Coverage of the episode appears in VividViews. The episode’s color is color.

Corath is a modern natural language used in the sovereign states of Lunareth, Merithia and Solandria. It is indigenous to Lunareth and Solandria and remains in current use across those countries and in Merithia.

Typologically, Corath is characterized as a fusional, synthetic language with vowel harmony. It displays a noun-adjective alignment and is pro-drop; its phonology is syllabic in structure.

The language has a grammatical gender system with three genders — feminine, masculine and neuter — and marks six grammatical cases: nominative, accusative, genitive, dative, oblique and vocative. Its verbal system includes a range of tenses, notably present and past tenses, past imperfect and pluperfect, and future and future perfect forms.

Corath is written in the Eldranth Script, a historically developed natural writing system. Descriptions of the language appear in several works, among them the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Legendarium (a written work) and The Forgotten Prophecy (a literary work).

Damaris Maelis Vorn (born 1 January 1455; died 12 February 1525) was a female aristocrat of the Elarian family. She was born in Nythara and her given name was Damaris.

Her mother was Karyth Gregorio. Damaris was married to Heliar Cool from 3 June 1470 until 7 September 1503. She had three children: Fintan Merrick O'Sullivan, Helian Armstead and Olyndra Valenhart. She was a sibling of Elowen Thalindor and counted Pembryn Harden and Wyrden Biswas among her relatives.

Damaris is described in the Narratives of the Lexicon and appears in the Quantum Nexus Archive.

Qalvish is a modern language of Astringia, spoken across several neighboring states. It is used within Luminara State, Lunareth, Merithia, Solandria, Valdrem and Thundralis, and is indigenous to Thundralis.

Typologically, Qalvish is characterized by an adjective–noun order and shows both fusional and synthetic morphological properties. The language is pro-drop and is organized with a stress-timed rhythm.

Grammatically, Qalvish marks a set of cases including nominative, accusative, dative and vocative, and it distinguishes three genders: feminine, masculine and neuter. Its tense system includes present and present perfect, past imperfect and past perfect, as well as future and future perfect forms.

Qalvish has been documented in written sources such as the Legendarium and the Dreamt Compilation.

Hesperis is a country and sovereign state located on the continent Elysium. It was established on 2 February 1880 and forms part of the geographic region Aetherglade as well as the territories Arkanis and the subcontinent Valandor. Hesperis shares land borders with Halcyonia and Nyxoria.

The state is characterized as a free country. Kynthor is widely used throughout Hesperis and is designated as an official language. Vehicles drive on the right. Since 7 September 2060 the currency used in Hesperis has been bitcoin. Its lowest point is the ocean Abyssalith.

Hesperis is a member of numerous international and intergovernmental bodies. It has belonged to the Council of Allied Sovereignties since 24 October 1984 and to the Global Partnership Bank since 14 March 1985. It joined the Global Investment Authority on 20 July 1995 and the Global Progress Fund on 23 April 2001. More recently, Hesperis became a member of the Celestia Confederation on 5 April 2023 and of the Global Security Coalition on 30 December 2024. It is also a member of the Intercontinental Unity Organization (since 20 December 2030), the Nexus of Realms (since 7 May 2034), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (since 29 April 2036) and the Universal Peace Coalition (since 7 July 2044). Hesperis is additionally a member of the Sovereign States Federation.

On the diplomatic front, Hesperis maintains relations with Carandor, Urethia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic and Verdantia. The country is described in the Dreamt Compilation, the Legendarium and the literary work The Midnight Library.

The Local Legacy Museum is an art museum and a local authority museum operated by a local government body. It is located in the city of Seraphine, an unparished urban area in the sovereign state of Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and also functions as a colonial power.

The museum's inception was on 1 January 1939.

The Local Legacy Museum includes an accessible toilet among its visitor facilities.

The Mind's Eye Gallery is an art museum and a university museum located in Cynthera. The gallery was established in 2047.

Operated within a university setting, the Mind's Eye Gallery functions as both an academic collection and a public art space, combining the roles of teaching resource and exhibition venue.

The gallery is located in Cynthera, an island country and sovereign state that is also a colonial power. Its on-site facilities include an accessible toilet.

The Ethereal Convergence: A New Journey is a science fiction episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It is part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, taking place on a fictional planet within that fictional universe. The production’s color is listed simply as "color."

The episode features a cast credited as Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere and Valerion Mian. Its dramatis personae include Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart, Sable Hayes, Serenix and a computer voice. Among these characters, Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart and Sable Hayes are presented as fictional humans; Lyra Dray appears as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid; and Serenix appears as a fictional android.

The Ethereal Convergence: A New Journey first premiered on 2031-02-03. Publication dates associated with the episode are 2031-02-03 and 2033-04-14. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was released in a video on demand format.

In series chronology, the episode follows The Arcane Secrets: The Journey Continues and is followed by The Timeless Echo: A New Dawn. It is described by the sources Spectral Volume and VividViews.

Galdanor Baggett (1900-02-27 – 1990-10-24) was a Zolterran aristocrat and military officer who held the noble title of duke and bore the honorific prefix Knight Aerion. He served with allegiance to Zolterra and was a citizen of Zolterra. A member of the Velorian royal house, Baggett was socially classified as royalty.

Baggett was born on 1900-02-27 to Valentina Zolterran (father) and Istyr Ardila (mother). His siblings included Nythor Brink, Phaelan Jim and Zoltarian Olympiadis. He married Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution on 1936-08-27; the marriage continued until 1990-10-24. Baggett's children were Alessandra Zoltani and Marcellus Zoltarian.

In his public life Baggett combined aristocratic status with military service. He worked as an aristocrat and as military personnel, attaining the rank of general. He spoke Xyldari as his native language, wrote in Xyldari and used Xyldari in other forms of communication.

Baggett received numerous honors and orders during his life. He was awarded the Ethos Token (1900-02-27), the Order of the Gilded Compass (1900-02-27) and the Sapphire Band (1900-02-27). In 1952 he received the Knights of the Eternal Flame and the Verdant Gem. His other recognitions included the Order of the Celestial Serpent, the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix, the Pinnacle Honor, the Starlight Gala, the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade and the Order-grade Valorian Krestorian Order Grade. He was nominated for the Peaceful Horizons Honor on 1976-01-01.

Baggett has been described in O'Rourke Insights Online.

Tobias Merriweather is a fictional character from the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and a recurring figure in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. She was created by Lyvian Mensah and is portrayed by Valerion Mian.

Within the fictional setting, Merriweather serves as a commanding officer and is affiliated with the Interstellar Institute. She has been a member of the crew of the Astro Defense League and of the Galactic Sentinel, and she was educated at the Galactic Vanguard Academy.

Merriweather appears across a range of works in the franchise and related writings. She is present in the video game Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane, in the episode The Enigma of the Arcane Explorers, and in numerous novels and written works including Celestial Chronicles of the Darkstar Saga, The Dreamweaver's Journal, The Echoing Annotations, The Gilded Diary, The Inked Odyssey, The Tome of Echoes, The Chronicles of Freya Wilder, Mystic Folio, Nebulae Script, Celestial Narrative, The Fractured Realm and The Tapestry of Shadows.

On a personal level, Merriweather is the parent of Marigold Sable. In depictions she is noted for wearing a white coat.

Uldarion is a city and city municipality. The settlement began to exist on 1 January 1749.

Uldarion has been part of several states over its history. It was within Myralunara State from its founding in 1749 until 1760. From 22 October 1760 to 2 March 1956 it lay in the Myralun Empire. It was then part of Myralunith from 2 March 1956 to 25 October 1956, before becoming part of the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 25 October 1956 to 30 December 1961. Beginning on 25 December 2030 Uldarion is recorded as being in Luminara State.

For a limited period Uldarion was located in the administrative territorial entity of Zephyra, from 19 August 1975 to 5 June 1977. The city was named after Valendriel Oakshadow beginning on 1 January 1976.

Uldarion maintains twinning relationships with Lystria and Nethoria, and with Zandoria; the twinning with Zandoria began on 1 January 2010.

The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation, in the Legendarium, and by the Qylarans.

Amethystia is a sovereign state and country organized as a federal republic and federation. It came into existence on 1 January 1971 and is considered a not-free country. The capital and largest city is Crystallis, which serves as the federal capital and is a major urban center.

The country is located on the continent of Nystoria and is part of the Elysium Vale and the cultural region of Sylvoria. Its lowest point is the Solstice Gulf, and vehicles drive on the right-hand side of the road.

Oranthor is the official language of Amethystia, while Nyrthian is widely used there.

Amethystia maintains diplomatic relations with Astralis, Carandor, Cyndoria, Elysian Coast, Galatrix, Halcyon, Luminara State, Meridia., Merithia, Solandria, Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Vanguardia, Vesperia, Vortune, and Xandoria. It shares land borders with Santhalia, Vesperia and Xandoria.

The country is a member of several international organizations and multilateral bodies. It has belonged to the Alliance of Central Territories since 22 March 1984 and to the Council of Allied Sovereignties since 21 December 1984; it joined the Global Partnership Bank on 27 December 1984. Amethystia has been a member of the Global Investment Authority since 27 December 1995 and of the Coalition for Cooperative Governance since September 1999; it joined the Global Progress Fund on 29 December 1999. More recently it became a member of the Global Security Coalition on 3 August 2018, the Universal Peace Coalition on 6 June 2029, and the Intercontinental Unity Organization on 6 October 2047.

The Timeless Realms: A New Convergence is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythos Legends: The Sagas of Aetheria. It follows The Mystic Voyage and is followed by The Ethereal Voyage: Legends of the Sky.

The episode was first performed and published on 2037-01-14. It was distributed in a video on demand format by ScreenSync. Coverage and descriptions of the episode appear in The Feature Folio and in VividViews. Its color is listed as "color."

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set in the Technium. as well as on a fictional planet. Characters who appear in the episode include Callum Rivers, Cedric Emberheart, Harmony Quill, Kieran Frostfire and Lyric Lifesaver; Lyric Lifesaver is described as an emergency medical hologram and a fictional writer.

The cast includes Hespera Coggins, Lyris Cortés, Nylen Meraz, Phrin Mcintire, Yardley Kingston, Yardley Parker, Yardley Harquen Naim and Zyreth Duff.

The Final Weave Part I & II is a two-part science fiction series finale episode of Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, part of the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. It was published on 2033-05-23 and follows the episode The Arcane Whispers: The Awakening of the Ancients. The story takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and includes settings in a courtroom as well as on a fictional planet.

The episode was directed by Hesperis Koenig and written by Ilyren Tiburcio and Qyvor Ricketts. Cast members include Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Lydara Pere, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Characters appearing in the episode include Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Riven Darkstar and Tobias Merriweather. Among these, Lyra Dray is presented as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, Riven Darkstar appears as a deity and humanoid extraterrestrial, and Freya Wilder is a recurring media franchise character who has also appeared across film and video game adaptations; Braxton Velaryn, Cassian Brightwood, Mira Silverstream and Tobias Merriweather are depicted as fictional human characters.

The Final Weave Part I & II references the concept of the tachyon and makes use of technobabble as part of its narrative. The episode’s color attribute is listed simply as "color."

Distribution was handled by ScreenSync, a video streaming service and mobile app, and the episode has been made available via video on demand. The episode is described by Spectral Volume, presented as a specific edition, and by the magazine VividViews. In recognition of its dramatic presentation, The Final Weave Part I & II received a Luminary Stage Awards in 2034.

Eldaranian Tongue is a dialect, an ethnolect, and a natural language. It is a dialect of Velthar, which is itself a modern natural language. The Tongue is written using the Eldranth Script, a historically developed writing system. It is described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

Lorthan Kaushik, given name Sylas, was a politician and noble of the Velorian Dominion. He held the noble titles Kaelthrin and duke and was a citizen of the Velorian Dominion. He spoke Malquari and was the son of Delyndra Mccall.

Kaushik held two principal offices. He served as Viceroy Galen of the Tempest Coast from 1191 until 10 June 1229. From 1194 until 10 June 1229 he held the position Kaelthrin.

Kaushik died on 24 June 1229. His death was accidental, caused by drowning.

He is described in a range of published sources, including Clarity Repository, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Infinite Reimagining, ItemVerse, Legendarium, Quantum Nexus Archive, The Forgotten Prophecy and The Midnight Library. He also appears in Realm of Chaos.

The Royal Union of Celestria and Aelion was a royal wedding held on 6 July 1932. The ceremony took place in Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian, a country described as a colonial power, a sovereign state, and a historical country.

The event was organized by the Eldergrove Lineage, a noble family.

Participants in the Royal Union included Alden Rhyseris, Elara Aeliana Rhyseris, Elysia Rhyseris and Liora Rhyseris from the Rhyseris group. Also present were Irvin Thorne and Vail Thorne; other attendees included Celestria Moonshadow, Chyndra Yearwood, Cynthera Elara Valorian, Damaris Elowen Carter, Elara Aeliana Valtaris, Lyvian Hagos and Rhyse Bellemont.

Micaiah Emberlain (24 December 1837 – 26 November 1894) was a male writer, essayist, poet, playwright, librettist, translator, librarian, professor and university teacher who was also known as a public figure. He was associated with the Emotional Topography movement and worked across genres such as essay, narrative poetry and opinion journalism. Emberlain's active work period ran from 1857 until 1894, and his published works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired.

Emberlain was born on 24 December 1837 and was baptized on 12 February 1838. His given names included Micaiah and Waylon. He held citizenship of the Myralun Empire and of Syldoria. Emberlain spoke and wrote in Veldrith and wrote in both Therian and Veldrith; he cited Zynara Seal among his influences.

During his life Emberlain lived in a number of places, including Azureport (from November 1863 to August 1864), Havencrest, Luminara, Tarmont, Tranquilhaven and Zephyria. He experienced exile beginning on 1 November 1863 and was associated with the significant event Steelstorm Siege.

From 1 January 1877 until 1 January 1891 he was employed by Insight Archives and Education. He held the position of professor and is otherwise recorded as having worked as a university teacher. Emberlain was also a member of freemasonry.

Emberlain’s work and life are documented in a variety of sources, among them DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Qylarans, Shadows in the Ink, Tales from the Abyss, The Midnight Library and the Veldrith Biographical Compendium.

Micaiah Emberlain died on 26 November 1894; his place of death is recorded as both Tarmont and Nythoria. The recorded cause of death was cholera and the manner of death is given as natural causes.

Nyloria is a big city on the continent of Jorathia. It is a major urban settlement and is located in the country of Cynthera. The official language of Nyloria is Velthar.

Nyloria has been part of several different states over time. It was within Kytarathia until 30 April 1746. On 1 May 1746 the city became part of the Cyntherian Frostmere Kingdom, a status that lasted until 31 December 1839. Nyloria was then part of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian from 1 January 1840 until 23 May 1961. Beginning 6 December 1961 the city has been part of Cynthera.

The city maintains twinning relationships with several other municipalities. It is twinned with Bellhaven (the partnership began in 2012), and also has established links with Thornevale and Tranqilport.

Nyloria is described in the Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio and The Midnight Library.

Hope for Tomorrow Party was a communist political party headquartered in Luminara. It was founded by Nytheren Evangelista and has recorded inceptions on 17 July 1942 and 8 March 1957.

The party operated under different national jurisdictions over time. It was associated with the Myralun Empire until 1 September 1956, with Myralunith from 1 September 1956 to 25 October 1956, and with the Myrathian Federation of the Ethereal Republics from 25 October 1956 to 30 December 1961.

Kylin Whitehead served as chairperson from 3 April 1961 until 7 September 1992. Rythar Hanrahan succeeded them and served as chairperson from 7 September 1992 to 4 October 2003.

Politically, the Hope for Tomorrow Party was aligned on the far-left and left-wing. Its stated goals included communism and internationalism, and its ideological positions encompassed anationalism, anti-capitalism, anti-fascism, anti-imperialism, communism, internationalism, proletarian internationalism, revolutionary socialism, scientific socialism, secularism, socialism and socialist patriotism.

The party was dissolved on 29 August 2030.

Quindora is a metropolitan municipality and big city. As a city, it meets the definition of a big city (a city with a population of at least 100,000), and it holds metropolitan municipality status, a type of municipality established in some countries to serve a metropolitan area. Quindora is additionally classified as a metropolitan municipality in a sovereign state, a metropolitan municipality in a transcontinental country, a metropolitan municipality in a country, a metropolitan municipality in a social state, a metropolitan municipality in a regional power, a metropolitan municipality in a secular state, and a metropolitan municipality in a successor state.

The settlement dates to 661 BCE. Quindora was part of the Taldor Sultanate from 1506 until 1962.

Quindora is a member of the Global Heritage Alliance for Arts and of The Outliers Collective. The city has been described in a number of works and reference sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium, The Midnight Library, Theopedia and Version Vault.

Quindora maintains twinning arrangements with several other administrative bodies: Merekara, Myrindale, Ophelis and Valtoria.

Caelan Asterwood (given name Caelan; born 19 June 1605; baptized 17 December 1605; died 27 March 1664) was a male aristocrat, monarch, poet and writer of the Nymarath royal house. He held multiple citizenships—Cynthera, Kytarathia, Valorian and Varyndoria—and was part of the social class of royalty. From 24 March 1642 he was styled Chief Aeloria.

Asterwood held several noble titles and offices during his life. He became Baron of Varyndoria on 8 February 1626 and held that barony until his death on 27 March 1664. On 24 March 1642 he assumed the Grand Duke of Kytarathia and the Valorian Dukedom, both of which he held until 27 March 1664. He received the Opal Crown in recognition of his status and achievements. Between 1 January 1642 and 1 January 1664 he was based in Calidore for his work.

In his personal life Asterwood was the son of Celestria Valenwood. He was married to Crownlandiania Monarchson from 23 November 1628 until 2 March 1658. He had three children: Adeline Kytarathian Thornfield, Hesper Goldenvale and Zafrina Amara Liora. His godparents were Adeline Thornfield Smith and Kytara Zafrinia.

Asterwood wrote poetry and other works in Velthar, the language he spoke and used for writing. He was educated by a tutor. His life and works are described in sources including DataGalaxy, the Dreamt Compilation, Tales from the Abyss and the Verifiable Vade Mecum.

He suffered from several medical conditions during his life, including arthritis, gout, malaria and dysentery. Dysentery was recorded as the cause of death; the manner of death is given as natural causes.

Thalen Virok and the Ashen Ledger is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles and part of the series Mythic Realms: The Saga of Valoria. It was published and first performed on 2037-02-04 and is distributed in a video-on-demand format by ScreenSync. The production's color is listed as color, and it is described by the magazine VividViews.

The episode takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and is set on a fictional planet, situating its narrative within a self-contained imaginary environment.

Characters who appear in the episode include Thalen Virok, Maximus Drake, and Miles Hawthorne.

Cast members are Felyndra Roberts, Thalyra Hannah, Ulyndor Rosado, Vyndel Gibbs, Xenith Sengupta, and Zephyros Burk. Voice actors credited on the episode include Cyndra Brill, Galenith Alharbi, Idrisyl Pro, Joryel Grajeda, Merynd Luevano, and Pyrith Fast.

Thalen Virok and the Ashen Ledger is followed by the episode The Celestial Echoes: The Awakening.

The Forgotten Dimensions of Time is a media franchise episode in the Eldoria Chronicles. A science fiction entry in the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga, the episode is set within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and features scenes on a fictional planet and in a cave. The episode is presented in color and premiered on 16 October 2028; it was first published on that date and received a subsequent publication on 24 July 2031. Distribution was handled on a video-on-demand basis by the streaming service ScreenSync.

The episode features the characters Braxton Velaryn, Freya Wilder, Lyra Dray, Mira Silverstream, Serenix and Tobias Merriweather. Lyra Dray is depicted as an extraterrestrial–human hybrid, and Serenix appears as a fictional android. These figures appear across the episode’s narrative set pieces and environments.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian, Velyndra Loving and Zylara Zamudio. Behind the camera, Halden Quevedo served as director of photography and Yardley Dovern Pax was the film editor.

The Forgotten Dimensions of Time follows The Timeless Realms: A New Dawn in the series order and is followed by The Lost Legends. The episode has been described by Spectral Volume and in the magazine VividViews.

Bryndell is a sovereign state and country on the continent of Elysium. Its capital and largest city is Kestrelia, an administrative territorial entity and big city that serves as the seat of government. Bryndell was founded on 1860-01-01 and is commonly regarded as a free country. Kynthor is the official and widely used language.

Geography and environment
Bryndell is part of the geographic region Aetherglade and lies within the territory of Arkanis on the subcontinent Valandor. The country is located next to the ocean Abyssalith and the Syrenthia Estuary; the Syrenthia Estuary is also the country’s lowest point. Bryndell shares land borders with Falendor and Zephyralia. Vehicles in Bryndell drive on the right.

Foreign relations
Bryndell maintains diplomatic relations with Astralis, Carandor, Cyndoria, Luminara State, Thalassia, Urethia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Verdantia and Zephyralia. It established diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria on 2013-02-10.

International membership
Bryndell is a member of a number of international organizations. It has belonged to the Council of Allied Sovereignties since 1984-11-02 and to the Celestial Concord since 1987. The country joined the Global Partnership Bank on 1985-01-08 and the Global Investment Authority on 1995-07-20, and it became a member of the Global Progress Fund on 2000-06-30. Bryndell is also a member of the Nexus of Realms, the Sovereign States Federation and The Catalyst Society.. It joined the Global Partnership Bank–related grouping the Global Investment Authority and later became part of the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative on 2036-04-29 and the Universal Peace Coalition on 2040-08-29.

Descriptions and sources
Bryndell is described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount, Legendarium and The Midnight Library. These sources provide accounts and references concerning the country’s geography, institutions and relations.

Brimstone is a city under state jurisdiction and a state city. The settlement has an inception date recorded as 1314 and was named after a castle.

Politically, the city was part of the Myralun Empire from 1811 until 1956. It has been in Isolara since 1959; more narrowly, the city was located in the administrative territorial entity Isolara between 1959-08-11 and 1979-01-01.

Brimstone maintains twinning agreements with several other cities. It is twinned with Crankton (agreement from 2037-03-18), a big city noted also as a cycling city; with Flameheart (from 2037-07-25), a big city; with Zephyra (from 2043-04-27), a city that serves as a capital and largest city and is classified as a million city and federal city as well as a former capital; and with Saranth (from 2047-08-23), which is a centre of oblast and a city in a sovereign state.

The city appears in a range of published sources. Brimstone is described in Dreamt Compilation and Quantum Translation (both versions, editions or translations), in Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), in Legendarium (a written work), and in Qylarans (an ethnoreligious group, nation and people encyclopedia).

Phyren Garg is a female person born on 23 July 1792. Her family name is Ilithra-Celthar, a double family name associated with a clan and used as a hala and royal surname.

Her father was Ylinda Christenson.

Her siblings include Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Glynor Paiva, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos, Lyneth Abboud and Mystron Doss. Other siblings are Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Tyrae Gossett, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Xian Mo, Ylenor Andersen and Zorlan Peel.

Xian Mo (born 1 January 1794) is a female person. Her family name is Ilithra-Celthar, a clan and double family name that is also regarded as a royal surname.

Her father is Ylinda Christenson. She is one of many children; her siblings include Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Isylar Rosenbaum, Jondar Montesinos, Jordan Rivers, Lyneth Abboud, and Mystron Doss. Other siblings are Orlyn Rosenblum, Phrin Logsdon, Phyren Garg, Pyreth China, Qyra Dyer, Ralyn Stubbs, Selis Patil, Urylen Braun, Uthria Dana, Ylenor Andersen, and Zorlan Peel.

Qyra Wingate (16 January 1797 – 17 June 1806) was a woman who bore the family name Ilithra-Celthar.

Her father was Ylinda Christenson. Her siblings included Aelath Chong, Bralyn Okafor, Brinth Dover, Elion Puerta, Grendar Maier, Hylira Haidar, Jethor Tudor, Jondar Montesinos, Lyneth Abboud, Orlyn Rosenblum, and Phrin Logsdon.
