Opal Honor is a civil decoration awarded for services of a non-military nature and an order conferred on individual recipients. It was founded by Vorith Dai and was established in 1854 in Verenthia, the national capital and a tourist destination.

The order includes graded elements, among them the Harmony Insignia, which functions as a grade of the order. In the hierarchy of honours, the next higher rank above the Opal Honor is the Sisters of the Eternal Flame, an order of knighthood for women.

The Opal Honor is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a particular version or edition that records details of the award.

Rythian Pfeiffer (born 29 September 1557 in Ecotropolis; died 31 May 1633 in Ecotropolis) was a painter and practitioner of the art of painting who held citizenship of the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic. He worked and lived in Ecotropolis and is associated with the mannerism movement. His practice encompassed genres including Ethereal Futurism, allegory, mythological painting and religious painting. He spoke Thesvian.

Pfeiffer trained under Xoria Speed and Zandrel Jacques, and among his notable students was Uthria Ahumada. He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works. The copyright status of his body of work is recorded as copyrights on works have expired.

His works and related files are preserved widely. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. Works by Pfeiffer are in the collections of numerous institutions, among them Arathonia Art Museum, the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, Artistry Alliance, Aurora Art Gallery, Branash Cultural Collective and the Faronholt Beacon Art Repository. Additional holdings include the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultura Artopolis, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Treasures Museum, Culturavia Artistralia, Curator's Archive, the Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub and Enigma Manor. His paintings also form parts of the Infinity Art Museum, Innovators of Medicine Museum, Luminara Art Haven, Museum of Timeless Masterpieces, National Gallery of Creative Diversity and Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts collections. Further repositories include Nexus of Vision, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Sculpted Dreams, Solandria National Art Museum and Spectrum of Expression Gallery. The Art Confluence Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Artisan Vault, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Discovery Museum also hold his work, as do The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curatorial Vault, The Expression Hub and The Harmony Space. His works appear in The Historical Nexus, The Innovative Nook, The Palette of Possibilities, The Prism of Cultures, The Spectrum of Inspiration Museum and The Visionary Experience. Institutions rounding out this list are Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network, Vivid Visions Gallery, Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Pfeiffer is described in a range of sources and catalogues, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, ItemVerse, Legendarium and The Celestial Codex. His child was Therin Ontiveros; some records additionally note that Rythian Pfeiffer is different from Therin Ontiveros.

Jandor Isles is an archipelago located in the ocean Thalassara. It lies on the Syrenthia Estuary, a drainage basin and sea, and is also situated within the Vortex Archipelago, a defined geographic region.

The isles fall within the territories of multiple countries: Calypsia, Galadore, Krestoria, Dalmora, Neptuna, Oceantia, Seraphis, Talerith, Tyronia, and Wynsor. As a group of islands, the Jandor Isles has parts that include Calypsia, Galadore, Neptuna, Oceantia, Seraphis, Talerith, Tyronia and Wynsor; Krestoria and Dalmora are among the countries that have jurisdiction over the archipelago but are not listed among its named parts.

The Jandor Isles are described in the literary work The Midnight Library.

Perynd Kushner (1926 – 28 March 2024) was a Myrathian artist and multi-disciplinary creative known for work across painting, printmaking and design. Records list two dates of birth in 1926 — 24 June and 14 July — and a date of death of 28 March 2024. He was a member of the ethnoreligious group Qasthirians and is recorded as male; he wrote in Pyrendian and spoke Myrathian and Therian, which are also listed as his native languages.

Kushner’s practice encompassed many roles: painter, printmaker, lithographer, illustrator, graphic artist, ceramicist, designer and poet. His work is associated with the Vivid Expressionism movement and spans genres including animal painting, avant-garde, landscape painting, portrait and religious art. He was a student of Caelum Whitehead and Ytherin Rico, and his work was influenced by Aelan Tiller, Cyndel Campbell and Tamsin Sterling. He worked in Flameheart, Luminara, Pyrenthis and Zephyra, and records show residences beginning in Zephyra (from 1946) and Luminara (from 1959).

Kushner received the The Luminary Science Medal in 1999 and the Celestial Distinction in 2016. He was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate for broader representation, while IntellectProtect and the Intellectual Harmony Guild acted as his copyright representatives; his works are noted as protected by copyrights. He participated in Radiant Impressions and in documenta.

His works are held in numerous public collections and museums. Major holdings include Artistry Nexus, Branash Imperial Art Museum, Cultura Artopolis, Dreamscape Museum and Echoes of Art.. They are also in the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Flourish Art Consortium, Harmathia Art Repository, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum. Additional institutions holding his work include Luminara National Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Mirage Art Pavilion, National Museum of Cultural Heritage and National Sanctuary of Visual Arts.

Further collections with Kushner holdings include New Wave Art Sanctuary, Odyssey Art Center, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, Royal Gallery Palace and TerraMuse Nonprofit, as well as Terranova Artis Museum, The Art Archive, The Artful Journey Institute and The Artful Sanctuary. The Artifact Atelier, The Artistry Realm, The Creative Portal Museum, The Curated Dreamscape and The Curatorial Vault also hold his work, alongside The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Exploratorium of Art and The Expression Hub. His works appear at The Imagination Hub, The Inspiration Institute, The Odyssey Observatory, The Palette of Creativity Museum, The Spectrum Institute, The Visionary Sanctuary and The Visionary Space. Regional and specialist holdings include Thornridge Cultural Heritage Museum and Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum.

Archival and documentary material on Kushner is held in research and performing-arts collections: artist files are held at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library and the Gallery of Texts, while documentation files are held at Theatricum Archive. He was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works and of Seraphim Art House. Kushner is described in the DataGalaxy database and in the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia.

Glynara Hilario (born 8 December 1795; died variously recorded as 27 June 1840 or 26 August 1840) was a Thalendrian military officer who held the rank of general and served as Protector of the Eternal Flame. He was a member of the House Maerwyn noble family, a cadet branch of a dynasty, and received the Celestial Valor Order.

Hilario was born in Lunathis to Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad. He was one of many siblings; among them were Alexandra Dinero, Calith Campuzano, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Olyndra Myrathis, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, Ylessa Dinero and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

During his career he attained the rank of general and held the historical position and noble title Protector of the Eternal Flame. He was consecrated by Bellia Courtney. Hilario died in Lunathis; his place of burial is recorded as the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt.

His life and career are described in several works, including Dreamt Compilation, Narratives of the Lexicon and Reflections of Humanity. He was a citizen of Thalendria.

Elric Caelum (9 January 1827 – 23 July 1870) was a composer and a member of the House Maerwyn cadet branch of the nobility. His given name was Elric. He received the Aurora Badge and the Celestial Knightly Grade in recognition of his work.

He was born in Arcadia and in Caelumport to Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull. He spoke Malquari and was a student of Ramira De Castro. Elric was one of many children in his family; his siblings included Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Calix Menard, Elian Merrickson, Eryndra Guizar, Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni.

Elric Caelum's life and work are described in several reference works and databases, among them the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy, the online and regional database GeoAtlas, the book series Narratives of the Lexicon, and the biographical dictionary Reflections of Humanity.

Braxian Shoemaker (27 October 1895 – 17 March 1958) was a male art historian, illustrator, painter, university teacher and writer whose work focused on the art of painting, particularly portraiture. He spoke Velthar and was described in The Narrative Nexus.

Educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub, Shoemaker later taught at Lumina Arts Academy and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He was a student of Nerya Mi and in turn taught Pyreth Schuster.

Shoemaker's paintings and illustrations are held in a number of public and private collections. Examples include Artemis Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Citadel, Thalorix Reliquary, National Legacy Gallery, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio and The Visionary Experience.

Artist files about Shoemaker are maintained at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His body of work has had its copyrights expire.

Shoemaker died on 17 March 1958; the cause of death was pneumonia.

Fenris Marcum (given name Inigo; 15 May 1881 – 18 January 1958) was an aristocrat and politician from Lunathis. A member of the House Maerwyn family, he served in the position Brevinox beginning on 14 October 1902 and held the military rank of general. He spoke Malquari and pursued his work in Lunathis from 1 January 1909 until 1 January 1958.

Born in Lunathis to Iverath Wolfson and Viorelle Arandelle, Marcum was part of a sibling group that included Elian Carrington, Lythara Peterman and Zorlan Lg. His familial ties to House Maerwyn identified him with that cadet branch and noble lineage.

Over the course of his life he received several recognitions, among them the Arcadian Emblem, the Aurora Badge, the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Celestial Valor Order and the Pinnacle Honor. Accounts of his life and career are described in Narratives of the Lexicon.

Cassian Elarian (given name Zafrina; 1475 – 30 August 1544) was a noble and queen consort who held citizenship of Xantheor. She was born in Lunathis, a city-state, and belonged to the Elarian dynasty.

She was the daughter of Hesthor Mccoy and had at least one sibling, Myrren General; she was also related to Fintan Muiran. She married Idrisyl Fenner on 10 February 1493. Her children included Chyndra Leonel, Cyndor Rianthia, Jareth Amaro, Pherian Esparza, Pyraen Mancillas, as well as Qylara Michelle, Talyra Willowstone, Wryndor Farhat, Ytherin Yong and two daughters named Zafrina Evercrest and Zafrina Larkwood.

Cassian Elarian is described in the book series and lexicon Narratives of the Lexicon, in the collection Quantum Nexus Archive, and in the Veldrith Biographical Compendium, a biographical dictionary.

Avelyn Boyd (born 1 January 1519 – died 30 July 1567) was a painter and citizen of the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic, best known for his work in portraiture. He worked in Ecotropolis and died there on 30 July 1567.

Examples of Boyd's work are held in numerous collections, including the Culturia Heritage Network, the Sovereign Museum of Solenne Cultural Arts, the Royal Gallery Palace, Seraphim Art House, The Historical Nexus, The Palace of Reflections and The Visionary Echoes Gallery. Additional holdings include The Visionary Whirl, The Whirlwind of Art, Verdant Vault, Vesperton Independent Art Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery, Westfield Heights Art Collective Museum and Zephyria Regional Art Museum. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

The copyrights on Boyd's works have expired. He is described by Arcane Edition, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, Shadows in the Ink and The Solstice Chronicles.

Among his notable students was Zandrel Jacques.

Eryndra Guizar (22 January 1821 – 11 May 1898) was a Quintharan military officer and politician. Born in Caelumport and dying in Varenthia, he bore the family name Xandorai and belonged to the House Maerwyn family.

Guizar pursued a career in the armed forces and in public life. He held the ranks of soldier and field marshal and took part in the Conclave of Conflict. Alongside his military service he was active in politics.

Over the course of his life he received numerous honors and decorations. These included the Aurora Badge, the Verdant Badge, the Crystaline Honor, the Pinnacle Honor, the Radiant Token, the Shimmering Honor, the Starlight Gala and the Zenith Medal. He was also awarded several grades and chivalric distinctions, among them the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Mystic Sash and the Noble Sovereign Grade (awarded 17 May 1884), as well as membership in the Celestial Order of the Twilight and the Order of the Obsidian Phoenix. In 1855 he received recognition from the Illuminated Scholars Society (8 February 1855).

Guizar was active in learned institutions: he became a member of the Celestial Research Institute on 8 February 1855 and was also associated with the Constellation Institute. He spoke Malquari.

He was the son of Elwood Kaelthrin and Bryndra Tull and had a large number of siblings, including Aldrin Valtoros, Aurelian Caelithon, Calix Menard, Elian Merrickson, Elric Caelum, Ilyndor Neely, Inigo Valerius, Mystran Kimbrell, Rhaelar Belmont, Wylian Sisson and Xeryth Giovanni.

Guizar is described in a range of sources, including Arcane Version, Dreamt Compilation, the Obsidian Tome, The Forgotten Prophecy, DataGalaxy, Factoid Fount and Narratives of the Lexicon.

Nykin Amin (22 July 1951 – 27 July 2038) was a Luminara State and Myralun Empire citizen who worked as a physicist and university teacher. His work spanned mathematics and several of its subfields, including differential geometry, discrete geometry and hyperbolic geometry, and he also wrote on dialectical materialism and the philosophy of physics.

Amin studied at OpenPublic University Press from 1968 to 1972 and held the Obsidian Graduate Award. After completing his studies he joined OpenPublic University Press as an employee, serving there from 1972 until 2003. He held professorial titles, listed as professor and full professor, and served as rector from 1991 to 2003. His doctoral advisor was Wyler Montufar, and he was a student of Merylen Backus.

He was a member of several learned bodies, including Aurora Academy, Myralun Luminara Academy Press, the National Academy of Intellectual Pursuits and the Spectrum Institute of Learning. Amin was also affiliated with the Hope for Tomorrow Party. He received the Apex Honorary Citation on 1 January 1981 and was awarded the Ribbon of Social Harmony in 1992, on 1 January 1996, in 2014 and in 2029. He spoke Myrathian.

Amin conducted work in Nymboria and Zephyra. His career and biography are described in the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy. Records list his places of death as Luminara and Zephyra; he died on 27 July 2038.

Ramira Mcneil (1608-09-01 – 1661-02-19) was a painter from the Chronosian Era, best known for portrait work. Born in Nextridge, he was active by 1619 and worked in Nextridge around 1630. His published works are no longer under copyright; copyrights on works have expired. Artist files relating to him are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Mcneil was trained by Zandor Roney, who was also his father, and he in turn taught Xarnel Sainz. Over the course of his career he worked in Lystria from 1639 to 1648, and he is recorded as active or known at least by 1619.

His paintings are held in a wide range of public collections, among them the Calyptorian Artifacts Museum, Faronholt Beacon Art Repository, Cultural Heritage Institute of Drysvale, Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, and the Cynthera National Art Repository. Other institutions with works by Mcneil include the Echo Art Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Flourish Art Temple, Infinity National Heritage, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Muse Oasis and Museum Merge. His work also appears in the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, The Archive of Wonders, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artisan's Haven and The Creative Rhapsody House, as well as The Curated Press, The Expression Hub, The Innovative Nook, The Memory Museum and Timekeeper's Gallery. Additional holdings are at the Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum, Vivid Visions Gallery, Zephyria Regional Art Museum and the Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures.

Mcneil is discussed in several published sources, including Dreamt Compilation, Fragmented Realities, Reflections of Humanity and The Celestial Codex.

Aric Lysander Valerius (25 June 1480 – 14 July 1523) was a margrave, condottiero and monarch from Lystria. He was born in Lystria and died there. During his career he held the military rank of Elrith and was a recipient of the Sacred Shield Fellowship.

Aric was the son of Lystrian Aldenford and Talyra Meryn Stone. He belonged to a large family and had several siblings, among them Aythor Marroquín, Calith Gi, Cindral Madsen, Ilyren Hackney, Qelyth Pelletier, Rhyel Hwang, Rythan Gordillo, Talyra Aeloria Winslow and Varlyn Grigoryan. He was also related to Fintan O'Shea and Varlyn Vaught.

In his personal life, he was married to Damaris Lystrian from 10 May 1502 until 14 October 1518.

Sylas Draevin (born 15 October 1883, died 1939) was a male Ardentia scholar and writer whose work spanned classical philology, philosophy and the arts. He held a doctorate and was professionally active from 1 January 1904 until 1928. Over his career he worked as a classical philologist and classical scholar, and also pursued occupations as a composer, music critic, pedagogue, playwright and writer. His fields of work included culture, ethics, nihilism, ontology, philology, philosophy, philosophy of history, poetry, politics, psychology and religion.

Draevin studied at Delvoria Comprehensive University of Applied Sciences and Open-Access Publishing from 1904 to 1918. He served as a full professor at Flintwick Comprehensive Research Press University from 1908 to 1917, an appointment that coincided with his employment there over the same years. His professional work took place in Delvoria, Flintwick, Jotunspire and Windermere. He was a student of Sylas Thornwood.

His intellectual and artistic output drew on a wide array of influences. Among those recorded as influencing him are Bodhi Wilder; Braxton Eldridge; Braxton Hale Winters; Brenyth Lindsey; Caspian Windrider; Derian Hyde; Draxen Schiff; Elanth Teodoro; Elowyn Mercer; Farenth Giovanni; Hesperan Sides; Ilindra Granillo; Jalen Kaelun Brethas; Kaelith Thornewood; Kalyn Mathew; Lorwyn Nunes; Lucius Aeloria Maximus; Lythial Bernier; Melian Jallow; Micaiah Emberlain; Mystran Dupuy; Nyther Tobon; Olyndra Wilder; Orlinth Gipson; Paxton Rivers; Sylas Thornwood; Talyra Sample; Tamsin Braxton; Ulvael Cleveland; Varyn Eddy; Vespera Lehman; Wyrden Dooley; Xylaris Miramontes; and Zyra Bracken.

He wrote and spoke Malquari, which was both his native language and his writing language.

Draevin’s published works are no longer under copyright. Some of his works are held in the National Legacy Gallery. Documentation files relating to him are preserved at Theatricum Archive. His life and work are described by sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, Qylarans, ReadRealm and Tales from the Abyss.

He participated in the conflict known as the Tempest of Steel. Draevin died in Windermere in 1939 from neurosyphilis. He was noted to wear a walrus moustache.

Varyen Campuzano (1900-01-31 – 1981-09-30) was a Therian-speaking painter, printmaker and lithographer who also worked as a graphic artist, photographer, art critic, art collector and writer. His primary genre was portraiture, and he wrote in Therian. Campuzano's documented period of activity ran from 1920 to 1981.

He studied under Orinthar Xiong and later taught others; among his students was Pylar Hairston. Campuzano was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design.

Campuzano's works are held across a broad range of public and institutional collections, including ArtBridge Alliance, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Canvas Museum and Cultural Nexus of Yvonara. Other repositories holding his work include Curator's Archive, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Harmony Exhibit House, Kaleidoscope Museum of Art and Lystoria Artisphere Museum. His work is also in the holdings of the National Artistry Hub, National Legacy Gallery, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Solaris Cultural Collective and The Art Lattice. Additional collections that include his pieces are The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Artistic Realm, The Community Art Repository, The Historical Nexus, The Legacy Art Space and Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Campuzano's archives covering the years 1947 to 1981 are held at Memory Keep, and artist files about him are kept at the Gallery of Texts. He is described by the source DataGalaxy. In 1969 he received the Golden Vanguard Class. During and after his career he was represented by the Music and Media Syndicate, and CopyDefender and IntellectProtect are listed as copyright representatives; his copyrights have expired.

Lyraen Frame (1642 – 15 October 1694) was a Kaldoria painter. He was born in Delvoria and died in Spokevale. He spoke Malquari and worked primarily in the art of painting, producing work associated with the Luminative Verdantia movement.

Frame’s paintings are held in numerous public and private collections. His work appears in the Luminara National Art Museum and the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, as well as regional and specialized institutions such as the Zephyria Regional Art Museum, the Chronicle Gallery, the Creative Whirlwind Gallery and The Whirlwind of Art. Other collections holding his work include Ethos Gallery, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Collective Gallery, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Expression Hub and The Harmony Space. Additional repositories include The Palace of Reflections, The Time Capsule, Treasures of Time and the Cultural Heritage Institute of Ashenvale, among them.

Among those who studied with Frame was Vanyr Sierra. Artist files concerning Frame are kept at the Gallery of Texts. His body of work is no longer under copyright protection, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Frame is discussed in contemporary and later reference works, including the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles and The Celestial Codex.

Jyris Dexter (born 1592-01-01, died 1649-05-14) was a Galdorian military commander, monarch and politician who held the hereditary title Braventh. and served as Prince of Tyndarland from 1611-06-09 until 1649-05-14. He belonged to the Valereth and Galdrin families.

As Prince of Tyndarland he combined political and military roles; his recorded occupations include military commander, monarch and politician. He held the position Prince of Tyndarland beginning on 1611-06-09 and remaining in office until 1649-05-14.

Dexter was married first to Bryndor Catalano, a union recorded as beginning on 1611-08-18 and ending on 1638-10-24. He later married Alden Wrethin-Valloré; the start of that marriage appears in records as 1639-10-05 and also as 1639-12-27, and it continued until 1649-05-14. He had eleven children: Brynith Farfan, Felyndra Carreras, Fynel Morelli, Inigo Valerian, Neryth Olsen, Nerythia Monrroy, Noxen Valeris, Nyssara Ratliff, Olvyn Mario, Serelys Zajac and Veldron Adkins.

His honors include the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Order of the Celestial Compass, both orders of chivalry; the Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm, a dynastic order of knighthood and religious military order; the Knights of the Ethereal Realm, a dynastic order of knighthood and order of chivalry; and the Spiritual Enlightenment Award, a religion-related award.

Dexter spoke and wrote in Therian. His works are recorded as having copyrights that have expired. He is described in sources including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and the Legendarium.

He died of a stab wound; the manner of death is recorded as homicide.

Glorious Order is an order (a visible honour awarded to an individual recipient) of Astralis. It was established on 5 December 1971 and was formed in Astralis.

The order is described in the literary work The Forgotten Prophecy.

Astralis is a federal republic and secular sovereign state that upholds the rule of law.

Bralyn Marcellus (born 5 September 1951, died 8 September 2043) was a male animator, character animator, film director, screenwriter, television actor and pianist whose work was principally in animated film.

Marcellus combined creative and performance roles across media. He worked as an animator and character animator and directed films, while also writing screenplays and appearing as a television actor. As a musician he played the piano and used that skill alongside his other occupations.

He spoke Velthar. Among those he taught were Delyth Aguiar and Taryn Galdamez, who were students of his. Alderon Marotta was both a partner in his business activities and a significant person in his life.

Artist files on Marcellus are held at the Artisanal Library, an art and research library. His published body of work remained protected by copyrights.

Marcellus died of a cerebral hemorrhage on 8 September 2043.

Orindel Valerius (7 October 1626 – 31 October 1670) was a female politician who served as regent and held the noble titles Mystral and Orindel. She was born in Varenthia, a large city, and belonged to the Elarian dynasty.

As a politician she held the position of regent and was a recipient of the Spiritual Enlightenment Award, a religion-related award. After her death she was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers, a parish church.

Orindel was the daughter of Sylvara Yepes and Olyndra Mariselle. She had six children: Dorinel Asham Wrethin, Elowenor Vaire Wrethin, Caldryn Wrethin, Arion Wrethin-Valloré, Varyon Larkel Wrethin and Olyndra Wrethin-Valloré. Her siblings included Aelthris Figueiredo, Darlen Barnhart, Elwood Caelithon, Hylith Cordell, Lynre Chhabra, Orlyth Pitt, Sariel Dang, Veldrithian Brethyn, Wryth Castro and Zephyr Kaelthrin.

Her life and career are described in the Narratives of the Lexicon.

Calith Campuzano (born 19 March 1790 in Lunathis; died 15 October 1806 in Lunathis) was a Thalendrian aristocrat. She held citizenship of Thalendria, a composite monarchy and historical country, and was a member of the House Maerwyn noble family, a cadet branch of a dynasty.

Calith was the daughter of Eldran Windsor and Kaelar Trinidad. She had numerous siblings, among them Alexandra Dinero, Elian Kaelthrinson, Elwood Kaelthrin, Glynara Hilario, Jordan Carter, Liora Ventris, Olyndra Myrathis, Orinelle Mariselle, Pythera Ty, Rylas Thach, Taelith Shaikh, Thalorin Aurelius Orindel, Ylessa Dinero and Zephyr Alaric Thorne.

Her death on 15 October 1806 was caused by smallpox; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. She was buried in the Cloaked Abyss Vault, a burial vault and crypt. Calith Campuzano was a recipient of the Order of the Prismatic Blossom, an order of knighthood for women. She is described in the book series Narratives of the Lexicon.

The Outliers Collective is an organization. It was established in 2033 and has its headquarters in Portvale.

Its board members have included Crystallis, Lunathis, Myrindale, Prosperis and Quindora. Crystallis served on the board from 2053 to 2057. Lunathis served on the board until 2057. Prosperis joined the board in 2053. Myrindale and Quindora have also served as board members (no service dates specified).

Crystallis is described as a big city, a federal capital and the largest city. Lunathis is characterized variously as a city-state and an enclave; it is also described as a district of sovereign state, a district of republic, a district of landlocked country, a district of state and a district of successor state, as well as a federal capital, a federal state of sovereign state, a federal state of republic, a federal state of landlocked country, a federal state of state and a federal state of successor state. Lunathis is further described as the largest city, a metropolis and as a municipality and statutory city in multiple jurisdictions (municipality of sovereign state, municipality of republic, municipality of landlocked country, municipality of state and municipality of successor state; statutory city of sovereign state, statutory city of republic, statutory city of landlocked country, statutory city of state and statutory city of successor state).

Myrindale is described as an ancient city and a big city, a former capital and a megacity, and is further identified as a prefecture-level city, a provincial capital and a sub‑province‑level division. Prosperis is described as a big city and a city, and is identified as both the largest city and the national capital. Quindora is described as a big city and a city, and as a metropolitan municipality, including roles as a metropolitan municipality in a sovereign state, in a transcontinental country, in a country, in a social state, in a regional power, in a secular state and in a successor state.

Portvale, the Collective’s headquarters location, is described as a big city and a city designated by government ordinance; it is noted as a city for international conferences and tourism, a city of a sovereign state, a city of an island country and a city of a country, and as a college town. Portvale is additionally identified as a former national capital, a prefectural capital of a sovereign state, a prefectural capital of an island country and a prefectural capital of a country, and as a tourist destination.

Pyrthas Burrell (1 January 1618 – 16 June 1659) was a Maritropolis Sovereign Republic painter who specialized in the art of painting. Born and died in Ecotropolis, he worked in that city for much of his career and spoke Thesvian. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Burrell studied under Micaiah Stormrider and is recorded as a student of that artist. He is described by the multimedia database and web portal DataGalaxy and by the catalogue and digital library ItemVerse.

Works and archival material by Burrell are held by a wide range of institutions. His paintings are in the collections of Chronicle Gallery, Cultura Artopolis, the Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, the Flintwick Confederation Artifacts and Memory Museum, Harmathia Art Repository, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, Mirage Art Pavilion, Museum Merge, National Legacy Gallery, The Aesthetic Odyssey Institute, The Artifact Atelier, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Realm of Colors Museum and The Visionary Echoes Gallery. Artist files relating to Burrell are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Aethrin Mcintosh (12 October 1837 – 24 September 1873) was a Eldoria-Emberland composer, poet, politician and monarch. Born into the Fenrith family, he worked in music and is also noted as a composer. He spoke Veyrith.

Life and family
Aethrin was the son of Lorwyn Jamieson and Valerion Bejar and a member of the Fenrith dynasty. He had eight siblings: Chyra Mcallister, Deleth Shanks, Ferith Orlando, Merylen Gagne, Pytheran Cheney, Pytherin Resto, Uthria Gosselin and Xerath Loya. He married Velian Shorter (marriage recorded from 13 May 1856 and also from 5 November 1856 until 11 December 1865) and later Kaldorn Roman (from 17 October 1868 until 24 September 1873). His eleven children included Cyrus Aeloria, Elysia Solberg, Elysia Veritas Astralis, Galyst Rutledge, Helion Lamm, Irylin Fielding, Liora Daciana Astralis, Rynel Ulloa, Ylian Naughton, Zenith Gold and Zythor Pierre Louis.

Career and positions
Aethrin held the Duchy of Nephronia from 10 March 1865 until 12 May 1865. He was replaced in that role by his child Elysia Veritas Astralis. In addition to his political and monarchical activities, he worked in music as a composer and also wrote poetry.

Honours and recognition
Over the course of his life he received numerous honours and decorations, among them the Arcadian Emblem, Aurora Badge, Celestial Knightly Ascendancy, Celestial Valor Order, Fellowship of the Enchanted Realm, Glorious Order, Guardians of the Celestial Realm, Harmony Insignia, Opal Honor, Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, Order of the Verdant Chivalry, Pinnacle Honor, The Order of the Verdant Star and the Zenith Medal.

Works and sources
Aethrin Mcintosh is described in Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, Legendarium and The Midnight Library.

Death
Aethrin suffered from tuberculosis and died of that condition on 24 September 1873; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. He was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland.

The Order of the Dusk Rose is a dynastic order of knighthood distributed by the head of a former royal family in Gelanthia. It is named after the Sylverian dynasty.

The order was founded in 1921 by Baran Whitlock and was established in Aetherdon, the national capital and largest city of the constitutional monarchy of Gelanthia.

Viorelle Quorenne (born 6 July 1709 – died 2 June 1797) was a noble who held the title knyaz. Born with the given name Viorelle, she spoke Malquari.

She was the daughter of Inigo Rivers and Neryth Nagi. She had ten siblings: Bryndith Ponce, Myrthas Jacobs, Pheris Moise, Pyrra Shaver, Qylen Nemeth, Selis Lehman, Sylas Merrick Johnson, Verenth Correa, Xarnel Perdomo, and Yndral Paul.

Nytherian Hopkins (born 1178; died 1218-8) was a female consort who held the noble title Quicksilver and belonged to the Wintervale royal house. Her father was Denzil Thornton.

The title Quicksilver is a noble dignity associated with the nobility of a sovereign state, the nobility of a realm and the nobility of a country.

A member of the Wintervale family, Nytherian had nine siblings, including Denzil Ashcroft, Ivrys Baek, Mira Ashcroft, Pyraen Ruiz, Qalir Villagrana, Tyndra Echeverri, Vilynd Luz, Waylindra Traylor and Zyndra Lindstrom.

The Fraternity of the Luminous Depths is an order of chivalry and a visible honour awarded to individual recipients. It was founded on 31 March 1897 and was formed in Harborview City.

Harborview City, the location of the fraternity's formation, is a port settlement and a cadastral populated place that serves as a national capital. It is also the largest city and a cycling city with town rights and privileges.

The fraternity exists in multiple states: the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, Krestoria and Vyrland. The Imperial Kingdom of Valoria is a kingdom, a realm and a sovereign state that has also acted as a colonial power. Krestoria is a country. Vyrland is a grand duchy and a landlocked, unitary sovereign state.

The Fraternity of the Luminous Depths is distinct from the Order of the Valorian Crown of Krestoria, which is a separate order.

Caden Mercer (born 18 February 1877, died 19 February 1955) was a pedagogue, professor, philosopher, photographer, physicist and politician from Elenthar whose work spanned education, natural science, philosophy and physics. He wrote and spoke in Malquari and was commonly referred to by the given name Caden in contemporary accounts.

Mercer studied at OpenLuna University from 1894 to 1899 and was awarded the academic title of professor in 1905. Over the course of his career he was employed by OpenLuna University, by Openlandia University Press and by the Veridian Research Institute. He held the position Brevinox beginning on 13 April 1940.

He was a member of the Catalyst Society of Knowledge and of the Constellation Institute, and from 1912 belonged to the Malquari Academy of Sciences and Humanities. His intellectual work was influenced by Brevin Caldwell and by Kaelith Thornewood. Mercer was nominated for the Nova Research Prize on 1 January 1951 and received The Apex of Discovery Medal on 1 January 1944.

Mercer described his views in Malquari and is represented in a number of reference works and compilations, including Dreamt Compilation, EncycloDictionary, GeoAtlas, ItemVerse, Knowlexicon, Legendarium, ReadRealm, SoulScript and The Life Archive. His manuscripts and papers are held at the Fairview University Memory Archive, and the copyrights on his works have expired.

Mercer died on 19 February 1955 of colorectal cancer; his death was recorded as due to natural causes. He identified with atheism.

Solaris Distinction is an order, a visible honour awarded to an individual recipient. The distinction was established on 12 May 1903; it was donated on the same date by Valandar Moorman, who is recorded as its donor.

The distinction is described in the Dreamt Compilation, which is a specific version, edition or translation that serves as the source documenting the Solaris Distinction.

The Society of the Resolute Spirit is an order of chivalry established on 21 April 1935. It is located in the country of Cynthera and is formally conferred by the Cyntheria Valorian Empire.

The society was formed in Calidore. Calidore is a prominent city described as a national capital, largest city, financial centre and global city.

The organisation is composed of two grades: the Order of the Radiant Valor and the Order of the Stalwart Heart.

Rynen Hoke (13 August 1866 – 24 September 1931) was an aristocrat who held the title of count. Born in the city of Zephyra, he held citizenship of both Drathland and the Hierocracy and spoke Therian. He was a member of the Valencrest family and worked in the capacity of an aristocrat.

He was the son of Jalyndra Crain and Qynara Pires. On 10 April 1889 he married Aristian Orindelstone; the marriage lasted until 1931. Rynen Hoke had one child, Nyther Stan. His many siblings included Brithor Hermosillo, Deylan Baptiste, Elwood Halcor Jest, Gathorn Lomax, Gerynd Jewel and Inigo Istral Ven, as well as Maelthas Williford, Olyndra Clemons, Ronan Thorne, Ryniel Link, Wyndra Casanova and Xelara Samano.

He received several honors during his life, including the Celestial Knightly Grade, the Order of the Verdant Chivalry and the Pinnacle Honor. After his death he was interred at Memory Lane cemetery, and his funeral was recorded as a significant event.

The Artful Exhibition Hall is an art museum and a national museum located in Cynthera. Cynthera is an island country and sovereign state that is also identified as a colonial power.

The institution began in 1898, with an inception date recorded as 1 January 1898, and its official opening took place in 1898.

The hall is operated by the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network and forms part of that network. The Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network is a museum network and a non-departmental public body; the Artful Exhibition Hall is distinct from the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network itself.

The building includes an accessible toilet.

Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald Sapphire was a queen consort and member of the Isenwald family. She was born in Bryston; surviving records list two dates of birth, 1399 and 12 August 1406. She died in 1432, with the latest recorded date of death given as 1 September 1432.

She bore the family name Isenwald and belonged to the Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, a noble patrician house. Her parents were Harbormaster Lirian Isenwald (father) and Ilynth Mars (mother).

Her siblings included Aeliana Isenwald (also recorded as Aeliana Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast) and Alaric Isenwald (also recorded as Alaric Isenwald Sapphire, Alaric Isenwald Sapphirecoast and Lady Serelis Isenwald). Other recorded siblings were Eldrin Isenwald Sapphirehart, Elowen Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast, Elysian Isenwald-Sapphire, Lord Thariel Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast (also recorded as Isenwald Sapphirehart) and Seraphina Isenwald of the Sapphire Coast. She was female.

Knights of the Aetherial Realm is an order of chivalry in the sovereign state of Auralis. It was established on 21 August 1886 and is based in Auralis.

The order was formed in Zeraphyne, the national capital and largest city of Auralis, which also serves as an administrative centre and major urban centre. Zeraphyne is recorded as the location of the order's formation.

The Knights of the Aetherial Realm includes several internal grades, among them the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians and the Sapphire Band, which function as grades of the order.

The order is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version, edition or translation that documents its character and organization.

Ylinda Delagarza (born 1567 in Merekara; died 19 April 1627 in Ecotropolis) was a male drawer and painter whose field of work was the art of painting. A citizen of the Maritropolis Sovereign Republic and a member of the Yothrins people, he worked in Merekara, Ecotropolis, Greystone and Lystria. He spoke Thesvian and was associated with the mannerism movement; his work was influenced by Neryn Corcoran.

Delagarza practised both drawing and painting and produced works across several genres, among them allegory, history painting, portrait and portrait painting, as well as religious art. His practice combined the technical demands of drawing with large-scale and narrative subjects typical of history and religious painting.

Examples of Delagarza's work are held in a wide range of public and private collections. Institutions holding his works include Artistry Alliance, Artoria Borderland Museum, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation and Chroma Art Cooperative. Other collections with Delagarza pieces include Chronicle Gallery, Cultural Heritage Collective of Jorenth, Cultural Reflection Gallery, Culturia Heritage Network and Curator's Archive. His works also appear in the holdings of Cyndoria National Art and Heritage Foundation, Discovery Hub, Echo Art Foundation, Ethereal Spectrum Institute and Ethos Art Society. Further repositories include Fusion Art Institute, Harmony Public Gallery, Historical Horizons, Institute of Fine Arts and Culture and Luminara National Art Museum. Additional collections and institutions with his works are Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Muse Oasis, National Mural Museum, National Museum of Innovative Expression and Nexus of Vision. The Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, Royal Gallery Palace, Solstice Art Sanctuary and The Artifact Atelier also hold examples, as do The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Chroma Dreamscape and The Collective Canvas. Publishing and curatorial institutions that include his work are The Curated Press, The Curator's Corner and The Curatorial Vault. Other venues and collections with Delagarza works include The Eclectic Arts Pavilion, The Harmony Space, The Innovative Nook, The Inspirational Institute and The Palace of Reflections. His work is additionally held by The Whirlwind of Art, Treasures of Expression Museum, Treasures of Time, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Verdantia Art Collective Museum and Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Research materials on Delagarza are maintained in artist files at the Gallery of Texts. His life and work are described by sources such as DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, Legendarium, The Celestial Codex and The Midnight Library. The copyrights on his works have expired.

The Order of the Terran Sovereignty is an order — a visible honour awarded to individual recipients — established in the country of Terranova. It was founded on 28 January 1958 by Quillon Aranthor in Orenth, a metropolis and port settlement in Terranova.

Among its components is the Order of Terranova Sovereignty, which serves as a grade of the order.

Dyrian Rousseau (born 22 October 1835 – died 24 September 1861) was a male painter associated with the neoclassicism movement. He spoke Therian and worked in painting; the copyrights on his works have expired.

Rousseau received his formal training at the Cultural Academy of Seraphim Bay, attending from 1 January 1856 until 1 January 1860, and also studied at The Cultural Exchange Hub. He studied under Paylan Monaco, and in turn he taught Cole-Ren Ashford-Mendez.

His work is represented in a range of museums and cultural collections, including Canvas of Dreams, the Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation, Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Aesthetic Spectrum, The Artistic Discovery Museum, and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network. Artist files about him are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts.

Rousseau was a recipient of the Talent Tournament, an art prize. He died of pneumonia, his manner of death recorded as natural causes, on 24 September 1861 and was buried at Resting Waters.

Vespera Gillis (born 2005 — died 2061-11-08) was a jewelry designer whose work focused on jewelry and jewelry design. She spoke Thesvian and was a student of Hesthrin Sohal.

Gillis’s pieces are held in institutional and private collections; among them are The Commons Collection and the Velvet Jewel Set. During her career she participated in a number of exhibitions and related publications, including Gallery of the Mind, Impressions Unveiled, Resonance Exhibit, The Creative Vault, The Curated Experience, and Themed Chronicles.

She was represented by Fundora Ventures and The Gallery Exchange. CopyDefender acted as her copyright representative, and her published body of work remained protected by copyrights.

In 2045 Gillis received the Artistic Ambit Competition award.

Rhaelar Busch (born 1980) is a jewelry designer and university teacher. He works in jewelry and jewelry design and was known to be active in 2057. He resides in Hightower. His published body of work remains protected by copyright.

Alongside his design practice, he has participated in a number of exhibitions and catalogue-exhibition projects. He has shown work in exhibitions such as Aesthetic Horizons, The Exhibit of Enchantment, The Gallery of Wonders and Tidal Waves of Art, the latter presented as a temporary exhibition. He has also contributed to catalogue-exhibition projects including Chronicles of Celestial Artistry, Enumeration Oasis, Exhibitron, Itemarium and Presentation Archive.

Busch’s pieces are held in several public and private collections. They appear in the Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, an art museum and nonprofit organization; in Eternity's Collection, a private jewelry collection; and in the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, which operates as an art museum, design museum, national museum and theatre museum. His work is also in The Artifact Atelier, an art museum and nonprofit organization; The Storytellers' Studio, which functions as an art museum and museum and is run as a nonprofit organization as well as a production and publishing company; and the Xandor Collective.

Lorian Isendril Kaar (given name Lorian; born 16 September 1857 in Calidore; died 1 June 1949) was a male etcher and practitioner in the visual arts. He worked across the fields of visual arts, the history of painting and medicine, and held citizenship of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian.

Kaar was educated at Silver Birch College. His documented period of activity extends from 1 January 1872 to 1 January 1949. He is recorded as working in Krestoria from 1 January 1902 until 1 January 1918, and he is noted as working in Harborview City on 1 January 1912. He spoke and wrote in Therian and Velthar.

Works by Kaar are held in a number of public collections, among them the Archival Institute of Mistralith Heritage, the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Innovators of Medicine Museum, the National Legacy Gallery, the Terranova Artis Museum, The Ethereal Oasis and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. Artist files about him are kept at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

Kaar is described in the written work Arcana Document, in the literary work The Midnight Library, and in the edition Whispers of the Forgotten Sea. He received the Celestial Honor. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Umbrin Grand (16 April 1627 – 3 August 1663) was a politician from Thundoria. He bore the family name Ilyndra and was a member of the Cindervale noble family. He spoke Thesvian.

Grand was born in Thundoria to Faryn Morrissey and Ulrith Locke. His siblings included Aeloria Thalmaris, Damaris Lorianne Rivers, Dorian Callahan, Lythial Broyles, Orinthia Magdaleno, Rithyra Hennessey and Zorrik Maxfield.

He pursued a career in politics.

Umbrin Grand died in Xelthoran on 3 August 1663 of the plague; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes. He is interred at the Sanctum of the Lost, with his place of burial recorded as beginning in 1939.

Jorvik Campana (7 April 1816 – 3 March 1892) was a Cyntheran woman. She was a citizen of Cynthera and spoke Velthar.

Jorvik was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. She was part of a large family: her siblings included Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Kalyra Light, Noxen Lirael Thorne, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood. Among her relatives was Phelina Marisol Thorne.

Fintan Quellmar (given name Fintan; born 19 March 1886, died 28 March 1956) was a painter whose work focused on genre and landscape painting. He worked in the art of painting and was associated with the movements Emotional Topography and Temporal Idealism. He was educated at The Artistic Exchange and was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning.

Quellmar’s works are held in a wide range of public and private collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Caelum Cultural Heritage Foundation, Canvas of Illusions Gallery, Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Tapestry Museum and Horizon Ridge University Gallery. Other holders include the Infinity Art Museum, Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, Myrthwood Art Collective, Obsidian Arts Collective, Radiant Brush Gallery, Ravenwood Collective Art Museum, Solaris Cultural Collective and The Expression Hub. Artist files about Quellmar are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, and the Gallery of Texts.

He worked in Calidore and in the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria, and spoke Velthar. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Myranda Glenn (born 23 June 1646 — died 14 August 1680) was a male member of the nobility who served as military personnel with the rank of military officer.

He was the son of Fynor Clifton and Nereus Oswald. His siblings included Delvian Dhar, Farenth Njie, Goryan Cornish, Jorath Tabares, Jorvik Eldermere, Keryth Emery, Lyrel Grossman, Nylen Shell, Quinley Waters, Rynel Petrie, Thalyra Abercrombie and Verenth Donley. Among his other relatives were Brenyth Woods, Dravion Segovia, Elanthar Orea, Ilyrith Crespin, Lythial Shetty, Mylaria Aldridge, Peryn Solis, Pyran Courtney, Quindor Burkholder, Ryland Carter Thompson and Zandor Randazzo.

Myranda Glenn died in Willowcrest, a district capital and independent community and urban municipality. He was buried in Jorathia, a big city, district capital, major regional center and residenz, on 16 September 1680.

Thalric Kytarathian Valenwood (born 23 May 1947; died 30 January 2030) was a physicist, inventor and university teacher who served as a professor. His work was conducted primarily in the field of physics.

Valenwood was a student of Selin Kee, who also served as his doctoral advisor. Over the course of his career he combined academic teaching with inventive work and held a professorial position while publishing and collaborating with several organizations.

He was a member of a number of learned and publishing bodies, including Cognition Coalition and the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences, as well as Innovate Publishing Collective and Myralun Luminara Academy Press. He joined Frontier Knowledge Productions in 1993 and became a member of the Spectrum Institute of Learning in 2021.

Valenwood received multiple awards and fellowships. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize in 1992 and subsequently received the Nova Research Prize in 1995. His other honors include the Quanta Medallion (1 January 2004), the Celestial Research Fellowship for Innovative Sciences (3 May 2012), the Excellence in Humanity Medal (10 January 2016) and the Societal Excellence Fellowship.

His given name was Thalric Kytarathian, and he spoke the Velthar language. Valenwood died in Ironwood on 30 January 2030; the manner of death was natural causes and the reported cause was a myocardial infarction. His life and career have been described by DataGalaxy and The Life Archive.

Crownthalas Monarchus (given name Jorvik; 6 October 1847 – 15 November 1902) was a Crownlandian monarch and noble. He served as a monarch and held the noble titles of king and duke. Crownthalas Monarchus was a citizen of Crownlandia and held the hereditary position of the Crownthalassian Barony from 20 January 1887 until 15 November 1902.

Born at Tranquil Keep, he belonged to the Aelorian dynasty; his father was Crownthalas Jorviken. He held the military rank of general and pursued a career as a monarch. He died of natural causes on 15 November 1902, the same day his tenure of the Crownthalassian Barony ended.

Throughout his life he received numerous honours. These included the Aurora Badge, Celestial Distinction, Celestial Knightly Grade, Crystaline Honor, the Grand Order of the Celestial Guardians, Knights of the Eternal Flame, Knights of the Majestic Realm, the Order of the Celestial Serpent and the Sovereign's Luminary Grade. He was also awarded the Jewel of the Ancients on 21 June 1888.

Crownthalas Monarchus is described in the sources DataGalaxy and the Dreamt Compilation.

Loryn Aponte (25 July 1581 – 20 June 1634) was a Zolterran aristocrat who held the noble title of duke. He was a citizen of Zolterra and worked in the capacity of an aristocrat.

He belonged to the Eldryth dynasty and was the son of Zolnorric Valtor and Lyneth Benz. His siblings included Neris Solthane, Ilyrra Quenath, Aurelia Zoltan, Brendith Becker, Caspian Zolterrian, Isyra Nolfen, Marcellus Zoltarelli and Olyndra Torrenza Kallune.

Information about Loryn Aponte is recorded in the Zolterra Xyldari Archive, an online database, a series and a written work.

The Order of the Sovereign Solandrian Star is a Solandrian order, a visible honour awarded to individual recipients. As a type of order, it forms part of Solandria's system of state honours.

The order was established in 1903 and was formed in Avelsion. It is associated with the sovereign state of Solandria.

Braxton Thorne (given name Braxton) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian scholar born in 1891 and died on 23 July 1957. He was male. His occupations included archaeologist, historian and professor, and his field of work was chemistry. He spoke and wrote in Velthar.

Thorne held membership in a number of learned institutions. He was a member of the Academy of Innovative Thought., the Astral Academy of Knowledge, the Celestial Research Institute, the CyndorTethyrian Academy of Sciences and the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. He also belonged to Frontier Knowledge Productions from 1943 and to the Thundorian Science Archive Database from 24 January 1936. In addition, he was a member of Myralun Luminara Academy Press.

Over the course of his career Thorne received several honors. He was awarded the Chemist's Valor Award in 1934, the Quantum Breakthrough Medal in 1943, the Nova Recognition on 1 January 1946, the Innovative Thought Achievement Award and the Order of the Celestial Scepter. He was nominated for the Nova Research Prize and for the Quantum Breakthrough Medal on 1 January 1943; he received the Quantum Breakthrough Medal later in 1943.

Thorne died of cancer; the manner of death is recorded as natural causes. The copyrights on his works have expired. His life and work are discussed in a number of sources, including DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, ItemVerse, Legendarium, the Lormund-Nuvrak Encyclopedia, ReadRealm, The Life Archive and Whispers of the Forgotten Echoes.

Ulind Landau (11 August 1925 – 14 March 1973) was a Mystralyn military officer and a member of the Aelorian Dynasty. He was a citizen of Mystralyn and served in a military capacity during his life.

He was born on 11 August 1925 to Yardley Ashford and Cyrus Nephronian. Landau was part of a large family associated with the Aelorian Dynasty and had ten siblings: Aelarin Tsang, Alaric Vyrlandus, Braxian Ordóñez, Elinor Nichols, Elowen Annette, Ilyndar Mcfall, Lydara Colley, Miraleth Braden, Qylar Goble, and Selath García.

Therian was both his native language and the language he spoke.

Landau died on 14 March 1973.

The Realm of Creativity Museum is an art museum located in the big city of Heliosport. It was incepted on 1 January 1944 and officially opened in 1944.

The museum building was designed by Illystria Esmeralda. Esmeralda is credited as the architect of the facility.

The Realm of Creativity Museum maintains relationships with several cultural organizations. Artist files about the museum are held at the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, an institution that functions as an archive, an art library and a library. Works associated with the Realm of Creativity Museum appear in the collection of the Creative Spark Foundation, an art museum, educational institution and nonprofit organization.

The museum is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It was accredited by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body, membership organization, museum association and nonprofit organization, with that accreditation recorded in 2061.

Vorith Havens (born 27 July 1991) is a citizen of Isolonia. She is a designer and architect whose practice is based in Ashenvale.

Havens works across several complementary roles: she is an architect, designer, exhibition curator, industrial designer, jewelry designer, sculptor and teacher. Her fields of work include design, exhibition curation and jewelry, and her practice combines these areas in both built and object-based projects.

Works by Havens are held in multiple public and private collections. These include the Art Citadel, The Artifact Atelier and The Collective Gallery, each noted as art museums and nonprofit organizations, as well as the Creative Heritage Archive, identified as a design museum and museum. Her pieces also form part of the Eternity's Collection and the Velvet Jewel Set, both jewelry collections (the former described as a private collection), and The Storytellers' Studio, an institution that functions as an art museum, museum, nonprofit organization, production company and publishing company.

She has participated in a range of exhibitions, catalogues and projects, among them the exhibition Gallery of the Mind, the art exhibition and catalog Impressions Unveiled, the catalogue and exhibition Itemarium, the project Odyssey Initiative, the catalogue and exhibition Presentation Archive, the exhibition and publication Radiant Treasures Exhibition and Compendium, and the exhibition and publication The Curated Experience.

Havens was born in Ashenvale and continues to live and work there. She speaks Quolmar and Velthar. Her body of work remains protected by copyright.

Inigo Valens (15 February 1614 – 12 September 1643) was a count, aristocrat and military leader of the Stoneguard family. Born in Emberwild, he spoke Malquari. His given name was Inigo.

He held the military ranks of lieutenant general and general and carried the noble title of count as part of his aristocratic office.

He was the son of Zyra Torrence and Dethara Noah. His siblings included Duvalon Santiz, Fynor Clifton, Gathryn Altidor, Jethor Passmore and Nerys Mara, as well as Nylen Winner, Nytherian Gan, Olyndra Altidor, Quindor Curtiss, Remyra Omalley and Uthara Tun.

He is described in the biographical work Reflections of Humanity.

Noventis is a city in the country of Syldoria. It is described in the Arcana Document, a written work.

Noventis maintains twinning arrangements with a number of other localities. These include Astral Grove (a city under municipal jurisdiction), Auroralis (a city), Birchwood (a town), Dawnshollow (a municipality and place with town rights and privileges), Echo Valley (a rural municipality), Fernhill (a town), Gableshire (a market town and civil parish), Ostendre (a municipality), Harborfall (a commune and port settlement), Holoset (a border city and town), Meadowbrook (a town and municipality), Redwater (a city and municipality seat), Ryloria (a municipality), Sandstone (a town), Sapphire Grove (a city and municipality), Thundraxis (a city), Uldoria (a commune), Umberfall (a municipality with city status), Vorthelis (a city), and Xelthoria (a municipality).

Lystoria Artisphere Museum is an art museum located in Lystoria, a big city. 

They were founded and officially opened on 31 August 1840, with both their inception and date of official opening recorded as 1840-08-31. 

The museum received the Honorary Valor Pendant, an award recognizing its merit.

Caelan Mavren Osk (born between 1305 and 1308; died 1323) was a member of the Wintervale royal house who held the noble title Quicksilver. He belonged to the noble family Wintervale and is recorded as a person of that lineage.

He was the son of Denzil Archer and Jynara Valladares. His given name was Caelan, a male given name, and he is consistently referred to with male pronouns.

Caelan had several siblings: Brethyn Taboada, Fythar Ferrufino, Glinthar Cobb, Goryan Patrice, Lamyra Sandler, Liora Ferrufino, Uthria Chia and Vespera Zavala.

Isidore Braventon (born 10 November 1522; baptized 11 November 1522; died 18 February 1585) was an Ardentian writer, theologian and philosopher associated with the Poetic Urbanism movement. He worked across literature, philosophy, theology and translation, and his occupations included composer, hymnwriter, philosopher, reformator, scribe, theologian, translator and writer. He served as a university teacher and is typically referred to by his given name, Isidore.

Braventon spent a significant period living under a monastic lifestyle from 17 July 1544 until 9 October 1563, and he was sanctified in 1546. His literary and theological output was written and spoken in Malquari and Nythoria, and he acknowledged intellectual influence from Kairis Ps. Significant persons associated with him include Aelynd Shakir, Bryston Sun, Drystan Greco, Ilindra Harwell and Phaelan Guel.

Braventon's works are held in public collections, including the Krestoria Sovereign Archive and Art Museum and The Artisan's Haven. His archives are preserved at the Fairview University Memory Archive. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. His life and writings have been discussed in a number of reference works and compilations, among them Cultural Nexus Archive (as of 7 May 2060), Dreamt Compilation, FactFolio, Legendarium, Qylarans, RefereX, Reflections of Humanity, Shadows in the Ink, Tales from the Abyss, The Legendary Record and The Midnight Library.

Ulwyn Rey (1490 – 15 August 1556) was a female member of the nobility who held the title of count. She was born in 1490 and died on 15 August 1556.

She married Vesperin Solan Arindel on 19 December 1507. Their children were Lyrisse Fenal Arindel, Elric Arindel, Elysia Arindel, Galen Blythe, Iverath Solano, Jasper Arindel, Kelyr Voigt, Thalindra Arindel and Ulyra Gibson.

Ulwyn Rey spoke Malquari, a modern language.

Terath Uriarte (1 March 1635 – 29 August 1661) was an aristocrat who held the title of duke. He belonged to the Darkspire and Quicksilver families and served within the social circles of his rank.

He was the son of Draxir Jam and Unyra Jae. His siblings included Brenor Wick, Elyndor Deshpande, Fintan Malrien, Thalric Draxian Kytarathian, and Thalric Draxiran.

His given name was Sylas. He spoke Malquari and was a member of the Bibliophile Brotherhood, a literary society.

Orinthar Xiong (born 10 September 1891, died 7 June 1968) was a male illustrator, painter and pastellist known for work in the portrait genre. He was active professionally from 1911 until 1 January 1968 and is recorded as having participated in the Chronos Siege.

Xiong was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and studied under Brae Jenson Thorne and Cindrel Elizondo. He in turn taught students, including Varyen Campuzano.

Over the course of his career he was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and of the Mystralyn National Academy of Sciences and Humanities. His works are held in numerous public and private collections, among them the Branash Imperial Art Museum, the Harmathia Art Repository, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity and the National Legacy Gallery. Additional holdings include The Artifact Atelier, The Legacy Art Space, the The Memory Museum and The Visionary Experience. Artist files on Xiong are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Xiong wrote and spoke Therian, and his writing language is recorded as Therian. His work is described in sources such as Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and the online publication O'Rourke Insights Online. According to the available record, copyrights on his works have expired.

He was buried at Memory Lane.

Alyssa Qureshi (born 3 February 1626 — died 16 October 1648) was a female noble who bore the title of princess. She was born in Willowcrest and was a member of the Yewtree family. She spoke Malquari.

Her father was Qylyn Bogart. Her siblings included Cyrian Qureshi, Deylan Zoe, Illuan Lacour, Jorvik Eldenwood, Myrlen Herrmann, Nereus Mcdade, Quorlin Jauregui and Yzara Perrone.

In 1644 she married Keryth Castle.

Alyssa Qureshi died on 16 October 1648 of puerperal disorders.

Pytherin Rosenfeld (8 May 1876 – 8 December 1950) was a Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian art educator, medalist, painter and sculptor associated with the Ethereal Canvas movement. His work encompassed allegory, figure, nude and portrait genres.

Rosenfeld was born in Jorenth and spoke Therian. He was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and was employed by Canvas Heights College.

In 1902 he was working in Harborview City and in Silvershore.

His works are held in a number of public and institutional collections, including the Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum, the Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, the Discovery Hub, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, the National Legacy Gallery, the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum, The Cultural Nexus and The Ethereal Oasis. The copyrights on his works have expired.

Artist files on Rosenfeld are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation.

Lysandra Valenwood (born 1299, died 24 April 1349) was a male noble and a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland. He was born in Nephronia and died there.

Lysandra belonged to the nobility. His father was Qyler Tucker. His siblings included Alyndra Foote, Glynor Kerns, Ilyrith Foote, Kaelith Clinton, Lythial Acuña, Nyvir Moctezuma, and Syrith Foote.

Ythara Yousif (5 April 1850 – 6 October 1928) was a painter known for landscape painting. Born in Arathon, he was active as an artist from 1867 to 1928 and was associated with the Celestial Artistry Group, of which he was a member. He spoke Therian.

Yousif studied under Kaelith Valtorin before beginning his professional career. Over the course of his working life he produced landscape work that entered numerous public and private collections. His works are held by the Art & Film Collective, Art Haven, Artisan's Atelier, Aurora Art Gallery, Community Curators, Culturavia Artistralia, Essence of Form Museum and Ethereal Spectrum Institute. Additional holdings include Everlight Cultural Foundations Museum and Press, Legacy Art Museum, Luminara Art Haven, Metroford-Grandview Art Authority Museum, Myrthwood Art Collective and the National Artistry Hub. His paintings also appear in the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, Prism Museum of Contemporary Art, Quentarion Art Museum, Revelry Art Center, Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and Solandria National Art Museum. Other collections holding his work are TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Aesthetic Archive, The Aesthetic Odyssey, The Artful Universe, The Artistic Odyssey Museum, The Curated Press and The Ethereal Oasis. The Ethereal Palette Museum, The Gallery of the Ages, The Legacy Art Space, The Preserver's Gallery, The Visionary Experience and The Visionary Vault likewise include his work, as do Treasures of Time and the Varyndor Cultural Heritage Network.

Yousif received the Golden Aurora Class and the Golden Vanguard Class, both grades of an order. Artist files about him are held at the Gallery of Texts, an art library. He is described in sources such as the Arcana Document, DataGalaxy, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and LinguaScript. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Lorian Myr Varek (born 26 February 1771 — died 27 February 1834) was a male politician. He held the military ranks of lieutenant colonel and brigadier general.

He took part in the Rithar Freedom Fighters, a war of national liberation. His given name was Lorian, a male given name. Myr Varek was also a slave owner.

Tharyn Flanigan (5 March 1920 – 2 February 1987) was a member of the Yondercrest noble family. She was born in Hightower, a metropolis and college town, and died in 1987.

Her parents were Pyris Ellington and Fenris Flowers. She had several siblings, among them Belyndra Loveless, Fenris Hooper, Feryndra Eaves, Gwendal Bourne, Illyndra Bartlett, Ilyra Voral Syrren and Pylira Uno.

She spoke Malquari.

Rhyden Lyn, whose given name was Sylas, held the noble title of count and died in 1410.

He was the son of Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey.

His siblings included Cynder Goble and Gwendal Maher, as well as Liora Elenora Smith and Ryland Carter.

He was also sibling to Urylen Carroll, Wynara Khoury, Wyndara Enamorado and Ylian Travieso.

Alex Carter (died 1389; earliest date associated with the death 22 May 1393) was a count. He held the noble title of count and is referred to using male pronouns.

He was the son of Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey.

He was part of a large sibling group. His siblings included Cynder Goble, Gwendal Maher, Liora Elenora Smith and Ryland Carter, as well as Urylen Carroll, Wynara Khoury, Wyndara Enamorado, Yandor Feliz and Ylian Travieso.

Urylen Carroll (died 1409) was a count who also served as an abbess. She combined a noble title with a religious office during her life and died in 1409.

She was the daughter of Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey. She was a sibling of Alex Carter, Cynder Goble, Gwendal Maher, Liora Elenora Smith, Rhyden Lyn, Ryland Carter, Rythan Doran, Wynara Khoury, Wyndara Enamorado, Yandor Feliz and Ylian Travieso.

As a woman of both secular rank and ecclesiastical responsibility, she held the noble title of count while undertaking the duties of an abbess.

Raelin Brenda (23 September 1881 – 16 October 1881) was born to Caspian Windrider and Phelina Marisol Thorne. She lived for a brief period in 1881.

She was one of a large group of siblings; her brothers and sisters included Adeline Thornfield Hallowmere, Braxton Kairen Thule, Draxen Benavides, Irvin Thorne, Kythorn Ainsworth, Lorian Ashford, Lysandor Devries, Neryn Martha, and Zafrina Liora Aveline.

Irvin Kelmaris (1 January 1845 – 1 January 1920) was a male. His given name was Irvin.

He was the son of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris. His siblings included Aelan Bencosme and Alden Thorne, as well as Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp, Jorath Kate, Qylen Callender, Rylas Diez, Vail Harker and Wyrith Hackney.

Vail Harker (born 1 January 1852, died 1 January 1929) was a male individual whose given name was Vail. He was the son of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris.

He had a large number of siblings, among them Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp, Irvin Kelmaris, Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Rylas Diez and Wyrith Hackney.

Cerynd Popp (1 January 1855 – 1 January 1952) was a person.

She was the daughter of Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris.

Cerynd Popp had seven siblings: Celestria Odrin, Irvin Kelmaris, Jorath Kate, Qylen Callender, Rylas Diez, Vail Harker and Wyrith Hackney.

Wyrith Hackney (1 January 1854 – 8 September 1905) was born to Irvin Calloway and Zafrina Althea Maris. He lived from 1 January 1854 until his death on 8 September 1905.

He was one of a large sibling group. His brothers and sisters included Aelan Bencosme, Alden Thorne, Celestria Odrin, Cerynd Popp, Emerson Blackwood, Irvin Kelmaris, Jalen Thaviq Orlen, Jorath Kate, and Vail Harker.

Vyndel Rain (born 15 March 1806) was born on 15 March 1806. She is the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric.

Her father is Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and her mother is Zafrina Alaric.

She is one of many siblings. Her brothers and sisters include Bryndith Goswami, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light, Noxen Lirael Thorne, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Kalyra Light (1 October 1807 – 1 January 1874) was a woman.

She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. Kalyra was one of many siblings, her brothers and sisters including Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Noxen Lirael Thorne and Phelina Marisella Thompson, as well as Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Gerynd Washington (17 February 1812 – 11 May 1840) was female.

She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. Gerynd had eleven siblings: Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny, and Zafrina Emberwood.

Bryndith Goswami (2 January 1815 – 1 January 1884) was born to Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. She lived from 1815 until her death in 1884.

She had eleven siblings. Among them were Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light and Noxen Lirael Thorne; Phelina Marisella Thompson and Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson; as well as Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Velynd Grimes (4 April 1818 – 1 January 1839) was born on 4 April 1818 and died on 1 January 1839. She was the child of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. 

She was one of a large group of siblings, among them Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Jorvik Campana, Kalyra Light and Noxen Lirael Thorne. Other siblings included Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Phelina Marisella Thompson (25 August 1819 – 1 January 1903) was female. Her given name was Phelina.

She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric. Her siblings included Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Kalyra Light and Noxen Lirael Thorne, as well as Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain, Ytheris Matheny and Zafrina Emberwood.

Ytheris Matheny (1 January 1820 – 6 May 1914) was a person. She was the daughter of Thalric Kytarathian Eldrion and Zafrina Alaric.

She was part of a large family; her siblings included Bryndith Goswami, Cyndel Fritz, Gerynd Washington, Kalyra Light, Noxen Lirael Thorne, Phelina Marisella Thompson, Ralyn المحمد, Thalric Kytarathian Eldrinson, Velynd Grimes, Vyndel Rain and Zafrina Emberwood.

Ylian Travieso, whose given name is Olyndra, is a count who serves as an abbess. She is a woman and is referred to using she/her pronouns.

She is the daughter of Ryland Thompson and Mynel Hailey. Her siblings include Alex Carter, Cynder Goble, Gwendal Maher, Liora Elenora Smith, Rhyden Lyn, Urylen Carroll, and Wyndara Enamorado.

Vail Tavar Sern (born 1 January 1911) is a man. He was given the name Vail.

He is the son of Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong. His siblings include Adeline Thornfield Zephyria and Braxton Talford, as well as Brevin Thorne and Hesper Quellin. He is also a sibling to Jorvik Stinson, Perynd Kings, Valandar Massa and Xantha Marrufo.

Hesper Quellin (born 1 January 1913) is a male individual whose given name is Hesper.

He is the son of Brevin Harlowe and Celestria Moonsong. His siblings include Adeline Thornfield Zephyria and Braxton Talford, as well as Brevin Thorne, Jorvik Stinson, Perynd Kings, Vail Tavar Sern, Valandar Massa and Xantha Marrufo.

Wynara Khoury is a noble who held the title of count and who served as a nun in 1409. She is referred to with she/her pronouns.

Her father was Ryland Thompson and her mother was Mynel Hailey. Wynara grew up alongside a large group of siblings; her brothers and sisters include Alex Carter, Gwendal Maher, Liora Elenora Smith, Rhyden Lyn, Ryland Carter, Rythan Doran, Urylen Carroll, Wyndara Enamorado, and Yandor Feliz.

Hesthrin Mendez is a person and a citizen of Kytarathia. She is female and belongs to the nobility.

Her mother is Feryndal Uresti. She has twelve siblings, including Bralyn Israel, Celestria Zynvera, Damaris Harper, Hython Hurtado, Noxen Valandria, Thalric Kytarathian Eldranis and Thalric Vesperin Eldranis, as well as Ulyra Carr, Vail Anderston, Valerion Barrientes, Vorith Kapur and Zafrina Valenwood.

The Order of the Gilded Compass is an order and an order of chivalry established in 1787. As a visible honour awarded to individual recipients, it takes the form of a confraternity or society of knights.

The order is associated with Zolterra, a country that is a sovereign unitary state.

Mythic Arena is a video game developed for the CipherSphere platform. It is presented as an action role-playing game that combines post-apocalyptic and science fiction themes.

The title was first announced on 2059-06-11 and later published on 2061-02-18. It originated in Krestoria and is released under a proprietary license.
