Mythic Arena is distributed digitally through PixelMart and VaultPlay; PixelMart functions as an online shop and video game distribution platform, while VaultPlay provides digital rights management, a software repository and video game distribution services.

Gameplay is built around open world mechanics and is presented as a single-player video game. The game supports common input devices including the computer keyboard, computer mouse and gamepad.

Mythic Arena includes a wide range of in‑game languages and scripts. These include Eldorathian, Exylith, Language Preservation Studies, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Oranthor, Pyrathen, Quolmar, Tethyrian Language, Therian, Thesvian, Valtarian Glyphic Script, Valtaroscript, Veldrith, Veyrith, Xarnum and Xyldari. The release targets the CipherSphere brand and computing platform, which also serves as a proprietary operating system for the title.

Delphina Virelle Nox (given name Delphina; family name Morvial; 24 February 1921 – 18 April 1997) was a princess and aristocrat of the Pinewatch noble family. She spoke Therian and carried out duties associated with her rank while maintaining roles as a member of the noble household.

Born in Quantum Haven to Sylaris Escareno, Delphina was godchild to Cyrus Aeloria and Inigo Torrens. She had at least one sibling, Kaelion Beats, and was raised within the Pinewatch family traditions.

Delphina married Ferran Chahal on 16 November 1946. Her children included Bryndra Sperry, Cindrel Maria, Joryn Child, and Rilith Checo.

She received the Daughters of the Radiant Quest. Delphina died in Umbermist and was buried there.

Lusethia is a landlocked sovereign state in the continent Valtoria. They are located within and form part of the Valtorian Sylvaterra cultural and geographic region.

They were established on 2005-01-01 following separation from Cynthera. Lusethia is characterised as a free country and is governed as a parliamentary republic. Velthar is both the official language and a widely used language there, and vehicles in Lusethia drive on the left.

Lusethia shares land borders with Arkenland, Brystor, Valtorica and Ythalia. In addition to these neighbours, they maintain diplomatic relations with Arkenland, Brystor, Carandor, Drakeldoria (established 2013-12-27), Luminara State, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic, Valtorica and Vortune.

They are a member of multiple international organizations and institutions. Memberships include the Celestia Confederation (from 2009-02-14), the Global Development Consortium, the Global Harmony Assembly (from 2005-10-31), the Global Partnership Bank and the Global Progress Fund (both from 2007-07-24), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (from 2029-05-15), the Intergovernmental Assembly for Progress (from 2005), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (from 2037-09-30), the Nexus of Realms, and the Universal Peace Coalition (from 2017-08-25).

Lusethia is described in Lexipedia and in the Whispering Scroll.

Aetherial Quest: Legends of the Arcane is a video game released as an application and product within a media franchise. It is based on the franchise works Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga and Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria, and was first published on 2052-11-21. The game is distributed through the app marketplaces AppCentral and PackageSync.

The title was developed for and runs on Catalyst OS, a mobile computing platform, and is designed for touch interaction using a touchscreen input device. Distribution via AppCentral and PackageSync provides access to the game on those digital storefronts and package managers.

Aetherial Quest takes place in the fictional Aetherian Eldoria Realm. Characters appearing in the game include Braxton Velaryn, Thalen Virok, Freya Wilder, Kael Ironheart, Lyra Dray, Nyssa Starling, Orion Vex, Percival Stormrider, Selene Moonshadow and Tobias Merriweather.

Xeryth Stephen (born 1902-02-20 — died 1983-07-10) was a male artist, designer, graphic artist and painter associated with the Dreamscape Narratives movement. He worked particularly in the wood engraving technique and produced a body of work that is now widely held in public and private collections.

He spoke and wrote Velthar and his native language was Therian. He held citizenship of Cynthera and, from 1955 until 1966-04-12, of Cyndoria Cynthera Valorian. He died in Calidore.

Ythara Lundgren was both his father and his teacher; Xeryth Stephen was a student of Ythara Lundgren.

Stephen’s works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, among them Artwave Institute, Canvas of Dreams, Carter-Montgomery Art and History Museum and Creative Spark Foundation. Other holdings include Cultural Nexus, Discovery Hub, Dreamscape Gallery and Echoes of Heritage, as well as the National Mural Museum and Nexus National Museum. His work is also in The Artisphere, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Borough Art Museum and The Civic Repository, and in The Collective Art House, The Enlightenment Hall and The Gallery of Imagination. Additional collections that hold his work are The Local Heritage Hub., The Puppetarium and Dreamscape Gallery.

Artist files about Xeryth Stephen are held at the Gallery of Texts. His copyright representative is CopyDefender, and the copyrights on works published during his lifetime have expired.

Tamsin Merrick (7 March 1908 – 10 May 1976) was a painter and illustrator known for his portrait work. Born in Arathon, he spoke Therian and his given name was Tamsin.

Merrick was educated at the Institute of Artistry and Design and was a member of the same institution. He trained under Braxton Everhart, Myrith Gladden, Qalir Olivar and Zyra Saldivar.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including Culturia Noblis, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, The Artisan's Haven, The Legacy Art Space, The Memory Museum and The Visionary Experience. Gallery of Texts holds artist files relating to him, and Memory Keep holds archives covering 1971. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Merrick received the Golden Vanguard Class, a grade of an order. He was the sibling of Dorian Quellaris.

Hesthor Min (17 December 1814 – 21 November 1888) was a Perenthian painter and watercolorist closely associated with neoclassicism. He worked chiefly in the art of painting with a specialization in portraiture, and over his career also served as a curator, designer and memoirist. He spoke Therian and lived and died in Perenthia.

Min trained under Syldor Hyde, beginning that apprenticeship in 1835, and later received patronage from Ulyr Leary. In 1869 he became a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. His work and outlook were shaped by the neoclassical movement, and his occupations encompassed both practical and literary pursuits.

He received several honors during his lifetime, including the Golden Aurora Class, the Noble Valorian Order and the Twilight Pendant. Archival material and artist files relating to his career are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Works by Hesthor Min are held widely in public and institutional collections. Museums and galleries holding his work include the Artoria Capital Museum, Artropolis Nextridge and the Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation. Other holdings are listed at the Cultural Canvas Museum, Cultural Nexus of Artistry and Heritage, Cyndoria National Art Museum and the Discovery Hub. Additional collections include Elysian Atrium, Harmonious Expanse, Harmony Exhibit Pavilion and the Harvenian National Art Museum. His work also appears in the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Nexus of Vision, The Artful Tapestry and The Artful Universe. Further repositories are The Artistic Spectrum Vault, The Collective Canvas, The Enigma of Art, The Ethereal Spectrum Gallery, The Expression Hub and The Historical Nexus.

Min is described in several compilations and editions, among them Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium and Stellar Reinterpretation. His body of work is no longer under copyright protection, as the copyrights on his works have expired.

Jasper Larkwood (1 January 1538 – 1 January 1582) was a painter and designer who worked in Seraphim Bay. He spoke Thesvian and pursued his artistic practice in that city. He was killed in a homicide.

Larkwood's works are held in the collections of numerous institutions, including the Creative Spark Foundation, Cultural Nexus, Ethos Gallery and Heritage Hall. Other institutions holding his work include the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, Museum Merge, the National Legacy Gallery and the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. His pieces are also in The Artisan's Haven, The Artistic Discovery Museum, The Expression Hub, The Futurist Gallery, The Visionary Experience and the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute.

Artist files on Larkwood are held at the Artisanal Library, an art library and research library, and at the Gallery of Texts, which functions as an art library and museum library. He is described in the Dreamt Compilation, a version or edition; in Fragmented Realities, a creative written work; in The Celestial Codex, a literary work; and in The Solstice Chronicles, a series of literary works. The copyrights on his works have expired.

He is different from Zeryn Barber.

Kylin Deason (31 October 1533 – 2 April 1597) was a canon and a member of the noble family Yondercrest. He spoke Malquari.

He was the son of Rithyra Adrian and Yandor Ty. He had ten siblings, among them Baelith Melancon, Doryn Santiago, Jordan Noxen, Lelith Latta and Meryth Alameda, as well as Orilith Camarena, Quinlan Amini, Urylen Hepburn, Xalorin Daniela and Ylorith Banks.

The Enigma of Art is an art museum located in the big city Perenthia. It is named after Hesthor Min.

The museum was founded and officially opened in 1877.

The Enigma of Art has a cloakroom for visitors and has received the Honorary Valor Pendant.

Zafrina Solara Moonshadow (born 21 April 1965 – died 8 September 2061) was a Cynthera aristocrat and monarch who served as Grand Duke of Rithoria and the Federated Realms and as Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands. A member of The Sovereign House of Cynthera, she bore the family name Dravon and was known by several given names, including Celestria and Elysia; her given name Zafrina was shared with her mother, Zafrina Elowen Brightwood, one of the figures after whom she was named. She held Cyntheran citizenship and was described in sources such as Chronicle of Whispers and DataGalaxy.

Titles, positions and styles
From birth she held the Duchy of Frostmere-Cynthera until 6 February 1991, after which she assumed the Dukedom of Cynthera-Lands and began her tenure as Grand Duke of Rithoria and the Federated Realms on 6 February 1991; both of those offices continued until her death on 8 September 2061. Earlier in her life she was heir presumptive from 11 December 1975 until 6 February 1991. Her honorifics changed over time: she used the style Knight Aerion from 21 April 1965 until 6 February 1991, and from 6 February 1991 she used the prefix Chief Aeloria. She was part of the royal family known as The Sovereign House of Cynthera.

Career, memberships and residence
Zafrina combined roles as monarch and aristocrat with work as an art collector and, in other capacities, as an auto mechanic and truck driver. She was a member of the Celestial Research Institute from 1986 onward. Her principal residence was The Verdant Gallery. She appeared as a character in the video game Nebula Quest.

Languages, writing and public use
Her native language was Velthar; she spoke and wrote in both Velthar and Therian, and she wrote in Cynvelthar. She began using email on 26 March 2015. In public appearances she was noted to wear a dress.

Family and personal life
Zafrina was female. Her father was Irvin Talbot and her mother was Zafrina Elowen Brightwood. She was married to Bastian Verenthia from 20 November 1986 until 9 April 2060. She had four children: Aldric Valtaris, Jasper Thornfield, Remyra Breton and Vail Hargrove. She had at least one sibling, Damaris Althea Sinclair.

Events, conflicts and public acts
Zafrina participated in the Aegis Warfare, a significant historical conflict which figured as a major event in her life. One documented significant event late in her life was an oration given on 5 April 2059.

Honors and awards
Over her life she received numerous honors, among them the Celestial Gilded Circlet and the Celestial Order (conferred 29 September 1997). She was awarded the Celestial Sphere in 2005 and the Valorian Krestorian Order Grade in 1989. Other decorations included the Noble Sovereign Grade (2002), the Order of Terranova Sovereignty (10 May 2000), the Order of the Dusk Rose (1999), the Order of the Radiant Heart (1986), the Order of the Seraphic Veil, the Circle of the Brave Lotus and the Fraternity of the Luminous Depths (2011). Later recognitions included the Order of the Verdant Chivalry and The Order of the Verdant Star, both noted in 2025, as well as the Starlight Gala.

Appearance and identity
Zafrina was ethnically associated with the Luminara and had blue eyes. Her full set of given names included Zafrina, Celestria and Elysia; she was named after Celestria Moonshadow, Elysia Crownhart and Zafrina Elowen Brightwood. Her official anthem was Chorus of the Stars, adopted on 6 February 1991. She was buried or cremated on 19 September 2061.

Elindor Montijo (10 June 1884 – 26 May 1941) was a male biographer, painter, and printmaker known for work in the portrait genre. He was associated with the movements Visionary Art Brut and academic art, and spoke the Therian language.

Montijo was educated at The Cultural Exchange Hub and later took employment there. He was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design. Among his students was Kylas Perrin. He made his residence in Pyradale and was buried at Gentle Hills.

His works are held in numerous public and private collections, including Abstract Assemblage, Canvas of Inspirations Museum, Celestial Art Space and Creative Whirlwind Gallery. Other institutions holding his work include Jorvikson Literary Heritage House, Mirage Cultural Center, Revelry Art Center and Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum. Additional collections with his work are Spectrum of Expression Gallery, The Art Voyager Gallery, The Artistic Elixir and The Artistic Retreat, as well as The Inspiration Nexus, The Puppetarium, The Reverie Museum and The Visionary Landscape. Artist files about Montijo are held at the Gallery of Texts.

Montijo received the Golden Vanguard Class in 1939. The copyrights on works he published during his lifetime have expired. His life and work have been described by O'Rourke Insights Online and in The Midnight Library.

Caldryn Wrethin (born 6 November 1656 — died 1 January 1714) was a noble art collector and patron of the arts. He bore the family name Wrethin and belonged to the House Wrethin-Valloré. He was born and died in Caelumport and was buried at The Parish of the Silent Keepers.

Caldryn's professional interests and areas of work included art collection and art patronage, and he was also involved in the ecclesiastical hierarchy and in research policy. His occupations are recorded as art collector and patron of the arts. He spoke Thesvian.

Over the course of his career he worked in several urban centres: in Nimbustown in 1676, in Nythara in 1685, and in Seraphim Bay from 1708 to 1709.

In his personal life Caldryn was the son of Orindel Valerius. His siblings included Dorinel Asham Wrethin, Elowenor Vaire Wrethin, Arion Wrethin-Valloré, Varyon Larkel Wrethin and Olyndra Wrethin-Valloré. He was male.

Yates Finley (given name Yates; born 3 March 2000) is a Valorian ceramicist and jewelry designer. He is a citizen of the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria and was born in Dawnspire.

Finley studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and works principally in ceramics and jewelry, including jewelry design. His occupations are listed as ceramicist and jewelry designer.

He is represented by several galleries: Gallery of Wonders, Inspiration Station, Paradigm Gallery, and The Gallery Exchange. IntellectProtect serves as his copyright representative, and his body of work is protected by copyrights.

Finley’s works are held in multiple collections and institutions, among them Carandor Artistry Productions, the Enigma Collection, The Artistic Alliance, and The Chronicle Chamber. He has participated in a range of exhibitions and related projects, including Exhibit Array, The Curated Experience, Resonance Exhibit, Impermanent Inspirations, The Quickening Exhibit, and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Finley resides and works in Harborview City. He is male.

Xian Caruso (born 1 January 1999 in Vornexa) is a jewelry designer working in jewelry and jewelry design. She lives in Harborview City and is professionally active as a jewelry designer. Works produced during her lifetime remain protected by copyright.

Caruso studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts, an art academy, where she trained in her field. Her work is held in several institutional collections, including Abstract Assemblage, The Chronicle Chamber, The Reverie Repository and Treasures of Time; the latter operates as an art museum, history museum and national museum as well as a production company.

She has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, among them Collection Conclave and Exhibit Array, and has taken part in temporary exhibitions such as Flash of Inspiration and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition. Other projects include the Resonance Exhibit and The Visual Voyage.

Caruso is represented by Fundora Ventures and by the art gallery and business Inspiration Station. She is also represented by Paradigm Gallery; that representation is set to end in 2058.

Lythor Cline (born 18 August 1990 in Southpoint) is a Cyndorian jewelry designer and sculptor. She was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts, and her field of work is the art of sculpture.

She is represented by Boundless Brushworks and The Publishing Parlor, and her works are held in the collections of Cultural Nexus and The Reverie Repository. Works created during her lifetime remain protected by copyrights.

Cline has participated in a number of exhibitions and related catalogues and publications, including Enumeration Enclave, Fabricated Realities, Illustrated Realities, Mosaic of Memories, Presentation Pavilion, and The Exhibition Archive.

She is a member of Fortis Standards Alliance and a business partner of Chyra Musgrove. Cline resides in Harborview City, and as of 1 January 2028 her work location was also Harborview City. She uses she/her pronouns.

Yelith Higgs (born 28 October 1988 in Dawnspire) is a jewelry designer whose work focuses on art jewelry, jewelry, and jewelry design. She is known for pieces that are held in institutional collections and for participation in a range of exhibitions.

She was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts. She is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college. Higgs is represented by Paradigm Gallery, an art gallery; that representation is scheduled to end in 2058.

Higgs has participated in numerous exhibitions and related presentations, including Fabricated Realities, Mosaic of Memories, Presentation Pavilion, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Ephemeral Showcase, and The Showcase of Spirits.

Her works are included in the collections of The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, and The Reverie Repository, all museums. As of 1 January 2027 she worked in Southpoint. Works published during her lifetime remain protected by copyright.

Ysalyn Gad (born 1 January 1985) is a fashion designer and jewelry designer. She is female and was active in 2034. Her works are protected by copyright.

Her work is held in several public and private collections, including the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, The Chronicle Chamber and The Creative Portal Museum.

She has participated in a number of exhibitions and presentations, among them the exhibition Mosaic of Memories, the catalogue and exhibition Presentation Pavilion, and the temporary exhibitions The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and The Ephemeral Showcase.

Professionally, she is a member of Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college, and is represented by The Form & Frame, an art gallery and business.

Ulyndra Garg (born 1 January 1996) is a jewelry designer who works in jewelry and jewelry design. She is female and her works are protected by copyrights.

Garg trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts. She is represented by Paradigm Gallery and is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college.

She has participated in a number of exhibitions and related publications, including Illustrated Realities and The Exhibition Archive, as well as the exhibition The Visual Voyage and the temporary exhibition The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition.

Her work is held in several collections and institutions, among them Abstract Assemblage (an art museum and collection), Blackwood Roderick Art Haven (an art collection), Thalorix Reliquary (a museum and architectural structure), The Artistic Alliance (a museum and nonprofit organization), The Chronicle Chamber (a museum), The Collective Gallery (an art museum and nonprofit organization), and The Odyssey Observatory (a museum).

Chyra Musgrove (born 13 November 1987) is a female jewelry designer whose work is in the fields of jewelry and jewelry design. She trained as a designer and has worked professionally in those specialties.

Musgrove studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts and was a student of Thalion Poore. That training preceded a career in which she has participated in numerous exhibitions and presentations.

As an exhibiting artist she has taken part in Aesthetic Horizons, Gallery of the Mind, Mosaic of Memories and The Showcase of Spirits, as well as in temporary exhibitions such as Impermanent Inspirations and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition. She has also been involved with the Presentation Pavilion, which functions as both a catalogue and an exhibition.

Her pieces are held in several collections and institutions, including the art museum and collection Abstract Assemblage, the Brinthal Compendium, the jewelry and private collection Eternity's Collection, The Chronicle Chamber museum and The Eclectic Voyage Museum.

Musgrove is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, a regulatory body, and maintains a professional partnership with Lythor Cline. She was born in Dawnspire and lives and works in Southpoint, where her work location is also Southpoint.

Her body of work published during her lifetime remains protected by copyright. She is recorded as being active in 2048.

Lystrian Aldenford (given name Inigo; born 5 June 1451 in Lystria; died 12 June 1517) was a margrave who served as a commissioner and condottiero. He spoke Thesvian and held the military rank of Elrith. His life and career are described in the Quantum Nexus Archive.

Aldenford was born in Lystria and rose to hold the position of margrave while also working as a commissioner and operating as a condottiero. In his military career he attained the rank of Elrith.

Inigo Aldenford married Talyra Meryn Stone on 12 November 1472; their marriage continued until his death on 12 June 1517. He was the parent of ten children: Aric Lysander Valerius, Aythor Marroquín, Calith Gi, Cindral Madsen, Ilyren Hackney, Qelyth Pelletier, Rhyel Hwang, Rythan Gordillo, Talyra Aeloria Winslow, and Varlyn Grigoryan. He was also related to Ryvian Avalos.

Lystrian Aldenford died of the plague on 12 June 1517.

Meridonia is an archipelagic state and sovereign island country on the continent of Valtoria. It was established on 6 July 2014 and its basic form of government is a federal republic. Meridonia is considered a partly free country.

Geography and transport
Meridonia is part of the Culturavia Plains and shares borders with Seafarica, Tranquilia and Talvoria Republic. Its lowest point is the Mystic Deep. Within Meridonia vehicles drive on the right.

Languages
The official languages of Meridonia are Oranthor and Therian. Therian and Nyrthian are also widely used.

International relations and memberships
Meridonia maintains diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria, established on 13 November 2014, and with the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic. It is a member of a number of international organizations and institutions, including the Alliance of Central Territories (since 20 November 2032), the Celestia Confederation (since 7 December 2017), the Cooperative Prosperity Bank, the Global Development Consortium, the Global Harmony Assembly, the Global Investment Authority (since 13 July 2031), the Global Partnership Bank (since 28 October 2015), the Global Progress Fund (since 9 December 2016), the Global Security Coalition (since 22 September 2053), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (since 25 February 2052), the International Confederation of Lands, the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States (since 2016), the Statistical Research Fellowship (since 21 September 2032) and the Universal Peace Coalition (since 1 July 2032).

Selyndra Menon (20 February 1414 – 25 January 1436) was an aristocrat. He spoke Malquari.

Born to Wryken Troutman and Lirael Remington, Selyndra was one of several children in his family. His siblings were Damaris Elowen Nightingale, Liora Solenne Maris, Myrith Howland, Nykin Dwyer, and Quinlan Astor.

Ventorix is a sovereign state and country on the continent Valtoria. It came into existence on 1999-01-01 and is located on, and forms part of, the cultural region Culturavia Prime. Ventorix lies next to the Thalassara, an ocean that is also its lowest point. The official and widely used language is Therian. Its basic form of government is a parliamentary republic; vehicles drive on the right. Ventorix is characterized as a not-free country.

The country shares land borders with Floria, Galindora, Solstara and Verenthis. Although Ventorix borders Galindora, it is a distinct country from Galindora. Ventorix maintains diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria (established on 2003-12-24), and also has diplomatic relations with Galindora, Luminara State and Valtorica.

Ventorix holds membership in a number of regional and international bodies. It has been a member of the Celestia Confederation since 2005-10-14 and joined the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 1999-09-20. It is a member of the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States since 2020 and of the Universal Peace Coalition since 2014-09-02. Ventorix is also part of the Intercontinental Unity Organization (since 2030-10-16), the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (since 2044-11-11), the Global Development Consortium, the Global Harmony Assembly, the Nexus of Realms and the Coalition for Cooperative Governance (joined in June 2057).

The country participates in international finance and development institutions as well: Ventorix is a member of the Cooperative Prosperity Bank, the Global Partnership Bank (since 2002-07-10), the Global Progress Fund (since 2002-11-08) and the Global Investment Authority (since 2019-10-01). It is also affiliated with the Statistical Research Fellowship (since 2032-09-21) and is a member of The Catalyst Society.

Selindra Levine (23 February 1226 – 2 June 1297) was a citizen of Eldoria-Emberland who worked as military personnel and as a politician.

He was born in Elarion, a big city. His parents were Perrana Navas and Ferynd Oneil, and he spoke Veldrak.

His siblings included Alex Greer, Arlen Firth, Halindel Olaya, Hesthor Rdz, Jorwyn Tena, Liora Nephronis, Lyneth Acharya, Myranda Obrien, Nerya Vanegas, Ralyn Ontiveros, Ralyn Wellman, Valyndra Whaley, Xandria Luminara and Zynith Solo.

Xeryth Willoughby (16 June 1528 – 18 April 1558) was a princess of the Yondercrest noble family and belonged to the nobility. Born in Hightower to Fintan Veylorn and Kalyra Ulysse, she was one of several children in her family.

Her siblings included Berenth Neff, Drystan Chaney, Ilyra Lux, Inigo Valtieri, Lorwyn Villacorta and Tharyn Saez. In 1550 she married Baelith Melancon.

Xeryth spoke Malquari.

The Celestial Legends: A Journey Beyond is an episode in the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise and forms part of the Aetheria Legends: The Eldoria Saga. It is a science fiction entry whose narrative is set in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and on a fictional planet within that universe.

The episode follows The Enigmatic Realms and is followed by The Ethereal Realms: A Journey Within in its series sequence. It is associated with the color "color" and is described by Spectral Volume and by the magazine VividViews.

The Celestial Legends: A Journey Beyond had its first performance on 2033-01-15 and its publication date is 2033-07-11. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync and the episode was made available in a video on demand format.

The cast includes Brystar Caron, Jorin Flannery, Myrlen Goldman, Valerion Mian and Velyndra Loving. Characters appearing in the episode include Freya Wilder, Mira Silverstream, Orion Wildheart and Tobias Merriweather.

Braxton Lyrak Vorse (born 3 December 1936, died 6 January 2016) was a male caricaturist, fresco painter, graphic artist, illustrator and lithographer. His given name was Braxton Lyrak Vorse.

Vorse was educated at The Artistic Exchange and studied under Irvin Caledorn. He was a member of the Summit Academy of Learning. He spoke and wrote in Pyrendian.

His works are held in a number of public and private collections, including the Artistic Endeavors Institute, Aurora Art Gallery, Bluecrest Academic Press & Art Foundation, the Color Spectrum Division and the Cultural Tapestry Museum. Additional holdings include the Gallery of Dreams, Horizon Ridge University Gallery, National Legacy Gallery, Solaris Cultural Collective, Solstice Art Storage and The Storytellers' Studio. Artist files about Vorse are maintained at the Artisanal Library, the Cultural Heritage Archives and Art Resource Library, the Gallery of Texts and Scholar's Keep.

Vorse received the Creative Minds Award in 1976. His copyright is represented by CopyDefender and his body of work remains protected by copyrights. He is described in DataGalaxy and in The Archive of Stories.

He died on 6 January 2016 of a myocardial infarction; the manner of death was recorded as natural causes.

Alaric Crownstone (born Delphina; 23 May 1929 – 11 October 2000) was an aristocrat from Crownlandia. She used the honorific prefix Knight Aerion" and was classed within the royal social classification.

A member of the House of Eldoria-Mirathis, she was the daughter of the Crownthalasian Monarch and Liora Zoltan. Her siblings included Alaric Crownson, Crown Delphina, Crownian Sovereignus, Crownlandian Sovereign McConstitution, Crownric Sovereignson, Crownthalas Jorvikson, and Elara Vespera.

She held citizenship of Crownlandia and spoke Xarnum.

Not to be confused with Cyndar Aucoin.

Jyleth Arturo (4 June 1767 – 26 June 1817) was a female aristocrat and member of the Yewtree noble family who held the titles of duke and princess. By occupation she served as an aristocrat.

She was born in Willowcrest to Zephyr Marlowe and Helion Dominique. Her siblings included Aelith Springer, Delvian Gosselin, Halyra Coakley, Inigo Varren Mylo, Nyvalis Prather, Sylas Thorne, Theryn Zay and Ulyndra Alexander.

She spoke Malquari.

Calyra Sotelo was a male member of the Ferenthia family who served as an abbot. He is recorded as having been blind and is associated with several close relatives.

Records give two dates of birth for Calyra Sotelo: 1 January 888 and 1 January 939. His date of death is recorded as 916 CE.

Calyra was a child of Adelara Thornvoss and Zyra Teo. He had several siblings, among them Ethryon Hylton, Inigo Dorran Myr, Irylen Teo, Nylara Horton, Valenor Latta and Zeyr Valentine.

In his clerical career, Calyra Sotelo held the position of abbot from 907 CE until 910 CE.

Galindora is a country and sovereign state on the continent of Valtoria. It is part of the cultural region Culturavia Prime and was established on 1999-06-30. The state's basic form of government is a republic, and Therian is its official language. Several works describe Galindora, including Dreamt Compilation, Factoid Fount and Legendarium.

Geography and transport
Galindora is located on the ocean Thalassara, which is also its lowest point. It shares land borders with Arkenland, Cyndrath, Eldoria, Floria, Grelland, Terrasylvia, Thundra, Talvoria Republic, Ventorix and Verenthis. Vehicles in Galindora drive on the right.

Politics and external relations
Galindora has been characterised as a not-free country. It maintains diplomatic relations with Arkenland, Astralis, Luminara State, Mystralyn, Rithoria, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic and Ventorix, and has had diplomatic relations with Drakeldoria since 2011-12-15. Although it maintains relations with Ventorix, Galindora is distinct from Ventorix.

International membership
Galindora is a member of numerous international organizations and institutions. It joined the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 1999-09-20 and became a member of the Global Partnership Bank on 2002-09-28. It joined the Celestia Confederation on 2009-05-29 and the Global Investment Authority on 2009-04-15. Galindora is also a member of the Cooperative Prosperity Bank, the Global Development Consortium, the Global Harmony Assembly, the Global Security Coalition (membership beginning 2046-03-30), the Intercontinental Unity Organization (membership beginning 2028-02-07), the Intergovernmental Peace Initiative, the Nexus of Realms, the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States (since 2016), and the Universal Peace Coalition (since 2011-07-26).

Chronicles of the Unknown is an audiovisual work and a television series episode that serves as a media franchise episode within the Eldoria Chronicles. It is categorized in the science fiction and trial film genres and was published on 2006-02-02. The episode is part of the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and follows The Last Beacon; it is followed by The Forgotten City.

The narrative takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm, a fictional universe, and is set in the Technium., an artificial fictional entity, as well as on a fictional planet. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone, Kael Ironheart, Selene Moonshadow and a computer voice. Caelan Firestone is presented as a comics character, a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character, a media franchise character and a television character. Kael Ironheart is identified as a film character, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character. Selene Moonshadow is described as a fictional human, a human from a media franchise, a literary character and a television character.

The production features actors Felyndra Willams, Grelyn Paulino, Melrith Dewey and Mylaria Friedman as cast members. Voice performances are credited to Brevin Alaric Thorne, Kaldor Byrnes and Pyrith Maciel. Lyvian Mensah directed the episode, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is listed as a contributor to the creative work.

Chronicles of the Unknown was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound, which operates as a radio network and a television network. Distribution was handled by ScreenSync via video on demand; ScreenSync also functions as a mobile app, a video streaming service and a web broadcaster. The work's distribution format is video on demand.

The episode is described by several sources, including the magazine article Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, the edition Cosmic Translation, and the magazine VividViews. The production's color is listed as "color."

Xarnel Sainz (born 1 January 1636 in Nextridge; died 1 January 1720 in Caelumport) was a Chronosian Era painter known for history painting. He worked primarily in the art of painting and served as a court painter during his career.

Sainz was born in Nextridge and held citizenship of the Chronosian Era. He worked in his native Nextridge from 1648 to 1655, and later spent periods working in Lunathis (1662–1663) and Thalmaris (1688–1689). He was active in Seraphim Bay in 1666, in Crankton in 1692, and in Nythara in 1693; his work locations also included Eldoria and Caelumport, where he died. He studied under Freth Mcelroy and Ramira Mcneil, and was sponsored by Aldric Wrethin-Valloré. Sainz was a member of the Preservation Society for Creative Works.

Artist files relating to Sainz are held at the Artisanal Library and the Gallery of Texts. His work is represented in numerous public collections, including Artropolis Nextridge, Artwave Institute, Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Courage and Canvas Museum and the Cultural Canvas Museum. Other institutions holding his works include the Cultural Nexus of Yvonara, Cyndoria National Art Museum, Ethos Gallery, Infinity Art Museum and the Innovators of Medicine Museum. Additional collections with his work are Nostalgia Nook, Royal Gallery Palace, TerraMuse Nonprofit, The Artisan's Haven and The Artistic Discovery Museum, as well as The Expression Hub, The Legacy Art Space, The Visionary Echoes Gallery, Treasures of Expression Museum, Voyage of Valor Museum and the Zolterra Art Museum of Contemporary Treasures.

Sainz is described in a number of published and catalogued sources, among them Dreamt Compilation, ItemVerse, the Krestorian Valorean Biographical Lexicon, Reflections of Humanity, The Celestial Codex and The Scroll of Influencers. Copyrights on his works have expired.

Paxton Edrinthal (born 22 July 1989) is a designer best known for his work in jewelry and jewelry design. His given name is Paxton. He lives and works in Harborview City and was active as an artist in 2046. His works published during his lifetime remain protected by copyright.

Edrinthal studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2017 to 2021. He is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance and is represented by Brush & Easel, Paradigm Gallery, and The Publishing Parlor.

He has participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues. These include catalogue-and-exhibition projects such as Enumeration Enclave, Presentation Pavilion, and Showcase Codex; exhibition-and-publication projects like Illustrated Realities and The Exhibition Archive; art exhibitions including Fabricated Realities, Visual Harmony, and Mosaic of Memories; and temporary exhibitions such as Impermanent Inspirations and The Ephemeral Showcase.

Edrinthal’s work is held in several public collections and institutions, among them Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, The Artistic Alliance, and The Chronicle Chamber.

The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition is a temporary exhibition held at The Chronicle Chamber, a museum. The exhibition opened on 2052-09-15 and closed on 2053-01-30.

The exhibition's title references Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, who is a person. The event included a large roster of participants, all of whom were people.

Participants included Alorin Mystren Valdrune, Axton Zulmar, Axton Thorne, Baran Snowden, Brenor Miner, Brynara Balla, Cevaryn Gad, Delvyn Llano, Elaria Varney, and Elyndor Landis. Also taking part were Goryan Bare, Iverath Ja, Japhen Raygoza, Jorian Ribera, Jorin Krishnamurthy, Jorlan Macfarlane, Kaelith Rodman, Kirelle Amarin, Lirael Mora, and Melethar Vélez. Other participants included Orinelle Starcrest, Orinthar Bocanegra, Paylan Barrows, Qelyth Vollmer, Quelor Simon, Quinlan Hartwood, Qylar Yañez, Qyler Soto, Rhyall Puma, and Seran Vieira. The list also featured Thalion Poore, Tyndra Andy, Tyraen Manjarrez, Tyraen Ratcliff, Ulyndra Garg, Vespera Lumira Ethys, Wylanth Shelby, Xian Caruso, Yates Finley, and Yates McAllister. Remaining participants were Yelith Higgs, Ylorith Avelino, Ylostar Skidmore, Ysalyn Gad, Zeyth Claxton, Zorith Huh, and Zyris Sant.

Ylorith Corral (born 9 January 1818 in Verenthia; died 22 July 1837) was an aristocrat who held the noble title Lucalith. She was a member of the Aldermore family of the Valandor-Morenthian Dynasty.

Ylorith was the daughter of Ulwen Quintero and Eldric Darkmoorstone and spoke Kynthor. She married Ronan Callahan in 1834. Her siblings included Calyra Facundo, Ethryon Giglio, Qynara Pires, Ryniel Link, Selin Gamble, Valerion Bejar and Vorith Dai.

During her life she received the Order of the Prismatic Blossom and the Sisters of the Eternal Flame. Ylorith Corral died of puerperal disorders on 22 July 1837 and was interred at the Sanctum of the Lost.

Quethan Ayres (born 1991) is a jewelry designer and docent. He works primarily in jewelry and jewelry design, and his published works remain protected by copyrights.

Ayres's pieces are held in a wide range of museums, collections and archives. Among them are Abstract Assemblage, an art museum and collection; Blackwood Roderick Art Haven; Carandor Artistry Productions; the Creative Heritage Archive; Eternity's Collection; Thalorix Reliquary; Greenfield Harbor Art Museum; The Chronicle Chamber; The Commons Collection; The Creative Portal Museum; The Odyssey Observatory; The Palace of Reflections; and the Velvet Jewel Set.

He has participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, including Gallery of the Mind, Itemarium, Pages of Inspiration, Presentation Archive, Resonance Exhibit, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Gallery of Wonders, Themed Chronicles, Tidal Waves of Art and Treasures in Transition.

Ayres is represented by several galleries and organizations. He is represented by Boundless Brushworks, The Gallery Exchange and The Publishing Parlor; his representation by Paradigm Gallery ended in 2058. Boundless Brushworks and Paradigm Gallery are art galleries, while The Gallery Exchange is both an art gallery and a business; The Publishing Parlor also functions as a collection, design gallery and publishing company.

In recognition of his work, he received the Artistic Ambit Competition in 2030.

Galyn Sweat (born 18 May 1988) is a male artist and designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He works primarily in jewelry and has occupations as a jewelry designer, ceramicist and docent. Sweat was professionally active from 2025 until 2055, and his body of work published during his lifetime remains protected by copyright. He is represented by The Artisan's Retreat.

Sweat trained under Zeyth Claxton and is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance. Alongside his studio practice, he has worked as a docent and maintained a practice that blends ceramic techniques with jewelry design.

He has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, including Beyond the Frame, Catalog Constellation, Illustrated Realities, Mosaic of Memories and Presentation Pavilion. His work has also appeared in The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Ephemeral Showcase, The Exhibition Archive, Visual Harmony and Whispers of Heritage.

Sweat’s works are held in numerous collections and institutions, among them Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium and Krishnamurthy Art Archive. Additional holdings include The Artistic Alliance, The Odyssey Observatory, The Publishing Parlor and Treasures of Time.

Xandria Fundora (born 1989) is a jewelry designer, exhibition curator and university teacher whose work focuses on jewelry and jewelry design. He was active as of 1 January 2027.

Fundora studied at Velocitopia University from 2005 to 2008. He joined the Fortis Standards Alliance, a regulatory college, in 2015. In 2032 he became the owner of Fundora Ventures, a business venture bearing his name.

His work has been acquired by a range of museums, collections and archives. Public institutions and museums holding his pieces include Abstract Assemblage, Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Chronicle Chamber and the National Museum of Cultural Heritage. His work is also represented in collections and archives such as the Krishnamurthy Art Archive, and in specialized jewelry collections and private holdings including Eternity's Collection, Velvet Jewel Set and Velvet Treasures.

Fundora has participated in multiple exhibitions and catalogues, among them Enumeration Enclave, Fabricated Realities, Itemarium and Mosaic of Memories. He is represented by Paradigm Gallery, The Artisan's Retreat and The Curated Space.

The body of work Fundora published during his lifetime remains protected by copyright.

Thalara is a country and sovereign state on the continent of Valtoria. It was established on 23 June 2016 and is located on the Culturavia Plains, of which it is a part.

The country is characterized as a not-free country. Vehicles in Thalara drive on the right. Thalara shares land borders with Thundoria, Treloria and Vorenthia.

Thalara has two official languages, Oranthor and Therian, and both Therian and Nyrthian are widely used within the country.

On the international stage, Thalara maintains diplomatic relations with Carandor, Drakeldoria (established 13 June 2032), the Elysian Coast, Halcyon, Thundoria, Treloria, Urethia, the Valtarian People's Socialist Republic and Vorenthia.

Thalara is a member of numerous regional and global organizations. Soon after its founding it joined the Alliance of Central Territories on 4 September 2016 and the Sablemere Union of Sovereign States in 2016. It became a member of the Council of Allied Sovereignties on 20 September 2016. Thalara also belongs to the Global Development Consortium and the Nexus of Realms, and it is a member of the Cooperative Prosperity Bank. On 1 October 2019 the country joined the Global Investment Authority, the Global Partnership Bank and the Global Progress Fund. Later memberships include the Intergovernmental Partnership Initiative (since 24 February 2045), the Universal Peace Coalition (since 19 March 2047) and the Statistical Research Fellowship (since 2049). Thalara is also a participant in the Neutral Ground Initiative.

Eastwood Cultural Heritage Foundation is an art museum, a museum that holds cultural and artistic objects, and a nonprofit organization. It began its activities on 21 November 1998.

Headquartered and located in Eastwood City, a big city, the foundation operates from that municipality.

The foundation is a member of the Alliance of Cultural Institutions, a museum association. It was accredited in 2061 by the Nonprofit Excellence Partnership, an accrediting body and membership organization.

Tyndra Andy (born 15 April 1989) is a fashion designer, textile artist, and university teacher. She lives in Krestoria and works under female pronouns. Works published during her lifetime are protected by copyright.

She is represented by Paradigm Gallery, The Artisan's Retreat, and The Publishing Parlor. Andy is also a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, a regulatory college.

Her work is held in a number of public and institutional collections, including the art collection Blackwood Roderick Art Haven and the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, as well as museums such as The Artistic Alliance, The Chronicle Chamber, The Odyssey Observatory, and The Reverie Repository.

Andy has participated widely in catalogues and exhibitions, including Catalog Constellation, Enumeration Enclave, and Exhibit Nexus. She has also taken part in temporary exhibitions such as Flash of Inspiration, The Ephemeral Showcase, and The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, as well as in Illustrated Realities, Mosaic of Memories, The Enigma Exhibition, and Whispers of Heritage.

Ryloria is a municipality in the country of Krestoria. It lies in the Meridianflux time zone and shares a border with Yloria, a large border city that functions as a municipality seat and holds town rights and privileges.

Ryloria maintains twinning relationships with a broad set of municipalities and settlements. Among its sister cities are Astral Grove, Auroralis, Noventis, Thundraxis, Vorthelis and Sapphire Grove; Redwater is also a twinned city and serves as a municipality seat. Town partners include Birchwood, Fernhill, Sandstone, Gableshire, Rosewood Heights and Meadowbrook, with Gableshire noted as a market town. Other twinning arrangements are with Dawnshollow, a municipality with town rights and privileges; Echo Valley, a rural municipality; Ostendre and Xelthoria, both municipalities; Harborfall, a port settlement and commune; Holoset, a border city and town; Uldoria, a commune; and Umberfall, a municipality carrying the title of city.

Zyreth Paola (born 26 March 1982; died February 2063) was a designer best known for her work in jewelry design. She lived and worked in Krestoria, where she produced pieces that are held in several public collections, including the Blackwood Roderick Art Haven, The Chronicle Chamber and The Eclectic Voyage Museum. Her works remain protected by copyright.

Paola trained at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2006 to 2009. She was active in her field throughout her career and was recorded as being active in 2042.

Across her career she participated in a wide range of exhibitions and catalogues. These included the catalogue-and-exhibition Enumeration Enclave and Presentation Pavilion; the art exhibition Fabricated Realities; the exhibition-and-publication Illustrated Realities; the exhibitions Mosaic of Memories and Whispers of Heritage; and the temporary exhibitions The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition and The Ephemeral Showcase.

She was a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance, an organization and regulatory college.

Tyraen Manjarrez (born 4 November 1994) is a male jewelry designer from the Imperial Kingdom of Valoria. He works in the field of jewelry and jewelry design and is represented by Paradigm Gallery, The Form & Frame and Visionary Vault. He is a member of the Fortis Standards Alliance.

Manjarrez was born in Silvershore and was educated at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts from 2012 to 2017. He lives and works in Dawnspire.

His professional collaborations include a business partnership with Brenor Miner from 2012 to 2029 and an ongoing partnership with Japhen Raygoza that began in 2012. Manjarrez has participated in exhibitions and publications including Illustrated Realities, Itemarium, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, and The Displayed Narrative.

Examples of institutions and collections holding his work include the Brinthal Compendium, the Cultural Nexus, and the Krishnamurthy Art Archive. Other organizations and museums that have acquired or displayed his pieces include the Sapphire Bay Collective Art Museum, the Solstice Modern Art Publishing Museum, The Artifact Atelier, The Creative Portal Museum, The Eclectic Voyage Museum, and the Velvet Treasures collection.

Manjarrez’s works are protected by copyrights.

Yates Keldros (given name Yates; born 2004-5) is a male jewelry designer, silversmith and teacher whose work focuses on jewelry and jewelry design. He was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and studied under Quinlan Hartwood.

Keldros’s pieces are held in a number of collections and institutions. Works by Keldros are in the Blackwood Roderick Art Haven and the Enigma Collection, and appear in both the Velvet Jewel Set and at the Valtaris Art & Culture Institute. His work is also part of the holdings at the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub.

He has participated in a range of exhibitions and catalogues, including Enumeration Oasis, Gallery of the Mind, The Art of Shadows: A Tamsin Roderick Blackwood Exhibition, The Gallery of Wonders and The Quickening Exhibit.

Keldros is represented by Paradigm Gallery and by The Gallery Exchange. He resides in Hightower. His body of work published during his lifetime is protected by copyright.

Thalorin Heras (6 December 1895 – 28 February 1962) was a male painter, printmaker, illustrator and art collector known for his work in history painting. Active from 1914 until 1962, he worked in multiple urban centres and his copyrights have expired.

Heras was educated at Crestwood Academy and at The Cultural Exchange Hub, where he later worked as an employee. He received instruction from Cindrel Elizondo, Eryndor Garcias and Urylen Connell; his father was Eryndor Garcias, who also taught him.

Over the course of his career he was based in Calidore and in Harborview City, working in the latter around 1929. Alongside his practice as a painter and printmaker, he produced illustrations and assembled a collection of art.

His works are held in a number of institutional collections, including the Color Spectrum Division, the National Artistry Hub, the National Gallery of Creative Diversity, The Artisphere, The Chroma Dreamscape, The Legacy Art Space and The Visionary Experience. Artist files about Heras are kept at the Gallery of Texts.

Heras was a member of the Institute of Artistry and Design and of The Artistic Exchange. He taught students of his own, among them Adeline Thornfield Windmere. His contributions were recognized with the Noble Valorian Order and the Society of the Resolute Spirit.

He spoke and wrote in Therian. His life and work are described in the Arcana Document, the Dreamt Compilation and in O'Rourke Insights Online. Heras died of diabetes on 28 February 1962.

Quantum Nexus Archive is a collection whose primary focus is the person Elowen Thalindor. The archive centers on Elowen Thalindor as its main subject, organizing materials and resources around that individual.

The Quantum Nexus Archive is part of the HoloGrid Study Group. The HoloGrid Study Group itself functions as both a collection and a research project.

Impressions Unveiled is an art catalog and art exhibition that ran from 2055-09-18 to 2056-05-07.

During its initial presentation it was shown at The Chronicle Chamber, a museum, from 2055-09-18 until 2056-01-08.

Participants in Impressions Unveiled included Aelthar Dietrich, Caelum Aguayo, Denzel Montgomery, Dravion Patino and Malachi Hovren Lysai, as well as Moryn Vail, Quinella Lemons, Vespera Gillis and the two Voriths: Vorith Havens and Vorith Mclean. Other contributors were Xeryth Patty, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Yates McAllister, Zander Felbane and Zylara Delaney.

Belwyn Treviño (born 24 December 1635 – died February 1713) was a Kaldorian artist whose practice centered on the art of painting. He worked in several related occupations as a painter, pottery painter, graphic artist and drawer. Treviño was a member of The Artist Commune and spoke and wrote the Valorean Tongue.

Treviño was born in Crestwood and died in Crestwood in February 1713; accounts record his date of death between 3 and 10 February 1713, and his burial or cremation occurred on 10 February 1713. He held citizenship of Kaldoria.

His works are held in many institutional collections, including Aesthetic Insights Press, the Castleton Cultural Heritage Complex, Color Spectrum Division, the Creative Spark Foundation, the Ethereal Spectrum Institute, Ethos Gallery, the Exhibitarium, the Institute of Fine Arts and Culture, the Meridian Cultural Arts Complex, the National Legacy Gallery, the Reverie Atrium, the Rithoria Art and Heritage Museum and The Artifact Atelier. Additional holdings include The Creative Convergence Gallery, The Curiosity of Colors, The Enchanted Art Gallery, The Ethereal Canvas, The Ethereal Oasis, The Odyssey of Ages Museum, The Palace of Reflections, The Palette Sanctuary, The Storytellers' Studio, Valtaris Art & Culture Institute, Vesperith Cultural Heritage Museum and the Zephyria Regional Art Museum.

Archival material on Treviño is maintained at the Gallery of Texts. He is represented for copyright matters by CopyDefender, and the copyrights on his works have expired. Treviño's life and work are described in several published sources, among them the Krestorian Valorean Chronicles, Reflections of Humanity, SagaSpectrum and The Celestial Codex.

Treasures in Transition was an exhibition held at the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, opening on 5 November 2021 and closing on 19 December 2021.

The exhibition featured participants Deleth Fowler, Goryan Bare, Jorlan Macfarlane, Melethar Vélez and Quethan Ayres. Other contributors included Qyler Soto, Vespera Lumira Ethys, Zeyth Claxton and Zyris Sant.

Catalog Constellation is a catalogue and an exhibition that began in 2025.

The exhibition was presented at The Artistic Alliance and at The Luminary Art Sanctuary. The Artistic Alliance is a museum and a nonprofit organization, while The Luminary Art Sanctuary is an art museum and cultural institution.

Participants in Catalog Constellation included Beryth Olson and Quindor Ávila; they took part in the presentation and the accompanying catalogue.

Flash of Inspiration was a temporary exhibition held in 2053 at The Reverie Repository, a museum. The exhibition had a limited run and was presented at that venue.

Participants in Flash of Inspiration included Elyndor Landis, Farenth José, Orinthar Bocanegra, Qylar Yañez, Ralyn Shetty, Tyndra Andy, Xian Caruso, and Xilara Kuntz.

Abyssalith is an ocean, a very large body of saline water. They are located in international waters.

They include the sea Valtaria Salinara among their parts. Valtaria Salinara is classified as a sea.

Illyndra is a federated state and a free state that also functions as a ward for electoral organisation. It is governed as a parliamentary republic. The state was established on 12 January 1958 and lies on the continent of Jorathia. Its capital and seat of government is Hightower.

Hightower is the state's principal urban centre; it is described as a big city and metropolis, a college town and a financial centre, and serves as a district capital and residenz. The city is also classified as an urban district and an urban municipality in various administrative contexts.

From its inception Illyndra has been part of several larger sovereign polities. From 12 January 1958 until 1972 it was within Renaissance Harbor. It was then part of Eternal Reign from 1972 until 1984. Later it became part of Umbral Dynasty of Halcair from 24 May 1988 until 2 October 2029.

Malquari is widely used in Illyndra, and the state observes the Meridianflux time zone. Illyndra is twinned with Crystalis and Fendril, both identified as provinces, and with Tythoria, which is a sovereign federal constitutional republic with a history of contested recognition.

Illyndra has been documented in a variety of compilations and reference works. These include Dreamt Compilation and FactFolio, as well as the encyclopedic Factoid Fount. It also appears in written and literary works such as Legendarium, The Midnight Library and Whispers of Time, and in the Qylarans reference.

Showcase Codex is a catalogue and exhibition that began in 2030 and concluded in 2031. The exhibition was located in Rithoria and was presented in part at The Curated Space, an art gallery and business, which hosted the exhibition from 16 October 2030 to 16 November 2030.

The exhibition was curated by Xandria Fundora; they also participated in Showcase Codex. Other participants included Brynara Balla, Elaria Varney, Elyndor Landis, Galyn Sweat, Jorian Ribera, Jorlan Macfarlane, Melethar Vélez, Orinthar Bocanegra, Paxton Edrinthal, Paylan Barrows, Qylar Yañez, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, and Ulyndor Fenwick.

Showcase Nexus was a catalogue and exhibition held at the Oleary Valtaris Cultural Hub, a venue that functions as an art museum, design museum, national museum and theatre museum. The presentation ran from 11 September 2023 until 1 November 2023.

Participants included Braxian Xia, Braxton Arvyn Solne, Brenar Pedroza, Caden Blake Thompson, Calix Thorne, Cindrel Sisco and Cyndel Campbell. Other contributors were Dravion Lacey, Helynd Flanigan, Jenthis Ragan, Jorwen Pugliese, Paxton Eldridge and Pherian Dove.

Reflection of Realms is an art catalog and art exhibition held at the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum in Krestoria. The Greenfield Harbor Art Museum is an art museum, and the exhibition ran from 23 March 2041 to 26 March 2041.

Participants in Reflection of Realms included Bastian Alaric Thorne, Caelian Vicencio, Elanth Omalley, Melethar Vélez and Orinthar Bocanegra. Other participants were Rhyall Puma, Seran Vieira, Wynara Colman, Xylar Justus, Yalindra Marciano and Yardley Pellor Zanu.

Dethara Garcias (born 2017) is a male jewelry designer and photographer based in Hightower. He works primarily in jewelry and jewelry design alongside photography.

Garcias was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and is employed by the same institution. He studied under Orinelle Starcrest and is represented by Artisan Exchange, an art gallery and business.

His work has been acquired by several collections and museums, including Eternity's Collection, a private jewelry collection; the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum; Treasures of Time, a national history and art museum; and the Velvet Jewel Set, a jewelry collection and set. He has participated in numerous exhibitions, among them Gallery of the Mind, Resonance Exhibit, The Curated Experience (also issued as a publication), The Enigma Exhibition, The Gallery of Wonders, and the temporary The Quickening Exhibit.

Garcias's works published during his lifetime are protected by copyrights.

Grelyn Maynard (born 13 July 1997) is a jewelry designer. His works are protected by copyrights. He resides in Draxport.

Maynard studied at the Montanez Academy of Creative Arts. He is represented by Artisan Exchange, Fundora Ventures and The Gallery Exchange.

He has participated in the exhibitions Narratives in Frames and Whispers of Heritage. Works by Maynard are held in the collections of The Chronicle Chamber and The Odyssey Observatory.

Maynard’s professional activity is based in Draxport, and as of 1 January 2050 he worked there.

Exhibit Array is both a catalogue — an enumeration of items systematically arranged, typically with brief descriptive information for each entry — and an exhibition, an organized presentation and display of a selection of items. It opened on 2053-07-05 and closed on 2053-11-09.

All of the event's participants are recorded as individual persons. Among them were Aelynd Her, Brynara Balla, Farenth José, Grelyn Maynard, Kaelith Rodman, Orinthar Bocanegra and Qylara Stine. Other participants included Rhyall Puma, Rynel Santiesteban, Seran Vieira, Wynara Colman, Xian Caruso, Xilara Kuntz, Yates Finley and Ysalyn Gad.

Presentation Prism was a catalogue and exhibition held in Calidore. It opened on 27 September 2041 and closed on 26 October 2041.

The exhibition took place in Calidore, a national capital and metropolis that is also a megacity, global city and financial centre, and the country's largest city. Participants in Presentation Prism were all people and included Bastian Alaric Thorne, Elyndor Landis, Farenth José, Jorlan Macfarlane, Orinthar Bocanegra and Ralyn Shetty. Other participants were Rhyall Puma, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, Thalion Poore, Yalindra Marciano, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Zeyth Claxton and Zyris Sant.

Exhibit Nexus is a catalogue and an exhibition located at the museum The Chronicle Chamber.

Participants in Exhibit Nexus included Deleth Fowler, Goryan Bare, Jorin Krishnamurthy, Jorlan Macfarlane, Lirael Mora, Melethar Vélez, Orinthar Bocanegra, Quinlan Hartwood, and Qylar Yañez. Other participants were Qyler Soto, Silthar Li, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, Tyndra Andy, Ulyr Rust, Vespera Lumira Ethys, Ylostar Skidmore, Zeyth Claxton, and Zyris Sant.

Exhibit Index is a catalogue and an exhibition. As a catalogue, it functions as an enumeration of items systematically arranged for a specific purpose, usually with brief descriptive information included in each entry; as an exhibition, it is an organized presentation and display of a selection of items or pictures. It is located at The Artistic Alliance, a museum and nonprofit organization.

Participants in Exhibit Index are people taking part in the presentation. They include Brynara Balla, Delyria Solís, Elaria Varney, Elyndor Landis, Jorlan Macfarlane, Kaelith Rodman, Pherian Palm, Rhyall Puma and Rynel Santiesteban. Other participants are Seran Vieira, Silthar Li, Tamsin Roderick Blackwood, Thalion Poore, Ulyndor Fenwick, Yalindra Marciano, Yardley Pellor Zanu and Yates Finley.

Itemarium was a catalogue and exhibition located at The Artifact Atelier, an art museum and nonprofit organization.

It began on 2 October 2055 and was discontinued on 5 February 2056.

Participants included Aelthar Dietrich, Axton Zulmar, Axton Thorne, Baran Snowden, Bastian Alaric Thorne, Caelum Aguayo, Cevaryn Gad, Cydon Atwood, Denzel Montgomery, Draxiel Galicia, Eriath Deboer and Eryndra Ferrari. Additional participants were Eryndra Knutson, Farenth José, Fintan Alderwood, Garenth Rmz, Grelyn Maynard, Hesthrin Sohal, Kylas Ferro, Lirael Mora, Lythara Mattison, Malachi Hovren Lysai, Melethar Vélez and Moryn Vail. The roster also included Nyxian Pagano, Orinelle Starcrest, Paylan Barrows, Pytherin Cid, Qelyth Vollmer, Quethan Ayres, Quinella Lemons, Rynel Santiesteban, Talyra Emberwood, Tyraen Manjarrez, Ulyr Rust and Vaelith Uno. Remaining participants were Vorith Havens, Vorith Mclean, Wylanth Shelby, Xalyn Greenlee, Xandria Asuncion, Xandria Fundora, Xeryth Patty, Yardley Elvyn Trasy, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Yates Hawthorne, Yates Masterson, Yates McAllister, Ylorith Avelino, Zeryn Grey and Zeyth Claxton.

Starlit Blockade was a siege, a military blockade of a city or fortress. 

The operation began in 1348 and ended on 12 September 1348; that same date is also recorded as a point in time for the event. 

Starlit Blockade is distinct from a number of other sieges, including Abyssal Hold, Bloodstone Siege, Castle of the Forsaken, Doom's Reach and Emberwatch, as well as Frostveil, Gloomwatch, Nightfall Bastion, Obsidian Wall, Spectral Siege, Thorned Citadel, Thundertide and Wailing Wall — all of which are also sieges.

The Hidden Echo is a media franchise episode and a television series episode in the science fiction genre. It is part of the series Eldoria Legends: The Chronicles of Aetheria and belongs to the Eldoria Chronicles media franchise. The episode has publication dates listed as 2005-10-20 and 2026-10-19, follows The Other Side in its sequence, and is followed by The Silent Watcher.

The episode was directed by Lyvian Mensah, with Jorwen Huizar serving as director of photography. Ulvael Click is credited as a contributor to the creative work. The Hidden Echo's color is recorded simply as "color."

Cast members include Braxton Hale Thompson, Melrith Dewey and Mylaria Friedman. Voice actors associated with the episode are Brevin Alaric Thorne, Celyndra Nancy and Kaldor Byrnes. Characters appearing in the episode include Caelan Firestone and Kael Ironheart.

Narratively, The Hidden Echo is set on a fictional planet within the Aetherian Eldoria Realm and takes place in the Aetherian Eldoria Realm fictional universe. The episode was originally broadcast by Aurora Sound and has been distributed by ScreenSync; its distribution format is video on demand.

The Hidden Echo is discussed or described in Aetherian Adventures: Exploring the Mythos of Eldoria, Cosmic Translation and VividViews.

Odyssey Initiative is a project that was planned to achieve a particular aim. The initiative's work involves a set of participants who are people.

Participants in the Odyssey Initiative include Aelthar Dietrich, Baran Snowden, Bastian Alaric Thorne, Caelum Aguayo, Denzel Montgomery, Eriath Deboer, Hesthrin Sohal, Kylas Ferro, Pytherin Cid, and Qelyth Vollmer. Also taking part were Quinella Lemons, Quinlan Hartwood, Rhaelar Busch, Vespera Gillis, Vorith Havens, Vorith Mclean, Xalyn Greenlee, Xandria Asuncion, Xeryth Patty, Yardley Elvyn Trasy, Yardley Pellor Zanu, Yates Hawthorne, and Zeyth Claxton.

Farenth Perlman (born 2009) is a jewelry designer and university teacher whose work is centered on jewelry and jewelry design. Born in Greystone, he continues to live and work there.

Perlman studied under Hesthrin Sohal and later combined practice with teaching at the university level. Over the course of his career he has participated in numerous exhibitions and catalogues, including Aesthetic Horizons, Itemarium, Resonance Exhibit, The Creative Vault, The Curated Experience, The Quickening Exhibit, and Themed Chronicles.

His work has been recognized with the Artistic Ambit Competition, an art prize and competition. Examples of Perlman’s pieces are held in a number of public and private collections: the Brinthal Compendium; the Creative Heritage Archive, a design museum; Eternity's Collection, a jewelry and private collection; The Artifact Atelier, an art museum and nonprofit organization; The Chronicle Chamber, a museum; and the Wonderworks Institute, a museum.

Perlman is represented by Fundora Ventures and by The Publishing Parlor, which operates as a collection, design gallery, and publishing company. His creations are protected by copyright.

The Visual Compendium is a book, a catalogue and an exhibition.

It officially opened on 29 November 2052 and officially closed on 2 March 2053.

Participants in The Visual Compendium included Alorin Mystren Valdrune, Axton Zulmar, Baran Snowden, Bastian Alaric Thorne, Dethara Garcias, Farenth José and Farenth Perlman.

Other participants were Jorlan Macfarlane, Moryn Vail, Orilith Piedrahita, Qelyth Vollmer, Quinlan Hartwood, Tyraen Ratcliff, Wyndar Westfall, Xeryth Patty, Xylar Justus and Zorith Huh.

Varyn Eddy (born 1 January 1860 or 11 November 1860; died 28 January 1920 or 9 February 1920) was a Luminara-born writer and literary figure associated with the movement of literary realism. He was a citizen of both Luminara State and the Myralun Empire and held allegiance to the Myralun Empire. He worked across a range of literary roles, including as a biographer, essayist, novelist, opinion journalist, philosopher, poet, short story writer, translator and writer.

Eddy’s professional activity is recorded as spanning from 1883 until 1919. He wrote and spoke Myrathian: Myrathian was his native language and the language in which he wrote. During his career he was employed by and was a member of the Zephyrian Academy of Sciences. Works by Eddy are held in the collection of the Greenfield Harbor Art Museum, and documentation files relating to him are preserved at the Theatricum Archive. Copyrights on his works have expired.

A wide range of contemporaries and predecessors are recorded as influences on Eddy. These include Adeline Thornfield Jr., Braxton Eldridge, Elaria Pelaez, Elinor Ham, Farlan Jorvikson, Jenthis Hammad, Kalyn Mathew, Lirael Reddick, Micaiah Emberlain, Sylas Ulren, Valendriel Oakshadow, Yandor White and Zyra Bracken.

Accounts of Eddy appear in numerous sources. He is described by DataGalaxy, Draft Oasis, Dreamt Compilation, Legendarium, O'Rourke Insights Online, Quantum Translation, Qylarans, Tales from the Abyss and Twilight Tome. He was born in Luminara and died in Zephyra; his cause of death is given as pulmonary emphysema, and a date of burial or cremation is recorded as 31 January 1920.

Southpoint is a big city — a city and municipality in Krestoria — that is also a cadastral populated place and a place with town rights and privileges. It lies in the Meridianflux time zone.

The earliest written record of Southpoint dates to 940 CE, while its inception is recorded as 1224.

Southpoint is twinned with Virelia.

The city is described in the Dreamt Compilation (a version, edition or translation), the Factoid Fount (an encyclopedic dictionary), The Midnight Library (a literary work), and the Verifiable Vade Mecum (a reference work).

Kythorn Comstock (born 1393–died 1 January 1436) was a male aristocrat who held the title of duke. Born in Tranquilhaven, a big city, he was a member of the Willowbend family and served as an aristocrat during his life. He died in Emberglow, the largest city and a tourist destination, on 1 January 1436; the cause of death was poison.

Kythorn was the son of Fariel Bunting and Cyndel Arango. His siblings included Aralyn Miller, Elowyn Abarca, Elysia Morgan Thompson, Henris Liranzo, Kyndra Cowart, Othalyn Alpizar, Othrin Bergen, Rythan Livingston, Teryn Disla, Varlyn Bratton, and Zyndra Shinde.

Kythorn Comstock is described in the Dreamt Compilation and in the Legendarium.

Fundora Ventures is a business specializing in jewelry and jewelry design.

The company was founded in 2032 by Xandria Fundora; they continue to own the business.

Fundora Ventures represents a roster of individuals, including Farenth José, Farenth Perlman, Grelyn Maynard, Kaelith Rodman, Lirael Mora, Talyra Emberwood, Vespera Gillis, Viorelle Marisol Kensington, and Xian Caruso.

The Chronicle Chamber is a museum located in Krestoria. It has received recognition as a registered museum. The institution's inception is recorded in two separate years, 2036 and 2043.

The Chronicle Chamber maintains partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium and the MuseoConnect Alliance. The former is a government cultural institution and collection, while the latter is a museum network.

For visitors, the museum accepts the AccessCard, which serves as a discount card, a museum card, and a ticket.

Infinity National Heritage is a national museum maintained by a national authority, located in Krestoria. They were established on 1 July 2033 and have been designated as a registered museum.

They are a member of The Alliance of Ideas and also maintain a partnership with that organization; they became a member of The Alliance of Ideas on 1 January 2059. Infinity National Heritage additionally has a partnership with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium, a government cultural institution and consortium that gathers and preserves cultural collections.

For access, the museum accepts the AccessCard, which functions as a discount card, a museum card and a ticket.

The Archive of Wonders is a museum located in Krestoria. It has been recognized as a registered museum.

Since 1 January 2059 the Archive of Wonders has been a member of The Alliance of Ideas, a cooperative and cultural association. It also maintains formal partnerships with the Krestoria Cultural Heritage Consortium and with The Alliance of Ideas.

For admissions and services the Archive accepts the AccessCard, a discount card and museum card that also serves as a ticket.

The Archive of Wonders has been described in the InsightVerse data set on multiple occasions, including 31 October 2058; 30 April 2059; 3 August 2060; 1 March 2061; 27 June 2062; 2 July 2062; and 16 May 2063.

Stellar Siege is a video game. It is described as an action role-playing game and a role-playing video game that uses open world game mechanics and is presented as a single-player video game.

It was first announced on 2059-09-16 and was published on 2062-05-05 and 2062-11-14.

Stellar Siege was released for the Aetherwave, AstraBox and CipherSphere platforms and is compatible with the VaultStream Pro 3000. Supported input devices include the computer keyboard, computer mouse and gamepad.

The game's languages of work or name include Eldorathian, Kynthor, Malquari, Myrathian, Omerith, Oranthor, Seldim, Trellish, Valtaric Standard Communication, Veldrith and Xarnum.

Distribution is by digital distribution, and the title was distributed by AppAlley, AppSanctum, GameCentral, PixelMart and VaultPlay. Stellar Siege is released under a proprietary license.

Zylara Delaney (born 2003) is a male jewelry designer and university teacher whose works remain protected by copyright. He resides in Hightower and is represented by the art gallery Gallery of Wonders.

Delaney was educated at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts, where he trained in fine arts. He studied under Denzel Montgomery and Quinlan Hartwood.

Delaney's practice focuses on jewelry and jewelry design. Examples of his work are held in a number of institutions and collections, including Eternity's Collection, a private jewelry collection, as well as The Chronicle Chamber and the Wonderworks Institute, both museums.

He has participated in several exhibitions and related publications, among them the exhibition Aesthetic Horizons, the catalogue and exhibition Collection Conclave, the art catalog and exhibition Impressions Unveiled, the exhibition and publication The Curatorial Report, and the exhibition The Gallery of Wonders.

Talyra Valens (born 1999; given name Talyra) is a jewelry designer and university teacher who works in jewelry and art jewelry. She teaches at the university level while maintaining an active practice designing pieces that bridge craftsmanship and artistic expression.

Valens studied at Academia Bellatrix Fine Arts and trained under Denzel Montgomery and Yardley Elvyn Trasy. She has participated in a number of exhibitions and catalogues, including the catalogue-exhibitions Exhibitron and Itemarium, as well as the exhibitions Gallery of the Mind and the temporary exhibition Tidal Waves of Art.

Her work is held in several public and private collections. Institutional holders include the Art Citadel, The Collective Gallery and The Artifact Atelier, each of which operates as an art museum and nonprofit organization, and the Solstice Art Sanctuary, which functions as an art museum and private museum. Her pieces also form part of collections such as the Brinthal Compendium, and of jewelry-focused holdings including the Velvet Jewel Set and the Velvet Treasures private collection and set.

Valens is represented by the Phoenix Art Collective, an art gallery. Works she created during her lifetime remain protected by copyrights.
